en.text: First, we asked the branch for permission.
Once they gave us approval,
we began to make preparations for the assembly,
though we had absolutely nothing.
So one brother lent us a property for the assembly site.
Our brothers have brought many different skills to the project.
There are metalworkers,
cabinetmakers, and bricklayers.
Many brothers
have given of their resources
and used their abilities
so that this project could go ahead.
This has really made us stand out here.
People were asking each other:
“What is happening here?”
and “Who paid for all of this?”
They say people are surprised at how many workers are coming to help.
And I wonder,
‘If this is getting attention now,
what will the assembly be like?’
A comfortable, practical, and secure Assembly Hall
was constructed using materials acquired locally.
Expectations grew as the special day drew closer,
and when it finally arrived, those in attendance
experienced something truly moving.
With Jehovah’s help, many interested ones,
along with our brothers and sisters, have come here today
to celebrate our first assembly in the Bribri language.
Friends, this is wonderful!
When the program started in Bribri, I cried.
I’m so happy
to have participated in the assembly,
especially because it’s in my own language.
It’s what we wanted.
We hope it continues just like this.
We walked a long way to invite these people,
and to see them here, it makes me very happy.
The information presented in the local language
touched many hearts.
This was truly a historic event
for our indigenous brothers in Costa Rica.
Jehovah has made it possible
for more people in this isolated region to enjoy his spiritual blessing.

ko.text: 여호와 하느님은 인간이 고난을 겪기를 바라지 않으셨습니다.
행복하게 사는 데 필요한 모든 것을 주셨습니다.
첫 인간 부부가 하느님이 가지신 권위에
무엇이 옳고 그른지 스스로 결정하는 길을 택했습니다.
교사가 문제를 푸는 방법이 틀렸다고 하면서,
자기가 맞는 방법을 알고 있다고 주장합니다.
물론 반항적인 학생들을 그냥 혼낼 수도 있습니다.
하지만 그렇게 하면 다른 학생들은 어떻게 생각하겠습니까?
교사가 자기가 틀렸다는 게 드러날까 봐 그런다고 생각하면서
교사를 더는 존경하지 않을 수도 있습니다.
그 학생이 원하는 방법대로 문제를 풀어 보게 하면 어떻게 될까요?
누가 가르칠 자격이 있는지를 모두가 알게 될 것입니다.
지성을 가진 모든 창조물에게 큰 영향을 미칠 것이었습니다.
여호와께서는 그 점을 알고 계셨기 때문에
사탄이 이 세상을 통치해 보도록 시간을 주셨습니다.
사탄의 통치는 이루 말할 수 없는 고통을 가져왔습니다.
하지만 여호와께서 인간을 통치할 권리와 능력을 갖고 계시다는 것이
그분은 사탄의 반역으로 인한 모든 피해를
이 질문들과 그 밖의 질문들에 대한 성경의 답을 알아보려면

en.text: Why does God allow suffering?
Jehovah God didn’t intend for humans to suffer.
On the contrary,
he gave the first human couple
a wonderful start.
But Satan, a rebel angel,
called God a liar
and influenced the first humans
to reject God’s authority.
When Adam and Eve disobeyed God,
they chose to follow Satan.
They rebelled against Jehovah
and decided for themselves
what was right and wrong.
Was Satan correct?
Could humans rule themselves successfully
without help from God?
Time would be needed to settle
the crucial issues raised by the rebels.
To illustrate:
A rebellious student claims
that the teacher’s method of instruction is wrong.
He insists that he knows a much better way.
Some students think that he is right,
and they also become rebellious.
What should the teacher do?
He has the authority to reprimand the rebellious students.
But what effect would that choice have
on the other students?
They may lose respect for the teacher,
thinking that he is afraid of being proved wrong.
But suppose the teacher allows
the student to show the class his  method.
Then it would be proved to all present
who is qualified to teach.
Jehovah has done something similar
to what the teacher does.
When Satan challenged Jehovah,
millions of angels were watching.
How Jehovah handled the rebellion
would greatly affect all those angels
and eventually all intelligent creation.
Knowing this, Jehovah allowed Satan
to rule this world for a time.
Satan’s rule has caused
untold pain and suffering.
However,
once Jehovah’s right and ability to rule
is established beyond any doubt,
Jehovah will undo
all the damage caused by Satan’s rebellion.
At that time,
only people who choose
to follow God’s standards
will inhabit the earth.
Until then,
how can you cope with suffering?
Where can you find comfort?
To learn more about what the Bible says
on this and many other topics,
go to jw.org.

cn.text: 上帝为什么容许苦难存在？
耶和华上帝并没有想过要人经历苦难
他让人类的祖先有一个完美的开始
可是
撒但这个反叛上帝的天使声称上帝说谎
并引诱亚当和夏娃拒绝上帝的统治
亚当和夏娃不听从上帝
其实等于选择跟随撒但
他们反叛耶和华
按自己的标准决定什么是对、什么是错
撒但说的是真的吗？
人真的不需要上帝的统治
也能管理好自己吗？
要解决这些叛徒挑起的重大争议
是需要时间的
打个比方
有一个叛逆的学生声称老师教错了
他自认为懂得更好的解题方法
有些学生认为他说得对
也表现出叛逆的态度
这位老师该怎么做呢？
他当然有权训斥那些叛逆的学生
但如果他这样做，其他学生会怎么想呢？
他们也许会认为老师真的教错了
怕被人揭穿
这些学生可能就不再尊重老师了
但如果老师让这个学生给同学演示
他自己的解题方法
那么所有人就能看出谁才有资格当老师了
耶和华处理问题的方法跟这位老师很类似
撒但挑战耶和华的权威时
千千万万的天使都在看着
耶和华怎么处理这个反叛事件
将会深深影响所有天使以及全人类
所以，耶和华容许撒但暂时统治这个世界
撒但的统治使这个世界充满灾难和痛苦
不过，一旦事实证明
只有耶和华才有权力和能力施行统治
耶和华就会采取行动
彻底消除撒但造成的所有苦难
到时，只有选择按照上帝标准生活的人
才会永远居住在地球上
在这个日子来到前
想了解更多内容
请上jw.org网站

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—특별 전파 활동이 놀라운 결과를 거두다

ko.text: 바울과 그의 동료들은 기쁜 마음으로 그 초대를 받아들였으며,
그곳에서 전파 활동을 하면서 많은 좋은 결과를 거두었습니다.
여호와께서 그들의 노력을 풍성히 축복해 주셨던 것이죠.
오늘날 봉사 위원회는 1세기에 바울이 그랬던 것처럼
성령의 인도를 따르기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
여전히 세계 전역의 여러 나라에서는 철저히 증거하기 위해
그러한 나라의 지부들에게 도움을 주기 위해
그리고 다른 나라에 사는 본이 되는 형제 자매들이
그러한 초대를 받아들인 전도인들 중 상당수는
최근 몇 년 동안에는 이러한 특별 전파 활동이
이 특별 전파 활동으로 인해 어떤 결과가 있었습니까?
이 특별 전파 활동에 참여했고, 약 3만 부의 출판물을 전했습니다.
많은 난민들이 좋은 소식에 아주 호의적인 반응을 보였죠.
어떤 사람들은 전시대에 있는 전도인에게 와서
성경에 어떤 내용이 있는지 알고 싶어요” 하고 말하기도 했죠.
이 특별 활동은 아랍어 지역 대회를 끝으로 막을 내렸습니다.
이 대회는 아랍어 밭에서 이정표가 된 행사였습니다.
2009년 이래로 그곳에서 네 차례의 특별 전파 활동이 있었는데,
유럽 전역에서 온 전도인 1782명이 이 활동에 참여했습니다.
그런데 그해에 특별 전파 활동이 조직되었고,
그로 인해 증인들은 고쇼라는 남자를 만나게 되었습니다.
교회가 진리를 가르치지 않는다는 것을 깨달았습니다.
그래서 교회 예배에 가는 걸 그만두었지만
그런데 특별 활동 기간 중에 길에서 증인을 만난 거죠.
증인들이 성경에 대해 이야기를 꺼내려고 하자
그러자 고쇼는 “그럼 우리 집에 오셔도 됩니다”
고쇼와 아내 이반카와 아들 보고밀이 연구를 시작한 겁니다.
세네갈에는 아직 전파되지 않은 구역이 매우 많습니다.
일례로 2015년 기준으로 전도인 대 인구의 비율이
봉사 위원회는 최근에 세네갈에서 세 차례에 걸쳐
포르투갈에서 온 한 자매는 어떤 여자에게
하느님께서 죽은 사람을 부활시키실 거라는 걸 아는지 물었습니다.
그 여자는 코웃음을 치면서 이렇게 말했습니다.
다시 살아날 거라고요? 아니, 그게 말이 돼요?”
그분은 아주머니의 남편을 부활시켜 주실 거예요”
자매가 확신 있게 말하자 그 여자는 “그게 정말 가능한가요?”
자매는 하느님의 말씀에서 그렇게 알려 준다고 대답했습니다.
그러자 그 여자는 너무 기뻐서 춤을 췄죠.
그 여자는 기뻐하면서 또다시 춤을 췄습니다.
루마니아에서는 회중이 없는 구역에 사는 사람들이
특별 활동이 진행된 두 달 동안 전도인들은
그 결과 1000건이 넘는 성서 연구가 시작되었죠.
하지만 루미니차는 자신이 가진 성경 질문에 대한 답을 찾지 못했고,
코스텔은 사제들의 위선적인 행동을 많이 봤습니다.
루미니차는 한 이웃으로부터 여호와의 증인에 대해 들었는데,
그는 친척과 전화로 성서 연구를 하고 있었습니다.
전도하러 온 것을 보고 매우 기뻤습니다.
곧바로 그는 성서 연구를 하기로 했습니다.
얼마 안 있어 남편 코스텔과 두 십 대 자녀도
이 가족은 성경에서 배운 것을 바로바로 적용했습니다.
증인들이 생일을 지키지 않는다는 것을 알게 된 그 가족은
우리가 하는 일 중에 여호와께서 싫어하시는 일들이 또 있나요?
그런 건 다 그만두고 싶으니까 전부 알려 주세요!”
7개월 만에 가족 모두가 회중과 함께 봉사를 하기 시작했습니다.
마을에서 성서 연구 세 건을 사회하게 되었습니다.
그리고 여호와의 증인을 만난 지 1년이 되었을 때
코스텔과 루미니차는 처음 참석한 지역 대회에서 침례를 받았습니다.
두 자녀도 영적으로 잘 발전하고 있습니다.
거의 전파되지 않았거나 회중이 없는 구역에서
많은 그리스도인이 힘을 합쳐 노력한 덕분에
아마존 강을 따라 사는 많은 사람들에게 증거하기 위해
지부 구역 내에 사는 전도인들에게 그 활동에 참여하도록 권했고,
만 명이 넘는 형제 자매들이 그 활동에 자원했습니다.
한 회중 구역에서는 약 400명이나 되는 사람이
그중 얼마의 사람은 아마존 지역으로 이주하기로 결정했습니다.
그런데 2016년 7월 무렵에는 그 수가 크게 증가했습니다.
아마존 지역으로 완전히 ‘건너왔고’ 7개의 새로운 회중이 생겼습니다.
분명 여호와께서는 이러한 전파 활동을 풍성히 축복하고 계십니다.
우리 모두도 자신의 상황에서 최선을 다해
좋은 소식을 널리 전해야겠다는 결심이 더욱더 강해집니다.

en.text: In the first century,
the apostle Paul received a vision
in which he was invited to “step over into Macedonia.”
Paul and his traveling companions eagerly accepted the invitation,
and they enjoyed Jehovah’s rich blessing
as evidenced in the positive results they experienced in their ministry.
Today, the Service Committee is as eager
to follow the lead of the holy spirit
as Paul was in the first century.
There are still many parts of the world
where branches need publishers
to “step over” and help them give a thorough witness.
To meet the need, the Service Committee has arranged for such branches
to receive assistance by means of special preaching campaigns.
Local publishers
and exemplary brothers and sisters
from other lands are invited to participate.
Often, such publishers who respond to the initial invitation,
later decide to move to these areas of need.
In recent years, special preaching campaigns
have been held in Africa, Asia,
Europe, and South America.
What have been some of the results of such special preaching campaigns?
In the recent past,
more than a million Arabic-speaking refugees
have fled to Europe.
The Service Committee arranged for the Central Europe branch
to hold a special preaching campaign to reach these refugees.
More than 600 publishers
from different parts of the world participated,
and they distributed some 30,000 pieces of literature.
Many of the refugees have been very receptive to the good news,
even approaching publishers at the literature carts and asking:
“Can you help us? What does the Bible actually teach?”
This special campaign concluded
with an Arabic-language regional convention,
which was a milestone for the Arabic field.
Over 1,600 attended
from 43 different countries.
Approximately 25 percent of those in attendance
were interested persons.
Outstanding campaigns have also been held in Bulgaria.
Bulgaria reported a publisher-to-population ratio
Since then, four special preaching campaigns have been held there
and 1,782 publishers
from countries throughout Europe participated.
They placed over 175,000 pieces of literature,
started 1,775 Bible studies,
and 8 congregations and 7 groups have been formed.
Consider one example:
Before 2010,
there were no Witnesses in the village of Karlovo.
That year a special preaching campaign was organized.
As a result, a man named Gosho was contacted.
From his own reading of the Bible,
he realized that the local churches do not teach the truth.
So he stopped attending church services
but never stopped praying.
During the campaign, he met Jehovah’s Witnesses on the street.
They wanted to talk with him about the Bible,
but he interrupted them and asked,
“Do you believe that Jesus is equal to God?”
The brothers answered, “No.”
“Do you believe that God is a trinity?
Do you collect a tithe?”
The brothers again answered, “No.”
“Then you are welcome in my home,” said Gosho.
Immediately, a Bible study was started
with him and his wife, Ivanka,
and their son, Bogomil.
Both Ivanka and Bogomil
are now baptized.
Senegal has a vast untouched territory.
the country’s publisher-to-population ratio
was 1 to more than 12,000.
In recent years, the Service Committee arranged
for three special preaching campaigns in Senegal.
One sister from Portugal asked a householder
if she believed that God had the power to resurrect the dead.
In a ridiculing way, the woman replied:
“You mean my dead husband
“who’s been dead a long time will come out of the grave?
Is this what you are telling me?”
The sister answered:
“That is what God has promised to do.
He will resurrect him alive in the flesh.”
Seeing that the sister was serious, the woman asked,
“Is it really possible?”
The sister answered, “It is written in God’s Word.”
With great joy,
the woman started to dance.
The sister highlighted information on the resurrection
in the Listen to God  brochure.
Again, the woman started dancing with joy.
In Romania, there are some four and a half million people
who live in unassigned territories.
During a two-month campaign,
publishers covered 1,359 localities
with a population of 1.8 million.
The publishers started more than 1,000 Bible studies.
Here is just one experience:
Costel and Luminitza were very active in their Orthodox religion.
However, Luminitza could not find answers
to her Bible questions,
and Costel saw much hypocrisy with the priests.
Luminitza heard about Jehovah’s Witnesses from her neighbor
who studied the Bible by telephone with a Witness relative.
During the special campaign,
two brothers knocked on the couple’s door.
Luminitza was happy
that Jehovah’s Witnesses had finally come to preach in her village.
She immediately accepted a Bible study.
Eventually, Costel and their two teenage children
joined in the study.
The family immediately put into practice what they learned from the Bible.
After the family learned on their own
that Witnesses do not celebrate birthdays,
they told their study conductors:
“We don’t want to keep sinning against Jehovah.
“How many other things are we doing that Jehovah hates?
Tell us everything that we are doing wrong so that we can stop!”
In seven months,
the entire family began preaching with the congregation.
After one month of sharing in the ministry,
they had started three Bible studies in the village.
One year after their first contact with Jehovah’s Witnesses,
Costel and Luminitza were baptized
at their first regional convention.
Now Costel is a ministerial servant,
and both children are progressing very well spiritually.
Have you ever shared in preaching in seldom-worked or unassigned territories?
Such concerted efforts have yielded
great success in many countries.
For example,
the Brazil branch invited publishers throughout the branch territory
to participate in a preaching effort
that focused on the thousands living along the Amazon River.
More than 10,000 local brothers and sisters gave their support.
In one congregation’s territory,
some 400 people requested a Bible study.
Many of those who participated in the preaching effort
described it as “a life-changing experience,”
and some decided to move to the Amazon region.
In December 2015,
5 congregations in this region had a total
of 6 elders, 2 ministerial servants,
9 regular pioneers, and 50 publishers.
By July 2016,
those numbers had increased tremendously.
In those 5 congregations, the 6 elders
increased to 22,
the 2 ministerial servants increased to 17,
the 9 regular pioneers became 80,
and the 50 publishers grew to 177.
In total, over 865 publishers from Brazil
permanently ‘stepped over’ into the Amazon region,
and 7 new congregations were formed.
It’s clear that Jehovah is richly blessing such preaching efforts.
Reports such as this,
strengthen our resolve to do all that our circumstances allow
to reach as many as possible with the good news.

cn.text: 公元1世纪
使徒保罗在异象中看见有一个人说
“请到马其顿来帮助我们吧”
保罗和他的传道同伴
积极地响应了这个邀请
他们有很好的传道成果
得到了耶和华丰盛的赐福
今天  中央长老团的传道委员会
也很渴望像保罗那样顺应圣灵的指引
全球还有很多分部辖下的地区
都需要更多传道员前来协助
才能做彻底的见证
因此  传道委员会帮助这些分部
安排了一些特别传道活动
受邀参加的有本地的传道员
和其他地区堪作榜样的弟兄姐妹
他们很多人参加完特别传道活动后
都决定搬到当地服务
最近几年
开展过特别传道活动的地区
有非洲  亚洲  欧洲和南美洲
这些特别传道活动取得了哪些成果呢?
在过去的几年中
有超过一百万说阿拉伯语的难民逃到欧洲
于是传道委员会为中欧分部
安排了一次特别的传道活动
来帮助这些难民
来自世界各地的600多位传道员踊跃参与
分发了大约3万份出版物
许多难民都对好消息反应良好
他们甚至会主动走到手推车旁
问传道员说
你们能帮助我们吗?
我想知道圣经到底说了什么
后来我们举办了一次阿拉伯语的区域大会
为这次特别传道活动画上了圆满的句号
这次大会是阿拉伯语传道地区的一个里程碑
有来自43个国家超过1600人参加大会
其中有接近四分之一
是前来参加的感兴趣人士
保加利亚的特别传道活动也很成功
保加利亚的传道员与人口比例是1:4600
从那时起
我们举办了四次特别传道活动
欧洲各地共计1782位传道员前来参加
他们分发了超过17万5000份出版物
建立圣经讨论1775个
成立了8群会众和7个小组
我们来看一个例子
2010年之前
卡尔洛沃小镇还没有一位耶和华见证人
那一年我们举办了一次特别传道活动
当时我们找到一个男子  名叫戈肖
他自己阅读圣经时发现
教堂里说的并不是真理
于是他不再上教堂了
但是依然坚持祷告
在那次特别传道活动中
戈肖在街上遇到了耶和华见证人
我们的弟兄想跟他聊圣经
但他却先问了几个问题
你们相信耶稣就是上帝吗?
弟兄回答说  不相信啊
那你们相信上帝是三位一体的吗?
你们会收取什一奉献吗?
我们的弟兄还是回答  不
这时戈肖说  那欢迎你们来我家
很快  弟兄们就和他
还有他的妻子伊万卡
和儿子博戈米尔开始讨论圣经
现在伊万卡和博戈米尔都受浸了
塞內加尔也有很大一片区域还没有传道员去传道
这里的传道员与人口比例低于1:12000
近几年
传道委员会在那个地区
安排了三次特别传道活动
一位来自葡萄牙的姐妹问一个妇女
是否相信上帝有能力复活死人
这个妇女带着嘲笑的口吻反问姐妹说
你的意思是我丈夫死了那么久
还能从坟墓里出来?
你开玩笑吧?
这个姐妹说
这确实是上帝答应会做的事
他一定会复活你的丈夫
让他在地上复活
看到我们的姐妹表情很认真
这个妇女又问
你说的是真的吗?
姐妹说
这已经写在了上帝的话语里
这时  妇女高兴得不得了
竟然跳起舞来
姐妹把《要听从上帝》册子里复活的內容给她看
看到后  这个妇女又高兴地手舞足蹈
在罗马尼亚  有大约450万人
住在没有传道员传道的地区
在一次为期两个月的传道活动中
传道员去了1359个地方
住在这些地方的人口接近180万
结果传道员建立了超过1000个圣经讨论
我想分享一个经历
科斯特尔和妻子卢米尼察
原本是活跃的东正教徒
不过卢米尼察还是对圣经有很多疑问
而科斯特尔也看到牧师有很多虚伪行径
卢米尼察听说过她的邻居
通过电话跟耶和华见证人学习圣经
在这次特别传道活动时
有两个弟兄来到了这对夫妻的家门口
卢米尼察很高兴
因为耶和华见证人终于到他们的小镇传道了
他们很快就开始学习圣经
后来
科斯特尔和两个十几岁的孩子也开始学习
这家人马上就把学到的实践出来
他们自己了解到耶和华见证人不庆祝生日
就跟圣经老师说
我们不想再得罪耶和华了
我们还做了什么事是耶和华讨厌的
通通都告诉我们吧
我们再也不做了
七个月后
这家人开始参与会众的传道
他们传道一个月之后
就在小镇上建立了三个圣经讨论
这对夫妻开始学习后仅仅一年
就在他们参加的第一个区域大会上受了浸
现在科斯特尔是一位助理仆人
他们的孩子也在属灵上进步得非常好
你有没有去过很少有人传道的地区
向那里的人传道呢?
大家齐心协力  努力工作
在许多国家都有良好的成果
例如
巴西分部曾邀请分部辖下地区的传道员
去亚马逊河流域
专门向那里的数千名居民传道
有超过一万名当地的弟兄姐妹积极响应
在一个会众负责的地区中
有大约400人想要学习圣经
许多弟兄姐妹觉得参加这次特别传道活动
改变了他们的一生
当中不少人也决定搬到亚马逊河流域
这个地区总共只有五群会众
六位长老  两位助理仆人
九位先驱以及50位传道员
但到了2016年7月
这些数字就大幅增长
在原来那五群会众里
长老由6人增加到22人
助理仆人由两人增长到17人
正规先驱的人数由9人增长到80人
传道员的人数由50人增长到177人
那次特别传道活动后
有超过865位传道员扩大服务
搬到了亚马逊地区
帮助当地成立了七群新的会众
很显然
耶和华大大赐福给这些特别传道活动
这些报告也能加强你我的决心
让我们继续尽己所能
向更多人传讲王国的好消息

en.text: The text today is taken
from The Watchtower of 2016, January,
and the theme
“Be Compelled
by God’s ‘Indescribable Free Gift.’”
Well, this Memorial season really does move us
to contemplate what Jehovah has done for us,
and we should be compelled.
The Insight volume has a very interesting article
on this matter of forgiveness.
And in one of the statements it mentions
that “the Hebrew verb sa·lachʹ
“[for] (forgive)
is used only with regard to [Jehovah’s] pardoning a sinner.”
It’s never used in connection with a human forgiving a human.
So the extent of and reasons for Jehovah’s forgiveness
really are unmatchable.
So, what should we be compelled to do?
Well, let’s reflect on the illustration that Jesus gave
in Matthew chapter 18, and if you turn there
you’ll recall that in verse 21
Peter had asked:
‘Lord, how many times am I to forgive
‘my brother if he sins against me?
Up to seven times?’
Now, what was wrong with that question?
Well, Peter had been influenced by a hard-hearted spirit
that was prevalent in those days, and in some instances even today.
Well, what do we mean?
Well, Peter measured forgiveness,
and that was common among the Pharisees.
Jesus went on to say what in verse 22?
We know it very well: “I say to you,
not up to seven times, but up to 77 times.”
And then, in connection with divine forgiveness he
—Jesus— responds in a way
that helps us to see the contrast
in the human understanding of forgiveness and God’s.
Notice what he says in verse 23:
“That is why the Kingdom of the heavens
“may be likened to a king who wanted
to settle accounts with his slaves.”
Now notice, the king wanted to settle accounts.
It wasn’t the slaves.
The slaves had built up a debt with the king,
and justice called for the king to handle matters
—balance the books, as it were.
But then, he found one slave
“who owed him 10,000 talents”
—40 million dollars.
That’s a lot of money.
Jehovah
—if we think about that illustration— is telling us something.
He has given those
that are his slaves —us—
a lot of leeway.
He has forgiven us
thousands of times, so often that we are not aware,
really, of the many sins we commit against Jehovah.
Now, going back to the illustration, verse 26.
This slave begs because he can’t afford to pay,
and he says to the master: ‘Be patient with me,
and I’ll pay everything I owe you.’
Well, how in the world could he do that?
He was a slave. How could he pay back 40 million dollars?
And the master knew that there was no way he could pay this back.
Well now, putting the illustration in today’s terms,
the average yearly wage for the United States
—I googled this—
was almost 52,000 dollars.
That’s just averaging out everybody.
There’s a lot of people who don’t make that much,
and many who make more than that, but the average was 52,000 dollars.
Now, if the 10,000 talents equaled 40 million dollars,
it would take a man 770 years
to pay off that debt
if he gave everything that he made to pay off the debt.
So the master knew,
‘This slave, he can’t— he can’t pay me.’
So verse 27 says: “Moved with pity at this,
the master of that slave let him off and canceled his debt.”
Oh, boy, what a relief that would be.
But the slave should have recognized something.
He could never be in the same position as the master.
He didn’t have the resources.
Nor could anyone possibly owe him
what he owed the master.
Now, if he had captured the spirit
of forgiveness shown to him,
there would hardly be any debt owed to him
that he couldn’t tolerate or even forget.
But in verse 28, look at his attitude:
“That slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves,
[on the same plane as him] who owed him 100 denarii [70 dollars].”
Now notice, he “went out and found” that slave.
So rather than looking to overlook
the debts of those who were indebted to him,
he was looking for those who owed him.
Now, we’re going to read
Notice:
“So his fellow slave fell down
“and began to beg him, saying,
“‘Be patient with me, and I will pay you back.’
However, he was not willing.”
Now, let’s stop there.
Is it possible that this slave that owed him could pay him back?
Yes, it was possible he could work it out
within his resources —70 dollars.
But then, what was the reaction?
The account says: “He went and had him thrown into prison
until he could pay back what he owed.”
Boy, how petty.
Verse 32: “Then [the] master summoned him and said to him:
“‘Wicked slave, I canceled all that debt for you
“‘when you pleaded with me
“‘[that debt that you could never have paid off].
“‘Should you not also have shown mercy to your fellow slave
“‘[that slave who possibly could have paid it off the same]
as I showed mercy to you?’”
And then the clincher, verse 35, Jesus’ point:
“My heavenly Father will also deal with you
“[that’s me, and that’s you]
“in the same way
if each of you does not forgive your brother.”
Not by rote,
not by formula, but ‘from our heart.’
Now the king, as we said,
forgave the debt of 40 million dollars.
That slave was unwilling to forgive his fellow slave
for the amount of 70 dollars.
Jehovah is a big Forgiver,
and we thank him for that.
Last evening helped us to see how big.
Really, grasping the depth of our indebtedness to Jehovah
and the depth of his forgiveness
should compel us to constantly work
at having a forgiving spirit.
The Insight volume says that in the Bible
“the Hebrew word na·saʼʹ
“may denote the pardon, or forgiveness,
extended by God or by humans.”
But as we stated originally,
“sa·lachʹ
“is used exclusively [for] God’s forgiveness,
the act by which [a] sinner is restored to divine favor.”
Now remember, our forgiveness
can’t begin to match Jehovah’s.
So there’s nothing that any human
can do to us that matches what we
—born in sin, alienated from God, inclined to do wrong—
have done to offend Jehovah.
And yet
—as we discussed yesterday, last evening, and we’re reminded of—
God recommends his own love to us,
and that “while we were yet sinners”
he had his Son die for us.
I’d like to quote to you The Watchtower of October 15, 1999,
page 13 —October 15, 1999.
The article is “Forgive From Your Heart.”
It says this:
“You should see in God’s willingness to forgive a pattern
“as to how you ought to treat other humans.
“Paul focused on this, writing:
“‘Become kind to one another,
tenderly compassionate, freely forgiving.’”
Not like an accountant keeping track,
but “freely forgiving one another
just as God also by Christ freely forgave you.”
Then The Watchtower says this: “Do you see the link?
“Jehovah God forgave you, [that’s me]
“so —Paul forcefully reasons—
“you need to imitate [God] Him
and be ‘tenderly compassionate, freely forgiving’ of others.”
And then The Watchtower asked some penetrating questions.
It said: “Ask yourself, ‘Am I [really] doing that?
“‘If it is not [in] my nature, am I working in that direction,
really striving to imitate God in being forgiving?’”
Now, we might say: ‘Well, I’m forgiving.
I forgive a lot of people.’
Proof?
Proverbs 17:9:
“Whoever forgives a transgression seeks love,
but the one who keeps harping on a matter separates close friends.”
If we keep talking about what somebody has done to us,
we haven’t forgiven in the heart.
Jehovah doesn’t do that.
So forgiving others for personal offenses,
regardless of the number of times involved,
is a Christian requirement.
God’s forgiveness is not extended
toward those who refuse to forgive.
Remember what Jesus said: “Forgive us our debts,
as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
And what a beautiful God we have.
His action and that of his Son compels us
to be freely forgiving.

cn.text: 今天的资料取自于
2016年1月《守望台》的一篇文章
题目是
《上帝白白给人的恩赐催逼我们》
耶稣受难纪念聚会前后的这段时期
我们的确应该仔细沉思
耶和华为我们所做的一切
也该采取相应的行动
《洞悉圣经》里有一篇文章是关于宽恕的
其中有一句话这样说
希伯来语动词“萨拉”意即宽恕
只用来指上帝赦免人的罪过
而不是用来描述人与人之间的宽恕
由此可见
耶和华宽恕我们的程度
和理由是人无法做到的
这该推动我们怎样做呢?
我们可以讨论一下耶稣讲的一个比喻
请打开圣经到马太福音18章
在21节  彼得问耶稣说
“主啊  我的弟兄得罪我”
“我要宽恕他多少次呢?”
“到七次够吗?”
彼得的这句话有什么问题呢?
很明显
彼得的想法受到当时社会风气的影响
今天  很多人也有同样的态度
什么样的态度呢?
彼得像当日的法利赛派一样
为宽恕别人限定了次数
耶稣的回答记载在22节
他这样说  “我告诉你”
“不是到七次  而是到七十七次”
接着  耶稣就讲了一个比喻
帮我们看出上帝在宽恕方面
与人多么的不同
我们继续读23节
“因此  天上的王国好比一个作王的人”
“要跟众奴隶结账”
请留意  采取主动的是王
而不是奴隶
奴隶向王借了钱
王现在要跟他们结帐
这样做合情合理
当时  王发现有一个奴隶
“欠了六千万银元”
也就是相当于现在的四千万美元
这是很大一笔钱啊
耶和华通过这个比喻
帮我们明白一个道理
他甘心宽恕了奴隶的罪
也就是我们的罪
许多时候
我们都犯错得罪了耶和华
可能连自己都没有意识到
但耶和华还是选择屡次宽恕我们
现在请继续看耶稣的比喻
在26节
这个奴隶根本没有能力清还债务
于是他请求王说
“求你通融一下”
“我一定给你还清的”
他怎么可能还清呢?
他是个奴隶
在哪里找四千万美元呢?
王也知道这个奴隶根本无力还债
按现在的工资水平来讲
2014年美国人的年均工资
差不多是5万2千美元
这是我在谷歌上查到的数据
当然
有些人一年挣不了这么多钱
另一些人的工资则远高于这个数字
但平均来讲就是5万2千美元
奴隶要想还清欠下的六千万银元
也就是四千万美元
他需要不吃不喝连续工作770年才可以还清
王当然知道
这个奴隶根本无力还债
27节说  “奴隶的主人动了怜悯的心”
“就放了他  把他的债取消了”
这是多大的纾解啊!
奴隶应该学到一些道理
他自己没有钱
因此他永远也不可能像主人那样
借给别人那么多钱
如果他因为得到主人的宽恕而心怀感激
那么他也应该像主人那样
宽恕甚至忘掉别人欠下他的任何债务
但请看28节他怎么做
“这个奴隶出来  遇见另一个奴隶”
而这个人“欠他一百银元”

en.text: Hello, and welcome to this month’s broadcast!
With me I have a good friend as my cohost, Leon Weaver.
Leon, what do we have to look forward to this time?
Thanks, Brother Lösch.
We’ll see a young brother who must choose
between his loyalty to Jehovah
or to a close friend.
Which will he choose?
Then we’ll hear the story of Rafika Morris,
a young woman who desperately fought for racial equality
but eventually discovers the real path to peace.
And we’ll also enjoy a new music video
that beautifully highlights the importance
of putting our confidence in Jehovah.
We have much to look forward to
in this March 2018 edition
of JW Broadcasting!
The theme for this month is
“In Whom Do You Trust?”
Do you trust me?
I hope so.
All of us want to be trusted.
Trust is a basic element of everyday life.
To trust others is a normal reaction.
Many of us have traveled on a train or a bus.
Did we worry whether the conductor or driver
would bring us safely to our destination?
Normally, we do not worry.
We trust an airplane captain to take us safely to our destination.
We trust that when we enter an elevator,
it will not crash at the bottom of the shaft,
but safely take us to the desired floor.
When we marry, we trust that our partner will remain faithful.
In many situations in life we need trust.
What is trust?
Trust is the “firm belief in the reliability,
truth, or ability of someone or something.”
Webster’s dictionary says that it is “confidence”;
a “reliance [or] resting of the mind on the integrity,
“veracity, justice, friendship,
or other sound principle, of another person.”
Trust is related to confidence,
belief, faith, and assurance.
Experiments conducted by Professor Dr. Michael Kosfeld,
a professor at a university in Frankfurt, Germany,
led him to the conclusion that trust
is “a biologically-based part of human nature.”
Kosfeld discovered that when there is interaction between two people,
the human brain releases a hormone that stimulates trust.
“It is, in fact, one of the distinguishing features
of the human species,” Kosfeld states.
In everyday life, how discouraged some are if they are not trusted.
The phrase “Don’t you trust me?”
is frequently heard with an undertone of sadness or complaint.
Sometimes children or teenagers ask their parents
“Don’t you trust me?” when the parents place some restrictions on them,
perhaps in connection with leisure-time activities.
Parents do that because they love you young ones
and want to prevent any spiritual or physical harm befalling you.
If you cooperate, you will see that parents
will gradually trust you ever more
and grant more liberty to you.
You can prove to them that you are trustworthy.
In the world, many people are not trustworthy.
Since we are living in the time of the end
and the demons are desperate and have influenced many people,
we have to admit that trusting in everybody is not wise.
Many trusted in religion and were disappointed.
Others trusted in governments or the United Nations,
but they were disappointed.
They trusted political leaders that made all kinds of promises
but did not keep all of them.
Some politicians were even exposed as being liars.
Proverbs 14:15 says:
“The naive person believes every word,
but the shrewd one ponders each step.”
If somebody, even in the truth, promises us big monetary returns
if we give him money for his planned investment,
we need to be careful and not believe every word.
Some that spent their money were in for a disappointment
when they learned that everything was lost.
We also should not trust everything we read
in newspapers or see on television.
There is another thing we should not trust in—riches.
Psalm 49:6 speaks about “those who are trusting in their wealth
and who boast about their great riches.”
Trusting in riches often leads to disappointment.
“The one trusting in his riches will fall,”
says Proverbs 11:28.
It is not wrong to be rich; just do not trust in riches.
Riches are a risk factor.
Many people today are dishonest and cheat.
Some business owners have installed
cameras at the workplace,
since they do not trust their employees to put in a full day of work.
They know that some would play video games during work hours.
But Jehovah created us with the inclination to trust.
We can especially trust our spiritual brothers.
True, once in a while such trust is misplaced.
A few commit serious sins and have to be disfellowshipped.
But that is rare.
Jehovah himself is the best example of trusting in others.
He trusted the Logos to faithfully cooperate
with him as the “master worker” in creating the universe,
the earth, and all the living things on earth, including mankind.
What tremendous trust Jehovah showed in Jesus when He sent him to the earth.
Jehovah trusted that Jesus would remain faithful
and redeem mankind so that His will and purpose with mankind
and the earth could be accomplished.
Jehovah trusted him so much that he arranged for prophecies
to be written that foretold that he would die faithfully.
This trust on the part of Jehovah was not a risk.
It was based on the collaboration between the two for aeons of time.
Think of the prophecy at Psalm 16:10:
“For you will not leave me in the Grave.”
Jesus had free will.
This means that theoretically he could have sinned.
If he could not have sinned,
Satan probably would not have tried three times to tempt Jesus to sin.
If Jesus could not have sinned,
why would he be so heavily distressed
in the garden of Gethsemane that he was sweating blood?
Why send an angel to comfort and strengthen him
if he could not sin or fail anyway?
No question that Jesus felt the unfathomable load
on his shoulders to remain faithful,
since not only the salvation of mankind depended on him
but also the vindication of Jehovah’s sovereignty.
He did not want to disappoint Jehovah.
Jesus used his own free will
and was determined to stay loyal.
How glad we are that he did!
On the other hand, Jesus also trusted Jehovah completely.
He trusted Jehovah that he would resurrect him if he would die faithfully.
Actually, Jesus was publicly known to trust in Jehovah.
People that passed by when he was on the torture stake were saying:
“He has put his trust in God;
“let Him now rescue him if He wants him,
for he said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
Another example of trust was Abraham.
When God told him to kill his beloved son Isaac,
Abraham was willing to do so.
He trusted that Jehovah could resurrect him.
Hebrews 11:19 says:
“He reasoned that God was able to raise him up even from the dead,
and he did receive him from there in an illustrative way.”
First Corinthians 13:7 says that
love “believes all things.”
Love trusts that prophecies will come true.
It also believes what our brothers tell us.
It also helps to grant others the benefit of the doubt
if a matter could be interpreted in different ways.
Yes, trusting others is an expression of love.
If you love somebody, you only assume and think the best of him.
Another example of trust in Jehovah was Moses.
He led the nation of Israel out of Egypt into the desert
—a nation upwards of three million people.
And they had flocks of cattle and sheep with them.
When he left Egypt, did he know how to provide
these great crowds with water in the desert?
Did he know what they would be eating
after the initial foodstuffs that they took out of Egypt ran out?
Did he know in advance that Jehovah would miraculously provide the manna?
It doesn’t seem so.
But he trusted that Jehovah would take care of the people.
The three friends of Daniel were another fine example of trust.
They did not bow and worship in front of an idol
that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
They were told they would be thrown into a fiery furnace if they disobeyed.
They remained firm and were protected by an angel,
so that the fire did not do any harm to them.
After that
“Nebuchadnezzar then declared:
“‘Praised be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego,
“‘who sent his angel and rescued his servants.
“‘They trusted in him and went against the command of the king
“‘and were willing to die rather than serve
or worship any god except their own God.’”
As we are getting ever closer to the great tribulation,
we might be confronted with scary challenges
and tests related to nationalism.
Will we keep trusting Jehovah?
We trust we will.
Jehovah will miraculously save his people throughout the great tribulation
and arrange for their survival.
Today, the faithful slave is put in charge of providing spiritual food for God’s people,
who number into the millions.
The slave also shows complete trust in Jehovah
that he will guide them with his holy spirit.
What makes it possible for the “faithful and discreet slave”
to provide precious spiritual food?
“I will give you insight and instruct you in the way you should go,”
says Jehovah at Psalm 32:8.
Today, Jehovah provides direction to the slave through Jesus.
Jesus, in turn, provides direction for his people
through “the faithful and discreet slave.”
We can therefore have full confidence
in the Scriptural insight, understanding, and guidance.
Satan tries to sow mistrust.
Under Communist dictatorship in Romania,
secret police officers forced a responsible brother
to walk with them on a heavily frequented street
hoping that other brothers would see this
and wrongly conclude that this brother works with the secret police.
Did the scheme work out?
No, it failed.
Brothers did see him but kept trusting him.
We learn that we should not quickly lose trust in our brothers.
Satan also has the scheme to spread rumors about faithful brothers,
including the faithful slave.
The method of spreading rumors is not new.
When Jesus was resurrected and the tomb was empty,
the soldiers who reported it were told to spread the rumor
that the disciples came and stole the body at night.
Matthew 28:15 relates:
“So they took the silver pieces and did as they were instructed,
and this story has been spread abroad among the Jews up to this very day.”
Another rumor in the first century was that Christians
were responsible for the great fire of Rome.
Could such an accusation be true?
Historians say that it was Nero,
the emperor, who set fire to the city.
Today, rumors are occasionally being spread in electronic form about the faithful slave.
This has caused some concern on the part of some brothers,
especially when the reports are commenting on court cases
where some in the organization were accused.
Sometimes reference is made to certain quotes and then readers think,
‘How can a quote be a rumor?’
A quote can be taken out of context.
Critical reports often give only part of a matter
and leave out other aspects.
Often, such rumors play on the emotions.
Ask yourself: ‘Am I prone to believe rumors?
‘And even if I am, should I spread it
‘and undermine the trust that others have in the slave
or in representatives of the branch office?’
Avoid sensationalism by not saying something like
“Can you believe what I heard about this matter or that matter
or this person or that person?” referring to a statement
that may have appeared on Facebook, YouTube, or Twitter.
The spread of rumors is like wildfire that is hard to control.
It spreads distrust and can undermine someone’s faith.
This is not to say that the slave is perfect and never makes mistakes.
But Jehovah and Jesus trust the imperfect slave
who cares for things to the best of his ability
and with the best of motives.
Shouldn’t we then trust the imperfect slave as well?
To appreciate the extent of Jehovah and Jesus’ trust in the faithful slave,
reflect on what he has promised its members.
He has promised them immortality and incorruption.
Soon, just before Armageddon,
the remaining members of the slave will be taken to heaven.
Since 1919 of our Common Era,
the slave has been put in charge of some belongings of Christ.
According to Matthew 24:47,
when the anointed are taken to heaven, Jesus will at that point entrust
“all his belongings” to them.
Does this not reveal immense trust?
Revelation 4:4 describes these resurrected anointed
as corulers with Christ.
Revelation 22:5 says they will rule,
not only for a thousand years
but “forever and ever.”
What immense trust Jesus shows toward them!
Since Jehovah God and Jesus Christ
completely trust “the faithful and discreet slave,”
should we not do the same?
Many servants of Jehovah in the past showed trust in Jehovah
when confronted with obstacles or opposition.
We can trust that Jehovah will not let us be tested beyond what we can bear
but will provide a “way out”
so we can remain faithful under trials.
So whom do you trust?
You fully trust in Jehovah, Jesus, and the faithful slave.
To a reasonable degree, you also trust all your fellow brothers and sisters.
The writer of Psalm 119:42 mentioned something else we need to trust in
—God’s Word.
He wrote:
“For I put my trust in your word.”
The prophecies in God’s Word have always come true at the proper time.
Based on that, we can fully trust that the remaining prophecies
pointing to the survival of the great tribulation
and to the Paradise to follow will also come true,
without the slightest possibility of failure.
Of course, we should trust not only Jehovah, Jesus,
the faithful slave, and the Bible but also our fellow brothers.
The apostle Paul is a fine example of this.
He wrote to Philemon
asking him to kindly receive back
the runaway slave Onesimus who had become a brother.
Paul wrote at Philemon 21:
“I am confident that you will comply,
so I am writing you, knowing that you will do even more than what I say.”
When we speak of trust,
we sometimes think of a little child
walking hand in hand with his father.
The child does not question where the father will take him.
The child trusts the father.
All throughout the last days,
true Christians have faced hostility of so many in the world.
How strengthening Jehovah’s promise is
in view of the impending attack by Satan’s hordes!
When they attack, Jehovah’s people will seem as defenseless.
But we do not need to quake with fear.
We trust that Jehovah, Jesus, and the angels
will fight to deliver us.
We will not shrink back in fear.
At Hebrews 10:39, Paul wrote:
“Now we are not the sort who shrink back to destruction,
but the sort who have faith for the preserving of our lives.”
Today and after Armageddon, all can say,
according to Psalm 26:1 and 52:8:
“I have trusted [in Jehovah] without wavering.”
“My trust is in God’s loyal love, forever and ever.”
Therefore, keep trusting in Jehovah and those who are proving loyal to him.
Back to you, Leon.
Thank you, Brother Lösch.
In line with that,
we all want
good friends
we can trust
—the type
mentioned at Proverbs 18:24, where it says:
“There is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.”
But at times, we may find that a close friend
needs spiritual help.
Do we fear losing that friendship if we speak up?
What does Jehovah want us to do?
In the following dramatization,
the young man Danny faces these same questions.
I had a secret.
Only it wasn’t mine to tell.
It was my best friend’s, Julian.
This was not the Julian I knew.
At the end of the meeting,
Brother Max wanted to know if I was OK.
I shrugged it off.
I just didn’t know who to talk to at that point.
A few years ago,
when my parents stopped attending meetings,
Julian was there for me.
I didn’t want to lose my friend.
But did I really know him?
I decided to ask Julian about the pictures he posted.
I told him it wasn’t right.
He needed to talk to the elders.
Then he got really defensive about it.
I knew I did the right thing.
When was I supposed to take care of this bill?
I’ve been telling you for the past month!
I just needed someone to talk to.
When did you tell me?
I’ve been working for the past couple of weeks.
Well, as if I don’t work?
Oh! Now you’re going to blame everything on me.
Brother Max wanted to know how I was really doing.
He could tell something was wrong.
So I opened up.
I told him everything.
I didn’t want to get my friend in trouble.
Max understood.
He asked me to read James 5:14, 15:
“Is there anyone sick among you?
“Let him call the elders of the congregation to him,
“and let them pray over him,
“applying oil to him in the name of Jehovah.
“And the prayer of faith
“will make the sick one well,
and Jehovah will raise him up.”
Max showed me that the elders can encourage and strengthen
a spiritually weak person.
Covering up a friend’s wrongdoing
prevents him from getting the spiritual help he needs.
All this time, I was focused on Julian and his deception,
and I didn’t speak up.
I’m glad I was honest with Brother Max.
The elders are like our spiritual doctors,
and even more, they’re our friends.
They want to help us.
Julian might receive discipline,
but that’s an expression of Jehovah’s love.
It could save his spiritual life.
Julian got the spiritual help he needed.
And I kept my best friend.
Did you notice how our young brother
put trust in the Bible and acted accordingly?
How can we do the same?
Brother Ron Curzan’s morning worship comments share some thoughts
on specific ways we can continue to make spiritual adjustments
as we encounter a variety of life’s challenges.
These were very practical comments.
And they all tie in well
with what the apostle Paul was trying to tell
those in the Ephesian congregation
about examining themselves.
The same way we have to do today
—examining ourselves so that we please Jehovah.
If you’d like, please open up to Ephesians chapter 5,
and we’ll read verse 10, which is our theme scripture.
Ephesians 5:10, it says:
“Keep on making sure of what is acceptable to the Lord.”
And then it goes on in verse 11:
“And stop sharing in the unfruitful works that belong to the darkness;
rather, expose them for what they are.”
So it’s very clear to us, in this chapter of Ephesians chapter 5,
that there are things that Jehovah views as acceptable
and things he views as unacceptable.
Jehovah’s standard of what is unacceptable
is outlined in quite a few of the verses in chapter 5 here.
If you would just scan through verses 3, 4, and 5,
we’ll see that unwholesome talk about sex,
shameful conduct, obscene jesting
—and then verse 18, drunkenness—
well, these are things that will bar us from God’s Kingdom.
When you think about entertainment today,
it’s nearly impossible to try to find something
that is acceptable to Jehovah
that does not have immoral sex, pornography,
spiritism, and violence.
Satan has thoroughly saturated all forms of the media.
So thoroughly, that it’s in our literature,
it’s in movies, it’s in electronic games,
and everything that we can think of Satan has infiltrated.
Yes, he knows that Jehovah hates these things,
and he doesn’t mind if part of our heart hates these things
as long as part of our heart loves these things.
So we do well to ask ourselves:
‘Does the entertainment that I choose help me
‘in my being acceptable to Jehovah?
‘Does it help me to have the qualities
‘that Jehovah endears in me,
and will he draw closer to me?’
Well, the spirit of the world reflects rebellion of the Bible,
which outlines Jehovah’s qualities and his standards.
We want to show respect for the Bible,
which teaches us to love what Jehovah loves
and hate what he hates.
And what will help us to do this and resist the spirit of the world
and draw closer to Jehovah and be acceptable to him?
Let’s notice verse 17,
chapter 5 and verse 17, it says:
“On this account stop being unreasonable,
but keep perceiving what the will of Jehovah is.”
We need to constantly think:
‘What would Jehovah want me to do?’
Well, verse 1 and verse 2 help us to appreciate this, it says:
“Become imitators of God, as beloved children,
“and go on walking in love, just as the Christ also loved us
“and [he] gave himself [up] for us as an offering
and a sacrifice, a sweet fragrance to God.”
So, bottom line, we need to imitate Jehovah and Jesus.
Our sacrifices need to be acceptable to Jehovah
as was Jesus’.
What made Jesus so pleasing?
Well, he did everything the way Jehovah wanted him to do.
In fact, he said something that we want to say one day:
“I always do the things pleasing to him.”
And one day in perfection, we will be able to say that.
Jesus was pleasing in his word, in his deed, in his actions.
Well, how can we imitate Jesus and thus imitate Jehovah?
Well, let’s briefly discuss three ways.
First: Pray for God’s holy spirit.
When confronted with trials, what did Jesus do?
He did not rely on himself; he petitioned Jehovah for help.
So if we’re struggling with a temptation
—a certain fleshly weakness—
it’s vital that we do the same.
We can also talk to the elders —our loving shepherds—
who will pray with us, and they will definitely help us
to remain faithful with words of encouragement.
Number two: Obey Jehovah completely.
Jesus always did things that were pleasing to his Father.
Luke 22:42 says:
“Let, not my will, but yours take place.”
Remember, there is no substitute for obedience.
We cannot be acceptable without obedience.
Number three: Know the Scriptures well.
Jesus used God’s Word as his authority.
His whole life revolved around knowing
and obeying and encouraging others about God’s laws.
We all have busy schedules.
We have work to do —busy in the congregation.
It’s more than just trying to find time to dig deep into God’s Word;
we must make the time.
So, what do our schedules tell us
about our love for Jehovah?
our love for his Word?
Do we read the Bible daily?
And if we do, how much time do we take
to let it sink into our mind and our heart and to meditate?
Are we content with just looking
at the basics —the surface—
or digging deeper and deeper below the surface?
It’s vital that we train our minds and our hearts,
but it takes time and it takes effort,
just as a marathon runner must devote much time and effort
to his training to run a race.
In fact, as we know, Christians are likened
to running a race, and it’s a race for life.
Let’s see what the apostle Paul had to tell us.
If we go over to 1 Corinthians,
1 Corinthians chapter 9,
a scripture we know very well, and we’ll start in verse 24.
And there are a few key elements
that we would like to extract as we’re reading these verses.
Here Paul said:
“Do you not know that the runners in a race all run,
“but only one receives the prize?
“Run in such a way that you may win it.
“Now everyone competing in a contest
“exercises self-control in all things [there’s a key].
“Of course, they do it to receive a crown that can perish,
“but we, one that does not perish.
“Therefore, the way I am running is not aimlessly;
“the way I am aiming my blows
“is so as not to be striking the air;
“but I pummel my body
“[and the footnote says, “punish; strictly discipline”]
“and lead it as a slave, so that after I have preached to others,
“I myself should not become disapproved
[or the footnote says, “disqualified”] somehow.”
So we definitely want to have self-control like a runner.
We need to say no to Satan’s world
and yes to things that are acceptable to Jehovah.
And we definitely want to make sure that we are acceptable
and never to be disapproved.
Perhaps we can illustrate this.
In the 1994 New York City Marathon,
there was a young man named German Silva,
and he ran an outstanding race.
In fact, there was only half a mile to the finish line in Central Park,
and somehow he got distracted.
He took the wrong path.
Did he lose the race?
Well, the lead runner took over.
Well, he got redirected; he went back on the path;
he began to run faster and faster.
He passed up the lead runner,
and he won the New York City Marathon by two seconds.
What does this tell us?
It tells us that sometimes we can lose our focus, we can be sidetracked,
or we could get involved in unacceptable conduct.
But allow God’s Word and loving shepherds to readjust our course.
Never give up.
Just a few years later, after that —1997—
German began running again in a New York City Marathon.
He thought he had this one all in the bag;
he thought he was going to win this race.
But he started to run slower.
He began to— He dehydrated.
Instead of taking just a few seconds to hydrate,
he skipped that.
He thought he could do it.
Well, what could this tell us?
Well, we cannot afford to take shortcuts.
We need to have a regular intake of spiritual food
to keep pace with Jehovah’s organization.
We do this by what the commenters told us today,
that is, a regular intake of God’s Word and meditation.
As we run the Christian course —the race for life—
remember, it’s not the speed, it’s the direction
—that’s what matters the most.
And may we always run in such a way that is acceptable to Jehovah.
As Brother Curzan mentioned,
certainly a regular intake of God’s Word
can have a dramatic effect on our lives.
Take the example of Rafika Morris.
Her life led her on a search
for ways to achieve racial harmony
through human means.
But after years of frustration and disappointments,
how would studying the Bible
affect her search for answers?
Growing up in the South
during the time of segregation
—blacks and whites— we couldn’t mix.
And not only that, they had signs
to keep you knowing where you were supposed to go.
I couldn’t understand why we couldn’t get along.
Fifty cents.
Yes, Sir.
Thank you, Sir.
Grandma, he’s just a boy. Why are you saying “Sir”?
Be quiet. I want you to know your place.
I told her after we got back on the truck:
“You know what? I’ll never hold my head down!”
My grandmother knew I had a love for the Bible
because I would always read the Bible as a kid.
But I couldn’t understand it.
I used to pray, “What makes us so different?”
You know, “Why can’t we live together?”
I met a group,
and this group was like what I really wanted to be in.
They were about politics.
They said, “We’re fighting injustice.”
And when they said that word “injustice,” it was like,
‘Yeah, this is what I want to be in, right?
‘To be part of something that can change
and make people united, right?’
That was my goal.
We started protesting about police brutality,
and I think that’s what a lot of people,
you know, were focusing on.
I liked some of the things that they were doing,
but they trained us every, every day in military training.
We learned how to use weapons and stuff like that.
And so I’m thinking:
‘This is not what I want to be in. This is not what I joined.’
So I started going back to God again —to reading the Bible—
because it was like I’m not changing anything.
The Bible that I was reading was the King James Version.
So I was reading it, reading it, reading it,
but I couldn’t understand it.
We went to Jamaica,
and we saw this Bible, the New World Translation.
And I started reading it, and it made so much sense!
And I could understand it, and it wasn’t “thee” and “thou.”
I was like, ‘Wow!’
You know, like, ‘This is the one I want to get.’
One day, two women knocked on the door.
I didn’t know they were Jehovah’s Witnesses.
All I could see was that Bible.
And I said, “Where did you get that Bible from?”
And they said, “OK, we’ll bring you one.”
And they did. So they brought me the Bible,
but I didn’t know I was going to have a Bible study that came along with it.
The first time I went to a convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
it was like ten thousand people.
When I went in there and I saw
all these different faces and different colors,
it was like Jehovah showing me:
“Hey, Rafika, remember you were asking me
“about all different people getting together and being one?
See, I’m not partial; they do get along; we are unified.”
And it just made me feel so good inside.
Yes!
This is the organization that I want to be in.
I just see people as people, you know,
and I can preach and be friends with anybody.
Now that I know what the Bible really teaches,
I have a wonderful life
because I know that only God and his government
can bring about peace.
Just like how Jehovah unified everybody,
I want everybody to be unified
and come to know Jehovah, just like I know him.
Jehovah answered my prayer.
While Rafika faced unique challenges
early in her spiritual life,
she learned to trust in Jehovah.
Trust is also needed
if we choose to extend ourselves
in a new form of Kingdom service.
This is especially true of those who have had the privilege
to attend the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
Their personal experiences confirm this.
I have an illness that affects my level of energy,
so I didn’t feel that I could accept just any kind of assignment.
Since the end of this system is near,
I want to do whatever I can
that Jehovah wants down to the very end.
So I applied.
Before attending SKE, when I received my invitation,
all of a sudden I had challenges or worries about myself.
I felt unworthy, even unqualified.
Being a single sister, going into the class with so many couples,
I thought I would be out of place.
I used all my abilities.
I felt like my head was swelling up.
Even so, I felt that I was really being refined
and ended each day feeling fulfilled.
Something that I
really enjoyed about SKE
was Friday afternoons.
That’s when we had a talk
from one of the Governing Body members.
That was special.
During the eight weeks of school,
such an emphasis was placed
on serving where the need is greater.
So this way of thinking became more important to us.
After eight weeks of attending the school,
you are even ready to be sent to the moon.
When I was told
that my next assignment
would be in Mesa, Arizona,
I thought, ‘Where is that?’
And then I thought, ‘Oh, no, scorpions!’
And then I thought, ‘OK,
this is where Jehovah thinks I should be, so I’m ready to go.’
One of the challenges in my new assignment
was finding suitable accommodations.
There was a couple in the congregation
who had two rooms that they rented in the back of their property,
but it needed some renovations.
So the brothers very quickly came together, helped sort it out,
and even built an extra little kitchenette lounge.
So now we have a beautiful little home
to go back to after a long, hot day in the ministry.
I always thought that I’d do much better in the cold than I would in the heat.
So the brothers and sisters were very helpful
in making sure that I stayed hydrated,
making sure I knew how to handle myself in the heat,
giving me pointers on things to carry,
and they made sure that I had
an extra-large water bottle with me.
We really felt supported by the congregation
because they found us an apartment.
This meant that we could concentrate on our ministry.
One of the things that really helped me was an experienced brother
who gave an encouraging comment about whether my health
would permit me to attend the school.
He said, “If she can pioneer,
then it’s also possible for her to attend the school.”
The education that we received at SKE
especially helped us with our qualities,
our personality —putting on the new personality.
That really will help us not only now in our assignment
but right through into the new world.
I think there are many who could meet the qualifications
with just a little more effort.
Please know that there is a wonderful education program,
and we were able to experience it in our 60’s.
We could get through it.
So if others are thinking of applying,
I want to tell them that we were able to do it,
and by all means,
I want them to taste the same joy that we experienced.
You could be nervous
and have performance anxiety and worry about,
‘How will I handle answering,
‘and how about all of the student assignments
and the tests?’ —worries like that.
But for my own part,
it was two months with an incredible amount of joy.
And you have to focus on that.
It is a gift —it is a wonderful gift from Jehovah.
I wasn’t sure if I was going to put in the application
because I thought maybe I wanted to do it as a couple
rather than as a single person.
But I prayed to Jehovah about it, and I put my application in.
I wouldn’t be experiencing the happiness
that I have now if I had waited.
So I’m happy that I just put my application in
and let Jehovah do the rest.
And now, sometimes I’m driving down the freeway, and I think:
‘Wow, Jehovah, I am so happy! Thank you!’
These experiences remind me
of Colossians 3:23, 24 which reads:
“Whatever you are doing,
“work at it whole-souled as for Jehovah,
“and not for men, for you know that it is from Jehovah
“you will receive the inheritance as a reward.
Slave for the Master, Christ.”
Certainly, these brothers and sisters are doing just that.
If you personally find yourself in a position
to reach out for a privilege, such as attending this school
or moving to where the need is great,
give it consideration.
Now we travel to Costa Rica,
where we find our brothers and sisters relying on Jehovah
as they prepare for a very special assembly.
Why was trust in Jehovah essential for this project?
First, we asked the branch for permission.
Once they gave us approval,
we began to make preparations for the assembly,
though we had absolutely nothing.
So one brother lent us a property for the assembly site.
Our brothers have brought many different skills to the project.
There are metalworkers ,
cabinetmakers, and bricklayers.
Many brothers
have given of their resources
and used their abilities
so that this project could go ahead.
This has really made us stand out here.
People were asking each other:
“What is happening here?”
and “Who paid for all of this?”
They say people are surprised at how many workers are coming to help.
And I wonder,
‘If this is getting attention now,
what will the assembly be like?’
A comfortable, practical, and secure Assembly Hall
was constructed using materials acquired locally.
Expectations grew as the special day drew closer,
and when it finally arrived, those in attendance
experienced something truly moving.
With Jehovah’s help, many interested ones,
along with our brothers and sisters, have come here today
to celebrate our first assembly in the Bribri language.
Friends, this is wonderful!
When the program started in Bribri, I cried.
I’m so happy
to have participated in the assembly,
especially because it’s in my own language.
It’s what we wanted.
We hope it continues just like this.
We walked a long way to invite these people,
and to see them here, it makes me very happy.
The information presented in the local language
touched many hearts.
This was truly a historic event
for our indigenous brothers in Costa Rica.
Jehovah has made it possible
for more people in this isolated region to enjoy his spiritual blessing.
Did you note why trust in Jehovah
was so essential for this project?
At the start the brothers had nothing.
But they trusted that Jehovah would assist them,
and he did through donated land,
materials, and willing volunteers.
Yes, we can truly put our confidence in Jehovah
as he guides us through this system of things.
Such trust in Jehovah
is highlighted in this month’s music video entitled
Confident in You.
Like a tree planted in the ground, Your words have sunk deep down
Into my heart and soothed my mind with gentle thoughts of peace.
’Cause no matter what may come, With this wisdom from above,
I always have these truths to keep reminding me to
Go on; don’t be afraid. Hold on to what Jehovah says.
Through all the storms, your words have Given me strength to endure.
And every day I am more confident in you.
When this world tries to pull me down, To give up on what I’ve found,
I turn to you and know that you are always there.
It takes time to meditate— Get the words from off the page
And in my heart so they can help and guide me to
Go on; don’t be afraid. Hold on to what Jehovah says.
Look beyond any adversity. Focus on the things that I can’t see.
Through all the storms, your words have Given me strength to endure.
And every day I am more confident in you—
In you.
Go on; don’t be afraid. Hold on to what Jehovah says.
Look beyond any adversity. Focus on the things that I can’t see.
Through all the storms, your words have Given me strength to endure.
And every day I am more confident in you.
This month we have seen how trusting in Jehovah
and his guidance can assist us in a variety of ways:
addressing issues with a close friend,
our choices in entertainment,
and even coping with a world filled with social injustice.
Certainly, Jehovah is someone in whom we can trust!
But we have one last treat for you before we end our program.
We’ll briefly travel to Cádiz, Spain.
Cádiz is considered to be one of the oldest cities in Western Europe
and was founded by the Phoenicians.
It is situated on a narrow slice of land surrounded by the sea.
Cádiz has a wealth of vistas
and well-preserved historical landmarks.
On the outskirts lies Puerto de Santa María,
where an English-speaking congregation meets.
This congregation is made up mainly
of brothers and sisters serving as need-greaters.
They have come from other parts of Spain as well as distant lands,
such as Australia, Britain, Canada, and the United States.
Cádiz has a high rate of unemployment,
so finding work is not easy.
One couple travels nearly 300 miles
(or 483 km)
every Thursday to their territory,
and on Monday morning they make the trip back to where they live and work.
In spite of these financial challenges,
many are still serving as construction volunteers,
remote Bethel workers, and pioneers.
Our brothers and sisters in Puerto de Santa María
are thrilled to send their love and greetings to you all.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

和我一起主持节目的是我的好朋友
利昂·韦弗
利昂  这个月的节目有哪些內容呢?
谢谢勒施弟兄
首先  我们将会认识一位年轻的弟兄
他会忠于耶和华还是忠于好朋友呢?
请看他如何选择
然后我们会听听拉菲卡·莫里斯的经历
她年轻时曾一度热衷于种族平等运动
后来她才找到了真正的和平之道
此外  本月的音乐短片
会帮助我们明白信赖耶和华有多重要
欢迎大家收看2018年3月份的节目
本月节目的主题是“谁值得信赖?”
你信任我吗?
希望如此
我们都想得到别人的信任
在日常生活中  信任是必不可少的
相信别人也是很自然的反应
在乘坐火车或公交车时
我们会担心
司机不能安全地开到目的地吗?
通常我们不会担心
乘坐飞机时
我们相信飞行员
会平安地送我们到目的地
坐电梯时
我们也相信电梯不会掉下去
而是会把我们送到要去的楼层
结婚的时候
我们也相信配偶会忠贞不二
是的  生活中的很多时候
信任都必不可少
什么是信任呢?
信任是指对某人或某物的能力
及其真实性可靠性怀有坚定的信念
《韦伯斯特词典》说
信任是一种信心
是确信某个人具有美好的品格
包括正直  诚实  公正  忠贞等
可以说信任和信心  信念
信仰及信赖息息相关
德国法兰克福大学的教授
迈克尔·科泽费尔博士做了一些实验
他得出一个结论
原来“信任是人类生理上的一部分”
科泽费尔发现
当两个人互相交流的时候
脑部会分泌出催产素
这种激素会大幅度增加人类的信任感
科泽费尔说
信任感其实是人类的特征之一
使人类有别于其他物种
在生活中  如果我们不被信任
就会感到很失落
难道你不相信我吗?
我们经常会听到别人这样抱怨
有时父母会限制孩子的娱乐时间
这时孩子可能会说
你怎么不相信我呢?
其实父母之所以这样做
是因为他们很爱你
不想让你在属灵和身体上受到伤害
如果你听父母的话
父母就会更信任你
也会给你更多的自由
所以你要向父母证明
自己是值得信任的
现在的社会很多人都不可靠
因为我们正生活在最后的日子
撒但和他手下的邪灵变得愤怒若狂
迷惑了很多人
所以我们盲目地相信别人是不明智的
有些人信奉错误宗教
结果感到失望
还有些人信赖政府或者联合国
结果也很失望
世人所仰赖的政治领袖
说了很多漂亮话
但不能信守承诺
有些政客表面上为别人服务
其实却是在欺骗民众
如果别人
包括会众里的弟兄姐妹在內
邀请你参与投资计划
还承诺会赚很多钱
也一定要小心
不要凡话都信
有些人投入大笔资金参与投资
后来大失所望  但为时已晚
对于报纸和电视报道的內容
我们也不要凡事都信
另外  我们也不该信赖财富
诗篇49:6谈到财富时说
“信赖财物的人  常常夸耀家财丰足”
信赖财富的人最后通常都感到失望
“信赖财富的必然跌倒”
拥有财富没有错
但不要仰赖财富
因为有时财富会带来考验
现在许多人为了钱不惜欺骗别人
一些老板由于担心
员工在工作时间做其他事
不得不安装摄像头
因为的确有些员工上班时会玩游戏
耶和华创造人类时
就赋予人彼此信任的本能
我们尤其要信任弟兄姐妹
当然他们有时也会令我们灰心失望
有些人甚至犯下严重的罪
最后被开除
但这只是个别的情况
在信任别人方面
耶和华立下了最佳典范
他信任耶稣
相信耶稣会做个“好工匠”
忠心地协助他创造宇宙
地球和地上的一切生物
包括人类
他派耶稣来到地上时
也给予了耶稣极大的信任
耶和华相信耶稣会保持忠贞救赎人类
好让上帝对人类
和地球的旨意完全实现
耶和华信任耶稣
甚至让人在圣经中写下预言
说耶稣会至死忠心
而耶稣也没有辜负他的信任
耶和华和耶稣相处了亿万年
因此有充分的理由信任耶稣
请想想诗篇16:10的预言
这节经文说
耶稣有自由选择的权利
这意味着耶稣可以选择犯错
如果他没有机会犯错
撒但又怎么会三次引诱他呢?
如果他没有机会犯错
在客西马尼园时
他为什么会承受巨大的压力
汗珠像血滴似的滴下来呢?
如果他没有机会犯错
耶和华又怎么会差遣天使去安慰他
给他添加力量呢?
毫无疑问
耶稣很清楚自己肩负的责任有多重大
他能否保持忠贞
不仅会影响到人类的得救
还会影响到耶和华的至高统治权
耶稣决不想让耶和华失望
所以他善用自由选择的权利

근데 그때 그 동영상이 나와서 깜짝 놀랐어요!
훌륭한 선물을 풍부히 주심으로 계속해서 사랑을 나타내십니다.
240면으로 된 이 새로운 책은 총 103개의 장으로 되어 있으며,
나이에 관계없이 누구나 읽을 수 있지만,
삽화는 철저한 조사를 거쳐 모두 새로 그렸으며,
성경 기록과 인물들의 감정을 생생히 묘사합니다.
부모들이 자녀들에게 꼭 가르쳐 주어야 할 요점이 나옵니다.
각 장에는 복습 질문이 있으며 주요점을 강조하는 성구가 나옵니다.
예를 들어, 35장 “한나가 아들을 달라고 기도하다”의 주요 성구로는
이 주요 성구는 성경 기록의 주제를 강조하며
자녀가 교훈점을 이끌어 낼 수 있도록 도와줍니다.
사랑 많은 아버지 여호와께서 선물로 주신 이 책을 읽으면서
성경에 들어 있는 새로운 교훈들을 발견하기를 바랍니다.

en.text: Jehovah loves children,
and he has shown this by providing help
and guidance for them down to our day.
For example, at the 1978 “Victorious Faith” International Convention,
this release entitled My Book of Bible Stories
was soon treasured by young ones around the world.
Over the years, it’s helped millions to come to love Jehovah
and become his faithful worshippers.
The story that always meant a lot to me was that of Samson,
especially the images that we had in the My Book of Bible Stories.
They were so vivid —to see the strength that Jehovah gave him
and the way he supported him.
But at the same time, the story always carried
that if you weren’t obedient to Jehovah, you lost that blessing and that strength.
So I think that as a young one growing up in the truth
—especially when you went to school and you had to stand out and be different—
to remember that Jehovah could support you
and give you that kind of extraordinary strength.
It gave you the power that you needed to make that stand.
Even earlier, The Watchtower began a series of articles
that became the basis for the book Listening to the Great Teacher.
And later, that was rewritten and reillustrated
to become Learn From the Great Teacher.
It tells us what kind of qualities a friend should have.
I like chapter 35 called “We Can Wake Up From Death!”
because I used to be afraid, and now I know
that Jesus will resurrect us no matter what,
and so I’m not afraid anymore.
In 2006, the Awake! magazine started including
numerous activities and puzzles
for children of various ages;
jw.org expanded on this content
to include over 40 Bible-character cards,
illustrated Bible stories, games, coloring activities,
and two series entitled
“My Bible Lessons” for younger children
and “Teach Your Children” for those slightly older.
And who can forget
the Become Jehovah’s Friend video series
with Caleb and Sophia?
The videos help me to be bold for Jehovah.
There’s this little booklet/magazine called My Bible Lessons
that I remember when I was younger
—things to be thankful about, like the Paradise
and what Jehovah gave us and friends.
But what has Jehovah provided for tweens and teens?
In the early ‘70’s,
articles were written
to help those in this age group
to cope with the challenges
of becoming an adult.
These later became the basis for the books
Your Youth —Getting the Best out of It
and, more recently,
Questions Young People Ask —Answers That Work.
Add to that the ever-expanding online content,
such as Answers to 10 Questions Young People Ask,
the video series What Your Peers Say,
as well as whiteboard animations
and feature-length films designed to tackle serious
and sometimes emotional subjects.
When I was in middle school, I used to be bullied, and it was harsh.
Once that video came out, I mean, I was just amazed!
It felt like Jehovah was literally talking to me.
Yes, Jehovah loves young ones,
and he continues to express that love
with an abundance of wonderful gifts.
People of all ages, but especially young ones,
will enjoy this new 240-page book
containing 103 lessons.
The artwork is new
and has been extensively researched,
bringing the Bible to life
and capturing the feelings of those depicted.
Parents will appreciate that each section starts
with a preview of the key lessons you can emphasize.
Each lesson includes review questions
and a caption scripture that summarizes it.
For example, the caption scripture
for the lesson “Hannah Prays for a Son”
is Matthew 7:7:
“Keep on asking, and it will be given you;
keep on seeking, and you will find.”
This scripture serves as the main theme of this account,
allowing you to help your child
focus on the key lesson of the story.
Our hope is that all ages
will enjoy this gift from our loving Father, Jehovah,
as we all discover new lessons
we can learn from the Bible.

cn.text: 耶和华很爱小孩子
所以他从以前到现在
都一直为孩子提供帮助和指引
比方说，1978年举行的
“胜利的信心”国际大会
就为孩子发行了《我的圣经故事书》
全世界的小朋友都很喜欢这本书
多年来
这本书帮助了世界各地的孩子
培养对耶和华的爱
也忠心地事奉他
我印象最深刻的是参孙的故事
特别是《我的圣经故事书》里的
图画都很生动
就好像真的看到耶和华
给参孙力量、支持他
故事也提醒我们
如果不服从耶和华
就不会蒙他赐福
还会失去力量
一个从小学习真理的人
要在学校坚持立场很不容易
但要记得耶和华会支持你，给你力量
你就能对上帝保持忠心
早期《守望台》曾刊登一系列文章
后来都收录在
《聆听伟大的导师》这本书里
这本书后来重新编写
加上新的插图
书名为《向伟大的导师学习》
我学到要怎么做别人的好朋友
我喜欢第35章《死人会复活！》
因为我觉得死掉很可怕
但现在我知道不管怎么样
耶稣都会把我们复活
所以我就不再害怕了
《警醒！》杂志为不同年龄的孩子
增加了很多游戏和拼图
jw.org网站也增加了
40多个圣经人物卡
和圣经故事漫画、游戏、着色游戏
以及专为幼儿设计的“宝宝学圣经”
和为学龄儿童设计的
“教导孩子”系列文章
还有《成为耶和华的朋友》系列影片
大家一定都知道的志轩和盈盈！
这些影片教我要为耶和华而勇敢
我记得我小时候
看过《宝宝学圣经》册子
我真的很谢谢耶和华
他给我们一个美丽的乐园
也给我很多好朋友
耶和华还给了十几岁的年轻人
什么礼物呢？
在70年代早期
组织特别为青少年写了一些文章
帮助他们应付青春期带来的挑战
那些文章后来都收进
《尽量善用你的青春》这本书里
以及之后发行的
《青年人所提出的问题——
有实效的答案》里
网站的资料也不断增加
像是《年轻人的10个问与答》
《有些青少年说》系列影片
以及白板动画片和电影
这些影片丰富多元
有严肃的事件，也有感人的情节
我念中学的时候
曾被恶霸欺负
后来影片出来时
我真的吓了一大跳
我觉得耶和华好像真的在跟我说话
真的，耶和华很爱孩子
他不断送给小朋友数之不尽的礼物
来表达他的爱
相信我们所有人
特别是小朋友
一定会很喜欢这本全新的故事书
这本书有103课，共240页
书中的插图事前都经过仔细考究
让读者可以身临其境
体会圣经人物的喜怒哀乐
每部分开头都有简介
让父母可以向孩子强调
该部分的重要道理
每一课也都包含温习题
和一个主题经文做为参考
比方说，《哈拿祈求有个儿子》
这一课的主题经文
就是马太福音7：7
父母帮助孩子留意主题经文
就可以让他们明白故事的主要道理
这本新书是来自天父耶和华的礼物
希望所有大人小孩都会喜欢
也能更加了解圣经的重要道理

titles.ko: 어린이 여러분—여러분이 포기하지 않으면 여호와께서 기뻐하세요!
titles.en: Young Ones—Your Endurance Makes Jehovah Rejoice!
titles.cn: 孩子们，你们坚持不放弃，耶和华很高兴！

ko.text: 낙타는 어떻게 이러한 사막에서 생존할 수 있습니까?
여호와께서는 낙타에게 아주 특별한 능력을 주셨습니다.
낙타의 등에 있는 혹에는 무엇이 들어 있습니까?
또한 목이 마른 낙타는 물을 발견하면,
단지 몇 분만에 95리터나 되는 물을 마실 수 있습니다.
낙타의 몸은 강렬한 열기 아래서도 수분을 조금밖에 잃지 않습니다.
그 때문에 낙타는 물을 마시지 않고도
수 주에서 수개월까지 살아갈 수 있습니다.
물과 영양분을 흡수하고 비축하는 이러한 놀라운 능력 덕분에
낙타는 혹독한 환경을 견뎌 낼 수 있습니다.
강털소나무는 해발 약 3000미터 높이에서도 아주 잘 자랍니다.
이 놀라운 나무는 수천 년을 살 수 있습니다.
작은 뿌리들은 지면 가까이 넓게 퍼져 있으면서
크고 강한 뿌리들은 땅속 깊숙이 박혀
나무가 강풍에도 견딜 수 있게 해 줍니다.
이 나무가 지구 상에 가장 오래 존재해 온 생명체 중
하나가 된 것도 이러한 이유 때문입니다.
나비는 꽃을 수분시키는 데 중요한 역할을 합니다.
또한 나비는 아주 먼 거리를 여행할 수 있는 능력이 있습니다.
3억 마리나 되는 황제나비들이 긴 여행을 떠납니다.
이 나비들은 북쪽 캐나다에서부터 약 4천 킬로미터를 날아
계속 날아다니며 먹이를 먹을 수 있습니다.
우리에게 인내라는 특성에 대해 많은 것을 가르쳐 줍니다.
대부분의 북극제비갈매기들은 지구의 최북단 지역에서 번식합니다.
이 새들은 북극의 짧은 여름 동안 새끼를 낳아 키웁니다.
남반구의 최남단 지역으로 날아가 그곳에서 여름을 맞이합니다.
이들은 매년 이주를 하는 동물 중
가장 먼 거리를 여행하는 것으로 알려져 있습니다.
지구의 자기장을 감지해 방향을 찾는다고 생각합니다.
하지만 확실한 것은 아직 밝혀지지 않았습니다.
여호와께서 주신 정확한 방향 인도 장치 덕분에
북극제비갈매기는 이 긴 여행을 무사히 마칠 수 있습니다.
이 물떼새는 보통 물가에 있는 땅에 둥지를 트는데,
이 때문에 자기보다 덩치가 훨씬 더 큰 동물의 위협을 받기도 합니다.
어떤 때는 침입자를 둥지에서 멀리 쫓아내려고 시도하기도 하고,
또 어떤 때는 그 자리에 용기 있게 버티고 서서
뾰족한 부리로 그런 큰 동물을 쪼는 경우도 있습니다.
여호와께서는 물떼새가 새끼를 보호하고 생존할 수 있도록
메마른 시나이 광야에는 비가 거의 내리지 않습니다.
아카시아나무는 이곳에서 자라는 몇 안 되는 식물 중 하나입니다.
이 나무는 목질이 단단하고 해충의 피해를 잘 입지 않습니다.
흔히 아카시아나무는 무리 지어 함께 자랍니다.
어떤 아카시아나무들은 가지가 서로 촘촘히 얽혀서 그늘막을 만듭니다.
또 어떤 종들은 덤불처럼 자라기도 합니다.
아카시아나무는 이러한 타고난 보호막 덕분에 잘 생존할 수 있습니다.

en.text: How does a camel survive
in this harsh environment?
Jehovah has uniquely equipped
the camel for desert life.
What is inside the camel’s famous hump?
It’s mostly fat.
A healthy camel’s hump can weigh 36 kilograms,
or 80 pounds.
It can draw on this fat reserve when food is limited.
When given an opportunity, a thirsty camel
can drink up to 95 liters, or 25 gallons, of water
in just a few minutes.
Yet, their bodies lose little moisture,
even in extreme heat.
As a result, they can go weeks
or even months without drinking water.
The camel’s impressive ability
to absorb and conserve nourishment and water
enables it to endure.
High in the mountains of North America,
living conditions are unfavorable for most plants.
Yet, the bristlecone pine
not only survives but can thrive at some 3,000 meters,
or 10,000 feet, above sea level.
These remarkable trees can live for thousands of years.
One key to their survival lies in their roots.
Shallow branching roots spread out and gather up
as much water as possible.
Large, strong roots
firmly anchor the trees against intense winds.
These remarkable trees are designed
to make the most of a challenging environment.
As a result,
they are among the oldest living organisms
on the planet.
Butterflies play a vital role in pollinating flowers.
They also accomplish amazing feats of endurance.
Each year in North America,
as many as 300 million monarch butterflies
complete a migration of some 4,000 kilometers,
or 2,500 miles,
from as far north as Canada
to a forest in Mexico.
Butterflies are also surprisingly resilient.
Some butterflies have been observed feeding and flying
with up to 70 percent of their wing surfaces missing.
Butterflies may appear to be delicate and fragile,
but these small creatures display remarkable endurance.
As its name suggests, most arctic terns
breed in the earth’s far northern regions, where they take advantage
of the short Arctic summer to feed and raise chicks.
But as winter approaches,
they fly south to the Antarctic region, where they greet
the arrival of summer in the Southern Hemisphere.
When summer ends, they return to the Arctic,
completing the longest-known annual migration of any animal.
What guides the arctic tern to reach its destination?
Scientists believe that the arctic terns
can sense the earth’s magnetic field
and use it for orientation.
But how they do this still remains a mystery.
Jehovah has given the arctic tern an accurate means of guidance
to complete its long journey.
The blacksmith lapwing, or plover, is found in Africa.
It nests on the ground, often near water.
Its choice of nest location
can bring it in contact with much larger animals.
When its nest is threatened,
the lapwing sounds the alarm.
Sometimes a lapwing will attempt
to draw an intruder away from its nest.
At other times, the bird will courageously stand its ground,
spreading its wings and crying harshly.
Lapwings have been known to attack humans
and square off against elephants and buffalo,
at times giving the larger animal
a sharp strike with its beak.
Jehovah gave the lapwing the instinctive courage
to protect its young, enabling it to survive.
Very little rain falls in the arid wilderness of Sinai.
One of the few types of trees
to grow here is the acacia.
The wood of the acacia tree is dense,
hard, and resistant to insects.
Some types of acacia trees are protected by thick bark
and long, sharp thorns.
Acacia trees often grow closely together.
The branches of some acacias interlock together,
forming dense canopies.
Other acacias grow in tangled thickets.
These natural defenses
help the acacia tree to endure.

cn.text: 为什么骆驼能忍受沙漠中
恶劣的环境呢？
因为耶和华为骆驼设计了
一个很特别的装置
骆驼最显著的特色就是驼峰
驼峰中大部分是脂肪
一般来说
骆驼的驼峰重达36公斤
也就是80磅
在食物有限的沙漠
它可以从驼峰得到营养
一有机会，它就会补充水分
一只骆驼可以在几分钟内
就喝掉95升，相当于25加仑的水
即使在酷热的环境里
它们流失的水分也只有一点点
因此，它们可以连续走好几个星期
甚至好几个月
都不用喝一滴水
骆驼吸收、储存水分和
营养的特殊能力
使它可以忍受恶劣的环境
继续前进
对大部分的植物来说
北美洲高山上的生存环境非常不利
但是，刺果松不仅能在海拔3000米
相当于1万英尺高的环境存活下来
甚至能成长茁壮
这些树能存活好几千年
关键就在于它们的树根
这些树根分佈得很广
能吸收大量的水分
粗壮的树根会牢牢抓住土地
在强风吹袭下
依然屹立不移
刺果松是地球上寿命最长的物种之一
上帝绝妙的设计
使这些树木能适应艰难的环境
成为参天大树
蝴蝶在传播花粉方面
扮演了重要的角色
它们有长途飞行的本领
表现出惊人的耐力
在北美洲
每年有三亿多只帝王蝶
集体迁移到墨西哥的一个森林
其中最远的从加拿大启程
它们飞了将近4000公里
相当于2500英里
蝴蝶也有绝佳的复原能力
有一些蝴蝶
虽然失去了将近百分之70的翅膀
却还是能够正常地飞行和觅食
小小的蝴蝶看似柔弱
却在忍耐方面表现惊人的韧性
北极燕鸥
它们大部分都是在北极地区下蛋筑巢
并趁着北极短暂的夏天
在那里喂养幼鸟
当北极的冬天快来时
它们就会起程飞到南极附近
在南半球迎接夏天的来临
当夏天接近尾声时
它们又会飞回北极
就这样，它们完成了动物界
最远的年度大迁徙
是什么指引北极燕鸥
飞到它们要去的地方呢？
科学家认为北极燕鸥会
感应地球的磁场来定位
辨认方向
但它们到底是如何做到的
至今仍是个谜
耶和华给了北极燕鸥
精密的导航系统
指引它们完成这趟长途飞行
黑背麦鸡又称为千鸟
主要分佈于非洲
它们通常在岸边的地面上筑巢
因为靠近水源
它们很容易接触到体型庞大的动物
一旦出现威胁
它们会发出声音警告同伴
有时候
它们会试图诱使入侵者远离鸟巢
有时候
它们会勇敢地站着不动
张开翅膀
对敌人发出尖锐刺耳的叫声
麦鸡的一大特色是
它们总是做好战斗的准备
它们除了会攻击人类
也会用它们锐利的鸟嘴
攻击大象或水牛等大型动物
耶和华设计的麦鸡是天生勇者
它们尽全力保护幼鸟
展现无比的勇气
西奈半岛的荒野很少下雨
是一片干旱之地
能在这里生长的树木种类稀少
其中一种是金合欢树
这种树的木质坚硬
纹理细致
也不怕虫蛀
有些金合欢树的树皮很厚
还带有长长的尖刺
具有保护的作用
这种树通常会聚在一起生长
而且树枝会彼此缠绕
形成严密的保护罩
另一些金合欢树则会形成
蓬乱的灌木丛
这些天然的防御功能
