en.text: “They.”
“They gathered them together
“to the place that is called in Hebrew
Armageddon.”
Who are “they”?
Who is being “gathered”?
And what is the significance of that to us
as we go about our sacred service today?
The answers can be found in the context.
I invite you to find Revelation chapter 16,
and let’s begin reading in verse 13,
which says:
“And I saw three
“unclean inspired expressions
“that looked like frogs
“come out of the mouth of the dragon
“and out of the mouth of the wild beast
“and out of the mouth of the false prophet.
“They are, in fact, expressions inspired by demons
“and they perform signs,
“and they go out to the kings of the entire inhabited earth,
to gather them together to the war of the great day of God the Almighty.”
And verse 16 says:
“And they [these “expressions”]
“gathered them [“the kings of the entire inhabited earth”]
to the place that is called in Hebrew Armageddon.”
“Expressions.”
Now, these must be very persuasive expressions
because they compel
not just a few isolated kings here and there
but “the kings of the entire inhabited earth”
to this situation called Armageddon.
Now, these expressions, you notice, are unclean,
so they cannot originate with Jehovah.
And yet, they are inspired
—“inspired by demons.”
And yet, they have their ultimate source
in “the mouth of the dragon,” Satan the Devil
—“the father of the lie.”
But, now, who actually gives voice
to these expressions?
Well, notice in verse 13 that the expressions
also ‘come out of the mouths of the wild beast and the false prophet’
—political entities of Satan’s world.
So here we have unclean expressions inspired by demons
—originating with Satan but voiced, repeated,
parroted, and echoed by people
who constitute Satan’s wicked world.
But, now, just what are these expressions
that are so persuasive that they compel kings?
What concept would be so compelling?
Since 1914, Satan has been stepping up his efforts
to mislead “the entire inhabited earth.”
And one of his goals
is to deceive mankind into thinking that humans
—that Satan’s way of ruling is the best—
that humans can actually achieve
peace and security
through their own systems and governments.
Moreover, according to 1 Thessalonians 5:1-3,
they will soon be saying that they have actually achieved
“peace and security.”
Now, adding to the power of these inspired expressions
are the signs.
The signs make it seem
as if these expressions are actually coming true
and perhaps that they even have the backing of God.
But the only god backing these particular inspired expressions
is “the god of this system of things.”
Is it unprecedented
that Satan the Devil would use miracles
in an attempt to lend credibility
to his ideas, his wicked lies?
At Exodus 7:10-12,
Jehovah empowers Aaron’s rod to become a snake,
but Pharaoh’s magic-practicing priests
mimicked that very sign.
Likewise, they mimicked the first and the second of the Ten Plagues.
OK, but what about after the Christian congregation came into existence?
Paul indicated at 2 Thessalonians 2:3-12
that the apostate movement,
which eventually gave birth to the clergy of Christendom,
would be backed “by the operation of Satan
“with every powerful work
and lying signs and wonders.”
—2 Thessalonians 2:9.
Moreover, Mark 13:22 says—
In the prophecy of the last days, Jesus said:
“False Christs and false prophets
“will arise and will perform signs
“and wonders to lead astray, if possible,
[even] the chosen ones.”
So, clearly, demons teach.
And it is not beyond Satan and the demons
to back up their false claims with wonders at times,
although, obviously, their power in that regard is limited.
A subtle reminder of that fact
is found at Revelation 16:16,
which says that they are ‘gathered together to the place called Armageddon,’
“to the war of the great day of God the Almighty.”
“The Almighty” —only Jehovah can hold that title.
And that very word is a guarantee that Jehovah’s will
will ultimately prevail.
Still, is it possible
that some professed Christians could start to believe
“expressions inspired by demons”
that “perform signs”?
If it weren’t possible, at least for individuals,
then why would Revelation chapter 16 contain this warning
right in the middle of the discussion about Armageddon that we just read?
The verse that we skipped, verse 15,
contains a very relevant reminder
for each and every one of us.
Now, sometimes we skip it
because we keep all the verses about Armageddon together.
But, this is not an afterthought, a sidebar,
just a wise saying plunked in for no apparent reason.
It’s totally relevant.
Let’s read it:
“Look! [verse 15]
“I am coming as a thief.
“Happy is the one who stays awake and keeps his outer garments,
“so that he may not walk naked
and people look upon his shamefulness.”
So here we are, right on the cusp
of the outbreak of the great tribulation.
You have an identity —“garments”—
an identity as a faithful witness of Jehovah God.
Keep your identity.
How?
By keeping awake spiritually.
The article from which our text is taken,
entitled “‘Your Deliverance Is Getting Near’!”
in the July 15, 2015, issue of The Watchtower, points out
—in harmony with the Scriptures, boiling down a number of Scriptural facts—
that Babylon the Great will be destroyed.
Then, the initial part of the great tribulation will be cut short.
There will be a brief respite,
during which the majority of mankind
will seek refuge in human organizations.
Our message of good news will change to one of judgment.
Then, the coalition of nations referred to as Gog of Magog
will be bent on attacking Jehovah’s anointed ones
and their associates.
Now, only loyal love for Jehovah
and obedient support of his anointed ones will get us through.
That will mean everything!
So, what must we do now?
Stay awake.
You have an identity
—not just a Bethelite or Gilead graduate.
No.
You’ve worked hard, with Jehovah’s help,
to establish an identity
as a Christian worshipper of Jehovah
—keep it.
Perform “holy acts of conduct.”
We could say, things we don’t do
—things we don’t watch, things we don’t read,
things we don’t think about, things we don’t say.
Don’t let the demons tamper with your identity as a Christian
with their “unclean inspired expressions.”
Perform “deeds of godly devotion,”
we could say, things we do
—preaching, lingering in prayer,
continuing in your personal study.
Much is covered in Gilead, yes, but not everything.
The online Study Bible is amazing,
and it just keeps getting better day after day,
helping us to forge a closer bond,
a close personal attachment, with Jehovah.
Continue devoting time to such “deeds of godly devotion” now
and you will succeed then.
You will not be duped by the expressions
that perform signs,
as others are.
No, you will survive
“the great day of God the Almighty,”
now so very near at hand.

“我看见三个受邪灵启示的不洁主张”
“好像青蛙从龙的口  野兽的口”
“假先知的口出来”

“前往普天下的列王那里”
“召集他们在全能上帝的大日子投入战争”

也就是普天下的列王
“召集到一个地方”
“希伯来语叫哈米吉多顿”

这些主张是不洁的

这些主张是“受邪灵启示的”
归根结底
这些主张其实都源于“龙的口”
也就是“魔鬼撒但”
这位“谎话之父”的口
那么撒但通过谁
把这些主张说出去呢?
请留意第13节说
这些主张就是通过“野兽的口”
“假先知的口”
也就是撒但世界的政治机构说出去的
那总结一下
受邪灵启示的不洁主张
是源于撒但的
这些主张是借着撒但邪恶世界的人
大肆传播出去的
那么
到底是什么主张这么有力量
竟然能把普天下的列王
召集到一起呢?
这是一个什么样的主张呢?
自1914年以来
撒但一直极力迷惑“普天下的人”
他的一个目标
就是让人误以为
撒但的统治方式是最好的
让人觉得人就是靠着自己的政府
和自己制定的体制
也可以实现和平安全
帖撒罗尼迦前书5:1-3也提到
他们不久就会宣布
“和平安全”已经实现了
此外  撒但也会通过神迹
让这些主张显得更有说服力
因为神迹会让人以为
这些主张真的实现了
而且背后还有上帝的支持
但其实
真正支持这些主张的
只不过是“现行制度的神”
那么魔鬼撒但以前
也曾经使用过神迹
使人相信他的邪恶谎言吗?

耶和华施行奇迹将亚伦的杖变成蛇

耶和华降下的十场灾殃中的头两场
魔法祭司也照着做了

叛道的势力孕育了假基督教的教士
帖撒罗尼迦后书2:9
他们“靠着撒但所施展的力量而存在”
“用各样异能和虚假的神迹异兆”
另外  耶稣提及最后日子的预言时
在马可福音13:22也说道
“必有假基督和假先知兴起”
“行神迹和奇事”
“如果可能”
“就想把蒙拣选的人也引入歧途”

有时候
撒但和邪灵也通过神迹异兆
来支持自己错误的主张

“它们把列王召集到一个”
叫哈米吉多顿的地方

耶和华的旨意一定会彻底实现
那么
对于邪灵的神迹和主张
自称是基督徒的人
也有可能被误导吗?
如果他们不会被误导
那在谈论哈米吉多顿时
为什么启示录16:15记载了一个警告呢?
我们刚才跳过了这节经文
不是因为它不重要
有时候
我们在谈论与哈米吉多顿有关的经文时
会跳过这节经文
但其实
这节经文绝不是无关紧要的
它对我们每一个人来说
都密切相关  非常重要
那我们一起来读一下第15节的经文  好吗?

“看哪!我要像贼一样来到”
“警醒而保住外衣的人多么有福!”
“因为他不用赤身行走”
“不致让人看见他的可耻模样”
所以  我们可以清楚看出
大患难真的离我们很近了
那么  我们的外衣是什么呢?
就是上帝忠仆的身份
是的
要保住这个身份!
怎么做呢?
就是要保持警醒
今天的內容取自于
守望台2015年7月15日刊的一篇文章
标题为《你们快要得救了!》
这篇文章以经文为根据
预告了前面要发生的一连串的大事
大患难发生的头一件事
就是大巴比伦会遭受毁灭
然后
大患难的第一阶段将被“缩短”
在之后短暂的平静时期
大多数人都会向
这个世界的组织和机构寻求庇护
我们传讲的将不再是好消息了
而是审判的信息
接下来  玛歌革地的歌革
也就是指联合起来的列国
会合力攻击受膏基督徒和他们的同伴
想要渡过大患难
就必须忠于耶和华
支持并服从耶稣在地上的受膏门徒
这极为重要!
那么  我们现在该怎么做呢?
要保持警醒
我们最重要的身份
不只是伯特利成员或基列毕业生
而是上帝名下的子民
在上帝的帮助下
我们付出了很多努力
才得到了这个身份
因此  要保住这个身份
怎么做呢?
要表现“圣洁的品行”
也就是要避开令上帝不悦的事
有些东西  有些事情  我们不该读
不该看  不该想  不该说
不要让“邪灵启示的不洁主张”
玷污了你真基督徒的身份
另外  还要体现“敬虔的行为”
也就是继续做上帝喜悦的事
比如传道  祷告和个人研读
基列学校会让人学到很多东西
不过  要学的东西还有很多
线上《精读本圣经》真的很棒
而且每天都在完善
如果我们加以善用
就会使自己和上帝建立更亲密的关系
我们现在努力表现“敬虔的行为”
日后就一定会成功脱险
有些人因为邪灵显出的神迹
就听信了他们不洁的主张
但我们不会受骗
是的
“全能上帝的大日子”已近在眼前
愿我们能够保全性命!

en.text: At times,

And I find sexual education a difficult topic to talk about.
In our culture, talking about sex is taboo,
so much so that our parents do not talk to us about it.
It is hard to know how much information we should give to our children.
Children are naturally curious.
Our fear is: What if they get wrong thoughts?
It is not easy to bring up children
in the last days of this system of things.
It is very difficult to train children in a blended family,
but with the help of Jehovah,
it is Jehovah who has helped us to train them.
It’s true that Jehovah has given us an incredible task
to raise our children in the truth,
but I am calm and confident
because thanks to his organization, we always have what we need,
in due time, to successfully carry out this task.
I use the videos provided by “the faithful and discreet slave”
that relate to the topics Emilien wants to talk about,
in particular, the video Protect Your Children,
which speaks about sexual predators,
is a good starting point for a discussion on this.
Even before Satan’s world can teach our children about sex,
we can teach them.
Learn From the Great Teacher, chapter 32,
has beautiful questions.
It helps us to understand what is in their hearts
and how much information they already know.
Since we have already spoken to them about sex at this age,
we can talk about any serious matters in the future without feeling awkward.
We lean on the counsel from the Bible regarding sexuality,
and this has helped the children to fear Jehovah.
Every time that we go out to the fields to do our work,
we are talking all the time with the children.
I see that Jehovah has blessed these efforts.
We do not have any problems amongst the children or with others.

At first, you feel a little like,
this is strange;
you’re at Bethel; you’re not out pioneering.
But then, when you’ve gone to the school
and you’ve seen what the school actually does for your ministry,
it was really—
You can see why the Governing Body—
It was such a kind gift for them to give us this privilege of coming.
You’re surrounded by people who have been pioneers for years;
some have been to Gilead; some have been in the traveling work;
some have conducted pioneer schools themselves.
It’s the best.
Even though they’re in this spiritual environment,
they need to be upbuilt.
As Bethelites, we go out in service
not as much as we did when we were pioneering.
So being able to have an effective use of our time
in the ministry makes a big difference.
You learn a lot about the field ministry in pioneer school.
So in a month when 30 hours was an option,
I applied to auxiliary pioneer
and I also tried to participate a lot in the ministry on weekends.
This way I was able to prepare for the school.
I think that every Christian needs to have goals,
and even for us serving in Bethel, we need goals.
So the main thing I learned from the school
is that even while working in Bethel,
I can do more for the congregation
and make a bigger effort in the ministry.
After the pioneer school,
I realized I needed to cultivate
more humility in my Bethel service
and the field ministry.
Because there’s so much spiritual food
available at Bethel,
it can become easy to neglect personal study.
Listening to the deeply meditated comments
from the students and the instructors really stimulated me
to also meditate more deeply.
During the school,
I had to study more than usual,
so I had to set aside more time for reading
so as to be well-prepared for class.
It was really practical for me
to improve my ministry,
and it was really nice because with this new school,
we had a demonstration
of what we have to avoid and what is good to do.
There was a demonstration about what not to do on a Bible study,
and I saw myself doing some of those things.
So I realized that I really needed
to get better at conducting Bible studies.
I remember one demonstration that taught us
how we can witness informally in a supermarket line, for example.
That demonstration gave me more confidence
to witness informally.
In the school, we learned a lot about Jesus
—how he was hardworking, zealous,
and showed genuine interest in the people around him.
That example helped me to be more hardworking and zealous,
as well as to be more approachable to those whom I work with.
That’s why we’re here in Bethel
—it’s to support the preaching work.
So it doesn’t matter what assignment we have.
In a way, it’s connected to that.
The fruitage of the spirit is good not just for the ministry
but it’s good for everything in everyday life toward our brothers and sisters.
Love is such an important quality for Bethelites.
I work in the Computer Department,
but I don’t treat computers with love.
But the school strengthened my determination
to treat my brothers and sisters with love.
Out of all the other schools I’ve attended,
this school had the most impact on my life.
In just one week, it strengthens our faith,
widens our view of things, trains our conscience,
and deepens our love.
It definitely
stimulated the pioneer spirit.
Even though we’re not pioneers,
it helped us to understand
the importance of the pioneer service
and how it contributes to our overall joy
in serving Jehovah.
So that’s something that we would never want to neglect.
We really appreciated the emphasis that was placed on that
and how it also helps to keep our close relationship with Jehovah.

title: 국립 공원에서 마음에 감동을 주는 활동

en.text: In the book of Romans, the first chapter, verse 20,
it talks about how you can perceive Jehovah’s creative power
by what we see in creation around us.
When you’re in a national park and you see the beauty of these parks,
you immediately think of that scripture.
We have individuals driving
from an hour and a half
to over three hours one-way
to share in this form of witnessing.
National parks generally have
what is called a freeness of speech area.
So that allows us to be able to get permission
to go into the parks to set up our carts there.
It’s just a nice place to come and relax,
and when people are relaxed, they’re wanting to talk.
They already kind of have a sense of closeness with God;
it kind of gets them thinking about their spirituality,
and then when they see our cart displayed so nicely about that,
it kind of draws them toward that.
You will find visitors from all parts of the world.
Many cultures are represented.
And quite often, we will have literature in their language.
There are many that benefit from our work at the carts.
But especially noteworthy are those
who do not have access to Bible literature.
A Chinese couple came up, and they said,
“Thank you for giving us the Bible in our language.”
That made our day.
It was fabulous!
They may not stop.
They may not talk to us.
But they see it, and that registers in their mind
—that they’ve seen this at an airport or in their city.
And now they’re going to look into it or go to the website and wonder:
‘What was that all about? What were those people doing there?’
We sit here sometimes
thinking we need to pinch ourselves
because it’s so beautiful that we’ve been given the privilege
of doing the cart work in a location like this.
Very soon, these national parks will not just be
isolated places that we have to travel to
—the entire world will be that national park.
And what a joy it will be
when every single person alive
can enjoy that beautiful painting that our Creator has made for us!

title: 로버트 시렌코: “더 중요한 것들”을 위해 시간을 내십시오

en.text: I would like to talk about a valuable asset
that every one of us possesses
—time.
It certainly is something that is on our minds
as we go about our day’s activities.
Just think of how often you look at a clock, your watch,
or your cell phone to check the time.
Why do we do that?
Probably to see if we are ahead of time, on time,
behind time, or out of time!
But what exactly is time?
One dictionary says it is “a nonspatial continuum.”
Another says it is “the thing that is measured
as seconds, minutes, hours, days, and years.”
To explain exactly what time is in simple terms is nearly impossible,
and the Bible does not define it,
which may suggest that Jehovah knows
it is beyond our ability to understand fully.
But the Bible does discuss time.
It shows that Jehovah is very time conscious.
It speaks of time as something that we should use wisely.
And it gives us the amazing hope of living into infinity
—that is, endless time.
We do know this about time:
Every human has exactly the same number
of hours and minutes in each day.
Rich people cannot buy more hours,
and scientists cannot invent new minutes.
We can never recoup the time we have wasted;
neither can we save it to spend on another day.
Just think, we have exactly the same number of hours
to use each day that Jesus Christ had when he was on the earth!
And we can be sure that no human used his time more wisely
than did God’s Son.
It has been said that time
is the most valuable thing a human can spend.
And so it is up to us how we will use the time
that is at our disposal.
In this regard, there is a Bible principle that gives us good direction,
a principle that was shared with us by the apostle Paul
at Philippians 1:9, 10.
He wrote in verse 9:
“And this is what I continue praying,”
and in verse 10,
“that you may make sure of the more important things.”
Therefore, the theme of this month’s program
is “Make Time for ‘the More Important Things.’”
This presents us with a two-fold challenge.
First, we have to determine
what are the more important things of life.
In the scripture we just read, some Bible translations say
“have a sense of what is vital.”
So we must distinguish between activities that are merely trivial
and those that really matter.
In addition to the obligation to work to support one’s family,
to care for necessary household chores,
and to look after one’s children or aging parents,
we have many important things of a spiritual nature
that deserve our full attention:
reading and meditating on God’s Word,
studying the Bible personally and in family worship,
preparing for and attending congregation meetings,
caring for any responsibilities that we have in the congregation,
and participating in the Christian ministry.
Besides all of that, who does not want some time to rest,
to exercise, to work in the garden,
to enjoy some recreation,
or to visit with family and friends?
Have you ever felt that you did not have enough time to do all those things
—that you have difficulty fitting all the spiritual activities
into your busy life?
As much as we might like to, we cannot add an extra hour to our day
or another day to our week to accomplish more things.
So we have to be selective
about how we spend the time that we have.
We will get the most accomplished
if we prioritize the things that really matter.
And what does that mean?
To prioritize means to decide
which tasks are more important and to do them first.
In other words, decide what must be given attention
prior to other things.
There is a Bible proverb that nicely illustrates
the importance of prioritizing life’s activities.
Proverbs 12:11 states:
“The one who cultivates his land
“will be satisfied with food,
“but the one pursuing worthless things
is lacking good sense.”
What a clear warning that is for a farmer
not to fill up his day with worthless endeavors
and waste the precious time that he should be spending working in his field!
Likewise, a Christian who diligently cultivates his spirituality
can be confident of Jehovah’s blessing,
whereas a person who is distracted by worthless activities
puts his relationship with God in danger.
How can we avoid that?
By not taking valuable time away from spiritual pursuits
to spend on the things that distract us
from serving Jehovah whole-souled.
For example, when it comes to communicating with others,
what should take priority?
Starting our day by giving Jehovah praise and thanks
in prayer for another day of life
or telephoning an old friend to catch up
on the latest news in his or her life?
There’s nothing wrong with talking to a friend.
But we need to make sure we take the time
to talk to our very best Friend, Jehovah.
Obviously, it is more important to communicate with our heavenly Father,
so praying to him should be a priority.
The apostle Paul had more to say about time management.
At Ephesians 5:15-17, he wrote:
“So keep strict watch that how you walk
“is not as unwise but as wise persons,
“making the best use of your time,
“because the days are wicked.
“On this account stop being unreasonable,
“but keep perceiving what
the will of Jehovah is.”
Now we can address the second part of our challenge:
to make ample time to care
for the more important things of life.
What does Paul’s counsel
to ‘make the best use of your time’ actually mean?
Literally, in Greek, it means to ‘buy out the appointed time.’
That implies buying time at the expense of something else.
So it helps to analyze how our time is actually being spent
and to see what adjustments are needed
so that we can buy out, or make, time for the more important things.
If we ‘perceive what the will of Jehovah is,’
then we certainly will want to use as much time as possible
to forge an ever stronger relationship with him
and to share fully in sacred service.
Do you have definite periods set aside for the spiritual activities of life?
For congregation meetings, the schedule is set for us.
We know exactly when our congregation meets
for its midweek and weekend meetings.
We just have to be sure that we do not let
anything else get in the way of our attending
because the meetings are a priority.
Hebrews 10:25 says ‘not to forsake’ them.
For everything else
—reading the Bible, preparing for meetings,
family worship, field service activity—
we have to set our own schedule
and stick to it as part of a good spiritual routine.
As an example, what does your family do
most Saturday mornings?
Many families have the routine of going in field service every Saturday.
Rarely is anything allowed to get in the way of that routine.
For them, Saturday morning is not the time
for music lessons, dance classes, cooking courses,
working out at the gym, or anything else
—it is their time for field service.
Having a routine like that makes life easier for everyone in the family.
No one has to wonder Friday night
what is going to happen Saturday morning.
The decision has already been made
to go out in the ministry that day.
Otherwise, if we leave it up to chance every week,
then it means that 52 times during the year
we have to decide whether to go in service on Saturday.
How much simpler it is to make the decision once and for all
that we will use that time slot for the ministry,
barring any serious, unforeseen circumstances.
Of course, given your family’s situation,
another day of the week may work better.
But you get the point.
Sharing regularly in the Christian ministry cannot be left up to chance.
At Mark 13:10,
Jesus prioritized the ministry when he said:
“The good news has to be preached first.”
So if spiritual matters are going to take precedence in our lives,
we first have to make them priorities,
and second,
make ample time to care for those priorities.
That means setting aside definite periods of time
to build up our spirituality
and to stay fully involved in our worship and service.
Ecclesiastes 3:1 reinforces this thought.
It states:
“There is an appointed time for everything,
a time for every activity under the heavens.”
We have to decide when that “appointed time” is
for each of our spiritual activities.
If we are having difficulty with this,
can we shorten the time we spend on hobbies, recreation,
sports, social networking
and devote that time to our Bible reading, family worship,
meeting preparation, or field ministry?
If we can, we will find it to be spiritually refreshing
and invigorating.
This was the experience of a family man that I know
who began preparing better so as to participate each week
in the “Digging for Spiritual Gems” portion of the midweek meeting.
He made time on Sunday evenings for this.
All in his family and congregation have benefited
from the excellent points he has learned
as he does research on the assigned Bible reading,
and he feels good because of it.
One married couple decided to eliminate
some of their hobbies and personal projects.
They even packed them up and put them out of sight.
Why?
So as not to be distracted by those things.
They were nonessential activities that they decided they could do without.
Likely, we could all benefit from taking inventory of our lives
and limiting any unnecessary activities
that may be interfering with our spiritual routine.
Imagine how rewarding that would be!
Just think, if we could buy out 30 minutes each day
from doing something that is not essential,
that is about how much time it would take
to read the entire Bible in one year.
Or if we could buy out an extra hour or two
each week for the field ministry,
think of how much more we could accomplish
and how happy that would make God and Christ,
as they see us making time for the more important things!
Now, why have we felt the need to spend this time
discussing how to manage time?
It is because of something else that the Bible tells us.
First Corinthians 7:29 says
that “the time left is reduced.”
That certainly is true of the time
that is left between now and the great tribulation!
This is not the time to neglect
the most important activity of all
—our worship of Jehovah.

title: 존 실러와 섀런 실러: 모든 기회를 놓치지 않았다

en.text: Let’s turn our attention to the Schiller family.
Is it possible to balance raising a family with a busy spiritual routine?
And if circumstances allow, can parents reach out for spiritual goals
—even full-time service?
Let’s listen to their answers to those questions.
Sometimes people say: “Well, you know, what was your secret?
How did you raise six kids?”
We got married September 16, 1972.
Two things started coming quickly
—spiritual privileges came along and the children came along—
together.
I was made an elder
shortly after the elder arrangement came into effect.
The kids were just part of all that,
and you might think that sometimes they didn’t know it.
We were doing substitute work with five children,
and I don’t think they even knew what we were doing.
In 1989, we were pioneering,
and then we had the opportunity to help out at Bethel,
maybe a week or two at a time.
About that time, Patterson was starting up.
And we kind of recognized
that maybe we were getting too comfortable.
We went one time to Bethel and said:
“Hey, if you need a doctor out at Patterson, why, we’d be available.
Or we could make ourselves available, maybe.”
And wouldn’t you know it, shortly after, we got a call,
“How quickly could you sell your place and be up here?”
So we went to Bethel with six kids,
sold our house at a loss so we could do that,
and started a new life there.
So we learned pretty quickly: Don’t turn down any privileges
—and especially not because we had kids.
When we went to Bethel, the oldest one was 17.
Having children
kept my husband and me very humble
because as soon as you thought you had something figured out,
each child needed to be disciplined in a different way.
And as soon as you thought, ‘Boy, you know, I’ve got this figured out,’
you’re thrown a curve.
A challenge was to keep doing the basic things.
You’d come home tired.
It would be so easy not to have the family study
maybe one Monday.
It’s those basic, simple things
that I think kept us on an even keel.
I often think of the illustration that Jesus gave
at the end of the Sermon on the Mount,
what he said about this foundation that was washed away.
And Jesus never blamed the storm; he blamed the foundation.
And so we recognize that any child anywhere
—in fact, even adults— can get their faith tested.
So we tried to really make sure
they had a good foundation that didn’t get washed away.
Prepare them, let them learn how to deal with people
while they’re under your care,
and get them ready for life.
We got to thinking, ‘Other parents require their kids to go to college,’
so we just required them
to pioneer for a year.
Any kind of education—
Any kind of secular education can teach you
how to have a skill so that you have a job.
But the Bible teaches you how to live,
and it teaches you principles that you can live your life by.
And all of them kept pioneering.
You know, they did various jobs to support themselves.
They cleaned; they worked at lumberyards; they worked on roofing.
And none of them have
a complicated life that holds them down.
I wanted everlasting life for my children,
and I knew I would have to give them back to Jehovah.
We have to realize we don’t own our children —Jehovah does.
And we have to respect that.
We’re not telling them what to do anymore.
We appreciate and we’re very, very thankful
when our children, as far away as they are
and as busy as they are,
take the time to communicate with us.
And I know you won’t remember this,
but I remember one time, before you fell asleep at night,
I said, “With all that you have done for Jehovah,
what would you like in return?”
Do you remember what you said?
You said three words, “All my children.”
In Deuteronomy it says: “I have put life and death before you,
. . . and you must choose.”
So we can do what we can as parents
—some things good, some things not so good.
In the end, each one had to make
his or her own decision.
And that’s why, again, it was not any secret we had.
We’re so proud of what the kids decided
and how they turned out because it was their decision.
I think that’s the thing that we’ve learned:
Don’t turn down opportunities.
Isn’t it wonderful to hear of ones like Brother and Sister Schiller
who have offered their gifts to Jehovah?
Brother Schiller said that it was doing the basic things
that kept his family focused spiritually.
So when opportunities came along, he was able to do more,
which included pioneering, substitute circuit work,
and using the medical training he had already acquired
to volunteer at the Patterson Educational Center.
Proverbs 10:22 says:
“It is the blessing of Jehovah that makes one rich,
and He adds no hardship with it.”(Ftn.)
That certainly has proved true for Brother Schiller and his family.

en.text: This morning I’d like you to imagine
for a few moments
that you’ve been asked to write
your life story for The Watchtower.
Well, once you get over the shock,
how would you go about doing that?
You’ve probably noticed with many of the life experiences in The Watchtower,
usually the first paragraph,
have a defining moment in that person’s life.
For example, Brother Eric Beveridge, who serves with us here in the United States,
he started off this way:
“‘I hereby sentence you to six months in prison.’
“With those words ringing in my ears, I was taken off to . . .
“[p]rison in Manchester, England. . . .
“I had just faced one of the toughest tests of my young life
—I had refused to be conscripted for military service.”
Or another brother, Brother Harley Harris,
who served as a missionary in Ecuador for many years,
he referred to the date September 2, 1950.
He said: “We were at a circuit assembly, surrounded by a mob.
“The mayor brought in the National Guard to protect us from the unruly crowd.
“Soldiers with drawn rifles and bayonets lined the street.
“Amid insults, we walked to our cars and drove to . . .
“the remaining sessions of the assembly.
It was there that I was baptized at the age of 14.”
Or another brother, Brother Don MacLean
—who serves on the Branch Committee in Australasia,
a brother originally from Canada—
made this comment.
He started his life experience:
“There I sat, hour after hour,
“with one of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police by my side.
“I was his prisoner.
“We were headed for the prison camp at . . . Ontario, Canada,
“and it seemed [that] the 1,500-mile train trip
would never end.”
Well, those certainly were defining moments
in the lives of those brothers.
What about you?
What is your defining moment?
Well, you might be thinking,
‘No one put a gun to my head and said,
“Decide now whether you’ll serve Jehovah or not.”’
But for many of us, there have been defining moments in our lives.
Perhaps it’s the moment you decided to serve Jehovah
or the moment you decided to become a full-time servant.
Perhaps it involved some decisions, such as selling a home,
selling a business, deciding to move to Bethel,
or perhaps leaving your country and going somewhere else.
Or it may have involved certain tests or trials,
perhaps giving up opportunities for education
or for lucrative job opportunities.
Well, whatever the case,
I’m sure most of us have had some defining moments
in our lives that we remember
—the decisions that were made that resulted in much good.
Let’s think for a moment about the faithful man Abraham.
What was the defining moment in his life?
Well, if you take your Bibles and turn with me to Hebrews chapter 11,
of course, here we see the apostle Paul giving us an outline
or history of many of the defining moments
in the lives of faithful ones.
At Hebrews 11:8, it says of Abraham:
“By faith Abraham, when he was called,
“obeyed by going out to a place
“he was to receive as an inheritance;
he went out, although not knowing where he was going.”
Yes, that was a defining moment in the life of Abraham, wasn’t it?
He decided to obey Jehovah, to leave Ur,
and to travel to a distant country that he didn’t really know about.
But was that all that was involved
with Abraham receiving the reward?
No.
Let’s read on a little further in verse 9.
There it says:
“By faith he lived as a foreigner
“in the land of the promise as in a foreign land,
“living in tents with Isaac and Jacob,
the heirs with him of the very same promise.”
Now, this is not a defining moment, is it?
This is a course of faithfulness,
day in, day out.
So, what’s the point?
Well, in the case of Abraham,
we remember that eventually he and his family
crossed the Euphrates River and into the Promised Land
in the year 1943 B.C.E.
But he had to wait 25 years before his son Isaac was born
and then another 60 years
before his grandsons Esau and Jacob were born.
And eventually, he died after being in the Promised Land
as a foreigner for about 100 years.
So, what’s the point?
Although there was a definite decision he made
—a defining moment in his life—
that was backed up as verse 9 says,
by his faithfulness
—day in, day out—
serving Jehovah.
So the lesson we learn from that is
that it’s not just the defining moments
that define who we are.
Rather, those moments and those decisions
need to be backed up by faithful service.
Let’s be quite frank.
Many of the life experiences that we read in The Watchtower
may have a very exciting first paragraph.
“Yes, they put a gun to my head.
“Make your decision.
“Will you die?
Would you be willing to die for Jehovah?”
But then, when you read the rest of the article,
nothing really exciting happened in that person’s life.
I’m sorry to say it.
That includes my life experience as well.
Why?
Because the majority of our lives
are not involved with defining moments
—exciting things that are happening.
Rather, they involve our faithfulness to Jehovah.
So we can’t just rely upon these defining moments and say,
“Well, I made this decision to serve Jehovah;
I passed this test, so everything is good.”
No, we need to continue to back up those defining moments
with faithful service.
Remember that in the Scriptures,
there were many who had defining moments in their lives.
Take, for example, Solomon.
He had a defining moment, didn’t he, when he prayed to Jehovah
and he was praised for the fact that he asked for wisdom rather than wealth?
But that wasn’t backed up by faithfulness.
Eventually, that defining moment in his life
really wasn’t as valuable as it could’ve been
because of his lack of faithfulness.
And what about Judas Iscariot?
Were there some defining moments in his life?
Obviously, he decided to follow Jesus at one point.
And during that time, when he faithfully followed Jesus,
no doubt, there were very exciting, interesting things that happened.
But again, those defining moments in his life
proved to be of little value
because of the lack of faithfulness on his part.
So that helps us to understand
why the apostle Paul said some very interesting points
just before he started this list that he gives us in Hebrews chapter 11.
Let’s turn to Hebrews chapter 10,
Hebrews 10:35-39.
Notice, this is the point that we should gain from this lesson.
Paul says starting in verse 35:
“Therefore, do not throw away your boldness,
“which will be richly rewarded.
For you need endurance,”
now, that reminds us of what Jesus said
about ‘the one who endures to the end will be saved,’
“so that after you have done the will of God,
“you may receive the fulfillment of the promise.
“For yet ‘a very little while,’
“and ‘the one who is coming will arrive and will not delay.’
“‘But my righteous one will live by reason of faith,’
“and ‘if he shrinks back, I have no pleasure in him.’
“Now we are not the sort who shrink back to destruction,
but the sort who have faith for the preserving of our lives.”
What a very positive comment that is.
So when we think of our life experience,
don’t be disappointed if you don’t have some spectacular things
that you can mention as defining moments.
Remember, the important thing
is not just the decisions that we make along the way
but the fact that we remain faithful to Jehovah
day in, day out.

cn.text: 请想象一下
假如你现在受到邀请
为《守望台》写自己的人物生平
你高兴之余
打算如何着手去写呢？
通常来说《守望台》登载的人物生平
一开头都是从主人公
一生最重要的时刻开始讲起
比如，现在也在美国服务的
埃里克·贝弗里奇弟兄
他以这样的方式开始介绍自己
我宣判你将入狱六个月
伴随着耳边响起的这些话
我被押送到
英国曼彻斯特的一个监狱
因为拒绝被征召服兵役
我开始面对自己年轻时最大的考验
在厄瓜多尔做特派传道员多年的
哈利·哈里斯弟兄
特别提到1950年9月2号这一天
他说
我们正参加分区大会
这期间一群暴民包围会场
他们失去控制
市长就召国民警卫队来保护我们
手持步枪和刺刀的士兵
排列在马路两旁，阻截暴民
我们在辱骂声中走到自己的汽车
然后去继续参加大会的其余节目
我就在那里受浸，当时14岁
另外一位是加拿大
唐·麦克莱恩弟兄
目前在南太平洋区分部委员会服务
他这样开始讲述
我坐在这里
旁边是一名加拿大皇家骑警
而我是他看守的犯人
我们正乘火车前往
加拿大安大略省的一个监狱
这2400公里的路程竟如此漫长
仿佛永远不会到达终点
这些时刻
的确都是这几位弟兄人生的关键时刻
那么你呢？
你人生中的重要时刻是什么时候？
你也许会说
从没有人用枪指着我的头说
你必须选择还要不要崇拜耶和华
不过话说回来
几乎每个人
生活中也都有重要的时刻
也许是你决定献身给耶和华
或者决心成为全时仆人的那一刻
也许是你做重要决定的时刻
比如卖掉房子、卖掉公司
决定到伯特利服务
或者决定离开家乡去扩大服务
也有可能是你面对考验的时刻
比如放弃深造的机会
拒绝收入很高的工作等
不论是哪种情况
我相信大多数人
都有一些难以忘记的重要时刻
那时候做的重大决定
后来带来了美好的结果
我们现在考虑一下亚伯拉罕
这位信心的榜样
什么时候是他人生的
一个重要时刻呢？
请你打开圣经
我们一起读一下希伯来书11章
在这一章
使徒保罗列出了很多有信心的人
并提到他们人生中的重要时刻
希伯来书11:8提到亚伯拉罕说
“凭着信心
亚伯拉罕受上帝呼召时就服从命令
前往上帝要给他做产业的地方
他虽然不知道要去哪里
却还是去了”
没错，这的确是亚伯拉罕
人生中的重要时刻对吗？
他决定服从耶和华
离开吾珥
搬到一个自己一无所知的很远的地方
但仅仅因这一个举动
亚伯拉罕就能得到奖赏吗？
不是的
我们接着往下看第9节说
“凭着信心
他住在上帝承诺赐予的土地上
就像外族人住在异乡一样
与得到同一个承诺的以撒、雅各
都住在帐篷里”
这里说的
可不是一个重要时刻对吗？
这是每天都保持忠贞的现实生活
日复一日、年复一年
那么要点是什么呢？
就亚伯拉罕来说
他和家人后来在公元前1943年
渡过幼发拉底河
进入了应许之地
但他一直等了25年
儿子以撒才出生
之后他又等了60年
孙子以扫和雅各才出生
他作为侨居的人
在应许之地生活了100年
并最终死在那里
要点是什么呢？
亚伯拉罕一生中
的确有重要时刻，就是
他做明确的决定的时候
但刚才所读的第九节说
他需要每天都忠心地事奉耶和华
日复一日、年复一年
从中可以看出，我们是怎样的人
不只是通过某几个重要时刻来证明的
而是要看我们有没有
一直忠贞地为上帝服务
坦率说
很多《守望台》的“人物生平”
开篇都非常精彩
是的，他们拿枪对准我的头，说
做决定吧，你真的想死吗？
你想为了耶和华去死吗？
但当你把文章读完后
发现那个人的生活
其实也没有你想的那样激动人心
很抱歉这样说
但我们的人生经历大都如此
包括我自己的也是
为什么呢？
因为我们生活的大部分时间
并不总是这样的重要时刻
也不会总有激动人心的事情发生
其实，我们需要时刻都保持忠贞
而不只是凭着这些重要时刻就断言说
嗯，我决定事奉耶和华
我通过了考验
以后我肯定都会永远忠贞
这还不够
我们在经历了重要的时刻之后
需要继续忠心地事奉上帝
在圣经中
有许多人都经历过重要时刻
比如所罗门
他曾向耶和华求智慧而不是财富
令上帝很喜悦
这是他的重要时刻，对吗？
但很可惜，他后来变得不忠
最后，由于他偏离正道
他人生中的重要时刻
也变得不再那么有价值了
加略人犹大又怎样？
他一生中也有重要的时刻吗？
当然有
他曾做出决定，跟随耶稣
在他紧紧跟随耶稣的那段时期
一定有很多
令人振奋而又有趣的事发生
但同样，由于他变得不忠贞
那些重要时刻也被证明是没有价值的
这些事例，都帮助我们明白
使徒保罗在希伯来书11章
列举那些忠仆之前
他为什么说了这样的话
请打开希伯来书第10章
希伯来书第10章
留意我们可以从中学到什么
保罗从35节开始说
“因此要勇敢，不要放弃
因为会有丰厚的奖赏
你们必须忍耐”
这让我们想起耶稣的话:
忍耐到底的人，必然得救
“这样你们遵行了上帝的旨意之后
就可以得到他承诺的福分
再过‘一会儿’
‘要来的那位就会来到，不会延迟’
‘我正义的仆人会因信心而活下去’
‘如果他退缩，我就不喜欢他’
我们不是退缩以致灭亡的人
而是有信心得以保全生命的人”
这是多么鼓舞人的话
所以，当我们回想
自己的人生经历时
不要因为没有精彩的重要时刻
就感到失望
要记得
重要的不只是
我们所做的重要决定
更是我们要始终如一地忠于耶和华
日复一日、年复一年

titles.ko: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 아브라함처럼 충실함을 유지하십시오 (창세 12:2)
titles.en: Geoffrey W. Jackson: Be Faithful Like Abraham (Gen. 12:2)
titles.cn: 杰弗里·杰克逊：效法亚伯拉罕的榜样，时刻忠贞（创12:2）

en.text: This is a report of the branch visit
to the Central America branch and Cuba,
in April.
My wife, Jean, and I
had the privilege to visit the Bethel
in Mexico City and then, after that,
the Bethel in Havana.
At Haggai 2:7 the words of Jehovah state:
“‘And I will shake all the nations,
“‘and the precious things
“‘of all the nations will come in;
and I will fill this house with glory,’
says Jehovah of armies.”
In this part of the world,
hundreds of thousands of people
are flocking to Jehovah.
And currently, there are over one million preachers
who regularly bring glory to His house.
These two branches are responsible
to care for the spiritual needs of people
in Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador,
Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua,
Panama, Mexico, and Cuba.
In all these places, there are many people
who are really precious to Jehovah.
What makes them precious?
They are fully devoted to Jehovah,
and they display qualities that he appreciates
—qualities that mean a lot to him.
Let us introduce you to some of them.
Each experience is summarized
by one of the qualities precious to Jehovah.
Please note them as we briefly relate their stories.
The first experience is about the brothers and sisters
in the Rio Coco Miskito congregation, in Asang.
The publishers in that village wanted to go up the river
to preach to people in that very remote part of Nicaragua.
But they did not have the money to buy a boat.
They found a big tree that had fallen,
cut it up, hollowed it out, and made a boat out of it.
It took 50 of them just to move this boat into the water.
Then they went up the river into those remote villages
to preach to the people.
Guess what they used?
—electronic tablets.
Wherever they went they showed the people
the new video publications
in the Miskito language using their tablets.
They gave a tremendous witness.
So even though they used ancient technology to travel
to these remote places,
they used the latest technology
to preach once they got there.
These brothers and sisters are very creative,
and they make the most of their resources
to accomplish what needs to be done.
The next story is a story of determination.
In Mexico there is a young girl, 8 years old,
named Zurisadai Moreno Humarán.
She was diagnosed with leukemia
and went through a tortuous path of going
to many different doctors and hospitals
where people tried to force blood on her.
Of course, the Hospital Liaison Committee was working hard to help.
Zuri was flown all over the country
looking for a doctor to treat her,
and eventually she was able to get the right treatment.
She made a strong stand for Jehovah,
defending her faith.
She was going to obey Jehovah no matter what.
While all of this was happening,
she decided to get baptized.
She could not do all of this without her parents and family.
Her face gleams with determination, doesn’t it?
A circuit overseer in El Salvador
told this experience:
“One time after I finished accompanying publishers on Bible studies,
“we said good-bye, and I went down another street.
“A group of gang members came out of a house.
“I immediately went into the nearest house to avoid a confrontation.
“I was so glad that the householder kindly told me to come inside.
“I began to preach to her.
“The lady patiently listened to me.
“About an hour later, they either got bored or tired and left.
So I took advantage of the opportunity and left right away.”
The following experience illustrates how the fear of God
can motivate us to do the right thing.
In a small village in Mexico,
about 2,000 people got together
and expelled the Witnesses from their village.
They were forced out of their homes
and were not allowed to bring their possessions.
Among them were grandparents, parents,
little children, and even babies.
They were forced into cars and trucks
and driven out of the village
and dropped off in the mountains.
That night was a cold night.
They were shivering; they had no food,
but they trusted in Jehovah.
I have felt fear,
but it’s a fear of not doing Jehovah’s will,
because many lives would be lost.
Many people would remain in spiritual darkness.
They would not come to know Jehovah.
So the next day, he and his family went back to the village
they had been thrown out of
and spoke to the leading men there.
These men agreed that they could come back.
The brothers all came home,
and now the congregation is flourishing in this village,
and the brothers freely preach from door to door.
Many young people have left behind
opportunities for higher education.
They’ve stepped out of the boat and walked on water.
They left behind so-called security and safety,
and they put their lives in Jehovah’s hands.
Even though they’ve chosen to give up
some comforts of life to serve in remote areas,
they are happy and live fulfilling lives.
Having our minds focused on the ministry
has helped us as a young couple.
It’s helped us not to set materialistic goals,
which would enslave us to work toward financial goals,
but rather to think about the ministry.
I learned that if you put all your energies into this world,
the world will only use them to its convenience.
But if you use it for Jehovah,
he will help you feel full and he will give meaning to your life.
Next, we went to Cuba.
Cuba is a beautiful place.
Although, at this time, Cuba may not be known
for its physical riches,
it is full of the most amazing spiritual riches
—what Jehovah calls ‘the precious things of the nations.’
Most of our brothers do not have much in a material way,
but they are happy as they work hard to give Jehovah
their very best.
Spiritually, they are rich.
Despite many challenges, they have around 96,000 publishers,
and many more are coming into the truth.
While they cannot have Kingdom Halls, they do have meeting places.
The following pictures show the outside of a meeting place,
and then a view of the inside.
It might not be impressive from the physical perspective,
but all of them are precious to Jehovah.
The amazing thing is that even though
these brothers do not have much materially,
they are able to offer part of their property as a meeting place.
Under Cuban law, you inherit property
from your parents, and so on.
Sometimes it’s just a hallway, a room,
or an attachment at the back of the house.
Fifty or sixty publishers can fit into these small places.
But the point is that they have meeting places,
and they are able to have all the meetings.
A remarkable feature of Cuba
is that vintage cars are used as taxis and family cars.
But the brothers
are up-to-date with JW Broadcasting
and convention videos.
For example,
at the weekly Christian Life and Ministry meetings,
the videos are used as normal.
They have it all.
How do they do that without much Internet access?
This is how:
The few brothers who do have some Internet access
make copies of the programs.
Then they copy them from phone, to phone, to phone.
Everybody seems to have a cell phone.
Maybe some of the phones don’t have video,
but at least they have sound.
When they go to the meeting, they play the program on the TV screen,
and everyone gets the full benefit of the program.
Among Jehovah’s precious people in Cuba
are six brothers and sisters
who are both deaf and blind.
Two deaf and blind sisters
came to Bethel for an interview.
It was amazing to watch
when they met for the first time.
The brothers translate the study edition of The Watchtower
into Cuban Sign Language.
One local census taken by our brothers suggests
that about 1 in 5 deaf people that we have encountered
is studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
This couple, who assist with translation, are both deaf.
The “precious things” of Central America and Cuba
are indeed praising Jehovah.
They are fully devoted to serving Jehovah,
and they always seem to be smiling.
At meetings and at larger gatherings,
it is evident that they know who they are
and that they represent Jehovah worthily.
These precious ones truly appreciate
all the provisions from Jehovah’s temple arrangement.
And currently, they are helping
about one and a half million Bible students
to bring praise and glory to Jehovah’s name.
And the brothers at these two branches asked us
to bring to you their love and deep affection.

cn.text: 去年4月
我和妻子琼一起探访了
中美洲分部和古巴分部
我们先参观了位于墨西哥城的伯特利
接着又参观了位于哈瓦那的伯特利
在哈该书2:7  耶和华说
“我要震动万国”
“万国的珍宝必都前来”
“我要使这座圣殿充满荣耀”
“这是万军之主耶和华说的”
在这里有成千上万的人
正通过学习圣经
开始崇拜耶和华
有一百多万传道员
正热心参与传道工作
来荣耀耶和华
中美洲分部和古巴分部
负责照顾一些国家弟兄姐妹的属灵需要
这些国家有伯利玆  哥斯达黎加
萨尔瓦多  危地马拉  洪都拉斯
尼加拉瓜  巴拿马  墨西哥和古巴
这里有许多宝贵的弟兄姐妹
耶和华非常珍视他们
因为他们尽心竭力地事奉耶和华
也表现了美好的基督徒特质
而这些宝贵的特质
是上帝非常欣赏的
接下来
我们会分享一些朋友的经历
每个经历
都集中体现了耶和华悦纳的一种特质
这几种特质已经列了出来
请大家在观看时留意一下
首先  我们一起认识一下
位于奥森小镇的里约科库
米斯基托会众的弟兄姐妹
这里的传道员
很想乘船到尼加拉瓜的偏远地方
帮助那里的人认识上帝
但他们没有钱买船
后来  他们发现了一棵倒下的大树
就把它锯开  中间挖空
这样船就造好了
他们当时用了50个人
才把船拉进了河里
然后
他们乘船到那些偏远的小村庄传道
他们用什么传道工具呢?
就是平板电脑
这样  不管他们去哪里
都可以向当地人播放
米斯基托语的影片
结果  他们做了许多美好的见证
有意思的是
他们乘坐的交通工具很古老
但使用的电子产品却很现代
这些弟兄姐妹真的很有创意
他们善用一切资源
努力完成上帝交托的工作
接下来的故事
会告诉我们什么是坚定的信念
在墨西哥  有一个8岁的小女孩
她叫苏蕾莎迪
她被查出患有白血病
就四处求医治病
但是很多医生
都试图说服她接受输血疗法
当然  在这个过程中
我们的医院联络委员会
也提供了许多帮助
为了治病  家人带着苏蕾
几乎跑遍了整个墨西哥
最后终于找到了适合她的疗法
苏蕾立场非常坚定
不管遇到什么困难
她都决心服从耶和华
尽管面对这么多的难题
她还是决定受浸
当然  她能够成功地克服这些困难
与家人的帮助是分不开的
你看她的脸
是不是散发着坚定的信念呢?
在萨尔瓦多的一位分区监督
和我们分享了一个经历
他说  有一次
我和传道员们工作结束后
大家就分开了
我独自一个人走了另一条路
突然  一群歹徒走了过来
为了避免和他们发生正面冲突
我就赶快向离我最近的房子走去
让我高兴的是
这个房子的主人很友善
还示意让我进去
接着我就向她传道
她听得非常认真
大约一小时后
我发现这些人不见了
也许他们等得不耐烦了
或者是累了吧
于是  我就趁机赶快离开了
接下来的经历会讲述
敬畏上帝
可以怎样推动我们做对的事
在墨西哥的一个小村庄
大约有2000人聚集起来
把这个村庄的耶和华见证人都赶了出去
他们被迫离开家园
而且不允许携带任何东西
被驱赶的人群中有老人
孩子  婴儿还有他们的父母
这些人把弟兄姐妹强行带到车上
当车抵达村外的荒山后
就把他们扔在那里
那天晚上真的非常冷
他们冻得直打哆嗦  而且没有吃的
但是他们仍然信赖耶和华
当时我很害怕
害怕再也不能帮助村里的人认识上帝了
如果他们不能认识上帝
就只能一直留在属灵的黑暗里
不能得救了
第二天
他和家人去找那些带头的人见面商量
结果他们居然同意让所有人回来
现在  所有被赶出去的弟兄姐妹
终于可以回到自己的家了!
目前  这里会众的人数不断增加
而且弟兄们
也可以自由地挨家挨户传道了
彼得因为有信心
就从船上下来  在水上行走
同样  这里的年轻人
放弃了追求高等教育的机会
放弃了这个世界提供的“保障”
把自己的前途交给耶和华
全心信赖他
他们放弃了舒适的生活
甘愿到偏远地区服务
结果得到了心满意足的生活
对于我们这样的年轻夫妻来说
专注于传道工作对我们的帮助很大
因为我们专注于为耶和华服务
就不会一心只想着赚钱
这样就不会成为财富的奴隶
我学到
如果你拼尽全力追求世界的事
这个世界只会把你榨干  毫不吝惜
如果你全心为耶和华服务
你就会感到很充实
人生也会充满意义
下一站是古巴
古巴是个美丽的地方
虽然在经济上古巴不是很富裕
但在属灵方面却十分富足
正如耶和华所说
他们是“万国的珍宝”
这里许多弟兄姐妹的生活并不富裕
但他们还是因把最好的献给耶和华
而大感喜乐
因此在属灵的意义上
他们的确很富足
虽然面对不少挑战
但仍有大约9万6000个传道员
热心参与传道工作
也有越来越多的人开始学习圣经
虽然这里没有正式的王国聚会所
但他们却有聚会的地方
照片中我们看到的是聚会场所的外面
现在我们再来看一下里面
虽然这里的聚会场所看上去没那么美观
但在耶和华眼中
这些地方却十分宝贵
令我们大受鼓励的是
虽然弟兄们并不富裕
但他们
还是愿意把自己所继承房产的一部分
贡献出来作为聚会的地方
有时聚会的地方可能是一个门厅
一个房间
或是房子后面临时搭建的场所

en.text: Welcome to this special update.
Pure worship is under attack
in the country of Russia.
In this program, we will update you
on our efforts to defend God’s precious Word, the Bible,
from those who would seek to ban it in Russia.
We will interview a brother who was present in the courtroom
for the recent appeal hearing
regarding the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures.
We will also update you on the court case
to seize the property of our branch office in Russia
and show you what has recently taken place
to seize the Assembly Hall complex in St. Petersburg.
As you may be aware, on December 20,
the Leningrad Regional Court denied our appeal of a decision
to ban the Russian-language New World Translation,
declaring it an “extremist” publication.
This is against Russian law.
Specifically, according to an amendment to Article 3
of the Federal Law on Extremism,
signed by President Putin himself
in the fall of 2015:
“The Bible, the Koran,
“the Tanakh, and the Kangyur,
“their contents and quotations from them
cannot be recognized as extremist materials.”
With such a clear law like that in force,
any reasonable person would wonder,
‘How could a Russian court ban a Bible?’
We are pleased to have with us Brother Moses Ajiboye,
who was present in the courtroom for the recent appeal hearing.
Moses, it’s good to see you. Welcome.
Thank you, Mark. It’s a privilege to be with you.
Now, Moses, before we discuss the appeal hearing,
could you help us understand how the proceedings
against the New World Translation have unfolded up until now?
Yes, Mark.
This case began back on August 13, 2015,
after a prosecutor filed a claim
to declare the New World Translation in Russian to be “extremist.”
At the beginning of the trial
back then in April 2016,
the prosecutor demanded
that the court request an “expert” study
from a panel of “experts”
who have consistently provided
biased reports against Jehovah’s Witnesses in the past.
Their so-called studies have been refuted
by other unbiased scientific experts as well.
Well, the judge then ruled to adjourn the case
and allow time for this “expert” study of the Bible.
The study was completed and submitted to the court
more than a year later on May 22, 2017.
As expected,
the biased study was full of outrageous statements
that were not based on the facts.
The study even concluded
that the New World Translation was not a Bible,
since it did not say “Bible” on the cover.
So in late July 2017,
the court resumed its hearings of the case.
Well, Moses, can you tell us what it was like in the courtroom
when the trial resumed in July?
Over a period of 4 days, there were 30 hours of court hearings.
During that time, our attorneys exposed
the so-called expert study
and its key claims as unfounded, biased,
absurd, inconsistent, and invalid.
Our attorneys proved that the New World Translation is consistent
with other Russian Bible translations by having many verses read
in two or more Bible translations for comparison.
In fact, some 25 Bible passages
were read in the courtroom.
On one occasion, Mark,
the judge selected a verse in the New World Translation
that may have appeared to him as controversial
and asked our lawyer to explain it.
Of course, our lawyer simply asked that the verse be read
in all three different translations.
And after that, they all had the same idea
and no further explanation was needed.
One of our attorneys described the scene
in the courtroom this way,
and I will quote him, Mark, if I may.
He said: “Yesterday, the judge read a great many scriptures
“from various translations of the Bible:
“the New World Translation, the synodal translation,
“the modern translation, and others.
“Many scriptures were read about family life,
“raising children, and loving our neighbors.
“We read Psalm 23
“in three different translations for comparison.
“The judge himself read all the scriptures.
“Just imagine the scene:
“the courtroom, two prosecutors,
“three attorneys, and the audience.
“In the center of the table sits the judge
“with five to seven translations of the Bible.
“The judge opens the various Bible translations,
“reads aloud, and asks questions.
“It was a stunning picture!
It reminded us of a well-prepared Bible study.”
Well, that’s just incredible, Moses!
Well, what were some of the ways
that God’s Word was attacked during this hearing,
and how did our brothers put up a defense for the Bible?
Yes, the so-called experts attacked the use of God’s holy name, Jehovah,
in the New World Translation.
The “expert” study states:
“In the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures,
“the dominant factor of the text is the ‘Jehovah’ concept.
“The ‘Jehovah’ concept expresses a personified god
“with such names as ‘Jehovah God,’
“‘Jehovah of armies,’ ‘the King, Jehovah of armies,’
“‘the Holy One of Israel,’ et cetera.
“Thus, in the opinion of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
“he has the personal name ‘Jehovah.’
“So the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures
“does not qualify as a Christian Bible
but is an independent text.”
So in order to expose this attack,
the lawyers introduced to the court
ten other Russian Bibles that use the name Jehovah.
They allowed—
They also showed the court poetry
by renowned Russian poets
Tsvetaeva and Pushkin;
and books by Kuprin, Goncharov, and Dostoyevsky;
and excerpts from other classic Russian literature
where the name Jehovah is used.
They also pointed to the 19th-century Russian-language Makarios Bible,
produced by Russian Orthodox Church translators,
in which the name Jehovah occurs
more than 3,500 times.
Oh, Moses, it’s so good to hear that the brothers
were able to defend Jehovah’s holy name in the courtroom.
Well, were the brothers able to interview any experts
who could also defend God’s name? defend the Bible?
Yes, Mark,
the court allowed two experts to present testimony.
Regarding the use of God’s name,
Professor Mikhail Odintsov,
a religious scholar well respected in Russia
who is not one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
confirmed in front of the court that the name Jehovah
has been used by other Russian translations
and translators as well,
including the translators of the official Bible translation
of the Russian Orthodox Church
where the divine name, Jehovah, occurs some ten times.
Professor Odintsov read two verses from the church Bible
that contains God’s personal name, Jehovah.
He also mentioned two Orthodox Church translators,
namely, Pavsky and Makarii,
who both used God’s name, Jehovah, extensively in their translations.
Professor Odintsov gave a thorough explanation
regarding the history and meaning of the name Jehovah
as well as the long history of its use in Bible translation
and in the literature of Christendom.
Thus, he completely refuted their attack
on Jehovah’s name in the New World Translation.
Excellent!
Well, what a powerful defense for God’s name, Jehovah!
Well, now, didn’t you also say, Moses,
that these so-called experts had said that the New World Translation
was not a Bible because the word “Bible” did not appear on the cover?
Yes, Mark, that’s right.
The study also claimed that the New World Translation is not a Bible
because it does not expressly say that it is a Bible.
However, Professor Odintsov explained to the court
that in line with scientific criteria,
the words “Scriptures” and “Holy Scriptures”
are quite appropriate to describe the Bible.
In addition, our lawyers explained to the court
that they were amazed that the court-appointed so-called experts
claimed to have worked for 287 days
on their research
and yet missed the simple fact
that in the third paragraph of the Bible’s Foreword,
on page 5, it clearly states:
“This new translation of the Bible.”
Well, that’s just unbelievable, Moses.
What other arguments did these so-called experts
try to use against God’s Word, the Bible?
Well, the “expert” study also claimed
that Jehovah’s Witnesses do not recognize Jesus Christ
as the savior of mankind.
But the first paragraph of the Foreword
to the New World Translation Russian edition
says exactly the opposite
and quotes John 3:16.
The “experts” also claimed
that the New World Translation is not a Bible
because it allegedly has been modified
to refute the doctrine of the Trinity.
Yet, our lawyers read
from the Russian Orthodox Church Synodal version,
two verses from that translation,
1 Corinthians 11:3, where it says:
“The head of the Christ is God”
and John 14:28, where Jesus said:
“For the Father is greater than I am.”
So these two verses show
that the official Russian Orthodox Church Bible
also refutes the Trinity doctrine.
We could go on and on, Mark.
But the fact is that the lower court ruled
to ban the New World Translation,
and so we appealed to a higher court.
And the appeal hearing was held on December 20, 2017,
as you rightly said in the beginning.
Well, Moses, could you tell us a little bit
about the appeal hearing that took place in December?
I know you were in the courtroom.
What was it like?
As during the first trials,
foreign diplomats from at least four nations
(Britain, Netherlands, Switzerland, and the United States)
attended the December 20, 2017, appeal hearing.
Again, there were many brothers and sisters present in the courtroom
because they cared so much about the New World Translation.
At the appeal hearing,
when none of the three so-called experts
could explain the methods they used to carry out their study,
the court itself intervened and ended the questioning of the “experts.”
In fact, Ms. Kryukova, one of the three “experts,”
made a very revealing statement
when she said that the only book
that can be called a Bible
is one approved by the Russian Orthodox Church
and that “is marked ‘by the blessing of the patriarch’
or that matches word for word with such a translation.”
When asked, Ms. Kryukova refused to state why she believed
that the New World Translation is “extremist,”
calling this a legal question.
So you see, Mark, neither the prosecutors
nor the so-called experts
who were questioned could cite even one verse
as an example of “extremism” in the New World Translation Bible.
Thus, again and again our attorneys exposed
the outrageous and false claims of these so-called experts.
Our attorneys presented a total
of 35 scholarly documents
containing overwhelming evidence
to prove that the New World Translation Bible
is truly the Word of God.
But these were all ignored by the court.
So again and again we had the impression, sitting there in the courtroom, Mark,
that the purpose of the hearing was not to find out
the facts, evidence, et cetera,
but, rather, to go through the legal formalities quickly,
since the decision had already been made
and must be announced today.
In fact, the judges deliberated
on the seven hours of testimony
for only four minutes
before announcing their decision to ban the New World Translation.
Well, Moses, thank you so much for sharing this powerful defense
that our brothers made in behalf of Jehovah’s holy name
and his precious Word, the Bible.
We appreciate this report so much.
Thank you, Mark.
It was a privilege to be there with the brothers
in the courtroom in St. Petersburg.
The attack on pure worship in Russia
includes an outright ban on our activities in that land.
Now the authorities are moving forward
in seizing properties owned by Jehovah’s people.
For example,
on December 7, 2017, a hearing was held
in the Sestroretsk District Court
regarding the seizing of the Russia branch property
at Solnechnoye.
Brother Richard Devine, a member of the board of directors
of the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society of Pennsylvania,
had the privilege of being in attendance at the hearing.
Richard, it’s good to see you. Welcome.
Thank you, Mark. It’s a pleasure to be here.
Could you tell us a little bit about the nature of this hearing
that you went to Russia to attend?
Sure.
When the Administrative Center of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Russia
was declared “extremist” late last year by the courts,
it gave the government the ability
to seize the Administrative Center’s property.
However, when they tried to seize the Bethel complex,
they found out that it legally belonged, not to the Administrative Center,
but actually to the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society of Pennsylvania
and that for 17 years,
the Administrative Center had been merely a tenant.
Since the Pennsylvania Corporation hadn’t been banned,
this created a legal obstacle for the government in seizing our property.
So, what argument did the government use
to try to justify the seizure of the branch property?
Well, the government was trying to prove that the transfer of title of the property
to the Pennsylvania Corporation 17 years ago wasn’t valid
and that the Bethel property
still really belonged to the Administrative Center,
and therefore it was fair game for them to seize it.
Richard, can you tell us what it was like
to be there in the courtroom for this very historic hearing?
Well, a couple of things really impressed me very much.
One was the courage of the local brothers and sisters who came to the hearing
despite the ban just to support the brothers presenting our case.
It was truly a remarkable demonstration of strong faith and determination.
The hearing was held in a small, drab room
in Sestroretsk, a town not far from the former Bethel facility.
There was barely room for everyone to fit inside.
Our attorneys and the prosecutors were literally two feet apart,
facing each other over a small table.
The brothers and sisters crammed into any space they could find,
some even sitting inside the barred cell
reserved for criminal defendants.
Well now, Richard, what can you tell us about the hearing itself?
What actually took place in the courtroom?
Well, I knew from meeting with them the night before
how well our attorneys prepared for this case
and how hard they worked on it.
And to see them both
—one a relatively young brother— courageously stand up
and defend the interests of Jehovah’s people,
it was really an amazing sight.
They had real conviction and passion.
They demonstrated unequivocally that according to Russian law,
the international business law,
and the provisions of the European Convention on Human Rights
that they were squarely in our favor
and that to seize our property was not only legally wrong
but it was really morally wrong.
The prosecutors, on the other hand, appeared to be not long out of high school
and limited themselves to reading a few short prewritten statements
and asked no questions during the hearing.
Well now, Richard, what was it like
when the decision was finally read in the courtroom?
Well, I don’t think the decision was really a surprise to anyone.
However, it seemed to me that the judge
was very uncomfortable reading that verdict.
At the end, she announced that there would be
30 days to file an appeal.
Now, the spirit of the brothers and sisters leaving the courtroom
was somber at first.
But once we were out in the hallway, the conversations got going;
the brothers and sisters began congratulating the attorneys
for the fine witness they had given.
Once again, they were all smiling, laughing, hugging,
and even giving little gifts to one another.
They were once again just happy to be together serving Jehovah.
Well, then, what happens now?
Where do we go from here, Richard?
Well, the brothers are planning to file an appeal within the given time.
And if this first appeal goes against us,
then the property will be seized by the government
and used for other purposes.
However, further appeals, possibly even to the European Court of Human Rights,
will be pursued.
Richard, thank you very, very much for giving us that report.
And even more, we want to thank you
for the courage that you demonstrated in going to Russia
to stand with our brothers during that hearing.
It really was my privilege. Thank you.
However, the seizure of our other properties
has already begun in Russia.
For example, on December 14, 2017,
just after 9:00 a.m.,
about 40 people, including police and others,
appeared outside the Assembly Hall of Jehovah’s Witnesses
in St. Petersburg.
Some of the men were armed with automatic weapons,
and others had the tools needed to forcibly enter
the locked Assembly Hall compound.
Thankfully, none of our brothers
were inside the Assembly Hall during this raid.
Russian news agencies have reported
that based on the Russian Supreme Court ruling earlier this year,
the government has seized the property
and has transferred it to the neighboring medical center
for use as a lecture hall.
They have already posted a new sign on the gate.
In addition to these actions,
you may be wondering about our Brother Dennis Christensen
who has been in pretrial detention
since May 25, 2017.
The court has extended his pretrial detention several times.
Most recently, on December 22, 2017,
the court extended his detention
until February 23, 2018.
The authorities are allowing Brother Christensen’s wife
to visit him now twice a month.
We expect that his trial will begin sometime
in the coming weeks.
What can we say, brothers,
about this attack on pure worship in Russia?
Jehovah foretold that during Christ’s presence,
‘the kings of the earth and high officials
would take their stand against Jehovah and his anointed one.’
We find that in Psalm 2:1-3.
Thus, we are not surprised to see this direct attack
on Jehovah’s name;
his precious Word, the Bible;
and his faithful worshippers on this earth.
We must keep in our minds the warning from our Lord Jesus
when he said at Matthew 10:17-22:
“Be on your guard against men,
“for they will hand you over to local courts
“and they will scourge you in their synagogues.
“And you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake,
“for a witness to them and the nations.
“However, when they hand you over,
“do not become anxious about how or what you are to speak,
“for what you are to speak will be given you in that hour;
“for the ones speaking are not just you,
“but it is the spirit of your Father that speaks by you.
“Further, brother will hand brother over to death,
“and a father his child,
“and children will rise up against parents
“and will have them put to death.
“And you will be hated by all people
“on account of my name,
“but the one who has endured to the end
will be saved.”
Yes, as Jesus said,
all who endure faithfully will ultimately be saved.
Jehovah stated through his prophet
at Ezekiel 39:7:
“The nations will have to know
that I am Jehovah.”
Soon, Jehovah will act in behalf of all his servants who,
despite opposition and adverse circumstances,
prove that they are truly “a people for his name.”
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

cn.text: 欢迎收看这个特别报道
纯正崇拜正受到无理攻击
在俄罗斯
上帝的宝贵话语圣经遭到禁止
本节目会报道
我们努力辩护的最新消息
最近法院审理了
有关圣经《新世界译本》的案件
我们会采访一位在场的弟兄
我们也会报道
俄罗斯政府怎样试图没收
耶和华见证人分部办事处的财产
以及他们最近怎样强行占有
耶和华见证人在圣彼得堡的大会堂
你也许已经知道
列宁格勒区域法院驳回了
耶和华见证人就俄语版
《新世界译本》被列为禁书的上诉
并裁定该译本为“极端主义”书刊
这个裁决  直接违反了俄罗斯法律
有关反极端主义的
联邦法律第3条的修正案说
《圣经》《古兰经》
《塔纳克》和《甘珠尔》的內容与引述
都不能被视为极端主义
这条修正案由俄罗斯总统
普京于2015年秋季亲自签署
既然有这样一条明确的法律
任何有理智的人都不能理解
俄罗斯法院怎么可以将圣经列为禁书?
我们很高兴可以采访
摩西·阿居博伊弟兄
最近他参加了在法院进行的听证会
摩西弟兄  很高兴看见你
谢谢你  马克弟兄
我也深感荣幸!
摩西弟兄
在讨论听证会的情况之前
你可以介绍一下到目前为止
俄语《新世界译本》遭到禁止的经过吗?
好的
这个案件是从2015年8月13日开始的
当时有检察官起诉
指控俄语《新世界译本》
为“极端主义”书刊
在审理初期
检察官于2016年4月26日提请法院
指定一个专家小组进行调查研究
于是法院宣布休庭
好让这些专家有时间做调查
值得留意的是
这些专家过去为法院提供的报告
一直对耶和华见证人有偏见
而其他客观公正的学者
并不认可那些所谓的“研究”
这个小组花了一年多的时间
将研究结果呈交法院
果不其然  报告非常偏激
毫无事实依据
报告甚至声称《新世界译本》不是圣经
理由是封面上没有“圣经”这两个字
后来在2017年7月下旬
法院重新开庭审理这个案件
摩西  可以给我们讲一下
7月再次开庭时的情况吗?
听证会为期四天
总共耗时30个小时
审理期间  我们的律师证明
这份所谓的“专家报告”毫无根据
含糊不清  充满偏见
前后矛盾
我们的律师
选择了至少两个俄语圣经译本
比较了很多节经文
证明《新世界译本》
与其他俄语圣经是一致的
在法庭上  我们一共读了25段经文
有一次  法官从《新世界译本》中
找出一条他认为有争议的经文
要求我们的律师做出解释
我们的律师就提议
查看三个译本中的这同一节经文
读完之后  大家都看出
三个译本的意思其实是一样的
无须再做任何解释
我们的一位律师记述了当时法庭的场景
他是这样写的  昨天
法官读了不同圣经译本中的许多经文
有《新世界译本》《圣会议译本》
《现代译本》等
经文涉及的內容包括家庭生活
抚养儿女  关爱他人等
我们比较了三个圣经译本中的诗篇23篇
法官亲自读了所有的经文
请想象当时的场景
法庭上有两位检察官
三位律师以及很多出席听证会的人
法官坐在中间
他面前的桌上摆着五六个圣经译本
法官打开不同的译本
大声读出经文  然后提问
场面真的很震撼
给人的感觉就像是在参加一个
精心准备的圣经讨论
真是难以置信!
那这次听证会上
上帝的话语受到了哪些指控?
弟兄们又是怎样维护圣经的呢?
那些所谓的专家质疑《新世界译本》
使用上帝的名字耶和华  这一做法
他们在提交的专家报告中说
《新世界译本》一直在强调耶和华
强调一个具有个性特征的神
也一直称呼上帝为耶和华上帝
万军之耶和华  万军之主耶和华
以色列的圣者等
总之  耶和华见证人认为
上帝有个专有名字耶和华
因此  《新世界译本》
只是他们组织出版的一本书而已
不能算作基督教的圣经
作为回应
我们的律师举证了
其他十个俄语圣经译本
这些译本都使用了“耶和华”这个名字
我们的律师也读出了一些俄罗斯名诗

en.text: From the moment we can talk, we ask questions.
Why is the sky blue?
What are the stars made of?
Why do bad things happen?
Where do we come from?
Why do people die?
People go to great lengths to find answers.
Today, there is more information available than ever before.
But the big questions —questions about life,
suffering, and death—still remain.
Where can we find answers?
What if the answers have been there all along in the Bible?
A lot of people say,
the Bible is full of myths and legends.
That it’s outdated.
Or it’s just too hard to understand.
But is the Bible really the problem,
or is it what people think they know about the Bible?
People think the Bible says that God controls the world.
But how could that be?
This world is out of control!
It’s full of pain and suffering,
sickness and death,
poverty and disaster.
How could a loving God be responsible for all of this?
What the Bible says may surprise you.
It says: “The Evil One controls the whole world.”
In other words, there’s an evil power
behind the world’s problems,
someone who’s pulling the strings behind the scenes.
That’s why, no matter how hard we try,
humans just cannot solve the world’s problems.
The good news is:
The Bible says things will not always be like this!
It tells us why we’re in this situation,
how God will fix it,
and how we can deal with it in the meantime.
The Bible is providing answers to life’s big questions
for millions of people around the world.
Would you like to be one of them?
Jehovah’s Witnesses would be happy to study the Bible with you.
Fill in the online request for a Bible study,
and a Witness in your area will call to discuss the Bible
at a time and place convenient for you.

ko.text: 저와 저희 가족은 건강이 좋지 않아서
치료비를 마련하는 게 정말 쉽지 않습니다.
한 주 한 주 돈을 모아야
애들이 먹을 음식이나 필요한 것들이 없어서
외국에 나가서 일을 하는 수밖에 없겠다는 생각이 들었어요.
디모데 전서 5:8에서도 가족 부양이 중요하다고 하잖아요.
제가 다른 나라로 가지 않기로 한 건
저에게 가장 중요한 건 가족의 영성입니다.
장로 한 분이 해 주신 조언이 도움이 됐어요.
물질이 아니라 가족의 영성이라는 걸 깨닫게 됐죠.
이 세상의 물질은 언제든 사라질 수 있으니까요.
전 보조 파이오니아를 하며 봉사의 종으로 일하고 있고,
우리처럼 다른 형제 자매들도 경제적 어려움을 겪죠.
우리 가족이 올바른 결정을 내렸다고 확신해요.
지금 우리 가족은 가진 게 얼마 없지만
흔히들, 만족하면 가진 게 많게 느껴진다고 하죠.

en.text: The biggest challenge for me and my family has been illness,
not having enough money to pay for the treatment we need.
Each week I have to save up enough money
just to feed my family.
We were deeply saddened by our situation.
First, it was a challenge
for us to make ends meet
because I didn’t have a regular job.
I also worried about how my children would suffer
if we did not have sufficient food and other material needs.
I began to think that moving to another country
was the only way to provide for my family.
As 1 Timothy 5:8 says,
it is my responsibility to support them.
What kept me from moving to another country
is my love for Jehovah and for my family.
As Philippians 1:10 says,
we should “make sure of the more important things,”
and for my family, our spirituality is very important.
The fine advice of an elder strengthened me.
He asked, “Does Jehovah only shower blessings abroad?”
I remember what he said.
From then on,
I realized that the most important thing in life
is our spirituality,
not the material things that we can get from this world,
for it will also vanish.
A great blessing has been keeping our family united
and happy despite our difficult situation.
I serve as a ministerial servant and an auxiliary pioneer.
My daughter, Fátima, is a regular pioneer.
Without a doubt, Jehovah blesses our efforts.
Giving makes me happy.
Other brothers and sisters go through times of need just as we do.
Thinking of this helps me to focus, not on my problems,
but rather on our brotherhood and Jehovah.
I am deeply convinced
that we made the right decision as a family.
And now we are very happy
despite having little materially because I feel content.
They say: If you are content, you are rich.
And the scripture says
it is “Jehovah that makes one rich, and He adds no pain with it.”

有人说
知足的人最富有
圣经也说
耶和华所赐的福使人富足
