en.text: Jehovah’s Witnesses are known around the world
for preaching the good news of the Kingdom.
How is this work accomplished here in Indonesia?
It is certainly a challenging assignment.
This lifesaving message needs to be brought
to over 250 million people
living on thousands of different islands.
To support this tremendous work,
the Indonesia branch office was relocated
to the 31st floor of the Central Park building in Jakarta
in April 2014.
A number of apartments at an adjacent apartment tower
are being used to house the Bethel family,
which has approximately 100 members
that support the work of the branch office.
Each morning they commute to this office, ready for their work assignments.
We call this place Bethel, which means “House of God.”
By means of this brief video presentation,
we would like to warmly welcome you to our branch office and Bethel home
and provide you with an overview of what is being accomplished here.
Our day always starts with a morning worship program at 7:20 a.m.
What is being considered?
Every day an interesting Bible verse is being read,
commented on,
and explained so as to make its practical value
clear to the Bethel family.
After a closing prayer,
all are ready to start working.
Would you like to know what the Bethel family is doing?
Let’s have a look at a few of the activities being done here.
Our receptionist welcomes our many visitors in the main lobby
and will make arrangements for tours.
Also, all incoming calls are answered here,
and some additional secretarial work is done whenever time permits.
An ever-growing work at our branch is related to audio and video recordings.
In addition to Indonesian language material,
in recent years we have started recording in many indigenous languages as well.
What is being recorded?
A wide variety of publications in audio format,
as well as convention dramas, videos, and Web materials.
The process is very involved.
Readers and voice participants are auditioned,
selected, and coached.
Hours are spent doing the actual recording.
Next, the material
is reviewed and edited to achieve the best possible quality.
When satisfied, the final product will be uploaded to jw.org
for the benefit of you and millions of other people
all around the world.
Producing publications in many different languages,
whether in electronic or printed format, requires translation.
Some of this work is done at our branch office.
The translation process can be challenging,
but it is a very important and rewarding work.
Teams of translators work hard every day
to keep up with the steady flow of new material.
They are trained to translate the English text into Indonesian.
They are also provided with various research tools.
The English text is also made available to local language teams
located at remote translation offices,
or RTOs, throughout the country.
It is then translated into Indonesian Sign Language
and many other local languages.
This entire translation process
can take weeks or even months to complete,
and even then the work is not yet done.
What’s next?
The translated text is now ready for the composition process,
where a print-ready file is created.
Most of our publications are printed
at the Japan branch office of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Cleanliness is also observed in the Bethel residences and offices.
Each Bethel family member is responsible for cleaning their own room.
Housekeepers assist the family by cleaning each residence room once a month.
Besides the kitchen and laundry operations,
the Bethel Office is responsible for organizing spiritual programs
and for the overall management of all branch office properties.
Back at the office, more work is being accomplished.
Hundreds of letters and reports from the field
are received on a weekly basis.
Where is this correspondence handled?
Here in the Service Department,
they are responsible to communicate with
and direct the activities in the field.
They also handle the organizing of various Bible schools,
conventions, assemblies,
and approve the formation of new congregations and groups.
Interest shown in our Bible educational work is followed up carefully.
When someone requests a visit from Jehovah’s Witnesses
by filling out the form on the jw.org website,
brothers locate the nearest congregation and inform them
in order to send someone as soon as possible.
All this work would be much harder to accomplish
without the use of technology.
Therefore, a vital part of our operation here
is the Computer Department.
Existing systems need to be maintained and upgraded.
New equipment is bought and installed not only at the branch office
but also at satellite locations and remote translation offices.
As a result of the good news being preached,
there is a growing need for more dignified places of worship.
The building of such Kingdom Halls
is organized by the Local Design/Construction Department.
Along with new construction, the LDC is responsible for overseeing
the renovation and maintenance of existing Kingdom Halls
as well as maintenance training.
In addition to Kingdom Hall upkeep,
this department is involved with searching for properties
to be used as RTOs or missionary homes.
Operating our branch office facilities requires a constant supply of various items.
The Purchasing Department cares for this responsibility
by managing vendor accounts and receiving shipments.
These goods are then processed
and sent to the branch facilities where they are needed.
Some activities need to be handled administratively and legally.
Who is doing this?
The Governing Body appoints a Branch Committee,
who in turn receives the support of office personnel
to see to it that guidelines and instructions
are being implemented appropriately and in a timely manner.
This includes giving attention to those in need when natural disasters strike.
The Legal Department makes sure that all legal requirements
are being fulfilled.
As you have just seen, much is being accomplished here at Bethel.
And amazingly, all of this is being accomplished
by volunteers who have dedicated themselves fully
to support the Kingdom preaching work here in Indonesia.
We thank you for your visit
and sincerely hope you will enjoy touring our branch office.

cn.text: 耶和华见证人因在全球
传讲上帝王国的好消息而广为人知
这项工作在印度尼西亚是如何开展的呢?
这个国家的人口超过2.5亿
他们居住在许多不同的小岛上
向这么多人传讲救生信息
的确是个富有挑战性的工作
为了支持这项艰巨的工作
印尼的分部办事处
搬迁到雅加达中央公园大厦的31层
大约有100位伯特利成员
在这个办事处工作
他们就住在附近的公寓楼里
每天早上  他们会来到办公室
准备开始一天的工作
我们把这个地方称为伯特利
意思是“上帝的居所 ”
我们热烈地欢迎你
来参观我们的分部办事处
通过接下来的这个短片
我们会简单地介绍这里的工作情况
我们每天早上7点20分
会举行早晨崇拜
早晨崇拜包括什么內容呢?
每天我们都会读一节经文
也会有评论环节
为了强化伯特利家庭成员
讲者会解释并强调经文的实用价值
在结束祷告后
大家就都准备好开始新一天的工作了
你想知道伯特利都有哪些工作吗?
让我们一起来看看吧
接待员会在大厅欢迎来访的朋友
并安排参观
此外
他们也会在这里接听所有的来电
如果时间允许
他们也会帮忙分担一些秘书的工作
现在音频和视频的录制工作不断增多
除印度尼西亚语之外
近年来我们也开始录制
许多原住民语言的內容
那我们录制什么內容呢?
这包括各种出版物的音频
大会戏剧  视频
还有我们网站上的资料
录音工作需要很多步骤
首先  我们会请一些人试音
然后从中选出合适的朗读员和配音员
并进行指导
当然
实际的录音工作需要花很多时间
录音结束后
我们会编辑并多次检查录制的內容
确保达到最佳效果
最后
编辑好的成品将会上传到jw.org网站
这样全球数百万人都会从中获益
制作多种语言的出版物
无论是电子版还是印刷版
都需要翻译
其中一些工作
是在我们的分部办事处完成的
这么浩大的翻译工作虽然富有挑战性
但也深具价值
为了努力和英语资料更新的速度同步
翻译员们每天都在努力地工作
为了做好翻译工作
他们需要先接受培训
也需要查考不同的资料
全国各地的远程翻译处
也会收到同样的英语文本
然后由负责翻译当地语言的小组
把资料翻译成印度尼西亚手语
和许多当地语言
整个翻译过程可能需要几周
甚至几个月才能完成
即使这样  工作还没有结束
下一步是什么呢?
就是将翻译好的文本排版
排版工作一旦完成
就可以准备印刷了
我们大部分的出版物
都会在日本分部办事处印刷
伯特利的住所和办公室都需要保持清洁
每位伯特利成员都负责打扫自己的房间
家务员会每月一次定期协助打扫房间
除了管理厨房和洗衣部之外
伯特利办事处还负责组织安排属灵活动
也负责管理分部的所有设施
办公室的工作又是怎样的呢?
有很多的工作都在这里完成
每周这里会收到数百封
来自地区的信件和报告
谁来处理这些信件呢?
就是传道部
传道部主要负责督导地区的传道活动
此外
他们还负责组织各种训练班
筹备大会
也会负责审批新会众和小组的成立
传道部也会及时跟进对圣经感兴趣的人
当有人在jw.org网站上
填写了免费学习圣经的表格时
传道部会联络离申请人最近的会众
派人尽快探访他
要想完成这么多工作
就需要有技术的支持
所以电脑部发挥了重要的作用
他们负责维护并升级电脑系统
同时  电脑部也负责为分部办事处
远程翻译处及分部其它的办公地点
购买并安装所需的设备
由于好消息不断传扬开去
我们需要更多举行聚会的地方
王国聚会所的兴建工作
由本地设计及建筑部负责
除了兴建新的王国聚会所
LDC也负责翻修和维护已有的聚会所
还会提供相关的培训
此外
他们也为远程翻译处
寻找合适的办公地点
并帮助特派传道员寻找合适的住所
分部想要运作顺畅
需要源源不断的物资供应
这项工作是由采购部负责的
他们需要与供应商沟通
安排采购  接收货物
然后对货物进行检查  整理  分类
再送到所需的部门
有些活动涉及到行政和法律
由谁来负责呢?
中央长老团委派了一个分部委员会
在当地分部办事处的工作人员
会协助这个委员会
确保组织的指引
可以准确迅速地实施
比如  当灾难发生时
他们会按照组织的指引
援助受灾地区
法律部的工作
就是要确保这些活动
在当地合法地进行
在印度尼西亚
很多的工作都是在伯特利完成的
这些工作是谁做的呢?
就是那些参与志愿服务的弟兄姐妹们
他们甘心献出自己
全力支持王国传道工作
我们真挚地邀请你来参观印尼分部

en.text: Well, now we look forward to the next speaker.
This is Brother Stephen Lett,
also of the Governing Body.
He gives us the theme here:
“Never Give Up Much for Little.”
Jesus gave a parable about a young man
who exchanged peace and prosperity
in his father’s household
for a debauched, miserable, desperate life.
Foolishly
he exchanged much for little.
It’s the story of the prodigal son, Luke chapter 15.
In contrast, in Matthew chapter 13,
Jesus gave a story about a traveling merchant
who sold everything he had
to buy one pearl of high value.
When we understand the meaning of that parable,
in actuality
he exchanged a little for much.
Now, obviously you brothers and sisters
do not want to imitate the prodigal son.
You want to imitate the traveling merchant,
and Jehovah doesn’t want you
to give away much for little.
He wants you to give away little for much.
And Jehovah is anxious to give you this much.
That’s why he’s recorded parables
such as the two we just mentioned
and also real life stories in his Word
that depict both scenarios so that we can be wise.
In fact, let’s briefly discuss
four Bible examples
of ones who foolishly gave up much for little,
and then we’ll talk about four Bible examples
of ones who gave up little for much.
Our first example: Satan.
Now, Satan gave up a priceless,
honored position of trust in Jehovah’s service
that he may have enjoyed
for aeons of time.
And what did he receive for what he gave up?
A relatively short,
miserable life of independence from Jehovah,
and ultimately he will have earned for himself
the “lake of fire.”
We know right now that Satan cannot be happy at all.
Jehovah is described as a “happy God” (1 Timothy 1:11);
Jesus, the happy Potentate (1 Timothy 6:15);
“happy is the nation whose God is Jehovah” (Psalm 33:12),
but Satan is never described as anything close to happy, is he?
He’s described as an enraged roaring lion,
an accuser who accuses day and night,
one who has great anger because he knows his time is short.
Does that sound like a happy person?
But what caused Satan
to give up so much for so little?
Pride.
Pride actually caused him to think
that he was smarter than Jehovah.
Can you imagine that the clay was smarter than the potter?
Pride caused him to think
that life without Jehovah would actually be a better life.
Well, may we never pridefully feel
that we know better than Jehovah in any area
—for example, how to treat disfellowshipped ones,
the need to avoid bad association,
marrying only in the Lord are a few examples.
May we never pridefully feel
that the so-called freedom from Jehovah that the world offers
will bring happiness.
Let’s learn from Satan.
Never allow pride to cause you
to give up much for little.
Now our second example: Adam and Eve.
Satan offered them opportunity to be like God,
his own aspiration.
And stupidly
—I mean stupidly—
they bought into his hoax.
They selfishly
gave up their invaluable family ties
with the best Father they could ever have.
They gave up their Paradise home,
perfect everlasting life,
their children’s future welfare.
All for what?
A relatively short,
miserable life of independence from Jehovah
and finally nonexistence
—a total loss.
What an outstanding example of giving up much for little!
So may we learn from Adam and Eve.
Never allow Satan’s lies
to cause you to give up much for little
—lies such as “Material things will make you happy”
or “Immorality will make you happy.”
Unlike Adam and Eve,
let’s refuse to allow Satan’s lies
to cause us to give up much for little.
Esau, our third example,
knew the history of Satan and Adam and Eve.
But did he learn from them?
No, he too lacked appreciation for sacred things.
Esau was Isaac’s firstborn son,
and in Bible times, this had great value,
but he thought only of his immediate physical cravings.
Genesis 25:32 says
that he became very hungry and cried out:
“I am about to die!”
Was he really?
Should he not have endured a little bit longer
rather than sell his birthright?
Now pretty quick, he realized his mistake.
He sold something with real value.
For what?
What did he receive?
Some bread and lentil stew.
Apparently, this stew didn’t even have any meat in it.
We Bethelites,
we can get bread, lentils, and meat
for free in the Bethel pantry.
What is a lesson that we can learn from Esau?
Well, open up to Hebrews chapter 12, please.
And here’s a very interesting lesson
Jehovah teaches us about Esau.
Hebrews 12:16:
“And watch that among you
“there is no one who is sexually immoral
“nor anyone who does not appreciate sacred things,
“like Esau,
“who gave up his rights as firstborn
in exchange for one meal.”
But, you know, interestingly,
Jehovah compares a person who commits sexual immorality
to what Esau did.
And if you think about it, both lack self-control
and give in to fleshly desires.
That’s what Esau did.
That’s what a person who commits sexual immorality does.
Well, may none of us allow immorality
to cause us to sell our figurative birthright,
our inheritance in Jehovah’s new world.
And think about this:
How long did that bread and lentil stew
last Esau?
How long did it benefit him?
A few hours?
Soon he would have been hungry again.
Well, similarly, how long does
the so-called pleasure of an immoral person last?
Only a short time followed by horrible consequences,
including a bad conscience.
Now our fourth example:
the rich young ruler in Jesus’ day.
He held a high position and had many possessions.
Jesus even felt love for him.
But was he prepared to give up his wealth
for something infinitely more valuable and permanent,
the treasure of following Jesus?
No.
When Jesus invited him, the Bible says:
“He went away grieved.”
He couldn’t bring himself to give up his many possessions.
Instead, he gave up a wonderful future.
Obviously, he gave up the wrong thing, didn’t he?
Where are those who did follow Jesus now?
Immortal kings and priests
with Christ in heaven in Jehovah’s presence.
But unless that young ruler later changed his ways,
he and all that was his are now dust.
What a classic example of giving up so much for so little!
May we never allow
any of the material attractions of this world
to cause us to give up our wonderful future
in Jehovah’s new world.
Well, we’ve considered our four negative examples,
but now let’s move to our four positive examples
—ones who gave up little for much.
First: Abraham.
At Jehovah’s invitation,
Abraham gave up a comfortable life
in upscale Ur.
At Jehovah’s invitation,
he took his family on a long, dangerous trek
to the land of promise,
and there he willingly lived the rest of his life in tents.
But what did Abraham receive for what he gave up?
He gained a permanent place in Jehovah’s heart.
Jehovah himself called him “my friend.”
Because of his faith, Jehovah swore
that through one of his descendants
all nations would be blessed
and that descendant —the Messiah, Jesus—
will soon resurrect Abraham
to enjoy the real life.
But now, are we willing
to give up material possessions and comforts
in order, for example, to enter the full-time ministry?
Or maybe be able to move and serve where the need is greater
in order to secure
a permanent place in Jehovah’s heart?
Like Abraham,
are we willing to give up little for much?
Our second example: Moses.
Centuries after Abraham,
Moses also gave up the right things.
Raised as royalty
in Pharaoh’s palace,
he was groomed for greatness in the world of his day.
He knew all about Egypt’s advanced civilization and culture.
But the Bible doesn’t elaborate on anything
that Moses accomplished in Egypt.
Why?
Because anything he may have achieved there
was utterly insignificant
compared to what he did in Jehovah’s service.
Moses received the Law
that led Israel to the Messiah.
No other prophet knew Jehovah
“face-to-face.”
He did well in giving up life in Egypt
in order to carry out God’s commission.
As for the wealth and grandeur of ancient Egypt,
we can see crumbling remnants of it
in museums.
But Moses gained God’s favor.
He gained the real life.
He gained a permanent place in our spiritual heritage
and a permanent place in all of our hearts.
Well, let’s go to our third example: Jesus
—the best example of gaining a lot more than he gave up.
Like Abraham and Moses,
he willingly gave up a comfortable life
—now in his case, life in heaven alongside Jehovah.
But he emptied himself, became a human,
ministered to other humans,
even gave his life
trusting that Jehovah would give life back to him.
He gained the great joy
of fulfilling his Father’s righteous purpose
and redeeming those he was especially fond of
—humans.
If you think about it, apparently, Jesus didn’t really realize
how much he would receive for what he gave up.
Because remember at John 17:5,
he said: “Father, glorify me . . .
“with the glory that I had alongside you
before the world was.”
In other words: ‘Father, please give me back what I had before.’
But Jehovah gave him a lot more, didn’t he?
And that’s always true of Jehovah, really, if you think about it.
You can’t outgive Jehovah.
Jehovah gave him a name more excellent
than the angels.
Jehovah gave him all authority
in heaven and earth.
He even gave him immortality
and incorruption.
And we know that means an indestructible life,
an indestructible organism, or body.
Now a fourth example:
Jesus’ apostles.
Peter, Andrew, James, and John
abandoned their fishing businesses, didn’t they?
All the other apostles, the Bible says, “left all things.”
And remember, Peter asked: “Look!
“We have left all things and followed you;
what, then, will there be for us?”
Well, Jesus assured him
that anyone who gives up material things
or even family relationships
for him or for the sake of the good news
would receive a hundredfold even now.
If you think about that, that’s a 10,000 percent return.
Plus, he will get everlasting life.
In fact, think about it.
Where are these apostles now?
Like Jesus—immortal, incorruptible spirit creatures.
Open up to Revelation chapter 20,
and notice what is said about these ones.
Revelation chapter 20, please,
and notice verse 6.
It says: “Happy [notice that word happy]
“and holy is anyone having part
“in the first resurrection;
“over these the second death has no authority,
“but they will be priests of God and of the Christ,
and they will rule as kings with him for the 1,000 years.”
So they’re going to be happy in their assignment.
This is assured in this scripture.
Why are they going to be so happy?
Acts 20:35: “There is more happiness in giving than . . . receiving.”
And what an occasion the thousand years will be for giving!
Can you imagine assisting humans
to transform the entire planet
into its originally intended condition?
Imagine working closely with the Christ to empty the grave
and gradually helping humans
to come to perfection
and then, after the thousand years,
being able to share in the final crushing
of evil Satan and his wicked demons.
What happifying work all of this will be!
But what will be their main source of happiness?
Well, being part of the main instrument, the Kingdom,
that Jehovah will use
to sanctify and vindicate his holy name.
I thought I’d go ahead and put to work
that new understanding Brother Jackson revealed earlier.
But it’s true
to vindicate Jehovah’s name, his reputation,
that will bring the greatest happiness to them.
You can be sure
that when the apostles gave up their little fishing businesses
and the other apostles their worldly pursuits,
they had no idea
how much they would receive in return.
Well, now we’ve discussed Abraham, Moses, Jesus, the apostles.
And there’s no doubt about it,
they would all wholeheartedly agree that what they gave up
was very small compared to what they gained.
Well, what about us?
We all give up things, don’t we, great and small for Jehovah?
We may give up time, energy, money, possessions.
We may have to give up a little face, prestige in this world.
But we will experience
what all those good Bible examples did.
What we get back always far outweighs any loss.
In fact, most of us would probably say
that we feel like we haven’t given up anything.
We’re receiving, like those men of old,
a hundred times more now.
And we are sure to gain life,
the real life,
if we never give up much for little.
I’m sure we all totally enjoyed that encouragement.
Well now, at this point, you’re probably thinking that we said
there was an adjusted understanding: got that one;
a lot of encouragement, yes;
then there was the one about the yeartext, yes.
What was the other one?
Well, we’ve come to the final talk.
If we don’t get it now, it’s not going to come.
Remember, we said an adjustment to the way we do our ministry.
So with eager anticipation, we look forward to hearing
from Brother Anthony Morris
who will talk to us about “Making Our Blows Count.”
We are involved in the greatest preaching campaign
in all history.
We publish quality literature
in 240 lands.
It’s amazing.
However, we’re not about seeking praise
for the quality of our magazines
or the hundreds of languages
that we’re translating in.
What’s our focus?
Well, we want to imitate
what the apostle Paul wrote about himself.
And the Governing Body really wants this message
to be clear to all of God’s people
who are preachers and teachers of the Kingdom.
So find what I’m referring to
in 1 Corinthians chapter 9.
And you’ll remember
he’s describing his pursuit of the prize.
And it’s quite profound when you reflect on it.
And you’ll see where it fits everyone of us
that are dedicated to the true God.
Verse 26:
“Therefore,
“the way I am running is not aimlessly;
“the way I am aiming my blows
is so as not to be striking the air.”
So you can picture running aimlessly.
It’s a waste of time and energy
—striking the air,
a waste of time and energy.
So the time left is reduced.
The end is so close.
Like I’ve told folks, if you look around
and you don’t see how different it is and how close it is,
you must be in a coma.
And that’s OK.
God can bring you out of a coma
if you were all right before that.
But the Governing Body is concerned
that with the limited time we have left
that we make our blows count.
So to truly make our blows count,
what should be the focus of our work?
We’re not left without knowing how Jehovah thinks.
It’s been here all along.
But sometimes we can individually
and even organizationally get distracted.
Turn to Acts chapter 13
—Acts chapter 13.
And they were preaching there in the first century,
and we get some results,
but we also get God’s thinking on the matter
and what he wants us to focus on.
Acts 13:48:
“When those of the nations heard this [this message],
they began to rejoice and to glorify the word of Jehovah.”
Now notice:
“All those who were rightly disposed
for everlasting life became believers.”
There it is.
That’s the focus of our work:
searching for those “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
It’s not complicated.
And to try to help somebody who’s not rightly disposed,
frankly, is a waste of time.
Now, we don’t read hearts.
We understand that people can change, and we continue with that.
But overall, Jehovah wants us to understand:
Let’s search out
for those who are rightly disposed for everlasting life
because no one comes to the truth, remember, as Jesus taught us,
unless Jehovah draws him.
We don’t want to get to thinking that our personality
draws people to the truth.
You might be likable.
That’s wonderful.
However, Jehovah draws those rightly disposed.
And you become friends and such
if you have the privilege to study with people.
But that’s what it’s about:
searching for those rightly disposed ones.
That’s who he draws.
Those who are righteously— He reads the heart.
And so we’re in this search work,
but we’re looking to focus on those rightly disposed.
So with that clear,
the Governing Body has identified two problems.
And this is what we want to pass on,
and it can adversely affect our effectiveness in the ministry.
This is what we’re about:
a preaching and teaching organization.
This is who we are.
So for many years, and we acknowledge it,
there was a focus on placing magazines,
developing magazine routes.
That helped some come into the truth, no denying it,
because our literature is the best on the earth.
Others have accepted our magazines
for many years,
many years,
and they’ve never done a thing about the truth.
But they’re still going back.
You know, coming back from a day of service,
“How many magazines did you place?”
Now, they mean well. God loves us.
But excuse me, that’s not the focus of our work.
It has to refocus on what we’re all about.
And just think about it, Jesus commanded:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples of people of all the nations.”
We don’t have the authority to change
what the head of the congregation has said
and go along the lines of,
‘Go, therefore, and place a lot of literature’;
that’s not our focus,
even though it’s the best on the planet.
We’re about searching for the rightly disposed
so they can become disciples of Christ.
And you know, these ones
who have taken our literature for years
(and you know, as we said, individuals might change)
they remind us of what happened in Ezekiel’s day.
And some of you are Bible readers
—scholars, if you will—
but let’s read it anyway in Ezekiel 33
and find what he faced.
And we face this. It’s a reality.
So given the limited time,
we have to make sure that Jehovah’s spirit
is moving us this way,
and that we accept that this is the way it is
in our day as well.
Now notice verse 31 of Ezekiel 33:31, 32:
“They will crowd in to sit before you as my people;
“and they will hear your words, but they will not do them.
“For with their mouth they flatter you,
“but their heart is greedy for dishonest gain.
“Look!
“You are to them like a romantic love song,
“sung with a beautiful voice
“and skillfully played on a stringed instrument.
“They will hear your words,
but no one will act on them.”
That’s every territory.
And as you’ve worked it for many years,
you can have faces come to mind just like that,
come to occasional meetings and such.
Well, time is running out.
God is making that very clear to us.
We need to help people come into the truth.
We don’t need the flattery and such
—that kind of experience.
This is a time for decision.
We’re looking for people who will act on what they learn.
That’s where our blows are going to be effective.
People have to act on it.
And if you’re not seeing that,
just get searching
and let the angels and Jehovah’s spirit
take you to the rightly disposed ones.
And something that we forget, our work is twofold.
We can forget that sometimes.
We’re searching and bringing in the rightly disposed,
and the other is we’re praising and honoring Jehovah,
like Brother Lösch mentioned,
because they’re hearing about Jehovah’s judgment day.
So it’s twofold. It’s a warning work.
You could go a whole morning
and not have what you thought was an effective day
—no literature— but you praised God
because they’re still thinking about Jehovah’s Witnesses
and your efforts to preach in that territory.
So we have to keep that in mind.
So that’s the one problem.
Here is problem two that we want to address.
We have so many tools to use in the ministry;
it can be overwhelming and confusing
even to the best minds.
So you older ones, don’t feel:
‘I’m slipping here. I’m confused.’
No, the young ones are trying too,
often overwhelmed and confused.
So our Teaching Toolbox
that we emphasized in recent years,
what happened is that it became a huge toolshed.
A lot of you are nodding your heads.
That’s OK. That’s not disloyal.
It’s true.
It’s become a huge toolshed.
Now, we appreciate the sample presentations at the midweek meeting,
but frankly, many of us are so busy
we can’t keep up with all the latest presentations
no matter how good they are.
‘Well, that was good.’
And then Saturday morning or Sunday:
‘OK, what am I doing today?
‘We had three of them at our midweek meeting.
I don’t know, what am I supposed to do here?’
And then if you get a critic nearby,
you know, ‘Oh, Lord.’
You know?
Plus many struggle to keep up
with reading all the magazines.
You’re not a bad person.
Jehovah loves you.
We understand.
So in view of this,
the Governing Body is adjusting
the focus of our ministry.
You’re getting the message;
we are addressing these two problems.
And we are 100 percent with this, unanimous.
Everybody in the departments connected are with it.
They can sense Jehovah’s spirit moving,
and this is what Jehovah’s doing.
It’s his chariot. He’s the driver.
So here are the adjustments.
Starting January 2018,
there will only be three public editions of The Watchtower.
For those who are tied in,
I heard some expressions down in front here.
I couldn’t help it.
Only three public editions of The Watchtower
and three of the Awake! magazines
—the whole year.
Yeah.
I’m excited too.
I really am.
Now—
And what’s beautiful about this,
they’re going to cover one subject in the whole magazine
—start to finish—
one subject.
Now, I have here a hard copy
of the first one.
So I’m excited about it.
And mind you, these are special.
This one is special. It’s the first one.
And Jehovah is moving it toward
those rightly disposed for everlasting life
because he knows his day and hour.
And this one
is quite easy to start a conversation with,
and once you have a question, you’re in a conversation already.
So whether it’s “Get off my porch”
or they want to get involved in the answering of that question,
it’s effective.
And the rightly disposed are going to be intrigued.
The first one, this question here:
“Is the Bible Still Relevant Today?”
Certain territories, maybe not,
but there may be righteously disposed ones there.
You have a nice cover picture
—a woman in the back reading her Bible as the train is going by,
people distracted with their watches, their phones, etcetera.
And then, on the inside
—and you’re going to become familiar with this.
You got plenty of time to use it—
this tool, over and over.
Oh, yeah. You’ll know right where to go.
You might decide, well,
I’ll go where it comments
“Outdated or Ahead of Its Time?”
depending on what the person may have said.
You have that freedom.
So appropriate: “Help to Avoid Problems,”
“Help to Resolve Problems,”
“Help to Cope With Problems.”
Boy, do people need that.
And those that are
rightly disposed for everlasting life
know they have problems.
They’re honest about it.
And so this will touch their heart, and Jehovah will draw them.
Now, what’s nice about it
is that you’re going to be able to get very familiar with it, use it,
and it’ll become part of our permanent Teaching Toolbox.
And it’ll go in the Teaching Toolbox.
Even like these skilled craftsmen —they have their toolbox.
Why are they so good at what they do in many cases?
Because they keep using these tools.
It’s not rocket science.
These are craftsmen with these tools.
“I need this; I need that,”
to accomplish what they need here.
So we only need so many tools in the box
—the ones that we can get very good at using.
And what’s nice,
when it’s in a permanent Teaching Toolbox there,
you’re not changing all the time.
And was all that sincere?
Yes, but I could tell you stories,
but time is running out,
of some of the things I’ve heard out in the ministry.
And I could tell they never read that.
But they’re out there. God love them.
They were knocking on doors with me.
You get familiar with the tool.
Now, what we’ll do is we’ll evaluate after two years.
And it might be, we’ll see what the Governing Body decides,
that we think we’ve got sufficient subjects
in the magazines for the toolbox,
and then we’ll just reprint
what’s already been written.
So you’ve got your tools.
Now, you’re going to get more details
on the Teaching Toolbox soon.
And you’ll also be pleased to know this
that (the brothers have been working hard on this)
there’s going to be an update on the box
—Teaching Toolbox— and the JW Library.
And we love the JW Library.
It’ll be on the home page there.
It’ll be happening in the near future.
And this question will arise now because territories are different.
We understand that.
What if you find that the Teaching Toolbox
doesn’t contain a tool that you have found effective in your territory,
like a video that you think is
and you’ve experienced effectiveness with it?
It’s OK.
Put it in your “Favorites” section.
That’s all.
Don’t write in and say,
“I think that should be in the Teaching Toolbox.”
We’ve gone through all of this at headquarters.
It’s OK.
But you go ahead and put it in your “Favorites” section and use it.
Not a problem.
Not a problem.
Now, so that’s covered,
those with the preaching and the focus of our ministry.
And there’s another adjustment
that I’ve been asked to announce here.
We all enjoy the latest reports on the worldwide work
that we have on jw.org and JW Broadcasting.
We love it.
And I know recently someone told me they didn’t know about Venezuela.
It was on jw.org, but you don’t want to try and make him feel bad.
But there’s so much we’re getting all throughout the year,
and it’s timely and a blessing.
So with this in mind, the Governing Body has decided
that with all of the information
on jw.org and JW Broadcasting,
that as of 2018, we will no longer produce
the Yearbook of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Especially if you’ve been in the truth a long time,
yes, the 2017 is your last one.
So that’s historic.
But come on,
try to convince me you’ve seen everything we’ve put
on jw.org and JW Broadcasting.
God is watching.
You’re well-fed.
You’ve got plenty there.
These latest developments are indeed exciting.
And as the end fast approaches,
let’s honor Jehovah and make our blows count.
Let’s go forth and make disciples
of people that are righteously disposed
for everlasting life.
What an exciting announcement!
I don’t know about you, I’m really excited about this
because we can see the end is so close.
And really, isn’t the main thing that we should be thinking about
is helping people to know Jehovah?
That’s the prime goal.
So the Governing Body is helping us to see how to have this toolbox.
We’re all looking forward to seeing what’s in the toolbox.
In addition to that,
we’ve got a few other announcements to make.
We’d like to inform you of some changes
that are planned with regard to the study edition of The Watchtower.
Now, since 2011, in English we’ve been producing
two different versions of the study edition.
We’ve had the standard edition and the simplified.
And each of those has filled a vital need.
However, in recent months the Governing Body
has asked the Writing Committee to investigate ways
to simplify the style of the standard edition.
Additionally, the Governing Body has approved a new design
for the standard edition,
which allows for a larger font style
and also has certain features that are only in the simplified edition,
such as “Some Expressions Explained.”
So with this in mind, the Governing Body has decided
as of January 1, 2019,
they are going to combine both versions of the magazines.
This will not only simplify our work but it will also be less confusing,
and we all will have the same magazine that we’re using.
Now, you’ll be interested to note
that many of the larger languages
that were producing two editions
—languages such as Spanish, Portuguese, French, and Italian—
have recently already combined their editions,
trying to simplify the language used in their standard edition.
And this has been very successful.
We will continue to produce an electronic version
of the English simplified magazine,
and that will be used mainly by translators
to help them to make sure their translation
is still clear and understandable.
Now, in addition,
we’d like to let you know that early next year
we’ll be receiving a new publication,
and it will be one of the ones
that we use in the toolbox.
It is called How to Remain in God’s Love.
And you see it here on the screen.
It’s 256 pages,
and it uses the same simplified style
as the Teach Us book.
So it’s going to replace
the current “God’s Love” book.
These two publications,
that is, How to Remain in God’s Love
and the Teach Us books
will be used in the toolbox
for helping students to become disciples.
Now, you look forward to getting that.
Well, I know we’ll be going away from here,
our minds and hearts spinning around
thinking of all the interesting changes and developments.

cn.text: 现在  我们很期待下一位讲者
中央长老团成员斯蒂芬·莱特弟兄
他演讲的题目是
《千万不要贪小失大》
耶稣讲过一个比喻
一个年轻人原本可以在父亲家里
过着安稳舒适的生活
但后来他却变得堕落绝望  穷困潦倒
他贪小失大  真是太愚蠢了
这就是路加福音15章中浪子的故事
与此不同  在马太福音13章
耶稣讲述了一个商旅的故事
他为了买一颗昂贵的珍珠
卖掉了所有家当
这个比喻想说明
商旅看似失去了很多
实际上得到的却更多
显然  大家都想学习商旅
而不是那个浪子
耶和华不希望我们贪小失大
反而他希望我们得到更多
他很渴望大大赐福给我们
因此  他在圣经中记载了这两个比喻
也记载了很多类似的人物经历
希望帮助我们行事明智
接下来  我们会讨论
圣经中四个贪小失大的例子
然后  我们会再看看
四个与之相反的好榜样
第一个例子  就是撒但
他本可以一直事奉耶和华
受上帝信任并享有尊贵的地位
但是  他放弃了这一切
那么他换来了什么呢?
只为了得到片刻的自由
就脱离上帝的统治
最后换来的将是
在“火湖”里彻底的毁灭
我们知道
撒但现在一点儿都不快乐
但提摩太前书1:11说
耶和华是“快乐的上帝”
提摩太前书6:15说
耶稣是快乐的“掌权者”
“有耶和华作上帝的国家多么有福!”
可是  从来没有哪个地方说
撒但是快乐的  对吗?
圣经把撒但描述为咆哮的狮子
昼夜不停的指控者
因为他知道自己时候不多了
就变得更加愤怒
他看起来一点儿都不快乐  对吗?
那么  撒但贪小失大的原因是什么呢?
就是骄傲
因为骄傲
撒但觉得自己比上帝还聪明
陶泥能够比造他的陶匠更聪明吗?
撒但却自以为是
认为脱离上帝的统治生活会更好
所以  在处理某些问题时
我们千万不要自以为是
认为自己比耶和华懂得还多
比如怎样对待被开除的人
避开不良的交往
只和主里的人结婚等等
希望我们不要被这个世界
所提倡的“自由”骗倒
以为不服从上帝也会快乐
撒但就是个鉴戒
所以  千万不要因为骄傲
而放弃已经享有的美好福分
第二个例子是亚当和夏娃
为了满足自己的野心
撒但骗他们说
他们会变得像上帝一样
可他们真的很愚蠢
真的很愚蠢  居然相信了撒但!
他们就这样放弃了全宇宙中最好的父亲
放弃了和他之间的宝贵关系
放弃了乐园的生活  完美的生命
也放弃了子孙后代本可以享有的福分
放弃了这么多  为了什么呢?
就为了脱离耶和华的统治  自行其是
最后赔上性命  永远地死去
这是多么惨重的代价呀!
我们可以学到什么呢?
千万不要被撒但所骗
撒但也许声称
追求物质会让你快乐
过不道德的生活会让你快乐
让我们不要像亚当夏娃那样
相信撒但的谎言
放弃已有的福分
结果贪小失大
第三个例子是以扫
他清楚知道撒但
亚当  夏娃的下场
但他吸取教训了吗?
没有
他不重视圣物
本可以享有宝贵的长子权
他却只顾满足自己一时的肉体欲望
创世记25:32说  以扫很饿
嚷着说  我快要死了!
真的快饿死了吗?
难道不能再多忍一会儿吗?
非要为此卖掉长子权吗?
他很快就意识到自己错了
他卖掉了非常宝贵的东西
为了什么呢?
他又得到了什么呢?
就是饼和扁豆羹
而且  扁豆羹里连一点肉也没有
在伯特利
起码我们可以吃到面包
扁豆羹  还有肉
而且还是免费的
那么  从以扫的例子可以学到什么呢?
请打开圣经到希伯来书12章
看看耶和华想提醒我们什么
希伯来书12:16说
“也免得有人淫乱  不重视圣物”
“像以扫一样”
“他竟为了一点食物”
“就出卖了自己的长子权”
请留意  在这里
耶和华把以扫所做的事和淫乱进行比较
可以说  两者都是缺乏自制
屈服于肉体的欲望
以扫就是这样
犯淫乱的人也是这样
愿我们不要贪恋一时之欢
因此出卖自己的“长子权”
也就是在新世界生活的机会
想一想  饼和扁豆
能为以扫带来什么长远的益处呢?
几个小时过后  他还会再饿
同样  性不道德可以带来
多久所谓的快乐呢?
罪中之乐过后
带来的就是一连串的恶果
良心也会饱受折磨
我们讨论的第四个例子
是耶稣时代的一位年轻的官长
他身居高位  财产丰厚
圣经说耶稣也很爱他
那他愿意撇下这些
去追求更有恒久价值的东西
也就是跟随耶稣吗?
很遗憾  当耶稣邀请他时
他“忧忧愁愁地走了”
他舍不得所拥有的财富
结果  放弃了美好的前途
显然  这位年轻的官长作了错误的决定
当初跟随耶稣的人  现在都在哪里呢?
他们和耶稣一起在天上作王作祭司
侍立在耶和华面前
如果那位年轻的官长
后来还没有改变想法的话
他的财富
还有他自己现在早就化为灰烬了
为了财富
他失去了多么美好的福分啊!
我们千万不要
为了追求这个世界的物质财富
舍弃在新世界生活的光明前景
我们已经考虑了四个反面的例子
接下来  再看看四个正面的例子
他们为了真正有价值的事物
甘愿舍弃一切
第一个例子是亚伯拉罕
他接受耶和华的邀请
放弃了在家乡吾珥的舒适生活
之后  他带领家人  长途跋涉
历尽艰险  终于来到应许之地
他甘愿终其一生和家人住在帐幕里
但亚伯拉罕的付出换来了什么呢?
就是在耶和华心目中宝贵的位置
和上帝的友谊
耶和华把他称为“我的朋友”
他这么有信心  因此耶和华发誓
让万国都因他的苗裔而赢得福分
这个苗裔就是弥赛亚  耶稣
不久  耶稣就会复活亚伯拉罕
让他得享真正的生命
我们呢?为了参与全时服务
我们愿意放弃物质财富吗?
愿意放弃安逸的生活吗?
或者  我们愿意搬到传道员
需求更大的地区服务吗?
我们愿意效法亚伯拉罕的榜样
选择最有价值的事吗?
第二个好榜样是摩西
他比亚伯拉罕晚了几个世纪
但他也很懂得怎样明智取舍
摩西从小在法老的王宫里长大
通晓埃及人的一切智慧
有机会成为那个时代名声显赫的人物
不过圣经并没有记述
摩西在埃及取得了什么成就
为什么呢?
因为与他为耶和华所做的服务相比
这些事的价值显得微不足道
摩西受上帝任用
颁布律法指引以色列人归向弥赛亚
没有哪位先知能像摩西那样
可以“面对面”地认识耶和华
为了完成上帝交托的任务
他放弃了埃及的舒适生活
至于古埃及昔日的辉煌
如今只能在博物馆里
看到一些遗留下来的碎片
但摩西却赢得了上帝的奖赏
也就是真正的生命
摩西的榜样也收录在圣经里
在我们的心目中也占有重要的位置
接下来我们会讨论的榜样是  耶稣
在这方面  耶稣立下最好的榜样
像亚伯拉罕和摩西一样
耶稣甘愿舍弃舒适的生活
对他来说  就是要离开天上和父亲
他彻底舍了自己  成了人的模样
还要为别人服务
他甚至牺牲自己的生命
因为他坚信
耶和华会让他再次得回生命
能够遵行天父的旨意
救赎人类让他充满喜乐
我们仔细想想  就能看出
其实耶稣并不知道
他付出这一切会得到什么
请留意耶稣在约翰福音17:5  怎么说
“父亲啊  现在求你让我在你身旁得荣耀”
“就是未有世人以前”
“我在你身旁所享有的荣耀”
换句话说  就是
父亲  求你把我之前
所享有的给我就足够了
结果  耶和华赐给他的
远远超出他所求的
这就是耶和华
他赐给我们的总是
远远超过我们为他所付出的

‎‪진정한 행복의 비결은 여호와를 계속 충실히 섬기는 것임을 깨달았습니다.
‎‪처음엔 좀 재미 없어도, 포기하면 안 돼.

‎‪그래, 어떤 내용이 어려웠는지 한번 보여 줄래?
‪아빠는 먼저 내용을 이해할 수 있게 도와 달라고

‪또 공부의 목적이 그냥 집회 준비가 아니라,

‎‪그리고 꼭 책만 봐야 하는 건 아니라고 하시더라고요.
‎‪그래서 창조물도 관찰해 보고 배운 걸 그림으로도 그려 봤어요.

‎‪혹시 이따 오후에 시간 되면 연구 안 갈래요?

en.text: Ah, you’re up early today.
Dad?
Yeah?
I want to get baptized.
OK, let’s talk about it.
I was thinking, you know, Mom was baptized when she was 12, and, you know, I . . .
And now you’re 12, is that it?
I know what you’re thinking, Dad, but I’m ready.
I know I am.
I tell you what,
let’s do a special family study series first.
OK?
On what?
Well, we’ll start with faith.
Being dedicated to Jehovah
and staying dedicated to him,
it requires that we have strong faith.
“By faith Noah, after receiving divine warning of things not yet seen,
showed godly fear and constructed an ark.”
Abraham just “as good as offered up Isaac.”
So how did that take a lot of faith?
So the Bible says that Abel was faithful his whole life,
but he was also faithful until death.
So, what do you think that means?
Rachel,
keep your faith strong and you will never fail.
Love, Dad.
How do you like the pictures?
I really like this one of us.
Oh, your mom would have really liked this one.
I just wish she could have been there today.
I know, me too.
Which is why I’ve been thinking that if she were here,
I think she would have wanted you to have this.
Mom’s memory book.
I thought you could pick up where she left off
and fill it with your theocratic memories.
And then, one day soon, we can share those memories with her in the new world.
What do you say?
Yeah, I would love that.
Yeah? Good.
Thanks, Dad.
You’re welcome.
Hey, Dad.
Hey, Rachel.
I was just looking at some old pictures of you.
Wow, that was a long time ago.
Yeah, it was.
Hey, is there any mail for me?
Yeah, it’s right here on the counter.
Ah, OK.
It’s just another wedding invitation.
How was your day?
How was the museum?
Oh, it was OK.
Is something bothering you?
Yeah.
I feel like all my friends are getting married.
People at work wonder why I’m not dating.
And they’ve even tried to set me up.
I mean, come on, aren’t you interested in, you know, being with a guy?
I met someone at the museum today.
He was really nice.
I’m finally getting the attention I want,
but it’s not from a Witness.
Just call me, OK?
Maybe, maybe.
It’ll be fun.
So, what are you going to do about it?
Rachel, always remember,
virtue is a beautiful quality.
It’s not just passive avoidance but has real power
—power to do good.
Treasure virtue and Jehovah will treasure you.
Love, Dad.
Virtue is based on our love for Jehovah.
As it says in the book of Psalms:
“O you lovers of Jehovah, hate what is bad.”
Just call me, OK?
It’ll be fun.
Do I love Jehovah enough to hate what is bad?
Hey, any mail for me today?
No, not today.
Ah, the printing company called though.
I picked up this package for you.
The invitations arrived.
Yeah.
Eventually, I ended up getting engaged to a wonderful brother.
But even so,
I realized that marriage wasn’t the solution to my problem.
Remaining faithful to Jehovah is what really made me happy.
Mom, do we have anything to eat?
I can’t believe you’re still hungry.
He is a growing boy.
What are you going to do with all that energy, Son?
I’m trying to study.
For school?
No, it’s for the meeting tomorrow.
I want to be able to give a comment.
That’s good.
I’m sensing there’s a problem though.
Yeah, a big one.
I don’t like to study.
It’s so boring.
You know, I used to find it hard to study too,
and then I realized study can be like exercise.
It may not seem enjoyable at first,
but once you make the effort and then establish a regular routine,
it becomes enjoyable
—even fun.
And soon, it won’t feel like work anymore.
I agree.
I’ll tell you what, we can go up to your room,
and I’ll show you how to get the most out of your study.
OK, sounds good.
All right,
I thought we’d start by showing me, maybe, where you’re stuck.
Well, I’m trying to find the answer. . .
Dad reminded me to pray to Jehovah first,
asking for help to understand what I’m studying.
He said it’s important to look up the scriptures
and make sure I review the main points.
Then, think about how the material applies to me.
I learned that study isn’t just preparing for meetings;
it’s learning about Jehovah and how to live a good life.
And it doesn’t always mean reading.
Sometimes I can even look at creation
or draw pictures about something I learned.
After a few weeks, I really started to enjoy it
and my study time flew by.
Where’s Noah?
He’s up in his room studying.
Really?
Are you still studying?
Oh, man, Grandpa and Dad were right.
About what?
Well, they said that studying wouldn’t feel like work anymore.
I remember when Grandpa said the same thing to me.
Really?
I brought this for you.
He gave this to me when I was about your age.
Rachel, apply yourself to study,
and soon it won’t feel like work.
Love, Dad.
Hey, Mom.
Morning, Noah.
You going out in service?
No, actually, I have some things I need to get done,
and then I was hoping to do some painting or sketching later.
Nice.
Oh, good. You must be ahead on your schedule.
You ready, Son?
Ready.
Thanks for lunch.
You’re welcome. See you.
Have a good day.
Bye, Mom. Love you.
I’ve been planning this day off for months now.
I really want a chance to relax and paint.
I hardly ever get to take some time off.
Nothing is going to get in the way.
Hi, Anne.
Hey, Rach. How are you?
Good. How are you?
Good. Well, I’m on the way to the hall for service,
and I was wondering if later today, maybe if you had some time—
I started a new study with this young girl.
Oh, nice.
Actually, you know, I already have plans for the day.
Oh, OK.
What about Sarah?
I checked.
She has plans.
Daisy?
No.
Simone?
No, but that’s OK.
I’ll find somebody.
Thanks so much for understanding, Anne.
I felt bad, but she didn’t seem to mind.
Like she said, I’m sure she’ll find someone.
Well, look at that.
My old memory book.
I haven’t seen this in a while.
Dad’s cards always gave me such good advice.
Rachel, self-control is more than just refraining from doing bad.
It compels us to do good,
like Kingdom preaching.
Don’t let the unwilling flesh extinguish the fire of a willing spirit.
Love, Dad.
Self-control —I never thought of it that way before.
There’s nothing wrong with taking a day off,
but Anne does need help.
And I’ll still have time to paint when I get back.
Change of plans, Rachel.
Hi, Anne. This is Rachel.
Did you find anybody to go on the Bible study with you?
Could I go with you?
Perfect, where can I meet you?
See you soon.
I’m glad I decided to help Anne.
That was such a good Bible study,
and I still have time to paint.
This turned out to be a great day.
So how was pioneer school?
It was great.
We had Brother Daniels
as our primary instructor.
He’s incredible.
He’s a good teacher.
And, Noah, what was it like to be in pioneer school with your grandpa?
It was great; it really was.
Hard to believe, though,
I never thought this system would last so long.
And I certainly never thought I’d be a grandfather.
So, Grandpa, what was it like when you were my age?
Well, when I was about your age, I had just become a new father.
I could tell even then that your mother was going to be an artist.
Those were good times for us.
A few years later, though,
your grandmother became seriously ill.
Hey, Sweetie.
We didn’t know it at the time, but she wasn’t going to get better.
Watching your best friend die a little each day,
it just tears you up inside.
With Jehovah’s help
and with the support of the brothers and sisters,
we got through it.
We learned to rely on Jehovah
in ways we never had before.
And that helped when, years later,
another test came our way.
You see, back then, some were looking
to a certain date as signifying the end of this old system of things.
A few even went so far
as selling their homes and quitting their jobs.
I admit that I was ready to see this old system go away too,
but something just didn’t seem right.
Both at meetings and in my personal study,
I was reminded of what Jesus said
—nobody knows the day or hour.
I was dedicated to Jehovah,
not a date.
After that year came and went,
most of those who had wrong expectations
made the needed adjustments and they stayed.
We didn’t run away, and we didn’t give up.
We trusted in Jehovah.
When I see older ones now,
I don’t just see gray hair,
I see living, breathing examples of endurance.
Wow, Grandpa, I didn’t know you had to endure through all that.
We got through it with Jehovah’s help.
But, Scott, you were in pioneer school recently, right?
Yeah, just a year ago.
Who were your instructors?
We had Brother Smith and Brother Harris.
But, Scott, you were in pioneer school recently, right?
Yeah, just a year ago.
Who were your instructors?
I didn’t know
that evening would be one of our last together.
If I had known, I would have thanked Dad
for all that he did
—teaching me how to study,
meditate,
and put into practice beautiful qualities.
A gift he shared,
not just with me,
but a gift and Scriptural reminders that somehow seemed to keep giving.
No matter how hard it got,
the Bible training he gave me never steered me wrong.
I had no idea the impact it would have on me,
but he did.
I thank Jehovah that he raised me in the truth
the way he did.
Rachel,
as a parent, you pray
that your child always stays close to Jehovah.
So I made it my goal to instill the qualities
at 2 Peter 1:5-10
into your heart as best I could.
“Put forth all earnest effort
“to supply to your faith virtue,
“to your virtue knowledge,
“to your knowledge self-control,
“to your self-control endurance,
“to your endurance godly devotion,
“to your godly devotion brotherly affection,
“to your brotherly affection love.
“For if you keep on doing these things,
you will by no means ever fail.”
Love, Dad.

ko.text: 그 후로 여호와께서 기뻐하시는 일을 하는 데
이민 와서 얼마 안 되었을 때,
한 형제가 저를 탐탁지 않게 여기면서 불친절하게 대했어요.
그래서 그 형제한테 반감을 갖게 됐습니다.
저는 지부 사무실에서 편지를 받을 때가 있는데,
어떨 때는 제가 잘못한 일에 대해 지적을 받기도 합니다.
하지만 여호와의 지혜로운 조언을 따르는 것이
그분이 필요한 인도를 베푸실 것을 확신하는 게
시편은 여호와께서 “우리가 흙임을” 아신다고 알려 주죠.
마치 여호와께서 제게 이렇게 말씀하시는 거 같아요.
“아들아, 니가 잘못이 많지만 난 널 사랑한단다.
여호와를 섬기는 우리 모두는 불완전한 사람들입니다.
어느 날 전기 일을 하다가 그만 감전이 됐습니다.
의사가 상태를 보더니 양손을 모두 절단해야 한다고 말했어요.
전 가장 먼저 성경을 갖다 달라고 했어요.
성경을 펼 수 있어서 너무 행복했습니다.
지금 전 일을 하면서 가족을 잘 부양하고 있습니다.
무엇보다 가족이 영적으로 계속 발전하도록 돕고 있습니다.
장애 때문에 낙담하지 않는 데 도움이 됩니다.
저한테 장애가 있다는 사실조차 잊을 때가 있어요.
그리고 회중 형제 자매들을 통해 계속 도와주셨어요.
덕분에 어려움을 잘 이겨 낼 수 있었죠.
어린 꼬마가 와서 저를 그린 그림과 편지를 줬어요.
낙원에서 제 손을 되찾게 해 주실 거라고 말했죠.
낙원에 가서 다시 아내의 손도 잡아 보고
우리 아이들의 손을 잡고 함께 놀아 주고 싶어요.
여호와께선 틀림없이 제 소원을 이뤄 주실 겁니다.
감옥에 들어서자 모든 게 낯설고 겁이 났죠.
아는 사람도 없었고 감옥 생활이 어떤 건지도 몰랐어요.
어떤 어려움이든 견딜 수 있게 능력과 힘을 달라고
그 안에서 제게 위로가 된 건 기도와 하느님의 말씀뿐이었죠.
출판물도 볼 수 있었는데, 조건이 있었어요.
근데 그렇다고 해서 말도 하면 안 되는 건 아니잖아요?
전 무슨 일이 있어도 충실을 유지하겠다고 결심했습니다.
제 행실을 보고 다른 수감자들이 좋은 인상을 받았어요.
제가 읽을 차례에 성경을 돌려받지 못한 적도 많았어요.
전 욕을 안 했고 청결을 유지했는데,
계속 정규 파이오니아를 할 수 있었습니다.
연합된 형제들 모두가 저와 같은 고난을 겪고 있다는
베드로 전서 5장 9절의 말씀이 제게 큰 힘이 되었어요.
앞으로 어떤 상황에 처하게 되든, 누가 우리를 위협하든
여호와께서 우릴 절대 버리지 않으실 거라고 확신합니다.
마침내 출소일이 되어 집에 갔을 때
어머니를 다시 만난 그날을 절대 잊지 못할 겁니다.

en.text: I learned the truth as a child
and since then have always had to struggle
to conduct myself in a way that pleases Jehovah.
I don’t find it easy to control my temper or to keep calm.
When I first arrived in this country,
a brother treated me in an unkind manner
and was not very hospitable.
Because of this, I started feeling resentment toward him,
so much so that when he called me on the phone,
I spoke to him very rudely.
My wife had to help me,
reminding me that both the brother and I are imperfect
and that the feelings I had toward him were not healthy.
During that time, I felt awful and really bad
about my relationship with Jehovah.
Discipline is never a cause for joy,
and especially when I receive a letter from the branch
correcting and counseling me
for something I have not been doing right.
It certainly makes me feel uncomfortable.
But I try to reflect
on the fact that acting in accord with Jehovah’s wisdom
will bring me blessings.
Prayer to Jehovah, Bible principles,
and trusting that Jehovah will give me the needed direction
has really helped me.
As the Psalms mention, Jehovah is aware “that we are dust.”
It’s as if he were saying to me:
“Son, you make so many mistakes,
“but I love you anyway.
“I can use you in my service,
and I know that you will succeed.”
And, of course,
it’s possible because Jehovah has always helped his servants
—all of them, from Abel down to our day.
All of us who are serving him are imperfect people.
One day I was doing some electrical work,
and I was electrocuted.
When the doctor saw me,
he decided that it was necessary to amputate both my hands.
I had lost my hands!
There was so much I wouldn’t be able to do.
How would I work?
How would I care for my children? for my wife?
The first thing I asked for was a Bible
to see if I would be able to turn the pages,
and I could!
That made me so happy.
Now I am able to work to support my family.
I work as a painter, welder, and carpenter.
I can even drive myself to and from work.
I have been able to work on my spiritual goals
as I continue serving Jehovah, like being an elder in the congregation and,
above all,
helping my family to continue to grow spiritually.
Keeping myself occupied with spiritual matters
has meant that I don’t dwell on my disability.
In fact, sometimes I even forget that I’m disabled.
Jehovah has always sustained me.
Since the day of the accident,
I have seen how Jehovah God
by means of my family —my wife and kids—
and the brothers and sisters in the congregation
has helped me to move on.
Once, after giving a talk,
a young girl came up to me and gave me a letter
and a drawing she had done of me.
She thanked me and encouraged me by saying that very soon
Jehovah would give me my hands back in the Paradise.
Things like that, like being able to hold my wife’s hand,
my children’s too, to carry them and play with them,
that’s my hope,
and I have complete confidence that Jehovah will bring it about.
I was arrested and sentenced to two and a half years in prison
for my neutrality.
The surroundings in prison were unfamiliar and overwhelming.
I didn’t know anyone, and I didn’t know what to expect from them.
I was the only Witness.
I was continually praying to Jehovah for power and strength
to be able to resolve any problems in a peaceful manner
and withstand any difficulties.
In that situation, only prayer and God’s Word brought me comfort.
But then my Bible was taken away from me.
It was returned to me, though, some time later.
I was allowed to have literature on one condition:
That I would not preach.
True, preaching wasn’t allowed,
but that didn’t mean I wasn’t allowed to speak, did it?
I was determined that no matter what happened,
I would remain faithful.
My good conduct had a positive effect on the other prisoners.
Some of them started reading the Bible.
Quite often, I couldn’t even get my turn to read it.
I didn’t swear, and I kept myself physically clean.
This didn’t go unnoticed by the prison officials.
One day, they said to me,
“Because you are morally and physically clean,
we want you to be our head cook.”
That’s how I became their chef.
I constantly saw evidence of Jehovah’s hand.
The ministry was amazing.
There were months when I served up to 120 hours.
I placed more than 100 pieces of literature.
Thanks to Jehovah, I was able to stay in the full-time ministry
the whole time I was in prison.
This filled my heart with joy.
The thought at 1 Peter 5:9,
which says that the entire association of brothers
is experiencing the same kind of suffering I was, strengthened me.
I am confident that no matter what circumstances we find ourselves in,
no matter who is around us, Jehovah will never abandon us.
The day for my release finally arrived.
It was a complete surprise for my mother.
I hadn’t told her.
I will never forget that moment when we were reunited.

ko.text: 전 영국의 디닝턴이란 마을에서 자랐고 쌍둥이 자매가 있어요.
둘 다 사람들에게 말을 건넬 엄두도 못 냈어요.
할머니께선 제가 영적 목표를 정하는 데 많은 도움을 주셨어요.
건강이 많이 안 좋아지셨는데, 돌아가시기 전에 이렇게 말씀하셨죠.
“‘여호와께서 얼마나 선하신 분인지 맛보아 알아’ 보렴.
여호와를 섬기는 데 네 모든 걸 바치겠다고 약속해 주겠니?”
바로 지금이 변화를 할 기회라고 생각했어요.
그때부터 토요일마다 봉사를 갔고 곧 침례를 받았죠.
하지만 너무 수줍음이 많아 집회 때 해설을 잘 못했고,
회중 사람에게 말 거는 것도 어려웠죠.
우리 부부는 평생 최선을 다해 전 시간 봉사를 하기로 했어요.
봉사의 직무에서 느끼는 만족감과 베델에서 느끼는 행복은 깊은 관련이 있죠.
그래서 야외 봉사를 사랑하는 사람이라면 베델도 아주 좋아할 거예요.
모두를 잘 알게 됐고 금세 서로 아주 가까워졌어요.
다들 우리가 한 가족이라고 느끼도록 도와주셨죠.
날마다 베델에서 온종일, 온 힘을 다해 여호와를 섬기는 건
여호와께 모든 걸 드렸다는 생각에 정말 행복해져요.

en.text: My name is Laura.
I’ve served at Bethel for eight years.
I’m from a village called Dinnington,
and I have a twin sister.
And we were very shy.
I mean, really; I can’t stress how shy we were.
Neither of us dared speak to anyone.
My nana was a really big spiritual influence in my life.
She got really ill, and she knew she was going to die,
and she said: “‘Taste and see that Jehovah is good.’
“Please promise me you will try
to put everything into serving Jehovah.”
That affected me a lot.
I thought: ‘This is it. This is my chance.’
So I went out every Saturday from that moment on,
and I got baptized as soon as I could.
I still couldn’t answer at the meetings because I was too shy.
I still struggled to speak to people in the congregation.
But in the ministry, I was fine.
After pioneering five years, I got married.
We were going to try our best
to do full-time ministry for the rest of our lives.
I really do love Bethel.
I think there’s a real link between a good ministry
and happiness at Bethel.
So if you love the ministry, then Bethel is an excellent place.
For the full eight years, I’ve been in the laundry.
It’s a small team —there are only 40.
I got to know everyone so well.
I felt so integrated very quickly.
They helped me to feel like I was part of a family.
Knowing every day
that here at Bethel all our time and energy
goes to serving Jehovah is so satisfying.
You feel happy at the end of every day,
even if you’re tired mentally or physically.
You’ve done everything you can for Jehovah,
and you can’t beat it, really.

cn.text: 我叫劳拉
已经在伯特利服务8年了

不知道怎么形容!
以前我们连跟人说话都不敢
奶奶对我的影响很大

去世前她对我说
要尝尝主恩
你就会知道耶和华是良善的

她的话真的打动了我
我想  是时候采取行动了

做先驱5年后  我结婚了
我和丈夫都想一直做全时服务
