Jehovah looks for opportunities to bless his people.
That makes him happy.
And now you turn it around,
and you look at all the work that’s gone into this
—when he sees all those who volunteered to come on the project,
all of our brothers and sisters around the world who made donations,
those who included it in their prayers, those who helped others to come—
how proud that must make Jehovah!
And he’s just looking to bless them for that.
I sometimes try to imagine the conversations in heaven
between the angels and the kings in heaven
and how they’re so proud of all these workers down here.
And no doubt many of them were involved in the project.
We think of the workers here on earth, but how about the workers in heaven?
They may have been involved more than a few times
with safety issues and with legal matters.
So Jehovah was proud of everyone —his universal family—
both in heaven and on earth with these projects.
I feel that it’s going to build up the spirituality
of our brothers and sisters as they come.
And as we know, they’re coming from all over the world,
and that’s only going to further advance the work.
These buildings are beautiful, and it’s a beautiful setting.
That brings praise to Jehovah.
But what will bring the greatest praise is how these buildings,
these tools, will be used
—to honor his name, to bring attention to his Kingdom,
to spearhead the preaching work.
What these buildings will help the Governing Body accomplish
will bring the greatest praise to Jehovah.
So now we will be passing out those tests.
No.
No, now is the time for an interactive part of our program
where we have an opportunity to raise our voices in praise to Jehovah.
So if you’d like to stand, if you’re able,
we’re going to sing our new dedication song at this time.
And remember that’s entitled
“A Place That Will Bring You Praise.”
What a beautiful song —sung beautifully.
If you’d like to take your seats,
we’ve now arrived at the time
for a highlight of our program —the dedication talk.
And this is going to be given to us by the longest-serving member
of the current Governing Body, Brother Gerrit Lösch.
And the title of his talk is “Expansion That Glorifies Jehovah.”
Modern-day worship of Jehovah began in a small way.
It calls to mind the scripture that says,
according to Zechariah 4:10:
“Who has despised the day of small beginnings?”
What is the context of the scripture?
In the year 537 before our Common Era,
Jehovah moved Persian King Cyrus —who had conquered Babylon—
to release the Israelites that were held captive there for 70 years,
opening the way for them to return to Jerusalem and Judah.
They were to restore true worship
and rebuild the temple that Nebuchadnezzar had destroyed.
How many exiles returned to Jerusalem from Babylon
in 537 B.C.E.?
According to Ezra 2:64, about 50,000.
The footnote in the sixth edition of Isaac Leeser’s translation of the Bible
suggests that including women and children,
the number amounted to about 200,000.
In the seventh month of the year 537 B.C.E.,
the altar was set up.
And in the following year, 536 B.C.E.,
the foundation of the new temple was laid.
But after laying the foundation,
they neglected to rebuild the temple on that foundation.
Enemies round about also discouraged them from doing so.
The enemies succeeded to place a ban on the work
about 15 years later
in 522 before our Common Era.
Two years after that, in 520 B.C.E.
—stirred up by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah—
Governor Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest
courageously resumed the construction of the temple despite the ban.
Jehovah proclaimed that:
“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house,
“and his own hands will finish it.
. . . For who has despised the day of small beginnings?”
—Zechariah 4:9, 10.
The rebuilding of Jehovah’s temple at Jerusalem had a modest beginning,
yes, but it was not to be despised.
After all, it involved true worship
—pure worship of Jehovah.
The year 520 B.C.E. saw this “day of small beginnings,”
but in 515 B.C.E.,
22 years after the return from Babylon
and 5 years after the construction project was resumed,
the temple was completed.
The former exiles held the inauguration,
or we could say dedication of this house with joy
and this resulted in Jehovah’s praise.
He was glorified by the rebuilt temple.
There were also small beginnings for the Christian congregation
at Pentecost 33 of our Common Era.
And Jesus related this illustration
at Matthew 13:31, 32:
“The Kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard grain
“that a man took and planted in his field.
“It is, in fact, the tiniest of all the seeds,
“but when it has grown,
“it is the largest of the vegetable plants and becomes a tree,
so that the birds of heaven come and find lodging among its branches.”
What’s the meaning of Jesus’ illustration of the mustard grain?
The grain itself represents the Kingdom message
as well as what results from the preaching of that message
—the Christian congregation.
Like the mustard grain that is “the tiniest of all the seeds,”
the Christian congregation had small beginnings
in 33 of our Common Era.
However, within a few decades, the congregation grew rapidly.
It expanded beyond all expectations.
Jesus tells us that “the birds of heaven”
were able to “find lodging among its branches.”
These figurative birds picture righthearted individuals
who find spiritual food, shade, and shelter
within the Christian congregation.
There were also small beginnings in modern times.
Consider our first headquarters.
In modern times, Bible Students, as we were called,
had headquarters offices first at 101 Fifth Avenue in Pittsburgh,
and thereafter at 44 Federal Street,
Allegheny, Pennsylvania.
By the late 1880’s, they built their own structure.
Completed in 1889 at Arch Street,
it was known as the Bible House.
Because of continued expansion,
headquarters was transferred to Brooklyn, New York,
in the years 1908-1909.
In 1908, the old “Plymouth Bethel,”
13-17 Hicks Street, Brooklyn, was purchased.
It belonged to the Plymouth Congregational Church.
Also, 124 Columbia Heights, close by,
was purchased from the Plymouth Church.
It soon became the new home
of our headquarters staff of —at that time— 30 persons,
and they called it Bethel, meaning “House of God.”
“Bethel” was the name the Plymouth Church
had given to their building on Hicks Street.
The remodeled Hicks Street building
then became known as the Brooklyn Tabernacle.
It housed offices and an auditorium.
On January 31, 1909,
350 persons were present
for the dedication of the new headquarters.
But there were also small beginnings in a different sense
in 1919 of our Common Era.
The statement at Zechariah 4:10 about “small beginnings”
applied after the Israelites had returned from Babylon.
Was there a parallel in modern times?
Yes.
In our century, for Jehovah’s anointed Christians,
it was a “day of small beginnings” in 1919,
when they were completely freed
from domination by Babylon the Great
—the world conglomerate of false religion—
in order to restore true worship.
Already in the years before,
they had progressively cleansed themselves from Babylon the Great.
From 1914 to 1919,
the brothers lived through a number of crises and tests,
but this came to an end in 1919.
The Memorial of Christ’s death
was celebrated on Sunday, April 13, 1919,
with 17,961 attending in many lands.
This was, of course, a lot less than the number of returnees
from literal Babylon.
And of these 18,000,
about 4,000 also reported field service.
Many looked down on the brothers.
Yes, there were again small beginnings, but still they were approved by Jehovah,
and therefore he caused expansion ever since.
There is expansion in the material sense.
In order to meet together in worship,
last year about 1,000 properties were purchased
and new Kingdom Halls constructed on them.
In addition, there were many more
where major or minor renovations were done.
Branch offices are being expanded
and also newly built remote translation offices,
Bible school facilities, and Assembly Halls.
In the United States, we now have 47 active Assembly Halls.
Also, there is expansion in numbers.
In the Democratic Republic of Congo,
there were almost 1.2 million
who attended the Memorial this year.
In Mexico, without Central America,
there were about 2.2 million who attended.
Worldwide, about 20 million
attended the Memorial of Christ’s death last year.
Each weekend, an average of 5,300 new ones
are getting baptized and becoming our brothers and sisters.
Our worldwide family and brotherhood grows.
But our numerical expansion in itself is not proof that we have the truth.
Other religions have many more members and some grow quickly.
There are about 1.5 billion Muslims in the world,
second only to the number of named Christians.
But numbers alone prove nothing.
Truth is not measured in numbers.
But the combination of true teaching, true love,
high moral standards, neutrality,
carrying and sanctifying God’s holy name
—together with the increase—
that does prove beyond a doubt that Jehovah has chosen us as his people.
At Isaiah 60:22,
there’s this prophecy that was foretold,
and it says:
“The little one will become a thousand
“and the small one a mighty nation.
I myself, Jehovah, will speed it up in its own time.”
Who is that “mighty nation”?
It’s the great crowd and the anointed together.
They constitute a combined “mighty nation,”
although they are relatively few when compared
to the present total world population
of more than 7.5 billion,
as of March of this year.
Many who visit us at Warwick, Wallkill, or Patterson say,
“Oh, you live here like in a paradise.”
And those saying this may have in mind
the loving fellowship that we enjoy
and also the beautiful surroundings.
And the fact is that we do live in a paradise
—a spiritual paradise.
But what about you visitors and all those who are watching this program
by streaming and otherwise?
The good news is that you are also in the spiritual paradise.
All of our worldwide brotherhood
live in this spiritual paradise.
Now, what is the spiritual paradise?
It involves our relationship with Jehovah.
It involves the spiritual food that we enjoy served by the faithful slave.
It also involves the loving relationship with our brothers
in the congregation and our worldwide brotherhood.
It includes personal blessings from Jehovah
that he bestows upon us in everyday life.
The spiritual paradise
is the spiritually secure, prosperous environment
or realm of activity in which we worship Jehovah.
No matter where we live on earth,
we are in this paradise as long as we actively support
the worship of Jehovah and endeavor to display the new personality.
The spiritual paradise began in a limited way
in 33 of our Common Era at Pentecost.
It underwent changes during the centuries
but was restored in 1919.
The spiritual paradise relates to the divine approval of the anointed
that became evident that year in 1919.
In comparison with the first century,
the anointed enjoy increased spiritual prosperity
since that time.
And since the 1930’s,
those with an earthly hope also enter the spiritual paradise.
And ultimately, the spiritual paradise will be in full existence,
in perfection, in the new world.
Do we appreciate that spiritual paradise?
Satan will try to destroy our spiritual paradise.
He thinks he can succeed because we seem vulnerable.
He may try to disrupt the flow of spiritual food
or break up our unity or stop us from zealously preaching
—all elements of the spiritual paradise.
Through political governments,
he will try to efface true worshippers and true worship from the earth,
but he will not succeed.
He will be thrown into an abyss for a thousand years,
and after that he will be crushed out of existence.
What about the governments that he controls now?
They will already be crushed at Armageddon —forever.
The Messianic Kingdom will take control of the earth,
which eventually will become a perfect, literal paradise,
and then the spiritual paradise
and the physical paradise will exist concurrently.
The expansion of the spiritual paradise since 1919
was paralleled by material expansion.
Let me take you back on history lane.
First, let’s talk about our printing efforts.
In 1920, we started with a rotary press at Myrtle Avenue, New York.
In 1922, the printery was relocated
to 18 Concord Street.
From 1927 to 1986,
additional printery buildings were bought
and erected on Adams Street.
But what about residence and office expansion?
On October 10, 1960,
there was the dedication of a new residence
and office building at 107 Columbia Heights;
630 brothers attended in the ground-floor Kingdom Hall.
The new building, Brother Franz said,
reminds us of the psalmist’s words:
that everyone in Jehovah’s temple would speak his glory.
In 1969, the 119 Columbia Heights residence was built
and dedicated on May 2.
In the same year, the complex was bought
from Squibb Pharmaceuticals,
and it served as world headquarters until we moved here to Warwick.
The address was 25-30 Columbia Heights,
and it was dedicated on March 15, 1982.
Later, buildings number 48 and 50
were also joined to the number 30 building.
Close by is the 85 Jay Street lot,
a whole city block that was used for parking.
Then, September 18, 1995,
there was another important dedication program.
Seventeen residences had been added
since the previous dedication of the Bethel residence
on May 2, 1969.
Among the added residences
there was the Towers Hotel that we bought in 1975,
the Bossert Hotel, Standish Hotel, Sliver building,
the 108 Joralemon Street building,
the 30-story Sands Street building,
and the 97 Columbia Heights building
—formerly there was the Margaret Hotel on that property.
The 360 Furman Street building,
which housed our shipping department and some other departments,
was purchased by us on March 15, 1983,
and was totally renovated.
It had a million square feet (93,000 sq m) of floor space.
As of this date, most of our properties —almost all of them—
have already been sold,
and this more than covered the expenses
needed to build headquarters here.
Well, what about expansion at Wallkill?
the farm at Wallkill was purchased from brothers.
It is 75 miles or 120 kilometers away from New York City.
New residence buildings were completed
The large printery was eventually built in 1973
and expanded in 1975.
In 2004, printing in New York was discontinued,
and all printing was consolidated at Wallkill.
there was the dedication program
for the expanded Wallkill complex and facilities.
Today, we also dedicate a new residence,
a new parking garage, a new office building at Wallkill,
as well as the Montgomery Warehouse,
and two nearby hotels and a diner that you saw before in the video.
Wallkill has become the national headquarters
for the United States branch,
and most of the Branch Committee members live at Wallkill.
Warwick is the worldwide headquarters —so that’s the difference.
But there was also a complex built at Patterson
in the mid-1990’s with offices, residences,
and theocratic schools.
And on May 19, 1999,
was the dedication program.
Recently, the Mount Ebo video studios on Route 22,
close to Patterson, were added and also another building.
Now, Patterson is also considered as part of world headquarters.
Also, the Tuxedo building that we bought from the paper company
and where our broadcasting studio is now,
is part of world headquarters.
It’s situated just about 10 minutes from here on the same country road.
Finally, we also dedicate the Rivercrest complex
that was bought in Fishkill,
where several hundred Bethelites live.
Today, we will focus on the dedication
of our beautiful world headquarters complex at Warwick.
Now, why was it built here?
Well, we trust that it was Jehovah
that wanted us to build it here.
Well, what we learn from ancient times
is that according to 2 Kings 23:27,
Jehovah was the one who chose Jerusalem as a center of worship.
And in our time,
our world headquarters is a center that promotes true worship worldwide,
and we believe it was chosen by Jehovah.
All the expansion that we talked about glorifies Jehovah.
The apostle Paul had the right attitude.
He wrote at 1 Thessalonians 2:6:
“Nor have we been seeking glory from men.”
Yes, we seek Jehovah’s glory, not our own glory.
He is the one that caused and blessed the construction of our complexes.
I’m sure you agree.
Jehovah is the one who blessed the rebuilding of the physical temple
in the times of Zerubbabel.
And Jehovah said back then, according to Isaiah 60:7:
“I will beautify my glorious house.”
Now, the prophecy about the “glorious house” in our time refers,
not to the literal structures of world headquarters,
but to our spiritual temple.
Many would come, according to prophecy,
and worship in that spiritual temple.
It is a figurative ‘house of prayer for all the nations,’
according to Isaiah 56:7.
Revelation 7:9 prophesies
about ‘a great crowd out of all the nations.’
Now, what is their role and position?
Well, let’s look at it in the Bible
in Revelation chapter 7.
And in verse 9, it says:
“After this I saw, and look! a great crowd,
“which no man was able to number,
“out of all nations and tribes and peoples and tongues,
“standing before the throne and before the Lamb,
“dressed in white robes;
and there were palm branches in their hands.”
It says that they ‘stand before the throne of God.’
Does this mean that they go to heaven?
No.
The earth is called God’s “footstool”
—Isaiah 66:1.
So even on earth,
the great crowd stands before the throne of Jehovah.
The great crowd consists of Christians
with the hope to live forever in Paradise on earth.
Revelation 7:15 says about them:
“They are rendering him sacred service day and night.”
Where?
In front of the temple?
No, it says: “In his temple.”
Where, exactly, is the great crowd serving?
Yes, all of us, no matter what hope we have,
serve Jehovah in the spiritual temple
because we all worship Jehovah based on Jesus’ sacrifice.
So, what is the spiritual temple?
True or false?
It’s the same as the spiritual paradise.
False.
Or it refers to anointed Christians.
False, again.
The temples in Bible times constituted a provision
or arrangement for worshipping Jehovah.
So the spiritual temple is also an arrangement of worship
based on Jesus’ perfect ransom sacrifice,
and all who worship Jehovah based on his sacrifice
are in the spiritual temple.
Now, the spiritual paradise, on the other hand,
refers to a condition
that allows us to serve Jehovah
with his approval and in peace with our brothers.
We can enhance the beauty of the spiritual paradise
and extend its borders by making disciples
and also by displaying the Christian personality.
All in the spiritual paradise sing Jehovah’s praise without letup.
It is as if they preach day and night.
Isaiah 62:6 goes on to say:
“Continuously, all day long and all night long,
“they should not be silent.
You who make mention of Jehovah, do not rest.”
Yes, we are determined not to be silent,
not to rest mentioning Jehovah.
At chapter 60, verse 6, in Isaiah, we read:
“They will proclaim the praises of Jehovah.”
By preaching the good news and by our expressions in Kingdom Halls,
we all contribute to Jehovah’s praise.
Praising Jehovah is one of the primary objectives
of our meeting attendance and our preaching activity.
We understand that we do not primarily preach
to save people’s lives.
Jehovah’s praise is more important than the salvation of people.
Why?
Because Jehovah is more important than people.
At Hebrews 13:15, it says:
“Through him [Christ] let us always offer to God
“a sacrifice of praise,
“that is, the fruit of our lips
that make public declaration to his name.”
Nobody can stop the expansion.
Even dictatorial governments, including communist governments,
could not stop the expansion of God’s organization.
Hitler could not; Stalin could not;
Trujillo in the Dominican Republic could not;
Mussolini in Italy could not;
Ceausescu of Romania could not;
Mao Tse-tung could not;
Enver Hoxha, dictator of communist Albania, could not.
Nobody can because Jehovah is with us.
What about the former Soviet Union
that included Ukraine, Moldova, Belarus, and Russia?
In 1991, there were less than 50,000 publishers
in the former Soviet Union.
Now they are approaching 400,000 publishers.
Imagine that increase, or expansion.
Within the period from 1991 to 1998,
a total of 220,492 were baptized
in the former Soviet Union.
In 1990, in Kiev, the capital of Ukraine,
there was just one congregation.
Now there are about 75.
And 1993 saw the largest baptism of true Christians ever.
It happened also in Kiev, Ukraine, at the convention
—7,402 were baptized.
Restrictions cannot stop the work.
Jehovah promised:
“I will oppose those who oppose you,
and I will save your own sons.”
—Isaiah 49:25.
Shortly before Armageddon, prophecy shows
that we will be attacked by a coalition of nations
or governments directed by Satan and the demons.
We do not need to fear, though.
Jehovah will protect his people during the great tribulation,
and it stands to reason that he will also protect
the physical headquarters.
At Zechariah 2:8, he says:
“Whoever touches you touches the pupil of my eye.”
Zechariah 2:5:
“‘And I will become to her,’ declares Jehovah,
“‘a wall of fire all around [in protection],
and I will become the glory in her midst.’”
Yes, our headquarters bring glory to Jehovah.
These headquarters facilities and related buildings
were built to glorify and praise Jehovah.
Isaiah 43:21 says:
“The people whom I formed for myself [What for?]
so that they might declare my praise.”
Isaiah 43:21 —good to remember that text.
It shows that the purpose why Jehovah has formed us as his people
is to glorify and praise him.
And so, what is the purpose of the Christian congregation in general?
Well, again, to bring praise to Jehovah.
What’s the purpose of Warwick headquarters?
To praise Jehovah.
Ephesians 1:12 encourages us
to “serve for the praise of his glory.”
May this new complex and the other buildings
that we dedicate today
glorify and praise our dear heavenly Father, Jehovah.
It is now appropriate that we say a dedication prayer
to dedicate all the buildings that have not been dedicated yet.
And Brother Leon Weaver,
who serves on the Branch Committee in the United States,
will now represent us in prayer.
With this prayer and your consent,
I now declare all of our new buildings as dedicated to Jehovah.
And we thank all of you for your contributions in various ways
—manual labor, financial contributions, and prayers.
Now, what is the opposite of “the day of small beginnings”?
The day of a big finish?
Well, is the dedication of our headquarters
the big finish, or ending?
No ending is in sight.
It is all relative.
In the new world, we might even consider the dedication of Warwick
as a small beginning
in comparison with the huge work that will be accomplished
in Paradise to teach billions,
because billions will be resurrected.
Isaiah 11:9 says:
“The earth will certainly be filled with the knowledge of Jehovah
as the waters cover the sea.”
Yes, we have a glorious God,
and Jehovah has a glorious name.
We have the glorious good news,
and we have a glorious hope for the future.
When Solomon inaugurated the temple,
the glory of Jehovah filled the house.
Today, the spiritual temple
in which millions of us find ourselves in
is also filled with Jehovah’s glory.
At Isaiah 26:12,
it says:
“O Jehovah, you will grant us peace,
“because everything we have done
you have accomplished for us.”
Yes, we want to give credit and praise to Jehovah God.
Even opposers come to realize
that Jehovah’s blessing was involved in the construction,
as was the case in the days of Nehemiah.
Nehemiah 6:16 says:
“They realized [the opposers] that it was with our God’s help
that this work had been done.”
And this is in line with 1 Peter 4:11:
“So that in all things
“God may be glorified through Jesus Christ.
“The glory and the might are his forever and ever.
Amen.”
Revelation 5:13 agrees with this, saying:
“To the One sitting on the throne and to the Lamb
“be the blessing and the honor
and the glory and the might forever and ever.”
Hallelujah!
Thank you very much, Brother Lösch,
for helping us to focus on the real meaning
of the dedication of these facilities.
The thousands that attended in person or were tied in for that event
thoroughly enjoyed the dedication program.
And now millions more of you have been able to enjoy the same experience.
I know, I know,
you can’t wait to see the rest of the program.
So I’m happy to inform you that the spiritual portion
of the annual meeting program
will be posted later this month in two installments
in the Video On Demand section of our site.
Part 2 will be posted on Monday, January 15.
Part 3 is to be posted on Monday, January 29.
So by the end of the month, you will have heard talks
from five members of the Governing Body.
We are well-fed spiritually, that is for sure.
Well, that’s all for now.
This program is from the studio of JW Broadcasting
at the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

cn.text: 这里是JW电视网一月份的节目
欢迎大家
马克·努玛尔弟兄上个月提到
中央长老团已经批准
以后宾夕法尼亚州
守望台圣经书社举办的年会
将会在JW电视网
“每月节目”中呈现给大家
世界各地的翻译小组
将这些节目
翻译成许多不同的语言
让更多的人有机会欣赏
去年10月7日举办的年会
的确意义重大
年会內容包括为美国分部
新建大楼举办的呈献礼
也包括为世界总部的落成
举办的呈献礼
这次年会在纽约沃威克的
伯特利礼堂举行
中央长老团的杰弗里·杰克逊弟兄
担任本次年会主席
在本期节目中
你将会看到和呈献礼有关的报道
相信你们一定会非常喜欢本期节目
节目开始前
我想问大家一个问题
实际上  中央长老团特别嘱咐我
要问问母语是英语的弟兄这个问题
如果  刚才史慕理弟兄在祷告中说
愿你的名得到洗雪
你会怎么想呢?
也许你会想
没搞错吧  我没听错吧
的确  过去许多年
在英文的表达当中
特别是提及彰显上帝的圣名
和证明他的至高统治权时
我们都非常谨慎  对吗?
不过“洗雪上帝的圣名”
这样的说法是错误的吗?
1965年的一期《警醒!》说
这种说法是错的
后来到了1995年
《守望台》也再次强调了同样的观点
文章说
没有人可以质疑上帝的圣名
所以我们也不需要洗雪上帝的圣名
不过  随着深入的研究
我们发现  需要修订以往的解释
特别是英语中的说法
现在我们一起考虑一下
跟这句话有关的一些词
先看下“彰显为圣”这个词
它是什么意思呢?
它的意思是使之圣洁
或把某件事物看作圣洁
耶稣也吩咐我们这样祷告
“愿你的名彰显为圣”
所以  别紧张
这个说法没有调整
所以我们祷告祈求
上帝的名“彰显为圣”很合适
那“洗雪”这个词呢?
一般来说“洗雪”的意思
是指证实并告知某个人所做的是正确的
也许他们正遭受指责
但后来却证实  他们是正确的
“名字”这个词呢?
名字只是身份标签或代号吗?
圣经里的名字不只如此  对吧?
名字有时也牵涉到一个人的名声
比如
箴言22:1说
“选择巨财不如选择美名”
在这里“名字”这个词
就是指一个人的名声
我们再考虑一下
一直以来
撒但都在质疑什么呢?
首先  他一直诋毁耶和华的圣名
也就是损害了上帝的名声
其次呢

en.text: At the age of 40,
a man of the royal house of Egypt
becomes a shepherd.
Forty years later,
that shepherd leaves his flock
to shepherd people,
a nation of slaves
numbering in the millions.
Moses is that 80-year-old shepherd.
He leads the people of Israel
out of the hands of their cruel master, Egypt,
after they have resided in that land
for more than two centuries.
When Moses was 40 years of age,
he thought he was qualified
to break Egypt’s iron grip over his people.
How did he show this?
Moses witnessed an incident of terrible injustice,
“an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his brothers.”
He was eager to act,
so “he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.”
Commenting on this, the Christian disciple Stephen said:
“He thought that his brothers would grasp
“that God was giving them salvation by his hand,
but they did not grasp it.”
His own people branded him a killer.
Fearing for his life,
Moses fled Egypt
and journeyed across the wilderness to Midian.
During those 40 years,
Moses would cultivate patience, meekness,
humility, mildness of temper, self-control,
and the ability to wait on Jehovah.
Who of us has not experienced challenges similar to Moses?
Have we had to overcome shyness
or stand up to bullying?
How do we react when faced with injustice
or opposition from family or from government?
Do we tend to get impatient
as we wait on Jehovah to make things right?
Or do we put too much confidence in ourselves
and too little in Jehovah?
If so, then we can learn a lesson in endurance
from the example of Moses.
Let us start by reading Exodus 3:1-10.
Moses now had a divine commission.
The time had come for Jehovah to free his people.
The time had come for Moses
to be a faithful leader who does not give up.
Would he accept this assignment,
one that he had been only too eager
to take up 40 years earlier in Egypt?
Let’s pick up the Bible account at Exodus 3:11-22.
What a dramatic change 40 years has brought to Moses!
Here is a different Moses,
one who is uncertain, shy.
Moses has serious doubts about his own qualifications.
He believes that his commission is too much for him.
In effect, he says: “Oh, no!
Please don’t ask me to do this!”
Can you put yourself in Moses’ sandals?
Have you ever been given an assignment
that you feel is beyond your ability?
Yet, you don’t give up.
Earnest prayer helps restore your confidence.
You obey.
What about Moses?
Jehovah reassures him by saying:
“I will prove to be with you.”
Yet, Moses is still hesitant.
Will he give up
and ask Jehovah to find someone else?
Note what Exodus 4:1-9 says:
Moses needs reassurance.
So Jehovah gives Moses, not just one,
but three signs to show the older men
proof of divine backing.
And what powerful credentials these are!
For the first time,
a human is empowered to perform miracles.
As the rest of Exodus chapter 4 shows,
Moses feels inadequate to speak to Pharaoh.
He pleads that he is “slow of tongue,”
even asking Jehovah
to excuse him from the task.
Jehovah gives him help.
Jehovah assigns Aaron
as Moses’ mouthpiece.
Both men proceed to meet Pharaoh.
Listen to what is said to Pharaoh
as found at Exodus 5:1-9:
Pharaoh defiantly says no to Jehovah.
He is angry at the Hebrews.
In turn, the people are angry at Moses.
They blame him for their hardship.
Moses feels sorry for the people
and asks Jehovah:
“Why have you sent me?”
Jehovah patiently gives Moses
a reassuring message,
beginning at Exodus 6:1.
Jehovah backs up his promise of deliverance
by means of his unique name.
Moses, therefore, does not give up.
He obeys Jehovah,
and he and Aaron prepare
to meet Pharaoh again.
Let’s read Exodus 7:1-7.
Moses now can be confident of Jehovah’s backing
because Moses is doing things Jehovah’s way
and at a time that fits Jehovah’s prophetic timetable.
Jehovah is about to use ten plagues
to bring Pharaoh to his knees.
These disasters will show
that Jehovah’s sovereignty is real
and that he is worthy of worship.
The Ten Plagues will also expose
the Egyptian gods as nothing
—as mere unreality.
The first three plagues
strike both the Egyptians and the Hebrews.
However, the next seven plagues
do not touch the Hebrews
—proof that Jehovah can set apart
and protect his worshippers
if they do not give up their trust in him.
Now let’s summarize the Ten Plagues
listed at Exodus 7:14–11:10.
Plague 1: Water is turned into blood.
Plague 2: Frogs invade the land and houses.
Plague 3: Gnats pester man and beast.
Plague 4: Gadflies swarm and bite only the Egyptians.
Plague 5: Livestock die.
Plague 6: Boils fester on man and beast.
Plague 7: Hail strikes man, beast, and vegetation.
Plague 8: Locusts swarm and eat all vegetation
left after the hailstorm.
Plague 9: Thick darkness
blankets Egypt for three days.
Plague 10: The firstborn of man and livestock is killed.
Pharaoh sees his firstborn dead.
He hears great outcries of bitter grief
rise from the houses of all the Egyptians
because they too see their firstborn dead.
Pharaoh quickly summons Moses and Aaron
and tells them to go, to hurry away.
Will Pharaoh’s heart soften?
Let’s have Exodus 14:5-10 answer.
Will Jehovah hear their cry for help?
Let’s read Exodus 14:13-31.
Are the Hebrews happy that they endured
to see the salvation of Jehovah?
Yes!
They break out in a joyful victory song.
Listen to them sing!
You too can stand and sing along.
Song number 149 represents what is found
at Exodus 15:1-21.
If you can,
let us all stand and sing song 149.
Please be seated.
The account we just read
vividly illustrates Jehovah’s use of power
in a way that serves notice on all who defy him.
Thus, what can we take away from our Bible reading?
The fact that the Hebrews suffered in Egypt
and Jehovah delivered them is concrete proof
that our hope for deliverance from Satan’s world
is not an empty one.
When you seem trapped in a corner by life’s problems,
do not give up!
The God who parted the Red Sea
can provide escape for you too.
If, during the coming great tribulation,
you feel trapped by Satan’s hoards,
remember: Endure to the end!
Jehovah will provide escape for you
and for all his worshippers
who don’t give up!

cn.text: 古埃及有一位皇室贵族
他40岁的时候
离开皇宫成为一个牧羊人
但他牧羊40年后
却转而带领一个受奴役的民族
这个牧羊人就是80岁的摩西
他带领几百万以色列人
离开住了200多年的地方
摆脱埃及人的魔掌
摩西40岁时
他以为自己有能力帮助同胞
脱离埃及的魔掌
我们怎么知道呢?
因为当时摩西看到一件不公平的事
就是一个埃及人在鞭打他的希伯来弟兄
摩西当场挺身而出
把那个埃及人杀了 藏在沙里
关于这件事 耶稣的门徒司提反说
摩西以为弟兄们一定明白
上帝要通过他的手拯救他们
谁知道以色列人并不明白
后来摩西的同胞还叫他“杀人凶手”
摩西很害怕 于是他逃离埃及
横越旷野 流亡米甸
在米甸流亡的40年间
摩西培养了耐心 谦和
谦卑 温和 自制
以及耐心等候耶和华的特质
我们之中
有谁没碰到摩西面对的困难呢?
我们也曾克服害怕人的心理
也曾起身对抗恶霸 不是吗?
当遇到不公平的事
或面对来自家人 政府的反对时
我们会怎么做呢?
我们会不会等不及上帝来解决问题呢?
还是我们对自己信心满满
反而对上帝没什么信心呢?
如果是这样的话
我们可以从摩西身上学习怎样忍耐
让我们来看看出埃及记3:1-10
摩西替他的岳父
米甸的祭司叶忒罗牧养羊群

耶和华的天使在荆棘丛中的火焰里
向他显现

摩西说
我要过去查看这个大奇观

耶和华见他过去查看

他说
我在这里

不要走近这里

以撒的上帝 雅各的上帝

我的子民在埃及的苦况

他们在监工手下发出的呼号

我要下来从埃及人手里搭救他们

现在你来 我要差你去见法老
把我的子民以色列人从埃及领出来

摩西终于可以做一个

他会接受这个任务吗?
接受这个他40年前

上帝说

证明是我差你去的

你们祖先的上帝差我到你们这里来

上帝又对摩西说

向我显现 说

带你们到迦南人 赫人 亚摩利人

이 친구 귀에서 불이 나오는 줄 알았다니까요!
사실, 알려 주고 싶은 좋은 소식이 있어서요.
그럼 안에 들어와서 맥주나 한잔 하면서 얘기해요.
엄마, 이 집 평수도 크고 엄청 좋아.
오늘 이 계약만 성공하면 나한테도 많이 떨어질 거야.
니네 이모부네 제약 회사 인턴 하기로 했지?
왜 지난 번에 말한 그 새로 지은 아파트
열심히 해서 수화 회중 가고 싶어.
네, 근데 제가 어디 가 봐야 돼서요.
오후 회기는 다음 주에 볼 거예요.
새로 시작한 부동산 일이 좀 바빠서요.
어떻게든 최선을 다해 가족을 영적으로 보호하세요.
내일 저희 집에서 저녁 같이 드실래요?
어, 그럼 물에다 레몬 좀 넣어 줄래?
언니랑 북부 회중에 있는 언니 친구도 오는 거죠?
덕분에 일도 더 많이 하게 됐고
저번에 예전에 살던 집 근처를 봉사했었어요.
티나, 윌리엄스 형제 집 구경 좀 시켜 드릴래?
혹시 평소에 하고 싶었던 게 있니?
나는 니가 지금 정말 잘하고 있다고 생각해.
새로운 언어를 배워서 봉사할 생각을 한다는 게.
우린 언니도 절대 포기하지 않을 거야.
시간이 지나면 분명히 올바른 결정을 내릴 거야.
전 가서 엄마 좀 도와 드리고 올게요.
아마 당분간은 계속 야근해야 될 거야.
엄마한테 안 될 거 같다고 문자할게.
내 차로 같이 퇴근하면서 너네 집에 들러서,
드디어 그 꽉 막힌 애나네 부모님 만나는 건가?
애나, 오늘 윌리엄스 형제랑 약속 잊었니?
모처럼 영적으로 교제할 수 있는 자리였는데.
아빠, 별일 아닌데 왜 이렇게 심각해요?
지금 개발하는 약 출시가 얼마 안 남아서 그래요.
우리가 얼마나 중요한 일 하고 있는데.
저기, 두 분께 정말 죄송하게 됐어요.
요즘 스케줄이 밀려서 팀 전체가 비상이거든요.
우리 팀에서 큰 역할을 하고 있어요.
그리고 정말 좋은 친구들이랑 일하고 있어요.
우린 성경의 도덕 원칙을 따르는 사람들이야.
결혼한 남자와 여자 사이에서만 허용된다고 말해.
아 저기요, 시비 거는 건 아닌데요,
여보, 우리가 너무 예민한 걸지도 몰라.
하지만 그분 말씀을 어기면 해를 입게 돼.
죄송한데, 저희가 내일도 할 일이 정말 많아서요.
이제 가 봐야 할 거 같아요.
내가 준 청구서 중에 빠진 거 없죠?
필요한 거 다 있고 문제 없죠?
브라이언, 형제한테 고마운 게 정말 많아요.
내가 형제랑 처음 연구 시작했을 때 기억나요?
그때 형제가 자주 말해 줬던 성구가
다른 사람의 기대에 자신을 맞추지 말라고.
그런데 지금 형제가 그러고 있는 거 같아요.
아니 지금 무슨 소릴 하는 거예요?
그러면 나한테 그렇게 말하면 안 되죠.
내가 아는 건 다 형제한테 배운 거예요.
나한테 정말 소중한 걸 가르쳐 줬잖아요.
형제가 가르쳐 준 것 때문에 완전히 달라졌어요.
나랑 메리, 애들도 다 희망을 가지고 살게 됐어요.
새 삶을 살 수 있게 됐잖아요.
뭔가 중요한 걸 잊어버린 것 같아요.
니가 잘 살아야, 내 체면이 서니까.
종교에 지나치게 빠져 있지 말라는 거다.
안 바쁘면 좀 더 얘기해 주고 싶은데.

en.text: Previously on Remember the Wife of Lot.
We wanted to invite you, all of you,
uh, to the hall this Sunday.
We have a special speaker.
We’ll have to talk about that.
Yeah.
The safest road is to get a good job with a good company.
Yeah, but should we be pushing Anna and Tina
to succeed in this system?
We are living at a time when it is vital that
we do not look back in a figurative sense.
Brian, this stock is going so well.
You’ve got to join us.
Thanks for thinking of me, Henry, but I can’t accept it.
Why not?
This is a good opportunity,
and you need more income.
You seem confident, Henry,
but, uh, I’m sorry, I just can’t accept it.
You don’t trust my investment strategy.
That’s it, isn’t it?
Just say so.
Look, you already know I think your latest investments are risky.
And, no, I’m not going to gamble my meager funds,
but that’s not it.
Brian, these days we’ve got to risk money to make money.
Don’t you understand that?
Even if there weren’t any risk involved,
I can’t accept a job offer that’s going to take
so much of my time and money.
Brian, I don’t get it.
All you have to do is sacrifice a little time for a couple of years
and you’d have all the money you need.
Henry, I hope it works out for you, OK?
But I can’t accept, all right?
Just—just say hi to Jennifer for me, OK?
All right, bye.
Who was that?
Your client?
That was just your brother.
He wants to get me involved in one of his investment businesses.
But I don’t have the time or money for that.
Well, I think we need to invest our money
into something more secure like real estate.
And we need to move across town where we can network
with more influential people.
Is this your mom’s idea?
Because we can’t afford this.
We’re already too much in debt.
Well, look!
We can mortgage this place
and then rent it out.
We’re not taking full advantage of this opportunity.
We need to put the Kingdom first.
I am putting the Kingdom first,
but this is the time to think about our future.
How many working years do we have left anyway?
But if you don’t plan ahead, we’ll end up living on the street.
Why are you all dressed up like this?
Are-are you going out in service?
I’m going to real estate classes.
What? We didn’t talk about this!
Why?
If you made more money, I wouldn’t have to!
We’ve never gone without.
Gloria, wait.
Do you have cash?
I need it for a taxi.
Please?
Hey, boys, I just heard your dad pull up.
Start getting ready for dinner.
Nice.
Hey, boys.
Hey, Dad.
Hey, Babe.
How is it going?
Oh, all right. How are you doing?
Good.
What a day.
Hey, dinner is going to be ready soon,
so go wash up, OK?
Oh, all right, yeah.
Hey, guys, you want to wrap this game up?
Let’s get ready for dinner.
Here you go.
Hey!
What did I just say?
Put this furniture back, and get ready for dinner!
There’s something important we got to talk about tonight.
So, what did you want to talk about that was so important?
All right. OK.
Look. I’ve decided something.
I decided that I want to—
Well, I—I want us all
to start studying the Bible together.
What?
Do you mean you want me to become a priest?
Come on, Rick.
It’s Jehovah’s Witnesses, isn’t it, Dad?
I borrowed your book.
I liked it.
Well, I think it’s a good idea.
You know, I really like those people,
and it seems to be helping you, Joe.
You seem so much happier.
Yeah, oh, yeah, yeah, I am.
So like I said, that’s what I decided.
But I really want us all to be in on this together.
All right?
So...
what do you say, boys?
Sure, Dad.
Rick?
Come on, Rick.
Gloria? Is that you?
Yeah, it’s me.
Gloria, what is all of this?
Oh, it’s some new things that I picked up today.
I made my first sale today.
Aren’t you happy?
Yeah, that’s-that’s great.
We need the extra income, but it looks like you spent it already.
Yeah, it’s just a few things.
Uncle told me that I have to look professional to work for him.
If I’m going to move up and attract the right type of upscale client,
I have to look the part, you know?
But, Gloria, I thought you were doing this just to get
a little extra income for our necessities?
How much time are you planning to spend on this?
As much as it takes.
You can’t be successful by working less.
We already have a very full schedule
with our spiritual routine.
We have to make sacrifices for what’s most important in life.
You know that.
This new job—I’m worried.
It may mean sacrificing time
we should be spending on spiritual things.
What about your pioneering?
What about it?
I can do both.
All right. Here you go, Joe, your first door.
OK.
Good morning, Sir, how are you?
Oh, you people again?
Look, don’t you have real jobs?
I have a real job, and you keep waking me up.
OK?
I’m sorry, Frank. Forgive us.
We didn’t mean to upset you, man.
Joe?
Yeah, it’s me, Joe.
I didn’t even recognize you, man.
How are you doing, Joe, man?
Hey, how are you doing, Frank?
I’m sorry.
I’m good. It’s been a while.
It has.
We used to work together back in the day.
Oh, OK.
When was the last time we saw each other?
I think it was that time we were hauling that lumber.
Oh, when we were loading it, and then it all fell over in the street.
It fell all over the street.
It took us forever to clean it up.
Forever. It was terrible.
What you should have seen was how mad this guy got.
Oh.
He was so mad, man.
You could almost see the fumes coming out of his ears.
Yeah, that was the old Joe, Frank.
It looks like I got a new Joe here though.
You’re all dressed up and everything.
Yeah, yeah.
What brings you by?
Well, actually, we have some good news
we’d like to share with you.
Good news, huh?
OK, I like good news.
Well, why don’t you come on in?
And I’ll get some beers, and we can talk about this good news.
OK.
But no thanks on the beers this morning.
Oh, OK. Well, come on in anyway.
Mom,
this place is so big and fancy.
I could make so much money if I close this deal today.
Uncle would be so proud.
That’s my little Gloria.
You make me so proud now.
I’ll tell all my relatives
what a big important realtor my daughter is.
What about Anna?
Did she accept the internship with your cousin’s business?
You know how hard I worked to set it up.
I know, Mom.
Thank you so much for everything.
She starts next week.
You make me so happy.
There’s something else.
If I make this sale today,
I’ll have enough to make the down payment
on the bigger apartment that I told you about,
the one on the East Side.
The fancy one your uncle’s firm owns?
Yes. That one.
Oh, I’m so excited.
I know, me too.
I can’t wait to tell everybody.
Mom, I think my clients are here.
I got to go.
Talk to you later, OK?
OK.
Hello, come on in.
Good to see you guys.
The color contrast is very nice and flows into this living area.
Here’s the contract.
Please sign at the bottom of the page.
Congratulations.
Thank you.
It’s all yours.
Thank you, Gloria.
Enjoy it.
Thank you.
Joe, Mary.
Hi, boys.
Congratulations.
Thanks, Brother Williams.
Thanks so much.
I’m really proud of them all.
Yeah, so am I.
Yeah.
Well, how have you been?
You know, we’ve been good.
Um, it’s like Jesus said,
we always have enough to pay the bills
and sometimes, even a little extra.
Ricky, congratulations.
Aw, thank you. Thank you so much.
I’m so happy for you.
Yeah, but, hey, I know it’s just the beginning.
Really? So, what’s next?
Actually, I want to learn sign language.
Wow!
Maybe join the congregation, hopefully pretty soon.
That sounds exciting. Good for you.
I’ve been teaching myself so far.
Yeah.
Um, as far as I’ve gotten is,
“I’m learning sign language.”
And that’s all I know.
That’s very impressive.
You’ve got to start somewhere.
Yeah, that’s true.
Tina.
Come over here.
What are you doing?
I was just congratulating Ricky.
Hi, Tina.
Hi, Gloria.
Hi, Brother Williams.
How are you?
Good.
I would love to talk to you, but I have an appointment.
I got to go.
Oh.
Talk to you later, OK?
Oh, OK.
Brian,
where is Gloria going?
Is she OK?
Oh, yeah, Brother Williams, uh, she-she had to leave.
Um, Gloria is going to catch the rest of the assembly next week.
Um, it’s just been so busy with her real estate job lately.
We needed the extra money.
You know, we moved into a better place
over on the east side of town,
well, I’m working a little bit more too.
I’m just trying to make her happy.
True happiness, Brian
—joy—it’s spiritual.
You can’t satisfy spiritual needs with material things.
I know, Brother Williams,
but this extra stress, it’s just temporary.
I’ve-I’ve thought it all through.
We’ve prayed about it, and we’ve asked
for Jehovah to bless this decision.
Now you know, Brian,
Jehovah God cannot bless a decision
if it is not in harmony with his will.
Look at yourself.
You don’t seem happy.
But what can I do now?
Do all you can to protect your family spiritually
and to save your girls.
I appreciate the encouragement, Brother Williams.
You’re welcome.
You know, it seems like it’s been a while
since we’ve been able to talk like this.
Oh, it has been.
If you’re not busy, would you be able to come over
and join us for dinner tomorrow night?
You know, I would love to do that.
Why don’t you text me your new address and the time,
and I’ll look forward to seeing you tomorrow.
That sounds good?
That sounds great.
Excellent.
Thank you, Brother Williams.
I look forward to seeing you tomorrow.
OK.
OK. Bye-bye.
Hey, Mom, can I help with anything?
Oh, yeah.
Can you put the lemons in the water?
OK.
Hey, guys, Brother Williams is going to be here any minute, OK?
OK.
And Anna and her friend from the North Congregation
are supposed to come too, right?
Yep, that’s the plan.
I’ll get it.
Thank you, Tina.
Hey, Brother Williams.
Hi, Tina.
Come on in.
How are you?
Good.
It’s good to see you.
Brother Williams, you made it.
Thanks for coming over.
Of course. Thanks for the invitation.
Very nice.
Welcome.
Hi, Gloria.
Hi, Brother Williams.
I think I’d get lost in this big apartment.
Jehovah blessed us for our hard work.
Really, it just means longer hours
on the job and more work around the house.
You know, the other day in field service,
we passed by your old house.
I liked that place.
I remember our nice visits there.
I do too.
That was a great place.
Well, Tina, do you want to show
Brother Williams around while I finish the coffee?
OK, come on in.
Brother Williams likes the old place.
It seems like he likes it here too.
It all seems very nice.
What do you think of this place, Tina?
Well, honestly,
I wish we never left the other place.
Really?
Why do you feel that way?
Everything is so different here.
Everything has to look good
for you to fit in.
You have to wear the nicest clothes.
You have to drive the most expensive car.
Everything is— It’s just— It’s just different, that’s all.
Yeah, you know, I understand.
I was about your age when we moved into a new neighborhood,
and it can certainly be challenging.
But you know what might help?
If you set a new goal.
OK, like what?
Well, what do you think?
What interests you?
Well, I was thinking of learning a new language.
Really?
That’s an excellent goal.
What do you think of Ricky learning sign language?
Ah, I think it’s really exciting.
I do too.
You know, he is really making the truth his own,
and if he keeps on applying himself,
Jehovah God is going to really bless him.
Yeah.
I was hoping to see Anna.
Is Anna here?
Oh, she is with Kevin.
Kevin?
Kevin who?
Kevin is one of our relatives.
They work together at a pharmaceutical company.
He’s a pretty nice guy and from a nice family too.
Tina, are you OK?
How do you think Anna is doing?
Um, she’s—
she’s going through different things right now.
We invited her friend over from the other congregation
to maybe encourage her.
That’s nice.
But you know, I have to commend you
because you’re doing so well spiritually,
keeping up with your spiritual routine,
and you’re thinking about learning a new language so you can help out.
Keep up the good work.
Don’t give up.
But, Tina, we’re not going to give up on your sister.
She has the potential of being a fine servant of Jehovah.
And she has a good heart.
I’m confident that in time, she’s going to make the right decisions.
Brother Williams, here is your coffee.
Thank you.
Sorry, Brother Williams, I have to finish getting ready.
Oh, OK.
This looks really good, Anna.
Good job.
Really?
Thanks.
Hey, we’re still behind schedule, though,
so I’m going to have to ask you to work overtime
with the rest of the team just until we get caught up.
OK?
But I can’t tonight.
I have a family dinner I have to go to.
Dinner?
Anna, if you want to be successful, work needs to come first.
Everyone else is doing it.
Fine.
I’ll text my mom and tell her I can’t make it.
Good.
Don’t worry. She’ll understand.
It’s not my mom I’m worried about; it’s my dad.
He doesn’t want me working late anymore.
Fine, um, I’ll cover for you.
We’re all working late anyways, so I’ll give everyone a ride home
and afterwards we’ll step in for a few minutes
and I’ll explain that it’s all my fault.
OK?
OK.
So does this mean
we’re going to meet those uptight parents of yours?
They’re not that uptight.
I’m kidding.
Lighten up.
Hey, Anna’s family is pretty conservative,
so just be careful what you do say.
This should be interesting.
Tess, just be nice, OK?
I had a really good time tonight.
I’m glad Brother Williams could make it.
Yeah, it was very nice.
Yeah, I think he had a good time too.
Yeah.
Oh, Anna is home.
Hi.
Hey.
It’s customary to take our shoes off.
So—
Oh, OK.
Hey, Kevin is here too.
Come on in, guys.
Um, I know Kevin, but who are your friends, Anna?
Oh, yeah.
Mom, Dad, this is Tess and Eric.
We’re in the same intern program.
Nice to meet you all.
Come on in. Have a seat.
Anna, come here.
Um, would you like something to eat or drink?
Anna,
you missed dinner with Brother Williams tonight.
And your friend from the North Congregation, she came too.
What happened?
Dad, I know, but we had to work late.
I sent Mom a text.
Anna,
I was trying to do something spiritually encouraging for the family.
We’re worried about you, Honey.
OK, Dad,
I’m sorry, but it’s no big deal.
It’s just that the new medication we’re working on,
it goes to market soon.
It’s really important.
It could save people’s lives.
No big deal?
Anna, first of all, you know only God’s Kingdom will solve our problems.
These kids and your work,
it’s getting in the way of what’s most important.
Dad, these kids are on my team,
and they understand what I’m working on, the brothers don’t.
It’s way over their heads.
Anna, don’t you see?
They’re changing you.
Would you relax?
Just go talk to them, OK?
You know,
I really wanted to apologize to both of you.
It’s my fault that Anna is late today.
I asked the entire team to work overtime
so we could get caught up on the schedule.
But just to let you know, she’s doing really good.
And we really do enjoy having her on the team.
OK, thank you.
You know,
not just that, she’s working with some good people.
Tess and Eric, they’re some of the best
up-and-coming talents we have in the field.
Your parents must be really proud of you.
Well, my moms are both really proud of me.
I was raised by two wonderful women,
you know, life partners.
Oh, huh.
Yeah.
Um, you know, my assistant, Marty?
I recently found out that he’s gay.
You say that like there’s something wrong with it.
Do you have a problem?
Tess, don’t do this.
Why?
There’s nothing wrong with being gay.
Tess,
we live by the Bible’s moral standards,
but we don’t force our beliefs on other people,
and we don’t judge anyone either.
But you do think being gay is wrong.
Eric, remember where we’re at.
Well, we believe there are standards of right and wrong
that we should live by,
and God’s Word says that
sex is meant to be between a man and a woman
who are married to each other.
Look,
I don’t mean to be rude, Sir, but the world has changed.
Honey, maybe we’re being too harsh on gays.
Some people just seem to be programmed that way.
Look, I know not everyone agrees with us,
but we all have free will,
and God lets us choose to live by his standards or not.
If we go against his standards, we end up hurting ourselves.
He just wants what’s best for us.
Anna, what about you?
Do you agree with your father?
Well—
You know, we actually have another project due tomorrow.
It’s probably best that we get going.
Yeah.
Wait.
At least let me walk you guys outside.
So this is our Anna’s association.
They’re just kids.
Kids talk like they know everything.
Our Anna believes them.
OK, so I think you have all the invoices, right?
I gave you all the receipts, right?
Yep, I just got a couple more steps.
OK, Joe,
your books are clean.
I have no more concerns,
and amazingly, you’re out of debt.
Amazingly.
I don’t-I don’t think so, man.
It’s like you’ve always said,
“If you do things Jehovah’s way,”
right?
“He’ll help us.”
Hey, um, I got to go.
Um, you’ve got everything that you need.
I think it looks good.
So I’m just going to leave, OK?
Oh, oh, all right, OK.
Hey-hey, Brian, um, could you stick around for another minute?
There’s something I need to talk to you about.
Um, yeah, sure.
Yeah, thanks.
Look, Brian, I owe you a huge debt of gratitude, man.
Um, I was thinking back on when we first started studying.
Do you remember that?
I had all sorts of issues with my life,
my family, my business.
And my whole life was messed up,
and one of the things that you always talked to me about was Matthew 6:24.
Do you remember that?
‘No one can serve two masters.
You cannot slave for God and for Riches.’
I’m sorry, Joe, I’m not getting it.
What are you trying to say?
Well, I guess what I’m trying to say is
I’m concerned about you.
About me?
Yes, yes, about you
and your family.
And I’m not talking about financially.
Brian, I’m talking about spiritually.
I mean, you’re the one who —who always taught me
to never cave in to other people’s expectations of me.

우리 볼 시간도 없는 거 아니고?
저희 증인들은 명절이나 특정한 날을 안 지켜요.

그게 늘 내 마음에 안 들었던 거, 너도 알지?
이 비싼 아파트에서 살게도 해 주고.
내가 세 번이나 전화했는데, 받지도 않고.
그러니까 니가 엄마 좀 자주 찾아와야지.
너 여기 이사 온 뒤로 니 얼굴 잊어버리겠어.
그러다가 나 죽고 나서 후회하려고 그러니?
이번엔 의사 말 잘 들으실 거죠?
이러다간 우리 손녀들 시집가는 것도 못 보고 죽겠어.
우리 아파트는 오래돼서 그런가 좀 춥네.
그날 아주 중요한 고객들 만나는 날인데.
이번에 내가 큰 건 하나 맡았거든.
내가 세팅해 놓고 마티한테 맡기면 돼.
근데 아까 베란다에서 삼촌하고 무슨 얘기한 거야?
물질에 너무 빠져 있는 거 같아서.
좀 잘살아 보려고 하는 게 뭐 잘못이야?
영적인 게 그런 것들 때문에 밀려난다는 게 문제지.

우리 요즘 가족 숭배도 못 하고
개인 연구랑 봉사도 잘 안 하고.
아니 너무 부끄러워서 같이 기도도 못 하잖아.
그리고 우리 옛날 집, 아직 세도 안 나갔잖아.
근데 더 큰 문제는 따로 있어.
우리가 애들 어릴 때부터 어떻게 가르쳤는지 생각해 봐.
몇 년 전에 윌리엄스 형제가 한 연설 기억나?
우린 두 주인을 섬길 수 없어.
롯의 아내는 자기 집을 여호와보다 중요하게 여겼잖아.
하늘에 계신 우리 아버지 여호와 하느님 ...
당신의 아들이신 예수 그리스도 이름으로 기도드립니다.
아 근데, 내일 우리 일 몇 시쯤 끝나?
애나, 지금 우리 업무가 많이 밀렸거든?
특별 대우 받는다고 하는 팀원들이 있어.
미안하지만 너만 편의를 봐 줄 순 없어.
내가 언제 특별 대우 받았다 그래?
너 봐 주는 것도 한계가 있어.
처음에 일 시작할 땐 괜찮을 거라고 했잖아.
이번 주엔 매일 야근이니까 그런 줄 알아.
그래, 아는데 너만 빼 줄 순 없다고.
내일 일찍 끝나서 갈 수도 있고.
내일까지 해서 나한테 넘겨주면 될 것 같은데
야, 쟤네 저기서 또 저러고 있다
나야 도움이 된다면 뭐든지 할 수 있죠.
제시간에 와서 나랑 교대해 줘야 돼요, 알았죠?
난 세팅만 하고 바로 가야 되니까,
마티가 내일 일해 줄 수 있대?
그럼, 우리 같이 기념식 성경 읽기 하자.
아까 리키랑 메리 아줌마가 봉사하는 거 봤는데요.
같이 일하는 사람들도, 생각한 거랑 달라요.
돈 걱정 안 하고 살면 좋겠어.
그래야 파이오니아도 할 수 있는 거야.
그럼, 우리 이제 어떻게 해야 돼요?
일단 언니 머리부터 좀 어떻게 하고.
이웃 분들께 이 초대장을 드리고 있어요.
전에 하던 일보다 훨씬 더 좋고
안 바쁘면 좀 더 얘기해 주고 싶은데.
좋죠. 들어와서 커피 한잔 하고 가세요.
조가 사진 보여 주면서 가족 얘기 많이 했거든요.
같이 성경을 공부하자고 한 건 남편이었어요.
혹시 직장 그만두고 파이오니아 하신 거
더 일찍 못 한 걸 후회할 뿐이죠.
생활하는 데 필요한 만큼만 벌 수 있음 돼.
그리고 난 가장 중요한 걸 잊고 있었어.
여호와를 의지하면 그분이 늘 도와주신다는 거.

여호와께 드릴 수 있는 건 하나도 안 남아.
근데 오늘 저녁에 꼭 일하러 가셔야 돼요?
잠깐 갔다 와야 할 거 같아.
마티 온댔으니까 대충 준비되면 바로 갈게.
그래도 혹시 모르니까 다시 확인은 해 봐.
“전화기가 꺼져 있어 삐 소리 후 음성 사서함으로 연결됩니다.”
지금 몇 신데 아직도 안 나왔어요?
그리고 와인은 지금 가서 바로 오픈해 놓구요.
그런 건 묻지 말고 그냥 알아서 좀 해요.
안내 책자는 어디서 구할 수 있을까요?
근데 혹시 어느 분이랑 연락하고 오셨어요?
근데 마티는 대체 언제 오는 거죠?
이 건물에 대해 설명해 주기로 했었는데.
그래, 한번 전화해 보는 게 좋겠다.
준비만 해 놓고 금방 나올 거라고 했잖아.
그럴려고 했는데, 마티가 아직도 안 왔어.
진짜 중요한 고객 분한테 인사 먼저 해요.

삼촌이 시키신 건 빠짐없이 다 했고요.
쓸데없는 소리 말고 가서 손님이나 챙겨.
잘한다 잘한다 하니까, 이제 나까지 무시하는 거냐?

en.text: Previously on Remember the Wife of Lot.
I’m going to real estate classes.
What? We didn’t talk about this!
Why?
If you made more money, I wouldn’t have to!
Gloria, wait.
I’ve decided something.
What is it?
To start studying the Bible together.
Do you mean you want me to become a priest?
Come on, Rick.
It’s Jehovah’s Witnesses, isn’t it, Dad?
What are you trying to say?
All I see is an unhappy man.
You have no idea how much pressure Gloria is putting on me.
You’re not the same person that I once knew.
Everybody, squeeze in.
Smile.
How did it turn out?
Oh, it turned out good.
Oh, it’s nice.
Very nice.
It’s very nice.
Sure.
It was time for something new.
Actually, we got many new things.
We even got a new piano for Anna.
Oh, nice.
Yeah.
Oh, Brian is home.
Have some dessert, OK?
Thank you.
Hey, Brian.
Hey.
I’ve invited some relatives for dinner.
Yeah, so I see.
Are you hungry?
Do you want some?
Oh, here are the oranges.
Oh, thank you.
Hey, let’s go.
Come on.
Wait a minute.
Hold—hold on, Gloria.
Why did you arrange this without telling me?
Well, surprise!
Why did you arrange this without telling me?
I thought it would be nice to have a family dinner.
But none of them are in the truth.
How else are we going to witness to them?
They’re only here to socialize.
They’re not here to talk about Jehovah.
Come on, Brian.
They’re family.
Let’s go and talk.
Oh.
Is your mother OK?
Eh, she’s fine.
Hey, Henry.
Hey.
I’ll let you guys talk.
Oh, OK.
Hello, Henry, how are you?
OK.
We haven’t seen much of you lately.
Yeah, well, we’ve been pretty busy.
Busy?
Well, I can tell you spend a lot of time
with your church but not with us.
We feel really left out.
Hey, guys.
Hey.
How are you guys doing?
We have other relatives who are Christians.
I mean, they really spend time with us during holidays.
Henry, as I’ve explained before,
when we became Witnesses,
there are just certain practices we don’t want to compromise on.
Our beliefs are very important to us.
Between that and—and work, we really do have busy schedules.
Well, speaking of work, um, I’m out of work at this moment.
I’m sorry to hear that, Henry.
So if you hear of any job openings, I mean, I’ve got a lot of experience.
Would you excuse us for a moment?
Of course.
Gloria, recently you have done well.
I must congratulate you on your hard work with my company.
Thank you, Uncle.
But do not forget, it’s not just your
hard work that has given you all this.
Yes, Uncle.
I understand,
and thank you for everything.
Then you must not let me down.
What do you mean, Uncle?
I am talking about your priorities.
What about them?
You must learn to keep your religion in its place.
Of course, you can have your God,
but it must not interfere with what’s most
important in your life —your relatives and your career.
Your religion gets in the way of what’s expected of you.
Well, Uncle, I understand
how important those things are to you and to all of my relatives,
but as I explained to you before,
when I became one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
spiritual things also became very important to me.
Yes.
And I have never agreed with your choice, have I?
No.
And yet I’ve given you this job.
I helped you get this beautiful apartment
because the way you live reflects on me.
You know that since your father passed away,
I’ve taken the responsibility as family head
towards you as well as your mother and your brother.
Have you forgotten all I have done for you?
No.
I do remember.
Then you must serve my company and work hard for me.
This is for family, Gloria.
This must be your priority.
You must make me proud.
Remember what I’ve said to you.
You could lose all this very easily.
Do you understand?
Yes, I understand.
Good.
Mom, why are you reading a medical book?
I’m reading about my problem.
Problem?
What problem?
The pain in my back.
You didn’t tell me you had any pain.
I called you three times, but you didn’t answer.
Mom, I didn’t see any calls from you.
I wouldn’t need to call you if you would visit me.
I hardly see you anymore since you moved here.
Mom, I came by only three days ago.
One day, you’ll come by
and find me on the floor, not breathing.
I want you to take me to the doctor.
Go ahead and laugh.
Are you going to follow his instructions this time?
At this rate, I may not be around
to see my granddaughters get married.
Mom, listen.
We’re going to see the doctor tomorrow.
OK?
Gloria,
when you were little, my mom used to live with us
and later your father’s mother too.
Remember that?
Yes.
My apartment is not like this,
big and warm.
Mine is cold and drafty, you know?
I think that’s why I have this pain.
Come on, Mom.
“That’s why I have this pain.”
Oh, she wants to move in with us.
Oh, man.
Hey.
Hey.
Oh, Brother Williams’ next visit
is the third week of March.
That’s the same week of the Memorial.
So make sure you put that in your calendar.
OK.
Oh, I have a big showing on the same day as the Memorial.
It—it’s the new property that Uncle asked me to handle.
The—the day of the Memorial?
Yeah.
Ah, it’s OK.
I—I can get Marty to cover for me once I set up.
OK, you better make sure that he can handle that.
Yeah, I will.
All right.
Hey, what were you and Uncle talking about on the balcony tonight?
It’s nothing.
We were just talking about business.
Are you sure?
Because it seemed like it bothered you.
Well,
he’s putting a lot of pressure on me.
It’s OK.
I can handle it.
Really?
I mean, but can we?
What do you mean?
I’m just saying, look at us.
Actually,
Joe spoke with me today.
About what?
Well, he’s concerned about us spiritually.
He feels we’ve become materialistic.
Joe doesn’t understand our background.
And is it really wrong to try to improve our life?
No, but, not if it means putting anything
or anyone ahead of Jehovah.
But don’t you think that we need to make some sacrifices if we want nice things?
We have made sacrifices, all the wrong ones.
You’ve even had to quit pioneering.
We’re neglecting family worship, study, service.
We’ve even become too busy, or maybe too ashamed,
to even pray together.
Gloria, we’re drifting apart from each other.
But look at this place.
It is so nice.
I don’t want to give it up.
Gloria,
we don’t want this place if it takes us
or you away from Jehovah.
Besides, we haven’t been able to rent out the old place yet.
We have two mortgages.
But more than that, Gloria,
think of all we taught the girls when they were little
about putting Jehovah ahead of everything else.
Do you remember Brother Williams’ talk a couple years ago
about not being able to serve two masters
and how Lot’s wife put her home ahead of Jehovah?
Jesus told her story as a lesson for us.
We have to “remember the wife of Lot.”
It didn’t have to end that way for her,
and it doesn’t have to end that way for us.
Do you think we are that bad?
Come here.
I want us to get back to where we were, spiritually.
I want you close to me again, remember?
Let’s say a prayer.
OK.
Jehovah God, our heavenly Father, we come before you.
We pray all of this in Jesus’ name.
Amen.
Amen.
We can turn this around.
We can do it.
OK?
Jehovah will help us.
OK.
I’m proud of you.
I’m going to finish cleaning up, OK?
OK.
We have to “remember the wife of Lot.”
It didn’t have to end that way for her,
and it doesn’t have to end that way for us.
“Remember the wife of Lot.”
Hey, so I was wondering, tomorrow, what time do you think we’ll finish?
Look, Anna, we’re really behind schedule,
so I need you to be a team player on this.
OK.
When have I not been a team player?
Some people on the team feel that you’re getting special treatment
because we’re related,
and I have to make sure that everyone gets treated equally.
When have I ever asked for special treatment?
It’s your church meetings, Anna.
If we’re all working overtime,
I can’t keep covering for you so you can go while everyone else stays.
But you said when I started that it wouldn’t be a problem.
Look, I remember what I said, but things change, Anna.
And if you want to be part of this team,
you need to do your part,
and that’s starting now.
We’re working overtime every night this week until we get caught up.
Every night? I can’t do that, Kevin.
Tomorrow is a really important meeting; it’s the Memorial.
I told you already.
I remember,
but I can’t make an exception for you.
But who knows?
Maybe if we work hard enough, we’ll get caught up and you could still go.
Fine.
Hey, it’s close to lunch.
Let’s grab the rest of the team and get some food,
and we can talk about this later.
OK?
Fine.
Nice haircut, by the way.
Thanks, my dad doesn’t like it though.
Of course.
It was so gross.
Hey, look at those religious fanatics over there.
I bet they get along great with your strict parents.
Hey, Anna!
Did you see that?
These are the top headlines from BNC News.
Death tolls continue to rise
in the wake of a massive earthquake
with a magnitude of 8.1
that struck off the northern coast of Taiwan on Tuesday
and was felt as far away as Tokyo, Japan.
The resulting tsunami has caused devastation in the entire region.
Meanwhile, the global financial meltdown continues to plague stocks
as market prices dropped drastically once again today.
China’s government suspended trading early in fears of a sell off.
Hello?
Gloria. Hi.
I was just catching up on where we stand.
I’m really looking forward to helping out with this new property.
Yes, Marty, remember, the showing is on for tomorrow.
And you can still help me out when I need to leave, right?
Yes, of course. I wouldn’t miss it.
There’s going to be a ton of big investors there.
Just be sure you can be there on time.
I have to leave once everything is set up.
And this is really important to me, Marty.
I’m counting on you.
Absolutely,
anything for you.
Talk to you later, bye.
You made sure with Marty that he can cover?
Yes, he’ll be there.
Well, why don’t you come over?
We’re going to start our Memorial Bible reading.
OK.
OK, so we’re starting with Mark 14:1.
Anna?
I thought you had a big day at work.
I did.
Then why are you home so early?
I just— I’m just so ashamed of myself.
Ashamed?
Honey, come over here.
Anna,
what are you talking about?
I saw Mary and Ricky
out in service today.
I couldn’t even acknowledge them.
Mom, I don’t know why I’m doing this anymore.
The people I’m working with,
they’re not who I thought they were.
And this job, it’s not making me happy.
And I know it’s not making Jehovah happy.
Anna, you can’t just quit like this.
I want you to have a comfortable life
so that you don’t need to worry about money.
You have to be successful with a secure job and it will—
it will help you to pioneer.
Mom.
I know you care about me,
but if I keep this job, I know where it will take me.
It’s changed me so much already.
I want to be a success,
but I want to be a success in Jehovah’s eyes.
I had no idea you felt that way.
I am sorry.
Are you sure that’s what you want to do?
Yes.
Anna,
I am so proud of you
because you have the courage to do
what I should have done.
So,
what are we going to do now?
We need to examine our priorities together.
But if we make the changes that we need to,
we might give up this place.
Is that all right with everyone?
Finally. I never liked this place anyway.
Really?
Yeah.
Can we at least keep the new piano?
Only if we do something about your hair first.
Good point.
Can I help you?
Hey, good morning, Sir. How are you?
Good. Thank you.
Good.
My name is Joe, and this morning
we’re leaving this invitation with your neighbors.
This is your copy here.
OK, thank you.
OK.
Director Williams,
this is a nice surprise.
I haven’t seen you since you were overseeing our division.
Donald,
I didn’t know this was your home.
Yeah, but I mean, what brings you here?

en.text: “Always Allow Jehovah to Direct Your Steps”
is the theme Brother Geoffrey Jackson,
a member of the Governing Body, will now share with us.
Well, it’s a real privilege and pleasure for me
to stand before you again.
It just seems like a few days ago when I had the privilege
of giving you the first lecture that I give at Gilead.
And now, here it is, your very special day of graduation.
Before you go on to your assignments after graduation,
we’d like to leave you with a question,
Are you willing
to allow Jehovah to direct your steps?
Now, we all know how you’re going to answer
because we know that you’ve been willing
to allow Jehovah to direct your steps right up to this moment.
That’s why you dedicated yourselves to Jehovah,
why you entered full-time service, special full-time service,
and that’s why you’re here —having attended Gilead.
And that’s why we love you, and we’re proud of you
because you are willing to allow Jehovah to direct your steps.
But, you know, perhaps it seems a little presumptuous on our part
to ask the question about are we willing to allow Jehovah.
Can mere man allow Jehovah to do anything?
Well, the reason behind that question is,
of course, that Jehovah doesn’t force himself on us.
It doesn’t automatically happen
that Jehovah directs our steps.
In fact, something is required of us,
and this, in a sense, allows Jehovah to work with us.
Let’s have a look in our Bibles at an interesting scripture
in the book of Psalms.
It’s Psalm 37,
a section of Scripture that we all use
over and over again in the service.
But this time, we’re going to look at verse 23,
Psalm 37:23:
“Jehovah guides the steps of a man
when He finds pleasure in his way.”
Now, if you were just listening to that
and you didn’t have a printed or electronic copy in front of you,
it would be easy to misunderstand this verse.
Why?
Well, if you hear it read “when He finds pleasure in his way,”
you naturally assume “when [the man] finds pleasure in [Jehovah’s] way.”
But you notice the New World Translation capitalizes the “He”
—“when He finds pleasure in his way.”
So now if we were to substitute the pronouns there,
what does it really say?
“Jehovah guides the steps of a man
when [Jehovah] finds pleasure in [the man’s] way.”
Now, isn’t that an interesting concept?
So for us to have our steps guided by Jehovah,
we have to do things that bring pleasure to Jehovah.
And when Jehovah finds pleasure in our way,
then he directs our steps.
Isn’t that a profound thought?
So in that way, once we do things in accordance with Jehovah’s will,
it’s as if we figuratively allow Jehovah
to direct our steps.
Now, that doesn’t come automatically just because we pray to Jehovah,
“Please, direct my steps.”
Let’s think of two examples from the Scriptures,
two negative examples, that help us in this regard.
First of all, let’s think about Balaam.
Now, remember this is in the 15th century B.C.E.,
when the Israelites were about to go into the Promised Land.
The Moabites were very worried about it.
Balaam was a man who had some connection to the worship of Jehovah.
And now all of a sudden, these messengers come to Balaam,
and they ask him to curse God’s people.
And do you remember what happened? What did Balaam do?
He didn’t automatically answer, did he?
He said: ‘Wait here overnight.
I want to hear from Jehovah.’
And what did Jehovah say to him?
Basically, ‘Don’t go!’
Now, that’s not hard to understand, is it?
‘Don’t go’ is simple;
you don’t need a lawyer to try and work out what that means.
But then what happened?
Well, the pressure intensified, didn’t it?
And more messengers came
—this time, princes and more offers of material gain.
Now, what did Balaam do?
Well, he had clearly heard Jehovah’s direction: ‘Don’t go.’
But what did he do?
Well, his heart was already leaning in a certain direction.
So he was hoping this would change a little.
So he said: ‘Well, let’s just wait and see what Jehovah says.’
Now, this time what did Jehovah say?
‘Go,
but don’t say anything I don’t tell you to say.’
In other words: ‘Only say what I tell you.’
Now, was this because Jehovah was directing Balaam’s steps?
Or was it because he allowed Balaam to go his own way?
Well, we see what happened —three times, resistance.
But then what happened?
Well, notice, if we turn across to Numbers 22,
we hear a very clear statement.
In fact, nearly as clear as the statement, ‘Don’t go.’
Numbers 22:32:
“Then Jehovah’s angel said to him:
“‘Why have you beaten your donkey these three times?
“‘Look! I myself came out to offer resistance,
because your way is in defiance of my will.’”
So there we see the answer, don’t we?
It wasn’t Jehovah directing his steps.
Jehovah was resisting what he was doing.
So, what do we learn from this?
Well, even though Balaam initially
wanted to get Jehovah’s direction,
Jehovah didn’t force himself on Balaam.
And when Balaam was determined to go down a certain course,
yes, Jehovah gave him signals of ‘don’t go’ and again ‘don’t go.’
But Jehovah allowed him to go and, of course,
eventually he ended up dying because of that.
And, of course, many others died because of that as well.
So, what’s the lesson for us?
Well, sometimes we may feel that at a certain point in our life,
we say: “Jehovah, what do you want me to do?
What’s your will?”
And that’s good that we pray to Jehovah that way.
But what do we need to do?
We need to do what Jehovah wants us to do.
Then, when he finds pleasure in what we’re doing,
he directs our step.
So that’s a good lesson, isn’t it?
The second example we want to use is of the unnamed prophet.
Do you remember the one that’s mentioned in 1 Kings chapter 13,
who was instructed to go up to Israel
and to utter a pronouncement there to King Jeroboam?
Now, remember the instructions again that Jehovah gave him:
‘Go up one way; come back the other way.
Don’t eat or drink.’
Now, even when the king said: ‘Come and eat and drink,’
what did he say?
‘Oh, no. I know what Jehovah wants me to do.’
But then what happened?
Although he was doing very well up to that point,
remember the old prophet tricked him by saying:
‘Oh, don’t worry.
An angel spoke to me and said: “It’s OK.”’
What did the unnamed prophet say?
‘Let me check with Jehovah again.
I mean, he did actually tell me.’
No. ‘OK, let’s eat!’
Well, again it resulted in disaster, didn’t it?
What’s the lesson we learned there?
Well, although he started a course
that was allowing Jehovah to direct his steps,
he didn’t continue to follow the direction that Jehovah had given him.
Now, that’s a good lesson for us too, isn’t it?
We may do the same.
There could be friends —could even be people we respect—
who give us advice contrary
to what Jehovah is telling us,
and that could also lead to disaster.
What would have helped in both of those situations?
Well, I’d like to read you a quote from The Watchtower
from back in 1950 before any of you were ever born
and, incidentally, before I was born too.
But I’m sure Brother Herd read it.
Anyway, the quote says:
“It is far better
“to take a few moments for quiet reflection,
“fully considering God’s requirements
“before rushing into an action
that might bring God’s reproof.”
Let me read it again:
“It is far better to take a few moments for quiet reflection,
“fully considering God’s requirements
“before rushing into an action
that might bring God’s reproof.”
So how can we summarize that in a nice little expression?
Well, we could say: “Don’t rush in.
“Pause,
“ponder,
“pray,
“and prove.
Prove to yourself what Jehovah really wants you to do.”
So with that in mind, as you go do your assignments,
you’re going to find all sorts of challenges.
But how can you apply this principle
of don’t rush in,
pause, ponder, pray,
and prove to yourself what Jehovah wants?
Well, let’s consider three different circumstances.
So we always want to allow Jehovah to direct our steps
when we’re excited about something.
We’re excited —we want to get in and do something.
Now let’s take, for example, Jacob.
We all remember, it describes to us in the Scriptures
how he felt when he was told that his son Joseph supposedly had died.
He was grief-stricken,
and for years
he was left with that impression that his son was dead.
Now, can you imagine?
Just try to imagine the joy that he would have felt
when all of a sudden his sons return back from Egypt.
There are wagons —I mean, not just the average wagons—
I’m sure they were pretty fancy wagons.
They’re coming to pick him up.
He finds out Joseph is alive.
Not only that, he’s in Egypt.
He’s got a very high position there.
How do you think—?
Do you think excited is the word? Of course!
He’s extremely excited and overjoyed.
So he left Hebron, went down to Beer-sheba.
But what did he do
before he left the Promised Land to go into Egypt?
Well, let’s have a look in Genesis chapter 46.
Genesis chapter 46
and we’ll read verses 1-4:
“So Israel [Jacob] took all that he had and departed.
When he arrived at Beer-sheba, he offered sacrifices to . . . God.”
You see, he stopped, he paused, he pondered.
Yes, verse 2:
“Then God spoke to Israel in a vision by night and said:
“‘Jacob, Jacob!’ to which he said: ‘Here I am!’
“He said: ‘I am the true God, the God of your father.
“‘Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt,
“‘for there I will make you into a great nation.
“‘I myself will go down with you to Egypt,
“‘and I myself will also bring you back from there,
and Joseph will lay his hand on your eyes.’”
Do we see what happened?
You see, he stopped, he paused, he pondered,
he wanted to prove to himself what Jehovah wanted.
And Jehovah gave him the go-ahead.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Malachi.
The prophet Malachi wrote this book in Jerusalem
after the Jews returned from Babylon.
He proved to be a fearless spokesman for Jehovah.
Malachi completed writing his prophecy
sometime after 443 B.C.E.,
many years after Haggai and Zechariah
wrote their books
but about the same time
Nehemiah wrote his book.
About a century had passed
since the first Jewish exiles
returned to Jerusalem.
The temple had been rebuilt,
and the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s walls
was completed.
But the nation still needed spiritual guidance.
The book of Malachi has four chapters.
In chapters 1 and 2,
Jehovah denounces the priests for their corrupt practices.
Jehovah calls them to account
because they are offering him inferior animals for sacrifice.
The priests have been negligent in teaching the people
who are unjustly divorcing their wives
and marrying new wives from pagan nations,
something that Jehovah hates.
Chapter 3 indicates
there would be a forerunner to the Messiah.
The Messiah, or “messenger of the covenant,”
will come to the temple to cleanse it.
Jesus did this when he threw greedy merchants out of the temple.
Did you know?
Malachi mentions Elijah the prophet.
However, Elijah had been long dead
by the time Malachi wrote his prophecy.
Jesus identified John the Baptizer
as the “Elijah” that Malachi foresaw.
In chapter 4,
Malachi makes a prophetic reference to “the sun of righteousness,”
which highlights Jesus’ role as mankind’s savior.
As you read the book of Malachi,
notice how Jehovah expects us
to give him our best,
how Jehovah hates unjust divorce,
and how “the messenger of the covenant,”
the foretold King of God’s Kingdom,
supports true worship.

cn.text: 犹太人离开巴比伦返回耶路撒冷后
玛拉基在那里写下这本书
玛拉基勇敢地为耶和华发言
玛拉基书在公元前443年后成书
距离哈该书和撒迦利亚书的
成书时间已有多年
但是与尼希米记的成书时间差不多
第一批返乡的犹太人
已回到耶路撒冷将近100年
当时耶路撒冷的圣殿和城墙
已完成多年
但犹太人在崇拜方面
还是需要受到纠正
玛拉基书共有四章
第一和二章
耶和华谴责祭司们的恶行
因为他们将残疾和生病的牲畜
献给上帝做祭物
祭司也没有尽到教导的责任
纵容人民诡诈背信
抛弃妻子，另娶异教女子

你知道吗？

但是当时以利亚早已去世多年
后来，耶稣指出
玛拉基所预告的以利亚
就是施浸者约翰
在第四章，玛拉基预告
正义的太阳必照耀
借此强调耶稣是人类的救世主
你读玛拉基书时，请留意
耶和华希望我们把最好的献给他
上帝憎恨人用诡诈的手段离婚
“立约使者”也就是预言中
上帝王国的君王热心支持正确崇拜
