게리 브로 형제의 아침 숭배 내용을 들어 보시기 바랍니다
“형제 여러분, 나는 하느님의 동정심으로 여러분에게 호소합니다.
여러분의 몸을 거룩하고 하느님께서 받아들이실 만한 산 희생 제물로 바치십시오
그것이 여러분이 이지력으로 드리는 신성한 봉사입니다.”
이지력이라고 했으니 이치적인 사고에는 힘이 있다는 것이죠
힘이 있다는 건 영향을 준다는 말입니다
그래서 어떤 문제를 이치적으로 생각하면 그것이 영향을 미쳐 올바른 결정을 내릴 수 있는 거죠
그런데 바울은 오늘의 성구에서 또 한 가지를 소개하는데
“형제 여러분, 우리 주 예수 그리스도의 임재와
우리가 그분에게 함께 모이게 되는 일에 관해 여러분에게 부탁합니다
영감받은 말이나 전하는 말이나 우리가 보낸 것처럼 보이는 편지로
여러분은 쉽게 이성을 잃고 흔들리거나 놀라지 마십시오.”
여기서 바울은 어떤 문제를 논리적으로 생각해 결론을 내렸는데도
그 뒤에 쉽게 흔들리는 것에 대해 말하고 있습니다
다시 말해, 일단 합리적인 사고를 거쳐 결론을 내렸다면
이것은 바울이 데살로니가 회중에 한 말인데
바울은 그들에게 보낸 첫째 편지에서 여호와의 날이 가깝다고
그 날이 오고 있다고 경고한 적이 있었습니다
그런데 일부 사람들은 그보다 더 앞서 나가
사실, 2절을 보면 마치 바울이 보낸 것처럼 보이는 편지가 있었는데
그 편지에 따르면 여호와의 날이 오고 있는 게 아니라
그래서 일부 사람들은 주의 깊이 생각하지 못한 결과
혼란에 빠져 믿음이 흔들리게 되었던 것 같습니다
여호와의 날이 오기 전에 일어나야 하는 일들을 언급함으로
따라서 우리 역시 쉽게 믿음이 흔들리는 문제에 관해 생각해 볼 필요가 있습니다
튼튼한 믿음을 갖게 되려면 여러 해가 걸리기 때문이죠
사실 믿음이 쉽게 흔들릴 수 있다는 바울의 말은 썩 달가운 이야기가 아닙니다
하지만 우리 중 누구에게나 생길 수 있는 문제죠
요한 6:64을 보면 예수께선 배반자가 누구인지 처음부터 아셨다고 나오는데
불완전성과 죄짓기 쉬운 성향에 굴복하기 시작한 때의 ‘처음부터’”라고 설명합니다
그 과정은 유다가 사도로 임명된 때로부터 1년도 안 걸렸죠
아시다시피 그가 사도로 임명된 건 실수가 아니었습니다
그러니까 그 짧은 기간 동안 유다는 사도에서 배교자로 변질된 겁니다
따라서 이치적으로 생각해서 내린 확실한 결론에 대해
쉽게 믿음이 흔들려선 안 된다는 바울의 조언은 참으로 적절한 것입니다
더 쉽게 흔들릴 수 있는 경우들이 있을 수 있습니다
그 점에 대해 잠시 말씀 드리도록 하죠
스트레스를 받거나, 우울하거나, 걱정이 있을 때, 그럴 수 있습니다
“감정적 스트레스를 많이 받게 되면 판단력이 흐려질 수 있습니다.”
가상의 예지만 있을 수 있는 일이죠
부모와 아주 사이가 좋은 한 형제가 있는데
그러다 보니 개인 연구와 영적인 활동이 느슨해지게 됩니다
그런데 얼마 후 동생이 제명 처분을 받습니다
그러다가 그만 부적절한 영상을 보게 됩니다
본인의 정상적인 튼튼한 감정 기능이 다소 약화되었을 수도 있고,
혹은 현명한 결정을 내리기가 극히 어렵게 되었을지도 모른다.”
또 영적 활동이 느슨해졌다는 걸 처음 감지했을 때
누군가의 도움을 받아 문제의 원인을 파악했다면 좋았을 겁니다
우리가 조심하지 않는다면 믿음이 쉽게 흔들릴 수 있는
어떤 상황이 또 있을 수 있습니까?
배교자들이 증인들을 비방하면서 하는 말들이 있는데
일부 사람들이 그런 내용을 언급하기도 합니다
성경에 근거한 우리 입장은 고백이 없다면
두 명의 증인이 있어야 사법적 조처를 취할 수 있다는 것이죠
그러한 이치적인 생각에는 이런 확실한 근거가 있죠
단 한 명의 증인으로는 유죄 판결을 내릴 수 없습니다
두 증인의 증언이나 세 증인의 증언으로 그 일을 확증해야 합니다.”
증인이 한 명뿐인 경우 사법 위원회를 구성할 수 없습니다
구약에는 간음한 여자는 돌로 쳐서 죽여야 한다는 말도 있죠.
당신들은 그건 안 하면서 두 증인이 있어야 한다는 규정은 왜 지키는 겁니까?”
조심하지 않으면 이런 말을 듣고 우리도 혼란스러울 수 있습니다
예수 그리스도께서 세우신 분명한 그리스도인 마련이 나오는데
“그러나 그가 듣지 않으면, 한두 사람을 더 데리고 가십시오.
그것은 두세 증인의 증언으로 모든 일이 확증되게 하려는 것입니다.”
그러니까 두 증인이 있어야 한다는 원칙은 예수께서 세우신 겁니다
물론 증인이 한 명만 있으면 아무런 조처도 없다는 의미는 아니죠
상황에 따라 조처가 취해질 수도 있겠지만
사법 위원회가 구성되려면 고백이 있거나 두 명의 증인이 있어야 합니다
우리는 이 문제에 관한 성경에 근거한 이런 입장을 결코 바꾸지 않을 것입니다
여호와께선 우리에게 이지력 즉 이치적으로 생각할 수 있는 역량을 주셨습니다
그 역량을 잘 사용해 우리의 믿음이 쉽게 흔들리지 않게 합시다
그러면 우리도 데살로니가 후서 3:5에 언급된 이런 확신을 가질 수 있습니다
하느님에 대한 사랑과 그리스도를 위한 인내에 이르게 해 주시기를 바랍니다.”
우리는 사법 문제와 같은 어려운 상황이 생긴다 하더라도
확고한 태도로 성경을 통해 이해한 진리를 따릅니다
우리는 정확한 지식을 얻고 싶기 때문에
그분의 완전한 특성에 대해 더 배우려고 합니다
그분에 관해 얼마나 많은 걸 배울 수 있는지 한번 생각해 보십시오
이달 뮤직 비디오의 제목은 “하느님의 놀라운 일들”입니다
아침 햇살 저 멀리서 밝아져 오네
그들이 외치는 말 온 세상 가득해
우린 하느님 사랑을 더 깊이 알게 되네
시간을 내서 아름다운 창조물에 대해 생각해 보면
훨씬 뛰어난 지성을 가진 분이 계시다는 게 분명해지죠
벌써 이달 방송을 마칠 시간이 다 되었네요
맨츠 형제, 이달 방송에 함께해 주셔서 대단히 고맙습니다
이제 마치기 전에 페루의 쿠스코 시로 가 보겠는데요
이곳에는 우리의 현지 번역 사무실 즉 RTO가 있습니다
쿠스코 시는 여행자들이 마추픽추로 갈 때 잠시 들러가는 곳입니다
마추픽추는 고대 잉카 제국의 역사적 성지인데
거대한 돌들을 어찌나 정밀하게 잘라 만들었는지
돌들 사이에 종이 한 장 들어갈 틈도 없는 곳이 많습니다
안데스 산맥에서 기르는 라마도 볼 수 있습니다
오늘날 수백만 명의 페루인들도 이 언어를 사용하고 있죠
하지만 번역 일이 늘어감에 따라 더 많은 공간이 필요하게 되었습니다
그래서 2016년에 새로운 현지 번역 사무실이 봉헌되었죠
이러한 번역 작업은 참으로 큰 축복을 가져왔습니다
2007년에 「성서의 가르침」 책이 케추아어로 발행된 이후로 작년까지
그 가운데는 JW 방송 월간 프로그램과
페루에는 케추아어를 사용하는 지역이 여러 곳 있는데
지역마다 조금씩 다른 방언과 표현들을 사용합니다
그래서 각 번역 팀에 이런 지역들을 대표하는 사람들을 포함시켜서
모든 케추아어 사용자들이 두루 이해할 수 있게
약 40명의 형제 자매가 이 현지 번역 사무실에서 일하고 있으며
우리는 쿠스코에 있는 형제 자매들을 깊이 사랑합니다
그들도 여러분을 깊이 사랑하며 그 마음을 전하고 싶어하죠
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다

en.text: Greetings!
We’re so happy you could join us for this broadcast.
And I’m very happy because my cohost this month
is a good friend of mine and a fellow worker, Brother Jim Mantz.
Now, Jim and I work together in the Writing Department,
and Jim helps the Writing Department —Jim and his team.
They help the Writing Department
to keep track of all the projects that we have to work on.
And do you have any idea how many that is?
Two hundred and forty-one at any given time.
And Jim does a lot of other things as well.
Well, Jim, we’ve got another project on hand this month,
and that’s to get this broadcast under way.
So why don’t you tell the folks at home just what they have to look forward to?
Well, David, this month we’ll get acquainted with a family
that raised their children to put Jehovah first in their lives.
Let’s look for points we can apply in our families.
Later, our music video will emphasize the need
to take the time to marvel at Jehovah’s creation.
And we’ll visit the Writing Research Department.
The brothers and sisters there
help us to ensure that all our articles
and videos are accurate.
You’re going to enjoy this program,
and this is the November 2017 program
of JW Broadcasting!
This month I’d like to talk about the efforts
Jehovah’s organization is making
to produce literature, publications,
articles that are as accurate as possible.
We’re going to talk about accuracy —accuracy of statement.
Now, first, what’s the responsibility of the writer of the article?
When a writer submits an article for publication,
he is expected to supply references from reputable sources
to back up the facts that he’s included in his article.
And our Research Department will use those references
to check the accuracy of everything.
Reliable, respected sources.
What do we mean by a reliable source?
Well, first of all, we go with encyclopedias,
books, magazines, and then newspapers
—basically in that order.
We prefer encyclopedias over books,
books over magazines,
and magazines over newspapers
—generally because newspaper editors have a hard time checking their facts.
They have a very limited time in which to check their facts.
Even encyclopedias and books get updated,
so we have to go with the latest edition of those.
We have to make sure that our sources are reliable.
Now, when a writer quotes an expert,
our researchers will ask: “Who’s this expert?
“What’s his reputation?
“Is he working for a particular organization?
“Does this organization have an agenda?
Is it a special-interest group?”
If we find that the goals of the organization are questionable,
we won’t use the quote —even if it’s a really good quote.
Now, suppose that a writer wants to quote something from a book.
In the reference material,
he’ll supply a photocopy of the quote in the book,
but very often he’ll give us two or three pages before the quote
and two or three pages after as well.
And that way, our researchers can examine the quote
in context to make sure that what we’re saying in print
is really what the author of the quote had in mind.
For example, an evolutionist might make a statement
which on the surface
appears to confirm his support of creation.
Or perhaps an atheist will make a statement
that seems to indicate that he believes in God.
But when you examine the quote in context,
you realize that that isn’t what the author had in mind at all.
We would never deliberately distort a quotation.
We try very hard to use all of our quotations in context.
Now, it’s important to keep up with the very latest research.
Something that was stated years ago as a fact may have been disproved.
And the reason why is obvious.
Someone may spend his entire life
researching a very limited point in history
—a very small point in history—
and, of course, if he spends so much time researching,
he’s going to uncover things.
And so it’s not surprising that from time to time
we have to adjust our view of some historical points.
We have to check, check, check.
And later on in this discussion, we’re going to consider some examples of it.
It’ll be fun; you’ll love it!
Now, someone might ask, ‘Why is it necessary to be so picky,
to be so fussy, about accuracy?’
And in answer, I’d like to give an experience
that I heard about a few years ago.
In Northern Europe, there was a man
who accepted a Bible study from Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And when he was asked
what motivated him to want to study, he said:
“I read an article in your Awake! magazine on trees.
“Now, I happen to be a bit of an expert on trees.
“And after I read the article, I said to myself:
“‘That article was so well-documented.
“‘It was so precise.
“‘Any organization that is that careful when writing about trees
is going to be just as careful when teaching me the Bible.’”
And on that basis, he accepted a Bible study.
Now, an area where great care needs to be taken
is when we’re quoting statistics.
A newspaper may report on a disaster in a certain country
and say that 10,000 people were killed in the disaster.
Immediately, our researchers are going to ask,
“Where did they get that statistic?”
They might phone the newspaper and ask for the source.
And if the reporter can’t confirm the statistic,
our researchers will go to another source
—a more official source— to get the correct statistic.
Care is also taken when quoting personalities of the past.
Now, suppose we want to quote something that Napoleon Bonaparte said
—the French general.
Well, being French, Napoleon spoke French.
So if we’re quoting it in English,
that means that somebody translated the quote from French into English.
But did they translate the quote correctly?
Our researchers will probably go to the target language
and research the quote in French or in another language.
And more often than not, they find that what is presented in English
doesn’t accurately represent what the individual said at all.
Now, as we age, our memory can play tricks on us.
And our researchers are aware of that.
Suppose that an elderly brother writes in his life story
that he was baptized at a circuit assembly on a certain date.
Our researchers may look at the date.
They may check the date,
and suppose they find that the date the brother gave fell on a Tuesday.
Now, what are the chances that there was a circuit assembly on a Tuesday?
There may have been, but they’re going to check.
Is the brother’s memory failing him?
If they can’t confirm the date,
they may ask someone to help the brother
to remember the date more correctly, more accurately.
Perhaps someone was baptized at the same circuit assembly as he was,
and perhaps that person has an accurate note of the date.
Our translators also go to great lengths
to present accurate information to the brothers and sisters.
Some time ago, the Awake! magazine published an article
on a very rare species of butterfly.
Now, with all animals and insects,
we provide our translators
with the Latin name of the animal or the insect.
And so our translators had the Latin name.
But in one large country,
they were unable to find the name in the vernacular.
So, what did they do?
They phoned the country’s leading university,
and they were transferred to the Biology Department,
and there an expert gave them
the name in the vernacular of that particular butterfly.
But then he said: “Why is it that you’re worrying so much
“about the correct name of this butterfly?
“If you got it wrong, there are only two of us
in the whole country who would’ve known the difference.”
Well, that opened the way to give a witness to this expert.
Well, now, how well would you do
in spotting a statement that is slightly off
and making it more accurate?
Would you like to find out?
Of course you would! It’ll be fun.
So let’s take a quiz that I’ll call
You Be the Editor.
We’re going to put a number of statements on the screen,
and there’s a problem with each one of them.
Now your job is to figure out what’s wrong,
why it is wrong, and then suggest how to fix it.
It’s going to be fun.
Here’s the first statement:
“According to the Smithsonian Knowledge Encyclopedia,
“the Egyptian Sphinx
was constructed around 2550 B.C.E.”
“The Egyptian Sphinx
was constructed around 2550 B.C.E.”
Well, the problem
is with the date 2550 B.C.E.
The global Flood occurred
about 200 years after that date.
So, what are the chances that the Sphinx survived the Flood?
Unless, of course, you think that’s how the Sphinx lost his nose.
Now, these dates are good for you school children
to keep in mind when you’re writing reports.
Sometimes you copy something from an encyclopedia,
and it gives a certain date.
But think about the date of the Flood, 2370 B.C.E.,
so that what you put in your report is as accurate as possible.
Now let’s go on to the next one:
“In 29 C.E.,
“Jesus was baptized by a close relative,
John the Baptizer.”
Well, 29 C.E., that looks right.
And we know that Jesus
was baptized by John; that’s right.
So the problem must be
“close relative,” and it is.
Now, both of Jesus’ parents
were of the tribe of Judah, and their parents were of the tribe of Judah.
But, what about John’s parents, Zechariah and Elizabeth?
They were both of the tribe of Levi.
So Elizabeth and Mary couldn’t have been sisters.
Could they have been cousins?
Maybe.
We can’t even confirm that.
And if they were, that would make Jesus and John second cousins.
Well, is a second cousin a “close relative”?
Some would say yes; some would say no.
So it’s safer just to say,
“In 29 C.E., Jesus was baptized by a relative,
John the Baptizer.”
Here’s one.
Let’s see if you can spot the error in this one:
“While most of the early Christians
“were held in little esteem in the community,
“a few enjoyed an elevated social status.
For example, Luke was a respected physician.”
Well, the word we need
to look at is “respected.”
We respect our doctors today,
and our doctors have a very, very fine education.
But was that the case in the first century?
A reference work says this about first-century physicians:
“Many doctors were freed Greek slaves,
“hence the social standing of doctors was quite low.
“Because recovery rates were so low,
many people were skeptical or even scornful of doctors.”
Note this statement from the first century:
“Until recently, Diaulus was a doctor;
“now he is an undertaker.
“He is still doing as an undertaker,
what he used to do as a doctor.”
Not very flattering, is it?
Well, in this case, we’d probably have to use a different example.
Here’s one:
“the Roman Emperor Constantine
“established Christianity
“as the official religion
of the Roman Empire.”
Well, 325 C.E., that looks right.
And Constantine, that looks right.
But look at the word “official”
—“official religion.”
Constantine never established Christianity
as the official religion of the Roman Empire.

our Scriptural position on that subject.
Jehovah has given us the ability to reason things out, to think it through.
So let’s do our part
and not allow our faith to be quickly shaken.
Then we can have the confidence that Paul spoke of
at 2 Thessalonians 3:5 when he said:
“May the Lord continue to guide your hearts successfully
to the love of God and to the endurance for the Christ.”
Even when difficult circumstances arise,
such as judicial matters,
we cling to our accurate understanding of the Bible.
Yes, Jehovah is the God of truth.
And our desire for accurate knowledge
motivates us to draw ever closer to Jehovah
and to learn more about his perfect qualities.
Just think of everything we can learn about him
when we take the time to study his works of creation.
Psalm 104:24 reads:
“How many your works are, O Jehovah!
“You have made all of them in wisdom.
The earth is full of what you have made.”
In harmony with that, our music video for this month
is entitled Inspired by Your Wonders.
I hear the birds singing out to the sunrise.
I see the stars fading away in the morning light.
Golden sun shines on down through the treetops,
Where there is a summer breeze that whispers so soft.
And I sing, “O Jah, Jehovah my God,
The work of your hands fills us with awe.”
I stare at the stars, Wondering how you care who we are.
I see your wonders, and I sing to you.
I see your wonders, and I sing to you.
I sing to you.
These wondrous, moving, breathing creations—
Oh, in the night, in the day— can you hear what they say?
From mountaintops to the bottoms of oceans,
Let ev’ry living thing sing out to your praise.
And I sing, “O Jah, Jehovah my God,
The work of your hands fills us with awe.”
I stare at the stars, Wondering how you care who we are.
I see your wonders, and I sing to you.
I see your wonders, and I sing to you.
I sing to you.
Looking past what we can see with our eyes,
We will come to know more about the One who gave us life.
And I sing, “O Jah, Jehovah my God,
The work of your hands fills us with awe.”
I stare at the stars, Wondering how you care who we are.
I see your wonders, and I sing to you.
I see your wonders, and I sing to you.
I see your wonders, and I—I sing to you.
I see your wonders, and I—I sing to you.
I see your wonders, and I—I sing to you.
I sing to you.
When we take time to reflect on the beauties of creation,
it becomes clear that there is a higher intelligence
who made all these things.
Well, David, it’s hard to imagine
that we’ve already come to the end of another monthly broadcast.
And, Jim, I want to thank you very much for all your help with this program.
I really, really appreciate it.
Now, before we conclude,
we’d like to visit the city of Cuzco in Peru,
where we have a Remote Translation Office, or RTO.
The city of Cuzco is a stopover for travelers to Machu Picchu,
a historic sanctuary of the former Inca Empire,
located high up in the mountains.
Machu Picchu is an architectural marvel.
The design is earthquake resistant.
Giant stones were cut so precisely
that in many places a piece of paper
cannot fit in between them.
At such high altitudes, you can also see llamas,
which are raised in the Andes Mountains.
The Inca people spoke Quechua,
a language that is spoken
by millions of Peruvians today.
There has been a translation office in Cuzco
since 2004,
but as the work grew,
so did the need for more office space.
So in 2016, a new RTO was dedicated.
The blessings of the translation work have been evident.
Since the Bible Teach book was released in Quechua in 2007,
the number of publishers increased
from about 700
to nearly 1,700 last year.
In addition to The Watchtower
and the Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook,
videos are translated at this office,
ranging from JW Broadcasting monthly programs
to episodes of Become Jehovah’s Friend.
There are several regions in Peru where Quechua is spoken,
all with slightly different dialects and expressions.
Hence, each translation team
has representatives from these areas
in order to ensure that the translation
is universally understood
among Quechua speakers.
Approximately 40 brothers and sisters work at the RTO,
of which 15 are full-time.
In the Cuzco area,
there are 28 congregations and 38 groups,
with about 2,000 publishers.
We love our brothers and sisters in Cuzco very much indeed.
And they want you to know
how much they love you.
Well, until next time,
this is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Jonah.
Jehovah assigned the prophet Jonah
to deliver a warning
to the Assyrian city of Nineveh.
Jonah prophesied
sometime during the reign
of Israel’s King Jeroboam II.
Jonah wrote the book bearing his name
about 844 B.C.E.
This was about 100 years
before Assyria took Israel into exile
and some 200 years
before Nahum foretold the destruction
of the Assyrian city of Nineveh.
Jonah lived about the time of Amos,
who also prophesied
in the northern kingdom of Israel,
and Joel, who prophesied in Judah.
The book of Jonah has four chapters.
In chapters 1 and 2,
we learn of Jonah receiving an assignment from Jehovah
to go to Nineveh.
Overwhelmed, Jonah evades the assignment
by boarding a ship headed for Tarshish.
Jehovah causes a terrible storm to come up at sea.
Jonah knows that he is responsible for the storm
and tells the sailors to throw him overboard.
When they do, the storm abates.
Jehovah sends a huge fish to swallow Jonah.
From inside the fish’s belly,
Jonah prays to Jehovah,
and his prayer is heard.
Jehovah then commands the fish,
and it vomits Jonah out onto dry land.
Did you know?
Jesus foretold that he would die
and be resurrected on the third day.
He called this “the sign of Jonah the prophet,”
alluding to Jonah’s deliverance from the huge fish.
Chapter 3 describes
how Jonah carries out his assignment.
He preaches the message that Nineveh will soon be overthrown.
To Jonah’s surprise, however,
the Ninevites repent,
and Jehovah mercifully spares them.
Chapter 4 reveals
that instead of rejoicing over the repentance of the Ninevites,
Jonah becomes angry.
He sets up a shelter outside the city to see what will happen.
Jehovah uses a bottle-gourd plant and a worm
to teach Jonah a valuable lesson in loyal love and mercy.
As you read the book of Jonah,
note how Jonah accepted correction
and fulfilled his assignment,
how Jehovah displayed loyal love and mercy
toward the repentant Ninevites,
and how Jesus used Jonah’s experience
to foretell his own death and resurrection,
which opens the way to everlasting life
under God’s Kingdom.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Obadiah.
Obadiah was a prophet of Jehovah.
He recorded his prophecy about 607 B.C.E.,
after the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem.
Obadiah was a contemporary
of Jeremiah, Daniel, and Ezekiel.
The book of Obadiah is the shortest book in the Hebrew Scriptures.
It has just one chapter.
Obadiah conveys a judgment message
against the nation of Edom.
During the destruction of Jerusalem by the Babylonians,
the Edomites rejoice at Israel’s suffering.
Edomites capture fleeing Israelites,
they hand them over to the Babylonians,
and share in taking spoil from the conquered Jews.
Did you know?
The Edomites were related to the Israelites.
They were descendants
of Jacob’s twin brother, Esau.
He was given the name Edom,
meaning “red,”
after he sold his birthright
for some red lentil stew.
Obadiah prophesies
that the nation of Edom will be plundered
at the hands of her former allies.
This prophecy begins to be fulfilled
when the Babylonians conquer Edom.
In time, Edom ceases to exist.
In the closing verses,
Jehovah promises to restore His people as a unified nation
and reestablish true worship in Jerusalem.
The book concludes with the statement:
“The kingship will become Jehovah’s,”
indicating that Jehovah’s kingship will stand vindicated forever.
As you read Obadiah,
note how Jehovah is aware
of the persecution his people suffer,
how Jehovah gives his people hope
in times of distress,
and how Jehovah’s lasting kingship
will stand vindicated forever.

en.text: Just after the Supreme Court decision
banning our activity in Russia
that was given in April,
the Finland Branch Committee wrote to the Teaching Committee
and right away requested permission to arrange a convention
for about 4,000 of our dear brothers from Russia.
Well, now, quite coincidentally or perhaps not,
back in January, I was feeling a little bit tired,
and I have some good friends in Finland,
and so we arranged to go to a convention together
in the month of June —that was all approved back in January.
Well, by coincidence —can you imagine?—it turned out to be
the same weekend that this Russian convention
was being planned for Finland.
And so the Teaching Committee asked me if I’d be willing
to serve this Russian convention instead of the Finnish one.
And, of course, I was delighted.
Beds were needed for all of these 4,000 brothers.
Well—can you imagine?—in just a short time,
4,373 beds were offered.
In many cases, the brothers had no place to house visitors, but what did they do?
They called the branch and said: “We’ll pay for a hotel room.
“We don’t care who it’s for;
put whoever you want there, but we want to pay the cost.”
So everyone was able to be accommodated.
When the brothers arrived in Finland,
some had come from as far away as Vladivostok,
traveling some 6,000 miles (9,600 km),
if you can imagine, to attend this convention.
The brothers were at the train stations;
they were at the airport to welcome all the guests.
Now, when the first brothers and sisters
arrived at the convention venue,
they asked, “Well, where is the Russian section?”
since they believed that this was a Finnish convention
with Russian sessions.
Well, when they were told that this convention
had been organized just for them, they immediately began to cry.
Can you imagine the joy that the brothers had
when they were able to sing out with full voice?
The singing was so, so moving.
Well, the peak attendance
of the convention was 5,137,
and 33 were baptized.
Well, during the convention,
the Finland Branch Committee arranged for the delegates to be able to tour Bethel.
And to allow as many as possible to come through,
Bethel was kept open until 8:00 p.m.
on Thursday, Friday, and Monday,
and also on Sunday evening
from 6:00 p.m. until 8:00 p.m.
And can you imagine?
During the day, the kitchen arranged to feed
all of the brothers and sisters who came through in the dining room.
The love that was witnessed was amazing.
And although it’s perhaps not their culture,
do you know that the Finnish brothers hugged
every single brother and sister that came through.
Well, when it was time to say good-bye,
the bond of love that had been established between the Finnish
and the Russian brothers was just wonderful to see.
And although we all thought we would be crying
to see them go back to Russia and the challenges there,
you know, we just couldn’t cry because the brothers
were too happy about the convention.
And there was no one saying, “Poor me.”
They all went back with just a joyful spirit,
and it moved us.
Well, just a few weeks later,
we had to return to Russia again for the appeal hearing at the Supreme Court.
Most of you are aware, of course,
that an international delegation of 18 brothers
were present in the courtroom for the hearing,
but perhaps this last part of the story you haven’t heard.
World headquarters Legal Department had explained to us
that if the decision was negative,
we would have to leave the country of Russia that same night.
Well, of course, we didn’t know if the hearing
would be just that one day or if it would stretch on for other days.
So our only choice was to take all of our things with us to the court,
and if the decision came,
we would have to make immediate plans to leave Russia.
Well, sure enough, at 7:00 p.m. the negative decision was announced.
We had to leave Russia,
but the problem was that none of us had tickets.
So, what did we do?
Well, we told the brothers just get in the vehicles and head for the airport
while we were communicating with the world headquarters Travel Desk.
Well, thanks to the wonderful and very hard work
of those wonderful brothers and sisters that work with the Travel Desk,
about halfway to the airport,
I began to receive the tickets for all 18 brothers via e-mail.
By Jehovah’s undeserved kindness,
all 18 brothers were able to get out on the same flight
—can you imagine?— the last flight out of Moscow.
And here we are just before 1:00 a.m.
when we arrived in Riga, Latvia.
We truly felt as though we had been picked up by Jehovah
and safely carried out of Russia.
Well, all of the brothers and sisters that I met along the way on these trips
wanted to send their warm Christian love and greetings to all of you
and let you know that just as you are praying for them,
they’re also praying for you.

en.text: Nearly all religions teach
that part of a person survives death.
But what does the Bible teach?
God created the first man, Adam,
from the dust.
He had the opportunity to live forever.
But when he deliberately disobeyed God,
he was told that he would return to the dust
—ceasing to exist.
What about others who died after Adam?
When Jesus was told that his friend Lazarus died,
Jesus did not say that Lazarus had gone to heaven.
Rather, he said:
“Our friend has fallen asleep.”
What did he mean?
Just as someone in a deep sleep
is inactive and unaware of his surroundings,
the dead are not conscious of anything at all.
Further, just as a person can be awakened from a deep sleep,
the Bible shows that it is possible to be awakened from death.
Jesus did just that for his friend Lazarus.
Lazarus had been dead for four days.
If some part of Lazarus
had survived his death and gone to heaven,
would Jesus take him out of heaven
and force him to live on earth again?
No.
Lazarus was asleep in the grave.
Jesus gave him back his life
and reunited him with his family.
The Bible promises a time
when many people will be resurrected from the dead,
just as Lazarus was.
Jesus spoke of this wonderful hope when he said:
“The one who exercises faith in me,
even though he dies, will come to life.”
What is the resurrection?
How can you cope with the pain of grief?
To learn more about what the Bible says
on this and many other topics,
go to jw.org.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Amos.
Amos, the prophet who wrote the book bearing his name,
describes himself as having been a herdsman
and one who took care of sycamore figs.
Amos came from the Judean town of Tekoa,
located south of Jerusalem.
Jehovah sent Amos as a prophet
primarily to the northern kingdom of Israel.
Amos prophesied sometime within the period
from 829 to 804 B.C.E.,
during the reign of King Jeroboam II.
Amos recorded his prophecy
by about 804 B.C.E.
after he returned to Judah.
He was a contemporary of the prophets Jonah,
Joel, and Hosea.
The book of Amos has nine chapters.
Chapter 1 contains judgment messages
against a number of surrounding nations.
Chapter 2 records pronouncements against Moab, Judah,
and the northern ten-tribe kingdom of Israel.
Chapters 3 to 6
contain a message of judgment against Israel
because of the nation’s false religious practices
and stubborn refusal to accept discipline.
Israel has adopted a greedy, materialistic lifestyle.
Luxury-loving wives pressure their husbands
to defraud the poor and lowly.
Chapters 7 and 8
present a series of impressive visions.
Amos sees an unstoppable locust swarm
and then a destructive fire.
Next, a plumb line illustrates
how far Israel has deviated from Jehovah’s requirements.
Finally, a basket of summer fruit signifies that Israel’s end is near.
Did you know?
During a meeting of the first-century governing body,
James, Jesus’ half brother,
quoted from the book of Amos
to show that Jehovah would gather Kingdom heirs
from both Jews and Gentiles.
Chapter 9
includes Jehovah’s promise to “raise up the booth of David,”
referring to the royal line leading to the Messianic Kingdom.
As you read the book of Amos,
note how Jehovah uses humble people to do important work,
how those who put faith in material things and ignore God
will not prosper,
and how Jehovah foretells
the establishment of the Messianic Kingdom.

en.text: There were a few factors
that created the need at Bethel
for a more structured training program.
One of those factors included the regular changeover in personnel.
The brothers have to be more versatile
in their assignments.
They may have to do tasks they
previously weren’t trained on.
Printing equipment became more technologically advanced;
our building systems became more complicated;
computer systems were now starting
to be used to control virtually everything.
Well, I feel like Bethel has definitely always been good about training,
but especially now.
I think everyone sees the need to continue investing
in the brothers and sisters that are currently at Bethel.
I don’t think it’s possible for someone
to know less about the trades
than I did when I started.
I remember my first reaction
when I was invited to help
in electrical was fear.
So when I received my assignment,
I found out that it involved
running the heavy equipment.
So I called my parents.
I was really excited about it.
I said, “Mom and Dad, guess what I get to do?”
And Dad said, “OK, Son.
Well, did you tell them that you don’t know how to drive?”
It was decided to pull a group
of highly experienced, highly skilled brothers
to concentrate on developing and teaching
repeatable, consistent classes
that could bring people’s skill levels up to what was needed.
We teach well over 100 different classes
in 12 major categories.
Here at Bethel, I’ve probably been
a part of over 30 different classes,
so it’s been a variety, depending on
the needs at the time of the assignment.
I would estimate that I’ve taken about 15
or 20 different courses from safety and training
over the course of my 13 years in learning a trade.
I’ve become certified
in at least these seven different licensed requirements.
We teach people technical skills,
but that’s not the sole purpose
of the training.
If you aren’t skilled in safety,
you can’t be skilled in your trade and vice versa.
The objective in all of our safety courses
is to get them to view safety the same way Jehovah views it
—as a reflection of their spirituality.
So training in safety is essential.
So our goal is to take them
into the classroom
and give them some time
to consider the theoretical.
And then we take them out
where there is a lab set up, and we have them do some tests on it.
Typically, they will tell us
that they’ve been able to learn more in a week
than what they have learned in a year of trade school.
We’ve done over 60,000 instances of training.
And so now receiving this training,
it provides an area or an aspect
in which I can give my 100 percent to Jehovah.
You see it in their eyes.
They’re just so happy
that they now have maybe a new skill
or a new understanding that they can use to benefit Jehovah.
I love the fact that I came into Bethel with virtually no experience.
And not only did I receive a trade that I could use
to carry out a work that glorifies Jehovah
but I was trained well enough that I can share that with others,
and they can be trained too.
Helping someone else to go from that feeling
of not knowing anything to feeling productive
and feeling like they’re contributing is a real joy for me.
And they can take what they learn
wherever they go.
The confidence that people leave with once they’ve received
that investment —it’s confidence that they can carry out
whatever assignment Jehovah has given them,
and the confidence that Jehovah is going to train them
for whatever is being asked of them.
I think if younger brothers and sisters
are trying to learn a skill so that they can come to Bethel,
that’s commendable, but more important is spirituality.
Let Jehovah “finish your training.”
In regard to training, we’re really only getting started.
The training that we are getting in this system of things by Jehovah,
and especially related to safety,
is absolutely going to be vital in the new world.
I can imagine the idea
of being able to use some of the things I’ve learned
to figure out how
we can use the natural resources in a way without using them up.
We know that we serve a God who is known as the “Grand Instructor.”
So the things that we’re teaching and training right now,
it can only expand in the future.
And as long as you let him train you, you’re going to be all right.

en.text: A visit to the city of Salvador in Brazil
is an amazing experience.
The beaches and the city’s natural beauty
are appreciated by the almost three million people
that live here today.
The people of the city of Salvador
are known for their friendly smile,
hospitality, and united spirit.
But something else is remarkable in this city.
After serving in many parts of Brazil,
I noted a big difference
when I came to Salvador.
The people here have a strong inclination
toward spiritual things.
The city of Salvador alone has just over 2,900,000 inhabitants,
around 36,800 publishers,
and almost 41,400 Bible studies
—divided into 22 circuits
and 351 congregations.
This means that there is about 1 publisher
for every 78 inhabitants.
When we find someone who’s interested,
they have either studied in the past,
their parents are Witnesses,
they already study the Bible, or they want to study.
Such growth creates new difficulties and challenges for Jehovah’s people.
Where will all these interested people meet to serve Jehovah?
There in Salvador,
many brothers and sisters are concentrated
in a very small area.
We had a hard time finding properties.
Besides that, the city is very hilly.
It’s almost impossible to find level properties.
And then there’s the city’s zoning ordinance.
It’s very restrictive.
So finding a suitable property was a real challenge.
But then we came across this one.
We thought, ‘Why not build there?’
That’s why these complexes are needed.
Like this one in Pituba,
which has six Kingdom Halls on one property
for 15 congregations.
There are about 20 of these complexes.
Some have four Kingdom Halls,
others have three, or two,
according to the needs locally.
This is not a standard Kingdom Hall.
We usually don’t approve or recommend
a building this size due to the complexity
in planning the project and even in using the building.
There will be high traffic of both people and vehicles every day
for meetings throughout the week.
But the branch made an exception in this case
due to the large concentration of publishers in the area.
That’s why this six-auditorium complex was built.
It has three double Kingdom Halls with about 200 seats
in each auditorium.
One complex I visit has two Kingdom Halls
—six congregations with about 750 publishers.
That creates another challenge.
When I meet a brother,
it’s hard to know what congregation he belongs to,
since everybody lives so close to each other.
For many publishers, this was no more than just a dream:
‘A well-structured Kingdom Hall that’s comfortable and well-ventilated
—we can’t afford that.’
One brother even said, “It won’t happen in my lifetime.”
The hall is so big.
It has many pretty things.
I thank Jehovah so much for having used us
to build such a beautiful place for his worship,
and really, all credit goes to him.
I’m so grateful to him,
and I hope to praise him even more in this Kingdom Hall
that he’s prepared for us.
It’s like a dream come true.
And now we have a suitable place where we can worship Jehovah.
Thank you.
I don’t deserve something this wonderful.
Thank you so much.
In Salvador
and in many other regions of the earth,
we clearly see the prophecy
of Isaiah 54:2 being fulfilled
by means of the construction of Kingdom Halls.
The natural beauty of Salvador itself moves us
to praise the One who created it all.
But seeing how Jehovah is speeding things up
and caring for his servants’ needs in this crowded city
—now that’s something really special.

cn.text: 巴西的萨尔瓦多是一座非常美丽的城市
大约有三百万人口
迷人的海滩和其他优美的风光
让人流连忘返
这里的人都很热情开朗
慷慨好客  也很团结
不过  这座城市还有另一个特点
我在巴西的很多地方都服务过
来到萨尔瓦多时我发现
这里的人很想认识上帝
他们对圣经真理也很感兴趣
萨尔瓦多的人口超过了290万
有3万6800位传道员
主持了大约4万1400个圣经课程
这里一共有22个分区
351群会众
也就是说
每78个人里就有一个
是耶和华见证人
对圣经感兴趣的人当中
有些人的父母就是耶和华见证人
有的人以前跟我们讨论过圣经
有的是正在学习圣经的
还有的是想要学习的
不过  传道工作的迅速发展
也给我们带来了新的挑战
这些感兴趣的人
该在哪里聚集起来崇拜上帝呢？
在萨尔瓦多
即使在一个很小的地区
都住着很多弟兄姐妹
另外
要找到合适的地点建造聚会所并不容易
这个城市坡路很多
很难找到平坦的地方
再加上这里的建筑法规比较严格
所以想找到合适的场地
实在是难上加难
后来我们找到了这个地方
心想  就在这里建造吧！
所以我们真的需要聚会场地
在萨尔瓦多的皮图巴
我们在一块地上建造了6个聚会所
供15群会众使用
当然  每个地方的需要都不一样
有的在一块地上建造4个
有的建造3个  有的只建了2个
像这样的场地大约有20处
当然
这个聚会所和一般的聚会所很不一样
修建这么大的聚会所
设计很复杂
使用起来也不太方便
另外  在每周举行聚会的时段
也会造成人流量  车流量过大
所以我们通常不推荐这样的设计
但是分部也考虑到
这个地区的传道员特别密集
所以破例批准我们
可以建造3个王国聚会所
每个分为2层
每一层放200把椅子
这样  我们就有了6个聚会场地
我探访过一个地方
那里有两个王国聚会所
供6群会众  750位传道员使用
这也造成另一个问题
要是你遇到一位弟兄
你很难记得他到底属于哪一群会众
我们做梦都没想到
会有这么美观  舒服
通风又好的聚会所
我们根本负担不起这样的聚会所
有个弟兄甚至说
这辈子是等不到这样的事了
这个聚会所很大  很漂亮
真的很感谢耶和华
用我们来建造这么漂亮的聚会所
这都是他的功劳
耶和华为我们准备了这么漂亮的聚会所
我真的很感动
很想在这里赞美他
梦想终于成真了
现在  我们终于有合适的地方
可以崇拜耶和华了！
谢谢你  这个聚会所简直太棒了！
谢谢你！
在萨尔瓦多和世界的其他地方
王国聚会所的建造工作发展非常迅速
这也让我们清楚地看到
以赛亚书54:2的预言真的应验了
萨尔瓦多的自然风光
也让我们不禁赞美宇宙的造物主
在这个拥挤的城市里
看到耶和华亲自照顾他仆人的需要
看到他正加速成就的这一切
简直是个奇迹！

title: 윌리엄 맬렌폰트: 여러분의 달란트를 지혜롭게 사용하십시오 (마태 25:30)

en.text: In the printed comments on today’s text,
a reference is made to Matthew 25
and Luke 19.
In Matthew 25,
we have the illustration of the talents
—three slaves who received talents.
One slave receives five, another two,
and a third slave receives one talent.
And in Luke 19, the illustration is about ten slaves
with each slave receiving one mina.
These were all sums of money, you could say, talents or the minas.
Both illustrations were given some days before Jesus died,
and they were given in different places.
The illustration about the minas was given in Jericho.
The illustration about the talents that Jesus gave to his apostles
was on the Mount of Olives.
But there’s a key point in each illustration that we’ll focus on:
The slave in each account
who did nothing with his talent or his mina
is described as “wicked.”
That’s a powerful denunciation for someone to be called “wicked,”
particularly by the Master.
But to see how powerful it is,
at Matthew 6:13,
Jesus refers to Satan as “the wicked one.”
And Proverbs 10:7 says:
“The name of the wicked will rot.”
So that is a very strong term to apply to any human.
But why?
Why are these two slaves described as “wicked”?
Jesus didn’t say they broke any of the Ten Commandments.
No, but they did something that was extremely serious:
They failed to do something
with the talents or the minas that they were given;
they were guilty of sins of omission.
In Jesus’ parable, just to give you an example,
of the sheep and the goats at Matthew 25:41-46,
you remember in the account how the goats are condemned
to “everlasting cutting-off”
—not for doing something bad,
but because the scripture says that they didn’t help Christ’s brothers.
Again, it was a sin of omission
—not doing something that they should have done.
It’s also interesting to note that in Matthew’s account,
the talents were given to the slaves “according to [their] ability.”
So one received five, one received two,
and the third one, one talent.
Was the master being partial?
No, not at all.
The account explains clearly that the talents were given to the slaves
“according to [their] ability.”
So that was really being considerate on the part of the master
—the way he apportioned the responsibilities
to work for his interests,
to increase his belongings.
And, you know, that’s a very comforting thought
for all of us:
to realize that Jehovah takes into account what we can do
—not comparing us with others in the congregation.
We have to be careful about feeling worthless
or devaluing our own worth, because that can happen.
We can feel we just can’t ever do enough to please Jehovah God,
or there’s just too much going on.
No, we just have to do whatever we are able to do
and give our best to Jehovah God.
We never want to fall into the trap
that the sluggish and wicked slave fell into.
If you recall the account, he started to criticize the master:
“I know that you reap what you haven’t sowed.
“I know that you do this or that.
You’re harsh.”
He was really placing the blame on the master
for his own inactivity —for what he didn’t do.
But the master turned the tables on him,
and he said: “You say that I’m that way.
Well, now ‘wicked slave.’ . . .”
And then he told him that he wasn’t going to receive anything.
He was categorized as “wicked”!
So as long as we give our best —we give from the heart—
Jehovah is going to bless us.
And there’s another interesting thing too with the slaves
—the one slave who received five talents
and the one who received two talents.
The one who received two talents gained two talents.
The one who received five gained five.
But the one who had two and gained only two
didn’t look at the one who gained five and say:
“I can’t do what he did.
I only received two talents.”
No, he was just happy with what he had.
Isn’t that a good lesson for us?
Be happy with you and with what you’re able to do.
If you can reach out and do more, wonderful!
Do it.
But we don’t want to start comparing,
“I can’t keep up with him or with her.”
That’s just a bad, bad idea,
and it will not benefit anyone.
What did the master say to the slave who gained five talents
—a total of ten talents?
And that was a fortune in those days.
Well, let’s see what the scripture says, Matthew 25
—Matthew 25:21.
And these are the words of the master to the slave who gained five talents,
verse 21:
“His master said to him: ‘Well done, good and faithful slave!
“‘You were faithful over a few things.
“‘I will appoint you over many things.
Enter into the joy of your master.’”
What a reward from the master!
But what did he say to the slave
who gained only two talents?
Verse 23:
“His master said to him:
“‘Well done, good and faithful slave!
“‘You were faithful over a few things.
“‘I will appoint you over many things.
Enter into the joy of your master.’”
Same, same —isn’t that what it is?
It was according to each one’s ability.
The reward in each case was the same:
the approval of the master and,
undoubtedly, additional responsibilities.
Put simply, the Master is Jesus Christ.
The talents refer to the responsibility
that Jehovah gives to his anointed servants;
they have to preach and make disciples.
That commission was given to the anointed.
We of the other sheep,
we have the responsibility to do the same thing,
but that illustration was directed, truly, to the anointed.
But there is a scripture that helps us to appreciate what we need to do,
and it’s in Revelation chapter 22
—Revelation 22:17.
It’s not directly connected to the talents,
but it does give us direction on what we all should do
—whether we’re of the anointed or of the other sheep.
Revelation 22:17 says:
“And the spirit and the bride keep on saying, ‘Come!’
and let anyone hearing say, ‘Come!’”
Well, that would be “anyone hearing” —we of the other sheep.
Because the bride— We know who the bride is.
The bride is the anointed brothers of Christ.
And then it says: “And let anyone thirsting come;
let anyone who wishes take life’s water free.”
Well, “the spirit” says “Come!”
Yes, indeed!
At Pentecost, holy spirit was poured out upon 120 disciples.
They could go out and speak other languages.
They were sharing the good news —the hope—
with Jews in Jerusalem at that time.
The holy spirit inspired men to write the Scriptures;
holy spirit is behind the prophecies that we read in the Bible.
And the holy spirit is saying “Come!” —isn’t it?—
when you read a scripture to someone about the time of the end
(2 Timothy 3 or other scriptures)
and they say, “That’s what’s taking place today!”
“Come on, ‘Come!’”
The holy spirit is nudging, urging people when they read God’s Word
and they understand it and they accept what it says.
It says “Come!”
What about the bride?
Well, the bride’s been saying “Come!” for a long time.
One hundred and twenty disciples at Pentecost went down,
they preached in different languages, and they were saying
to the Jews there, “Come!”
And then down through the centuries,
we know that the few there who may have been of the bride class
did their best to serve Jehovah and honor him.
But in these last days
is when it has really expanded tremendously,
with the bride saying “Come!”
Think about it.
From 120 disciples at Pentecost
and preaching in one city —in this case, Jerusalem—
the work of the bride has increased
to 8,220,105 disciples
in 240 lands.
Has the bride been saying “Come!”?
Absolutely!
From one congregation at Pentecost
—you could call the 120 disciples a congregation—
to 118,016 congregations worldwide.
The Master, Jesus, must be very happy, joyful,
to see that his obedient slaves have truly covered the earth
with the Kingdom message.
What a privilege we have to share in that work!

cn.text: 今天经文的参考资料包括
马太福音25章和路加福音19章
马太福音25章记载了银元的比喻
三个奴隶受主人委托管理财物
一个奴隶领到三万银元
另一个领到一万二千银元
最后一个领到六千银元
路加福音19章记载的比喻中
共有十个奴隶
每个人收到一百银元
两个比喻都谈到银元
也可以说是财物
耶稣去世前不久
在不同的地方说了这两个比喻
路加福音记载的比喻
是耶稣在耶利哥城说的
马太福音记载的比喻
是耶稣在橄榄山上给他的门徒讲的
这两个比喻中
都有一个要点值得留意
那就是
两个比喻中
没有用主人交托的银元去赚钱的奴隶
都被称作“邪恶的”
在谴责人时
“邪恶的”“恶人”“恶者”
都是很强烈  很严厉的措辞
被主人称为“邪恶的”  就更是如此
我们可以再看两个例子
在马太福音6:13中
耶稣称撒但为“恶者”
箴言10:7说
“恶人的臭名却要腐朽湮没”
可以看出  邪恶这个词
不管用在谁身上
都是相当强烈的措辞
那么  为什么比喻中的奴隶
被称为“邪恶的”呢？
耶稣没有说他们违反了十诫中的哪一条
不过  他们的确犯下了严重的罪
他们本应该善用主人委托的银元去赚钱
而他们却没有去做
这就是他们的罪了
我们举个例子  来说明一下这种罪
你记得吗？
马太福音25:41-46记载的比喻里
被判定为山羊的人最终会
“永远被剪除”
他们被剪除是因为他们做了恶事吗？
不是
经文说
他们的罪是没有帮助基督的弟兄
他们没有去做自己本来应该去做的事
这就是他们的罪了
在马太福音的记载里
有一点很值得留意
主人是“按照奴隶各自的才能”
交托给他们财物的
因此  第一个奴隶得到三万银元
第二个得到一万二千
第三个得到六千
是主人偏心吗？
当然不是
经文说得很清楚
这是“按照奴隶各自的才能”分配的
虽然主人想增加自己的收入
可是他分配工作时却很体贴周到
知道这一点  令我们感到安舒
因为这让我们学到
耶和华总是留意我们的能力限度
而不会把我们与会众里其他人做比较
我们也需要留意
不要过度自卑
觉得自己一无是处
的确
有时我们自己觉得为耶和华做的不多
生活压力也很大
这时  请不要忘记
只要我们尽力而为
把最好的献给耶和华
他就非常赏识我们
我们都不希望自己变得
像那个懒散  邪恶的奴隶一样
你记得他后来怎么做吗？
他开始指责主人
“我知道你……没有撒种的地方也要收割”
“我知道你是个非常苛刻的人”
这个奴隶为自己的过错找借口
竟然开始怪罪起主人来
主人怎么做呢？
主人就对他说
你既然这样说
那么  现在你不会得到任何东西
除此之外
这个奴隶还被称作“邪恶的”！
所以我们学到
只要心甘情愿献出最好的
耶和华就会赐福给我们
这个关于银元的比喻
还有值得我们留意的地方
头两个奴隶  一个领到三万银元
一个领到一万二千银元
他们都赚了钱  都使银元翻了一倍
获得一万二千银元的奴隶
没有和获得三万银元的奴隶比较  说
我没他能干
我只赚了一万二千
相反  他为自己取得的成果而高兴
我们也该这样做  对吗？
要为自己能做到的感到高兴
如果你能做更多  很好！
那就去做吧
但我们都不该互相比较说
我没他那么能干
这样的想法非常糟糕
对谁都没有益处
获得三万银元的奴隶
最后得到了六万银元
这在当时  是一大笔钱啊！
我们可以一起打开马太福音25章
看看主人是怎样说的
马太福音25:21
记载了主人
对获得三万银元的奴隶说的话
“主人对他说”
“又良善又忠信的奴隶   你做得好！”
“你在不多的事上忠信”
“我要委派你管理很多的事”
“来分享你主人的喜乐吧”
这是多丰厚的奖赏啊！
对获得一万二千银元的奴隶
主人又怎样说呢？
马太福音25:23说
“主人对他说”
“又良善又忠信的奴隶”
“你做得好！”
“你在不多的事上忠信”
“我要委派你管理很多的事”
“来分享你主人的喜乐吧”
主人的话  竟然完全一样！
虽然委派时是按照每个人的能力
但最终的奖赏却都一样
什么奖赏呢？
就是主人的赞赏
以及受委任去管理更多的事
简单来说  主人指的就是耶稣基督
银元指的是
耶和华委派给受膏基督徒的工作
他们要去传道教人
帮助别人做基督的门徒
当然  另外的绵羊也要参与这份工作
但耶稣的比喻
主要是针对受膏基督徒说的
我们可以看一节经文  好明白
我们应该做的事
请打开启示录22:17
这节经文与银元的比喻没有直接关系
但不论是受膏基督徒还是另外的绵羊
都可以从这节经文看出自己该做什么
启示录22:17说
“圣灵和新娘不断说”
“来吧！”
“谁听见都要说”
“来吧！”
这里说的“谁”
指的就是另外的绵羊
那么新娘呢？
当然  我们都知道
指的就是基督的受膏弟兄
17节的经文接着说
“谁渴了都要来”
“谁愿意  都要白白取生命的水喝”
没错  “圣灵”的确在说 “来吧！”
公元33年五旬节
圣灵倾注在120个门徒身上
这些门徒就开始讲起不同的外语
向当时
在耶路撒冷的犹太人传讲好消息
圣经里面的预言
都是人受圣灵感动写下来的
现在  圣灵依然在说 “来吧！”
当和别人谈到末世征象时
我们一读出提摩太后书3章
或者别的经文
对方都会说
现在就是这样啊！
是的  那就“来吧！”
人读了上帝的话语
明白了其中的意思
并接受了真理
这都是圣灵在推动人  促请人
仿佛在说 “来吧！”
那么新娘呢？
其实  新娘一直在说 “来吧！”
从公元33年五旬节的120个门徒开始
新娘用不同的语言  对犹太人说
“来吧！”
之后在漫长的历史时期
属于新娘群体的人
都竭尽所能  敬奉耶和华
荣耀耶和华
到了最后的日子
传讲好消息的工作得以迅速扩展
因为新娘一直在说 “来吧！”
请想一想
五旬节时  120个门徒
在耶路撒冷一个城市传道
现在  门徒数目达到822万105
传道工作遍及240个国家和地区
新娘有没有一直在说 “来吧！”？
当然！
从120个门徒所组成的一群会众
增长到今天
遍布全球的11万8016群会众
忠心顺服的奴隶
把王国好消息传遍全世界
看到这些  主人耶稣一定非常喜乐
能够参与这项工作
是多大的殊荣啊！

en.text: While meditating on the text this morning,
I was reminded of an experience
I had many years ago as a missionary.
At the time,
I was studying with a young man
who was training to be a pastor
in his church.
This man had got to the point where he started to attend all our meetings
while at the same time still attending his church gatherings.
The church, obviously, was very disturbed
about the fact that he was coming to the meetings of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and their headquarters sent in a missionary from overseas
to try and rectify the situation.
The young man told me what happened.
He said the missionary asked him,
“What is it that impresses you about Jehovah’s Witnesses?”
He said, “Well, one of the things is that they do the preaching work.”
The missionary replied, “Well, our church can do that too.”
So the next time they had a service,
the missionary conducted the service and with great zeal and enthusiasm
demanded that everyone in the church take part in the preaching work.
He announced the time that they would have the group to go preaching.
The young man told me quite a number of people came along.
But there was just one thing missing, you guessed it, the missionary.
He felt that it was enough
just to encourage everybody else to do it without engaging in it himself.
How different was the example of Jesus and of our hard-working elders
who do take the lead with regard to the preaching work.
Now let’s take our Bibles and turn to a very interesting scripture
in Hebrews 13:7, 17.
Now, I’d like to highlight the beauty of the New World Translation
in these two verses.
You see at the beginning of verse 7:
“Remember those who are taking the lead among you.”
And then verse 17:
“Be obedient to those who are taking the lead among you.”
If you look at other Bibles, whether new or old,
most of them say “your leaders.”
Now, obviously, the New World Translation Committee
had in mind Jesus’ comments with regard
to no one being a leader among us,
and although it’s a different word in the Greek text,
still in English we can’t help but be sensitive to that matter.
And so this accurate translation of saying “taking the lead”
really summarizes, doesn’t it, what the role is of an elder.
We’re not leaders, but we set the right example.
Now, this accurate translation is also portrayed
in the words of our Lord Jesus Christ as recorded in Luke chapter 22,
and you’ll be interested to note
that this is part of the revision of the New World Translation text.
Luke 22:26, it now portrays accurately
the fact that both expressions in Hebrew
and this one here are the same word.
So, Luke 22:26,
it says: “You, though, are not to be that way.
But let the one who is the greatest among you become as the youngest.”
And then notice: “and the one taking the lead,”
now this is the same expression as in the Hebrews,
“as the one ministering.”
So, obviously, to take the lead means to do the work,
to be a minister, to be a servant, to serve others.
This also reminds me, many years ago,
when I worked with the translation team in the Pacific nation of Samoa.
At that point, we were trying to select an accurate expression
to convey this thought of “taking the lead.”
And there were two words eventually that the brothers
were trying to select between, or choose between.
One was the word ta’ita’i and the other ta’imua.
Now, you don’t have to remember those words,
but as a foreigner, I didn’t really understand
the subtleties between the difference of the two words.
So I asked the brothers, “How can you explain to me
what these two words mean?”
So one of the brothers was very eloquent.
He said: “Well, just imagine a procession, a parade.
“So a ta’ita’i is the old man who sits
“on the side of the road barking out the orders:
“‘You should do it this way; you should do it that way.’
“The ta’imua, on the other hand, is the one right in the front of the parade
taking the lead and everyone’s following him.”
Which word do you think we selected?
Doesn’t that summarize nicely just exactly what’s involved with being an elder?
It’s not a matter of sitting on the sidelines barking out orders
but getting involved,
setting the right example, and then others following.
And this is in harmony with one Greek lexicon
that describes this expression this way, it says,
“The concept of leading can be expressed
“by showing how to do something,
“demonstrating how we ought to do it,
and going ahead showing the way.”
Of course, on the other hand, some religions even view
the expression “elder” as a title.
You’ve probably heard of them introducing themselves,
“Good morning, I’m Elder Jackson.”
Well, of course, none of us would want to view
being an elder as a title in the sense of a position
that lords it over others.
And with that in mind, another subtlety to the revision
is seen in 1 Timothy chapter 3,
so please turn there with me,
1 Timothy 3:1.
These are well-known words
—particularly when brothers are considering the qualifications for elders—
but you may or may not have seen
the subtleties of the change here in this revision.
It says now: “This statement is trustworthy:
“If a man is reaching out to be an overseer,
he is desirous of a fine work.”
Do you remember before the original New World Translation said:
‘If someone is reaching out for the office of being an overseer?’
And that reflected and no doubt was influenced
by the King James and many of the older translations
that translated it that way.
But when we look at the rest of the verse,
we see that it’s not the office, or the position,
of being an overseer that someone reaches out for;
rather, it’s the work.
Yes, the hard work that needs to be done by an overseer.
An overseer recognizes
that he needs to work hard at setting the right example,
and then others will follow
—rather than just telling everyone what they should do.
So when we look at these subtleties in the New World Translation,
it only helps us to appreciate it even more, doesn’t it?
So with this in mind,
what does our text this morning help us to keep in mind?
Well, as elders, what do we need to do?
Not sit on the sidelines barking out orders but, rather,
to take the lead, be in the forefront, do the work,
and then others will follow our example,
just as we follow the example of Jesus.

cn.text: 我在思考今天的经文时
想起许多年前的一个经历
那时候我做特派传道员
帮助一个年轻人学习圣经
他打算做牧师，正在接受教会的培训
他进步得很快
开始参加我们的所有聚会
但与此同时也继续参加教会的活动
教会的人知道他参加耶和华见证人的聚会
就很不高兴
那个教会的总部从国外派一个传教士来
想要劝阻这位年轻人
年轻人告诉我后来发生了什么
传教士问他
“你觉得耶和华见证人有什么特别的地方呢？”
年轻人回答
“有很多，比如他们都传道。”
传教士说
“这个，我们教会也可以做啊。”
就在下一次做礼拜的时候
这位传教士在讲台上慷慨激昂地布道
要求在场所有听道的人都出去传道
也宣布了集体传道的时间
后来确实有不少人都去传道了
但有一个人没来
你猜得没错，就是那个传教士
他觉得只要让别人出去传道
那就足够了，自己是不用去的
耶稣和这个传教士相比多么不同！
今天在各群会众里
努力带头传道的长老们也一样
现在请打开你的圣经到希伯来书13:7,17
这两节经文很有意思
《新世界译本》在这里翻译得很好
我们来一起看一下
第7节说
“要记住那些在你们当中带头的人”
然后再看看第17节
“要服从那些在你们当中带头的人”
如果你看其他的译本
不管是古代的还是现代的，许多都译成“领袖”
很显然，新世界译本翻译委员会
记得耶稣曾经说过
我们当中没有一个人是领袖
尽管这两节经文使用的希腊语词与耶稣使用的词
不是同一个词
但我们在翻译的时候还是要小心谨慎
因此，《新世界译本》翻译成“带头的人”
准确地指明长老的职责
他们不是要做领袖，而是要做榜样
另一个翻译得很准确的例子
就是在路加福音的22章里耶稣所说过的一句话
请留意，对比之前的翻译
《新世界译本》在这里做出了修订
修订本的路加福音22:26里使用了
和希伯来书13章7节、17节
这两节经文同样的词
路加福音22章的26节，经文说
“可是你们不要这样，你们中间最大的
应该像最年轻的
带头的，应该像为人服务的。”
请留意，经文强调带头的
应该像为人服务的
这里所用的“带头”一词
和上面的希伯来书提到的是同一个词
所以，在会众中带头的人应该努力工作
为他人服务
我也想起许多年前在太平洋岛国萨摩亚
协助翻译工作时的一个经历
在那时候
我们要为“带头的”这个表达找一个准确的词
最终我们锁定了两个词
要在这两个词之中选一个最合适的
一个是“塔伊塔伊”（ta’ita’i）
一个是“塔伊姆阿”（ta’imua）
当然你不用费劲去记这两个词
作为外国人
我不清楚这两个词之间有什么细微的差别
于是，我就问那些弟兄:“能给我解释
这两个词到底有什么区别吗？”
其中一个弟兄的表达很到位，他对我说
“可以这么说，就像一个游行队伍
‘塔伊塔伊’
指的是一个老年人站在路旁发号施令
‘你该这么做’，‘不该那么做’
而‘塔伊姆阿’
指的是走在队伍最前面的那个人
大家都在后面跟着他。”
你觉得我们选择的是哪个词呢？
做长老到底意味着什么？
这个例子解释得是不是很清楚呢？
长老不是要站在一旁发号施令
而是要参与其中
给别人立下好榜样，让别人照着做
这也与一本希腊语词典的解释相吻合
这本词典这样解释“带头”这个词
“带头意味着向人做示范
让别人知道该怎样做
并且以自己的行动带领别人”
不过，有些教会却把“长老”
当作一个头衔来看待
他们彼此介绍时也许会这么说
“早上好，我是杰克逊长老。”
当然，我们没有人想把长老看成一个头衔
认为他们的地位高人一等
关于这一点，我们一起来看看
《新世界译本》对提摩太前书第3章
所做的细微的修订
请跟我一起打开提摩太前书3:1
这是大家非常熟悉的经文
特别是那些在考虑长老要符合哪些资格的弟兄们
但你们有没有留意到《新世界译本》修订版
对这节经文做了细微的调整呢？
现在的译法是“人竭力符合资格做监督
就是向往美好的工作
这句话真实可靠。”
你还记得，以前的《新世界译本》怎么说吗？
经文说:“人如果尽力追求监督的职分。”
英语《新世界译本》以前的这个译法
很可能是受到了英王钦定本
和其他一些古老的译本所影响
但如果我们看接下来的经文，就能看出
一个人应该努力追求的不是监督的职分或头衔本身
而是要做的工作
也就是身为监督必须要做的那些实际的工作
一个监督需要认识到，他应该以身作则
为别人立下好榜样
让别人也可以学习他是怎么做的
而不是只在一旁指挥别人怎么做
所以，如果我们明白这些细微的调整
我们就会更喜欢修订后的译法
讨论到这里
你从今天早上的经文学到什么呢？
如果你是个长老，你该怎么做呢？
不是站在一旁发号施令
而是要走在队伍的前列，带头行动
这样别人也可以学习我们的榜样
就像我们学习耶稣的榜样一样

en.text: The Assembly Hall is an educational center.
This is a center of pure worship for all the congregations that come.
Taking care of Jehovah’s house
is part of sacred service.
Even going back to the temple,
everyone had an assignment.
They had someone to open the doors.
So, of course, they also had somebody maintaining things.
As of December 2016,
there are 773 Assembly Halls worldwide.
There are so many details at an Assembly Hall;
you can’t do it all yourself.
To be overseer of an Assembly Hall—
We were excited to do it, but it seemed real heavy at the time.
It does take,
in our particular case, a couple of hundred.
There are about 200 or so volunteers
each and every week
that really are necessary
to care for the Assembly Hall —the grounds,
the accounting, the purchasing,
the maintenance,
and the cleaning.
Each and every one of these chairs —the seating—
all have moving parts and have to be maintained.
And with 4,050 seats in here,
we can say that every single one of them has been maintained.
John 2:17 says: “The zeal for your house will consume me.”
And I think we have an opportunity to show Jehovah that
—that we have zeal, we have an eagerness, a fire for his house,
and for caring for it.
So we appreciate all those who want to work at the Assembly Hall.
So many of the dear friends, after they just spent a whole day
doing some terribly dirty job, they thank you for the privilege.
Well, that’s zeal for Jehovah’s house.
Nowhere else does that happen.
And if we tried to do it ourselves or if we hired somebody,
it wouldn’t be as good as the work that the friends do when they come in.
When the friends come on the weekend,
this is an educational facility.
So they come here
to be educated about Jehovah.
And new ones come,
and it needs to be dignified
and reflect Jehovah’s qualities.
So the cleaning that goes on and the maintenance that goes on
—that’s what the purpose is.
At lunchtime, we do a spiritual program.
It could be a talk; it could be a discussion.
And we, really, generally try to cover a topic
that helps the volunteers see the connection
between their work at the Assembly Hall
and the Kingdom preaching work.
We are preachers.
That’s number one —to spread the good news.
And we see the results of that here.
We’re filling this place up.
It’s a real privilege.
You learn so much from the sacrifices that the friends make
in order to serve Jehovah
that it makes us feel very small, and we realize
what a blessing it is for us to be in that environment all the time.
The goal of any work in Jehovah’s service
is to help as many people as you can
to come to know him
and to take care of his interests
here on the earth.
And we all have the same goal
—trying to please him and doing what we can.
Our goal, really, as Assembly Hall servants
is to take care of the place in such a way
—take care of the Assembly Hall in such a way—
that not only saves and makes wise use
of dedicated funds and resources
but also makes things ready in such a way
that on Saturday morning when the brothers and sisters walk in
and the attendants and the sound
and the stage brothers are getting ready,
all they really have to do is come on in and flip the switches
—lights come on, air conditioning, heat.
Everything is functioning.
All they have to do is just focus on the program
and listen and take in instruction.
That’s what we’re asked to do —listen and take in instruction.
And we can do that when we’re not distracted by anything else.
So if everything
works well on an assembly day,
we know we’ve done our job.

cn.text: 大会堂是一个教育中心
供会众的弟兄姐妹崇拜上帝使用
照料属于耶和华的产业
是一项神圣的服务
在古代的圣殿里
每个人都有自己的委派
有些人甚至专门负责开门
当然肯定有人负责维修和保养
截止到2016年12月
全球共有773所大会堂
照料大会堂  需要做的事很多
一个人肯定忙不过来
被委任做大会堂监督
我们都很兴奋
但同时也觉得担子很重
我们照料的这所大会堂
需要上百人帮忙
每星期都会有两百多位弟兄姐妹
来做志愿服务
有人打扫院子
有人负责会计
有人负责采购
还有人做清洁和保养的工作
大会堂里的每把椅子
都需要维修和清洁
这里的4050把椅子
你可能不敢相信
每一把都是干干净净的
约翰福音2：17说
“我为你的殿热心  不能自已”
照料大会堂让人有机会向耶和华表明
自己多么渴望为他的殿服务
真的很欣赏那些乐意服务的弟兄姐妹
大会堂的工作又脏又累
但许多弟兄姐妹在这儿忙了一整天
还感谢你给他们服务的机会
这就是对耶和华殿的热心
别的地方绝不会有这样的事
就算我们花钱雇人来打扫
也不可能像弟兄姐妹做得这么好
周末大家来聚会时
这里就成了一个教育场所
帮助人学习耶和华的真理
我们的工作就是让这里
保持整洁  运作良好
这样  第一次来参加聚会的人
就能感觉到大会堂反映了
耶和华的特质
是庄重的场所
我们会在午饭期间
安排一个属灵的节目
有的时候是个演讲
有的时候是以讨论的方式进行
我们真的很希望帮助志愿人员看出
这里的服务与传道工作有什么关系
作为传道员
我们的首要工作是传讲好消息
在大会堂我们可以看到传道的成果
就是参加聚会的人越来越多
我们觉得很荣幸
能有机会看到许多弟兄姐妹
为耶和华所做的牺牲
与他们相比
我们觉得自己实在微不足道
处在这样的属灵环境中
的确是个福分
我们为耶和华服务
就是要帮助人认识上帝
也要照料好耶和华在地上的产业
我们的目标其实都一样
就是要努力让上帝的心欢喜
作为大会堂仆人
我们的责任就是要照料好大会堂
一方面善用捐款避免浪费
另一方面也要确保大会堂的设施
都正常运行
这样  在星期六早上
弟兄姐妹来的时候
招待员  负责音响和舞台的弟兄
就都可以各就其位
照明  空调等一切设备都运作良好
他们只需要按下开关就可以了
大家能够聚精会神聆听节目
我们参加大会就是要这样
专心聆听  避免被任何事干扰
如果整天的大会都顺利进行
我们就很欣慰了
因为我们做了自己该做的

en.text: Have you, though, ever felt alone in your assignment,
even if for just a few hours in the ministry?
Brother Pontien Mukanga may have felt that way early in his assignment.
He was the first circuit overseer for all of what is now
the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Republic of Congo.
He traveled great distances to visit the few brothers throughout the territory.
Listen to what encouraged him the most to keep going.
I was made a circuit overseer for the whole of Congo.
I was so happy to receive this privilege.
But I was shocked and scared.
The assignment was huge.
Congo is a vast country.
I was afraid to go to places I didn’t know.
I felt overwhelmed, so I turned to Jehovah.
Sometimes I had to go through savannahs and across the jungle.
There were wild animals.
One day, I climbed up a tree to find a place to sleep.
I tied myself to a branch with my belt.
I was afraid I would be taken by a boa snake.
I was afraid of getting lost in the forest.
Visiting the brothers was very difficult.
Sometimes the journey took many days.
I remember one day, I left my house
to visit the brothers to encourage them.
I left at 5:30 in the morning,
and I arrived at 7:30 that night.
I had to push my bicycle through sand
for up to 13 miles (21 km) or even more.
Other times, we traveled by truck.
That was not easy.
You had to climb on top of the truck.
I had to hold on tight so as not to fall.
Congregations, isolated groups were far away from one another.
There were no phones at that time either.
Even though they did not know I was coming,
they made me feel so welcome.
The brothers were really very hospitable.
When I arrived,
I was exhausted but so happy to see the brothers.
The Kitawala was a religion.
They sent many letters to the Belgium branch
asking to be recognized as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
These people used
our publications and used the name Watch Tower.
It created a lot of confusion.
To clarify the matter,
the organization prepared a booklet.
My mission was to check whether
there were any genuine Jehovah’s Witnesses in Kisangani.
We found out that these people were
not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
In all the confusion, people even tried to kill me
during the trip.
Fortunately, I managed to escape.
Since it was Jehovah who assigned me this privilege,
I was confident that he would always help me.
And today, I am very happy
to have at my side my children, my grandchildren,
and my great-grandchildren —all Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Jehovah has given me many blessings.
I am truly grateful.
What a joy to be used by Almighty God.
Through all these years, I have never lacked anything.
Jehovah has given me the strength
to serve him up until now—to the age of 86.
In everything and for everything,
my trust really is in Jehovah.
There were 46 publishers
in the whole of Congo.
Today, I hear there are more than
223,000 Jehovah’s Witnesses
in the Congo.
Today, when I see
the increase of Jehovah’s people,
to me it is like a miracle.
I thank Jehovah for allowing me to see
‘the little one become a thousand’
here in the Congo.
Brother Mukanga continues to serve as an elder at nearly 88 years old.
Can you imagine yourself experiencing both the joys
and difficulties he had as a circuit overseer?
He courageously visited the Kitawala religious groups
who claimed to serve Jehovah,
only to find some were violent and practiced immorality.
But it was his reliance on Jehovah
and watching Him turn the small group of brothers
into more than 200,000 that has kept him going.

cn.text: 在传道时  你曾经感到孤单吗？
蓬蒂恩·穆卡尼加弟兄
在受委派初期
可能有过同样的感受
他是刚果的第一位分区监督
当时他探访的地区
包括现在的刚果民主共和国
以及刚果共和国
那时弟兄不多
但他仍然长途跋涉去探访他们
他坚持不懈
勇往直前的最大动力是什么呢？
我受委任做分区监督
探访刚果境內的所有会众
我很高兴得到这个殊荣
但同时也很担心  害怕
因为任务很艰巨
刚果地域广大
去自己不熟悉的地方
我感到很害怕
所以就向耶和华求助
有时候  我要经过大草原
有时候要穿过丛林
到处有野生动物
有一次
我爬到树上
用皮带把自己捆在树枝上
才敢睡觉
因为我担心被蟒蛇吞掉
在丛林中迷路也让我很害怕
探访工作很不容易
有时候  在路上要花好几天时间
记得有一次去探访和鼓励弟兄
我早上5:30就出门
到了晚上7:30才到了目的地
有一段路
全是沙子
我推着自行车走了21公里
有时候  我也会搭上卡车
但这也不容易
需要爬到车顶
紧紧抓牢才不会掉下去
所有的会众
和偏远小组彼此离得都很远
当时也没有电话
弟兄们都不知道我去探访他们
但每次他们都热情地欢迎我
慷慨地款待我
虽然我很累
但见到他们真的很高兴
一个叫“基塔瓦拉”的教派

title: 조이 오롬: 여호와의 일을 할 수 있어서 감사해요

en.text: I had the privilege for two years
of sitting at the same table as Sister Orrom for morning worship.
She expected nothing and appreciated
everything that you did for her.
Sister Orrom was affectionately known as Joey.
And if you take the “e” out of Joey,
you’re left with the English word “joy,”
and that summed her up.
My impression of Joey when I first met her
was here is this frail old lady.
But then when you started to speak to Joey,
you were tapping into a tremendous depth.
About the age of 20,
round about that time,
I had the heavenly calling.
That was a big battle.
I couldn’t understand why Jehovah would use a person like me.
And when I was 21,
I got into pioneering, in 1939.
But the police were after me
because I wouldn’t join the armed forces, and I was tried under a new act.
And they kept taking me into a side room and saying,
“If you will say you are not connected with Jehovah’s Witnesses,
not connected with the Watch Tower, you’ll have a walk away.”
I said: “I am connected with the Watch Tower.
I’m proud to be connected with the Watch Tower.”
And they said, “Then they are directing you.”
I said, “No, my stand of not doing as you wish is my own personal stand.”
So this went on.
In the end, they sent me to prison just for two months
and then let me out.
I partnered with another sister,
and she and I went to Northern Ireland
and pioneered there for 18 months.
And it was in Northern Ireland that we had our call to Gilead.
In 1948, Joey was invited to Gilead,
and that was the 11th class.
It left an impression on me, which I will never ever, ever forget.
You pick up that spirit of good behavior, of love.
It’s something that leaves its mark, or it should.
It has left its mark on me —very, very much so.
One thing Brother Knorr impressed on us:
“You’ll be three years on your assignment before you really love it.”
And it was true because it was a hard assignment.
After Gilead, she was assigned to be a missionary
in Dublin, in the Irish Republic.
That was the time when Catholic priests
used to organize mobs against the pioneers.
She was full of joy, but that didn’t mean to say
that she’d had an easy life.
We never went out from door to door without being mobbed
and attacked and beaten up and thrown around.
And you could only do a few houses in a row,
and you’d have to get away very quickly.
But we made a very good name.
People got to know we were completely neutral.
They chose four of us to work the business property,
and I got some studies going in their offices.
But one place I went into, I walked the length of this draper shop,
and I asked if I could go into the manager’s office.
As I went in, I didn’t say a word.
I didn’t open my mouth and even say good morning,
but this man stood up, and he said, “Russellite!”
And he took hold of me by the scruff of my neck
and the seat of my pants, and he lifted me up
and he carried me the length of the store.
Well, like a silly one, I should’ve gone heavy on him, you see.
But instead of that, I let my legs paddle
and I was hanging onto my book bag, not wanting to lose it.
And when he got to the front door, the staff,
their eyes were absolutely aghast at what was happening.
He opened his front door and threw me out, literally.
And I went zoom! just managed to go zoom!
And one of the brothers was passing,
and he caught me —caught me steady—
and said, “Whatever is going on?”
And I couldn’t stop laughing.
To me it was very, very funny.
The rest were so cross about it, but I wasn’t at all cross.
I thought it was quite hilarious.
I could see myself being carried through this shop sky-high.
Things like that happened.
These experiences did not dampen her zeal.
She always retained that missionary spirit.
I first met Joey
when I was commuting to Bethel
in the infirmary.
She was sitting on that old-fashioned chair with this huge Bible,
and she stayed there hours reading the Bible,
praying to Jehovah.
Often, when you came in, she’d be in the middle of Bible reading.
And she’d be saying something like,
“Daniel has just been thrown into the lion’s den!”
or “Oh, Jehovah is really angry.
He’s thundering from the heavens!”
And it made me think, ‘Wow!
‘She must have read the Bible so many times,
but every time it was as if it was happening right in front of her.’
Right up until she became incapacitated,
she was conducting Bible studies
and helping people to come to know Jehovah.
She was looking forward to her heavenly reward.
And for her that was the culmination
of a life of joy in Jehovah’s service
and that she was just transferring to her next assignment.
I’m very, very grateful for work.
In fact, often in my prayers,
I’ll pray to Jehovah that I’ll have some good work to do today.
I’m very grateful to have work to do.

cn.text: 我有两年和奥罗姆姐妹
在同一张桌子参加早晨崇拜
她对别人没要求
但别人为她做什么  她都很感激
我们都亲切地
称奥罗姆姐妹乔伊（Joey）
如果去掉字母“e”
她的名字在英语里就是“喜乐”的意思
她确实人如其名
她给我的第一印象
是位年老体弱的老太太
但只要她一开口
你就会发现她有那么多的经历呢
我大约20岁的时候
意识到自己未来的希望是去天上
我也不明白耶和华为什么会拣选我
1939年  我21岁  开始做先驱
我不愿参军
警察就来找我的麻烦
指控我触犯了一条新法规
他们把我带到一边  说：
“如果你断绝跟耶和华见证人”
“跟守望台书社的关系”
“我们就放你走”
我说：
“可我的确和守望台书社有关系啊！”
“我为此感到很自豪”
警察又说：“是他们在指使你！”
我回答：
“不是  完全是我自己的选择”
后来他们把我在监狱里关了两个月
获释后  我和一个姐妹做同伴
在北爱尔兰做了一年半先驱
在那里  我们收到了基列学校的邀请
乔伊受邀请参加第11届基列学校
在基列学校的美好时光
我永远都不会忘记
弟兄姐妹的爱心和好行为
给我很大的影响  简直不可磨灭
到现在我都记得诺尔弟兄说的话
“你要花三年才能真正爱上你的委派”
他说的真的没错
因为我的委派确实很不容易
基列毕业以后  她被派到
爱尔兰的都柏林做特派传道员
那时候
天主教神父经常纠集暴民攻击我们
乔伊是个很喜乐的姐妹
但那时她也真的不容易
我们每次挨家挨户传道
都会遭到暴民袭击  被人毒打
在一条街上
只能探访几个住户就得赶快离开
但我们赢得了很好的名声
人们都知道我们会绝对中立
那时  我们有四个人也去商业区传道
我在办公楼还找到一些圣经学生
有一次  我走进一个布料店
想见他们的经理
我走进经理的办公室
还没来得及开口打招呼呢
那个经理就站起来
对我大喊：“你这个罗素派！”
说完一手抓住我衣领
一手抓住我的裤子  把我举了起来
我当时也真傻
其实我应该坐在地上
不过那时我两只脚就一直
踢来踢去  踢来踢去
为了保护书刊我死死抱着背包
经理举着我走到门口
店员都目瞪口呆
经理打开门  一下子就把我
给扔了出去
“嗖”的一声
我就飞了出去
还好  有个弟兄正好路过
一把抓住我  我才没有摔倒
弟兄问我：“出什么事了？”
我忍不住大笑起来
真的太好笑了
别人都很生气  但我一点也没有
只是觉得好笑  被人高高地举起来
这样的事真的很好玩吧
这样的经历并没有减弱乔伊的热心
她一直保持着特派传道员的精神
我做通勤人员时
在医疗部第一次见到乔伊
她坐在一个老式的沙发上
抱着本大大的圣经
好几个小时  她都在研读和祷告
每次到她的房间
她几乎都在读圣经
她会突然冒出一句
“但以理被扔到狮子坑里啦！”
或者“耶和华很生气”
“他从天上打雷了！”
我就想：“哇！”
“乔伊已经读过很多遍圣经了”
“但每次她还是读得那么投入！”
乔伊一直主持圣经讨论
帮助别人认识耶和华
后来她行动不便了才不得不停下来
她很期待得到天上的奖赏
她一生喜乐地为耶和华服务
对她而言
到天上去是一个新的委派
一个更喜乐的委派
我很高兴能为耶和华服务
我经常祷告  求耶和华让我每天
都能为他做点儿什么
因为这实在太美好了

en.text: My name is Miki.
I moved here one year ago.
Everyone was so nice and friendly.
Well, that’s how I felt in the beginning.
I am not your babysitter!
Didn’t you see we were talking?
Come on! This is not a park!
And the elders are always busy.
I’m not sure if they really want me here.
Yoko, a pioneer sister from my former congregation, visited me.
She asked me how I was doing.
I told her how I felt about my congregation.
Then she told me that she had a similar experience.
And she shared with me a Watchtower article that helped her.
I made this my next personal study project.
“What do you see when you look at others?
“Do you have the tendency to view what they say or do
“as either black or white,
as if no other colors or shades existed?”
“Having that viewpoint
“would be like a photographer who ignores the large variety
“of brilliant hues and shades in an autumn landscape,
as if only black and white images existed.”
Maybe I’ve been viewing the congregation as “black and white.”
The article then turned my attention to Jesus’ example.
“The spirit, of course, is eager,
but the flesh is weak.”
Why was Jesus able to say such kind words
to his disciples?
Insight is the ability to put yourself
in the other’s place.
Jesus did that with his disciples.
OK, I need to do the same.
She always looks after the children at home.
She also needs time to be refreshed
by association with friends at the Kingdom Hall.
She probably didn’t mean to be rude.
Since we looked like we were having an enjoyable conversation,
she may have just wanted to join us.
The elders are so busy caring for the needs
of the congregation.
I know they’re doing the best they can.
I want to do what I can to make their job easier.
Miki,
you are such a beautiful Christian.
We’re so glad to have you in our congregation.
“The insight of a man certainly
“slows down his anger, and it is beauty on his part
to overlook an offense.”
