en.text: Did Jesus explain to his disciples
how his perfect body came to be?
Did he take the time to do that?
We don’t know.
But what we do know is that how he used
that perfect body when he was on earth
has a profound effect upon our relationship with Jehovah God.
When we meditate and think about that,
that’s what we want to focus on in our discussion this morning.
But how did that body come about?
Let’s find out.
Let’s open our Bibles, please, to Luke chapter 1,
Luke chapter 1, and we’re going to look at verse 31.
Now, the angel Gabriel, in speaking to Mary, he says:
“Look! you will become pregnant
“and [you will] give birth to a son,
and you are to name him Jesus.”
‘Pregnant, me? I’m a virgin. How can that happen?’
Jehovah employed his holy spirit
in transferring the perfect life force of his only-begotten Son
to the womb of Mary,
thus causing conception.
Jehovah would cancel out any imperfection
that would be passed on to the child,
thereby producing a genetic pattern
that was perfect from its start.
Imperfection was not going to stop Jehovah’s purpose
from being accomplished.
He dealt with that; he handled that.
Very interesting here, too, in verse 35:
“In answer the angel said to her:
“‘Holy spirit will come upon you,
and power of the Most High will overshadow you.’”
So again, holy spirit is involved.
And in some manner, Jehovah guaranteed that it would be a boy,
and then he assured that that developing embryo would be shielded
from the taint of sin and protected from any harmful force.
So there she has this baby boy.
She was a Jewish mother, so no doubt Jesus would have had
some of the physical traits of Mary —his Jewish mother.
However, we need to remember
that he was not another personality;
he was not another person.
He was the only-begotten Son,
and he was able to identify himself as such in due time.
But now imagine Mary giving birth to this little baby,
and she’s holding this little baby in her arms.
Now, how many mothers have said to us when
that baby is born and they’re holding that baby,
and they say: “Look at my baby. It’s perfect.”
But Mary was right; she got it right.
She was the only one that could say, “My baby is perfect.”
She didn’t have to count the toes and the fingers and so forth.
She got it.
But the thought is that
though she didn’t fully understand all the details,
she’s holding this body
and it’s this body that for thirty-three and a half years
is holding the blood that’s going to be poured out
in behalf of mankind as a ransom sacrifice.
But before that blood was going to be poured out,
Jesus was going to use that body in a very special way.
He used his fleshly body to honor Jehovah God.
So again, understanding how
he used that fleshly body to honor Jehovah
has a profound effect upon our relationship with Jehovah.
Let’s see how.
Let’s open our Bibles now to 1 Peter chapter 4.
First Peter chapter 4,
we’re going to read verse 1:
“Since Christ suffered in the flesh [suffered in the flesh],
“you too arm yourselves with the same mental disposition;
“because the person who has suffered in the flesh
has desisted from sins.”
Let’s think about this for a moment.
Christ suffered in the flesh
—that fleshly body.
This is directly related to the issue of sovereignty.
His blood paid the ransom.
But why did Christ suffer in the flesh?
Because he chose to use his fleshly body to honor Jehovah;
he chose to use his fleshly body to defend Jehovah’s sovereignty;
he chose to use that fleshly body to prove that Satan is a liar.
He suffered in the flesh.
On Nisan 14, 33 C.E.,
Jesus allowed himself to be arrested by a mob;
he allowed himself to be subjected to an illegal trial;
he allowed his back to be torn by rivets and scourged through a scourging
and to be nailed —his hands and feet—to a pole.
He allowed that.
And this is why he said at John 10:17:
“This is why the Father loves me.”
‘The Father loves me.
‘Why? Because I surrender my life.
‘No man takes my life from me.
I surrender it of my own initiative.’
Now, that’s the example he set for us.
Now, let’s look at verse 1 again.
This time we see that “b” part where it says:
“Because the person who has suffered in the flesh.”
So who is that? That’s you;
that’s me; we’re the person.
We suffer in the flesh; we desist from sins.
Verse 2:
“So that he [you, me] may live
“the remainder of his time in the flesh,
no more for the desires of men, but for God’s will.”
The fact that Peter draws attention to suffering in the flesh for you and me
—this is what we’re expected to do.
We’re imitating Jesus Christ by doing that.
So here we are in this very special week of activity.
We think deeply upon the ransom sacrifice;
we think deeply about how Jesus used his life.
And we have opportunity to do that.
For example, some ask,
‘Why do we pass the emblems on Memorial night?’
They say, ‘If in a large congregation there are so many there,
‘wouldn’t it be more practical
‘if the servers just stood at the end of the aisle?
‘And if someone wanted to partake of the emblems,
‘they would just nod or give a sign to the server
‘and he would give them to that person.
Look at the time we would save.’
But that’s not the pattern in the Scriptures;
that’s not what Jesus did;
that’s not the procedure that was instituted.
We’re following the Biblical pattern.
But in addition to that
—in the actual passing of the emblems—
what does that do?
That deepens our appreciation
as we see the bread passed;
as we see the wine passed.
We are able to understand the sacred things
that are discussed even more so that evening.
And we’re able to get involved.
Our feelings get involved.
That event burns into our memory.
So this Friday as those emblems are being passed
—as the bread is being passed—
now you might say, ‘But I’ve been to so many Memorials.’
And some in our family have been to decades worth of Memorials.
But how about this Friday we do something different?
We just—as that bread passes— we just think;
we just take a moment to reflect
on what that bread represents.
And we ask ourselves:
‘Can I think of one way
‘that I can use my body, my mind,
‘my energy
‘to better worship Jehovah God?
‘Is there one way that I can do better?
‘To what extent am I slaving for others
‘as Jesus Christ did?
‘Like Jesus Christ,
‘to what extent am I pummeling my body
‘and leading it as a slave
‘even if it takes drastic measures
‘—at times with self-control—
‘to make sure that I am giving an answer
to the one who is taunting my heavenly Father?’
When we examine the life of Jesus Christ,
it’s as if he said to the Devil,
it’s as if he declared:
‘You want to attack my Father?
‘You go through me.
‘You’re going to go through me
‘because I am Michael (“Who is like God?”).
‘No one attacks my God.
‘I am the chief defender of His sovereignty.
‘I am the champion of my God.
‘I am the chief vindicator of Him.
That’s who I am.’
And we take that same stance —that same posture.
Someone wants to attack our heavenly Father?
‘You want to attack my heavenly Father, Devil?
‘You go through me; you go through me.
‘And my integrity, my obedience,
‘my faithful course, you know what it will do?
‘It will embarrass you;
‘it’s going to push you back; it’s going to humiliate you;
‘it’s going to disgrace you because I am using my body
as Jesus Christ did to honor my heavenly Father.’

cn.text: 耶稣有没有告诉过门徒
他完美的身体是怎么来的？
他解释过这件事吗？
我们不知道
但我们知道
他在地上时怎样运用自己完美的身体
而这对我们跟上帝的关系有深远的影响
今天我们就会谈谈这件事
这也会帮助我们好好沉思
那么耶稣的身体是怎么来的呢？
让我们看看
我们打开路加福音第1章
路加福音第1章，我们会读第31节

加百列说
“你会怀孕
生下一个儿子
你要给他取名叫耶稣。”
“怀孕？怎么可能？我还是个处女！”
耶和华用他的神圣力量
将他独生子完美的生命
转移到马利亚的腹中
马利亚就怀了孕
耶和华会消除所有不完美的遗传基因
以免影响到这个孩子
这样他从一开始就有完美的基因
不完美这个问题
绝对不会影响耶和华实现自己的旨意
他解决了这个问题
接下来的第35节也值得留意
“天使回答说
神圣力量会临到你身上
至高者的力量会保护你。”
所以，这件事跟神圣力量有关
耶和华确保
这个孩子是个男孩
并确保这个胚胎在成长期间
不会受到罪的影响
也不会受到任何伤害
现在，马利亚抱着刚出生的小耶稣
马利亚是个犹太人
耶稣自然会从母亲那里
遗传一些犹太人的特征
不过
我们要记得
这个孩子跟其他所有孩子都不一样
他是上帝的独生子
将来他也会知道自己的这个身份
现在想象一下
马利亚刚生下小耶稣
他把这个小宝宝抱在怀里
我们可能见过
很多妈妈都会抱着刚出生的宝宝说
“看看我的孩子，多完美啊！”
马利亚的确可以这样说
只有她这个母亲可以说
“我的孩子真完美！”
她不用去数孩子有几根脚趾头
有几根手指头
她知道他是完美的
虽然马利亚不完全了解所有的细节
但就是她怀里抱着的这个孩子的身体
在33年半以后，就是这个身体里的血
会流出来
成为赎价
而这个赎价可以拯救全人类
但是，在他的血流出来之前
耶稣会以一种特别的方式运用他的身体
他会运用这个身体使耶和华上帝得到荣耀
所以，我们了解耶稣怎样运用他的身体
使耶和华得到荣耀
会对我们跟上帝的关系有很大的影响
他是怎么做的呢？
我们打开圣经到彼得前书
第4章
彼得前书第4章
我们会读出第1节
“既然基督在身体上受过苦
［在身体上受过苦］
你们也要用同样的心志武装自己
因为在身体上受苦的人已经停止犯罪。”
我们想想看
基督在身体上受过苦
这件事
跟至高统治权的争议直接有关
基督用他的血付出赎价
但他为什么要在身体上受苦呢？
因为他选择用他的身体使耶和华得到荣耀
他选择用他的身体捍卫耶和华的至高统治权
他选择用他的身体证明撒但是个说谎者
所以他要在身体上受苦
公元33年尼散月十四日
耶稣甘愿被暴民抓住
甘愿接受不公正的审讯
甘愿被人鞭打

他的背部被人打得鲜血淋漓
他的手脚被人钉在柱上
没错

“父亲爱我。”
“父亲爱我
为什么呢？
因为我牺牲生命

经文提到
“在身体上受苦的人”

是你，也是我
我们在身体上受苦，已经停止犯罪

耶稣也不是这样做的
这不是当初设立的安排

但这一次的耶稣牺牲纪念聚会
在传递饼和酒的时候
我们可以试试这样做吗？
传递饼的时候

这个饼，象征什么？
问问自己
“在哪一方面
我可以用我的身体、思想、精力
来更好地崇拜耶和华呢？
我能在哪个方面做得更好呢？
到什么程度
我可以效法耶稣为其他人服务呢？
到什么程度
我可以效法耶稣痛打自己
使身体成为听命的奴隶呢？
哪怕要采取果断的行动
显出极大的自制
我也会竭尽全力回应撒但的讥讽
维护我的天父吗？”
我们仔细看看耶稣基督的一生
他好像在对魔鬼撒但宣告
“你想攻击我的父亲吗？
先过我这关
我是米迦勒
我名字的意思是“谁能跟上帝相比？”
谁也不能攻击上帝
我会捍卫上帝的至高统治权
我会全心拥护上帝
我会全力支持他
这就是我的立场。”
我们也要有同样的态度、同样的立场
有谁想攻击我们的天父吗？
“魔鬼，你想攻击我的天父吗？
先过我这一关
你得先过我这一关
我的忠义、我的服从、我忠贞的一生
都会让你丢脸
让你羞愧
让你颜面尽失
让你无地自容
因为我效法基督
用我的身体使天父得到荣耀！”

en.text: I think that when most think of Puerto Rico,
they think of sun, beach,
mofongo, good food,
and just a beautiful, loving, and joyful people.
But they don’t realize there’s a lot of spiritual activity
that’s been taking place on this island for decades.
And our goal is to make sure everybody on the island
knows about this beautiful work taking place.
Jesus said that we would be
“one flock, one shepherd.”
And sometimes if you live on an island
in the middle of the ocean, you may feel a little bit isolated.
But when the whole world comes to town and you get to experience it
on your own soil, it is just a tremendous experience.
And that’s what we’ve seen here in Puerto Rico.
The brothers have just been so excited about the program.
You can see Jehovah has really blessed the brothers and sisters in Puerto Rico.
Having delegates coming from the different countries
—from Cuba, Brazil, Guyana, the United States—
it’s drawn them together in love.
It’s just been like a big hug
for the whole branch territory.
Welcome, brothers.
We hope you will enjoy this spiritual food.
We love you very much!
Well, we heard about the convention here,
and so we applied immediately because we had been here 50 years before
—to the first international convention here.
Brother Knorr encouraged us to go into Spanish,
so we did —50 years ago.
We wanted to come back.
Well, I think of the work the brothers and sisters
have put into preparing for this convention.
We think of the negotiations that were taking place
over a year ago and then the preparation for the delegates
and all the work with the audio and video.
It really shows what these brothers have done and all the crews
and their families in making this happen.
And that just— That’s all out of love.
The brothers have gone above and beyond.
Nothing has stood in their way.
Well, as soon as I came through the door
from the baggage claim area,
there was a huge group of brothers and sisters
and everyone applauding.
It just made us feel like one big family.
Besides the overwhelming heat was the overwhelming love.
I feel like it’s been a lesson in hospitality,
you know, because the friends have been just so welcoming.
And I feel like it’s just made an imprint on my heart.
Well, I think the Puerto Rican and really the Caribbean spirit
has a lot of enthusiasm, a lot of hugging, a lot of kissing, a lot of love.
When there are two Puerto Ricans together, they sound like ten.
I already cried so much.
You have made me cry again.
Thank you, thank you, thank you!
When I’m on stage signing,
I see brothers crying and I realize
that I’m doing this for Jehovah and the brothers.
The highlight for me is always going out in the ministry
in the countries that we visit.
That’s a memory that I’ll take home with me
because when we unite together
in doing our preaching work,
that’s like the best form of unity that we can have.
We knocked on the door, and there came a lady,
and we invited her to the convention.
And she said,
“Oh, I think I can make it on Friday.”
I came because of an invitation that I received, which is this one.
Actually, she called me this morning at 6:30 a.m.
I was not going to answer the phone, but I did.
And it was her.
She was telling me that she was coming.
I liked the theme of the resurrection very much because,
well, it’s been two years since I lost my father
and I haven’t been able to get over that.
It helped me think more about God,
and it gives me comfort to know that my dad is OK.
This convention is so beautiful.
It moves you to the core.
You know, at this convention
we learned about loyalty,
and we learned that loyalty is really an aspect of love.
And so we had an opportunity to show our love
for our brothers and our love for Jehovah.
And it helped us to understand loyalty in just a whole different way.
And I think that when the brothers go home,
that picture of their desire to be loyal to Jehovah
and to be loyal to our brotherhood
is going to be fixed in their mind.
It’s going to be something unforgettable.

cn.text: 听到波多黎各
大部分人会立刻想到阳光、沙滩、美食
传统料理莫封戈，以及热情友善又快乐的人
其实很多人不知道
传道工作在这岛上也有几十年的历史了
我们的目标就是让传道工作
在这座岛上无人不知、无人不晓
耶稣说我们会“合成一群，归一个牧人”
有时身在汪洋大海中的一座小岛上
会让你觉得有点孤零零的
但当世界各地的人涌进你所在的这块土地
这样的经历会让你永生难忘
波多黎各的弟兄姊妹就有这样的感觉
他们都非常期待这次的大会
耶和华真的赐福给波多黎各的弟兄姊妹
让他们能够招待来自不同国家的宾客
包括古巴、巴西、圭亚那、美国等
他们因爱而团结一致
这整个地区就像被温情大大拥抱着
欢迎你们，希望你们喜欢这个大会
我们非常爱你们！
我们听说这里要举办大会，就立即申请
因为我们50年前来过
参加这里第一次的国际大会
当时诺尔弟兄鼓励我们学西班牙语，我们就学了
我们很想再回到这里
弟兄姊妹为这次的大会做了许多预备工作
我们一年前就开始开会讨论
为外国代表作出规划
也准备大会的影音器材
为了让一切可以顺利进行
弟兄们、工作人员和他们的家人都付出很多
也显出很大的爱心
弟兄们尽心尽力地准备
什么都不能阻碍他们
我一走出机场的行李领取处
就看到一大群弟兄姊妹在鼓掌欢迎
大家就像一家人一样
这里天气很热
但也热情洋溢
他们都慷慨好客
弟兄姊妹非常热情地欢迎我们
这个感觉会永远深印在我心里
我觉得加勒比海地区的人都充满热情
常常拥抱和亲吻，给人满满的爱
就算只有两个波多黎各人在一起
会听起来像有十个人
我哭好几次了
现在又想哭了
谢谢你们，谢谢，谢谢，谢谢，谢谢！
我在台上打手语的时候
看到弟兄们哭了
我才明白这都是为了耶和华和弟兄姊妹做的
我最喜欢的就是能够在举办大会的国家传道
我回家后还会记得弟兄姊妹一起传道的情景
因为这最能显出团结一致的精神
我们敲门后，有一位女子出来
我们邀请她参加大会
她说:“喔......我应该可以参加星期五的”
我是收到一张邀请单才来的
就是这张
其实今天早上6点半有一通电话打来
我本来不想接的
但接了之后才发现是那个女子
她说会来参加大会
我很喜欢关于复活的节目
因为......我父亲在两年前去世了
我到现在都还很难受
演讲让我多想想上帝
而且知道爸爸死后的真实情况
也让我感到安慰
大会实在太棒了，让大家非常感动
我们从这次大会学到忠贞这个特质
而忠贞是爱心的一个层面
我们有机会表现对弟兄姊妹以及对耶和华的爱
这帮助我们从另一个角度来理解忠贞的含意
我觉得，这次大会让大家更渴望
对耶和华和弟兄姊妹表现忠贞
这样的想法会深深地刻印在大家的脑海里
这绝对永志难忘

title: M. 스티븐 레트: 남편 여러분, 아내를 자기 자신처럼 사랑하십시오 (솔로몬의 노래 8:6)

en.text: My theme for this little discussion is
“Husbands, Love Your Wife as Yourself.”
What did Jesus say
was the second greatest commandment?
Well, you’re familiar with it.
At Matthew 22:39, he said:
“You must love your neighbor as yourself.”
Now, what an excellent illustration
is contained in this second greatest commandment!
If you think about it, we just naturally,
inherently, love ourselves, don’t we?
And we show love in many ways.
So Jesus is saying,
“Work hard to show the same love for others
you show for yourself.”
But, now, thinking of husbands
as addressed in our theme,
who is a husband’s closest neighbor?
Well, his wife.
So especially must a husband work hard
to show the love that he shows for himself just naturally and then
to show that love for his wife.
Now, what are some specific ways
that husbands just naturally love themselves?
Well, let’s talk about five.
And undoubtedly you can think of many others
that could be discussed during this discussion.
But number one:
A husband feeds himself.
Ephesians 5:29 says in part:
“For no man ever hated his own body,
but he feeds . . . it.”
Well, what does loving our wife, now, as ourself require?
Well, for one thing, we certainly would make sure
we provide for the food and for other material needs
that our wife has.
And regarding this, I think of our brothers
in concentration camps in Nazi Germany.
Food was very scarce.
But our brothers, even then, from their meager food ration
would share food with other brothers,
even, in some cases, with worldly people.
Well, similarly, a husband would do without himself,
if necessary, in order to provide what his wife really needs.
But even more importantly, an extended application,
he would make sure that she is well-fed spiritually.
He must make sure that she has opportunity
to benefit from periods of personal study,
congregation meetings, assemblies, conventions,
and family worship.
But now let’s talk about a second way
that a husband just naturally loves himself:
We cherish ourselves.
Ephesians 5:29 says in part:
“For no man ever hated his own body,
but he . . . cherishes it.”
Now, what does cherish mean?
Well, according to the dictionary,
it means to treat with affection and tenderness,
treasure, value, attach importance to.
See, because of this feeling we have toward ourselves,
we try to get rest when we’re sick or tired;
we try to be with friends and loved ones;
we play games; we exercise; we do things we enjoy.
Periodically, we treat ourselves, don’t we,
because we cherish ourselves?
So, what does loving our wife as ourself require?
Well, it certainly means more
than just being able to put up with our mate.
It means cherishing her,
cultivating affection, or fondness, for her.
Think of this: At Proverbs 8:31,
it says that Jesus in his prehuman existence
was fond of humans.
Now, don’t you think that fondness he had for us
made it easier for him to come to the earth,
take the difficult assignment he took,
and even die for us because he was fond of us?
Well, similarly,
if wives are cherished by their husbands
—if husbands are fond of their wives—
it’ll make it so much easier to forgive them,
to even die for them, if necessary, in the future.
But if we’re going to have this proper feeling, like Jehovah,
we have to focus on the good qualities of our wife, see,
not the flaws, the imperfections.
And as one of the brothers commented on
(I love the thoughts in The Watchtower comments):
“Love is best sensed when it is expressed.
“How vital that marriage mates
“not allow the activities of daily life
to rob them of exchanging expressions of affection!”
But now let’s get a third way
that husbands just naturally love themselves:
We adorn ourselves.
First Timothy 2:9 speaks
of women “adorn[ing] themselves in appropriate dress.”
Well, husbands try to do the same thing.
And in adorning ourselves, we try to cover over
and minimize our flaws
and cover our bulges, our blemishes.
We try to make ourselves look as good as possible, don’t we?
Well, what does loving our wife as ourself require?
For one thing, we certainly wouldn’t shine a spotlight on her flaws.
We wouldn’t do this in the presence of others.
We would try hard not to even do it in our own mind.
Rather, we seek to cover over minor sins and transgressions,
as encouraged at Proverbs 19:11, where it says:
“It is beauty . . . to overlook an offense.”
So we work hard to adorn our wives
—make her look as good as possible—
in the eyes of others, even in our own mind.
Well, let’s get a fourth way
that husbands just naturally love themselves:
We take steps to heal ourselves
when we’re sick or injured.
Mark 5:26
talks about a woman who was very sick.
‘She suffered at the hands of many physicians;
‘she spent all her resources;
she didn’t get any better; she got worse.’
But the point is,
she was really trying hard to heal herself.
Well, husbands try to do the same thing.
So if we’re sick or injured, we try to get extra rest,
we’ll buy medicine, we’ll take vitamins,
we’ll make an appointment with the doctor,
we’ll pursue therapy.
See, we try to get well.
What does loving our wife as ourself require then?
Well, we would certainly do all within our power
if she’s sick or injured
to try to help her get well.
But even more importantly,
if she happens to be ailing somewhat spiritually,
we would do everything we can possibly do
to help her get well spiritually.
What would be something, perhaps, we could do?
Well, Proverbs 12:18 says:
“The tongue of the wise is a healing”
—so the using of wise expressions.
Also, Proverbs 16:24:
“Pleasant sayings are a honeycomb,
“sweet to the soul
and a healing to the bones.”
So, “pleasant sayings,” we would use these
to try to help her get well spiritually.
But now here’s one more, a fifth way
that husbands just naturally love themselves:
We make allowances,
excuses, if we make mistakes.
Husbands who make mistakes
are often heard blaming it
on their heredity
or maybe the environment,
their blood-sugar level,
how much sleep they got or didn’t get the night before,
the weather, and so forth.
We tend to well understand our own limitations, don’t we?
And we allow for that.
Well, what about loving our wife as ourself?
We’d make the same allowances for her
—being positive, imputing good motives to her.
If she speaks a little roughly or acts a little thoughtlessly,
we’ll try to discern the feelings
behind the words or actions.
We’ll make allowance, especially if we can discern
that she’s under some kind of emotional pressure.
We’ll make that allowance for her like we would for ourselves.
Well, there we have five ways
that we as husbands show love for ourselves.
We feed, cherish, adorn,
try to heal ourselves;
and we make allowances, excuses,
when we make mistakes.
Let’s work hard to show the same love
in those five areas for our dear, beloved wives.
And I’m sure, as we said, you can think of other ways
that husbands just naturally love themselves.
But what a rich illustration Jesus gave!
And interestingly, he took it even a step further.
He further expanded the illustration
at John 13:34.
You’re familiar with this, 13:34.
He said: “I am giving you a new commandment,
“that you love one another;
“just as I have loved you,
you also love one another.”
So he’s saying that we should have
even deeper love for our brothers
—which would definitely include our Christian wives—
a deeper love than we have for ourselves.
And that deeper love would move us to treat
our dear wives even better
than we treat ourselves.

cn.text: 今天我要讨论的主题是
“丈夫们，要爱妻子好像爱自己”
耶稣提到的第二条
最重要的诫命是什么呢？
相信大家都很熟悉
马太福音22:39的经文
这里说“要爱人如己”
这样的说法很有意思
想想看
我们天生就会爱自己，不是吗？
不管发生什么事
我们都会好好地照顾自己
所以，耶稣的意思是
“要努力用爱自己的方式来爱其他人”
那么，我们现在就来谈谈丈夫吧
丈夫最亲密的人是谁呢？
就是他的妻子
所以，丈夫就更要努力
用爱自己的天性来爱妻子
那么，一般来说
丈夫会怎样爱自己呢？
让我们来谈谈五个方面
相信你会在接下来的讨论中
想到更多的例子
第一，丈夫不会让自己挨饿
以弗所书5:29的开头的一部分说
从来没有人恨恶自己的身体，只会喂养
所以，丈夫可以怎样爱妻子
好像爱自己呢？
丈夫一定会为妻子
提供所需的食物和其他的物质需求
这让我想起
德国纳粹时期在集中营的弟兄们
当时粮食短缺
但弟兄们还是会将自己分到的一点点粮食
分给需要的弟兄
甚至分给其他人
同样，丈夫一定会尽力照顾妻子
甚至甘愿作出牺牲
更重要的是
丈夫会确保妻子在信仰上受到良好的照顾
他会努力让妻子能够从个人研读
会众聚会、大会
及家庭崇拜中获得帮助
现在我们来谈谈第二个天性
丈夫会爱惜自己的身体
以弗所书5:29接着说
从来没有人恨恶自己的身体
只会爱护
那么，什么是爱护呢？
根据字典
这是向人表达亲切情感
重视并珍惜对方的一种美好特质
的确，因为我们懂得爱护自己
所以当我们生病或疲倦的时候
就会让自己好好休息一下
跟朋友或家人聚一聚
玩个小游戏、运动一下
或做自己喜欢做的事
有时，懂得爱护自己
也会让自己好好享受一下，不是吗？
所以，丈夫可以怎样爱妻子
好像爱自己呢？
只跟妻子一起相处是不够的
丈夫应该疼惜妻子
跟她培养感情，好好宠爱她
想想看，箴言8:31说
耶稣降世为人之前
所爱的离不开世间的人
耶稣愿意接受艰难的任务
来到地上，甚至为我们而死
原因就是他深爱我们
同样
如果丈夫疼惜自己的妻子，深爱她
那么当妻子犯错时
丈夫就会更容易原谅她
在未来必要的时候
甚至为妻子牺牲生命也在所不惜
丈夫如果要像耶和华一样
对妻子有这种爱
就必须多想想妻子的优点
而不是她的缺点或是不完美的地方
一位弟兄提过一篇守望台文章
我很喜欢这个守望台的论点
把爱意表达出来最令人心醉
千万别让生活琐事
妨碍你们彼此表达爱意！
第三个天性
丈夫会好好打扮自己
提摩太前书2:9说
女人服装整齐端庄，装饰自己
其实，男人也是一样
我们也会好好打扮自己
掩饰身材的缺点或瑕疵
谁不想让自己看起来更好看呢？
那么，丈夫可以怎样爱妻子
好像爱自己呢？
好好打扮妻子的一个方法是
我们绝对不要数落妻子的缺点
绝对不要在别人面前这样做
甚至也不要在心里埋怨妻子
做丈夫的应该要试着
不计较妻子所犯的一些小错误
就像在箴言19:11说的
不追究过犯，就是美德
所以，丈夫会好好打扮自己的妻子
让妻子在别人面前
甚至在我们心中
美丽又漂亮
第四个天性是什么呢？
丈夫生病或受伤时
自然会想努力恢复健康
马可福音5:26提到一个重病的妇女
她看过许多医生，吃尽无数苦头
资财耗尽了
病情不但没有好转，反而日趋恶化
这里的重点是
这个妇女努力想治好自己的病
男人也一样
当我们生病或受伤时
我们会好好休息、吃药
吃维他命、看医生
寻找不同的疗法等
我们都想要恢复健康
那么，丈夫可以怎样爱妻子
好像爱自己呢？
当妻子生病或受伤时
我们一定会尽全力帮助她赶快好起来
如果妻子在信仰方面生病了
做丈夫的一样要尽全力
帮助妻子恢复健康
丈夫可以做些什么呢？
明智人的舌如良药
就是用良言来鼓励她
箴言16:24也说
可喜的言语是蜂巢的蜜
叫人心甜，医治筋骨
没错，丈夫可以用“可喜的言语”
来帮助妻子恢复健康
最后, 第五个天性是
当丈夫犯错时
自然会为自己找借口, 找台阶下
做错事的丈夫常常说
我天生就是这样啊
或说
这是大环境的问题
血糖太低、睡眠不足
天气的问题等等
我们常常会为自己的弱点找理由

en.text: The trunk of the African elephant
is an impressive multitool.
It is both flexible
and strong.
It can pick up a blade of grass
or uproot a tree.
Some elephants can use their trunks to feed themselves
around 270 kilograms (600 lbs) of vegetation
every day.
With their trunks,
they can suck water like a straw,
spray like a fountain,
and swim with a snorkel.
The trunk can give a gentle touch,
give a strong push,
or sound a warning trumpet.
Engineers admire the elephant trunk’s remarkable flexibility.
This comes from having no bone.
Instead, it contains
about 150,000 muscle units
—an incredible marriage of strength and structure.
Inspired by the elephant’s trunk, researchers are designing robots
for the future with greater flexibility.
Industrial design often can be made better by copying
the perfectly beautiful solutions in the natural world.
What do you think?
Did the elephant’s trunk evolve?
Or . . .

My faith in Jehovah is stronger now.
I think that I am happier knowing Jehovah

You understand that singing is a huge part of our worship,
and Jehovah wants us to use it.

en.text: It’s not easy raising kids in the truth,
and I had ten.
I learned the truth when I was 19.
Some Witnesses came to preach in our town,
and my father offered them a place to stay.
He spoke with them all through the night
and then announced excitedly that he had found the truth.
Eventually, I was baptized in the 1950’s.
My husband was favorable toward the truth
but got involved in political affairs in the community,
and from there he began his political career.
When I read 1 Peter 3:1, 2,
I understood that I needed to be in subjection to my husband,
with the hope that he could be won over
“without a word” by means of my conduct.
When my children were young,
I made a weekly Bible study program for each of them,
and as they grew up,
the older kids helped me with their younger siblings.
I remember Mom always made an effort to teach me how to preach.
I would write presentations for the ministry on pieces of paper,
and the kids would practice while they did their chores around the house.
We set aside time one day a week for our family study.
It could be anything
—a sack of potatoes, a sack of flour, or a house plant.
She would tell me:
“Imagine that this is a person you meet in field service.
What would you say to them?”
When I finished, she would say to me,
“The way you did it just now,
do it like that when you go out in the ministry.”
My mom was very creative.
She would assign us to play the part of different Bible characters.
My mom taught us to appreciate the truth
through her example.
I served as a regular pioneer for many years,
and I encouraged my kids to reach out for spiritual goals.
My daughter left home at the age of 18
to serve as a special pioneer.
Later, my oldest son did the same.
These two proved to be excellent examples for their younger brothers.
Raising my son Noé was a challenge.
He was the youngest,
and at a very young age, he was diagnosed with epilepsy.
Despite his limitations,
he was able to serve as a ministerial servant
and regular pioneer.
He fought his illness for more than 40 years,
before passing away recently.
Losing my husband in death dealt me another blow.
Now my health and my memory are fading.
I can’t do as much
in the ministry as before.
But even so, thanks to the help of the brothers in the congregation,
I’m not giving up.
Even though my husband was not a Witness,
I respected him as the head of the family.
I will never forget the moment
when my husband asked me to study the Bible with him.
I remember that my eldest son gave the talk,
and his father was among the candidates for baptism.
Forty-two years after I received the Kingdom message,
my husband was baptized.
Another great blessing was seeing my children
grow in the truth and use their youth to serve Jehovah.
Some have served as special pioneers,
circuit overseers, or in Bethel.
If it wasn’t for her help
and the support of my siblings,
perhaps we wouldn’t be part of the organization today.
But thanks to her, we started out on the best course in life.
Words cannot express how grateful I am to her.
I now find great joy
in seeing my grandchildren and great-grandchildren
follow their parents’ example.
Thinking about all I have experienced
in over 60 years of service to Jehovah
—raising my ten children in the truth,
my husband becoming a servant of Jehovah,
and seeing 30 members of my family in full-time service—
I can do nothing but thank Jehovah
for his blessings.
It’s been worth all the effort.

en.text: Thousands of our sisters have been active
for many years in that “large army” of women.
Bertille Kupelian,
a special pioneer in West Virginia, in the United States,
entered the full-time service in 1958.
In that time, she’s helped more than 60 people to baptism.
How has her outlook toward the ministry
kept her going for almost 60 years?
My father was opposed
to the truth as I was growing up,
but my mother was very, very zealous.
I knew the things my mother was teaching me was the truth.
I knew that this was what I was going to do.
And it was not easy, but we did it.
I was Daddy’s girl,
but my mom made sure
that I and my siblings knew the truth.
And she studied with us when no other children
in the congregation had Bible studies at home.
Of course, we kind of kicked and didn’t like it,
but I was glad she did it.
My mother was a very, very positive person,
and although she had the opposition,
I saw how she dealt with it
and how firm and determined she was.
And that was something she taught us.
It’s a mind-set.
You know, your mind is a wonderful thing.
It can really influence you toward good or maybe not so good.
And so then, I was determined in my mind
that I was going to serve Jehovah then.
In our congregation, there were brothers and sisters of the anointed.
They were always very kind to me,
and they encouraged me.
I worked in service with them.
And I thought, ‘That’s the way I want to be.’
Children like attention.
And so then, if you give them attention
—you talk with them
and ask if you could work with them in the ministry
and help them prepare a presentation
and go over it and over it
so that they’re ready for the ministry
—then they’ll enjoy it more.
That was one of the things that the anointed
did in the congregation where I was.
They paid attention to me, and I loved it.
How I learned to teach was I think about the person,
and I think about their situation,
and I try to think in my mind what they are thinking,
and I work on that
and think of what kind of scriptures I can find to help them.
And so then,
I try to pattern our studies
to incorporate some of those things.
There are always challenges.
Some of the winters right on the lake where I lived were very harsh.
And my trailer was parked in such a way that every time
the wind blew and the snow came and the ice came,
it sealed the door.
And so then, I carried a big knife in my car,
and I would have to cut around the door
to get the door to open —break the ice seal.
It was interesting.
I had some opposition in the territories,
and one was this lady who was very irate.
And she went to kick me, and she kicked me right in the stomach,
and so then, anyway, I dismissed myself.
Then, a while later, it was time to work the territory again.
Nobody wanted to go there, and we didn’t have do-not-calls,
I don’t think, at that time, at least there wasn’t any in the territory.
So then anyway, I called by and I mentioned to her:
“Why, hello there.
I know I’ve had the opportunity to talk with you before.”
Yes, she remembered.
And I said, “Well, perhaps you were having a bad day that day.”
I hit a lull when I had few Bible studies,
and so I prayed diligently to Jehovah:
“Jehovah, help me. I need Bible studies.”
And then you have to be out there looking for them.
Well, I’ve lost my father, my mother,
my sister, my brother.
Well, naturally you feel at a loss,
but Jehovah strengthened me, and the friends strengthened me,
and I kept busy in the ministry.
But again, it goes back to that mind-set.
Are you going to let the challenge beat you,
or are you going to beat the challenge?
You and Jehovah can beat the challenge.
You know, discouragement is one of Satan’s biggest tools.
And I always tell myself,
‘I’m not going to let Satan beat me down.’
As far as health is concerned, my everyday health is very good.
But I have a leg that drives me crazy.
I think back to Jacob.
He served Jehovah with a limp.
And then I think of Paul.
And so then, those things keep you humble.
I’ve prayed and prayed and prayed about it,
but just like with the apostle Paul,
it didn’t disappear.
And so then, I just say: “Patch me up till Armageddon.
It’ll disappear then.”
If your mind is made up that this is what you’re going to do,
this is your life, this is what Jehovah wants you to do,
and so then you do it.
I’ve seen how he’s kept me going.
You know that I’ve needed work; I’ve needed money;
I’ve needed strength.
I’ve needed companionship
because a lot of times I’m in the ministry by myself.
I talk to Jehovah.
And so then, he’s always there for me.
I definitely want to keep pioneering
or serving Jehovah the best I can,
regardless of what comes up.
There is nothing more joyful
than to see that you have helped somebody to live forever.
Well, how much better could it be?
Sister Kupelian had a profound effect on those she witnessed to.
I know this because she found me in the door-to-door ministry
when I was 14 years old.
At that age, I had the goal to be a doctor.
One night after the meeting, Bertille said to me,
“Well, you know, in the new world,
we won’t need doctors because Jesus will do all the healing.”
Honestly, that hit me hard
because I wanted to help people as well as provide for my mother.
But she added,
“What we will need are teachers.”
I thought that was a good idea.
Still focused on a career, I had one type of teacher in mind,
but she had another.
Through her patience and reasoning,
she helped me to become the most important kind of teacher
—a teacher of God’s Word.
Is there someone like Sister Kupelian in your congregation?
We are grateful for these sisters’ zealous spirit
and for the personal interest they show toward us.
And we’re sure Jehovah values them like we do.

en.text: When I started learning sign language,
it just seemed to come natural for me.
After I transferred to the congregation,
I remember feeling so happy.
I was pioneering and really enjoying
this new way of communicating.
It’s funny how the thing you love can also be
the thing that tests you.
Soon, I took the test for a sign-language interpreter.
I couldn’t believe I passed!
I loved my new job.
My hope was that it would support my pioneering
and maybe
allow me to travel one day to a country
and preach where there was a need for sign language.
My boss was very happy with my work,
so much so that he began to give me more.
Everyone seemed appreciative,
and the extra money didn’t hurt.
I was handling it all fine.
Ahh, OK, for a while.
My boss asked me to work full-time
for a few months to get some extra training.
The raise could help me
with planning my trip abroad.
I knew my parents would be concerned.
I knew because I felt it too.
I was already dragging physically.
But then again, it would only be for a few months.
I was really torn.
Dad kindly commended me
for having good goals and trying my best to work toward them.
Then he showed me a scripture that really helped me,
1 Timothy 4:16:
“Pay constant attention to yourself and to your teaching.
“Persevere in these things,
“for by doing this you will save both yourself
and those who listen to you.”
He helped me
to see that Timothy set spiritual goals for himself while growing up.
But Paul was now telling him,
“Don’t stop!”
Even though Timothy was a grown spiritual man,
Paul encouraged him to continue setting new spiritual goals,
in fact, to ‘persevere in them.’
What was I persevering in?
I kindly turned down the offer
and explained to my boss that I’d like to keep my hours
to a minimum
so I could support my number one job.
It might take me longer to save my money,
but I’ll make that trip one day
with Jehovah’s help
and a little perseverance.

en.text: The theme for our program is
“The Women Proclaiming the Good News.”
Sadly, throughout human history
women have been subjected to injustice, violence, and abuse.
Why is that?
The Bible explains.
In the latter part of Genesis 3:16,
notice what God says:
“Your longing will be for your husband,
and he will dominate you.”
When God said that Adam would “dominate” his wife,
God was not indicating His approval of the subjugation of woman by man.
He was simply foretelling the sad consequences
of sin on the first couple.
So abuse of women is a direct outcome
of the sinful nature of humans, not of God’s will.
Right down to our day,
rarely have women been accorded
the dignity that God wants them to receive.
However, Jehovah makes clear in his Word, the Bible,
that women and men have equal standing before him.
In fact, he indicated that women would play a vital role
in the outworking of his purpose.
Our theme is based on Psalm 68:11.
Let’s read it:
“Jehovah gives the command;
the women proclaiming the good news are a large army.”
Those words were inspired by God.
But what did the psalmist have in mind when he penned them?
The context of Psalm 68
shows that David was praising Jehovah as a God of saving acts.
From the time of their Exodus from Egypt,
the men of Israel often had to fight against enemy nations.
With Jehovah’s help, they defeated them.
And the entire nation would then rejoice
over the victory Jehovah had given them.
The first of the victory celebrations recorded in the Bible
was at the time that Jehovah gave his people
the victory over Pharaoh and the Egyptians who were pursuing them.
Exodus 15:20, 21
tells what happened after this miraculous victory:
“Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister,
“took a tambourine in her hand,
“and all the women followed her with tambourines and with dances.
“Miriam sang in response to the men:
“‘Sing to Jehovah,
“‘for he has become highly exalted.
The horse and its rider he has hurled into the sea.’”
Picture that scene.
There were an estimated three million people
in the nation of Israel.
Imagine —out of that large number,
“all the women” were dancing and singing praises to Jehovah.
That was undoubtedly a large army!
What a great shout of praise to Jehovah that was!
Another example was when King Saul and his general David
returned from victory over the Philistines.
Let’s read the account
at 1 Samuel 18:6.
“When David and the others would return
“from striking down the Philistines,
“the women would come out
“from all the cities of Israel
“with song and dances to meet King Saul
“with tambourines,
with rejoicing, and with lutes.”
Notice that the account says
that the women came out of “all the cities”
to greet them with music, song, and dance.
Occasions such as these
were not simply expressions of rejoicing
that originated with human emotion.
Recall that under inspiration, David said:
“Jehovah gives the command;
the women proclaiming the good news are a large army.”
Yes, and Jehovah valued their expressions of praise,
just as he valued the contributions of the men who had engaged in battle.
What about today?
The report for the 2017 service year
shows that there were over 8.3 million publishers
proclaiming the good news throughout the earth.
Keep in mind that in most lands,
it is not unusual for our dear sisters
to make up over half of our special pioneers
and nearly three quarters of those who serve in the regular pioneer work.
In addition, many other sisters
are wholeheartedly spreading the good news of the Kingdom
to the best of their ability within their circumstances.
There are many single-parent families where our sisters
are providing materially and spiritually for their children.
Many of our faithful single sisters
are expending themselves in Jehovah’s service
in theocratic construction and maintenance work,
Bethel service, and serving where the need is greater
—which includes serving in foreign-language fields.
Faithful wives loyally support their husbands
as well as fulfill their own roles as preachers and teachers.
Yes, how Jehovah must be pleased
to see all of you who serve in various ways!
And we’re grateful
for the warm spirit and positive influence
our dear sisters have on our congregations.
Clearly,
Jehovah values this “large army” of sisters.
But does he take note of the individual circumstances
and sacrifices of each sister?
We do not have to wonder.
By means of his Word,
Jehovah makes it evident that he sees
and appreciates each of his servants.
For example,
did you notice when we read the scripture in Exodus chapter 15
that Miriam was described as a “prophetess”?
Evidently, she was privileged to be used
as an instrument of divine communication.
In some instances,
this no doubt included singing songs that were inspired by Jehovah.
Miriam was not the only one in the Scriptures with this designation.
Other women in the Bible record,
such as Anna and Isaiah’s wife,
were also spoken of as prophetesses.
In the book of Judges,
another faithful servant, Deborah, is identified.
Let’s read Judges 4:4, 5:
“Now Deborah, a prophetess,
“the wife of Lappidoth,
“was judging Israel at that time.
“She used to sit under Deborah’s palm tree
“between Ramah and Bethel
“in the mountainous region of Ephraim;
the Israelites would go up to her for judgment.”
Evidently,
Deborah was assigned to settle disputes that arose among Israelites
by giving Jehovah’s answer to problems that came up.
Much later in Israel’s history,
during the reign of faithful King Josiah,
Huldah served as a prophetess.
At 2 Kings 22:8,
we read that while the temple was being repaired,
the original book of the Law was found.
When it was read to Josiah,
he was distraught at seeing how far off
the nation had strayed from Jehovah’s Law.
In verse 13,
he directed the priest, the secretary,
and other influential men:
“Go, inquire of Jehovah in my behalf,
“in behalf of the people,
“and in behalf of all Judah concerning the words of this book
that has been found.”
How did they accomplish this?
Verse 14 continues:
“So Hilkiah the priest,
“Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah
went to Huldah the prophetess.”
It’s interesting that Jehovah used this faithful woman
to convey his direction
and that prominent men and priests
sought her divinely inspired advice.
The Christian Greek Scriptures, however,
do not permit sisters to serve in such a capacity
as did Deborah and other prophetesses
in the nation of Israel.
However,
Titus 2:3, 4
encourages “older women” to display spiritual qualities,
“so that they may advise the younger women”
in spiritual matters.
Let’s read those verses:
“Likewise, let the older women be reverent in behavior,
“not slanderous, not enslaved to a lot of wine,
“teachers of what is good,
“so that they may advise the younger women
to love their husbands, to love their children.”
How we appreciate the spiritually mature sisters among us
who provide such fine assistance to younger sisters
or those who are newer in the truth!
However, today Jehovah has delegated authority to men.
They Scripturally qualify to serve as elders and ministerial servants
in order to serve, guide, and protect his people.
It is obvious that this is not due to a lack of respect
for the gifts of our sisters in the congregation.
In fact, many responsible brothers will acknowledge
that they have benefited from the experience
and practical wisdom of our humble, spiritually mature sisters.
Finally,
think of the outstanding faith
of another woman mentioned in the Bible, Mary.
What an awesome responsibility Jehovah entrusted her with
—bearing and raising his own Son as a human!
We can only imagine the thoughts that were going through her mind
when she was told of this assignment.
But the account in Luke chapter 1
tells us much about her spirituality.
In verse 38,
after the angel Gabriel finished speaking with her,
Mary’s response was simply:
“Look! Jehovah’s slave girl!
May it happen to me according to your declaration.”
She must have wondered how Jehovah would accomplish these things,
but she was humble and obedient.
Faithful men such as Moses and Jeremiah hesitated
when given a challenging assignment from God.
Not Mary!
What a beautiful example she set for all of us
—men and women!
Clearly, Jehovah has always highly valued women.
And we are privileged to serve today
with millions of hardworking sisters.
How pleased Jehovah must be
to see dear sisters serving him humbly and faithfully!
We urge you sisters,
please keep up your good work
and continue to be a positive influence in the congregation.
God has indeed granted you faithful women
the privilege of participating in the fulfillment of the psalmist’s words:
“Jehovah gives the command;
the women proclaiming the good news are a large army.”

cn.text: 这个节目的主题是“宣扬好消息的妇女”
很遗憾的, 在人类的历史中
妇女经常遇到不公平的事
受到暴力伤害或被虐待
为什么会这样呢?
圣经在创世记3:16
上帝说
上帝说亚当会“管辖”他的妻子
这个意思不是说上帝认可男尊女卑
上帝只是预言第一对男女犯罪
所造成的悲惨后果而已
所以, 妇女受虐待
是人类与生俱来的罪所导致的
不是上帝的旨意
从古至今
女性很少能得到应有的尊重
但是
耶和华明确地在他的话语圣经中说明
妇女和男子在上帝面前具有同等的地位
事实上, 上帝指出
妇女在他的旨意中会扮演很重要的角色
我们的主题经文根据诗篇68:11
这是上帝启示写下的话
诗篇的执笔者写下这句话时
他心里想的是什么呢?
在诗篇68篇的内容中
大卫歌颂耶和华的救恩
在以色列人离开埃及之后
男子经常要和其他国族作战
在耶和华的帮助之下
他们战胜敌人
全国都因耶和华使他们获胜而满心喜乐
耶和华帮助他的子民
战胜追赶他们的法老和埃及人
这是圣经第一次记载庆祝胜利的活动
我们看看耶和华施行奇迹
取得胜利后发生的事情
当时, 以色列人大约有三百万
请想象, 这些人中
“所有妇女”一面唱歌
一面跳舞赞美耶和华
这确实是一支大军!
赞美的歌声一定响彻云霄!
另一个例子是
扫罗王和他的将军大卫
战胜非利士人后
凯旋归来时发生的事
我们一起看撒母耳记上18:6
请注意经文说
“妇女们从...各城出来”
用音乐、歌声和舞蹈欢呼迎接他们
这样的场合不只是充满欢乐而已
大卫受启示写道
耶和华下令
宣扬好消息的妇女就成了大军
没错
耶和华非常重视那些妇女的赞美声
她们就像那些上战场作战的人一样可贵
那现在又怎么样呢?
2017年工作年度的报告显示
全球有超过830万个
宣扬好消息的传道员
不要忘记在大部分地区
特别先驱中, 有一半以上都是姊妹
正规先驱当中
姊妹的人数几乎占了四分之三
这是很普遍的情况
还有
许多姊妹在她们的环境下竭尽全力
一心传讲王国的好消息
另外, 在单亲家庭中
我们的姊妹不论在物质或属灵方面
都努力照顾孩子
许多忠心的独身姊妹
献出自己为耶和华服务
包括参与建筑和维修工程
伯特利工作和在需求更大的地区
也包括外语地区服务
忠心的妻子们忠贞地支持自己的丈夫
同时也做好传道教人的工作
的确
耶和华一定很高兴看到你们所有人
以这么多种方式为他服务!
我们也很感激你们表现的热诚
和对会众产生的正面影响
显然
耶和华非常珍视姊妹们组成的“大军”
但是他关心姊妹的个别情况
和留意她们所付出的牺牲吗?
这是当然的
在圣经里, 耶和华明确地表示
他关心也赏识每一位仆人
例如, 刚刚我们看的
出埃及记第15章的经文
把米利暗称为“女先知”
显然, 米利暗有幸受到上帝任用
传达他的信息
在一些场合
上帝也会启示人
把他的话用歌曲唱出来
米利暗看来不是圣经中唯一的女先知
在圣经里, 其他的女子
像是安娜和以赛亚的妻子
也同样被称为女先知
在士师记中
圣经提到了另一个忠心的仆人底波拉
请看看士师记4:4,5
显然, 底波拉受委派
为以色列人解决争端
意思是她要负责
把耶和华的判决告诉大家
后来, 在以色列忠心的国王
约西亚统治期间
户勒大当时做女先知
在列王纪下22:8
我们看到圣殿修建期间
有人发现了律法书
忠心的约西亚王一听见律法书上的话
就非常难过
因为国民没有谨守耶和华的律法
在第13节, 他吩咐祭司、书记
以及其他有影响力的人说
然后他们怎么做呢?
请看第14节
很有意思
大人物和祭司为了获得来自上帝的指引
要去见女先知户勒大
因此, 耶和华也任用忠心的妇女
来传达他的指示
在希腊语经卷中
当时姊妹不能像古代以色列的底波拉
和其他人一样做先知
但是在提多书2:3,4
鼓励“老年妇女”表现基督徒特质
这样, 她们就能在属灵的事上
唤醒年轻妇女
我们一起念这个经文
我们多么赏识会众中属灵成熟的姊妹
她们努力协助年轻的姊妹
也帮助那些会众的新人!
然而, 今天耶和华把权柄交给男子
他们符合圣经的标准做长老或助理仆人
提供指引和保护上帝的子民
这并不是要轻视会众里姊妹的能力
事实上, 许多担负责任的弟兄承认
他们能从谦卑又成熟的姊妹身上
学到不少经验和实用的智慧
最后, 来看圣经中的另一位妇女马利亚
她所表现的杰出信心
耶和华交给她一个重大责任
要她生下并养育上帝的孩子!
我们可能很难想象
当听到这个委派时
她心里有什么想法
但是, 路加福音第1章的记载告诉我们
马利亚是个属灵成熟的女子
在38节, 天使加百列说完话后
马利亚这样回答
马利亚一定很想知道
耶和华怎么成就这些事
可是她还是表现谦卑和顺服
当上帝的忠仆摩西和耶利米
接获富于挑战的委派时
都曾犹豫不决
但马利亚却不是这样
她为我们立下了优良的榜样
不论男女都可以向她学习!
显然, 耶和华一直都非常重视妇女
今天, 我们很荣幸
跟几百万个忠心的姊妹
一起为耶和华服务
耶和华多么赏识亲爱的姊妹们
谦卑且忠心的为他服务!
各位姊妹, 我们希望你们紧守岗位
继续带给会众好的影响
忠心的妇女们
耶和华向你们承诺
你们会应验诗篇执笔者所写的话
耶和华下令
宣扬好消息的妇女就成了大军

en.text: Well, 100 classes ago,
in September of 1966,
the 42nd class of Gilead graduated.
Here’s their picture.
Now, if you look carefully back in the left corner,
you’ll see a young man
who graduated on that day.
That is our beloved Brother David Splane.
And so it seemed appropriate to mention this occasion,
being that it’s 100 classes ago.
I did say classes, not years.
We’re now looking forward to hearing from our dear Brother Splane.
He is going to give us the talk
“Don’t Forget the Purpose.”
I’m glad they didn’t get ahold of my baby picture.
That was my baby picture.
Well, I know that all of you students will agree
that Gilead School
has been a marvelous expression
of Jehovah’s undeserved kindness
—a dream come true.
But, really, all of us have been recipients
of Jehovah’s undeserved kindness in so many ways.
All of us have received training in so many ways.
So, really, the apostle Paul’s words
recorded at 2 Corinthians chapter 6 can apply to all of us.
Let’s look it up —2 Corinthians chapter 6.
We’re going to read verses 1 and 2
—2 Corinthians 6:1, 2.
And here Paul writes:
“Working together with him,
“we also urge you
“not to accept the undeserved kindness of God
and miss its purpose.”
That’s the theme of the talk, “Don’t Forget the Purpose.”
And then verse 2 says:
“For he says:
“‘In an acceptable time I heard you,
and in a day of salvation I helped you.’
“Look! Now is the especially acceptable time.
Look! Now is the day of salvation.”
Now, let’s focus first of all on the first words
that Paul writes here, “working together with him.”
That really explains why Paul’s ministry was such a success.
Now, Paul was a worker, but it wasn’t enough to be a worker.
Paul’s ministry was successful
because Paul was working together with Jehovah God.
It was Jehovah’s purpose that counted.
As Brother Samuelson brought out this morning,
it was Jehovah’s agenda that counted with the apostle Paul.
Well, our goal should be the same.
And we could be tested at times.
Perhaps back home you’re waiting for a decision
and the decision is a long-time coming.
And you could be tempted to run ahead as we’ve heard this morning
—act on your own.
You’d be working.
But when that temptation arises, keep repeating to yourself
“working together with him,”
“working together with him,”
and it’ll help.
It’ll help you to work within the bounds
that the organization has set.
And we heard about that this morning as well.
Now, notice at the beginning of verse 2,
Paul has been doing some reading.
His first words are “for he says,”
and then Paul quotes Scripture.
And it will be useful for us
to look up the scripture that Paul is quoting,
because it helps us to understand his thinking.
When Paul was reading this verse, or this passage,
what was it that helped him to make the connection
with the idea of working together with Jehovah?
The scripture, Isaiah 49:8, 9.
So let’s read that
—Isaiah 49:8, 9.
Now, as I read this,
I’d like you to see if you can guess
when this scripture had its first fulfillment.
It has two fulfillments.
See if you can guess when the scripture was first fulfilled.
Verse 8:
“This is what Jehovah says:
“‘In a time of favor I answered you,
“‘and in a day of salvation I helped you;
“‘I kept safeguarding you to give you as a covenant for the people,
“‘to rehabilitate the land,
“‘to cause them to possess
“‘their desolate inheritances,
to say to the prisoners, “Come out!”’”
You got it?
Sure.
This scripture was fulfilled
when the Israelites were being released
from Babylonian captivity.
We have a few hints there:
“to rehabilitate the land,” “desolate inheritances,”
“to say to the prisoners, ‘Come out!’”
But now, they were released from Babylon,
but what was the purpose?
It was twofold:
(a) to resettle Jerusalem,
and (b) to reestablish pure worship
—the pure worship of Jehovah.
Now, Paul is telling the Corinthians,
“We have to work together with Jehovah God.”
And he’s been reading Isaiah 49:8, 9.
What’s the connection?
Well, to rehabilitate a land
that had lain desolate for 70 years
would require a lot of work.
So those who agreed to leave Babylon
and come back to Jerusalem
would have to be hard workers,
but it wasn’t enough to be a hard worker.
To be successful, they would have to be working along with Jehovah God,
because Jehovah God had a purpose in bringing them back to Babylon.
It wasn’t just so that they could come back to Jerusalem.
His purpose was to get his pure worship reestablished.
So they were going to have to work together with him.
Now, as The Watchtower pointed out recently,
it would be a sacrifice on the part of some
to leave Babylon and go back to Jerusalem.
Why?
Well, do you remember what Jehovah had told the Israelites,
the Jews, when they went to Babylon?
“Build houses and live in them.
Plant gardens and eat their fruit.”
Pray for the peace of the city
because “in its peace you will have peace.”
So life in Babylon, captivity in Babylon,
wasn’t totally like slavery in Egypt.
In fact, some Jews got rich in Babylon.
Some became buyers and sellers of precious gems.
And it’s thought that it was in Babylon
that the Jews learned trade and commerce —how to buy and sell so well.
They didn’t learn that on the pastures of Judah; that’s for sure.
And so it would’ve been a sacrifice on the part of some
to leave Babylon and go to Jerusalem.
Hard workers were willing to do that.
Now, the returning Jews started out very well,
but they ran into problems.
They ran into problems with the building of the temple.
And as a result, they continued working
but they weren’t working together with Jehovah anymore.
They were building houses and decorating them;
they were starting a business; they were looking after their own families,
their own lives.
Now, could it be that some of them had reasoned:
‘I’ve sacrificed enough;
‘I’ve left a comfortable life in Babylon to come here
‘to this wasteland,
‘and that’s a lot more than my brothers in Babylon have done.
‘I’ve sacrificed enough.
‘It’s time to look after my own family, look after my own children.
Let the young people do their share.’
Well, we don’t know what they were reasoning.
But the fact is that part “b” of Jehovah’s purpose
—to reestablish pure worship—
was not being fulfilled.
So they were not working together with Jehovah God.
The application:
All of you have made considerable sacrifices
in order to go to your present assignments.
Most of you were not born in your assignments;
you went there of your own volition.
And you made a lot of sacrifices.
You learned another language;
you made financial, material sacrifices; and so on.
But, you know, there’s a danger.
As we get older, there can be a tendency for us to feel:
‘You know, I’ve sacrificed enough.
Why not let the young people do more?’
—especially when we see those our own age who are taking it easy.
‘They’ll be in the new world.
Why do I have to work so hard?’
And so if we’re not careful,
we could lose sight of the purpose of our training,
and we don’t want to do that.
Now, there’s a second application to Isaiah 49,
and we know that because of the way Paul puts it in 2 Corinthians 6.
Let’s go back there, 2 Corinthians 6.
And you can leave your Bibles open there
because for the rest of this discussion
we’re going to be considering verses in 2 Corinthians 6.
Now, I’m going to read verse 2,
and see if you can figure out how we know
that Paul sees more than one application
to this scripture at Isaiah 49.
Verse 2:
“For he says:
“‘In an acceptable time I heard you,
and in a day of salvation I helped you.’
“Look!
“Now is [not acceptable, but]
“the especially acceptable time.
“Look!
Now is the day of salvation.”
You got it, didn’t you?
The definite and indefinite articles.
And when Paul is thinking
about the deliverance of the Jews from Babylon,
quoting Jehovah God, it’s “an acceptable time”;
it’s “a day of salvation.”
That was one application of the prophecy.
But now Paul is telling the Christians that there’s something much better:
“Now is the especially acceptable time . . .
Now is the day of salvation.”
Yes, when the Jews were delivered from Babylon,
pure worship was going to be reestablished.
But what about today?
What about the work Christians are doing today?
The everlasting future of people is involved.
And so if workers were needed back then,
when the Jews were leaving Babylon,
how hard should we be working today?
The lives of people are at stake,
and so no matter how busy you are,
no matter whether you are at Bethel,
don’t neglect the field.
Have a zealous share in the preaching work.
This is the work that Jesus commanded us to do.
Jesus never spent a day at Bethel.
He’ll be very interested in what you do at Bethel,
but he’ll be even more interested in what you’re doing in the field.
Now, let’s focus on Jehovah’s undeserved kindness.
We talk about the undeserved kindness
of being able to come to Gilead and get this special training.
But, now, what was the purpose?
Why were you selected
to come to Gilead and get this training?
Well, you’re probably wondering that yourselves.
You were selected, first of all,
because you’re workers; you’re hard workers.
But you were also chosen because we believe
that you are going to use your training unselfishly
for the benefit of others.
And how many speakers on this platform today have made that point?
The training is not to be kept to yourselves.
You’ve been trained
so that you can unselfishly benefit other people.
You have been trained to be more effective
in serving others.
Now, when you return home,
we know that your friends and fellow workers
are going to be very pleased.
Your humility
—you’re not going to be flashing your diploma
either literally or figuratively;
you’re not going to be flaunting your knowledge;
you’re not going to be correcting every small mistake and procedure.
You’re going to earn the respect
of your fellow workers because of your humility
and because of your willingness to work alongside them
and to do whatever needs to be done.
In fact, the most powerful lesson that you teach
may not be in anything you say,
but it may be in your humility
and your willingness to work humbly along with any arrangement
or any assignment that is given you.
In this you’ll be copying Paul’s example.
If you’ve kept your Bible open at 2 Corinthians 6,
we’re going to be reading a few more verses.
Now, Paul mentions a lot in verses 4 to 6.
A lot is involved in humbly serving
the needs of our brothers.
And we’re going to just highlight a few of these.
Verses 4 to 6, Paul writes:
“But in every way we recommend ourselves as God’s ministers,
“by the endurance of much,
“by tribulations, by times of need,
“by difficulties,
“by beatings, by imprisonments, by riots,
“by hard work,
“by sleepless nights, by times without food;
“by purity, by knowledge,
“by patience, by kindness,
by holy spirit.”
Now, look at verse 4.
One of the things Paul mentions is “endurance.”
“We recommend ourselves as God’s ministers, by . . . endurance.”
Now, that’s something all of us need to give attention to.
Suppose that you were serving at Bethel before Gilead,
and you really, really enjoyed your work assignment.
Well, you’ve been away for five months.
What do you suppose has been happening while you were away?
Someone else got that work assignment.
And you know what?
He’s doing very, very well at that assignment.
In fact, it may be that the department
is not going to want to have you back when you return.
And so you’re given another assignment,
one that you don’t enjoy so much.
Now, someone else might say, “I’ve been trained at Gilead for this?”
But not you,
you’re going to have the attitude,
‘Well, if the work needs to be done, why shouldn’t I do it?’
You see, your humility is going to be so appreciated.
And remember, other Bethelites are watching you.
They’re intelligent.
They know that you’d have probably liked to have had your old job back,
but your humility
in cheerfully applying yourself to whatever you’re given to do
is going to make a tremendous impression on them.
In fact, you know what?
You’re going to go up ten points in their estimation.
“Well,” you say, “all right, I have to do it,
but do I really have to be cheerful about it?”
Yes, you do.
That’s a requirement.
And you know why?
At the regional convention last summer,
do you remember the definition of endurance?
It’s not just a matter of sticking it out until something better comes along.
But we have to be cheerful;
we have to do what we’re asked to do
with a happy, positive attitude
—not always looking for additional responsibility,
more privileges, a different work assignment—
being happy with what we are given to do.
Well, you folks understand that, and we love you for it.
Now, in the same verse, verse 4, Paul mentions “difficulties.”
And there will be problems in the field;
there’ll be problems at Bethel from time to time.
And the question is this, Will you be the type of person
that fellow Bethelites or those in the congregation
will want to talk to when difficulties arise,
because whenever they talk to you,
they always feel better after?
You have such a good, positive attitude.
Well, we know you will.
Now, in verse 5, Paul mentions “hard work.”
When brothers and sisters get together for a gathering,
we know that you’re going to be one of the ones in the kitchen
or one of the ones who stays behind after to help clean up.
You’re going to be volunteering to help clean the Kingdom Hall,
or you’re going to volunteer for a local construction project.
You’re going to be known as someone who enjoys serving others,
someone who loves to get his hands dirty
—not someone who shows up in a lovely white suit
when there’s work to be done.
Or if you have to wear a lovely white suit,
at least bring a change of clothes
so that you can roll up your sleeves and help with the work.
Well, notice in verse 6, Paul mentions “purity.”
We would certainly never want to think
that as long as we work hard in our assignment at Bethel or in the field,
Jehovah will turn a blind eye to any immorality on our part.
Jehovah has no blind eye.
Now, Paul mentions “kindness” in the same verse.
Now, some of you brothers may get into a position of authority.
And the question is,
How are you going to use your authority?
The proper use of authority is to help others,
to benefit others.
And you will never ever
use your authority vindictively to punish someone
or get even for some slight,
perhaps holding someone back from a deserved privilege
just because he offended you.
That’s not the way we use authority.
In the same verse, Paul talks about “holy spirit.”
And that’s going to help you to get along with others.
It’ll help elders and department heads
to work peacefully with one another,
to speak kindly and respectfully to one another,
to listen —to really listen—
to one another.
Now, you may have a little difference
with someone in the congregation or at Bethel.
Then you hear that person give a morning worship comment
or a fine public talk in the congregation,
and his eyes shine as he’s talking about the truth.
You’re sitting there, you observe that,
and it hits you that this man
—this man that I’m having a problem with—
really, really loves Jehovah;
and so do you.
You have that in common.
So now, can’t you get the rest to work?
Now, if we walk by the spirit,
as we heard from Brother Samuelson,
we’ll be careful not to lobby or push our own agenda,
because Jehovah might not agree with our agenda.
And we’d never want to make the other elders or the department feel
that they can’t make any decision without our input.
We would never want them to feel that in our absence
we would have to go back and revisit every decision that has been made,
as if they can’t do a single thing without us because we’re so clever
—we’ve graduated from Gilead.
No, we realize that they have Jehovah’s spirit too.
So don’t be too impressed with your own ideas.
I’m going to repeat that.
Don’t be too impressed with your own ideas.
When no Scriptural principle is involved,
we’ll be willing to yield
if the majority of the elders make a decision
that we don’t particularly agree with.
So when that happens, don’t pout
—pray!
Ask Jehovah to bless the decision that was made,
you know, the decision that you didn’t particularly agree with.
Ask Jehovah to bless that decision,
and ask Jehovah to help you to be fully supportive of the decision
—and that way you’ll be working along with Jehovah’s purpose.
And what’s his purpose?
To have a happy group of elders
serving the needs of their brothers and sisters.
If the elders are happy,
no doubt the congregation and the Bethel family will be happy.
Be resolved to allow nothing and no one
to interfere with your unity on the body of elders.
I’m going to repeat that.
Be resolved to allow nothing or no one
to interfere with your unity on the body of elders.
Well, you know all these things.
These were just helpful reminders.
Your time at Gilead has been a dream come true,
but now it’s time to use your training
to be of service to others.
Remember, you have been trained for a purpose.
And the purpose:
to be more effective in unselfishly serving others.
Never ever forget the purpose.
And may God bless you.
Well, we sincerely thank you, Brother Splane,
for those words of wisdom spoken from experience.
Well, now we’re privileged to hear greetings
from our brothers and sisters at many different branches
who are thinking about us here today.
In fact, can you imagine,
25 different branches have sent greetings.
So let me just share a few of these with you.
Of course, we can’t share all of them,
but perhaps I can just epitomize some of the messages.
For example, Armenia says:
“We are delighted to see how Jehovah is training more brothers and sisters
“to take on additional responsibilities
in his organization for the advancement of Kingdom interests.”
Benin says:
“We know that the Gilead School has left
“an indelible impression on your mind
“—with memories you’ll carry along all your life—
“and on your heart
“—with a deeper appreciation and joy
in serving Jehovah in a closer relationship with him.”
Bulgaria says:
“We wish all of you much joy on this special day.
“Bulgaria branch keenly anticipates the arrival of one couple from this class.
“We pray for Jehovah’s blessing on you students
wherever he asks you to serve him.”
Italy said:
“‘With what will I repay Jehovah for all the good he has done for me?’
“We are sure that these words well describe
“the feelings of you students of the 142nd class.
“We rejoice with you in this special occasion
“and give thanks to Jehovah for the spiritual enrichment you enjoyed.
“We are confident it will be of great value to yourselves
“and to the ones you’ll be sharing it with in the days to come.
“Please receive the warmest brotherly affection
of the brothers in Italy.”
And finally, Kazakhstan wrote and said:
“We would like to take this opportunity to pass our love and greetings
“to the 142nd class of Gilead on this graduation day.
“We are confident that they will never forget these past five months
“as they have walked hand in hand with our God, Jehovah,
“journeying page by page through his Word, the Bible.
Our thoughts and prayers are with them on this momentous day.”
Isn’t that wonderful?
Well, now, we know that many of you like to hear the statistics about the class.
So let me share with you some of the details about this class—the 142nd.
So the class was made up of nine single brothers
and four single sisters.
The average age
of the students was 44.2.
The average years in the truth was 28,
and the average years in the full-time ministry was 21.6.
So, obviously, a very mature class.
What a pleasure it’s been to have them here at Patterson!
Well, now we’re ready for the presentation of the diplomas.
The part that we always look forward to so much.
And Brother Ken Flodin, a helper to the Teaching Committee,
is going to assist me in presenting them.
We have Brother and Sister Ajiboye. They’ll be returning to Russia.
And this is Brother and Sister Alm. They’ll be returning to Nigeria.
Brother and Sister Andreopoulos, they’ll return to Greece.
This is Brother Antoine. He’s going back to Haiti.
Brother Bilous is returning to Ukraine.
And this is Brother and Sister Cripps. They’ll return to Peru.
Sister de Chavez is returning to the Philippines.
And this is Brother Dergevorkian. He’s going back to Armenia.
Brother and Sister Deschênes are returning to Canada.
Brother and Sister Francioli are going back to Italy.
And now we have Brother and Sister Hoffmann.
Now, Brother and Sister Hoffmann
have been serving in the circuit work in France,
but they’re receiving a new assignment today.
As some of you may know,
the Service Committee has set up some language circuits
that span all of Europe
in order to try to move different languages fields ahead.
And so Brother Hoffmann will be taking up
a circuit in the Romany field
that will span several countries in Europe.
Sister Huber.
Sister Huber has been serving as a special pioneer in Paraguay,
but now she is going to take up a field missionary assignment
in a country where there is a great need for missionaries
—the United States.
Brother Hurley.
Brother Hurley has been serving at the branch office,
as you heard, in Australasia.
But now he’s going to take up a new assignment
at the branch in Papua New Guinea.
And Brother and Sister Jaggernauth are going to return to Trinidad and Tobago.
Brother Kalaycı is returning to Turkey.
This is Brother Killgore.
Brother Killgore has been serving at the branch office in Canada,
but now he’ll be taking up a new assignment
at the branch office in Mexico, the Central America branch.
Brother and Sister Maraia are returning to Britain.
And Brother and Sister Mendías are returning to Central America.
This is Brother and Sister Mensah. They’re returning to Liberia.
Sister Ngoma is returning to Tanzania.
This is Brother Niyongere. He’s returning to Burundi.
Brother and Sister Palonen.
Now, Brother and Sister Palonen have been serving
for some years at the branch office in Finland,
but now they’re receiving a new assignment
to serve at the branch office in Bulgaria.
Next is Brother and Sister Szewczyk. They’ll be going back to Central Europe.
Brother Tamayo returns to Ecuador.
And Brother and Sister Tapia will also be going back to Ecuador.
Now, Brother Thomas has been serving at the branch office in Central Europe,
but now he’s going to take up a new assignment
in the branch office in Benin.
And this is our last couple, Brother and Sister Wikner.
They’re returning to Scandinavia.
Now that all of our students have officially graduated,
would you like to see now
the 142nd class of the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead?
Brother Sebastian Hoffmann has been selected to read the class letter.
“Dear Governing Body and Bethel Family:
“In one of the most beautiful inspired expressions
“of praise to Jehovah,
“King David of old said:
“‘And now, O our God, we thank you
and praise your beautiful name.’ (1 Chron. 29:13)
“With those words, at the close of his 40-year reign,
“David expressed his lifelong feelings for Jehovah.
“And here we are, the 142nd class of Gilead,
“at the close of our 20-week course of Bible education,
“with those very same feelings.
“As we have submitted to Jehovah’s molding of our hearts and minds,
“we have come to appreciate more than ever
“the beauty of the oldest personality in the universe
“—Jehovah’s personality.
“We have chosen it to be our own new personality.
“We have deeply appreciated being taught by you,
“members of the Governing Body.
“Despite your busy and demanding schedules,
“you made time to travel to Patterson
“to share with us your love for Jehovah’s name and for his Word.
“We heard it in your expressions, and we saw it
“in your eyes.
“The way you welcomed us into your beautiful new home in Warwick
“and gave us of your time will live long in our memory.
“You strengthened our trust and respect for Jehovah’s organization.
“Our prayer is that Jehovah give you brothers
“the holy spirit and energy you need
“to carry out your assignments as the end draws near.
“Throughout our schooling,
“we felt the power of God’s Word at work in us students.
“The Bible has proven to be a mirror
“in which we have examined ourselves.
“You, our dear instructors,
“held that mirror up in front of us every day.
“With kindness, love,
“patience, and reassurance,
“you helped us to look for attitudes, thoughts, and inclinations
“within ourselves that are not a reflection of Jehovah.
“We have come to see who we really are,
“who Jehovah wants us to be,
“and how we can bridge that gap.
“Every step of the way, you guided us with God’s Word
“and never your own opinion.
“What a lesson that has been to us all!
“In imitation of the apostle Paul,
“you imparted to us not only the good news of God
“but also your very selves,
“because we became beloved to you,
“and you have become beloved to us. —1 Thess. 2:8.
“As a class,
“we must acknowledge that part of the education we received
“has been outside of the Gilead classroom.
“From the very first day we arrived
“at the Patterson Educational Center,
“our education began.
“The friends at reception, our hosts,
“and the entire Bethel family
“immediately made us feel at home.
“We experienced the same love and brotherly affection
“when we visited Wallkill and Warwick.
“Over the last five months,
“we learned much observing you:
“how you responded to direction
“that you received and humbly followed through,
“how you reacted to the loss of members
“of the Bethel family in death,
“and how quick you were
“to offer comfort and assistance.
“Thank you for your constancy
“in making yourselves available for us.
“How can we ever forget the line of cars of Bethelites
“queuing up outside our residence building,
“ready and willing to take us to the meetings
“and in the ministry every week?
“You really went the extra mile for us.
“As we leave this awesome place,
“we take with us
“an unforgettable and rich spiritual heritage.
“What will we do with it?
“Our determination is the same as that of King David.
“At Psalm 145:1, 2, he promised Jehovah:
“‘I will exalt you, O my God the King,
“‘I will praise your name forever and ever.
“‘All day long I will praise you;
I will praise your name forever and ever.’
“May the blessing of Jehovah our God
“be upon all those who praise his name forever.
“With all our appreciation, we love you very much.
Your brothers, 142nd class of Gilead.”
We thank you very much for that beautiful, beautiful letter.
Well, we’ve come to the concluding remarks
of our Gilead program.
At the beginning, we discussed the importance
of praying to Jehovah to open our eyes
and help us see clearly his Word.
You know, over time because of imperfection,
our vision tends to deteriorate.
And as a result, we may have to constantly be seeking a brighter light
in order for us to see things more clearly.
Well, in the same way,
as you will deal with your own imperfections,
as you’ll deal with the imperfections of others,
as you’ll cope with health problems
and a host of other things that will come
to all of us as we live in this system,
you’ll need to look back to God’s Word again
and again and again.
In a sense, to turn up the light
so that you can see clearly
what Jehovah’s will will be in so many areas of your life.
And at times, you may scratch your head and say,
“Jehovah, I just don’t know what to do.”
But if you do not tire
of returning over and over again to God’s Word,
he will show you the way.
And the words of Joshua chapter 1
will prove to be true in your case.
Let’s read this together.
In Joshua 1:7,
this is what Jehovah said to Joshua:
“Only be courageous and very strong,
“and observe carefully the entire Law that Moses my servant commanded you.
“Do not deviate from it either to the right or to the left,
“so that you may act wisely wherever you go.
“This book of the Law should not depart from your mouth,
“and you must read it in an undertone day and night,
“in order to observe carefully all that is written in it;
“for then your way will be successful
“and then you will act wisely.
“Have I not commanded you?
“Be courageous and strong.
“Do not be struck with terror or fear,
for Jehovah your God is with you wherever you go.”
Well, please know that the good wishes,
the hopes, the prayers
of all of us go with you today
for your success in your assignment.
And may Jehovah God be with you wherever you go.
Well, I know you’ll want to know about our attendance.
We had many sites tied in today.
So here are the attendance figures.
For Canada, we had 838.
In the United States:
At Patterson, we had 3,469;
in Brooklyn, 328;
at Fishkill, 1,030;
at Wallkill, 2,502;
at Warwick, 1,571;
in Curaçao, 71;
in Florida, in Fort Lauderdale, 137;
in Jamaica, 14;
in Mira Loma, we’re not certain
because the program will not yet start for a few more minutes
(but we’ll find out in due time);
and in Puerto Rico, 149.
So that gives us a grand total of 10,109.
Well, brothers, we’ve had a wonderful program today.
We have one last chance to participate in the program
by standing now and singing song number 150,
“Seek God for Your Deliverance.”
And then following the song,
Brother Herman van Selm, a helper to the Writing Committee,
will offer our concluding prayer.
That’s song 150.

en.text: We really want to imitate our God, To be impartial, as we know he is.
To save all sorts of people is his will; He welcomes all to come and to be his.
It’s the person, not the place; It’s the heart and not the face.
God’s message to all people we extend. So because we really care,
We keep preaching ev’rywhere:
“All sorts of people can become God’s friend.”
It doesn’t matter where they may be found Or what at first they might appear to be.
What really counts is what they are at heart—
The inner self, the one Jehovah sees.
It’s the person, not the place; It’s the heart and not the face.
God’s message to all people we extend. So because we really care,
We keep preaching ev’rywhere:
“All sorts of people can become God’s friend.”
Jehovah welcomes all who make the choice To leave the world and all its ways behind.
This we have learned, and this we want to share,
And so we preach to people of all kinds.
It’s the person, not the place; It’s the heart and not the face.
God’s message to all people we extend. So because we really care,
We keep preaching ev’rywhere:
“All sorts of people can become God’s friend.”
