en.text: Well, dear brothers and sisters, it is my very great pleasure
to welcome you all to this graduation program
of the 142nd class
of the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead.
We have satellite locations tied in
across the United States branch territory,
as well as our dear brothers in Canada and, of course, in time,
we expect that this will also be shown
to our brothers via JW Broadcasting.
So, what a large audience will benefit
from our program today!
Well, you students are truly loved.
I checked with the Bethel Office just yesterday
and found out that guests have come
from 40 different countries
to be a part of this graduation program.
Isn’t that wonderful?
So we’re very much looking forward
to this spiritual feast that’s about to take place.
So now, if you’re able, let’s stand
and sing song number 54,
“This Is the Way,” and then following the song,
Brother Robert Butler, a helper
to the Publishing Committee of the Governing Body,
will offer our opening prayer, song 54.
Our marvelous God, Jehovah,
has the greatest and most far-reaching vision.
At Job 28:24,
we read: “For he looks to the ends of the earth,
and he sees everything under the heavens.”
Well, recognizing Jehovah’s almighty power
and his perfect penetrating vision,
it’s not surprising that the psalmist
prayed to Jehovah and expressed this
at Psalm 119:18.
Now, notice this very beautiful and heartfelt request
that the psalmist made.
He said: “Open my eyes
“so that I may see clearly
the wonderful things from your law.”
Well now, Jehovah
has truly fulfilled
this prayerful request.
In our day,
even though 2 Corinthians 4:4
tells us that Satan the Devil “has blinded
the minds of the unbelievers,”
Jehovah is opening up
the spiritual eyes of honesthearted ones
so that they can see the truth
that’s coming from his Word.
And it is truly amazing
to see how honesthearted ones
around this earth are receiving
spiritual sight from God.
Just take this one experience.
In May 2015,
a Lutheran priest visited
the Finland branch office with a pioneer couple.
At Bethel, she was deeply impressed
with the warm, loving atmosphere that she saw.
After a month, she attended
the “Imitate Jesus!” Convention from Friday to Sunday.
Her workmates at the church
asked her to take good notes of the program
and to share them —which she did.
In December 2015,
she visited the bishop
and resigned from her office
after 27 years
of service as an active priest.
The bishop started to cry
when she closed the door.
After resigning, she sent out this message:
“I have just resigned from the church.
“Now it is time for a new life
under Jehovah’s wise protection.”
In January of 2016,
she started serving as an unbaptized publisher,
and last year at the regional convention,
she was baptized.
She is now serving as an auxiliary pioneer
on a continuous basis,
and she says that she wants to have a share in public witnessing
with carts close to the church
where she served for decades.
Well now, isn’t this interesting though?
This is the last comment this dear sister made.
She said, “As a young girl,
“I made a promise to serve God,
“but it wasn’t until now
“that I actually realized how God
wanted to be served.”
Aren’t we glad to welcome this sister
into our worldwide brotherhood?
But going back to that Scriptural thought
in Psalm 119:18,
this is not simply the prayer
of honesthearted ones who are in the world.
Really, brothers, this is our prayer.
You see, we all want Jehovah
to open up our eyes
and help us to see his Word clearly.
Now, why is that so necessary for all of us?
Well, let’s just take one simple example from the Scriptures
of the faithful man Samuel.
Now, Samuel was obviously a very spiritual man;
he was a person who was used
throughout his life in Jehovah’s service.
But if you look at this account in 1 Samuel
chapter 16,
you’ll remember that here
Jehovah was sending Samuel to anoint
one of the sons of Jesse to become king.
Now, if you look at verse 7,
look at what Jehovah says to Samuel:
“Do not pay attention
“to his appearance
“and how tall he is,
“for I have rejected him.
“For the way man sees
“is not the way God sees,
“because mere man sees what appears to the eyes,
but Jehovah sees into the heart.”
Well now, do you see the point?
Do you see why we need to beg Jehovah to open our eyes
and help us to see clearly his Word?
You see, our imperfection
affects our vision, doesn’t it?
Our culture, the way we were raised,
our fleshly inclinations
can all distort our vision.
We so much need Jehovah God
to open our eyes and help us
so that we can see matters clearly.
Well, for the past 74 years,
Gilead School has been a wonderful tool
to help fine spiritual men and women
to focus and sharpen
their spiritual vision.
Now, during your five and a half months of schooling,
you’ve had the pleasure to study God’s Word.
Now, this has not been just a dry academic exercise.
But really, what you’ve done
is you’ve focused a light
upon God’s Word, the Bible.
Now, we’re not talking about a little flashlight;
we’re talking about a floodlight.
And what has happened as a result?
Well, Jehovah has helped
you to see yourself;
he’s helped you to see the Scriptures;
he’s helped you to see your brothers;
he’s helped you to see your assignments
much more clearly
through the enlightening influence
of his precious Word, the Bible.
Well, as a result of all of that,
you are no longer the people you were
when you arrived at Gilead.
You have changed.
But now, what are you going to do
with this wonderful gift

you have received now at Gilead as an opportunity
to continually and humbly serve others,
and for that, Jehovah will richly bless you.
We thank you very much, Brother Ciranko,
for those very heartwarming and very meaningful thoughts.
Well, now we’re going to begin to hear some comments
and thoughts from the instructors of the Gilead School.
First, we’re going to hear from Brother William Samuelson.
He’s going to speak to us on the subject
“Perfected Into One.”
Some years ago, back in the 1700’s,
Thomas Paine, an American writer, said:
“It’s not in numbers
“but in unity
that great strength lies.”
Well, that reminded me
of a medical emergency that arose
at a district convention some years ago.
A brother leaving the stadium
got to the sidewalk and fell
to the ground, or to the sidewalk,
apparently with a heart attack
or possibly a stroke.
Two ambulances eventually arrived,
and the two drivers got into a heated argument
over who had the authority, or jurisdiction,
to transport our brother
to the nearest emergency ward.
Well, what was it that kept
these two drivers
from being effective at their job?
It was a lack of unity.
So I was thinking, ‘How can you
‘promote unity in your job,
in your assignment, that you’ll be going to?’
Well, there are any number of ways.
And the list that I’m going to give you, is just three,
and it is by no means exhaustive
—good communication;
avoid promoting a personal agenda;
and if given oversight,
work within the boundaries
of the assignment and work hard
to be skilled at it.
Good communication.
At the time of the emergency that I just mentioned,
an unauthorized person
called 911.
Now, that lack of communication
—the unauthorized person
really should have communicated
with the attendants already on duty
and assigned to that particular job.
There were EMTs there,
but he saw what he thought was a serious situation
and called 911.
Now, that resulted in 911
sending the second ambulance.
We’ll talk about that a little later.
I got to thinking about a Bible account
—a huge project
that failed because of lack of communication.
Now, you probably can think of any number,
and the one I’m going to talk about we usually think of in a negative way.
But turn to Genesis chapter 11,
and we’re going to look at verses 6 through 8 in particular,
and we won’t read all of it, but just a few little excerpts from it.
In verse 5: “Jehovah went down to see the city
and the tower,” the city and Tower of Babel.
They had a project. “Jehovah then said: ‘Look!
They are one people,’” they’re united,
“‘with one language, and this is what they have started to do.
“‘Now there is nothing that they may have in mind to do
that will be impossible for them.’”
Because they had communication,
they were able to understand each other.
So Jehovah confused their languages.
But now, notice in verse 8,
he ‘scattered them over the entire face of the earth,
and they gradually left off building the tower.’
Because they couldn’t communicate,
the project failed.
Well, when we examine
our own situation,
the Scriptures tell us—
Paul wrote to the Philippians: “Look out
“not only for your own interests,
but also for the interests of others.”
How will you know
what is in the best interests of others
if you don’t communicate with them?
if you don’t talk to them?
if you don’t find out what their preferences are?
their thinking? their abilities?
And once you find out what these are,
then you act in harmony
with that and you look for their interests
rather than your own.
The second point:
Avoid promoting a personal agenda.
Personal agenda
was defined this way in one publication:
“An ambitious scheme or plan of action
“designed to make things work out for your benefit
“or your convenience
or so that you can gain control.”
Control seems to sometimes be a dominant thing.
Well, in our initial illustration,
or example, our two drivers,
both had a personal agenda.
The first ambulance
had been radioed for and was on-site
because it had been employed by the convention.
It was there for just such an emergency,
and obviously that driver felt that he had jurisdiction.
But you remember our unauthorized brother
called 911.
Now, 911 dispatched an ambulance,
and our brother had collapsed on the sidewalk.
So he felt because it wasn’t inside the stadium,
it was on the sidewalk, and because he
had been dispatched by 911,
he had jurisdiction.
So the two of them had their own agenda.
Of course, our poor brother is laying here
not knowing what’s happening to him.
Well, I got to thinking
about others in the Bible
that have gone out for their own agenda.
Satan obviously tops the list.
He had an agenda. He wanted worship.
But what about Korah, Dathan, Abiram?
Turn to Numbers
chapter 16,
verses 8 through 11, but we’re not going to read all of that.
You remember the account.
In fact, I think you studied it in detail.
But in verse 8:
“Moses then said to Korah: ‘Listen, please,
“‘you sons of Levi.
“‘Does it seem to you such a little thing
“‘that the God of Israel
“‘has separated you from the assembly of Israel
“‘and allowed you to approach him in order to perform
“‘the service of Jehovah’s tabernacle
and to stand before the assembly?’”
In other words, you’ve been given a special privilege.
Now, does that seem like such a little thing to you?
In verse 10, he said:
“Must you also try to secure the priesthood?”
Well, if you think about this matter of a personal agenda,
in your assignments, you can contribute much
to the unity of the group you’re with,
the branch, the department.
But if you start thinking about how this is going to give
honor and glory to you,
you could start thinking about getting
as much responsibility as you can
—working for your own interests
rather than the interests of others,
getting or developing
a personal agenda.
So in addition to the special privileges you have
in full-time service, must you also
try to get something else? try to get something greater?
Two others that fell victim to this
were James and John.
Turn to the book of Mark,
and again we’re just going to glance
at a couple of the scriptures, a couple of the verses.
Here, you remember —and Brother Ciranko
already commented on this account —James and John.
One account said they got their mother to do it,
but they knew, Jesus knew.
He answered them, and they said: “Teacher,”
verse 35, chapter 10, “Teacher,
we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”
‘We’ve got a personal agenda.
‘We want to sit on your right hand and your left.
‘We want to have honor; we want to have authority.
You see, we want this.’
Well, without doing all of the details here,
verse 41, what did it do to the unity
of the group of the 12?
Verse 41: “When the ten others heard about it,
“they became indignant
at James and John.”
It didn’t help the unity of the group
with a personal agenda.
And so it is with you.
If you promote a personal agenda,
it’s not going to help the unity of the department
or the branch that you’re serving with.
We might think, in conclusion,
of an illustration
of an orchestra.
Before a performance,
all of the instruments in an orchestra
generally adjust
to a single pitch
—one generated sometimes
by an electronic tone generator.
Now, once they have been tuned to a single tone,
all of the instruments are automatically
tuned to each other.
And so it is if you listen to the one tone,
you will all be tuned together.
You remember Jesus in his prayer
to his Father in John 17 before his death.
He prayed that they would be in union,
that they would be together as one.
If you turn to John 17:21,
he said: “So that they may all be one,” in his prayer to his Father,
“just as you, Father, are in union with me,” in other words,
united, one,
“. . . that they also may be in union with us,
so that the world may believe that you sent me.”
But now, drop down to verse 23:
“In union with them and you—”
“I in union with them and you in union with me,
in order that they may be perfected into one.”
Now, notice the footnote on “perfected into one.”
It says: “Or ‘be completely unified.’”
So for stability in the branch, the department,
whatever your assignment is,
unity is a must; it has to be.
Just as you’ve done for the past 20 weeks,
we encourage you to continue
to work together, united
—perfectly, completely united—
perfected into one.
As Gilead graduates, make sure you do your part
to help your brothers and sisters
become perfected into one.
We thank you very much, Brother Samuelson,
for those very practical comments.
I know the students are going to benefit from them.
Well, now we’re looking forward to hearing a talk
from another of our Gilead instructors, Brother Mark Noumair.
His theme for us today is “See the Cause.”
Well, this is a time of great change
for Jehovah’s people,
and you students have seen it firsthand
by being invited to Gilead.
In fact, some of you
will receive a change of assignment
after Gilead.
And still others might receive a change
in their circumstances once they get back
to their branch territory.
So change will be a part of your life.
And although change can be good,
many find unexpected change
stressful or even unsettling.
We may find ourselves asking,
‘Why me?’
And that question is not a sign of weak faith.
Rather, it is healthy to ask why
because when you ask the question why,
you usually begin to explore the cause
behind the change.
Now, a careful study of Bible history
reveals that Jehovah God is a Master of change.
He loves change.
In fact, when we studied the New World Translation,
Appendix A-4, what did we learn?
We learned that Jehovah causes,
or sets in motion,
anything he wants to happen in order to fulfill his purpose.
Now, we might accept that Jehovah permits this or that
when it comes to problems
in this imperfect system of things
and, perhaps, situations
that one goes through because of imperfection.
True.
But what about when adjustments are made
within Jehovah’s theocratic organization?
Now what?
If we have a difficult time
adjusting to a change
because it doesn’t match our thinking,
should we automatically conclude that Jehovah
is simply permitting this change?
Or is he, in fact,
causing it to happen?
Well, I want to consider two Bible accounts with you
that are going to help answer that question.
First one, 2 Chronicles chapter 11.
The setting is when the ten tribes
withdrew their support from Rehoboam.
They made Jeroboam their king.
Rehoboam wanted those ten tribes back,
no doubt thinking: ‘They have no right to break away.
‘Who do they think they are?
‘In fact, breaking away,
‘or splitting, the 12 tribes
‘will only create an abrupt change
‘to a stable arrangement which originated with God
‘since the days of Moses.
I want them back.’
This was unexpected, unsettling for Rehoboam.
And then Jehovah God
sends his prophet Shemaiah
to Rehoboam.
Second Chronicles 11, let’s read verse 4:
“This is what Jehovah says:
“‘You must not go up
“‘and fight against your [Rehoboam’s] brothers.
“‘Each of you return to his house,
“‘for I [Jehovah]
“‘have caused this
to happen.’”
‘I have caused
‘this split to happen, Rehoboam.
‘I caused it.
‘And anything that I cause can only have good results.
‘It’s going to be good.
I cause it; it’s going to be good.’
And we too can discern
the possible benefits of this split.
Think about it:
Individual Israelites in either kingdom now
would have an opportunity to demonstrate
if they would personally uphold true worship
at the temple, regardless of which king was ruling
and regardless of which territory they lived in.
Jehovah’s patience, his mercy,
his protection would be magnified
as he now dealt with two kingdoms
instead of one.
But we may wonder,
‘Since Jehovah caused this,
why did the apostasy occur afterwards?’
Well, Jehovah intended this split
to be a mere governmental division,
an organizational adjustment,
not a departure from true worship
as centered at the temple in Jerusalem.
If Jeroboam had continued faithful,
that separate kingdom of Israel
would have continued right alongside the kingdom of Judah.
They would have worked together to honor and praise Jehovah God.
That would have been wonderful. Jehovah would have made sure of that.
So Jehovah didn’t cause
the apostasy.
These problems, or human flaws,
resulted when Rehoboam and Jeroboam failed to see
that Jehovah expected obedience
no matter where they lived.
That’s the point: They failed to cooperate
with the new reality and reap the benefits
from what Jehovah was causing to happen.
So, what first lesson do we want you to think about,
to learn, to have etched into your memory?
When Jehovah causes a change, it can only be for the good.
All we need to do is cooperate with the change
and see the cause, or see
what Jehovah is setting in motion,
and then look to him for a blessing on the outcome.
See, this divine precedent teaches us
that it is vital
for you, for me,
vital to distinguish
the perfect cause
of Jehovah
from the imperfect flaws
of humans
who fail to cooperate
with what Jehovah God is doing.
That’s point number one.
Let’s go on to our second example.
This one has to do with Joseph.
The setting is when Joseph was in Egypt,
and he’s making himself known to his brothers.
Genesis chapter 45, let’s open our Bibles there.
Chapter 45, verse 7,
notice what Joseph says to his brothers, how he words this:
“But God sent me ahead of you,”
sent me ahead of you,
“in order to preserve for you a remnant,”
there was a purpose, “on the earth
and to keep you alive by a great deliverance.”
Do we see that?
Jehovah didn’t merely permit him to go to Egypt,
but he caused Joseph to go to Egypt.
‘I sent you; I caused you to go ahead
to preserve a remnant.’
You see, Joseph’s arrival in Egypt
was part of Jehovah’s purpose
in creating the conditions
that would result in preserving the offspring
that would lead to the Messiah.
However,
Jehovah causing a change,
at times,
the consequences of that change
are not what we expect.
And that’s what we have to think about.
He causes the change, but the consequences
might not be what we expect.
For example, think about Joseph.
He becomes a slave. He didn’t expect that.
He went to prison. ‘I don’t expect this.
‘I’m initially— I’m treated severely.
I didn’t like that.’
See, Joseph suffered many human injustices
or flaws along the way.
He could have easily resisted,
proudly reasoned: ‘Now, hold on here.
‘Me? A slave? A slave?
‘The prophetic dreams I received as a young man
‘indicated that others would bow down to me.
‘I don’t see anyone bowing down to me.
‘I’m bowing down to others as a slave. This doesn’t make sense.
‘This is not turning out the way I have expected
or preferred.’
In fact, some 13 years would pass
before Joseph would experience relief.
The changes in his life were unexpected,
unclear, and unsettling.
But he didn’t ask: “Jehovah,
what are you doing to me?”
Rather, he humbly asked,
“What are you doing with me?”
See, unlike proud Rehoboam and Jeroboam,
Joseph could see the cause
—what Jehovah was setting in motion—
not the human flaws.
He could discern the special work
to which he had been appointed.
Why, he even reassured his brothers
that Jehovah had directed
and caused his relocation to Egypt,
and it served for the preservation
of his family and for all families of the earth.
He got that.
And what’s the lesson
that you really need to think about?
Our personal response
—personal response— to what Jehovah causes
reveals a lot
about our humility and our patience.
Our attitude, our response
can lead to a spiritual fall
or success.
Now, let’s get specific with you.
How can you apply this?
There may be a time when organizational adjustments
make it seem that Jehovah
has handcuffed your talents,
clipped your wings.
And maybe this adjustment that you’re undergoing,
it just doesn’t match your thinking.
What are you going to do then? Now what happens?
Don’t let pride get in the way.
If you let pride get in the way, you could actually delay
the fruitage of organizational decisions.
And that’s not what you’ve been trained to do at Gilead.
It’s just the opposite.
We’ve talked for months about how you need to get on board
with the organizational direction.
But now, imagine if you begin to doubt
that instruction from headquarters.
“It doesn’t really apply to our country.
“Oh, these instructions, they won’t work here.
“We’re different. We do things differently.
“The brothers in New York, they’re really not—
“They don’t understand our circumstances.
We should apply it in a different way.”
You see, what have you just done?
If that type of thinking begins to take root,
you will only hesitate to implement
or halfheartedly support
the direction received.
And that’s not what you’ve been trained to do.
So do you understand how this might apply in the future?
And voicing such doubts can only create
an unhealthy spirit and weaken your brothers.
Instead, try to see what Jehovah
is really causing to happen.
What is he causing to happen?
Jehovah God is training you to better refine
such qualities as obedience and patience and loyalty
so that you can be used that much more
for Jehovah’s purpose, honor, and glory.
For your spiritual health,
you want to view decisions as from Jehovah,
causing his will to take place,
even if it is not convenient
or you don’t immediately discern the real benefits.
There is no spiritual risk
in wholeheartedly supporting decisions made
by Jehovah’s spirit-directed organization.
See the cause,
not the flaws.
There are plenty of human flaws to concentrate on.
Get away from that.
See what Jehovah is setting in motion.
Once you see it, help others to see it.
Like Joseph, use your words
to reassure and strengthen your brothers.
And then do you know what you will become part of?
What will you become a part of?
As Brother Sanderson said:
The Gilead legacy.
So stay with that understanding.
Stay with that attitude. Stay with that motive.
Let’s distill our discussion down to three points:
Be careful not to assume that Jehovah is permitting,
just permitting an organizational adjustment,
when in reality he is far more likely causing it to happen.
(2) When Jehovah causes a change,
it can only be for good,
and (3) don’t be quick to see the human flaws.
It takes patience and humility
to work along with Jehovah God as he progressively causes
his purpose to go forward.
Your maturity, your love for Jehovah God
and his way of doing things has been clearly manifest
while you’ve attended Gilead School, and that’s why Jehovah God loves you.
That’s why we love you.
So maintain this spirit as you work
along with God’s unfolding purpose.
For it is this attitude
that will lead to your spiritual success.
It is this attitude that will help you
to continue to see the cause.
Well, we thank you very much, Brother Noumair,
for that excellent discourse.
Well, now you have an opportunity to participate in the program.
If you’d like to stand, if you’re able,
we’re going to sing song number 84
which is entitled “Reaching Out,”
song 84.

en.text: Jehovah knows just what we need To bring us joy and to succeed.
So he provides so many ways In which to serve and spend our days.
Reaching out, giving all, for our God above.
And where the need is great, there we’ll be, reaching out in love.
There’s work to do in ev’ry land. Where there’s a need, we lend a hand.
By reaching out, we show we care. We want to help and want to share.
Reaching out, giving all, for our God above.
And where the need is great, there we’ll be, reaching out in love.
And here at home, in towns nearby, We plan, we build, new skills we try.
We learn to speak a foreign tongue And bring good news to ev’ryone.
Reaching out, giving all, for our God above.
And where the need is great, there we’ll be, reaching out in love.

en.text: Well, now we have something exciting.
We’re pleased to feature a new part
on our Gilead program this year.
Now, they’ve made me promise not to say another word.
So let’s enjoy this new feature together.
Thanks for coming.
Follow me.
I need to talk to Ken about something really important.
Come on!
Come in!
Ken, I have some interesting news I need to share with you.
It’s exciting!
I could tell by the look on your face something is up.
It is. It’s about the Gilead graduation program.
Oh, no! Not a change!
Yeah, a change. But it’s so intriguing; it’s positive.
You know, the student experiences part that we’ve had for many years?
They share their field service experiences.
I love that part.
And I do too, but the Teaching Committee wants to broaden it out.
Look, Ken, the students are from all over the world,
coming from various branches.
Yeah, that’s true.
They have experiences they can share,
perhaps from their own branch
or maybe something about the Kingdom work
that is taking place in that country.
It’s going to be exciting, different, interesting.
I like it, but I’m wondering. . .
It’s just broadening it out.
But I’m wondering, you know, everybody is used to that experiences format.
Mhm, I know.
What’s the format of this new segment going to be?
You’re going to love it—a talk show!
A talk show?
A talk show.
It means, though, you’re going to have to build a set.
You’re going to have to have lighting.
What about if they can sing
or there’s musical instruments that they can play?
We’ll need a little spot for them to actually perform a song.
I’m thinking, though, if it’s going to be a show,
it’s got to have a name.
What are you thinking? Make it unique.
OK. “The Inside Story.”
Ken, it resonates.
Because you’re getting it —you’re getting “the inside story.”
I love it! “The Inside Story.”
Let’s go with that.
OK.
But, Mark, we are weeks away from Gilead graduation.
I know, we’ll have to work hard to pull this off.
Do you think we can get this done in time?
Let’s see.
Friends, you are in for a real treat!
I’m here with the whole class of Gilead,
and they’ve gotten together to get better acquainted
with some of their classmates,
and we have been invited to this occasion.
You are going to meet some lovable brothers and sisters,
and you are going to hear some exciting,
faith-strengthening experiences.
You’re also going to hear some delightful music
because some in this class
have musical talent.
So, come with me, and we’re going to get
“the inside story.”
Our first guest is Sister Evelyn Huber
who is a single sister in this class,
and she’s serving in Paraguay.
Evelyn, thank you so much for coming.
You were living in a neighborhood like this
in Munich, a culturally rich city.
You lived in an apartment like this
—very sleek, modern, nice.
You had a good-paying job and you were pioneering.
How did you end up clear around the world in Paraguay?
Yes, that was actually quite a change for me.
So there was this German Kingdom Ministry
back then in 2005
that mentioned
a large German-speaking community in Paraguay,
and a great need for German-speaking publishers
there in South America.
And that call—that announcement— really touched my heart.
I wanted to go there; I wanted to serve there.
So I wrote my letter to the branch.
They invited me over,
and a few months later, I arrived in Paraguay.
And they sent me together with seven others
to Santa Rosa del Aguaray,
and there we started a German activity from zero.
Now, when you got there, though, you got a little bit of a surprise.
So we arrived in the first colony, and I talked to a man.
And after my nice introduction,
he just looked at me with big eyes and he said,
“Ekj kaun die nijch vestohne.”
So, “Sorry, I can’t understand you.”
And I looked at him and I said,
“I can’t understand you either.”
That was the moment when I realized these people
—the Mennonites— they don’t speak our German.
They have their own language, the so-called Low German.
How do you learn Low German?
There are no books that exist
for learning the language —Low German.
And we didn’t have Internet at that time in our area in Paraguay.
So we really didn’t know how to learn the language.
We prayed to Jehovah and we said,
“Jehovah, we really want to preach to these people.”
And an 80-year-old Mennonite man
was the answer to our prayer.
That’s him; that’s Willie.
He really wanted to study the Bible.
So we taught him the Bible,
and he taught us the language —Low German.
And he was an excellent Bible student
and also a fantastic language teacher.
Well, isn’t that amazing?
Now, I do understand, though,
that you learned a trick that helped you
to be better understood by those Low German speakers.
We found out that when we spoke our German
like Americans, with an American accent. . .
Now, with an American accent.
What do you mean by that?
I’ll give you an example: “Good morning.”
In German, we would say, “Guten Morgen,”
and Americans would say, “Guten Morgen” with the “rrr” sound.
Oh, OK. I get it.
And they said: “Please talk to us like that.
It is so much better to understand you.”
So for quite a while, we kept on going like that.
So the American accent r-r-really helped you.
Finally, you came to a realization
that you were beginning to get fluent in the language.
How did that happen?
We went out again in the ministry, and a very furious lady
—Mennonite lady— came out of her house.
And while she was yelling at us, I realized, ‘Wow!
I understand every single word that she’s saying to me!’
So I looked at my pioneer partner, Tanya, and she looked so happy too.
And the lady thought we couldn’t understand her.
Because you’re smiling at her.
So she repeated the whole thing again.
And that was our confirmation.
Wow!
We really understood her, and we really understood Low German.
So with a big smile and very happy, we left her farm.
I see. I’m sure she was really confused.
Evelyn, could you just kind of explain to us,
What are some of the challenges you face
as a single sister in your territory there in Paraguay?
Let’s go to Paraguay!
Would you join me in traveling to a Mennonite colony?
Let’s go!
The trip takes us approximately three hours.
Now we enter the real Paraguayan roads —bright red sand—
sometimes dry and dusty
and sometimes just muddy and dirty.
There we are traveling,
having time to enjoy Jehovah’s wonderful creation
and to think about the people we are going to visit today.
Do you know what we especially love?
When we enter a colony
and the following happens:
Children come running out of their homes
asking for new Caleb and Sophia videos.
Kids just love the videos,
and we are so happy to have them now also in Low German.
Ah, now you see what Mennonite homes look like.
They have nice houses, lovely gardens.
They all have their own farm.
It’s really a pleasure when you get to study with the Mennonites.
It’s so encouraging when one of your studies
progresses enough to come to the meetings;
it takes great courage for them.
And you really have to meet my congregation,
Santa Rosa Low German
—full of zealous pioneers and publishers.
Ah, look at them!
Here are my beloved brothers and sisters.
So good to see them all again.
They all send us their love.
That was a very touching video.
It seems like such an exciting life.
I realized how much Jehovah can do with single sisters
—how he uses them.
And in my congregation,
there are actually more than 50 percent of single sisters.
I see.
There’s a long heritage, actually, for sisters going to Gilead,
serving in foreign assignments.
Jehovah really loves single sisters.
They are precious to him.
Well, that’s certainly the truth.
And we are very proud of you and all the single sisters
and very appreciative of the huge contribution that you’ve made
to the worldwide work and the Kingdom efforts.
It’s amazing, and we know Jehovah loves you.
It’s been such a pleasure getting to know you, Evelyn.
Thank you so much for sharing your experiences with us.
That was my pleasure. Thank you.
Now, Evelyn, I have one more question for you.
Were you surprised to find out
that there was so much musical talent in your class?
Whoa! I definitely was, uh-hu.
Well, now it’s time to get a sample of that musical talent.
We have a band!
They’re going to perform an original song composed by one of your classmates.
And the song is entitled “Pronto Será Realidad.”
In English that means “soon it will be a reality.”
Let’s listen to “Pronto Será Realidad.”
That was a great song —very touching.
Our next guest is actually one of the band members.
Let’s welcome Brother Joel Hurley.
So, Joel, you’re serving at the branch in Australia now.
But you have a rich heritage in the truth
given to you by your grandparents, parents.
Could you just explain a little bit about that to us?
My grandfather actually learned the truth from a fellow band member.
He was so impressed with the use of God’s name
and that God’s name was Jehovah that he made sure
that he taught the truth to many family members.
But sometime later in 1960,
they decided as a family to move to serve where the need was greater,
so they moved to the Pacific islands in Fiji.
So my dad grew up in Fiji.
I see. I think we have a picture, yeah.
There’s my dad next to the car;
they’re witnessing to the village chief and his family
—so memories of them growing up in Fiji.
Later on, he married my mum
and they continued to serve there for some time.
They really did have a big impact on my early years
—preaching in the villages;
organizing special conventions;
events, such as the Around-the-World convention.
We see Brother Franz.
So now, as a young person, then, you decided to learn Japanese.
Why did you do that?
Well, in the early 80’s,
there was a Japanese group attached
to the Kingdom Hall where we attended,
so there was a need at the time in that group.
In fact, many from Japan came to help out.
They encouraged me to learn Japanese,
so I began to learn the language.
So you’ve been speaking Japanese now for how long?
Thirty-odd years.
My goodness!
Now, you went to MTS.
And after MTS graduation,
tell us about some of your assignments.
The first assignment was with the Japanese group,
and shortly after, it became a congregation.
A whole range of different backgrounds came into the truth:
CEOs in Japanese companies,
young ones for the first time who learned the truth,
and even a Buddhist monk learned the truth
and became a zealous pioneer in the congregation.
What was your next assignment?
It was the other side of the country
—to western Australia— to a country assignment.
Western Australia, now, is that the outback?
We’ve all heard about the outback.
Well, parts of it are called the Golden Outback,
but there’s a lot of bushland.
There’s a large farming community —wheat, sheep.
You have a picture here of some of the things.
In fact, there’s a variety of people
that we were able to speak to in that territory.
You say, “a variety of people.”
I don’t see too many people in that picture.
Where did this variety come from?
Well, there were townships, there were the farmers,
there were “bushies” —ones who live off the land—
Australian aborigines, and tourists.
Tourists?
So way out there in rural Australia there are tourists?
What is there to see?
They’d come to visit the famous icons in the area, for example, “Wave Rock.”
This is a natural rock formation in the shape of a breaking wave.
In fact, one time there was this Japanese man
who cycled across Australia and was camping not far from the rock.
I was able to speak to him and use my Japanese.
He was interested.
The next day, he traveled 100 or so kilometers (60 miles)
to where I was living.
I followed up the interest and then was able
to pass it on to Japan for further follow-up.
Was there a congregation out there in the rural areas?
It was a small family-like congregation.
We stuck together.
I see.
So how far would they have to drive sometimes?
Over 100 kilometers (60 miles) in many instances,
on gravel roads—roads whereby
a mob of kangaroos could actually come out.
So quite challenging.
Sorry, Joel, one second, a mob of kangaroos.
What’s that?
I was wondering the same thing. What do you mean a mob?
For example, coming home from a Bible study
at dusk one night on a dirt road,
suddenly I find this mob of kangaroos
—10, 15 kangaroos around the car.
So you just have to be careful in those areas
to make sure you take caution at all times.
That’s quite a picture —you know, mental picture—
all of these kangaroos bouncing around the car.
After that rural assignment,
you had some assignments to some bigger cities
and then you did some substitute circuit work
and then you were reassigned to Bethel.
So at Bethel, you are back in the Japanese congregation.
So, Joel, tell us, what is it like being at Bethel
serving in a Japanese congregation?
Well, would you like to have a look at a video
which explains what our territory is like?
Of course we would.
We only have one Japanese language congregation in Sydney,
so our territory is vast.
We typically spend long days in the ministry.
Some of us will leave early in the morning to catch the ferry
and go to a popular tourist place called Circular Quay.
There are many Japanese tourists here.
We’ll often find a group of Japanese tourists
setting up to take a photo.
We might approach them and say:
“Shyashin wo torimasho ka?”
“Can I take a photo for you?”
A good conversation then begins.
The many young Japanese pioneers still in school
may join up with us later in the afternoon.
The interested person may hear the message for the first time
and attend the meeting that night.
We often enjoy refreshing association
with each other in the congregation,
particularly after a long day in the ministry.
Recently, we just had our first pioneer school in Japanese.
They were so grateful that they didn’t have to travel
back to Japan to attend the school.
There’s really no separation between ministry and life.
It is life—the best life.
Kon’ichiwa!
Thank you for sharing that video.
It seems like you have a very nice assignment there.
Now, looking back over your life, Joel, would you have chosen
—now looking back— to do anything else?
At times there have been challenges,
whether that be loneliness or isolation
because of language or the environment.
But it’s really given me an opportunity
to rely on Jehovah God at that time
—to learn endurance.
He’s provided family, friends wherever I’ve gone.
And to be able to sense Jehovah’s pleasure
and Jehovah’s support at these times
is something that I’m really grateful for.
Joel, this has been very pleasurable
—talking to you— and very encouraging.
Thank you for sharing your experiences with us.
Now, Joel, it’s time for you to go back to the piano.
Our band is going to play another song for us.
And like the first one, this is an original composition
written by one of your classmates.
This song is entitled “The Promised Land.”
Let’s listen.
What a beautiful song!
What wonderful sentiments were expressed there.
Well, we’ve been to Paraguay;
we’ve been to Australia;
now it’s time to go to Russia.
Our final guest is Brother Moses Ajiboye, who’s serving in the Russia branch.
Back in 1988,
you were a man in your late teens pioneering in Britain,
but somehow you ended up in Soviet Russia
pioneering in a country under ban.
How did that happen, Moses?
My pioneer partner and myself, we were out in the ministry
and met a man who happened to be a diplomat from Russia,
and he was interested, and we would go back to him
and make return visits regularly.
And after a few weeks,
he asked us if we want to go to Moscow.
He offered us, actually,
a free language scholarship for three months.
That was back in 1988.
What happened in the meantime?
Following the three months, during the language course,
the professor—one of the professors who was teaching the language—
helped to upgrade my language scholarship
into a medical scholarship.
A medical scholarship?
Like a medical student.
My goodness, so now you’re going to medical school
and you’re pioneering.
That’s right, absolutely.
But, even so, you really didn’t plan to finish the medical degree.
But what happened?
I thought that the ban would be lifted pretty soon
and that I would be serving as a pioneer
in a territory where the need is great.
But, you see, the lifting of the ban took several years.
And so you kept going to medical school?
That’s right.
Nineteen ninety-one, March 27,
could you just explain to us about that?
The ban was lifted; we are registered.
It means that we have freedom of religion,
so we cannot stay in those private homes anymore.
I think we have a picture, yeah.
And so, yeah, this is the first place we actually got.
It was a movie theater
in one part of Moscow that we rented,
and we read the first letter that we got
from the organization about the lifting of the ban.
The brother who read it, it took him about 20 minutes
to read a one-and-a-half page letter.
Why did it take so long?
Wow, you can imagine.
Many years they were under ban,
and now the ban is lifted.
The friends cannot believe it, even the brother himself.
There was a lot of crying and cries of joy.
And, oh, it was a touching moment.
I’ll never forget that.
How did you care for all the new ones coming in?
By 1992, we already had four large congregations in Moscow.
When you say large, how many are we talking about?
Well, up to 800 publishers in each of them.
If we had enough elders,
those congregations would have split
into three, four, or even five.
We used to have, for example, book studies.
You only had a few elders.
How did you have enough book study conductors?
We figured out that any male member of the congregation
who gets baptized will get a book study.
We’re happy that they made themselves available.
They were very zealous.
But some of the material we discussed in the book study was pretty deep.
Yes.
How did they manage to teach it correctly?
We would put all these newly baptized brothers
who conducted book studies together on a Sunday evening
and have three to four-hour sessions with them.
Yes, there are some of them.
These brothers are newly baptized book study conductors.
Now, this was just one of the groups.
There were several groups like this.
Many.
My goodness.
How did you manage, even on the weekend,
to have enough speakers for public talks and things?
Absolutely.
And in Moscow at that time, there were only a few elders;
so we were all grouped together,
basically, into one body of elders;
and each one of us were
on a rotating list of giving public talks.
So some brothers on the weekends —Saturdays and Sundays—
we had many meetings.
They would go and give two to three talks.
Myself, because I was single,
very often gave four to five talks every weekend.
Oh, my goodness.
Amazing!
Now, let’s take a look at this next picture we have here.
So here we see Brother Jaracz.
This is shortly after the ban.
And can you tell us one of the things he’s explaining to you here?
We were all in the audience, and he told us of the importance
to go through the baptismal questions
with each one individually.
And then as we sat in the audience, most of us said,
“Oh, how on earth are we going to do that?”
Because before that —you know, Brother Stovall—
we would put 30, 40 people together
and just go through the questions with them
because the influx was so big;
we basically could not handle them individually.
But Brother Jaracz proved the point by telling us
that the Organized to Accomplish Our Ministry book is for that purpose,
because we want a spiritually strong organization,
not just the statistics.
We obeyed, but it was not easy in the beginning.
So how did you do it?
I mean, how long did it take to go through these questions
with these baptismal candidates?
Well, it took many hours for many elders to do that.
Myself, because I was single and young back then,
I remember occasions where I would sit at 8:00 a.m.
with the first candidate —baptismal candidate—
and end up at 12:00 midnight.
And they would take their turns;
after work, they would come; they were not going to miss their turn.
That was how zealous the harvest was and the brothers were.
So let me get this straight.
So you’re pioneering;
you’re going to medical school;
you’re giving five talks on the weekend;
you’re spending three hours in sessions with book study conductors;
you’re spending from eight to midnight with baptismal candidates.
How did you do it?
Holy spirit.
And we were young.
When we’re young, we think we can move mountains,
but the holy spirit was actually obvious.
The branch, then, has asked you
to come to the branch from the field.
And probably you were happy because that would have been relief,
I think, from this schedule.
You know, to be honest Brother Stovall,
it was the opposite.
It was the harvesttime.
And, you know, to experience
the joy of what Jesus said about the harvest
—that ‘the harvest is great and the workers are joyous.’
Many things were happening.
People were coming in.
We were studying the Bible with hundreds of people.
You say you’ve actually been involved
with helping hundreds of people into the truth?
Yes, directly or indirectly sitting and studying the Bible.
And so, I didn’t hurry to go down there.
Conventions were going on, all these meetings.
But they tracked you down.
Oh, yes, they did.
And I was obedient when they tracked me down
and later on apologized for my behavior.
So, what did you do when you went to the branch?
The branch actually wanted me to set up
the Hospital Information Desk work.
Amazing! So that medical training
really has been very valuable.
So, what is it like, then,
working with the HID in Russia?
How about if we look at a video?
It would be easier to just give you the gist
of what happens and how that work is going on in Russia.
That would be great.
One of our sisters was told that she needed a blood transfusion.
But the doctor said,
“They should forget about their religion
because I am like God to them.”
Incidentally, I caught a cockroach
crawling on the floor of his office.
Then I smashed the cockroach,
and I told him: “That cockroach is dead.
“Now if you can bring it back to life,
then I believe you are a god.”
Well, he could say nothing at all.
Righteous indignation gave me the courage
to go and clear our case with the director of the hospital.
There’s no doubt Jehovah really was helping us.
That director became one of our strongest advocates
in bloodless surgeries.
Later, he would even speak in our behalf
to many doctors and conferences.
Look at this beautiful little girl.
She was born with a blood condition.
It was a real fight not to give her blood.
Her case went all the way to the European Court,
and we won the case.
There she is now, healthy and happy.
Experiences like these in the HLC work
have really touched my heart.
Moses, thank you so much for those very encouraging experiences.
Wasn’t this just an amazingly enjoyable occasion?
It’s been so thrilling, so faith strengthening
to get to know these brothers and sisters who have worked so hard,
who Jehovah has blessed to such a degree.
Really, we wish and hope that Jehovah blesses you
as you continue to work hard in his service
until the next time we get together
to get “the inside story.”
Well, what did you think of the new feature?
I’m sure we’ll be seeing more of that in the future.
We can certainly hope.
Well, now it’s time for you to participate again.
If you can, would you please stand, and we’ll sing song number 110,
which is entitled “The Joy of Jehovah,” song 110.

title: 윌리엄 맬렌폰트: 자원하는 태도로 희생을 바치십시오 (시 54:6)

en.text: David’s prayer teaches us an important lesson,
especially since we know
that David enjoyed Jehovah’s favor.
And the key point is:
It was his attitude.
In willingness, he sacrificed to God.
His motive was good; it was from the heart.
And when we study David’s life, we realize that it was a constant.
Even when he sinned, it still was a constant
that he would approach Jehovah with an open heart,
willingly sacrificing to him.
Let’s read Psalm 54:6, the entire verse.
Psalm 54:6,
it starts out as we have already considered:
“I will sacrifice to you willingly.”
But then it says:
“I will praise your name, O Jehovah, for it is good.”
More directly said, really, it’s: Jehovah is good.
His name is good, but he is good.
And everything he requires of us is good.
There’s no command from God for his servants that is bad.
It’s always for our benefit.
Even the elimination of the wicked, really, is good
because it shows love for those who just want to live in peace
and worship their great God in joy and happiness.
So that’s also something that’s very good —what he’s going to do.
So why wouldn’t we want to offer sacrifices
to our great God willingly?
And as we know, Jehovah looks at more
than what we offer to him
or what we give up for him.
In each case, it’s sacrifice.
He can see why we’re making sacrifices to him.
And this is undoubtedly one of the reasons
why Jehovah rejected Cain’s sacrifice.
It wasn’t just because it was a vegetable,
but the scripture says he didn’t look with approval
on Cain and his sacrifice,
but on Cain, because Cain, evidently, had a bad attitude.
There was something wrong in his motive
and why he was offering sacrifices to Jehovah.
And this ties in with what Amos wrote about the Jews in his day.
If you’d like to look up the scripture, it’s Amos chapter 5
and we’re going to read verses 21-24,
to see what Jehovah’s feelings were
about sacrifices that the Jews were making
during the time of Amos.
Verse 21:
“I hate, I despise your festivals,
and I take no pleasure in the aroma of your solemn assemblies.”
Perhaps it was incense, whatever it may have been.
Then he says in verse 22:
“Even if you offer me whole burnt offerings and gift offerings,
“I will find no pleasure in them;
“and I will not look with favor
on your communion sacrifices of fattened animals.”
So, what we learn here is that it’s not what was offered to God.
The great God of the universe doesn’t need
some dead animal on an altar.
It has more to do with the attitude
of people and their worship of Jehovah,
why they were honoring him or doing these things.
And then what’s interesting is the way verse 23
expresses the feelings of Jehovah.
He says: “Spare me the din of your songs;
and let me not hear the melodies of your stringed instruments.”
And then after that he tells us what he wants:
“Let justice flow down like waters,” well, that has to do with the people
and their attitude and their service to God,
“and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.”
“The din of your songs” and the music
—you know, the word din means “loud.”
And it was apparently loud —the music that they played,
the din of their songs, their musical instruments.
And The Watchtower made an interesting comment on this.
Today, Christendom has a number
of celebrations where they use music,
and there’s the din of their songs.
They blend pagan customs with the name of Jesus;
“we honor God.”
And what you think of almost immediately is Christmastime,
the din of the music in all the big stores everywhere.
And the owners of the stores most likely are either nonbelievers, atheists,
or perhaps Jewish or some other background;
that they have no concern for the Lord Jesus
or honoring “the Mighty God.”
It’s all commercial.
And so it makes us think of those things.
An interesting item also
about sacrifice in the first century
was published in The Watchtower of February 1, 2014.
And this is the point it made:
“God’s Law stated that all the sacrifices offered
“at the temple were to be of the best quality possible.
“According to the first-century C.E.
“Jewish writer Philo,
“[he stated that] priests at that time
“scrutinized animals ‘from head to foot’
“to ensure that they were sound in all respects
and ‘without spot or defect of any kind.’”
So before they went into the temple or they sold it
—the animal— the animal had to be sound.
Now, this is what scholar E. P. Sanders has to say about it
—he states that “possibly the temple officials
“‘authorized reliable sellers of sacrificial victims
“‘to sell only animals and birds
“‘that priests had previously inspected.
“‘In this case, the seller would have to give the buyer
“‘some kind of chit, [or token, a guarantee]
indicating that the victim [the sacrifice sold] was unblemished.’”
And then the article goes on to say the following:
“In 2011, archaeologists found
“just such a chit, or token,
“in the vicinity of the temple
“—a coin-size clay seal dating
from between the first century B.C.E. and 70 C.E.”
So it covered the period of time when Jesus walked the earth.
It says: “Its two-word Aramaic inscription
“has been rendered ‘Pure for God.’
“[And] it is thought that temple officials would have attached such tokens
“to products for ritual use
or to animals intended for sacrifice.”
That’s pretty interesting.
Hebrews 13:15 says that we make sacrifices, doesn’t it,
praise from the lips, sacrifices to Jehovah God?
So, what might be our chit, or token,
that says that our sacrifices are pure for God?
Well, I’m not aware that the chit has any antitype,
so I’m not going to go into that.
But we’re thankful that we do not have to get a chit, or a token,
every time we put a few hours in service,
work at a construction site,
make a return visit, or conduct a Bible study.
And remember, no, your chit is not
your field service report at the end of the month.
Not at all!
Isn’t it wonderful? No human has been appointed
to scrutinize our sacrifices
and determine whether or not we merit a chit of approval
stating that our sacrifice was pure to God.
We just keep doing what David did;
willingly, we give of ourselves
to honor our great God, Jehovah.
And we acquire a good conscience that,
if properly trained in harmony with the Scriptures,
in a sense, it might be considered the chit
in that we feel comfortable because of a good conscience
and knowing that we’re giving Jehovah God our best.
We are not worried about some quota in itself,
feeling that that justifies us or makes us holy or honorable,
no, just always giving Jehovah God our best.
And The Watchtower of December 15, 2013, said the following:
“When we live up to Bible standards,
“our sacrifices bring much joy and satisfaction to us,
and they are ‘especially acceptable’ to Jehovah.”

cn.text: 我们都知道大卫蒙上帝悦纳
所以我们可以从他的祷告中
学到一个重要的事情
就是大卫的态度
他愿意为上帝服务
也有良好的动机
他是出于真心的
我们回顾大卫的一生
就会看出大卫就是这样的人
就算是他犯错的时候
大卫还是用同样的态度
向耶和华敞开心房
愿意为上帝做任何事
我们来看诗篇54：6的经文
诗篇54：6的开头
就是我们刚刚讨论过的
“我要甘心向你献上祭牲”
然后经文又说
耶和华啊，我要赞颂你的名
因为这实在美善
简单地说就是
耶和华真的是最好的
他的名字是美善的
他是良善的
上帝要求我们做的一切都是好的！
上帝给他的仆人的诫命都是好的
都是为我们着想的
上帝要铲除坏人坏事也是好的
因为这表明他很爱那些
想在地上安然居住
快快乐乐事奉他的人
上帝承诺给我们的未来是多么美好
我们不是更应该甘心乐意为上帝服务吗？
我们知道耶和华看的
不只是我们为他付出了什么
或放弃了什么
耶和华还会看我们的动机
他会看为什么我们愿意为他做这些牺牲
这也就是为什么耶和华拒绝接受该隐的祭物
并不是因为他献上的是蔬菜
圣经说上帝不喜欢该隐和他献上的祭物
是因为该隐本身
该隐的态度很明显有问题
该隐献祭给耶和华的动机并不单纯
在阿摩司的日子
犹太人表现出类似的态度
请打开你的圣经到阿摩司书第5章
然后读21-24节的经文
我们看看在阿摩司的日子
耶和华对犹太人献上的祭物有什么看法
21节说
你们的节期，我深恶痛绝
你们举行庄严集会时献祭的香气
我一点也不喜欢
香气可能指烧香的味道
也可能是其他东西
22节继续说
就算你们向我献全烧祭
我也不喜欢你们奉献的礼物
就算你们拿肥畜献做交谊祭
我也不屑一顾
现在我们知道
他们献上的祭物并不是冒犯上帝的原因
宇宙的至高主宰耶和华
根本不需要人献上的祭牲
其实，耶和华看重的是人崇拜他的态度和动机
崇拜他和做这些事的原因
接下来23节
经文提到耶和华的感觉
你们喧嚷的歌声不要让我听见
你们弹奏的琴声我不想听
24节告诉我们
上帝想要的态度是怎样的
“但愿公正像江河滚滚，正义如急流不息”
这才是为上帝服务的正确态度
经文也提到“你们喧嚷的歌声”和音乐
“喧嚷”的意思是 “大声吵闹”
通常他们播放的音乐、喧嚷的歌声
和所用的乐器都很大声
守望台曾提到
所谓基督教国家有许多庆祝活动
他们会播放歌曲和喧嚷的音乐
他们把耶稣的名字参杂在异教习俗中
声称崇拜上帝
我们很快就会联想到圣诞节
在大型商场内随处都可以听到喧嚷的音乐
这些商家大部分没有学习圣经
反而相信无神论、犹太教或其他信仰
他们根本不在乎主耶稣
也没有要荣耀 “大能的上帝”
这些全是商业广告
喧嚷的音乐会让我们想到这些事
《守望台》2014年2月1日刊
提到一世纪跟献祭有关的物品
文章说
上帝的律法规定
在圣殿里献上的祭物必须是最好的
公元1世纪的犹太作家斐洛说
当时的祭司会“从头到脚”仔细检查祭牲
确保祭牲完全“没有缺陷和瑕疵”
所以，不管是进去圣殿之前
或是在卖掉牲畜之前
他们必须确保献上的祭牲是健全的
接着，学者埃德·桑德斯说
负责圣殿事务的人可能会
准许一些信得过的商人售卖祭牲
但这些牲畜和飞鸟必须是祭司检查过的
按理来说
商人应该提供某些凭据(或是凭证)
证明他们给买家的祭牲没有瑕疵
文章继续说
考古学家在圣殿遗址附近
找到了这样的凭据
这是个硬币大小的封泥
制成于公元前1世纪到公元70年之间
看来这段时间也包含了耶稣在地上的时期
文章接着说
封泥上有两个阿拉米语的词
可以译作“纯全献给上帝”
专家认为
负责圣殿事务的人
可能会把这样的凭证
粘在祭牲或其他祭物上
这真的很有意思！
希伯来书13：15说
我们用嘴唇以赞美为祭献给耶和华上帝
不是吗？
那么，有什么凭据或者凭证
表示我们献给上帝的祭是没有瑕疵的呢？
我们并不知道凭据有什么预表意义
所以我们没有要讲这个部分的事
可是，我们很庆幸
我们传道、在建筑工地工作
做续访或主持圣经讨论时
不用拿凭据或凭证来印证我们的服务
还有，月底的传道报告不是你的凭据
绝对不是！
这样很棒，对吧?
没有人需要负责检查我们的祭物
或决定我们是否能得到凭证
证明献给上帝的祭物有没有瑕疵
我们要像大卫一样，甘心献出自己
荣耀伟大的上帝耶和华
要是我们的良心与圣经教导的一致
无愧的良心就会像凭证一样
我们有颗无愧的良心
也知道我们已经把最好的
献给耶和华上帝了
就会感到很安心
我们可以放心
为上帝服务，没有时间定额的压力
这也不会判定我们是怎样的人
或是让我们变得更高尚
我们只要尽力为耶和华服务就行了
2013年《守望台》12月15日刊说
我们按圣经所定的标准生活
自愿作出的牺牲
就一定蒙耶和华悦纳
我们也会大大喜乐，心满意足

title: 게리트 뢰시: 믿음을 강화시켜 주는 “예언의 말씀”

ko.text: 오늘 드릴 말씀은 베드로 후서 1:​19에 근거한 것입니다.
그렇습니다. 예언의 말씀은 믿음을 강화시켜 줍니다.
사실, 오늘날 성경 예언에 영향을 받지 않는 사람은 아무도 없습니다.
그 예언을 모르고 있다 해도 말이죠.
미래의 일을 예고하거나 알려 주는 것만을 의미하지 않습니다.
예언은 하느님의 명령이나 영감받은 교훈을 가리키기도 합니다.
우물가에 있던 사마리아 여자는 예수가 예언자라는 것을 알아보았습니다.
그분이 미래의 일을 밝혀 주셨기 때문이 아니라,
하느님의 능력으로만 알 수 있는 그 여자의 과거에 대해 말씀하셨기 때문이죠.
예언은 “사람들이 성령에 감동되어 하느님으로부터 받아 말한 것”입니다.
여호와께서는 성령을 통해 예언을 전달하기도 하셨고
천사를 통해 그런 소식을 전달하기도 하셨습니다.
탁월한 예언자 중 한 명으로 다니엘이 있죠.
기원전 536년경에 다니엘은 하느님의 종들에게 영향을 미치는
다니엘의 환상에 나오는 동물들은 정부들을 상징하죠.
다니엘 8:21, 22의 이러한 놀라운 예언에 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
두 눈 사이에 있는 큰 뿔은 첫 번째 왕을 가리키오.
그런데 그 뿔이 꺾이고 그 대신에 네 뿔이 일어났으니,
그 왕의 나라에서 네 왕국이 일어날 것이오.
그러나 그 왕만큼의 힘은 없을 것이오.”
그리스는 큰 뿔 즉 마케도니아의 알렉산더 대왕이 통치할 때,
하느님의 백성에게 영향을 미치는 세계 강국이 되었습니다.
그리스 제국이 분열되고 그 대신 네 왕국이 일어나게 될 것이라고 말했습니다.
그 네 왕국이 돌아가지 않을 것이라고 분명히 알려 주죠.
이 예언을 뒷받침하는 역사적 증거가 있을까요?
알렉산더에게는 배다른 두 아들인 헤라클레스와 알렉산더 4세가 있었지만,
둘 다 성인이 되기 전에 죽임을 당했죠.
통치권이 알렉산더의 후손들에게 돌아가지 않을 것이라는 예언이
또한 이 예언에서는 알렉산더의 제국이 분열되어
한 자료에서는 알렉산더 대왕 휘하에 72명의 장군이 있었다고 알려 줍니다.
하지만 예언에선 그중 네 명만이 그의 뒤를 이어 통치할 거라고 했죠.
실제로 알렉산더가 죽고 나서 72명의 장군들 사이에는
둘째로 리시마코스 장군이 소아시아와 유럽의 트라키아를 차지했습니다.
그리고 인더스강까지 이르는 동부 지방을 차지했습니다.
넷째로 라고스의 아들 프톨레마이오스 소테르 장군이
이집트, 리비아, 아라비아, 팔레스타인, 코엘레시리아를 차지했죠.
이 네 장군은 알렉산더가 죽은 지 18년 뒤인
이 예언이 세세한 점까지 성취된 사실은
성경에 대한 우리의 믿음이 더 강해지지 않습니까?
또 다른 예언으로, 성경 최초의 예언이 무엇이죠?
최초의 예언은 바로 창세기 3:15에 나오는 여호와께서 하신 예언입니다.
그 예언에선 하느님의 조직의 하늘 부분이 그분의 아내로 비유되는데,
그 여자의 자손이 사탄과 그 자손을 짓밟고
여자의 자손의 주된 부분인 예수 그리스도를 식별할 수 있도록,
여호와께서는 예수에 관한 예언이 많이 기록되게 하셨습니다.
계시록 19:10에서는 “예수에 대한 증언이 예언에 영감을 주는 것”이라고 말하는데,
직역하면 ‘예수에 대한 증언이 예언의 영’이라는 것입니다.
하느님의 종들이 영감을 받아 선포한 메시아에 관한 소식이 모두
메시아에 관한 모든 예언이 반드시 성취되어야 한다고 말씀하셨습니다.
예수에 관한 놀라운 예언 몇 가지와 그 성취에 대해 고려해 보겠습니다.
이새의 아들 다윗의 가계에서 태어날 것이라는 예언입니다.
예수께서 태어나기 700여 년 전에 미가 5장에서는 그분이
스불론 지파의 영토에도 베들레헴이 있었기 때문입니다.
또 놀랍게도 이사야는 메시아가 처녀에게서 태어날 것으로 예언했죠.
이것이 과연 사람이 생각해 낸 걸까요?
다니엘 9장에서는 예루살렘을 재건하라는 명령이 있은 지
이 예언은 예수께서 침례를 받으신 기원 29년에 성취되었습니다.
12장에선 그분의 몸이 찔릴 것이라고 알려 줍니다.
또한 메시아가 우리의 죄를 위해 희생적인 죽음을 겪고
부자의 무덤에 매장될 것이라는 예언도 있습니다.
그리고 그분이 사흘 동안 무덤에 계시다가 부활되실 것도 예언되었습니다.
어떤 사람은 예수께서 자신의 생애 중의 사건들이
그 모든 예언에 들어맞도록 의도적으로 준비했다고 주장하죠.
그리고 다윗이 출생한 베들레헴에서 태어나게 할 수 있었을까요?
그분이 어머니 배 속에서 ‘베들레헴으로 가 주세요.
성경에 제가 거기서 태어난다고 나와요’ 라고 하실 수 있었을까요?
분명 예수는 자신의 출생과 관련된 일을 제어할 수 없었습니다.
또한 그분은 제사장들이 유다에게 은 30닢을 주어
유다가 그분을 배반하게 해 놓으실 수 있었을까요?
적들이 그분의 얼굴에 침을 뱉도록 해 놓으실 수 있었을까요?
로마 당국이 그분을 형주에 못 박으라고 선고한 것은 어떻습니까?
군인들이 그분의 옷을 놓고 제비를 뽑은 것은요?
뼈를 꺾는 관습을 따르지 않은 것은 또 어떻습니까?
그럼 이 모든 예언이 그저 우연히 이루어질 수 있었을까요?
한 성서 학자에 따르면, 그 모든 예언의 성취는
대리석 조각상의 여러 부분을 한데 맞추는 일에 비할 수 있습니다.
서로 얘기 한 번 나눈 적 없는 여러 사람이 각자 대리석 한 조각을 갖고 방으로 들어오고,
이 여러 조각을 다 맞췄더니 완벽한 대리석 상이 됩니다.
그렇다면, 누군가가 대리석 상의 부분 부분을 자세히 그려서
각 사람에게 해당 도안을 주었다고 결론짓는 것이 논리적이 아니겠습니까?
메시아를 식별하는 데 필요한 중요한 정보들을 제공합니다.
우연히 한 사람에게 성취될 가능성은 얼마나 될까요?
연구가인 루이스 라피데스는 인터뷰에서 이렇게 말했습니다.
“한 사람이 수학 계산을 해 본 결과,
단지 여덟 가지 예언이 [예수에게] 성취될 가능성은 10경분의 1이었습니다.”
그가 말한 10경이란 숫자를 곱셈이 아니라 덧셈을 써서 만들어 내려면,
그는 그 확률을 이렇게 풀어서 설명했습니다.
미국 텍사스 주 전체를 60센티미터 높이로 뒤덮게 될 것입니다.’
그러면 텍사스 주의 총면적은 얼마나 될까요?
그 넓은 지역에 1달러짜리 은화가 60센티미터나 쌓여 있는 걸 상상해 보십시오.
이제 ‘그 은화들 중 단 하나에만 표시를 한 다음,
눈을 가린 사람에게 텍사스 주 전체를 돌아다니면서
몸을 숙여 은화를 딱 하나만 집으라고 합니다.
표시를 한 바로 그 은화를 집을 확률이 얼마나 될까요?’
그 학자는 말하길 바로 이 확률이
단지 여덟 개를 성취시킬 확률”이라고 설명했습니다.
그런데 예수께선 단지 여덟 개가 아니라 훨씬 더 많은 성서 예언을 성취시키셨죠.
이건 예언이 하느님의 영감을 받았다는 강력한 증거입니다.
‘하느님의 약속은 아무리 많더라도 예수에 의해 “예”가 되었다’고 알려 줍니다.
예수는 분명히 하느님이 보내신 약속된 메시아입니다.
우리가 그분을 믿고 따른다면, 우리도 진리를 갖게 됩니다.
의심의 여지 없이 성경의 예언은 하느님에게서 나왔습니다.
하지만 성경엔 과거에 성취된 예언들만 있는 게 아니라,
지금 우리 눈앞에서 놀랍게 성취되고 있는 예언들도 들어 있습니다!
이 점을 볼 때 우린 분명히 확신할 수 있습니다.
이 악한 세상 제도가 끝나고 온 땅이 낙원이 될 것이라는 놀라운 예언들도
참그리스도인인 우리도 예언을 하고 있다고 할 수 있습니다.
성경에 이미 기록되어 있는 예언들을 선포한다는 의미에서 그렇죠.
기원 33년 오순절에 120명의 남녀 제자에게 성령이 부어졌을 때,
베드로는 예언자 요엘의 말을 인용해서 이렇게 말했습니다.
‘마지막 날에 내가 모든 부류의 육체에게 나의 영 얼마를 부어 주리니,
그들이 새로운 일을 예언했다는 표현은 없지만
“저들이 ... 하느님의 장엄한 일들에 관해 말하는 것을 우리가 듣고 있소.”
바로 이 일을 예언이라고 한 거죠.
우리는 “하느님의 장엄한 일들”에 관해 말함으로 예언을 하고 있습니다.
그분이 과거에 하신 일과 지금 하고 계신 일, 가까운 장래에 하실 일을 선포하는 거죠.
이미 많은 예언이 성취된 것을 본 우리에게,
다른 사람들도 강한 믿음을 갖도록 돕습니다.
우리는 사람들이 영원한 생명에 이르는 길에 들어서고
우리의 위대한 하느님 여호와와 가까워지도록 돕고 있습니다.

en.text: My comments to you today
are based on 2 Peter 1:19.
There it states:
“We have the prophetic word made more sure.”
Yes, we are fortified by the prophetic word.
Actually, there is no one on earth today
that is not affected by prophecy,
even if he is not aware of it.
What is a prophecy?
The Hebrew term for prophecy is not limited
to predicting or foretelling something in the future.
It also includes divine commands
or inspired instruction.
The Samaritan woman at the well
recognized Jesus as a prophet
because he revealed, not future things,
but things about her past
that he could not have known except by divine power.
The source of all true prophecy is Jehovah God.
At 2 Peter 1:21
it is said of prophecy
that “men spoke from God as they were moved by holy spirit.”
In addition to transmitting prophecy by holy spirit,
Jehovah occasionally communicated
such messages by means of angels.
One outstanding prophet was Daniel.
In about 536 before our Common Era,
Daniel recorded a vision
involving world powers having interaction with God’s servants.
Turn with me to Daniel 8:21, 22.
Daniel’s vision was of animals representing governments.
Note this remarkable prophecy
at Daniel 8:21, 22:
“The hairy male goat stands for the king of Greece;
“and the great horn that was between its eyes
“stands for the first king.
“As for the horn that was broken,
“so that four stood up instead of it,
“there are four kingdoms from his nation
that will stand up, but not with his power.”
Interestingly, the Bible specifically named Greece.
The ruler under which Greece
became a world power in relation to God’s people,
like a great horn,
was the Macedonian Alexander the Great.
Alexander’s rulership was short-lived.
He died young
in the year 323 before our Common Era
—two hundred thirteen years after Daniel wrote his book.
Jehovah’s angel had told Daniel
that there would be four kingdoms
from his nation that will stand up in place of the Grecian empire.
And chapter 11, verse 4, specifically states
that the four regions would not go to his descendants.
Do the historical facts support these prophecies?
Yes.
Alexander’s two sons, from different women,
Heracles and Alexander IV,
both were killed before they reached adulthood.
Isn’t it astounding how precisely the prophecy came true
that the rulership would not be passed on to Alexander’s posterity?
But the prophecy also foretold that Alexander’s empire
would be divided up into four kingdoms.
Did that happen?
Yes!
One source listed 72 different military leaders
under Alexander the Great,
but the prophecy said only four
would eventually rule in his place.
After Alexander’s death,
there were constant fierce battles between these military leaders.
But finally, just four dynasties resulted
—just as the Bible prophesied.
One was that of General Cassander,
son of Antipater, in Macedonia and Greece.
The second was that of General Lysimachus
in Asia Minor and European Thrace.
Third was the one of General Seleucus Nicator,
the conqueror who secured
Babylon, Media, Syria, Persia,
and the provinces eastward into the Indus River.
And finally, the fourth was that
of General Ptolemy Soter, son of Lagus,
who secured Egypt, Libya, Arabia,
Palestine, and Celesyria [Coele-Syria].
These four proclaimed themselves king
around 305 before our Common Era,
18 years after the death of Alexander.
The prophecy was so detailed,
its fulfillment is fascinating proof
of divine inspiration.
Does this not strengthen your faith and trust in the Bible?
Here’s another point: What is the first prophecy in the Bible?
The first prophecy ever was the one uttered
by Jehovah at Genesis 3:15.
It foretold that the offspring of his figurative wife,
the heavenly part of his organization,
would crush Satan and his offspring,
bringing liberation to mankind.
To identify this offspring, primarily Christ Jesus,
Jehovah arranged for many prophecies pointing to him.
Revelation 19:10 says:
“The witness concerning Jesus is what inspires prophecy,”
or literally ‘is the spirit of prophecy.’
What does that mean?
That all inspired Messianic messages from God,
proclaimed by his servants pointed to his Son.
At Luke 24:44 Jesus himself said
that all the prophecies concerning the Messiah
must be fulfilled.
Let’s consider some outstanding prophecies
about Jesus and their fulfillment.
One was that he would be born
of the tribe of Judah,
from the family of David, the son of Jesse.
More than 700 years before Jesus was born,
Micah foretold in chapter 5
that he would be born in Bethlehem.
The prophecy speaks of “Bethlehem Ephrathah.”
Why is the designation “Ephrathah” important?
Because there existed another Bethlehem
in the territory of Zebulun.
It has been identified with Beit Lahm
about 7 miles, or 11 kilometers,
west-northwest of Nazareth.
Again, the prophecy was extremely specific.
And amazingly,
Isaiah prophesied he would be born of a virgin.
What human would ever think of such a thing?
Daniel chapter 9 foretold that the Messiah
would arrive 483 years after the command to rebuild Jerusalem.
This proved to be true in the year 29 of our Common Era
when Jesus was baptized.
Zechariah chapter 11 foretold that the Messiah
would be betrayed for “30 pieces of silver.”
Chapter 12 says that his body would be pierced.
It was foretold that the Messiah
would die a sacrificial death for our sins
and be buried in the tomb of a rich man.
Furthermore, prophecy proclaimed that he would be in the grave
for parts of three days and then be resurrected.
What about the argument
that Jesus deliberately arranged matters
so that the events in his life would fit all these prophecies?
What do you think?
Could Jesus have arranged to be born of the tribe of Judah,
in the town of David’s birth, Bethlehem?
His mother, Mary, lived in Nazareth.
Could he tell her, while in the womb,
‘Please take me to Bethlehem
because the scriptures say I must be born there?’
Obviously, the very start of his life on earth
was beyond his control.
Furthermore, could Jesus have arranged
for the priests to pay Judas the 30 pieces of silver to betray him?
Could he have arranged that his enemies spit in his face?
that the Roman authorities sentence him to be nailed to a stake?
that the soldiers cast lots for his garments?
Or that, while piercing his side with a spear,
they not follow the custom of breaking any of his bones?
Could the prophecies, just mentioned,
have been fulfilled by mere chance?
One Bible scholar likened this process
to the assembling of a statue
made of individual pieces of marble.
Imagine that many men
who had never communicated with one another
each brought a piece of marble into a room.
If those pieces fit together to form a perfect statue,
you would logically conclude that there must have been
someone behind the scenes
who had drawn the specifications
and sent an assignment to each man.
Fitting together like the pieces of a statue,
every Messianic prophecy would provide
a vital piece of information about the Messiah.
What, then, would be the likelihood
of all the prophecies about the Messiah
being fulfilled by coincidence in one person?
In an interview, researcher Louis Lapides said:
“Someone did the math and figured out
“that the probability of just eight prophecies
“being fulfilled [by Jesus]
is one chance in one hundred million billion.”
To arrive at the figure mentioned by this scholar,
by addition rather than by multiplication,
you would have to write down one million
and then copy that figure a billion times.
Putting those odds in perspective, the scholar stated:
‘If you took one hundred million billion silver dollars,
‘they would cover the state of Texas in the United States
to a depth of 2 feet, or .6 meters.’
Texas has a land area
of 266,807 square miles,
or 690,000 square kilometers.
Imagine that huge area covered
in silver dollars up to a depth of 2 feet.
Now what ‘if you put a mark on just one
‘of those silver dollars and then had a blindfolded person
‘wander the whole state and bend down
‘to pick up just one coin?
What would be the chance that he choose the only coin that had been marked?’
The scholar then stated that those
are “the same odds that anybody in history
could have fulfilled just eight of the [Messianic] prophecies.”
Yet, Jesus fulfilled not just eight
but many more Bible prophecies.
This is overwhelming proof of divine inspiration.
Second Corinthians 1:20 says:
‘No matter how many the promises of God are,
they have become “yes” by means of Jesus.’
What does this mean for us?
It means that Jesus was actually
the promised Messiah who was sent by God.
As such, he taught the truth.
If we believe him and follow him,
then we too have the truth.
There’s no doubt
about the divine origin of Bible prophecies.
But Bible prophecies deal not only with past events,
some prophecies are having remarkable fulfillment
right now before our eyes!
This gives us strong assurance
that the few outstanding prophecies
about the end of this wicked system of things
and the Paradise on earth to come
will also be fulfilled in the near future
without any possibility of failure.
As true Christians, we are engaged in a prophetic work.
This is, not in the sense that we initiate new prophecies,
but in the sense that we proclaim prophecies
already written down in the Bible.
At Pentecost 33 of our Common Era
when holy spirit was poured out on 120 disciples,
both men and women,
Peter quoted the prophet Joel saying:
“‘In the last days,’ God says, ‘I will pour out
“‘some of my spirit on every sort of flesh,
and your sons and your daughters will prophesy.’”
What did the 120 disciples do at Pentecost?
There is no indication that they foretold new events,
but Acts 2:11 says:
“We hear them speaking . . . about the magnificent things of God.”
This was called prophesying.
Today, too, whether brothers or sisters or children,
we share in a prophetic work,
speaking about “the magnificent things of God.”
We speak about what he has done,
what he is doing now,
and what he will do in the near future.
What a privilege!
Having seen many prophecies fulfilled,
we have the prophetic word made more sure.
And we are telling people about the prophetic word
in order to fortify their faith too.
Yes, we do it to help them to get to the road
to everlasting life and to develop
an intimate relationship with our great God, Jehovah.

cn.text: 今天我想跟大家谈谈
彼得后书1：19
经文提到
“我们所得的预言就更加可信了”
没错，预言可以强化我们的信心
不论人知不知道圣经的预言
这些预言都和他们息息相关
什么是“预言”呢？
在希伯来语
“预言”这个词的意思
不单是预告未来会发生什么事
也包含上帝给人的命令或指示
在井旁的撒马利亚妇人
从耶稣所说的话认出他是先知
当时耶稣并没有说预言
但他说出这个妇人以往的经历
这样的事只有上帝的力量才能办到
所有预言都是来自耶和华上帝的
彼得后书1：21说
预言是
人受圣灵感动
把上帝的话说出来
上帝除了通过圣灵启示先知
他有时候也会通过天使传达他的信息
但以理是一位杰出的先知
公元前536年
但以理写下了一个异象
这个异象预告
世界霸权对上帝子民造成的影响
在但以理书8：21， 22的异象中
各种动物象征世上的各个霸权
但以理书8：21，22说
多毛的公山羊代表希腊王
两眼中间的大角代表头一个王
大角被折断后
有四只角起来取而代之
就是有四个王国从他的民族中起来
只是没有他那样的权势
很有趣的一点是
圣经在这里预告希腊会成为世界霸权
对上帝的子民有所影响
而预言中的“大角”
指的就是将会统治希腊的亚历山大大帝
亚历山大在位时间很短
他在公元前323年英年早逝
在他去世前213年
但以理就写下这个预言了
耶和华的天使还向但以理透露
在亚历山大的王国中
会有另外四个王国兴起
取代希腊帝国
但以理书11：4明确指出
这四个分裂出来的王国
都不会由亚历山大的后代所统治
历史记录支持这个预言吗？
是的
亚历山大的两个儿子
赫拉克勒斯和亚历山大四世
是同父异母的兄弟
但他们还未成年就被杀
多么令人惊讶啊！
预言如此准确
亚历山大的后代中
确实没有人继承他的王位
另外，预言还提到亚历山大的帝国
会分裂成四个王国
这也是真的吗？
当然！
有一份历史资料列出在亚历山大大帝之下
有72位将军
但预言提到最后只有四位在希腊境内统治
亚历山大死后
他手下的将军不停地激烈战斗
到最后
只有四个将军得胜
就跟圣经的预言一样
第一个是卡山得将军
他是安提帕特的儿子
他统治马其顿和希腊
第二个是利西马科斯
他控制小亚细亚和色雷斯
第三个是塞琉古一世尼卡托
他占据巴比伦、米底亚
叙利亚、波斯和东至印度河的地区
最后，第四个将军托勒密·索特尔
他是拉古斯的儿子
他征服了埃及、利比亚
阿拉伯、巴勒斯坦和叙利亚谷地
这四个将军在大约公元前305年自立为王
当时亚历山大已去世18年
预言的细节都完全应验了
有力地证明是来自上帝的启示
这个预言是不是强化了你对圣经的信心呢？
现在让我们想想
圣经的第一个预言是什么呢？
就是耶和华说的
记在创世记3：15
预言中提到“女人的苗裔”
“女人”指的是上帝组织的天上部分
而这个苗裔会打碎撒但和他的苗裔
为全人类带来自由
为了让人认出“女人的苗裔”是谁
上帝用许多预言指出苗裔就是耶稣基督
启示录19：10提到
“圣灵启示人说预言，是要给耶稣作见证”
这是什么意思呢？
所有跟弥赛亚有关的预言
全都在上帝的儿子耶稣身上应验了
在路加福音24：44
耶稣也说所有关于弥赛亚的预言
都是在指他自己
都必定应验
我们来看看跟耶稣有关的重大预言是如何应验的
其中一个提到耶稣会出于犹大部族
成为耶西的儿子大卫的后代
另外，在耶稣出生前700多年
弥迦书第5章就预告他会在伯利恒诞生
预言说“伯利恒，以法他”
为什么要特别提到“以法他”呢？
因为在西布伦部族境内
还有另一个城也叫做“伯利恒”
位于拿撒勒西北方约11公里的地方
的确，我们再次看出圣经预言是多么精确
让人惊讶的是
以赛亚也曾预告耶稣会由一个处女所生
一般人怎么可能会想到这样的事呢？
但以理书第9章预言
在修复耶路撒冷的谕旨颁布483年后
弥赛亚就会出现
后来，耶稣在公元29年受浸
这个预言就准确地应验了！
撒迦利亚书第11章预告
弥赛亚会因“三十块银子”被出卖
第12章提到他的身体会被“刺”
弥赛亚将会为人类的罪而牺牲生命
也会被埋葬在一个富翁所买的墓穴里
此外，其他预言也提到
他被葬在墓穴后三天
就会被复活
有些人说发生在耶稣身上的事情
都是他事先安排好的
好让自己可以符合圣经预言
你觉得呢？
耶稣能够安排自己生在犹大部族
也跟大卫一样生在伯利恒吗？
耶稣的母亲马利亚原本住在拿撒勒
难道耶稣能够在妈妈的肚子里跟妈妈说
“你要去伯利恒生我
我才能应验圣经预言”吗？
毫无疑问
耶稣根本不能控制他自己在哪里出生
要怎么出生
另外，耶稣有办法控制祭司们
要付30块银子给犹大
让犹大来出卖他吗？
他能控制仇敌吐口水在他脸上吗？
他能叫罗马总督将他钉在柱上吗？
他能控制罗马士兵
以抽签的方式平分他的外衣吗？
还有，耶稣有办法告诉士兵
只可以刺他的肋旁
而不照惯例把他的骨头打断吗？
这些预言全都应验了
难道只是巧合吗？
一个圣经学者说
预言的应验
就好像是把不同的大理石块
组合成一个雕像
假设在一个房间里有一群人
他们彼此不认识
但他们都各自带来雕刻好的一块大理石
如果这些大理石块
能够组合成一个完美的雕像
这代表一定有人事先将
雕像每个部分的尺寸和大小画下来
然后将这些雕刻的指示
交给不同的人去做
跟弥赛亚有关的预言
就好像雕像的不同部分
每一个部分
都透露了弥赛亚的重要资料
所有跟弥赛亚有关的预言
都发生在同一个人身上的机率有多大呢？
一位学者路易斯·洛皮代什在受访时说
有人计算
光是其中八个预言
都在一个人〔耶稣〕身上应验的机率
只有十万兆分之一
想要计算出十万兆这个数字
你必须将一百万加一百万
连续加一千亿次才行
这位学者也打了一个比方
若是将十万兆元的银币
铺满整个得克萨斯州
这些银币还会堆叠0.6米高
美国的得克萨斯州
土地面积约69万平方公里
想象一下
这么大的地方
被0.6米高的银币所覆盖
他也说
假设你捡起一个银币
在上面作个记号
然后叫一个人蒙着眼睛
在得克萨斯州内四处走动
并随意捡起一个银币
而他捡起的银币
就是你作记号的那个银币
这个机率有多大呢？
这位学者说
这个机率就跟一个人
能符合八个弥赛亚预言的机率一样
然而，在耶稣身上所应验的预言
远远超过八个
这有力的证明圣经是上帝启示的
哥林多后书1：20说
上帝的应许无论多少
借着他都成为“是”了
这节经文是什么意思呢？
经文表明
耶稣就是上帝预告要来的弥赛亚
身为弥赛亚
他教导人真理
如果我们相信他、跟随他
我们也能得着真理
毫无疑问
圣经预言的确是受上帝所启示的
圣经预言除了在以前的日子获得应验
有些预言也在今天
正在我们的眼前应验！
这让我们更确信
圣经预告的未来必定实现
邪恶的世界制度一定会被终止
地球一定会成为乐园
预言绝不会落空
身为真基督徒
我们参与了预言的工作
这不是说我们会获得启示说新的预言
而是指我们会向人宣告
已经记载在圣经里的预言
公元33年五旬节
有120个门徒受圣灵膏立
男男女女都有
彼得引用了先知约珥的预言
上帝说
在最后的日子
我要把我的灵分给人
倾注在各样的人身上
你们的儿女必说预言
这120个门徒
在五旬节的时候做了什么呢？
没有任何迹象表明他们开口说新的预言
使徒行传2：11提到
我们竟然听见他们
传讲上帝威严伟大的事
这就是参与说预言的工作
今天也一样
无论是弟兄姐妹还是孩子
大家都参与说预言的工作
宣扬“上帝威严伟大的事”
让人知道上帝以往做的事
现在做的事和未来将要做的事
这是多大的殊荣！
看见这么多预言全都应验
我们对预言就更有信心了
我们要告诉人上帝的预言
强化他们的信心
没错，我们要帮助他们
走向通往永生的道路
跟我们的伟大上帝耶和华
培养亲密的关系
