en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting.
We have some encouraging things to look forward to in this month’s program.
We’ll hear the experiences of Sister Agapita Reyes.
As a Christian wife and mother,
she successfully met the challenges
of raising a family by applying Bible principles.
What helped her to remain steadfast throughout her life?
How can you maintain focus
even after you achieve a spiritual goal?
Could subtle temptations and distractions take you off course?
We’ll discuss an important quality that can help you.
Parents are proud of young ones who give their best to Jehovah.
Their feelings are a reflection of how Jehovah feels
and are the inspiration for this month’s music video.
This is JW Broadcasting for August 2017.
The complexity found in nature
has inspired amazing achievements in technology.
But it has also moved people to ask,
“Was It Designed?”
That’s the title of an Awake! series that first appeared in 2008.
It’s been a powerful tool to turn people’s attention to Jehovah,
the Creator of all things.
We’re pleased to introduce the first
in an exciting new video series based on those articles.
The trunk of the African elephant
is an impressive multitool.
It is both flexible
and strong.
It can pick up a blade of grass
or uproot a tree.
Some elephants can use their trunks to feed themselves
around 270 kilograms (600 lbs) of vegetation
every day.
With their trunks,
they can suck water like a straw,
spray like a fountain,
and swim with a snorkel.
The trunk can give a gentle touch,
give a strong push,
or sound a warning trumpet.
Engineers admire the elephant trunk’s remarkable flexibility.
This comes from having no bone.
Instead, it contains
about 150,000 muscle units
—an incredible marriage of strength and structure.
Inspired by the elephant’s trunk, researchers are designing robots
for the future with greater flexibility.
Industrial design often can be made better by copying
the perfectly beautiful solutions in the natural world.
What do you think?
Did the elephant’s trunk evolve?
Or . . .
This new video series can help you
to see the proof that there is a Creator.
It can especially help you young ones to recognize
and reject the false teaching of evolution.
Use these new videos in your personal study
and share them with classmates and teachers.
They’ll help you give an effective witness
and bring honor to Jehovah.
You’ll find them in the Video on Demand section
of JW Broadcasting.
Young ones need strong faith
in this difficult system of things,
but they are not alone.
They have Jehovah’s holy spirit,
a congregation of brothers and sisters,
and very often, loving Christian parents.
In Monterrey, Mexico,
Sister Agapita Reyes set a beautiful example
in building up the faith of her children.
What circumstances made that effort a special challenge?
It’s not easy raising kids in the truth,
and I had ten.
I learned the truth when I was 19.
Some Witnesses came to preach in our town,
and my father offered them a place to stay.
He spoke with them all through the night
and then announced excitedly that he had found the truth.
Eventually, I was baptized in the 1950’s.
My husband was favorable toward the truth
but got involved in political affairs in the community,
and from there he began his political career.
When I read 1 Peter 3:1, 2,
I understood that I needed to be in subjection to my husband,
with the hope that he could be won over
“without a word” by means of my conduct.
When my children were young,
I made a weekly Bible study program for each of them,
and as they grew up,
the older kids helped me with their younger siblings.
I remember Mom always made an effort to teach me how to preach.
I would write presentations for the ministry on pieces of paper,
and the kids would practice while they did their chores around the house.
We set aside time one day a week for our family study.
It could be anything
—a sack of potatoes, a sack of flour, or a house plant.
She would tell me:
“Imagine that this is a person you meet in field service.
What would you say to them?”
When I finished, she would say to me,
“The way you did it just now,
do it like that when you go out in the ministry.”
My mom was very creative.
She would assign us to play the part of different Bible characters.
My mom taught us to appreciate the truth
through her example.
I served as a regular pioneer for many years,
and I encouraged my kids to reach out for spiritual goals.
My daughter left home at the age of 18
to serve as a special pioneer.
Later, my oldest son did the same.
These two proved to be excellent examples for their younger brothers.
Raising my son Noé was a challenge.
He was the youngest,
and at a very young age, he was diagnosed with epilepsy.
Despite his limitations,
he was able to serve as a ministerial servant
and regular pioneer.
He fought his illness for more than 40 years,
before passing away recently.
Losing my husband in death dealt me another blow.
Now my health and my memory are fading.
I can’t do as much
in the ministry as before.
But even so, thanks to the help of the brothers in the congregation,
I’m not giving up.
Even though my husband was not a Witness,
I respected him as the head of the family.
I will never forget the moment
when my husband asked me to study the Bible with him.
I remember that my eldest son gave the talk,
and his father was among the candidates for baptism.
Forty-two years after I received the Kingdom message,
my husband was baptized.
Another great blessing was seeing my children
grow in the truth and use their youth to serve Jehovah.
Some have served as special pioneers,
circuit overseers, or in Bethel.
If it wasn’t for her help
and the support of my siblings,
perhaps we wouldn’t be part of the organization today.
But thanks to her, we started out on the best course in life.
Words cannot express how grateful I am to her.

Her story is an excellent start to our discussion.
The theme for our program is
“The Women Proclaiming the Good News.”
Sadly, throughout human history
women have been subjected to injustice, violence, and abuse.
Why is that?
The Bible explains.
In the latter part of Genesis 3:16,
notice what God says:
“Your longing will be for your husband,
and he will dominate you.”
When God said that Adam would “dominate” his wife,
God was not indicating His approval of the subjugation of woman by man.
He was simply foretelling the sad consequences
of sin on the first couple.
So abuse of women is a direct outcome
of the sinful nature of humans, not of God’s will.
Right down to our day,
rarely have women been accorded
the dignity that God wants them to receive.
However, Jehovah makes clear in his Word, the Bible,
that women and men have equal standing before him.
In fact, he indicated that women would play a vital role
in the outworking of his purpose.
Our theme is based on Psalm 68:11.
Let’s read it:
“Jehovah gives the command;
the women proclaiming the good news are a large army.”
Those words were inspired by God.
But what did the psalmist have in mind when he penned them?
The context of Psalm 68
shows that David was praising Jehovah as a God of saving acts.
From the time of their Exodus from Egypt,
the men of Israel often had to fight against enemy nations.
With Jehovah’s help, they defeated them.
And the entire nation would then rejoice
over the victory Jehovah had given them.
The first of the victory celebrations recorded in the Bible
was at the time that Jehovah gave his people
the victory over Pharaoh and the Egyptians who were pursuing them.
Exodus 15:20, 21
tells what happened after this miraculous victory:
“Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister,
“took a tambourine in her hand,
“and all the women followed her with tambourines and with dances.
“Miriam sang in response to the men:
“‘Sing to Jehovah,
“‘for he has become highly exalted.
The horse and its rider he has hurled into the sea.’”
Picture that scene.
There were an estimated three million people
in the nation of Israel.
Imagine —out of that large number,
“all the women” were dancing and singing praises to Jehovah.
That was undoubtedly a large army!
What a great shout of praise to Jehovah that was!
Another example was when King Saul and his general David
returned from victory over the Philistines.
Let’s read the account
at 1 Samuel 18:6.
“When David and the others would return
“from striking down the Philistines,
“the women would come out
“from all the cities of Israel
“with song and dances to meet King Saul
“with tambourines,
with rejoicing, and with lutes.”
Notice that the account says
that the women came out of “all the cities”
to greet them with music, song, and dance.
Occasions such as these
were not simply expressions of rejoicing
that originated with human emotion.
Recall that under inspiration, David said:
“Jehovah gives the command;
the women proclaiming the good news are a large army.”
Yes, and Jehovah valued their expressions of praise,
just as he valued the contributions of the men who had engaged in battle.

The report for the 2017 service year
shows that there were over 8.3 million publishers

And we’re grateful
for the warm spirit and positive influence

Clearly,
Jehovah values this “large army” of sisters.
But does he take note of the individual circumstances
and sacrifices of each sister?
We do not have to wonder.
By means of his Word,
Jehovah makes it evident that he sees
and appreciates each of his servants.
For example,
did you notice when we read the scripture in Exodus chapter 15
that Miriam was described as a “prophetess”?
Evidently, she was privileged to be used
as an instrument of divine communication.
In some instances,
this no doubt included singing songs that were inspired by Jehovah.
Miriam was not the only one in the Scriptures with this designation.
Other women in the Bible record,
such as Anna and Isaiah’s wife,
were also spoken of as prophetesses.
In the book of Judges,
another faithful servant, Deborah, is identified.
Let’s read Judges 4:4, 5:

“She used to sit under Deborah’s palm tree

the Israelites would go up to her for judgment.”
Evidently,
Deborah was assigned to settle disputes that arose among Israelites
by giving Jehovah’s answer to problems that came up.
Much later in Israel’s history,
during the reign of faithful King Josiah,
Huldah served as a prophetess.
At 2 Kings 22:8,
we read that while the temple was being repaired,
the original book of the Law was found.
When it was read to Josiah,
he was distraught at seeing how far off
the nation had strayed from Jehovah’s Law.
In verse 13,
he directed the priest, the secretary,
and other influential men:

How did they accomplish this?
Verse 14 continues:

It’s interesting that Jehovah used this faithful woman
to convey his direction
and that prominent men and priests
sought her divinely inspired advice.

Bertille Kupelian,
a special pioneer in West Virginia, in the United States,
entered the full-time service in 1958.
In that time, she’s helped more than 60 people to baptism.
How has her outlook toward the ministry
kept her going for almost 60 years?
My father was opposed
to the truth as I was growing up,
but my mother was very, very zealous.
I knew the things my mother was teaching me was the truth.
I knew that this was what I was going to do.
And it was not easy, but we did it.
I was Daddy’s girl,
but my mom made sure
that I and my siblings knew the truth.
And she studied with us when no other children
in the congregation had Bible studies at home.
Of course, we kind of kicked and didn’t like it,
but I was glad she did it.
My mother was a very, very positive person,
and although she had the opposition,
I saw how she dealt with it
and how firm and determined she was.
And that was something she taught us.
It’s a mind-set.
You know, your mind is a wonderful thing.
It can really influence you toward good or maybe not so good.
And so then, I was determined in my mind
that I was going to serve Jehovah then.
In our congregation, there were brothers and sisters of the anointed.
They were always very kind to me,
and they encouraged me.
I worked in service with them.
And I thought, ‘That’s the way I want to be.’
Children like attention.
And so then, if you give them attention
—you talk with them
and ask if you could work with them in the ministry
and help them prepare a presentation
and go over it and over it
so that they’re ready for the ministry
—then they’ll enjoy it more.
That was one of the things that the anointed
did in the congregation where I was.
They paid attention to me, and I loved it.
How I learned to teach was I think about the person,
and I think about their situation,
and I try to think in my mind what they are thinking,
and I work on that
and think of what kind of scriptures I can find to help them.
And so then,
I try to pattern our studies
to incorporate some of those things.
There are always challenges.
Some of the winters right on the lake where I lived were very harsh.
And my trailer was parked in such a way that every time
the wind blew and the snow came and the ice came,
it sealed the door.
And so then, I carried a big knife in my car,
and I would have to cut around the door
to get the door to open —break the ice seal.
It was interesting.
I had some opposition in the territories,
and one was this lady who was very irate.
And she went to kick me, and she kicked me right in the stomach,
and so then, anyway, I dismissed myself.
Then, a while later, it was time to work the territory again.
Nobody wanted to go there, and we didn’t have do-not-calls,
I don’t think, at that time, at least there wasn’t any in the territory.
So then anyway, I called by and I mentioned to her:
“Why, hello there.
I know I’ve had the opportunity to talk with you before.”
Yes, she remembered.
And I said, “Well, perhaps you were having a bad day that day.”
I hit a lull when I had few Bible studies,
and so I prayed diligently to Jehovah:
“Jehovah, help me. I need Bible studies.”
And then you have to be out there looking for them.
Well, I’ve lost my father, my mother,
my sister, my brother.
Well, naturally you feel at a loss,
but Jehovah strengthened me, and the friends strengthened me,
and I kept busy in the ministry.
But again, it goes back to that mind-set.
Are you going to let the challenge beat you,
or are you going to beat the challenge?
You and Jehovah can beat the challenge.
You know, discouragement is one of Satan’s biggest tools.
And I always tell myself,
‘I’m not going to let Satan beat me down.’
As far as health is concerned, my everyday health is very good.
But I have a leg that drives me crazy.
I think back to Jacob.
He served Jehovah with a limp.
And then I think of Paul.
And so then, those things keep you humble.
I’ve prayed and prayed and prayed about it,
but just like with the apostle Paul,
it didn’t disappear.
And so then, I just say: “Patch me up till Armageddon.
It’ll disappear then.”
If your mind is made up that this is what you’re going to do,
this is your life, this is what Jehovah wants you to do,
and so then you do it.
I’ve seen how he’s kept me going.
You know that I’ve needed work; I’ve needed money;
I’ve needed strength.
I’ve needed companionship
because a lot of times I’m in the ministry by myself.
I talk to Jehovah.
And so then, he’s always there for me.
I definitely want to keep pioneering
or serving Jehovah the best I can,
regardless of what comes up.

At a Bethel morning worship,
Brother Lett focused on the special relationship
between a husband and wife.
What can a husband do to show
that he shares Jehovah’s view of his wife?
My theme for this little discussion is
“Husbands, Love Your Wife as Yourself.”
What did Jesus say
was the second greatest commandment?
Well, you’re familiar with it.
At Matthew 22:39, he said:
“You must love your neighbor as yourself.”
Now, what an excellent illustration
is contained in this second greatest commandment!
If you think about it, we just naturally,
inherently, love ourselves, don’t we?
And we show love in many ways.
So Jesus is saying,
“Work hard to show the same love for others
you show for yourself.”
But, now, thinking of husbands
as addressed in our theme,
who is a husband’s closest neighbor?
Well, his wife.
So especially must a husband work hard
to show the love that he shows for himself just naturally and then
to show that love for his wife.
Now, what are some specific ways
that husbands just naturally love themselves?
Well, let’s talk about five.
And undoubtedly you can think of many others
that could be discussed during this discussion.
But number one:
A husband feeds himself.
Ephesians 5:29 says in part:
“For no man ever hated his own body,
but he feeds . . . it.”
Well, what does loving our wife, now, as ourself require?
Well, for one thing, we certainly would make sure
we provide for the food and for other material needs
that our wife has.
And regarding this, I think of our brothers
in concentration camps in Nazi Germany.
Food was very scarce.
But our brothers, even then, from their meager food ration
would share food with other brothers,
even, in some cases, with worldly people.
Well, similarly, a husband would do without himself,
if necessary, in order to provide what his wife really needs.
But even more importantly, an extended application,
he would make sure that she is well-fed spiritually.
He must make sure that she has opportunity
to benefit from periods of personal study,
congregation meetings, assemblies, conventions,
and family worship.
But now let’s talk about a second way
that a husband just naturally loves himself:
We cherish ourselves.
Ephesians 5:29 says in part:
“For no man ever hated his own body,
but he . . . cherishes it.”
Now, what does cherish mean?
Well, according to the dictionary,
it means to treat with affection and tenderness,
treasure, value, attach importance to.
See, because of this feeling we have toward ourselves,
we try to get rest when we’re sick or tired;
we try to be with friends and loved ones;
we play games; we exercise; we do things we enjoy.
Periodically, we treat ourselves, don’t we,
because we cherish ourselves?
So, what does loving our wife as ourself require?
Well, it certainly means more
than just being able to put up with our mate.
It means cherishing her,
cultivating affection, or fondness, for her.
Think of this: At Proverbs 8:31,
it says that Jesus in his prehuman existence
was fond of humans.
Now, don’t you think that fondness he had for us
made it easier for him to come to the earth,
take the difficult assignment he took,
and even die for us because he was fond of us?
Well, similarly,
if wives are cherished by their husbands
—if husbands are fond of their wives—
it’ll make it so much easier to forgive them,
to even die for them, if necessary, in the future.
But if we’re going to have this proper feeling, like Jehovah,
we have to focus on the good qualities of our wife, see,
not the flaws, the imperfections.
And as one of the brothers commented on
(I love the thoughts in The Watchtower comments):
“Love is best sensed when it is expressed.
“How vital that marriage mates
“not allow the activities of daily life
to rob them of exchanging expressions of affection!”
But now let’s get a third way
that husbands just naturally love themselves:
We adorn ourselves.
First Timothy 2:9 speaks
of women “adorn[ing] themselves in appropriate dress.”
Well, husbands try to do the same thing.
And in adorning ourselves, we try to cover over
and minimize our flaws
and cover our bulges, our blemishes.
We try to make ourselves look as good as possible, don’t we?
Well, what does loving our wife as ourself require?
For one thing, we certainly wouldn’t shine a spotlight on her flaws.
We wouldn’t do this in the presence of others.
We would try hard not to even do it in our own mind.
Rather, we seek to cover over minor sins and transgressions,
as encouraged at Proverbs 19:11, where it says:
“It is beauty . . . to overlook an offense.”
So we work hard to adorn our wives
—make her look as good as possible—
in the eyes of others, even in our own mind.
Well, let’s get a fourth way
that husbands just naturally love themselves:
We take steps to heal ourselves
when we’re sick or injured.
Mark 5:26
talks about a woman who was very sick.
‘She suffered at the hands of many physicians;
‘she spent all her resources;
she didn’t get any better; she got worse.’
But the point is,
she was really trying hard to heal herself.
Well, husbands try to do the same thing.
So if we’re sick or injured, we try to get extra rest,
we’ll buy medicine, we’ll take vitamins,
we’ll make an appointment with the doctor,
we’ll pursue therapy.
See, we try to get well.
What does loving our wife as ourself require then?
Well, we would certainly do all within our power
if she’s sick or injured
to try to help her get well.
But even more importantly,
if she happens to be ailing somewhat spiritually,
we would do everything we can possibly do
to help her get well spiritually.
What would be something, perhaps, we could do?
Well, Proverbs 12:18 says:
“The tongue of the wise is a healing”
—so the using of wise expressions.
Also, Proverbs 16:24:
“Pleasant sayings are a honeycomb,
“sweet to the soul
and a healing to the bones.”
So, “pleasant sayings,” we would use these
to try to help her get well spiritually.
But now here’s one more, a fifth way
that husbands just naturally love themselves:
We make allowances,
excuses, if we make mistakes.
Husbands who make mistakes
are often heard blaming it
on their heredity
or maybe the environment,
their blood-sugar level,
how much sleep they got or didn’t get the night before,
the weather, and so forth.
We tend to well understand our own limitations, don’t we?
And we allow for that.
Well, what about loving our wife as ourself?
We’d make the same allowances for her
—being positive, imputing good motives to her.
If she speaks a little roughly or acts a little thoughtlessly,
we’ll try to discern the feelings
behind the words or actions.
We’ll make allowance, especially if we can discern
that she’s under some kind of emotional pressure.
We’ll make that allowance for her like we would for ourselves.
Well, there we have five ways
that we as husbands show love for ourselves.
We feed, cherish, adorn,
try to heal ourselves;
and we make allowances, excuses,
when we make mistakes.
Let’s work hard to show the same love
in those five areas for our dear, beloved wives.
And I’m sure, as we said, you can think of other ways
that husbands just naturally love themselves.
But what a rich illustration Jesus gave!
And interestingly, he took it even a step further.
He further expanded the illustration
at John 13:34.
You’re familiar with this, 13:34.
He said: “I am giving you a new commandment,
“that you love one another;
“just as I have loved you,
you also love one another.”
So he’s saying that we should have
even deeper love for our brothers
—which would definitely include our Christian wives—
a deeper love than we have for ourselves.
And that deeper love would move us to treat
our dear wives even better
than we treat ourselves.
Husbands, we know your wife
will never grow tired of your efforts to apply that counsel.
Really, the whole family benefits when each member
loves their closest neighbor as themselves.
And when a family is happy and spiritually strong,
they can do so much for Jehovah.

When we are driving, like to the RTO
for the recordings and on other occasions,
we usually sing in the car.
I like to sing the songs because they are good
and have nice melodies.
I especially like the new songs
because they are so different.
One has African drums in it, and the next is a bit Irish
and like you are walking in a valley and on a mountain.
Alma plays the cello and has asked to get the sheet music
for the new Kingdom songs, which are her favorites right now.
It’s been a challenge for André and me
because we are not that musical.
There is also a serious part,
so we start with a prayer to Jehovah.
Then, we watch the video and talk
about the point of the video
and how other children and families
can benefit when listening to them.
Then, we need to loosen up a bit, so we warm up with some exercises,
and then we’re ready to sing.
It is clear to us that they appreciate
their privilege more and more.
They actually see it as praise to Jehovah.
The joy they have of singing for Jehovah
rubs off on us who work with them.
When the children sing with joy
and express themselves freely,
it has an effect on us as parents
and the ones in the congregation.
Jehovah becomes happy when he sees it,
and also many brothers and sisters
and children become happy.
It is fun to make the recordings.
You get so happy, and then it’s more fun
to sing at the meetings.
I see more clearly why we sing
and why it is a part of our worship.
We don’t go there just to spend time with our friends;
we go there to sing.
It is a part of praising Jehovah
Singing is like a prayer to him.
I have been humming the songs,
and people around me wonder what it is I am always humming.
So it has helped me, and it is an easy way to give a witness.
My faith in Jehovah is stronger now.
I think that I am happier knowing Jehovah
after I began singing.
You understand that singing is a huge part of our worship,
and Jehovah wants us to use it.
When children sing out joyfully to Jehovah,
they draw closer to him.
The choruses in Scandinavia are a good example of that fact.
Their excitement for singing
even gave them opportunities to witness to their classmates.
You probably already include singing as part of your family worship
and agree that we feel a special warmth
when the family sings to Jehovah together.
As you look ahead at the August midweek meetings,
you’ll notice a part for the week of August 28 that asks:
“When Can I Next Serve as an Auxiliary Pioneer?”
You’ll want to prepare by watching the video
With Jehovah, I Can Do Almost Anything.
It’s the life story of Sister Sabina Hernández,
which appeared in the December 2015 program.
You’ll find it in the Video on Demand section
under “Interviews and Experiences.”
At the midweek meeting, you’ll be ready to share
how Sabina’s example encouraged you.
Our program has shown us
how much Jehovah values what women do in the family,
in the congregation, and in the ministry.
To all of our sisters,
please be assured that we love you,
and it’s our prayer that Jehovah continues to bless your work.
We want to conclude with greetings
from our brothers and sisters on the island of Saipan.
Part of Micronesia, in the western Pacific Ocean,
Saipan is a popular destination for thousands of tourists.
But make no mistake,
this is a preacher’s paradise.
After early opposition to the preaching work,
the truth is now flourishing
with an average of 200 Kingdom publishers
in three congregations throughout the island,
including 33 regular pioneers.
The relaxing atmosphere and tropical climate
make public witnessing carts an effective way
to reach the hearts of receptive ones.
The large number of tourists —many from Asian lands—
are finding our literature in Japanese, Korean,
Tagalog, Chinese, and other languages.
Among the first baptized publishers in Saipan
are faithful sisters who are now in their 80’s.
Sister Taeko Castro was baptized in 1970,
and Tomasa Mafnas was baptized in 1973.
They continue to be zealous Kingdom proclaimers
and are fine examples of “the women proclaiming the good news.”
We send our love and greetings to these congregations in Saipan
and warmly commend them for their positive spirit
and hard work to make Jehovah’s name known.
Thank you for watching.
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

title: 데이비드 H. 스플레인: 새 노래를 부르기 위해 준비하십시오

ko.text: 물론 그 방송을 아직 못 본 분도 계시겠죠.
그런데 혹시 왜 노래책을 개정할 필요가 있는지 궁금하신가요?
현재의 노래책에 들어 있는 일부 표현들은
“모든 민족의 보배” 또는 “귀중한 것들”이라는 표현을 쓰고,
그 외에도 여러 가지 표현들이 바뀌었습니다.
노래책에 사용된 일부 표현들을 바꿔야 하기 때문에,
중앙장로회는 이 기회에 새 노래들도 추가하기로 결정했습니다.
연례 총회에 참석한 사람들은 새 노래 세 곡을 함께 불렀는데,
그중 한 곡은 왕국 설립 100주년을 기념하기 위해 특별히 작곡한 것입니다.
그 연례 총회에 참석하지 못했다 해도 걱정하지 마세요.
여러분도 곧 새 노래들을 배우게 될 것입니다!
새 노래책이 발표될 때까지 기다릴 필요도 없습니다.
새 노래들을 우리 웹사이트에 게시할 것이기 때문에
그뿐 아니라, 때때로 봉사회를 마칠 때
새 노래 한 곡을 부르게 될 것입니다.
왕국 노래를 인식하는 데 도움이 되는 내용을 살펴볼 것입니다.
그리고 새 노래 한 곡을 부를 텐데요.
짐작하신 대로, 이 노래는 왕국 설립 100주년을 기념하는 노래입니다.
들어 보고 싶으시죠? 함께 시청해 보시죠.
그러면 이 노래와 앞으로 나올 노래들을 부르기 위해 어떻게 준비할 수 있을까요?
뉴욕 주 패터슨의 스튜디오를 연결해 보겠습니다.
여러 해 동안 우리 오케스트라와 함께 일해 온
테드 애덤스 형제와 대니 베이커 형제를 만나 보시죠.
크리스 메이버와 수전 메이버 부부도 나와 계십니다.
애덤스 형제, 손님들과 함께, 우리가 새 노래를 부르기 위해 준비하도록 도와주시죠.
노래는 우리 숭배에서 중요한 역할을 합니다.
그래서 우린 회중에서 노래할 때 잘 부르기를 원하지만
새 노래를 배우는 건 쉽지 않죠.
새 노래를 배우는 건 새 구두를 신는 것과 비슷합니다.
처음엔 새로운 노래가 늘 부르던 노래처럼 편하진 않을 겁니다.
하지만 새 노래를 여러 번 불러 보면서 한동안 노력을 좀 기울이면
우리가 제일 좋아하는 노래가 될 수도 있죠.
새 노래를 익히는 게 쉽진 않죠.
하지만 새 노래를 만든 이유를 기억하면 도움이 될 텐데요.
그리고 성경에선 왜 새 노래를 만들고 불렀는지,
왜 오늘날 우리도 새 노래를 배우고 불러야 하는지 알려 줍니다.
시편 98:1은 한 가지 이유를 이렇게 말하죠.
오늘날 여호와께서 자신의 조직을 통해 하시는 일들을 생각해 볼 수 있는데요
그분의 이름을 영광스럽게 하고 땅에 있는 종들을 돕기 위해
그리고 우리는 각자 자신의 삶에서 여호와의 놀라운 일들을 직접 경험해 왔습니다.
또한 새 노래에는 성경에 대한 더 명확해진 이해도 반영되지요.
그분의 따뜻한 돌봄에 감사한다는 것도 표현됩니다.
네, 새 노래가 나오면 여호와께서 우리에게 개인적으로 해 주신 일도 생각해야 하지만,
현재 조직을 통해 하시는 일도 생각해 봐야겠네요.
그러면 올바른 마음 자세로 노래를 배우는 데 도움이 될 것 같습니다.
하지만 자신이 왕국 노래 합창단만큼 노래를 잘하진 못 한다고 느껴지면 어떻게 하죠?
실제 성악 앨범 녹음을 한 분들 중에
전문적인 훈련을 받았거나 그런 경험이 있는 분은 아주 드뭅니다.
사실 모두가 주로 연습을 통해 노래 실력을 향상시켜야 했죠.
그러니까 보통 사람들도 자신감을 가질 수 있어요.
노래를 잘 못한다는 생각이 들어도, 누구나 더 잘할 수 있죠.
그런데 음이 너무 높은 것 같아서 노래하기를 주저하는 경우가 있죠.
우리가 고음을 낼 수 있게 음역대를 높이는 방법이 있다면 좀 알려 주시겠어요?
사실, 젊은 사람들은 높은 음도 어렵지 않지만,
나이가 들면 안타깝게도, 몸이 점점 말을 안 듣는 것처럼
목소리도 마음대로 안 나올 수 있어요.
하지만 음역대를 어느 정도 되찾을 수 있는데,
운동 선수가 경기하기 전이나 달리기 전에 스트레칭을 하듯이,
우리 목소리도 스트레칭을 할 수 있죠.
그냥 콧노래를 하듯이, 샤워를 할 때, 또는 부엌이나 차 안이나 편한 곳에서,
허밍을 하면서 낮은 음부터 자신이 낼 수 있는 가장 높은 음까지 내 본 다음에,
살짝 더 높은 음을 내 보는 거예요.
이렇게 하면 우리의 음역대를 되찾고 유지할 수 있죠.
그렇군요. 그래도 높은 음은 쉽지 않잖아요?
네 맞아요. 높은 음을 내기가 쉽진 않죠.
하지만 그렇게 하는 데 정말 도움이 되는 몇 가지 방법이 있어요.
한 가지 방법은 높은 음이 있는 부분을 부르기 전에
숨을 깊이 들이쉴수록 높은 음을 더 쉽게 낼 수 있거든요.
그리고 생리학적으로, 입과 목 부분에 공간이 더 커져야
낮은 음에서 높은 음으로 갈 때 입을 더 크게 벌리죠.
이러면 목이 조이지 않아서 고음을 내기가 더 편해요.
높은 음을 내기 위해 숨을 깊게 들이마셔야 하고
그러면 작곡 팀은 고음 문제를 줄이려고 어떤 노력을 하나요?
작곡 팀은  사람이 어느 정도의 음역대를 소화할 수 있는지 고려하는데,
작곡을 할 때, 특히 고음이 있는 경우,
높은 음으로 올라가는 방법은 기본적으로 두 가지가 있는데요.
한 가지는 단계적으로 높이 올라가는 겁니다.
이것이 목소리로 높은 음을 내는 더 쉬운 방법입니다.
하지만 작곡에서 어떤 땐 낮은 음에서 높은 음으로 바로 올라가죠.
그런 경우에도 음악적으로 합리적인 범위 내에서 고음을 배치하면,
편안하게 느끼면서 노래하는 데 도움이 되죠.
작곡할 때 바로 그런 점들을 염두에 둡니다.
수전 메이버 자매가 말한 것처럼 발성을 더 잘하기 위해 노력해야 하고요,
이 두 가지를 잘 하면, 높은 음을 내는 게 생각보다 어렵지 않으실 겁니다.
기본적으로 연설을 잘하는 방법과 비슷한 것 같아요.
「전도 학교」 책에서 알려 주는 방법 같은 거요?
올바른 자세를 유지하고, 몸을 똑바로 펴고,
말하기 전에 숨을 깊이 들이마셔야 합니다.
사실이에요, 자세가 안 좋고 숨도 충분히 마시지 않으면
우리 목에 있는 성대는 아주 작지만,
우리가 충분히 숨을 들이쉰 다음 성대로 공기를 내보내면
뼈와 조직을 통해 울려 퍼지면서 소리가 잘 나와요.
이제 집회 때 생기는 문제를 생각해 보죠.
때때로 피아노 반주 소리가 작아서 잘 안 들리는 경우가 있는데요.
노랫소리가 커지면서 피아노 반주가 노래에 묻히는 거죠.
음향을 담당하는 형제가 주의 깊이 잘 듣는 게 중요합니다.
피아노 반주 소리만 신경 쓰는 게 아니라,
말씀하신 것처럼 청중이 노래하는 소리에도 신경을 써야 합니다.
예를 들어 청중이 서로 다른 박자로 노래를 부르거나,
피아노 반주보다 빠르거나 느리게 노래하는 경우가 생길 수 있는데,
그럴 때 음향을 담당하는 형제는 반주 소리를 크게 해야 돼요.
그러니까 음향 담당 형제는 그 일에만 집중해야겠네요.
운전을 할 때 계속 핸들을 잡고 조정해야만 갈 수 있는 것처럼요.
근데 현실적으로는 흔히 집회가 시작될 때 보면,
음향을 담당하는 형제들은 프로가 막 시작되려고 하는 시점에
이것저것 사소하게 신경 쓸 게 정말 많아요.
그러다 보면 피아노 반주 볼륨에는 신경을 못 쓰게 되죠.
그러니까 그때 적어도 한 사람은 이 일에만 집중해서
피아노 반주 소리를 잘 듣고 조정해야 합니다.
집회에서 새 노래를 부르게 되어 있는 경우에는
특히 더 신경을 써야 할 것 같습니다.

우리 각자는 노래에 익숙해져야 할 책임이 있죠.
집회에 오기 전에 미리, 노래를 부르기 위해 준비한다면,
집회 때 노래를 더 잘 부를 수 있습니다.
집회의 다른 프로를 준비하는 것처럼 말이죠.
가족 숭배 시간을 잘 활용하는 게 좋을 거 같습니다.
보통 가족 숭배 때 집회 준비를 많이들 하잖아요.
그때 노래도 연습하는 거죠. 가족 숭배 때요.
노래책을 꺼내고, 반주를 틀고, 노래하는 거죠.
피아노나 기타를 직접 연주할 수 있다면,
생음악에 맞춰 노래를 해 보면 더 좋겠네요.
jw.org에 있는 쉬운 악보를 다운로드할 수 있겠죠.
그뿐 아니라 형제 자매들과 함께 모여 시간을 보낼 때도 이 노래들을 부를 수 있고요.
숭배의 일부인 노래를 집회나 대회에서 부르기 위해 미리 준비하는 거죠.
충실한 종은 우리가 잘 준비할 수 있도록 여러 가지 도구를 마련해 줬습니다.
그 덕분에 회중 집회나 대회에서 우리가 노래를 더 잘 부를 수 있죠.
여러 달 앞서 대회 프로그램이 웹사이트에 게시되는데요.
프로그램에는 대회 때 부를 노래도 나와 있죠.
그러니까 방금 말씀하신 것처럼 jw.org 에서
그런 다음 대회를 위해 준비할 때 이 노래들도 미리 연습해 볼 수 있죠.
다운로드해야 한다고 하셨는데 방법이 어렵진 않나요?
그 탭을 누르면 왼쪽에 나오는 항목들 중에 음악이 있어요.

기타 연주를 위한 쉬운 악보도 있고요.
사실 웹사이트에서 자료 찾기를 어려워하는 분들도 많이 계시죠.
또 형제 자매들 중에는 그런 자료를 다운로드할 수 있는
컴퓨터나 전자 기기가 없는 분들도 있고요.
따라서 모두가 이런 자료를 활용할 수 있도록 회중 성원들,
특히 장로와 봉사의 종들이 적극적으로 도움을 베푸는 게 좋을 것 같습니다.
인도하는 형제들을 비롯해 우리 모두가 그렇게 서로를 돕는다면,
우리 숭배의 중요한 부면인 음악에 대해 관심과 열정을 불러일으킬 수 있을 겁니다.

필요한 도구는 다 있는 것 같네요.
말씀하신 것처럼 장로들의 도움도 받을 수 있고요.
근데 또 생각해 볼 점이 있는데요.
어떤 노래들은 멜로디나 가사도 익숙하지 않을 수 있지만,
작곡된 스타일 자체도 생소하게 느껴질 수 있습니다.
그래서 미리 시간을 내서 그 곡을 잘 들어 보는 게 중요하죠.
그래야 멜로디나 가사뿐 아니라 음악 스타일에도 익숙해질 수 있으니까요.

이 세상에선 엔터테인먼트 업계가 만들어 내는 것이

그들은 마치 사탕과 같은 노래를 팔아서 장사를 합니다.
다시 말해, 무슨 노래가 됐든 쉽게 귀를 사로잡는 음악이
큰 인기도 얻고 많이 팔려서 엄청난 돈을 벌죠.
사실, 그런 음악은 우리가 어릴 때 먹던 사탕과 비슷합니다.
어른이 돼도 사탕을 좋아할 순 있지만,
문제는 어릴 땐 사탕만 먹으려고 한다는 거죠.
커 가면서 우리는 자신에게 정말로 유익하고 꼭 필요한 음식의 가치를 알고
그 음식을 즐기는 법을 배워야 합니다.
우리 숭배에 사용되는 음악도 몸에 좋은 음식에 비할 수 있어요.
영적 건강에 좋은 음식이니까 자꾸 먹어서 맛을 들여야 하죠.
중앙장로회는 우리가 여호와께 찬양의 노래를 부르길 바랍니다.
성경을 보면 여호사밧 왕 시대에 군대가 전투에 나갈 때도
사람들이 군대 앞에서 ‘기뻐하며 여호와께 찬양의 노래를 불렀다’는 내용이 나오죠.
우리도 모든 도구를 활용해서 새 노래를 배우고 불러야 하겠습니다.
그 성경 기록에서 유의할 점이 있는데요.
그들이 여호와 하느님께 찬양의 노래를 부를 때
소심한 태도를 전혀 보이지 않았다는 거예요.
여호와께 찬양의 노래를 부르는 걸 부끄러워하거나 주저해선 안 되겠죠.
도구들을 잘 활용해서 새 노래를 배우고,
말씀을 듣고 보니, 정말 노래로 숭배를 드리는 것을
기도하는 것만큼 중요하게 생각해야 한다는 생각이 듭니다.
사실, 기도도 늘 쉽게 나오는 건 아녜요.
당시로선 뭔가 혼란스러운 문제에 대해 기도합니다.
그럴 땐 명확하게 생각하기가 쉽지 않죠.
개인적 기도에서도 어떻게 말해야 할지조차 막막할 수 있어요.
그분을 사랑하고 그분을 계속 숭배하고 싶으니까요.
바로 그런 이유 때문에 어휘가 부족한 사람이라도
여호와께 아주 의미 깊은 기도를 드릴 수가 있는 거죠.
노래 부르는 분들도 그럴 수 있습니다.
우리는 부족한 점이 많죠. 하지만 괜찮습니다.
여호와를 사랑하고 노래로 그분을 숭배하고 싶기 때문이죠.
새 노래가 나오면 정말 열심히 연습해야겠네요.
우린 새 노래로 여호와께 우리의 정성과 감정을 표현할 수 있습니다.
또한 새 노래는 성경에 대한 더 깊은 이해를 담고 있고
여호와께서 우리 각자를 어떻게 대하시는지 느끼게 해 주죠.

en.text: If you have seen our broadcast of the annual meeting
that was held last October,
you are aware of the fact that our songbook is being revised.
Well, perhaps some of you missed that broadcast.
So you may be wondering,
‘Why is it necessary to make changes to the songbook?’
Well, as we explained at the annual meeting,
some of the expressions used in our current songbook
were drawn from the earlier edition of the New World Translation.
That translation has been revised, as you know.
Instead of ‘the desirable things of the nations,’
we now say, ‘the precious things of the nations.’
Instead of “loving-kindness,” we use “loyal love”;
“long-suffering” is rendered “patience”;
and so forth.
Since some of the terminology used in the songbook had to be adjusted,
the Governing Body decided to add a few songs as well,
and we are very happy for that.
Now those in attendance at the annual meeting this year
were invited to sing three new songs,
and one of them was composed specially
to mark the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the Kingdom.
If you weren’t present at the annual meeting this year,
don’t worry, you’ll get your chance to learn the new songs—and soon!
And you won’t have to wait until the new songbook is released either.
From time to time, new songs will be released
on our website for you to download.
Not only that, but at times,
we will even conclude the service meeting
by singing one of the new songs.
Case in point: During the week of January 5th,
an entire service meeting has been set aside
to help us appreciate our Kingdom songs.
One of the new songs will be sung on that occasion.
It’s entitled “The Kingdom Is in Place—Let It Come!”
You guessed it.
That’s the song that was composed
to mark the Kingdom’s 100th anniversary.
Would you like to hear it?
Please listen and watch.
Jehovah, you always have been, And always you will be.
You’ve given the throne to your Son; He rules by your decree.
The Kingdom has been brought to birth; His rulership will fill the earth.
For now have come to pass Salvation and kingdom and might.
The Kingdom is in place. We pray: “Let it come, Let it come!”
The time for the Devil is short; We know what this will mean.
Though living in times of distress, We see the things unseen.
The Kingdom has been brought to birth; His rulership will fill the earth.
For now have come to pass Salvation and kingdom and might.
The Kingdom is in place. We pray: “Let it come, Let it come!”
What a majestic song of praise to Jehovah!
Isn’t that beautiful?
But how can we prepare to sing that song
as well as the others that will follow?
We take you now to our studios in Patterson, New York,
where our music choral arrangements are produced.
We’d like to introduce you to Brothers Ted Adams and Danny Baker
who have worked with our orchestra for years.
We also have with us Chris and Susan Mavor,
who both have a background in music.
Ted, we’re counting on you and your guests
to help us prepare to sing the new songs.
Thank you, Brother Splane.
Singing is an important, prominent feature of our worship.
So we want to be able to face the challenges
of singing in a congregation setting.
There is a special challenge when we are learning a new song.
What is that?
Well, I think learning a new song is like breaking in a new pair of shoes.
At first, the new songs aren’t as comfortable as the ones that we’re used to singing,
but after singing them for a while,
exerting a little effort,
well, these could become our most favorite songs to sing.
Now, some of us have a hard time learning new songs.
But we have to remember that these new songs
were composed for a good reason.
It’s actually a Scriptural reason, isn’t it?
That’s right.
You know throughout the Scriptures, we often see an expression like this:
“Sing to Jehovah a new song.”
And the Bible tells us why new songs were composed and sung
and why we should learn new songs today and sing them.
The 98th Psalm and verse 1 gives us a good reason.
It says: “Sing to Jehovah a new song,
for he has done wonderful things.”
Now, we think about what Jehovah is doing today with his organization
—truly wonderful things he’s accomplishing to glorify his name
and to help his servants here on earth.
And each of us, in our personal lives,
have experienced Jehovah’s wonderful things in our lives personally.
Not only that, the new songs also reflect
a clearer understanding of the Bible
as well as expressing the love that we have for Jehovah
and our appreciation for his tender care.
So when we get these new songs,
we can think about what Jehovah has done for us personally, that’s true,
but also, especially what he’s doing with the organization now.
This should put us in the right frame of mind and heart
to really learn the songs.
But what if we feel
that we’re just not as good as the singers on the recordings?
Well, actually the singers on the recordings,
some might be interested to know, very few of those used for vocal renditions
have had any professional training or professional experience.
So all of them have had to learn to sing better,
mainly through practice.
And that’s comforting for the rest of us.
We feel like we may not sing so well, but we all can improve.
We all can learn to sing better.
And, of course, the more you sing, the easier it will become.
Now some of us hesitate to sing
because we feel the notes are a bit too high for us.
Would you give us some ideas
how we can change the range of our voice
and be able to sing these higher notes?
Well, you know, for young people, the range is not a problem,
but as we age, unfortunately, like the rest of our bodies,
our voices can lose range like we lose range of motion.
So we can regain some of our range
by doing a type of stretching with our voice,
just as an athlete would stretch before a game or before going for a run.
We can do that very simply by using like a humming sound
maybe in the shower, the kitchen, the car, somewhere you feel comfortable
and just using a humming sound
to gently go through your full range of your voice,
and then gently pushing the limits of it.
In that way, we can regain and maintain the range of our voice.
So that helps us with the range, but now what about those high notes?
Well, those high notes can be a bit of a challenge, but you know,
there are a couple of things we can do that will really make them easier to produce.
One is: We need to make sure we take a really good breath
before we sing the phrase with the high note in it,
because more breath energy makes it much easier
to produce a higher note.
Also, physiologically, we need more space in the mouth
and throat area to make it easier to produce a high note.
So we would even see that on the outside,
when the mouth gets larger, going from a lower note to a higher note.
[Vocal exercise]
Then it won’t feel so tight, and it is easier to produce a higher note.
Good. So those two things are:
take a deeper, bigger breath for the high notes
and then more space created by the mouth.
Good.
Well, now how does the composing team
help us with some of these high note issues?
Well, the composers do take the musical range
of the human voice into account,
including the range of unskilled singers.
And in a musical composition,
in dealing with high notes in particular,
there are basically two ways to get up there as a composer.
One is to walk your way up there, going up the scale.
That’s the easier method vocally.
That’s easier to get up there.
At times, in a composition,
there are jumps from low notes to high notes,
but there are jumps which are more logical,
musically, which also makes them
more instinctively comfortable for us to sing,
even if we are not trained singers.
So the compositions have taken these factors into account,
and I think, two keys here:
Number one, what Susan has been talking about
is to try and develop our voices a little more;
couple that with learning the song.
And if you have those two things in place,
high notes are not the issue that maybe you thought they would be.
You know, it sounds like the fundamentals for good singing
are basically the same as for good public speaking.
Like the instructions we get in the Ministry School textbook.
Exactly!
Maintaining good posture, standing up nice and straight,
and being sure to take good, deep breaths before speaking.
It’s very true that poor posture and shallow breathing
are definitely the enemies of good singing.
It’s just the way that Jehovah created us.
Physiologically, we have these tiny little vocal chords,
but when we take a good breath and send the air through them,
then it resonates through our bones and tissues,
and we can produce sound easily.
Good. Thanks, Susan.
Good ideas on technique.
Now here’s a problem that comes up during our meetings.
Sometimes the piano can’t be heard.
The volume of the piano is not high enough.
And when you fill the auditorium with voices,
it just drowns the piano out.
Now, how can we handle that?
Well, the key to solving that problem is
for the brother at the sound console to be listening.
Listening not just to the piano volume
but listening also to what you referred to —how the singing is going.
For example, if the singers can’t stay together
or if they can’t stay with the piano recording,
they’re either ahead of it or behind it,
then that’s the cue for the sound operator to turn the piano up.
So the operator, then, has to be free to focus on the sound.
Just as when you are driving a car,
you have to keep your hand on the wheel and make adjustments to stay on the road.
Yes, I think “free” for that task is the key word there.
The reality is that at the beginning of many of our meeting programs,
the brother or brothers in our sound department
are trying to multitask with various little things
that happen right at the beginning of the program.
And this issue of the piano volume sometimes just gets overlooked.
So at least one person back there
has to be dedicated exclusively at that moment
to listening to and adjusting the piano volume.
And this would be especially true
whenever a new song is scheduled for a program.
Definitely, we need to be listening to
the cues or the music when it’s being played.
But you know this doesn’t relieve us of the personal responsibility
that each of us has to become familiar with the music,
even ahead of time, before going to the meeting,
and that way we can be prepared to sing the songs when we arrive.
The same way we prepare for other parts in the meeting.
That’s right.
Well, doesn’t that just put us right in mind of family worship then?
Because family worship is where
so much meeting preparation is done typically.
So include the music during family worship.
Get the songbook out.
Turn on the piano recording. Sing along.
Even better, if you can play the piano
or if you play the guitar, do it live, and sing to it live.
Simplified chords are up there on jw.org that we can download,
but even for social occasions,
social gatherings, we can sing the songs.
The idea is: Prepare for this part of our worship
with the congregation or even for our assemblies and conventions.
Yeah, you know, the faithful slave has really given us the tools
to be well prepared not only at our congregation meetings
but also at these events: the assemblies and conventions.
Months ahead of time the programs are posted on the website.
And in those programs are the songs that will be sung at these events,
and so we can be well-prepared by downloading, as you mentioned,
the piano music or the sheet music from jw.org
and include that in our preparation for these assemblies.
And you mentioned downloading a number of things, but is that hard to do?
Well, they’ve tried to make it as simple as possible.
On the home page is the Publications tab.
You click on that; it brings up a tab on the left side that says Music.
You click on that, and all the music products are right there:
the MP3s for the vocal renditions,
the piano accompaniment, orchestral arrangements.
There’s also a tab for the songbook Sing to Jehovah.
If you click on that, there’s a PDF tab,
and it gives you all the sheet music that you need,
including the simplified guitar chords.
Well, you know, Ted, as simple as that sounds, we do understand
that many still find navigating websites to be a challenging thing,
and at the same time we know that some of our brothers and sisters
still don’t own the equipment,
the computer equipment to do their own downloads.
This is where the congregation,
and in particular the elders and ministerial servants,
can take the lead in helping everyone to have these materials.
Because as we help each other that way,
especially the brothers taking the lead,
then this really engenders a spirit of enthusiasm,
interest in this feature of our worship.
It seems like we have all the tools that we need, then,
to learn the new songs and be well-prepared to sing them at our congregation meetings
with the help of the elders, even as brought out here.
And it really is important to do that because some of the songs,
besides not knowing the melodies or the words,
also could be written in a particular style
that maybe we’re not used to singing in.
And so when we listen to the music ahead of time,
then we can become better familiar not just with the tune and the words
but also the style in which they are written.
Well, Chris, because you mention musical style,
this brings up another personal matter, I think, for many of us,
and that’s how we view music itself.
The point here is that it’s all too common in this world
to just be the product of the entertainment industry
with respect to our musical tastes.
They’re in the business of selling what you might call “ear candy.”
What that means is that anything that just quickly catches the ear
and catches on and becomes popular, well,
that’s a very marketable product, and they make a lot of money selling it.
Well, it’s kind of like candy that we like to eat when we are children.
And we still like it when we grow up too,
but the point is that when we are children, that’s kind of all we want.
Later on, we have to learn
to appreciate and enjoy the foods
that are really better for us and the ones that we really need.
Well, the music that we use in our worship
is kind of like that healthy food.
We might not yet have the taste for it,
but we need to develop it
because it’s there to nourish us spiritually.
The Governing Body wants us all to sing praises to Jehovah.
Just like back in King Jehoshaphat’s time
when the army was going out into battle,
there was singing, and the scripture says
they were “joyfully singing praises” to Jehovah.
So we want to use all the tools that we have
to learn the new songs and just start singing.
You know, Ted, I couldn’t help but think about that Scriptural reference;
it really indicates that those men were not at all timid
about singing praises to Jehovah God.
And really that sets a pattern for us today.
We should not feel shy or timid about singing at the Kingdom Hall
or at any of our meetings —praises to Jehovah God.
And certainly we have the tools now to learn these new songs
and to be just like those ancient Israelites,
singing praises to Jehovah with full heart and joy.
What you just said, Chris, really helps to make the point
that we should view our singing in worship
as we view our prayers.
That matter of being timid,
well, prayer is not always easy,
even private prayer is not always easy.
Sometimes we are praying about something painful
or difficult or something that’s kind of confusing at the time.
So we’re struggling for the clear thought.
We’re struggling even for the words to use in the prayer,
even though it’s a private prayer.
But we still manage to give that prayer to Jehovah
because we love him
and because we want to continue worshipping him.
That’s why, even people with limited vocabularies
can still pray very successfully, very effectively to Jehovah.
And maybe that’s the way some of us are as singers.
We’re limited. But that’s OK.
We still do it, and we’re not timid about it.
We do it for the same important reasons that we love Jehovah
and that we want to worship him in this way.
When we get the new songs, we want to be excited about learning them.
These new songs express our devotion, our feeling for Jehovah.
They also keep us in harmony with the greater understanding of scriptures
and, of course, how Jehovah deals with us personally.
Now we’ll go back to our studio in Brooklyn.
Thank you so much, panel.
Your insights have been most helpful.

教我们怎么做好准备唱新诗歌
谢谢你，斯普莱恩弟兄！
唱诗歌是崇拜上帝非常重要的一部分
我们都想做好准备
克服唱诗歌时会碰到的困难
学唱新诗歌最常遇到什么困难呢？
我认为学唱新歌就像穿上新鞋子
一开始我们可能不太适应
觉得还是比较习惯以前的
但我们付出努力
唱了一段时间后
这些新歌可能会变成我们最喜欢唱的歌
有些人觉得很难学会唱新诗歌
不过编写新诗歌是有重要目的的
其实这是有圣经根据的，对吗？
没错
你会发现圣经许多经文都提到
“要向耶和华唱新歌”
圣经也告诉我们
为什么在古代要谱写并唱这些新歌
以及为什么我们今天应该要学会唱新诗歌
诗篇98：1说明了理由

想想看，今天耶和华正通过他的组织
显扬自己的名和帮助他地上的仆人
成就了多少了不起的事
另外，我们每个人都在生活上亲身体验过
耶和华的赐福

我们对圣经有更透彻的理解

我们可以想想耶和华为我们个人做了什么事

现在耶和华通过他的组织成就了什么事
这能让我们怀着正确的心态学习这些新歌
但如果我们觉得自己

嗯，有些人可能有兴趣知道
参与合唱的人中
只有非常少数是有经验的歌手或受过专业训练
所以其实所有录合唱的人

我们可能觉得自己唱得不好
但我们是可以进步的
我们都可以学习怎么唱得更好
而且你越常练习，就越容易学会

因为觉得一些音太高了
那么，我们可以怎样拓展音域

对年轻人来说，唱高音不是个问题
不过，随着年纪增加
我们的嗓子就跟身体其他部分一样

所以如果我们想要恢复自己的音域

试着用哼唱的
从最低音一路唱到最高音

这确实很有帮助
但要怎么唱到高音呢？
这的确是个挑战
但我们留意几件事就可以让唱高音容易一些
其中一点是
在快要唱到高音的地方时

另外，就生理学的角度来说
我们的口腔和喉咙的空间越大

所以你可以很明显地看到
唱歌的人从低音唱到高音时

这样嗓子就不会很紧
也比较容易发出高音
很好，所以要记得两件事
深吸一口气，然后唱到高音时要张大口腔的空间

作曲团队在这方面会考虑什么呢？

跟发表一个好的公众演讲很类似

姿势不良和呼吸太浅会妨碍人唱歌

可能唱得比音乐更快或更慢
这时候就应该再把音乐调大声一点
所以控制音响的弟兄要随时留意音量

手会一直放在方向盘上随时调整一样
没错
我想重点在于他要能
“专心地”做这件事
实际上有很多情况是
在聚会节目开始前

这时候他们就没办法注意听
钢琴的音量够不够大声

专心地聆听音乐并随时调整音量

但参加聚会的每个人

甚至在聚会之前就要这么做

我们能不能利用家庭崇拜的时间

我们通常会在这个时候准备其他聚会节目

拿出歌本，播放音乐，然后跟着唱

例如聚餐时唱新诗歌

如果我们愿意帮助其他人

提到音乐的风格

他们身在一个商业化的环境里
商人只顾销售那些好听但没有内容的歌曲
我的意思是，那些能快速抓住听众的耳朵
让人印象深刻的歌曲往往是最流行的
这些歌都是商业化的产物
商人靠这些歌曲赚了不少钱
这类音乐就像是孩子爱吃的糖果
虽然有些大人还是喜欢吃糖果
不过重点是
我们小时候喜欢吃糖果
但长大后我们学会品尝其他食物
那些对我们健康更有益和我们真正需要的食物
我们崇拜用的音乐就像这类健康的食物
也许我们还没有培养出对它们的喜爱
但我们必须这样做
因为这些歌曲能够在属灵方面滋养我们
中央长老团希望我们都能唱歌赞美耶和华
就像在约沙法王的时代
军队出征时，有人在军队前唱歌
经文说他们都“欢呼赞颂”耶和华
所以我们也想善用一切工具学习唱新诗歌
现在就开口唱

一点都不害羞
他们确实为我们立下了好榜样
我们不要害怕在王国聚会所

练习唱新诗歌

衷心地向耶和华欢呼歌唱
克里斯，你刚说的让我想到
我们可以看待唱歌像看待祷告一样
讲到害羞，其实祷告有时也不太容易
连私下的祷告也一样
有时我们在祷告里告诉上帝那些让我们觉得痛苦
困惑或难以应付的事
我们可能思绪很乱
挣扎着不知道该用什么词语表达自己的感受
即使是私下跟耶和华祷告也一样
但我们还是会向耶和华祷告，因为我们爱他
想继续崇拜他
这也是为什么即使一个人的词汇很有限

en.text: We would like to welcome all of you
to this update on the situation facing
our brothers in Russia.
As you know, on April 20th,
the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation
ruled against Jehovah’s Witnesses and decided to liquidate
the Administrative Center of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Russia
and all of our Local Religious Organizations.
We appealed this decision,
and the hearing for the appeal
took place in Moscow on July 17th.
Sadly, the three-judge panel upheld
this unjust decision against us,
which effectively bans
our religious activity in Russia.
In a few moments, we will be speaking
with Brother Mark Sanderson of the Governing Body,
who was with our brothers during the appeal hearing in Moscow.
But before we talk to Brother Sanderson,
let’s first visit with the delegation
that accompanied him
in attending the Supreme Court hearing.
The delegation’s resolve to help our brothers in Russia
reassures us of the unity
of our organization and the need for all of us
to face challenges with courage.
We are en route to Heathrow Airport.
I’m flying to Frankfurt to meet up with some brothers
who are heading off to Moscow together
to go to the Supreme Court hearing
on July the 17th.
Our delegation is made up of 20 brothers from 18 different lands.
I truly love the brothers in Russia.
I’ve had association with them for many years.
I was in a Russian congregation,
and so my heart is right with the brothers and sisters in Russia.
I worked in the Russian-language field for 13 years before I came to Bethel.
So I feel like the Russian brothers and sisters
are really my family.
Everywhere I go, the brothers are always asking,
“How are the friends in Russia?”
And they want me to reassure them that they have been praying for them,
and that’s not just mature brothers in the congregation
—young children ask the question as well because they have been taught to pray
for their brothers in Russia.
I could have filled up my luggage
with many drawings from the children in Belgium
for the brothers —their little brothers in Russia.
And we also have heard of some cases of inactive brothers and sisters
who have been deeply moved
by the determination of our brothers in Russia.
The brothers in Sweden
were so impressed
by their fine attitude,
especially when the police were raiding the Kingdom Halls.
Sometimes they were threatened,
but they were sitting there quiet and calm,
and they were not insulting in return.
Do I fear going to Russia where our work is under ban?
Not at all.
There is no reason to be afraid.
I am ready to join my brothers and stand by their side
in this historic moment.
I’m not afraid to go to Russia,
not because I feel I’m so strong,
but because I feel that Jehovah is going to be with us
and he’s the one who is going to be supporting us.
Our intent is to try to meet
with as many of the high officials
from the various embassies in Moscow as possible.
We have done those meetings
in the spirit of 1 Peter 3:15
where it says that we should defend our faith and our hope,
but do it “with a mild temper and deep respect.”
And that’s what we have done.
We don’t demand anything from the officials,
but we tell them what’s the situation with our brothers.
The court case against our brothers in Russia
in some aspects
resembles the court case against Jesus Christ.
In Luke 22:67,
when asked if he was the Christ,
Jesus said to the Sanhedrin:
“Even if I told you,
you would not believe it at all.”
Similarly, our brothers
have been able to show striking evidence
to prove that the charges against us
are completely unfounded.
But despite such evidence,
which is clear even to non-Witnesses,
it is as if we have said nothing.
Such treatment of God’s people, though,
is to be expected in these last days.
But now, we have
Brother Mark Sanderson of the Governing Body
tied in with us.
And first we’d like to say, Mark,
thank you very much for joining us for this interview.
And especially, thank you very much
for being with the brothers there in Russia.
Well, thank you so much, Steve.
It really was a joy and really an honor
to be with our brothers in the courtroom in Russia.
But now, let me ask you this:
What impact will this decision
have on our brothers and sisters in Russia?
Well, perhaps it’s too early to know exactly
what will take place.
But certainly, when we met with various officials
at the embassies in Moscow,
their feeling is that this is going to give open license
for individuals who are prejudiced
to really just take out their feelings on all of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Already we’ve seen incidences of Witnesses having their homes burned;
we’ve had Kingdom Halls be vandalized;
we’ve had children harassed at school by their teachers;
we’ve had brothers threatened with loss of employment,
so we can expect
that we will see greater persecution in that land.
Well, we’re sorry to hear that, but we know that’s reality.
But let me ask you,
Are there options for appeal available at this point?
Well, within the country of Russia,
we’ve exhausted all of the available appeals.
But of course, we are going to take this matter
to the European Court of Human Rights.
In fact, within the next day or two,
we will be applying for what is called “interim measures,”
where the European Court, if they choose,
can step in and even attempt to block
the carrying out of a major decision.
Of course, really it’s very uncertain as to whether Russia
will actually respect the actions of the European Court.
We’ll have to wait and see.
Mark, do you see any Scriptural parallels
to the events you witnessed at the Supreme Court?
You know, Steve, I couldn’t help but continually think
of what Jesus had said
in Matthew 5:11
when he said that they would “lyingly say
every sort of wicked thing against you.”
And that is just exactly what we heard again
this time during the appeal hearing.
These officials were just repeating
these ridiculous accusations against Jehovah’s Witnesses,
attempting to even equate us with terrorist groups.
Now, already the authorities of the world
are speaking out about this.
The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom,
on Monday, already issued a statement.
And maybe I can just read you the first paragraph
of this statement that was released.
They said: “The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF)
“denounces the Russian Supreme Court ruling on Monday
“rejecting an appeal by the Jehovah’s Witnesses
“against an April decision declaring them as extremist.
“USCIRF Chairman Daniel Mark commented
“that ‘The Supreme Court’s decision sadly reflects the government’s
“‘continued equating of peaceful religious freedom practice
“‘to extremism.
“‘The Witnesses are not an extremist group,
“‘and should be able to practice their faith openly
and freely and without government repression.’”
So these government officials of the world
—they recognize the truth.
They understand that these charges
that have been laid against us are truly ridiculous and absurd.
What a powerful statement you read there!
Now, we learned in the segment we just watched
that the brothers in the delegation
had an opportunity to speak
to embassy representatives in Moscow.
Let me ask you, Mark,
What were the results of those meetings?
Well, just to begin, Steve, I’d like to just comment
about the courage of these men
who accepted this assignment to go to Moscow.
You know, when they were invited to come on this assignment,
not one of these men even for a moment asked a question like:
“Is this safe?”
“Will I be in danger in going on this assignment?”
Immediately they said yes and began making their plans.
And then once in Moscow,
we divided into five different groups
so that we could visit the embassies
of the countries that we belonged to.
And so, myself, I was assigned to go
with the group that met with four different embassies.
We visited the United States, the United Kingdom,
the European Union, and Canada.
And at each of these four embassies,
we were given a beautiful reception.
In one case, we met with an ambassador;
in two cases, we met with deputy ambassadors;
and in the final one, we met with one of the secretaries.
But I have to say,
as these people listened to what we had to say,
of course they’re already very informed about our issue,
the question that kept coming over and over again was:
“Why Jehovah’s Witnesses?
“Why is it that Jehovah’s Witnesses are receiving
this kind of attention from the government?”
Well, we were able to give a very, very fine witness
and include many Scriptural thoughts.
And particularly to one ambassador who’s a real gentleman
and really listened to us patiently,
we were able to say that Jehovah’s Witnesses have come
through the concentration camps in the Nazi times,
we’ve survived being exiled to Siberia,
we survived the work camps in the Gulag,
and all of this because of the protection of our God, Jehovah.
That’s why we’re still here,
and we continue to look to our God, Jehovah, for his protection.
And so the reason that we had come to see these officials
was because we are reasonable people,
and we wanted to talk to other reasonable people
to see what might be done to help our brothers and sisters.
And these officials were so extremely receptive
to this type of approach.
And what an honor it was to be able
to praise the name of Jehovah before them!
Very encouraging, Mark.
How did the brothers, though, react
when they heard the negative decision?
Well, you know, Steve,
there’s always been a joyful presence in the courtroom
on these different occasions when I’ve been present in Russia,
but this time with the reading of this decision,
there is certainly a soberness among our brothers,
and they recognize the seriousness of this matter.
But I have to say, I think the apostle Paul
really sums up the way our brothers feel in Russia.
In 2 Corinthians 4:8, where he said:
“We are hard-pressed in every way,
“but not cramped beyond movement;
“we are perplexed,
“but not absolutely with no way out;
“we are persecuted, but not abandoned;
we are knocked down, but not destroyed.”
And I think just even in a small way, you know where it says
that “we are persecuted, but not abandoned,”
I think that to have
this international delegation in the courtroom;
to see that brothers were willing to come,
risking their own safety to support the brothers;
to be there with them in the courtroom at this difficult time
was just a reassurance that Jehovah himself was with them
and that these representatives,
in some small way,
represented to them Jehovah’s love, Jehovah’s care,
and that certainly we were not going to abandon
our dear brothers in Russia, no matter what situation may come.
I like that thought too, Mark,
that we’re knocked down
but we’re not destroyed.
We could say we’re knocked down but not knocked out.
That’s right.
With Jehovah’s help, we get back up again.
But now, how have our brothers and sisters in Russia been faring
since the first Supreme Court ruling in April?
Well, you know, Steve, as I mentioned earlier,
there have been many incidents
across the country of vandalism, of attacks, of course.
We’ve been reporting on jw.org
about our dear Brother Dennis Christensen
who was arrested and has been held now
for two months, basically, in the prison there in Russia.
He has not been allowed to communicate with his wife during this time.
And now we learned, when we were present in Russia,
that the officials only allow him to shower twice a week.
Can you imagine?
Treating him as though he was a very, very serious criminal
when all he did was attend a meeting
to read God’s Word and worship Jehovah.
What a horrible thing!
And of course, the officials from all the countries of the world
recognize the terrible, terrible injustice that’s being done here.
But having said that,
in spite of these attacks that we have seen across the country,
what we also see is that our brothers and sisters
are continuing in their worship for Jehovah.
They’re continuing to have their meetings.
One of the brothers commented to me, he said:
“Some who used to never comment at the meetings,
“now they love to come and comment and express themselves.
“Some who have been inactive
have begun to attend the meetings again.”
And one brother told me
that when they held a small mini-convention,
you know, watching some of the replays that have been made available,
that just in their small group, they had five baptized.
Can you imagine?
So we can say with confidence
that all of these efforts
that are being made to try to stop our worship of Jehovah,
to wipe it out, are not going to have any success.
It really reminds me, would it be OK
if I just shared this Scriptural thought?
Absolutely! Please.
It just makes me think of this thought in Psalm 124.
And this really has to be the confidence of our brothers in Russia,
but it needs to be the confidence, really, of God’s people all around the world.
We have to put our faith in these words.
It says: “If Jehovah had not been with us,”
this is verse 2: “If Jehovah had not been with us
“when men rose up to attack us,
“then they would have swallowed us up alive
“when their anger was burning against us.
“Then the waters would have washed us away,
“the torrent would have swept over us.
“The raging waters would have overwhelmed us.
“May Jehovah be praised,
“for he has not given us as prey to their teeth.
“We are like a bird that escaped from the hunter’s trap;
“the trap was broken, and we escaped.
“Our help is in the name of Jehovah,
the Maker of heaven and earth.”
Well, you know, so many times,
our enemies have thought that they had us locked in that trap
and that there was no way to escape,
but how Jehovah has proven them wrong,
and how he has come to the aid of his people!
And that is the same confidence that we have today,
and it’s the same confidence our brothers will have.
It’s the same confidence we’ll have no matter where we are in the world
as the scene of this world continues to change.
We wholeheartedly agree with you,
and it definitely warms our heart
to hear these strengthening comments.
Thank you very much, Mark,
and thank you again, too,
and the rest of the delegation,
for traveling to Russia
to be with our dear brothers and sisters.
And we’re confident that your presence assured them
of Jehovah’s love
and Jehovah’s care for them.
Thank you so much, Steve.
As I said, it was a great, great honor and privilege.
I truly love our dear brothers in Russia.
Although the appeal decision was not in our favor,
we are not disheartened.
As our regional convention theme for this year emphasizes,
we do not give up!
Brothers and sisters in Russia,
we encourage you
to stay close to Jehovah and his organization.
Continue to pray to Jehovah for strength
to face this persecution with boldness,
knowing he will provide you
with the strength needed
along with the guidance and wisdom that you need.
And please know
that you are excellent examples
for the rest of us to follow
when we face persecution.
We wholeheartedly agree
with the Bible writer’s expressions
in Habakkuk 3:18.
He said:
“Yet, as for me,
“I will exult in Jehovah;
“I will be joyful
in the God of my salvation.”
Yes, whatever the world does to us,
we maintain our faith in Jehovah’s saving power
and will do our utmost to remain
in Jehovah’s protective care.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: About every two or three minutes,
we prayed because the hurricane was so terrifying.
Imagine that your house just lifted up into the air and flew away.
At that time, we were standing in water,
so we just ran.
This is our Kingdom Hall.
When we saw that it was damaged,
we were deeply affected because we realized
we could not meet here anymore with our brothers and sisters
to sympathize with them.
That was very hard for us.
Even in this situation, I know we’re not alone
—even though our town was destroyed.
I know our brothers, no matter where they are,
will come to help us.
The priority of disaster relief
is for the Branch Committee to quickly appoint
qualified local brothers to respond
to the first immediate needs of our brothers and sisters.
Of course,
giving support to our brothers and sisters oftentimes means funds.
So it’s the worldwide brotherhood, the “Matthew 24:14 contributions,”
that really does help.
Here in Haiti, many brothers are overjoyed
that they can send something to help their brothers.
There are brothers who have even donated beyond their means.
In our brotherhood,
no matter where a brother is,
if he’s suffering from a disaster or he has a problem,
all the brothers feel
as if they’re also facing that problem.
We all do our best to support and help them.
We didn’t have any way to make a bed to lie down.
Eventually, our sisters in the Paillant Congregation helped us out.
They ran up and made beds for us out of plywood
that they would put on top of eight blocks.
And they brought sheets and pillows so that we could lie down.
That was very touching,
that kind deed our brothers did for us.
We truly felt that it was Jehovah who was coming
to our aid at that moment.
They brought boxes of Bibles, medical kits, food stuffs.
Besides that, they brought several tents.
That helped the brothers that lost all that they had,
even their houses,
so that they could have shelter from the rain.
In one of the talks given by a Governing Body member,
he showed that we have more difficult situations ahead.
The only thing we can do
is continue to rely on Jehovah.
A way we can help our brothers cope when they’re in such a circumstance
is to make them realize that it is the Kingdom hope
—to refresh their memory, to make them really believe
and feel that it’s the Kingdom hope— that’s going to change all of this.
They shared encouraging words and read Bible verses that really helped us
to see the power of God’s Word.
That boosted our faith in the promises
Jehovah made to remove all causes of suffering that afflict us today.
It’s like the Bible says:
“A righteous man’s supplication has a powerful effect.”
So the strength I regained makes me feel
that the entire worldwide brotherhood is praying for me.
I feel that it’s that strength that has allowed me
to resume my theocratic activities with zeal.
As Jehovah’s Witnesses, not only do we know
that these things must take place —since we are deep in the last days—
but we also know that our deliverance is closer.
I lost my livelihood;
it’s all completely gone.
But I have been so encouraged;
it’s as if the hurricane never even happened.
That’s how I feel, like it never even happened.
Many people say it would have been better if they had died in the hurricane.
But no matter what sufferings we endure,
we have hope.
We see beyond the suffering and see God’s Kingdom is coming.
This is extraordinary.
No matter what form suffering may take,
we are able to patiently endure
because we know that suffering will not last forever.
