en.text: There are people who believe
there is no need for a religious organization.
They feel they have their own personal relationship with God
and that is good enough.
They see no need to be associated with a specific organization.
However, what does God’s own inspired Word suggest?
That he would use an organization, or channel,
through which spiritual food would be dispensed
from his Word, the Bible.
For example, 1 Peter 2:17 says
to “have love for the whole association of brothers.”
One dictionary definition for “association”
is “an organization of persons having a common interest.”
We have a very interesting, insightful look
at the organization in the first century.
If we glance down through chapter 15 of the book of Acts,
we can gain some insight.
Verse 1 indicates there was an issue that caused a disagreement
between some of the members of the congregation.
Then verse 2 says:
“But after quite a bit of dissension and disputing
“by Paul and Barnabas with them,
“it was arranged for Paul, Barnabas, and some of the others
“to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem
regarding this issue.”
It sounds like an organization to me.
And after considerable discussion
and with the help of God’s holy spirit,
what transpired?
Verses 22 and 23 say:
“Then the apostles and the elders, together with the whole congregation,
“decided to send chosen men from among them to Antioch,
“along with Paul and Barnabas;
“they sent Judas who was called Barsabbas and Silas,
“who were leading men among the brothers.
They wrote this and sent it through them.”
Then in verses 23-29
is the letter of direction that was delivered to Antioch
and other congregations as well.
In fact, in verse 41, it says Paul and Silas
“went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the congregations.”
Chapter 16, verse 5 says:
“Then, indeed, the congregations continued to be made firm in the faith
and to increase in number day by day.”
So it was not a matter of isolated Christians sitting at home
claiming to have a personal relationship with God.
No, the work was organized,
and congregations kept being added “day by day.”
That is very similar to what we see in Jehovah’s organization today.
In fact, the organization of Jehovah’s Witnesses is patterned
after the first-century Christian congregation
as set forth in the Scriptures.
I would like to remind all of Jehovah’s Witnesses
—whether already baptized or working toward baptism—
of this book, Organized to Do Jehovah’s Will.
It provides an overall view
of how the Christian congregation is organized
for getting God’s work done.
The book also offers counsel and direction
to help us maintain unity with our brothers worldwide.
New ones need to become familiar
with the operation of Jehovah’s organization
and learn how they can have a share
in the modern-day preaching work.
In fact, when a Bible student progresses
and desires to join us in the ministry
as an unbaptized publisher,
the elders direct him to make a study of this book,
including the “Questions for Those Desiring to Get Baptized”
in the appendix.
Even for those of us who have been baptized many years,
it may be good to schedule the reading
of one chapter of the book each week
during our personal study or family worship.
It contains general information
concerning the duties of elders and ministerial servants,
judicial procedures,
and various other features of congregation organization.
I would like to take a few minutes and review some of the information
in chapter 1 of the publication.
Though there are thousands of national
and international organizations around the world,
they are organized
according to human viewpoints and philosophies.
But our organization is different;
it is theocratic.
That means it is ruled by Jehovah as Head over all.
Isaiah 33:22 says that he is our Judge,
Lawgiver, and King.
Many large organizations appoint
a chief executive officer, or CEO.
He is the executive with the chief decision-making authority
in a business or corporation.
In a similar way, Jehovah has appointed his Son, Jesus,
to be the one with chief decision-making authority
over the congregation of God.
Ephesians 1:22
is speaking of Jehovah’s actions in connection with Jesus.
It says:
“He also subjected all things under his feet
“and made him head over all things
with regard to the congregation.”
We see the structure of the organization taking shape.
Jehovah is the Universal Sovereign, the King,
directing the millions of angels
making up his heavenly organization.
But when it comes to directing
the visible earthly part of God’s organization,
he has delegated that responsibility to Jesus,
the head of the congregation of God.
Chapter 2 of the Organized book
explains this Scriptural position of Jesus.
And how does Jesus direct the organization here on earth?
Matthew 24:45 says that Jesus has appointed
a “faithful and discreet slave”
to serve spiritual “food at the proper time.”
Today,
seven anointed men make up the faithful slave,
and collectively, they are known as the Governing Body.
And Jesus uses the holy spirit to direct these men
in harmony with the Scriptures.
The Scriptural basis for this layer of organization
is set forth in chapter 3 of the book.
Chapter 4 is entitled
“How the Congregation Is Organized and Governed.”
The organizational structure incorporates Branch Committees,
circuit overseers, elders, and ministerial servants.
The subject index in the back of the book
can be useful to quickly gain access to information
on various aspects of the organization.
Suppose you’re a young person,
maybe even a relatively young married couple.
The circuit overseer is visiting,
and he asks you what spiritual goals you have.
How would you answer?
Would your mind start racing,
trying to think of various avenues of service available?
How about now, before you are asked such a question,
you look in the subject index under “Goals”?
There are 11 references to paragraphs in the book on that subject.
After reading about all
of the possibilities and different categories,
you would be in a better position to plan your life
for a great future
in the earthly part of Jehovah’s organization.
At this time,
I would like to draw your attention to a very important factor
in a new ones making progress
and attaining spiritual stability.
On page 213 of the Organized book,
it discusses a person interested in being baptized.
After the elders go over the questions in part 3 of the book,
it says this:
“If he has not completed his study of the Bible Teach and ‘God’s Love’ books,
the elders should make arrangements for someone to help him do so.”
The two books complement each other so well.
When someone becomes a dedicated and baptized servant of Jehovah,
we want them to stay closely attached to the organization.
Yet every year,
there are a number who stop attending meetings
and become inactive.
At times, it has been found
that they did not finish studying the two books.
You see,
the Bible Teach book helps new ones
to have an accurate knowledge of the Bible,
and they often learn to love Jehovah.
The “Keep Yourselves in God’s Love” book
helps us to learn to apply the Bible
and live in harmony with Jehovah’s standards.
Notice what Jesus told his faithful apostles
at John 15:10:
“If you observe my commandments, you will remain in my love,
“just as I have observed the commandments of the Father
and remain in his love.”
Did you notice that Jesus remained in God’s love
by observing his Father’s commandments?
The same is true of us today.
To remain in God’s love,
we need to apply the truth in our everyday life.
And what is the result if we keep ourselves in God’s love?
It is so clearly stated
in Jude 21:
“In order to keep yourselves in God’s love,
“while you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ
with everlasting life in view.”
Staying in God’s love results in everlasting life.
It is so important to make sure our Bible students
complete a study of both books,
and that applies to our children too.
Sometimes as parents,
we can assume that our children are developing
a trusting relationship with Jehovah
because they have been going to meetings since they were very small.
A relationship with Jehovah does not happen by means of osmosis.
A child does not simply absorb and assimilate truth
and a love for God
just by being in the presence of others
who have a close relationship with Jehovah.
We very much appreciate all of the videos we have,
including Become Jehovah’s Friend and JW Broadcasting.
But new ones and young ones
need to be able to go through the process of deep study
to get to the Bible’s truth
and get it etched into their minds
and lodged deep in their hearts.
Therefore,
if you parents realize that you have not studied
both books with your young ones,
it would be good to see that a schedule is established to do so.
The Governing Body gives all credit
for the success of this organization to Jehovah
and the appointed head of the congregation, Jesus Christ.
We are just imperfect men trying to follow
the lead of Christ and the holy spirit.
At 1 Corinthians 1:26,
Paul says:
“For you see his calling of you, brothers,
that there are not many wise in a fleshly way.”
Verse 27 says:
“But God chose the foolish things of the world
to put the wise men to shame.”
Then verse 30 says that Christ Jesus
“has become to us wisdom from God.”
That is where the direction and wisdom
of the organization come from,
not from mere man.
The words of Jehovah to the prophet Zechariah fit today
when we see the amazing advances in the organization.
Zechariah 4:6 says:
“‘Not by a military force, nor by power,
but by my spirit,’ says Jehovah of armies.”
While there are some well-educated and prominent men
who have accepted the truth and are now our fellow brothers,
the majority in the organization come from a more humble background.
For example,
among the first of Jehovah’s modern-day servants
to introduce the Kingdom message to people in Denmark
was a shoemaker.
In Switzerland and France, it was a gardener.
In many parts of Africa,
the message was carried by itinerant workers.
In Brazil, sailors had a share.
Quite a few of the Polish Witnesses in northern France
were coal miners.
Jehovah and Jesus use all of us
to get a remarkable work accomplished.
We are proud to be a part of this spirit-directed organization.
As one older circuit overseer was heard to say,
“This is the best imperfect organization on earth!”
There are no perfect organizations on earth.
However, this is the best of them all.
And we appreciate the contribution all of you make
to the success of the preaching work worldwide.

cn.text: 有些人也许觉得没必要加入
任何宗教团体
他们觉得只要自己跟上帝建立友谊就够了
根本就不需要属于某个宗教团体
不过，上帝的话语圣经怎么说呢？
圣经说上帝会通过一个组织、一个途径
把满足心灵的食物分发出去
例如，彼得前书2:17说
“要爱整个弟兄团体”
根据一部词典解释
“团体”就是
“由志趣相投的人构成的组织”
我们来深入了解一下
1世纪的基督徒是怎样组织起来的
如果看看使徒行传第15章
就能找到一些线索
第1节提到
会众里有一些人对一个问题有不同的意见
然后第2节说
很明显，他们是很有组织的
那么经过多次的讨论，还有神圣力量的指引
结果如何呢？
接着23-29节记录了这封信的内容
是给安提阿和其他会众的指示
41节说，保罗和西拉
然后16:5说
可见，基督徒不只是各自在自己的家里
向上帝祷告，崇拜上帝就够了
相反，当时的基督徒是很有组织的
而会众的人数也“天天增加”
今天，耶和华组织的情况也很类似
事实上
耶和华见证人就是根据圣经的记载
按照1世纪基督徒会众的模式组织起来的
在这里，我想请所有弟兄姐妹
不管已经受浸，还是有受浸目标的
不要忘记善用这本书
《组织起来遵行耶和华的旨意》
这本书详细说明了基督徒会众怎样组织起来
完成耶和华的工作
另外，也提供了建议和指引
让我们跟全球的弟兄姐妹团结地崇拜上帝
圣经学生需要熟悉耶和华的组织
是怎样组织起来的
并且学会怎样向人传道
事实上，当圣经学生不断进步
想要成为未受浸传道员的时候
长老会请他仔细读读这本书
包括附录中
“打算受浸的人要温习的问题”
就算我们已经受浸很多年
也不妨计划在个人研读
或者家庭崇拜时每次看一章
另外，这本书概述了长老和助理仆人的职责
司法程序
以及把会众组织起来的各种安排
现在我想用几分钟的时间
复习一下这本书第1章的内容
在全球各地，有很多社会团体和国际机构
它们都是按照人的想法和理念组织起来的
但我们的组织完全不同
我们是按照上帝的意思组织起来的
领导我们的是耶和华，不是任何人
以赛亚书33:22说
上帝是我们的“审判官”
“立法者”和“君王”
很多大型机构或企业
都有一位总经理或者行政总裁
在这个机构或企业里拥有决策的权力
同样
耶和华委任了他的儿子耶稣去管理会众
负责为耶和华的会众作出重要的决策
以弗所书1:22
就提到了耶和华委任耶稣的这件事
经文说
我们从中看到上帝的组织有怎样的架构
耶和华是宇宙的至高统治者、是君王
指挥亿万的天使
他们构成上帝在天上的组织
至于上帝组织在地上的部分
上帝把指挥会众的权力授予了耶稣
他是会众的元首
《组织》书的第2章就清楚解释了
上帝让耶稣担任的角色
耶稣怎么指挥上帝在地上的这个组织呢？
马太福音24:45说
耶稣委派“忠信睿智的奴隶”
在适当的时候给人心灵的食物
今天，七位受神圣力量任命的弟兄
组成忠信的奴隶，也就是中央长老团
耶稣用神圣力量引导他们
帮助他们按照圣经原则去做决定
组织的这些安排有什么圣经根据
第3章有详细的说明
第4章的题目是〈会众的组织和管理〉
组织的架构包括
分部委员会、分区监督、长老和助理仆人

title: 기대하지 않은 곳에서 친구를 찾아 보세요

ko.text: 친구들을 뒤에 두고 떠나오는 것도 정말 힘들었는데

성경에 기록된 가장 친밀한 우정 중 하나를 생각해 보면

여호와를 사랑하는 친구를 찾아 보면 어떠니?
평생 가는 친구들을 사귈 수 있을 거야
좋은 친구는 기대하지 않은 곳에서 나올 수 있어
그날 밤 우린 다 마음이 편치 않았죠
캐머런이 자기가 연 파티 사진을 올렸어요
그런데 어느 결혼 기념일에 내게 카메라를 사줘서
그럼. 사진 찍는 게 아주 재밌어
여호와의 창조물을 가까이하는 건 정말 특별하지
우리가 결코 혼자가 아니라는 걸 느끼게 해 주거든
기대하지 않은 나이층에서 나올 수 있습니다
저는 맥스 형제와 함께 더 시간을 보내면서
다윗과 요나단의 경우도 비슷하단 걸 깨달았어요
전 좋은 영적 습관을 계속 유지할 수 있었습니다
맥스 형제와 저는 좋은 친구가 되었어요
바로 눈앞에 좋은 친구가 있단 걸

en.text: My name is Akil.
When I was 18, my family moved to a new city.
It was bad enough leaving my friends behind.
But now,
I wasn’t sure if I could make new ones.
My parents seemed really happy.
I didn’t want to make them feel bad
by telling them how I really felt.
The new school wasn’t much better
until I met Cameron.
He seemed like a pretty cool guy.
Soon, his friends became my friends.
. . . something that David believed was true,
he actually proved it by the association that he kept.
We think about one of the closest friendships
recorded in the Scriptures,
and it was that of David and Jonathan.
What was it that David and Jonathan shared in common?
It wasn’t their age.
Akil, you were texting in the meeting.
I shouldn’t have sent the text.
I’m sorry.
But Cameron is a good person.
He might even study one day.
I understand that, Akil.
But we all have to be careful with how much time
we spend with people that don’t love Jehovah.
See, their values are just different.
You know what Proverbs 13:20 says:
‘Walk with those who are wise.’
So why don’t you seek out friends who love Jehovah?
And you will make friends that last a lifetime.
How am I supposed to do that?
There’s no one my age in the congregation.
Akil, good friends can come from unexpected places.
Mom, I had good friends
—back home.
We all felt bad that night.
The next day,
Cameron posted pictures of a party he had.
My parents were right.
I broke off my association with Cameron
and his friends,
but I still felt
lost.
Hi, Akil?
Do you have field service plans for Saturday?
Ah, no.
Good. Now you do.
I’ll see you at the 9:30 a.m. meeting, OK?
After service,
Max had the group over for refreshments.
Did you take these?
Do you like them?
Yeah.
My wife, she was always the photographer.
She loved photography.
And then one anniversary she went out and bought me a camera,
and from that moment on, I was hooked too.
Time flies so quickly.
It’s hard to believe she passed away 12 years ago now.
I’m sorry.
It’s OK.
But you still take pictures?
I do. I really enjoy photography.
There’s something about being close
to Jehovah’s creation.
It reminds me
that we’re never really alone, you know?
Good friends can come from unexpected places
and unexpected ages.
As I spent more time with Max,
I realized it was just like David and Jonathan.
Their friendship was based,
not on age, but on their love for Jehovah.
And they helped each other.
And with Max’s help,
I was able to keep a good spiritual routine
without interruption.
Although we weren’t the same age,
Max became my good friend.
I just needed to see what was right
in front of me.

en.text: Before I started pioneering,
I was really nervous that I wouldn’t be able to get my time in every month.
It was a bit hard when I started pioneering because I didn’t have a car.
My boss, he didn’t give me part-time work.
I found it really hard to balance schoolwork
and pioneering at the same time.
My biggest struggle was fear of man, so that really hindered me
because I wasn’t very good at talking to people.
Having a good routine was a struggle.
My brother and I are the only ones in the truth.
My family didn’t understand
why we wanted to go preaching.
I didn’t think that I’d make a good pioneer.
I’ve had Type 1 diabetes since I was five.
So I was always worried about whether or not
I could balance that health condition with pioneering.
The challenges don’t seem that big now,
but back at that time they were a really big deal.
But the coolest thing was how Jehovah helped me.
Prayer to Jehovah helped me overcome my fears.
My family was a massive help from Jehovah.
Because my dad was the one who first encouraged me to pioneer,
when I did start pioneering, he promised that I would have
the full support of my family.
When I spoke to brothers and sisters who spent their youth
in the full-time service that really helped me
because it was really encouraging, and it really motivated me
to want to make my own memories and my own experiences
in the full-time service.
So there were practical things I could do.
I didn’t have a car; I just walked or I caught the bus.
I had to work out what my priorities were first.
So I had to find out how many hours would I have to go witnessing every week.
So then I just sat down and I looked at every day
and planned out which days I could go witnessing,
which days I had to go to school,
and also allocated time so that I could do my homework and study.
Having a schedule was really good
because I could see it all out in front of me,
and I could see that the hour requirement
was actually attainable, so that made it a lot less daunting.
I first set short-term goals of pioneering in the special months of activity.
Then I was able to begin continuous auxiliary,
and then eventually I started regular pioneering.
One of the best things I did to prepare myself for pioneering
was to auxiliary pioneer beforehand.
It really set me up to be able to overcome
any challenges that I faced while I was pioneering.
I thought about Malachi 3:10.
I knew I trusted in Jehovah,
but this was my chance to test him out.
I prayed, put my trust in Jehovah,
and put my application in.
After my form was in for pioneering,
a brother, with time, a brother called me and offered me work.
I had unemployment for three months,
which wasn’t a good time.
But during that time, I had Jehovah as my main focus.
And so he supported me, and he didn’t let me down.
Asking brothers and sisters to come
and work with me, maybe on days that I knew
that I wouldn’t get as much support, really helped.
That helped me to organize my hours a little bit more,
and also I’d get to know my brothers and sisters more as well.
One of the greatest joys of pioneering has been to pioneer with Mum.
And we had the privilege of going
to the pioneer school together, which was really special.
Psalm 16:8 reminds me
that Jehovah is right beside me.
When I’m preaching, it’s like Jehovah is holding my hand.
So with full-time service, I love making Jehovah happy.
With everything that he has given me, I’m finally able to give something back.
Looking back —pioneering—
it was the best decision I’ve ever made.
It’s opened up so many different avenues
of service to Jehovah,
and it helped me also to have that real desire
to want to stay in full-time service.
Helping someone on the road to everlasting life,
it’s the best feeling ever; and it’s really irreplaceable.
The only thing I can say,
“As a young person, start pioneering!”

title: 워릭의 젊은 봉사자들이 여호와께 영예를 돌리다

ko.text: 우리는 여호와와 함께 미래를 만들어 가고 있는
몇몇 청소년들의 본을 볼 수 있었습니다.
청소년들의 그러한 노력은 우리 조직에 어떤 영향을 줄까요?
뉴욕 주 워릭에서 진행된 세계 본부 건축을 생각해 보시죠.
여호와의 증인은 4년이 채 안 되는 기간에
14만 9000 제곱 미터 규모에 달하는 건축 공사를 했죠.
아주 경험 많은 형제 자매들만 필요할 거라고 생각했습니다.
엄청난 일의 양 때문에 젊은이들의 활력 역시 필요했습니다.
나이 든 사람과 젊은이들이 함께 일한 게 큰 도움이 됐어요.
나이 든 사람들은 기술과 경험이 풍부하죠.
건축 공사 내내 신체적으로 힘든 일을 할 수 있는 근면성도 있죠.
젊은이들은 식당 일을 하거나, 야간 경비를 서거나,
새벽 5시부터 영하 12도의 날씨에 콘크리트 작업을 하거나,
필요한 일은 뭐든 기쁘고 겸손하게 받아들이는 면에서 아주 뛰어났어요.
많은 젊은 형제 자매들이 현장 근처로 이사 와서
심지어 다음 날 일을 미리 준비하려고 저녁 늦게까지 일할 때도 있었죠.
여호와께선 젊은이들을 사랑하셔서 그들에게 기꺼이 투자하시죠.
훈련을 베푸시고 그분의 조직의 일부로 삼으십니다.
전문 기술을 가진 많은 젊은이들이 기꺼이 자신을 바쳤습니다.
하지만 아무리 좋은 기술을 가지고 있어도
사실 여호와께선 그들을 사용하지 않으셨을 겁니다.
워릭에서 그들이 한 일은 그냥 건축 공사가 아니라
여호와를 위한 영적 건축 공사였단 걸 말이죠.
여호와의 영이 작용하고 있는 걸 볼 수 있었습니다.
그들이 아주 빠르게 장성해 가는 게 보였죠.
이 젊은 형제들은 앞으로 장로나 여행하는 감독자가 될 거예요.
이들이 젊은 때에 바친 이러한 수고는 정말
이들 모두 베델 봉사가 인생관에 어떤 영향을 주었는지,
또 세상과 일상사에 주의를 뺏기지 않는 데
어떻게 도움이 됐는지 얘길 많이 합니다.
이곳 현장과 베델에서 배운 기술을 사용하세요.
그렇게 하는 다른 사람들과 많이 교제하세요.
최고의 인생은 위대한 도공이신 여호와의 손에
진흙인 우리 자신을 맡기고 이렇게 말하는 거죠.

en.text: Earlier in the program,
we saw some examples of how young ones
are building a future with Jehovah.
But what impact are such efforts having on the organization?
Let’s look at one example:
the construction of the new world headquarters
at Warwick, New York.
Jehovah’s Witnesses built 1.6 million square feet (149,000 sq m)
in less than four years.
Of the 27,035 volunteers,
3,247 were between the ages of 19 and 25.
I thought this was a project
that was going to strictly need
very experienced brothers and sisters.
Early on, I realized I was wrong.
It was also going to take youthful energy
because of the volume of work.
The mix of older and younger ones
was really a helpful thing on the Warwick project.
The older ones brought skill and experience.
The younger ones brought the energy, the muscle,
and the diligence to stay with hard physical tasks
all the way through the project.
Whether it was in the kitchen or night watch
or the early 5:00 a.m. start with the concrete crew
at 10 degrees Fahrenheit (-12°C),
their joy and their humility was outstanding
to accept any work that needed to be done.
And a lot of young ones, brothers and sisters,
moved into the area so they could commute.
And they would work day after day tirelessly,
into the evenings even, to have the project ready for the next day.
Their energy was just astonishing.
Jehovah loves young ones, and he’s willing to invest in them
and train them and make them a part of his organization.
And I saw that so much.
We had a lot of young people who offered themselves
with technical skills.
But if the humility of these very technically-skilled young people
didn’t match or exceed their abilities,
then, really, Jehovah couldn’t use them.
And they were willing to adjust, and we really saw the benefit.
We knew and they knew
that they were building
not just a project at Warwick
—they were building a spiritual project for Jehovah.
You could see Jehovah’s spirit operating on them.
You could see them mature so quickly.
These young brothers are the next generation
of elders and traveling overseers.
They’re to be commended and highly respected
for the contribution they made as young men.
They all talk about the effect
that their Bethel service has had on their outlook
and how they don’t want to get caught up
in this world and its daily pursuits.
Use the skills you’ve learned
here on this project and in Bethel.
You are needed.
Continue to keep your spirituality up
and to keep your association at a high level.
The highest quality of life is when,
as clay, we put ourselves in the hands of the Great Potter, Jehovah,
and we say: “Here I am! Send me!”.
And I’m fully confident they will have no regrets
building their future with Jehovah.

en.text: In addition to the many avenues of full-time service
we mentioned earlier in the program,
making yourself available when a need arises locally
is a fine way to seek the Kingdom first.
For example, in San Antonio, in the state of Texas,
in the United States,
a large convention
with over 20,000 in attendance was planned.
However, the venue could only provide
about one third of the chairs needed for the convention.
Where would our brothers find the needed chairs?
Well, Jehovah provided,
and many young ones were eager to help.
When I heard that this needed to happen,
I was thinking, ‘How are we going to do this?’
I thought, ‘It’s a big job!’
It was amazing!
The first thing I was asked to do
was try to find a storage place that we could use
for six to eight thousand chairs.
A sister manages a storage place,
and we saw Jehovah’s blessing
because the owner said, “You can have this stall
“at no charge for a year as long as you sign a contract
that it’s for Jehovah’s Witnesses’ organization.”
Truckload after truckload after truckload came in.
We had to unload the trucks.
The brothers had to unstack the chairs,
repair the chairs, clean the chairs, put them back on pallets,
restack them,
load them onto trucks, and that was half of it.
Those were the ones in the warehouse.
On the other side, we got permission to ask
the San Antonio congregations if we could use their chairs
for the convention.
We were hoping to get three thousand chairs.
And then the numbers grew for the audience,
so we had to increase our numbers.
So we were able to gather six thousand chairs
from the willing volunteers of congregations around San Antonio.
So we prayed about it and the brothers started asking for volunteers,
and it was a great cooperation right at the beginning.
As soon as we let the friends know
that this was going to be the case,
all of them— all of them said,
“We’re going to get off of work early.”
We immediately wanted to clear our schedules
so that we could be available to help in any way that we could.
It was a privilege to know
that our congregation was going to be part of it.
We are so grateful to Jehovah that he has given us
this privilege to do.
We had thousands of chairs
of every color —green, red, brown, blue.
We even had some bright orange ones left out of the ‘70’s,
and we’re putting those in the back.
But it was not just the colors but the sizes.
They were all different sizes.
And so how do you make sections with straight rows
when the chairs are all different sizes?
But I knew somehow, as Jehovah’s people, we’d get it done.
And we definitely— As you see, a lot of volunteers,
and we’re here getting it done.
And it’s made for a beautiful experience
because the friends have gotten to know each other as never before.
And they’re willingly working together,
and the excitement is there.
It doesn’t matter whose venue it is, it’s all for Jehovah,
and that’s been the attitude everybody has had.
It just tells you that Jehovah is a God of order.
It’s good to feel that you’re doing your best for Jehovah.
Well, it reminds me of Psalm 127:1, where it mentions
that ‘unless Jehovah builds the house,
it’s in vain that his workers even work hard.’
So it’s because of Jehovah’s hand and his blessing
—that is why everything runs so smoothly.
What other organization!
No one else can do that except Jehovah’s people.

en.text: There is a saying
that experience is the best teacher,
but that is not really accurate.
Experience is often the hard way to learn.
Brother Fernando Casillas was born in Mexico,
but when he was a baby,
his family moved to the United States.
The neighborhood he grew up in had a lot of gang influence.
This had a very negative impact on him.
But despite these circumstances,
notice how the truth attracted him.
I used to love violence; I dreamed of violence.
My gang was my religion.
I got into the prison system at a young age.
At first, they sent me to a juvenile facility,
but I got kicked out of there for a riot.
Basically, they deemed me a threat to the safety and security
of the institution, the guards, and other inmates.
And I was sent to solitary confinement
to finish off my prison term.
Me thinking I was violent back then
was nothing compared to what I came out with.
Basically, what you try to come out to be
is the best killer out of all.
After my incarceration,
I was deported to Mexico.
I used to carry a weapon with me everywhere I went.
After a while, we started getting involved with bad people.
Eventually, my girlfriend got in trouble.
Once that was over,
she saw a Kingdom Hall.
My girlfriend had been to meetings as a child,
so she basically dragged me to the Kingdom Hall.
They treated me nice.
And that’s when I started to get to know Omar.
So I started hanging around with him and his wife
—me and my girlfriend at the time— and going to meetings.
But it wasn’t till I found out this guy
used to be one of my rivals
—I was very, very upset.
I felt betrayed because he never told me.
Everything that was going through my head was,
‘I’ve got to find a way to get him over here,
so I can hurt him.’
After thinking about all the things that I wanted to do to him that night
—I’d been running it through my head over and over again—
I decided to just stay friends with him.
And eventually, we decided to start studying together.
Being the way I was, I thought that there’s
no way a God can forgive me.
The scripture at Isaiah 55:7 really helped me,
where it says:
“Let the wicked man leave his way and the evil man his thoughts;
let him return to Jehovah, who will have mercy on him.”
As time went by, I started understanding clearly
that Jehovah does forgive.
By that time, I had already kind of made a decision
that I was done with doing time in prison.
I just decided to cut all ties with everybody
that had anything to do with anything illegal.
I felt like a free person.
And after progressing
and quitting the habits that I had of smoking and drinking a lot,
I became an unbaptized publisher.
But my father passed away;
I started hanging around with bad association again,
and eventually I had my privileges removed.
And as that was happening, Satan attacked me again.
So one day, my wife was crossing the border
to go take care of some paperwork for the kids
and was surprised by the border patrol
telling her that there were drugs in the vehicle.
We did not know that the previous owner
had stashed drugs in the truck.
Even though later they proved
that the drugs were not my wife’s and she was released,
they still decided to keep my kids.
What I was thinking of doing was going back to my old ways
—organizing a plot with my old friends
to bring my kids back to Mexico to me.
But I decided to rely
on Jehovah instead and on the brothers
coming to visit me on a regular basis
and giving me encouraging thoughts
of how Jehovah will take care of everything.
Eventually, our kids were returned to us,
with Jehovah’s help.
After a little struggle, of course, I had my privileges back.
A few months later, I was baptized.
I’m a lot happier now than what I was back then.
One day as I was preaching in the rehab centers,
I ran into a person I once knew before, growing up.
Once he found out who I was, he said:
“You’re the reason why I left town.
Every time you would see me, you would shoot at me.”
So after a while, I was able to convince him
that actually my purpose there
was not to hurt him anymore
but to teach him the truth
and how to gain everlasting life.
I’m no longer a violent person.
I enjoy the privileges that Jehovah now gives me.
I have now been serving as a ministerial servant
for the past two years.
I’m in charge of the accounting
for the Kingdom Hall,
instead of stealing money as I used to do before.
What I do for a living is I do gardening work.
Now I don’t carry around knives,
but I carry around my tools.
You could say that I did beat
my pistols into plowshares now
—or weed whacker or lawn mower.
I’m glad that I’m now serving a great God
who is loving, caring, and forgiving.
Fernando and his family are serving
in an English congregation in Mexico.
With everything Brother Casillas went through,
he could see
that Jehovah is the best teacher.
If you listen to Jehovah,
you won’t have to learn the hard way.
Jehovah is
“the One teaching you to benefit yourself.”

cn.text: 有些人说 经验是最好的老师
但并非总是如此
因为从经验汲取教训 往往会吃到不少苦头
费尔南多·卡西利亚斯弟兄
在墨西哥出生之后不久
他们全家就搬到了美国
他从小长大的地区里 有不少帮派活动
这给他带来许多负面的影响
虽然这样
请看看 真理是怎样吸引他的
我曾经非常喜爱暴力
帮派是我的信仰
我很年轻就入狱了
刚开始 我被送到少年看守所
后来因为一场暴动 被赶了出来
其实 他们认为我对他们的机构
警卫和其他的囚犯造成威胁
所以我被单独监禁 一直到刑期结束
回想刚出狱的我 真的非常凶狠
没有人可以跟我比
我想做最凶狠的杀手
出狱后 我被驱逐到墨西哥
我以前会随身携带武器
不久 我们和一些坏人扯上关系
结果 我的女朋友惹上了麻烦
事情过后 她找到王国聚会所
我女朋友小时候有参加过聚会
所以她就拉着我一起去聚会
他们对我很好
我就是这时候认识奥马尔的
我和女朋友开始跟他们夫妻来往
也参加聚会
后来我发现奥马尔以前是我的死对头
我非常非常生气
他从没提这些事 我觉得被欺骗了
当时我满脑子想的都是
我要想办法 好好教训他
我一整晚满脑子都想着怎么对付他
一直不停地想
但最后 我还是决定先和他做朋友
后来也跟他学习圣经
我认为上帝不可能原谅我以往的行为
但以赛亚书55:7的经文说
恶人应当离开歧途 坏人应当摒除恶念
他们当回来归向耶和华
就必蒙他大显慈悲
随着时间过去
我看出耶和华真的乐于宽恕人
我不想回到过去被监禁的生活
任何从事不法勾当的人
我决心要和他们断绝来往
我感觉重获新生
我不断进步 戒掉抽烟跟酗酒的习惯
成为未受浸传道员
但爸爸过世后
我又开始和那些坏朋友来往
结果失去了传道员的资格
后来 撒但又再一次攻击我
有一天
我太太要出境帮孩子办理一些文件
结果在边境被拦下来 说车子里有毒品
我们不知道前车主把毒品藏在车里
虽然后来证明
毒品不是我太太的 也释放了她
但他们却扣留了我的孩子
我原本想用老方法解决
叫以前帮派的朋友把孩子带回墨西哥
但后来我决定倚靠耶和华
弟兄定期来探望我、鼓励我
告诉我要把事情交给耶和华
在耶和华的帮助下
孩子终于回到我们身边
经过一番努力
我恢复了资格
几个月后受了浸
现在的我比以前更快乐
有一天 我去传道时
在一间戒毒中心
遇到了一个以前认识的人
我们从小一起长大
他发现我是谁后 说
就是因为你
每次你看到我 都想拿枪射我
我才离开家乡的
我向他解释 我来不是要伤害他
而是想教他真理 希望他得到永生
我不再是个喜爱暴力的人
我很珍惜耶和华给我的服务机会
我在会众里做助理仆人两年了
负责会众的会计工作
不再像以前一样会偷钱
我从事园艺的工作维持家计
现在我随身带着的不是武器
而是我的工具
我真的将枪矛打成镰刀
或者说打成除草机或割草机
我很高兴
我现在事奉一位有爱心、关心人
又乐意宽恕人的上帝
费尔南多跟家人
在墨西哥的一群英语会众服务

en.text: My theme for this month’s broadcast is
“Young Ones —Build Your Future With Jehovah!”
If you do, 1 Timothy 6:19 assures
that you will ‘safely treasure up for yourself
a fine foundation for the future,’
and you will “get a firm hold on the real life.”
Obviously, we will be directing many of our comments
directly to you dear young ones
in Jehovah’s organization.
Yet, if we think about it,
all of us figuratively
are very young ones
compared to eternity
—how long we hope to live.
So, in a sense, our comments during this broadcast
have application to all of us.
Personally, I am so thankful to Jehovah
that positive peer pressure was put on me
to enter the pioneer ministry right out of high school.
What a blessing and a protection
it was to enter the regular pioneer work
at age 17
and to be able to go to Bethel at 18.
Even though there was considerable worldly pressure put on me
to pursue university education,
I am so happy that with Jehovah’s help,
I decided to build my future
with Jehovah.
Truly, I have no regrets.
And this is always true of young ones
who serve Jehovah from their hearts
—they have no regrets.
In fact, you will enjoy these expressions from young ones
who are building their future with Jehovah.
Before I started pioneering,
I was really nervous that I wouldn’t be able to get my time in every month.
It was a bit hard when I started pioneering because I didn’t have a car.
My boss, he didn’t give me part-time work.
I found it really hard to balance schoolwork
and pioneering at the same time.
My biggest struggle was fear of man, so that really hindered me
because I wasn’t very good at talking to people.
Having a good routine was a struggle.
My brother and I are the only ones in the truth.
My family didn’t understand
why we wanted to go preaching.
I didn’t think that I’d make a good pioneer.
I’ve had Type 1 diabetes since I was five.
So I was always worried about whether or not
I could balance that health condition with pioneering.
The challenges don’t seem that big now,
but back at that time they were a really big deal.
But the coolest thing was how Jehovah helped me.
Prayer to Jehovah helped me overcome my fears.
My family was a massive help from Jehovah.
Because my dad was the one who first encouraged me to pioneer,
when I did start pioneering, he promised that I would have
the full support of my family.
When I spoke to brothers and sisters who spent their youth
in the full-time service that really helped me
because it was really encouraging, and it really motivated me
to want to make my own memories and my own experiences
in the full-time service.
So there were practical things I could do.
I didn’t have a car; I just walked or I caught the bus.
I had to work out what my priorities were first.
So I had to find out how many hours would I have to go witnessing every week.
So then I just sat down and I looked at every day
and planned out which days I could go witnessing,
which days I had to go to school,
and also allocated time so that I could do my homework and study.
Having a schedule was really good
because I could see it all out in front of me,
and I could see that the hour requirement
was actually attainable, so that made it a lot less daunting.
I first set short-term goals of pioneering in the special months of activity.
Then I was able to begin continuous auxiliary,
and then eventually I started regular pioneering.
One of the best things I did to prepare myself for pioneering
was to auxiliary pioneer beforehand.
It really set me up to be able to overcome
any challenges that I faced while I was pioneering.
I thought about Malachi 3:10.
I knew I trusted in Jehovah,
but this was my chance to test him out.
I prayed, put my trust in Jehovah,
and put my application in.
After my form was in for pioneering,
a brother, with time, a brother called me and offered me work.
I had unemployment for three months,
which wasn’t a good time.
But during that time, I had Jehovah as my main focus.
And so he supported me, and he didn’t let me down.
Asking brothers and sisters to come
and work with me, maybe on days that I knew
that I wouldn’t get as much support, really helped.
That helped me to organize my hours a little bit more,
and also I’d get to know my brothers and sisters more as well.
One of the greatest joys of pioneering has been to pioneer with Mum.
And we had the privilege of going
to the pioneer school together, which was really special.
Psalm 16:8 reminds me
that Jehovah is right beside me.
When I’m preaching, it’s like Jehovah is holding my hand.
So with full-time service, I love making Jehovah happy.
With everything that he has given me, I’m finally able to give something back.
Looking back —pioneering—
it was the best decision I’ve ever made.
It’s opened up so many different avenues
of service to Jehovah,
and it helped me also to have that real desire
to want to stay in full-time service.
Helping someone on the road to everlasting life,
it’s the best feeling ever; and it’s really irreplaceable.
The only thing I can say,
“As a young person, start pioneering!”
What a fine attitude those young ones have!
They are clearly following in Jesus’ footsteps.
Jesus was the wisest man
who ever walked the earth.
He could’ve pursued any career
and truly excelled at it.
He could’ve been the greatest carpenter who ever lived.
Think about it,
he helped his Father build the physical universe.
Can you imagine what kind of houses he could’ve built?
Or what if he had pursued being an inventor?
With his perfect brain,
he probably could’ve invented the telephone,
automobile, or computer
in the first century.
Or what about becoming a businessman?
With perfect intelligence,
he likely could’ve come out on top
of every business transaction that he entered,
becoming the richest businessman who ever lived.
Or have you ever thought about
if he had pursued becoming an athlete?
And excelling in athletic contests
was a huge endeavor in Jesus’ day.
With a little training,
it is likely that his perfect body
would have outperformed all people
with imperfect bodies,
enabling him to become
the most famous athlete who ever lived.
Or one more example,
what if he had decided to become a doctor?
He could cure sick people
—even raise the dead.
Can you imagine how much he could’ve charged rich people
to raise their dead loved ones?
But Jesus pursued none of these careers.
Why?
Because he knew that any of such endeavors
would have only very limited
and temporary benefits.
Instead, he pursued something
he knew would bring far-reaching and everlasting benefits:
the full-time ministry.
If this is how the wisest man who ever walked the earth—
If this is how he reasoned,
we are wise if we strive to think the same way.
That makes me think of the comments
of a well-adjusted teenage brother
whom we served while in the circuit work many years ago.
This young brother went straight into the regular pioneer work
out of high school,
and I asked him why he did so.
He explained that he knew
he could’ve gotten a full-time secular job
and bought a new car for himself,
but he reasoned that in a few years
that car would rust out and break down,
and he would have nothing.
But he knew that he could go into the pioneer work
and build a close relationship with Jehovah
and perhaps even find an honest-hearted person
and be able to teach that one the truth.
And he knew that would last forever.
Now, that is some wise thinking
on the part of that young brother.
And today, that brother has a beautiful Christian wife
and several spiritual children,
and he is serving as a fine elder.
But if you young ones are going to think this way
and continue to pursue spiritual goals,
it is vital that you wisely choose
your associates.
In a sense, our associates
can be likened to an elevator.
What do we mean?
Well, they can take you up
or they can take you down.
If you choose wisely,
they will take you up
—elevate your good qualities
and make you a better person.
But if you choose poorly,
they will take you down.
Depending on how badly you choose,
they can take you way down
—to the basement,
even the subbasement.
At Proverbs 13:20,
our loving heavenly Father,
who made us, explains how it works.
Jehovah tells us there:
“The one walking with the wise
“will become wise,
“but the one who has dealings with the stupid
will fare badly.”
“Walking with”
and “having dealings with”
mean “associating with.”
And who are the “stupid” ones?
Well, this scripture contrasts such a person
with those who are wise.
It is not talking about someone who lacks mental intellect.
It is talking about someone
who does not make wise decisions spiritually
from Jehovah’s standpoint.
And if we think about it,
anyone who is not really serving Jehovah
—at least right now—
that one is unwise indeed.
And if we associate closely with such ones,
Jehovah says that we “will fare badly.”
We could use another illustration.
Think about someone who is physically sick
and is running a high fever.
If we spend a lot of time with that person,
we will probably catch the same sickness.
Or worse,
if we spend a lot of time near a dead body—a corpse—
we will probably pick up a disease.
Well, it is similar
with spending time with a person
who is spiritually sick,
or worse, spiritually dead.
On the other hand,
if we choose as our associates
those who love Jehovah
and who are building their everlasting future with Jehovah,
we will benefit greatly.
Please observe carefully this variety of young ones
who are busy storing up treasures in heaven
with Jehovah.
How heartwarming it is to us
—and we know it is to Jehovah—
to see these beautiful young people
doing what Jesus encourages
at Matthew 6:20, 21.
There, Jesus encourages:
“Store up for yourselves treasures in heaven,
“where neither moth nor rust consumes,
“and where thieves do not break in and steal.
“For where your treasure is,
there your heart will be also.”
And if we think about it,
in the final analysis,
after all is said and done,
whether we are younger or older,
our net worth will be
what we have stored up in heaven with Jehovah.
We will not be able to take material treasures with us
through the great tribulation.
And if we die,
we certainly will not be able to take material treasures with us,
but we can take spiritual treasures
with us through the great tribulation
and even through death and resurrection.
It is true with all of Jehovah’s people,
as it is with the anointed,
what is stated at Revelation 14:13.
It says there:
“The things they did go right with them.”
And how encouraging it is
to see young ones getting baptized
—publicly demonstrating
that they are giving their lives to Jehovah.
And we sincerely hope
that you young ones who are not yet baptized
will not hold back from getting baptized
as soon as you qualify.
The sooner you can get baptized,
the sooner you will receive greater protection
and blessings from Jehovah.
Not long ago, it made me very happy
to observe a little ten-year-old brother
get baptized!
And young ones,
never be afraid to identify yourselves
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Never allow the fear of what others may think
to cause you to hesitate to do so.
Jehovah tells us
at Proverbs 29:25:
“Trembling at men is a snare,
“but the one trusting in Jehovah
will be protected.”
Many years ago when I was in school,
I can remember being at times somewhat worried
about how my fellow classmates would view me.
But then a little while later,
I got out of school
and never ever again even saw
most of those former classmates.
Then it dawned on me
that it doesn’t really matter what people think about us.
It is Jehovah’s rating of us
that truly counts.
Humans cannot add
even five seconds to our lifespan,
but Jehovah can add
or subtract eternity.
And he alone can also give us true happiness.
And as Proverbs 29:25 indicates,
what a protection
it is to courageously identify ourselves
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
fully trusting Jehovah
and taking our stand solidly with him.
Never be ashamed of who you are.
You are one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And please, dear young ones,
we warmly encourage you
to listen to those who love you.
Jehovah loves you very much;
the Governing Body loves you very much;
the elders love you very much;
your Christian parents love you very much.
And these ones will tell you the truth,
even though at times
it may not be what you want to hear.
They will not ‘tickle your ears,’
perhaps like ones at school
or in the neighborhood
who don’t really love you
or have your best interests at heart.
But please believe those
who will tell you the truth
because they love you.
And never view Jehovah’s laws and principles
as depriving you of something good.
View them as protecting you
from what will hurt you.
If you recall,
Satan convinced Eve
that she was being deprived by Jehovah
and was missing out on something good.
Now, it is true that Eve was missing out on something.
But what was she really missing out on?
A tormented conscience,
her beautiful hair turning gray,
her teeth falling out,
her perfect skin wrinkling up like a prune,
being bent over from old age,
hobbling around on a cane,
and finally dying!
But Satan convinced her
that Jehovah was depriving her,
so foolishly she reached out to get
what she thought she was missing out on.
Well, Satan will try to use
the same kind of strategy on you,
but please don’t let him do it!
This also makes me think of an experience a brother once related.
He said that he was visiting an animal observatory,
and a large lion lunged toward him
but was prevented from reaching him
by a thick glass pane
separating the animals from the observers.
As the lion stood on his hind legs,
clawing the glass
and baring his massive teeth,
the brother came to realize in a special way
the protective value of that barrier.
Previously, he said that he somewhat viewed the glass pane
as a restriction
because the smudges on it
partially blurred his view,
but now he viewed it
as a real protection.
Well, in a similar way,
Jehovah doesn’t want Satan,
who is described as ‘a roaring, devouring lion’
at 1 Peter 5:8—
He doesn’t want him to gobble down you young ones.
And His laws and principles
are designed to keep that from happening to you.
So please listen to Jehovah.
He loves you!

跟那些善用青春
投身全时服务的弟兄姊妹聊一聊
真的给我很大的帮助
他们的话很鼓励我
推动我也想参与全时服务
留下属于自己的回忆和经历
有些事是我可以做的
我没有车 但是可以走路或搭公车

也得计划每周的传道时间

计划哪几天要传道 哪几天要上课
我也会安排时间做功课和个人研读
规划时间表是个好方法

感觉就没那么难了
我先设立短期目标

年轻人 开始做先驱吧!

自己正跟随耶稣的脚踪走

曾和天父一起创造宇宙万物的耶稣

由于耶稣有完美的头脑

凭着完美的智力
耶稣一定能在每一笔交易中

如果他决定当一位医生呢?
他能医治百病 甚至复活死人

愿意花很多钱
请耶稣复活他们死去的至亲吗?

为什么呢?
他知道 如果他选择这些职业
带给他的 就只有有限且短暂的益处
相反
他追求的目标 全时传道工作
能为他带来永久的益处
如果这是史上最有智慧的人的看法
我们照着做
就代表我们也是一个明智的人了
这使我想起 许多年前
我还在做分区探访工作的时候
一位成熟稳重的年轻人他说的话
我问他
为什么他选择高中一毕业 就做正规先驱
他说
毕业后 他本来有机会做一份全时工作
可以为自己买一辆新车
可是他思考过这件事
他说
即使我买了一辆新车
几年后 车就会生锈、故障
最后不能用了
到那个时候 他就一无所有了
所以 他很清楚知道
如果他投入先驱工作
就能和耶和华建立亲密的关系
也许 他还能帮助一位心地正直的人
认识真理
他知道这些努力是不会随时间消失的
现在 那位弟兄
有了一位美丽的基督徒妻子
他帮助很多人成为上帝的子民
也成为一位优秀的长老
年轻人 如果你们和那位弟兄一样
专心追求属灵的目标
就要谨慎选择跟谁来往
要记得
我们的来往对象就好像电梯一样
可以带你上楼
也可以带你下楼

如果你选择对的朋友
他们就能带你上楼
也就是提升你的基督徒品质
帮助你成为一个更好的人
可是如果你选了错的人做朋友
他们就会带你下楼
你选择来往的对象越糟
你就会被带往越低的楼层
天父耶和华在箴言13:20
提醒我们谨慎择友的重要性
经文说
“同行”和“来往”
都有“做朋友”的意思
那么 谁是“愚昧人”呢?
这节经文把愚昧人和智慧人做了个对比
愚昧人并不是指智能不足的人
而是指那些
没有运用耶和华的观点作出明智决定的人
请想想 那些不愿意事奉耶和华
或者至少现在不想这么做的人
他们的想法是多么地不明智
耶和华提醒我们
如果我们和那些人密切来往
就“难免吃亏”
再来看另一个比喻
如果我们和一位
发高烧的病人频繁地接触
就很容易被他传染
或者
如果我们一直待在一具尸体旁
经过一段时间 也很有可能染上疾病
同样
如果我们和一位已经在属灵方面生病
甚至死去的人密切来往
我们就会受到影响
相反 如果我们选择和那些爱耶和华
决心一生与他同行的人做朋友
我们必定获益良多
让我们来看看以下影片中
这些年轻人怎样在天上积存财宝
蒙上帝喜悦
看到这些年轻人
服从耶稣在马太福音6:20,21的吩咐
我们不是感到很高兴吗?
更何况是耶和华呢?
马太福音6:20,21说
在大患难的时候 无论你年轻或年长
我们在天上积存了多少属灵的财宝

en.text: Have you ever considered helping out in a foreign-language field?
Perhaps there is a need in your local circuit.
All over the earth,
the organization provides language courses
with the goal of reaching every nation, tribe, tongue, and people
with the good news of God’s Word.
Brother Juan Carlos Chacón
serves as a special pioneer
in the rapidly growing Shuar language field
in Ecuador.
He was recently asked to attend
a course at the local branch
to become a language teacher
so that he could help willing publishers
learn the language.
[Speaking Shuar]
It has been said before,
“This is a language of the Devil”
—that it should be forgotten.
It serves no purpose.
But to Jehovah,
no nation is insignificant.
I grew up in an area of the Ecuadorian jungle
where there is a large community
of Shuar people.
Like many native languages,
Shuar is very complex.
We need many, many workers in the field.
But if we don’t give them a foundation,
if we don’t help them or give them a little push,
it’s difficult for them to enter this field.
I received an invitation to attend
a seminar for language instructors.
There were 58 students in the class,
representing 16 different languages or language groups.
We are learning fantastic teaching techniques,
real techniques that work.
The instructor told us how humor helps our minds to create a world of connections,
which stimulates our brain.
Yeah, I’m like a small child
when it comes to drawing.
I never learned to draw well.
We draw a scene,
and starting with our native language
along with large gestures,
we act out a dialogue.
Little by little,
we convert the scene into the new language.
What scares me?
That I’ve never done this before.
This will be my first time.
I don’t have any experience teaching languages.
Although I felt intimidated by this,
I knew that with Jehovah all things are possible.
Welcome to the first day of the Shuar language course.
The techniques they offered us in the course were like a box of tools
that we need to study more carefully and see how to apply them
in each circumstance.
When we are in the territory,
we see how people’s eyes light up when they learn
the name of God.
Just seeing that there is so much need for them to learn the truth,
that has motivated us to come here
and continue serving here.
Since God has created us,
we know that he will never abandon us.
He thinks about us all the time,
and he loves us very much.
I didn’t know that before.
I feel so happy now
because I can really understand the Word of God.
Being in an isolated group far from other congregations,
my wife and I have felt every day
how real Jehovah is.
Jehovah is now looking
and giving his attention to these small places,
no matter how small they are.
If people have a good heart and want to serve Jehovah,
he will send workers to give the help that is needed.
And in reality, this moves us to say to him with all of our heart,
“Thank you, Jehovah.”

en.text: When Paul wrote the letter to the Colossians,
it was in the year 60-61 C.E.,
just similar to the time that he wrote Ephesians,
which we talked about yesterday.
And he wrote for similar reasons
—to protect his brothers from the immoral environment
that was around them and to encourage them
to fight against the weaknesses of the flesh.
So let’s open our Bibles to Colossians chapter 3,
and we’ll read verse 5 in its entirety.
Colossians 3:5:
“Deaden, therefore, your body members
“that are on the earth as respects sexual immorality, uncleanness,
“uncontrolled sexual passion, hurtful desire,
and greediness, which is idolatry.”
And we’ve been told that these expressions
convey the idea of totally wiping out these desires.
When we sense them coming up in our heart and mind,
we slay them; we wipe them out.
And it’s very important because to fail to do that
puts us into all sorts of difficulties with Jehovah
and with others and causes problems for ourselves.
Look at verse 6:
“On account of those things the wrath of God is coming.”
So it affects our everlasting future as well, doesn’t it?
One thing that is highlighted here
is how serious these desires can become.
They get bound up with greediness,
covetousness, which is idolatry.
And covetousness has been described
as something that is insatiable.
It’s always after something that it should not have
or it does not have the right to have.
It’s ruthless and self-seeking; it has been defined as that.
And a covetous person, or a greedy person,
makes the object of his desire so strong
that in essence it can become his god.
And that reminds us of the inspired words
at Philippians 3:18, 19,
where Paul used a similar expression
about those who used to be with him in the truth but no longer were,
and he was very sad about that.
And what happened to them?
Well, “their god [became] their belly,”
and their desires overwhelmed even their love for Jehovah.
And it was back in 1978
that The Watchtower, in the April 1 issue,
said this about this quality of greed
—covetousness— and idolatry.
It said this:
‘If we become aware of a wrong desire
‘building up within ourselves,
‘we do well to call to mind
‘how precious our relationship with God is
‘and how senseless it would be to forfeit this
by making oneself an idolater.’
So that’s a very serious thought, isn’t it?
That a person could actually start worshipping something
other than Jehovah.
And that was a very serious sin
even in ancient Israel, wasn’t it, this matter of idolatry?
It carried the death penalty.
But, you know, another aspect of the Ten Commandments
that carried the death penalty
was adultery.
So, what is the similarity
between idolatry and the death penalty
and adultery and the death penalty?
Well, worshipping an idol,
a person would break his covenant with Jehovah.
And committing adultery,
he would break his covenant with his spouse.
So why would Jehovah feel so strongly about that?
Well, let’s open our Bibles to Psalm 33,
and we’ll look at the kind of person
Jehovah is when it comes to his word
and what he says.
Psalm 33, let’s read verse 4:
“For the word of Jehovah is upright,
and everything he does is trustworthy.”
And then look at verse 9:
“For he spoke, and it came to be;
he commanded, and it stood firm.”
So the psalmist is saying,
“When Jehovah says something, he means it.”
And so when a person says to Jehovah,
“I’m going to worship you exclusively” and he doesn’t,
it’s treachery.
It’s unlike God, Jehovah.
It’s like the Devil, who is a liar and untrustworthy.
So it adds weight, doesn’t it,
to our desire never to fall victim
to idolatry in any form?
Now, our comments in The Watchtower
(which we’ll read a little bit later today in the actual printed comment)
do focus on this matter of marriage
and adultery and avoiding that, of course.
And what we’d like to do now is just take a few moments
and highlight some dangers
that could come up for married people
and see how that applies
to deadening, or slaying, those desires
right from the very beginning
so that they do not flourish and cause a problem.
One of the principles that we can think about is Proverbs 22:3.
We see “the danger,” and we turn aside.
So, what are some things that we could see as a danger,
identify them, and slay them before they become a problem?
Well, obviously, what we look at,
listen to, and read
fills our mind with either good or bad,
so we avoid intake of bad things.
It only fuels bad desires.
But research has shown and our publications have often commented
that when a person gets involved in adultery,
it isn’t always just a sexual greed,
or the sexual desire,
that motivates him to go down that path in the first place
or her to go down that path the first time.
Well, what is it?
Well, what is the fundamental function of marriage?
It has often been said
that the fundamental function of marriage
is receiving and giving emotional support.
It’s a relationship where a person feels loved,
appreciated, wanted, and needed in a very special way.
And when a person begins to feel that that is missing,
then they begin looking for someone who can give them that
—not necessarily right away sexual gratification.
And that’s why
the Awake! of January 8, ʹ86 Awake! said
that being a good listener “has the capacity
“for making the other person feel that he is especially valued
and what he is saying is of concern and significance” to him.
So it’s this relationship that needs to be guarded
—the friendship.
And the 1994 Watchtower of July 15
added weight to this comment
when it quoted a divorce attorney, of all people.
And he said what was the single biggest reason couples break up.
And this is what he said, it was quoted in the magazine:
“The inability to talk honestly with each other,
bare their souls and treat each other as their best friend.”
That’s the main reason.
That can often lead to other physical contact.
But it often is not the one that gets it started.
So now, what can we do to avoid that?
Well, we want to treasure our relationships.
And it reminds us of an experience that was given
in the August 15, 2012, Watchtower,
about an elder and pioneer named Daniel
and his wife, also pioneering.
He was very involved in the congregation
—always took on assignments.
He had three Bible students —men—
who got baptized, but they needed a lot of help;
they were newly baptized.
He was busy with other assignments.
His wife spent a lot of time with these newly baptized brothers.
He was neglecting his wife.
She bonded emotionally with one of these brothers;
adultery was committed.
But Daniel said he bore a heavy responsibility in that respect.
In fact, at the end of the lessons learned,
he said this:
“There is much more to life than struggling to care for privileges
to the detriment of your own family.”
So a need for balance.
Pursuing Kingdom interests, of course
—and an understanding wife or husband can understand and support that—
but there is a balance.
And if it oversteps itself, then real problems can result.
So we want to do all we can
to slay desires when we sense them in ourselves.
And it’s going to take earnest effort;
it’s going to take endurance
because as long as we’re in this imperfect state,
no one can say, “I am immune to any of those desires
that could crop up at different times.”
So our love for Jehovah, our love for our mates,
our love for our brothers prevents us
from going down the path of greediness and idolatry,
which only results in harm.
How grateful we are to be with brothers and sisters like you who love Jehovah,
love their marriage mates, love the brotherhood,
and do all they can to stay morally clean!
Keep it up with Jehovah’s help.

都会影响我们的思想
这些内容有可能是好的
也有可能是坏的
所以我们要尽量避免吸收坏的讯息
因为这些讯息只会使不良的念头更加强烈
我们的出版物和其他研究报告都提到
一个人犯下通奸罪
一开始的原因并不是为了满足性欲
满足性的需要不一定是人外遇的动机
所以外遇的动机是什么呢?
先想想婚姻生活的基本功能是什么?
婚姻生活的基本功能
是接受和给予配偶感情上的支持
在婚姻关系中
一个人会感觉被爱
被对方欣赏、被配偶需要
这是一份很特殊的感情
如果配偶缺乏感情上的支持
就会开始在别人身上找寻这种感觉
但不一定马上就会和别人发生性关系
这就是为什么《警醒!》
1986年7月8日刊说
一个好的聆听者
有能力使别人自觉有特殊价值
所说的话是重要和有意义的
所以
夫妻之间的友谊关系是需要被保护的
《守望台》1994年7月15日刊
引述了一位专办离婚案件的律师的话
他谈到夫妻离婚的最大原因是什么
杂志引述律师的话说
夫妻未能忠实地彼此交谈、披露心事
而把对方视为自己最好的朋友
这个才是最主要的原因
通常, 肢体接触并不是外遇发生的原因
而是因为感情的需要无法满足
才导致已婚的人外遇
所以我们怎么避免外遇发生呢?
我们要珍惜自己与配偶的关系
2012年8月15日刊的《守望台》
讲述了一个经历
有一位叫做丹尼尔的长老
他和太太都是先驱
丹尼尔对会众的事非常热心
总是有很多服务委派
他的圣经学生中, 有三位男子受浸了
不过, 因为他们才刚刚受浸
还需要很多帮助
但丹尼尔又忙着其他的委派
所以他的太太花了很多时间
跟这些新受浸的弟兄在一起
丹尼尔忽略了太太感情上的需要
他的太太开始跟其中一位弟兄产生感情
结果就跟这位弟兄通奸了
丹尼尔说会发生这样的事情
他其实要负起最大的责任
他从这件事学到什么呢?
他说
因为埋头属灵的工作而牺牲家庭
这是万万不该的
所以我们都需要保持平衡
我们努力追求属灵的工作
虽然我们的配偶理解
也支持我们的工作
但还是需要平衡
一旦失去平衡, 结果就不堪设想了
如果我们发现自己有不好的念头
就要尽力消除这样的想法
这是需要付出努力去做的
而且也需要培养耐心
因为只要人一天不完美
就没有人可以说
不管在什么时候
我都绝不会有这些不好的念头
我们对耶和华的爱、对配偶的爱
还有对弟兄姊妹的爱
会帮助我们避免走上歧途
贪婪的精神和崇拜偶像
最终只会带来伤害
我们很高兴和你们这些爱耶和华
爱配偶
也爱弟兄姊妹的人在一起
愿我们都在道德上保持洁净!
靠着耶和华的帮助, 我们一定能做到!

en.text: Welcome to Bethel. Please come in.
The wonderful truths about Jehovah
and his purpose have touched the hearts of millions
of people earth wide.
This has moved many to visit the branch offices
of Jehovah’s Witnesses in countries around the world.
Why are such branch offices necessary?
In order for life-giving truths to reach everyone,
the preaching work
must be organized.
A Branch Committee oversees
all Bethel operations.
These brothers also look after the preaching work
throughout the branch territory.
Our translation teams
translate articles and videos into several local languages.
These are recorded and made available on jw.org
or sent electronically for printing.
The activity of traveling overseers
as well as nearly 200 special pioneers and missionaries
is coordinated by the Service Department.
These brothers also take care of organizing
the more than 130 congregations
throughout the branch territory.
With the growth of Kingdom interests,
comes a constant need for more theocratic buildings.
The Local Design/Construction Department
cares for construction projects
such as Kingdom Halls and Assembly Halls.
It also cares for operating and maintaining these buildings.
Jehovah’s Witnesses have a deep respect for life
and want the best possible medical care.
The Hospital Information Desk
provides assistance with nonblood medical management.
It coordinates with Hospital Liaison Committees (HLC)
and cooperative doctors around the country.
A lack of transport and poor road conditions
make it really a challenge for the HLC members
to travel around the country
to visit the hospitals and the clinics.
But their self-sacrificing spirit
and the love they have for the brothers,
along with some fine medical presentations,
have really had a positive effect on many doctors and hospital staff,
who are now willing to use nonblood treatment
in working with our brothers and sisters.
So we can honestly say that we have seen
Jehovah’s rich blessing and direction on the work of the HLC brothers.
All who live and work here
are part of what we call the Bethel family.
We call it a family because that is how we
truly feel about one another.
Just as you have your family worship every week,
so the Bethel family does the same.
We have the morning worship program.
We also have the weekly Watchtower Study.
These help to keep the family
spiritually strong.
They also help keep the family united.
Some Bethelites work in offices.
Others work in supportive departments.
Regardless of what job we are assigned, why are we willing
and happy to be doing this work?
Because it is sacred service.
It helps to promote the furthering
of Kingdom interests and brings glory
and honor to our God, Jehovah.

en.text: When we arrive at the Kingdom Hall for a meeting,
don’t you agree that we all feel refreshed
the moment we see the smiling faces of our brothers and sisters?
That’s how I feel.
Sometimes we can even take our beautiful meeting location for granted.
But did you know that a lot of work goes into making sure
that our Kingdom Halls are well utilized?
The Worldwide Design/Construction Department, or WDC,
is tasked with analyzing our worldwide needs
and providing direction to Local Design/Construction Departments
on how best to use our dedicated funds.
As we approach the end of the present system of things,
Jehovah continues to speed up the work.
We now have more than 62,000 Kingdom Halls worldwide,
and the demand is still growing.
Jehovah’s blessing on the Kingdom work is undeniable,
as this could not have been accomplished otherwise.
Many have been working for years in support of Kingdom Hall
and Assembly Hall construction projects,
most recently as part of the Local Design/Construction,
or LDC, program.
This program was implemented during the 2014 service year
and unifies the approach for construction of Kingdom Halls worldwide.
What has been accomplished since the program started?
At the end of the 2000 service year,
half of the publishers worldwide met in suitable meeting places.
However, the other half
—approximately three million publishers—
met in places that were overcrowded
or otherwise unsuitable as Kingdom Halls.
At that time,
27,000 Kingdom Halls were needed.
By 2014, the number of publishers meeting
in unsuitable facilities had been reduced.
But because of growth in the organization,
this still meant that 1.6 million publishers
did not have a suitable meeting place.
Since 2014,
that figure has been reduced
by 25 percent.
What accounts for this significant reduction in the backlog,
allowing us to catch up faster than in the past?
Part of the answer
lies in making efficient use of the facilities we already have.
When providing food for thousands,
Jesus made it clear that nothing should be wasted.
The LDC program applies that principle
to the seats in our Kingdom Halls.
As noted earlier,
we have 62,000 Kingdom Halls worldwide.
On average, only 60 percent of the seats
are filled for congregation meetings.
That means that approximately three to four million seats are empty
during congregation meetings each week.
There are a number of options to help make better use of these seats,
which will make the use of each Kingdom Hall more efficient.
Consider, for example,
a Kingdom Hall in an urban area.
It has 200 seats
and is used by four congregations sharing the facility.
That means the Kingdom Hall will be in use
for four weeknight meetings
and four weekend meetings.
It would definitely appear to be fully utilized
and suggests the need
for new construction for further growth.
However, how many seats were in the Kingdom Hall?
Two hundred.
Multiplied by meetings for the four congregations,
this facility has a total seating capacity
of 800 people.
Global records indicate that congregations
using this size Kingdom Hall
have an average attendance
of 120 at their meeting.
This could mean that only 480 seats are used
by the four congregations in this Kingdom Hall
and 320 seats remain empty
—not very efficient.
If the four congregations were redistributed
into three congregations,
average meeting attendance for each congregation
would increase to about 160 per meeting,
while still fitting comfortably in that Kingdom Hall.
And this would now allow for an open slot in the schedule,
which could be used to meet needs in the area
without requiring new construction.
In the first three years of the LDC program,
fully utilizing our existing facilities
played a part in reducing the backlog of Kingdom Hall projects
from 14,000 to approximately 10,000.
This saved millions of dollars.
Of course, this does not meet every need,
and there is still a significant need
to construct new Kingdom Halls to provide suitable places of worship.
How does the branch office make these decisions,
and how are priorities set?
All options are examined as the Branch Committees
work with their Local Design/Construction
and Service departments.
Transportation needs —such as distance,
opportunities for carpooling,
and availability of public transportation—
are taken into account.
In many cases, congregations can be sized
to make better use of available seats
in Kingdom Halls that have already been built.
However, when they are needed,
new Kingdom Halls can be constructed using simple, standard designs
that make wise use of donated funds.
Of course, all of this must be done with the big picture in mind.
It is the spiritual needs of the congregations
that are of the utmost priority.
The structures themselves are not the focus of these centers of pure worship,
but rather it is the people who use the facilities.
On one occasion, as they passed the temple,
Mark 13:1 quotes one of Jesus’ disciples
admiring the structure when he said:
“Teacher, see! what wonderful stones and buildings!”
However,
Jesus’ reply simply indicated
that the building itself would not last.
It was people Jesus was concerned with.
Likewise, the Kingdom Halls that we build today
will not last forever.
But these centers of pure worship bring people together
so that we can serve Jehovah as a united group
—and that will last forever.
Whether we assist in the construction
of the many Kingdom Halls that are still needed
or help to renovate and maintain existing Kingdom Halls,
it is our shared privilege to help provide
suitable meeting places for our brothers and sisters.
In this way,
we each support “the faithful and discreet slave”
as they provide what is needed so that each congregation
can praise Jehovah in a suitable place of worship.

cn.text: 每当我们到王国聚会所参加聚会时
看到弟兄姊妹喜乐的笑容
我们也很快乐, 不是吗?
那么, 看到聚会所又干净又漂亮
我们会不会觉得这是理所当然的呢?
其实, 保养维护聚会所
可说是一项大工程呢!
全球设计及建筑部, 简称WDC
弟兄们会分析世界各地聚会所的需要
提供本地设计及建筑部所需的帮助
以最好的方式运用我们的捐款
随着这个制度终结的日子越来越近
耶和华持续加快传道工作
在全球
我们已经有6万2000多个王国聚会所
但需求还是不断增加
看得出耶和华大大赐福王国工作
否则我们不可能完成
许多弟兄姊妹多年来
参与王国聚会所及大会堂建筑工程
最近他们当中很多人
成为本地设计及建筑部(LDC)的成员
这个部门在2014年开始运作
目的是统一全球王国聚会所的建筑方式
自从LDC设立以来
获得了什么成果呢?
在2000年工作年度的年底
全球有一半的传道员
可以在舒适的聚会所里聚会
但是, 还有一半
约300万个传道员
还在拥挤或不合适的场所参加聚会
那时, 全球需要2万7000个王国聚会所
到了2014年
在不合适的建筑物里聚会的传道员数目
已大幅减少
但因为组织不断扩展
还是有160万个传道员
没有合适的聚会场所
自2014年以来
这个数目已下降了百分之25
是什么原因让这个数字迅速降低
使我们很快赶上进度呢?
一个原因是
我们善加利用现有的王国聚会所
当耶稣喂饱几千人时
他清楚表示食物不应该浪费
LDC就将这个原则
运用在王国聚会所的座位安排上
就如刚才提到的
我们在全球有6万2000个王国聚会所
每次聚会平均只坐满百分之60的座位
换句话说, 每星期的聚会
有将近300到400万个空位
有几个不同的方法
可以充分利用这些空位
使我们更有效地使用王国聚会所
举例来说
一个在市区的王国聚会所
有200个座位
由四群会众来使用
也就是说
平日有四个晚上
以及周末有四个时段
都有人使用这个王国聚会所
看起来这个王国聚会所已经达到饱和
为了将来的扩展
势必需要另一间新的聚会所
不过, 这个王国聚会所有多少座位呢?
四群会众加起来
这个聚会所总共可容纳800人
全球报告显示
一般使用这样大小的聚会所的会众
聚会出席人数平均是120人
也就是说四群会众只用了480个座位
还有320个空位
在运用座位方面似乎不太有效率
假如把四群会众重整为三群
会众平均出席人数将会增加到160人
他们还是可以很舒适地参加聚会
而且, 时间表上还多出了一个时段
可供未来的扩展使用
不用再兴建一个新聚会所
LDC成立后的三年
借着充分的利用现存的设施
结果应该兴建的王国聚会所数量
从1万4000降到大约1万
这为我们省下了大笔的金钱
当然, 这个方法并不能适用于每个地方
一些地区新王国聚会所的需求还是很大
分部办事处是如何做决定
及订出优先次序呢?
分部委员会
会和LDC及传道部一起讨论所有方案
在交通方面
像是距离、车辆共乘、大众交通工具
也是他们考量的因素
以大部分情况而言
只须重新安排会众的人数
聚会所的座位就可以充分利用
不过, 当需要新聚会所时
工程会采用简单实用的设计
善用所收到的捐款
当然, 他们在做决定时
都会记得一件最重要的事
就是会众的属灵需要
这才是最该优先考量的事
正确崇拜的重心并不是在建筑物本身
而是在使用这些设施的人
有一次耶稣和门徒经过圣殿
根据马可福音13:1记载
一个门徒对圣殿的宏伟华丽赞叹不已, 说
老师, 请看
这是多壮观的石头, 多壮观的建筑!
但是耶稣却只是简单地说
这座圣殿并不会存留
人才是耶稣所关心的
同样的, 我们现在盖的王国聚会所
也不会永远存留
不过这些用作纯真崇拜的中心
可以把人聚集起来
让我们团结地敬拜耶和华
这才是永不消逝的
不管我们是协助建造新的王国聚会所
或是整修及保养现有的王国聚会所
能够为弟兄姊妹提供舒适的聚会场所
都是我们的荣幸
借着这么做
我们就是支持“忠信睿智的奴隶”
因为他们希望
所有会众都有合适的崇拜场所
一起赞美耶和华

ko.text: “대처하기 어려운 위급한 때”가 될 것이라고 경고하셨습니다.
우리는 산불, 화산 폭발, 파괴적인 폭풍, 인간에 의한 재난,
불법의 증가, 소요 사태, 전쟁도 겪고 있습니다.
그러한 자연재해나 인간에 의한 재난에 영향을 받을 수 있습니다.
“너희의 힘은 평온을 유지하고 신뢰하는 데 있을 것이다.”
따라서 여호와와 친밀한 관계를 맺고 유지해야 하며
지금 그분을 신뢰하는 법을 배워야 합니다.
우리는 하느님이 개입하실 것을 기대하지는 않습니다.
하지만 어려울 때에 기도한다면, 그분의 강력한 성령은 평온을 유지하고
좋은 결정을 내릴 지혜를 주는 성구를 생각나게 해 줄 것입니다.
둘째로, 비상 가방을 챙겨 놓음으로 실제적인 준비를 할 수 있습니다.
비상 가방에는 구급약품, 병에 든 생수, 상하지 않는 식품,
성경, 그 밖의 필요한 물품이 들어가야 합니다.
집 안에서 지내야 하는 기간이 길어질 경우를 대비해
합리적인 양의 기본 필수품들을 비축해 두어야 합니다.
이와 관련해 여러분의 지역에 적용되는 정부 당국의 권고 사항을 확인하십시오.
또, 장로들에게 항상 최신 연락처를 알려 주어야 합니다.
그러지 않으면, 재해가 있을 때 필요한 도움을 신속히 받을 수 없게 됩니다.
그에 더해, 가족 숭배 시간에 어떤 재해가 일어날 수 있는지 함께 토의할 수 있습니다.
테러 공격과 소요 사태와 같은 비상 상황은
어디서든 아무런 경고 없이 발생할 수 있습니다.
따라서 어디에서 만나야 할지, 어떻게 장로들과 연락할지 등
각 상황에 대처하는 방법을 생각해 보십시오.
셋째로, 다른 사람들이 재해를 당했을 때를 위해 도와줄 준비를 할 수 있습니다.
우리가 사는 지역에 재해가 발생했다고 생각해 보겠습니다.
재해에 대한 사전 경보가 내려진 경우,
집단 성원 모두가 안전한 곳에 있는지 확인할 것입니다.
재해가 발생한 직후, 각 야외 봉사 집단 감독자는
집단의 모든 성원과 연락해 무엇이 필요한지 파악할 것입니다.
구호 활동을 조직하는 데는 시간이 걸리며
특히 구호품이 제한된 경우에는 더욱 그렇습니다.
따라서 우리 각자가 잘 준비하고, 정부의 재난 경보를 따르고,
장로들에게 수시로 우리의 상황을 알려 주는 것이 중요합니다.
빌립보서 2:4은 ‘다른 사람들의 일에도 관심을 가지라’고 말합니다.
도움이 더 필요한 사람들에게 주의를 기울일 수 있을 것입니다.
회중이나 근처의 형제 자매들을 도울 수 있을 것입니다.
예를 들어, 어떤 경우에는 형제 자매들이 임시로 머물 장소가 필요할 수 있습니다.
그런 경우 그들을 우리의 집에 머물게 해 줄 수 있습니다.
또는 음식이나 필수품이 필요한 경우 우리의 것을 나누어 줄 수도 있습니다.
또 안전한 경우라면 형제들의 집을 청소하거나 수리해 줄 수 있습니다.
다른 지역에서 재해가 발생한 경우는 어떻습니까?
구호 활동을 조직하고 지원할 형제들을 임명할 것입니다.
따라서 돕기 위해 나설 수 있는 가장 좋은 때는
나중에 필요가 있을 때 지부 사무실은 여러분이 도울 수 있다는 것을 알 것입니다.
그리고 기도가 큰 힘이 된다는 것을 기억하십시오.
형제들을 위해 기도하고, 재해 구호 활동에 기꺼이 자원하고,
세계적인 활동을 위해 헌금함으로 형제 자매들을 도울 수 있습니다.
자연재해이든 인재이든 우리는 모든 재해를 피할 수는 없습니다.
하지만 우리가 여호와의 말씀과 조직의 지침에 순종한다면
영적으로 준비하고, 실제적으로 준비하고, 다른 사람을 돕기 위해 준비한다면,
여호와께서 재해에 대비하기 위한 우리의 노력을 축복하실 것이며

en.text: Jehovah warned that “in the last days,”
there would be “critical times hard to deal with.”
There would be “food shortages,” “pestilences,”
“earthquakes in one place after another,”
and other “fearful sights.”
We also contend with wildfires,
volcanic eruptions, destructive storms, and man-made disasters,
as well as an increase of lawlessness, civil unrest, and war.
No matter where we live, we will likely be affected by some form of disaster,
whether natural or man-made.
How can we be prepared?
First, we can prepare spiritually.
Isaiah 30:15 says:
“Your strength will be in keeping calm and showing trust.”
So we need to build and maintain a close relationship with Jehovah
and learn to trust in him now.
We do not expect divine intervention.
But when we pray during times of distress,
his powerful holy spirit
can bring Bible passages back to mind
to keep us calm and give us wisdom to make good decisions.
Second, we can prepare physically
by maintaining a go bag.
Our go bag could include items such as first-aid supplies,
bottled water, nonperishable food,
a Bible, and other necessary items.
If possible, each household should also have
a reasonable reserve
of basic supplies at home
in case it is necessary to shelter in place
for an extended period of time.
Check what government authorities
recommend for your community.
Also, we shouldn’t forget to update the elders
with our latest contact information.
If we don’t do so, valuable time could be lost in a disaster.
Additionally, during family worship,
our family could review the types of disasters that could happen.
Remember, emergencies like terrorist attacks and unrest
can occur anywhere and without warning.
So consider what could be done in each situation,
such as where to meet and how to contact the elders.
And third, we can prepare to help others
when they’re experiencing a disaster.
So, what can we expect if a disaster occurs locally?
If advance warning of a disaster is given,
field service group overseers will make sure
that everyone in their group is in a safe location.
Immediately after a disaster occurs,
each field service group overseer will contact everyone in his group
to learn of their needs.
It could take time to organize relief assistance,
especially if supplies are limited.
So it’s vital that each of us takes steps to prepare,
follows government warnings,
and keeps the elders informed of our circumstances.
Philippians 2:4 states:
“Look out . . . for the interests of others.”
When we are prepared, more attention can be given
to those with the most critical needs
and we may be able to help others in our own congregation and nearby,
even if we’re affected.
For example, in some circumstances,
brothers may need a place to stay temporarily.
Perhaps we could open our home and help them.
Or they might need food or basic supplies.
We could share what we have.
In other situations, our brothers may need help cleaning
or repairing their home when it’s safe to do so.
But what if a disaster occurs in another area?
Should we travel there to help?
If help is needed, the branch office will assign brothers
to coordinate and assist with relief efforts.
So the best time to make yourself available is now,
before a disaster occurs.
Ask your local elders for an application.
Then when there is a need, the branch office will know
you’re willing to assist.
And do not forget the power of prayer.
By offering prayers in their behalf,
by volunteering to assist with disaster relief efforts,
and by contributing donations to the worldwide work,
we can assist our brothers.
No, we can’t avoid all disasters,
whether natural or man-made.
But when we follow the direction from Jehovah’s Word and organization,
our obedience glorifies Jehovah.
If we prepare spiritually
and physically
and prepare to help others,
we can take comfort in knowing that Jehovah will bless our efforts
to be prepared for a disaster.

en.text: Brother Thomas Kalimeris,
who serves at the United States branch,
together with his wife,
has spent close to four decades supporting various aspects
of the organization’s construction projects.
What has that experience taught him?
That the work is not run by us.
Throughout history, men have built many beautiful and impressive buildings.
These structures have usually brought glory to men,
not to God.
But those men are long gone,
and even many of the structures no longer exist.
How true is the scripture at Psalm 127:1:
“Unless Jehovah builds the house,
it is in vain that its builders work hard on it.”
In our time too, Jehovah is using his people to build.
We’re working hard to build spirituality in interested ones,
and also we build structures
in order to help individuals to learn
about Jehovah and serve him.
In this type of construction
—both spiritual and physical construction—
I’ve been involved for most of my life.
I was born in Greece.
Our family came into contact with the truth in the early sixties.
I was baptized when I was in high school.
I left school to get some practical training in architecture,
but I made pioneering my career.
In 1973, I married my dear wife, Margaret,
and together we enjoyed many assignments.
We pioneered —special pioneering.
We went to Gilead.
We were invited to Bethel
in 1979 to work in the Engineering Department.
We worked on designing new branches,
Assembly Halls, Kingdom Halls,
renovation of existing branches
and remote translation offices.
Before we came to Bethel, we had seen how Jehovah provided for us individually.
But now we had the opportunity
to see how Jehovah provided for the needs of his organization globally.
By the year 2000, it became apparent that the present facility
of the Britain branch was not meeting their needs.
So a site was located 50 miles (80 km) north of London
to relocate the branch there.
However,
the Governing Body decided to cancel the project.
So in 2008,
the Governing Body wrote that now is the time
—Jehovah’s time— to find property
closer to London.
So a project team was formed,
and a few years went by, and a number of properties were searched,
and one was located closer to London.
If something we plan falls through,
it could mean that Jehovah has something else
—or better— in mind to meet the needs of his organization.
While working in the Haiti branch, we learned a lesson:
not to compromise on safety.
The Brooklyn Engineering Department did the drawings for the branch,
and a local contractor was hired
to build the structural work.
Now, the contractor, when he reviewed the drawings,
told the Branch Committee: “Really, this is overdesigned.
You’re wasting a lot of money by putting all the steel in the building.”
So we wrote back and said: “No, the drawings are OK.
“The branch is designed according to the seismic zone that it’s in.
And the contractor is to go ahead with the plans as drawn.”
In 2010, when the earthquake came to Haiti,
hundreds of thousands of people died
because of inferior materials and methods of construction.
However,
the branch did not suffer any damage,
and many people went there to find refuge.
We’re so glad that Jehovah did not allow us
to be swayed in this case.
Jehovah continues to direct a great physical building work
and a spiritual work.
Jehovah trains his people how to work together
for the work just ahead of us
—the beautification of this earth to a paradise.
It is so important that we ‘trust in Jehovah
and not to lean upon our own understanding.’
A life of building with Jehovah
has shown me the wisdom of Psalm 127:1.
If we keep building our lives with Jehovah,
our building work will never be in vain.

合力重建地球
我们一定要
“信赖耶和华, 不可依靠自己的聪明”
我的一生都与耶和华一同建造
我们看出诗篇127:1所蕴含的智慧
如果我们与耶和华一起建造人生
我们的工程就永不会白费!
