title: 게리 브로: 아무도 여러분을 사로잡지 못하게 하십시오 (골로새 2:8)

en.text: Our text today is highlighting the fact
that we do not want
to be trapped by the Devil.
And that’s what the apostle Paul
was concerned about with the Christians
in Colossae.
If we go to Colossians
where our text is found,
notice his words and his recommendations to them
in chapter 2 and verses 6 and 7.
He says: “Therefore, just as you have accepted
“Christ Jesus the Lord,
“go on walking in union with him,
“being rooted and built up in him
“and being stabilized in the faith,
“just as you were taught,
and overflowing with thanksgiving.”
So Paul was encouraging them: ‘Be strong Christians.
‘Have this deep,
‘spiritual taproot, so to speak.
Have your faith solid in Christ Jesus.’
I was in Louisiana last week,
and I tried to pull up a pecan seedling —a little plant of a pecan.
Have you ever tried that?
You cannot pull it up with your hands because the taproot goes so deep;
you have to have a shovel.
And so that’s what Paul was saying
—be sure that your spiritual strength
is solid and that it goes deep.
Well, why did he say that?
If you notice in verse 4, he says:
“I am saying this so that no one
may delude you with persuasive arguments.”
See, he was concerned
that even those with a strong spiritual foundation
may be deceived by persuasive arguments
and, as a result, destabilize their faith, so to speak.
So, what were some of the persuasive arguments?
Well, our text for today talks about them in verse 8.
He says: “Look out that no one takes you captive
“by means of the philosophy and empty deception
“according to human tradition,
“according to the elementary things of the world
and not according to Christ.”
So, what were the philosophies and empty deception?
Well, in Paul’s time, it included the Greek philosophies of Plato,
and that could affect
the spirituality of individuals in the congregation.
Also, that term “philosophy” was expanded;
it referred to more than just the Greek philosophers;
it also had reference to many, many groups,
many schools of thought
—even religious thoughts.
And Paul didn’t want them to become
—their faith to become destabilized
because of following those improper thoughts.
And notice, he said in verse 8,
so that you’re not made captive.
He didn’t want them to be captive to such thinking.
But is there something else besides the philosophies?
Well, verse 8 says also
“elementary things of the world.”
Now what is that?
In answering that question, The Watchtower
of August 15, 2008, page 28,
referred to 1 John 2:15, 16.
So let’s go there.
What’s included in “the elementary things of the world”?
First John 2:15, 16, it says:
“Do not love either the world or the things in the world.
“If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him;
“because everything in the world
“—the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes
“and the showy display of one’s means of life—
does not originate with the Father, but originates with the world.”
So The Watchtower introduces this as not just religious thinking
that could destabilize your faith;
it could be desires of the flesh.
The immoral thinking of the world
could affect us spiritually.
Over the years, over the thousands of years,
Satan really has carefully crafted the environment around us
as a trap,
and so he uses that effectively.
In fact, he maneuvers circumstances around each one of us
in order to try to work
on our personal inclinations.
So that’s why the second sentence
of our Watchtower summary says this:
“We can avert disaster
“if we quickly identify tendencies
that could lead us into temptation.”
Disaster —well, what’s that referring to?
Well, remember, Paul said in the scripture up there,
Colossians 2:8, don’t be captive.
Captive. That’s what Satan wants to do.
He wants to capture us.
We’ve heard of the poster “Wanted Dead or Alive.”
He doesn’t want us dead; he wants us alive.
Because why?
Well, it’s an interesting verse in 2 Timothy;
it tells us why the Devil would prefer to have us alive.
Second Timothy 2:26:
“And they may come to their senses and escape from the snare of the Devil,
seeing that they have been caught alive by him to do his will.”
If you’re dead, you can’t do Satan’s will.
So he wants to trap us alive
—or make us captive—
alive to do his will.
So, what do we need to do to keep from being trapped by Satan? is the question.
Well, we read that one sentence in our comments
to quickly identify tendencies.
OK. Now, where do the tendencies start?
This is an August 1, 1996, Watchtower,
page 12, paragraph 12,
and here’s what it says:
“Unholy actions are not just spontaneous
“or without prior basis.
“They are the result of defiling thoughts
that have been lurking in the heart.”
That’s what happened to Judas Iscariot.
Here was an individual that had
a very deep spiritual taproot, so to speak.
And apparently, Jesus didn’t know
that Judas would be the one betraying Him
when he was appointed as an apostle.
Sometime in 32 C.E., Jesus told his apostles:
“One of you is a slanderer.”
Apparently, by that time, he had identified Judas as that one.
Possibly by his actions,
a perfect man, Jesus, could identify it early.
And the Scriptures say
as a result of Judas acting on his thoughts,
Satan entered into Judas.
In other words, now he was going
to do the will of Satan.
But before that all happened,
there had to have been some wrong thinking
lurking in the heart of Judas.
What could it have been?
Well, it could have involved malice,
maybe greed, pride,
hypocrisy, scheming.
Somewhere in there was something that wasn’t right;
it was going to offend Jehovah God.
And he didn’t rip it out; he didn’t take care of it,
and look what happened to Judas.
So, what about us?
What’s lurking in our heart?
Now we all may be individuals with this deep spiritual taproot.
We’ve been in the truth many years; we’ve been at Bethel many years.
Or we may be young people,
and we’re serving Jehovah well right now,
but all of us have these improper thoughts
that we have to deal with.
Perhaps it could be something like this:
Maybe there is some scheming going on in our heart and mind,
maybe scheming of where we’re going to get the next drink of alcohol.
Maybe it’s an evil thought against someone that’s lurking in our heart.
Maybe it is a plan of action of how we can see pornography
or perhaps an unhealthy attraction
to someone of the opposite sex.
If that’s the case, what can we do?
Remember Isaiah 30:21.
It says to hear Jehovah’s voice “behind you saying, ‘This is the way.’”
Don’t give in to Satan’s way, but listen to Jehovah God.
Jehovah God has given us so many things
that can help us to address
the wrong thinking that’s lurking in our hearts.
In fact, he gives us guidance in his Word, the Bible.
Just think of all the scriptures that we can use,
no matter what tendency we may have,
that can address those tendencies.
He gives us the holy spirit.
Jesus conveys the voice of Jehovah God.
He does so by means of the congregation
through the direction of “the faithful and discreet slave.”
So if we are unable
to remove an improper tendency,
then get help
before Satan captures us to do his will.

cn.text: 今天的经文提到我们不想被魔鬼掳去
这也是使徒保罗担心歌罗西基督徒的事
让我们翻开歌罗西书
看看他在第二章６和７节写下的建议
他说
所以, 你们既然接纳了主基督耶稣
就要继续跟他联合同行
按着你们所受的教导
在他里面扎根和建造自己
巩固信心
洋溢信心和感恩之心
保罗鼓励他们
要当个坚强的基督徒
在属灵上深深地扎根
对耶稣有坚强的信心
我上个星期去了路易斯安那州
在那边我试着拔一棵胡桃树苗
一棵小胡桃树苗
你有试着拔过吗？
你没办法将它拔出来
因为它的根扎得很深
你需要用铲子才行
因此保罗的意思是
要在属灵方面保持健壮、稳固
深深地扎根
保罗为什么这样说呢？
请看第4节, 他说
我说这些话
是免得有人用花言巧语蒙骗你们
即使这些属灵根基稳固的基督徒
也有可能被花言巧语所骗
使得他们的信心动摇
那花言巧语包括些什么呢？
今天的经文在第8节回答
经文说
你们要当心, 免得有人根据人的传统
根据世人的肤浅想法, 不以基督为依归
用哲学和空虚骗人的话把你们掳去
经文提到的哲学
和空虚骗人的话又是什么呢？
在保罗的时代
这包括希腊的柏拉图哲学思想
这些哲学的思想
可能对会众成员的属灵情况产生影响
“哲学”也不是单单来自希腊的哲学家
也来自各种派系的学说、主张
还有宗教思想
保罗不希望
他们的信心因这些错误的思想而动摇
请注意
第8节说
“要当心...免得被掳去”
保罗不要他们被这些思想掳走
除了哲学之外还有其他要当心的吗？
第8节也提到“世人的肤浅想法”
现在我们来看看这是指什么
关于这个问题
《守望台》2008年8月15日刊28页
解释约翰一书2:15, 16
“世人的肤浅想法”指的是哪些事呢？
约翰一书2:15, 16说
不要爱世界和世界的事
谁爱世界, 爱父亲的心就不在他里面了
因为凡世界的事
比如肉体的欲望、眼睛的欲望
炫耀财物的行为
都不是源于父亲的
而是源于世界的
所以《守望台》指出
这不单指会动摇我们信心的宗教思想
也包括肉体的欲望
就是世上会影响我们属灵情况的
不道德思想
很多年来, 甚至几千年来
撒但运用我们周遭的环境
精心设计了一个陷阱
这个方法非常有效
事实上, 他会操控我们周遭的环境
来攻击我们的弱点
所以, 今天《守望台》评论的第二句话这样说
要是我们能及早察觉自己有不良倾向
就能避免跌进撒但所设的陷阱
防止悲剧发生
悲剧, 指的是什么呢？
请记得, 保罗在歌罗西书2:8说
不要被掳去
掳去
撒但想要俘虏我们
我们知道某些悬赏通缉令上
会写着“捉拿罪犯, 不论死活”
可是撒但却不要我们死
而是要我们活着
为什么呢？
一个有趣的经文在提摩太后书
它告诉我们为什么魔鬼想要活捉我们
请看提摩太后书2:26
这样
他们虽然被魔鬼活捉了去迎合他的意思
也许还可以醒悟过来, 摆脱魔鬼的网罗
如果你死了, 你就不能迎合撒但的意思了
所以他想要活捉我们
或说俘虏我们
让我们去做他要我们做的事
所以, 我们怎样做才不会被撒但俘虏呢？
今天的评论提到我们要及早
察觉自己有不良倾向
不良的倾向是怎么开始的呢？
以下这段话根据《守望台》
1996年8月1日刊12页的12段
它说
不圣洁的行为不是突发的
也不是无缘无故的
不圣洁的行为
是由心里潜伏着的不洁意念...所引发的
这就是加略人犹大的情况
他曾经在属灵方面根基稳固
显然, 当耶稣委任犹大做使徒时
耶稣并不知道犹大就是那个
未来要出卖他的人
直到公元32年的某一天
耶稣告诉使徒
“你们有一个人是毁谤者”
看来, 在那个时候
耶稣已经发现那个人就是犹大
也许是从犹大的行为
完美的耶稣
看出犹大就是要出卖他的人
然后有经文说
犹大将心中的想法付诸实行
撒但就进了他的心
换句话说, 他去做撒但要他做的事情
在这些事发生之前
犹大的内心
一定已经多少藏着错误的想法
可能是什么呢？
可能是恶念
也可能是贪婪、骄傲、虚伪、诡计
他的心有错误的想法
结果得罪耶和华上帝
可是他却没有排除这些想法
也没有好好解决这件事
结果你看犹大有怎样的下场
所以, 我们呢？
我们的心里隐藏着什么呢？
现在我们可能都在属灵方面扎根稳固
我们在真理中很多年
或在伯特利工作很多年了
又或者我们是年轻人
现在正热心事奉耶和华
但是我们每个人都需要面对
心中不当的想法
什么不当的想法呢？
也许是我们的心中开始出现一些诡计
也许是我们想找机会再多喝一杯酒
也许是心中产生了对某个人的恨意
或是计划偷看色情作品
或对某个异性想入非非
这时候, 我们该怎么办呢？
以赛亚书30:21说
耶和华从后面发出声音说
“这才是正路”
不要屈服于撒但
要听耶和华上帝的话
耶和华上帝给了我们很多帮助
让我们排除潜伏在心中的错误想法
其实, 他用他的话语圣经给我们指引
想想我们可以应用的经文
无论心中有什么不良倾向
都有适合的经文帮助我们排除
他赐下圣灵帮助我们
耶稣借着“忠信睿智的奴隶”
通过会众传达耶和华上帝的话
所以
如果我们没办法排除错误的倾向
要在撒但把我们掳走之前
赶快求助

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—여호와의 일을 수행하는 원격 자원봉사자들

ko.text: 중앙장로회 인사 위원회는 많은 자원봉사자의 복지를 돌봅니다.
자원하는 영을 가진 이 형제 자매들은
이사야처럼 “제가 여기 있습니다! 저를 보내십시오!”라고 말합니다.
전 시간 일하는 형제 자매들이 있습니다.
최근에는 베델 업무가 다른 여러 사무실들에서도 수행되고 있습니다.
그러한 베델 시설들에서 수행되는 모든 업무에 대해
열심히 일하는 우리 형제 자매들 가운데는
본이 되는 침례받은 전도인과 정규 파이오니아들로서
그들 중 다수는 세속 일을 하며 그렇게 하죠.
그런 부서 중에는 미술부, 컴퓨터부, 구매부 같은 부서가 있죠.
그보다 훨씬 더 많은 수의 장소에서
베델 업무가 원격으로 수행되고 있는 겁니다.
우리는 헌금을 지혜롭게 사용할 수 있게 되었습니다.
또 베델의 여러 부서들이 변화에 신속히 적응할 수 있게 되었죠.
이제 한국의 원격 자원봉사자들의 말을 들으면서
그들이 얼마나 큰 도움이 되고 있는지 살펴보시죠.
베델과 함께 일하고 있다는 느낌을 받기 위해서
신성한 봉사라는 그런 느낌을 계속 유지하기 위해서
야외 봉사를 하는 그런 옷차림으로 항상 준비하고
일과를 시작하기 전에 항상 기도로 업무에 임합니다.
월요일, 화요일, 목요일에 주로 일하고 있고요.
그리고 원격 일을 끝낸 그 이후 시간이나
또 일하지 않는 다른 요일들에는 제 개인적인 일을 보거나,
개인 연구와 공부하는 일에 시간을 보내고 있습니다.
사실 거리상으로는 지부와 많이 떨어져 있지만,
지부에서 일하는 것처럼 모든 시스템이나 환경이나
어~ 필요한 것들을 모두 마련해 주고 있기 때문에 원격 근무자로서도
마치 지부에서 일하는 거 같은 그런 환경으로
또 필요할 때면 언제든지 지부 형제들과 소통할 수 있기 때문에
지부에서 일하는 것 같은 그런 사명감과
최근에 그 변경된 그 LDC 왕국회관 건축 마련으로 인해서
전국에 그 건축 현장에 건축 자재를
지부에서 모두 공급해야 되는 필요가 생기게 되었죠.
그래서 그 많은 물량들을 저희가 공급을 해야 되는데
지부 내 성원들만 그 일을 해서는 역부족이었죠.
그런데 본부에서 원격 근무자를 사용해서 그 일을 해 보라고
그래서 비즈니스나 건축 자재에 대한 경험이 많은 형제들이
그분들을 통해서 물품을 원활하게 공급하고 있죠.
원격 자원봉사자로 베델 구매부 업무를 지원하고 있는데요.
건축 자재들을 구매하는 일을 담당하고 있습니다.
자기 부양과 가족 부양을 위해서 세속 일을 하고 있습니다.
외부에서 혼자 일을 하고 있긴 하지만
부서에서도 원격 근무자들의 어려움을 알기 때문에
다양한 지침을 주고 봉사 강연을 마련해 가지고
내부에 있는 사람이든 외부에 있는 원격 근무자든
영적으로 계속해서 좋은 그 상태를 유지할 수 있도록
격려해 주는 그런 마련들을 통해서 지원을 해 주고 있습니다.
여호와께서 이런 방법을 통해서 원격 근무자들이
여전히 그분의 관심 속에 있다라는 것을
알려 주시는 것 같아서 참 감사합니다.
디자인과 설명서를 만드는 작업을 하고 있습니다.
현장 사진과 또 설계 도면을 보내오게 됩니다.
또 얼마나 큰 사이즈로 부착을 하게 될지
디자인을 해서 다시 전용 네트웍을 통해서
저희들이 침례를 받고 과거에 10년간 디자인 회사를 운영하면서
이 사물의 제도에서는 우리가 가진 재능이
여호와의 조직에서 사용될 일이 없을 것이라고 사실은 생각했기 때문에
사실 파이오니아 봉사에 온전히 집중을 했었는데
여호와께서 여호와의 일에서 저희들을 사용해 주신다는 것 자체가
여호와께 너무 감사하고 큰 특권으로 여깁니다.
봉사부와 LDC와 관련된 문건들을 번역하는 일인데요.
그리고 여러 가지 웹사이트와 관련된 문건들을 번역하는 일을 합니다.
또 회중에 있는 저녁 봉사 마련을 잘 활용하려고 노력하고 있는데요.
조직에서 진행되는 이런 업무들을 제가 돕고 있는 일이
또 얼마나 소중한 일인지 또 얼마나 중요한지를 깨달으면서
일할 수 있는 또 힘을 얻고 있습니다.
지금 한국 지부 오디오 비디오 부 소속으로
원격 자원봉사자로 방송 관련 번역 일을 하고 있습니다.
가족의 필요를 돌보는 것이 여호와께서 주신
이 가족의 필요를 잘 돌보는 일을 희생하지 않는 한
어~ 여호와께 드리는 이 희생에 있어서
저 혼자만이 아니라 온 가족이 하나로서
이 일을 모두 함께 수행하고 있다는 그런 기분이 듭니다.
여호와께서 허락하셨다면 제 능력 밖의 일은
여호와께서 그 상황들을 조정해 주시고 또
분명히 여호와께서 이 일을 수행할 수 있도록 지원을 해 주신다는 것을
다양한 기회의 문이 열려 있다는 것을 더욱 느끼게 되었는데요.
그래서 이 원격 자원봉사는 우리가 이 마지막 시대에
우리 각자가 정말로 여호와께 우리의 것을 드릴 수 있는
정말 좋은 방법 가운데 하나인 것 같습니다.
계획을 하고 계시다면 반드시 이 일을 해 보시도록 권해 드립니다.
원격 자원봉사자 여러분의 수고에 진심으로 감사합니다.

cn.text: 中央长老团的人事委员会
十分荣幸能够为上帝的仆人服务
全球有很多弟兄姐妹甘心献出自己

这些仆人当中也包括全球数千名
全时在伯特利服务的弟兄姐妹们

还在伯特利以外的许多地方进行
我们非常珍视
在这些地方服务的弟兄姐妹所付出的努力
通过这个短片

远程志愿人员为了推广王国事务做了哪些工作

en.text: Sight, hearing, taste,
touch, smell:
Well, as you know,
those are the five primary senses
with which the Creator has endowed us.
But now, which one of these five
is perhaps related the closest
to our being able to gain the prize of everlasting life?
Well, is it not hearing?
It’s interesting that throughout history,
the churches of Babylon the Great have put the main emphasis,
not on hearing, but on seeing or perhaps touching
—seeing an image of their God, maybe touching or kissing that image.
But Jehovah has always put the emphasis on hearing.
“Hear, O Israel.”
“Give ear and listen.”
With commanding calls such as this,
the Israelites were summoned together
to hear Jehovah’s words read and explained.
Well, similarly today,
we have many opportunities
to hear Jehovah’s words read and explained.
But now, here’s a question:
Is it sufficient that we just hear
the sounds of Jehovah’s words?
Well, you know that’s not sufficient.
Here’s an experience that illustrates this.
Many years ago, I was working in service with a brother.
It was his turn to talk.
He was very nervous.
The lady came to the door.
He said, “How are you?”
She said, “Not very good.”
He said, “That’s good.”
And he proceeded with his presentation.
Well, he heard sounds coming out of her mouth,
but he didn’t hear so as to perceive what was said.
Well, obviously, Jehovah expects us to do
a whole lot better than that when it comes to hearing his words.
At Matthew 13:16, today’s scripture text,
Jesus commended his disciples by saying:
“Happy are . . . your ears because they hear.”
Now, he wasn’t commending them
for just hearing sounds coming out of his mouth,
but he was commending them because they heard with understanding.
They grasped the meaning,
and then they were in a position to make application of what they had heard.
Well, do we want Jehovah and Jesus
to pronounce our ears happy?
Do we want figuratively happy ears?
We do, don’t we?
Well, then, we must listen —like those disciples—
in a way that we grasp the meaning
and are in a position to make application.
Open up to Mark chapter 4, please.
And here’s an interesting scripture in this vein.
Notice the words of Jesus.
Mark chapter 4, beginning in verse 23, he said:
“Whoever has ears to listen,
“let him listen.
“He further said to them:
‘Pay attention to what you are hearing.’”
Now notice this:
“With the measure that you are measuring out,
“you will have it measured out to you,
yes, you will have more added to you.”
So notice, Jesus was saying
that if you measure out little interest and attention,
don’t expect to gain much.
In contrast, if you measure out
your full attention and interest to what I am saying,
then I will give you generously, even beyond your expectations.
Well, it works the same way today, doesn’t it?
We actually reap enlightenment in direct proportion
to how much interest and attention we measure out.
Go to Hebrews chapter 2.
Here’s another scripture— very familiar scripture in this regard
—Hebrews chapter 2,
and notice that we’re not to just pay casual attention
or even usual attention,
but notice how it’s worded.
Hebrews 2:1:
“That is why it is necessary for us to pay
“more than the usual attention
“to the things we have heard,
so that we never drift away.”
So it’s absolutely required
that if we’re not going to drift away from Jehovah or the truth,
we’ve got “to pay more than the usual attention.”
Now, let’s illustrate this point.
I’d like you to imagine
that you’re trapped in a building
that is engulfed in fire.
A fireman makes his way to you, and he says:
“I only have time to tell you this once; I’ve got to go help other people.
“But there’s only one way to escape:
“You’ve got to go down the stairs very quickly.
“When you get to the bottom,
“drop down on your stomach and begin crawling.
“You have to stay within three feet of the floor
“because above that there are poisonous gases.
“Crawl, though, to the right,
“and you will see a small hallway —a narrow hallway.
“Crawl through that hallway.
“When you get to the end, you’ll be in the lobby.
Stand up, turn left, run out the exit doors.”
Now, while those instructions were being given,
would you allow your mind to wander?
Would you be thinking: ‘I wonder what I’ll have for supper tonight?
I wonder what will be on TV?’
No, your attention would be riveted
because one missed detail could cost you your life.
And even after the fireman left,
you probably would still hear —ringing in your ears—
his words as you reviewed them in your mind, see.
‘Down the stairs, crawl through the hallway,
go out the left of the lobby through the exit doors.’
You’d be reviewing that information
with the idea that you were truly going to make application.
Well, that’s how we want to listen.
And if you think about it, we’re in a similar situation, aren’t we?
Satan’s world is on fire around us
and very soon it’s going to totally burn up.
But Jehovah is giving us escape instructions.
In fact, at 2 Peter 3:12 it says about this system
that it’s going to “be destroyed in flames
and the elements will melt in the intense heat!”
But we want to survive.
We don’t even slightly want to be like the idols
mentioned at Psalm 115:6
who ‘have ears but they don’t hear.’
Or like the cobra mentioned at Psalm 58:4
“that stops up its ear”
and refuses to hear “the voice of [the] charmers.”
Or like the disobedient Israelites described at Isaiah 6:10
as having “unresponsive” ears.
Or those disobedient Israelites that are described at Jeremiah 6:10
in the literal Hebrew as having ‘uncircumcised ears.’
We don’t even want to be like the Hebrew Christians
who were described at Hebrews 5:11
as being “dull in [their] hearing.”
We want to do our very best to ‘uncover our ear.’
Now, that’s an interesting expression
in the literal Hebrew at Job 33:16.
And, apparently, it comes from the fact
that the Orientals wore a headdress.
But to hear more clearly, they would partially remove that headdress
and uncover the ear.
Well, we want to do that ourselves.
We want to “incline [our] ear,” Psalm 78:1,
‘awaken our ear,’ ‘open our ear,’ “give ear,”
as different verses in Isaiah say.
And all of that is pay attention with a view of making application
of what we have heard.
Now, if we do this
—use our sense of hearing wisely as we’ve discussed—
then we’ll be in a position to survive
the cataclysmic end of this system of things.
As recorded at 2 Kings 21:12,
Jehovah said:
“Here I am bringing such a disaster on Jerusalem and Judah
“that it will make both ears
of anyone who hears about it tingle.”
Well, it’s true.
During the great tribulation, people of this world,
when they hear about the calamitous events
of the great tribulation,
undoubtedly both of their ears
—figuratively for sure but perhaps even literally—
will tingle.
But the ears of Jehovah’s people
will continue to be inclined
toward Jehovah’s directions that will come at that time,
such as found at Isaiah 26:20,
where Jehovah will say:
“Go, my people, enter your inner rooms,
“and shut your doors behind you.
Hide yourself for a brief moment until the wrath has passed by.”
And as Jesus declared
the ears of his disciples happy,
Jehovah and Jesus will be able to declare
the ears of the surviving great crowd happy.
They will say to them:
“Happy are your . . . ears because they hear.”

cn.text: 视觉
听觉
味觉
触觉
嗅觉
我们都知道创造主赋予我们
这五种主要的感官能力
那么，这五种感官中
哪一种跟我们能否得到永生奖赏
有最大的关系呢？
不就是听觉吗？
有趣的是，自古以来
大巴比伦一直忽略听觉
反而着重于视觉和触觉
像是要能看得到
也要摸得到神像
甚至要亲吻神像
可是，耶和华却总是强调听觉的重要性
圣经说：“以色列人啊...你们要听”
“你们要侧耳听我说话”
当时为了服从这个命令
以色列人就会被召集起来
一起聆听耶和华的话
今天，我们也有很多机会
能聆听上帝的话语
那么现在的问题是
我们光“听”耶和华的声音就够了吗？
大家都知道光“听”是不够的
我来说说一个例子
好几年前，我和一位弟兄一起传道
换他拜访住户的时候，他十分紧张
有一位女士来应门时
弟兄问：“您好吗？”
她说：“不太好”
然后弟兄说：“太好了！”
接着他就继续他的传道介绍词了
你看，这个弟兄听到住户说的话
却没有认真听她在说什么
当然，耶和华希望我们认真听他说的话
今天的经文，马太福音13：16
耶稣用以下的话来称赞他的门徒：
“你们的耳朵多么有福，因为听得见”
耶稣当然不是在称赞门徒的听力有多好
而是称赞他们理解所听的内容
他们了解话的涵义
并且愿意把听到的话应用出来
同样，我们希望耶和华和耶稣
称赞我们的“耳朵是有福的”吗？
我们想拥有这对比喻性的耳朵吗？
当然很想，不是吗？
所以，我们就要认真听
像门徒一样
了解话的涵义并实践出来
请翻开马可福音第四章
这里有一节值得留意的经文
请留意耶稣所说的话
马可福音第四章，从第23节开始
“凡有耳朵可听的，都应当听
耶稣又对他们说：
‘你们要留意自己听见的事’”
请留意接着的经文：
“你们用什么量器量给人
人也要用什么量器量给你们
而且要多多加给你们”
所以，耶稣的意思是如果你们不用心听
得到的益处就会很有限
换句话说，如果你们全神贯注
用心听我说的话
那么我就会慷慨地给你所需要的
甚至超乎你的想象
这对我们也同样适用，不是吗？
我们能获得多少益处都取决于
我们有多留心聆听
现在请看看希伯来书第二章
关于怎样留心聆听
一起来看看另一节大家熟悉的经文
其实，我们不是随意听听
或者是稍微注意就好
请看看这节经文怎么说
希伯来书2:1说：
“所以，我们务要格外留意所听见的话
免得随流漂去”
所以，我们如果不想随流漂去
离弃耶和华或者学到的真理
我们就必须要“格外留意所听见的话”
我用比喻来解释这个要点
想象一下你被困在一栋失火的大楼中
消防员好不容易在火场中找到你
跟你说：“没有时间了，我只能说一次
我还要去救其他人
这里只有一条逃生路线
现在你要马上下楼
到一楼以后，记得要趴下来爬行
因为上方的空气有毒
所以你只能在离地一米以下的地方呼吸
一直往右边爬行
然后你会看到一个又小又窄的走廊
一直爬到走廊的尽头，就是大厅了
之后，赶快站起来往左边的安全门跑出去”
想想看，当消防员告诉你这些逃生步骤时
你会专心聆听，还是会想：
今天晚上吃什么好呢？
有什么好看的电视节目呢？
当然不可能
你会专心聆听每一个逃生的细节
因为这牵涉到你的生命安全
甚至在消防员离开你之后
当你回想他的话时
你似乎还能在耳边清楚听到他说：
“走下楼、爬到走廊尽头
往大厅左方的安全门逃生”
你一定会仔细地回想这些逃生的细节
并且一一照着做
所以，这就是我们应该“听”的方式
想想看
其实我们不就是生活在类似的情况下吗？
撒但的世界就好像失火了一样
而且很快就会整个烧光
耶和华却给我们逃生的指示
彼得后书3:12 说
这个制度将会“着火而销毁
元素也因极热而熔化”
我们都想保命
千万不要像诗篇115:6所提到的偶像一样
“有耳，却不能听”
我们也不要像诗篇58:4所提到的眼镜蛇一样
“充耳不闻，不听念咒人的声音”
更不要像以赛亚书6:10
描述那些不服从的以色列人一样
“耳朵失灵”
也不要像耶利米书6:10
那些不愿服从的以色列人一样
希伯来语原文描述他们的“耳朵没有受割礼”
还有，我们绝对不要像那些
希伯来裔基督徒一样
因为希伯来书5：11说
他们的“听觉迟钝”
我们要尽力“开启我们的耳朵”
这是在约伯记33:16原文中
一种很有意思的表达方式
这种说法是因为当时的人习惯披上头巾
为了听得更清楚
他们会掀开盖住耳朵的头巾
没错，我们也要这样做
我们要像诗篇78:1一样
“侧耳听”
或像其他在以赛亚书的经文一样
“唤醒我的耳朵”
“开通我的耳朵”、“侧耳听”
这些都是指我们会留心聆听
而且把听到的应用出来
所以，如果我们像今天所讨论的一样
好好使用我们的听觉能力
我们就能平安渡过这个制度的终结
在列王纪下21:12，耶和华说：
“我要降祸给耶路撒冷和犹大
凡听见的人，都必耳鸣”
这是真的
在大患难期间
当这个世界的人听到
大患难要发生的事情时
他们那象征性的耳朵
也有可能是实际的耳朵，一定会耳鸣
但那时，耶和华子民的耳朵
会继续专心聆听耶和华的指示
就像以赛亚书26:20所描述的一样
耶和华会说：
“我的子民啊，进你们的内室去，关上门吧
要暂时匿藏，直到降怒完毕”
就像耶稣说门徒的耳朵多么有福
到时耶和华和耶稣也会说
那些生还的大群人
他们的耳朵多么有福
他们会对大群人说：
“你们的耳朵多么有福，因为听得见”

en.text: In the Netherlands, there was a need for a new,
suitable Assembly Hall, which could accommodate almost all
of the 300 congregations of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Additional building ground was acquired next to the existing hall,
so that a second, completely new hall could be constructed.
More than 200 volunteers worked on this project.
What challenges did they face?
And what blessings did they receive?
We had to sell our house and close our business.
It’s a step into the unknown.
I had to quit my job.
It was exciting to step
out of my comfort zone
and rely completely on Jehovah.
Everything is structured, organized.
That is why things run smoothly.
That doesn’t come naturally to me.
We were invited to come and work in the kitchen.
I love to cook at home.
I’m really fond of it.
What was my assignment?
Doing the dishes.
Working on yourself,
your Christian personality,
and cooperating with your brothers and sisters
—that has everlasting value.
It was wonderful training for the future
when we will be building together in Paradise.
You realize that everyone
sacrifices something and becomes happier.
No one regrets their decision.
That Jehovah takes into account your personal makeup,
that he is patient with us.
I’ve really learned how to work together
in a theocratic arrangement and still have fun.
You can work on yourself all day long
and therefore be able to improve.
I really learned to study more and to read the Bible more often.
Because we worked together so closely,
you got to know each other very well
and I really started to love and appreciate people.
We really came to appreciate
that every brother and sister has this beautiful inner person.
Visitors and contractors were always very surprised
that there were so many women working at the construction site.
It’s great working with sisters.
I have a construction background,
and communication with men can be really up front.
That doesn’t work with sisters.
You just have to be calm,
talk, and listen.
I had to work on a lift platform,
but that was kind of a problem because I’m afraid of heights.
The brothers were so kind to seal the sides up completely
so that I could not look down.
It was fun working together on that lift platform.
We called it our little flat.
The atmosphere was amazing, and we all had a great time.
Now we work in the kitchen
at the Swifterbant School Facility —a real privilege.
We’ve been trained to cook during construction,
but if needed, I’ll even do the dishes as well.
I’ll never work five days again.
Now I work three days,
and since July 1st, I started pioneering.
That’s just great.
He was offered a job.
He could even choose between two jobs.
Now he works three days a week, which always seemed impossible.
Eventually, we were in Swifterbant for one month only.
Then we went to Mozambique for three months.
Then for five months to Swifterbant again.
Then three months in South Africa.
Bethel called and assigned us to Congo (Kinshasa).
All the volunteers who helped to make a success of this project—
Well, they had to give up a lot.
As a result, we can enjoy this beautiful hall.
It’s amazing to be here.
It’s great to be encouraged
and to be strengthened for the ministry.
If you think about it,
every day we have around 700 new brothers and sisters.
That means every three days
we could fill a hall like this with new brothers and sisters.
These kinds of halls are really needed worldwide
in order to provide education to all those additional brothers and sisters.
It’s so faith-strengthening to be here.
Words cannot express it.
I feel so united, so warm, peaceful.
It’s so wonderful to be able to serve Jehovah together.

en.text: How do we know that Jehovah really sees each one of us,
no matter where we are?
Consider an example:
Thousands of refugees who faced
severe hardships in their home countries
have sought shelter in parts of Europe.
Watch how Jehovah has lovingly assured them
that they’re not alone by satisfying their spiritual thirst.
Welcome to Greece!
We really feel that Jehovah is blessing us
by opening a large door
of opportunities to preach the good news
to the many refugees who are streaming into the country.
For this reason, the brothers immediately informed us of the situation
and we directed the bodies of elders
to concentrate on the harbors, especially in Chios.
The brothers were willing to work in shifts
—24 hours a day.
The refugee shelters in our area only have families with children
and are located near a military airport.
Whenever military planes flew overhead
and the children would see and hear them,
they would immediately run and try to hide because they were afraid.
They sought protection from the tragic conditions
they had experienced during warfare.
This impressed upon us how greatly they needed
the comforting message of the good news,
so we felt the urge to approach them.
Therefore, the Service Department arranged
for four language classes to be held for the brothers.
We try to speak to people
in a language quite different from our own.
At times, we might think:
‘Will these people understand us?
Will we be able to reach their heart with these basic truths?’
Something that helped me not to hesitate
to approach these people
despite the language barrier
is what our teachers told us in the language class:
“Go and talk to them.
“Show them things from the Bible.
“Even if you don’t say things perfectly,
they will understand you.”
After we received permission
from the branch office, we also printed thousands of tracts,
since we did not have enough.
This whole effort created an atmosphere of enthusiasm.
I’m deeply moved when I see how lovingly
Jehovah cares for these people
who have never had the opportunity
to hear the Kingdom message
that gives them a future and a hope.
It was exciting
for them to hear that we have
a Bible-based video in their language.
We told them that the problems, calamities,
and the terrible war they had experienced
were not punishment from God,
but the result of the influence
Satan the Devil exercises over this system of things.
And this provided a good answer to their question.
On a return visit,
after two days, a refugee girl said something very touching:
“Now I understand why we have to go through all this.
It’s very difficult, but it’s not God’s fault.”
On another occasion, Gardinia, a refugee woman
who showed interest, told us:
“Since meeting you, I have a purpose in life.
“I have a reason to live.
Until now, I was just waiting to die.”
A refugee approached the Arabic witnessing cart,
and we read Revelation 21:4 to him.
He said, “Please, could you read that to me once again?”
So we read it a second time.
He replied,
“May I have a Bible of my own?”
So we gave him a Bible.
Then he said, “Would you please show me
the sentence you read in my Bible?”
So we marked the verse for him.
And on the way back
to our home at about 11 o’clock at night,
on the same road, at a well-lit point,
we saw that same refugee
sitting on the sidewalk reading the Bible.
About two and a half years ago, I met Moustafa.
He attended the meetings and made speedy progress.
Moustafa was baptized a few months
before the refugees started pouring in.
We do not believe that this was a coincidence.
He would say, “I want to speak about Jehovah,
but I can’t do that in the Greek language.”
When I can speak to people who are refugees
—just as I am a refugee—
in my own language,
this is a great opportunity for me.
And when I see that they listen to the truth and are loving it,
it makes my heart beat faster.
It touches my heart.
By expanding my ministry,
I’m sharing in a form of service
that could even be described as missionary work,
since I’m helping people hear about Jehovah
for the very first time.
I’m living what I have only read about in experiences.
Many were —perhaps for the first time—
discovering new skills in themselves,
indicating how Jehovah through his spirit can enable certain ones
to cultivate qualities they didn’t realize they had to such an extent.
We are so grateful to Jehovah for opening a door
leading to such wonderful activity.
It gives us great joy, and we praise him daily for this.
At the time this report was prepared,
over 100 Bible studies had been started.
One refugee told the brothers:
“You are the best thing that has happened to us here in Greece.
We thank Jehovah for meeting you.”
Another said: “We do not need material things.
“We need hope,
and you are giving this to us through the Bible.”

en.text: Perhaps for us,
our past mistakes are keeping us from moving forward.
That was the challenge for Jim Loyd.
He was raised in the truth
but did not progress to baptism.
By his teen years, he was getting into trouble.
As he describes it, in his heart he had left Jehovah.
His later involvement with gangs and violence
put him in a place he never expected to be.
But you will be greatly encouraged
to see where he is now.
Things that have happened to you, you can’t change
—but your personality you can.
We can change our personality with Jehovah’s help.
By the time I was 25,
I was associating with notorious criminals.
I guess I was a criminal too
—just took a wrong turn and kept going.
I found myself a fugitive on the run.
I was sentenced to many years in prison.
At 25, I felt like it might as well have been a life sentence.
Isolation and lockdown
was a very lonely place,
and I thought, ‘How did I get here?’
I remember a happier time in my life.
My mom would take us to meetings.
I was in the Theocratic Ministry School.
All the friends were so loving.
My mom sent me subscriptions to The Watchtower and Awake!
I had a box under my bunk,
and I’d toss them in there
—never opened them.
And I must have had a years’ worth.
You know, I never told her:
“Stop sending them, Mom.
I’m not reading them.”
I found out through my mom
that my dad had died.
I felt that I broke his heart.
I pulled out the box from under my bunk.
Right on top was a book,
The Truth That Leads to Eternal Life.
And at that moment, I knew
Jehovah hadn’t forgotten me.
I remembered that book.
I remembered that book when I was a boy.
I placed that book out in service.
I opened it up.
And, of course, the theme scripture for that publication
was Revelation 21:3, 4:
“The tent of God is with mankind.”
I read it that night the whole night.
I read the whole book.
Of course, that little bell went off.
I couldn’t deny that this was the truth.
So what was I going to do about it?
Shortly after that, I got transferred,
so I called my mom and told her.
It was funny; she asked,
“Do you think there are any Jehovah’s Witnesses
that go up there?”
I told her: “I don’t think so.
“It’s way up in the mountains.
I don’t think they go up there; it’s a little fire camp.”
I wasn’t a spiritual person yet.
All the magazines and books
went back into the box and back under my bunk.
I’d only been there five minutes,
and a guard came in and said,
“Are you a Jehovah’s Witness?”
I couldn’t believe it.
And I told him, “I studied with, been studying with Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
And he said: “Oh, good. Follow me.”
And I followed him, and he took me
and introduced me to a brother
who had been coming up there regularly
to study the Bible with inmates there.
And I realized
at that moment that once again
Jehovah had not forgotten me.
That brother faithfully came up there
for the next two years every Friday night.
He thought that it’d be a good idea to have
a Theocratic Ministry School, so he got it approved.
He would do the number one talk,
and the other brother that would come with him
would do the highlights, and then the three of us inmates
would do the other parts.
I was giving a talk every week.
And he started making
tape recordings of the meetings.
I’d listen to them over and over,
until the next week.
I knew that if I was going to return to Jehovah,
I had to make some adjustments.
With Jehovah’s help —I leaned on him more,
relied on his strength more—
it was then that I really felt that I could do this.
The beard became a goatee, and then it just became a mustache.
No drugs, no alcohol, no smoking,
and I cleaned up my language.
Then I finally got released,
got a job as an electrician,
and was able to get my own place
and started going to meetings.
I was listening to the Watchtower, and different ones were commenting.
‘Oh, that’s his wife’
—one of the brothers who came up to visit me.
I kept looking to see, so I could finally put a face
to the voices that I’d been listening to.
I let Jehovah mold me
into something good.
There are many blessings since dedicating my life to Jehovah.
I’ve been an elder for ten years now.
One of my sons came into the truth.
I met my wonderful wife.
She’s helped me
to grow spiritually and to love Jehovah even more.
One thing I kept praying for and he’s blessed me with is to forgive myself
—to have a clean conscience and freeness of speech.
And he’s done that.

cn.text: 我们可能因为自己过去犯的错
而在属灵方面停顿下来
吉姆·劳埃德就曾经这样
他在真理中长大, 但没有受浸
他十几岁的时候, 碰到了麻烦
他说, 那时他心里完全没有耶和华
后来, 他加入帮派, 又常常打架闹事
他从来没有想过自己会变成那样
不过, 你看到现在的他
一定会大受鼓励
你不能改变过去发生的事
但你可以改变你的性格
靠耶和华的帮助, 我们都能作出改变
我25岁时
身边的朋友都是恶名昭彰的罪犯
我跟他们同流合污, 做了很多坏事
我成了通缉犯
后来我被判入狱
刑期很长
只有25岁的我
觉得自己终生都要在监狱里
与世隔绝的生活非常孤单
我开始想:“我怎么会在这里?”
我还记得我快乐的童年生活
妈妈带我们去参加聚会
我还报名传道训练班
聚会所里的人都很有爱心
服刑时
妈妈帮我订阅《守望台》和《警醒!》杂志
在我的床铺下有一个箱子
我把一年来收到的所有杂志都扔进去
一本也没拆开来读过
但是, 我也从没有跟妈妈说
“别再寄了, 我根本就没看”
有一天妈妈告诉我, 爸爸去世了
我很难过, 觉得自己让爸爸伤透了心
那天, 我打开床铺底下的箱子
第一眼就看到《导致永生的真理》这本书
那瞬间, 我就知道耶和华没有忘记我
我记得这本书
我还是孩子的时候
在传道时向人分发这本书
我翻开它, 马上看到了这本书的主题经文
“上帝的帐幕在人间”
那天晚上, 我整晚没睡
整夜读这本书
直到把整本书都读完
我清楚地看出这就是真理
现在我该怎么做呢?
后来我通知妈妈
我被移送到另一个监狱
有趣的是, 妈妈问我
“你觉得那里有耶和华见证人吗?”
我说
应该没有, 那个监狱在偏远的山上
他们不会上去那里
那时我还不体会属灵的事
我把所有的杂志书籍扔回箱子
放回床铺底下
我才刚抵达新监狱不到5分钟
守卫就来问
“你是耶和华见证人吗?”
我简直不敢相信!
我说
“我以前...跟耶和华见证人学习圣经”
他说
“噢, 好, 跟我来!”
守卫带我去认识一位弟兄
这位弟兄定期来这里
跟监狱里的囚犯讨论圣经
再一次
我清楚地感受到
耶和华从来没有忘记我
接着的两年
这个弟兄每个星期五晚上都来这里
他觉得在监狱里举办传道训练班是好主意
监狱也批准了
他会发表第一号演讲
跟他一起来的弟兄会发表经文要点
其他部分由我和另外两位犯人担任
我每个星期都发表演讲
那位弟兄也为我录下聚会的内容
我会一直重复地听, 直到下一周的聚会
我知道如果我想要回头, 归向耶和华
就必须要作出调整
靠着耶和华的帮助, 仰望他
倚靠他的力量
我开始相信我能改变
我原本满脸胡子改成山羊胡
再改为八字胡
我不再吸毒、不再醉酒
不再抽烟、不再说脏话
我终于获释!
我找到一份电工技师的工作
也找到了住的地方和开始参加聚会
当大家在《守望台》研读回答问题时
“喔! 原来那是他的妻子”
那就是来监狱拜访我的弟兄的妻子
现在我终于能把声音和人连在一起了
我让耶和华塑造我成为更好的人
自从献身给耶和华之后
我得到了很多福分
我以长老的身分服务十年了
我有一个儿子也学习真理
我有个好妻子
她帮助我在属灵方面成长, 也更爱耶和华
我一直求耶和华宽恕我
让我有清白的良心, 能够向他坦然倾诉
他真的听我的祷告, 赐福给我

en.text: My name is Maska Mahamba.

prevent me from giving my all in the ministry.

At the same time,
he took into account the suffering of the people of his time.
He would take time to show kindness,
to encourage, and to heal.
The branch sees where there is a need
and then organizes a humanitarian mission.
I believe I can use my medical skills
to help our brothers.
It is love,
not just in writing,
but in action.
It’s a real joy
to help these brothers who need us
in remote locations far from towns.
It is always a pleasure.
Well, the two are the same; both eardrums are completely perforated.
Well, we are here
in the village of Walikale in the middle
of the forest on the main road
—well, the only road in the village.
It serves as our runway.
I can’t bear to see anyone suffer,
so I use all my skills to try
to find a solution.
What moves me to help the brothers
is what Jesus said,
that “there is more happiness in giving than
. . . in receiving.”
A long day —really very tiring—
but at the same time,
there was an encouraging case:
Brother Munyakaragwe, 68 years old,
10 years in the regular pioneer service, and he has 15 Bible studies.
This brother came from the territory on a motorcycle.
It took him two and a half hours on a very rough road
instead of an hour and a half
because he has a paralyzed leg.
And he was able to go back to his field service,
well, with some medication.
So it was really encouraging to see him
getting on the motorcycle with a smile on his face.
These are mosquito nets for those in need,
and there’s a big need here.
So we give them to each family.
You know, to protect your baby, one of the best things is for him
to sleep under a mosquito net.
Jehovah has done well because he has gone
through you to provide us with care.
We are very grateful.
We thank the many brothers
who have volunteered to serve us.
I thank Jehovah because without him
our identifying mark of unity wouldn’t exist.
You have helped me.
I had this problem for two years.
Now I’m so happy.
I will be able to hear at the meetings again.
Thank you.
The brothers are aware that they must thank Jehovah,
and we ourselves are aware
that all of this is possible
thanks to Jehovah’s holy spirit
and his organization.

en.text: But John, there’s still plenty
you can do in the congregation.
Sure, that sounds good.
But I’m no longer a ministerial servant.
Why did I let my zeal for the ministry cool off?
I know what the brothers must think of me now.
Hello?
Oh, good morning. My name is Jane.
How are you?
Not bad, thanks.
I know you may not be interested,
but I have this tract I’d like to leave with you . . .
“You may not be interested?”
Where did that come from?
Not my best presentation,
but it didn’t seem like she wanted to talk more anyway.
Well, what does that mean?
It may be manageable,
but long term, given your other conditions,
you’re looking at possibly some further tests . . .
Manageable?
Long term?
Oh, Jehovah, how can I do this by myself?
Of course Jehovah values you.
Try to think of someone in the Bible
who may have felt like you do, like Jonah.
Jonah?
Felt like I do?
“What comes to your mind when you think of Jonah?
Do you think of him as a disobedient prophet?”
“Reluctant to obey Jehovah’s command,
“Jonah boarded a ship that carried him
farther and farther away from his assignment.”
“Did Jonah’s recent actions
“disqualify him from ever again serving God
in an official capacity?”
He sure could have thought so.
I know I do.
“No,
“Jehovah mercifully and lovingly
renewed the prophet’s commission.”
So if Jehovah didn’t see Jonah as a total failure,
then what must he think of me?
First Samuel 16:7:
“For the way man sees
is not the way God sees.”
“Jonah did not see Nineveh as Jehovah did.”
Well,
with all that they were doing,
how could he view them any differently?
But the account says:
‘When God saw they had turned back from their evil ways,
‘he reconsidered the calamity,
and he did not bring it.’
“Despite the people’s badness,
“Jehovah cared about them.
“He values human life
“and the potential that each individual has
for repenting and learning to do what is right.”
Well, of course that’s true.
Why didn’t Jonah see that?
But am I seeing people the way Jehovah does?
Am I assuming they won’t listen
and then not giving my best?
How can I know how a person will respond?
‘Jonah learned to be merciful.
Will we?’
Matthew 5:7 says:
“Happy are the merciful,
since they will be shown mercy.”
“Then Jonah prayed to Jehovah his God
“from the belly of the fish, and he said:
“‘Out of my distress
“‘I called out to Jehovah,
“‘and he answered me.
“‘Out of the depths of the Grave I cried for help.
You heard my voice.’”
God heard Jonah and delivered him.
But I can’t expect a miracle.
“Then my prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.”
“My prayer.”
“My prayer came in to you.”
Jonah didn’t know
if Jehovah would rescue him,
but he prayed in faith that Jehovah cared.
“But as for me,
“with the voice of thanksgiving
“I will sacrifice to you.
“What I have vowed, I will pay.
Salvation is from Jehovah.”
As long as I still can,
I’ll keep sacrificing to God.
Salvation is from Jehovah!

en.text: There are many exciting things happening
in Jehovah’s organization.
Why, month after month, we read articles,
watch videos, and hear personal experiences
about our brothers and sisters who are doing more for Jehovah.
They are serving where the need is greater or reaching out
for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
They are working on construction, renovation,
maintenance of Kingdom Halls, or other theocratic projects.
No doubt, many of you watching this program
are excitedly looking forward
to expanding your ministry in one of these areas.
We encourage you to do so.
You can be assured that you will receive much fulfillment
and many blessings from Jehovah.
On the other hand,
there are others who are watching this program
who may feel discouraged because their circumstances
may seem to limit their being as involved as they would like.
What are some of these circumstances?
These may include our age, our health,
our economic situation, or our physical limitations.
For some of us, perhaps our upbringing
or past errors we have made in our life
may cause us to feel that we are limited
as to what we can do for Jehovah.
As we know well, focusing on our limitations
can affect our joy, causing discouragement.
What can we do?
There are many examples in the Scriptures of men and women
who had circumstances beyond their control
that seemed to limit how much they could do for Jehovah.
Others had to deal with the effects of their upbringing and family life
or with serious errors they made.
Did they allow themselves to be limited
by their circumstances or their past?
How did Jehovah feel about them?
How does Jehovah feel about us?
That is what we are going to discuss in this month’s broadcast,
which has the theme
“Are You Defined by Your Circumstances?”
Let’s start by looking at some
who could have let their circumstances limit them.
Consider first the example of Joseph in the book of Genesis.
Now, Joseph faced injustice at its worst.
His situation was especially hurtful
since it was initially brought on by those who should have been closest to him
—his family!
As a slave in Egypt and later as a prisoner,
Joseph was indeed limited in what he could do.
How might Joseph have reacted?
Well, Joseph could have become so preoccupied
with what he could not do
that he lost sight of what he could do.
Did Joseph let his circumstances
paralyze his life?
No!
He chose to make the best of his situation.
In fact, note what Joseph did
while serving as a slave in Potiphar’s house
if we turn together to Genesis 39:4:
“Joseph kept finding favor in his eyes,
“and he became his personal attendant.
“So he appointed him over his house,
and he put him in charge of all that was his.”
Joseph worked diligently
within the limitations of his circumstances.
He took a similar approach while in prison.
Joseph focused on what he could do
despite suffering the effects of injustice.
As a second example, consider Hezekiah.
Hezekiah is one who might easily have felt
that he was defined by his upbringing.
Look at the terrible example that was set by his father, Ahaz,
as recorded in 2 Kings chapter 16.
Second Kings chapter 16,
and notice what verse 3 says about Ahaz:
“Instead, he walked in the way of the kings of Israel,
“and he even made his own son pass through the fire,
“following the detestable practices of the nations
that Jehovah had driven out from before the Israelites.”
Hezekiah’s father did detestable things
in opposition to Jehovah.
But Hezekiah showed
that he was not the helpless victim
of a poor parental example.
What did he do?
Well, turn in your Bibles to 2 Kings chapter 18
and notice verse 3,
what it says about Hezekiah:
“He kept doing what was right in Jehovah’s eyes,
just as David his forefather had done.”
Verse 5 says of Hezekiah:
“There was no one like him among all the kings of Judah.”
He became fully involved in true worship.
Verses 6 and 7 say that Hezekiah
‘held fast to Jehovah, and Jehovah proved to be with him.’
How encouraging Hezekiah’s example is for us!
We can choose to be loyal to Jehovah
and do much in our worship of Jehovah,
even if we did not grow up in a family
that served Jehovah fully.
We are not helpless victims of our environment.
Hezekiah’s example reassures us that our past
does not have to control our future.
As a third example, consider the apostle Paul.
He did not let his own past mistakes
involving religious prejudice and violence
stop him from giving his all to Jehovah.
How did Paul feel about his past?
Well, let’s read together at 1 Corinthians 15:9:
“For I am the least of the apostles,
“and I am not worthy of being called an apostle,
because I persecuted the congregation of God.”
“I am the least of the apostles.”
Later, when writing to the Ephesians as recorded at Ephesians 3:8,
he calls himself “less than the least of all holy ones.”
Finally, at 1 Timothy 1:15,
he now calls himself the “foremost” of all sinners.
Yes, Paul’s prior treatment of the congregation
weighed heavily upon him.
Could Paul have reasoned that he was damaged?
Could he have reasoned that his past
limited what he could do for Jehovah?
He could have, but Paul did not do that.
He poured himself out for the congregation.
Why, Paul was privileged to write more books and letters
in the Christian Greek Scriptures than anyone else.
He demonstrated an outstanding zeal for the ministry.
Paul did not let his conduct in the past
dictate what he could do for Jehovah.
And there are many other examples as well.
For example, are we in a difficult economic situation?
The account in 2 Corinthians chapter 8
tells us about the Macedonians.
Paul says that they were in deep poverty.
Yet they begged to have a financial share
in the relief work.
Are we older in years?
We may think of Anna.
The account at Luke 2:36-38
tells us that she was 84 years old
and that her husband had died
after just seven years of marriage.
Yet, “she was never missing from the temple.”
She rendered ‘sacred service day and night.’
What lessons do we learn from these accounts?
Our dear brothers and sisters in Bible times were just like us.
Many were in circumstances that they would not have chosen.
Yet, they did not let their circumstances
or their past define them.
They joyfully did what they could
within the limits of their situation.
And these are just a few examples.
There are many others in the Bible.
Why not make it a personal study project
to research faithful ones
who were in circumstances similar to yours?
How did they stay involved in Jehovah’s work?
We are sure that you will be greatly encouraged.
Now, we’ve considered examples of those
who did not let their circumstances hinder them
from giving their all to Jehovah.
But another question is:
How does Jehovah view his faithful servants
despite their limitations?
Now, I’ve often thought about the example of John the Baptizer.
As we know, he was arrested shortly after Jesus started his ministry.
John could have felt
that he was no longer of use to Jehovah or the work.
Yet, as recorded at Matthew 11:11,
Jesus said about John:
“Among those born of women,
there has not been raised up anyone greater than John the Baptist.”
Jehovah’s and Jesus’ view of John
was not based on the man’s circumstances
of being in prison.
Their view of John was based on who he was on the inside
and on his relationship with Jehovah.
Jehovah did not focus on the limitations.
In Jehovah’s eyes, John was great.
He was still a faithful servant doing the best that he could,
and that was all that really mattered.
Another example that may come to your mind
is that of King David.
As we know, King David committed serious sins.
Yet, David repented for his sins,
and there is no record that he repeated them.
How did Jehovah view him?
Did Jehovah see David as damaged,
as a man who would always be limited in serving him?
Notice Jehovah’s words directed to King Jeroboam
at 1 Kings 14:8:
“But you have not become like my servant David,
“who kept my commandments
“and who walked after me with all his heart,
doing only what was right in my eyes.”
Jehovah viewed David as a special servant.
He says that he “kept my commandments.”
He did “what was right in my eyes.”
That’s what Jehovah remembered.
How encouraging that is for us!
If we have repented of our past mistakes
and set matters straight to the best of our circumstances,
we too can be assured that Jehovah loves us dearly.
He appreciates whatever we can do in our worship of him.
So, what’s the point?
Well, our past or our present circumstances
do not define our value before Jehovah.
Our Father loves us for who we are,
and he values our efforts
as we do the best that we can to serve him.
Why do you think it is important
that we strive to see ourselves as Jehovah does?
Because we can weaken, discourage, or limit ourselves
if we see ourselves only in the framework of our circumstances.
May we work hard not to do that.
What does Jehovah see
when he looks at his faithful servants today?
Well, turn, please, to 1 Samuel 16:7.
And the setting is that Samuel was about to go
to anoint the next king of Israel;
and he goes to the house of Jesse; and Jesse lines up all of his sons,
except for David, who is still out in the field;
and Samuel walks in and he sees Eliab.
And based on what he sees,
Samuel concludes that this surely must be
the next king of Israel.
Yet, note what Jehovah saw.
Please read with me 1 Samuel 16:7:
“But Jehovah said to Samuel:
“‘Do not pay attention to his appearance and how tall he is,
“‘for I have rejected him.
“‘For the way man sees is not the way God sees,
“‘because mere man sees what appears to the eyes,
but Jehovah sees into the heart.’”
That’s the way Jehovah sees.
He does not look at our outward appearance and our abilities;
he sees into our hearts.
He sees what we would be doing
if all of the limitations were lifted off of us.
Why, just the fact that we keep going,
that we keep putting one foot in front of the other,
endears us to Jehovah.
We understand the truth of that statement,
and we all may agree
that this is how Jehovah views his people.
However, we may have a hard time convincing ourselves
if this really applies to me.
Have you ever wondered: ‘Does Jehovah really see me?
‘Does he see what’s in my heart
and value my desire to do more for him?’
The answer is yes.
In fact, Jehovah has already seen what is in your heart.
Think about this:
Why are you watching this program?
Why do you care about spiritual things?
Why are you, perhaps, the only one in your family
who is a dedicated, baptized servant of Jehovah?
Or why are you, perhaps, the only one at your place of employment
or the only one near where you live who’s serving Jehovah?
Is it because you are so much more studious
or smarter than everyone else?
No!
Haggai 2:7 tells us
that Jehovah “will shake all the nations,
and the precious things of all the nations will come in.”
John 6:44 says
that ‘no man can come to Jesus
unless the Father draws him.’
Jeremiah 31:3, Jehovah says:
“I have loved you with an everlasting love.
That is why I have drawn you.”
So again, why are you serving Jehovah?
Because Jehovah loves you.
Jehovah drew you.
As he was shaking the nations,
he looked down into your heart and he saw something very precious
and he drew you to him.
He said, “I want to draw this person to my Son.
“I want to draw this person to me.
I love this person.”
Jehovah drew you,
not because you have perfect circumstances,
but because of your heart and because he loves you.
He greatly appreciates that his servants give their best to him.
Remember, not the way man sees is the way God sees
—Jehovah sees what the heart is.
May we work hard to see ourselves as Jehovah does
and be determined to never give up.
May we never forget that it is the privilege of bearing Jehovah’s name,
having a relationship with him,
and our love for Jehovah that defines us.
Jehovah is happy if we give the best that we can.
So may we do our part
by not limiting ourselves due to our circumstances,
but always look for ways to give our best to Jehovah.
You beautiful older ones,
even those with severe health problems,
can do much to help in the great work that’s taking place today.
Now, you may wonder what can you do.
You can pray for your brothers and sisters.
We need your prayers.
Pray for the Governing Body.
Pray for those who are taking the lead.
Pray for the elders in your congregations.
Pray for those who are going through difficult times.
Do such prayers help the work of the organization?
Absolutely!
James 5:16 tells us
that ‘a righteous person’s supplication
has a powerful effect.’
No matter who we are and whatever our situation in life,
may we find joy in giving what we can for Jehovah.
And may each one of us rejoice at the privilege we have
of being part of what Jehovah is accomplishing in these last days.

本月节目会谈谈这些问题
主题是
你的情况会限制
你为耶和华做更多服务吗?
让我们来看看一些圣经人物的例子
首先, 请想想创世记中约瑟的记载
约瑟受到极不公平的对待
这一定让他非常伤心
因为伤害他的不是别人, 是他亲爱的家人
约瑟在埃及做奴隶, 后来又被关进监牢
在这种情况下他能做的确实很有限
但约瑟有什么反应呢?
约瑟本来可以只想着自己受到的限制
却忽略自己能做的事
不过
约瑟没有因为不利的情况自暴自弃
还是尽力而为
请留意约瑟在波提乏的家做奴隶时
怎么做
创世记39:4这么说
虽然情况不利
约瑟仍尽心竭力的工作
即使被监禁的时候也一样
他始终把注意力集中在自己能做的事上
第二个例子是希西家
希西家大可以让自己受成长环境影响
我们读读列王纪下第16章
就可以知道他的父亲亚哈斯有多坏
列王纪下16:3说
虽然希西家的父亲
做了很多耶和华憎恶的事
但希西家没有因此就随波逐流
他怎么做呢?
请看圣经的列王纪下18:3
这里提到希西家说
接着第5节的经文说
在他以前或以后的犹大王中
没有一个像他
希西家全力支持正确崇拜
第6, 7节的经文也说
他“紧紧依附耶和华”
而耶和华也“与他同在”
希西家的榜样多么鼓励我们!
即便我们不是在基督徒家庭里长大
也可以避开不利影响而忠于耶和华
希西家的例子让我们相信
我们可以选择
不要让自己的过去左右我们的未来
第三个例子是使徒保罗
保罗曾因为宗教偏见而迫害基督徒
但他没有让过去的错误
阻碍自己忠心崇拜耶和华
保罗对于以前做过的事有什么感觉呢?
他在哥林多前书15:9说
“我在使徒中是最小的”
在以弗所书3:8
保罗后来写信给以弗所的弟兄时说
自己“比圣民中最小的还不如”
他甚至在提摩太前书1:15说
自己是罪人当中的“罪魁”
看来, 保罗迫害基督徒一事
确实让他久久不能释怀
保罗曾觉得自己一无是处吗?
他觉得自己曾犯错
所以不能为耶和华做更多服务吗?
保罗可能这样想过
但他并没有自暴自弃
他愿意为会众献出自己
后来保罗有荣幸写《希腊语经卷》
写过的书信比别人多
他非常热心传道
没有让过去犯的错误
阻碍他为耶和华服务
还有很多其他例子
我们经济上有困难吗?
哥林多后书8章记载马其顿人的榜样
保罗说他们极度贫困
但他们还是求保罗
让他们资助弟兄姊妹
我们年纪大了吗?
我们可以想到安娜
路加福音2:36-38提到安娜84岁
她的丈夫在结婚七年后就过世了
可是“她从没有不上圣殿”
“日夜都敬奉上帝”
我们从这个记载学到什么呢?
圣经时代的弟兄姊妹跟我们的情况很像
有很多事是他们无法掌握的
即使这样
他们没有让他们的情况或环境
限制他们为上帝服务
虽然困难
但他们还是喜乐地做自己能做的事
这只是其中几个例子而已
圣经里还有更多例子
何不做个研读计划
查查看有哪些忠仆跟你的情况类似呢?
他们怎样多一点为耶和华服务呢?
我们相信, 你一定会大受鼓励
我们已经看过一些人的榜样
他们没有让情况或环境
阻碍他们全心为耶和华服务
那么, 现在的问题是
耶和华又怎样看他的忠仆呢?
我常常想到施浸者约翰
耶稣开始传道后不久, 约翰就被逮捕了
约翰可能会觉得
自己对耶和华来说已经没有用了
不过马太福音11:11记载
耶稣对约翰的看法, 说
凡妇人所生的
从没有兴起一个比施浸者约翰大的
虽然约翰被关在监狱里
但耶和华和耶稣看的不是约翰的情况
而是他的内心和他跟上帝的关系
耶和华不会只看我们做不到的事
在耶和华看来, 约翰做得很好
他很忠心, 尽力做到他能做的事
而这才重要
你可能也想到大卫王的例子
我们知道, 大卫曾犯下严重的罪
后来他真心悔改
没有任何圣经记载说他重蹈覆辙
耶和华怎么看大卫呢?
耶和华有没有认为大卫没有用了
不能再为他服务了呢?
请留意列王纪上14:8
耶和华对耶罗波安怎么说
对耶和华来说, 大卫是特别的
因为大卫遵守耶和华的诫命
只行耶和华看为对的事
这是耶和华记得的事!
这真的很鼓励我们, 对吗?
如果我们也对自己的错感到痛悔
还尽力作出改变
我们也可以确定
耶和华一定会非常爱我们
他一定很高兴看到我们尽力崇拜他
那么重点是什么呢?
就是我们过去的背景或现在的情况
都不会影响耶和华怎样看我们
上帝爱我们
他看的是我们竭尽全力为他服务
为什么我们应该
努力按照耶和华的方式看自己呢?
如果我们只注意自己做不到的事
就容易灰心丧气
我们要尽量避免这样想
今天耶和华察看他的忠仆时
他看到什么呢?
请留意撒母耳记上16:7
经文是说
撒母耳要去膏立下一位以色列王
他到了耶西的家
耶西把儿子, 除了大卫, 都叫出来
因为大卫在野外
撒母耳看到以利押的外表
就认为这个人一定是下一个以色列王
不过, 请留意耶和华看的是什么?
撒母耳记上16:7说
这就是耶和华看人的方式了
他不是看人的外表和能力
而是看人的内心
耶和华相信
当不利的情况都消失的时候
我们一定会做得很好
我们继续努力做自己做得到的事
耶和华就会更爱我们
我们都知道耶和华是看人的内心
也知道他怎么看我们
但是, 有时候我们可能很难相信
上帝真的这样看我们
你是不是曾经想过
耶和华真的看到我吗?
他真的看到我的内心吗?
我想为他做更多服务, 他真的会重视吗?
耶和华会重视的!
耶和华已经看到你心里所想的了!
想想看
为什么你会看这个节目?
为什么你重视属灵的事?
为什么你是家里唯一献身受浸的人呢?
为什么你是公司里或社区里
唯一的耶和华见证人呢?
是因为你比其他人会念书吗?
比其他人聪明吗?
不是!
哈该书2:7说耶和华会“震动万国”
“万国的珍宝必都前来”
约翰福音6:44说
要不是“父亲吸引人”
就没有人能到耶稣这里来
耶利米书31:3
耶和华说“我以永恒之爱去爱你”
“因此我...吸引你”
所以, 你为什么会事奉耶和华呢?
因为耶和华爱你, 他吸引了你
当他震动万国的时候
他看到你的内心
发现了一些很宝贵的东西
他就吸引你归附他
他说
我要吸引这个人归附我, 做我的儿子
我爱这个人
耶和华吸引你
不是因为你的情况、环境很完美
而是因为你的内心
也因为他爱你
耶和华赏识他的仆人把自己最好的献给他
别忘了, 上帝看人不像人看人
耶和华看的是内心
希望我们都努力用耶和华的观点看自己
绝对不要放弃
也希望我们绝不忘记
我们有殊荣为耶和华的名作见证
可以跟他有紧密的关系
也不要忘记我们对耶和华的爱
如果我们把最好的献给耶和华
他一定很高兴
所以, 希望我们都不受自己的情况限制
而是一直把最好的献给耶和华
亲爱的长者
和那些可能有严重健康问题的人
你们也能在传道工作上尽一分力
你可能会怀疑自己到底可以做什么
其实你可以为弟兄姊妹祷告
我们需要你们为我们祷告
为中央长老团成员祷告
为带头的弟兄祷告
为会众的长老祷告
为那些有困难的弟兄姊妹祷告
你为这些人祷告
可以对组织的工作有帮助吗?
绝对有帮助!
雅各书5:16 说
义人恳切祈求所发挥的作用
是大有效力的
不管我们是谁, 不管我们的情况怎样
我们尽力敬奉耶和华会带来快乐
我们很荣幸能在最后的日子
为耶和华的工作尽一分力

en.text: One of the tools that can help us
to actively search out reminders
is JW Library.
This amazing app has been installed
on over 15 million devices.
But do you know how much work it takes
to develop and maintain this app?
Well, we are now going  to look behind the scenes
and meet some of the brothers who have either worked on this project
or helped to organize that work.
This really is an opportunity to visit
an area in Bethel that you don’t get to see on tour.
Of course, there are many brothers associated with the work.
But we would like you to get to know three
of these very hard-working brothers,
and let me introduce them to you.
First of all, Brother Per Christensen, the overseer of MEPS Programming.
Now, Per, you’ve been in this country
working in the U.S. Bethel for a number of years.
But where are you from originally?
I was born in Denmark
and served there in the branch for years.
So when did you and your wife, Berit, come to the United States?
And our first year was in Brooklyn.
And then we had 18 years in Patterson
and then back to Brooklyn again for three and a half years.
And now we’re in Warwick since November last year.
Well, I know you worked in Translation Services for a while
because, in fact, the two of us worked together
in the same department there for a while.
But what type of work have you been involved with
since you’ve come to the United States?
Lots of exciting and challenging jobs.
Working in Translation Services
—that was training and support for our translators worldwide.
Now in MEPS Programming
—that is all about distribution of spiritual food
to all our brothers and sisters.
So we have a ton of work and a lot of challenges.
But I’m also working with a lot
of very, very talented brothers and sisters.
So it’s a lot of fun, and it’s great going to work every day.
That’s great to hear, Per.
In fact, I’m even tempted to come back and work with you.
Oh, we would love that.
I think I’d love it too.
Well, let’s turn our attention to Brother Alfredo Serna.
Now, you are the assistant overseer of MEPS Programming.
In fact, you and I worked together in Mexico back in 2003.
Could you tell us a little bit about what you were doing at that time?
My last work assignment involved overseeing
the large Translation Department there.
It was an amazing privilege to work
with translators in sign language and the indigenous languages,
a true joy to contribute to preparing publications
for those in the minority groups.
So when did you and your wife, Gina, come to the United States to work here?
We arrived at Patterson in 2007.
We have fond memories of that time,
and it’s something we still treasure.
Very good.
And now, Brother Paul Willies,
where do you originally come from along with your wife, Su-lin,
and when did you come to the United States?
Well, we’re both originally from South Africa,
and we served there in Bethel for a number of years.
And then in 2010, we were transferred to work
along with MEPS Programming here in the U.S.
So, what type of work have you been involved with,
particularly recently?
Well, most of my time in Bethel
I’ve been working on the Watchtower Translation System,
or WTS.
Actually, I was working along with Per.
Per was in headquarters, and I was working
on the programming team that we had in South Africa.
WTS is the program that the translators use
to help organize and manage their translation work.
And then, of course, most recently I’ve been working on the mobile apps
—the JW Library app and the JW Library Sign Language app.
Very good.
Well, now all of you work in MEPS Programming.
Per, can you just tell us a little bit?
We’re familiar with the term MEPS, but what really is it?
Well, MEPS stands for
Multilanguage Electronic Publishing System.
That didn’t help me at all.
Sorry.
Can you make it a little bit more simple so we can understand?
We make the tools, or the programs, that the organization needs
to make publications
and have them translated into hundreds of languages.
So I can illustrate it this way:
that we are not making the spiritual food,
but we are building a conveyor belt for the spiritual food
from the faithful and discreet slave
down to the printing presses
or to our website or to Watchtower Library,
ONLINE LIBRARY or, like in this case, JW Library.
Thanks so much.
Now, at long last, I do understand a bit more
about what MEPS means.
Now, as I travel around, the brothers and sisters,
they tell me how much they love JW Library.
But there seems to be no end
to the suggestions for improvements and features
—and long lists of suggestions.
Can you give us a little bit of an idea of what’s involved
with trying to develop a new feature for JW Library?
Yes, the brothers and the sisters really love using the app,
and because of that, they’re keen to get many new features.
Of course, we wish we could just add all those new features into the app,
but the truth is we just can’t.
Yes, adding each new feature involves a lot of work.
And we also need to determine whether a feature
that’s requested is just a “nice to have”
or is it something that’s going to address a real need?
For example, will it really help an elder who is out on a shepherding call
or maybe a pioneer sister who is at the public witnessing carts
or at her Bible study or return visit?
Also, very important to us is trying to make
each new feature very simple to use . . .
Ah, thanks for doing that.
. . . especially for a first-time user, someone who’s never used the app before.
And then, of course, before we start working on anything,
we always get approval from the Governing Body.
Ah, that’s a good thing to do too.
Like one feature that many have been asking for
is the ability to add notes into the app.
And, of course, before we start programming it,
we have to make sure that it actually does what is wanted.
We made a video that shows how we go about that.
You have?
Would you like to see it?
Well, of course. I’d love to see it!
Hello. How are you?
Good, good, good.
Welcome! Thanks for coming.
How about yourself?
Fine, thank you. Have a seat.
All right, so glad you could be here!
Thank you so much.
Oh, so fancy.
Yeah! So we get to talk about JW Library today.
So, what are some ways that you use JW Library?
I mean, it’s revolutionized going to meetings.
Oh, my.
I go to meetings and sometimes I just carry my iPad.
So the fact that you can make the text larger. . .
It’s easy to listen to the readings right in the app now,
and so I—I find myself doing that.
So if we were to make a notes feature,
what are some things that you’d like to be able to do?
I mean, if you could see all your notes without tapping on
each one that would be great.
And even if you make a note in, maybe, your phone
and it can also be saved in your tablet, that would be really nice.
Yeah.
Well, what if I told you that in front of you
is an early version of JW Library?
Whoa! Cool!
Oh, fantastic!
This is it?
With notes—yeah.
Ooh.
So a few months ago, the Governing Body
gave us approval to start working on the notes feature.
We got together as a team, and we’ll do, like, these rough sketches,
and programmers write code.
But before we release an update,
we have a group of testers.
And, you know, they’ll find little glitches or bugs or things,
but they’ll try to work it out with the programmers.
After that, we have a pretty stable version of JW Library.
The goal is to show it to you,
and you can let us know what you think.
So now that you’ve seen the new notes feature
in JW Library, what do you think?
I love that I can tag the personal things that I need to work on
or a comment or a scripture that I can encourage someone with.
This is fantastic!
Yeah. It’s great.
I like that I can find my notes, especially using the search feature.
It’s great!
And it’s really neat how my comments—
I can place it right next to the paragraph for meetings,
and it doesn’t cover the actual text.
The ability to back it up so you can restore it to another device,
that’s going to be really helpful.
I love it!
Amazing!
OK. Go ahead.
Yeah. Go ahead!
So you’re telling us we can proceed.
That’s fantastic!
But, brothers, you can’t show us something like that
and not tell us when we’re going to get it.
Well, we said on the website that it was coming soon.
I know you said that on the website, but when?
Is it OK to be more specific than that?
I think that’s why they invited us here.
Paul, let’s hear it.
Well, we’re happy to tell you that the notes feature
in JW Library will be coming soon,
and by soon we mean during May of 2017—this month!
So we can go and check the app stores for an update.
Oh, that’s wonderful to hear.
So all of us will be happy to be able to put our own reminders
right there in the JW Library app.
Well, I’m looking forward to being able to do that as well.
But now, while I’ve got you here,
we’re not going to let you go until we ask this big question:
What are you working on now?
In other words, what can we expect to see soon with JW Library?
We have another brief video showing what the team is working on
to support the Study Bible on the JW Library app.
Would you like to see it?
That’s wonderful. Let’s have a look.
Later this year,
work will begin on adding the Study Edition
of the New World Translation to JW Library.
When this edition becomes available
in your language,
you will be able to discover
spiritual gems in the study notes.
And the new media gallery
will help you to visualize the people, places,
and things you read about.
You will also see the new overviews of each book,
play the introductory videos,
and study additional appendix material.
All of this and more
is coming soon to JW Library!
That sounds so exciting.
So we’ll all look forward to getting that feature.
You said, “coming soon,” didn’t you?
Anyway, we’d like to thank you very much
for the fact that you’ve come along and you’ve explained so much to us
about what goes on with MEPS Programming
and the JW Library app.
But before you go,
we’d like to ask you, when you go back to your department,
please, take an expression of our appreciation
back to the hard-working brothers and sisters
who are working behind the scenes in providing this tool for us.
Will do.
Happy to.
Thanks.
Thank you very much.

找出实用提醒的好工具
这个很棒的应用程式
已经安装在超过1500万台电子设备上
研发和维护这个应用程式
要花多少心血呢?
我们一起来看看
JW Library 的幕后工作
并且认识几位参与开发和设计的弟兄
这是你参观伯特利绝对看不到的
当然, 许多弟兄都尽全力协助这项工作
我们想介绍其中三位给大家认识
我来为大家介绍一下

佩尔, 你在美国伯特利已经多年了

嗯, 我知道你在翻译服务部

因为我们曾经在同一个部门

我做过很多有趣又有挑战性的工作
在翻译服务部训练和协助
世界各地的翻译员
而目前在MEPS程式设计部的工作

所以我们有庞大的工作量
遇到不少挑战

一起工作
工作充满乐趣
佩尔, 听到这连我都想回去
跟你一起工作了
我们会很高兴
我也是
接着访问阿尔弗雷多·塞尔纳弟兄
现在你是MEPS程式设计部监督的助手
还记得
2003年我们曾在墨西哥一起服务过

title: 마크 샌더슨: 그들은 박해의 대상이 될 것입니다 (마태 10:22)

en.text: Well, before his death,
Jesus warned all of those
who would be his followers in the future
that they would be objects of persecution.
In Matthew chapter 10, do you remember what Jesus said?
Let’s read this together, Matthew 10:22:
“And you will be hated.”
Verse 22: “And you will be hated by all people on account of my name,
“but the one who has endured to the end will be saved.
“When they persecute you in one city, flee to another;
“for truly I say to you, you will by no means
“complete the circuit of the cities of Israel
until the Son of man arrives.”
Well, interestingly, almost immediately
after the holy spirit had been poured out
and Jehovah began to select his anointed congregation,
those newly anointed disciples
became the targets of intense persecution.
Do you remember what happened in Acts chapter 4?
Let’s read this, Acts 4:1, it says:
“While the two were speaking to the people,
“the priests, the captain of the temple,
“and the Sadducees came up to them.
“These were annoyed because the apostles were teaching the people
“and were openly declaring the resurrection of Jesus from the dead.
“So they seized them and took them into custody
until the next day, for it was already evening.”
And then, if you turn over to chapter 5 and verse 17,
we remember the words, it says:
“But the high priest rose, and all those with him,
“who were of the sect of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy.
And they seized the apostles and put them in the public jail.”
Well, that’s the beginning.
That’s the very, very beginning of the Christian congregation
—intense persecution right from day one.
Well, roughly, about 25 years later,
in about the year 59 C.E.,
when the apostle Paul arrived in Rome,
by that time the prominent Jews in the city that Paul met with
had heard much about the early Christians.
Do you remember what they said?
Acts 28:22,
it says—
These prominent Jews said to Paul:
“But we think it proper to hear from you what your thoughts are,
“for truly as regards this sect,
we know that it is spoken against everywhere.”
Isn’t that interesting?
So they called it a “sect,”
and they said it was “spoken against everywhere.”
Well, what were some of the accusations
that were brought against the early Christians?
Well, writing of the Christians
in that first-century period in the Roman Empire,
historian K. S. Latourette said this:
“The accusations varied.
“Because they refused to participate in pagan ceremonies
“the Christians were dubbed atheists.
“Through their abstention from much of community life
“—the pagan festivals, the public amusements . . .
“—they were derided as haters of the human race.
“The fact that [the Memorial of Christ’s death]
“was celebrated only in the presence of believers
“fed the rumours that Christians regularly sacrificed an infant
and consumed its blood and flesh.”
In addition,
because the early Christians refused to practice emperor worship,
they were accused of being enemies of the State.
Well, does all that sound familiar?
We’ve heard things much like that recently, haven’t we?
Well, much time has passed since these events in the first century,
but the murderous hatred
that Satan the Devil has for all faithful servants of Jehovah God
is still very much active on this earth.
And we’re not surprised by that.
Do you remember what Revelation 12:17 says?
Let’s read it.
Revelation 12:17, it says:
“So the dragon became enraged at the woman
“and went off to wage war with the remaining ones of her offspring,
“who observe the commandments of God
and have the work of bearing witness concerning Jesus.”
Well, do you see the point?
You see, as a result of remaining faithful,
the remaining anointed ones who are on the earth
and all of those who associate with them
and who support them in their work are in a war
—a literal war
against Satan the Devil and the wicked spirit forces.
Now, recently, we’ve seen the Devil’s attack
on Jehovah’s people in the country of Russia.
Just yesterday the Interfax News Agency reported
that Metropolitan Hilarion,
head of the Russian Orthodox Synodal Department for External Church Relations,
said this:
“Jehovah’s Witnesses do not believe
“in Jesus Christ as the God and the Savior.
“They do not recognize the doctrine of the Trinity.
Therefore, they cannot be called Christians.”
He stated that he welcomed
the court ruling of the Russian Supreme Court
and suggested that the pernicious and harmful influence
of Jehovah’s Witnesses would now start to decline.
Wow!
Can you hear the hatred of the Devil in those comments?
But just as there have always been opposers
of Jehovah’s faithful servants,
there have also been individuals like Gamaliel
that Jehovah has raised up
who have come to the defense of Jehovah’s people.
Now, some of these people do not love Jehovah’s Witnesses.
But for their own purposes, they’re willing to defend God’s people.
Just take this example:
Andre Kuraev, a Protodeacon of the Russian Orthodox Church
and a professor of their spiritual academy in Moscow.
He’s a very, very outspoken critic of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
But after the decision of the Russian Supreme Court,
this is what he said:
“I argued that State agencies should not cooperate with this sect,
“and I do not retract my words.
“But to accuse them of extremism, that is not even funny.
“Such a decision is nothing other than idiotic,
a waste to accuse pacifists of extremism.”
Isn’t that something?
Yesterday, it was very amazing to me to see a news conference in Russia,
where German Chancellor Angela Merkel
was on a podium with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
There Chancellor Merkel said that she asked Mr. Putin
to utilize his influence to protect minority rights
as well as in the case of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Well, my eyes almost fell out of my head
as I saw Chancellor Merkel say that
in the presence of President Putin of Russia.
Well, there are many others who are willing
to come to the defense of Jehovah’s people.
Last week when I was in Kazakhstan,
a professor came to attend our talk for the entire country.
He sat right in the front row.
He’s written a book about Jehovah’s Witnesses
and is very eager always to defend us.
He wanted to speak to me, and so he came backstage.
We talked for about 15 or 20 minutes, and he asked me,
“What do you think is the source
of all of these bad reports about Jehovah’s Witnesses?”
And I said to the professor,
“Well, Professor,
“anyone who truly knows Jehovah’s Witnesses
“recognizes that all of these accusations
are completely ridiculous.”
Well, the professor looked at me
—and he’s a very distinguished white-haired man
of probably about 60 or 70 years of age—
and he says to me, “I know Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and I know that those charges are ridiculous.”
Isn’t it wonderful that we have people like this
who are willing to stand up for God’s people?
Well, in spite of the hatred that’s been spewed forth by the Devil,
it is amazing to see that persecution
never ever stops God’s faithful servants.
It has never stopped them in the past,
and it will not stop them in the future.
In fact, what did Jesus say here in Matthew chapter 5?
Matthew 5:11:
“Happy are you
“when people reproach you and persecute you
“and lyingly say every sort of wicked thing
“against you for my sake.
“Rejoice and be overjoyed,
“since your reward is great in the heavens,
for in that way they persecuted the prophets prior to you.”
Well, that’s the attitude of true Christians.
We know we’re doing the right thing
when we incur the hatred of these agents of the Devil.
Well, one thing that brought me joy last week
when I was in Russia and also in Kazakhstan
was that I heard so many reports from brothers and sisters
saying that inactive ones, former Bible students,
relatives of Witnesses are all contacting the brothers,
wanting to become involved again in the truth
because of what they see happening in Russia.
They know the end is close at hand.
So while we keep on praying
on behalf of our brothers who are being persecuted,
how vital it is, brothers, that we keep on the watch.
That we continue to watch what’s happening around the world
—being very alert to world events
and eagerly awaiting the time when our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ,
will appear and deliver us from this world
that is so firmly in the hands of the Devil.

以前不能阻止他们
未来也不能阻止
在马太福音第5章, 耶稣怎么说?
马太福音5:11说
人为我的缘故
侮辱你们, 迫害你们
用各样邪恶的话诬蔑你们
你们就有福了
要欢喜雀跃
因为你们在天上的奖赏是大的
在你们以前的先知
人也是这样迫害他们
这就是真基督徒该有的态度
只要我们继续做正确的事
魔鬼的手下就会非常生气
最近有件令我高兴的事
上个星期我在俄罗斯和哈萨克斯坦
听到当地的弟兄姊妹说
有很多停止传道的人
以前学习过圣经的人
和弟兄姊妹的亲戚
都主动联系耶和华见证人
因为他们看到俄罗斯所发生的事
决定再次学习真理
因为他们看出上帝的日子近了
所以我们要继续
为这些受迫害的弟兄姊妹祷告
更重要的是, 我们要不断守望
要留意最近世界上发生的事
不但要特别关注全球性的大事
也要热切等候
我们的君王和救主耶稣基督
他将要显现
并救我们脱离魔鬼掌控的世界
