title: “고생하며 무거운 짐을 진” 사람들에게 새 힘을 주다

en.text: Jesus’ words at Matthew 11:28
are very appropriate considering everything
we go through in this system of things:
“Come to me, all you who are toiling and loaded down,
and I will refresh you.”
Yes, conventions can be of refreshment to us,
giving us the boost we need.
But such refreshment is also available
when the world around us seems to be falling apart.
How does the organization help our brothers and sisters
in times of national crisis?
We met two Witness couples who personally experienced
two of the largest terrorist attacks in recent years.
Not a day goes by when we don’t think
about our son, Paulie.
There was horror and suffering,
things we don’t want to witness anymore.
September 11 was a very scary, terrifying day.
As for me,
when I really understood what was happening, I got scared.
I didn’t know what to do.
I didn’t know what to think.
I felt helpless.
When the second tower fell,
Paulie was on the 110th floor
and everybody was shouting, crying.
I was praying to Jehovah
because I was heartbroken.
We live on Voltaire Boulevard; it’s a broad avenue.
There is a concert hall called the Bataclan.
When the doors of the Bataclan are open,
we can hear everything that goes on inside.
That night, three men entered the Bataclan concert hall,
and they started shooting into the crowd.
We immediately grabbed our “go bag.”
And then we sat in front of the sofa,
and we begged Jehovah for his holy spirit
so we could face the situation.
It was around 10:00 p.m. when there was a news flash
that announced that there was an attack.
I was in shock when I heard the news,
and then I immediately thought about our brothers and sisters.
I quickly got in contact with the circuit overseer
in order to get some news about our brothers and sisters,
to know how they were doing.
Then,
very early the next morning,
we set up an emergency committee made up of several brothers
from the Service Department.
We decided to write a letter and make other arrangements
to assist the friends who, in one way or another,
were affected by this event.
In turn,
the circuit overseer would make an effort
to rapidly get in touch with the elders
who oversee the affected territory.
One of our challenges, on a personal level,
was whether we would even be able
to encourage our brothers and sisters
because we had never experienced such a terrible event.
We organized ourselves;
we paired up as elders and headed off to do shepherding.
We started calling midmorning on Tuesday.
We received a report back
from all the traveling overseers
by the end of Thursday.
And unfortunately,
we learned that 14 of our brothers and sisters
had lost their lives.
We knew that we needed to encourage the families;
we knew that we needed to shepherd them as soon as possible.
The elders immediately came.
We went over the book of Job,
and I just listened.
You know, I was just listening.
I’ve heard the same words before, but it was different now.
The things that were being said went straight to my heart.
A few days later, we were visited by two brothers from Bethel.
It was very touching that they came to see us
and that they were concerned about us.
It shows us that Jehovah was aware of how we felt that night.
Our brothers were there.
They were ready to help one another out.
Then there was so much empathy and love shown.
When we were ultimately granted
access to ground zero
and we started encountering
the first responders,
we let them know how much we appreciated their hard work
and that they had a skill set
that we didn’t have.
But yet our skill set
was trying to offer comfort to them.
We shared a scripture with them.
Immediately, we could tell that that was something
that caused emotion to rise up in them right away.
And they expressed
great appreciation for that.
It’s one of the beautiful things about the Scriptures
—that they’re calming, soothing, comforting.
And the Scriptures did not let down the workers
that were there at ground zero either.
The visit of the brothers from Bethel was really
a gift from Jehovah.
It showed his genuine interest in us.
It was really wonderful.
After the brothers visited us,
we felt so comforted,
so encouraged,
that we said to each other:
“We have to get back in the ministry
“and comfort people in the territory.
We have to console our brothers and sisters as well.”
We can only thank and glorify Jehovah,
who really is a God of love.
I kind of felt
Jehovah’s hand just reaching out to me,
which I needed.
But I cannot wait till the day that I’m totally refreshed.
Where I can see, I can actually see,
Paulie.
I can see him just coming back
into our lives,
and I want to embrace him so much.
After something like this, we are not the same.
But
with the help of the organization
—the brothers—
Jehovah is there for us.
So that—
That is refreshing.
And I thank Jehovah a lot
for what he wants to do for me
and also for the millions of people
that feel the same way.

cn.text: 耶稣在马太福音11:28所说的话
说明了我们在这个制度会经历的一切
经文说
你们所有辛苦劳碌
担子沉重的人啊
到我这里来吧
我要叫你们安舒
大会能够帮助我们重新得力
给我们所需的鼓励
就算这个世界正在瓦解
我们还是能获得安舒
在发生灾难时
我们的组织怎么帮助弟兄姊妹呢?
我们访问了两对夫妻
他们最近亲身经历了
两次最大的恐怖攻击
我们没有一天不想念儿子保利
那天真的太可怕, 太痛苦!
我们永远不想再看到那样的事
9月11日, 是令人非常惊恐的一天
当我意识到发生了什么事
真的是吓坏了
我惊慌失措, 不知如何是好
感觉非常无助
第二栋大楼倒塌的时候
保利在第110层
所有人都在尖叫、哭号
我不断向耶和华祷告
我的心都碎了
我们住在伏尔泰大道上
这是一条宽广的大道
这里有巴塔克兰剧院
剧院的门打开时
我们就可以听见里面的声音
那晚, 有三个男子闯进剧院
开始朝民众扫射
我们马上拿着急难包, 坐在沙发前
求耶和华给我们圣灵
帮助我们应付这样的情况
那天差不多晚上10点
即时新闻报道发生了恐怖攻击
听到报道, 我非常震惊
我马上就想到我们的弟兄姊妹
我随即联络分区监督
想要知道当地弟兄姊妹目前的情况
隔天一大早
我们几个传道部的弟兄们
成立了一个紧急委员会
我们决定写封信也作出安排
帮助所有受这次事件影响的弟兄姊妹
之后, 分区监督就迅速作出安排
联系当地的长老们
以个人的角度而言
我们都不知道
自己是否真的能带给这些弟兄姊妹鼓励
因为我们从来没有经历过
这么恐怖的事件
这真是一项挑战
弟兄们组织起来
长老们一组一组的去牧养探访
星期二早上10点左右
我们开始打电话给所有探访会众的监督
星期四, 我们收到他们回传的报告
不幸的是, 有14位弟兄姊妹丧生
我们需要去鼓励他们的家人
需要尽快去探访他们
长老们很快就来拜访我们
我们读了约伯记
但我就只是听, 专心地听
其实这些内容我以前都听过
但现在却不一样
他们说的话, 完全打动了我的心
几天后，有两位弟兄从伯特利来看我们
他们关心我们, 使我们很感动
这让我们明白
耶和华清楚知道我们当时的感受
弟兄们甘心乐意, 彼此帮助
大大表现出体恤和友爱的精神
当我们终于受批准进入灾难现场时
我们向那些在前线的救难人员表达感激
因为, 他们很努力善用自己的专业技能
投身救灾行动
我们也善用能力, 尽力安慰受灾的人
我们分享圣经
他们一看到经文
内心的情感就马上被触动
他们也表达对我们的感激
圣经真的很美好
可以使人内心平静、抚慰人心
也大大鼓舞了现场的救难人员
伯特利的弟兄来看我们
真的是耶和华的礼物
我们体会到耶和华的关心
真的很感动
弟兄的探访使我们大受安慰和鼓励
我们彼此说
我们应该要回到地区传道, 安慰别人
我们也需要安慰我们的弟兄姊妹
耶和华真的是充满爱心的上帝
配得我们的感激和赞美
我仿佛感受到
耶和华在我最需要的时候
对我伸出援手
但我也实在等不及
再见到保利的那一天
那一天, 他会真实的在我面前
保利他会再回到我们身边
我要一定要紧紧的抱住他
经历了这样的事件之后
一切都改变了
但借着组织、弟兄们的帮助
我们感受到耶和华在身边
使我们重新得力
我非常感激耶和华, 为我...
也为千百万和我有相同遭遇的人
所做的一切

title: 탈리타 알나시: ‘눈먼 사람들의 눈이 뜨일 것이다’

en.text: Let’s begin by visiting a family in Stockholm, Sweden.
The parents, Usama and Kristina, have two daughters,
Talita and Isabella.
When Talita was born,
the doctor found cataracts in both of her eyes.
A cataract is a clouding of the eye’s natural lens.
So the doctor had to operate
so that Talita wouldn’t lose her sight completely
—a terrifying situation for any parent.
Today, Talita is seven years old
and almost blind in one eye
but completely blind in the other.
Teaching a child about Jehovah
in this system of things is already a challenge
even without physical ailments involved.
But let’s find out how Talita’s parents rose to the challenge,
making sure that she received a proper spiritual education
despite her poor vision.
I look forward to not having poor sight anymore
and that I can play with a bear and a lion
and to sit on the back of a tiger.
Jehovah gives us a fantastic promise at Isaiah 35:5:
“The eyes of the blind will be opened.”
It’s been a challenge to get to where we are today.
We thank Jehovah for all the help he has given us.
As soon as Talita was able to leave the house after the operation,
we made sure to go to the meetings.
It helped us a lot to be able to throw our burden on Jehovah.
We prayed together;
we cried a lot together because it was so hard.
One of the challenges
is that we have to give Talita audio description constantly.
We have to tell her who is coming in and what is happening.
We get so many amazing materials on jw.org
and also through the congregation.
She really loves to read Learn From the Great Teacher.
It has questions which make her a part of the story.
She has a very good memory,
and therefore she remembers a lot of what she reads.
So when we are with friends, she often quizzes them.
I really like to sing the songs in my songbook.
Talita’s spiritual goal
is to learn more of our Kingdom songs.
We get so much help
from the beautiful music on the website
and also from the Caleb and Sophia videos.
She knows many of the stories from My Book of Bible Stories,
so she can answer in her own words.
We will ask a question like, Do you know this about David?
And if she knows the answer,
then we encourage her to answer at the meeting.
When I give an answer at the meetings,
Jehovah becomes happy
because he loves children.
She often asks the friends,
“Do you love Jehovah?”
So she feels very united with them.
One of the best moments where we saw
that Talita’s spirituality had grown
was when she came home from a sleepover
at her grandparents’ house.
My parents are not Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and her grandmother had said
that God doesn’t exist.
So when Talita came home, she said,
“And then when I was going to sleep, I prayed to Jehovah,
“‘Would you please help Grandmother
to realize that you do exist —that you are real?’”
We try to keep our wonderful hope alive,
so we often talk  about what we will do
in Paradise.
We really look forward to when Talita will be able to see again
and live in a paradise with all our friends.
It’s going to be wonderful!
I think that Jehovah looks forward to looking at me
when I play with a tiger.

她的一只眼睛全盲

她的记忆力很好
可以记得很多读过的内容
大家聚在一起的时候
她就常常拿这些问题考他们

塔莉塔立下目标
要学会唱更多王国诗歌
网站上美妙的音乐

她从《我的圣经故事书》学到很多
所以她可以用自己的话回答
我们会问她
你知道这个关于大卫的事吗?
如果她知道
我们会鼓励她在聚会时回答问题

因为他很爱小朋友

这使她觉得和大家的关系很亲密
看着塔莉塔在属灵方面进步

有一次, 塔莉塔到我父母家过夜

我的妈妈告诉塔莉塔

塔莉塔回家后就说
那天睡觉前, 我向耶和华祷告说
请让外婆知道你是存在的
你是真实的!
我们努力让美好的希望
在脑海中保持清晰
所以我们常常讨论
在乐园里想做什么
我们真的很期待塔莉塔能够恢复视力
和所有弟兄姐妹住在乐园里
那一定会很棒!
我觉得耶和华也很想看到
我和老虎一起玩

title: 「“오 여호와여 … 내가 당신을 신뢰합니다”」—제작 비하인드 스토리

en.text: Do you remember the beautiful dramas
we had at the regional convention last year?
One of them was about King Hezekiah.
We saw not only the threat Jehovah’s people faced
but also the protection Jehovah provided.
In producing the drama,
the Audio/Video Services Department used a lot of visual effects.
Let’s go behind the scenes and find out what the work entailed.
The goal of our visual effects team
is to take the work done during film production and expand it.
Our work was driven by the Bible account.
The audience needed to feel
the intimidating power of the Assyrian army
while not endangering our actors.
And the use of visual effects had the added benefit
of drastically saving donated funds.
But this meant creating hundreds of digital arrows, war machines,
cities, tents, soldiers,
and even an Assyrian palace.
In some cases, the foreground elements
had to be separated from the background
so digital components could be added.
This was a time-consuming process,
as many foreground elements had to be cut out frame by frame,
24 times for each second of video.
Our research team ensured that the world created
was as accurate as possible.
For example,
having period-correct materials for the temple
as well as accurate stone reliefs.
After filming was complete,
the research team noted some scenes in the treasury
were accidentally shot showing priests wearing sandals.
As this was inaccurate,
the issue was corrected by generating additional digital treasures
and placing them in the foreground.
As we didn’t have the luxury of 185,000 extras,
actors were dressed in ancient costumes and their pictures were taken.
We then used these pictures to create digital extras,
using crowd-simulating software
to place them in the scenes and drive their movements.
The angel shot proved to be one of the most challenging.
The original version didn’t have the dramatic feel needed for the scene.
So the entire sequence was recreated
to more accurately convey the immense power
that those present must have witnessed.
Finishing this project on schedule had many challenges.
After hearing about just a few of them,
one industry expert said
what we were attempting was impossible.
But like Hezekiah when hearing negative reports,
we stayed positive and relied on Jehovah.
With His help, the film was completed on time
and is now a wonderful tool to bring this Bible account to life.

cn.text: 还记得我们去年区域大会
看过的精彩戏剧吗?
其中一个是关于希西家王
我们不只看到
耶和华的子民面对的威胁
也看到上帝的保护
为了制作这部戏剧
影音服务部的弟兄们
使用了很多视觉效果
让我们到幕后
看看他们做了些什么
视觉特效小组的工作
是制作电影画面所需的特效
这部影片是以圣经时代为背景
我们希望能在安全的情况下拍摄
也想让观众感受到
亚述军队的强大威胁
视觉特效能大大节省开销
善用捐款
要达到这个目的
我们用特效制造大量的箭
攻城武器、城市、帐篷、士兵
甚至亚述王宫也是用特效做的
有时, 前景要和背景分开拍摄
才能加入特效
工作非常耗时
因为前景的很多物件
需要一个画格一个画格剪裁
每一秒的镜头要剪24次
研究小组帮助我们
尽可能还原当时的场景
例如, 圣殿的建材要和当时一致
也要正确地刻画石像上的浮雕
拍摄完成后
研究小组发现在宝库的镜头中
不小心拍到祭司穿着凉鞋
为了修正这个错误
我们在前景中
用特效制作了一些宝物
遮住他们的脚
我们不可能找来18万5千个临时演员
所以我们请演员穿上古装拍照
然后用这些照片来制作虚拟演员
再用人群模拟特效
把他们放在画面上, 加上动作
制作天使出现的画面非常困难
第一个设计的版本缺乏震撼效果
所以我们重新制作整个画面
尽力呈现天使的强大力量
为了按时完成影片
我们面对很多挑战
一位业界专家
听到我们想做的事之后
就说根本不可能做到
就像希西家一样
即使收到负面消息
我们继续保持积极, 信赖耶和华
在上帝的帮助下
我们按时完成了影片
让圣经的历史故事
精彩地活现眼前

title: 재프리 W. 잭슨: 여호와의 생각나게 하는 것을 소중히 여기십시오

en.text: The theme for our program this month is
“Treasure Jehovah’s Reminders.”
And it’s based on Psalm 19:7,
where we’re told:
“The reminder of Jehovah is trustworthy,
making the inexperienced one wise.”
In the original language, the word here translated as “reminder”
comes from a root word meaning “to go over again, to repeat.”
Reminders have always been an essential part of Jehovah’s teaching.
In ancient Israel, God’s people continually received
commandments, regulations, and reminders.
In fact, Jehovah tells us
that he sent his prophets “again and again”
to repeatedly remind his people of their responsibilities.
The apostle Peter felt the need to give reminders
even to those who were “well-established in the truth.”
Notice how he describes this
at 2 Peter 1:12, 13:
“For this reason I intend always
“to remind you of these things,
“although you know them and are well-established
“in the truth that is present in you.
“But I consider it right,
“as long as I am in this tabernacle,
to stir you with reminders.”
In verse 15, he goes on to give the reason
why he felt the need to give the brothers reminders.
He says:
“I will always do my utmost so that after my departure,
you may be able to recall these things for yourselves.”
So Peter was determined to help the brothers and sisters
in his day to remember, or recall,
the teachings they had already learned.
It shouldn’t come as a surprise, then,
if today a lot of our teaching involves reminders.
It follows the pattern set by Jehovah in ancient Israel
and with the first-century Christians.
But why do we need reminders?
Let’s consider three reasons.
First, let’s look at Psalm 103:2.
There it says:
“Let me praise Jehovah;
may I never forget all that he has done.”
Why, then, do we need reminders?
Simply put, because we forget.
If we had perfect memories,
we wouldn’t need so many reminders.
Even in everyday life, many of us use little notes
to remind ourselves of what we need to do.
And who of us hasn’t seen the need
for a list of reminders when going shopping,
only to realize when we returned
that we forgot to get one of the important items
we needed to purchase?
If reminders are important in everyday life,
how much more so in matters
that involve our relationship with Jehovah.
Let’s read Luke 10:39, 40.
Speaking of Martha, we are told:
“She also had a sister called Mary,
“who sat down at the feet of the Lord
“and kept listening to what he was saying.
“Martha, on the other hand,
was distracted with attending to many duties.”
What was Martha’s problem?
She was distracted.
So the second reason why we need reminders
is that, like Martha, at times we too become distracted.
Although we may already know a vital fact,
that fact might get put into the back of our mind,
figuratively speaking,
because other matters are demanding our attention.
Satan is the great Distracter.
He tries to turn our attention away from the true issues of our day.
People in general have become more and more distracted
by entertainment and other nonessential matters.
No wonder that Satan has succeeded in misleading so many.
They don’t even realize what has happened.
Reason number three is alluded to
at Matthew 24:45:
“Who really is the faithful and discreet slave
“whom his master appointed over his domestics,
to give them their food at the proper time?”
Notice that the spiritual food is given to us “at the proper time.”
Our circumstances in life are continually changing.
How often do we hear,
“That was just what I needed?”
We’ve all experienced that, haven’t we?
So, what are three of the reasons why we need reminders?
One, because we tend to forget things.
Two, we often become distracted.
Three, our changed circumstances
may require a reminder of something we already knew
but didn’t fully need at that time.
So that brings us to the next question:
What will help us to remember?
It’s interesting to note that Jehovah has used many ways
to remind his people of what they should do.
At Numbers 10:10, we’re told
that the various festivals were given as reminders,
especially the celebration of the Passover.
That means that every time the Israelites
prepared and celebrated one of these festivals,
they were reminded of important matters,
such as how Jehovah provides for his people
and how he has saved them in the past.
Something similar happens today
at the commemoration of the Lord’s Evening Meal.
Not only do we hear the reminders from God’s Word
but the act of passing the bread and wine
also serves as an action that reminds us
of what Jesus did in our behalf.
But what do we need to do in order for those reminders
to have a beneficial impact on our lives?
Notice what Psalm 119:99 says.
It tells us:
“I have more insight than all my teachers,
because I ponder over your reminders.”
Yes, we need to ponder over these reminders.
That means not just listening to or reading them,
but it involves thinking deeply about them—
meditating on their value.
Just to listen or read without meditating
is like looking through the lens of a movie camera
without pressing the record button.
We see things and hear things,
but nothing is recorded.
So we need to meditate, visualize,
and review these reminders.
This will help us to remember what we learn.
But, figuratively speaking, there is something else
that we can do to press the record button.
That means we don’t have to wait
for someone else to give us a reminder.
We can make our own reminder.
How can we do so?
The answer to that question
is highlighted in Jehovah’s instructions to Moses
as found at Exodus 17:14:
“Jehovah now said to Moses:
“‘Write this as a memorial
“‘[or the footnote says: “reminder”]
in the book and repeat it to Joshua.’”
What’s the point?
Write down new things we want to remember.
Some brothers use a notebook, or exercise book,
to write down a list of interesting points that they want to remember.
Then they look through the book from time to time
to remind themselves of those points.
Many of us do this with our notes from conventions and assemblies.
Of course, to do that successfully,
you need to remember where you put the notebook.
Additionally, we have to be careful
that we don’t write down every little fact.
Otherwise, we may become overwhelmed with all the information.
We can make these notes either on paper
or electronically using computers or electronic devices.
Whatever system we use, let’s make lists of things
that we want to remember.
Many brothers have found it good to have two separate lists.
One list could be subjects
—perhaps points that we want to use
in the ministry or in our own lives.
Another, scriptures
—explanations that clarify the meaning of certain verses.
With regard to notes on scriptures,
let’s ask a very important question:
Do you have a study Bible?
What is a study Bible?
Perhaps it’s a separate Bible
to the one you take in the ministry.
It’s a Bible for you to write in
so that you’re reminded of things that you’ve learned.
These are some of the things we can do with a study Bible:
Highlight or underline some words or verses.
That will make it easier to find them again.
But remember not to make too many highlights or marks;
otherwise, nothing will stand out.
Write a summary of points and scriptures you want to remember
on the blank pages in the front or the back of your Bible.
Write notes in the margin
—that’s what Gilead students often do.
Of course, you need the right type of pen or pencil
that won’t bleed through to the other side of the page.
What type of things could you write in the margin?
Perhaps new points that you learn while reading magazines
or attending meetings and assemblies.
If you learn a new point, ask yourself,
‘What verse is being explained?’
And then write a brief comment in the margin next to that verse.
Let’s take an example.
Perhaps you are reading the Sermon on the Mount
and you get to Matthew 7:24-27.
That’s the illustration
about the two men who built houses
—one on sand and the other on rock.
As you research this in Watchtower Library
or the Research Guide,
you come across the article
“Are You Building on Sand or on Rock?”
in the November 1, 2008, Watchtower.
What points could you write in the margin
to help you remember the explanation?
Well, perhaps you could write:
Sand equals build on the surface.
Rock equals dig down deep.
Digging equals doing and applying.
You might even put Luke 6:46-48 there.
Now, if you still have room and your writing is small,
you could add something like this:
Not hearers only, but doers.
Both houses in same location,
same tests, foundations different.
Now every time you read those verses,
you will be reminded of what they mean.
Perhaps like me,
you’ve had several study Bibles over the years.
I think back to the first one I used.
It was like this big green Bible.
Then, later that was replaced by another Bible
—this black covered Bible.
And then, further still,
we had another Bible —the Reference Bible.
And, of course, now for most of us,
we have the large-print Bible.
This does, however,
highlight a challenge we might experience.
It can be frustrating
when a new edition of the Bible comes out.
How do you transfer all your study notes
over to the new Bible?
Additionally, our beloved study Bible may wear out
or, worse still, be lost, stolen, burned, ruined, run over, blown away.
So that’s the advantage of using an electronic list;
it doesn’t matter what type of file you use.
It can be updated very easily, and you can even make copies
—not like the printed copy
that already has the old idea written in the margin.
Even now in English,
we have the books of Matthew, Mark, and Luke
in our electronic study Bible
on jw.org and WOL.
Later in the program, we have some exciting news
about how JW Library will help us in this regard.
But I’ll leave that for later.
Really, having a study Bible is not only helpful
but it also makes our personal study far more interesting.
How so?
Every time we read or study a publication,
we’ll find ourselves searching for new points
that we can write in our study Bible.
This way, we’ll be doing what the psalmist expressed
at Psalm 119:111:
‘We will take Jehovah’s reminders
‘as our permanent possession (or heritage),
for his reminders are the joy of our hearts!’

cn.text: 本月节目的主题是
“要珍视耶和华的提醒”
主题经文是诗篇19:7
经文说
经文中“提醒”一词的原文
来自一个字根
意思是“再一次、重复”
耶和华教导人时
提醒是很重要的一部分
在古代以色列
上帝的子民经常获得诫命、规定
也经常受到提醒
事实上
耶和华会“一次又一次”地通过先知
来提醒他的子民应负的责任
使徒彼得认为
即使是在“真理上也坚定不移”的人
还是要受到提醒
请留意他在彼得后书1:12, 13怎么说
15节彼得继续说明
为什么他觉得有需要提醒弟兄们
他说
彼得决心要提醒当时的弟兄姊妹
谨记自己所学到的真理
我们也需要受到提醒
正如耶和华提醒古代以色列
和第一世纪的基督徒
今天他也会以同样的方式提醒我们
但为什么我们需要提醒呢?
有三个原因
第一, 请翻开诗篇103:2
经文说
没错, 因为我们都会忘记事情
所以需要受到提醒
如果有完美的记忆
我们就不需要一直被提醒了
即使在日常生活里
我们也可能会写便条纸
来提醒自己该做什么
如果出门买东西前
没有先列好购物清单
我们可能就会忘记该买什么
如果我们在日常生活中
会提醒自己该做什么事
那么跟耶和华有关的事
就更需要受到提醒了
接着我们来看路加福音10:39, 40
经文提到马大说
马大的问题是什么呢?
她分心了
所以
我们需要提醒的第二个原因是
和马大一样,有时我们也会分心
虽然我们知道某件事很重要
但其他事情却吸引我们的注意
使我们把重要的事置之脑后
撒但是使人分心的高手
他想要分散我们的注意力
使我们不再留心真正重要的事
结果
很多人受娱乐及其他事影响而分了心
撒但的伎俩非常成功
他们甚至不知道自己受迷惑
第三个原因记载在马太福音24:45
请留意
属灵的食物会在“适当的时候”
供应给我们
我们的情况都会不断改变
所以当我们受到提醒时
都常常会想:“这就是我需要的!”
不是吗?
所以, 为什么我们需要提醒呢?
第一, 因为我们容易忘记事情
第二, 我们很容易分心
第三
当情况改变时
提醒能唤起我们的记忆
想起过去的哪些灵粮能帮助我们
可是
什么能帮助我们记得重要的事情呢?
耶和华在古代就通过很多方法
提醒他的子民应该怎么做
根据民数记10:10
耶和华通过节日作为提醒
特别是逾越节
每次以色列人准备和庆祝这些节日
都是为了要谨记重要的事情
例如耶和华怎样赐福给他们
以及过去上帝怎样拯救他们
今天
耶稣受难纪念聚会也有同样的目的
我们不只是听到来自上帝话语的提醒
传递饼和酒的仪式也使我们谨记
耶稣为我们作出的牺牲有多大
可是, 我们要怎样做
才能从这些提醒获益呢?
请留意诗篇119:99怎么说
没错, 我们需要沉思这些提醒
这代表我们不仅要听、要读
也要深入思考, 仔细沉思其中的价值
只有聆听跟阅读而没有沉思
就好像通过摄影机镜头捕捉画面
却没有按下录影键
虽然我们能看见能听见
却什么也没有录下来
所以, 我们要仔细沉思
让记载活现眼前
也要常常复习这些提醒
这样, 我们就能记住所学到的真理
不过, 就像刚刚在比喻中说的一样
要亲自按下录影键
我们不用总是要别人提醒
我们自己就能时常提醒自己
要怎么做呢?
我们来看出埃及记17:14
耶和华给摩西什么指示
重点是什么呢?
把想要记的事情写下来
有些弟兄姊妹会把一些有趣的要点
写在笔记本里
之后, 他们会经常翻阅笔记本
复习他们记下的要点
很多人参加大会时也会做笔记
当然, 你也不能忘了你把笔记本放在哪
另外
做笔记也不是要把所有细节都写下来
否则你就找不到重点了
我们可以把要点写在纸上
也可以记在电脑或电子产品里
不论我们是手写还是打字
都要整齐清楚地记下要点
很多弟兄姊妹发现
把要点分成两大类是个好方法
第一类是主题
里面包含了我们想在传道时
或是在生活上应用出来的要点
另一类是经文
也就是某段经文的含义或解释
既然谈到了跟经文有关的笔记
我想问你们一个重要的问题
你有一本专门研读用的圣经吗?
这本圣经, 和你在传道时用的不同
研读用的圣经可以写下很多个人笔记
你可以写的笔记有很多
举个例, 为了方便找出某节经文
你可以在经文或关键字词底下划线
但是要记得
不要标示太多经文或字词
不然就没办法突出要点了
你也可以在圣经前后的空白页
写下经文的摘要
此外
你还能在每一页的空白处做笔记
基列学校的学员们经常这么做
当然, 记得要准备合适的笔或铅笔
这样墨水才不会渗透到另一面
你可以在空白处写什么呢?
也许你可以记下你在杂志里
或聚会和大会中学到的新要点
要问问自己
“这个要点用的是哪节经文呢?”
然后在那节经文旁写下简短的评论
举个例, 假设你正在读登山宝训
这时, 你读到马太福音7:24-27
这个比喻谈到两个建造房子的人
一个人建在沙上, 另一个人建在磐石上
你从《守望台书库》
或《检索手册》搜寻资料
找到一篇出自2008年
11月1日的《守望台》文章
〈你在沙上还是在磐石上建造? 〉
你可以在空白处写下什么要点
好帮助记忆呢?
你可以写:
你甚至可以把
路加福音6:46-48写在旁边
如果你字写得够小, 还有空间
你还可以加上
这样, 当你每次读到这节经文
都能提醒自己经文的含义
你可能跟我一样
换过好几本研读用的圣经
我第一本用来研读的圣经是这本
大本的绿色圣经
后来换成这本, 黑色的圣经
再来就是《新世界译本详注本》
现在, 许多人用的则是这本
大字本圣经
不过, 纸本的圣经却有潜在的问题
如果发行了新版的圣经
你之前写的笔记该怎么办?
另外, 我们的圣经也可能会破损
不小心弄丢、被偷、被烧毁
被破坏、被车辗过、甚至被强风吹走
但是, 用电子产品做笔记
就不用担心这些了
不管用什么档案格式
我们都可以快速地更新
甚至能复制笔记
这样就不会像纸本圣经一样
上面还留着以往对经文的理解
此外, 在JW.ORG网站
和守望台线上书库里
英语《新世界译本》精读本
已经收录了马太福音
马可福音和路加福音
稍后的节目会告诉你们
JW Library app
会怎样加入这项新功能
你一定会同意
拥有一本研读专用的圣经
对个人研读更有帮助
也能增添更多乐趣
每次研读出版物时
我们都可以找找看有没有新的要点
然后写在圣经里
这样, 我们就像诗篇119:111说的
你提醒世人的圣谕
我视为万世长存的产业
因为你的话叫我的心欢跃

title: 윌리엄 맬렌폰트: 마지막 날의 도덕성 (디모데 후서 3:13)

en.text: You know, there are many people today
who say that we’re not living in the time of the end.
They say: “The world is just the same as it’s always been.
There are no real changes that have taken place.”
But, of course, we know they’re deceiving themselves.
Never before have so many people around the globe
openly practiced and flaunted
sexual immorality,
not just among themselves
but they’re seeing that it’s brought into the homes
by means of Internet, television, and other means.
Never before has man had the power
to decimate entire populations
by dropping just one bomb
or by means of chemical warfare.
Never before has there been
such widespread lack of love
and of natural affection
that results in the death of children.
It’s interesting that some calculate
that over one billion abortions
have taken place since 1980.
That’s really something.
That’s just about the population of China
—if you can imagine.
And that is something that’s accepted;
it’s commonplace in our day.
So some people think, ‘Well, things haven’t changed.’
But is that true?
No, quite to the contrary.
And something else that we’re fully aware of
is that people around the earth
are making a garbage dump out of the planet that we live on
—polluting the air, the seas,
the land.
And yet, some still insist that things haven’t changed.
Now, why is it?
Why do people have that attitude?
Well, part of it lies in what the Scriptures tell us,
what Paul wrote at 2 Corinthians 4:3, 4.
And there it says that Satan ‘blinds the minds of the unbelievers.’
And the “unbelievers” are not just atheists.
The “unbelievers” are found throughout the churches of Christendom.
They don’t believe —really believe—
what the Bible has to say about prophecy,
about morality,
or that God is really going to clean up this planet
and that it’s going to be a wonderful new world
of peace and happiness.
And so to help people understand these things,
we go out and we preach.
We tell them about what Matthew 24 says
and Mark 13 and Luke 21 and 2 Timothy 3
—that we’re living in the time of the end.
But there is something we have to remember
if we get a little bit discouraged
when people don’t respond as we feel they should
to all of the evidence that we see and we appreciate.
The Bible indicates very clearly
that many people would not see the sign;
they would not accept what the Bible has to say.
And what’s most interesting about that
is that the people who ignore
and who deny the sign that we’re living in the time of the end
are part of the sign themselves
—what they do and the way they think.
Turn to Second Peter
—2 Peter chapter 3.
And we’ll read verses 3 and 4 and the first line in verse 5
—2 Peter 3:3, 4 and the first line in verse 5.
Peter wrote: “First of all know this, that in the last days,”
so this is something Peter is saying would happen during our time,
“ridiculers will come with their ridicule,
“proceeding according to their own desires
“and saying: ‘Where is this promised presence of his?
“‘Why, from the day our forefathers fell asleep in death,
“‘all things are continuing exactly
as they were from creation’s beginning.’”
And then the reason for it is given in the next line:
“For they deliberately ignore this fact.”
Well, here the fact was that they ignored the Flood of Noah’s day.
The fact for us today is that they ignore what the Bible clearly says
or what Jesus said would be the sign of the last days.
So they don’t realize it, but they’re part of the fulfillment.
What contributes to an unbelieving attitude?
Well, one of the things is what we could call gradualism.
The Watchtower of January 15, 2014, paragraph 30,
or page 30, paragraph 11 stated the following:
“It seems that the more familiar a situation is,
“the less people are inclined to pay attention to it.
“A steady decline in the morality
“of society in general may seem less shocking
“than a sudden, unexpected change
in the behavior of a close acquaintance.”
And then it says: “Nevertheless,
this gradual decay of morality is dangerous.”
And isn’t it true that most of us were raised
in an environment that was not so good?
There were immoral things taking place around us, wars, crime.
And so people get to the point where they accept it as normal.
And as it escalates,
it really doesn’t impress on them that ‘No!
‘Times have changed.
They’re becoming far worse than ever before.’
Gradual decay of morality is dangerous.
It makes me think of an illustration
about how to boil a frog.
If you heat up a pot
and you have the water boiling and drop a frog into it,
what’s going to happen?
He’s out of there; he’s not going to stay.
That frog isn’t stupid.
He hits the water, and it’s terribly hot, and out he jumps.
But if you fill the pot with cool water,
drop the frog in,
and then gradually (little by little) you heat it up
until it gets to the boiling point,
he’s cooked!
And that’s what’s happening in the world today.
The gradualism is not perceived by people in the world,
but they’re being cooked.
It’s getting hot.
And so we know that wicked men
are going to continue to increase
—impostors, scoffing at the truth.
World conditions are escalating; they’re getting worse constantly.
But they’re going to have to deal with the Creator and his judgment.
And there are three Psalms I’d like to just mention briefly
that I find very interesting that tie in nicely
with the wickedness of the world and what Jehovah will do.
Psalm 10:4:
“In his haughtiness, the wicked man makes no investigation;
“all his thoughts are:
‘There is no God.’”
Psalm 12:8:
“The wicked walk around unrestrained
because the sons of men promote depravity.”
That could’ve been this morning’s headlines
in The New York Times.
And the last, Psalm 92:7:
“When the wicked sprout like weeds
“and all the wrongdoers flourish,
it is that they may be annihilated forever.”
And to that we say:
“Amen. So be it!”

cn.text: 今天很多人觉得
我们并不是生活在最后的日子
他们说
这个世界还是和以前一样
根本没有什么真正的改变
不过, 我们知道他们是在自欺
以前, 从没有那么多人
明目张胆地做性不道德的事
他们甚至通过互联网
电视或其他方式
将这些恶事带进人的家里
而且人类以前没有能力
通过投掷炸弹或使用化学武器
让无数的人失去生命
从来没有像现在这样
人类普遍缺乏爱心和亲情
造成许多无辜儿童丧生
根据一些报道
他们估计自1980年以来
有超过十亿件堕胎的案例
这实在令人难以置信
这个数字几乎要等于中国的人口了
但由于堕胎非常普遍
人们早就习以为常了
所以有些人认为
“一切都没有改变啊”
真的是这样吗?
不, 事实完全相反
另外, 我们都知道
世界各地的人把我们居住的地球
当作一个大垃圾场
污染了空气、海洋和土地
即使如此
有些人还是认为世界没有改变
为什么人会有这种态度呢?
圣经告诉我们其中一个原因
保罗在哥林多后书4:3, 4说
这些不信的人被[撒但]弄瞎了心眼
这些“不信的人”
不单指无神论者
也指所有假基督教的信徒
他们不相信圣经的预言和道德标准
也不相信上帝会洁净地球
使它成为一个和平又快乐的新世界
为了帮助人明白圣经, 我们会出去传道
我们告诉人马太福音24章
马可福音13章、路加福音21章
和提摩太后书3章的信息
告诉他们现在是最后的日子
不过, 不要忘记一件事
我们可能因人的反应不如预期而灰心
可能觉得他们应该看见
我们所看见的证据
圣经清楚地指出
许多人看不出这些征象
他们也不想接受圣经里所说的话
有意思的是
他们这种不理不睬的态度
正好就是在最后的日子里
我们会看见的情况
让我们翻开彼得后书3章
我们会读出3, 4节和第5节的前半段
彼得后书3:3, 4
彼得说
“首先, 你们知道, 在最后的日子...”
看来彼得的话会在我们的日子应验
会有好讥诮的人来讥诮你们
顺着私欲而行, 说
他应许要临在, 哪里会实现呢?
其实, 自从我们列祖长眠以来
一切始终跟创世的开头一模一样
接着的话就说明了
为什么他们会这么想
“有一件事他们故意忽视了”
他们故意忽视了挪亚时代的大洪水
而今天
人们也故意忽视了圣经的明确的信息
以及耶稣谈到的末世征象
所以, 他们不知道
自己其实正应验了圣经的预言
不信的态度会导致什么后果呢?
其中一项可以用渐进主义来解释
《守望台》2014年1月15日刊30页11段说
看来, 有些事人们看多了
就觉得平平无奇
社会道德是逐渐变坏的
所以大众不会感到惊讶
如果一下子改变就不同了
正如密友突然一反常态
我们会感到吃惊一样
段落接着说
不过, 道德渐渐恶化
不表示情况不严重, 可以掉以轻心
我们不就是在这么恶劣的环境下成长的吗?
对于身边常有的战争、罪行、不道德的事
人们早已见怪不怪了
所以, 即使世界情况越来越糟糕
他们也不会认为
唉!  时代不同了
现在的世界比以前还要糟糕
道德渐渐恶化, 我们绝不能掉以轻心
这让我想到温水煮青蛙的比喻
如果你将一锅水加热
然后把青蛙丢进滚烫的热水里
会发生什么事呢?
它肯定不会乖乖地待在锅子里
青蛙一点也不傻
当它一碰到滚烫的热水
就会马上跳出来
但是, 你将青蛙放进装了冷水的锅子里
然后慢慢加热, 一直加热到水沸腾
青蛙就被煮熟了!
今天的世界就是这样
人们好像待在逐渐加温的热锅里
他们不觉得这个世界有什么改变
我们很清楚
邪恶的人只会越来越多
他们是冒名的骗子
他们嘲笑圣经的标准
世界的情形每况愈下
而且已经无药可救了
他们需要向造物主交账
也绝对逃不过他的审判
我想和大家分享三节诗篇的经文
刚好与这邪恶的世界
以及耶和华即将采取的行动息息相关
恶人傲慢自高, 不寻求上帝
他的一切想法不过是:“没有上帝”
“邪恶的人到处横行, 因为世人崇尚恶事”
这句话都可以当作
《纽约时报》的头版标题了
最后的是
邪恶的人如青草滋长
作恶的人如花木繁茂
到头来却必永远灭绝
相信你我都会说
“阿们! 确实如此!”

바빌론으로 끌고 간 유대인들 중 한 사람이었습니다
외경심을 불러일으키는 환상에 관해 알려 줍니다
에스겔은 장엄한 네 생물 즉 그룹들을 봅니다

즉 사람과 사자와 수소와 독수리의 얼굴을 가지고 있습니다
이 얼굴들은 여호와의 네 가지 속성을 상징합니다

en.text: An introduction to the book of Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was the son of a priest
and served as a prophet of Jehovah.
He lived in Judah until 617 B.C.E.
when Judean King Jehoiachin
was forced to surrender to Babylon.
Ezekiel was among the Jewish exiles
whom King Nebuchadnezzar took
to Babylon at that time.
In 613 B.C.E.,
Jehovah commissioned Ezekiel
to prophesy to the exiled Jews
living in Babylonian captivity.
Ezekiel faithfully fulfilled his assignment
for at least 22 years.
He completed his book in about 591 B.C.E.
Ezekiel’s prophetic work overlapped
that of Obadiah and Jeremiah, in Judah,
and of Daniel, in Babylon.
The sanctification of Jehovah’s name
is highlighted throughout the book of Ezekiel.
The expression “Sovereign Lord Jehovah”
appears 217 times.
The book of Ezekiel has 48 chapters.
In chapters 1 to 3,
we read about the awe-inspiring visions
Ezekiel sees by the river Chebar.
During an intense windstorm,
Ezekiel beholds four magnificent living creatures,
or cherubs.
Each one has four faces
—that of a man,
a lion,
a bull,
and an eagle.
These faces reflect attributes
that Jehovah possesses.
Ezekiel is awed by a vision
of the heavenly part of Jehovah’s organization,
which is represented by a celestial chariot
directed by God’s spirit.
Chapters 4 to 24
contain Jehovah’s judgment against Jerusalem
and her rebellious, idolatrous people.
Ezekiel often communicated Jehovah’s prophecies
by means of symbolic actions.
For example,
Jehovah had Ezekiel engrave the city of Jerusalem on a brick
and stage a mock siege against it.
As a sign of the coming siege,
he lay on his side for 430 days.
In chapters 25 to 32,
Jehovah turns his attention
to the surrounding nations.
They receive an adverse judgment
because of their opposition to his people.
Through Ezekiel,
Jehovah foretells destruction for the city of Tyre and her king.
Did you know?
The prophecy against Tyre was fulfilled in two stages.
Years after Nebuchadnezzar devastated the mainland city,
Alexander the Great completed the destruction
by building a causeway to the island city of Tyre,
using the rubble remaining from Nebuchadnezzar’s conquest.
Chapters 33 to 48 contain a message of hope
and of the restoration of pure worship.
In chapters 40 to 48,
we read of Jehovah giving Ezekiel a vision of a temple.
This vision of the temple underscores
Jehovah’s high standards for true worship.
As you study this prophetic book,
take note of Jehovah’s awe-inspiring qualities,
Ezekiel’s unswerving obedience to His instructions,
and Jehovah’s promise
to unite all mankind in pure worship
by means of the Kingdom.

cn.text: 以西结是祭司的儿子
他受到耶和华委任成为先知
他原本住在犹大国
后来，公元前617年
犹大王约雅斤被迫向巴比伦投降
以西结跟流亡的犹太人一起
被尼布甲尼撒掳去巴比伦
公元前613年
耶和华委派以西结向被掳的犹太人说预言
以西结忠心地执行任务至少22年
他在公元前591年完成以西结书
跟以西结同时期的先知有
犹大国的俄巴底亚和耶利米
还有巴比伦的但以理
上帝在以西结书多次强调
他必使自己的名彰显为圣
“至高主宰耶和华”这个词组出现了217次
以西结书共有48章
1至3章记载
以西结在迦巴鲁的河边
看见一个壮观的异象
在狂风中
以西结看见了4个使人凛然生畏的活物
他们是基路伯天使
每个天使都有人
狮子
公牛
还有鹰的脸
这些脸分别代表耶和华的特质
以西结还看见一辆天上的战车
战车受神圣力量指挥
代表上帝组织的天上部分
这令他惊歎不已
在4到24章
耶和华对耶路撒冷城
和叛逆、崇拜假神的居民宣告判决
以西结常以具有象征意义的动作
来传达上帝的预言
例如，耶和华吩咐以西结拿一块砖
在上面刻一座城代表耶路撒冷
模拟城被围困的情况
然后要侧卧430天
在25章到32章
耶和华对耶路撒冷四周的国族
宣告不利的判决
因为他们欺压上帝的子民
耶和华通过以西结预告
泰尔城必被摧毁，泰尔王必被消灭
你知道吗？
关于泰尔的预言，应验了两次
第一次是尼布甲尼撒摧毁位于大陆的城
第二次是亚历山大大帝
用旧城废墟中的石头
筑了一条堤道通往泰尔的岛城
彻底摧毁了泰尔
以西结书33章到48章提到未来的希望
以及正确崇拜复兴的信息
在40章到48章
耶和华让以西结看见一个圣殿的异象
耶和华借着这个异象
强调他对正确宗教有崇高的标准
你读以西结书的时候，请留意
耶和华令人崇敬的特质
以西结怎样忠心地执行上帝托付的任务
还有耶和华会通过他的王国
让所有人团结一致地崇拜他

en.text: Our text, Ecclesiastes 7:8,
says in its entirety:
‘Better is the end of a matter
than the beginning.’
But then it adds: ‘Better to be patient
than to show a haughty spirit.’
Well, if we’re patient,
sometimes a very grim-looking circumstance
becomes much better in the end
than we could have ever imagined at the beginning.
Well, do we have a Bible example
where this principle actually plays out that way?
First Kings chapter 20, please
—1 Kings 20.
King Ben-hadad of Syria and 32 other kings
are fighting against Israel.
So the beginning is not looking very good for Israel.
In fact, if you look at verse 7, 1 Kings 20:7,
it says that “the king of Israel called all the elders of the land and said:
“‘Take note, please, and see that this man [Ben-hadad]
“‘is bent on bringing calamity,
“‘for he demanded my wives, my sons, my silver, and my gold,
and I did not refuse him.’”
Well, pretty bleak-looking circumstances.
But then after another interchange between the two kings,
it’s obvious that Ben-hadad was haughty.
In verse 10, you can almost see him swaggering when he says:
“So may the gods do to me and add to it
“if there is enough dust in Samaria
to give each of the people following me a handful!”
Well, again, the beginning looks grim.
But then Ahab, in response,
he basically uses the principle of our text for today.
In verse 11: “The king of Israel answered:
“‘Tell him, “The one who puts on his armor [you see, in the beginning]
“‘“should not boast about himself
like one who takes it off [in the end].”’”
Well, the end of the matter proved much better for Israel.
Verse 21 says that the king of Israel
“inflicted a great defeat on the Syrians.”
Better was the end of the matter than its beginning.
Well, do we have another example where it states it very similarly?
Yes, Judges —Judges 15.
This is one of the accounts about Samson,
and Samson wreaked havoc.
He wreaked destruction upon the Philistines.
So much so that they are now coming
to Judah in all-out revenge.
Well, the men of Judah realized this,
and they’re worried about being slaughtered.
So they caught up with Samson
and handed him over to the Philistines.
the situation appears grim for Samson at first.
Thirteen says in the last sentence:
“They bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the crag.”
Well, the haughty Philistines were thrilled
to have him bound and just handed over to them.
In fact, in verse 14 it says: “When he came to Lehi,
the Philistines shouted triumphantly at meeting him.”
They couldn’t wait to get their hands on him.
Well, how did the situation for Samson
prove better in the end than at the beginning?
Well, the verse says that “Jehovah’s spirit empowered him”
and the fetters just “melted off his hands.”
And then in 15 and 16,
Samson finds the jawbone of a donkey
and he struck down a thousand Philistines.
For Samson, the end of the matter was better than the beginning.
Well, how about Job?
Job 42
—Job 42.
We’re all familiar with how Job’s tests
in the beginning were so trialsome
—one tragic circumstance after another—
and then he was humiliated with verbal abuse
from his false comforters.
It can’t get much worse than that.
But because of his endurance and patience,
how did it turn out in the end?
Well, verse 12 sounds very much like our text for today.
Job 42:12, it says:
“So Jehovah blessed the last part of Job’s life
more than the beginning.”
Well, how has this scripture,
Ecclesiastes 7:8, been treated in our literature?
How has it been applied?
A couple of examples:
A 1998 Watchtower applied it to parents counseling their children.
Now, for some during their teen years,
they go through a phase in life
and their attitude is very frustrating to the parent.
In fact, during the teen years, sometimes a parent will think,
‘There’s no hope for this child.’
But if they’re patient, what often results?
Oh, we’ve read countless experiences in our magazines
and heard them on JW Broadcasting of a wayward teen
who is now an adult faithfully serving Jehovah.
Better was the end of the matter than its beginning.
A 1994 Watchtower applied this to one who feels
that he’s being overlooked for privileges.
Well, instead of manifesting a prideful spirit,
how much better to wait patiently.
In time, when that privilege comes our way,
the end of the matter is much better than at first.
Some years ago,
an older brother who had been serving as an elder
moved to a new congregation.
Well, the elders in the new congregation did not reappoint him right away.
A couple of years went by, and he was appointed
as a ministerial servant, not an elder.
Well, a couple more years went by,
and the former elder is now doing a slow burn inside.
And it manifested itself in his comments,
even being critical of some of the decisions of the elders.
Well, please find Philippians 2 with me.
One of the elders on that body spoke to the brother,
and he explained that with his current disturbed attitude,
it was very unlikely the body of elders would welcome him aboard.
He explained that his attitude was rooted in his view of position.
And the elder used Philippians 2:5-9.
Now, verse 5 counsels that we’re to have the “mental attitude” of Jesus.
Well, what was Jesus’ attitude about position?
Verse 6 —it’s talking about position—
it says that Jesus did not try to seize Jehovah’s position.
And verse 7, just the opposite of going up the ladder,
Jesus was willing to go down the ladder
to assume a lower position —become a human.
And then verse 8 says:
“More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself
and became obedient to the point of death,
yes, death on a torture stake.”
And then the bottom line, in verse 9:
“For this very reason.”
For what reason?
Because of Jesus’ humble attitude
in accepting a lesser assignment
to do Jehovah’s further will.
And what was the result?
The verse continues:
“For this very reason, God exalted him to a superior position
and . . . gave him [a] name . . . above every other name.”
Well, the elder asked the brother if he thought
that he was manifesting the “mental attitude” of Jesus,
and that brother said, “No.”
He said, “I’m too caught up in the position of being an elder.”
So the elder asked him, “Well, what are you going to do?”
The older brother said,
“I need to reach out for the office of overseer all over again
and stop sulking about my position.”
Well, what was the result?
For years he had not been reappointed as an elder.
Six months after that conversation,
the body of elders unanimously recommended
he be appointed as an elder.
Why?
Ecclesiastes 7:8:
“Better to be patient than . . . haughty in spirit.”
Well, that older brother, he died some years later,
happily serving as an elder.
Better was the end of the matter than its beginning.
Another application of the verse:
In the beginning, in the rebellion in Eden,
it looked very bleak for the human family.
But Jehovah had an arrangement to rectify matters,
Jesus cooperated, and what does that result in
for you and me if we remain faithful?
No question about it
—our reward at the end of this system
will be better than at the first!

cn.text: 今天的经文传道书7:8说
事情的结果胜过事情的开端
接着说
耐心的人胜过心高气傲之辈
要是我们耐心等待
虽然事情的开始看起来并不乐观
但结果却可能出乎我们意料
那么，圣经有哪些例子说明这种情况呢？
请看列王纪上20章
叙利亚王便哈达和32个王联合攻打以色列
一开始的情势看来对以色列很不利
我们一起看看第七节的经文
列王纪上20：7
经文说
以色列王召了境内的所有长老来，说
请你们想想
这个人［便哈达］存心谋害我
他打发人到我这里来
要我把妻儿和金银交出来
我都没有拒绝他
看来情况真的很糟糕
后来，这两个王再次交涉
便哈达也显出心高气傲的态度
在第10节，便哈达傲慢地说
如果撒马利亚的尘土
足够跟随我的人每人抓一把的话
愿神明处置我，加倍惩罚我！
看来情况真的很糟糕
但亚哈怎样反应呢?
他用了今天经文的原则
列王纪上20：11节说
以色列王回答说
你们去告诉他说
才束上腰带的［如同事情的开始］
不可像除下腰带的
〔如同事情的结果〕那样自夸
最终的结果
果然对以色列有利
21节说以色列的王
大大击杀叙利亚人
的确，事情的结果胜过事情的开端
圣经还有其他例子吗？
有的
在士师记15章提到参孙的例子
参孙造成了非利士人极大的损失
使得非利士人气冲冲地来到犹大
当犹大人知道这件事
他们担心非利士人会残杀他们
于是他们捉拿参孙
要把他交给非利士人
在15章13节
刚开始的情势看起来对参孙不利
13节后半段说
于是他们用两条新绳索捆绑参孙
把他从岩洞带上去
这些骄傲的非利士人看到参孙被捆绑
任由他们处置，一定非常高兴
14节说
参孙来到利希
非利士人迎着他欢呼喊叫
非利士人迫不及待要教训参孙
对参孙来说
事情的结果真的胜过事情的开端吗？
接着的经文说
耶和华的灵作用在参孙身上
捆绑他双手的绳索都熔掉了
在15和16节说
参孙找到一块驴腮骨
并用驴腮骨击杀了一千个非利士人
对参孙来说
事情的结果真的胜过事情的开端
那么约伯呢？
我们看看约伯记42章
我们都知道约伯面对艰难的考验
开始时他的灾祸一个接着一个地来
后来他又被假朋友羞辱责骂
这应该是最糟糕的情况了吧！
由于约伯表现坚忍和耐心
他最后的结果是怎样的呢？
12节记载的结果
跟今天经文的论点一致
约伯记42:12说
耶和华后来赐福给约伯
比先前更多
关于传道书7：8
我们过去的刊物怎样解释这节经文呢？
请想想以下的例子
1998年的《守望台》文章
将这个经文用在父母教导儿女方面
有些儿女在青春期的时候
他们的态度令父母非常头痛
有些父母甚至想
这个孩子没救了！
不过，要是父母耐心地对待孩子
结果会如何呢？
在我们的杂志里
或是JW电视网的报道
我们都看过许多类似的经历
一个原本叛逆的青少年
长大后忠心地崇拜上帝
没错，事情的结果的确胜过事情的开端
一篇1994 年的《守望台》文章
则将经文用在觉得自己没有受到重用的人身上
与其显出骄傲的态度
不如耐心等待
当你受到重用时
事情的结果就会胜过事情的开端
几年前
一个年长的长老搬到新的会众
但是新会众的长老团没有马上推荐他做长老
过了几年，这个弟兄获得任命
但不是做长老，而是助理仆人
再过几年
这个曾经是长老的弟兄开始心生不满
他的评论也显出这种态度
甚至开始批评长老所做的决定
我们先翻圣经到腓立比书2章
长老团中的一个成员跟这个弟兄说
如果他一直抱着不满的态度
其他的长老就更难以推荐他做长老
长老也指出
弟兄之所以有这样的态度
问题是在于
他过度重视自己在会众的职位
长老给弟兄看腓立比书2章5－9节
第5节说
我们要怀有耶稣基督的“精神”
那耶稣对地位有什么看法呢？
请看第6节
说到地位
经文说
耶稣从没有想过
要攫取跟上帝同等的地位
第7节也说
耶稣没想过要提高自己的地位
相反，他愿意降为卑
成为人类
然后第8节说
不但这样，他见自己成了人的样式
就谦卑自抑，服从至死
甚至死在苦刑柱上
重点来了
请看第9节
所以什么？
耶稣为了执行上帝的旨意
谦卑地接受卑微的任务
结果怎么样呢？
经文继续说
所以上帝把他提升到更高的地位
惠然赐给他凌驾其他一切名字的名字
长老请弟兄想想
他有没有表现出跟耶稣一样的态度
弟兄回答说
我没有，我太想要当长老了
长老又问他
那你接下来会怎么做呢？
这位年长的弟兄说
我要克服不满的态度
重新用正确的观点追求监督的职分
结果呢？
这个弟兄这么多年来
都没有被任命成为会众长老
但他跟长老谈过之后六个月
长老团就一致推荐他成为长老
为什么呢？
传道书7:8说
“耐心的人胜过心高气傲之辈”
后来这位弟兄在去世之前
都一直快乐地以长老的身份服务
的确，事情的结果胜过事情的开端
经文也适用于另一种情况
最初人类在伊甸园反叛上帝
人类的前途看似毫无希望
可是耶和华却做出安排扭转事态
耶稣也全力支持
这对保持忠贞的我们来说
结果又是什么呢？
毫无疑问
我们最终所得到的奖赏
一定比最初的情况更好

title: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 예수께서 율법을 성취하셨다 (마태 5:43)

en.text: In your ministry, have you ever met someone
who strongly believes that we are still
under the Ten Commandments?
Now, that can happen at times because many people
—especially in the southern parts of this country—
feel very strongly about the Ten Commandments.
There are even legal battles going on
as to whether monuments displaying the Ten Commandments
can be displayed on government property.
And, of course, many people feel that the Ten Commandments
are basically what was used for the Constitution
and for the laws of many countries.
So at one point, perhaps, a person might say to us,
‘Do you believe that we are still under the Ten Commandments?’
Perhaps you may diplomatically answer,
‘Well, I believe we are under the principles of the Ten Commandments
and the law of love —the law of the Christ.’
But a person may push the point and say,
‘But do you believe the Ten Commandments are binding today?’
Well, when we give them an explanation from the Scriptures,
perhaps they may feel disappointed and maybe they realize
that there’s a verse in the Bible that they feel supports their belief.
So let’s take our Bibles
and turn to Matthew chapter five, the Sermon on the Mount,
from which our text is taken this morning.
And perhaps they may point
to verses 17 and 18.
Now that reads:
“Do not think I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets.
“I came, not to destroy, but to fulfill.
“Truly I say to you that sooner would heaven and earth pass away
“than for one stroke of a letter to pass away from the Law
until all things take place.”
Now, this person, in presenting their explanation,
may show that they believe this expression “fulfilled”
means “established permanently.”
And even some Bible commentaries
say that this involves total commitment.
Well, how would you answer the person at that stage?
How can we help them?
Perhaps you might take them through a series of scriptures,
such as Romans 10:4 where it says:
“Christ is the end of the Law.”
You might read Galatians 4:4,5 where it says,
‘those under the law were released.’
Or Ephesians 2:15 where it speaks of the Law being “abolished.”
But if you’ve done that,
perhaps you’ve had the same experience that I have
—that a person may agree with those scriptures but say:
‘That’s not referring to the Ten Commandments.
‘That’s referring to all the other laws in the Mosaic Law arrangement.
But the Ten Commandments remain forever.’
Well, how can you help someone to reason on that matter?
Well, let’s look back again at Matthew chapter 5,
and we notice there in verses 17 and 18,
it mentions that Jesus came “not to destroy, but to fulfill.”
And we could ask the person how they understand the word “fulfill”
—what they feel that means.
And perhaps they might say, ‘Established permanently.’
Well, then we could point out
that Jesus then continues to talk about various aspects of the Law.
If we look at verse 21, what do we notice?
“You heard that it was said to those of ancient times:
‘You must not murder.’”
So, yes, this is one of the Ten Commandments.
Interestingly, the study Bible has a note on this verse that says
this phrase, “You heard that is was said:
“. . . can refer both to things stated in the inspired Hebrew Scriptures
and to teachings of Jewish tradition.”
Now, we’ll see this as we go on.
If we go to verse 23,
what does it talk about here?
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
and there you remember your brother has something against you.”
This is not part of the Ten Commandments, is it?
It’s talking about the arrangements for sacrifices.
Then, if we look at verse 27:
“You heard that it was said: ‘You must not commit adultery.’”
Well, again we have the Ten Commandments.
But if we look at verse 31, Jesus here says:
“Moreover, it was said: ‘Whoever divorces his wife,
let him give her a certificate of divorce.’”
That’s not one of the Ten Commandments, is it?
Reading on further in verse 33, it says:
“Again you heard that it was said to those of ancient times:
‘You must not swear without performing.’”
Again, not one of the Ten Commandments.
Verse 38: “You heard that it was said:
‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’”
Again, not one of the Ten Commandments.
And then we come to the scripture we’ve been considering this morning
in verse 43:
“You heard that it was said:
‘You must love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’”
Now, when we consider this
—we look at the study Bible notes on this verse—
it makes this comment about “hate your enemy.”
It says: “The Mosaic Law contained no such command.
“Some Jewish rabbis believed that the command to love their neighbor
implied that they should hate their enemy.”
So this wasn’t really part of the Law that Moses gave.
But what do we see from this?
Well, if a person argues very strongly that the word “fulfilled,”
when Jesus is talking about the Law,
applies to the Ten Commandments only
—we look down here— Jesus when he’s talking about the Law,
doesn’t just talk about the Ten Commandments, does he?
He talks about all these things, including even the oral tradition.
So if a person were to believe that Jesus’ words, when saying “fulfilled,”
refer to absolutely establishing something permanently,
would also feel —or have to feel—
that he’s referring to this law of “eye for eye, tooth for tooth”
when, in fact, he showed something better than that, didn’t he?
And the same too with the scripture for today’s text.
So, what do we see here?
Well, we can’t make that comment about Jesus’ words.
So, what does it mean when it says,
‘to fulfill and not to destroy’?
Perhaps a simple illustration would help us.
If someone signs a contract as a builder
to build a home for someone else,
what does it mean to destroy the contract?
Well, perhaps it means ripping it up, burning it, getting rid of it
—certainly not building the house.
But on the other hand, what does it mean
to fulfill the contract to build the house?
Well, it means that the person builds the house.
But once the house is built,
then the contract is completed, or fulfilled.
This person isn’t under obligation to continue over and over again
to keep building the same house.
So perhaps an illustration such as that
may help someone of humble heart
to see that when Jesus said
he “came, not to destroy, but to fulfill,”
that he wasn’t there to eradicate the Law.
In Galatians 4, it mentions he was ‘born under Law.’
So he had to fulfill, or complete, or do what the Law stated.
But, of course, the other scriptures help us when they tell us
that the Law was completed,
that the Christ was the end to the Law.
Now, perhaps a person might still find this
a little difficult to comprehend.
One final scripture we could share with them
is in the book of Romans,
Romans 7:6, 7.
Romans 7:6, 7, verse 6 says:
“But now we have been released from the Law,
“because we have died to that which restrained us,
“in order that we might be slaves in a new sense by the spirit
and not in the old sense by the written code.”
Now, if we pause there, perhaps the person might jump in and say:
‘Ah, yes. That’s the Law that doesn’t include the Ten Commandments.
Those are all the other laws, but the Ten Commandments remain forever.’
Well, then we ask them, ‘Just let’s read on, verse 7,
what does it say?’
“What, then, are we to say?
“Is the Law sin?
“Certainly not!
“Really, I would not have come to know sin
“had it not been for the Law.
For example, . . .”
Now, what example is Paul going to use?
It says: “For example, I would not have known covetousness
if the Law had not said: ‘You must not covet.’”
So, obviously, the apostle Paul and our Lord Jesus Christ
did not separate the Law into two parts
—the Ten Commandments and the other laws.
So we can see clearly from here that we have a good answer
to give persons when they adamantly state
that the Ten Commandments are still binding.
Hopefully, we can go on then to help them to see
that Jesus was teaching us the principles behind the laws
and that “the law of the Christ” involves loving Jehovah
and loving our neighbors,
and then following what direction Jehovah has given us.
So you may think this is quite a complicated subject
to discuss early in the morning.
But next time when someone does ask you,
“Do you believe the Ten Commandments are binding?”
hopefully, you’ll remember these comments.

cn.text: 传道时
你有没有碰过一些人觉得
现在依旧需要遵守十诫?
直到今天
的确有很多人
特别是住在美国南部的人
觉得一定要守十诫
甚至有些官司
都跟是否该在国家纪念碑上
刻上十诫有关
当然, 也有很多人认为
十诫基本上
是许多国家的宪法和法律的基础
所以有人可能会问
“你觉得我们现在还要守十诫吗?”
也许你会婉转地回答
我们会遵守十诫的原则
也要遵守爱的律法
就是基督的律法
可是对方可能不死心
继续问
那你觉得我们现在
还是要受十诫约束吗?
这时, 如果我们用圣经跟他解释
他可能无法接受
因为他可能觉得有一节经文
能够支持他的想法
让我们打开圣经
翻到马太福音第5章
耶稣的登山宝训
这正好就是今天的当日经文
对方也许会指出
经文说
不要以为我来
是要废除律法和先知的话
我来不是要废除, 而是要实现
我实在告诉你们
就算天地都消逝了
律法的一点一画也绝不会消逝
倒要全部实现
所以, 对方可能会说
根据他们的理解
“实现”就是指“永远确立”
有些圣经评注甚至说
这个词包含了全面保证的意思
这时, 我们可以怎样回答呢?
我们可以怎么帮助他们呢?
可能你已经想到几节经文来回答他了
例如, 罗马书10:4
“基督是律法的终点”
加拉太书4:4, 5说
律法之下的人会被“救赎出来”
或者, 以弗所书2:15说
律法被“废除”了
如果你用这几节经文来解释的话
你可能会遇到和我一样的情况
就是对方虽然同意这些经文, 却回答
这些经文说的不是十诫
而是指摩西律法安排下的其他所有诫命
但十诫是永远存在的
这时, 你可以怎样帮助对方推理呢?
让我们再看一次
经文说
耶稣来“不是要废除, 而是要实现”
我们可以问对方
他觉得这里的“实现”是什么意思
对方可能会回答是
“永远确立”的意思
那么, 我们可以指出
耶稣接下来谈到律法的不同层面
第21节怎么说呢?
耶稣说
你们听见有话对古人说:“不可杀人”
对, 没错, 这是十诫的一条
有趣的是
英语《新世界译本》精读本的注解说
“你们听见有话说...”
这句话代表
接着的话是来自《希伯来语经卷》
或是犹太人的传统道理
我们继续看下去就知道了
第23节说什么呢?
所以, 你把礼物带到坛来的时候
要是在那里想起有弟兄对你不满
这不是十诫的一部分
而是指献祭的安排, 对吗?
我们再看27节
你们听见有话说:“不可通奸”
在这里, 耶稣再次提到十诫
但31节耶稣说
又有话说
“谁跟妻子离婚, 就该给她离婚的文书”
这又不是十诫的一部分了, 对吗?
第33节又说
你们又听见有话对古人说
“不可违背誓言”
这也不是十诫
你们听见有话说
“以眼还眼, 以牙还牙”
这也不是十诫
然后我们再来看看第43节
也就是今天的当日经文
你们听见有话说
“要爱你的朋友, 恨你的仇敌”
精读本对“恨你的仇敌”这句话
下了一条注解
摩西律法里并没有这条诫命
可是有些犹太拉比认为
“爱你的朋友”这条诫命
暗示着要恨你的仇敌
所以, “恨你的仇敌”这句话
其实也不是出自摩西律法
这么一来, 我们可以看出什么呢?
如果有人坚持说
耶稣要“实现”的律法是单指十诫
但刚刚所看的经文中
当耶稣谈到律法时
他其实不只提到十诫而已
还提到其他的律法, 甚至是口传律法
所以, 如果一个人坚持
耶稣所说的“实现”律法的意思
就是要“永远确立”律法
这就代表这个人觉得
或者说他一定认为
耶稣也要我们守
“以眼还眼, 以牙还牙”这条律法了
但事实上
耶稣其实带来更优越的原则
包括今天当日经文的诫命
所以, 重点是什么呢?
耶稣的话绝不是刚刚所说的那样
那么, 当耶稣说
“不是要废除, 而是要实现”
到底是什么意思呢?
请想想一个简单的比喻
当建筑承包商
为业主建造一栋房屋前
会签署合约
那怎么样算是废除合约呢?
如果承包商把合同撕掉、烧掉、丢掉
也就是连房子都没盖
这就叫废除合约
不过, 另一方面
怎样才算是履行合约呢?
就是承包商按照合约完成建筑工程
一旦房子盖好后, 合约也就结束了
也可以说是实现了
之后, 承包商就没有义务
继续再盖一样的房子
这个比喻
也许会帮助谦卑的人看出
当耶稣说
他来“不是要废除, 而是要实现”
就是指他不是要来废除律法
加拉太书4:4谈到
耶稣“生在律法之下”
因此, 耶稣来就是要实现
完成或履行律法
当然, 其他经文也让我们看出
律法已经完成, 基督就是律法的终点
如果有人还是无法理解
我们可以再给他看
第6节说
可是
现在我们脱离了律法的约束
因为我们在律法的事上死了
不再被紧紧绑住
这样
我们就不再以旧方式本着法典做奴隶
而是以新方式本着灵做奴隶
读到这里, 有些人可能就会说
你看, 这里说的律法不包括十诫
这里说的是其他的律法
所以十诫是永远存在的
这时, 我们可以请对方继续看第7节
那么, 我们该说什么呢?
律法是罪吗?
当然不是!
其实, 如果没有律法
我根本就不认识罪, 例如...
这里, 保罗要用的例子是什么呢?
经文继续说
例如, 要不是律法说“不可贪婪”
我根本就不知道贪婪是什么
显然
使徒保罗和主耶稣基督都没有认为
十诫和其他律法是分开的
所以, 我们现在知道
如果有人坚持十诫依然具有约束力
我们可以尽力帮助对方看出
其实耶稣要教导我们的
是律法背后的原则
以及“基督的律法”
这包括要爱耶和华, 爱别人
也要听从上帝的指引
一早就讨论这个复杂的话题
可能有点吃不消
不过, 若下次真的有人问你
“你觉得我们现在还要守十诫吗?”
相信你就知道该怎样回答了

en.text: Welcome to another edition of JW Broadcasting!
Have you ever felt discouraged
due to circumstances beyond your control?
We’ll discuss how we can still have joy despite our limitations.
And we’ll see examples, both Biblical and modern day,
that will encourage us to keep giving Jehovah our best.
Jonah had faced several reasons
to become discouraged and give up.
How did Jehovah help him carry on with courage and faith?
And what lessons from his experience
can we apply to problems we face today?
Can we change our personality for the better?
We can with Jehovah’s spirit and diligent effort.
This brother describes
how far his personality and lifestyle
took him away from Jehovah.
He explains how he regained a clean conscience
and freeness of speech.
Jehovah can turn tragic events caused by man
into open doors of activity for His loyal Witnesses.
In this report from Greece,
we’ll learn how our brothers are bringing spiritual comfort
to refugees.
You’re watching the June 2017 edition
of JW Broadcasting!
There are many exciting things happening
in Jehovah’s organization.
Why, month after month, we read articles,
watch videos, and hear personal experiences
about our brothers and sisters who are doing more for Jehovah.
They are serving where the need is greater or reaching out
for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
They are working on construction, renovation,
maintenance of Kingdom Halls, or other theocratic projects.
No doubt, many of you watching this program
are excitedly looking forward
to expanding your ministry in one of these areas.
We encourage you to do so.
You can be assured that you will receive much fulfillment
and many blessings from Jehovah.
On the other hand,
there are others who are watching this program
who may feel discouraged because their circumstances
may seem to limit their being as involved as they would like.
What are some of these circumstances?
These may include our age, our health,
our economic situation, or our physical limitations.
For some of us, perhaps our upbringing
or past errors we have made in our life
may cause us to feel that we are limited
as to what we can do for Jehovah.
As we know well, focusing on our limitations
can affect our joy, causing discouragement.
What can we do?
There are many examples in the Scriptures of men and women
who had circumstances beyond their control
that seemed to limit how much they could do for Jehovah.
Others had to deal with the effects of their upbringing and family life
or with serious errors they made.
Did they allow themselves to be limited
by their circumstances or their past?
How did Jehovah feel about them?
How does Jehovah feel about us?
That is what we are going to discuss in this month’s broadcast,
which has the theme
“Are You Defined by Your Circumstances?”
Let’s start by looking at some
who could have let their circumstances limit them.
Consider first the example of Joseph in the book of Genesis.
Now, Joseph faced injustice at its worst.
His situation was especially hurtful

I wasn’t a spiritual person yet.
All the magazines and books
went back into the box and back under my bunk.
I’d only been there five minutes,
and a guard came in and said,
“Are you a Jehovah’s Witness?”
I couldn’t believe it.
And I told him, “I studied with, been studying with Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
And he said: “Oh, good. Follow me.”
And I followed him, and he took me
and introduced me to a brother
who had been coming up there regularly
to study the Bible with inmates there.
And I realized
at that moment that once again
Jehovah had not forgotten me.
That brother faithfully came up there
for the next two years every Friday night.
He thought that it’d be a good idea to have
a Theocratic Ministry School, so he got it approved.
He would do the number one talk,
and the other brother that would come with him
would do the highlights, and then the three of us inmates
would do the other parts.
I was giving a talk every week.
And he started making
tape recordings of the meetings.
I’d listen to them over and over,
until the next week.
I knew that if I was going to return to Jehovah,
I had to make some adjustments.
With Jehovah’s help —I leaned on him more,
relied on his strength more—
it was then that I really felt that I could do this.
The beard became a goatee, and then it just became a mustache.
No drugs, no alcohol, no smoking,
and I cleaned up my language.
Then I finally got released,
got a job as an electrician,
and was able to get my own place
and started going to meetings.
I was listening to the Watchtower, and different ones were commenting.
‘Oh, that’s his wife’
—one of the brothers who came up to visit me.
I kept looking to see, so I could finally put a face
to the voices that I’d been listening to.
I let Jehovah mold me
into something good.
There are many blessings since dedicating my life to Jehovah.
I’ve been an elder for ten years now.
One of my sons came into the truth.
I met my wonderful wife.
She’s helped me
to grow spiritually and to love Jehovah even more.
One thing I kept praying for and he’s blessed me with is to forgive myself
—to have a clean conscience and freeness of speech.
And he’s done that.
Jim shares the same joy as so many others
who return to Jehovah.
The feelings common in such real-life experiences
are what we’ll see depicted in our music video.
It’s called I Can Get Back Up.
It is especially touching for those of us who have stumbled
but need encouragement to move ahead with Jehovah’s help.
This loneliness I feel inside is hard to bear.
Jehovah, I can see where I went wrong.
Feeling so downhearted, I need strength to carry on.
I’m yearning to be back where I belong.
I remember things you taught me —things I still recall—
The precious truths found in your Holy Word.
That even if I stumble, even if I fall, I can get back up.
I know the ones who care for me, Who showed their love before,
Those who love Jehovah from the heart.
Your word is like a lamp that lights the way that leads me back.
The road to life is where I want to be.
Ev’rywhere I go, ev’rything I see, reminds me of the truth:
The end is drawing near.
So Jehovah, Father, please hear my prayer tonight
And help me now, I’m in my time of need.
You know that when I stumble so many times,
I can get back up.
I know Jehovah understands; sometimes I need a helping hand.
He knows that I am weak and sees what others cannot see.
He’s looking for the best in me.
So I’m going to the hall tonight to feel the love I lost,
Back to where I know I belong.
And even if I stumble, even if I fall, I will get back up.
I can get back up.
What a beautiful reminder that if we stumble,
we can get back up!
Having seen the examples throughout the program,
can you confidently answer the question of our theme,
“Are You Defined by Your Circumstances?”
What do you think?
Remember, not the way man sees is the way God sees
—Jehovah sees what the heart is.
May we work hard to see ourselves as Jehovah does
and be determined to never give up.
May we never forget that it is the privilege of bearing Jehovah’s name,
having a relationship with him,
and our love for Jehovah that defines us.
Jehovah is happy if we give the best that we can.
So may we do our part
by not limiting ourselves due to our circumstances,
but always look for ways to give our best to Jehovah.
You beautiful older ones,
even those with severe health problems,
can do much to help in the great work that’s taking place today.
Now, you may wonder what can you do.
You can pray for your brothers and sisters.
We need your prayers.
Pray for the Governing Body.
Pray for those who are taking the lead.
Pray for the elders in your congregations.
Pray for those who are going through difficult times.
Do such prayers help the work of the organization?
Absolutely!
James 5:16 tells us
that ‘a righteous person’s supplication
has a powerful effect.’
No matter who we are and whatever our situation in life,
may we find joy in giving what we can for Jehovah.
And may each one of us rejoice at the privilege we have
of being part of what Jehovah is accomplishing
in these last days.
Of course, we share that privilege with our worldwide brotherhood
—a part of which we enjoy seeing each month.
To conclude this program,
we visit with our brothers and sisters in Togo.
Located in western Africa,
Togo enjoys a very pleasant climate year-round.
The southern coast contains extensive lagoons with sandy beaches,
while farther north are rolling forested hills
and yellow tinges of savanna land.
Togo may be one of the smaller countries in Africa.
Yet, it is sending up a great shout of praise to Jehovah.
In the town of Kpalimé,
there are 577 of our brothers and sisters,
56 of whom are pioneers.
Kpalimé is located on a scenic woodland plateau.
Steep hillsides can sometimes make service a challenge
but not a deterrent.
Our faithful brothers and sisters not only meet this challenge
but are very zealous in carrying out their ministry.
They diligently search out all persons,
no matter where they are.
And many honesthearted ones are listening
to the good news from God’s Word.
The first congregation in Kpalimé was formed in 1961.
Now there are seven in this small town alone!
The Kingdom Halls are very well cared for by the brothers.
This is the newest Kingdom Hall,
Kpalimé-Nogo.
It was just dedicated in December 2016.
And here is their Assembly Hall, constructed in 2008.
All 577 send you their love and greetings.
And we, in turn, send them our love
and pray for Jehovah’s strength and blessing
to be upon each and every one of them.
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

en.text: And so we’re talking about technology today.
And as has been mentioned
by our commenters,
Jehovah’s organization is certainly making
good, positive use of technology
to get the good news preached.
Every week, we receive letters of appreciation
from those who have been watching JWB —JW Broadcasting.
They just love to watch the programs.
And this morning, I’d like to talk a little bit more
about our website —jw.org.
Did you know that many people
are first recognizing the sound of the truth
through jw.org
even before they have had personal contact with a Jehovah’s Witness?
It’s true.
I’d like to share some experiences with you this morning.
The first one has to do with Cadja.
She was dissatisfied with her church,
and so she decided to investigate various religions.
Now in the old days,
people would just go from one church to the other,
but modern-day people go on the website;
and they want to know what various churches teach.
And as she was investigating the teaching of various religions,
she noticed that there were a lot of negative comments
about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Did that stop her?
No, because she was a fair-minded person.
So she went online and found our website,
and she found
the “Frequently Asked Questions” section of the website,
and she loved it.
Every question was answered with the Bible,
and that’s what she wanted in a religion.
Well, she noticed on our website
that there was an invitation to attend our meetings.
And so she talked a schoolmate into going with her to the Kingdom Hall.
She was a schoolgirl.
Now, she loved what she heard at the Kingdom Hall,
and she was so warmly welcomed.
But wouldn’t you know it?
Her parents were opposed.
And soon after she made that one foray to the Kingdom Hall,
they moved to an isolated area
where there were none of Jehovah’s Witnesses
and Cadja was cut off from any association
with the Witnesses for one year.
But not to be deterred,
she studied all of our publications on the website.
And she kept up-to-date with the truth.
In September of 2014,
she was again able to make contact with the Witnesses
and she accepted a Bible study.
And in July 2015, she was baptized.
So she got the truth.
Her initial contact with the truth was on jw.org.
Now, speaking of being cut off from the Witnesses,
that’s Kenji’s problem.
He’s a fifteen-year-old boy in Japan.
He would love to attend meetings at the Kingdom Hall,
but his father forbids him from attending.
But here’s what Kenji has to say.
He says: “I watch JW Broadcasting
“and jw.org every day.
“I see brothers doing their best, and that encourages me.
“One day I will become a great brother.
Please wait.”
Well, speaking of lifelines,
we were at a circuit assembly in St. Louis, Missouri, over the weekend,
and a sister told me
that she had been very gravely ill for a whole year
—so ill that she couldn’t attend the meetings,
and she wasn’t able to tie in to the meetings.
But she said her lifeline
was JW Broadcasting and jw.org.
So these technological innovations
are really accomplishing a good work.
Let’s talk about Alenka.
She’s a physics teacher.
And one day, she was at the home of an acquaintance
and there was a strange man there —a man that she didn’t know.
But she was really impressed with this man.
He was so friendly —so warm and kind and balanced too.
And after he left, she mentioned that to the householder.
And the householder said: “It’s all true what you say.
“But there’s one problem.
He’s one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
Another negative comment about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
What did she do?
She went home and she went online
and she found our website.
For five months,
she carefully studied all of the material on our website.
And at the end of five months, she decided to go to the Kingdom Hall.
She made a very interesting comment, something I hadn’t really thought about,
she said, “Thanks to jw.org,
“nothing in the hall seemed strange to me
—the program, the people— all of it was familiar.”
After she attended meetings for a month,
she asked for a Bible study.
So she was careful, but she got the truth,
and her first encounter after that man was our website.
Dregan was a Franciscan monk in Slovenia.
He’d been in the order for a number of years,
but there was something missing.
There was a void in his life.
He realized that his religion
was not satisfying his spiritual need.
So he went online
and he joined a chat room with a bunch of evangelicals.
Well, as you can imagine,
eventually some negative comments were made about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Did that stop Dregan?
No, another fair-minded person.
He thought,
‘It’s not fair to criticize Jehovah’s Witnesses when,’
thankfully, ‘none of Jehovah’s Witnesses are in that chat room.’
So he went online and found our website.
And he was delighted with the quality of the website.
Now, he was a monk,
and in the Franciscan Order, that particular Franciscan Order,
the monks were only allowed to leave the monastery on Mondays.
So one day, he found the address of the branch office in Slovenia,
and on a Monday morning, he went to the branch and got a tour.
The brothers received him very warmly.
He was very impressed with what he saw,
and he came away with a novel idea.
He came away with the thought
that he should be reading the Bible every day.
And so he went back to the monastery, went online,
and started reading the Bible online every day.
His fellow monks observed this,
and they thought this was hilarious.
What’s a Catholic monk doing reading the Bible?
But he didn’t allow their opposition to deter him.
He kept reading the Bible and then kept consulting jw.org,
and he realized, on consulting the website,
that the Memorial that year was on a Monday.
So he was going to be able to attend, and he did.
And that did it —that meeting.
He made the decision to leave the Catholic Church
and to leave the monastery.
So now, there were a lot of challenges to overcome.
It wasn’t so easy, but he persevered.
And in June of 2014, he left the church;
he left the monastery;
and then in the month of October of that same year,
he was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Since, he has served as an auxiliary pioneer.
A sister in Finland is studying with a Bulgarian woman,
and one day the woman asked her to drive her to the hospital.
“Oh, are you ill?”
Well, the woman hemmed and hawed, and finally she admitted
she wanted to have an abortion.
Well, the sister said: “I can’t.
My conscience won’t allow me to drive you to the hospital for that.”
And then she shared some scriptures with the woman
on God’s view of life.
But then she had an idea.
At the end of every study
—and here is something that you might want to implement—
at the end of every study,
she shows the woman something from the website.
And she remembered something.
Song number 88 —“Children Are a Trust From God”—
had come out in the Bulgarian language
as sung by a children’s chorus.
So she played song 88 to the woman in the Bulgarian language.
The woman’s heart was touched, and she canceled the abortion.
She said: “I’m going to have the baby.
“If it’s a boy, his name will be Angel.
“If it’s a girl, Angelina
because God protected the child.”
And I think the children’s chorus helped a little bit too.
Now, we have for years
been encouraging pioneers and publishers who conduct Bible studies
to direct interest to the organization.
And we printed a brochure.
And then we printed a simplified brochure with many pictures.
And these brochures have had some success.
But I think what has really opened the eyes of the brothers
and our Bible students to the organization
has been JW Broadcasting and jw.org.
And you see now as you go from one congregation to another
or one circuit to another
that the brothers are really talking about the organization
as they never did before.
So it’s obvious that technology
has contributed to the understanding of the brothers
and to the spread of the good news.
Now here’s a warning:
Technology has a place; it has a big place.
But there is a danger.
Have you ever heard the term “phubbing”?
“Phubbing.”
P-H-U-B-B-I-N-G.
It’s a combination of phone and snubbing,
and it refers to the act of ignoring real people
while consulting an electronic device.
So picture a man and a woman in a restaurant,
and each one is online.
Each one is consulting a different website or answering mail,
and they’re not talking to each other.
It’s a real problem according to a study by Baylor University.
So, what we want to do is stay connected,
not just to the Internet,
but to stay connected to real people, to those around us.
Brother John Barr of the Governing Body used to say
that if we shut out those around us
while consulting an electronic device,
we’re really not focusing on the sounds of life.
We are missing the sounds of life.
And we’re also missing out on opportunities
to strengthen our bond with others.

cn.text: 今天我们会谈谈现代的科技
我们得到不少称赞
因为耶和华的组织善用现代科技
将好消息传出去
每个星期
都会有JW电视网的观众
寄感谢信来
因为他们真的很喜欢这些节目
但今天早上
我想谈谈跟 jw.org网站有关的经历
其实, 有很多人是在 jw.org网站上
接触到好消息的
当时还没有耶和华见证人拜访他们
很特别吧!
我们来听听几个经历吧
第一个是一位叫做卡迪娅的女子
她觉得无法从教会中得到属灵的满足
所以决定去研究其他宗教
以前, 人会亲自去不同的教会看看
但现在的人
都会先上网查查各宗教的道理
卡迪娅也一样
但她上网查的时候
就发现很多关于耶和华见证人的负面评论
她有因此停止吗?
没有, 她很客观
后来她找到耶和华见证人的官方网站
并看了“常见的问题”这个页面
她非常喜欢
所有答案都有圣经根据
这就是她在寻找的
她也在网站上看到我们邀请人参加聚会
她就说服一个同学陪她去
当时她还只是个中小学生
但她非常喜欢聚会的节目
也觉得那边的人很友善
令人遗憾的是
她的父母很反对
她第一次参加聚会后没多久
他们全家就搬到一个偏远
没有任何耶和华见证人的地方
有长达一年的时间
卡迪娅无法跟我们联系
但她没有放弃
她继续研读网站上的资料
也不断留意组织对真理的最新理解
她终于和耶和华见证人联系上
也开始讨论圣经
并在2015年7月献身受浸
卡迪娅能认识真理
就是从 jw.org网站开始的
现在, 让我们再听听另一个
被迫跟耶和华见证人中断联系的经历
健次是个15岁的日本男孩
他很喜欢参加聚会
不过他的爸爸不让他去
但健次想要怎么做呢?
他说
我每天都会看JW电视网
和 jw.org网站
看到那些弟兄做的那么好
我大受鼓励
有朝一日
我一定也要成为一个好弟兄
谈到维持属灵生命
周末的时候
我们参加在密苏里州
圣路易斯举行的大会
一个姊妹告诉我
她整整一年都在生病
病情严重到她无法参加任何聚会
很难跟会众保持联系
当时维持她的属灵生命的
就是JW电视网和 jw.org网站
这些科技发展
确实为我们带来许多好处
我们再来看看阿伦卡的经历
她是个物理老师
有一天, 她在一个朋友家里作客
有个陌生人也在那里
一个她不认识的男人
但她对这个男人印象深刻
因为这名男子态度很好
亲切温和却毫不做作
这个男人离开后
阿伦卡跟朋友说
她觉得这个人不错
她的朋友说
你说的很对
但问题是, 他是一个耶和华见证人
又是另一个对耶和华见证人的批评
阿伦卡怎么做呢?
她回家后上网, 找到了我们的网站
有五个月的时间
她仔细阅读我们在网站上的所有资料
之后, 她决定去王国聚会所
她后来说的话很有意思
我之前没想过这点
她说
幸好有 jw.org
聚会的所有一切
都让我觉得好熟悉
不论是节目还是人, 全都似曾相识
她参加聚会一个月之后
就要求学习圣经
阿伦卡做事谨慎
而她通过一名男子和我们的网站
找到真理
德雷甘是一位在斯洛文尼亚
方济各会的修道士
他做修道士许多年
但总觉得心里空虚, 人生有欠缺
他发觉
自己的宗教无法填补那份空虚感
所以他上网, 加入一个聊天室
跟很多支持福音派的人聊天
不出所料
有人开始批评耶和华见证人
德雷甘有因此产生偏见吗?
没有, 他是个客观的人
他心想
这样批评耶和华见证人实在不公平
幸好没有耶和华见证人来这里聊天
后来他上网找到我们的网站
他觉得网站设计得非常好
开头提过
他是个方济各会的修道士
他所属的修道院
只准他们在每周一离开修道院
有一天
他查询到斯洛文尼亚的分部地址
在接着的星期一早上就去分部参观
弟兄们都很欢迎他
他在分部看到的都令他印象深刻
他心中萌生一个想法
决定要每天阅读圣经
他回到修道院就每天上网读圣经
其他修道士看到他这样做
就觉得很可笑
一个天主教修道士何必读圣经?
但是他没有因为人的嘲笑而停止
他继续阅读圣经
继续浏览 jw.org网站
后来他发现那年的耶稣受难纪念聚会
正好在星期一晚上
所以他也真的去参加了
那个聚会改变了一切
他决定离开天主教教会
离开修道院
当然, 他需要克服不少困难
也遇上许多挑战
但他忍耐到底
后来
他终于在2014年6月
正式脱离天主教教会
离开修道院
同一年的10月
他受浸成为耶和华见证人
然后他开始做辅助先驱
另一个在芬兰的姊妹
跟一个保加利亚妇人讨论圣经
有一天, 妇人请姊妹带她去医院
姊妹问:“你哪里不舒服?”
妇人支支吾吾的
终于说她想堕胎
姊妹说:“不行!”
我的良心不准我为这个原因带你去医院
接着给妇人看经文
说明上帝对生命的看法
这时, 姊妹灵机一动
其实, 你以后也可以试试
这个姊妹的做法
她们每次圣经课程结束时
姊妹都会给妇人看网站上的资料
所以, 姊妹就想到诗歌第88首
“儿女是上帝所托付的”
这首歌刚好有保加利亚语
儿童合唱版
她就放给那位妇人听
这首歌触动妇人心弦
她就打消堕胎的念头
妇人说
我决定把孩子生下来
如果是男孩, 就叫他安杰尔
如果是女孩, 就叫安杰利娜
这两个名字都有天使的意思
因为上帝保护这个孩子
我想唱歌的孩子也打动了她吧
多年来
我们都一直鼓励先驱和传道员
在跟人讨论圣经时
要多谈我们的组织
我们原来有一本册子
后来又出版一本
更简单、图片丰富的册子
这些册子都有达到一些成果
但是我认为
帮助弟兄姊妹和圣经学生
打开眼界、真正认识组织的是
JW电视网以及 jw.org网站
现在, 你会发现
不管去哪个会众或分区
弟兄姊妹对组织的认识和体会
是前所未有的
很明显地
现代科技加深我们对组织的认识
也帮助我们宣扬好消息
但是要记得
科技不是我们生活的全部
它在我们生活中的确占有重要地位
但也有潜在的危险
你听过“低头族”吗?
英文是“phubbing”
P-H-U-B-B-I-N-G
它是“电话”跟“冷落”合成的新字
用来形容在现实生活中
只顾滑手机
却把别人晾在一旁的行为
想象一下, 一对男女在餐厅里
自顾自地上网浏览网站
收发电子邮件
两人之间却连一句话都不说
根据贝勒大学的一项研究
这是一个普遍的社会问题
当然, 我们不能过与世隔绝的生活
但是除了网路的联系
我们更需要跟周遭的人
有真实的互动
中央长老团成员约翰·巴尔常说
要是我们一直使用电子产品
我们就会跟周遭的世界产生隔阂
跟现实生活断线
也阻断我们
跟别人加深友谊的机会

cn.text: 我叫比尔 · 霍毕
我是沃威克镇的检验员
这个工程我参加了一年半
是工程的最后一年半
真的很开心看到工程进展顺利
一直到完工
变成现在这么棒的地方
能参加这个工程是我的荣幸
我很少看到这么专业的建筑工人
这里的人很友善也很亲切
我参与过很多工程
他们比任何一个工程的人都来的有能力
