ko.text: 이제 마크 샌더슨 형제가 열심히 준비한 연설에
오하이오 주 시더포인트에 모인 무리 앞에서,
러더퍼드 형제는 지금도 잊혀지지 않은 다음과 같은 유명한 말을 했습니다.
러더퍼드 형제는 그 짧은 말을 통해
그가 매우 중요한 점을 인식하고 있다는 걸 보여 주었습니다.
바로 여호와의 전파자가 되어야 한다는 점이었습니다.
그들은 하느님의 왕국의 좋은 소식의 전파자이자
우리의 하늘 아버지 여호와에 관한 한 가지 놀라운 점을 알려 줍니다.
또 단지 한 천사가 하룻밤 사이에 18만 5000명을 죽일 수도 있고요.
여호와께선 이 전파 활동을 이루기 위해
하지만 그분은 어떻게 이 일을 이루어 오셨나요?
바로 여러분과 저와 같은 불완전하고 평범한 인간 남녀들을 사용해서
역사상 유래가 없는 대규모 전파 활동을 이루어 오신 것입니다.
이 점은 사도 바울이 고린도 전서 1장에 기록한 내용을 생각나게 합니다.
여러분이 부르심을 받았을 때에 육적인 면에서 지혜로운 사람이 많지 않았고
유력한 사람도 많지 않았으며 귀족 출신도 많지 않았습니다.
그러나 하느님께서는 지혜로운 사람들이 수치를 당하게 하시려고
또한 강한 것들이 수치를 당하게 하시려고
하느님께서는 있는 것들을 아무것도 아닌 것이 되게 하시려고
세상의 보잘것없는 것들과 멸시 받는 것들,
그것은 어떤 사람도 하느님 앞에서 자랑하지 못하게 하려는 것입니다."
어쩌면 고린도 사람들은 여호와께서 강력한 사람들,
새로운 운동을 이끌게 하실 거라 생각했을지 모르죠.
하지만 여호와께서 사용하실 수단은 그런 사람들이 아니었습니다.
오히려 “교육을 받지 못한 보통 사람들”로 묘사된 사람들을
그분 자신과 그분의 전능하심을 두드러지게 하기 위해서였습니다.
불완전한 사람들을 사용해서 이처럼 엄청난 일을 이루셨기 때문에,
사실 아무도 이루어진 일에 대해 자랑할 수 없는 것이죠.
앞서 언급한 대로 러더퍼드 형제가 행동을 촉구하는 말을 하자,
시더 포인트 대회 때 직접 그 말을 들은 분인데,
“주의 조직 안에 있는 우리는 가능한 모든 면으로
그들의 주의를 생명의 소식에 돌리게 하려고 애썼다.
우리는 구호, 전면 광고, 라디오 방송,
소식을 적은 간판을 걸고 다니는 행렬,
점점 증가하고 있는 호별 방문 봉사자들의 군대를 사용해 왔다.”
이 자리에도 이러한 활동에 참여해 봤거나
그런 도구들을 사용해 보신 분이 계실지 모릅니다.
오늘날 우리는 놀라운 도구들을 사용해서 이 일을 수행합니다.
전에는 상상도 할 수 없었던 것들이죠.
jw.org, 「JW 라이브러리」 앱, 「랭귀지」 앱, JW 방송,
그리고 문자적으로 수백 개의 언어로 구할 수 있는 출판물도 있습니다.
우리가 결코 잊어선 안 될 한 가지 분명한 점이 있습니다.
다시 말하면, 이 일을 이루기 위해서는
즉 하느님의 왕국의 좋은 소식의 전파자들이
여러분이 집집을 다니며 담대하게 전파하는 모습을 보게 됩니다.
여러분의 출판물 전시 카트를 공항에서, 길거리에서, 기차역에서 봅니다.
전파 활동을 위한 여러분의 수고는 칭찬받아 마땅합니다.
사도 바울이 고린도 전서 15:58에서 이렇게 말한 바와 같습니다.
“그러므로 사랑하는 형제 여러분, 확고하고 흔들리지 말며
여러분은 주와 관련된 여러분의 수고가 헛되지 않음을 알고 있습니다.”
그렇습니다, 여러분은 "주의 일을 많이" 하고 계십니다.
물론 우린 우리의 "수고가 헛되지 않음을" 알지만,
때때로 그런 잘못된 결론을 내릴 때도 있지 않습니까?
우리의 수고가 사실 헛되다는 생각이 들기 시작할 수 있습니까?
그런 잘못된 결론을 내리게 될 수 있는 세 가지 상황을 고려해 보겠습니다.
나이가 들거나 건강 문제가 늘어갈 때,
이런 생각을 하게 될 수 있습니다.
‘이젠 내가 기여할 수 있는 게 너무나 적어.
좋은 소식을 전하는 데 난 더 이상 별 도움이 안 되는 것 같아.’
만약 그런 느낌이 드신 적이 있다면,
오늘 있었던 일을 생각해 보면 격려가 되실 겁니다,
우리의 합창 노랫소리를 들으면 정말 좋지 않습니까?
두 세 명의 크고 요란한 목소리 때문인가요?
여호와를 찬양하는 아름다운 음악을 만들기 때문인 것입니다.
아니면 아주 부드럽거나 또는 아주 작든 상관 없이,
우리 모두는 지구 전역에서 아름답게 울려 퍼지고 있는
여호와를 찬양하는 합창 소리에 기여할 수 있습니다.
고린도 후서 8:12의 원칙이 우리 정신에 강력하게 작용해야 합니다.
그분은 우리가 가지지 않은 것이 아니라 가진 것에 따라 주기를 바라십니다.”
이 성구를 여러 형태의 주는 일에 적용할 수 있습니다.
물질적인 것을 기부하는 데 적용할 수도 있고,
또 우리의 시간, 활력, 재능 등 좋은 소식을 전파하는 데
우리가 바치는 모든 것에 적용할 수 있습니다.
중요한 건 내가 무엇을 가지지 않았는가가 아니라,
내가 가진 것이 무엇인가 하는 거죠.
하느님의 왕국의 좋은 소식을 전해줄 수 있습니다.
인도에 사는 성서 연구생에 대한 경험담을 보내왔는데,
그는 듣지 못할뿐더러 날 때부터 팔도 없는 분이었습니다.
이분은 발을 사용해서 수화하는 법을 배웠고,
그런 식으로 의사소통을 하고 표현을 할 수 있습니다.
네, 우리가 가진 것을 사용해, 여호와를 찬양할 수 있습니다.
중앙장로회는 여러분 형제 자매들이 하고 계신 모든 수고에
전파하기 위해 하고 있는 일에 대해 감사드립니다.
이제 우리의 수고가 헛되다는 생각이 들게 될 수 있는
“그 사람이 나보다 훨씬 더 잘할 텐데.
나보다 훨씬 더 많이 할 수 있을 거야.”
자신을 다른 사람과 비교하는 것은 인간이 가진 성향입니다.
하지만 이 점에 관해 하느님의 말씀은 어떤 조언을 할까요?
자기 자신과 관련해서만 기뻐할 이유가 있을 것입니다.”
네, 우리가 할 수 있는 것, 우리가 기여할 수 있는 것을 보아야 합니다.
이 점과 관련해서 우리의 현대 역사 중에 멋진 예가 있는데,
웨버 형제는 펜실베이니아 앨러게니에서 침례를 받았는데,
성경에 관한 매우 깊은 지식을 얻게 됐죠.
얼마 후 웨버 형제는 유럽으로 돌아가
프랑스어 구역에서 봉사하고 싶은 마음이 가득했습니다.
개인적으로 몰라서 전 뭐라고 할 순 없지만
「선포자」 책에 나온 형제의 사진을 보면 동의하실지 모릅니다.
하지만 동시에 연감 책에선 이렇게 말하죠.
“그는 영어와 불어 그리고 독일어를 잘 아는
사실 그는 「성경 연구」를 비롯한 초창기 출판물들을
어쨌든, 웨버 형제는 스위스로 돌아가자마자 바빠졌습니다.
프랑스어판 종교 신문과 잡지들에 「성경 연구」 제1권과
러셀 형제의 다른 서적들을 광고하는 글을 올렸죠.
그러자 사람들이 러셀 형제의 출판물을 주문하기 시작했습니다.
웨버 형제는 큰 규모로 전파 활동을 계속했습니다.
또 프랑스와 벨기에로 가서 출판물을 주문했거나
벌목이나 정원사 일을 해서 생활비를 벌어가며,
그러면, 이러한 그의 노력을 여호와께서 축복하셨습니까?
그가 봉사한 구역인, 스위스, 프랑스, 벨기에 전역에서,
많은 사람이 연합해 여호와를 섬기기 시작했습니다.
스위스 제네바에 프랑스어 사무실을 개설하기로 결정했습니다.
교육을 더 많이 받은 다른 형제들이
그 일을 인계 받는 것이 좋겠다고 생각했습니다.
그간 그 모든 기반을 닦느라 열심히 일한 이 겸손한 형제는
이제 모든 권한을 넘기라는 요청을 받은 셈입니다.
연감에 따르면, 그는 더 교육을 잘 받은 형제들에게
아뇨, 연감은 그가 계속 좋은 태도를 유지했다고 알려줍니다.
계속 여러 회중을 다니며 순례자 방문을 했고,
더 교육을 잘 받은 그 책임 맡은 형제들에게
이 겸손하고 소중한 형제를 찾아 다시 데려와야죠.
네, 그는 형제들을 찾아가 강화하고, 격려하고,
시정해 달라는 부탁을 받았고, 기꺼이 그렇게 했습니다.
형제들을 격려하고 강하게 하는 일을 멈추지 않았습니다.
자신의 재능과 영성을 다른 사람을 격려하는 데 사용했습니다.
자신을 남과 비교하느라 시간을 다 소모한 것이 아니라
자신이 가진 것을 사용해서 여호와를 영예롭게 했습니다.
웨버 형제가 오래 전에 봉사한 구역에
지금은 여호와의 이름을 찬양하는 전도인의 수가
참으로 큰 교훈을 배울 수 있지 않습니까!
이제 우리의 수고가 헛되다는 생각이 들 수 있는 마지막 상황을
수십 년간 아주 오랫동안 베델에서 봉사했는데,
야외로 임지가 바뀐 분이 계실지 모릅니다.
그런가 하면 순회 감독자로 일하다가 70세가 되어서
정규 또는 특별 파이오니아로 봉사하게 된 분들도 계실 수 있죠.
그 동안의 자신의 수고가 헛되다고 느낄 것입니까?
가능하다면 베델에 있는 우리 모두가 야외로 돌아가야죠.
야외로 돌아가 지금 파이오니아 봉사를 하고 있는 형제 자매들은
참으로 엄청난 일을 이루고 있는 것입니다.
길르앗 학교가 이제는 특별 전시간 종들을 훈련해
강하게 하고 안정시키는 일을 하도록 조정된 것과 마찬가지로,
회중들을 굳건하게 하고 강하게 하는 영향을 미치고 있습니다.
그들은 여러 해 동안 베델 봉사나 여행하는 일을 하면서 얻은 경험과
장성된 특성들과 또 많은 훌륭한 교훈들을 나누어 주고 있습니다.
중앙장로회는 야외로부터 많은 감사의 편지를 받습니다.
그중 최근에 받은 한 편지의 일부를 인용해 드리죠.
야외로 보내 주셔서 감사하다는 말을 전하고 싶습니다.
그것이 얼마나 힘든 결정이었을지 저는 잘 모르지만,
그 소중한 분들과 한 회중에 있으면서
말로는 다 할 수 없는 유익을 얻고 있습니다.
참으로 큰 축복이 아닐 수 없습니다!
자신들의 회중에 자격을 잘 갖춘 이 사람들을 맞아들인,
이 자매가 속한 나라와 전 세계의 전도인들 모두가 똑같은 말을 합니다.
그러므로 임명이 바뀐 우리 형제 자매 여러분,
얼마나 여러분의 수고에 감사하는지 알아주시기 바랍니다.
여호와의 조직에 속해 있다는 건 가슴 설레는 일입니다.
이루어진 일들을 보면 그저 놀라울 뿐입니다.
현재 좋은 소식의 전도인은 8백만 명이 넘습니다.
이 어마어마한 전파 활동을 이루어 오셨습니다.
우리는 그분의 동료 일꾼이 되는 엄청난 특권을 받았습니다.
형제 여러분, 이 일이 마침내 완수되었다고 말할 때까지,
우리의 수고가 결코 헛되지 않을 것이라는 확신을 가지고,
우리 모두 “주의 일을 많이” 하도록 하십시다.
좋은 연설을 해 준 샌더스 형제 감사합니다.
우리 수고가 결코 헛되지 않는다는 사실은 격려가 되죠.
여호와께서는 우리가 봉사에 기울인 노력을 잊지 않으시고,
이제 게리트 뢰시 형제가 흥미로운 주제로 연설할 것입니다.
‘정복자’에 해당하는 영어 단어는 이기는 사람을 가리킵니다.
정복한다는 건 “누군가 또는 무엇을 패배시킨다”는 뜻이죠.
그들 중 하나인 에르난 코르테스는 아스텍 제국을 정복했죠.
스페인보다 더 넓은 땅을 정복한 나라는 어디였을까요?
최고 전성기 때의 대영 제국은 역사상 가장 큰 제국으로 알려졌는데,

사람들이 이 점을 알아야 하기에, 우린 전파하고 가르쳐야 합니다.
그들은 너무 늦기 전인 지금 여호와께 달려가야 합니다.
예수께서 임재하셔서 적들 가운데 다스리시는 기간 동안,
폭력의 정도가 정신을 못 차릴 만큼 심해진다는 사실에 주목해야 합니다.
단순히 매체나 인터넷에 그렇게 비춰지는 게 아니라,
오늘날 우린 바로 그런 상황을 보고 있죠.
예수께서 자신의 임재를 노아의 날과 비교하면서 언급하신
심판을 하실 때가 매우 가까웠음을 분명히 보여 주는
어떤 나라들에선 우리가 이런 이야기를 하는 것에 대해
하지만 우린 여호와의 말씀을 희석시키지 않고,
그분께 이의를 제기하겠다는 사람은 그렇게 하게 둡시다.
누가 17장에서 바리새인들은 왕국이 언제 오는지 알고 싶어 합니다.
누가복음 17:26에서 예수께선 노아의 날과 연관 지어 말씀하시는데,
“또한 롯의 날과 같은 일이 있을 것입니다.
사람들은 먹고 마시고 사고 팔고 심고 집을 짓고 하다가,
하늘에서 불과 유황이 비 오듯 내려 모두 멸망되었습니다.
‘사람의 아들’이 나타나는 그날에도 그와 같을 것입니다.”
큰 환난에서 예수가 나타나실 때, 그렇게 될 겁니다.
여호와께선 성적 타락에도 염증을 느끼고 계시죠.
두 명의 다른 성서 필자도 이 두 사건을 연관 짓는데,
끝이 가까웠다는 걸 알 수 있는 이유이죠.
오늘날 세상을 보면, 정말 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
우릴 격려하는데 특히 이미 여호와께 달려간 사람들을 격려합니다.
“또한 그분은 자기의 본래 위치를 지키지 않고
자기가 있어야 할 처소를 버린 천사들을
큰 날의 심판을 위해 영원한 사슬로 묶어
변태적이고 부자연스러운 행위에 대해 말하고 있는 것인데,
여호와께서 유다에게 영감을 주어 기록하게 하셨죠.
아시는 것처럼, 여자들과 동거하고 후손을 낳았는데,
아주 좋지 않은 때였고, 여호와께선 가증스럽게 여기셨습니다.
바로, 노아 홍수 이전에 있었던 그런 상황이 7절에 나와 있는데,
“그와 같이 소돔과 고모라와 그 주변 도시들도
그들은 영원한 불의 사법적 처벌을 받아
이러한 성적 타락을 더 이상 지켜볼 수 없다고 느끼셨죠.
그분은 소돔과 고모라 뿐 아니라 주변 도시의 모든 타락한 자들로 인한
불평의 부르짖음을 더 이상 참을 수 없으셨고,
그들 보기엔 우리 말이 판단하는 것 같아 기분 나쁘겠죠.
하지만 우린 사람들의 기분을 상하게 하려는 의도가 아니라,
우린 그에 관한 여호와의 판결을 지지합니다.
“대홍수와 소돔과 고모라 이야기를 사실로 믿다니 정말 어리석군.
베드로는 영감을 받아서 이 내용을 기록했을 때 그 점을 분명히 했는데,
여호와께서 베드로에게 영감을 주셔서 이점을 분명히 하신 덕분에,
우리가 끝이 얼마나 가까운지를 이해할 수 있는 거죠.
“사실 하느님께서는 죄지은 천사들을 처벌하기를 주저하지 않으시고,
심판을 위해 짙은 어둠의 사슬로 묶어 두셨습니다.
그분은 옛 세상을 처벌하기를 주저하지 않으시고,
경건하지 않은 사람들의 세상에 홍수를 가져오셨습니다.
다른 일곱 사람과 함께 안전하게 지켜 주셨습니다.”
“그리고 소돔과 고모라 도시들을 정죄하시고 재가 되게 하셔서,
경건하지 않은 사람들에게 닥칠 일의 본보기로 삼으셨습니다.”
모든 불경건한 자들에게 닥칠 일의 본보기죠.
여호와께서 대홍수 때와 소돔과 고모라 시대에 하신 일,
여호와께로 달려가지 않기로 선택한 자들의 미래인 것이죠.
이런 성경의 증거를 고려해 봤을 때,
땅이 폭력과 성적 타락으로 가득 찬 지금,
큰 환난이 가깝다는 것은 자명한 사실입니다.
앞으로 일어날 일을 숙고해 볼 때
또 잭슨 형제가 큰 환난에 관해 한 설명과도 일치하게
자신과 사랑하는 사람의 안전에 대해 염려하지 않아도 되니
이 마지막 날의 폭력은 사라질 것입니다.
소돔과 고모라의 경우처럼, 모두 멸망될 것입니다.
참 하느님의 의로운 숭배자 여러분, 모두 이점을 기억합시다.
의로운 자는 그리로 달려 들어가서 보호를 받는다.”
의롭고, 순결하고, 사랑스럽고, 좋은 말을 듣고,
건물을 나가실 때는 가시는 방향에 따라서
파노비아 애비뉴 쪽으로 난 옆 문을 사용하거나
메인 로비를 통해 정면으로 나가실 수 있습니다.
이제, 말씀드릴 다른 광고가 더 있나요?
사실 중앙장로회는 오늘 다음과 같은 광고를 해 줄 것을 요청했습니다.
월킬과 워릭의 완공된 시설을 위해 있게 될 봉헌식 프로그램에 대해
많은 질문이 있었고, 여러 가지 추측들이 있었습니다.
세계 본부의 워릭 강당에서 송출될 것입니다.
따라서, 강당에서 직접 프로를 즐길 참석자의 수는
이 프로그램을 미국 내의 모든 베델 시설과
이곳 저지 시티 대회 회관을 포함한 미국 내의 모든 대회 회관으로
월킬과 워릭 공사를 위해 수고한 모든 자원봉사자들이
연례 총회와 봉헌식 프로그램에 참석할 수 있을 것입니다.
하지만 이 프로그램을 다른 나라에 있는
지부 사무실이나 대회 회관으로는 스트리밍하지 않을 것입니다.
이 마련에 대한 세부 사항들을 알려드릴 것입니다.
다시 말씀 드리지만, 월킬과 워릭 시설의 봉헌식은
2017년 10월 7일 연례 총회와 맞물려서 있게 될 것입니다.
그러면 오늘 프로그램을 모두 마치기 위해,
함께 일어나셔서 새 노래 중 하나를 부르시겠습니다.
이 웅장한 노래를 모두 함께 힘차게 부르도록 하십니다.

en.text: Brother Mark Sanderson has labored over his material
and is looking forward to presenting his talk.
It’s entitled “Your Labor Is Not in Vain.”
Brother Sanderson, you have our ears.
The date was September 8, 1922,
Cedar Point, Ohio.
Brother Rutherford, before that assembled crowd,
said those words that still ring in our ears.
He said: “Behold! The King reigns!
“You are his publicity agents.
“Therefore advertise, advertise, advertise
the King and his kingdom.”
Well, what a call to action that was by Brother Rutherford.
And in those few words,
Brother Rutherford showed
that he recognized something that is very important.
The faithful men and women that were in that audience
and so many others who have followed them since
were to be Jehovah’s publicity agents.
They were to be preachers and teachers
of the good news of God’s Kingdom.
Now, that’s a simple fact,
but it reveals something amazing
about our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
Although he is so almighty,
although just one angel
could kill 185,000 in one night,
we know Jehovah could use any miraculous means
in order to accomplish this preaching work.
But how has Jehovah chosen to accomplish it?
By using imperfect,
ordinary men and women like you and like me
in order to accomplish the greatest preaching work
that has ever been accomplished in history.
It reminds us of what the apostle Paul wrote here
in 1 Corinthians chapter 1.
Will you open your Bibles and read it with me?
First Corinthians 1:26, the apostle Paul said:
“For you see his calling of you, brothers,
“that there are not many wise in a fleshly way,
“not many powerful, not many of noble birth,
“but God chose the foolish things of the world
“to put the wise men to shame;
“and God chose the weak things of the world
“to put the strong things to shame;
“and God chose the insignificant things of the world
“and the things looked down on, the things that are not,
“to bring to nothing the things that are,
so that no one might boast in the sight of God.”
Well, perhaps those in Corinth
thought that being a new movement,
Jehovah would raise up people who were powerful
—people from important families or people who had great worldly wisdom—
but that was not the means that Jehovah was going to use.
He was going to use people who were described
as “unlettered and ordinary.”
Well, for what purpose?
Well, really, to magnify him and to magnify his almightiness.
He could use these imperfect people
to accomplish this tremendous work
and, really, so that no human
could ever boast in what was accomplished.
Well, when those words of Brother Rutherford went out
—that call to action— our brothers got busy.
Brother Melvin Sargent, who was baptized in 1912
and who was present there in Cedar Point to hear those words, said this:
“Those of us inside the Lord’s organization
“have tried, in every way possible,
“to turn their attention to the message of life.
“We have used slogans, full-page advertisements,
“radio, sound cars, portable phonographs,
“gigantic conventions,
“parades of information-walkers carrying signs,
and a growing army of house-to-house ministers.”
How true!
And perhaps some of you shared in some of those
different activities, and you used those tools.
Well, what about today?
Today, brothers, we have amazing tools to help us to accomplish the work,
things that we could never even have imagined:
jw.org, the JW Library app,
our Language app, JW Broadcasting,
as well as literature that’s now available
in literally hundreds and hundreds of languages.
But, brothers,
no matter how wonderful any of these tools are,
no matter how many tools
we ever produce, we cannot forget one simple point:
Tools need users.
And that means that every one of you
—every publisher of the good news of God’s Kingdom—
is absolutely essential
and is absolutely needed to accomplish this work.
Do you agree with me?
And we have to say that as a Governing Body, as we travel,
we see you preaching boldly from house to house.
We see your literature carts in airports,
on public corners, in train stations.
The work that you are accomplishing is amazing,
and you are to be commended for your hard work in preaching.
It’s much like the apostle Paul said here
in 1 Corinthians 15:58,
he said: “Therefore, my beloved brothers,
“be steadfast, immovable,
“always having plenty to do in the work of the Lord,
“knowing that your labor is not in vain
in connection with the Lord.”
Well, that’s what you’re doing!
You see, you have “plenty to do in the work of the Lord.”
But, let’s ask another question.
We know, of course, that our “labor is not in vain,”
but could we from time to time come to that wrong conclusion?
Could we begin to think
that our labor really is in vain?
Well, let’s consider three different areas
where we might wrongfully come to that conclusion.
Here’s the first.
With advancing age
or with increasing health challenges,
we may begin to think:
‘Well, my voice is really very, very small.
‘I really cannot contribute very much anymore
to the preaching of the good news.’
Well, if that’s the way you may have felt,
it might be encouraging to think about what we did today
—the release of our brand new songbook.
Now, isn’t it true?
We love to listen to our choral singing.
But now, when you listen to that choral singing,
what is it that makes it beautiful?
Is it the fact that there are two or three loud,
booming voices that overpower everyone?
No, the beauty lies
in all of the voices coming together, harmonizing,
making beautiful music that praises Jehovah.
So, what can we learn from that?
Well, you see, whether our voice is loud
or whether our voice is very soft —or very small—
we all can contribute to this wonderful chorus
that’s being sung around this earth to praise Jehovah.
And, as Brother Splane so nicely mentioned in his talk,
the principle of 2 Corinthians 8:12
must be very powerful in our minds.
You see, there, the apostle Paul said:
“For if the readiness is there first,
“it is especially acceptable according to what a person has,
not according to what a person does not have.”
Well, now, we apply that to many different types of giving.
We apply it to our literal contributions of material things.
But we also can apply it to our use of our time,
our energy, our abilities
—everything that we give for the preaching of this good news.
So the question is not, What do you not have?
But the question is, What do you have?
Do you have a voice?
Well, whether it’s strong or soft, use it.
Continue to use it to praise Jehovah.
If you use sign language to communicate,
well, then, use your hands
to be able to tell others about the good news of God’s Kingdom.
Just recently, a brother sent me an experience of a Bible student
in India who is both deaf
and also was born with no arms.
Now, how can this man communicate?
Can you imagine?
He’s learned to do sign language with his feet,
and he is able to communicate and express his voice in that way.
Isn’t that wonderful?
We can use what we have to praise Jehovah.
And, I have to say, the Governing Body
deeply appreciates all of the hard work that you brothers
are doing whether your voice is loud and strong or quite weak.
We appreciate every one of you and the work that you’re doing
in preaching the good news of God’s Kingdom.
But now let’s talk about a second area
where we might think that our labor is in vain.
This is when we say:
“Well, someone’s work is really far better than mine.
They can do so much more than I can.”
Well, it is a human tendency
for us to want to compare ourselves with others.
But, what is the counsel that we have from God’s Word in this regard?
Let’s read Galatians 6:4.
Galatians 6:4, it says:
“But let each one examine his own actions,
“and then he will have cause for rejoicing in regard
“to himself alone,
and not in comparison with the other person.”
Yes, we have to look at what we can do
and what we can contribute to the work ourselves.
And in this regard, we have a beautiful example
that comes from our modern-day history that I’d like to share with you.
It’s the example of a brother named Adolf Weber.
Now, Brother Weber was baptized in Allegheny, Pennsylvania,
all the way back in the year 1890.
Now, that’s a long time ago, isn’t it?
Now, who was this man?
He was a Swiss woodcutter.
He had come to America,
and he worked with Brother Russell as a gardener.
He obtained a very deep knowledge of the Scriptures
from working with Brother Russell.
After a time, Brother Weber wanted with all his heart
to go back to Europe and begin preaching
in the French-language territories.
But, now, who was he?
Well, the yearbook— I’ll quote it.
I won’t try to make any judgments because I didn’t know Brother Weber.
But here’s what it said, ‘Brother Weber was
a simple man of peasantlike appearance.’
Well, if you see his picture in the Proclaimers book,
you might agree with that.
But, at the same time, the yearbook said:
“He was a devout, mature Christian
who knew well the English, French, and German languages.”
In fact, he translated the Studies in the Scriptures
and other early publications into French.
Well, as soon as he got back to Switzerland,
Brother Weber got busy.
He placed advertisements
in French-language religious newspapers and magazines
for Volume 1 of the Studies in the Scriptures and other books of Brother Russell.
Well, as a result,
people began to order Brother Russell’s publications.
They began to subscribe to The Watchtower in French.
Brother Weber went on big preaching campaigns.
He would go through Switzerland placing tracts.
He would go to France and Belgium, and he would meet with people
who had ordered literature or who had subscribed to The Watchtower,
all the while supporting himself
by doing woodcutting or gardening.
But now, were all of these efforts blessed by Jehovah?
Yes, because throughout that territory
—in Switzerland, in France, in Belgium—
many began to associate and began to serve Jehovah.
But then what happened?
In 1912, Brother Russell was on a trip through Europe,
and he decided to arrange to open a French-language office
in Geneva, Switzerland.
And so when Brother Russell looked at the candidates available,
he felt that there were other brothers
who were better educated who should now take over the work.
Well, now, how would that affect Brother Weber?
Here this humble man who had worked so hard
to get everything established was now being asked, as it were,
to turn over the reins.
Well, Brother Weber didn’t hesitate a bit.
The yearbook said he gladly stepped down
in favor of the more educated brothers.
Well, was he discouraged? Did he give up?
Did he try to compare himself with those other men?
No, the yearbook went on to say that he kept a good spirit.
He continued making his pilgrim visits to the congregations
and visiting the isolated brothers who spoke French.
But what happened?
Do you know the end of the story?
Well, just after a few years,
those well-educated brothers who had been placed in charge of the work—
Do you know what happened to them?
They all proved to be unfaithful.
And what happened?
Well, where’s Brother Weber?
We have to go and find this dear, humble man and bring him back.
He had to go and strengthen the brothers,
encourage them, readjust them, which he gladly did.
Despite the many challenges that this brother experienced,
he continued to strengthen and fortify the brothers
until he finished his earthly course
sometime about the year 1947.
What’s the lesson that we can learn?
See, Brother Weber
demonstrated the truth of Galatians 6:4.
He proved what his own work was.
He was content to be a lesser one
and to use his abilities and his spirituality
to be a source of encouragement to others.
He did not spend all of his time
comparing himself with others, but he brought what he had
and he used it to honor Jehovah.
Well, his labor was not in vain.
Do you know in the area where he opened up the work so long ago,
there are well over 100,000 publishers
who are praising Jehovah’s name?
What a powerful lesson we can learn
from this simple, humble brother, Adolf Weber.
But, now, let’s talk about our final area
where we might begin to think that our labor is in vain.
Perhaps some of you here have been serving
at Bethel for decades —many, many years—
and now you have been reassigned to the field.
Others of you may be circuit overseers
who have reached the age of 70,
and now you’ve begun to serve as regular or as special pioneers.
Well, now, should any of you in that situation
feel that your labors have been in vain?
Absolutely not!
Quite frankly, brothers, if possible,
all of us at Bethel should return to the field, if it were possible.
Because what did Jesus say at Matthew 9:37?
“Yes, the harvest is great,
“but the workers are few.
“Therefore, beg the Master of the harvest
to send out workers into his harvest.”
Yes, the workers are needed out in the field.
And these dear brothers and sisters who have returned to the field
who are now in the pioneer service,
they are accomplishing tremendous work.
Just as the Gilead School now has been designed
to train special full-time servants
to strengthen and stabilize,
well, now these ones who have returned to the field are having a powerful
and strengthening effect on the congregations.
They’re sharing their experience, their maturity,
the many wonderful lessons that they learned
from all of those years either in Bethel service or in traveling work.
Now, you know the Governing Body receives many letters from the field
—many letters of appreciation.
But I’d like to just quote from one that we recently received.
A sister wrote to the Governing Body and she said this:
“I want to thank you for sending into the field
“those who have served in special full-time service.
“While I cannot imagine how hard the decision must have been,
“I know I have benefited beyond words
“from having such dear ones in my congregation.
“They are truly a treasure from Jehovah.
“What a blessing to all those
“that have such ones in their congregation!
I thank you so much!”
Well, now, that’s just one letter.
But those words have been echoed
by publishers in this country and all around the world
who have received these well-qualified individuals
coming to their congregations.
So, dear brothers and sisters,
we’d like to say to all those of you who have been reassigned
how much we love you, how much we respect you,
how much we appreciate your work.
“Your labor is not in vain”!
Well, it truly is thrilling to be a part of Jehovah’s organization at this time.
From those small beginnings back in 1922 until today,
it’s amazing to see what has been accomplished
—now more than 8 million publishers of the good news.
Our magnificent and our wonderful God, Jehovah,
has chosen to accomplish this tremendous preaching work
using ordinary, imperfect people.
And we have been given the tremendous privilege
to be his fellow workers.
Brothers, are you determined to continue to preach along with us
until we say that this work is finally completed?
Then may all of us have “plenty to do in the work of the Lord”
with full confidence
that our labor will never be in vain.
We certainly want to thank Mark for that fine talk,
and it’s encouraging to know that our labor will never be in vain.
So Jehovah remembers us for the effort that we put forth
in our service, and he remembers us for good.
Next, we have Brother Gerrit Lösch with a rousing subject for us.
The theme is “Be a Conqueror.”
The English word “conqueror” refers to one that conquers.
To conquer means “to defeat someone or something.”
The Spanish explorers and warriors
who successfully conquered much of America in the 16th century
are called conquistadores, or conquerors.
One of them was Hernán Cortés, who conquered the Aztec Empire.
At the peak, the Spanish Empire
ruled over 19.4 million
square kilometers,
or 7.5 million square miles.
But who conquered more land than the Spanish?
The Mongols and the British.
At its greatest extent, the British Empire was known
as the largest empire in history,
as it covered more than 13,000,000 square miles,
or 33.7 million square kilometers,
which is approximately a quarter
of the earth’s total land area.
Despite its overseas holdings,
it was barely bigger than the Mongol Empire under Kublai Khan.
The British Empire was bigger
only because of its overseas landholdings.
The Mongols were a nomadic people
who originated from the grassland plateau of what is today Mongolia,
in central and northeast Asia.
Their speedy conquests,
beginning in the early 13th century of our Common Era,
changed the face of Asia and half of Europe.
In just 25 years,
the Mongols subjugated the inhabitants
of more territories than the Romans
had conquered in four centuries.
At the peak of their power, they ruled from Vietnam to Hungary
(a distance of about 5,500 miles,
or 8,700 kilometers)
and from Siberia to India
—the largest contiguous land empire
in recorded history, including modern times.
Then there was Hitler who saw himself as a world conqueror.
He promoted the slogan
“Today, Germany belongs to us;
tomorrow, the whole world.”
His attempt to conquer the world failed miserably.
How about conquests in Bible times?
After the Exodus of the Israelites
from Egypt in 1513 before our Common Era,
Jehovah told the Israelites to conquer the land of Canaan.
They were afraid and disobeyed.
Besides Moses, only Joshua and Caleb were willing to fight.
Numbers 13:30 says:
“Then Caleb tried to calm the people
“as they stood before Moses by saying:
“‘Let us go up immediately, and we are sure to take possession of it,
because we can surely conquer it.’”
For their lack of faith,
the Israelites had to wander for 40 years in the wilderness.
After that, they conquered Canaan during a period of about five years.
In King Jehoshaphat’s day, Jehovah caused a victory
over the Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites
from Seir—an alliance of nations.
Israel did not conquer in their own strength,
but Jehovah gave them the victory
by confusing the enemy alliance so that they killed each other,
according to 2 Chronicles 20:1-4.
What about conquests in the time of the end?
Do you know a world conqueror that conquered a larger area
than the Mongol and the British Empires?
Well, Revelation 6:2 gives the answer.
We can read about that conqueror:
“And I saw, and look! a white horse, and the one seated on it had a bow;
“and a crown was given him [well we know it refers to Jesus],
and he went out conquering and to complete his conquest.”
Well, Jesus now rules over the whole earth.
When did he go out to conquer?
In 1914 of our Common Era.
And when will he complete his conquest?
At Armageddon.
Whom did Jesus already conquer?
First, he conquered Satan and the demons, throwing them out of heaven
and restricting their movements to the earth and its vicinity.
This war is described in Revelation chapter 12.
But in 1914, his conquest was not complete yet.
At Armageddon, it will be.
Satan will be thrown into an abyss of inactivity,
and at the end of the foretold thousand years,
he will be totally destroyed.
What a conquest that will be!
At Armageddon, also, all human governments
will likewise be conquered.
Let’s read Revelation 17:14,
where we find this prophecy.
It says:
“These will battle with the Lamb,
“but because he is Lord of lords
“and King of kings, the Lamb will conquer them.
“Also, those with him who are called
“and chosen and faithful [anointed Christians]
will do so.”
How about spiritual conquests?
In Revelation chapters 2 and 3, seven times Jesus says
with reference to the anointed: “To the one who conquers.”
One example is Revelation 3:21, it says:
“To the one who conquers I will grant to sit down with me on my throne,
just as I conquered and sat down with my Father on his throne.”
How do the anointed conquer even right now before Armageddon?
They conquer by remaining loyal to Jehovah.
They conquer due to their faith, due to their love for Jehovah and Jesus.
They also conquer the evil with the good in everyday life.
What about the “great crowd” mentioned in Revelation chapter 7?
Talking about the situation on earth under the Messianic Kingdom,
Revelation 21:7 says:
“To anyone thirsting
“I will give from the spring of water of life free.
“Anyone conquering will inherit these things,
and I will be his God and he will be my son.”
The Revelation Climax book,
therefore, says on page 304:
“The great crowd . . . too must conquer.”
Even children can be conquerors.
When a child is shoved by a sibling,
usually the child’s first reaction is to shove back.
Sadly, such behavior is not limited to children.
Many adults act similarly.
When offended by someone, they want to get even.
Granted, most adults will not give a literal shove,
but many will push back in more subtle ways.
Whatever method is used, the intent is the same—to retaliate.
Although the urge to get even is deep-seated,
true Christians resist giving in to that urge.
Instead, they strive to follow
the apostle Paul’s admonition of Romans 12:17:
“Return evil for evil to no one.”
Paul explains in detail how all of us
can conquer in everyday life.
He wrote in Romans 12:20, 21:
“‘If your enemy is hungry, feed him;
“‘if he is thirsty, give him something to drink;
“for by doing this you will heap fiery coals on his head.’
“Do not let yourself be conquered by the evil,
but keep conquering the evil with the good.”
Back to you children.
How can you conquer the evil with the good
if a sibling or a classmate says something or does something unkind?
You conquer by not retaliating.
A worldly nursery rhyme puts it this way:
“Tit for tat. You kill my dog; I kill your cat.”
Maybe some of you know that.
But Jesus tells us to forgive.
Do something good.
Pray for the other child.
Because another has made a mistake,
it is no reason for us to make one also, is it?
Jehovah does not want us to retaliate.
In 1 Thessalonians 5:15,
it says: “See that no one renders
“injury for injury to anyone else,
but always pursue what is good toward one another and to all others.”
Therefore, children,
are you willing to conquer the evil with the good?
We want to commend you for your effort to do that.
You are making Jehovah’s heart glad this way.
How can we all conquer spiritually?
We do so by not retaliating.
This is the way of love.
Many came into the truth because of a Christian mate
doing good to an unbelieving mate for decades,
although having been treated terribly.
In the domestic setting, a wife who shows genuine kindness
to her husband after he makes unpleasant comments
about her beliefs or yells at her may well diffuse
a potentially explosive situation.
Such sisters conquer evil with good.
We want to commend all of you
who are not giving up on your unbelieving marriage mates.
If you show understanding and compassion
to the person who is treating you badly,
you might make him or her want to learn more about
the Bible and more about Jehovah.
No matter how he or she responds,
your mild and kind actions and words
make the person wonder why you are different.
1 Peter 3:4 refers
to “the incorruptible adornment
of the quiet and mild spirit”
—quiet and mild spirit.
On one island, a Pentecostal woman started to study the Bible.
But her opposed husband did, of course, not like it.
He even threatened the elders.
But then he fell sick and was taken to a hospital,
where he fell into a coma.
When he eventually regained consciousness,
two sisters visited and brought him some soup,
which he first thought was for his wife.
“No, the soup is for you!” said the sisters.
“That touched me deeply,” he recalls.
“No Pentecostal had visited me, yet two of Jehovah’s Witnesses
—the very people I had strongly opposed— brought me a meal.”
He recovered from his illness.
He studied twice a week
and was baptized in 1998.
You want to hear another soup experience?
Two brothers in Russia were preaching from house to house one morning.
A woman listened to their introduction and then excused herself.
She returned with a pot of borscht —a red beet soup—
and threw this on the brothers,
adding angrily, “Do not visit me again!”
The brothers returned home to change their clothes
and then continued their activity.
Later that day, they went to the market
to order ingredients
needed for a good borscht.
That evening, they visited the same woman again.
They told her that this time they came, not to preach, but to compensate her
for the loss of her family’s food,
knowing that the soup she had wasted
might have been the entire family meal.
Then they handed her the foodstuffs that they had purchased.
The woman was so surprised that she invited the brothers in to talk.
In time, a Bible study was started with this woman.
When non-Witnesses treat us badly, it is to be expected.
But when problems occur with a spiritual brother or sister,
the pain can be much deeper.
One brother recalled, “My biggest hurdle when coming into the truth
was accepting the fact that Jehovah’s people are not perfect.”
Thus, if a fellow Christian,
especially one with privileges in the congregation,
is thoughtless and acts in an unchristian way,
it can hurt us.
‘How can such things occur among Jehovah’s people?’ some may ask.
Actually, such things did occur even among anointed Christians
in the days of the apostles.
How should we respond when we are affected?
We can forgive, and we can pray for them.
In this way, we prove ourselves to be conquerors.
Recall the experience of Joseph.
His brothers dealt cruelly with him, but he conquered the bad
they did to him with good, resulting in happiness for all
and certainly also for Jehovah.
Brothers in Nazi times and in concentration camps
did not retaliate when mistreated by SS officers.

Some officers in camps preferred to be shaved by the brothers
—only the brothers.
They were nervous if other prisoners would do it,
fearing that one would, perhaps,
retaliate and cut their throats in revenge.
Twelve sisters were in the camp of Birkenau only a few days,
then they were taken to another camp, Auschwitz,
to work in the homes of SS officers.
They wanted only Jehovah’s Witnesses for that.
These officers were afraid of having others
working in their households.
They trusted that the sisters would not try to poison them.
In the 1960’s, I met Franz Desch, from Jenbach, Austria.

How much progress was made?
Well, imagine the great joy of both of them when,
some years later,

I used to give talks like that when I was young.
We have another blessing,
and it’s to be presented by the tongue of Brother Anthony Morris.
Listen carefully as he develops the theme “Run to Jehovah.”
I have to say, I remember those talks.
I miss them so much, Sam.
Oh boy!
Expect the unexpected!
Thank you very much.
Oh boy!
Now I have to get very serious.
Jehovah in his Holy Word forewarned us to expect ridicule
for our conviction that he’s going to destroy
Satan’s wicked system of things.
Quoting Scripture: “Where is this promised presence of his? . . .
All things are continuing exactly as they were from creation’s beginning.”
In other words, everything is the same; nothing has really changed.
Are things really the same?
Well, here in the United States, among the many shootings
—I’m thinking of the one not too long ago down in Dallas, Texas—
this man was shooting at police officers, and they caught video of it.
And people didn’t know what the shooting was about
or who was the particular target, so they started to run.
They didn’t know where they were running,
but they were just looking for safety
—running, looking for safety.
Panic was in their faces.
You could see it on the video.
Now, during these final days of Satan’s rule,
all over the world, people are frightened.
They don’t know where to go to be safe.
But we have something to direct them to.
Turn to Proverbs chapter 18,
and this is where we have the theme
for this final talk here at our annual meeting.
Proverbs 18:10:
“The name of Jehovah is a strong tower.
Into it the righteous one runs and receives protection.”
Yes, as wickedness advances from bad to worse,
we have to run to Jehovah
to be protected, to be safe.
And once we’re in the tower —to remain there—
that means we look to Jehovah in faith, in obedience,
and we recognize
how important it is to faithfully represent that name.
So the purpose of this talk
is to encourage all of us to run to Jehovah.
Those of us that have run to him, don’t lose heart,
and be busy teaching others
that they better run to Jehovah before it’s too late.
Now, the end is very close, and it’s obvious.
Why is it obvious?
Well, we’re going to review some fundamental truths
that are so spiritually fortifying.
And you really can’t review them often enough.
Matthew chapter 24,
and we’re going to clearly emphasize
why we know we’re close.
Matthew 24.
After Jesus here has mentioned what’s going to happen to the temple
and, of course, he gets to the third verse here
where the disciples in private approach him,
which were Peter, James, John, and Andrew.
And they want to know: “When will these things be,
“and what will be the sign of your presence
and of the conclusion of the system of things?”
So this presence is referring to
Jesus’ enthronement as King in his royal visit to this earth.
Now, what stands out, we have the increase of lawlessness
—and you might keep in mind— that’s not just criminal lawlessness,
that’s disdain for Jehovah’s law.
See, people forget that.
And look at the disdain for Jehovah’s law.
Now, after he emphasizes in verse 36
that no human is going to know the day or the hour,
notice what Jesus stated, verse 37:
“For just as the days of Noah were,
“so the presence of the Son of man will be.
“For as they were in those days before the Flood,
“eating and drinking, men marrying and women being given in marriage,
“until the day that Noah entered into the ark,
“and they took no note until the Flood came and swept them all away,
so the presence of the Son of man will be.”
So there we have this clear comparison
—it goes back to the days of Noah.
They took no note,
and we see the same today.
While we rejoice with the thousands
that are dedicating themselves to Jehovah God
and getting baptized each year, the fact is, all over the earth,
by far the majority take no note.
They are busy about their daily affairs,
and they’re not interested.
They don’t want to run to Jehovah.
It just doesn’t have any appeal to make such changes.
Now, what sometimes seems
to be forgotten is found here in Genesis 6.
Why did Jehovah take the action?
Genesis chapter 6.
Let’s remind ourselves of what really
brought this to a head
to where Jehovah took action.
And it’s connected with our day
because this is what’s motivating him
to soon take action.
Here we find Genesis 6:5:
“Consequently, Jehovah saw that man’s wickedness was great on the earth
“and that every inclination
of the thoughts of his heart was only bad all the time.”
Now, notice this —it’s very significant—verse 11:
“But the earth had become ruined in the sight of the true God.”
Why?
“The earth was filled with violence.”
Sound familiar?
“The earth was filled with violence.”
It stayed that way for some time, and then, finally,
Jehovah is fed up with the violence.
And notice verse 13:
“After that God said to Noah:
“‘I have decided to put an end to all flesh,
“‘because the earth is full of violence
“‘on account of them,
so I am bringing them to ruin together with the earth.’”
“Full of violence.”
See?
Same thing today —this earth is full of violence.
But that’s what moved Jehovah to act.
And then the violence continued, and finally, in chapter 7, verse 1:
“Go into the ark.” After years of constructing it,
Jehovah had had enough of the violence.
Now, this is pertinent.
In 1987, the May 15 Watchtower, page 20,
paragraph 18,
made this profound statement
related to the Flood and connecting it with our day:
“Many of those who died in the Flood no doubt
“considered themselves ‘nice’ people,
“not being involved in the violence that filled society in those days.
“But just being ‘nice’ did not save them.
“By their apathy
“they condoned the evil of their day.
“The crucial thing was that they did not ‘run’ to Jehovah;
“they did not listen when God’s servant spoke.
“So they did not take the proper steps
for survival.”
And that’s where we are now.
People must understand.
We have to preach and teach them.
They need to run to Jehovah now before it’s too late.
And during his presence, all through these decades
ruling in the midst of his enemies,
you have to accept the fact that the degree of violence
at this point is mind-numbing.
It’s just all over the earth—violence.
And it isn’t just because of the media and the Internet and such;
it’s just filled with violence.
So keep that in mind, and we see that today.
And something else Jesus connected
when he was comparing his presence with the days of Noah
—note this here in Luke 17.
And this is the second thing that just makes it very obvious
we are so close,
and Jehovah is going to take action.
And this is his judgment.
Now, we would have people in general—
Some countries would find
what we’re going to discuss here hate-mongering,
but we will never water down Jehovah’s Word,
sticking close with it.
These are the words of Jesus Christ.
If they want to take issue with him, let them go ahead.
Luke chapter 17, the Pharisees want to know when the Kingdom is coming.
Now, in verse 26 of Luke 17,
he makes the connection about the days of Noah,
which we just addressed and how he entered into the ark.
Now, let’s read 28 through 30:
“Likewise, just as it occurred in the days of Lot:
“they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling,
“they were planting, they were building.
“But on the day that Lot went out of Sodom,
“it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed them all.
“It will be the same on that day
when the Son of man is revealed.”
Oh yeah.
When Jesus is revealed at the great tribulation, that’s it.
Jehovah is fed up with the sexual depravity as well.
Now, two other Bible writers connect these two events,
and that’s why we see how close we are.
If you look at the world today, it’s right before our eyes.
Notice Jude, here.
Let’s turn over to Jude.
And he was inspired
to encourage us, especially those who’ve already run to Jehovah.
Jude 6,
and we’re going to read 6 in the letter of Jude:
“And the angels who did not keep their original position
“but forsook their own proper dwelling place,
“he has reserved with eternal bonds in dense darkness
for the judgment of the great day.”
So here we have it.
This was a perversion —unnatural—
and he was addressing this.
Jehovah inspired Jude to write this.
These disobedient angels materialized bodies, as we all know,
and cohabited with women, and they produced offspring
—half-human, half-demon.
A very difficult time for the earth,
and Jehovah found that despicable.
Now, this part of what happened prior
to the Flood of Noah’s day
is connected with verse 7, this sexual depravity.
Let’s read verse 7:
“In the same manner,
“Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them
“also gave themselves over
“to gross sexual immorality
“and pursued unnatural fleshly desires;
“they are placed before us as a warning example
“by undergoing the judicial punishment
of everlasting fire.”
So Jehovah doesn’t mince any words here.
This sexual depravity
found in the cities throughout this earth,
he’s had enough of it.
And you’d have to admit
that just like the Scriptures bring out
in Genesis chapters 13 and 18,
Jehovah said this “cry of complaint” was going up.
And all of the perverted ones
—and not just Sodom and Gomorrah, but the cities nearby—
and this cry of complaint was just too much
for Jehovah to take, and he took action.
However, what about our day?
Well, the sexual depravity—
They don’t think they’re depraved,
and our saying so
is judgmental, offensive
—at least to them.
And we don’t intend to try to deliberately offend people.
We just— This is what the Scriptures teach.
It’s perverted,
and we support Jehovah’s judgment on that.
However, the spirit of Satan’s world is:
“How foolish to believe that the story
“of the Flood and the story of Sodom and Gomorrah are true.
You people are foolish!”
Well, these stories are true.
And Peter really makes it very clear here
as he was inspired to write this,
2 Peter and the second chapter.
And so we love Jehovah
for inspiring him to make this so clear
because it helps us to understand how close we are.
And 2 Peter 2:4-6:
“Certainly God did not refrain
“from punishing the angels who sinned, but threw them into Tartarus,
“putting them in chains of dense darkness to be reserved for judgment.
“And he did not refrain from punishing an ancient world,
“but kept Noah, a preacher of righteousness,
“safe with seven others when he brought a flood
upon a world of ungodly people.”
Now, notice this profound point, verse 6:
“And by reducing the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes,
“he condemned them,
“setting a pattern
for ungodly people of things to come.”
That’s the pattern
for all these ungodly people.
What Jehovah did in the Flood
as well as in the day of Sodom and Gomorrah
and judged them there —there’s the pattern.
That’s their future if they choose not to run to Jehovah.
So considering this Scriptural evidence
—the earth is filled with violence and sexual depravity—
it’s just so clear we’re so close to the great tribulation.
And contemplating what may occur
—and it connects with Brother Jackson’s comments about the great tribulation—
we just need to ‘trust in Jehovah with all our heart
and not lean on our own understanding.’
And how reassuring to know that very soon no one will worry
about their safety or the safety of their loved ones.
The violence of the last days will be done away with.
All the sexually immoral people who brazenly flaunt
our precious Jehovah’s laws will be destroyed,
just as they were in Sodom and Gomorrah.
So rest assured, Jehovah hears our cry of complaint.
Do not lose heart.
All you righteous worshippers of the true God, remember:
“The name of Jehovah is a strong tower.
Into it the righteous one runs and receives protection.”
Thank you very much, Brother Morris.
That was a fine conclusion to this wonderful program.
We have received blessings galore
in the form of things
that ‘are true, serious concern,
‘righteous, chaste,
‘lovable, well-spoken-of,
virtuous, praiseworthy,’
“good and acceptable.”
We already announced that depending
on the direction you will be going
when you leave the building,
you can use the side doors onto Pavonia Avenue
or go through the main lobby and exit through the front.
Well, is there any other announcement that I could make?
Yes, there is.
In fact, the Governing Body requested
that the following announcement be made today.
Are you ready?
Well, let me set the stage for the announcement.
As you might have guessed,
there have been many questions
and some wild speculations
about the upcoming dedication program
for the Wallkill and Warwick completed facilities.
You’re about to get the definitive answer.
Our announcement reads this way:
“The Governing Body is pleased to inform you that the new facilities
“at Wallkill and Warwick will be dedicated in conjunction
“with the annual meeting program on October 7, 2017.
“The annual meeting and dedication program will originate
“from world headquarters in the auditorium at Warwick.
“Hence, the number of attendees that will enjoy it live
“in the auditorium will be limited.
“However, the Governing Body has approved that the program
“will be streamed to all Bethel facilities in the United States
“and all Assembly Halls in the United States,
“including here at the Jersey City Assembly Hall.
“In this way, it is hoped that all who volunteered to work
“on the Wallkill and Warwick projects will be able to attend the annual meeting
“and the dedication program associated therewith.
“However, the program will not be streamed
“to other branch offices or Assembly Halls in other lands.
“The United States Branch Committee
“will be providing more details about the arrangements in due time.
“Again, the dedication of Wallkill and Warwick facilities
“will be in connection with the annual meeting
“on October 7, 2017.
Your brothers, the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
That brings us to the conclusion of our program,
and I invite all of you to stand and sing another of our new songs.
We know it for the time being as song number 136:
“The Kingdom Is in Place—Let It Come!”
Please sing this majestic song with full throat,
just as it deserves, song number 136.

en.text: When is your turn, Dad?
Our family was contacted by Jehovah’s Witnesses
a few years ago.
Rachel started studying first.
Soon, we all joined in.
For the first time, we were all learning
what the Bible really teaches.
It wasn’t long
before we were sharing the truth with others.
Well, most of us were.
I knew it was the truth,
but I didn’t know if I could live up to
everything Jehovah asks.
Get away.
What if I let everyone down?
What if I let Jehovah down?
You know, can you just give me one second?
Yeah, no problem.
All right. Yeah.
A kind elder named Ben noticed I was struggling.
You OK?
He took the initiative to help.
He asked, “What drew you to Jehovah
in the first place?”
I guess it was learning that Jehovah isn’t harsh and demanding,
but that he’s a loving Father.
Ben agreed and said,
“When we do our best to serve Jehovah,
he does the rest.”
He explained that Jehovah knows our limitations
and doesn’t expect perfection.
And he’s always there to help
because he wants us to succeed.
Then he read Isaiah 41:10:
“Do not be afraid,
“for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious,
“for I am your God.
I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,”
Help!
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
I don’t need to be perfect to serve Jehovah.
I just need to love him and trust him.
And he’ll do the rest.

en.text: During his earthly ministry,
Jesus miraculously healed
many sick or disabled persons.
At times, he would say to such ones
the expression we find at Matthew 9:29:
“According to your faith let it happen to you.”
The principle of what Jesus stated
applies in every aspect of our Christian life and ministry.
But today we will discuss how this principle
that faith in Jehovah makes things happen
can work for us in three areas.
We will see:
1) how our faith has made positive things happen in our personal life,
2) how we can accomplish things in God’s service
that would not be possible without faith in Jehovah God,
and 3) how faith moves us to step out of our comfort zone
to do more in Jehovah’s service.
The principle that faith in Jehovah makes things happen
is well illustrated in one of the miracles Jesus performed.
Please open your Bible to Mark chapter 5,
and let’s read verses 25-29:
“Now there was a woman
“who had had a flow of blood for 12 years.
“She had suffered much at the hands of many physicians
“and had spent all her resources,
“and she was no better but, rather, had become worse.
“When she heard the reports about Jesus,
“she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his outer garment,
“for she kept saying:
“‘If I touch just his outer garments, I will get well.’
“And immediately her flow of blood dried up,
“and she sensed in her body
that she had been healed of the grievous sickness.”
In the following verses, Jesus asked who had touched him.
The woman then revealed before the crowd
what she had done and how she’d been cured.
Now notice Jesus’ response in verse 34:
“He said to her:
“‘Daughter, your faith has made you well.
“‘Go in peace, and be healed
from your grievous sickness.’”
What comforting words
Jesus spoke to this trembling woman:
“Your faith has made you well.”
What did Jesus mean?
Let’s examine the account more closely.
It says that the woman heard “reports about Jesus.”
Many others heard the same reports,
but not all put faith in Jesus.
And think of the circumstances
that could have prevented her from even coming to Jesus.
She had been disappointed many times
over the past 12 years.
She might well have thought:
‘What’s the use?
‘I’m tired and weak and poor.
I’m staying home.’
Or ‘I would like for Jesus to see me,
‘but there is such a crowd.
‘How will I ever get through to him?
‘And after all, I’m in an unclean state,
‘and if the people discover this,
perhaps they will punish me.’
No, she did not allow these negative thoughts
or doubts to fill her mind.
She left her home.
She found Jesus despite the large crowd.
And what was she saying?
Did she say,
“If I touch just his outer garments,
maybe I will get well”?
No, she said,
“I will get well.”
Now, it was not the case
that her faith healed her.
No, but her faith moved her to come to Jesus,
and she was healed by the power from Jehovah
that flowed through his Son.
Faith to approach Jesus
made it happen for her.
If you are a dedicated, baptized Christian,
don’t you agree that your faith has already made
positive things happen in your personal life?
No, you were not miraculously healed
of your physical sicknesses.
We look forward to physical healing of our ills
during the Thousand Year Reign of Christ.
But today Jesus Christ directs a program
of spiritual healing.
When we were a part of this godless world,
many of us were sick spiritually, morally, and emotionally.
No one could cure us.
Perhaps we desperately tried material things or pleasures
to fill our spiritual need,
but our condition only got worse.
We were helpless and hopeless.
But then we heard “reports”
—the good news of God’s Kingdom under Christ!
We studied the Bible.
Our faith moved us to make positive changes in our life
and to associate with the Christian congregation.
Today, we enjoy good spiritual health and happiness.
Our faith has made it happen.
Faith has also made it possible
to accomplish things in God’s service
that perhaps we never thought we could do.
Please open your Bibles to Hebrews chapter 11.
In this portion of Paul’s letter to the Hebrews,
he focuses on faith.
He begins with a definition of faith.
But then, starting in verse 4,
Paul acts as a sort of tour guide,
walking us through the corridor
of thousands of years of Bible history.
He stops along the way
to point out the extraordinary things
that men and women of the past did
by means of faith in Jehovah God.
Just glance down the columns in this chapter
and notice how Paul introduces each paragraph
with the words “by faith.”
This expression “by faith”
appears 18 times in this one chapter.
Now, when we look at the names
Paul lists in this chapter,
we may think,
‘Well, these were spiritual “giants.”’
But in reality, they were ordinary humans
with weaknesses like all of us have today.
The thing they all had in common
was faith,
and faith in Jehovah
made it possible for them to do amazing things.
Let’s look at some of them and compare what they did
with what many of you are doing today
by faith.
Let’s read verse 5:
“By faith Enoch was transferred
“so as not to see death,
“and he was nowhere to be found
“because God had transferred him;
“for before he was transferred
“he received the witness
that he had pleased God well.”
The book of Jude, verses 14 and 15,
informs us that Enoch boldly proclaimed
that Jehovah was going to destroy
that ungodly world.
It appears that wicked, violent men
were going to take Enoch’s life
because of his bold witness.
So God chose to take him
—that is, gently cutting short his life,
sparing him the pangs of a violent death.
In modern times, like Enoch,
many brothers and sisters
have boldly declared God’s judgments
even when faced with death.
One brother, after receiving a death sentence
at Nazi hands during World War II,
wrote these words shortly before his execution:
“I have such peace, such tranquillity,
that you can’t possibly imagine!”
Faith made such boldness
and calmness possible.
In many ways, you very likely
have shown the same faith as Enoch.
By faith, you stand up to an ungodly world
by not adopting its corrupt ways.
By faith, you boldly declare God’s Word
from house to house and in public places.
Before you became a baptized Witness,
you may have thought you would never do this preaching work!
But you are doing it,
sometimes even in the face
of verbal abuse and opposition.
Faith has made it happen.
Let’s read verse 7:
“By faith Noah,
“after receiving divine warning of things not yet seen,
“showed godly fear and constructed an ark
“for the saving of his household;
“and through this faith he condemned the world,
“and he became an heir of the righteousness
that results from faith.”
Nothing in the Bible indicates
that Jehovah chose Noah to construct an ark
because he was an experienced builder.
Certainly, he never had built such a gigantic vessel
as what Jehovah had asked him to construct.
Noah likely pondered many questions:
‘How will I get all the building materials?
‘Do I have the right tools to do the job?
‘How will I gather all the animals?
‘What food will they need, and how much?
‘When, exactly, will the Deluge begin?
‘How long will it last?
Where will the ark land after the Flood subsides?’
Nothing in the record indicates
that Jehovah gave Noah all the details in advance.
What Noah did have was faith.
Faith moved him to begin building.
His faith saved him and his family.
Faith in Jehovah made it happen.
Like Noah, during this time of the end,
Jehovah’s people have taken on
challenging theocratic building projects.
Certainly, constructing the new world headquarters
at Warwick, New York,
was one of these projects that required much faith.
A committee of brothers was assigned
to complete this vast project
in less than four years.
To do so, they knew they had to begin
by July 2013.
They moved ahead in faith.
Though the town had not yet approved the site permits,
they began inviting workers to the site
with that date in mind.
Time was passing quickly.
The invited volunteers were buying plane tickets.
Bethel was arranging rooming and other details.
Yet, the committee still did not have site permits.
Would they cancel these invitations?
They state:
“We spent a lot of time praying about it.
“We decided we needed to act in faith.
“And we were just convinced
Jehovah was going to make it happen.”
As the deadline approached,
the brothers had done everything possible
to obtain the permits.
The town planning board was holding a public hearing.
And to the brothers’ great surprise,
within 15 minutes of the start of the meeting,
the town board voted to approve the project.
These overseers commented,
“When the approval came through,
“we knew it was only by Jehovah’s spirit
that that happened.”
True, but it was also the brothers’ faith
to act that made it happen.
Those experiences are found in the video
World Headquarters —History Is Being Written.
You can find it in the “Our Activities” section
under the “Construction” category.
Now let’s read Hebrews 11:8:
“By faith Abraham, when he was called,
“obeyed by going out to a place
“he was to receive as an inheritance;
“he went out, although not knowing
where he was going.”
What faith it took
for Abraham and his submissive wife, Sarah,
to leave the prosperous city of Ur
and to go wherever Jehovah would lead them!
It meant leaving the security of a pleasant home
and moving to some strange and potentially hostile land
some 1,000 miles, or 1,609 kilometers,  away.
Do we see such faith today?
Absolutely!
Since 2014,
thousands of brothers and sisters
have attended the School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
agreeing to be assigned to wherever
there is a need by the organization.
Faith has made it happen.
When a call goes out for skilled volunteers
to help build or expand branch facilities,
faith moves brothers and sisters to simplify their lives
and to leave their comfort zone in order to assist.
For example, in 2009,
the congregations in the United States were informed
that an expansion project at Wallkill, New York,
was being planned.
One couple moved out of their newly built
2,200-square-foot, or 200-square-meter, dream home
and into a 270-square-foot, or 25-square-meter, apartment
so that they could make themselves available.
What happened?
They explain:
“One month after we moved into our small apartment,
“we received an invitation to serve
“as temporary volunteers at Wallkill.
“It was clear to us that by simplifying our life,
we had given Jehovah something to bless.”
Faith made it happen for them.
So, what have we learned today?
Faith in Jehovah God is a powerful motivating force
that impels us to act in harmony with his will.
Jehovah rewards such faith.
Remember, the very meaning of the name of our God, Jehovah,
is “He Causes to Become.”
Truly, he is a God who makes things happen!
Brothers and sisters, let us continue to act in faith.
Jehovah will continue to make wonderful things
happen in our personal life.
We will accomplish things we never could do
through our own personal efforts.
We will be able to do more in Jehovah’s service.
May it happen to you “according to your faith.”

如果你已献身受浸

现在,你的病痛不会神奇地消失
因为我们要等到基督千年统治期间
才能摆脱疾病的折磨

我们在属灵、道德、情绪上生了病

也许我们不顾一切
想通过物质的东西来满足属灵需要

en.text: An introduction to the book of Lamentations.
The prophet Jeremiah composed the book of Lamentations
shortly after witnessing the siege
and destruction of Jerusalem
by Babylon in 607 B.C.E.
Jeremiah expresses deep sadness
over the catastrophe that befell Jerusalem.
The book is organized into five chapters, or poems.
In chapter 1, the city of Jerusalem
is described as a princess who is desolated by her enemies
and becomes an abandoned widow and slave
on account of her many sins.
Chapter 2 reveals that it was Jehovah himself
who brought about Jerusalem’s destruction.
Those who pass by its ruined walls
are amazed at the complete devastation.
In chapter 3, Jeremiah speaks of the desolate nation
as an afflicted man who pleads with Jehovah
to remember his pitiable and homeless state.
However, Jeremiah shows a waiting attitude
and expresses hope that Jehovah will,
in his loyal love and mercy, restore the nation.
Chapter 4 shifts attention to Jehovah’s temple.
Although it was once the glorious center of true worship,
it was now devastated.
Jeremiah relates the horrific conditions
—deprivation, famine, and death—
that existed in Jerusalem during its final siege.
Did you know?
The first four chapters are acrostic poems.
In each one, successive verses,
or groups of verses,
begin with a different letter
of the Hebrew alphabet.
Chapter 5 is written from the perspective
of Jerusalem’s former inhabitants,
who have lost their homes and freedom.
Jeremiah likens them to orphans without a father
who humbly beg Jehovah for mercy and salvation.
As you consider the five poems of Lamentations,
notice how rebellion brings divine judgment,
how repentance leads to divine mercy,
and how sorrow will give way to rejoicing
under the rule of God’s Kingdom.

en.text: Our text for discussion today,
here at Matthew 6:33,
contains two parts.
The first part is what we have to do;
it says: “Keep on, then, seeking first the Kingdom
and his righteousness.”
The second part is what Jehovah will do:
“And all these other things will be added to you.”
We think carefully about these words.
Jesus actually was educating his disciples
to make a dramatic change in their lifestyle.
What do we mean by that?
Well, look at verse 31.
He says: “So never be anxious and say,
“‘What are we to eat?’ or, ‘What are we to drink?’
or, ‘What are we to wear?’”
Did Jesus say never?
Yes!
But those are the things we normally do.
We are anxious about our existence,
and Jesus recognizes that most people are that way.
He says in verse 32:
“For all these are the things
the nations are eagerly pursuing.”
But then he says:
“Your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.”
Here in this chapter,
Jesus outlines a number of very important principles
that actually change the way we look at life
and the way we see our existence
in relationship to Jehovah God.
He puts service to Jehovah
in the first place,
regardless of our circumstances.
Let us have a look at two of these principles.
The one that’s here at Matthew 6:24,
he says:
“No one can slave for two masters;
“for either he will hate the one and love the other,
“or he will stick to the one and despise the other.
“You cannot slave
for God and for Riches.”
It is just not possible.
Some have tried, but they’ve failed.
Satan approached Jesus and said to him: ‘I will give you riches.
I’ll give you all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.’
Of course, Jesus refused. Why?
Because he knew there was a price attached to it.
What is the price?
Worship
—divided worship— which is impossible.
He knew that it is impossible
to worship both Jehovah and Riches.
In verse 21, Jesus says:
“For where your treasure is,
there your heart will be also.”
The second principle is in verse 25:
“On this account I say to you:
“Stop being anxious about your lives
“as to what you will eat or what you will drink,
or about your bodies as to what you will wear.”
And here is the principle:
“Does not life mean more than food
and the body [more] than clothing?”
You can have a storehouse full of food;
if you don’t have life, you cannot eat it.
You can have a warehouse full of clothes;
but if there’s no body, you cannot wear it.
Jesus illustrated this principle beautifully in Luke.
Turn to Luke
chapter 12
and from verse 16:
“With that he told them an illustration, saying:
“‘The land of a rich man produced well.
“‘So he began reasoning within himself,
“‘“What should I do now that I have nowhere to gather my crops?”
“‘Then he said, “I will do this:
“‘“I will tear down my storehouses and build bigger ones,
“‘“and there I will gather all my grain and all my goods,
“‘“and I will say to myself:
“‘“‘You have many good things stored up for many years;
“‘“‘take it easy, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.’”
“‘But God said to him,
“‘“Unreasonable one,
“‘“this night they are demanding your life from you.
“‘“Who, then, is to have the things you stored up?”
“‘So it goes with the man who stores up treasure for himself
but is not rich toward God.’”
Jesus didn’t say this man was dishonest
or that he’d never thought about God.
The mistake the man made was
that his priorities were wrong.
He focused primarily on amassing wealth.
He did not do what it says in verse 21.
He did not store up treasure for himself—
He ‘stored up treasure for himself,’
but did not store up treasure with God in heaven.
He was “not rich toward God.”
And that is the key element, isn’t it?
Our service to Jehovah God,
our life for Jehovah,
that is the key element.
And as Jesus says in verse 15,
the second part of verse 15:
“Because even when a person has an abundance,
“his life does not result
from the things he possesses.”
So these are
the two very important principles we’ve covered.
First of all,
make our service to God a priority
and not amassing wealth.
And the second one:
“Keep on, then, seeking first the Kingdom
“and [God’s] righteousness,
and all these other things will be added to you.”
We do not know precisely when the end will come,
but we want to keep on seeking first the Kingdom.
Rather than putting our trust in the securities of this world,
we want to put our trust in our heavenly Father.
Jehovah gives everything;
he gives more than what we need.
In Ecclesiastes 5:19,
it summarizes this whole principle.
It establishes the truth —the reality of the matter.
It says, Ecclesiastes 5:19:
“Also, when the true God gives a man riches
“and material possessions
“along with the ability to enjoy them,
“he should take his reward
“and rejoice in his hard work.
This is the gift of God.”

同时事奉耶和华和财富
这两个主人是不可能的
所以,耶稣在6:21,他说
你的财宝在哪里
你的心也在哪里
第二个原则记载在第25节
所以我告诉你们
不要再为生命忧虑吃什么、喝什么
为身体忧虑穿什么
请留意接着的原则
生命不是比食物重要吗?
身体不是比衣裳重要吗?
如果没了生命
即使有满屋子的食物,你也吃不到
如果没了身体
即使有成堆的衣服,你也没办法穿
耶稣在路加福音用了一个很好的比喻
来解释这个原则的含义
请翻开路加福音12章
我们从16节开始读
耶稣又对他们说了个比喻
有一个富翁,田产丰饶
就在心里盘算说
我的收成没有地方收藏了
怎么办呢?
他说
对了,我要把我这些仓房拆掉
建造更大的
我要把我的五谷和美物全都收藏在那里
我要告诉自己说
你积蓄了许多美物,够多年享用
只管优哉游哉,吃喝快乐吧!
可是上帝对他说
不明事理的人
今天晚上就要取你的性命
你所积存的要归谁呢?
谁为自己积蓄财宝
在上帝眼中却不富足,也是这样
耶稣没有说这位富翁不是个老实人
也没有说他从不把上帝放在眼里
富翁的问题是,他没有分清主次
他的目光集中在积聚财富
像21节说的
他“为自己积蓄财宝”
却没有为自己积存天上的财宝
所以在上帝眼中并不富足
没错
献出自己,为耶和华服务是个关键
就像耶稣在15节下半部说的
因为人不管怎样富裕
他的生命也不在于他拥有的财物
今天,我们学了两个重要的原则
第一
我们应该把事奉上帝置于生活首位
而不是老想着赚钱
第二
要不断先追求王国和上帝的正义
这一切别的东西也必赐给我们了
虽然不知道终结什么时候会来
我们还是决心不断先追求王国
我们绝不会投靠这个世界
相反,我们全心信赖我们的天父
耶和华给我们的
常常超过我们所需要的
传道书5:19
为今天的原则做了个有力的总结
也道出了一项重要的真理
传道书5:19说
上帝赐谁财富资产
就让谁能够享用
得着应有的成果
在辛劳中欢乐
这是上帝的恩赐

title: 로키 웨브: 우리는 모두 시험을 받을 겁니다

en.text: When we build strong faith in times of peace,
we can find courage during times of testing and persecution.
Brother Rocky Webb from the United States
learned to be a fighter as a young man.
But as his faith grew, he learned that Jehovah is there
“to help us and to fight our battles.”
All of us are going to be tested one way or the other
before we make it into the new world.
And if we can endure those tests faithfully,
faithfully, then we’ll make it.
My dad and my mother taught me the truth.
What drove me to be baptized
was the convention in Washington, D.C.
Brother Rutherford gave the talk on “the meek shall inherit the earth.”
It touched my heart in a way that it’s never left
from that minute on, right on up to now.
It gave me faith to stay
with Jehovah all the way.
The bullies would come and jump onto me,
and I would come home pretty well beat up.
So that’s when I started training for boxing.
I was offered $40,000 for a fight —win or lose.
And if I won the second fight, they would double the amount.
Brother Macmillan was like a second dad to me and my brother.
And he asked me, and he said, “Would you do me a favor?”
He said, “Don’t put the gloves on no more.”
And so I didn’t put them on anymore.
I think he knew that it wouldn’t be very long
before there’d be an article on it.
It came out and told that boxing wasn’t for Christians.
I was drafted during this time,
and I refused to serve and was sent to prison.
All the time,
I never, never, ever slowed down
on my theocratic deals,
never.
I kept right on on it.
The jail warden overheard me
witnessing to another inmate.
He told me,
“Don’t do anymore of that.”
He said, “We don’t allow it here.”
Three days had passed by, and he’d seen me talking to him again.
And they put me in a car that was shaded
—you couldn’t see out.
I didn’t know where I was going.
It was an old, old prison,
just dark as could be in there.
It was three feet (1 m) around.
And they called it “the Sweat Box.”
All the time I was in there, I’d just sweat, sweat, sweat.
And I went in weighing 213 pounds (97 kg),
and I came out weighing 133 pounds (60 kg).
Psalm 144 says:
“May Jehovah, my Rock, be praised,
“who trains my hands for battle,
my fingers for warfare.”
I gave my life
to give Jehovah my faith.
I lived in Wewoka.
Several congregations would come together to work.
We were confronted by mobs.
There were a lot of them that were injured.
I had 80 stitches up here,
and I had 13 in the side there,
on each stab.
I was really, really beat up.
But I couldn’t have stood up if it hadn’t been for Jehovah.
I knew he was with me some way or another.
So we sued the town and won $20,000.
The Society called us and said:
“You did very good in what all you’ve done”
but said, “Remember, we’re not out for money.
Make sure that that’s made known to them.”
When we walked up to the desk,
they slid the papers out to us
and said, “Sign them up.”
And we just took them and slid them back.
It came out in the papers,
‘Tell them to come back and do all they want to do
in the way of their witnessing.’
It said, ‘We won’t touch them.’
They really highly respected us for what we did,
and so that opened it up.
And we had a real good congregation there
that got started and everything.
My first wife was a blessing for me,
but when she died,
Jehovah stepped in and gave me another good one.
We mow the lawns together.
No, no, we do most everything together.
We study to where we can feel it in our hearts.
When you give your faith to Jehovah,
you’re giving your life to him.
He’s permitted these things to come upon me;
I knew that.
But he protected me.
Brother Webb is now 94 years old.
But as we saw, he and his wife, Charlene,
keep themselves spiritually active.
What lessons did you see in Rocky’s experience?
For one, we heard that Rocky learned to be a boxer
to protect himself from bullies;
yet he responded in faith to loving counsel to quit
—even before God’s people
had a clear understanding of violent sports.
Making that change
helped Rocky to continue cultivating
a Christlike personality.
That prepared him to stand firm
when imprisoned for his faith,
and it helped him to not return evil for evil
when persecuted for his ministry.
He had faith that although Jehovah
permitted these things to happen,
He was also there to protect him.
Examples like those of Rocky and the others we’ve considered
warm our hearts and let us know
we’re never alone in our fight for the faith.

cn.text: 我们在平静的日子建立坚强的信心
遇到考验和迫害时就会大有力量
来自美国的洛奇‧韦布弟兄
在年轻时成了拳击手
随着信心不断增加
他明白耶和华会“帮助我们,为我们作战”
我们每个人在进入新世界之前
都一定会面对考验
只要我们能在考验下保持忠贞
忠贞到底
就能进入新世界
我在父母的教导下认识真理
在华盛顿特区举行的一个区域大会中
卢述福弟兄发表了一个演讲
题目是“谦和的人必承受大地”
那个演讲使我决定受浸
当时的感动我到今天还记得
使我有信心对耶和华忠贞到底
有些恶霸会攻击我
打得我满身是伤
所以我开始练拳击
有人找我去打拳击
不论输赢,一场都可以赚四万块
要是赢了第二场,钱就会加倍
麦克米伦弟兄对我们兄弟来说
就像第二个父亲
他对我说
“拜托,别再练拳了,好吗?”
所以我就不再练拳击了
他说不定早就知道相关的文章快出版了
文章提到基督徒不该从事拳击运动
后来,我被征召入伍
并因拒服兵役被关进监狱
我从来、从来都没有
在崇拜上帝方面缓慢下来
我仍然卯足全力
有一次
典狱长听到我跟一位狱友做见证
他警告我说
不准再这么做!
这里是不允许你这么做的
三天后,他又看到我跟那位狱友说话
他们就把我丢进一辆被罩起来的车子里
我完全看不到外面
也不知道要开往哪去
我被送到一间很旧很旧的监禁室
那里很暗,伸手不见五指
这个监禁室的范围大概1公尺
他们称那为“蒸汗室”
我在里面一直流汗一直流汗
被关进去之前,我97公斤
我出来的时候剩60公斤
诗篇144篇说
我把一生献给耶和华
表明我对他的忠心
我住在韦沃卡
当时几群会众会一起传道
我们被暴民攻击
很多人都受伤
我这边缝了80针
这边也是
被刺的每个伤口都缝了13针
真的被打得很惨
当时要不是有耶和华的帮助
我一定站不起来
但我知道耶和华一定在支持我
后来我们打赢了官司
他们得赔偿我们两万块
分部打电话跟我们说
你们做得很好
但记住,我们这么做不是为了钱
要确保他们的人也知道这一点
所以我们走到柜台
他们把文件递给我们说
“快点签了!”
但我们没签名就把文件递还给他们
他们很尊敬我们所做的决定
就这样打开了在当地做见证的大门
他们登报说
让那群人回来用他们想要的方式传道吧
我们不会再伤害他们了
后来我们还在那里建立了会众
好消息也渐渐传开了
我的第一任妻子对我来说是个福分
但她去世之后
耶和华又赐给我另一位美好的伴侣
我们会一起在院子除草
哦,不只!
我们几乎所有的事都是一起做的
我们一起研读,让资料打动我们的心
当你全心信赖耶和华
就是把你的一生都献给他了
我知道我经历的种种遭遇,都是他允许的
但他也保护了我!
韦布弟兄今年94岁
像我们看到的
他和妻子雪琳
仍然在崇拜活动上保持活跃
我们从洛奇的经历学到什么呢?
当初他本来为了不再被恶霸攻击
去学拳击
即使当时上帝的子民对暴力的运动
还没有明确的理解
但当他受到仁慈的劝告后
就不再从事这项运动了
做出这种调整
使洛奇能继续培养像基督一样的好品格
这帮助他在被监禁期间保持忠贞
就算在传道时受迫害,也不以恶报恶
他坚信
虽然耶和华容许这些事发生在他身上
但耶和华也保护了他
洛奇以及其他人的经历
都让我们感到非常温馨
也知道在这场信心的保卫战上
我们并非孤军奋斗

en.text: We were brought up in a small town in Saskatchewan.
It was friendly.
I don’t think they moved to other places.
They stayed right there.
One time, our father said:
“Why do you have to go so far as India?
Why can’t you preach in Canada?”
Dad was very strict.
Very strict.
When we were out playing and he came out and called us,
we had to come immediately.
They were strict.
Don’t question; just do what you’re told.
Yeah, do what you’re told.
Yeah. That’s right.
Strict.
My father was the one that was interested,
but he never came into the truth.
He enjoyed having Witnesses come to our home,
but he never ever thought
of himself as being one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Coming into the truth, I think, changed our life,
and we had a different purpose.
So that was when we decided,
“Well, I guess we should pioneer now too.”
And we only pioneered two years,
and we were called to Gilead.
So then we graduated in 1953.
On your application for Gilead, one question is:
Are you willing to go any place in the world?
Brother Knorr always would say, “A one-way ticket.”
So that was on your mind.
We were happy to go.
And if we didn’t get back, that was OK.
And then the 13 of us, for one month,
we all went together back to India
on a ship.
Well, we were a bit nervous because we didn’t know
just what kind of people we would be meeting
or what kind of atmosphere we’d be experiencing.
That was why it was a shock when we landed in Bombay
because all we could see
was people, people everywhere and noise.
And then they gave us such hot food.
We were burning all the way down.
And then when we arrived there, the missionary home had no furniture
and we had to sleep on the floor for quite a few months
before the furniture was made.
We boiled our water; we filtered our water.
When we went to the market, we’d bring all our vegetables and fruit home
and we washed them with a solution.
And we were very careful in that respect.
It was all a shock to us in many things.
Yes.
We made up our mind, I guess,
that it’s not going to be the same as Canada, we know.
We didn’t worry about the things we had to put up with
because we had the joy in the ministry.
The Society wanted us to get the Joy booklet out,
and we had to just stand on the street with this carton of literature
and just keep calling out to the people,
and everybody would take it.
And they were so appreciative, really appreciative.
Yeah, they were. Yeah.
In those days, we had to put in 150 hours.
And in South India, after 4:00 p.m.,
women were not out.
So we had to get all our time in
early in the morning and work right through until four o’clock.
We sure did.
We were using the Malayalam language,
and the children repeated what we said.
They’d run ahead and tell people
what we were talking about.
And they’d all yell, “Ma’damma, ma’damma.”
“White woman, white woman.”
Yeah, and we had many studies then.
We enjoyed the ministry, and we enjoyed the hospitality.
Be with the brothers and go to their homes
and eat their food and do things the way they do things.
So we had to make India our home.
We lived in India about 50 years.
And then the news came that we had to leave.
So that was why the Governing Body said,
“Well, you go to the Canada branch then.”
Well, it was like a culture shock too after being so many years in India.
Yes.
A lot of things we had to sort of adjust to here now.
I’m working down in the laundry, folding.
Same.
Folding and folding until we fold in.
Well, we always tell the younger ones
to be in the full-time service serving Jehovah.
This, we think, is a wonderful life to choose.
It’s good for the young people to learn when they’re young like that.
And, no doubt, they’ll make progress in the truth too.
We’re glad we started pioneering and moved about.
Yeah. We lacked nothing, really.
We have nothing to complain about.

我们在外面玩的时候

改变了我们的生活

我们决定做先驱

诺尔弟兄总是说,这是张单程票
我们都心里有数
我们高兴地上路了
如果真的一去不回,也没有关系
我们13个人
坐了一个月的船到达印度

会体验到怎样的文化

人山人海,非常热闹

在这方面,我们很谨慎
什么事都跟家乡很不一样
我们告诉自己
在这里,一切肯定都跟加拿大不一样
我们并不担心要适应各种困难
因为传道工作带来很多喜乐
组织要我们分发《喜乐》册子
当时我们只要把一整箱的刊物搬到街上
并大声呼喊
路过的人都会来拿
人们的反应都非常、非常好    -对啊
那时候,我们一个月传道150个小时
在印度南部
妇女下午四点后就不会外出
为了达到时间定额
我们一大早就会出门传道
直到下午四点
是啊
我们说的是马拉亚拉姆语
孩子们会复述我们的话
他们会跑在前面
告诉别人我们在讲什么
他们会大喊
“Ma’damma, ma’damma”
意思是白人妇女
我们有很多圣经学生

和他们慷慨好客的精神
到弟兄姊妹的家坐坐
吃当地的食物
学习他们的生活习惯
我们把印度当作自己的家
在那里住了将近50年
后来收到通知要离开那里
中央长老团告诉我们

在印度那么多年了,要再回到这里
又是另一次的文化冲击
对啊

我们常常鼓励年轻人参与全时服务
事奉耶和华
我们觉得这是最棒的生活
趁他们还年轻的时候学习是最好的
当然,他们和上帝的关系也会更加深厚
我们很庆幸自己做先驱,到外地传道
是啊,没什么好抱怨的
我们真的一无所缺
