en.text: Jehovah gives us his holy spirit,
both individually and as a group.
To see evidence of that, we need only go to a part of the world
where Jehovah’s people were put under intense pressure.
In South Africa, for example,
the government’s policy of racial segregation, called apartheid,
lasted for 46 years, until 1994.
Our brothers were pressured to take sides in armed conflict.
Their freedom to worship together was limited.
And the prevailing attitudes towards people of different races
threatened their unity.
In this report, we learn how our South African brothers
remained united and neutral and in support of God’s Kingdom.
One afternoon when we came to the station,
there were men who were directing things and we were directed
to a coach for whites only.
That was the first time
that we saw apartheid being law enforced.
You could not leave the black areas
where your home was without getting a permit.
We were even given a permit that stipulated which area we were allowed
to do the preaching work in.
People would always ask us:
“What are you doing to fight apartheid?”
We had to boldly tell them:
“God’s Kingdom is the only solution.
“God will help the whole earth to live in peace one day,
so we cannot take sides on political issues now.”
Here at home in Soweto, we heard the sound
of children running in the streets.
We heard the sound of gunshots;
tear gas was everywhere.
When my husband came home that day,
we sat with the children and took out the book
Your Youth—Getting the Best out of It
and we studied the topic “How Do You View Your Parents?”
This was appropriate
because children had the spirit of rebelling
against their own parents.
They went as far as burning people.
They came shouting my son’s name:
“Aquila, Mathiba, come out, come out!”
And one of them defended him and said:
“No, no, no, not Aquila!
“Aquila does not do these things.
He will never protest.”
Ahh, I saw Jehovah’s hand in this.
Even under those circumstances,
Jehovah helped our children
not to dwell on the madness in the streets,
and we focused on spiritual things.
In 1968, when I was 19 years old,
I was sentenced to jail
for refusing to do military service.
Over a period of 20 years,
close to 1,000 young white Witness men
similarly took their stand for neutrality in this country.
We used to pray for our white brothers in prison.
People in the black townships respected us
for the stand these brothers were taking.
over 30,000 black and white brothers met
for the afternoon session of the “Divine Victory” Assembly.
When we first arrived,
there were policemen everywhere.
But after half an hour,
they saw how peaceful it was
and so they left.
For those few hours
in the dark era of apartheid,
we felt
the glorious brotherly love as we praised Jehovah
together.
Brother Moses Nyamussua was asked
by a group on their way to a political rally
to weld weapons for them.
He refused to do so.
After their rally, they went back to him and said:
“You refused to weld our weapons,
“and some of our comrades were killed in a fight at the rally.
Now you will die.”
Brother Nyamussua maintained his neutrality
all the way to death,
and Jehovah will remember him.
In 1993, I was amazed
when a white person came preaching house to house.
They came with another white man
who could speak Venda fluently.
That excited me a lot, and as time went by,
I came to realize
that this is the true religion because they were faithful friends
and they spoke to me like we were family.
In the late 1980’s, the government granted us permission
to come in and build Kingdom Halls
in the black townships.
The local community was absolutely amazed
to see all these whites
pouring in and working hard
along with their black brothers
to build these beautiful Kingdom Halls.
It was a wonderful privilege to get to know other young people
of different races.
Everyone in the congregation feels like family
as long as they serve Jehovah.
Just see yourself.
Just see me too.
Just see us all. . .
. . . in a world that is new.
Today, in South Africa,
there are more than 100,000 Witnesses
worshipping together in spirit and truth.
South Africa has 11 official languages.
Yet, across that cultural variety,
our brothers and sisters are all speaking the “pure language”
—the truth about Jehovah God and his purposes.

title: 마크 누매어: 충절을 지킬 수 있도록 기도하십시오 (마태 26:2)

ko.text: “그때에 예수께서 제자들과 함께 겟세마네라는 곳으로 가서 그들에게
‘내가 저기 가서 기도하는 동안 여기 앉아 있으십시오’ 하고 말씀하셨다.”
네, 온 인류의 영원한 미래가 예수의 어깨에 지워져 있었죠.
그렇지 못한다면 그건 여호와를 배신하는 것이나 다름없다는 걸 예수는 잘 알았죠.
이 순간 예수께 가장 중요한 것은
죽은 사람도 부활시키고 기적도 행할 수 있지.
창조 작업에 참여한 우주에서 두 번째로 위대한 존재야.
하지만 지금 난 그런 것에 의지하지 않을 거야.
초자연적인 힘이나 타고난 능력에 의지하지 않을 거야.
내 아버지에게 의지하고 그분을 바라볼 거야.
그래, 지금 이 순간 내게 꼭 필요한 건
내가 오늘 아버지께 영예를 돌리는 방식으로 내 생명을 내어 주고
충절을 지키는 사람이 되려면, 기도를 해야 해.
난 저기 가서 기도를 할 거야.’
“두려움과 떨림”으로 지금 ‘우리의 구원을 이루어 나가야’ 한다는 것입니다.
그리고 여러 해 동안 봉사하면서 충실히 해 온 일들이
마치 신세계로 가는 승차권이라고 생각하지 않도록 주의해야 합니다.
해야 할 일은 바로 기도하는 것입니다.
큰 환난이 이제 코 앞으로 다가왔으므로 지금은 우리가 자기 점검을 해 보아야 할 때입니다.
만약 자신이 노란 색 신호등을 무시하고 달리고 있다는 걸 알게 되었다면,
자신의 아버지 여호와 하느님께 치욕이 될 수 있다는 걸 아셨기 때문입니다.
그건 예수에게 너무나 견디기 힘든 일이었고, 그래서 몹시 비통해했습니다.
자신의 안위나 명성이 아니라 아버지의 이름과 명성 때문이었습니다.
여기서 또 한 가지 교훈을 얻게 됩니다.
오해를 받아서, 또는 어떤 특별한 임명을 받지 못했기 때문입니까?
우리는 여호와의 이름, 그 이름에 치욕이 돌아가는 것에 대해 비통해합니다.
그래서 그 이름을 영예롭게 하기 위해 가능한 모든 일을 하고자 합니다.
우리가 이곳 미국 베델에서 일하는 건
우리가 받은 임명, 우리에게 주신 일들,
이곳에서 그분을 섬기며 공석에서든 사석에서든 그분의 이름에 영예를 돌리고
그 어떤 치욕도 초래하지 않는 것,
여호와께 모독이 돌아간다는 생각만으로도 우리는 몹시 비통해하고 괴로워해야 합니다.
여호와는 바로 우리 옆에 앉은 사람처럼
“그리고 조금 앞으로 나아가 얼굴을 숙이고 엎드려 기도하셨다.”
그분이 느꼈을 중압감을 한번 생각해 보시죠.
“그분이 몹시 괴로워서 더욱 간절히 계속 기도하시니, 땀이 핏방울같이 되어 땅에 떨어졌다.”
핏방울같이 된 땀이 얼굴을 타고 흘러내렸습니다.
사랑하는 아들이 형주에 매달려 잔혹하게 취급받는 모습을 지켜 보면서,
아버지께서 얼마나 큰 아픔을 겪으실지 예수는 너무나도 잘 아셨습니다.
그 이유 때문에 예수께서 베드로에게 그토록 강하게 반응하신 겁니다.
그분이 앞으로 자신이 죽어야 한다는 점을 제자들에게 설명하시자
베드로가 ‘주여, 자신에게 좀 더 너그러워지십시오. 그런 일은 일어나지 않을 것입니다’라고 했죠.
내가 이곳에서 지금 땀이 핏방울로 변할 정도로 괴로운데 나에게 좀 더 너그러워지라고?’
예수에게 있어서, 지금은 자신에게 너그러워질 때가 아니었습니다.
그 말은 걸림돌이 될 수 있는 말이었죠.
“아버지, 가능하다면 이 잔을 제게서 지나가게 해 주십시오.”
‘당신의 이름에 불명예를 돌리는 이 잔은 제가 감당할 수 없으니 이 잔이 지나가게 해 주십시오.’
하지만 여호와께서 원하시는 방식은 그것이 아니었고,
그래서 그리스도는 자신의 뜻을 여호와의 뜻과 일치시키셨습니다.
그분은 자신의 기도를 여호와께서 듣고 계시며, 자신의 간청이 하늘에 올라갔다는 걸 아셨습니다.
자신이 하늘에 있을 때 아버지께서 기도에 응답하시는 모습을 지켜 보셨으니까요.
맏아들로서 하늘에서 아버지와 함께 계셨을 때 그 증거를 보았죠.
아버지께서 한나나 룻, 다윗 같은 사람들의 간청과 청원에 응답하시는 모습을 보셨습니다.
동일한 사건을 묘사한 복음서 기록을 보면, 이때 한 천사가 와서 예수를 격려했다고 알려 줍니다.
분명, 그 천사는 예수께서 하늘에 계실 때 알고 지내던 천사였을 겁니다.
그 천사는 “아버지께서 당신을 승인하십니다”라는 안심이 되는 말을 하면서,
그날 밤을 지탱할 힘을 예수께 주었습니다.
그 천사가 예수에게 그의 죽음이 아버지의 이름에 치욕이 되는 것이 아니라, 오히려
여호와 하느님께서 바로 예수의 죽음을 통해 자신의 이름을 거룩하게 하실 거라고 말했을 수 있다는 점입니다.
예수를 그토록 짓누르던 바로 그 점에 대해 여호와께서는
“아니다. 치욕이 아니라 내 이름을 거룩하게 하는 데 너의 죽음을 사용할 것이다”라고 하신 거죠.
우리가 기억해야 할 중요한 교훈은 이겁니다.
우리가 우리의 뜻을 여호와의 뜻과 일치시킬 때,
여호와께서 우리의 충성스러운 행동을 어떻게 사용하실지 우리가 어떻게 알겠습니까?
쉽지 않을 때에도 여호와의 뜻을 실천한다면,
그것이 차곡차곡 쌓여서 마귀에게 불리한 증거로 사용될 수 있습니다.
“이것 좀 봐라! 저 사람이 내 이름을 거룩하게 하고 있다.
이 베델 성원도 저 베델 성원도 나를 거룩하게 하고 있다.”
우리가 절대 잊을 수 없는 영예입니다.
여기 “일어나 갑시다”라는 말씀 이면에 담긴 강한 힘을 생각해 보십시오.
“이제 무릎을 털고 일어나 전투를 시작할 시간입니다.
나는 일어나 유다의 배신을 당하겠습니다. 나는 일어나 불법 재판을 당하겠습니다.
나는 일어나 형주에 달리고, 빰을 맞고, 구타를 당하고, 끔찍한 방식으로 못박히겠습니다.
우리는 시련을 당당히 마주할 수 있게 해 달라고 하느님께 간청합니다.
우리는 기도하고 일어나 일을 계속해 나갑니다.
예수는 아버지께 간구의 기도를 드렸기 때문에 충실을 증명하실 수 있었습니다.
여호와께서 우리에게도 그렇게 할 힘을 주시기 바랍니다.

en.text: Let’s open our Bibles, please,
to Matthew chapter 26,
and we will begin at verse 36.
Matthew 26:36:
“Then Jesus came with them [his disciples]
“to the spot called Gethsemane,
“and he said to [his] disciples:
“‘Sit down here while I go over there
[to] pray.’”
“While I go over there [to] pray.”
The eternal future of all mankind rested on Jesus’ shoulders.
His remaining faithful to God was essential.
He knew that if he did not remain faithful,
it would be a slap in the face of Jehovah.
It was prayer at this time in his life
that was the most important thing.
‘Yes, I am perfect;
‘I have supernatural powers;
‘I can resurrect the dead; I can perform miracles;
‘I’m the second greatest personage in the universe;
‘I shared in the creation.
‘But no, I’m not depending on that at this time.
‘I’m not depending on supernatural powers and natural abilities.
‘I’m depending on my Father; I’m leaning on him.
‘It is prayer; it is supplication.
‘That’s what I am depending on at this time.
‘I need my Father’s help.
‘If I’m going to surrender my life today in a way
‘that brings honor to him and remain as an integrity keeper,
‘I need to pray.
So I’m going over there to pray.’
The first valuable lesson we learn right here is
that we ‘work out our salvation’ today “with fear and trembling.”
We’re careful that overconfidence does not overtake us
or just thinking that years of service
or somehow past acts of loyalty
would be a license into the new world.
No! Now is the time to pray.
Now is the time.
As we come into the great tribulation —it’s in the offing—
now is the time to take stock of ourselves.
And if we find ourselves running any yellow lights
and we haven’t gotten in an accident yet,
now is the time to put on the brakes.
Now is the time to “go over there and pray.”
Let’s read verse 37:
“And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee,
he began to feel grieved and . . . greatly troubled.”
Verse 38, and He said: “I am deeply grieved, even to death.”
This was no act.
This was no show.
Jesus’ feelings were real.
He was deeply grieved, greatly troubled.
Why? Because he knew his death
as a criminal on a stake
would be a reproach to his Father, Jehovah God.
That’s what he was concerned about
—blaspheming his Father, being accused of cursing God.
It was just too much for him to bear.
This is what grieves him greatly,
not himself and his reputation
but his Father’s name and reputation.
So again, think about the lesson that we learn.
What is the most important thing in our life?
What are we deeply grieved about?
Being misunderstood
or not getting a particular privilege, and so forth?
No, that’s not what grieves us.
What grieves us is Jehovah’s name,
bringing reproach on that name.
We want to do everything we can to honor that name.
Here we are as the United States Bethel family.
And we owe it to Jehovah, because of our privileges
and what he has allowed us to do,
to be here and to serve him
—honoring his name and bringing no reproach,
whether in public or in private.
That’s our goal.
We should feel deeply grieved and sorely troubled
in just the thought of bringing reproach upon Jehovah.
And Jehovah is just as real to us
as the person sitting next to us.
Now let’s read verse 39:
“And going a little way forward,
“he fell facedown,
praying.”
He falls “facedown, praying.”
Think of the intensity that he was under.
“Facedown, praying.”
Luke reports that at this point,
He got “into an agony”
and “he continued praying more earnestly;
and his sweat became as drops of blood.”
“Facedown, praying.”
Facedown and his sweat becoming drops of blood.
He was keenly aware of the pain of what his Father would go through
as He would watch His beloved Son
put on a stake and treated in such a barbaric fashion.
He knew that.
No wonder,
no wonder that during his ministry
when he’s explaining to his disciples that he would have to die,
no wonder he reacted so strongly to Peter’s words
when Peter said: ‘Be kind to yourself, Lord;
this isn’t going to happen to you.’
‘Be kind to yourself; this isn’t going to happen to you.’
‘What? “Be kind” to myself.
‘Here I am in this garden;
‘my sweat has become as drops of blood;
and you’re telling me “be kind” to myself.’
No wonder He said: “Get behind me, Satan!”
What a strong rebuke.
Because in Jesus’ mind,
no, this is not a time to “be kind” to himself.
Those were words that could have caused a stumbling block.
Now, let’s go further in verse 39:
“My Father, if it is possible,
let this cup pass away from me.”
Let the cup, the cup of reproach,
the cup of dishonoring your name —I can’t handle that—
let it pass away; but Jehovah didn’t.
Jehovah said: “No. This is the way I want it to be.”
So Christ lined up his will along with Jehovah’s will.
And he knew Jehovah was hearing him;
he knew this supplication was ascending to the heavens.
He knew because from his prehuman existence
he watched his Father answer prayers.
He watched it.
He saw evidence when he was the Firstborn
there in the heavens with his Father.
He watched his Father answer these supplications and pleadings
of whether it be Hannah or Ruth or David.
He saw that.
So he knew, ‘My Father is listening and will answer this prayer,’
and He did,
because, again, the Gospel accounts that parallel this say
that an angel was sent to encourage Jesus at this time.
What an encouragement that angel must have been!
Obviously, Jesus would have known him from His prehuman existence.
He gave reassuring words,
“You have your Father’s favor”;
he gave Him fresh strength to continue that night.
And it is of interest that apparently
that angel was able to tell Jesus
that your death will not be of reproach
on your Father’s name.
In fact, your death is going to be the very thing
that Jehovah God uses to sanctify his name.
So the very thing that was weighing on Jesus so much,
Jehovah said: “No, it won’t reproach me.
I am going to use it to sanctify my name.”
So just think about how encouraged Jesus was by that.
And the lesson for you and for me,
again another vital lesson:
How do you know
how Jehovah uses our acts of loyalty
when we line up our will with his?
Even when it’s not easy, we do what Jehovah asks us to do.
These acts of loyalty are piling up,
and it’s evidence that he can use against the Devil to say:
“Look! Look!
“That is sanctifying my name.
That Bethelite is sanctifying me, that Bethelite and that Bethelite.”
You see, that’s an honor that we never want to forget.
Finally, verse 46:
“Get up, let us go. . . .
My betrayer has drawn near.”
“Get up.” What did he mean by those words?
Think of the power behind them: “Get up, let us go.”
The time for prayer is over; now it’s time for action.
It’s as if Jesus was saying:
“It’s time to rise from my knees
“and get up and go into the battle.
“Let me get up and be betrayed by Judas;
“let me get up and be subjected to an illegal trial;
“let me get up and be put on that torture stake,
“slapped, beaten, and even nailed in an excruciating manner.
“It’s time to do it. Let’s do it.
Get up. Let’s go.”
We kneel before God so that we may stand erect
to face our challenges.
So, what a powerful lesson that is, again, for you and me.
We pray, we pray, and then it’s time to get up.
We get up; go to work.
Get up; go hit the publications.
Get up; go in the field service.
In other words, we pray and we get up and we follow through.
Christ Jesus proved faithful
because of supplication in prayer that he uttered to his Father,
and may Jehovah give us the strength to do the same.

en.text: We now have a special treat.
Brother Stephen Lett of the Governing Body
will give a talk based on a specific Bible verse.
His talk is “‘Sing Out Joyfully’ to Jehovah!”
Mark my words, this is a special treat!
I hope I can live up to his comments.
David did it as he played on his harp.
The Levites did it regularly at the temple.
Jesus did it shortly before being executed.
Paul and Silas did it while in stocks, deep in a prison dungeon.
The resurrected anointed do it
as they stand before Jehovah’s throne.
What activity are we talking about?
We’re talking about singing songs of praise to Jehovah.
And, of course, all of us want to imitate these fine Bible examples.
But now, how do we want to sing these songs?
What approach?
Well, let’s go to 1 Chronicles 15,
and let’s see how we want to sing
these songs of praise.
First Chronicles 15:16:
“David then told the chiefs of the Levites
“to appoint their brothers the singers,”
now notice, “to sing out joyfully,
“accompanied by musical instruments:
stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals.”
Now, does this scripture say that we should move our lips
but with no sound coming out of our mouth?
Can you imagine Jesus singing like that?
Does this scripture indicate we should mumble our words?
speak in an undertone, like we do sometimes when we read the Bible?
No, we’re told “to sing out”!
That means, obviously, enthusiastically projecting our voices.
Perhaps you remember a picture
in the inside cover pages of one of our previous songbooks.
It was a picture of the Levites singing.
And obviously they were projecting their voices.
In fact, their mouths were so wide open, you could almost see their tonsils.
Well, good example for us.
Think about this:
Many worldly people will sing out
worldly songs with a joyful attitude.
Well, much more so to our God,
who is worthy of such worshipful praise,
do we want to give it to him enthusiastically.
But now let’s look at a brief video
that highlights some of the history of how Jehovah’s people
have always felt about singing songs of praise to Jehovah.
I love singing to Jehovah.
It’s something that I find so personally strengthening.
I think it’s such a wonderful privilege
to be able to praise
Jehovah’s name by singing.
Mind you, I would never be called a professional singer.
We know that birds sing,
but they’re not singing praises to Jehovah.
And, of course, dogs bark and cats meow,
but humans can really sing and praise Jehovah with their words.
And it always reminds me of the account in the book of Acts,
Acts chapter 16,
where it talks about the apostle Paul and Silas when they were in prison.
It says: “But about the middle of the night,
“Paul and Silas were praying
“and praising God with song,
and the prisoners were listening to them.”
Obviously, the songs that they sang at that time
helped them to ease the pain of their very sore backs;
they had been beaten.
So the spiritual side of us becomes stronger when we sing.
In our organization
from the very beginning, hymns were used.
But then the brothers and sisters
began producing their own songs,
and they put them into a book form.
Back in 1944, we released a songbook
that was called the Kingdom Service Songbook.
And after a half million copies had been released
and just six years later (1950),
we came out with a brand new songbook, Songs to Jehovah’s Praise.
Now, no doubt many of the brothers wondered,
‘Why are we doing this?’
But, of course, you see,
the New World Translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures
had just been released in 1950.
And then we’ve had several books that have been released
down through the decades.
So it’s always been a part of the modern-day worship.
You know, when you ponder what we’ve discussed thus far,
you’re probably beginning to ask yourself,
‘When are we going to get our new songbook?’
Well, I must tell you that the songbook project
has proved to be more challenging,
more complex than the Governing Body anticipated.
But, nevertheless, despite the challenges and the complications,
we’re confident that we’re going to be able to release this book
to you within less than 12 months.
In fact, we’re talking about much less than 12 months.
We’re talking about right now!
The Governing Body is very happy to release . . .
I don’t think I had most of you fooled.
We are so happy to release this new songbook,
entitled “Sing Out Joyfully” to Jehovah.
That’s the “SOJJ” book, Brother Herd.
This new songbook, “Sing Out Joyfully” to Jehovah,
is being provided in three formats:
There’s the small and the large with musical notations,
and then there’s (in the large size only) lyrics only.
And you’re going to be able to obtain your personal copy
electronically in English.
This will be Monday, October the 3rd.
So we’re talking about just two days from now.
You can go on jw.org,
Watchtower ONLINE LIBRARY,
or JW Library,
and you can get that copy of this beautiful songbook.
But now, here’s a question,
How soon are we going to sing songs from the new songbook?
Well, you’ll be happy to know that beginning in January,
just three months from now,
English-speaking congregations will begin to sing these new songs.
And you’ll be happy to know, too,
that the Governing Body has arranged for a new provision
to come along with the new songbook.
We’re going to have the lyrics in video format.
Now, we enjoyed right here having the lyrics on the screen,
and we enjoyed it during the summer conventions
—the regional and the special conventions.
Instead of having to look down
and try to look at your songbook or your tablet,
we were able to hold our heads erect
and sing out joyfully to Jehovah.
Well, you’ll be able to do that in the congregation.
But now, we talked about receiving our songbook electronically,
and we noticed that many of you are using electronic devices
in order to receive the publications and to use them.
And this is commendable.
This saves the organization considerable funds.
But what if you want a hard copy of the new songbook?
Well, we’re happy to inform you that you can order
through the congregation a hard copy.
Within a few days, English-speaking congregations
and also several other foreign-language speaking congregations
will receive a letter
telling you how you may submit the order.
And we’re happy to inform you too
that the hard copy songbook will have,
whether it’s the small or the large,
it’ll have the same beautiful gray deluxe cover
that our revised New World Translation Bible has.
So what a beautiful compliment the songbook will be to the Bible.
For those who use hard copy,
you will truly enjoy using
the beautiful “gray twins.”
But now, we talked about English mostly.
What about other languages?
Well, translations are being made into other languages as we speak.
And as soon as possible, these other language releases will be made.
In fact, I’ve been informed
that there will be quite a number of other languages.
We’ll be able to release the songbook in those languages
within less than 12 months.
And this time, I’m not teasing.
But additional information will be provided as soon as available.
But now, let’s discuss some interesting information
about the new songbook.
First, we’re going to talk about the composition of the songs
and then a little bit about the structure of the songbook.
But now you’re probably thinking:
‘Why is Brother Splane not presenting this information?
Why is Brother Lett trying to present this?’
Well, I can understand your question;
I had the same question.
But the truth is,
all seven members of the Governing Body love, very much,
singing songs of praise to Jehovah.
Of course, some are a lot better singers than the rest of us.
And all of us are happy that we don’t have student singing assignments
on the midweek meeting
because we wouldn’t want to send the brothers running for their earplugs.
But now I’ve got to get serious.
Let’s talk about the composition of the songs.
Well, here’s an interesting point:
Rather than request contributed songs from various songwriters,
the Governing Body assigned a composer
and a lyricist team to work specifically on the project.
And then the Governing Body closely supervised that team.
For example, providing subject themes for songs
that would be very relevant to our meetings,
assemblies, conventions, and the field ministry.
And the team worked very hard
specifically crafting each song
according to that direction.
Here’s another point that you can imagine:
The revised New World Translation
resulted in changing a lot of the lyrics
—a replacement of different words and expressions.
Just a few examples:
Most references to Sheol, seed, long-suffering have been replaced.
The song “Long-Suffering” is now “Exercise Patience.”
The expression “loving-kindness” is now “loyal love.”
“Time indefinite” has been replaced
with expressions such as “forevermore” or “eternal life.”
Here’s another point:
Doctrinal refinements, of course, affected some of the lyrics.
Just one example:
The expanded explanation of the meaning of Jehovah’s name
resulted in opening the door to more application
of Jehovah ‘Causing to Become.’
Here’s another point:
An effort was made to have
less direct counsel in the songs.
So rather than some feeling awkward as they were singing praises
and that they were maybe giving counsel to others as they were singing
—well, we’ve changed that.
That has been taken out.
Here’s another thing:
Certain awkward expressions
have been removed from the songs.
Just one example:
In one of our current songs,
there’s an expression that makes it appear
that single people are probably lonely.
Well, we took that out.
Here’s another detail,
and we present this in the form of a caution:
Be careful when you are singing from the new songbook
because the majority of the songs
—these older songs— have had lyrics adjusted.
So if you just sing from your previous memory bank,
you’re going to find yourself often in trouble.
But now, just a few comments about the structure of the songbook:
An effort has been made to put the songs in subject order.
And there are 15 categories now,
and the categories are listed in the index in the front of the songbook.
The first 12 songs
appropriately are under the category “Jehovah,”
and these are songs of direct praise to Jehovah
or songs about his name or his qualities.
“Meeting Together” —that’s another category—
songs about our meeting together and worshipping together.
The category “Godly Qualities”
—and included among other songs in this section
are songs that develop each one
of the aspects of the fruitage of the holy spirit
mentioned at Galatians 5:22, 23.
And they’re developed in the order in the songbook
that they’re listed in that scripture.
So that’s very helpful.
But now here’s something we’d like to say regarding the structure:
There is no significance to the song numbers
assigned to each song.
Over the years, some have worked very hard
to try to figure out the significance of the song numbers.
For example,
many concluded it wasn’t just coincidence
that the song “Be Forgiving” was song number 77.
Similarly,
the song “We’re Jehovah’s Witnesses,”
many thought it was no coincidence that that song
was song number 1931; I mean 31.
But we want to tell you up front,
there is no significance to the numbering and,
for that matter, there was not in the current songbook.
The numbers are random,
with the songs placed in the category they fit best in
and where they fit best in regard to the engraving layout.
Now, here’s another thought:
Three of the older songs have been removed
from the new songbook.
And quite a number have been totally revised with new subjects.
For example, the song “The Scene of This World Is Changing”
has now been totally revised to a more positive subject,
“Keep Working, Watching, and Waiting.”
The song “Making Our Way Successful”
is now “Life Depends on God’s Word.”
The song formerly “Content With God’s Good Gifts,”
which had limited use,
is now “Teaching the Word of God”
—a much more practical subject for our meetings or our field ministry.
Now, here’s one more point regarding the structure:
Many of the songs have been reformatted
and spread out over more pages.
Why?
Well, for one thing, it gives more space for other languages
that need more space
to be able to put the lyrics under the musical notes.
Another advantage by spreading them out:
It makes it easier to read the music
in the case of those who enjoy playing
the songs on piano.
But now, let’s look at another video,
and this one shows us some interesting facts
about the making of our new songbook.
The Governing Body’s support for this project was unanimous.
One of the reasons we felt it was especially important
was because of the revised New World Translation.
It was important for us to change the songs as well,
so that all the terminology in the revised version would match the songs.
In our audience, we have some of our brothers and sisters
who have the heavenly hope.
And, of course, the majority in our audience
are looking forward to life everlasting right here on the earth.
So the words of our songs would have to include both groups.
There are a few songs that were very rarely used
at meetings and assemblies because of the subject.
They may have been relevant subjects years back but not anymore.
So those songs,
the same melody is being used
but you’ll find there’s a brand new theme.
In our songbook in recent years,
there has definitely been an effort
to have more diversity of style.
It really helps all of us
—no matter what our background
or from what part of the world we come from—
to be unified in our worship.
When we get the music from the arranger,
we have to format it so it fits properly
to the page as it will appear in the songbook.
We supply the branches
with music-only notation,
and this way they can pour in the translated lyrics.
Songs really are
probably the most difficult translation project that you can handle.
Take an English verse like “listen, obey, and be blessed.”
It’s not difficult to express that idea in another language,
but the music there
has only seven notes: la, la, la, la, la, la, la.
So the challenge is to express those ideas
and make them fit into those seven notes.
So for all of these reasons, this is the work of a lyricist
—someone who can rewrite the song
and make sure that it conveys the right ideas, the right mood,
but at the same time that it is poetic
and that it touches the heart of those who are going to sing it.
What a wonderful thing to think
that worldwide in hundreds of languages our brothers and sisters
are having the very same experience:
being able to use their words to praise Jehovah in song.
The Governing Body feels very strongly about singing.
So that’s why they actually created a cover
that looks just like the New World Translation.
The songbook has been organized into subject order.
There are more songs in the book; there are 151 songs.
But also the songs have been spread out a little bit more.
That’s mainly for translation.
The website will have easier navigation tools
to help us to find the song number we’re looking for.
So we can listen to the song or the vocal rendition
while the phrase that is to be sung
during that portion of the song will highlight
as the song plays through.
We need to take the time right now to learn these new songs
and then to sing them.
You know, sing them all the time
—sing them when we’re working around the house,
sing them when we’re in the car,
sing them when we come together for social gatherings with our brothers.
They have the power to strengthen us.

Now, why could David adopt this attitude
when he was being betrayed?
He had a warm personal relationship with Jehovah God;
he knew his God.
He knew that Jehovah hears everything;
He sees everything.
He knew that God cares.
And notice Psalm 37:18.
David writes:
“Jehovah is aware of what the blameless go through.”
Isn’t that reassuring?
“And their inheritance will last forever.”
Now, David was a strong man,
a valiant warrior.
We recall when David would return from battle
that the women would sing:
‘Saul has killed his thousands,
David his tens of thousands.’
But David did not rely on his military prowess
in dealing with his enemies
—he turned to Jehovah.
And we find evidence of that in verses 12 and 13 of the 37th Psalm.
David writes:
“The wicked man plots against the righteous;
“he grinds his teeth at him.
“But Jehovah will laugh at him,
for He knows that his day will come.”
So there’s always this sense with David that whatever is happening,
Jehovah sees it; Jehovah is observing it,
and Jehovah is going to step in in due time
—very encouraging.
And so often in the Psalms—
We’ve been reading in the Psalms now in our Bible reading,
and haven’t you noticed so often in the Psalms
that this strong man,
this rugged man —David—
beseeches Jehovah to give him
a way of escape from his enemies?
Now, a lot of people in this country
would think that that was a coward’s act.
In this country, there are so many people who say:
“Don’t give in. Don’t back down.
“Stand your ground. Buy a weapon.
Keep it by your bedside.”
Not David
—David took comfort
in what we read in verse 28 of Psalm 37:
“Jehovah loves justice.”
So he placed his case before Jehovah God.
David had to struggle with his conscience on more than one occasion.
Do you remember what happened when David was running away from Saul
and he came to Ahimelech the priest?
Now, Ahimelech didn’t know that David was a fugitive,
and David wasn’t interested in letting him know that.
Instead, he told the priest:
“The king instructed me to do something, but he said,
“‘Do not let anyone know anything about the mission
on which I am sending you.’”
Well, that wasn’t true.
Then David asked for bread for his men,
and the priest was happy to give him bread and provisions.
Saul found out about it, and he was furious.
He directed that Ahimelech and his household
be put to death
and, in all, 85 priests were slaughtered.
Ahimelech was deceived.
He thought he was helping an emissary of King Saul.
Do you think he would have been so willing to help
if he had known the true situation?
Maybe not.
When those 85 priests are resurrected,
I think David is going to have a little explaining to do.
Well, was David’s conscience stricken?
You better believe it.
He told Ahimelech’s only surviving son:
“I am personally responsible
for the death of everyone in your father’s house.”
How do you live with that?
How do you live with being responsible for the death of so many people?
What could David do?
What was done was done.
He couldn’t change the past.
Would he become paralyzed with guilt
or overwhelmed by feelings of worthlessness
and become inactive in Jehovah’s service?
Not David.
What he could do was protect the last remaining member
of the house of Ahimelech,
and that’s exactly what he did.
As we know, there were other conscience matters.
David committed adultery with Bath-sheba
and had her husband, Uriah, killed.
So he sinned against Jehovah, he sinned against Uriah,
and he sinned against his other wives.
Imagine poor Abigail.
She’d been rescued from one bad marriage,
and now her new husband had betrayed her.
When his sins came to light, how did David react?
Well, here’s what he could not do:
He could not resurrect Uriah.
But he could sincerely repent of his sins, and he did.
And, in turn, the prophet Nathan told him:
“Jehovah . . . forgives your sin.”
What else could David do?
He could have faith
—faith that Jehovah really meant it
when He said that He forgave His servant.
Well, what about us?
In some cases, we may not be able
to undo our mistakes in our current lifetime.
We may have to live with the consequences.
But here’s what we can do:
We can take Jehovah at his word,
trusting that he will support us through difficult times
—even if the difficult times are of our own making.
David allowed Jehovah
to help him recover spiritually.
I’m going to repeat that.
David allowed Jehovah
to help him recover spiritually.
How did he do that?
Well, one way was by humbly accepting the counsel
of an experienced elder, the prophet Nathan.
His repentance was sincere.
There was no— There was no facade about it.
We know that.
We know that David repented with a good attitude
because later David and Bath-sheba
even named one of their sons Nathan,
and you don’t do that if you resent someone.
He took the counsel with a good attitude.
David learned from his mistakes,
and he kept on doing what was good.
Now, he may have been thinking of himself when he wrote
what we read at Psalm 37:23, 24:
“Jehovah guides the steps of a man when He finds pleasure in his way.
“Although he may fall, he will not be hurled down,
for Jehovah supports him by the hand.”
And David felt that support on many occasions.
Well, how can we learn from David’s example?
If we sin, we have to let Jehovah help us recover.
And more often than not, he’ll use the elders for that purpose.
What about you faithful parents whose child has gone astray?
David would understand your sorrow
—the sleepless nights, the tears,
the heartache, the worry.
One of his own sons, Amnon, raped his daughter Tamar.
Another of his sons, Absalom,
killed Amnon and then fled the country for three years.
Finally, the Bible says:
“David longed to go to Absalom,
for he had become reconciled to the death of Amnon.”
So he called him back.
You might say, in effect,
that Absalom got a three-year time-out for murder.
Did he appreciate the mercy?
No, he did not.
He tried to take the throne from David,
conspired against his own father.
And you wonder, ‘What was he thinking?’
Because at the time he was plotting against David,
he must have known that Jehovah had declared
that it was Solomon who was going to succeed his father and not Absalom.
He must have known that.
Did he really think that he could frustrate Jehovah’s purpose?
Wicked Absalom was finally put to death,
and David was devastated.
The poor young man
—seems he had a weak spot for his wicked sons.
You know, when we think of permissive parents,
we often think of High Priest Eli and his sons, Hophni and Phinehas.
But when you think about it, David was a bit permissive himself.
And you wonder if Solomon wasn’t thinking of his own half brothers
when he encouraged parents to use the rod.
Now, David couldn’t force his wicked sons
to respect Jehovah’s standards,
but there was something he could do.
He had a faithful son at home, Solomon.
And so David and Bath-sheba could lavish Solomon
with the love and affection that he deserved
and also help him to grow spiritually.
And they obviously did, because at Proverbs 4:3 we read—
These are Solomon’s words:
“I was a true son to my father
and the one especially loved by my mother.”
And then he added:
“He taught me.”
So David obviously was teaching his son to grow spiritually.
Now, it doesn’t always happen that way.
Consider this true-to-life scenario:
A brother and sister have two sons.
One leaves the truth and the other remains faithful.
The parents are heartbroken, and like David,
they go into mourning for their son.
And that’s completely understandable,
but we have to ask:
What about the son at home who has remained faithful?
What about the son who has never given his parents a moment’s grief?
Will he continue to get the love and affection
that he so richly deserves,
or will it be all about his brother?
Many of our modern-day fellow believers
have demonstrated their trust in Jehovah.
One brother who remained faithful till his death in 2015,
said this:
“Life is unpredictable at times,
“uncertain, and even hard to deal with.
But Jehovah blesses those who lean on him.”
And his advice:
“Pray to be as productive
“and as active in Jehovah’s service
as you can be.”
And notice this:
“Focus on what you can do,
not on what you cannot do.”
That excellent advice is being followed by traveling overseers
who are transitioning into other forms of service.
It’s also being applied by longtime members of the Bethel family
who are no longer serving as department overseers.
They are grateful to Jehovah for what they can do,
and they focus on that.
As this system of things degenerates from bad to worse,
we can expect difficult times.
When that coalition of nations, known as Gog of Magog,
launches its final attack on God’s people,
it will seem that there is no way out.
Our most formidable weapon at that time will be our faith.
And so, brothers, it’s fitting
that our yeartext for 2017 should be
Psalm 37:3:
“Trust in Jehovah and do what is good.”
Thank you very much, Brother Splane.
We’ll remember that talk at least until the end of next year.
Your talk was well-spoken, as usual.

en.text: You are probably
the most obedient group of people this size
that has ever entered Jersey City.
So we say, “Thank you very much
for being in your seats.”
It’s now my pleasure to invite you to stand
and to sing song number 150,
“Reaching Out,” Matthew 9:37, 38.
What a marvelous gift from God it is.
We all have one.
It’s a bit larger in men than it is in women.
What is it?
It’s in your mouth.
It’s your tongue.
A small muscle, a little over three inches long.
We do so many things with it
—you can whisper with it; you can yell with it;
you can swallow your food with its help;
and it’s so versatile; you can stick it out.
Over in Tibet,
they stick out the tongue, some of them,
and it’s a sign of friendship and greeting.
Don’t you try that here!
It stays out of the way of your teeth
when you chew, well, most of the time.
It is an arduous job
trying to control the tongue,
but James had something to say about it.
Let’s see what he had to say.
Let’s turn to James
in our Bibles or iPads.
That’s the third chapter of his book,
and we’re going to read 5 through 10:
“So, too, the tongue is a small part of the body,
“and yet it makes great brags.
“See how small a fire it takes
“to set a great forest ablaze!
“The tongue is also a fire.
“The tongue represents a world of unrighteousness
“among our body members,
“for it defiles all the body
“and sets the whole course of life on fire,
“and it is set on fire by Gehenna.
“For every kind of wild animal and bird
“and reptile and sea creature
“is to be tamed and has been tamed by humans.
“But no human can tame the tongue.
“It is unruly and injurious,
“full of deadly poison.
“With it we praise Jehovah, the Father,
“and yet with it we curse men
“who have come into existence
“‘in the likeness of God.’
“Out of the same mouth
come blessing and cursing.”
In our imperfect state,
we can’t completely control it.
Oh, we try, and we must try,
but we just can’t get the job completely done.
But we’re not going to give up.
We’re going to keep trying.
We’re going to watch, though, what we have to say
—what comes out of the mouth, what rolls as a result of the tongue.
We’re going to be very careful.
And we know that we must rein in
a runaway tongue
and curb its wagging.
Although blessing and cursing can come out
of the mouth by use of the tongue
you will only hear blessings out of the mouths
of the speakers and participants today.
These Christians have bridled their tongues.
Thank God for that.
Today we are going to consider things that are—
Now, you want to jot these down
because we’re going to mention them several times through the day.
Here they are:
‘true,
‘things of serious concern,
‘righteous, chaste,
‘lovable, well-spoken-of,
virtuous, praiseworthy,’
“good and acceptable.”
The tongue will work good for us today, not bad.
So we say, “sit still,”
and may your ears
keep up with the tongues
of all of our participants.
And as you know,
in our September JW Broadcasting program,
Brother Splane told us that the move of Bethel family members
to the world headquarters facility
in Warwick, New York, is in progress.
It is already a bustling complex
with so many relocated
and caring for their assignments.
This represents a historic change
since the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses
had been located in Brooklyn, New York,
for over 100 years.
We’re all happy,
and it’s good for us who live there.
It’s such a beautiful place indeed
and so restful.
All of us feel like we have been able
to add years to our lives.
We can hear birds sing,
crickets at night, frogs
—every now and then, there’s an eagle that flies over—
bears, and snakes.
But we’ve been warned to watch out.
We know what to do.
And we’re just enjoying ourselves
as much as we possibly can.
Well, we now invite you
to enjoy a video presentation
about the history of headquarters in Brooklyn
and the move to Warwick.
So we say, “Enjoy what you see.”
And here is
—look at your notes—
true.
Why are we here at Bethel today in New York City?
Why did Pastor Russell leave Pittsburgh?
To expand the ministry worldwide.
But look at it today.
The satisfaction to see
and the blessing of seeing the work expand “to the ends of the earth”
and God’s will being done.
In 1909, Jehovah led his people
in making a move that would become
an indelible part of our spiritual heritage.
For years, the Pennsylvania location
had been adequate for the work of spreading the good news.
But as time went on, challenges arose.
Pittsburgh’s reputation was one of steel and industry,
not really one of religion and faith.
The organization at that time was trying to get the preaching work accomplished,
and it wasn’t really well-suited in Pittsburgh.
So they struggled to find a city that would work for them,
and one of the cities that they came across was Brooklyn.
It was very famous for its pastors and its churches.
It was actually nicknamed “The City of Churches,”
and that was a good reputation
to springboard the preaching work from.
They were trying to preach the good news to the entire earth,
but with so few Bible Students, how could they possibly do it?
And then they realized the cultural base
that existed in New York City was broad,
and so they felt that this put them in the perfect position
to preach to people
and have them help the Bible Students take the message back to their homelands.
Brooklyn, just far and above, was the obvious choice to them.
Officially, Brooklyn Bethel
opened its doors in April 1909.
These were years of tremendous activity
leading up to 1914.
They also proved to be times of test.
The United States had declared war on Germany.
From March through July of 1918,
eight different brothers who were taking the lead at that time
were arrested, sentenced, and taken off
to a federal penitentiary.
The Executive Committee at headquarters
consulted with other brothers.
It was decided to sell the Brooklyn Tabernacle
and to close the Bethel home.
So we moved here in 1909,
and within ten years, Brooklyn Bethel was closed.
The headquarters operations were moved back to Pittsburgh.
In the year 1919,
when the brothers were finally released from prison,
Brother Rutherford apprehended rapidly:
‘There’s still great interest in the work,
‘and Jehovah is still blessing and backing us.
‘We need to get back, organize it, and get on
with the work that has been started.’
So should they start from scratch
and build a Bethel there in Allegheny, or should they utilize
the property that they already owned in Brooklyn?
They wanted to see if that was actually Jehovah’s will.
So, what Judge Rutherford did is he asked
Brother C. A. Wise, who was his vice president,
‘We need to do a test to see if Jehovah is going to bless this direction.’
During wartime, any raw materials
—paper, fuel, all of those things— are regulated
because the war effort is going on.
So this was a perfect test to see
if it would enable the brothers to get coal.
He sent him back here, and he said: ‘Don’t just get a little coal.
‘Get enough so that it is obvious
that if we get this coal, it is only by Jehovah’s blessing.’
Brother Rutherford directed Brother Wise
to order 500 tons of coal.
And what was the outcome?
When he applied to the authorities,
he was granted a certificate to obtain 500 tons of coal
—enough to care for their needs for years to come.
So in 1919 —September, I believe—
is when they actually moved back from Allegheny to Brooklyn.
Once it was determined that Brooklyn, New York,
would be the new world headquarters,
how would Jehovah use this new location
to advance the preaching work?
Well, we were dependent back then on commercial printeries.
Brother Rutherford wondered whether
we could print The Watchtower ourselves.
And so a printing press was obtained, and a printery was set up.
And in time, the book printing began.
Outside commercial companies thought that we would never be capable
of printing and binding books.
But the brothers applied themselves, learned,
and with the support of the Lord, they got it going.
It was so evident that Jehovah was using Brooklyn Bethel.
All the printing and binding was done for the world
here in Brooklyn.
After that,
the organization took in brothers, under the direction of the Governing Body,
to come and learn what they could in Brooklyn and take it with them
back to their countries and see what they could do
about lightening the load a little as far as the printing
and distribution was concerned.
Soon after I got to Bethel in Japan,
I worked on the web press.
We always looked up to Brooklyn as our “big brother,”
and we always looked to them for direction.
Anytime we were able to come back to the United States on a brief visit,
I would always make sure
to see what was new and to talk with the brothers.
And the brothers were always very helpful.
So you saw how Jehovah used
this place to get the spiritual food out
to the worldwide association of the brothers.
It is clear that Jehovah had blessed the advancement
of the printing and distribution work in Brooklyn Bethel.
But to further share the truth globally
in a way that would truly touch hearts,
other challenges needed to be addressed.
Zechariah 8:23 says
that ‘ten men out of all the languages of the nations
will grab hold of the skirt of a man who is a Jew.’
Now, that’s a lot of languages.
But for every person
to understand,
they have to hear it in their language.
Though we were translating
into many languages, many of these were not simultaneous with English.
Some of them lagged behind for many months.
And, of course, there were many languages
that didn’t have any literature at all.
And so the Governing Body saw the situation,
and they created the department Translation Services.
Some of the early languages
were translated right here in Brooklyn.
Eventually, translation work was moved out
to the branches where they speak those languages.
The 20th century saw many technological advancements.
How did Jehovah guide his servants
at Brooklyn Bethel to make progressive use
of these advancements to further the preaching work
to “all the languages of the nations”?
Well, the challenges
of developing a computer
that could actually type and compose in all of those languages
were enormous in the late seventies and early eighties.
I think the brothers could see that technology was changing.
Things were changing from letterpress to offset printing;
things were going from black and white
to color.
So I think all the pieces began to be there
to look at the idea of MEPS.
I kind of liken it to our “moon shot.”
In other words, can you get there and back?
Jehovah provided the right people at the right time
—people who had previous expertise with building computer systems
and people who had some expertise with languages.
And what has always fascinated me
is Jehovah’s use of the timing of when to use the technologies.
Jehovah put Bethel in Brooklyn.
And he would know at any given time
—strategically and geographically— where would be the best place
for his world headquarters, and for decades,
it was Brooklyn.
In 1971, when you looked out over the East River,
you know what you saw along the shoreline?
A whole row of freighters.
And then the fact that we had our printery just a few blocks away,
revealed why it was beneficial to have Bethel here in Brooklyn.
Now, you look out over the East River, what do you see?
It’s a park.
You have swimming pools there; it’s full of people.
The purpose has changed,
and the reasons for our being here have in many ways disappeared.
Because of the way things are developing in the world
and because of Brooklyn in New York City
being where it is in the world scene,
it’s time for us to get things moved out of Brooklyn
and to a new world headquarters where we can be even more fruitful.
Jehovah was again leading his people
in another historic move.
We’d like to let you know that the Governing Body has decided
that if the approvals are received for the Warwick project,
we will be moving completely out of Brooklyn.
The world headquarters will be relocated at Warwick.
When it was announced, the plans of establishing world headquarters
in what is going to be in Warwick,
it just seemed like it was so far away.
We may not even live to that.
But the time has passed quite quickly,
and now it’s virtually on our doorstep.
It’s happening!
We have seen that Jehovah
can use any location.
We have beautiful facilities now
at Wallkill, Patterson, soon Warwick
—beautiful facilities
that Jehovah will use to the full just as he used Brooklyn.
And it becomes so evident
that this is not an organization of men.
We’re not dedicated to a building or to a city;
we are dedicated to Jehovah.
And when you sense his direction
in this matter of relocating
and doing things differently, you can’t help but—
OK, we back off the sentimentality,
and let’s go ahead and do the work
as Jehovah has outlined for us today.
I’ve always concluded that when it works,
Jehovah is behind it.
So Warwick worked beautifully.
And if you ever get to Warwick and you see
Warwick as it is now, you’ll say,
“This is the place that Jehovah wanted us to be.”
Jehovah had Brooklyn in place,
some parts of it for over a hundred years.
And it served so well as a base for the Governing Body,
as a base for printing and providing spiritual food worldwide,
as a base for direction
for congregations worldwide,
and now Jehovah has something else in mind.
With the way things turned out,
it wasn’t a man or a group of men
who back in the early 1900’s said:
“You know what we need to do?
“We’ll stay here about a hundred years.
“And then we’ll have a place up north of the city
“and we’ll move there and we’ll sell all these buildings
and then it’ll be a real boost to the work.”
No man or a group of men did that.
But Jehovah and Christ Jesus
—they direct the brothers
at the right time in the right place to make the decisions
that may seem for the present, just for the present.
But Jehovah sees the end
from the very beginning.
Yes, world headquarters in Brooklyn
has been the hub of our global preaching work
throughout the 20th century.
Despite many twists and turns,
Jehovah has used this location
to advance his will in unprecedented ways.
While we think back fondly on all that was accomplished here,
we know going forward, there is only more to come.
That was most interesting.
But save your hands; there’s more coming.
So we’re not looking back on Brooklyn,
but we are moving forward
—one step closer to our future hope.
And as you know,
I just love acronyms and abbreviations
—PC, WC,
WDC, LDC—
but what does CPC stand for?
Well, in the video just seen,
you got a glimpse of the beautiful new little city
built on a lake in Warwick.
So the CPC helped make that happen.
What does the CPC stand for?
CPC stands for Construction Project Committee.
Lock that in.
Though that committee lived and breathed
the Warwick project for a number of years,
it was really a Governing Body directed project.
However, the Construction Project Committee
was given the latitude to make many
of the detail-oriented decisions
on their own.
Now, how did this assignment affect these brothers?
Did they give it
serious concern?
Let’s pay attention to a prerecorded interview
of the CPC
conducted by Brother Harold Corkern,
a helper for the Publishing Committee of the Governing Body.
The video is entitled
Building for the Future.
The construction of the new world headquarters
at Warwick, New York, was indeed a historic project.
The Construction Project Committee certainly saw evidence
of Jehovah’s blessing and guidance upon them.
But they also realized
that he was building more than just a new facility;
he was building qualities
that are so necessary for his people.
And this we’ll see as we talk to our CPC members.
At this time, it would be good for us
to introduce the Construction Project Committee.
We’ll do so alphabetically.
We have Brother Ken Caughron,
Brother Kenneth Chernish,
Brother Richard Devine,
Brother Enrique Ford, and
Brother Troy Snyder.
One of the first questions we’d like to ask you is:
When you first got this assignment
and you learned of the scope
and all the work that was involved
and the established completion date,
what was your first reaction?
And we’ll start with Brother Richard Devine.
Well, I was excited but overwhelmed
—overwhelmed not just by the size of the project
and the expedited schedule
but especially by the level of trust
that the Governing Body had put in the five of us.
I was used to recommendations being reviewed
by multiple layers of oversight
and decisions taking weeks or months to arrive at.
And here the Governing Body told us
that we were to report only to the Publishing Committee.
And once a budget was established,
to use our best judgment, carry out the work,
and come back to them for direction only if we exceeded our budget.
Brother Troy Snyder, what would you like to add?
The emotions varied from being scared to excited.
And like any new assignment, you think about how much work
is going to be needed to accomplish it.
But then when really meditating on the scope of the job
and the time frame that was desired,
you started to feel inadequate,
and there was just no way you could do it.
But then you started to realize that Jehovah was behind you.
He was the one who was directing matters.
He had confidence that we could do it.
And so as a result, you knew you could really lean on him
and look at him as a fellow worker.
And that really helped set the pace.
Brother Ford.
The first thing I realized is
that if this project was going to be successful,
it was going to be because of Jehovah’s holy spirit.
That was clear because from a human perspective
it was literally impossible,
but it was what Jehovah had asked us to do.
And the other thing that occurred to me
was that Jehovah wasn’t going to bless
our standard approach of developing projects.
Brother Ken Caughron?
We were living and working on the Nigeria branch construction project
at Igieduma out in the beautiful African bush.
So my first feeling was,
‘Did they dial the wrong number?’
But within 30 minutes, we returned the phone call.
We were very happy to accept the privilege to go.
As far as a completion date,
if we would have known all the details at that time
of how Warwick would be constructed,
where would the faith have been?
So it wasn’t our assignment
at that time to know all the details.
It was our assignment to have faith
in the invisible One, Jehovah,
and move forward with that conviction.
Brother Ken Chernish, what would you like to add?
I could not believe
that Jehovah would put that much trust in me.
I’ll never forget going to bed that night,
laying down, eyes wide open
—they remained open all night long—
just praying to Jehovah.
We didn’t have construction documents.
We didn’t have permits.
We didn’t even have design on some of the buildings.
From a secular perspective, it couldn’t be done in four years.
And I realized I just needed to have the faith
to follow Jehovah’s lead and to work with these brothers
and that schedule would become attainable.
When you first started working as a committee,
were there any challenges
on learning how to work together as a committee?
And if so, how did you address them?
And we’ll start with Brother Ford.
I remember a visit from one Governing Body member,
and he made the statement
that they wanted this not to be a Bethel project,
not to be an RBC project, but to be a CPC project
—a totally different approach.
So that assured me that the Governing Body
deliberately wanted us to blend together
these five different approaches and personalities.
Brother Richard Devine?
We all brought different paradigms to the table,
different ways of thinking, even a different language in some cases.
And so it took a while for us to understand each other.
And so we, early on, decided to try to take advantage
of everything that the brotherhood could offer
and try to blend the different approaches to achieve the success
that, really, we were hoping for with Jehovah’s blessing.
And as time went on, we really began to respect each other
and draw close together as a committee and as friends.
What I appreciated was in our meetings,
the brothers felt comfortable expressing themselves
and their viewpoints even if it differed from others.
My challenge was lack of Bethel experience
—still is.
Yet, these brothers were so patient with me,
so protective of me, even, and in caring for me,
in understanding how much different my background was,
the way I went about making decisions, the way I expressed myself.
Yet, they understood that.
I also prayed to show honor
to these brothers and to take the lead.
I did a good job of it sometimes and not so good at other times.
But I have really tried to rely on Jehovah
in that way to overcome the challenge.
The biggest challenge for me was myself.
I could quickly see
why Jehovah had brought the other brothers together
with their experience in construction,
in engineering, in business administration,
and many years at world headquarters.
But I felt apprehensive about my experience
and even hesitant sometimes to express myself.
But I kept up my spiritual routines
—field service, prayer, meditation, and so forth.
And in time, I realized that I needed
to show more personal faith
—well, specifically to show more faith
in not comparing ourselves to others
and not neglecting the gifts
that we do have to offer to Jehovah.
So I benefited from every brother on the committee.
I’m refined, and I’m very thankful
to Jehovah for helping me grow.
It’s very commendable, a good example for us.
Our next question:
Given the magnitude
of this project
and the date that was established for completion,
what organizational and logistical challenges
did you find most daunting?
Brother Devine?
At our peak, we were processing
over 11,000 requisition lines a month.
We were delivering over 1,000 pallets a week to the site.
It was an incredible challenge.
And it really would have been impossible without Jehovah’s blessing
and the hard work of our Procurement and Purchasing Departments.
Designers, by their training and background, are used to planning.
They’re used to starting a project
with the determination of how long it would take
to get the design finished and then scheduling forward.
So from day one,
I realized that if we could not find a way
completed very quickly and on time, the project would grind to a halt.
So that was very daunting for me.
At that time, the Wallkill project was still in full swing.
And they were feeding us volunteers and overseers,
really, at will when we asked for them,
but they were still not going to be enough.
We were going to need to do heavy site work
simultaneous with building and construction.
That’s not necessarily the best way to go about it.
There are a lot of clashes when that happens.
It makes workers less productive
because it’s hard to move around the spaces.
We were going to have all six major buildings
in construction simultaneously.
We’d come to find out we were going to need
to have 11 cranes swinging in the air.
These things, along with 20 telehandlers going around the site,
moving this material that Rich talked about,
were going to be daunting.
And Brother Ken Caughron?
One aspect of my assignment was to work with safety.
So it was very daunting in the beginning to imagine:
How will we provide safety orientation and training
to thousands of volunteers coming in?
And then, what would be the best way
to motivate our brothers and sisters
on the very serious subject of safety?
And safety is a concern of all of Jehovah’s people
no matter what we’re doing.
Brother Troy Snyder.
We needed the high skill.
We needed the friends to come.
We needed large amounts as Brother Chernish mentioned.
But how would we care for them?
At one point, we grew in an eight-month period over a thousand,
and we did.
What type of rooming would we have for them?
How would we care for them spiritually and physically?
At one time, we found ourselves
with a kitchen and dining room designed for 200 and trying to feed
about 1,000 people.
We certainly could feel that it was as if Jesus
was in that kitchen multiplying the loaves.
You had good support.
But now, you’ve enumerated understandable
concerns and challenges.
Could you give some examples on how those were resolved?
And we’ll come back to Brother Caughron for this one.
We realized that we wanted
to move away from any inclination or thinking
that safety is somehow the first responsibility of a safety department
or a safety brother coming around to check on us.
We wanted to put forth more effort
to teach that safety is an expression of our spirituality.
Once we started focusing on that teaching
—that there are certain values such as the sanctity of life,
we love our brother,
we must maintain a good conscience before Jehovah—
then the whole subject of safety
became very inspiring to work with.
It was a real joy.
In a practical way, on Sunday afternoon,
instead of having a three-hour safety orientation and training,
we developed a series of videos
that could be streamed to volunteers.
Before they came (several weeks ahead of time)
they could watch a video, take notes,
and watch it again if they wanted to.
And what it did is it significantly increased the quality
of our safety orientation and training for the entire project.
Enrique Ford.
We realized that we couldn’t be paralyzed by fear
just because we’d never done something this way before.
We had to move forward with faith.
An example of that was as a committee
we made the decision to model the building in three dimensions
on a computer before we started construction.
Now, we had never done that before
—and not to speak of doing it
on a project of this scale, complexity, with this deadline—
but we moved ahead in faith, and Jehovah blessed that effort.
We’d like to develop that a little bit further.
You’ve given us some examples
of how Jehovah’s holy spirit was certainly there,
his guidance, and his blessing.
Could you give us some more examples of that?
We’ll start with Brother Chernish.
A lot of decisions that were going to have to be made.
What could we self-perform?
What would we need to outsource
to get done in four years?
And we would also come to learn through this process
that if we stopped, if we prayed,
if we talked about it, and if we were all in unison,
we would see Jehovah’s direction.
It was very faith-strengthening,
and we would see Jehovah’s spirit
work upon the contractors that were working here.
They would come to us: “We’ve never swung
“this many panels on a building in a day.
“We did 33 today!
We’re accustomed to doing 16!”
We would chuckle off on the side.
We knew what they were benefiting from.
Jehovah too was moving their actions
because it was his will and his purpose for this to be done.
So seeing this level of blessing and holy spirit
was really faith-strengthening.
Troy Snyder.
Early on, we received a letter from the Governing Body
to our committee reminding us
that although they wanted the project done in an expedited fashion,
they didn’t want it done in a way that hurt the brothers spiritually.
And so we started consciously making efforts
to adjust ones’ schedules
so that they could attend their meetings,
so they could participate in the field ministry,
so that they would be able to benefit
from all the spiritual programs
that Bethel provides and has for us.
We were even able to adjust some of our dear sisters’ schedules
so that they too could keep up their spiritual routine.
And every time we did that,
it didn’t seem logical from a human standpoint,
but the project accelerated.
Rich Devine.
Well, I think we’ve prayed more on this project
than any other theocratic project I’ve ever been involved with
not only as a committee but every department
and every crew would pray together.
If we talked about work, we prayed.
Whether it was technical discussions
or anything else, we always prayed.
And it really made us feel that Jehovah was a part of our daily work
—that we were really fellow workers with him—
and we really felt that.
But also, I think the most dramatic evidence of Jehovah’s spirit
was the manifestation of the fruitage of the spirit
in our brothers and sisters.
Despite long work hours, hard working conditions,
difficult living conditions, an expedited schedule,
you could still see the love, the hope,
and the joy in the brothers every day.
And this really helped me to understand
how Jehovah’s spirit was so active here.
What would you like to say
to the Bethel family
and to the thousands of willing,
hard-working volunteers that came from the field to assist you?
Perhaps we can start with Ken Caughron.
Well, many thousands of years ago,
we remember the sacrifice of Abel
because out of love he gave the best he had.
So we say “thank you” to the brothers and sisters
who supported the project out in the field
—out of love giving the best they had was often their prayers.
Others came physically, giving out of love the best they had.
So may all the brothers and sisters remember
that this was the reason they shared in the project,
and it is something that they and Jehovah
can remember for an eternity.
Ken Chernish.
Like Brother Caughron said,
I would just like to say “thank you”
and especially to all of the brothers and sisters
in the Bethel complexes in the U.S. branch territory.
They treated us like a parent
would treat a child —so lovingly.
They gave us everything we asked for that we needed.
The friends out in the field, we’ve talked about them so much.
They turned their lives upside down
to come here and work with us.
Did they benefit? Absolutely!
And we so appreciate
how they put up with us, how things changed,
and the schedules that we imputed upon them to get this work done.
We know they benefited as we did,
and we’d like to thank them so much.
Rich Devine.
Thank you for sacrificing your money
and your time to come and help us.
Thank you for interviewing and sending such capable volunteers.
Thanks for working in the rain and the snow.
Thanks for enduring long bus rides and living in hotels.
Thanks for being our friends,
and thanks for the wonderful spirit that you showed through the whole project.
Enrique Ford.
As we had the opportunity to eat with the volunteers,
work with them, and travel with them,
it became evident that every one of them
had a story as to how they got here.
Sometimes it was the supportive mate
Other times, they talked about their children
and how their children encouraged them
and supported them so that they could be here.
There are even some brothers that told us
about how the entire congregation
supported them financially
as well as covering their assignments back home
because the congregation wanted to sponsor someone since they couldn’t come.
So we just want to thank all of those volunteers
and the support that made it possible for them to come.
Troy Snyder?
We love you very much.
And Jehovah united us as a family
in a period of time to accomplish something for his glory.
And I think we personally would love
to be able to express our appreciation
and reward each person for what they’ve done.
But we take such comfort in knowing that Jehovah has seen their love,
has seen their work, and he will reward them.
And that will be a rich blessing.
Thank you for those heartfelt expressions.
And in conclusion, we just have a few brief comments.
We have heard, and rightfully so, the Governing Body
offer warm commendation and appreciation
to all of you on this committee
as well as to the thousands who have supported the project.
And at this time,
we’d also like to take this opportunity
to thank your wives
for their hard work on this project,
their patience, their endurance,
and their absolute support that they gave.
It’s most appreciated.
And I know you appreciate their support,
and we do too.
So the lessons that we all learned
—thanks to you, from this project
and thanks to Jehovah most of all—
will benefit us now
and right on into the future as your comments have alluded to.
So once again, thank you for taking the time to share these observations.
Thank you for your hard work.
And it will be a privilege
for all of us to continue to work “shoulder to shoulder”
with “the one who constructed all things,” Jehovah God.
There was one word that stood out in this interview,
and it was the word “daunting.”
And, of course, that is a beautiful word.
It’s a good word.
But when you see what was accomplished in the past four years,
you’ll see why we’re going to change
the word “daunting” to “amazing.”
So lock that one in.
I mentioned earlier
that this was a Governing Body directed project.
CPC was indeed a unique way
to expedite the construction.
However, all that was accomplished on the Warwick project
is a result of the base of experience and, of course,
all the wonderful training
that had been laid for the last several decades
by the Design/Build Department— that’s DBD.
They did a lot in planning and executing
construction projects around the world.
And the amazing Warwick project
would not have happened in that time frame
without the thousands of volunteers,
many of whom for years tirelessly assisted
Regional Building Committees —RBC.
They are sent to them to build so many
Assembly and Kingdom Halls month after month.
And the same is true of all of the volunteers
that came and assisted
with the monumental expansion
of the Wallkill branch facility.
Now, would you brothers and sisters like
to thank all of these ones who supported
two of the largest construction projects to date?
I might mention
that on Friday, October 14, 2016,
a new video about moving out of Brooklyn
will be posted on JW Broadcasting.
You will find it under “Latest Videos.”
At the end of that video, a letter from the Governing Body is read
sharing sincere appreciation for all those who worked
on these two construction projects.
It will be posted in English first
with other languages being posted at a later time.
Look for the English edition on JW Broadcasting
on October 14, 2016.
For your further information,
the CPC was dissolved
as of September 29, 2016.
They will all be moving on to other assignments.
And we appreciate very much their intense labor of love.
