en.text: Welcome, brothers and sisters!
Here are some of this month’s highlights:
How should we view counsel?
Does it apply to us even if we don’t like
the way it was given?
In times of crisis,
how does the organization respond to help our brothers and sisters?
And we will go behind the scenes of last year’s convention drama
about King Hezekiah.
This is the May program of JW Broadcasting!
Let’s begin by visiting a family in Stockholm, Sweden.
The parents, Usama and Kristina, have two daughters,
Talita and Isabella.
When Talita was born,
the doctor found cataracts in both of her eyes.
A cataract is a clouding of the eye’s natural lens.
So the doctor had to operate
so that Talita wouldn’t lose her sight completely
—a terrifying situation for any parent.
Today, Talita is seven years old
and almost blind in one eye
but completely blind in the other.
Teaching a child about Jehovah
in this system of things is already a challenge
even without physical ailments involved.
But let’s find out how Talita’s parents rose to the challenge,
making sure that she received a proper spiritual education
despite her poor vision.
I look forward to not having poor sight anymore
and that I can play with a bear and a lion
and to sit on the back of a tiger.
Jehovah gives us a fantastic promise at Isaiah 35:5:
“The eyes of the blind will be opened.”
It’s been a challenge to get to where we are today.
We thank Jehovah for all the help he has given us.
As soon as Talita was able to leave the house after the operation,
we made sure to go to the meetings.
It helped us a lot to be able to throw our burden on Jehovah.
We prayed together;
we cried a lot together because it was so hard.
One of the challenges
is that we have to give Talita audio description constantly.
We have to tell her who is coming in and what is happening.
We get so many amazing materials on jw.org
and also through the congregation.
She really loves to read Learn From the Great Teacher.
It has questions which make her a part of the story.
She has a very good memory,
and therefore she remembers a lot of what she reads.
So when we are with friends, she often quizzes them.
I really like to sing the songs in my songbook.
Talita’s spiritual goal
is to learn more of our Kingdom songs.
We get so much help
from the beautiful music on the website
and also from the Caleb and Sophia videos.
She knows many of the stories from My Book of Bible Stories,
so she can answer in her own words.
We will ask a question like, Do you know this about David?
And if she knows the answer,
then we encourage her to answer at the meeting.
When I give an answer at the meetings,
Jehovah becomes happy
because he loves children.
She often asks the friends,
“Do you love Jehovah?”
So she feels very united with them.
One of the best moments where we saw
that Talita’s spirituality had grown
was when she came home from a sleepover
at her grandparents’ house.
My parents are not Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and her grandmother had said
that God doesn’t exist.
So when Talita came home, she said,
“And then when I was going to sleep, I prayed to Jehovah,
“‘Would you please help Grandmother
to realize that you do exist —that you are real?’”
We try to keep our wonderful hope alive,
so we often talk  about what we will do
in Paradise.
We really look forward to when Talita will be able to see again
and live in a paradise with all our friends.
It’s going to be wonderful!
I think that Jehovah looks forward to looking at me
when I play with a tiger.
I’ll have to make sure that I remember the names of Joseph’s brothers
in case I meet Talita and she decides to quiz me!
Her parents have done a good job in raising such a fine young sister.
And together with them,
we eagerly look forward to the benefits of the new system.
Isaiah 35:5 says:
“At that time the eyes of the blind will be opened.”
Such divine reminders can truly warm our heart.
And Jehovah’s reminders not only provide us comfort
but can also help us make important decisions
in our everyday life.
This brings us to our music video which is entitled
I Keep Your Reminders.
What should I do? Who should I look to?
This could just be harmless, could be respectable.
There may be no need for me to reject it all.
Oh, what is the right course for me? Which path will it be?
What should I do? Take which point of view?
It could be excessive, with many dangers there—
All the kinds of things that could prove to be a snare.
Oh, what is the right course for me? Jehovah, give ear to my plea.
I keep your reminders, and I love them dearly.
I’ll treasure them every day, monthly, yearly.
All the things I have heard in accord with your Word, help me understand.
I know what’s required. I’d better inquire.
I don’t want to act in a way to cause offense,
But it sounds like there likely would be consequence.
It’s clear what’s the right course for me —the key, the guarantee.
I keep your reminders, and I love them dearly.
They strengthen my heart and help me to see clearly.
All the things I have heard in accord with your Word, help me understand.
I keep your reminders, and I love them dearly.
They strengthen my heart and help me to see clearly.
As I read day and night, my life fills up with light.
I’ve got you by my side as I think of your might.
All the things I have heard in accord with your Word, help me understand.
Did you notice that it was a Bible-trained conscience
that helped our sister make a wise decision?
She knew what potential danger lay ahead.
Yes, the reminders from God’s Word guided her.
The theme for our program this month is
“Treasure Jehovah’s Reminders.”
And it’s based on Psalm 19:7,
where we’re told:
“The reminder of Jehovah is trustworthy,
making the inexperienced one wise.”
In the original language, the word here translated as “reminder”
comes from a root word meaning “to go over again, to repeat.”
Reminders have always been an essential part of Jehovah’s teaching.
In ancient Israel, God’s people continually received
commandments, regulations, and reminders.
In fact, Jehovah tells us
that he sent his prophets “again and again”
to repeatedly remind his people of their responsibilities.
The apostle Peter felt the need to give reminders
even to those who were “well-established in the truth.”
Notice how he describes this
at 2 Peter 1:12, 13:
“For this reason I intend always
“to remind you of these things,
“although you know them and are well-established
“in the truth that is present in you.
“But I consider it right,
“as long as I am in this tabernacle,
to stir you with reminders.”
In verse 15, he goes on to give the reason
why he felt the need to give the brothers reminders.
He says:
“I will always do my utmost so that after my departure,
you may be able to recall these things for yourselves.”
So Peter was determined to help the brothers and sisters
in his day to remember, or recall,
the teachings they had already learned.
It shouldn’t come as a surprise, then,
if today a lot of our teaching involves reminders.
It follows the pattern set by Jehovah in ancient Israel
and with the first-century Christians.
But why do we need reminders?
Let’s consider three reasons.
First, let’s look at Psalm 103:2.
There it says:
“Let me praise Jehovah;
may I never forget all that he has done.”
Why, then, do we need reminders?
Simply put, because we forget.
If we had perfect memories,
we wouldn’t need so many reminders.
Even in everyday life, many of us use little notes
to remind ourselves of what we need to do.
And who of us hasn’t seen the need
for a list of reminders when going shopping,
only to realize when we returned
that we forgot to get one of the important items
we needed to purchase?
If reminders are important in everyday life,
how much more so in matters
that involve our relationship with Jehovah.
Let’s read Luke 10:39, 40.
Speaking of Martha, we are told:
“She also had a sister called Mary,
“who sat down at the feet of the Lord
“and kept listening to what he was saying.
“Martha, on the other hand,
was distracted with attending to many duties.”
What was Martha’s problem?
She was distracted.
So the second reason why we need reminders
is that, like Martha, at times we too become distracted.
Although we may already know a vital fact,
that fact might get put into the back of our mind,
figuratively speaking,
because other matters are demanding our attention.
Satan is the great Distracter.
He tries to turn our attention away from the true issues of our day.
People in general have become more and more distracted
by entertainment and other nonessential matters.
No wonder that Satan has succeeded in misleading so many.
They don’t even realize what has happened.
Reason number three is alluded to
at Matthew 24:45:
“Who really is the faithful and discreet slave
“whom his master appointed over his domestics,
to give them their food at the proper time?”
Notice that the spiritual food is given to us “at the proper time.”
Our circumstances in life are continually changing.
How often do we hear,
“That was just what I needed?”
We’ve all experienced that, haven’t we?
So, what are three of the reasons why we need reminders?
One, because we tend to forget things.
Two, we often become distracted.
Three, our changed circumstances
may require a reminder of something we already knew
but didn’t fully need at that time.
So that brings us to the next question:
What will help us to remember?
It’s interesting to note that Jehovah has used many ways
to remind his people of what they should do.
At Numbers 10:10, we’re told
that the various festivals were given as reminders,
especially the celebration of the Passover.
That means that every time the Israelites
prepared and celebrated one of these festivals,
they were reminded of important matters,
such as how Jehovah provides for his people
and how he has saved them in the past.
Something similar happens today
at the commemoration of the Lord’s Evening Meal.
Not only do we hear the reminders from God’s Word
but the act of passing the bread and wine
also serves as an action that reminds us
of what Jesus did in our behalf.
But what do we need to do in order for those reminders
to have a beneficial impact on our lives?
Notice what Psalm 119:99 says.
It tells us:
“I have more insight than all my teachers,
because I ponder over your reminders.”
Yes, we need to ponder over these reminders.
That means not just listening to or reading them,
but it involves thinking deeply about them—
meditating on their value.
Just to listen or read without meditating
is like looking through the lens of a movie camera
without pressing the record button.
We see things and hear things,
but nothing is recorded.
So we need to meditate, visualize,
and review these reminders.
This will help us to remember what we learn.
But, figuratively speaking, there is something else
that we can do to press the record button.
That means we don’t have to wait
for someone else to give us a reminder.
We can make our own reminder.
How can we do so?
The answer to that question
is highlighted in Jehovah’s instructions to Moses
as found at Exodus 17:14:
“Jehovah now said to Moses:
“‘Write this as a memorial
“‘[or the footnote says: “reminder”]
in the book and repeat it to Joshua.’”
What’s the point?
Write down new things we want to remember.
Some brothers use a notebook, or exercise book,
to write down a list of interesting points that they want to remember.
Then they look through the book from time to time
to remind themselves of those points.
Many of us do this with our notes from conventions and assemblies.
Of course, to do that successfully,
you need to remember where you put the notebook.
Additionally, we have to be careful
that we don’t write down every little fact.
Otherwise, we may become overwhelmed with all the information.
We can make these notes either on paper
or electronically using computers or electronic devices.
Whatever system we use, let’s make lists of things
that we want to remember.
Many brothers have found it good to have two separate lists.
One list could be subjects
—perhaps points that we want to use
in the ministry or in our own lives.
Another, scriptures
—explanations that clarify the meaning of certain verses.
With regard to notes on scriptures,
let’s ask a very important question:
Do you have a study Bible?
What is a study Bible?
Perhaps it’s a separate Bible
to the one you take in the ministry.
It’s a Bible for you to write in
so that you’re reminded of things that you’ve learned.
These are some of the things we can do with a study Bible:
Highlight or underline some words or verses.
That will make it easier to find them again.
But remember not to make too many highlights or marks;
otherwise, nothing will stand out.
Write a summary of points and scriptures you want to remember
on the blank pages in the front or the back of your Bible.
Write notes in the margin
—that’s what Gilead students often do.
Of course, you need the right type of pen or pencil
that won’t bleed through to the other side of the page.
What type of things could you write in the margin?
Perhaps new points that you learn while reading magazines
or attending meetings and assemblies.
If you learn a new point, ask yourself,
‘What verse is being explained?’
And then write a brief comment in the margin next to that verse.
Let’s take an example.
Perhaps you are reading the Sermon on the Mount
and you get to Matthew 7:24-27.
That’s the illustration
about the two men who built houses
—one on sand and the other on rock.
As you research this in Watchtower Library
or the Research Guide,
you come across the article
“Are You Building on Sand or on Rock?”
in the November 1, 2008, Watchtower.
What points could you write in the margin
to help you remember the explanation?
Well, perhaps you could write:
Sand equals build on the surface.
Rock equals dig down deep.
Digging equals doing and applying.
You might even put Luke 6:46-48 there.
Now, if you still have room and your writing is small,
you could add something like this:
Not hearers only, but doers.
Both houses in same location,
same tests, foundations different.
Now every time you read those verses,
you will be reminded of what they mean.
Perhaps like me,
you’ve had several study Bibles over the years.
I think back to the first one I used.
It was like this big green Bible.
Then, later that was replaced by another Bible
—this black covered Bible.
And then, further still,
we had another Bible —the Reference Bible.
And, of course, now for most of us,
we have the large-print Bible.
This does, however,
highlight a challenge we might experience.
It can be frustrating
when a new edition of the Bible comes out.
How do you transfer all your study notes
over to the new Bible?
Additionally, our beloved study Bible may wear out
or, worse still, be lost, stolen, burned, ruined, run over, blown away.
So that’s the advantage of using an electronic list;
it doesn’t matter what type of file you use.
It can be updated very easily, and you can even make copies
—not like the printed copy
that already has the old idea written in the margin.
Even now in English,
we have the books of Matthew, Mark, and Luke
in our electronic study Bible
on jw.org and WOL.
Later in the program, we have some exciting news
about how JW Library will help us in this regard.
But I’ll leave that for later.
Really, having a study Bible is not only helpful
but it also makes our personal study far more interesting.
How so?
Every time we read or study a publication,
we’ll find ourselves searching for new points
that we can write in our study Bible.
This way, we’ll be doing what the psalmist expressed
at Psalm 119:111:
‘We will take Jehovah’s reminders
‘as our permanent possession (or heritage),
for his reminders are the joy of our hearts!’
But do you agree that sometimes the reminders we get
may be less than pleasant?
Maybe they even hurt!
In this dramatization,
pay attention to how we should respond to counsel.
Today started out well.
But after the meeting tonight,
my feelings were hurt.
Earlier in the week, we invited some friends over to watch a movie.
And apparently,
this new young elder heard about it,
so he counseled me about it after the meeting,
saying that I should give my movie choices
some thought.
I just didn’t like the way he gave the counsel.
He’s only 27.
That’s too young.
The next day, we had plans to go out in the ministry
with Brother Kang and his wife.
But the motivation
just wasn’t there.
I asked to speak with Brother Kang alone.
I told him what happened
and how we didn’t feel the counsel applied to us.
I can understand how you might feel.
But, Byong Soo,
be absolutely honest with me.
Do you feel there is no valid reason for that counsel?
Mm.
Well, maybe there were some scenes
that could have been less violent.
But the way he gave the counsel
—he didn’t even ask how we felt.
Byong Soo, what is the only way
for us to receive perfect counsel?
From a perfect man.
That’s right.
And is Jesus here on the earth today?
He was right.
Counsel can only be perfect
if it’s given from a perfect person.
Still, this counsel about our movie choices
would have been so much easier
if it came from someone older and more experienced,
like Brother Kang.
Well, he must have sensed what I was thinking
because he helped me to remember
something from the Bible.
When Job underwent severe trials,
it was the younger Elihu who helped Job
adjust his thinking correctly.
It required humility on Job’s part
to listen to someone younger and less experienced.
He then read Proverbs 19:20:
“Listen to counsel and accept discipline,
in order to become wise in your future.”
The point was clear:
Keep our focus on the counsel,
not the counselor.
I later shared Brother Kang’s comments with my wife.
We both realized that we should welcome
all counsel from Jehovah.
It’s for our good.
I’m sure it took courage
for that young elder to approach me about the matter.
But I’m so glad he did because,
in the end, his counsel
was just another example
of God’s love.
Yes, we all need reminders.
And did you notice some of the main teaching points
in this dramatization?
First, we need to be humble
when we receive counsel.
Second, we need to keep our focus on the counsel,
not the counselor.
And the young elder likely learned from the experience too.
Perhaps next time, after conferring with a seasoned elder,
he might handle matters with a little bit more tact and discretion.
But we can’t rely solely on receiving reminders from others
to keep our spirituality intact.
We need to do our part.
One of the tools that can help us
to actively search out reminders
is JW Library.
This amazing app has been installed
on over 15 million devices.
But do you know how much work it takes
to develop and maintain this app?
Well, we are now going  to look behind the scenes
and meet some of the brothers who have either worked on this project
or helped to organize that work.
This really is an opportunity to visit
an area in Bethel that you don’t get to see on tour.
Of course, there are many brothers associated with the work.
But we would like you to get to know three
of these very hard-working brothers,
and let me introduce them to you.
First of all, Brother Per Christensen, the overseer of MEPS Programming.
Now, Per, you’ve been in this country
working in the U.S. Bethel for a number of years.
But where are you from originally?
I was born in Denmark
and served there in the branch for years.
So when did you and your wife, Berit, come to the United States?
And our first year was in Brooklyn.
And then we had 18 years in Patterson
and then back to Brooklyn again for three and a half years.
And now we’re in Warwick since November last year.
Well, I know you worked in Translation Services for a while
because, in fact, the two of us worked together
in the same department there for a while.
But what type of work have you been involved with
since you’ve come to the United States?
Lots of exciting and challenging jobs.
Working in Translation Services
—that was training and support for our translators worldwide.
Now in MEPS Programming
—that is all about distribution of spiritual food
to all our brothers and sisters.
So we have a ton of work and a lot of challenges.
But I’m also working with a lot
of very, very talented brothers and sisters.
So it’s a lot of fun, and it’s great going to work every day.
That’s great to hear, Per.
In fact, I’m even tempted to come back and work with you.
Oh, we would love that.
I think I’d love it too.
Well, let’s turn our attention to Brother Alfredo Serna.
Now, you are the assistant overseer of MEPS Programming.
In fact, you and I worked together in Mexico back in 2003.
Could you tell us a little bit about what you were doing at that time?
My last work assignment involved overseeing
the large Translation Department there.
It was an amazing privilege to work
with translators in sign language and the indigenous languages,
a true joy to contribute to preparing publications
for those in the minority groups.
So when did you and your wife, Gina, come to the United States to work here?
We arrived at Patterson in 2007.
We have fond memories of that time,
and it’s something we still treasure.
Very good.
And now, Brother Paul Willies,
where do you originally come from along with your wife, Su-lin,
and when did you come to the United States?
Well, we’re both originally from South Africa,
and we served there in Bethel for a number of years.
And then in 2010, we were transferred to work
along with MEPS Programming here in the U.S.
So, what type of work have you been involved with,
particularly recently?
Well, most of my time in Bethel
I’ve been working on the Watchtower Translation System,
or WTS.
Actually, I was working along with Per.
Per was in headquarters, and I was working
on the programming team that we had in South Africa.
WTS is the program that the translators use
to help organize and manage their translation work.
And then, of course, most recently I’ve been working on the mobile apps
—the JW Library app and the JW Library Sign Language app.
Very good.
Well, now all of you work in MEPS Programming.
Per, can you just tell us a little bit?
We’re familiar with the term MEPS, but what really is it?
Well, MEPS stands for
Multilanguage Electronic Publishing System.
That didn’t help me at all.
Sorry.
Can you make it a little bit more simple so we can understand?
We make the tools, or the programs, that the organization needs
to make publications
and have them translated into hundreds of languages.
So I can illustrate it this way:
that we are not making the spiritual food,
but we are building a conveyor belt for the spiritual food
from the faithful and discreet slave
down to the printing presses
or to our website or to Watchtower Library,
ONLINE LIBRARY or, like in this case, JW Library.
Thanks so much.
Now, at long last, I do understand a bit more
about what MEPS means.
Now, as I travel around, the brothers and sisters,
they tell me how much they love JW Library.
But there seems to be no end
to the suggestions for improvements and features
—and long lists of suggestions.
Can you give us a little bit of an idea of what’s involved
with trying to develop a new feature for JW Library?
Yes, the brothers and the sisters really love using the app,
and because of that, they’re keen to get many new features.
Of course, we wish we could just add all those new features into the app,
but the truth is we just can’t.
Yes, adding each new feature involves a lot of work.
And we also need to determine whether a feature
that’s requested is just a “nice to have”
or is it something that’s going to address a real need?
For example, will it really help an elder who is out on a shepherding call
or maybe a pioneer sister who is at the public witnessing carts
or at her Bible study or return visit?
Also, very important to us is trying to make
each new feature very simple to use . . .
Ah, thanks for doing that.
. . . especially for a first-time user, someone who’s never used the app before.
And then, of course, before we start working on anything,
we always get approval from the Governing Body.
Ah, that’s a good thing to do too.
Like one feature that many have been asking for
is the ability to add notes into the app.
And, of course, before we start programming it,
we have to make sure that it actually does what is wanted.
We made a video that shows how we go about that.
You have?
Would you like to see it?
Well, of course. I’d love to see it!
Hello. How are you?
Good, good, good.
Welcome! Thanks for coming.
How about yourself?
Fine, thank you. Have a seat.
All right, so glad you could be here!
Thank you so much.
Oh, so fancy.
Yeah! So we get to talk about JW Library today.
So, what are some ways that you use JW Library?
I mean, it’s revolutionized going to meetings.
Oh, my.
I go to meetings and sometimes I just carry my iPad.
So the fact that you can make the text larger. . .
It’s easy to listen to the readings right in the app now,
and so I—I find myself doing that.
So if we were to make a notes feature,
what are some things that you’d like to be able to do?
I mean, if you could see all your notes without tapping on
each one that would be great.
And even if you make a note in, maybe, your phone
and it can also be saved in your tablet, that would be really nice.
Yeah.
Well, what if I told you that in front of you
is an early version of JW Library?
Whoa! Cool!
Oh, fantastic!
This is it?
With notes—yeah.
Ooh.
So a few months ago, the Governing Body
gave us approval to start working on the notes feature.
We got together as a team, and we’ll do, like, these rough sketches,
and programmers write code.
But before we release an update,
we have a group of testers.
And, you know, they’ll find little glitches or bugs or things,
but they’ll try to work it out with the programmers.
After that, we have a pretty stable version of JW Library.
The goal is to show it to you,
and you can let us know what you think.
So now that you’ve seen the new notes feature
in JW Library, what do you think?
I love that I can tag the personal things that I need to work on
or a comment or a scripture that I can encourage someone with.
This is fantastic!
Yeah. It’s great.
I like that I can find my notes, especially using the search feature.
It’s great!
And it’s really neat how my comments—
I can place it right next to the paragraph for meetings,
and it doesn’t cover the actual text.
The ability to back it up so you can restore it to another device,
that’s going to be really helpful.
I love it!
Amazing!
OK. Go ahead.
Yeah. Go ahead!
So you’re telling us we can proceed.
That’s fantastic!
But, brothers, you can’t show us something like that
and not tell us when we’re going to get it.
Well, we said on the website that it was coming soon.
I know you said that on the website, but when?
Is it OK to be more specific than that?
I think that’s why they invited us here.
Paul, let’s hear it.
Well, we’re happy to tell you that the notes feature
in JW Library will be coming soon,
and by soon we mean during May of 2017—this month!
So we can go and check the app stores for an update.
Oh, that’s wonderful to hear.
So all of us will be happy to be able to put our own reminders
right there in the JW Library app.
Well, I’m looking forward to being able to do that as well.
But now, while I’ve got you here,
we’re not going to let you go until we ask this big question:
What are you working on now?
In other words, what can we expect to see soon with JW Library?
We have another brief video showing what the team is working on
to support the Study Bible on the JW Library app.
Would you like to see it?
That’s wonderful. Let’s have a look.
Later this year,
work will begin on adding the Study Edition
of the New World Translation to JW Library.
When this edition becomes available
in your language,
you will be able to discover
spiritual gems in the study notes.
And the new media gallery
will help you to visualize the people, places,
and things you read about.
You will also see the new overviews of each book,
play the introductory videos,
and study additional appendix material.
All of this and more
is coming soon to JW Library!
That sounds so exciting.
So we’ll all look forward to getting that feature.
You said, “coming soon,” didn’t you?
Anyway, we’d like to thank you very much
for the fact that you’ve come along and you’ve explained so much to us
about what goes on with MEPS Programming
and the JW Library app.
But before you go,
we’d like to ask you, when you go back to your department,
please, take an expression of our appreciation
back to the hard-working brothers and sisters
who are working behind the scenes in providing this tool for us.
Will do.
Happy to.
Thanks.
Thank you very much.
And speaking of behind the scenes,
do you remember the beautiful dramas
we had at the regional convention last year?
One of them was about King Hezekiah.
We saw not only the threat Jehovah’s people faced
but also the protection Jehovah provided.
In producing the drama,
the Audio/Video Services Department used a lot of visual effects.
Let’s go behind the scenes and find out what the work entailed.
The goal of our visual effects team
is to take the work done during film production and expand it.
Our work was driven by the Bible account.
The audience needed to feel
the intimidating power of the Assyrian army
while not endangering our actors.
And the use of visual effects had the added benefit
of drastically saving donated funds.
But this meant creating hundreds of digital arrows, war machines,
cities, tents, soldiers,
and even an Assyrian palace.
In some cases, the foreground elements
had to be separated from the background
so digital components could be added.
This was a time-consuming process,
as many foreground elements had to be cut out frame by frame,
24 times for each second of video.
Our research team ensured that the world created
was as accurate as possible.
For example,
having period-correct materials for the temple
as well as accurate stone reliefs.
After filming was complete,
the research team noted some scenes in the treasury
were accidentally shot showing priests wearing sandals.
As this was inaccurate,
the issue was corrected by generating additional digital treasures
and placing them in the foreground.
As we didn’t have the luxury of 185,000 extras,
actors were dressed in ancient costumes and their pictures were taken.
We then used these pictures to create digital extras,
using crowd-simulating software
to place them in the scenes and drive their movements.
The angel shot proved to be one of the most challenging.
The original version didn’t have the dramatic feel needed for the scene.
So the entire sequence was recreated
to more accurately convey the immense power
that those present must have witnessed.
Finishing this project on schedule had many challenges.
After hearing about just a few of them,
one industry expert said
what we were attempting was impossible.
But like Hezekiah when hearing negative reports,
we stayed positive and relied on Jehovah.
With His help, the film was completed on time
and is now a wonderful tool to bring this Bible account to life.
A beautiful drama,
and how encouraging it was
to see Jehovah rescue his people!
The 2016 regional convention was excellent,
don’t you agree?
But you’ll be happy to know that we have prepared a little glimpse
of what is to come at this year’s convention
to whet your appetite.
Are you OK?
Brian, I’m worried.
You need more money.
Jehovah will take care of us.
He always has.
We have enough.
Maybe enough for today,
but what if you get sick?
Gloria’s mother keeps badgering her and me to move up.
I can get a job at my uncle’s real estate firm.
Maybe this is an answer to our prayers.
What about your pioneering?
What about it? I can do both.
Gloria, I must congratulate you
on your hard work with my company.
But you must learn to keep your religion in its place.
We’re neglecting family worship, study, service.
We’ve even become too busy,
or maybe too ashamed, to even pray together.
I’m concerned about you.
One of the things that you always talked to me about
was Matthew 6:24:
‘You cannot slave for God and for Riches.’
You’re not the same person that I once knew.
Dad,
where is Mom?
She is coming, right?
Is it really wrong
to try to improve our life?
Mom.
“Remember the wife of Lot.”
“Remember the wife of Lot.”
“Remember the wife of Lot.”
If you have yet to make definite plans
to attend your regional convention this year,
don’t delay.
Our conventions are a loving provision from Jehovah.
Whatever it takes
—talking to your boss to get time off work
or making travel plans—
yes, whatever it takes, our efforts are worth it
because we truly treasure Jehovah’s reminders.
Jesus’ words at Matthew 11:28
are very appropriate considering everything
we go through in this system of things:
“Come to me, all you who are toiling and loaded down,
and I will refresh you.”
Yes, conventions can be of refreshment to us,
giving us the boost we need.
But such refreshment is also available
when the world around us seems to be falling apart.
How does the organization help our brothers and sisters
in times of national crisis?
We met two Witness couples who personally experienced
two of the largest terrorist attacks in recent years.
Not a day goes by when we don’t think
about our son, Paulie.
There was horror and suffering,
things we don’t want to witness anymore.
September 11 was a very scary, terrifying day.
As for me,
when I really understood what was happening, I got scared.
I didn’t know what to do.
I didn’t know what to think.
I felt helpless.
When the second tower fell,
Paulie was on the 110th floor
and everybody was shouting, crying.
I was praying to Jehovah
because I was heartbroken.
We live on Voltaire Boulevard; it’s a broad avenue.
There is a concert hall called the Bataclan.
When the doors of the Bataclan are open,
we can hear everything that goes on inside.
That night, three men entered the Bataclan concert hall,
and they started shooting into the crowd.
We immediately grabbed our “go bag.”
And then we sat in front of the sofa,
and we begged Jehovah for his holy spirit
so we could face the situation.
It was around 10:00 p.m. when there was a news flash
that announced that there was an attack.
I was in shock when I heard the news,
and then I immediately thought about our brothers and sisters.
I quickly got in contact with the circuit overseer
in order to get some news about our brothers and sisters,
to know how they were doing.
Then,
very early the next morning,
we set up an emergency committee made up of several brothers
from the Service Department.
We decided to write a letter and make other arrangements
to assist the friends who, in one way or another,
were affected by this event.
In turn,
the circuit overseer would make an effort
to rapidly get in touch with the elders
who oversee the affected territory.
One of our challenges, on a personal level,
was whether we would even be able
to encourage our brothers and sisters
because we had never experienced such a terrible event.
We organized ourselves;
we paired up as elders and headed off to do shepherding.
We started calling midmorning on Tuesday.
We received a report back
from all the traveling overseers
by the end of Thursday.
And unfortunately,
we learned that 14 of our brothers and sisters
had lost their lives.
We knew that we needed to encourage the families;
we knew that we needed to shepherd them as soon as possible.
The elders immediately came.
We went over the book of Job,
and I just listened.
You know, I was just listening.
I’ve heard the same words before, but it was different now.
The things that were being said went straight to my heart.
A few days later, we were visited by two brothers from Bethel.
It was very touching that they came to see us
and that they were concerned about us.
It shows us that Jehovah was aware of how we felt that night.
Our brothers were there.
They were ready to help one another out.
Then there was so much empathy and love shown.
When we were ultimately granted
access to ground zero
and we started encountering
the first responders,
we let them know how much we appreciated their hard work
and that they had a skill set
that we didn’t have.
But yet our skill set
was trying to offer comfort to them.
We shared a scripture with them.
Immediately, we could tell that that was something
that caused emotion to rise up in them right away.
And they expressed
great appreciation for that.
It’s one of the beautiful things about the Scriptures
—that they’re calming, soothing, comforting.
And the Scriptures did not let down the workers
that were there at ground zero either.
The visit of the brothers from Bethel was really
a gift from Jehovah.
It showed his genuine interest in us.
It was really wonderful.
After the brothers visited us,
we felt so comforted,
so encouraged,
that we said to each other:
“We have to get back in the ministry
“and comfort people in the territory.
We have to console our brothers and sisters as well.”
We can only thank and glorify Jehovah,
who really is a God of love.
I kind of felt
Jehovah’s hand just reaching out to me,
which I needed.
But I cannot wait till the day that I’m totally refreshed.
Where I can see, I can actually see,
Paulie.
I can see him just coming back
into our lives,
and I want to embrace him so much.
After something like this, we are not the same.
But
with the help of the organization
—the brothers—
Jehovah is there for us.
So that—
That is refreshing.
And I thank Jehovah a lot
for what he wants to do for me
and also for the millions of people
that feel the same way.
What these couples went through
was a horrible reminder of Satan’s rule,
but we look forward to the relief from Jehovah
—the only true hope we have.
Reminders of Jehovah’s care, such as these interviews,
can be ‘the joy of our heart,’ as the psalmist said.
Yes, “the reminder of Jehovah is trustworthy,
making the inexperienced one wise.”
Before we conclude,
let’s visit our brothers and sisters in India.
India is the second-most-populated country in the world,
with a population of some 1.2 billion people.
The Kingdom preaching work is conducted
by some 45,000 brothers and sisters
in 627 congregations,
and last year,
close to 125,000 people attended
the Memorial of Christ’s death.
Our visit brings us to Peermedu,
which is located in the southern tip
of the Indian Peninsula, in the state of Kerala.
This town is located
some 914 meters, or almost 3,000 feet, above sea level.
It is a land of spices and lush greenery,
with tea and coffee plantations.
The two congregations there have a total of 70 publishers.
Many of them work in tea estates
and struggle to make a living.
They are eager users of the JW Library app,
which they use to share our videos
and publications in the ministry.
As Peermedu is a hill station,
their territory consists of rugged and uneven terrain.
Since the congregations there are watching
this program together with all of us,
we wanted to take this opportunity
to convey their warm Christian greetings
to all of Jehovah’s people around the world.
We love you very much.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: We would like to welcome all of you
to a special broadcast
from the world headquarters
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As you may have already heard,
yesterday, April 20,
the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation
ruled against Jehovah’s Witnesses
and decided to liquidate
the Administrative Center of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Russia
and all 395 Local Religious Organizations.
In essence, this means
that the properties owned by the organization,
such as our Kingdom Halls and our beautiful branch office,
have been unjustly confiscated
by the Russian government.
The ruling goes into effect immediately.
Our hearts go out to you dear brothers and sisters in Russia,
but we know that you deeply appreciate the support given to you
by the worldwide brotherhood.
Just think of how many letters were sent to Russian officials
by your fellow worshippers around the world!
Contemplate how many prayers
and supplications were offered up to Jehovah
and will continue to be made in your behalf!
Your confidence in Jehovah warms our heart.
In just a moment,
we will be speaking with Brother Mark Sanderson,
who was present in the courtroom
when the decision was announced.
However, before speaking with him,
we know you will be very interested
in this account of the six days of proceedings
that led up to this very disappointing decision.
The report includes comments from a delegation of brothers
sent by the Governing Body to meet with officials
and to be present
for portions of the trial.
The Governing Body assigned me to come here,
not only for the trial
that’s to take place today,
but also to try
and see if we could do something
to encourage our brothers here on a small scale.
When we arrived at the airport, there was a large group of brothers.
Many of them were of considerable size;
they just kind of shepherded us through the airport.
We were standing there with them for a few minutes,
and then one of the brothers suddenly smiled,
and he said to me in Russian, “Thank you so much for coming.”
The fundamental question in this case
is whether Jehovah’s Witnesses
are engaged in extremist activity
and whether the Administrative Center
is guilty of having organized this extremist activity.
When it became known
that the Supreme Court of Russia was considering a ban
on the worship of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
embassies from around the world requested
information as to what led up to this.
We were successful in getting high-level meetings
with a number of different officials at embassies here in Moscow,
and it’s really been quite impressive
to see the reaction of these people in high station.
It impressed me that so many of them were eager
to want to do something within the limited sphere that they have.
And uniformly,
they are just amazed
that Jehovah’s Witnesses, of all people,
are subject to criticism
or ban on the basis of being extremists.
Now, that comes across to them
as completely absurd because if there’s one group
of people that’s known for their neutrality,
it is Jehovah’s people.
Really,
now our eyes are poised toward the trial.
We’re getting ready to go to the court,
and we’ll wait and see what’s going to happen.
As we were going to the court, there were about 200
waiting to get into the courtroom, mostly our brothers,
but then some who were just interested in the hearing.
We could see the cameramen, the microphones,
and the many reporters who were there.
It was clear that this was now an international event.
Just when we were in the entranceway,
we stepped in and here was a couple
that I had met many years ago in Siberia.
And here they had come all the way from Siberia
to testify in the hearing, to be witnesses.
We had four different brothers representing the Administrative Center.
Each one would take the lead in arguing one motion.
The judge would listen to what the brothers had to say,
turn to the Ministry of Justice, and ask,
“Does the Ministry of Justice have any input on this?”
The prosecutor would stand,
literally say two or three sentences, sit down,
and the judge would say:
The brothers raised 20 motions
that they wanted the court to hear.
Of those 20 motions,
the court granted only two of them to see how
evidence that would exonerate us
was not going to be allowed in the hearing.
After seeing so many of them be dismissed,
then you began to say,
“Well, they really weren’t going
to take any of them seriously.”
For example, the brothers were able to show clearly
that the congregations that had been liquidated
were the result
of the planting of literature, and that this was on video,
and that the Supreme Court would refuse
to even see the video.
And that was really a lasting impression
that this was a little bit of a sham,
and it was designed
to go through the formalities,
but you got the sense that the decision
had already been taken.
At the hearing, representatives from many embassies were there,
and as they listened to the court hear whether local congregations
would be allowed to defend themselves
and to hear that the court said “no,” they were not going to be heard,
these embassy representatives were appalled.
And I thought it was quite interesting that when they saw
how ridiculous some of the rejections of the motions were at the trial,
there was a murmur of laughter in the audience,
particularly when the judge cut off our lawyers
when they were presenting the evidence of the planted publications.
This to them is evidence that it’s so absurd
that you haven’t got the real evidence
to bring a charge of extremism so you plant evidence.
Although we were in the Supreme Court,
they don’t have so many formalities in the court
as perhaps they have in other lands,
and so the brothers were allowed to stand up and walk around.
To me it had more the atmosphere of a circuit assembly
than being in a courtroom.
I think it made the charge
that’s been brought upon us
all the more absurd and ridiculous.
You know, just so many came up and said how grateful they were
to feel the support from the Governing Body,
that they were not facing this situation alone.
It occurred to me that it was really a small thing
to travel here,
but for them, it was symbolic.
They felt that the Governing Body was there with them.
The decision has not been made.
We’ll have to wait and see.
The government had only given us a six-day visa,
and so it was impossible for us to stay any longer.
So our entire delegation, of course,
with the exception of Brother Kalin,
we all had to leave the next day.
We had in our mind that we were going to go and strengthen them,
but as is always the case, I think we were the ones
who came away even more strengthened
in our own faith.
One ten-year-old wrote this note to the visiting delegation,
“Thank you for coming to support us
and for your ministry.”
—Sascha, ten years old, Moscow.
As we were leaving
and saying good-bye to these brothers,
there was not a dry eye among us.
They were hugging Brother Sanderson and telling him,
“This is the spiritual high point of my life.”
Something occurred in day two
that was unexpected and surprising to us.
Interestingly, the judge became very active,
and he began to really question
the Ministry of Justice.
Why are you bringing this case?
What evidence do you have
that they are engaged in extremist activities?
The third day of the hearing reminded us
of Matthew 10:18.
“And you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake.”
But then, what’s the reason?
It says, “for a witness to them and the nations.”
The international community, worldwide,
has now heard the testimony
of six Jehovah’s Witnesses, clearly, cogently,
convincingly explaining to the court
that we are law-abiding, peaceful citizens
—the farthest thing from extremists.
For example, one longtime member of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
Vasiliy Kalin, explained to the judge
that as a child, he had been forced into exile with his parents
and was forced to live in Siberia for years.
Decades later, he was exonerated
and cleared of all charges against him.
In Russia, he’s considered or referred to as a rehabilitated person,
meaning that the charges against him have now been expunged.
And now at this point in his life, they’re saying he’s an extremist.
Anyone could see that the same efforts
that had been made so long ago to try to hunt down
and wipe out Jehovah’s Witnesses
were just reappearing now at this particular time.
I was texting with one of the brothers at the Russia branch
asking how things were going.
He says: “Wow!
“They just announced that the court
“has been suspended until Wednesday, April 12,
the day after the Memorial.”
And we were all just—
We could hardly believe it that the court is ending on a Friday
but being postponed until Wednesday.
How wonderful!
We had an adjournment up until April 19.
That gives the brotherhood in Russia the opportunity
to attend the special talk.
And that special talk is all about peace
—“How to Cultivate Peace in an Angry World.”
So we really hope to be in the courtroom with our brothers
at the time when the decision is issued,
even though it would seem almost impossible
that we could get a visa to return to Russia.
Basically,
we would have to make application from Kazakhstan.
If Jehovah wills and we are able to get the visa,
then Tuesday evening, I’ll return to Russia
and then on Wednesday morning, we will be in the court.
Brothers were hugging each other;
at lunchtime everybody was sharing their sandwiches with each other.
The atmosphere of joy and love was unforgettable.
The judge began to go through all of the evidence,
and so there were 43 volumes of evidence
that had been brought forth in the trial
either by the Ministry of Justice or by our attorneys.
And so every one of those volumes
had to be reviewed.
And so it was kind of a long process.
Our attorneys were able
to ask the Ministry of Justice,
“Where is the evidence
“that funding from the Administrative Center
was used for any improper activities?”
And so the brothers came back:
“Well, tell me how much money? how many rubles?
how many kopecks were spent to fund this improper activity?”
And the ministry:
“Well we don’t have any; we don’t have any information like that.”
I thought it was quite a surprise to me that one single judge
could deliberate on six days of evidence
and within an hour come back and ban
a religion from practicing its faith.
When one part of the body suffers, we all suffer,
and that will be the feeling throughout the world, I’m sure.
We will allow Jehovah our God to correct the injustices.
We will continue to be peaceable with all men.
We will never ‘return evil for evil to anybody.’
We have Brother Mark Sanderson
of the Governing Body tied in with us.
We’re so happy to have you with us, Mark.
And first, we’d just like to thank you very much
for making the trip to Russia, Moscow,
to be with the brothers during this critical time.
And we heard so many comments
about how much the brothers appreciated
having you there with them.
Oh, thank you so much, Steve.
You know, to stand unitedly with our brothers in Russia
in that courtroom when they were facing
such a vicious attack on their worship from the Devil
was a tremendous privilege.
I have to say, you know, in all my years in serving Jehovah,
I don’t think I ever felt so proud to be one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
as when I was standing in that courtroom.
Very encouraging, Mark.
But tell us, please, a little more
about what was the reaction of the brothers
when they heard this negative decision?
Well, you know, Steve,
to understand their reaction,
I think we have to just kind of recap with what’s been happening
because for the last couple of days,
there has been such a joyful spirit in the courtroom.
The brothers and sisters have been walking around,
greeting one another,
taking photographs, you know,
hugging one another, there’s just been this tremendous, joyful feeling
within this courtroom.
And so then, just before the decision was given,
we heard the closing statements from our four attorneys
and also from Brother Sergey Cherepanov
and Brother Vasiliy Kalin
who are both on the Branch Committee in Russia.
And, you know, these brothers made such powerful statements;
their arguments were so compelling
that we all felt just very pumped up by what they said.
And then, one of the statements that several of these brothers made
was that really we’re not really standing
before the Russian Supreme Court
but really the Great Judge of the universe, Jehovah,
is the one who’s judging all matters.
And they reminded everyone in that courtroom
that everyone is going to have to stand
before the judgment seat of God.
And when we heard that,
we all just felt so inspired by those comments.
Well, then after a few moments
when the judge actually issued his decision
and the brothers and sisters heard that it was negative,
it was just totally silent in the courtroom.
There was no outcry; there was no comment.
Some of the brothers shook their head.
I think we were just all in total disbelief
that the judge could issue such an unjust decision,
after hearing these tremendous arguments from our brothers.
But I have to say,
although we were stunned by the unjust decision
there was no hint in that courtroom
that our brothers are backing down,
that they’re cowering,
or that they’re going to give up their service to Jehovah.
In fact, you could see that they
were even strengthened by this decision
to go on serving Jehovah faithfully
under their new circumstances.
Those comments, Mark,
are so heartening to us to hear.
But even though there was a negative decision,
how would you say
that a great shout of praise
has gone up to Jehovah’s name?
You know, Steve, I just keep coming back
to what Jesus said at Matthew 10:18.
He said that we would ‘be brought before kings and governors,
for a witness to them and to the nations.’
Well, that’s exactly what’s happened here.
We have been brought before kings and governors.
But what a tremendous witness
has been given to them and to the nations!
For example,
we did this letter-writing campaign.
Our brothers participated all around the world,
and then the news media caught on to that,
and many newspapers and other media outlets reported
on this tremendous effort
to write letters to the officials of the Russian government.
Then the delegation that was sent by the Governing Body to Moscow,
we were able to meet with three different ambassadors
from the largest countries on this earth.
And these ambassadors who are so difficult to meet with
welcomed us in;
they listened to us patiently;
and they showed that they had
a very deep respect for Jehovah’s Witnesses,
being very familiar with our work
and really wanting to do things to help Jehovah’s people.
It was wonderful!
And then, consider all the media coverage
that’s been taking place
on the court case day after day after day.
And now, we have a decision.
And so now this court decision is going to be publicized
by the media all over the world again.
And still to come,
we have our appeals that are going to be made in the Russian Supreme Court,
in the European Court of Human Rights, with the Human Rights Commission.
All of this is going to result in more publicity.
And in the end, really, what can we say?
Well, people who know Jehovah’s Witnesses
—people who have Jehovah’s Witnesses as their neighbors,
as their workmates, as their schoolmates,
who really know who we are—
when they hear these reports, they are going to immediately recognize
that these charges are ridiculous and absurd.
And they are perhaps even going to want to ask questions
and perhaps even become interested in the truth.
So even through this negative decision,
Jehovah’s name is being exalted and glorified in all the earth.
That is so wonderful, Brother Sanderson,
what you’ve expressed.
And one thing that we’re just so happy about
is that the brothers were able to celebrate
the Memorial of Christ’s death
before the negative decision was rendered.
I know many of us —I was praying and others—
were praying that if it be Jehovah’s will
—now of course, we always want his will to take place—
but if it was his will,
that at least they could celebrate the Memorial in peace.
And so that happened, and we’re so happy.
Yes, that was my prayer too.
And, really, when the decision was made
to adjourn the court until the day after the Memorial,
you know, we really had to see Jehovah’s hand in it
because across Russia now that all of the reports have come in,
we understand that only in three cases
did the police come to a location
where the Memorial was being celebrated.
But even in those cases,
they did not attempt to disturb the occasion.
So we can say that our brothers
were able to celebrate the Memorial
all across Russia in peace.
And, of course, even with the special talk,
because again the court adjourned,
the special talk was also held across Russia in peace.
And so in a mighty way,
Jehovah stood by his people and allowed them to have
these two very important spiritual occasions
before this decision.
We thank Jehovah for that blessing.
We thank you, Mark,
for those very encouraging comments,
and we thank you again for representing the Governing Body
there in Russia and supporting the brothers.
We really appreciate it.
And please, travel home safely.
Thank you so much, Steve.
It was such a wonderful privilege
to be able to be in Russia with our dear brothers
at this historic moment.
I look forward to seeing you when I return.
And we would like to thank
all of you for your support.
You dear brothers and sisters gave heartfelt prayers;
you willingly supported the letter-writing campaign.
For some of you, sending a letter
to one or more of the six Russian officials
came at a great expense.
We commend you
for your strong love for your brothers in Russia
and for your loyalty to Jehovah’s organization.
But does the Supreme Court’s decision against us
mean that the letter-writing campaign failed
or that Jehovah did not hear our prayers?
Absolutely not!
It simply means that we have yet to see
how Jehovah will maneuver events in harmony with his will.
In the meantime, we are confident
that our dear brothers and sisters in Russia
will remain steadfast
and that Psalm 112:7, 8
will be true of them.
There it says of Jehovah’s righteous one:
“He will not fear bad news.
“His heart is steadfast, trusting in Jehovah.
“His heart is unshakable; he is not afraid;
“in the end
he will look in triumph on his adversaries.”
As long as we’re still living in this old system,
as we have seen in Russia and many other lands,
we can expect persecution
for simply wanting to worship Jehovah in peace.
But do we need to fear such persecution?
No!
Jesus Christ and the heavenly armies
are ready to take the lead in defending Jehovah’s people.
We can rest assured
that according to Isaiah 54:17:
“No weapon formed against [us]
will have any success.”
And why?
Because Jehovah is on our side.
May we all continue to pray
for our dear brothers and sisters in Russia
whom we love very much.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: Since the 1980’s,
the Central America branch has been organizing
special preaching campaigns to seldom-worked territories
and unassigned territories —both here in Mexico
and also throughout all of Central America.
Matter of fact, in the last campaign,
we had 13,000 regular pioneers
assigned to over 900 congregations
and in some areas where there weren’t even congregations,
for example, in El Salvador.
When we were assigned here,
we were told that there were no Witnesses,
no Bible studies, and no publishers.
This is the second meeting that we’ve had the public talk,
and today we had 12 new ones attend.
Well, since we’re in a rural area,
you have to do a lot of walking.
We’ve had to deal with the cows
and other smaller creatures, like ticks.
Eight or nine brothers
were staying in one house,
so they had to get up super early
—sometimes at four in the morning—
just to get ready on time.
The brothers who come on these campaigns
come resolved to help the congregation.
They’re really enthusiastic
about the ministry, and it’s contagious.
We’ve found many studies and many return visits.
We just don’t have enough time to care for them all.
Some of the publishers are assigned
to areas where the congregations are small or they’re isolated.
For example, here in Mexico there was a group
of willing, energetic pioneers that were assigned to an area,
and it just injected life into the local publishers,
and even the entire congregation benefited.
We could see that the congregation
really blossomed in showing
hospitality, generosity, and love.
It made the congregation more united,
and we could tell they were happier.
They encourage me
and make me want to preach more.
At one point, we were surrounded by people;
they were so spiritually starved
that they were just asking us for publications.
It always seems that the ones that go on these campaigns
never forget the experiences that they’ve had.
The brothers in Costa Rica are going to share their stories with us.
I remember one sister
who said she had to sell bread
and other products for an entire year
just to be able to come and serve in our congregation.
On one occasion, we preached to a lady who had ten children.
It really moved me when she showed up
at the Kingdom Hall with all of her ten children.
The effort I make has even motivated
my mom to renew her Bible study
and get to know more about Jehovah.
In fact, there were some territories
that we hadn’t preached in for four years
because they are so far away.
But thanks to these brothers
and the effort they made, we were able to cover
all of our congregation’s territory.
Wow! I’m really happy
because just seeing the brothers here gives me strength to keep going.
We met a young woman who had been praying all week
because she wanted to get to know God better.
She was going through a really tough time.
So when we showed her one of our tracts
and she saw that it was based on the Bible,
she burst into tears.
She realized it was the answer to her prayers.
In Panama, the brothers and sisters have seen
the results of their hard work and effort.
Second Corinthians 9:6 says,
‘those that sow bountifully will reap bountifully.’
And they’ve seen the truthfulness of those words.
My family has benefited.
For example, my daughter got baptized
at the last assembly, and I’ve been encouraged as well.
Now I’m a regular pioneer.
It generates a real pioneer spirit in the congregation
and that spurs the brothers on to greater activity.
Some even want to fill out auxiliary pioneer applications.
When you come on a campaign like this,
something enjoyable is
that people you didn’t even know before
become your closest friends.
My relationship with Jehovah has gotten stronger.
I’ve seen how he never abandons me.
For many, these campaigns are a life-altering or life-changing experience.
All the work that the brothers and sisters
put forth is worth it
when they see the gratitude and the appreciation
of their Bible students.
And Nicaragua is a country
where people show that gratefulness for spiritual things.
We spoke with a farmer on one occasion.
And farmers in Nicaragua do not make very much,
but he was so appreciative of the publications we had placed with him
that he gave us a sum that could possibly amount
to a good fourth or a third of his daily wages.
Anyone who has the opportunity to go on these campaigns
—they would not regret it.
They would have amazing experiences.
I’ve done it myself.
And these experiences
—these wonderful opportunities that one would have
to preach on these campaigns—
would be remembered for the rest of their lives.

cn.text: 中美洲分部就一直组织墨西哥
和整个中美洲的特别传道运动
邀请传道员到不常探访的地区
和未分配的地区传道
单是在最近一次的传道运动
就有1万3000个正规先驱
被派到900多群不同的会众
另外有些人被委派的地区甚至没有会众
例如萨尔瓦多
我们来到这里之前
得知当地没有耶和华见证人
没有圣经学生
也没有传道员
今天是第二次举行公众演讲的聚会
就有12个人第一次来参加
我们在乡村地区
要走很多的路
我们常常碰到牛
或是蜱虫这样的小虫
八、九个弟兄同住一间房子
他们为了准时, 要很早就起床
有时清晨四点就要起来
参加特别传道运动的弟兄们
都决心前来帮助当地的会众
他们传道的热诚很有感染力
我们找到许多圣经学生和续访
可是没有时间照顾所有人
有些传道员被委派的地区
会众很小或地点偏远
在墨西哥，就有一群活力充沛的先驱
乐意被派到这样的地区
当地的传道员大受激励
整个会众都获益不浅
我们看出整个会众都充满爱心
洋溢着慷慨好客的精神
会众里的弟兄姊妹也更团结
大家更快乐了
他们鼓励我
让我更想多传道
有一次很多人来找我们
他们很渴望在属灵方面得到饱足
不断向我们要书刊
参加特别传道运动的弟兄姐妹
总是会有令他们难以忘怀的事
哥斯达黎加的弟兄会告诉我们他们的经历
我记得一位姐妹说
她卖了整整一年的面包和其他东西
就是希望能来到我们会众服务
有一次，我们向一位女士传道
她有十个孩子
她后来带着所有孩子来到王国聚会所
令我非常感动
我付出的努力甚至感动我妈妈恢复圣经讨论
学习耶和华的知识
说真的，有些地区因为太远
我们已经四年没有去那里传道了
真的要感谢这些努力付出的弟兄
让我们这次能够传遍会众所有的地区
哇！我真的太开心了！
看到弟兄们来到这里
让我得到力量继续为上帝服务
我们遇到一个年轻女子
她祷告了一个星期就是为了更认识上帝
当时她面对很大的难题
所以收到传单时
她发现是来自圣经就哭了出来
她看出上帝回应了她的祷告
巴拿马的弟兄姐妹
看到所付出的辛劳的成果
哥林多后书9:6说
“慷慨撒种的，收获必多。”
他们亲身体验到经文说得一点也没错
我们整家人都获益不浅
我的女儿在上一个大会受浸
我也受到鼓励开始做正规先驱了
会众弥漫着先驱精神
这激励弟兄们做更多服务
有些还打算报名辅助先驱
参与这样的传道运动
让我跟以往不认识的人成为最要好的朋友
真的很有意思
我和耶和华的友谊更巩固了
我看出他绝不会撇弃我
对很多人来说
这项传道运动改变了他们的一生
弟兄姐妹看到圣经学生对真理深怀感激
就觉得一切付出都是值得的
尼加拉瓜那里的人的确很赏识属灵的事物
我们跟一个农夫交谈
虽然在尼加拉瓜，农夫赚得钱不多
但他非常赏识我们的书刊
他捐了一笔钱
大约是一天收入的三或四分之一
参加这项传道运动的人都有美好的经历
绝对不会后悔
我自己也参加了
相信只有参加这项传道运动的人
才能体验到这种毕生难忘的美好经历

en.text: A little deeper study helps you to draw close to Jehovah.
The interactions that Jehovah has with his faithful servants
—we think about them, we meditate on them,
it actually becomes a personal matter.
Drawing close to God becomes personal,
and then we can use that in our circumstances in life.
If we are dealing with a sickness or the illness of a mate
or even with the great tribulation in the offing,
how are we going to handle our relationship with Jehovah?
How are we going to stay strong?
Well, we had this beautiful drama
“O Jehovah, . . . I Trust in You,”
the Hezekiah drama, that we had for our regional convention.
Since that is still ringing very clearly in our minds and hearts,
let’s open our Bibles to 2 Kings chapter 19.
Let’s review a few thoughts from the life of Hezekiah
and that time period with Sennacherib —the king of Assyria—
the attack on Jerusalem in the year 732 B.C.E.,
and Isaiah’s words to Hezekiah.
Again, with the focus of:
‘How can I draw close to Jehovah God?
What can this account continue to teach me?’
So chapter 19, let’s start with verse 6:
“Isaiah said to them: ‘This is what you should say to your lord,
“This is what Jehovah says.”’”
Now this was to Hezekiah: “Do not be afraid.”
Four words, but so powerful. Why?
Because positive assurance, Hezekiah,
that Sennacherib will be defeated.
‘Do not be afraid because I’ve heard all the things
that Sennacherib has said, and he’s blasphemed me.’
“Do not be afraid.”
Think about that. It engenders confidence.
It engenders in us to approach Jehovah God.
He wants to help us. He wanted to help Hezekiah.
He saw his situation.
Hezekiah was emerging as one of the greatest kings of all Israel.
He was beating the odds. He had an apostate father.
And yet, Jehovah had his eye on Hezekiah and wanted to help him.
“Do not be afraid.”
You see, trusting in Jehovah as Hezekiah did is an act of worship.
It’s something that gets Jehovah’s blessing.
When Jehovah tells us under our circumstances:
“Do not be afraid. I will help you.
I want to help you,” that helps us to be loyal to him.
We draw close to him.
Now when we show loyalty to Jehovah,
then he acts in loyalty toward us.
There’s an action; it’s not passive.
He acts in loyalty toward us.
He gives us his holy spirit.
He draws closer to us.
We feel his support; we can sense that he has helped us.
Our personal relationship with Jehovah becomes more keen, you see.
And that is because Jehovah is telling us as our heavenly Father,
“Do not be afraid.”
He did that to Hezekiah, and he does it with us.
It’s part of drawing close to him.
Next, Hezekiah senses what really is important,
and this is so valuable to you and me.
Let’s go now to verse 19:
“But now, O Jehovah our God,
please save us out of his hand,”
now that is Sennacherib’s hand, we know that,
“so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know
that you alone are God, O Jehovah.”
So “all the kingdoms of the earth,” see,
Hezekiah was interested in Jehovah’s name
—the sanctification of that name.
He was interested in the reputation of Jehovah God.
Now, he didn’t talk about himself,
but he just spoke about Jehovah God.
And again, that is the lesson that we can learn.
If we’re going to draw close to Jehovah,
we think about his reputation, his name,
we think about the issue of universal sovereignty,
we think about what that Kingdom is going to do to cleanse the earth.
Now, I know that oftentimes we think about our own suffering
and ‘I need to get into the new world.’
And we think about the relief that we’re going to have,
and that is, of course, important.
But the core issues —the greater issues—
are Jehovah’s name,
proving the Devil a liar,
our loyalty at this time.
This is what Jehovah is looking at. This is the real issue.
Imagine as the great tribulation approaches
how delightful, how exciting, it’s going to be
as we see even “the sign of the Son of man.”
There at Matthew 24:30,
some supernatural demonstration
displayed of Christ’s kingly power
as Jehovah demonstrates His sovereignty.
“All the kingdoms of the earth”
must know that Jehovah is God.
Again, thinking about these things
really brings our attention to the important things in life,
and it helps us to draw close to Jehovah God.
Let’s go a little bit further.
Let’s look at verse 28.
Now here,
Sennacherib is going to learn a big lesson, we know.
Verse 28: “Because your rage,”
now, Jehovah is speaking to Sennacherib, of course, through Isaiah.
‘Because your rage against me
‘and your roaring have reached my ears.
‘I’m going to put a hook in your nose and a bridle in your lips,
‘and I’m going to lead you back to the way you came,’
right back to Nineveh.
Sennacherib, you made a big mistake
by planting yourself in the land that I gave my people.
You made a big mistake. You shouldn’t have done that.
You’re used to putting hooks
in the noses of other people and bridles in their lips.
Well, I’m going to put a hook in your nose and drag you right back,
yank you back to Nineveh.
This is encouraging.
This helps us to see exactly what Jehovah God is going to do
to this modern-day Assyrian
as they try to attack us in the near future.
Whether it be the modern-day Assyrian or ‘Gog of Magog,’
“the king of the north,” “the kings of the earth,”
they don’t stand a chance.
This helps us to draw close to Jehovah God.
Now verse 29.
Imagine this time period as we saw through that beautiful drama.
How are they going to eat? What are they going to eat?
With the Assyrian invasion,
it’s not possible to have a harvest to sow seed.
What would they do?
Verse 29: “And this will be the sign,”
a miraculous sign, “for you,” Hezekiah,
“This year you will eat what grows on its own.”
So imagine that!
Jehovah says: “Don’t worry!
“From those spilled kernels from last year,
“I’m going to have food shoot up
from the old grain from last year.”
That is amazing!
A miraculous provision of food.
And then notice it goes on, it says:
“And in the second year
you will eat grain that sprouts from that.”
So again, even the second year,
but what is even more interesting,
according to Bible chronology,
that second year would be a Sabbath year of the Jubilee cycle.
And the Sabbath year of the Jubilee cycle,
the faithful Jews would not be able to plant; they wouldn’t sow seed;
they would let the land lay dormant or let it rest.
And Jehovah said, “I’m still going to provide for you.”
And then, of course, it goes on and says:
‘In the third year you can sow seed and reap a harvest.’
You see the faith it must have taken
on the part of these faithful Jews at that time.
Would they really trust that sufficient crops would be available
for two years in a row without working their fields?
How would you have felt?
Maybe it was going through their minds:
‘Well, maybe we should go to Sennacherib.
‘He’s offering us food. He’s offering us survival.
Maybe we should surrender.’
This was portrayed in the drama so beautifully.
So again, what’s the big point for us?
Jehovah wants to help us,
and we draw close to Jehovah God knowing
that as the great tribulation even approaches,
geographical location has no bearing
on Jehovah rendering assistance to his people.
But now is the time:
As we study these accounts, we draw close to Jehovah,
we gain confidence—trusting him,
being loyal, knowing that he will loyally support us
under any circumstances.
So meditating on these accounts
should help us to continue to stay loyal,
not be afraid as God’s enemies will not succeed,
keeping focused that “all the kingdoms of the earth”
must know that Jehovah is God
and that his sovereignty will be the main issue in the universe,
and that Jehovah’s fatherly eye is upon us
as we continue to draw close to God
and serve him for an eternity.

cn.text: 深入研读圣经
能帮助你亲近耶和华
沉思耶和华怎样对待他的忠心仆人
使我们个人更亲近上帝
也能把学到的应用在自己的生活上
当我们自己或配偶生病
或是将来面临大患难时
我们会怎样维系我们与耶和华的关系?
我们怎样才能保持坚强呢?
相信大家记得区域大会的精彩戏剧
《耶和华啊......我信赖你》

就让我们一起翻到圣经列王纪下19章
复习一下希西家的经历
亚述王西拿基立
在公元前732年攻打耶路撒冷

注意力请放在

在列王纪下19:6
以赛亚对他们说

同样, 我们可以学到

他的名字、宇宙至高统治权的争议
以及上帝的王国会怎样洁净地球
有时我们只在乎自己的遭遇
常常想:“我要进入新世界”
也会想我们会得到什么舒解
这对我们来说当然很重要
不过, 更重要的是耶和华的圣名
证明撒但是说谎者
以及我们所表现的忠贞
对耶和华来说, 这才是最重要的事
请想想
当大患难来临时, 我们会多么激动
尤其是看到人子显现的凭证出现的时候
马太福音24:30说
基督的力量会伴随着超自然现象而来
显示耶和华的至高统治权
“地上所有民族”必须知道耶和华是上帝
沉思这段记载
可以帮助我们把焦点
集中在生活重要的事上
并使我们更亲近耶和华上帝
接着, 我们继续看下去, 第28节
上帝要西拿基立学一个重大的教训
耶和华通过以赛亚对西拿基立说
因为你向我动怒, 你的咆哮传到我耳中
我必用钩子钩住你的鼻
拿辔头套住你的嘴
你从哪条路来, 我就使你从哪条路回去
就是回到尼尼微去
上帝仿佛对他说
西拿基立, 你犯下大错了!
你不该来占领我子民的土地
你不应该这么做!
我要拿钩子钩你的鼻, 把你拖回尼尼微
这段话帮助我们看出
当我们在不久的将来
受到现代亚述人的攻击时
耶和华会怎样做
无论是现代的亚述人
“玛歌革地的歌革”、“北方王”
还是“地上的列王”, 都打不倒我们
这项保证能使我们亲近耶和华
第29节, 同时也回想戏剧的情景
他们要如何取得食物呢?
他们要吃什么呢?
面对亚述人大举入侵
根本无法撒种和耕作
那么他们该怎么办?
29节说：“以下是我给你的征兆”
就是给希西家的一个不可思议的征兆
今年你们要吃
收割时掉落地上自生的谷物
你能想象吗?
耶和华说：不要担心！
我会使去年收割时掉落的谷物
长出新芽, 让你们有食物吃
这真是令人难以置信!
上帝通过奇迹, 供应食物给他们
请留意, 经文继续说
“第二年要吃自生的谷物”
耶和华保证
甚至是第二年也会提供食物
有趣的是, 根据圣经年代考究
经文中的第二年
是禧年周期中的一个安息年
在安息年期间, 忠贞的犹太人
不能栽种农作物, 也不能撒种
他们会让土地休耕
但耶和华保证
“我还是会继续供应食物给你们”
经文继续说
“到了第三年, 你们要撒种收割”
你不难看出
当时忠贞的犹太人所需要的信心
他们能够相信不用耕作
也能连续两年有足够的食物吃吗?
你觉得呢?
也许他们想
我们还是向西拿基立投降吧
他会给我们食物吃, 放我们一条生路
我们还是投降吧
影片把这段情节呈现出来
那么, 我们学到什么重点呢?
耶和华很想帮助我们
当我们跟上帝保持亲密的关系
即使大患难来临时
一切地理因素都不会影响
耶和华保护他的子民
现在就是时候了
我们要研读圣经、亲近耶和华
增强对他的信心、信赖他
对他保持忠贞
不论任何情况, 他都会忠贞地扶持我们
我们仔细沉思这些记载
就能继续对耶和华保持忠贞
不惧怕上帝的仇敌
因为他们一定不会得逞
也要谨记
“天下万国”都必知道耶和华是上帝
他的至高统治权
是宇宙众生最该重视的事
耶和华像父亲一直看顾我们
愿我们继续亲近上帝, 永远崇拜他

en.text: As we enter Kyrgyzstan,
one of the seven countries on the Eurasian continent
with “stan” at the end of its name,
you will find many hospitable
and openhearted local residents.
Many people raise livestock,
and so they well understand the words of David
that are recorded in the 23rd Psalm.
The truth about the caring Shepherd, Jehovah,
reached this region in the 1950’s.
More than 20 years ago,
Jehovah’s Witnesses gave literature
in the Russian language to one Kirghiz woman.
Her small daughter, who stood nearby,
said, “Mommy,
“please teach me Russian,
since God talks to people in Russian.”
Today, Bible-based publications are also translated
into the Kirghiz language,
and the Great Shepherd, Jehovah, leads many
to “grassy pastures.”
Jehovah uses the branch office
in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan,
to refresh his people throughout the whole country
and lead them “in the paths of righteousness.”
Fellow believers arrived from different countries
to help the local brothers with the reconstruction of the branch.
All worked hand in hand
to accomplish a tremendous amount of work.
The brothers and sisters who wholeheartedly supported the project
were strengthened and encouraged very much.
We were apprehensive of coming at first,
but we have enjoyed ourselves thoroughly
on construction.
I thought that this is such a great privilege for us
to give all of our strength —everything—to Jehovah
and to feel that you didn’t waste your youth,
and this is so important.
I was touched by the fact that brothers that came
from different countries and were of different nationalities
worked together in unity.
It’s yet another proof that this is Jehovah’s organization.
This project really strengthened
my faith.
Jehovah always gives us more than we could ever need or ever want.
For me, those days were the best time in my life.
I would never trade those days for anything.
Participation in the reconstruction was a real gift from Jehovah.
And Jehovah really knows how to give good gifts.
I am grateful to him for this.
While construction work was coming to its conclusion,
preparation for the branch dedication began.
It was to take place on October 24, 2015.
Brothers built a yurt on the branch property
several days before the dedication program.
Finally, the long-awaited day arrived.
The many guests that came from faraway countries
were invited into the yurt and could try the local cuisine.
In one of the talks on the program,
the speaker compared the branch office to a yurt.
Shepherds caring for their flocks in the mountains live in yurts nearby.
They are able to hear the sound of their flock from inside the yurt.
If something happens,
the shepherd can immediately step in to help the sheep.
Similarly, the branch office listens to the sheep in the field
and renders needed assistance.
Therefore, the publishers
“fear no harm.”
Brother Stephen Lett, a member of the Governing Body,
came for the special dedication program.
This program and another special meeting held the following day
were streamed to meeting places throughout the whole country,
with a total attendance of over 6,000.
Many listeners were touched,
and their eyes were filled with tears of joy.
Now there are
more than 5,000 active Witnesses in Kyrgyzstan,
a country with a population of over six million.
They continue to search for honesthearted people
that are thirsty for the truth.
Yes, our Great Shepherd, Jehovah, prepares a rich table
and fills the cup until it “is well-filled.”
The prophet David sang:
“Surely goodness and loyal love
“will pursue me all the days of my life,
“and I will dwell in the house of Jehovah
for all my days.”
Jehovah’s servants in Kyrgyzstan want to serve Jehovah together
with their brothers and sisters earth wide
now and forever.
