en.text: Welcome, brothers and sisters!
As Jesus’ followers, we’re happy to be related in the faith.
This month’s program is full of faithful examples and ways
you and I can act in faith to make things happen.
We’ll visit with the Lachmuth sisters
at the Canada branch.
How did their faith help them adjust to leaving their home in Canada
to serve in a missionary assignment
in India?
For decades, the apartheid laws in South Africa
separated our brothers from one another.
How were their neutrality, brotherly love, and faith in Jehovah
put to the test?
And our music video depicts how a person’s faith grows
from when they first study the Bible
to when they face trials as a dedicated Witness of Jehovah.
This is the April 2017 edition
of JW Broadcasting!
Has fear of failure
ever held you back from doing something good,
even something for Jehovah?
Some have hesitated to dedicate themselves to God
and get baptized, for fear of breaking God’s laws.
In other cases, we might not reach out for a form of service
because we feel we cannot do a good job.
In this dramatization,
a Bible student faces his fear of failure.
It’s based on lessons found in chapter 1 of the book
“Keep Yourselves in God’s Love.”
Look for what helps him overcome his fear
and move ahead in faith.
When is your turn, Dad?
Our family was contacted by Jehovah’s Witnesses
a few years ago.
Rachel started studying first.
Soon, we all joined in.
For the first time, we were all learning
what the Bible really teaches.
It wasn’t long
before we were sharing the truth with others.
Well, most of us were.
I knew it was the truth,
but I didn’t know if I could live up to
everything Jehovah asks.
Get away.
What if I let everyone down?
What if I let Jehovah down?
You know, can you just give me one second?
Yeah, no problem.
All right. Yeah.
A kind elder named Ben noticed I was struggling.
You OK?
He took the initiative to help.
He asked, “What drew you to Jehovah
in the first place?”
I guess it was learning that Jehovah isn’t harsh and demanding,
but that he’s a loving Father.
Ben agreed and said,
“When we do our best to serve Jehovah,
he does the rest.”
He explained that Jehovah knows our limitations
and doesn’t expect perfection.
And he’s always there to help
because he wants us to succeed.
Then he read Isaiah 41:10:
“Do not be afraid,
“for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious,
“for I am your God.
I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,”
Help!
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
I don’t need to be perfect to serve Jehovah.
I just need to love him and trust him.
And he’ll do the rest.
Our brother learned what the love of God means.
As 1 John 5:3 tells us,
it means “that we observe his commandments;
and yet his commandments are not burdensome.”
Jehovah is a loving Father who wants us to succeed.
As our brother concluded, we need to trust Jehovah,
knowing He’ll do the rest.
That lesson provides an excellent introduction
to our discussion for this month.
The theme is “Faith in Jehovah Makes It Happen.”
During his earthly ministry,
Jesus miraculously healed
many sick or disabled persons.
At times, he would say to such ones
the expression we find at Matthew 9:29:
“According to your faith let it happen to you.”
The principle of what Jesus stated
applies in every aspect of our Christian life and ministry.
But today we will discuss how this principle
that faith in Jehovah makes things happen
can work for us in three areas.
We will see:
1) how our faith has made positive things happen in our personal life,
2) how we can accomplish things in God’s service
that would not be possible without faith in Jehovah God,
and 3) how faith moves us to step out of our comfort zone
to do more in Jehovah’s service.
The principle that faith in Jehovah makes things happen
is well illustrated in one of the miracles Jesus performed.
Please open your Bible to Mark chapter 5,
and let’s read verses 25-29:
“Now there was a woman
“who had had a flow of blood for 12 years.
“She had suffered much at the hands of many physicians
“and had spent all her resources,
“and she was no better but, rather, had become worse.
“When she heard the reports about Jesus,
“she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his outer garment,
“for she kept saying:
“‘If I touch just his outer garments, I will get well.’
“And immediately her flow of blood dried up,
“and she sensed in her body
that she had been healed of the grievous sickness.”
In the following verses, Jesus asked who had touched him.
The woman then revealed before the crowd
what she had done and how she’d been cured.
Now notice Jesus’ response in verse 34:
“He said to her:
“‘Daughter, your faith has made you well.
“‘Go in peace, and be healed
from your grievous sickness.’”
What comforting words
Jesus spoke to this trembling woman:
“Your faith has made you well.”
What did Jesus mean?
Let’s examine the account more closely.
It says that the woman heard “reports about Jesus.”
Many others heard the same reports,
but not all put faith in Jesus.
And think of the circumstances
that could have prevented her from even coming to Jesus.
She had been disappointed many times
over the past 12 years.
She might well have thought:
‘What’s the use?
‘I’m tired and weak and poor.
I’m staying home.’
Or ‘I would like for Jesus to see me,
‘but there is such a crowd.
‘How will I ever get through to him?
‘And after all, I’m in an unclean state,
‘and if the people discover this,
perhaps they will punish me.’
No, she did not allow these negative thoughts
or doubts to fill her mind.
She left her home.
She found Jesus despite the large crowd.
And what was she saying?
Did she say,
“If I touch just his outer garments,
maybe I will get well”?
No, she said,
“I will get well.”
Now, it was not the case
that her faith healed her.
No, but her faith moved her to come to Jesus,
and she was healed by the power from Jehovah
that flowed through his Son.
Faith to approach Jesus
made it happen for her.
If you are a dedicated, baptized Christian,
don’t you agree that your faith has already made
positive things happen in your personal life?
No, you were not miraculously healed
of your physical sicknesses.
We look forward to physical healing of our ills
during the Thousand Year Reign of Christ.
But today Jesus Christ directs a program
of spiritual healing.
When we were a part of this godless world,
many of us were sick spiritually, morally, and emotionally.
No one could cure us.
Perhaps we desperately tried material things or pleasures
to fill our spiritual need,
but our condition only got worse.
We were helpless and hopeless.
But then we heard “reports”
—the good news of God’s Kingdom under Christ!
We studied the Bible.
Our faith moved us to make positive changes in our life
and to associate with the Christian congregation.
Today, we enjoy good spiritual health and happiness.
Our faith has made it happen.
Faith has also made it possible
to accomplish things in God’s service
that perhaps we never thought we could do.
Please open your Bibles to Hebrews chapter 11.
In this portion of Paul’s letter to the Hebrews,
he focuses on faith.
He begins with a definition of faith.
But then, starting in verse 4,
Paul acts as a sort of tour guide,
walking us through the corridor
of thousands of years of Bible history.
He stops along the way
to point out the extraordinary things
that men and women of the past did
by means of faith in Jehovah God.
Just glance down the columns in this chapter
and notice how Paul introduces each paragraph
with the words “by faith.”
This expression “by faith”
appears 18 times in this one chapter.
Now, when we look at the names
Paul lists in this chapter,
we may think,
‘Well, these were spiritual “giants.”’
But in reality, they were ordinary humans
with weaknesses like all of us have today.
The thing they all had in common
was faith,
and faith in Jehovah
made it possible for them to do amazing things.
Let’s look at some of them and compare what they did
with what many of you are doing today
by faith.
Let’s read verse 5:
“By faith Enoch was transferred
“so as not to see death,
“and he was nowhere to be found
“because God had transferred him;
“for before he was transferred
“he received the witness
that he had pleased God well.”
The book of Jude, verses 14 and 15,
informs us that Enoch boldly proclaimed
that Jehovah was going to destroy
that ungodly world.
It appears that wicked, violent men
were going to take Enoch’s life
because of his bold witness.
So God chose to take him
—that is, gently cutting short his life,
sparing him the pangs of a violent death.
In modern times, like Enoch,
many brothers and sisters
have boldly declared God’s judgments
even when faced with death.
One brother, after receiving a death sentence
at Nazi hands during World War II,
wrote these words shortly before his execution:
“I have such peace, such tranquillity,
that you can’t possibly imagine!”
Faith made such boldness
and calmness possible.
In many ways, you very likely
have shown the same faith as Enoch.
By faith, you stand up to an ungodly world
by not adopting its corrupt ways.
By faith, you boldly declare God’s Word
from house to house and in public places.
Before you became a baptized Witness,
you may have thought you would never do this preaching work!
But you are doing it,
sometimes even in the face
of verbal abuse and opposition.
Faith has made it happen.
Let’s read verse 7:
“By faith Noah,
“after receiving divine warning of things not yet seen,
“showed godly fear and constructed an ark
“for the saving of his household;
“and through this faith he condemned the world,
“and he became an heir of the righteousness
that results from faith.”
Nothing in the Bible indicates
that Jehovah chose Noah to construct an ark
because he was an experienced builder.
Certainly, he never had built such a gigantic vessel
as what Jehovah had asked him to construct.
Noah likely pondered many questions:
‘How will I get all the building materials?
‘Do I have the right tools to do the job?
‘How will I gather all the animals?
‘What food will they need, and how much?
‘When, exactly, will the Deluge begin?
‘How long will it last?
Where will the ark land after the Flood subsides?’
Nothing in the record indicates
that Jehovah gave Noah all the details in advance.
What Noah did have was faith.
Faith moved him to begin building.
His faith saved him and his family.
Faith in Jehovah made it happen.
Like Noah, during this time of the end,
Jehovah’s people have taken on
challenging theocratic building projects.
Certainly, constructing the new world headquarters
at Warwick, New York,
was one of these projects that required much faith.
A committee of brothers was assigned
to complete this vast project
in less than four years.
To do so, they knew they had to begin
by July 2013.
They moved ahead in faith.
Though the town had not yet approved the site permits,
they began inviting workers to the site
with that date in mind.
Time was passing quickly.
The invited volunteers were buying plane tickets.
Bethel was arranging rooming and other details.
Yet, the committee still did not have site permits.
Would they cancel these invitations?
They state:
“We spent a lot of time praying about it.
“We decided we needed to act in faith.
“And we were just convinced
Jehovah was going to make it happen.”
As the deadline approached,
the brothers had done everything possible
to obtain the permits.
The town planning board was holding a public hearing.
And to the brothers’ great surprise,
within 15 minutes of the start of the meeting,
the town board voted to approve the project.
These overseers commented,
“When the approval came through,
“we knew it was only by Jehovah’s spirit
that that happened.”
True, but it was also the brothers’ faith
to act that made it happen.

World Headquarters —History Is Being Written.

What faith it took
for Abraham and his submissive wife, Sarah,
to leave the prosperous city of Ur
and to go wherever Jehovah would lead them!
It meant leaving the security of a pleasant home
and moving to some strange and potentially hostile land
some 1,000 miles, or 1,609 kilometers, away.
Do we see such faith today?
Absolutely!
Since 2014,
thousands of brothers and sisters
have attended the School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
agreeing to be assigned to wherever
there is a need by the organization.
Faith has made it happen.
When a call goes out for skilled volunteers
to help build or expand branch facilities,
faith moves brothers and sisters to simplify their lives
and to leave their comfort zone in order to assist.
For example, in 2009,
the congregations in the United States were informed
that an expansion project at Wallkill, New York,
was being planned.
One couple moved out of their newly built
2,200-square-foot, or 200-square-meter, dream home
and into a 270-square-foot, or 25-square-meter, apartment
so that they could make themselves available.
What happened?
They explain:
“One month after we moved into our small apartment,
“we received an invitation to serve
“as temporary volunteers at Wallkill.
“It was clear to us that by simplifying our life,
we had given Jehovah something to bless.”
Faith made it happen for them.
So, what have we learned today?
Faith in Jehovah God is a powerful motivating force
that impels us to act in harmony with his will.
Jehovah rewards such faith.
Remember, the very meaning of the name of our God, Jehovah,
is “He Causes to Become.”
Truly, he is a God who makes things happen!
Brothers and sisters, let us continue to act in faith.

We will accomplish things we never could do

We will be able to do more in Jehovah’s service.

Here in this chapter,
Jesus outlines a number of very important principles
that actually change the way we look at life
and the way we see our existence
in relationship to Jehovah God.
He puts service to Jehovah
in the first place,
regardless of our circumstances.
Let us have a look at two of these principles.
The one that’s here at Matthew 6:24,
he says:
“No one can slave for two masters;
“for either he will hate the one and love the other,
“or he will stick to the one and despise the other.
“You cannot slave

Worship
—divided worship— which is impossible.
He knew that it is impossible
to worship both Jehovah and Riches.
In verse 21, Jesus says:
“For where your treasure is,

The second principle is in verse 25:
“On this account I say to you:

“Does not life mean more than food

You can have a storehouse full of food;
if you don’t have life, you cannot eat it.
You can have a warehouse full of clothes;
but if there’s no body, you cannot wear it.

and earnestly seeking out people
to show them what the Bible teaches.
Later this month,
you’ll enjoy hearing a report from the Central America branch.

in seldom-worked territories across several countries,
such as Mexico, El Salvador,
Costa Rica, Panama,
Nicaragua, and Guatemala.
Later, when it is posted,
you’ll find it in the “Video on Demand” section
under “Our Meetings and Ministry.”
We’d like to conclude our program
with a visit to the Catania Fleming English Congregation
on the beautiful island of Sicily.
The small congregation has 46 publishers
and 16 pioneers,
but they’re conducting on average
more than 60 Bible studies.
Critical times in this system of things
are also giving them special opportunities
in the ministry.
Their territory includes
one of the largest refugee camps in Europe.
It provides shelter to people coming from countries
such as Nigeria, Gambia, Ghana,
Eritrea, and Somalia.
Each week, a group of publishers drives an hour to the camp
to give a witness and conduct studies.
Residents from the camp also come by bus to attend the weekend meeting.
The brothers and sisters
of the Catania Fleming English Congregation
send you their love and greetings.
We thank Jehovah for their willing spirit
to bring comfort to others with the good news.
Thank you for being with us this month.
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

en.text: How many times
have you read in our publications
experiences whereby someone is praying
to be guided by God
while at the same time
one of our Kingdom proclaimers
is praying to be directed to someone with whom they can share
Jehovah’s inspired wisdom?
What happens?
South Africa: A sister begins her auxiliary pioneer service
praying for Jehovah to help her find someone
with whom she can study the Bible.
The territory includes the home of a person
who had been very rude to her in the past.
Courageously, she knocks on the door anyway
and discovers that new tenants live there
—a mother and daughter who had been praying for someone
to help them understand the Bible.
Soon, all three were out in service together.
The angels certainly know how to work these things out.
Is it reasonable, then, to believe that the angels could also play a role
in ensuring that baptized Christians get the information that they need
either to receive or to give?
As our text indicates, Jehovah ‘guides us with his advice.’
How does that work?
Well, often we find ourselves in need of wisdom.
We pray to Jehovah for direction;
we search the Bible; we search our Christian publications;
and at times, we ask people who are already wise for their advice.
After all, Insight,  Volume 2, under “wisdom”
refers to this as “a superior
and timesaving way to wisdom.”
Superior, that is, to experiencing punishment
or watching other people go through it.
The Insight  book then cites Proverbs 22:17.
Let’s read that together,
Proverbs 22:17,
which says: “Incline your ear and listen to the words of the wise,
“in order to apply your heart
to my knowledge.”
Who is the “my” in the expression “my knowledge”?
Well, Jehovah is speaking to us through the pages of his Word,
indicating that if we listen to counsel
from wise people,
we can, in fact, detect the wisdom of Jehovah.
Moreover, Psalm 32:8 gives us this promise:
“I will give you insight
“and instruct you in the way you should go.
I will give you advice with my eye upon you.”
Now, does that mean that if we pray intensely,
Jehovah will give us tailor-made counsel
designed to fit our individual circumstances
—that somehow through either an encouraging visit by a mature Christian,
a talk at one of the meetings,
or some information in one of our publications,
we will find exactly what we need?
Yes, prayers are often answered
in that exact way.
Now, with regard to elders’ meetings,
our brothers are trained to recognize
that Christ by means of his holy spirit can influence any  elder
(even the youngest, most reticent elder on the body)
to make an expression
that results in wise decisions
—decisions that may not have been reached
if each elder had been consulted individually.
But, now, does that mean that every expression made by an elder
automatically reflects the knowledge of God?
We have to remember that just as one who desires wisdom
has a responsibility to seek it,
so likewise one who gives advice
has a responsibility to base his comments on Jehovah’s inspired Word.
Sometimes emotion may get the better of an adviser.
How can we tell whether that is taking place?
Turn with me, please, to 1 Samuel chapter 23
—1 Samuel 23.
Now, how many times did King David receive advice from the likes of Gad,
Nathan, Abigail, Abishai, others?
How did David respond to it?
Well, first, please note that David
had the admirable habit of inquiring of Jehovah
before making decisions.
Look at what it says here in chapter 23,
1 Samuel 23:2:
“So David inquired of Jehovah:
“‘Should I go and strike down these Philistines?’
“Jehovah said to David:
“‘Go, strike down the Philistines and rescue Keilah.’
“But the men of David said to him: ‘Look!
“‘We are afraid while here in Judah;
“how much more so if we go to Keilah against the battle line of the Philistines!’
So David inquired once again of Jehovah.”
And many other texts show that this was David’s practice.
Of course, there were also notable occasions
when David did not first inquire of Jehovah,
such as when he determined to destroy Nabal
and every male in his household,
as reported in chapter 25.
But David recognized in the words of Abigail
the knowledge of Jehovah.
Notice what he said
at 1 Samuel 25:32, 33:
“At this David said to Abigail: ‘Praise Jehovah the God of Israel,
“‘who sent you this day to meet me!
“‘And blessed be your good sense!
“‘May you be blessed for restraining me this day
from incurring bloodguilt and from taking revenge with my own hands.’”
Abigail brought Bible principles back to David’s mind,
and he could see that this was from Jehovah.
And yet, there were other times when David’s advisers
were pointing to what they considered to be proof
of Jehovah’s divine intervention,
but David did not buy into it.
Notice what it says
at 1 Samuel 24:4:
“David’s men said to him: ‘This is the day
“‘on which Jehovah is saying to you, “Look!
“‘“I am giving your enemy into your hand,
and you can do to him whatever seems good to you.”’”
Now, how would David respond to that?
Would he say: “You’re right.
“Saul tried to kill me three times. He’s been hunting me for years.
“He’s obviously lost Jehovah’s holy spirit.
“Isn’t that why Samuel anointed me?
“And now, look, here he is by himself, vulnerable, in our very cave.
“When does that ever happen?
Clearly, Jehovah has given me this opportunity to seize the kingship.”
David did not draw that conclusion.
Why not?
We get a clue in 1 Samuel chapter 26.
Notice, once again, the counsel he receives in verse 8.
Was it a coincidence that David and his men
now find Saul and his army of 3,000 men
totally incapacitated by deep sleep?
When does that ever happen?
Clearly, that was a gift from God.
That was what Abishai thought, and so he said in verse 8:
“Today God has surrendered your enemy into your hand.
“And now, please, let me pin him to the ground
with the spear just once, and I will not need to do it twice.”
Now, was that really counsel from God
or just well-intentioned advice driven by emotion?
David rejected it.
Why?
Was he thinking about Bible principles?
Was he thinking about Leviticus 19:18?
‘You must not take revenge.’
Likely, as we read what it says in verses 10 and 11,
notice what it says:
“As surely as Jehovah is living,
“Jehovah himself will strike him down,
“or his day will come and he will die,
“or he will go down into battle and perish.
“It is unthinkable from Jehovah’s standpoint
for me to lift my hand against the anointed of Jehovah!”
David loved Jehovah’s Word.
He tried to consider each situation from Jehovah’s standpoint.
He sought to discern the difference between God’s knowledge
and human reasoning.
Today, we too may face a difficult situation, a decision.
Someone might even encourage us
to take action without fully considering God’s will.
We need to pray for Jehovah
to direct our hearts to his knowledge
not only that we may receive it
but even that we might convey it when appropriate.
Sometimes you may be the one who needs to give the word of guidance.
Inquire of Jehovah.
Make sure your counsel is in harmony with his Word.
If it is and if the recipient also has a prayerful attitude,
then he too may feel
as in the words of today’s inspired text writer
—that Jehovah is guiding us with his advice.

cn.text: 你是不是常常听到类似的经验
某个人正向上帝祷告，寻求上帝的帮助
在这个时候
一个传道员也在祈求上帝的指引
帮助他找到愿意认识真理的人
结果呢？
南非就有类似的经验
一个做辅助先驱的姐妹
求上帝让她找到想学习圣经的人
在她的传道地区里
有一户人家曾经对她很凶
不过她还是鼓起勇气敲了门
结果出来的是新的住户，是一对母女
她们之前一直祷告
希望有人能帮助她们明白圣经
她们进步很快
不久也开始传道了
很明显，一定是天使在帮忙
那么，如果我们认为基督徒
在寻求指引或给别人建议时
也有天使在背后帮忙
这样的想法是合理的吗？
就像今天的经文说的
上帝会以劝告引导我们
怎样引导呢？
我们都缺乏智慧
所以我们会向耶和华祷告
寻求他的指引
也会查考圣经或上帝组织出版的刊物
有时我们也会向有智慧的人请教
在《洞悉圣经》下册“智慧”这个条目下说
这样汲取智慧
比从自己或别人痛苦的经历学习好得多
也更节省时间
《洞悉圣经》接着引用了箴言22:17
我们一起来看一下这节经文
经文是这么说的
“你要侧耳细听智者的话
这样就能用心领会我的知识。”
这里说的“我”是指谁呢？
是耶和华
没错，耶和华通过圣经跟我们说话
只要我们愿意接受智慧人的劝告
我们就是在领受耶和华的智慧了
在诗篇32:8，上帝保证说
“我要让你洞悉事理
指教你该走的路
我的眼要看顾你
为要给你劝告。”
这是不是说如果我们热切地祷告
耶和华就会按照我们的情况和需要
给我们合适的劝告呢？
例如，耶和华上帝
会不会通过一个成熟的基督徒
来探访我们给我们鼓励
通过聚会里的一个演讲
或是我们出版物里的一些内容
给我们需要的指引呢？
没错！
上帝确实会用这些方法回应祷告
另外，长老团开会时
长老们都明白基督能通过神圣力量
引导任何一个长老发言
这个长老有可能是最年轻
或是最不常发言的一位
但就是因为他的建议
长老团作出了明智的决定
如果个别听取长老的意见
结果可能就不是这样了
这是不是说长老说的每一句话
都一定反映出上帝的智慧呢？
我们要记得
渴求智慧的人有责任去寻找智慧
同样，提出建议的人
也有责任确保自己说的话
是有上帝的话语圣经作为依据的
有时
提出建议的人可能会受当下的情绪所影响
我们怎么知道
提出建议的人有没有感情用事呢？
请看看圣经的撒母耳记上23章
很多人都向大卫提出过建议
包括迦得、拿单、亚比该、亚比筛等等
大卫有没有接受呢？
首先，大卫做决定前有一个好习惯
他一定会先求问耶和华
请看撒母耳记上23:2，经文说
“大卫就求问耶和华
我应该去攻打非利士人吗？
耶和华对大卫说
去吧，你要去攻打非利士人
拯救基伊拉
大卫的手下却对他说
我们在犹大境内都感到害怕
何况是去基伊拉跟非利士人的军队打仗呢？
大卫就再次求问耶和华。”
其他很多记载也显示
这的确是大卫的好习惯
不过也有几次
大卫做决定前没有先求问耶和华
例如，有一次大卫怒气冲冲
要把拿八和他家里的所有男丁全都杀死
幸好大卫接受了亚比该的劝阻
还看出她说的话反映了耶和华的智慧
请翻开撒母耳记上25:32,33
“大卫对亚比该说
以色列的上帝耶和华应当受到赞美！
因为他今天派你来见我
愿上帝赐福给你，因为你明白事理
今天阻止我杀人害命
制止我自行报复。”
亚比该说的话让大卫恢复了理智
看出这是来自耶和华的劝告
不过有好几次，有些人给大卫一些建议
还说，这显然是上帝的指引
想要劝大卫采取行动
但大卫却没有接受
请看撒母耳记上24:4，经文说
“大卫的手下对他说
今天耶和华对你说
我把你的敌人交在你手里了
你看怎样处置他好，就怎样处置他吧。”
大卫有什么反应呢？
他有没有说:“对！
扫罗一直追杀我
神圣力量肯定已经不在他身上
所以上帝才会派撒母耳来任命我
他就一个人在山洞里
现在不下手，还要等到什么时候？
这个机会千载难逢啊！
很明显，这是耶和华给我的机会
让我马上做王。”
没有
大卫绝对没有这样想
为什么呢？
撒母耳记上26章给了我们一个线索
请看看他的另一个手下给他的建议
大卫和他的手下
发现扫罗和他的3000个士兵都睡得很沉
亚比筛应该是这么想的
“这绝不是巧合
这样的机会可不是天天都有的
一定是耶和华在指引我们。”
所以他在第8节说
“今天上帝把你的敌人交在你手里了
现在请让我用矛把他刺透在地上
一下就行了，不用刺两下。”
亚比筛出于好意提出的建议
真的是上帝的指引吗？
还是凭感觉说的？
当时大卫并没有接受
为什么呢？
大卫是不是想到某节经文呢？
比如利未记19:18上帝的一个吩咐
“不可报复。”
有可能
我们可以看看他在
撒母耳记上26:10,11说的话
“永活的耶和华可以作证
他会被耶和华处决
或者有一天会寿终而死
或者会在战场上阵亡
在耶和华看来
我动手伤害耶和华任命的领袖
是万万不该的！”
大卫喜爱耶和华的话语
无论在什么情况下
他都尽力从上帝的观点看事情
分辨哪些建议反映上帝的智慧
哪些只是人的想法
我们现在也会面对一些艰难的抉择
有些人可能没有认真考虑上帝的想法
就劝我们做某些事
无论我们是寻求指引，还是向人提出建议
我们都要向耶和华祷告
求他引导我们的心
让我们按照他的想法去做
如果我们要给别人提建议
就要先求问耶和华
要确保我们提出的建议和他的话语一致
我们这样做
而且对方也怀着谦卑的态度寻求上帝的指引
我们就都能体验到
今天的经文说的一点也没错
耶和华确实以劝告引导我们

en.text: My childhood was not easy.
Actually, it was a hard one.
All my life I thought and dreamed,
‘Why can’t all of us live free?’
You are not allowed to express your opinion,
or to go where you want;
the Jews can, but you are not allowed
because you are an Arab.
I felt angry because of the injustice and animosity.
So I started to say to myself,
‘I want to take action! I want to push the Jews away.’
So I became the leader of a cell that opposed the occupation.
Because of this, I was imprisoned from 1985 for four years.
‘Why?’
I had this question on my mind all the time.
‘Why? Why?’
Then something happened that changed my whole life.
A subscription to The Watchtower magazine was made for me.
This is what I had been looking for
—peace, security, happiness, and satisfaction.
These things had been missing since my childhood.
I looked and found them in the truth.
Nothing will stop the bloodshed on the earth,
nothing but the Kingdom.
I maintain my relationship with Jehovah
and hold on to what I learned.
This changed me.
I was raised as a Jew.
We are taught from childhood
that we are the chosen nation,
that God supports this nation.
Where I lived,
I was surrounded by people who hated Arabs.
I remembered people saying the expression
that “a good Arab is a dead Arab.”
There was a saying,
“If someone comes to kill you,
kill him first.”
They used to claim that this was a quote from the Bible.
When I learned the truth,
all the barriers between us
fell down.
For me, this was something that was very refreshing,
to know that Jehovah expects us to love everyone,
people from all backgrounds,
including Arabs.
Today, I am happy to be in Jehovah’s army
where millions of people belong to Jehovah’s army,
and they don’t serve to fight other people.
They serve him to save other people’s lives
from all the nations and from all sorts of backgrounds.

그런 사람들은 조직에서 수행하는 일에 대해 불만이 많았어요.

이 흥미로운 기록에 대한 새로 조정된 견해가
그들은 마음에 안 드는 가르침이나 마련들이 있을 때마다
그런 비판적인 태도는 그들 자신의 충성심을 약하게 만들었고,
하지만 우리 가족은 여호와께서 주신 것들에 감사했어요.
우린 여호와께서, 우리를 위해 하신 모든 일,
그분의 조직을 위해 하신 모든 일에 대해,
감사하는 마음은 우리 가족이 지금까지 한 것처럼,
남은 큰 환난 내내 충성을 유지하는 데 도움이 될 겁니다.
표정을 보니까, 누나도 뭔가 있었나 본데?
동생 앞에서는 별로 꺼내고 싶지 않은 이야기라서.
일레인 자매, 부담 되면 얘기 안 해도 돼요.
하지만 한 자매가 친구처럼 잘 들어 주면서 조언을 해 주셨죠.
그때 받은 도움을, 두고두고 못 잊을 거예요.
때로는 부정적인 감정이 너무 강해서 사라지지 않았죠.
왜 자꾸 이런 감정이 드는 거죠?
너무 걱정하지 말고, 부정적인 생각을 어떻게 제어할 수 있는지
성경은 우리가 행동에서 자제를 나타낼 수 있게
그런데 사실 생각에서도 자제를 보여야 해요.
그런 생각은 한 번도 안 해 봤어요.
“우리는 헛된 추리와 하느님에 대한 지식을 거슬러 일어난
그리고 모든 생각을 사로잡아 그리스도께 순종하게 합니다.”
그리스도께 순종하게 한다는 게 무슨 의미인지를 알려 주셨어요.
우선 내가 어떤 부정적인 생각을 갖고 있는지 알아야 했죠.
그래서 생각나는 대로 다 적어 봤어요.
그에 대한 여호와의 견해가 뭔지 찾아봤어요.
또 부정적인 생각이 들 때마다 살펴볼 수 있게
시간이 좀 걸리기는 했지만 여호와의 도움과 캐런 자매 덕분에
음, 다른 분들이 충성을 지킨 이야길 듣고 있으니까,
제 경험을 다시 생각해 보게 되더라고요.
음, 내가 적은 성구 중에 고린도 전서 9:25이 있는데
거기엔 ‘경기에 참가하는 사람은 모든 일에서 자제를 나타낸다’고 나와요.
생각을 제어하는 건 그분께 충성을 지키는 거죠.
일레인 자매, 분명히 여호와께서도 기뻐하셨을 거예요.
상황이 이렇게 안 좋은데, 집단들을 다 다니신 거예요?
그래도 최대한 집단들을 돌보기 위해 노력해야죠.
희생적으로 형제들을 돌보는 일에 힘써 줘서 고마워요,
물질적으로 넉넉하지는 않지만, 잘 적응하고 있어요.
형제 부부가 단순하게 사는 데 좋은 본을 보였죠.
하루는 「단순한 삶을 살게 되었습니다」 동영상을 봤어요.
그 동영상은 우리 생활을 되돌아보는 계기가 됐죠.
그보다 더 많은 일을 할 수는 없을까?
우린 이 문제에 대해 묵상하고 기도했고,
우린 집을 팔고 구역에 있는 작은 아파트로 이사했죠.
여호와와 더 가까워질 수 있어서 정말 행복했어요.
필요한 곳으로 이사할 수 있는 상황이 된 우리는
왕국 전파자 학교에 초대받는 축복도 받았죠.
그리고 이 회중에 오게 된 거고요.
두 분 이사 오셨을 때, 짐이 엄청 적었던 거 아직도 생각나요.
크리스 형제, 기도 좀 해 주실래요?
그리고 도움이 되는 성구들을 더 살펴보죠.
악한 자들이 내 살을 삼키려고 나를 공격했으나,
내가 여호와께 청한 것이 하나 있어 •••.
그리고 지금 전 세계에 있는 우리 형제들 모두는
여호와의 약속에 대한 믿음을 열심히 키워 왔습니다.
또는 끝이 언제 올지에만 관심을 갖고
우린 그리스도인인 것처럼 행동하기만 하는 게 아니라
진정한 믿음, 진실한 믿음을 가지고 있습니다.
바로, 바울이 말한 “위선이 없는 믿음”을 가지고 있는 거죠.
여러분이 그런 믿음을 키워 나가는 걸 보는 건
그분의 길과 약속을 더 잘 알게 되었습니다.
그렇게 해서 지금 같은 강한 믿음을 갖게 되었죠.
그로 인해 시험을 받을 때 충성을 유지할 수 있었습니다.
여러분이, 지금 이 순간까지 충성을 지킬 수 있었던 건

en.text: Darren, could you read Psalm 116:12?
It says: “With what will I repay Jehovah
for all the good he has done for me?”
How can Psalm 116:12
give us courage right now?
Elaine.
Well, Jehovah has always done well for us in the past,
so we can trust he’ll do the same for us now and in the future.
Thank you.
Josh.
That’s so true
that he has always done good things for us.
But from what I’ve seen, what really makes a difference
is how we respond to that goodness.
For some in the congregation,
those good things became a test of their loyalty.
. . . continue with our meeting.
We have a letter to read.
“To all congregations of Jehovah’s Witnesses:
“Dear Brothers and Sisters,
If we are to have Jehovah’s favor and blessing as individuals, . . . ”
They found fault
with what the organization was doing or not doing.
“. . .  as we work together with you shoulder to shoulder.
Your brothers, The Christian . . . ”
Now, paragraph 12 gives more detail
on our adjusted understanding of this exciting account.
Let’s read it.
Brother Perez, please read paragraph 12 for us.
“Soon . . . ”
They criticized any teaching or arrangement they didn’t agree with.
And whether they realized it or not,
their critical attitude
was eroding their own loyalty,
and it was affecting others.
Now, before we ask the question for that paragraph,
who would like to read Psalm 116:12?
Kyle, please.
Eventually,
some were no longer our brothers.
But the more grateful our family was
for what Jehovah gave us,
the stronger our attachment to him became.
So I’ve learned to have appreciation for everything,
everything Jehovah has done for us
and for his organization.
It’s helped us all make it to this point,
and I’m sure it will help us stay loyal
through the rest of the great tribulation.
I know that look.
You have an experience, don’t you?
I do, but it’s. . .
It can’t be anything I don’t already know!
Well, it’s not exactly on my list of things
to share with my little brother.
There’s no pressure, Elaine.
Only tell it if you want to.
It’s OK.
For me,
I struggled with negative thinking.
No way!
Yeah.
But I had a good friend
who always helped and listened
and helped me learn how to fight it,
and I’ll always be grateful.
I would pray,
but at times the feelings were so strong,
I didn’t know what to do.
I know. I know.
That must be so hard for you.
Will I ever stop feeling like this?
Don’t worry about if it’s going to stop.
Let’s talk about ways you can take control
when it happens.
Take control?
Uh-huh.
You know, the Scriptures tell us as Christians
that we pray for self-control in our actions.
But do you know, we need that same self-control
for our thoughts?
I never thought about it that way before.
Uh-huh.
The Scriptures tell us how.
Can we read one together?
Yeah. I’d really like that.
It’s in 2 Corinthians chapter 10,
in verse number 5.
You’re going to like this scripture,
chapter 10 and verse 5.
Do you feel like reading it?
OK.
“For we are overturning
“reasonings and every lofty thing
“raised up against the knowledge of God,
“and we are bringing every thought into captivity
to make it obedient to the Christ.”
Karen showed me what it meant
to bring my negative thoughts into captivity
and then make them obedient to the Christ.
I had to know what my negative thoughts were,
all of them, and write them down.
And for each one,
find what Jehovah thinks,
and then find scriptures
that I could remember each time that negative thought returned.
I kept that list with me at all times.
It was a slow process,
but with Jehovah’s help, and with Karen’s,
I’ve learned how to fight the battle against negative thoughts.
Elaine, that was so brave of you to share.
Well, just listening to everyone else’s stories about loyalty,
it made me think about what I needed to do to stay loyal.
Now, Elaine, if you don’t mind me asking,
how did you see that as a test of loyalty?
Well, one scripture I memorized,
1 Corinthians 9:25, says:
“Now everyone competing in a contest
exercises self-control in all things.”
So if Jehovah is telling me
I need to exercise self-control in all things,
even my thinking,
then I’m loyal to Jehovah when I try.
Elaine, you are to be commended for what you did
and for seeing the need. . .
Hey.
Shelly!
Hey.
Shelly!
Hey.
I’m so glad you guys made it safely.
It’s getting bad out there now.
Chris, were you able to check on all of the other groups?
Yes, Brother Brown.
I took a count of each group.
Thank you.
So you’ve been visiting each group,
even with all that’s going on out there?
Yes, but there have been some scary moments.
Still, we’re going to shepherd
all the groups for as long as we still can.
The brothers really appreciate you making the sacrifice to do this,
and you too, Shelly, for supporting Chris.
Is everybody OK?
Everyone’s fine.
They’re getting used to doing without,
some for the first time.
You and Shelly set a good example for keeping your life simple.
Thanks, but honestly,
that wasn’t always the case.
What do you mean?
Well, one day,
we were watching the video We Live a Simple Life,
and it really helped us to take a good look at our lives.
We were both pioneering but still living a comfortable life.
And we started wondering.
Our love for Jehovah moved us to pioneer,
but could it move us to take the next step?
After meditating and praying about it,
the answer became obvious.
We sold our house,
found a little apartment in the territory,
took some time to adjust,
but what it did for our relationship with Jehovah
was so worth it.
With nothing to tie us down,
we were blessed to go to the School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
and then that’s when you all met us.
I remember when you guys moved here,
everything you owned fit into your car and trailer.
Yeah.
How much longer will this keep up?
Chris, please say another prayer for us.
Then I think we should look at some more scriptures
that will help us.
Do you see anything?
Do you see any Witnesses?
Where are they?
Psalm 27 is really going to help us:
“Jehovah is my light and my salvation.
“Whom should I fear?
“Jehovah is the stronghold of my life.
“Whom should I dread?
“When evil men attacked me to devour my flesh,
“my adversaries and my enemies
“were the ones who stumbled and fell.
“Though an army should set up camp against me,
“my heart will not fear.
“Though war should break out against me,
“even then I will remain confident.
“One thing I have asked from Jehovah . . .
“Where would I be if I did not have faith
“that I would see Jehovah’s goodness in the land of the living?
“Hope in Jehovah;
“be courageous and strong of heart.
“Yes,
hope in Jehovah.”
Thank you, Brother Brown.
That psalm is very faith-strengthening.
It is, Chris.
Especially the question at verse 13:
“Where would I be if I did not have faith?”
I think all of us can identify with that question.
Absolutely!
Without faith, none of us would be here.
All of us here
and all of our brothers everywhere
at this hour,
we can all feel good that we’ve worked hard
to build faith in Jehovah’s promises.
We’ve all resisted temptations
to serve God halfheartedly,
with a date in mind or for some selfish reason.
Instead of just going through the motions
of being a disciple,
our faith is real.
It’s genuine.
Paul called that faith, “faith without hypocrisy.”
And to have seen you build that kind of faith
just warms my heart.
You studied God’s Word
to better understand his ways
and his promises.
That has made your faith strong today.
You reasoned
on Jehovah’s past dealings with you,
and that has given you strength
to remain loyal under test.
And your faith
has led you here
as loyal servants of Jehovah,
confident that Psalm 97:10
applies to you personally:
“[Jehovah] is guarding the lives of his loyal ones.”
Where are they?
Check the basement!
Check that door!

en.text: In the Bible book of Job,
Jehovah described examples of his power
observable in the natural world.
Consider just a few.
Thunderhead clouds.
It is estimated that a single thunderstorm
can release more energy than a 20-kiloton nuclear explosion.
We see some of that energy as lightning.
But lightning is only half the show.
Thunder is produced when lightning heats up the surrounding air.
The superheated air rapidly expands,
causing a tremendous boom and crackling.
This is followed by rumbles,
as the air continues to vibrate.
Although usually associated with destructive power,
lightning strikes can be very beneficial.
As lightning rips through the air,
nitrogen is converted
to a form that nourishes plants.
“Who . . . made a path for the thunderous storm cloud?
“Can you send out lightning bolts?
Will they come and say to you, ‘Here we are!’”
Waves can start far out in the open sea.
They can begin as tiny ripples formed by the wind.
As the wind continues to add energy,
the waves increase in size.
The stronger the wind and longer the gust,
the bigger the wave.
Hurricane winds can produce waves
of 100 feet or more in height.
Long after the wind stops,
the tremendous wave energy continues to move.
It can travel great distances from where it originated.
The amount of energy contained in all the oceans
could theoretically power the entire globe
without air pollution.
“Who barricaded the sea behind doors when it burst out from the womb,
“. . . when I established my limit for it and put its bars and doors in place,
“and I said, ‘You may come this far, and no farther;
here is where your proud waves will stop’?”
The evening sky.
Job could see familiar constellations.
What controls the motion of the stars?
Only thousands of years later did scientists
learn more about these invisible laws.
Today, we understand that the motion of stars is controlled by gravity.
Although they are in motion,
we perceive their positions as fixed
because they are so far away.
Thus, they can serve as reliable navigational markers
down to this day.
Yet, despite increasing knowledge
about the force of gravity,
humans are still unable to give a complete answer
to the questions God posed to Job.
“Do you know the laws governing the heavens,
or can you impose their authority on the earth?”
All around us,
daily reminders
of Jehovah’s great power can be seen.
What do you see?

这股强大的能量

让植物可以吸收

到很远的地方

还不会造成空气污染
夜空
在夜晚时
约伯能认出天上的星座

科学家才发现

控制着星体的运行
今日

所以看起来好像静止不动一样
因此从古至今
星体一直是人们可靠的导航标志
尽管人类对万有引力的知识
比以前增加不少
但还是没有人能完全回答
上帝问约伯的问题
每一天
耶和华的力量在大自然当中随处可见
你看见了吗？

it gives us courage.

when you know there is only one outcome?

take him!

“Just as it is written:

“For I am convinced

“nor life
“nor angels
“nor governments
“nor things now here
“nor things to come
“nor powers
“nor height
“nor depth
“nor any other creation
“will be able to separate us from God’s love
that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
“For I am convinced.”

and I want to hate what Jehovah hates.
That verse also says,
‘Jehovah will guard his loyal ones.’
I want to show him that I’m
one of “his loyal ones.”

Now it’s all I think about.
Let me check something first.
Gambling.
Gambling is a form of greed?
Whoa!
Judas Iscariot?
Started off good, gave in to greed,
consumed him,
betrayed Jesus.
If I sign up for online gambling, what could happen?
Yes!
“Flee from these things.
But pursue righteousness, godly devotion . . .”
If I sign up for this,
I could lose a lot of money,
or worse yet,
I could win, and the love of money
could easily consume me,
like it did Judas.
I could fall right out of the truth!
Judas could have sought help from others.
I’m going to talk to my parents about this whole thing.

ko.text: 산염소의 발굽이 붙어 있는 두 발가락은
넓게 벌어질 수 있는 구조로 되어 있습니다.
그 덕분에 좁은 바위 사이에서 뛰어다니고,
균형을 잃지 않고 다닐 수 있습니다.
말은 최대 시속 50킬로미터로 달릴 수 있습니다.
더욱 놀라운 점은 말이 에너지를 매우
말의 다리는 스프링 같은 역할을 합니다.
땅을 내디딜 때 받는 에너지를 흡수했다가
땅에서 발을 뗄 때 에너지를 방출하여
또한 다리에 있는 특수한 근육들은 충격을 흡수해 줍니다.
연구가들은 말 다리를 모방하려고 노력하고 있지만
그 구조가 매우 복잡해서 어려움을 겪고 있습니다.
독수리는 비행할 때 날개 끝부분의 깃털이
독수리와 같이 활공하는 새들을 연구해 왔습니다.
비행기의 날개 끝에 작은 날개를 단 결과
더 많은 화물과 사람을 싣고, 더 멀리 날 수 있습니다.
가장자리가 위로 꺾인 구조의 날개가 도입되고 난 후 10년 동안
하지만 독수리는 비행 능력만 놀라운 것이 아닙니다.
먹잇감을 향해 하강할 때, 독수리의 눈은
인간이 만든 어떤 고속 초점 조절 카메라도
독수리의 이러한 능력에는 비교가 되지 않습니다.
욥기에 나오는 베헤못은 하마를 가리키는 것 같습니다.
다 자란 하마는 길이가 4에서 5미터 정도 되고,
하마의 뼈, 특히 척추뼈는 매우 튼튼하고 단단합니다.
하마는 돌투성이의 강바닥과 같은 지형을 다녀도 끄떡없습니다.
하지만 하마의 뼈만 튼튼한 것은 아닙니다.
철근 콘크리트는 철로 인해 인장 강도가 생기고
시멘트, 모래, 자갈로 인해 압축 강도가 생깁니다.
다른 여러 가지 면에서도 뼈는 콘크리트보다 우수합니다.
뼈는 호르몬에 반응하여 발육하고 성장할 뿐만 아니라,
뼈는 하중을 점점 세게 가할수록 서서히 더 강해집니다.
욥기에 나오는 리워야단은 악어인 것으로 보이는데,
어떤 악어의 무는 힘은 사자보다 거의 세 배나 강합니다.
그런데 악어의 턱은 사람의 손끝보다 더 예민합니다.
두개골에 있는 구멍들에서 나온 수많은 감각 기관이
따라서 어미 악어는 새끼를 조심스럽게 입안에 넣어 옮길 수 있습니다.
그분의 “보이지 않는 특성들”을 “분명히 볼 수 있습니다.”
또한 욥기에 나오는 다른 동물들을 통해서도 많은 점을 배울 수 있습니다.
가족 숭배 시간에 그러한 동물들을 조사해 보십시오.
여호와의 특성들에 대해 더 많은 것을 알게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Observers find it difficult
even to get near the nimble mountain goat.
What accounts for this?
Their hooves are designed with two toes
that can be spread wide apart.
This feature enables mountain goats to run, jump,
and feed between narrow ledges.
They can maintain their footing
on a near-vertical incline.
Researchers have tried to apply these design features
to advanced footwear, with only limited success.
A horse can gallop at speeds
up to 50 kilometers [or 30 miles] per hour.
Even more impressive is how efficiently
the horse expends energy.
The secret is in its legs.
Like a spring, a horse’s leg absorbs energy.
As its leg leaves the ground, that energy is released.
Specialized muscles act as shock absorbers.
Engineers are trying to imitate this design
but are finding it a challenge.
During an eagle’s flight,
the feathers on the tips of its wings
are practically vertical.
This configuration gives maximum lift
with minimum wing length.
Engineers have studied such soaring birds as eagles
with a view to designing more efficient aircraft.
The introduction of modified wing design
that includes winglets
has improved aircraft performance by as much as 15 percent.
Planes can now fly farther and carry more
while saving fuel.
In the decade following the introduction of upturned wingtips,
airlines worldwide saved 7,600 million liters
[or 2 billion gallons] of jet fuel.
But the eagle’s amazing design is not limited to flight.
As the eagle descends upon its prey,
its eyes continuously adjust
to maintain sharp focus throughout the approach.
What man-made camera comes even close
to this ability of rapid refocus?
The Behemoth mentioned in Job
is generally identified as the hippopotamus.
A full-grown hippo may be as large as 15 feet
[or 4 to 5 meters] long
and weigh around 8,000 pounds [or 3,600 kilograms].
Its bones, particularly the vertebrae,
form a strong, rigid structure.
Its ribs and thick hide protect it
as it navigates such areas as rocky river beds.
You don’t have to have bones like a hippo
to appreciate their strength.
Bone is an essential part of countless living organisms.
Researchers say that bones are constructed in exactly the same way
that reinforced concrete is constructed.
The steel of reinforced concrete provides the tensile strength,
while the cement, sand, and rock
provide the compressional strength.
However, the compressional strength of bone
is greater than that of even the best reinforced concrete.
Bone is superior to concrete in many other ways.
It responds to hormones that affect its growth and development
and is even able to repair itself.
Also, like muscle,
it slowly grows stronger as the load on it increases.
Leviathan, likely the crocodile,
has an enormously powerful bite.
Some have a bite nearly three times more powerful
than that of a lion.
Yet, the crocodile’s jaw is also more sensitive
than the human fingertip.
It is covered with thousands of sense organs
that come out of holes in the skull.
This design allows a mother to pick up her babies
and gently carry them in her mouth.
Without a doubt,
God’s “invisible qualities
are clearly seen” in the things he made.
We can also learn much
from the other animal creation mentioned in Job:
the wild bull,
the stork,
and the ostrich.
Why not study these animals during family worship
and see what more can be learned
about Jehovah’s qualities?

en.text: Now, when you think of it,
the apostle Paul was a very humble man.
He was flexible.
He says: “To the Jews I became as a Jew,”
and “to those under law I became as under law.”
But there were limits to Paul’s flexibility,
and we’re going to talk about that in just a few moments.
First of all, though, when Paul came down to Jerusalem,
the elders explained that thousands of Jews had become believers
and they were all zealous for the Law.
Now, they’d heard a rumor about Paul.
They’d heard the rumor that Paul was telling the Jews
not to circumcise their children,
and the elders were worried about it.
They had a plan.
We read about that plan in Acts chapter 21,
if you would like to turn there,
Here’s their plan: “So do what we tell you:
“We have four men who have put themselves under a vow.
“Take these men with you
“and cleanse yourself ceremonially together with them
“and take care of their expenses,
“so that they may have their heads shaved.
“Then everyone will know that there is nothing
“to the rumors they were told about you,
“but that you are walking orderly
and you are also keeping the Law.”
Now, it says they have heard a rumor about you,
that you were telling Jews not to circumcise their children.
Paul was probably not telling Jews
not to circumcise their children.
As has already been mentioned,
Paul took Timothy and circumcised him
so as not to stumble the Jews.
Paul realized that there was nothing wrong
with circumcision per se.
It was when people proclaimed that circumcision
was necessary in order to gain salvation that the problem arose.
So this was a rumor.
But some brothers and sisters were willing to believe a rumor
about a faithful brother rather than to trust Paul.
Just as today, some believe everything they read in the newspaper
and they don’t even ask any questions.
So now here’s the question:
What were they going to do about it?
The elders had a suggestion.
They said: “We have four men who have put themselves under a vow.”
And they wanted Paul to take these men to the temple
and pay their expenses.
Paul agreed.
Now, that took humility.
We all know how strongly Paul felt about keeping the Law,
and yet Paul was willing to see the bigger picture.
He had strong feelings, but at the same time,
these Jews were probably new in the truth,
and Paul wanted to go as far as he could go
so as not to stumble those new in the truth.
Now the vow. What was the vow?
Most scholars agree that the vow
was probably a Nazarite vow.
And if it was, that was going to be tricky for Paul.
Because, you see, Nazarites were required to offer a sin offering
when their vow came to a completion.
Now, Paul would never have agreed to that.
It would have showed—
It would have shown disrespect for the sacrifice of Christ.
So Paul and those four men were going to have to be very careful
about how far they would go in the completion of this vow.
And we can be sure that they would never do anything
that would go against their conscience.
Now, we can see that on this occasion
Paul went a long way
so as not to stumble the Jews.
But on another occasion,
he refused to cater to the Jews.
We read about that in Galatians chapter 2.
Let’s turn there.
Galatians chapter 2,
and we’ll read verses 11-14.
Galatians 2:11-14:
“However, when Cephas came to Antioch,
“I resisted him face-to-face,
“because he was clearly in the wrong.
“For before certain men from James arrived,
“he used to eat with people of the nations;
“but when they arrived, he stopped doing this and separated himself,
“fearing those of the circumcised class.
“The rest of the Jews also joined him
“in putting on this pretense,
“so that even Barnabas was led along with them in their pretense.
“But when I saw that they were not walking in step
“with the truth of the good news,
“I said to Cephas before them all:
“‘If you, though you are a Jew, live as the nations do and not as Jews do,
how can you compel people of the nations to live according to Jewish practice?’”
So we see what was happening here.
Up till the time when men from James
came down to Antioch,
Peter and Barnabas and the other Jewish Christians
were happily eating with the Gentiles.
But now men from James came down,
and suddenly Peter
starts to separate himself from the Gentiles.
And, following his lead,
other Jewish Christians begin doing the same thing.
Now, who was probably new in the truth?
In this case, it was probably the Gentile Christians.
In Acts 21, it was probably the Jews who were newer in the truth
and Paul didn’t want to stumble the Jews.
But at this point, Paul could not be all things to all people.
He couldn’t please the Jews;
he couldn’t please the men from James and also please the Gentiles.
He was either going to have to stumble
—if you will— the men from James,
or he was going to have to stumble the Gentiles.
He had to make a choice.
And so Paul made his choice.
And what did he do about it?
He followed the advice
that he recorded in this same book of Galatians.
Can you think of what that was?
Galatians chapter 6
—what is it saying?
“If a man takes a false step before he is aware of it.”
What did Paul say about Peter?
He was not walking in step with the good news.
So Peter was taking a false step.
“You who have spiritual qualifications,” that would be Paul,
“try to readjust such a man in a spirit of mildness.”
And that’s what the apostle Paul did.
Now, we love to pick on Peter.
But let’s give the poor man a break.
Let’s give him credit for what he was doing right.
This was Antioch.
Now, what do we know about Antioch?
It was in Antioch when the whole matter
of keeping the Law blew up in the first place.
And who was it who were stirring things up in Antioch?
It was men from Jerusalem
—men from James.
Now, up until this point
—Peter and Barnabas and the others— they’re happily eating with the Gentiles
until men from Jerusalem come down
and start stirring up trouble.
You kind of think that if they’d stayed home once in a while
there would have been a lot less trouble in the Christian congregation.
So Peter was doing the right thing
up until the men from James came down.
Now, Peter knew how critical men from James could be
—or men from Jerusalem could be.
You might say, he’d seen that movie before
in 36 C.E.,
just after the conversion of Cornelius.
Notice a detail at Acts 11:2, 3,
and this might help us to at least understand Peter’s concern,
and perhaps misguided effort,
not to stumble the men from James.
“So when Peter came up to Jerusalem,”
this is in 33 C.E.,
“the supporters of circumcision began to criticize him, saying:
“‘You went into the house of men who were not circumcised
and ate with them.’”
Well, Peter knew how sensitive Jews were
about eating with the Gentiles,
but he was moved by the fear of man.
And the apostle Paul did right
to reprove him because, after all,
he was going to have to make a choice:
You stumble the Jews or you stumble the Gentiles.
The lesson to take away:
There are times when you can’t please everyone.
There are times when you cannot be all things to all people.
Our young people have to realize that.
You have to take a stand for what is right
and let the chips fall where they may.
Now, you have to appreciate the wisdom
that Jesus used in selecting Paul
as an apostle to the nations.
A note to the elders:
Paul was flexible.
He didn’t insist on his own ideas
even when he felt strongly about a matter,
and he didn’t create unnecessary issues.
Paul looked at the big picture.
What a marvelous example for us.
And we can say that humble Paul
was the right man for the job.

en.text: My father was a patriotic man,
and he passed away while in combat when I was only a year old.
I decided that I wanted to do what he highly valued,
so I decided to serve in the army.
However, when I began seriously studying the Bible,
I cultivated a desire to please only Jehovah,
which helped me to change my decision.
When I read Isaiah 2:4,
I understood that the person who wants
to live a life pleasing to Jehovah will not learn combat
and will not participate in wars.
My stand on neutrality was challenged
when I became an adult and was required to serve
in the army.
But my Bible beliefs did not allow me to perform such service.
That was why I was arrested and sentenced
to two and a half years of imprisonment.
In prison, prayers really helped me.
I asked Jehovah many times to give me
“the power beyond what is normal so that I could endure.”
And in order for me to receive the answers to my prayers,
I regularly did personal study and Bible reading.
The visits the elders made were very encouraging.
At those times, I felt Jehovah’s warm care.
Jehovah has been my support
through his organization, his Word,
the holy spirit, and also through his “gifts in men.”
It is true that I suffered
both physically and emotionally,
but I never regretted the position I took.

en.text: Over the last several years,
the U.S. branch and world headquarters
have had the responsibility of constructing several new buildings.
Nine of these buildings were awarded a Four Green Globes rating,
which is the highest Green Globes certification possible.
The two at Wallkill were the Office Building
and F Residence.
The seven at the new Warwick complex
were the four residence buildings, the Maintenance Building,
Office and Services Building, and Vehicle Maintenance Building.
Now, a good number of you may be asking right about now,
‘What exactly is this Green Globes program?’
Well, it is a program
which assesses the “eco-friendliness” of a building
starting from design through construction.
An independent third party assesses
the environmental impact of a completed building
on a scale of one to four Globes.
The organization that coordinates the program stated
that a Four Green Globes rating
“demonstrates national leadership
“and excellence in the practice of water, energy
and environmental efficiency to reduce environmental impact.”
The organization that coordinates the Green Globes program
drew our attention to how significant an accomplishment
receiving this award is
by mentioning that only 4 percent
of properties that apply
are able to achieve the top rating for even one of their buildings.
In spite of this,
on September 14, 2016,
the Warwick project was simultaneously awarded
seven of these Four Green Globes
for all buildings that qualified for consideration.
Now, understanding the significance of this award,
you probably feel a measure
of pride and satisfaction with this milestone.
Another question you may have is,
‘How does this environmental design
at Warwick and Wallkill benefit the organization?’
Well, since Revelation 11:18 points out that it is
Jehovah that will ultimately need
to step in to save our earth from ruin,
the intent is not to join some
sustainable design fad
or try to do what only Jehovah can do.
This means that we don’t design
simply to be “green” as many in the world would.
Rather, we saw four noteworthy benefits
from this level of design.
First and foremost,
Jehovah’s name is glorified.
It often happens that during the design phase of a project,
claims are made
as to the anticipated environmental impact of a building’s design.
However, the final outcome
after construction often falls short
of what is promised,
which can leave officials quite frustrated.
With Warwick, we modestly made known
our goal to the local officials and community
that we would strive to achieve three of four Green Globes.
In contrast,
this award confirms
that Jehovah’s Witnesses have kept our word by achieving
not three but four Green Globes.
Keeping our word
has brought honor to Jehovah
and built a trustworthy reputation in the community.
And that leads to our second benefit.
This top environmental rating confirms
that we, as an organization, respect Jehovah’s creation.
Being known
as responsible stewards of the environment
allows us to have many benefits, one of which
is in the case of Wallkill.
Our reputation made it easier to gain approvals
to expand our facilities there.
A third benefit
is to our neighbors in the surrounding community.
For example, the drinking water in the adjoining lake is not contaminated.
Our site lighting doesn’t light the night sky.
The use of native plants serves to protect the health
of the beautiful surrounding forest that we all enjoy.
And the design and location of the buildings on-site
preserve the spectacular views
from the adjoining forest trails.
Yet, a fourth benefit to the organization
is that this level of design
makes the best use of donated funds.
While experts vary on the exact percentages,
over the lifetime
of a typical building, operational and maintenance costs can be
four to six times the initial construction costs.
So the more efficient the design and construction, the more long-term savings
are realized for the organization.
For instance,
an independent energy consultant recently calculated
that we could expect to see savings
of over one million dollars annually
from the energy-efficient measures incorporated
into our project as compared to a standard construction
of similar facilities.
But you may be curious as to what
energy and environmental features
were incorporated into the Warwick project
to earn these awards and save funds.
These features covered multiple aspects of design.
They basically fall into five categories:
landscaping,
rainwater control,
lighting control,
energy efficiency,
and water usage.
With respect to the first category —landscaping—
a control system checks rainfall and local weather conditions
to determine how much water is needed
in each irrigation zone,
and drought-resistant native plants and trees
also reduce water needs.
The second category is rainwater control.
All rainwater
from the roofs and building surfaces is treated with green roofs,
bioretention areas,
permeable concrete paving,
underground sand filters,
and storm-water planters.
Yet a third category is lighting control.
Lighting sensors
in perimeter window spaces are linked to a control system
that balances natural lighting with fluorescent lighting,
while still permitting the occupant control as desired.
The fourth category is energy efficiency.
High-efficiency HVAC equipment,
boilers, and chillers were incorporated.
A geothermal well field
consisting of some 120 wells
takes advantage of renewable energy
to supplement building heating and cooling needs.
And with respect to our fifth category —water usage—
water is conserved in all the buildings
by means of plumbing fixtures that use
lower volumes of water.
As we stated earlier, the operation and maintenance expense
is the greatest part of a building’s total cost.
To the extent that we practice water,
lighting, and energy conservation
in our individual rooms and work places
—to that extent we can have
a personal share in realizing the full benefit,
potential, and purpose
of these new facilities at Wallkill and Warwick.
And what knitted together all of these features,
making the awards possible though, were the people.
This was only because of the close cooperation
and tireless efforts of the thousands
who worked in various areas
such as design, purchasing and construction.
It truly was a strong testimony to the power of unity.
Certainly, Jehovah’s heart is filled with joy
as he sees all the fine work that has been accomplished
and the glory that it’s brought
and will continue to bring to his name.

cn.text: 过去几年
美国分部和世界总部兴建了许多新的建筑物

有两栋是华基尔的办公大楼和宿舍F

分别是四栋宿舍、维修大楼
办公及后勤服务大楼、汽车维修大楼
刚才提到“绿色地球”时
有些人可能会想
“绿色地球”到底是什么？
“绿色地球”是一套认证标准
评估建筑物从设计到完工是否符合环保标准
第三方的专家会评估建筑物的环保程度
并给予一至四个绿色地球的评分
“绿色地球”的认证机构说明
建筑物得到“四个绿色地球”的评分
表示这个建筑物在水资源管理
节能
环保方面具有顶尖的水准
能减轻建筑物对自然环境的冲击
“绿色地球”的认证机构说
我们能获得“四个绿色地球”
实在很不容易！
怎么说呢？
在所有申请认证的团体中
只有百分之四的建筑物
得到四个绿色地球的级别
而获奖的团体中可能也只有一栋建筑物得奖
然而，在2016年9月14日
沃威克有七栋建筑物接受评估
而七栋都得到四个绿色地球的认证
在这么严格的评估标准下
我们能获得“四个绿色地球”的最高认证
真是一项值得骄傲的成就！
我们在沃威克和华基尔的建筑物
采用环保低碳的设计
对组织有什么益处呢？
我们知道启示录11:18说的
最终会拯救地球和环境的是耶和华上帝
所以我们采用环保设计
不是为了拯救地球，也不是为了跟流行
要得到一个“环保低碳”的认证而已
我们采用环保设计，有以下这四个原因
第一个原因，也是最重要的原因
就是这么做可以荣耀耶和华上帝
一般的建商在设计建筑物的时候
都保证工程不会对环境造成伤害
结果却往往不如预期
没有达到原定的目标
让政府机关感到头痛
不过
我们向沃威克的官员和当地居民
解释工程计划时
并没有夸大自己的能力
只说我们会尽力
达到“三个绿色地球”的认证标准
结果呢？
我们超越了原定目标
获得“四个绿色地球”的最高认证
这证明耶和华见证人会信守承诺
我们也获得当地人的信任和尊重
为耶和华的名增光
第二
这个认证表示我们尊重上帝创造的大自然
我们的组织爱护环境
这样的名声可以为我们带来很多益处
举一个例子
当我们要扩建华基尔的建筑时

第三
采用环保的设计也是体贴当地居民的作法
例如
我们保护邻近的湖泊，确保饮用水不受污染
采用不会造成光害的照明设备
种植原生植物保护邻近的美丽森林
建筑物的设计和位置
让在森林步行的人
可以看到美丽的景色，而不会看到建筑物
第四
我们采用环保设计就是善用弟兄姐妹的捐款
虽然专家没有准确的数据
但一般建筑物的运作和保养费用
累积起来可能是当初建造费用的四到六倍
因此，采用环保节能的设计
长期下来可以为组织节省很多费用
举个例子
跟类似的建筑物相比
采用节能设计会比传统设计省钱
每年能省下一百多万美元的开销
你可能会想
沃威克的建筑物究竟用了哪些环保节能设计
让我们得到认证并节省开销呢？
我们采纳的环保节能设计非常多
基本上可以分为五大类
庭园造景
雨水调节
灯光照明
节能设备
省水设备
我们来谈谈第一类
庭园造景
举个例
我们安装雨水和气象侦测系统
系统会依照天气决定各个花圃应该浇多少水
除此之外
我们也种耐旱的
原生植物和树木来节省水资源
第二类就是雨水调节
我们为了善用雨水和减少雨水径流量
在屋顶采用了绿化设计
在周边设置生态调节池
在地面铺设透水性混凝土
在地底设置砂滤器
也设置了滞洪植栽区
第三类是灯光照明
建筑物外围靠窗的灯由照明感应器调节
感应器会感应自然光
自动调整灯光的亮度
当然，也能手动调整亮度
第四类是节能设备
我们安装高效率暖通空调
锅炉、冷冻机
我们钻了120个地热井
设置地能空调系统
利用再生能源提供建筑物所需的冷暖气
最后，第五类是省水设备
我们在所有的建筑物里安装省水装置
以降低用水量
我们先前也提到
建筑物的保养和运作占总开销的一大部分
因此，我们不论是在自己的房间
还是在工作的地方都节约用水、用电
就能帮忙节省开销
也能让华基尔和沃威克的设施长久运作
虽然我们拥有顶尖的设备
但能获得“四个地球”的最高认证
我们也应该感谢所有参与的人
数千名工作人员互相合作、辛勤工作
有的人负责设计、有的负责采购
有的负责施工等不同领域
我们看出团结的力量的确很强大
耶和华看到这些工程完成
而且能一直为他的名带来荣耀
一定感到非常开心！

title: 부모님과 어떻게 대화를 잘할 수 있을까?

ko.text: 근데 지금은 부모님이랑 도무지 말이 안 통한다는 생각이 들지 몰라.
그래도 사실은 부모님이랑 대화하고 싶을 걸?
근데 말을 걸어 봐도 얘기를 잘 안 들어 주시니?
목소리를 높이면 잘 들어 주실 것 같단 생각이 들지 모르지만
아예 말을 안 하는 게 낫겠다고 생각할 수도 있을 거야.
대화를 안 하면 상황이 더 나빠진다고 알려 주지.
말을 안 하면 문제가 해결이 안 돼.
적절한 기회를 기다렸다 대화를 나누는 게 훨씬 낫지.
아니면 감정을 솔직하게 편지로 써 보는 건 어때?
학교에서 안 좋은 일이 있으면 그럴 수 있지.
물론, 마음에 내키지 않는데 억지로 이야기를 하다 보면
서로 신경이 날카로워질 수 있고 대화도 제대로 안 될 수 있어.
하지만 계속 말을 안 하려고 하면 스트레스에서 벗어날 수 없을 거야.
부모님이 더 많이 걱정하실 수도 있고
기분 좋은 일이나 다른 일부터 먼저 이야기해 보는 거야.
그러면 서로 편안하게 이야기를 나누기가 더 쉬워질 거야.
그러니까 어떤 말을 할지 잘 생각해 보고, 공손하게 말해 봐.
부모님은 늘 너의 곁에 있는 좋은 친구란 걸 기억해.
어떤 고민이나 어려움도 잘 헤쳐 나갈 수 있을 거야.

en.text: When you were younger,
your parents were probably the first ones
you ran to for advice.
But now you might feel that your parents
just don’t understand you.
Deep down, you still want to talk to them.
But what if you try,
and you feel they just aren’t listening?
Well, you could raise your voice,
but shouting won’t make
your parents more receptive
and won’t show them the respect they deserve.
You could give your parents
the silent treatment,
but the Bible suggests at Proverbs 15:22
that things only get more frustrating
when you don’t talk.
So saying nothing
really gets you nowhere.
It’s smarter to just wait
for a better time to talk.
Or you might even write them
an honest but respectful letter
expressing how you feel.
But what if the situation is flipped?
Yeah, that’s right.
Your parents want to talk,
but you don’t.
Maybe you had a bad day at school.
It’s true that choosing to talk
when you don’t feel like it could mean
the conversation will be forced,
which makes everyone tense
and leads to poor communication.
But refusing to talk
means you’ll still be stressed,
and your parents might think
that the problem is bigger than it is,
or worse, that you’re hiding something.
Instead, you could start off talking with them
on a subject that isn’t as stressful
or even one that makes you happy.
That will ease the tension
or get rid of it all together.
The bottom line:
Your parents want to help you
and you can use their help.
So choose your words carefully,
deliver them respectfully,
and think of your parents as friends,
not enemies.
Because let’s face it,
you’ll need all the allies you can get to cope
with the challenges that lie ahead.
