title: 마크 샌더슨: 여호와께서는 병든 사람들을 지원해 주십니다 (사도행전 15:29)

en.text: None of us like to contemplate
being in a serious accident or receiving news
that we have a very serious illness
that may even be life threatening.
When the blood issue also arises, at such times,
of course we’re all determined that we’re going to keep our integrity.
But we also feel the need for comfort and for support
so that we can remain faithful.
Now, Jehovah never promised for this period of time
that we would receive miraculous healing.
But he did promise that we would receive something very significant.
Would you open your Bibles with me?
Let’s look together at Psalm 41:3.
It says: “Jehovah will sustain him on his sickbed;
during his sickness you will completely change his bed.”
Well, now, The Watchtower, back in 2008, the September 15 issue,
just made a nice little comment on this verse.
It said: “David did not expect Jehovah
“to perform a miracle and remove [his] sickness.
“Rather, David felt certain that Jehovah would ‘sustain him’
“—that is, give him support and strength
while he was lying on his sickbed.”
Well, that’s what Jehovah has promised.
He’s promised that he’s going to provide us with the support and the strength
that we need so that we can keep our integrity.
Well, Hospital Information Services (HIS) here in Brooklyn,
the Hospital Information Desks at each of the branches,
and the Hospital Liaison Committees (HLC)
have been very powerful tools in the hand of Jehovah
to provide this support and strength
when the blood issue arises.
Did you know that now worldwide
there are some 1,700 —that is 1,700—
Hospital Liaison Committees with over 13,000 members?
This is not easy work.
The vast majority of these brothers are not physicians;
they’re not connected to the medical community in any way.
Often, they have to get up in the middle of the night
to go to the hospital.
Sometimes they deal with very confrontational situations.
Usually all of the situations that they deal with are emotionally charged.
Their work is very seldom seen by others.
They are not in the spotlight.
Well, when we reflect on the work of these wonderful brothers
who are willing to accomplish this work
of giving assistance and support and help to our brothers,
we can’t help but think of this scripture in Jeremiah chapter 23,
where Jehovah says—
Jeremiah 23:4:
“‘And I will raise up over them shepherds
“‘who will really shepherd them.
“‘They will no longer be afraid or be terrified,
and none will be missing,’ declares Jehovah.”
Well, that’s exactly
what the Hospital Liaison Committee brothers do.
They are wonderful shepherds who are there to help the brothers
to have the information and the assistance they need
so that they can maintain their integrity.
I recall one experience when I was working
with the Hospital Information Desk in Canada.
A sister in a northern Canadian city,
she had been very, very seriously injured.
She had to be airlifted to a larger center
where she would be able to receive more intensive care.
A Hospital Liaison Committee member was immediately notified;
he went to the hospital.
And so, as soon as the aircraft landed
and the sister was being taken off and wheeled into the hospital,
there the brother was waiting in the hallway.
And so, when he approached her lying on the stretcher,
the sister was trembling with fear.
Well, when he looked down at her,
she looked up and she said, “Are you a doctor?”
And he said, “No, I’m your brother.”
Well, immediately the sister
—this huge sigh of relief because now there was someone
who could give her the practical help that she so much needed.
Well, what are some of the ways
that this arrangement does provide practical support?
Well, I’m not sure if you know this,
but at 89 branch offices around the world
—including the United States and Canada—
we have brothers who are on call
24 hours a day, seven days a week
to answer calls from Hospital Liaison Committee members
and also from doctors
who request assistance
on how to treat Jehovah’s Witnesses without the use of blood.
This is an amazing arrangement.
When I worked with HIS,
I recall many times in the middle of the night,
we would receive calls from a brother or a sister
or from an HLC or from a doctor
about someone who was desperately in need of assistance.
And the organization had provided such wonderful tools.
For example, a database has been assembled
of literally thousands of medical articles
from respected medical journals.
Now these articles can be sent to a doctor or to a medical team,
and they explain very specifically
what can be done to address a situation
without the use of a blood transfusion.
Often, when a doctor receives an article like that
—he sees it’s from one of his peers, it’s been published in a respected journal—
he is much more willing to cooperate.
And also, he sees in a practical way what can be done.
But even better, each Hospital Information Desk
maintains a list of consulting doctors.
Now, these are very well-respected physicians
who are not afraid to confer with other doctors
and explain to them how even very complex, very difficult cases
can be managed without the use of blood.
I recall one time in the middle of the night,
we received a call about a sister who had just given birth,
and she had lost a significant amount of blood.
The doctor managing her case was very interested in receiving help.
Well, we called a very, very well-respected professor
of obstetrics and gyneocology in Canada
who was always willing to provide assistance.
Well, I started off the call by saying,
“I’m so sorry to call you so late at night.”
Well, the doctor said: “Please don’t apologize, Mark.
I’m always happy to do anything I can to help the sisters.”
Well, of course, he was not a Witness himself.
But he viewed those dear ones as his own sisters,
and he was willing to help them.
Well, such courageous and skilled physicians all around the world
have done so much to help our brothers.
And the tools just keep on improving.
Many of you may know
that now we have a section for medical professionals
on our jw.org website.
Now, I’ll reiterate:
This is not a site or an area for Jehovah’s people;
it’s specifically designed for medical professionals.
But that area,
although it’s only recently been established,
is already having a wonderful effect.
Let me relate this experience.
A sister wrote this into the branch.
She said: “Recently my husband took me to the emergency room,
“and we discovered I had a mass of some sort near my appendix
“and that a huge and possibly messy surgery
“was needed to discover the problem.
“When I told the surgeon that was assigned to me
“that I was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
“he became agitated when I reinforced
“my nonnegotiable stand.
“He never became rude or harsh,
“but I could tell that he was very troubled.
“My husband left to make a phone call to the brothers.
“Five minutes later, a resident came to tell me
“that the surgeon had just gone to the jw.org website
“and was downloading information.
“We had never mentioned the website.
“How he knew or who told him, we’ll never know.
“But ten minutes later, he came back with copies of the information.
“He had read it, he had marked the pages,
“and he went over everything with my husband and me.
“Then he took my hand, and he smiled.
“He asked if I was ready,
“and he promised to do his very best for me.
“He said he too had made
“some nonnegotiable decisions with God in his lifetime.
“He saw me about 12 hours after the surgery,
“and I teased him about being a trouble.
“He said, ‘No, it was extraordinary.’
“We know he meant what he had just learned
“about the Hospital Liaison Committee
and Jehovah’s provision for information for His people.”
The sister concluded by saying,
“I have never felt such a wave of peace from Jehovah
in all my years in the truth.”
Well, Jehovah did not promise us
miraculous healing at this time,
but he did promise that he would provide us
with support and strength when we are sick.
What a beautiful gift Jehovah has given his people
through the fine work of the Hospital Liaison Committees!
Truly, this has been a strengthening aid for us
“to keep abstaining from . . . blood.”

cn.text: 在座的各位一定都不喜欢遭遇严重的意外
或听到医生说
我们得了非常严重的疾病，甚至危及生命
如果我们真的遇到这样的情况
又牵涉到输血
毫无疑问，我们一定会对耶和华坚守忠义
但我们也一定需要安慰和帮助
让我们能保持忠贞
现今耶和华没有保证他会施行奇迹
让我们神奇地康复过来
但他却承诺会给我们一些特别的帮助
邀请你打开手上的圣经
我们看诗篇41:3
“他卧病在床，耶和华会扶持他
他生病的时候，你会为他更换床铺”
2008年9月15日刊的《守望台》杂志
对这段经文做了有意思的评论
它说，大卫并没有期望耶和华施行奇迹
除去他的疾病
不过大卫坚信耶和华一定会扶持他
也就是在他卧病的时候支持他、给他力量
这就是耶和华的承诺
他保证他会给我们所需的帮助和力量
让我们能坚守忠义
世界总部的医院资讯服务部
每个分部的医院资讯处
和各地的医院联络委员会
都是耶和华上帝特别运用的安排
给我们提供支持，帮助我们应对输血的问题
你知道吗？
现在在全球
大约有1700个
没错，1700个医院联络委员会
参与服务的人超过1万3000
这工作不简单
大部分的弟兄都不是医生
他们也没有受过医学的专业训练
常常他们要在半夜起来赶到医院
有时他们要处理一些非常棘手的状况
通常他们面对的情况都让人情绪紧张
另外，他们做这些工作所付出的辛劳
也不容易被注意
我们想想这些弟兄
他们都甘心乐意地献出自己为弟兄姐妹付出
帮助和支持遇到医疗问题的人
他们完成的工作让我们想到耶利米书第23章
这里耶和华说，耶利米书23:4
“我要委任牧人好好牧养他们
他们一个都不会少，再也不用担惊受怕
这是耶和华宣告的”
经文说的也包括
医院联络委员会的弟兄们所做的事
这些弟兄们都是有爱心的牧人
他们提供资讯和协助
帮助弟兄姐妹坚守忠义
这让我想到
当我在加拿大的医院资讯处服务时
一个姐妹，她住在加拿大北部的城市
她受了伤，而且非常非常地严重
需要立即转院
她被直升机送到一间
更大的医疗中心接受治疗
一个医院联络委员会的弟兄，他接到了通知
就马上赶去医院
这个直升机一落地
姐妹被医护人员用担架推进医院的时候
这个弟兄已经在走廊等她
弟兄走上前靠近病床
看到姐妹害怕地浑身颤抖
弟兄看着姐妹
姐妹问他说:“你是医生吗？”
弟兄回答:“不是，我是你的弟兄”
姐妹听到了之后，她马上松了一口气
因为她知道
身边的这个弟兄能给她实际的帮助
接下来我们说说
这项安排怎样提供实际的帮助
你可能从来都不知道
其实在全球89个分部办事处
包括美国和加拿大
都有弟兄全天候24小时、全年无休地
接听来自医院联络委员会和医生的电话
协助那些医生
治疗不愿接受输血的耶和华见证人
这是一个很不可思议的安排
记得我在医院资讯服务部工作的时候
常常在深夜接到电话
弟兄姐妹、医院联络委员会或医生打来说
有人急需帮助
上帝的组织为他们提供很多实用的工具
例如，我们建立了一个资料库
包含数千份医学文章
都来自可靠的医学期刊
我们会将这些文章提供给医生或医疗团队
文章会特别提到怎样在不同的情况下
使用不输血的方法来为病人进行治疗
通常一个医生拿到这些文章
他看到是专业的文章出自权威的期刊
他就会更乐意配合
也会更清楚该怎样进行治疗
除此之外
每个医院资讯处
都有一份可供咨询的医生名单
这些医生在业界都受人敬重
在面对复杂棘手的病例时
他们也敢向其他医生解释
怎样在不用输血的情况下进行治疗
记得有天在半夜，我们接到电话
一位姐妹她刚生完孩子
她在生产的过程中大量失血
她的主治医生非常希望我们提供协助
所以我们马上联络一位
在加拿大非常德高望重的妇产科教授
他一直很乐意协助我们
他一接起电话，我就说
“真的很抱歉这么晚打电话打扰你”
可是他说:“别这么说，马克
我非常愿意尽己所能帮助姐妹”
当然，他不是我们的弟兄
可是他把这些病人当作自己的姐妹
也非常乐意帮助她们
在世界各地
这些既勇敢又医术高明的医生
真的帮了弟兄姐妹很多忙
当然，组织也一直在进步
也许你们都知道jw.org网站里有一个部分
是为了专业医疗人员设置的
现在我想说
这个网页不是为耶和华的子民设立的
而是特别为医疗人员开设的
虽然网站上的这个部分才刚建立没多久
但成效却十分显著
这让我想到另一个经历
有位姐妹写信给分部
她说:“最近我丈夫送我到急诊室
医生发现我的阑尾附近有不明的肿块
我需要接受大型
而且可能复杂的手术才能找出病因
我告诉主治医生
我是一位耶和华见证人
而且我绝对不输血时
这时他开始感到焦躁不安
虽然他没有变得无理，但我感觉到他很烦恼
这时我丈夫马上打电话给弟兄
5分钟后，一位住院医生过来告诉我
我的医生已经上了jw.org网站
正在下载相关资料
我们没有提过网站
所以到现在我们还不晓得他怎么会知道
10分钟之后，他带着那些资料回来找我们
他读完了，也画了重点
还跟我们解释了所有事
他握着我的手，对我微笑
他问我准备好了吗
他保证会尽力帮助我
他说，他跟我一样
一生中也有跟上帝约定绝不妥协的事
手术后12小时，他来看我
我不好意思地说，我真是个麻烦
他说
不，你真是个奇迹！
我们知道他指的是医院联络委员会的安排
以及耶和华通过网站帮助他子民的资料”
最后姐妹说
“这样的安宁是我认识真理这么多年来
第一次感受到的”
今天虽然耶和华没有保证会神奇地治好我们
但他保证我们生病时
他会赐下力量，给我们帮助
世界各地的医院联络委员会
是耶和华上帝送给他子民的宝贵礼物
的确，有这些帮助
我们一定能像经文说的禁戒血

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—디지털 시대에 영적 양식을 공급하는 일

cn.text: 越来越多的人
喜欢通过电子设备了解时事动态
因此
中央长老团决定将JW.ORG网站作为另一种途径
在适当的时候分发灵粮
通过这个网站
我们可以在全球用几百种语言
将信息同时传达给上百万人
这种方法既经济又高效
发行电子出版物也会大大降低成本
那么，弟兄姐妹是如何善用这个网站的呢
我们传道的目标是打动人心
JW.ORG网站就可以帮助我们在传道时达到这个目标
我很喜欢用JW网站名片传道
这种方法既方便又快捷
我在不同的场合都用过
特别是遇到一些忙碌的人时
你只需要给他一张卡片
他就可以随时登录我们的网站了
我很喜欢在公众场所作见证时使用JW.ORG网站
如果有人不想交谈
我就让网站上的影片替我说话
即使他们没接受刊物
还是会留意到手拉车和网址
有些人忙着赶飞机
说不定以后会上网看看
这也很好啊
我会遇到很多忙碌的人
他们可能说不同的语言
我可以用这个网站向这些人传道
我很喜欢跟带孩子的妈妈讨论圣经
在讨论时也会使用志轩和盈盈的动画片
这样的方法可以帮助父母
让孩子从小就把圣经原则谨记在心
我有一次让一个小朋友看了《偷东西是错的》那一集
他一看就明白了，说：我们不该偷东西
用JW.ORG网站可以让我跨越语言的障碍，打动人心
真该感谢耶和华
我做不到的，这个网站都做到了
和学生讨论圣经时，我常常用《检索手册》
有时学生会问我一个问题
我真的不知道该怎么回答
那时我就会查查这个主题
不到30秒就能找到答案
我一直用JW.ORG网站查找一些可能对同事有用的资料
帮助他们看出圣经的实用价值
比如最近
我在查找一些跟丧失亲人有关的文章
方法其实很简单，动动手就可以了
能够随时找到想要的资料，简直太棒了
这个新闻专题的栏目
让我能及时了解那些在其他国家正被囚禁的弟兄姐妹
我试着学会读出他们的名字
并在祷告中具体提及他们的名字，恳求耶和华看顾他们
一想到天父会亲自照看保护他们，就让我感到很安心
不过，做出调整的确不容易
但不少弟兄姐妹为此付出很多努力
比方说，他们努力学习使用上帝赐给我们的新工具
其实，只要我们愿意尝试，就会有意想不到的收获
有了现代科技研读圣经就容易多了
花同样的时间，可以学到更多的內容
因为只需点击屏幕就可以找到经文了
组织制作的JW Library应用程序非常方便
我很容易就学会了
对我来说，这是个高科技
当我试着用的时候，我才发现还挺有意思的
什么事都这个道理，熟能生巧
组织给我们提供的工具实在太好了
JW.ORG网站上的资源帮助我更好地主持家庭崇拜
我们通常会一起练习唱新的王国诗歌
熟悉这些歌曲，我们才能唱好
我们很想通过唱诗赞美上帝
因为唱诗是崇拜的一部分
我们的网站真的使我和家人更加亲密了
也使我们更加亲近耶和华、耶稣还有我们的组织
JW.ORG网站帮助我更深入地挖掘上帝话语的宝藏
当我们把看的內容实践出来的时候
我们和上帝的关系就更亲近了
我深受打动，禁不住流下泪来
真的感谢你，耶和华
能这么直接地受耶和华的教导我真的感觉很荣幸
天父清楚知道我们需要什么
所以在传道和生活方面赐给我们这么宝贵的工具
好让我们和他更亲近

en.text: So we welcome you to the graduation
of the 141st class of Gilead.
And as a reminder,
it’s requested that no flash cameras
be used during the program.
Any picture taken without flash
must be taken from your seat location.
No recordings of any kind are permitted.
Cellular telephones, electronic tablets,
or similar devices should not be used
to transmit any part of the program.
Program notes, whether hard copy or electronic,
should not be distributed to others.
Now to begin our program,
we’ll open and sing song number 107,
“Come to Jehovah’s Mountain.”
And then, Brother Troy Snyder, a member of the United States Branch Committee,
will offer our opening prayer.
So we invite you to stand. It’s song 107.
So the special day has finally arrived.
And we know your family and close friends
are pleased to be here to share this special occasion.
Of course, all the rest are enjoying
the moment with you because it’s a spiritual program.
And, of course, now we broadcast it later.
And the whole brotherhood, for the most part,
is able to benefit from this special activity
that for many years was only at Bethel itself.
Now,
your class enjoyed the spring here at Patterson
and enjoyed the summer at Patterson
—beautiful surroundings.
And Jehovah sure did bless his earthly part of his organization
to have such a place to be educated.
However, now you’ll be leaving for your assignments,
and we’re going to be entering into the fall season.
So . . .
Most years that can be spectacular in upstate New York.
Of course, New England is renowned
for the beauty of the leaves changing
—these radiant colors.
It’s just— Jehovah just amazes us
with what can happen each fall season.
And it put me in mind
(because we’re soon to experience it,
and hopefully it’ll be a good season this year)
of a picture I had in the past, and I appreciated it.
It was a beautiful picture of a lake
with trees surrounding the lake,
very nice, and it was a fall scene.
And so all of these beautiful trees,
the radiant colors around the water
—it just kind of makes you think about the site there at Warwick
and what’s coming this fall.
And the reason I bring it up
is because the caption for the picture was,
“Change—The only thing permanent is change.”
Is that true?
I see some heads going like that.
No, not all the time.
But we can understand why imperfect humans would come to that conclusion.
But Jehovah is permanently the true God.
Thankfully that will never change!
And there are other things that don’t change.
Integrity-keepers that are already experiencing Jehovah’s favor
—those holy angels— they didn’t change, see.
But I bring it up because we’ve entered such a time
where all these changes are going on,
and your class has been held
during some historic changes
—can’t minimize that.
It’s been quite phenomenal.
Now, when you think about the class you’re in
and the historic things that are going on,
yours is the last class to be held
when headquarters was in Brooklyn.
Yep. Had you thought about that?
Last one.
Now, many of us have already moved to Warwick.
So the headquarters staff that’ll be living there
is just moving in on it.
We’ve been moving for months
—all these three different sites—
and there’s more moving to come.
And we rejoice that it worked out
(as the Construction Project Committee
and the thousands that supported them, brothers and sisters),
things speeded up, and we got in there
or are going in there a few months early.
So that’s a rejoicing moment.
Tours, as was mentioned in the broadcast this September,
don’t begin till next year, but Jehovah was kind to you
and brought you over this week to see some of Warwick.
And I see your big smiles.
You enjoyed that, even though there are things
you might want to come back in the future
to see when the tours really do begin to function.
So we know you’re enjoying
the experience here of being educated.
But if you think about it,
what does this tell us about Jehovah?
With moving— And I’ve been telling folks for some months,
“Years back we made the statement that
“(and this was according to some studies that were done)
“the death of a loved one, divorce, and moving
—three top stressors in life!”
Ugh! And those that are moving can tell you, “Oh yeah!”
But it’s right up there with the death of a loved one and divorce.
So that’s stress!

There are a number of definitions for the expression “ego.”
But for our brief discussion this morning,
we want to focus on the definition of “ego”
as it’s used in “egotist”:
An unhealthy belief in our own importance;
the notion of ourselves that distorts reality.
Now, we’re not picking that subject
because we’ve noticed any particular problem
and, believe me, it’s just been the opposite.
But there is a tendency, or leaning,
that we have as imperfect people
to become just a little bit too self-assured
—maybe a little bit too full of ourselves.
And that’s why the apostle Paul,
when he was talking about putting on the new personality,
in Romans chapter 12
he gave this reminder in verse 3.
He said: “For through the undeserved kindness given to me,
“I tell everyone there among you
“not to think more of himself than it is necessary to think,
but to think so as to have a sound mind.”
Now, without going further, we can see the balance.
If we have the right view of ourselves,
well, we have “a sound mind.”
But as soon as we have an unbalanced view,
then we have an unsound mind.
We have a tendency to become unbalanced.
But the culture we live in today
also fans the flames of ego.
For example,
it’s never been easier than today to talk oneself up,
to puff oneself up, to brag oneself up
to thousands, if not millions,
of so-called followers
on social media.
But humility will help us to see
that perhaps others are not quite as interested
in our accomplishments as we are.
So self-worth
is realizing that you have value;
self-importance
is wanting everyone else to know it.
Open your Bibles, if you would,
to 1 Corinthians chapter 8.
First Corinthians chapter 8,
and we want to give just four brief reminders.
First Corinthians 8:1,

It’s not enough to be a student at the beginning.

we are also putting our own faith
in his promises to the test.
This has been —and still is—
your experience.
By seeking first the Kingdom, you Gilead students,
haven’t you been blessed abundantly?
Materially —you have what you need.
Spiritually —a superabundance of blessings
have been poured out on you.
Have you not received blessings beyond measure
in acquaintances, fellowship, happiness and joy
—the people now that you’re close to in your class
and also here at Patterson?
You know what life is all about.
You know what the purpose of life is —why we’re here.
To serve God, to know Jehovah,
and to learn about our great Creator
and the way we should worship him.
And, what— The blessings that we’re receiving
—all of the good things we have—
are just a foretaste of things to come,
things in the near future.
And, I might add, you students are not
the only ones who are testing Jehovah out.
I found this quote interesting from The Watchtower about another group.
The Watchtower stated:
“Most of those who have assisted with the construction work in New York
“could have found reasons not to volunteer.
“However, they put Jehovah to the test
—just as he invites all of us to do.”
And, have they not received rich blessings from Jehovah in return?
Just ask them. They’ll tell you.
And the last part, I like very much.
And, do we not love them for their faith?
Absolutely!
Another group —the anointed—
test Jehovah,
and they are being tested.
Revelation 2:10:
“Prove yourself faithful even to death”
—the test, but the reward—
“and I will give you the crown of life.”
Isn’t that remarkable —the promises that God makes?
That principle applies to all of us.
When we make our dedication and are baptized,
we vow to serve Jehovah God forever.
You know that; we know that.
But there is an interesting point connected to that.
There is more involved than just our person.
Consider this comment from The Watchtower:
“From that time on,” dedication and baptism,
“everything we have belongs to Jehovah.”
Now some may separate their person from their possessions,
not realizing that, really, when you give yourself to God,
it’s all you are and all that you have.
And yet, here is where the tithe, or the principle of the tithe, comes in.
“Still,” and this is part of that quote
from The Watchtower of 2007, December 15:
“Still, he allows us to choose
“a portion of what we have
“—a symbolic tithe—
“to use in his service.
It is whatever our circumstances allow,”
and this second part is touching,
“and our heart impels us to use.”
Isn’t that wonderful on Jehovah’s part?
He doesn’t set forth a specific requirement.
He allows us to display our heartfelt appreciation for him
and for all the good things that he does for us.
The heart is truly involved.
We test Jehovah God out by doing what Proverbs 23:26 says:
“My son, do give your heart to me,
and may your eyes take pleasure in my ways.”
We give Jehovah God our heart,
and we give him everything else
that we have as the needs arise.
What a wonderful opportunity we have!
It gives us this opportunity of showing
how much we appreciate our great God
and how much we trust him.
And this interesting statement was made:
“To fail to give Jehovah our best
is to deprive ourselves of his blessing[s].”
Isn’t that true?
You brothers and sisters of the 141st class of Gilead,
you are not depriving yourselves of anything.
You have the spiritual blessings,
and you have what you need materially —no doubt about it.
And as you continue testing Jehovah out
by responding to his promises,
the quality of your faith
will continue to be tested and refined.
And so, keep on testing Jehovah out;
keep on doing the best you can to obey him,
to comply, to show your faith in his promises.
And then you will also be tested
to your eternal joy and happiness!
Thank you, Brother Malenfant, for that fine counsel.
We invite you all to stand now.
We’ll sing song number 43,
“Stay Awake, Stand Firm, Grow Mighty,”
song number 43.

en.text: Welcome to another edition
of JW Broadcasting!
This month we will see examples
of what young ones
around the world have done to seek
the Kingdom first.
Also,
you will meet a brother who got into a lot of trouble
early in his life.
But how did the truth help him
to straighten out his life?
We look forward to his story.
We will also visit a language course in Ecuador.
What is it like to learn a new language
to expand our ministry?
We will find out.
This is the March program
of JW Broadcasting!
My theme for this month’s broadcast is
“Young Ones—Build Your Future With Jehovah!”
If you do, 1 Timothy 6:19 assures
that you will ‘safely treasure up for yourself
a fine foundation for the future,’
and you will “get a firm hold on the real life.”
Obviously, we will be directing many of our comments
directly to you dear young ones
in Jehovah’s organization.
Yet, if we think about it,
all of us figuratively
are very young ones
compared to eternity
—how long we hope to live.
So, in a sense, our comments during this broadcast
have application to all of us.
Personally, I am so thankful to Jehovah
that positive peer pressure was put on me
to enter the pioneer ministry right out of high school.
What a blessing and a protection it was
to enter the regular pioneer work
at age 17
and to be able to go to Bethel at 18.
Even though there was considerable worldly pressure put on me
to pursue university education,
I am so happy that with Jehovah’s help,
I decided to build my future
with Jehovah.
Truly, I have no regrets.
And this is always true of young ones
who serve Jehovah from their hearts
—they have no regrets.
In fact, you will enjoy these expressions from young ones
who are building their future with Jehovah.
Before I started pioneering,
I was really nervous that I wouldn’t be able to get my time in every month.
It was a bit hard when I started pioneering because I didn’t have a car.
My boss, he didn’t give me part-time work.
I found it really hard to balance schoolwork
and pioneering at the same time.
My biggest struggle was fear of man, so that really hindered me
because I wasn’t very good at talking to people.
Having a good routine was a struggle.
My brother and I are the only ones in the truth.
My family didn’t understand
why we wanted to go preaching.
I didn’t think that I’d make a good pioneer.
I’ve had Type 1 diabetes since I was five.
So I was always worried about whether or not
I could balance that health condition with pioneering.
The challenges don’t seem that big now,
but back at that time they were a really big deal.
But the coolest thing was how Jehovah helped me.
Prayer to Jehovah helped me overcome my fears.
My family was a massive help from Jehovah.
Because my dad was the one who first encouraged me to pioneer,
when I did start pioneering, he promised that I would have
the full support of my family.
When I spoke to brothers and sisters who spent their youth
in the full-time service that really helped me
because it was really encouraging, and it really motivated me
to want to make my own memories and my own experiences
in the full-time service.
So there were practical things I could do.
I didn’t have a car; I just walked or I caught the bus.
I had to work out what my priorities were first.
So I had to find out how many hours would I have to go witnessing every week.
So then I just sat down and I looked at every day
and planned out which days I could go witnessing,
which days I had to go to school,
and also allocated time so that I could do my homework and study.
Having a schedule was really good
because I could see it all out in front of me,
and I could see that the hour requirement
was actually attainable, so that made it a lot less daunting.
I first set short-term goals of pioneering in the special months of activity.
Then I was able to begin continuous auxiliary,
and then eventually I started regular pioneering.
One of the best things I did to prepare myself for pioneering
was to auxiliary pioneer beforehand.
It really set me up to be able to overcome
any challenges that I faced while I was pioneering.
I thought about Malachi 3:10.
I knew I trusted in Jehovah,
but this was my chance to test him out.
I prayed, put my trust in Jehovah,
and put my application in.
After my form was in for pioneering,
a brother, with time, a brother called me and offered me work.
I had unemployment for three months,
which wasn’t a good time.
But during that time, I had Jehovah as my main focus.
And so he supported me, and he didn’t let me down.
Asking brothers and sisters to come
and work with me, maybe on days that I knew
that I wouldn’t get as much support, really helped.
That helped me to organize my hours a little bit more,
and also I’d get to know my brothers and sisters more as well.
One of the greatest joys of pioneering has been to pioneer with Mum.
And we had the privilege of going
to the pioneer school together, which was really special.
Psalm 16:8 reminds me
that Jehovah is right beside me.
When I’m preaching, it’s like Jehovah is holding my hand.
So with full-time service, I love making Jehovah happy.
With everything that he has given me, I’m finally able to give something back.
Looking back —pioneering—
it was the best decision I’ve ever made.
It’s opened up so many different avenues
of service to Jehovah,
and it helped me also to have that real desire
to want to stay in full-time service.
Helping someone on the road to everlasting life,
it’s the best feeling ever; and it’s really irreplaceable.
The only thing I can say,
“As a young person, start pioneering!”
What a fine attitude those young ones have!
They are clearly following in Jesus’ footsteps.
Jesus was the wisest man
who ever walked the earth.
He could’ve pursued any career
and truly excelled at it.
He could’ve been the greatest carpenter who ever lived.
Think about it,
he helped his Father build the physical universe.
Can you imagine what kind of houses he could’ve built?
Or what if he had pursued being an inventor?
With his perfect brain,
he probably could’ve invented the telephone,
automobile, or computer
in the first century.
Or what about becoming a businessman?
With perfect intelligence,
he likely could’ve come out on top
of every business transaction that he entered,
becoming the richest businessman who ever lived.
Or have you ever thought about
if he had pursued becoming an athlete?
And excelling in athletic contests
was a huge endeavor in Jesus’ day.
With a little training,
it is likely that his perfect body
would have outperformed all people
with imperfect bodies,
enabling him to become
the most famous athlete who ever lived.
Or one more example,
what if he had decided to become a doctor?
He could cure sick people
—even raise the dead.
Can you imagine how much he could’ve charged rich people
to raise their dead loved ones?
But Jesus pursued none of these careers.
Why?
Because he knew that any of such endeavors
would have only very limited
and temporary benefits.
Instead, he pursued something
he knew would bring far-reaching and everlasting benefits:
the full-time ministry.
If this is how the wisest man who ever walked the earth—
If this is how he reasoned,
we are wise if we strive to think the same way.
That makes me think of the comments
of a well-adjusted teenage brother
whom we served while in the circuit work many years ago.
This young brother went straight into the regular pioneer work
out of high school,
and I asked him why he did so.
He explained that he knew
he could’ve gotten a full-time secular job
and bought a new car for himself,
but he reasoned that in a few years
that car would rust out and break down,
and he would have nothing.
But he knew that he could go into the pioneer work
and build a close relationship with Jehovah
and perhaps even find an honest-hearted person
and be able to teach that one the truth.
And he knew that would last forever.
Now, that is some wise thinking
on the part of that young brother.
And today, that brother has a beautiful Christian wife
and several spiritual children,
and he is serving as a fine elder.
But if you young ones are going to think this way
and continue to pursue spiritual goals,
it is vital that you wisely choose
your associates.
In a sense, our associates
can be likened to an elevator.
What do we mean?
Well, they can take you up
or they can take you down.
If you choose wisely,
they will take you up
—elevate your good qualities
and make you a better person.
But if you choose poorly,
they will take you down.
Depending on how badly you choose,
they can take you way down
—to the basement,
even the subbasement.
At Proverbs 13:20,
our loving heavenly Father,
who made us, explains how it works.
Jehovah tells us there:
“The one walking with the wise
“will become wise,
“but the one who has dealings with the stupid
will fare badly.”
“Walking with”
and “having dealings with”
mean “associating with.”
And who are the “stupid” ones?
Well, this scripture contrasts such a person
with those who are wise.
It is not talking about someone who lacks mental intellect.
It is talking about someone
who does not make wise decisions spiritually
from Jehovah’s standpoint.
And if we think about it,
anyone who is not really serving Jehovah
—at least right now—
that one is unwise indeed.
And if we associate closely with such ones,
Jehovah says that we “will fare badly.”
We could use another illustration.
Think about someone who is physically sick
and is running a high fever.
If we spend a lot of time with that person,
we will probably catch the same sickness.
Or worse,
if we spend a lot of time near a dead body—a corpse—
we will probably pick up a disease.
Well, it is similar
with spending time with a person
who is spiritually sick,
or worse, spiritually dead.
On the other hand,
if we choose as our associates
those who love Jehovah
and who are building their everlasting future with Jehovah,
we will benefit greatly.
Please observe carefully this variety of young ones
who are busy storing up treasures in heaven
with Jehovah.
How heartwarming it is to us
—and we know it is to Jehovah—
to see these beautiful young people
doing what Jesus encourages
at Matthew 6:20, 21.
There, Jesus encourages:
“Store up for yourselves treasures in heaven,
“where neither moth nor rust consumes,
“and where thieves do not break in and steal.
“For where your treasure is,
there your heart will be also.”
And if we think about it,
in the final analysis,
after all is said and done,
whether we are younger or older,
our net worth will be
what we have stored up in heaven with Jehovah.
We will not be able to take material treasures with us
through the great tribulation.
And if we die,
we certainly will not be able to take material treasures with us,
but we can take spiritual treasures
with us through the great tribulation
and even through death and resurrection.
It is true with all of Jehovah’s people,
as it is with the anointed,
what is stated at Revelation 14:13.
It says there:
“The things they did go right with them.”
And how encouraging it is
to see young ones getting baptized
—publicly demonstrating
that they are giving their lives to Jehovah.
And we sincerely hope
that you young ones who are not yet baptized
will not hold back from getting baptized
as soon as you qualify.
The sooner you can get baptized,
the sooner you will receive greater protection
and blessings from Jehovah.
Not long ago, it made me very happy
to observe a little ten-year-old brother
get baptized!
And young ones,
never be afraid to identify yourselves
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Never allow the fear of what others may think
to cause you to hesitate to do so.
Jehovah tells us
at Proverbs 29:25:
“Trembling at men is a snare,
“but the one trusting in Jehovah
will be protected.”
Many years ago when I was in school,
I can remember being at times somewhat worried
about how my fellow classmates would view me.
But then a little while later,
I got out of school
and never ever again even saw
most of those former classmates.
Then it dawned on me
that it doesn’t really matter what people think about us.
It is Jehovah’s rating of us
that truly counts.
Humans cannot add
even five seconds to our lifespan,
but Jehovah can add
or subtract eternity.
And he alone can also give us true happiness.
And as Proverbs 29:25 indicates,
what a protection
it is to courageously identify ourselves
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
fully trusting Jehovah
and taking our stand solidly with him.
Never be ashamed of who you are.
You are one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And please, dear young ones,
we warmly encourage you
to listen to those who love you.
Jehovah loves you very much;
the Governing Body loves you very much;
the elders love you very much;
your Christian parents love you very much.
And these ones will tell you the truth,
even though at times
it may not be what you want to hear.
They will not ‘tickle your ears,’
perhaps like ones at school
or in the neighborhood
who don’t really love you
or have your best interests at heart.
But please believe those
who will tell you the truth
because they love you.
And never view Jehovah’s laws and principles
as depriving you of something good.
View them as protecting you
from what will hurt you.
If you recall,
Satan convinced Eve
that she was being deprived by Jehovah
and was missing out on something good.
Now, it is true that Eve was missing out on something.
But what was she really missing out on?
A tormented conscience,
her beautiful hair turning gray,
her teeth falling out,
her perfect skin wrinkling up like a prune,
being bent over from old age,
hobbling around on a cane,
and finally dying!
But Satan convinced her
that Jehovah was depriving her,
so foolishly she reached out to get
what she thought she was missing out on.
Well, Satan will try to use
the same kind of strategy on you,
but please don’t let him do it
This also makes me think of an experience a brother once related.
He said that he was visiting an animal observatory,
and a large lion lunged toward him
but was prevented from reaching him
by a thick glass pane
separating the animals from the observers.
As the lion stood on his hind legs,
clawing the glass
and baring his massive teeth,
the brother came to realize in a special way
the protective value of that barrier.
Previously, he said that he somewhat viewed the glass pane
as a restriction
because the smudges on it
partially blurred his view,
but now he viewed it
as a real protection.
Well, in a similar way,
Jehovah doesn’t want Satan,
who is described as ‘a roaring, devouring lion’
at 1 Peter 5:8—
He doesn’t want him to gobble down you young ones.
And His laws and principles
are designed to keep that from happening to you.
So please listen to Jehovah.
He loves you!
You would probably agree that having good friends
is of great encouragement in your service to Jehovah.
You may also recognize
that there is more to being a friend
than simply clicking links on a computer screen
or a smartphone.
But where can you find good friends
when there seems to be no one to choose from?
In this dramatization,
consider the example of this young brother
who struggled with this very question.
My name is Akil.
When I was 18, my family moved to a new city.
It was bad enough leaving my friends behind.
But now,
I wasn’t sure if I could make new ones.
My parents seemed really happy.
I didn’t want to make them feel bad
by telling them how I really felt.
The new school wasn’t much better
until I met Cameron.
He seemed like a pretty cool guy.
Soon, his friends became my friends.
. . . something that David believed was true,
he actually proved it by the association that he kept.
We think about one of the closest friendships
recorded in the Scriptures,
and it was that of David and Jonathan.
What was it that David and Jonathan shared in common?
It wasn’t their age.
Akil, you were texting in the meeting.
I shouldn’t have sent the text.
I’m sorry.
But Cameron is a good person.
He might even study one day.
I understand that, Akil.
But we all have to be careful with how much time
we spend with people that don’t love Jehovah.
See, their values are just different.
You know what Proverbs 13:20 says:
‘Walk with those who are wise.’
So why don’t you seek out friends who love Jehovah?
And you will make friends that last a lifetime.
How am I supposed to do that?
There’s no one my age in the congregation.
Akil, good friends can come from unexpected places.
Mom, I had good friends
—back home.
We all felt bad that night.
The next day,
Cameron posted pictures of a party he had.
My parents were right.
I broke off my association with Cameron
and his friends,
but I still felt
lost.
Hi, Akil?
Do you have field service plans for Saturday?
Ah, no.
Good. Now you do.
I’ll see you at the 9:30 a.m. meeting, OK?
After service,
Max had the group over for refreshments.
Did you take these?
Do you like them?
Yeah.
My wife, she was always the photographer.
She loved photography.
And then one anniversary she went out and bought me a camera,
and from that moment on, I was hooked too.
Time flies so quickly.
It’s hard to believe she passed away 12 years ago now.
I’m sorry.
It’s OK.
But you still take pictures?
I do. I really enjoy photography.
There’s something about being close
to Jehovah’s creation.
It reminds me
that we’re never really alone, you know?
Good friends can come from unexpected places
and unexpected ages.
As I spent more time with Max,
I realized it was just like David and Jonathan.
Their friendship was based,
not on age, but on their love for Jehovah.
And they helped each other.
And with Max’s help,
I was able to keep a good spiritual routine
without interruption.
Although we weren’t the same age,
Max became my good friend.
I just needed to see what was right
in front of me.
Yes, friends can come in various ages.
And the best kind of friend
is one who encourages us in our service to Jehovah.
We all need to work hard on making spiritual progress
—learning new things about Jehovah and his qualities.
So we want friends who will help us do that.
There is a saying
that experience is the best teacher,
but that is not really accurate.
Experience is often the hard way to learn.
Brother Fernando Casillas was born in Mexico,
but when he was a baby,
his family moved to the United States.
The neighborhood he grew up in
had a lot of gang influence.
This had a very negative impact on him.
But despite these circumstances,
notice how the truth attracted him.
I used to love violence; I dreamed  of violence.
My gang was my religion.
I got into the prison system at a young age.
At first, they sent me to a juvenile facility,
but I got kicked out of there for a riot.
Basically, they deemed me a threat to the safety and security
of the institution, the guards, and other inmates.
And I was sent to solitary confinement
to finish off my prison term.
Me thinking I was violent back then
was nothing compared to what I came out with.
Basically, what you try to come out to be
is the best killer out of all.
After my incarceration,
I was deported to Mexico.
I used to carry a weapon with me everywhere I went.
After a while, we started getting involved with bad people.
Eventually, my girlfriend got in trouble.
Once that was over,
she saw a Kingdom Hall.
My girlfriend had been to meetings as a child,
so she basically dragged me to the Kingdom Hall.
They treated me nice.
And that’s when I started to get to know Omar.
So I started hanging around with him and his wife
—me and my girlfriend at the time— and going to meetings.
But it wasn’t till I found out this guy
used to be one of my rivals
—I was very, very upset.
I felt betrayed because he never told me.
Everything that was going through my head was,
‘I’ve got to find a way to get him over here,
so I can hurt him.’
After thinking about all the things that I wanted to do to him that nigh
—I’d been running it through my head over and over again—
I decided to just stay friends with him.
And eventually, we decided to start studying together.
Being the way I was, I thought that there’s
no way a God can forgive me.
The scripture at Isaiah 55:7 really helped me,
where it says:
“Let the wicked man leave his way and the evil man his thoughts;
let him return to Jehovah, who will have mercy on him.”
As time went by, I started understanding clearly
that Jehovah does forgive.
By that time, I had already kind of made a decision
that I was done with doing time in prison.
I just decided to cut all ties with everybody
that had anything to do with anything illegal.
I felt like a free person.
And after progressing
and quitting the habits that I had of smoking and drinking a lot,
I became an unbaptized publisher.
But my father passed away;
I started hanging around with bad association again,
and eventually I had my privileges removed.
And as that was happening, Satan attacked me again.
So one day, my wife was crossing the border
to go take care of some paperwork for the kids
and was surprised by the border patrol
telling her that there were drugs in the vehicle.
We did not know that the previous owner
had stashed drugs in the truck.
Even though later they proved
that the drugs were not my wife’s and she was released,
they still decided to keep my kids.
What I was thinking of doing was going back to my old ways
—organizing a plot with my old friends
to bring my kids back to Mexico to me.
But I decided to rely
on Jehovah instead and on the brothers
coming to visit me on a regular basis
and giving me encouraging thoughts
of how Jehovah will take care of everything.
Eventually, our kids were returned to us,
with Jehovah’s help.
After a little struggle, of course, I had my privileges back.
A few months later, I was baptized.
I’m a lot happier now than what I was back then.
One day as I was preaching in the rehab centers,
I ran into a person I once knew before, growing up.
Once he found out who I was, he said:
“You’re the reason why I left town.
Every time you would see me, you would shoot at me.”
So after a while, I was able to convince him
that actually my purpose there
was not to hurt him anymore
but to teach him the truth
and how to gain everlasting life.
I’m no longer a violent person.
I enjoy the privileges that Jehovah now gives me.
I have now been serving as a ministerial servant
for the past two years.
I’m in charge of the accounting
for the Kingdom Hall,
instead of stealing money as I used to do before.
What I do for a living is I do gardening work.
Now I don’t carry around knives,
but I carry around my tools.
You could say that I did beat
my pistols into plowshares now
—or weed whacker or lawn mower.
I’m glad that I’m now serving a great God
who is loving, caring, and forgiving.
Fernando and his family are serving
in an English congregation in Mexico.
With everything Brother Casillas went through,
he could see that Jehovah is the best teacher.
If you listen to Jehovah,
you won’t have to learn the hard way.
Jehovah is
“the One teaching you to benefit yourself.”
Jeremiah 17:13 conveys the thought
that those who do not serve Jehovah
will have their names “written in the dust.”
But by building your future with Jehovah,
you young ones are ensuring
that Jehovah will keep your individual names
written in his “book of life”
that is mentioned at Philippians 4:3
and Revelation 3:5.
Earlier in the program,
we saw some examples of how young ones
are building a future with Jehovah.
But what impact are such efforts having on the organization?
Let’s look at one example:
the construction of the new world headquarters
at Warwick, New York.
Jehovah’s Witnesses built 1.6 million square feet (149,000 sq m)
in less than four years.
Of the 27,035 volunteers,
3,247 were between the ages of 19 and 25.
I thought this was a project
that was going to strictly need
very experienced brothers and sisters.
Early on, I realized I was wrong.
It was also going to take youthful energy
because of the volume of work.
The mix of older and younger ones
was really a helpful thing on the Warwick project.
The older ones brought skill and experience.
The younger ones brought the energy, the muscle,
and the diligence to stay with hard physical tasks
all the way through the project.
Whether it was in the kitchen
or night watch
or the early 5:00 a.m. start with the concrete crew
at 10 degrees Fahrenheit (-12°C),
their joy and their humility was outstanding
to accept any work that needed to be done.
And a lot of young ones,
brothers and sisters,
moved into the area so they could commute.
And they would work day after day tirelessly,
into the evenings even, to have the project ready for the next day.
Their energy was just astonishing.
Jehovah loves young ones, and he’s willing to invest in them
and train them and make them a part of his organization.
And I saw that so much.
We had a lot of young people
who offered themselves
with technical skills.
But if the humility of these very technically-skilled young people
didn’t match or exceed their abilities,
then, really, Jehovah couldn’t use them.
And they were willing to adjust, and we really saw the benefit.
We knew and they knew
that they were building
not just a project at Warwick
—they were building a spiritual project for Jehovah.
You could see Jehovah’s spirit operating on them.
You could see them mature so quickly.
These young brothers are the next generation
of elders and traveling overseers.
They’re to be commended and highly respected
for the contribution they made as young men.
They all talk about the effect
that their Bethel service has had on their outlook
and how they don’t want to get caught up
in this world and its daily pursuits.
Use the skills you’ve learned
here on this project and in Bethel.
You are needed.
Continue to keep your spirituality up
and to keep your association at a high level.
The highest quality of life is when,
as clay, we put ourselves in the hands of the Great Potter, Jehovah,
and we say: “Here I am! Send me!”.
And I’m fully confident they will have no regrets
building their future with Jehovah.
Yes, young ones truly had a beautiful impact
on the construction project of world headquarters!
By the way, you may find it interesting to know
that the Warwick and Wallkill construction projects
were not funded by the donations
that you have made to the worldwide work.
Your donations are being used to support the work
in the worldwide field.
The massive construction projects at Warwick and Wallkill
were funded by the sale of properties in Brooklyn.
In effect, we just traded locations.
We traded the value of the properties in Brooklyn
for the beautiful facilities at Warwick and Wallkill.
And I must say,
the Governing Body is truly enjoying
the new facility at Warwick,
thanks to the hard work,
both of the young and the older ones
who labored in our behalf,
and we truly appreciate it.
The apostle Paul said of Timothy
as recorded at Philippians 2:20-23:
“For I have no one else of a disposition like his
“who will genuinely care for your concerns.
“For all the others are seeking their own interests,
“not those of Jesus Christ.
“But you know the proof he gave of himself,
“that like a child with a father
“he slaved with me to advance the good news.
Therefore, he is the one I am hoping to send.”
It is obvious that Paul
loved the young man Timothy very much
because of his unselfish hard work
in behalf of Kingdom interests.
Well, the Governing Body feels exactly the same way
about you dear young ones who are working hard
in your various theocratic assignments.
In addition to the many avenues of full-time service
we mentioned earlier in the program,
making yourself available when a need arises locally
is a fine way to seek the Kingdom first.
For example, in San Antonio, in the state of Texas,
in the United States,
a large convention
with over 20,000 in attendance was planned.
However, the venue could only provide
about one third of the chairs needed for the convention.
Where would our brothers find the needed chairs?
Well, Jehovah provided,
and many young ones were eager to help.
When I heard that this needed to happen,
I was thinking, ‘How are we going to do this?’
I thought, ‘It’s a big job!’
It was amazing!
The first thing I was asked to do
was try to find a storage place that we could use
for six to eight thousand chairs.
A sister manages a storage place,
and we saw Jehovah’s blessing
because the owner said, “You can have this stall
“at no charge for a year as long as you sign a contract
that it’s for Jehovah’s Witnesses’ organization.”
Truckload after truckload after truckload came in.
We had to unload the trucks.
The brothers had to unstack the chairs,
repair the chairs, clean the chairs, put them back on pallets,
restack them,
load them onto trucks, and that was half of it.
Those were the ones in the warehouse.
On the other side, we got permission to ask
the San Antonio congregations if we could use their chairs
for the convention.
We were hoping to get three thousand chairs.
And then the numbers grew for the audience,
so we had to increase our numbers.
So we were able to gather six thousand chairs
from the willing volunteers of congregations around San Antonio.
So we prayed about it and the brothers started asking for volunteers,
and it was a great cooperation right at the beginning.
As soon as we let the friends know
that this was going to be the case,
all of them— all of them said,
“We’re going to get off of work early.”
We immediately wanted to clear our schedules
so that we could be available to help in any way that we could.
It was a privilege to know
that our congregation was going to be part of it.
We are so grateful to Jehovah that he has given us
this privilege to do.
We had thousands of chairs
of every color —green, red, brown, blue.
We even had some bright orange ones left out of the ‘70’s,
and we’re putting those in the back.
But it was not just the colors but the sizes.
They were all different sizes.
And so how do you make sections with straight rows
when the chairs are all different sizes?
But I knew somehow, as Jehovah’s people, we’d get it done.
And we definitely— As you see, a lot of volunteers,
and we’re here getting it done.
And it’s made for a beautiful experience
because the friends have gotten to know each other as never before.
And they’re willingly working together,
and the excitement is there.
It doesn’t matter whose venue it is, it’s all for Jehovah,
and that’s been the attitude everybody has had.
It just tells you that Jehovah is a God of order.
It’s good to feel that you’re doing your best for Jehovah.
Well, it reminds me of Psalm 127:1, where it mentions
that ‘unless Jehovah builds the house,
it’s in vain that his workers even work hard.’
So it’s because of Jehovah’s hand and his blessing
—that is why everything runs so smoothly.
What other organization!
No one else can do that except Jehovah’s people.
It truly is a fine witness when our young ones
wholeheartedly give of their time.
Proverbs 20:29 says:
“The glory of young men is their strength.”
And commendably, you young men and women
are using your strength
to make a name with Jehovah.
Have you ever considered helping out in a foreign-language field?
Perhaps there is a need in your local circuit.
All over the earth,
the organization provides language courses
with the goal of reaching every nation, tribe, tongue, and people
with the good news of God’s Word.
Brother Juan Carlos Chacón
serves as a special pioneer
in the rapidly growing Shuar language field
in Ecuador.
He was recently asked to attend
a course at the local branch
to become a language teacher
so that he could help willing publishers
learn the language.
[Speaking Shuar ]
It has been said before,
“This is a language of the Devil”
—that it should be forgotten.
It serves no purpose.
But to Jehovah,
no nation is insignificant.
I grew up in an area of the Ecuadorian jungle
where there is a large community
of Shuar people.
Like many native languages,
Shuar is very complex.
We need many, many workers in the field.
But if we don’t give them a foundation,
if we don’t help them or give them a little push,
it’s difficult for them to enter this field.
I received an invitation to attend
a seminar for language instructors.
There were 58 students in the class,
representing 16 different languages or language groups.
We are learning fantastic teaching techniques,
real techniques that work
The instructor told us how humor helps our minds to create a world of connections,
which stimulates our brain.
Yeah, I’m like a small child
when it comes to drawing.
I never learned to draw well.
We draw a scene,
and starting with our native language
along with large gestures,
we act out a dialogue.
Little by little,
we convert the scene into the new language.
What scares me?
That I’ve never done this before.
This will be my first time.
I don’t have any experience teaching languages.
Although I felt intimidated by this,
I knew that with Jehovah all things are possible.
Welcome to the first day of the Shuar language course.
The techniques they offered us in the course were like a box of tools
that we need to study more carefully and see how to apply them
in each circumstance.
When we are in the territory,
we see how people’s eyes light up when they learn
the name of God.
Just seeing that there is so much need for them to learn the truth,
that has motivated us to come here
and continue serving here.
Since God has created us,
we know that he will never abandon us.
He thinks about us all the time,
and he loves us very much.
I didn’t know that before.
I feel so happy now
because I can really understand the Word of God.
Being in an isolated group far from other congregations,
my wife and I have felt every day
how real Jehovah is.
Jehovah is now looking
and giving his attention to these small places,
no matter how small they are.
If people have a good heart and want to serve Jehovah,
he will send workers to give the help that is needed.
And in reality, this moves us to say to him with all of our heart,
“Thank you, Jehovah.”
There is a lot to do in Jehovah’s organization
regardless of our age.
Even if our circumstances may restrict us,
Jehovah sees and values
all of our efforts to expand our ministry
and to build an everlasting future with him.
Our music video for this month
is appropriately entitled
Building My Future With Jehovah.
At times, I wish I could see exactly what my future will be
And how my life will turn out and which road is the right one for me.
But one thing’s for sure, no matter what comes along,
I live for Jehovah, to him I belong.
Of all the people and things my life could be filled with,
The best one of all, the best one to build with,
Is pleasing Jehovah each day with the choices I make.
He gave me all that I have; I’ll never forget it.
I’m safe in his hands; I’ll never regret it.
I’m building my future with him ev’ry step that I take.
At times, the chance comes along to take a path I know to be wrong,
A path that leads me away from the place that I know I belong.
But keeping in mind the dedication I made
Can give me the firmness and faith that won’t fade.
Of all the people and things my life could be filled with,
The best one of all, the best one to build with,
Is pleasing Jehovah each day with the choices I make.
He gave me all that I have; I’ll never forget it.
I’m safe in his hands; I’ll never regret it.
I’m building my future with him ev’ry step that I take.
I’m building a future that never will end
If I build it with help from Jehovah, my Friend.
The happiest moments, the best life can give,
Come from pleasing Jehovah each day that I live.
Of all the people and things my life could be filled with,
The best one of all, the best one to build with,
Is pleasing Jehovah each day with the choices I make.
He gave me all that I have; I’ll never forget it.
I’m safe in his hands; I’ll never regret it.
I’m building my future with him ev’ry step that I take.
I’m building my future with him ev’ry step that I take.
An encouraging song indeed!
We encourage all young ones
to take the message of this program
—to build a future with Jehovah—
to heart.
Prayerfully consider what you can do
to expand your ministry.
Always safeguard your most valuable possession
—your precious relationship with Jehovah.
Never forget that there are more with you
than there are against you.
It is true that Satan, the demons,
and this world are against you.
But your brothers and sisters,
including the Governing Body, are with you;
the angels are with you;
the resurrected immortal anointed ones are with you;
Jesus is with you;
and most important, Jehovah is with you.
You are never alone!
To conclude,
we have greetings to share with you
from the special convention that was held
in July of last year
in Paris, France.
I had the privilege of attending this convention
with Brother Kenneth Flodin,
a helper to the Teaching Committee.
While most of the convention program was in French
it was simultaneously interpreted
into Croatian, English,
and Polish for the benefit
of the international delegates.
You will be happy to know
that 71 new sisters
and 41 new brothers
symbolized their dedication through water baptism.
The oldest baptismal candidate was an 80-year-old sister
and the youngest was a 10-year-old.
The young candidates had to overcome
various challenges in order to reach their goal
of baptism.
Four of them took this step
even though their parents
are not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Many of these dear young ones had to overcome
peer pressure at school
—pressure to do things
Jehovah does not like.
Two of the young brothers, also fleshly brothers,
used to play violent video games.
Through their personal Bible study
and the personal interest shown in them,
they came to understand Jehovah’s viewpoint on violence
and made the necessary changes to progress spiritually.
By taking this first step
of getting baptized, these brothers and sisters have shown
that they want to build a future
with Jehovah.
Let us all do everything
we can to continue making spiritual progress,
which will bring Jehovah’s smile of approval.
Brothers and sisters, we love you very much.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

专心追求属灵的目标

我们的来往对象就好像电梯一样

如果你选择对的朋友

也就是提升你的基督徒品质
帮助你成为一个更好的人
可是如果你选了错的人做朋友
他们就会带你下楼
你选择来往的对象越糟
你就会被带往越低的楼层

提醒我们谨慎择友的重要性
经文说
“同行”和“来往”
都有“做朋友”的意思

这节经文把愚昧人和智慧人做了个对比
愚昧人并不是指智能不足的人
而是指那些
没有运用耶和华的观点作出明智决定的人
请想想 那些不愿意事奉耶和华
或者至少现在不想这么做的人
他们的想法是多么地不明智
耶和华提醒我们
如果我们和那些人密切来往
就“难免吃亏”
再来看另一个比喻
如果我们和一位
发高烧的病人频繁地接触
就很容易被他传染
或者
如果我们一直待在一具尸体旁
经过一段时间 也很有可能染上疾病
同样
如果我们和一位已经在属灵方面生病
甚至死去的人密切来往
我们就会受到影响
相反 如果我们选择和那些爱耶和华
决心一生与他同行的人做朋友
我们必定获益良多
让我们来看看以下影片中
这些年轻人怎样在天上积存财宝
蒙上帝喜悦
看到这些年轻人
服从耶稣在马太福音6:20,21的吩咐
我们不是感到很高兴吗?
更何况是耶和华呢?
马太福音6:20,21说
在大患难的时候 无论你年轻或年长
我们在天上积存了多少属灵的财宝
在于我们所说过和做过的任何事情
我们没办法带着金银财宝渡过大患难
更不能在死去的时候
带着这些财宝一起走
属灵的财宝却不一样
我们能带着这些属灵财宝渡过大患难
甚至在死去或复活之后
还会一直在我们身边
耶和华的所有子民 包括受膏基督徒
为自己积存属灵财宝 实在有福
就像启示录14:13说的
“他们所做的事紧紧随着他们”
看到年轻人受浸
公开表明自己已经献身给耶和华
实在令人振奋
如果你已经符合资格受浸
我们衷心希望你采取行动 不要迟疑
你越早受浸
就能越早体验到耶和华赐下的福分

en.text: An introduction to the book of Jeremiah.
Jehovah used the prophet Jeremiah
to write one of the largest books
in the Bible.
In addition to being a prophetic book,
the book of Jeremiah provides an account
of the prophet’s own experiences
and personal feelings.
Before Jeremiah was born,
Jehovah took special interest in this boy
who would be born into a priestly family.
Jeremiah became a researcher
and an accurate historian.
He wrote the books of First and Second Kings
and Lamentations.
He may have been close to 25 years old
when Jehovah appointed him as a prophet
in the year 647 B.C.E.
This was less than 100 years after the fall
of the northern kingdom of Israel.
It was a time of turbulent changes
as rival powers jockeyed
for control of the region.
Jeremiah served as a prophet
for about 67 years until 580 B.C.E.
His career as a prophet spanned
the reigns of good King Josiah
and wicked kings Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim,
Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah.
Jeremiah had been a prophet
for about 40 years
when, in 607 B.C.E.,
Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed
and a remnant of survivors
taken captive to Babylon.
Later, Jeremiah was taken to Egypt,
where he continued in his assignment
as Jehovah’s prophet.
The book of Jeremiah was completed
in 580 B.C.E.,
27 years after Jerusalem’s destruction.
The prophets Nahum, Habakkuk,
Obadiah, and Ezekiel
were also inspired to write
during this time period.
The prophet Daniel was another contemporary,
but he did not complete his book
until about 536 B.C.E.
The book of Jeremiah contains 52 chapters.
The events are not written in chronological order,
but according to subject.
In the opening chapter,
Jehovah commissions Jeremiah as his prophet
to convey both a message of judgment
and a message of hope.
Chapters 2 to 24
include Jehovah pronouncing judgment
on the people of Jerusalem
for such wicked actions as idolatry
and violence.
At Jehovah’s direction,
Jeremiah smashes an earthenware flask
to illustrate that God would punish the nation
for its bad conduct.
Chapters 29 to 34 contain
comfort for faithful Jewish exiles.
Jeremiah restates Jehovah’s promise
to restore the Jews to Jerusalem
and to fulfill his covenant with David
for an everlasting kingdom
that will bring about righteousness in all the earth.
Did you know?
The prophet Daniel discerned
from the book of Jeremiah
that the desolation of Jerusalem
would last for 70 years
and that God’s people
were about to be released.
Many chapters recount
how Jeremiah boldly proclaimed Jehovah’s message
in the face of fierce persecution.
In chapter 36,
Jeremiah dictates to his secretary, Baruch,
the words Jehovah directed
against God’s people and all the nations.
On hearing the message read to him,
King Jehoiakim cuts up the scroll
and throws it into the fire.
However, Jehovah directs Jeremiah
to have it written again.
Chapter 38 relates how King Zedekiah
hands Jeremiah over to his enemies,
who throw the prophet into a muddy cistern.
He is rescued later by Ebed-melech,
a faithful worshipper of Jehovah.
The book of Jeremiah contains strong pronouncements of judgment
against many nations,
including Egypt, Philistia, Moab,
Ammon, Edom, and Babylon.
These nations were condemned
for their enmity toward God’s people.
Among the events that Jeremiah recorded
are the last days of Jerusalem,
Babylon’s destruction of the city,
and the aftermath of the destruction.
As you study the book of Jeremiah,
observe how Jehovah condemned the wicked
but gave hope to the faithful,
how Jeremiah faithfully stuck to his assignment
despite hardship,
and how Jehovah promised to establish a Kingdom
that will bring about righteousness
in all the earth.

cn.text: 当时我在西里西亚从事地下工作
我将《守望台》杂志送到不同的家庭
后来我在德累斯顿被逮捕了
在那里我受到一连串的审问
我感受到
耶和华以奇妙的方式帮助我
他们审问我的时候
连我自己都被自己的答案吓一跳
他们问我
你知道守望台组织
在这里是受当局禁止的吗?
我回答 当然知道
他们说
为什么你还违反我们的命令
从事地下工作呢?
我回答
德国法庭承认这项命令
不可偷窃 不可说谎 不可杀人
这是来自圣经的摩西律法
如果你们承认这项命令
也就应该承认其他命令
圣经说
你们要聚集起来 彼此鼓励
如果
我因为和他们见面而感到羞耻
那我就没有遵守圣经里的命令了
我想遵行上帝的旨意 服从他的命令
法官不知道该说什么
他和身旁的法官交谈
但对方也无话可说
一开始我被判处五年刑期
但因为我还年轻
他们将我的刑期减到三年半
当时我25岁
虽然我被独自监禁
但耶和华的圣灵帮助我得到真正的喜乐
我心想
我要每天沉思一件事
首先
我想沉思耶和华的特质
我想从智慧这个品质开始
我用手捂住耳朵 来回不停地走着
我不想听到外界的声音
真好的想法
之后我心想
什么是希望?
什么是信心?
我开始沉思圣灵的果实
圣灵的果实不少
有很多是我可以想的
时间很快就过去了
刑期满了
盖世太保再次传唤我
他们要我签署一份声明
内容是 我和耶和华见证人断绝往来
并且不再学习圣经
我说 我绝不答应!
他说
你有一个晚上的时间可以考虑
我回答
我不需要考虑!
我绝不会签署这份声明!
他说
你要自己承担后果
你会被转送到
拉文斯布吕克集中营
我一到那里
他们就命令我
脱下身上所有衣物
他们拿走了我的衣物
有数小时之久
我必须和其他囚犯
待在一间大寝室
我们要等医师来检查
这很令人难堪
他们想羞辱我们
让我们不开心
年长的妇女站在年轻的女孩当中
她们很难为情
看得出来她们很痛苦
我永远也忘不了当时的情景
之后
他们发给我们囚服
命令我们走到营房接受惩罚
接下来那个晚上真的很可怕
许多囚犯不停地哭泣
也有人不停地呕吐
真的是可怕的一晚
隔天 我们必须工作
我们需要从早到晚
很努力工作
在夏季
早上5点钟就要集合点名
一直工作到晚上7点钟
后来 我们被隔离
不能外出
他们将门关上
从窗户递食物给我们
终于有机会可以好好休息了
我们谈论属灵的事
彼此鼓励
后来医师走来
敲了敲窗户
他问
你们当中有谁死了吗?
我们回答 没有人
一个也没有
我们当中年长体弱的姊妹们
熬过了这一切
从没有人生病
这向营里其他人
做了很好的见证
当时我的丈夫在集中营
起初在达豪
后来在毛特豪森
他们在采石场工作
我丈夫工作的小组里
有一位弟兄
他有一双不合脚的鞋子
这双鞋对他而言太紧了
所以他脱下鞋子
但他忘记从采石场带走这双鞋
我的丈夫想帮助他
于是跑过去捡起这双鞋
警卫发现他离开了草地
离开了队伍
于是他被挂在柱上一个小时
作为惩罚
后来我问他
你是怎么熬过这种折磨的?
他说 我当时想
亚伯拉罕要听从吩咐杀了儿子
当时的情景是怎样的?
那是一条漫长的路
我常常想
他当时在想什么?
他如何克服内心的情感?
以及耶和华希望他怎么做呢?
当他这样想
就感觉不到痛苦了
一个小时后
他从柱上下来
其他弟兄告诉他
看不出来
你刚才是被绑在那个刑柱上!
无论情况如何
耶和华都能帮助我们
很多时候 情况并不容易
但在每种情况下
我们都可以得到耶和华的圣灵
我们可以向他祷告
在我们的生活里
耶和华的名是至为重要的
也没有什么比他的名更重要的了

en.text: You and I make a lot of decisions every day.
Now, some have a little impact on our lives;
others have a very big impact.
And we can appreciate that we can make
choices and decisions for ourselves.
Think of how life would be if you made no decisions for yourself
—someone tells you when to go to bed,
they pick out your clothes,
and they tell you what to do for work.
Well, none of us would like that!
Jehovah gave each of us free will,
and that’s the precious gift
of making choices for ourselves.
Now, have you ever thought about why Jehovah gave us this gift?
I mean, why trust us with free will
when he knew that we could make bad choices or decisions?
Well, one powerful reason is love.
The only way to give us the gift of love
is also to give us the gift of free will.
The two are tied together.
You really can’t have one without the other.
For example, if I programmed my computer
to give me a message every day at 2:00 p.m.:
“John, I love you. I think you’re a wonderful guy,”
I think there’d be a little something wrong with me if I thought:
‘Aw, isn’t that nice? My computer, it loves me.’
Yeah, love only exists
if it comes truly from a free-will expression.
Now, did Jehovah place any boundaries on free will?
Yes.
They were stated in the Law to the nation of Israel.
And Jesus later repeated them
at Matthew 22:37-40:
“He said to him:
“‘“You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart
“‘“and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.”
“‘This is the greatest and first commandment.
“‘The second, like it, is this:
“‘“You must love your neighbor as yourself.”
“‘On these two commandments
the whole Law hangs, and the Prophets.’”
So our use of free will
has love of God and love of neighbor
as its boundaries.
Notice, for example,
what people are doing in this picture,
both inside the circle boundary and outside.
See, free will allows us to do
any of the things we see in the picture.
But love of God and love of neighbor
move us to reject what’s outside the circle
and choose to do the kinds of things
that we see inside the circle.
Now, to stay within those boundaries,
Jehovah gave us a marvelous brain
and a built-in conscience,
but he also knows we need more help.
And that’s why he also gave us Bible principles
—basic truths from the Bible
that can help us to make good decisions.
And it can safely be said that any decision we face
can be guided by Bible principles.
Now, our Creator, Jehovah, knows what’s best for us.
And he also trusts us to make decisions
based on Bible principles
because he knows that when we do that,
then we’re really, truly going to be happy, content,
and at peace with him and with others.
So in review so far:
Jehovah gave us free will
—that’s the privilege to make choices for ourselves—
and he also gave us Bible principles
as the boundaries to our choices.
But making difficult decisions requires that we train ourselves
to recognize Bible principles and apply them.
Now let’s read Romans 12:1,
and let’s see how this verse
describes the decision-making process.
“Therefore, I appeal to you
“by the compassions of God, brothers,
“to present your bodies as a living sacrifice,
“holy and acceptable to God,
a sacred service with your power of reason.”
So are we using our “power of reason”
to understand Bible principles?
For example, young children
ask lots of questions.
But has a child ever asked you:
“What happens when I drop a ball?
a pencil? a book?”
No, they don’t ask that.
They know what happens to anything they drop.
It falls down!
See, the child doesn’t need rules for every object
but has quickly grasped the principle.
Anything he drops falls down.
Now, what if an 18-year-old asked you,
“What’s going to happen when I drop this pen?”
Well, it’s obvious he’s not been paying attention
to basic principles of life.
So by us paying attention to Bible principles,
it won’t obey,
but it’ll pull the person back from danger.
Now, it can take a year or more of training for the dog to learn
the amazing skills that are so helpful to a blind person.
Likewise, our raw, untrained “power of reason”
can help us to a degree.
However, it can be amazing
if we take the time to train it.
Now, here are three skills that we can use
to train our “power of reason.”
They are illustrating,
analyzing,
and balancing.
Now, to consider our first skill, illustrating,
let’s use the general topic of forgiveness.
What Bible principles could help with forgiveness?
Please think of as many principles and scriptures as you can.
Proverbs 12:18 says:
“The tongue of the wise is a healing”;
and Colossians 3:13 tells us
to ‘forgive one another freely.’
Now, the skill we want to learn is illustrating
and it can also be quite enjoyable.
You know, try at your family worship
to take the principles for a topic
and see how many similarities,
nf
Did you notice, for example, what appears to be
a reverse order of the steps leading to sin?
This verse works its way from sexual immorality
back to the very roots of the problem.
Now, let’s take each phrase starting with the last,
“greediness, which is idolatry.”
So, sexual immorality starts with selfishness,
greedily putting our needs ahead of anything else.
smelling the bread and cakes when he can’t pay for it.
Likewise, hanging around immoral entertainment
until we’ve learned all that we can.
And we can use the many research tools we have
to find valuable comments and application.
Now, let’s consider our third
and final skill: balancing.
And to do that,
let’s use a question on the topic of alcohol.
What Bible principles could help a couple to decide
whether to serve alcohol at their wedding?
What principles and scriptures do you think would help them
make a balanced decision?
Again, you’re welcome to pause the program
if you’d like to write down what comes to mind
or to research something.
Now, your list probably has some of these principles.
At John 2:9, Jesus made wine for a wedding.

cn.text: 我们每天都要做许多决定
有些决定对我们的影响很小
有些却非常大
我们都很高兴可以自己做决定
怎么说呢?
想想看
你喜欢每天都让别人告诉你
几点该上床睡觉
穿什么样的衣服
做什么工作吗?
当然不喜欢!
耶和华赐给人自由意志
让我们有选择的自由
可是
既然耶和华知道我们都会犯错
为什么他还是赐给我们
这份宝贵的礼物呢?
最大的原因就是爱
爱心和自由意志是密不可分
缺一不可的
如果耶和华要给我们
表现爱心的能力
就一定会让我们拥有自由意志
举个例
假如我在电脑中输入一个程式
每天下午两点
就会跳出一个讯息说
嗨 约翰 我觉得你好迷人 我爱你
会因为这样 我就觉得
我的电脑很爱我 真是太好了
当然不会
只有运用自由意志
才能表现真正的爱心
不过 上帝有定下一些原则作为规范
告诉我们该怎样使用自由意志吗?
有的
这个原则就记载在摩西律法里
耶稣在马太福音22:37-40
重申这条命令
经文说
所以 我们会善用自由意志
去爱上帝和爱别人
请留意 在这张图片里
圆圈之内和圆圈之外的人在做什么
我们虽然有选择的自由
可以做图片上的任何事
但由于爱上帝和爱别人
我们拒绝做圆圈之外的人所做的事
而选择做圆圈之内的事
为了能够善用自由意志
耶和华设计了超凡的人脑
也赐给我们一颗良心
但他知道我们需要更多的帮助
所以他给了我们圣经的原则
让我们可以做出正确的决定
可以说 我们做的所有决定
都可以从圣经找到指引
身为造物主
耶和华知道什么对我们最好
所以他让我们根据圣经的原则
自己做决定
这样 我们就能够感到
真正的快乐和满足
也能跟耶和华和别人 享有和睦的关系
复习一下 我们学到了什么呢?
耶和华给我们自由意志
让我们有殊荣可以为自己做决定
耶和华也赐给我们圣经的原则作为规范
帮助我们做正确的决定
但是 我们需要锻炼自己
好能在做重大决定时
正确地运用圣经原则
现在 我们来看看罗马书12:1
经文谈到怎样做正确的选择
我们有运用“理智”了解圣经的原则吗?
举个例子
小孩会问很多问题
但他们会不会问
如果把一颗球、一枝笔、一本书
从手里放掉  会发生什么事吗?
当然不会
他们知道只要手一放开
东西就会掉下来
你不需要实际告诉他
每个物体放开后会发生什么事
他们很快就会了解这个自然法则
不会每次都问相同的问题
但是 如果有一个18岁的人问你
如果我把这支笔放掉
会发生什么事呢?
显然 他根本没有留意生活中
很多基本的原则
同样
我们仔细留意圣经的原则
很快就能看出
怎样在生活中爱上帝和爱别人
而不需要一大串的规条
告诉我们该怎么做
我们可以怎样锻炼“理智”呢?
当然 我们不需要很多规定
告诉我们什么电影可以看
什么音乐可以听
什么衣服可以穿
只要在阅读圣经时
仔细留意所读到的内容
圣经的原则就能锻炼我们的良心
帮助我们做出正确的决定
锻炼“理智”
好比盲人的导盲犬一样
没有受到训练的狗
对盲人很有帮助
有人接近时 它就会叫
但是 一只受到专业训练的狗
对一个盲人的帮助更大
它知道什么时候该停下来
怎样绕过障碍物
避免主人被撞到
它们也受到一种特别的训练
如果主人不知道前方有危险
仍要导盲犬往前走时
导盲犬不会服从
反而会把主人拉回来 避免发生危险
你知道吗?
训练一只导盲犬
可能需要花上一年多的时间
同样地
我们没有受到锻炼的“理智”
可以在某种程度上
对我们有帮助
可是 如果我们花时间锻炼它
对我们的帮助就更大了
有三种技巧
可以帮助我们锻炼自己的“理智”
分别是 运用想象力
分析经文
找出平衡点
首先
我们来谈谈运用想象力
我想用宽恕这个品格为例
你想到哪些圣经原则和经文
可以帮助我们表现宽恕呢?
试试看先暂停一下
把所有你能想到的圣经原则写下来
你想到的经文
可能有马太福音18:22
经文说要宽恕人“到七十七次”
“明智人的舌却如良药”
歌罗西书3:13谈到的
要“彼此甘心宽恕”
我们想学习运用想象力
在脑海中将这些原则灵活运用
虽然我们不都是艺术家
但我们都有能力
在脑海中描绘鲜明的景象
现在 请试着运用想象力
将圣经的原则
和日常生活的事物连结起来
例如 如果罪像债务
宽恕就好像一个人
免除了别人的债务
如果伤人的话像伤口
宽恕就好像伤口愈合了
如果罪像黑板上的字
宽恕就好像把这些字擦掉
也是一个运用想象力的好例子
经文说
请想想
如果耶和华
没有给人体自我修复的能力
我们从小到大所受的伤
就都无法痊愈了
从这个比喻我们看出
宽恕可以给人的安慰有多大
当然 学会如何运用想象力
是需要时间和练习的
不过 这种技巧不仅有趣
还能成为锻炼“理智”的强大工具
你可以试着在家庭崇拜时
找一些圣经原则
然后想想生活中有哪些事物的概念
与这些原则相似
用新的角度去看圣经原则
也许会有意想不到的收获
我们来看第二个技巧
分析经文
“分析”是指彻底地了解一件事
我们来谈谈 错误的欲望这个例子
我想到的原则 记载在歌罗西书3:5
当我们和错误的欲望缠斗时
我们可以怎样从分析
歌罗西书3:5得到帮助呢?
你可以再暂停一下
仔细想一想
经文中每件事的关联
你有发现吗?
这节经文把问题产生的原因
以倒序的方式依次列出
一步步让我们看出
问题的根本原因是什么
我们从最后一句话开始看起
“贪婪 贪婪等于拜偶像”
这表示
自私、只顾满足自己的需要
是导致淫乱的第一步
接着 贪婪会产生“有害的欲望”
就好像一个人没有带钱
还一直在香味四溢的面包店前
徘徊一样
接触不道德的娱乐及不良的来往
也会滋长“有害的欲望”
使人心怀不轨
这样的欲望会产生经文接着说的
“肉欲”
心怀肉欲的人
不只是心里想而已
还会寻找机会 满足自己的欲望
先前的步骤会导致
他和别人有不当的肢体接触
这就是“不洁”了
最后
由于未婚的两人有亲密接触
他们就犯下了严重的罪
“淫乱”
仔细分析歌罗西书3:5
能帮助我们根除心里的错误欲望
我们也借此看出
立刻将这些错误的欲望根除
有多重要
越早发现心中的错误欲望
就越容易根除它
因此 不要只是匆匆读过经文
要仔细分析
找出值得活用的地方
我们也可以使用不同的检索工具
查找相关的评论和应用方式
现在 我们来看最后一项技巧
找出平衡点
我们拿酒精饮料做个例子
一对即将结婚的情侣
该怎样运用圣经原则
决定是否在婚宴场合
提供酒精饮料呢?
你有想到哪些原则
能帮助他们作出平衡的决定吗?
你可以再一次暂停一下
查查资料
并把你想到的写下来
也许你有想到约翰福音2:9
耶稣在一场婚礼将水变成酒
哥林多前书6:10却说
醉酒的不能承受上帝的王国
另外 哥林多前书10:31, 32也说
你们无论或吃或喝
一切都要为荣耀上帝而做
不可成了他们的绊脚石
看起来
没有一个原则提供了明确的答案
一对情侣可能认为
既然耶稣在婚礼上提供酒
为什么我们不行?
但问题并没有想象中那么简单
想解决问题
就要找出这些原则的平衡点
在做决定前 我们得想想
受邀参加婚礼的亲朋好友
有人在饮酒方面不懂得节制吗?
依照当地的习俗
在婚礼上提供酒精饮料
会不会使人良心不安呢?
我们必须从圣经原则中
找出平衡点
而不是只用一节经文
就草草下定论
耶和华希望我们运用“理智”
找出圣经原则的平衡点
然后做出正确的决定
给了我们很好的提醒
经文说
这段经文说得多有道理
在运用圣经原则方面
我们要找出平衡点
而不是以偏概全
我们平衡合理地运用圣经的原则
就能显示我们真的爱耶和华
也爱人如己

en.text: Growing up in the truth,
I felt like I fit in
more with my friends at school
or people who weren’t Witnesses.
I was living a double life and I knew it.
I was not baptized.
I had always tried to make the truth fit in with the world.
And this time I decided that I just want to give
the world a shot and see what that’s like.
I came right to my parents, and I said,
“I want to move to LA and pursue modeling.”
I had my first job within the week.
It looked so glamorous.
There were a lot of parties
—going to the coolest houses, getting to hang out with celebrities.
There are no rules.
You have the money to do whatever you want.
That lifestyle was so far from what I was raised knowing as right
that I basically had no relationship with Jehovah.
Once all the smoke and mirrors are gone,
you see these things for what they are.
I remember I called my mom,
and I told her: “It’s like Sodom and Gomorrah.
I’m literally in the middle of it all.”
And I thought, like, this is it;
this is what everyone says is the best, and I’m not happy.
And I just felt so dull —empty.
And I actually thought to myself:
‘I wish— I wish I was never raised a Witness.
I wish I never even knew Jehovah existed.’
There were certain nights where I needed Him.
I was thinking, ‘Just pray; just go to him.’
And I couldn’t.
I thought I would never be able to come back to Jehovah.
One of the jobs I got hired to do
was to work for this young fashion company.
In between different outfits and shoots, you would, you know,
talk with the photographer.
So, what are you guys going to be for Halloween?
Matt doesn’t celebrate Halloween.
He’s one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
So am I.
It’s not a joke.
No, I’m not kidding.
I was raised as a Witness.
Yeah, I was raised as one as well.
Do you, um— do you go to meetings?
No, I haven’t been in forever.
What about you?
No, no, I haven’t.
I got a last-minute job to New York.
I decided to walk the Brooklyn Bridge.
I knew Bethel was there, and I’d never been to Bethel.
This sister stopped me on my tour, and she invited me up to her office.
There were different paintings of the resurrection.
She asked me, “Do you know why the people are waiting on the balcony?”
And I was like, “I—I don’t know. Why?”
And she said, “Because they’re waiting for their loved ones to be resurrected.”
It was as if something just went straight to my heart.
I’ve never felt something like that.
I had for the first time actually seen the resurrection and believed it.
It wasn’t just this thing that might happen —it was for sure.
I knew exactly what it was going to look like.
I would be standing there on that balcony
looking for my loved ones to come back,
and I wanted to be there.
The resurrection was so real to me.
And the second I got out of Bethel,
I—I called my mom, and I told her, and I said:
“Mom, Mom, I’m coming back.
“I know exactly what I need to do.
I’m coming back to Jehovah.”
I had made up my mind, you know, I’m going to give Jehovah a chance.
But, you know, I’m coming back to the truth.
I’m going to do it right.
There was an elder who was doing the Watchtower,
and he just came off so kind
that I thought, you know, when this meeting ends,
I want to talk with him, and I’m going to explain to him why I’m here.
I knew I had so many changes to make.
Matthew 6:33 is so important to me,
‘Seek first the Kingdom.’
My entire life I sought everything else before Jehovah.
I never put him first, and I for the first time was saying,
“OK, Jehovah, I’m going to put you first.”
The job I have right now isn’t necessarily my dream job,
but it allows me to do exactly what I want to do for Jehovah
—and that’s pioneer.
I used to walk down Hollywood Boulevard
going from casting to casting with my portfolio in hand,
and now I walk down Hollywood Boulevard with the cart in my hand.
Out in the ministry, I see models that I used to work with,
and I love getting to show them that this is my new life,
and this has changed my life.
I am so happy.
I know what it’s like to superficially feel good.
But to literally have the joy, the happiness
—I want to share that with everybody.
Jehovah completely changed my life.
