우리가 있어야 할 곳을 아시고, 결국 우린 그곳에 있게 되죠.
세상에선 어떤 프로젝트를 빨리 달성하는 데 주력합니다.
그들은 시간을 가장 중요한 요소로 여기지요.
워릭 공사가 다른 공사들과 달랐던 건,
영적 양식이 필요하단 걸 아신다는 거였죠.
우린 버스나 밴을 타고 도착해서 먼저 아침 숭배에 참석했습니다.
많은 사람에게 이 신권 공사가 깊은 인상을 남긴 건
우리가 영적인 것을 앞자리에 두는 걸 보고 이렇게 칭찬했습니다.
“우린 도착하면 일부터 하는데, 여러분은 하느님께 숭배부터 드리는군요.”
브루클린에서 워릭으로의 이전을 위한 팀을 구성하도록 했죠.
정말 이제 브루클린을 완전히 비워 줘야 할 때가 된 거였죠.
누구나 건물을 사면 즉시 입주하기를 바라거든요.
지하 터널로 연결되는 건물이 여섯 동 있습니다.
한 매입자가 여러 건물을 다 사들이는 게 아니라면,
건물들을 팔면서 이 터널들을 끊어야 하는 거죠.
뉴욕 법에 따르면 거길 다 콘크리트로 메워야 합니다.
터널을 메우면 건물들로 연결된 공공 설비가 차단되죠.
그럼 건물의 난방은 어떻게 할 건지, 전기와 통신 문제는 어떻게 할 건지,
또 언제 차단할 건지, 언제 사람들이 빠질지도 문제죠.
그런 복잡한 문제를 다 해결해야 했습니다.
일이 얼마나 커졌을지 짐작이 되실 겁니다.
이 부서가 옮기기 때문에 해당 서비스를 중지할 경우,
이 서비스에 의존하고 있는 인원이 여전히 1200에서 1500명 되죠.
그런데 그 위치를 잘못 잡으면 이전하는 과정에서 방해가 되죠.
그래서 이걸 어디에 둘지도 알아야 합니다.
이 일은 여러 달에서 길게는 1년 이상을 내다보고 착수해야 하는데,
예를 들어, 이 부서에는 남편이 있고,
다른 부서엔 아내가 있는데, 일정이 서로 다르게 잡혀 있습니다.
동시에 두 가지 일을 다루기 위한 지원 시스템이 필요했습니다.
이전 과정 내내 이런 문제들을 동시에 고려해야 했습니다.
한 번에 하나가 아니라 두 세 가지를 같이 계획하는 거죠.
동시에 현장 가족들은 떠나고 있었기 때문입니다.
이 모든 이전 과정을 제때에 잘 계획하는 게 중요했습니다.
그런가 하면, 브루클린에서 이사를 나오기 시작하면서
모든 매각한 건물에 들어가서 청소를 해야 했습니다.
부서들 간에 협력이 정말 멋지게 이루어졌습니다.
저희가 부서들과 상의를 시작하면 모두들 100퍼센트 협조적이었죠.
다들 뭘, 어떻게 하면 도움이 될지 알고 싶어 했고,
다른 부서를 위해 도울 게 없는지 궁금해했죠.
“우리 부서가 영향 안 받게 최대한 보호해야지" 하는 게 아니라
그런 규모의 이전은 우리끼리라면 못 했죠.
심지어 패터슨과 월킬의 도서실에서 일하는 형제들까지 와서
짐을 싸고 중앙 도서실에 놓을 책들을 추리는 일을 도와줬어요.
최근에 세었을 때만 해도 책이 6만 5000권이나 됐었거든요.
이 서적들은 연구•조사를 위한 지식의 보고이죠.
그냥 손 놓고 “두 달 간은 아무것도 못해”라고 할 순 없죠.
다들 합심해서 부서가 이전하는 일을 도와주었습니다.
스튜디오 하나만도 얼마나 많은 부서가 지원했는지
그 모든 다른 형제 자매들의 도움이 없었다면
어떻게 이전을 하는지 알고 싶어 했죠.
보도를 오가는 행인들, 버스를 타려는 사람들에,
오피스 건물 바로 뒤편으론 공사도 한창이죠.
그래서 그들은 우리가 일을 어떻게 조직했고
무엇을 어떻게 할 건지 이미 경찰과 상의했다는 사실을 알고는
그 일을 통해서도 여호와의 축복을 볼 수 있었습니다.
베델의 연로한 분들은 모범을 보여 주셨습니다.
전 세계 밭을 바라보는 넓은 시야와 같이
조직에 꼭 필요한 것들을 가르쳐 주셨습니다.
그래서 저는 그분들을 도울 수 있어 더할 나위 없이 기쁩니다.
연로한 분들은 정말 충실하게 여호와의 조직과 함께 일하길 원하시죠.
주위에 돕는 사람이 많으면 일을 그르칠 리가 없어요.
다들 절 손바닥 보듯 훤히 알죠.
우리가 뭘 하든 관대하게 지원을 베풀어 줍니다.
미국 지부 감독 아래 참여했던 다른 모든 건축 공사와
워릭 공사가 어떻게 달랐는지 저한테 물은 분들이 계셨어요.
다른 부서에 양보할 줄도 알아야 했습니다.
전 이곳이 앞으로를 위한 훈련장이 되어 왔다는 생각이 듭니다.
또 우리가 앞으로 영원히 사용할 기술들을 가르치고 계신 거죠.
깊은 인상을 받았을 거라고 저는 생각합니다.
워릭에 거주하기 시작하면, 중요한 변화들을 보시게 될 겁니다.
전 세계 우리 형제들에게 어떤 영향을 줄지 빨리 보고 싶습니다.
세계 어디를 가나 가장 먼저 받는 질문 하나는
‘워릭에 가 볼 계획이에요. 꼭 가 보고 싶어요’ 하고 말씀들 하시죠.
많은 분이 와서 아름다운 환경과 박물관과
그 밖에 여기 있는 것들을 보면 분명 큰 감동을 받게 되실 겁니다.
앞으로 어떤 일이 있을진 알 수 없지만,
분명 여호와께선 놀라운 것들을 준비해 두고 계십니다.
이 조직의 구성원들이 모여서 공동의 목표를 달성하는 모습을 보면
이 일을 이루실 수 있는 분은 여호와뿐이심을 알게 되죠.
여호와께서 이 조직을 이끌고 계시다는 걸요.
이 조직의 지상 부분은 정말 놀라울 뿐입니다.
이 아름다운 새로운 본부에서 갖게 된 첫 아침 숭배를 위해서,
중앙장로회는 이 프로젝트를 위해 수고한 모든 분들에게
그러면 중앙장로회를 대신해서 이 편지를 읽어 드리겠습니다.
이곳 워릭 베델에 아름다운 새 집을 갖게 된 것에 대해
우리는 새 숙소동과 사무실들이 정말 마음에 듭니다!
상쾌한 공기, 조용한 환경, 아름다운 경치만으로도
이제 확신하건대, 여호와의 축복과 도움으로 우리는
왕국 권익을 위해 더 열심히 일하고 더 많은 일을 이룰 수 있을 것입니다.
우리가 이처럼 멋진 곳에서 살고 일할 자격이 있는지는 모르겠지만,
여호와의 과분한 친절의 이 관대한 표현에 대해
2만 7000명이 넘는 형제 자매들이 이 공사를 위해
많은 우리 형제 자매들이 휴가를 내고,
새벽같이 일어나 버스나 셔틀을 타고 현장으로 왔습니다.
그리고는 날씨가 어떻든 지칠 줄 모르고 일하면서,
이 신권 건축 공사를 마음을 다해서 지원해 주셨습니다.
많은 분이 여러 차례 와서 일해 주셨습니다.
여호와께서는 여러분이 하신 일 때문에 여러분을 매우 사랑하십니다.
중앙장로회 역시 여러분을 매우 사랑한다는 것을 기억해 주시기 바랍니다.
바울이 데살로니가 사람들에게 한 말을 빌리자면,
실제 건축 일에 참여한 분들 외에도,
수많은 형제 자매들이 멀리서 이 공사에 힘을 보탰습니다.
희생적인 아내들은 이 일에 참여하는 남편을 지원했고,
다른 충성스러운 분들은 워릭 현장에서 일할 수 있도록
하느님의 말씀은 짐 곁에 남아 있던 사람도
전투에 내려간 사람과 똑같은 몫을 받았다고 알려 줍니다.
이 공사를 지원한 형제 자매 여러분 대부분을
분명 여호와께서는 여러분 한 사람 한 사람을 알고 계십니다.
여러분이 거룩한 자들을 섬기면서 행한 일과
그분의 이름을 위해 나타낸 사랑을 잊지 않으십니다.’
여호와께선 우리가 그분께 제일 좋은 걸 드리기를 기대하십니다.
그 이유로 그분은 가인의 희생을 불쾌하게 여기셨는데,
그분은 가인이 더 좋은 걸 드릴 수 있음을 아셨습니다.—창세기 4:5.
아벨처럼 여호와께 가장 좋은 것을 드렸습니다.
여호와께 마음을 다한 사랑을 나타낼 것이라고
그에 더해서, 중앙장로회는 지칠 줄 모르고 사랑으로 수고한
워릭 건축 공사 위원회의 다섯 명의 형제들에게
또한 이 대규모 신권 공사와 관련해서
우리와 ‘어깨를 나란히 하여’ 수고한 많은 베델 성원들에게도
그중에는 미국 지부 위원회 형제들을 비롯해서
브로드캐스팅부, 운송부에서 열심히 일하는 형제 자매들
워릭으로 이사하는 엄청난 일을 지금도 계속 지원하고 있는
우리는 월킬 공사를 위해 헌신적으로 수고한 수많은 형제 자매들에게도
그 일 역시 실로 엄청난 일이었습니다!
여호와께서 여러분이 나타낸 자진하는 태도를 축복하시길 바랍니다.
성경에서는 강조를 위해 어떤 사상을 세 번 반복할 때가 있는데,
본부에서 진행되어 온 이 놀라운 신권 공사를 위해
지금껏 우리를 도와주셨고 끝까지 계속 도와주실 모든 분들께 말입니다!
‘여호와께서 여러분이 행한 일에 대해 상 주시기를 바랍니다.
여러분이 그분의 날개 아래로 도피처를 구하려고 왔으니,
여러분 모두에게 우리의 따뜻한 사랑과 애정을 전합니다!

en.text: Now we invite you to enjoy a special presentation
that highlights the relocation of headquarters
from Brooklyn to Warwick.
We’d like to let you know
that the Governing Body has decided that if the approvals
are received for the Warwick project,
we will be moving completely out of Brooklyn.
The world headquarters will be relocated at Warwick.
Jehovah is telling us through the Governing Body,
“It’s time to move out of Brooklyn.”
The Governing Body, these brothers,
as soon as they see Jehovah’s direction, they just move.
It doesn’t matter if it’s long-held cherished ideas.
This is the way it has to be done.
As soon as they see Jehovah’s direction, it’s done.
Jehovah had everything in control.
He just kept nudging imperfect humans.
You know, he knew where he wanted us,
and then we end up where we’re supposed to be.
In the world, actually, they can accomplish projects quickly.
They basically say,
“Time is of the essence,” and they mean it.
Cost has to be almost not a consideration.
People are not a consideration.
Jehovah’s organization is different.
What made the Warwick project different than all the others,
and Jehovah knew, is the fact that he realized
that we needed constant spiritual food.
We would arrive on our buses, arrive in our vans,
and we would go to morning worship.
The spirituality of the family
really made this a theocratic project
that stood out in the minds of many.
The outside contractors there,
they noticed that we were putting spiritual things before physical things,
and they commented on that,
“While we arrive and get right to work,
you arrive and you worship your God.”
The Branch Committee contacted four of us
to set up a team to do the move out from Brooklyn to Warwick.
Now it became the reality of completely clearing out,
and I mean that’s everything.
That was a pretty daunting thing
because when people want to buy your properties,
they want to take possession right away.
There are six buildings that are connected through tunnels underground.
And so, if a buyer is not interested in purchasing multiple buildings,
the sale of the properties are going to disconnect those tunnels.
New York City law requires we fill those up with concrete.
We didn’t anticipate that.
Once we fill those tunnels,
that cuts off the utilities to the rest of the buildings.
So how do you heat the other buildings?
How do you keep their electricity, their communication going?
When can you shut it off? When will the people be moving?
Those are all the logistics that came into question
and that we had to work through.
When we look at the work, it’s like an iceberg
—16 properties to empty; 1.6 million square feet;
over 2,000 individuals to get moved out
in 13 months;
take that and look at 70 departments
—and you start to get a picture of the growth
of the job already expanded.
If you shut down this service to the Bethel family
because you’re moving that department,
you still have maybe 1,500,
1,200 people relying on that type of service.
So now you put in a temporary service.
But if you locate it in the wrong location,
well, now, that can hinder the operation of the move out.
So you have to know where to put it;
so your job just grows again.
The process starts many months, even more than a year previous,
as you identify who from departments are coming.
You realize that in this department is perhaps a husband,
but in this other department is a wife,
and they’re scheduled for two different times.
So now, how do you make that work?
Do we have the support system in place in order
to handle both of those assignments at the same time?
Those logistics are all part of the process that we had to go through at the same time.
You’re planning for two things, not one, or sometimes even three.
Because at the same time,
when we were ramping up the movement into Warwick,
the construction family was leaving.
So all that was part of it.
Then it was just a matter of making sure that we could schedule
all the moves in the necessary time.
On the other side, once you start moving out of Brooklyn
—once we began the move out of Brooklyn and every building that got sold—
someone had to go in and clean the place.
Everything had to be cleared out.
So the collaboration between departments
has been really nice to see.
When we would come in and start to speak with groups,
they were 100% cooperative.
Then they wanted to know: How can they help? What can they do?
Are there other areas that they can help out —other departments?
So it was not a, “This is my department,
and I’m going to protect everything.”
It was more: “This is the arrangement.
How can we help out?”
A move that size—
We couldn’t do it on our own, so we had the help
of the Furniture Moving Department.
Brothers even at the other sites
—in Patterson and Wallkill, in those libraries—
helped us to pack
and somehow to extract books that we needed in our main library
because we have, I would say,
some 65,000 books at last counting.
The main repository, really,
for research are our books.
Writers, they have to work.
They can’t just say,
“OK, now for two months, I won’t do anything.”
Thanks to all those moving
—they did a wonderful job helping us out.
Without them, I think we still would be in Brooklyn
counting our books.
A lot of things go into moving the Broadcasting Department.
Even in just the studio, the number of departments
that have assisted in some way is staggering.
And really, there was no other way it could have gotten done
without the help of all those different brothers and sisters.
We got contacted by the Brooklyn Heights Association.
They wanted to know: How is this move going to happen?
Brooklyn is very complicated
—there’s traffic everywhere,
people crossing the sidewalk,
trying to get around buses,
construction right behind the office building here.
So they were very appreciative
of how we had it organized
—how we’d already communicated with the police
on what we were doing and how we were going to handle it.
So it was sort of an unexpected,
but we saw Jehovah’s blessing in that activity as well.
The older ones in Bethel were the ones who set the pace for us.
The things we learn from them —their work ethic,
their broad view of the worldwide field—
to me, is what our organization is about.
And so for me, it’s extremely gratifying
to be able to help.
Are they nervous? Yes.
But really, they are faithful and want to work
along with Jehovah’s organization, so they’ve been very cooperative.
When you have a lot of people helping you, you can’t go wrong.
They know me like the back of their hand.
But, we’ve laughed about it, and we’re all happy.
And they’re providing us a lot of assistance in whatever we’re doing,
and I love them for that.
It’s encouraging to see those ones do that.
It sets a nice example for the rest of us.
So some have asked me the question, “What was the difference between Warwick
and all the other construction projects that you did under the U.S. branch?”
This one was a little unique.
There was a need for great communication,
not good communication, great communication.
We had to trust our brothers and sisters —implicit trust.
We had to yield to other departments.
I think it’s only been a training ground, really,
for Jesus Christ to use it to teach people
and to teach us skills that we’re going to use for an eternity.
I think it has made a great impression
on all those who have had the privilege of working on it.
Once the Bethel family makes the move out of Brooklyn
and begins to inhabit Warwick,
that’s when you’re going to see some significant changes.
I am looking forward to the effect that it has on the brotherhood.
Everywhere we go around the world, that’s one of the first questions
people ask is: “How is Warwick?
We’re planning to come to Warwick. We want to come see it.”
And when they come and they see the beautiful surroundings,
when they see what is there —the museum that will be there—
it is really going to touch many people.
As we look to the future, we have no idea,
but we know that Jehovah has amazing things in store.
When you see an organization like this
come together to accomplish a common goal,
you know it can only be done by Jehovah.
It touches your heart.
It touches your faith.
It helps you to really see that, yes,
Jehovah is running this organization.
And his earthly part of the organization
is amazing.
When we think about this first morning worship
from our beautiful new headquarters,
the Governing Body thought it would be appropriate
to provide an open letter
to thank all who have shared
in the hard work that went into this project.
How we appreciate it!
But permit me, please,
to read this open letter from the Governing Body.
“Dear Brothers:
“On behalf of the Warwick Bethel family,
“the Governing Body would like to express deep appreciation
“for our lovely new home here at Warwick Bethel.
“How we love our new residences and offices!
“The fresh air, quiet environment,
“and beautiful scenery
“are already having a beneficial effect on how we feel.
“We are confident that now
“—with Jehovah’s blessing and help—
“we will be able to work even harder
“and accomplish even more in behalf of Kingdom interests.
“Even though we do not deserve
“such a wonderful place to live and work,
“we truly appreciate this generous expression
“of Jehovah’s undeserved kindness.
“We are most grateful to Jehovah
“for the more than 27,000 different brothers and sisters
“who volunteered to work on the construction of this project.
“Many of you dear friends took vacation time,
“paid your own transportation costs, lived in small rooms,
“and got up very early in the morning
“to ride buses or shuttles to the work site.
“Then you worked tirelessly in all kinds of weather,
“putting your heart into supporting
“this theocratic building project.
“Many of you accepted multiple invitations to work here.
“Unquestionably, Jehovah loves you very much
“for what you have done.
“Please be assured that the Governing Body
“loves you very much too!
“To borrow Paul’s words to the Thessalonians,
“‘you have become so beloved to us.’
“—1 Thessalonians 2:8.
“In addition to those who shared in the actual construction work,
“countless other dear brothers and sisters
“supported this project from afar.
“Self-sacrificing wives backed their husbands’ participation,
“diligent remote workers lent a hand,
“generous publishers assisted financially,
“and other loyal ones
“encouraged and provided practical help
“to those who were able to work at the Warwick site.
“Reflecting on those who helped from far away
“reminds us of 1 Samuel 30:24.
“God’s Word tells us that the ones who stayed behind with the baggage
“received the same share
“as the ones who went into battle.
“Even though we do not personally know the vast majority
“of you brothers and sisters who have supported this project,
“for a certainty, Jehovah knows each and every one of you.
“As Hebrews 6:10 assures:
“‘God is not unrighteous so as to forget your work
“‘and the love you showed for his name
“‘by ministering . . . to the holy ones.’
“Jehovah expects us to give him our best.
“That is why He found Cain’s sacrifice displeasing.
“He knew that Cain could have done better.
“—Genesis 4:5.
“But like Abel,
“you dear friends have given Jehovah your best.
“We are confident that you will continue to show your wholehearted love
“for Jehovah in harmony with your circumstances.
“—Genesis 4:4; Matthew 22:37.
“Additionally, the Governing Body
“would like to thank from the bottom of our heart
“the five brothers
“who served on the Warwick Construction Project Committee
“for their inexhaustible labors of love.
“We also want to thank profusely the many Bethelites
“who worked ‘shoulder to shoulder’ with us
“in connection with this massive theocratic endeavor.
“—Zephaniah 3:9.
“Included are the brothers on the United States Branch Committee
“and the hardworking brothers and sisters
“in the Furniture Moving Department,
“the Maintenance Department, the Computer Department,
“the Broadcasting Department, the Transportation Department,
“and the Bethel Office
“who are still carrying out the gigantic task
“of moving the Bethel family from Brooklyn to Warwick.
“We would certainly be remiss if we failed to thank also
“the thousands upon thousands of devoted brothers and sisters
“who labored on the project at Wallkill.
“That too was a massive undertaking!
“May Jehovah bless the willing spirit that you dear ones have shown.
“In the Bible, sometimes a thought
“is repeated three times for emphasis.
“In this vein, we say,
“‘thank you, thank you, thank you’
“to all who have helped us
“and are continuing to help us bring
“this wonderful theocratic project at headquarters to completion!
“‘May Jehovah reward you for what you have done,
“‘and may there be a perfect wage for you
“‘from Jehovah the God of Israel,
“‘under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.’
“We express our warm love
“and affection for all of you!
Your brothers, Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses.”

en.text: Most people use electronic devices for things like homework, . . .
. . .research, . . .
. . .social networking, . . .
. . .entertainment, and more.
But if you’re not careful,
you could become overly attached to your devices.
You could even have withdrawal symptoms
if you’re away from your devices.
This addiction could cost you your job, . . .
. . . your friends, . . .
. . . or more.
Are you addicted to your device?
The Bible says to “make sure of the more important things.”
So ask yourself these questions:
Do I become uneasy or irritated when I can’t use my device?
Do I keep using my device longer than I intended to?
Am I losing sleep because I can’t stop checking for messages?
Do my devices cause me to neglect my family?
What would my family say?
If you answered yes to some or all these questions, don’t give up.
It’s not too late!
Take back control!
For example, set a time limit.
Then stick to it!
When driving,
keep your devices out of sight and reach.
Suggest that your family try “phone-stacking” during a meal.
The first one that reaches for it has to do the dishes.
Set aside a screen-free evening.
And keep your tech out of the bedroom.
You’ll sleep better.
The Bible says that “two are better than one.”
Ask a trusted family member or friend
to help you make the needed changes.
At 1 Corinthians 9:25,
the Bible tells us to exercise “self-control in all things.”
So remember, you may live in a wired world,
but it doesn’t have to control you.
Take breaks from your devices.
You’ll be happier and enjoy more out of life.

is now a reality in this prison, the prison of Bollate.

who every Thursday and every Sunday
freely choose to take part in the meetings.

with the authorities, relationships with,

The knowledge that so many people
attend the meetings of the Kingdom Hall

has convinced us that it was an excellent choice, worthwhile.
A Kingdom Hall in other detention centers,
well, that would be a great idea.

en.text: During the past five years,
over 1.3 million faithful ones
have symbolized their dedication
to Jehovah by water baptism.
That’s an average of over 700 each day.
And among those courageously taking their stand
for true worship are thousands of children,
teenagers, and young adults.
Young brothers and sisters,
we know it is not always easy
to serve Jehovah and live up to your dedication.
Like older ones,
you need to be encouraged and strengthened spiritually.
With that in mind, our theme this month is
“Young Ones, ‘Become an Example to the Faithful Ones.’”
It is based on the inspiring true-life story
of a young Christian named Timothy.
Before we discuss Timothy’s example,
did you know that the Bible specifically foretold
that many young people would take sides with Jehovah in our time?
Let’s look at this at Psalm 110:3.
And as we read it together,
note how young ones are having a share in fulfilling this prophecy.
Notice the first part of verse 3,
David sang:
“Your people will offer themselves willingly
on the day of your military force.”
According to this prophecy, Jesus, the Messianic King,
would have a large army of willing supporters.
Since 1914, millions have carefully investigated the facts
and chosen to side with Jehovah God and Jesus Christ.
But where do young ones come into this picture?
The rest of the verse continues:
“In splendid holiness, from the womb of the dawn,
“you have your company of young men
just like dewdrops.”
Here, the prophecy refers to a “company,” or group, of young ones.
They also would study the evidence and support God’s Kingdom.
How many young people did Jehovah foresee
supporting true worship?
We get an idea by the comparison made to dewdrops.
Have you have ever gone outside early in the morning
and noticed a light, sparkling coating of water on the ground?
That may have been dew.
Jehovah designed our atmosphere so that, under certain conditions,
when the temperature cools during the night,
a blanket of moisture forms on the ground.
That coating is made up of a multitude of little drops.
Young ones, what does dew have to do with you?
In the Bible, dew is connected with blessing and abundance.
Dewdrops are also refreshing,
life-sustaining, and numerous.
Now, remember in Psalm 110:3,
Jehovah was looking ahead to our time.
And what did he see?
The September 15, 2002, Watchtower on page 8
explained it this way:
“Just like refreshing dewdrops,
“many young men and women cheerfully serve God
and assist their fellow worshipers.”
Today, there are so many mature,
bright, happy young ones in the Christian congregation
that they are like countless dewdrops that sparkle in the morning sun.
You faithful children, teenagers,
and young adults who have dedicated your life to Jehovah
or who are working toward that goal
are living proof that Jehovah’s confidence
in young people was never misplaced.
He cherishes you very much and so do we.
Of course, knowing that Jehovah has confidence in us
can be very encouraging.
But what if doubts or negative thoughts
tend to bring us down?
On occasion, a young Witness might wonder,
‘Does anyone other than Jehovah notice me?
Does my example really matter to others?’
To address these questions,
let’s now consider Timothy’s example.
Open your Bible, please,
to our theme text at 1 Timothy 4:12.
When you find it, you might want to bookmark the verse
because we want to first understand the setting.
How old was Timothy at this time?
Often, when thinking of Timothy,
I picture a teenager or a young man in his early twenties.
And when he first started traveling with Paul,
he was about that age.
But several years passed before Paul wrote letters to Timothy.
So by the time First Timothy was written,
Timothy was likely in his early thirties.
Now, what do you think?
Was Timothy young or old?
Some of you younger ones may be thinking to yourselves,
‘If he was over 30, then he was old!’
But remember, a much older man like Paul
would say that Timothy was quite young.
In fact, notice the expression he uses when writing to Timothy.
First Timothy 4:12, Paul says:
“Never let anyone look down on your youth.
“Instead, become an example to the faithful ones
“in speaking, in conduct, in love,
in faith, in chasteness.”
Paul called Timothy a youth and urged him to be a good example.
While Timothy may have been in his early thirties at this time,
remember that he was taught about Jehovah
from the time he was a baby,
and he did well in the truth as a young person.
In fact, when he was still a teenager or in his early twenties,
the elders recommended him to serve as a missionary with Paul.
So, in effect, Paul here is urging Timothy
to continue to be a good example for others.
What else do we know about Timothy?
He was not proud, or haughty.
He likely did not view himself as some amazing example.
I’m sure he never dreamed that one day Christians all over the world
would study his life in detail so as to imitate his faith.
Timothy was modest —and this despite his privileges.
Paul’s words may indicate that Timothy was somewhat shy.
Like many of us,
he may have battled with feelings of self-doubt on occasion.
Based on this information, let’s do something interesting now.
Let’s use our imagination to visualize Timothy,
an elder in his early thirties,
coming to give a Scriptural talk in the congregation.
Got the picture?
In your mind, please look at Timothy
and then look at the audience.
Who do we see?
Many in attendance are old enough
to be Timothy’s parents or grandparents.
How do you think Timothy felt?
Super confident?
Are you visualizing him proudly walking into the meeting place, saying,
“I sure wish my friends back in Lystra could see me now.
Look at the crowds that come to hear me speak!”
No, that’s not the Timothy we know.
It’s much more likely that Timothy, like most of us,
rehearsed his presentation over and over again.
He probably prayed constantly,
and he probably still got nervous, like all of us.
And remember, Timothy did not have the benefit
of theocratic schools like we do today.
In summary,
what can we say about Timothy?
Like so many of you,
he was an example of faith and obedience.
He was exceptional in displaying Christian qualities,
such as modesty and humility.
But Timothy was a person with normal human feelings,
like all of us.
Though he had a rich, happy life in Jehovah’s service,
life in the old world brought real tests and challenges.
Timothy also dealt with frequent cases of sickness,
and he was imprisoned for a time.
Some of you in various countries
can relate to those bitter experiences.
But Timothy endured.
Was he some “super Christian” with superpowers?
No, but he did prove to be a super example!
How does all of this help you Christian youths
who have taken the commendable step
to dedicate your lives to Jehovah?
We just read how Paul told Timothy to let no one look down on his youth.
A few of you may be thinking,
‘I wish someone would tell my parents
‘or my elders not to look down on me.
They still treat me like a little kid.’
If that’s the case, we feel for you.
No progressive young one wants to be treated as if he were a child.
But let’s look again at 1 Timothy 4:12.
Is the apostle Paul speaking to the congregation,
to parents, or to the elders?
“Never let anyone look down
“on your youth.
“Instead, become an example to the faithful ones in speaking,
in conduct, in love, in faith, in chasteness.”
It’s clear, isn’t it?
Paul said your youth.
He was speaking only to Timothy.
Young ones, by extension, what is Jehovah saying to each of you?
It’s this: To gain and maintain the respect of faithful ones,
you have to work at proving yourself as a Christian.
The key is not wanting or hoping that others will respect you.
Rather, it’s earning such respect by setting a good example
in all areas of life.
If you do that,
then no one will have any legitimate reason to look down on your youth.
Doesn’t it make sense that we gain respect by earning it?
We are confident that you young ones are trying hard
to live by Christian principles at school and in the neighborhood.
But in verse 12, did you notice who Timothy was to be an example to?
To “the faithful ones.”
Are you an example to Christians, both younger and older,
in your congregation and in your circuit?
If you work on Kingdom Hall construction projects or at Bethel,
are you an example to your fellow workers?
Well, what are some specific ways you can become an example
to all of these “faithful ones”?
In our theme text, Timothy was first directed
to become an example in speaking.
On this topic, I’ll never forget an illustration
used in the “Young People Ask” article from the January 2012 Awake!
It quoted a young man, James, who said:
“Once you squeeze toothpaste out, you can’t put it back in the tube.
“The same is true with our words.
Once we say something hurtful, we can’t take it back.”
God’s Word agrees with James.
Note what it says at Ephesians 4:29.
It tells us:
“Let a rotten word not come out of your mouth,
“but only what is good for building up as the need may be,
to impart what is beneficial to the hearers.”
For some years now, those getting baptized
have been encouraged to complete a study of the book,
“Keep Yourselves in God’s Love.”
Chapter 12 is entitled “Speak What ‘Is Good for Building Up.’”
On page 140, there is a box with five questions
that can help us evaluate our speech.
For example:
“When was the last time I offered someone specific commendation?
“Do I express my respect for others by saying please and thank you?
“In conversation, do I speak mainly about myself,
or am I also interested in the thoughts and feelings of others?”
Young ones, over the next few days,
why not review that box on page 140, look up the scriptures,
and think about what Jehovah is saying?
Then apply what you learn to your speech.
Doing this will draw you closer to Jehovah
and help you to become an even better example
to the faithful ones.
The second area mentioned in our theme text
is becoming an example in conduct.
Of course, upbuilding speech would be empty
or hypocritical if our conduct was questionable.
Think again about Timothy.
It wasn’t enough for him to give comments and talks at the meetings
or preach from door to door.
Later in the same letter, Paul reminded Timothy
that he needed to treat older men and women as fathers and mothers;
younger men and women were to be treated as brothers and sisters.
Second Peter 3:11
provides a similar urgent reminder about our conduct.
Let’s read that together.
Again, that’s 2 Peter 3:11.
There it tells us:
“Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way,
“consider what sort of people you ought to be
in holy acts of conduct.”
Let’s think about that.
For a person’s conduct to be holy from Jehovah’s perspective,
he or she must be morally clean.
While physical cleanness is on the outside,
moral cleanness is on the inside —in our thoughts and desires.
Is being morally clean really important?
Think about it this way.
When eating a meal, would you be content to eat from a bowl
that had been washed only on the outside?
Of course not!
We want to eat from clean dishes
—dishes that are thoroughly clean inside and out.
So when we wash dishes, we wash the outside and the inside.
Similarly, Jehovah expects his servants
to be clean through and through.
And because Jehovah —the perfect reader of hearts—
will soon dissolve, yes, eliminate this dirty system of things,
it’s urgent that we do so.
This means that we have to work very hard
so that nothing unclean enters our mind.
That means firmly rejecting
so-called fun and exciting entertainment,
which features sex, violence, or spiritism.
At 1 Corinthians 14:20, the Bible tells us
that we should become like “young children as to badness.”
No matter our age,
we don’t need and we don’t want
any experience with the wickedness of this world.
Rather, we keep the inside of the dish,
our mind and heart, clean at all times.
And when we do so, our exemplary conduct
pleases Jehovah and it strengthens our faithful brothers and sisters.
Really, it’s the only way to respect ourselves
and to gain the respect of others.
Our theme text at 1 Timothy 4:12
goes on to mention other areas
where we can make steady progress in becoming an example,
such as in love, in faith, and in chasteness.
During your personal study,
that is, your personal time with your best Friend, Jehovah,
why not examine these areas in more detail?
The treasures you gain from such a study project
can last a lifetime —an everlasting lifetime.
So, what have we learned?
In fulfillment of Bible prophecy,
a large company of young people from around the world
are taking a stand with Jehovah and Jesus.
That includes all of you.
Like dewdrops, you’re not only abundant in number
but you sparkle in our congregations.
Your presence is very refreshing.
So please, don’t look down on your youth.
Rather, rejoice in your youth!
Yes, “become an example to the faithful ones”!

“说强化人的好话”
在140页的附栏

我们说的话有没有强化人?

我上一次明确地称赞别人

要留意自己的行为

真的那么重要吗?
请想想一个比喻
假如你吃饭时

你敢用吗?

我们也要坚决抵抗
那些看起来好玩、刺激
但内容却包含色情、暴力
通灵术的消遣娱乐
哥林多前书14:20告诉我们

无论我们几岁
我们都不想 也不要沾染
这世界上的任何恶习
相反 我们会让自己的思想
和内心时常保持洁净
就像我们会让碗的里面
常常保持干净一样
我们的好行为 不但能使耶和华欢喜
更能强化忠贞的弟兄姐妹
我们能借此表明
我们尊重自己 并得到别人的尊重
提摩太前书4:12 还继续谈到
我们可以在爱心、信心、贞洁上
不断进步 成为别人的榜样
何不试试在个人研读
也就是
你和你最好的朋友耶和华相处时
深入研读这些课题呢?
你从圣经里挖掘到的属灵宝藏
一定能使你的一生得益不浅
我们从今天的演讲学到什么呢?

将有一大群从世界各地来的年轻人

你们人数众多

en.text: So, if the Devil tempted Jesus,
don’t you think he will try to tempt us
in order to jeopardize our relationship with God?
This is the best contract we’ve ever offered you.
Listen, I’ll get you a plan
so you can attend your religious meetings during the week.
Just do the concert for us on the weekend!
People always ask me,
“Why did you leave the music world?”
When I was still a boy,
I had dreams about becoming a famous singer.
Then I learned the truth,
but I never fully removed those dreams from my heart.
And then I started listening to some bad influences from my past,
and they got me hooked.
Then they reeled me into the recording studio.
The lyrics in the songs
—they really bothered my conscience.
So they offered me some liquor to loosen me up,
and then I started to feel more comfortable.
I started singing, and they liked what they were hearing.
And those songs ended up all over the radio stations.
It was as if Satan gave me a trophy
for abandoning Jehovah.
I became addicted to the applause.
Everything looks so beautiful,
but when you’re on top
—when you’re really at the top of Satan’s world—
there’s nothing beautiful there.
I was an actor,
and when the cameras turned on,
my face and my smile turned on too.
But when I would get back to the hotel,
it was a huge letdown.
There was no applause
—just that silence that tormented my conscience.
So basically, you had to find
other distractions, and one of those for me
was the slot machine.
And, of course, casinos don’t just come with slot machines.
They also expose you to prostitution and alcohol.
My conscience would ask,
‘What are you doing here?’
I remember those times on tour,
from my limousine, I’d see the brothers preaching,
and that would always touch my heart.
I would say to myself, ‘Wow!
‘Jehovah trained you to be doing that,
and look at what you’re doing!’
That really cut deep into my heart.
The road back to the truth was, really, very hard.
Every time I was going to retire, I’d say, “This is it!”
But then there would always be a bigger contract.
I had to make drastic decisions.
But finally I said:
“I don’t care what they offer me.
“I have to return to Jehovah.
“I have to fulfill the vow
“I made to him when I was a young man,
when I dedicated my life to him.”
So I prayed to Jehovah very earnestly and said:
“Jehovah, I need to return to you.
“I need to return to your loving arms.
“Satan has ripped me away from you.
Please help me.”
I remember that before I went in to that first meeting,
I told Jehovah, “Please give me a sign that you will take me back.”
And there was an elderly sister there.
She gave me a great big hug
and said, “Welcome back, son!”
And she took my hand
and sat by me during the entire meeting.
I had betrayed Jehovah, but I thank—
I thank the brothers
because Jehovah put brothers at every turn.
They showed me with the Bible
how far I had strayed
from the paths of the true God,
and everything you do has consequences.
I have asked Jehovah many times to forgive me for all the things
I have done —and the brothers too—
all the people I offended by my actions.
All those trophies I won
—every last one of them—
are there collecting dust.
But Jehovah has given me
a different kind of trophy in his organization
—helping others to dedicate their lives to him.
That’s something no one can take away from you.
We don’t all have to learn the hard way.
We have to keep enduring
and never turn our backs on Jehovah.
That’s the worst mistake anyone could make.
We know that it’s Jehovah who gives us our talents,
so we should use them all in his service.
I have found happiness, and that gives me
a glow that’s not just for the cameras.
Everyone who knows me can see it.

en.text: It was very difficult to reach these territories
because we had to navigate through part of the Orinoco
and then onto other smaller rivers.
Many of their communities are far away.
The first time we came, we traveled on the roof of a boat.
We are within days (approximately seven days)
from our place of origin, where our family is.
Another challenge is the language.
We realized that many did not understand a word.
In this assignment,
we have come across seven different languages.
Initially, this was a demanding task.
Imagine having so much to say and not being understood.
We were able to overcome it because, at this point,
we feel that what we preach in their language —it is reaching their hearts.
They understand.
They understand.
We can see it in their faces.
And that motivates them to make changes in their life.
This led a group of brothers to put forward
the idea of having our own boat for the purpose
of preaching the good news of the Kingdom in this area.
And that’s when finally the project
of El Precursor del Amazonas was born.
The branch arranged for a committee to handle
the task of managing and caring for the boat.
They also prepare the travel itinerary during the year.
They conduct important meetings,
such as the pre-departure meeting
—which aims to train the assigned passengers,
giving them necessary guidelines and instructions
to be observed during the trip.
They also assign the different crews to man the boat.
In the morning, you get up before dawn
—most likely six in the morning,
half past five.
It’s still a little dark.
Morning worship is conducted at approximately seven o’clock;
some instructions are given; and after offering up a prayer,
we eat calmly at about half past seven.
During the trip, there’s a chance to read.
There are assignments, such as cleaning the boat, cooking.
Actually, we stay pretty busy.
And at the end of the day, we arrive at a beach or a community.
No comparison between traveling before and traveling now.
Now we travel by limousine.
It’s luxurious —“five star” or something like that.
Yes,
traveling in seats, for example,
with a group of brothers,
with a formal meal service,
with electricity.
Meetings are held; we consider the daily text.
We share experiences, tell stories; we do everything!
It’s like being in a miniature Kingdom Hall,
traveling for five days.
We also preach in the different communities along the way.
It has its own publications and a literature cart.
That makes it a very spiritual
and upbuilding experience for all of us.
The way the boat looked to them,
captured the indigenous peoples’ interest.
The dignified presentation of the boat
is something worthy of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I also noticed that where we were sitting,
we had a little area, like a locker for each person.
That made it very comfortable
—things that didn’t exist in boats for rent.
El Precursor del Amazonas has been a blessing for us.
We were able to bring our food and some of the things we needed,
such as a refrigerator to keep it in.
Those things have been made possible,
thanks to Jehovah, who allowed us to have this boat.
At times, we have arrived at a point where
we nearly run out of all the supplies,
and something always happens —brothers arrive
or El Precursor del Amazonas comes.
At the end, we learned to be in want
but also to have an abundance.
Seeing all this makes us feel protected
—even though we are here in the middle of the jungle.
People here in Amazonas know that there is a God
who gives them food, provides them the river,
gives them the rain that keeps them alive.
But they didn’t know
that Jehovah is that God.
And that is our job
—to teach these people that Jehovah is the true God.
When you see the sparkle
in the eyes of your Bible students when they understand the truth,
there is nothing like it.
It compensates for any discomfort.
That’s priceless!
So being in this work is the best thing you can do
because it causes true happiness.
I am proud of being with Jehovah’s people.
Now I enjoy watching the videos with my family.
I conduct a family study, and I preach with my children,
giving the message to the people.
Sometimes you have to reject Bible studies —something that seems a strange thing
for a Jehovah’s Witness to do, turn down Bible studies.
Rather, we always want to have studies.
But there are so many
that if we start giving them all, it will be impossible.
So, then, sometimes we choose to tell people to wait a bit
and that we’ll return on another occasion.
And sometimes up to one year will pass by.
We have visited people from a year ago
that had not been spoken to since, and they say:
“Hey, a year ago you said you’d return, and now here you are.
But it’s been a year, brother!”
I feel good,
and I am teaching them in Curripaco.
So they can speak to people about Jehovah in Curripaco.
To share in one of the preaching trips
of El Precursor del Amazonas
is a unique and unforgettable experience.
Your faith is strengthened when you return,
and you are made more aware of the need
for additional workers for the harvest.

他们也被分组委派照料这艘船
我们早上5点半到6点之间起床

大约7点的时候
我们会先举行早晨崇拜  说明今天的活动

其实挺忙的
晚上我们会将船停靠在沙滩或社区附近
以前的船和现在的根本没得比
现在我们搭的是五星级的“豪华邮轮”
对啊  船上什么都有
有弟兄姊妹
有好吃的食物
也有电力供应
我们照常举行聚会
讨论当日经文、分享经验和故事
我们能做的事可多了!
这5天  我们就好像
坐在一个迷你的聚会所里面  到处航行
沿途向不同的居民传道
我们也使用出版物和书刊手拉车
这些美好的经验  真的大大强化我们所有人
船的样子吸引了当地人的注意
它的外观跟耶和华见证人的身份是相称的
我也注意到我们的座位  有个小小的区域
每个人都有置物的箱子
这样的设计非常舒适
是一般租借的船上没有的
拥有“亚马逊先驱”号实在是我们的福分
我们可以把食物还有其他需要的东西
像是存放食物的冰箱带上船
感谢耶和华让我们拥有这艘船
每次  我们的生活必需品快要用完时
弟兄或“亚马逊先驱”号就会出现!
我们学会处匮乏  也处丰裕

亚马逊的人们相信有上帝
他们相信上帝给他们食物
上帝创造河川
上帝降雨让他们存活
但是  他们不知道耶和华就是这位上帝
我们的任务就是教导人认识耶和华
看到圣经学生因为明白真理
眼中闪烁着光芒
这是无可取代的
这种快乐是无价的  远远超过我们所付出的
能参与这份工作  真的是最棒的事了
能作为耶和华的子民  我觉得很自豪
我很喜欢和家人一起看组织出版的影片
我也主持家庭崇拜
跟孩子一起传道  分享好消息
有时候  我们得“拒绝”和人讨论圣经
听起来很奇怪
耶和华见证人怎么会拒绝跟别人讨论圣经呢?
我们都渴望分享真理
因为要说的东西实在太多了

结果

他们就会说
一年前你说会再来  现在你真的来了
不过老兄  已经一年过去了!
我觉得很开心
我用库里帕科语和他们讨论圣经

能和“亚马逊先驱”号一起传道旅行

title: 청소년 여러분—‘여호와가 얼마나 선하신 분인지 맛보아 아십시오’

en.text: Our relationship with Jehovah can start when we’re young.
For me, it was the example that others set
of putting Jehovah first
and the happiness that came as a result,
as well as being in that sort of environment
that really helped me to want to reach out
as well as be available for those opportunities.
And once we do give our life to Jehovah,
it’s amazing to see the blessings that he has in store for us.
But in order to build that relationship,
we need to read God’s Word;
we also need to pray to him.
The more you get to know him,
the more appealing things you learn about him.
That makes you not want to lose him as your friend.
I always knew it was the truth
and that I wanted to serve Jehovah forever.
But I needed to reassure myself of certain aspects,
so I did some research projects with my parents,
using the Creator book and some items from the Bible Teach book.
After that, it only became more obvious.
And I was certain that I wanted it
and that I was ready to get baptized.
To strengthen my relationship with Jehovah,
I read the Bible daily and I pray.
Especially when there is no one around or it’s quiet,
I talk to Jehovah with all my heart at that time.
Making myself available for spiritual opportunities
was a little bit difficult for me at first,
but I didn’t give up.
After my baptism,
I became a ministerial servant,
and I also served almost two years in Bethel.
And now I’m a regular pioneer
in Hpado in a Karen-speaking congregation.
I didn’t know or speak the Karen S’gaw language,
so the local brothers helped me to learn not only how to speak
but also how to read.
Prayers are important to strengthen
my relationship with Jehovah.
For me, it’s like talking
to a friend, and that’s always helpful.
He’s someone real to me,
and I fully trust that he listens to me.
I support the elders by helping with the cleaning of the hall,
serving as an attendant,
handling microphones,
as well as helping the congregation spiritually.
When I share Jehovah’s promises of eternal life with others,
I too am encouraged.
I’m constantly remembering what Jehovah promises,
and that motivates me to keep preaching.
There’s a family in our congregation
who took me into their home
and served as my spiritual parents.
Through our family worship,
they helped me to progress spiritually.
The elderly ones in our congregation have been helping me a lot.
First, they’re good examples.
They also remind me to keep my eye simple.
Despite their limited circumstances because of age,
they are determined to serve Jehovah God.
And that made me reflect on my situation.
I’m very young.
What prevents me from doing the things that they do?
Before I began pioneering,
I used to sell fish seven days a week,
but now I sell fish four days a week,
so three days are available for pioneering.
To be able to be available for spiritual opportunities,
I closely associate with my congregation.
I offer some older ones a ride to the meetings
or in the preaching work.
The reason I’m doing this is because I want to give
my youth and energy to Jehovah God.
When I was at school,
I would conduct Bible studies
with some of my classmates.
In time, they joined me in serving Jehovah.
When I think about being with them in the future Paradise,
it gives me deep joy.
I have the privilege of studying with a deaf girl
who lives two hours from where I live.
We have to walk all the way.
She is very happy with what she’s learning,
and her family is very supportive.
So knowing that Jehovah is helping her
and I have a part in it, it’s just priceless.
Auxiliary pioneering definitely helped me
because it was like a stepping stone to regular pioneering.
The ministry definitely gives you the opportunity
to be able to work closely with Jehovah.
And then it— By doing that, you’re reaffirming
your faith in what you already believe in,
and then you’re drawing closer to Jehovah in friendship.
Having jw.org and the broadcast
has definitely drawn me closer to our brothers
and sisters but also to Jehovah as well.
Just by nature, I feel like I’m more of a timid person,
so going door to door can be a little scary.
But seeing other young ones in different parts of the world
that are enduring very difficult circumstances
and living conditions
and yet are still giving their best to Jehovah
is so encouraging for me.
And it helps me to keep going on and give Jehovah my best as well.
When I think personally about all the avenues of service
that we can have a hand in today,
there are so many that are exciting
—whether it be pioneering in a foreign country,
serving where the need is great,
even serving at Bethel.
Unless we “taste and see that Jehovah is good,”
unless we put ourself out there
and are available to try that at least once,
we’ll never know what it would be like
to really serve Jehovah.
And in doing that, you will see how Jehovah
does want the best life for us.

titles.ko: 청소년 여러분—‘여호와가 얼마나 선하신 분인지 맛보아 아십시오’
titles.en: Youths—"Taste and See That Jehovah Is Good"
titles.cn: 年轻人——“尝尝主恩，就知道耶和华良善”

en.text: People often tell me,
“Why, I never talked to a person
that was 107 years old.”
And I tell them, “You know what?
I never did either.”
I would describe Alma
as probably the most energetic
100-plus-year-old lady that I’ve ever met.
She has, pretty much,
the whole theocratic history in her mind that she carries with her.
So you can ask her anything about the organization,
and she can be able to tell you about it
because she’s even met a lot of those people.
We read about it, but she lived it. She’s amazing.
Even though she’s 107, she has an incredible memory.
I go back quite a ways.
When I was very young, ten years old,
we saw the “Photo-Drama of Creation.”
And it was just packed with people.
They were even standing in the back.
We were so thrilled. We never forgot it.
And we realized that we found the truth.
My father left the church
and he became one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
and they were called Bible Students at that time.
In the early days, we went to special conventions,
and some places, they had a big field
where they put the cars and they set up their tents.
They even named different streets.
It was just like a little city.
I was really thrilled to see Brother Rutherford speak
at the conventions I attended.
I got married to Harold Miller in 1931.
That was when the depression was going on,
and times were very difficult.
Everything was scarce.
There were no jobs to be had.
Food was rationed.
People were really hungry.
And they moved in any little shack
that they could just to get by.
We didn’t have anything.
And we couldn’t drive the car,
so we used to have a little white horse
—the name was Lou.
And we went out witnessing with the horse and buggy.
She took us all over the place, far distances.
They would take this buggy, and they would go
20-30 miles in one direction;
20-30 miles the other direction.
All the hard work that they put forth
has resulted in several congregations in the area.
We used to carry that magazine bag
when we were witnessing for awhile there.
And so we put it around the horse’s neck,
so the horse was taking part in our witnessing.
People knew who was coming when they saw
the little white horse come into their yard.
Sometimes it was cold,
and I remember wearing two coats.
Yeah, it was tiresome,
but we were young.
They would just go out regardless of rain or shine
or whatever was going on at the time, and they didn’t have a car.
And to me, that’s amazing because we get so used to
the conveniences —I guess you could call it—
the coffee breaks, the cars, and everything.
It’s like, well, if Alma can do it, surely I can do it.
One time, Harold went out witnessing,
and 50 years later, he talked to the same man.
He said, “50 years ago,
“there was a young guy that came through here
“riding on horseback
and telling people that,” he said,
“I think it’s ‘Armaggigon,’
he said was coming soon.”
And he remembered Harold riding horseback
50 years ago in that territory,
and he got there again.
And that happened a couple times more.
So it was a long life of witnessing.
Alma is so zealous for the ministry.
She does not like not-at-homes.
She wants to talk to people.
Yeah, I enjoy the ministry.
I go out as much as I can in my old age.
We want to help the people to see the truth.
There’s no greater joy.
I try to read the publications,
so I have a reading machine.
The letters come right out of the screen,
and I can study all my lessons.
I would be lost without it.
It helps me to keep up in present truth.
What does dedication mean?
Sister Miller, please.
Dedication means that. . .
Some young ones might be concerned about what they should do
with their life, what choices they should make.
Well, here we see an example of somebody who has served Jehovah
for over 100 years.
And we see that she’s happy and has no regrets with her life.
And that’s an example that we want to imitate.
Well, giving my life to Jehovah,
that’s the best thing I could do for myself.
If I have any advice for young ones today,
I would say to keep on in the truth.
They have a whole world before them
to serve Jehovah
—something that endures forever.

titles.en: Alma Miller: Serving Jehovah at 107 Years Old
titles.cn: 艾尔玛 · 米勒：在107岁的高龄事奉耶和华

en.text: Before the meeting starts, I need to get things ready.
I’m Ben.
And as a ministerial servant,
I can do a lot to help the congregation.
And that night I was given another assignment.
Brother Richards asked if I could help him update the territory maps
and organize our schedules for public witnessing.
I think the brothers know I can modernize all of this.
Brother Richards said to talk to Brother Bello, first.
He was the service overseer for years.
Great idea!
But I can already imagine the possibilities.
By that weekend, I had almost finished.
I couldn’t believe the outdated ways our records were kept.
This is going to be way better for the congregation.
And who knows what else could be improved?
I thought I had everything ready to show Brother Richards.
He liked the new ideas, but then he asked me,
“What did Brother Bello think?”
Oh, Brother Bello! I forgot.
I should have asked him,
but at this point, did it really matter?
Brother Richards suggested we read about Elisha.
When the older Elijah’s work was ending,
Elisha stuck close to his teacher.
Urged to stay behind, Elisha repeatedly said:
“As surely as Jehovah is living and as you are living,
I will not leave you.”
Until the moment Elijah left,
Elisha wanted to learn from him.
Like a son asking his father,
he wanted a double portion of Elijah’s spirit
to continue the work he started.
And Elisha’s first miracle
was the same as Elijah’s last:
dividing the Jordan with Elijah’s official garment.
Everything Elisha did revealed his respect
for the experienced man Elijah.
I wasn’t finished with my new assignment after all.
There was a lot I needed to learn from Brother Bello.
He really understood our preaching territory

en.text: My name is Irène Hof Laurenceau.
I studied medicine at the University of Zurich in Switzerland.
And afterward, I specialized in orthopedic surgery.
I didn’t believe in a Creator because I believed that the species
came into existence through evolution.
By comparing the anatomies of various organisms,
we recognize similarities.
To me, it was logical that there was a link
between these similarities;
that it indicated that we descend from a common ancestor.
After my studies in medicine,
I worked in hospitals in surgical departments.
In orthopedics —a large part of orthopedics
involves the insertion of prosthetics
to replace joints that are sick or no longer work.
Because the knee not only bends and straightens,
there is also a sliding movement,
a small rotation.
With a prosthetic knee, we cannot achieve
the complete mobility of a normal healthy knee.
If we see someone skating or dancing,
we have to believe that there is a designer
who is superior to us.
For a foot to function properly,
there has to be harmony between the joints,
the tendons, the muscles, and the nervous system.
It’s difficult to imagine
that it could be the result of evolution.
When someone came to my home to speak about the Bible,
I found the arguments in favor of creation more logical.
Also, I learned there are
renowned scientists who have doubts
themselves about the theory of evolution.
By studying the Bible,
I came to better know who God is.
It’s like food.
You have to taste it to know if it’s good.
Likewise, you have to study the Bible
to realize that what it says is true.

en.text: Welcome to our program!
Here are just a few of the things we can look forward to:
Can the lure of fame draw us away from Jehovah?
How does this brother feel about the decisions
he made as a young person?
What does his story teach us
about how to use our God-given abilities and talents?
Throughout the organization, young brothers and sisters are reaching out
to do more in Jehovah’s service.
Their spirituality and youthful energy
are helping to advance the Kingdom work.
But how is showing respect for experienced brothers
an important part of any theocratic assignment?
We’ll also hear from young brothers and sisters
from around the world.
Why is their relationship with Jehovah so important to them?
What do they do to build and maintain their spirituality?
And we’ll consider even more ways Christian youths
are setting a beautiful example for our worldwide brotherhood.
This is JW Broadcasting for December 2016!
During the past five years,
over 1.3 million faithful ones
have symbolized their dedication
to Jehovah by water baptism.
That’s an average of over 700 each day.
And among those courageously taking their stand
for true worship are thousands of children,
teenagers, and young adults.
Young brothers and sisters,
we know it is not always easy
to serve Jehovah and live up to your dedication.
Like older ones,
you need to be encouraged and strengthened spiritually.
With that in mind, our theme this month is
“Young Ones, ‘Become an Example to the Faithful Ones.’”
It is based on the inspiring true-life story
of a young Christian named Timothy.
Before we discuss Timothy’s example,
did you know that the Bible specifically foretold
that many young people would take sides with Jehovah in our time?
Let’s look at this at Psalm 110:3.
And as we read it together,
note how young ones are having a share in fulfilling this prophecy.
Notice the first part of verse 3,
David sang:
“Your people will offer themselves willingly
on the day of your military force.”
According to this prophecy, Jesus, the Messianic King,
would have a large army of willing supporters.
Since 1914, millions have carefully investigated the facts
and chosen to side with Jehovah God and Jesus Christ.
But where do young ones come into this picture?
The rest of the verse continues:
“In splendid holiness, from the womb of the dawn,
“you have your company of young men
just like dewdrops.”
Here, the prophecy refers to a “company,” or group, of young ones.
They also would study the evidence and support God’s Kingdom.
How many young people did Jehovah foresee
supporting true worship?
We get an idea by the comparison made to dewdrops.
Have you have ever gone outside early in the morning
and noticed a light, sparkling coating of water on the ground?
That may have been dew.
Jehovah designed our atmosphere so that, under certain conditions,
when the temperature cools during the night,
a blanket of moisture forms on the ground.
That coating is made up of a multitude of little drops.
Young ones, what does dew have to do with you?
In the Bible, dew is connected with blessing and abundance.
Dewdrops are also refreshing,
life-sustaining, and numerous.
Now, remember in Psalm 110:3,
Jehovah was looking ahead to our time.
And what did he see?
The September 15, 2002, Watchtower on page 8
explained it this way:
“Just like refreshing dewdrops,
“many young men and women cheerfully serve God
and assist their fellow worshipers.”
Today, there are so many mature,
bright, happy young ones in the Christian congregation
that they are like countless dewdrops that sparkle in the morning sun.
You faithful children, teenagers,
and young adults who have dedicated your life to Jehovah
or who are working toward that goal
are living proof that Jehovah’s confidence
in young people was never misplaced.
He cherishes you very much and so do we.
Of course, knowing that Jehovah has confidence in us
can be very encouraging.
But what if doubts or negative thoughts
tend to bring us down?
On occasion, a young Witness might wonder,
‘Does anyone other than Jehovah notice me?
Does my example really matter to others?’
To address these questions,
let’s now consider Timothy’s example.
Open your Bible, please,
to our theme text at 1 Timothy 4:12.
When you find it, you might want to bookmark the verse
because we want to first understand the setting.
How old was Timothy at this time?
Often, when thinking of Timothy,
I picture a teenager or a young man in his early twenties.
And when he first started traveling with Paul,
he was about that age.
But several years passed before Paul wrote letters to Timothy.
So by the time First Timothy was written,
Timothy was likely in his early thirties.
Now, what do you think?
Was Timothy young or old?
Some of you younger ones may be thinking to yourselves,
‘If he was over 30, then he was old!’
But remember, a much older man like Paul
would say that Timothy was quite young.
In fact, notice the expression he uses when writing to Timothy.
First Timothy 4:12, Paul says:
“Never let anyone look down on your youth.
“Instead, become an example to the faithful ones
“in speaking, in conduct, in love,
in faith, in chasteness.”
Paul called Timothy a youth and urged him to be a good example.
While Timothy may have been in his early thirties at this time,
remember that he was taught about Jehovah
from the time he was a baby,
and he did well in the truth as a young person.
In fact, when he was still a teenager or in his early twenties,
the elders recommended him to serve as a missionary with Paul.
So, in effect, Paul here is urging Timothy
to continue to be a good example for others.
What else do we know about Timothy?
He was not proud, or haughty.
He likely did not view himself as some amazing example.
I’m sure he never dreamed that one day Christians all over the world
would study his life in detail so as to imitate his faith.
Timothy was modest —and this despite his privileges.
Paul’s words may indicate that Timothy was somewhat shy.
Like many of us,
he may have battled with feelings of self-doubt on occasion.
Based on this information, let’s do something interesting now.
Let’s use our imagination to visualize Timothy,
an elder in his early thirties,
coming to give a Scriptural talk in the congregation.
Got the picture?
In your mind, please look at Timothy
and then look at the audience.
Who do we see?
Many in attendance are old enough
to be Timothy’s parents or grandparents.
How do you think Timothy felt?
Super confident?
Are you visualizing him proudly walking into the meeting place, saying:
“I sure wish my friends back in Lystra could see me now.
Look at the crowds that come to hear me speak!”
No, that’s not the Timothy we know.
It’s much more likely that Timothy, like most of us,
rehearsed his presentation over and over again.
He probably prayed constantly,
and he probably still got nervous, like all of us.
And remember, Timothy did not have the benefit
of theocratic schools like we do today.
In summary,
what can we say about Timothy?
Like so many of you,
he was an example of faith and obedience.
He was exceptional in displaying Christian qualities,
such as modesty and humility.
But Timothy was a person with normal human feelings,
like all of us.
Though he had a rich, happy life in Jehovah’s service,
life in the old world brought real tests and challenges.
Timothy also dealt with frequent cases of sickness,
and he was imprisoned for a time.
Some of you in various countries
can relate to those bitter experiences.
But Timothy endured.
Was he some “super Christian” with superpowers?
No, but he did prove to be a super example!
How does all of this help you Christian youths
who have taken the commendable step
to dedicate your lives to Jehovah?
We just read how Paul told Timothy to let no one look down on his youth.
A few of you may be thinking,
‘I wish someone would tell my parents
‘or my elders not to look down on me.
They still treat me like a little kid.’
If that’s the case, we feel for you.
No progressive young one wants to be treated as if he were a child.
But let’s look again at 1 Timothy 4:12.
Is the apostle Paul speaking to the congregation,
to parents, or to the elders?
“Never let anyone look down
“on your youth.
“Instead, become an example to the faithful ones in speaking,
in conduct, in love, in faith, in chasteness.”
It’s clear, isn’t it?
Paul said your youth.
He was speaking only to Timothy.
Young ones, by extension, what is Jehovah saying to each of you?
It’s this: To gain and maintain the respect of faithful ones,
you have to work at proving yourself as a Christian.
The key is not wanting or hoping that others will respect you.
Rather, it’s earning such respect by setting a good example
in all areas of life.
If you do that,
then no one will have any legitimate reason to look down on your youth.
Doesn’t it make sense that we gain respect by earning it?
We are confident that you young ones are trying hard
to live by Christian principles at school and in the neighborhood.
But in verse 12, did you notice who Timothy was to be an example to?
To “the faithful ones.”
Are you an example to Christians, both younger and older,
in your congregation and in your circuit?
If you work on Kingdom Hall construction projects or at Bethel,
are you an example to your fellow workers?
Well, what are some specific ways you can become an example
to all of these “faithful ones”?
In our theme text, Timothy was first directed
to become an example in speaking.
On this topic, I’ll never forget an illustration
used in the “Young People Ask” article from the January 2012 Awake!
It quoted a young man, James, who said:
“Once you squeeze toothpaste out, you can’t put it back in the tube.
“The same is true with our words.
Once we say something hurtful, we can’t take it back.”
God’s Word agrees with James.
Note what it says at Ephesians 4:29.
It tells us:
“Let a rotten word not come out of your mouth,
“but only what is good for building up as the need may be,
to impart what is beneficial to the hearers.”
For some years now, those getting baptized
have been encouraged to complete a study of the book,
“Keep Yourselves in God’s Love.”
Chapter 12 is entitled “Speak What ‘Is Good for Building Up.’”
On page 140, there is a box with five questions
that can help us evaluate our speech.
For example:
“When was the last time I offered someone specific commendation?
“Do I express my respect for others by saying please and thank you?
“In conversation, do I speak mainly about myself,
or am I also interested in the thoughts and feelings of others?”
Young ones, over the next few days,
why not review that box on page 140, look up the scriptures,
and think about what Jehovah is saying?
Then apply what you learn to your speech.
Doing this will draw you closer to Jehovah
and help you to become an even better example
to the faithful ones.
The second area mentioned in our theme text
is becoming an example in conduct.
Of course, upbuilding speech would be empty
or hypocritical if our conduct was questionable.
Think again about Timothy.
It wasn’t enough for him to give comments and talks at the meetings
or preach from door to door.
Later in the same letter, Paul reminded Timothy
that he needed to treat older men and women as fathers and mothers;
younger men and women were to be treated as brothers and sisters.
Second Peter 3:11
provides a similar urgent reminder about our conduct.
Let’s read that together.
Again, that’s 2 Peter 3:11.
There it tells us:
“Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way,

Of course not!

Similarly, Jehovah expects his servants
to be clean through and through.
And because Jehovah —the perfect reader of hearts—
will soon dissolve, yes, eliminate this dirty system of things,
it’s urgent that we do so.
This means that we have to work very hard
so that nothing unclean enters our mind.

so-called fun and exciting entertainment,

any experience with the wickedness of this world.

our mind and heart, clean at all times.

pleases Jehovah and it strengthens our faithful brothers and sisters.

and to gain the respect of others.

Numbers chapter 13, and look at verse 33.
