이렇게 또 뵈니까 정말 좋네요. 잘 오셨어요.
어제 마트에서 필요한 물건 사다 줘서 정말 고마워요.
우리 자매가 고맙다고 꼭 인사 전해 달래요.
존, 정말 잘 왔어요. 우리 계속 봐요.
다들 저한테만 아니라 서로에게도 정말 친절하신 것 같아요.
말 따로 행동 따로가 아닌 것 같네요.
저흰 그 명령에 따르려고 최선을 다하는 거죠.
하지만 계속 와 보시면, 저희도 불완전하단 걸 느끼실 거예요.
그래도, 지금까지 와 보니까, 전에 말씀하신 성경 공부를 해 보고 싶네요.
형제 자매 여러분, 이제 곧 집회가 시작될 겁니다.
이제 집회 시작하는 거 같으니까 끝나고 마저 얘기하죠.

en.text: I am so tired.
I’m really not up to talking to anyone tonight.
All I want to do is just find my seat
and enjoy the meeting.
I know Jehovah will understand if I just . . .
Joanne! I am so glad to see you!
I could really use your help with preparing for my next Bible study with Lori.
Well, actually, you know, I was trying to just get to my . . .
OK, so let me tell you . . .
Wow, she didn’t even hear me.
I don’t need this right now.
This is really trying my patience.
. . . not saying a word.
But how many times was Jesus
interrupted when he was tired?
“Love is patient and kind.”
Let me listen closely to what she has to say.
That’s when I remembered what you told me.
Really? What did I say?
Remember, you said, “Always be patient and kind.”
So I kindly pointed out the key words in the scripture,
and then after asking her the question again,
I patiently waited for her to give me an answer
—which, by the way, is not the easiest thing for me to do.
But, just when I thought that I couldn’t wait any longer,
she gave me the right answer.
She got the point! I was so excited!
But now I’m kind of wondering,
‘Does she really believe what she said?
And if not, how am I going to help her to see the truth of the matter?’
And that’s where I need your help, Joanne.
I’ve been trying to look for articles; I can’t find anything.
Joanne, can you please help me with finding an article
on how to reason with a Bible student?
Angela, of course, I’d be glad to help you.
Um, could we get together, maybe, tomorrow afternoon?
Thank you so much, Joanne, for being willing to help me.
I really appreciate it.
Thank you.
Bill.
Carl, how are you?
Good. How are you feeling?
Good.
Awesome. Alex . . .
Hey.
I didn’t get a chance to tell you last week,
but that was a really nice job you did on your talk.
Yeah, good job.
Ah, thanks, guys!
Believe me, I’ve been so busy
it was hard to make time to prepare it.
Oh, tell me about it!
I think the whole congregation has had a lot going on lately.
Yeah, it has.
That’s true, but I think I’ve been extra busy.
Why? What’s going on?
You’re not sick, are you?
No, no, it’s nothing like that.
It’s all this theocratic stuff
—pioneering, congregation duties,
and other things.
Like this Saturday, I need to be at the Kingdom Hall all afternoon and . . .
Saturday? Here?
Why?
Wait a second, I see where this is going.
Isn’t there a circuit assembly rehearsal here on Saturday?
Oh yeah, that’s right.
So you’re on the program?
Well, I’m not sure if I’m supposed to say.
Well, you just did.
So, what is it? You’re in a demonstration?
An interview? You can’t just leave us hanging!
OK.
Well, it’s not just an interview.
It’s an interview with a reenactment,
and then they are going to ask me questions at the end.
I’m actually on stage for most of the part.
Come to think of it, guys, I am the part!
You are the part?
Are you sure you’re not stretching that a little bit?
No, I don’t think I am.
OK. Brother Jones’ part is ten minutes;
I’m up there for six.
That’s more than half the part.
Anyway, so let me tell you how it’s supposed to go:
They are going to ask me about the time I did this amazing job out in field service.
I walk up to the door. Of course, I ring the bell.
But what happens? It doesn’t work.
I knock louder than any man ever has.
Bill.
Carl, how are you?
Good. How are you feeling?
Good.
Awesome. Alex . . .
Hey.
I didn’t get a chance to tell you last week,
but that was a really nice job you did on your talk.
Yeah, good job.
Thanks, guys!
With Jehovah’s help, it came together.
Believe me, I’ve been so busy.
It was just . . . It was hard to make time to prepare it.
Oh, tell me about it!
I think the whole congregation has had a lot going on lately.
Yeah, it has.
You both would know. Aren’t you both auxiliary pioneering?
How’s that going?
It’s going.
Actually, yesterday I was able to show one of our jw.org videos to a man.
He said that I can come back this Saturday.
I think he might even agree to a study.
You want to come with me, Alex?
You know, I’m sorry.
I’m going to be tied up for most of this Saturday.
But maybe Bill can go with you.
How about it, Bill?
Sure. I have a call to make too.
Maybe we can do both calls together.
All right, deal.
So, Bill, you have a good call too?
Tell us about it.
Oh, yes, well I met a man . . .
Brother Harris, do you have a moment?
Sure, Faye, how can we help you?
Well, you probably heard by now,
David and I got engaged this past weekend!
We heard.
Congratulations!
We’re so happy for both of you.
Thanks so much!
And since this is where I grew up,
it would mean a lot to us if we could get married in this Kingdom Hall.
So we were hoping that since you’re the coordinator of the body of elders,
you’d be able to let us know today if we can use the hall.
Then David and I can start working on our wedding invitations.
David asked me to give you this letter making our official request.
OK.
OK.
Let’s take a look.
Oh, yeah, this is a good letter.
This gives me all the information I need.
Faye, I can’t imagine you getting married anywhere else.
You can count on using the Kingdom Hall.
I’ll let the elders know that I have already given my approval.
Let David know we’re looking forward to your big day.
Thanks so much, Brother Harris!
I knew you’d come through for me!
Brother Harris, do you have a moment?
Sure, Faye, how can we help you?
Well, you probably heard by now,
David and I got engaged this past weekend!
We heard.
Congratulations!
We’re so happy for both of you.
Thanks so much!
And since this is where I grew up,
it would mean a lot to us if we could get married in this Kingdom Hall.
So we were hoping that since you’re the coordinator of the body of elders,
you’d be able to let us know today if we can use the hall.
Then David and I can start working on our wedding invitations.
David asked me to give you this letter making our official request.
OK.
OK.
Yes, this is a good letter.
This has all the information that we need.
I’m going to check with the other elders and we’re going to discuss it,
then we’ll get right back to you.
Oh, you mean you can’t tell me right now?
I thought that since you’re the coordinator,
you’d have the authority to —you know . . .
I understand.
But, there is a theocratic arrangement
that we all have to follow, even the elders.
And the arrangement is for the entire service committee
to discuss this and to consider the matter thoroughly
before any approval can be given.
So I don’t have the authority to make a decision on my own.
Of course, that makes sense.
I understand.
But don’t worry, Faye, we’re going to get on this as soon as possible.
Then you can move forward with your wedding plans.
Thank you so much, Brother Harris.
I really appreciate it.
You’re welcome.
I’m going to get started right on this.
OK. Thanks.
Excuse me,
Larry, Frank.
Have either of you seen Kevin tonight?
Yes, he’s over by the literature counter.
OK.
I can go get him if you’d like.
Ah, that would be great. Thank you very much.
Larry, perhaps you’ve heard
that Faye Carter and David Thomas
have recently gotten engaged.
Uh-huh.
And they want to use the Kingdom Hall for their wedding.
So perhaps you and Kevin and myself
we could get together for a few minutes tonight,
and then they could move forward with their wedding plans.
Tonight?
How many times are you going to do this to us, Tom?
Do what?
Keep having these unscheduled meetings.
Look,
maybe you’re not so eager to get home and spend time with your family,
but some of us are.
‘Not want to spend time with my family!’
What is that supposed to mean?
He is way out of line.
I should set him straight right now.
No, wait.
What am I thinking?
If I react poorly right now,
I could cause a major rift between us
—even between our families.
And if we elders don’t show love among ourselves,
imagine how this could affect the congregation.
What a dishonor that would be to Jehovah and Jesus!
What do the Scriptures say?
“Do not leave your place.”
“Love . . . does not become provoked.”
Uh, you’re right, Larry.
Um, I’m sorry, I just thought that maybe it would take a few minutes.
But, uh, we can schedule a better time for this,
and that way we can all get home earlier.
No, Tom,
it’s me who needs to apologize.
I overreacted.
Look, you’re right.
Since all of us are here,
it would be good for us to take care of this if we can.
OK.
OK.
Here comes Kevin.
Let’s see if he’s available.
OK.
Hey, Kevin, good to see you.
Good to see you too.
Excuse me.
Um, Larry, Frank . . .
We had such a good time this morning.
I always enjoy working with you in service.
Same here.
And I hope Ms. Johnson comes to the meeting this Sunday.
That would be so nice.
Hey, did you ever find your sunglasses?
No. I looked all over!
I have no idea where they could be.
Hey.
Hey, Susan.
Good to see you.
Good to see you.
You left these at my house last night.
Ah, can you believe it? I should have known.
What?
Susan had another gathering at her home last night,
and I wasn’t invited —again!
I just don’t get it.
I knew they had to be yours.
Thanks again.
I’m always leaving my stuff behind.
And, Helen, how are you doing?
I’m fine. Sorry, I gotta go.
Helen?
What just happened?
I have no idea.
Hey, Helen, got a second?
What do you want, Susan?
Helen,
I feel like I must have done something to hurt you,
and I want to apologize if I have.
Is there something wrong?
I guess you had some more of the friends over last night?
Well, yes, a few.
Do you mind telling me why I’m never invited?
Helen, I’m sorry; I never thought—
Never thought what?
That I would have noticed how many times you’ve done this to me?
Well, I’ve noticed!
Yesterday makes the third time
in the last couple of months
you’ve had people to your home without me.
Not to mention the four other times earlier this year!
I’m so sorry, Helen.
I didn’t mean to slight you in any way.
And I promise, it was nothing personal.
“Nothing personal?”
How can you invite everybody in the congregation
over to your home for a good time
—except me—
and say that it’s “nothing personal”?
Good evening, brothers and sisters.
We invite you to please find your seats.
Our meeting is about to begin.
Excuse me.
Um, Larry, Frank . . .
We had such a good time this morning.
I always enjoy working with you in service.
Same here.
And I hope Ms. Johnson comes to the meeting this Sunday.
That would be so nice.
Hey, did you ever find your sunglasses?
No. I looked all over!
I have no idea where they could be.
Hey.
Hey, Susan.
Good to see you.
Good to see you.
You left these at my house last night.
Ah, can you believe it?
I should have known.
Thank you so much, Susan.
Where were they?
Wow.
Susan had another gathering at her home.
I wonder why I wasn’t invited again?
Wait. That’s not important.
She is so hospitable!
I’m going to pray that Jehovah continues to bless her for it.
And maybe there’s something I can do.
And, Helen, how are you doing?
Fine. How are you, Susan?
Great.
Hey, would you and you too, Alice,
would you like to work together in service this Saturday
and then come to my house for lunch?
That sounds so nice!
Would I like to? I would love to.
Thank you, Helen!
What can I bring?
Both of you just bring yourselves; I’ll have everything ready.
Oh, that sounds good!
Oh, I got to go.
Oh, Alice!
Oh, hi, Debbie.
I’ve got to tell you what I just heard yesterday.
Well, . . .
Remember Bethany, who used to attend some of our meetings years ago?
Yes, has she started going back to the meetings again?
Not at all.
She left the man that she was living with
to move in with another!
Wait! You’ve been keeping in touch with her?
Well, no, I haven’t talked to her directly,
but, you know, word gets around.
Anyway, can you believe it?
Debbie, we both know that Bethany has done a lot of bad things
since she stopped attending the meetings.
And I really hope she makes changes and comes back.
But in the meantime,
do you really think we should be spending our time
talking about all the bad things she’s doing right now?
Well, probably not.
I just figured that since we all grew up together,
you’d want to know how far from the truth she has gotten.
But, Debbie,
“love . . . does not rejoice over unrighteousness,
but rejoices with the truth.”
You know what?
You’re right. Why talk about this?
We have so many good things to talk about.
Yes, we do, like this morning.
Do you remember that call we went on last week?
Well, Helen and I went back again this morning,
and the lady was home!
She invited us in, and we placed a book.
Really!
Yes!
We even got to show her one of our videos,
and she said she may come to the meeting this Sunday!
That’s wonderful! I hope she . . .
Alice, Alice.
Oh, hi, Debbie.
Wow, Brother Green,
I didn’t know it was that bad.
The storm was far worse than expected.
I had already followed the order to evacuate the city,
but I had no idea I’d never see my home again.
My wife had passed away a few years before the disaster,
and I didn’t have any family to stay with.
So I really didn’t have anything to go back to.
So, what did you do next?
Next?
Next, I learned what real love is all about.
Wow, they took all of you into their home?
Yes, six of us.
It wasn’t easy sometimes for any of us.
But in the end,
we knew
we could get through anything together
because
“love . . . endures all things.”
Hey, John, nice to see you again.
Hey, if you don’t have a seat already, we’d love to have you join us.
Thanks.
This is what, . . . your fourth time here?
Yeah, yeah, I’ve just . . .
I’ve never seen anything like this before.
Like what?
Hello, John.
I just wanted to say hi
and tell you how glad I am to see you here.
Thank you, Sir. Nice to see you too.
And, Jimmy, . . .
Hi, Brother Thompson.
I want to thank you so much
for that package you dropped off yesterday.
Chloe and I really appreciate your thoughtfulness.
Anytime, Brother Thompson, anytime.
Sorry, don’t mean to interrupt.
Just wanted to come over and say hello to you both.
John, really nice to see you here.
Please keep coming.
Thanks. I will.
And, Jim, as always, good to see you.
Same here, Gary.
We’re still on for tomorrow, right?
I’m counting on it. Six o’clock?
That’s right.
Great. I’ll see you then.
Now, where were we?
Well, I was about to say how friendly everyone is here!
And it’s not just with me. I mean, it’s with each other.
You people really practice what you preach.
Well, thanks, John.
You know, Jesus said for us to ‘have love among ourselves.’
And we really try our best to follow that command.
Of course, if you keep coming, you’ll see we’re not perfect.
Well, I think I’ve seen enough to know that I’m ready
for that Bible study you’ve been offering me.
Oh, that’s great, John.
Good evening, brothers and sisters.
You know, let’s take our seats,
and we’ll talk more about the Bible study after the meeting.
OK.

titles.cn: 要“彼此相爱”

title: 폭풍이 다가오고 있는 지금, 예수께 계속 초점을 맞추십시오!—앞으로 왕국이 가져올 축복

ko.text: 한 번의 반역 행위로 인해, 인류는 길을 잃고
그 결과, 이 땅에 태어난 사람은
아무도 죄와 죽음에서 벗어날 수 없었습니다.
그분은 하느님이 주신 능력으로 사람들의 병을 고쳐 주셨고,
예수께서 이 땅에서 행하신 많은 기적은
그러한 기적은 앞으로 훨씬 더 큰 규모로 일어날
놀라운 일들을 미리 보여 주는 것입니다.
하느님께서는 자신을 충실히 섬기는 모든 사람에게
우리가 이처럼 아름다운 미래를 누리는 것이
예수께서 우리를 위해 하신 일 덕분입니다.
그분이 이 땅에 오신 데는 중요한 목적이 있었습니다.
유전받은 죄와 죽음의 저주에서 풀려날 수 있게 되었습니다.
우리는 더 이상 길을 잃고 헤매지 않을 것입니다.
그분이 우리에게 ‘아버지께로’ 가는 길을 알려 주실 것입니다.

en.text: With one act of defiance,
mankind became lost,
“alienated from the life that belongs to God.”
Sin and death have become inescapable
for every human born on earth,
with the exception of one—Jesus Christ.
He used his God-given powers to heal sicknesses,
feed thousands
—he even resurrected people back to life.
Jesus performed many miracles while on earth.
But are they simply a collection of stories from the past
or clues to something far grander
—a glimpse into a wondrous future,
a future where God will “satisfy the desire of every living thing,”
the “real life” that God promises
to each of his faithful servants?
But how can this beautiful future be possible?
Because of what Jesus did for us.
He came to earth for a purpose.
He gave his life for those he loved.
The curse of inherited sin and death could now be lifted
from each one of us.
If we look intently to Jesus, we will no longer be lost.
He will show us the way “to the Father.”

cn.text: 由于一个反叛的行动
人类迷失了方向
跟上帝所赐的生命疏远
从此地上的每个人
都摆脱不了罪和死亡
除了一个人
耶稣基督
他用上帝给他的力量
医治病人
喂饱了数千人
他甚至复活死去的人
耶稣在地上施行了许多奇迹
但这只是过去的事吗？
还是预示着一个极其美好的前景
一个奇妙的未来？
上帝会满足众生的愿望
上帝会实现应许
赐给他的忠仆真正的生命
怎么可能有这么美好的未来呢？
因为耶稣为我们所做的一切
他肩负使命来到地上
他为自己所爱的人献出生命
我们每个人
就可以从遗传的罪和死亡中
解救出来
我们定睛注视耶稣
就不再迷失方向
他会指明道路
领我们到父亲那里去

ko.text: 학교에서 여호와의 증인인 걸 밝히지 않았어요.
애들이 나에 대해 뭐라고 말할지 두려웠거든요.
주변 사람들에게 압력을 받는 건 정말 힘든 일이에요.
친구들만 아니라 선생님도 그런 압력을 주시죠.
새로 생긴 기독교 모임에 가입한 친구 몇 명이
여호와의 증인에 대해 나쁜 소문을 내고 다녔어요.
걔네들은 우리가 정체 모를 교주를 따른다고 말했죠.
나는 질이 나쁜 애들이랑 어울리기 시작했어요.
한번은 애들이 학교 끝나고 나가서 놀자고 했죠.
가선 안 된다는 생각이 들었지만 결국 같이 갔어요.
근데 갑자기 젊은 남자 두 명이 나타나더니
우리랑 같이 간 남자애들하고 그 사람들하고 싸움이 붙었죠.
곧 주먹이 오가기 시작했고 경찰이 왔어요.
문제가 커지겠다는 생각에 덜컥 겁이 나서 얼른 도망쳤죠.
선생님이 종교들을 전부 나쁘게 말씀하신 적이 있었어요.
“하느님이 있다는 걸 어떻게 알 수 있니?
성경은 사람들이 수도 없이 고쳐 썼는데
어떻게 진리라고 할 수 있니?” 라고 하셨죠.
나는 뭔가 말을 해야겠다고 생각하기는 했어요.
근데 갑자기 어떤 애가 내가 여호와의 증인이라고 말했어요.
선생님은 놀라시면서 나에게 할 말이 있냐고 하셨죠.
어떻게 해야 할지 몰라 그냥 서 있었어요.
베드로가 어떤 기분이었을지 알 것 같았어요.
그런 애들과 어울리는 걸 여호와께서 싫어하시니까요.
사람들 앞에서 내 입장을 설명해야 한다고 생각하니까
몸이 굳어 버려 입이 떨어지지 않았어요.
여호와의 증인인 걸 밝힐 수 있게 용기를 달라고 했어요.
한 형제가 연설에서 마가복음 8:38을 언급하셨던 게 기억났어요.
그 성구에서는 우리가 예수를 따르는 걸 부끄럽게 여기면
그분도 우리를 부끄럽게 여기실 거라고 알려 주죠.
그 말씀이 정말 마음에 와 닿았고

en.text: I didn’t identify myself
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
because I was scared of what kids
at school would say about me.
Peer pressure is probably the worst challenge
because you don’t just get
peer pressure from friends,
but you also get it from your teachers.
Some of my friends
who joined this new Christian group
started spreading false rumors
about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Many of them said we were led
by some unknown leader at the top.
At first, I wanted
to stand up and say, “Well, that’s not true!”
However,
I started to become fearful.
I was hanging out with the wrong crowd,
and girls invited me to go play
in the park after school.
Something kind of told me
that I shouldn’t have gone with them,
but I still went.
Out of nowhere, I see two young men come,
and they tried to steal our backpacks.
They started arguing with the boys in our group,
and they started fighting too.
The police came,
and when I saw the police,
I thought I was going to get into a lot of trouble,
so I just ran away.
One time, the teacher at school was mocking
all religions saying: “The Bible is outdated,”
and “How can you know that God exists?
“People have rewritten it so many times.
How can you know it’s the truth?”
And I remember thinking to myself,
‘I should say something.’
I did this the night before, ‘I should say something.’
And then my friend next to me said,
“Bianca is a Jehovah’s Witness.”
The teacher looked at me wide-eyed
and said, “Do you have anything to say?”
And I just stood there.
I didn’t know what to say, and then the bell rang,
and I was just relieved.
I felt how I imagine
Peter would have felt.
My conscience kept bothering me,
and I knew that Jehovah
didn’t approve of my association.
The fact that I had to open my mouth
and kind of prove myself
made me just cramp up inside,
and I felt very disappointed in myself.
I said a prayer to Jehovah,
and I asked him to give me courage
to stand up and say
that I was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I remember a brother who gave a talk once,
and he cited from the words
of Mark 8:38, where it says
that we shouldn’t be ashamed of following Jesus
because he would be ashamed of us.
Those words really touched my heart,
and I knew that I had to make changes soon.
After I had considered the example of Jesus,
I prayed to Jehovah
for courage and also for another opportunity
to defend his name.
Talking to Mum was probably the biggest help.
Her experience
and her knowledge kind of helped
to give me the courage to keep going.
Identifying myself as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
has served as a protection.
In biology class,
we were talking about the topic of blood,
and my teacher made the comment
that those JW people will let their kids die.
I said a really quick prayer to Jehovah
because I knew that was not the truth.
So I stood up, and I said,
“We’re called Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and we don’t allow our kids to die.”
I was so happy after that moment.
I was able to give a witness
when my schoolmates started asking me
about what we really believe and practice.
I was able to give them
a much more accurate understanding
of how our organization functions.
Now that I’m able to stand firm in my beliefs,
I feel much better.
You’re doing it for Jehovah,
and you’re doing it for yourself.
You’re not doing it to make them happy;
you’re doing it to make Jehovah happy.
When I feel scared or afraid,
I say a quick prayer to Jehovah,
and he gives me the courage
to defend my faith and keep going.
I have gained the respect
and admiration of my schoolmates.
I’m not ashamed anymore of identifying myself
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Now I’m proud to represent Jehovah.

ko.text: 독신으로 지내면 자신보다 남에게 더 관심을 쏟을 수 있어요.
독신이라 시간이 더 많고 더 자유롭기 때문에
정규 파이오니아라는 목표에 도달하기가 더 유리했죠.
제가 독신 생활을 선물로 여기는 이유는
봉사를 더 다양하게, 더 집중해서 할 기회가 많아서죠.
개인 연구와 봉사를 더 할 수 있죠.
친구나 다른 사람들에게 시간을 더 낼 수 있어요.
여호와를 위해 올바로 사용한다면 독신은 분명히 선물이에요.
살면서 어떤 시기나 어떤 나이가 되면
사람들이, 심지어 형제 자매들도 좀 안됐다는 듯이 쳐다볼 때가 있어요.
그러면 하고 있는 일에서 주의가 약간 흐트러지죠.
저는 독신을 지키려고 영화를 신중하게 선택해요.
부부보다는 독신이 예수를 밀접히 따르기가 더 쉬운 것 같아요.
왜냐하면 예수의 생활을 곰곰이 생각해 보면,
그분은 언제라도 사람들을 돕고 가르치실 수 있었고,
예수께서는 아주 바쁘게 봉사하셨고, 그 일에 전념하셨어요.
봉사를 하면서 여호와를 더 온전히 섬기는 데
힘과 노력을 더 집중할 수 있어요.
중요한 건 그냥 독신으로 지내는 게 아니라,
독신으로 살면서 어떻게 여호와의 마련을 지원하느냐죠.
독신이라면 현재 주어진 환경에서 뭐든 할 수 있는 걸 해야죠.
현재 갖가지 형태로 여호와를 섬기는 데
이제는 자매들을 포함하여 독신들에게 기회가 아주 많지요.
다른 나라로 이주하거나 베델에서 봉사할 수 있어요.
이런 기회가 있는 지금, 시간을 잘 사용하세요.

en.text: Being single can help you focus more on other people
rather than concentrating on yourself.
Being single, having more time, more flexibility
really helped me to attain this goal
which was regular pioneering.
I view singleness as a gift
because it opens up opportunities
to serve in a more focused
and more flexible way.
You can study more
and have more time in the field ministry.
You have more time for the friends.
You’re more available.
Singleness definitely is a gift
if it’s used in the right way for Jehovah.
Singleness has not always been easy.
Sometimes there comes a period in life,
a certain age, where people start to ask,
“Anja, did you find somebody?
Are you not yet married?”
And that’s not always easy.
Sometimes people look at you, even brothers and sisters,
and feel a bit of pity for you maybe because you’re still single.
That sort of draws your attention away from what you are doing.
That sometimes can be difficult.
I think I guard my singleness in the sense
that I look out for what kind of movies I watch
—not too romantic because it’s easy
to fall into this type of thinking.
So I’ve also always made sure that I associate
with a range of brothers and sisters from different age groups
but ones that have similar sorts of goals
and they have a very positive outlook.
Following Jesus closely as a single person,
I think, is easier than as a couple
because if we reflect on Jesus’ life
—early to rise, late to bed,
fully focused on the ministry, on his Father
—that, I think, is easier for a single person.
He was available to help others, he was available to teach others,
even for children he was available for them to give comfort.
Jesus was so busy in his ministry and was focused.
And when you’re single, you’re able to do that.
You’re able to concentrate more of your energy
and effort into the ministry,
into serving Jehovah more fully.
It’s not a matter of just being single;
it’s a matter of how you use it
to support Jehovah’s arrangement.
It doesn’t matter whatever age we are,
if we are single,
use the circumstances that you’ve got at the moment
to do whatever you can
because we’re just living in a momentous time.
There is so much work for us to do.
Just go and pioneer
or do something for Jehovah,
and wait for him to surprise you.
You can use this time
to do all sorts of different things in Jehovah’s service at the moment,
there are so many opportunities opened up for single ones,
including single sisters, now
—going where the need is greater,
moving to different countries, serving in Bethel.
So while you’ve got these circumstances,
use the time now because it’s wonderful.

en.text: Tim, thanks for reading all the Appendix
“1914—A Significant Year in Bible Prophecy.”
You understood it, right?
Well, it’s not completely clear.
OK, well, let’s go through it again.
If you remember, Luke 21:24,
said that Jersusalem would “be trampled on by the nations
until the appointed times of the nations are fulfilled.”
Now, we know that began in 607 B.C.E.,
and at Daniel 4:16,
it said that seven times would have to pass over it,
and at Revelation 12: 6, 14,
it indicates that three and a half times
equals 1,260 days;
so seven times would be 2,520 days,
but of course, we got the Bible principle
at Numbers 14:34,
“a day for a year, a day for a year.”
So that 2,520 days would be
2,520 years.
So counting 2,520 years
from 607 B.C.E.
brings us to 1914
when Jesus began to rule as king in the heavens.
You got it now.
Um, it’s still not clear.
That’s OK,
I didn’t understand it the first time I went through it.
Just read the Appendix
a few more times,
and it will make sense.
Come on, let’s finish our study of chapter 8.
So based on what we’ve been learning in chapter 8,
can you think of a good reason why it’s so important
that we know when God’s Kingdom began to rule?
Well, I think that if you knew when God’s Kingdom began to rule,
then you would know
that the blessings of the Kingdom are soon to follow.
That’s an excellent answer.
Of course, the Appendix here contains the scriptural proof
of when God’s Kingdom began to rule in 1914.
Would you like to read
just the first two paragraphs in the Appendix there,
under the heading on page 215,
“1914-A Significant Year in Bible Prophecy.”
Sure. “Decades in advance, Bible students . . .”
Thank you.
So notice there that Jesus said that the city of Jerusalem
would be “trampled on by the nations
until the appointed times of the nations are fulfilled.”
Now for us to understand Jesus’ words,
we have to know, Why was Jerusalem special?
What did Jersusalem symbolize?
So, what did we learn about Jerusalem there in paragraph 2?
Um, well, Jerusalem was where the Jewish kings ruled, right?
So they would have ruled for Jehovah,
which meant that Jerusalem was a symbol of Jehovah’s rulership.
Very good.
Now you have the key
to understanding when Jesus began to rule as king.
Wow, this is really interesting.
It’s like solving a mystery.
Isn’t it? Let’s read the next paragraph.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Isaiah.
Isaiah served as Jehovah’s prophet.
He wrote the book bearing his name while stationed in Jerusalem,
the capital of the two-tribe kingdom of Judah.
Isaiah had two sons
—Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
Their names signified events
that would soon affect the kingdom of Judah.
Isaiah prophesied for at least 46 years
during the reigns of Judean kings
Uzziah, Jotham,
Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
He completed the book
sometime after 732 B.C.E.
Hosea and Micah recorded their prophecies
around the same time.
Some of the events foretold by Isaiah
were the fall of the northern kingdom of Israel,
which occurred in Isaiah’s lifetime;
the destruction of Jerusalem,
which happened more than 100 years later;
the fall of Babylon,
about 200 years after Isaiah’s day;
and the appearance of the Messiah,
which occurred over 700 years
after the prophecy was recorded.
Did you know?
Isaiah’s prophecy about the fall of Babylon
foretold details such as how the city would fall
and even the name of its conqueror, Cyrus.
The book of Isaiah contains 66 chapters.
The first six chapters are largely warnings
about the calamity that was to come upon Jerusalem and Judah
for the sinful conduct of their inhabitants.
In chapter 6,
Isaiah responds to Jehovah’s invitation
to be His messenger
and shows his willing spirit with the words:
“Here I am! Send me!”
Chapters 7 to 12 deal with the threat of enemy invasion
from the combined forces of Syria
and the northern ten-tribe kingdom of Israel.
But, in fulfillment of Isaiah’s prophecy,
Assyria defeated these two nations,
removing the threat.
Chapters 13 to 23 include pronouncements
against Babylon and other nations
for their cruelty to God’s people.
Chapters 24 to 35
contain messages of desolation
and of restoration for Jehovah’s people.
Among their acts of unfaithfulness,
the people of Judah
turned to Assyria for protection
instead of looking to Jehovah.
The people of Israel turned to Egypt.
In chapters 36 to 39,
we read about thrilling events that occurred
during King Hezekiah’s reign.
The Assyrian King Sennacherib
invades Judah
and threatens to destroy Jerusalem if the city does not surrender.
Hezekiah prays to Jehovah for deliverance.
Jehovah reassured Hezekiah that Jerusalem would be safe
and then miraculously delivered His people by sending an angel
who destroyed 185,000 Assyrian warriors
in just one night.
Despite this deliverance,
Judah’s sins would eventually lead
to Jerusalem’s destruction
and the Jews’ exile in Babylon.
In chapters 40 to 66,
Jehovah comforts his people
and promises to restore true worship to Jerusalem
after they return from exile.
You will notice that often Isaiah’s prophecy
focuses on God’s Kingdom,
in which the Messiah rules
and restores true worship forever.
Isaiah foretold many details about the Messiah,
for example, that he would be born of a virgin,
come from the family line of David,
reside in Galilee,
and cure the sick.
Jesus Christ and his apostles
quoted Isaiah’s prophecy more than any other
to make clear the identification of the Messiah.
Jesus even read Isaiah 61:1, 2
in the synagogue in Nazareth
and applied the words to himself.
As you read the book of Isaiah,
note how Jehovah’s prophetic judgments
always come true,
how Jehovah provides salvation
for those who trust him,
and how the foretold reign of the Messiah
will bring everlasting peace to the earth.

en.text: Nurdup is a small island about 10 to 15 minutes by boat
from the Panama mainland.
Life on these islands is simple,
though this one in particular is special.
Even though the island only has 24 inhabitants,
7 of them, along with 5 from other islands,
attend the only congregation
of Jehovah’s Witnesses in the region.
Buna Tejada is one of them.
Though until very recently, she could neither read nor write.
I wanted to learn about the Bible,
even though I didn’t know how to read.
My parents didn’t send me to school,
but my brother taught me a little.
I felt that books spoke to people,
but to me they were speechless.
My teacher even said that books could talk.
But I was never able to hear them.
When I saw people going to the Kingdom Hall,
I thought: ‘These meetings look good.
I should go too.’
I knew that no one would say: “Why are you here?
You won’t understand anything.”
That’s why I started going to meetings,
and I’ve never stopped since.
Sometimes it’s difficult.
But I know if I miss a meeting, I will feel bad.
So even if I can only listen, I still go.
Some people don’t like to see you progressing.
They say, “Buna thinks she’s a man —always with her books.”
Even one of my brothers, who has since passed away,
used to tell me the same.
At first, I felt ashamed reading in front of others,
and sometimes I still feel ashamed.
So I would wait until I was alone at night before I read.
But I did not always understand.
I needed someone to help me
—to encourage me and explain what I was reading.
At first,
there was only material in Spanish, so that’s all I had.
I don’t speak Spanish.
So I didn’t understand anything,
and nobody could explain to me in Guna what was written.
It was like a secret.
I really appreciate what I’ve learned about Jehovah.
If I didn’t know about him, I would be like everyone else.
Studying the Bible has helped me to understand right from wrong.
When the videos are in Guna,
I can understand them very well.
I love that the videos encourage
Guna speakers to attend the meetings.
I have seen that preaching from door to door makes you happy.
When I think about it,
I would like to be able to preach more freely, like others do.
But we’re very isolated here,
and it is hard to leave this island.
When I see pictures of the Paradise,
I want to be there.
I want to survive and live there.
In the future, the earth will be a paradise.
There is no doubt at all!
This motivates me to learn more.
I really want it to reach my heart.
Thanks to the efforts of our brothers
in translation offices, even those with little or no education
can grasp Bible truths
and come to know God.
Jehovah’s organization cares for us all,
even the little ones.
I want to be among those taught by Jehovah
and this organization.
By the work they do,
I can see that Jehovah cares
—even for me.

en.text: My name is Gabriella.
Ben and I have always enjoyed
attending the meetings.
But lately,
it’s been difficult.
Something was missing
—our son.
It was like watching a movie of someone else’s family.
I couldn’t believe this was happening to us.
Our son, Levi,
was no longer one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The elders and friends in the congregation
were so supportive and understanding.
Many of them watched Levi grow up,
give his first talk,
get baptized.
I was so torn.
I was disappointed in Levi for leaving Jehovah,
but I was more disappointed in myself.
I felt like we failed him somehow.
I kept wondering how he was doing.
Was he OK?
Then, as hard as the past few weeks had been,
it just got harder.
I knew what the Bible said
about “quit mixing in company with anyone”
who is not living according to Christian standards.
But I never thought that scripture would one day apply to me.
Later that evening, a brother was talking
about the example of Korah’s sons.
Jehovah confirmed that He was using Moses
to lead His people, not Korah.
When the people were told to move away
from the rebels’ tents, what would Korah’s sons do?
Would they put loyalty to family ahead of loyalty to Jehovah?
The Bible tells us that his sons remained loyal
to Jehovah and were blessed for it.
That night, after the meeting,
I told Ben about the text I received from Levi.
I told him everything
—how I missed Levi so much,
but that I also wanted to be loyal to Jehovah like Korah’s sons.
Ben admitted that he too
had been struggling with feelings like mine.
But then he said something
that I hadn’t thought of.
If we were to stand between Levi
and the discipline he needs,
we would, in effect, be blocking
an expression of Jehovah’s love
from reaching him.
In fact, it’s our very loyalty
to Jehovah that could save his life.
We agreed to continue to put our trust
in Jehovah and stay loyal to him.
It’s been five years now,
and while Levi still hasn’t returned to Jehovah,
I haven’t given up hope on him.
Until that day,
I’m staying busy as a regular pioneer and focusing my energies
on helping others learn about Jehovah.
I’ve come to experience firsthand
the truth of Psalm 97:10.
Jehovah really does guard his loyal ones.

en.text: Armenia is an ancient country with rich history,
situated in the lands of Mount Ararat.
In the Caucasus region, Lake Sevan
is considered to be a prized jewel.
Diversity of its flora and fauna
contribute to the unique and beautiful countryside.
Yerevan, the capital,
is a modern metropolis with picturesque views
that remind many of Paris with its trees, cafés,
and beautiful water fountains.
Recently, a special three-week preaching campaign took place.
Groups of Armenian-speaking Jehovah’s Witnesses
from six different countries
wholeheartedly responded to the invitation.
The main purpose of the campaign was to cover as many
of the 512 unassigned territories as possible
with the Kingdom good news.
Thus, an opportunity
for an interchange of encouragement was created
for both the local friends and the campaign participants.
They were warmly greeted at the airport
by local brothers and sisters.
The Witnesses made good use of their tablets and smartphones to show
videos from the jw.org website.
Armenia is also currently home
to over 11,000 Western-Armenian refugees.
A special effort was made to share with these individuals
the positive message of hope and peace from the Bible
in their native tongue, West Armenian.
Metropolitan witnessing served as an effective way
to reach these ones.
It was the first time in my life
that I participated in public witnessing,
and it was very encouraging.
When individuals would approach us and show interest,
I could explain to them the truth in their own language.
It was amazing.
It’s been very heartwarming.
People have really responded well.
They were in need of comfort
and the good news, especially those that
we came for, the Western Armenians.
Pretty much every door invited us in,
and they were very hospitable and receptive.
After we heard the announcement about the special campaign
in the Western language that’s going to take place in Armenia,
we said: “We cannot miss this.
“We have to be there and bring our share
in this very joyful preaching campaign.”
During the three-week campaign,
over 15,000 pieces
of Bible-based literature were left with interested ones,
and over 200 Bible studies were started.
We were very happy to see
how many brothers and sisters were ready to come
for the campaign in Armenia
from different countries around the world.
That response showed
that Jehovah has blessed our efforts.
Those who came from far and wide

en.text: While we enjoy relative freedom in many countries around the world,
at times governments impose
bans or restrictions on the preaching work.
Brother Stephanos Demsas serves
as a special pioneer in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia,
along with his wife, Leteberhan.
Their faith was tested during many years of adversity.
What helped them champion the truth?
Their story began in what is today Eritrea.
I come from a family of nine children.
I joined the navy in 1956.
That was during the time
when Eritrea was part of Ethiopia.
My brother Gebrehiwot
asked me to come to Asmara.
He was studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I was so impressed with what he shared with me
that for the rest of my vacation,
Bible study became my priority.
In time, I was discharged from the navy and started working in Addis Ababa,
so I was able to continue studying the Bible and get baptized.
Leti was also doing the same.
In 1960, I was attending a nursing college.
There, a nurse shared some interesting thoughts with me
from the Bible.
Ten other student nurses
also showed interest,
but the college threatened us with dismissal
because there was a ban on Jehovah’s Witnesses.
When we were shown from the Bible
why true Christians are persecuted,
we renewed our determination.
Eventually, five of us were baptized.
In time, I met Stephanos, and we were married in 1964.
Because of the ban, the brothers were meeting in small groups.
Our trust was in Jehovah, and we made the preaching work a matter of prayer,
confident that he would help us.
We saw evidence of this
with the underground production
of The Watchtower.
Our brothers were of modest means,
but they used what they had to buy a hand-operated duplicating machine
which was used in our home.
After returning from our secular work,
Leti and I would get busy making copies of The Watchtower.
We would play music so our neighbors wouldn’t hear
the sound of the duplicator.
Emperor Haile Selassie was deposed.
This Communist government quickly began
a campaign called “Red Terror”
against any supposed political opposer.
Now, just having a typewriter or a duplicating machine
could put you in prison or even have you killed.
Picking up a paper from the street
with something printed on it against the government
could put one’s life in danger.
It was common for people to disappear.
Sadly, my youngest brother, Eyob, was a victim.
He disappeared on his way home
and was never seen again.
With the situation being very dangerous, we were quite concerned
raising our daughter, Janet.
But as we fully trusted in Jehovah,
we felt his loving protection.
From time to time, sections of the city
were suddenly blockaded.
This happened one morning as a translator
was heading to our home to deliver stencils for printing.
Urgently, he telephoned informing us that a house-to-house search
was under way.
Our house was full of publications
along with a duplicator and typewriters!
Just after the phone call,
three soldiers entered our compound to search.
At that moment, I prayed silently
that Jehovah would blind them.
Entering the room where the duplicator
and stacks of freshly printed literature were,
one soldier asked, “What is all this?”
“Oh, this is a duplicator that we use
to print these Bible materials.”
Completing his search, he went outside to the commander,
who asked him, “What did you find?”
To our utter amazement, after seeing everything,
he answered: “Nothing!
We won’t find anything here.”
In the late 1970’s and into the early 1980’s,
another wave of vicious persecution occurred.
A number of faithful brothers
were imprisoned, tortured, and murdered.
I was taken from my workplace because of my neutral stand
and put in prison.
When I think about living through those difficult times,
I am reminded of Isaiah 54:17
where Jehovah promised us:
“No weapon formed against you will have any success.”
Finally, in 1991,
a liberal government came to power.
They gave us legal recognition
and freedom of worship.
With these difficult, dangerous years now behind us,
we were assigned to the circuit work
in Eritrea and Ethiopia.
By now, Eritrea was becoming an independent country,
and this brought about
new challenges for the brothers.
Some young brothers were arrested
and imprisoned
because of their Christian stand.
Paul wrote at Hebrews 13:3:
“Keep in mind those in prison,
as though you were imprisoned with them.”
After enjoying the circuit work for 15 years,
we faced another change.
We were invited to serve at Bethel
as full-time commuters.
What has helped us to endure through the ban years
and to adjust to the many changes
is our spiritual study program.
We’re in full agreement
with Jeremiah 17:7:
“Blessed is the man who puts his trust in Jehovah.”
It also brings us much happiness
to know that our daughter, Janet,
has been serving as a regular pioneer for 20 years now.
Each assignment has had its challenges
but many rewards and blessings.
I’m not young anymore;
I’m 77 years old.
And I’m 74 years old.
We are now serving as special pioneers.
When we think about all the changes that we’ve been through,
we realize that the words at Isaiah 6:8:
“Here I am! Send me!”
are, not just for young people, but for all of us.

en.text: ‎Preaching in the province of Quebec ‎was a real challenge.
‎The Catholic Church
‎was present ‎in every sphere of public life.
‎In the early ’40s, ‎the persecution
‎took on quite a bit
‎of emphasis.
‎Many Witnesses were being arrested.
‎Any excuse was used.
‎Peddling without a license
‎—this was a favorite excuse.
‎Jehovah’s Witnesses were put in prison
‎whenever they were seen ‎with religious literature.
‎It had got so bad in Quebec
‎that it was decided to circulate a petition,
‎and this petition was circulated ‎throughout Canada.
‎And it called ‎on the government of Quebec
‎to put an end ‎to this persecution.
‎And interestingly,
‎some 600,000 people ‎signed the petition.
‎The Witnesses distributed
‎a very fiery tract
‎called the Burning Hate of Quebec.
‎And in this tract,
‎they showed ‎what was really happening
‎—the actions of the policemen,
‎the illegal arrests, ‎the mob action.
‎Within four months,
‎there were 800 new court cases.
‎So here, ‎for 400 Jehovah’s Witnesses,
‎you had 1,600 court cases.
‎The seriousness
‎of the court cases increased, ‎in that now
‎they were accusing ‎the brothers of sedition.
‎If convicted, ‎it was more than 10
‎—maybe 12 or 15— ‎years in prison.
‎We had one brother, ‎Aimé Boucher,
‎who was arrested ‎and charged with sedition.
‎Aimé Boucher ‎was a very poor brother,
‎who lived ‎in a rural part of Quebec.
‎And he actually
‎went to court ‎with his ox and buggy.
‎And on the way to court,
‎he was preaching, ‎so he was arrested again.
‎They had the court hearing, ‎and he was condemned.
‎He was found guilty of sedition.
‎And his case went up ‎to the Court of Appeal
‎—and at that time, the Court of Appeal ‎of Quebec was very hostile—
‎and he lost on appeal,
‎so it went up ‎to the Supreme Court of Canada.
‎And by this time,
‎there were several ‎other brothers and sisters
‎also charged on sedition,
‎which meant that if he lost his case,
‎we had several going to prison
‎for very lengthy prison terms.
‎When Brother Boucher’s case
‎came before the Supreme Court,
‎he lost by a majority of one.
‎The Catholic judges ‎all ruled against him,
‎and they found that the tract
‎the Burning Hate of Quebec ‎was seditious.
‎Our lawyers looked at the situation,
‎prayed about it, and thought:
‎‘What can we do? ‎We can’t lose this battle.’
‎And they realized that in Canada
‎there was a very rarely used provision
‎of asking the Supreme Court ‎for a rehearing.
‎At the rehearing, ‎one of the Catholic judges
‎was willing to discuss further
‎the issue of sedition.
‎And to be guilty of sedition,
‎you have to incite to violence.
‎So our attorney asked them:
‎“Please, look at the record.
‎“Show the court ‎where Jehovah’s Witnesses
‎incited to violence.”
‎And finally, they were able ‎to convince a court they were wrong.
‎And so they overturned ‎their initial decision,
‎and Brother Boucher’s case
‎was victorious.
‎This dealt with all ‎the accusations of sedition
‎and really brought to an end ‎the vicious opposition,
‎because that case ‎was the one the government
‎was hoping would work out for them.
‎There is one case ‎that’s quite noteworthy in Quebec.
‎And it’s a case of the priest
‎calling up the federal police
‎to come and interrupt
‎a meeting of Jehovah’s Witnesses
‎and expel the speaker ‎from the province of Quebec.
‎The police obeyed the priest.
‎They went to the meeting, ‎they took the brother,
‎and they escorted him ‎out of the province into Ontario.
‎And to disrupt a religious meeting ‎was a criminal act.
‎For the first time ‎—and it’s at the level of the Supreme Court—
‎they found that the three policemen
‎had to pay moral damages ‎to the brothers
‎for intercepting, ‎or interrupting, the meeting.
‎This has never happened before.
‎And when it came up ‎to the Supreme Court,
‎they unanimously ruled
‎against the province of Quebec.
‎The section on religious freedom
‎is the result of these court cases.
‎Every lawyer in Canada ‎(whether in Quebec or in English Canada),
‎when he studies law, ‎must review these cases.
‎They are the fundamentals ‎of religious freedom.
‎And they represent ‎the different areas
‎—police action, government action, ‎criminal action—
‎and they lay a very nice basis
‎for our freedoms today.
‎Our purpose is to be able ‎to preach the good news
‎and to direct people’s attention ‎toward the Bible.
‎But our court cases ‎have helped governments,
‎courts, judges,
‎and officials ‎to have the right point of view
‎on the issue of religious freedom.

en.text: We have selected the theme
“Be a Champion of Truth!”
You may have heard of the word “champion”
used in the context of sports.
What is a champion?
The word can have different meanings.
The word is related to the French word champ,
meaning “field.”
That word has its origin in the Latin word campus,
also meaning “field” or “battlefield.”
The Bible speaks of a champion on a battlefield
in 1 Samuel 17:4:
“Then a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines;
his name was Goliath.”
Goliath was a champion for a wrong cause,
namely, to take the lead in defeating
the ancient Israelites in battle.
In our modern time, according to one definition,
a champion is “an ardent defender
“or supporter of a cause
or another person.”
Christians today are ardent defenders
and supporters of the truth.
The Watchtower of January 15, 2012,
said on page 8: “Other champions
of Bible truth rose up in the centuries that followed.”
Years before, The Watchtower said:
“This magazine will never shrink in fear
from championing the truth!”
“The Watchtower has been championing
‘the cause of Kingdom truth.’”
So, are you a champion?
In a sports competition,
only one individual gets to be the champion.
But in the case of true Christians,
all can be champions of the truth.
All Christians are to defend the truth
and become conquerors —winners.
It’s necessary to defend the truth
because in today’s world
truth is being attacked and distorted.
We are surrounded by a sea of lies
and misrepresentations.
How did such lies get started?
They started in the garden of Eden
when Satan told Eve lies.
Satan, through his deceptive statements,
became “the father of the lie.”
All the problems in the world
—all calamities (also your personal calamities),
all wars, all diseases, all crimes,
all unhappiness, sorrow, and death
—started with the original lies
in the garden of Eden.
Satan is “the father of the lie.”
But today there are many “children” of the lie.
Every one of us is affected.
We are surrounded by a sea of lies.
A lie is “a false statement
“deliberately presented as being true;
a falsehood.”
A lie is the opposite of the truth.
Lying involves saying something incorrect
to a person who is entitled to know the truth about a matter.
But there is also something that is called a half-truth.
The Bible tells Christians to be honest with each other.
“Now that you have put away deceit,
. . . speak truth,” wrote the apostle Paul
at Ephesians 4:25.
Lies and half-truths undermine trust.
A German proverb says,
“Who lies once is not believed,
even if he says the truth.”
So we need to speak openly
and honestly with each other,
not withholding bits of information
that could change the perception of the listener
or mislead him.
As to lies, there are different types.
Some politicians have lied about matters
they wanted to keep secret.
Companies sometimes lie in advertisements
regarding their products.
What about the news media?
Many try to report events truthfully.
But we should not be gullible
and believe everything newspapers write
or everything we hear on radio
or see on television.
Then there are religious lies.
If Satan is called “the father of the lie,”
then Babylon the Great, the global empire of false religion,
can be called the “mother” of the lie.
Individual false religions
could be called “daughters” of the lie.
Some lie by saying that sinners
will get tormented in hell forever.
Others lie by saying,
“Once saved, always saved.”
Again, others lie by saying that the earth
will be burned up on Judgment Day
and all good people will go to heaven.
Some worship idols.
Paul wrote at Romans 1:25:
“They exchanged the truth of God for the lie
“and venerated and rendered sacred service
to the creation rather than the Creator.”
Then there are many lies of a personal nature
that people express in everyday life.
A businessman may get a phone call
but tell his secretary to answer the caller
by saying he is not in.
This may be considered a small lie.
There are small lies, big lies,
and malicious lies.
A child may have broken something but when asked initially,
out of fear of punishment, denies having done it.
This does not make the child a malicious liar.
In contrast, what if an entrepreneur
tells his bookkeeper to falsify the entries
in the books in order to save on taxes?
This lying to the tax office
is certainly a serious lie.
It is a deliberate attempt to mislead somebody
that has the right to know.
It also robs the government of what they have established
as legal income.
We can see that not all lies are the same;
there are small lies, big lies,
and malicious lies.
Satan is a malicious liar.
He is the champion of the lie.
Since Jehovah hates liars,
we should avoid all lies,
not just big or malicious lies.
But can we find the truth?
Some say, “Truth is relative.”
It is like saying, “This is truth for you,
and this is truth for me.”
This claim is not logical
when it comes to religious truth.
Either God is a Trinity or he’s not.
Either the soul is mortal or it is not.
Either there is a future paradise on earth or there is not.
Either homosexuality is acceptable to God or it is not.
Either participating in wars is permissible or it is not.
Truth is definite, not relative,
because Jehovah conveyed the truth to his servants.
Psalm 43:3 says:
“Send out your light and your truth.”
Jehovah is a Revealer of truth.
One of several reasons why Jesus came into the world
was to “witness to the truth.”
At John 18:37b,
he said: “For this I have been born,
“and for this I have come into the world,
“that I should bear witness to the truth.
Everyone who is on the side of the truth listens to my voice.”
So if we listen to Jesus, or read in the Bible
what he taught, we can learn the truth.
Jesus was the personification of the truth.
He said: “I am the way
and the truth and the life.”
We can find out what the truth is
by diligently studying the Bible.
Truth is that which is a fact.
For true Christians, the entire text
of the Hebrew and Christian Greek Scriptures
constitutes the truth.
Psalm 119:160
says of Jehovah:
‘The essence of your word is truth.’
That is why it is good to do
daily Bible reading with meditation
and weekly family worship.
At Matthew 24:45-47, we read
that for the time of the end, Jesus would appoint
a “faithful and discreet slave,” or Governing Body,
to explain the Bible to His followers
and help them to grow in understanding of the truth.
Whereas Jesus’ teachings
and the written Word of God are inspired,
“the faithful and discreet slave” is not inspired,
although it champions the truth.
Nevertheless, the faithful slave
provides spiritual food.
Whereas in the first century
there was supernatural knowledge
available for apostles and Bible writers,
in the time of the end, Jehovah does not bestow
this miraculous gift anymore, as explained
at 1 Corinthians 13:8.
Although there is no divine inspiration today,
still Jesus leads his people progressively
through the services of the faithful slave.
Jesus trusts that the imperfect faithful slave
will do its best to convey spiritual food.
Do you also trust the slave?
Whereas the truth of God’s Word does not change,
our understanding of the truth does change
because we are not perfect yet.
We understand more about the truth today
than Christians in the first century.
Do we keep up with the progressive understanding of truth?
Daniel was told: “Many will rove about,
and the true knowledge will become abundant.”
This is a gradual process.
We are still roving about.
During the Millennium, Jehovah will reveal
additional truths to mankind.
At Revelation 20:12,
it mentions scrolls that will be opened.
The apostle John reports that the dead are to be “judged
“out of those things written in the scrolls
according to their deeds.”
Evidently, then, these scrolls will contain
additional information for mankind during the thousand years.
It stands to reason that after the end of the Millennium,
there will be additional truths to learn.
Still, according to Ecclesiastes
chapter 3, verse 11:
“Mankind will never find out
the work that the true God has made.”
But how do we know we have the truth?
At Pentecost 33 of our Common Era,
true Christians numbered only about 3,000.
Today, we are millions.
And on average, every weekend
more than 5,000 are getting baptized.
But this in itself
is not proof that we have the truth.
Truth is not measured in numbers.
Why do we know we have the truth?
For one, because we remain
in Jesus’ teaching, John 8:31.
Second, we know we have the truth
because of the deep bond of love
for each other, John 13:35.
Third, we know we have the truth because our conduct
adheres to the high moral standards of truth,
John 15:10.
Fourth, we know we have the truth
because we remain neutral in the controversies of the world,
as Jesus advised at John 17:14.
Fifth, we know we have the truth
because we are God’s name people.
Acts 15:14 speaks
of “a people for his name.”
Jesus said: “The truth will set you free.”
It sets us free from fears —like the fear of death,
fear of the future, and an exaggerated fear of man.
It also sets us free from false teachings,
from spiritism, and from astrology and magic.
It frees us from immorality and its consequences.
There are no other people on earth
that are as spiritually free as we are.
Do we appreciate that freedom?
Truth leads to freedom.
Second Corinthians 3:17 says:
“Where the spirit of Jehovah is,
there is freedom.”
The truth penetrates schools. How so?
By means of our children who preach the truth
to classmates and to teachers.
Do you go to school?
Do you champion the truth at school?
How can you do this?
You do this not only by preaching but also by your conduct,
by your dress and grooming,
and by taking a stand for the truth when others want you
to participate in unchristian practices.
You also champion the truth by remaining honest
and not cheating on your exams.
And Jehovah will love you for that.
The truth also penetrates prisons.
Reports have come in from many countries
telling of the good work brothers are doing
in contacting prisoners in various prisons,
helping some to rehabilitate their lives spiritually.
In a number of such institutions,
regular meetings are being held
and several prisoners have studied to the point
of dedication and baptism.
The truth penetrates even walls of monasteries.
In Mexico, in 2009,
a nun was baptized who, because of the truth,
had left her monastery and order,
although she was the mother superior.
The world is in utter confusion.
What a blessing to know the truth!
We rejoice in it!
We have the truth on our lips.
We have the truth around our hips.
Ephesians chapter 6 says that “the belt of truth”
is fastened around our waists.
We are ready to teach it.
We talk the truth, and we walk in the truth.
Those who continue to walk
in the truth will walk in it forever.
Help your students to love the truth
and to live the truth but, if necessary,
to be willing to die for the truth and for Jehovah.
The truth is invincible
and will conquer this wicked world.
In some countries, we may have many enemies
who may want to silence us.
But the apostle Paul said
at 2 Corinthians 13:8:
“For we can do nothing against the truth.”
Neither can our enemies suppress the truth.
Do we appreciate that we have the truth
—the only truth?
Is this arrogant to say? By no means!
It would be a sin if we would not say so.
Jesus was not arrogant when he said:
‘I am the truth.’
To know the truth is not enough.
We need to champion it.
There are still many lovers of truth out there;
search for them.
Who will help you in your search?
According to John 4:23,
Jesus said that Jehovah is searching for ones
that want to worship in truth.
The majority will not listen to the truth
because ‘they love the darkness rather than the light.’
The truth may expose their sinful conduct,
and they may not have the humility
to want to repent and change.
We still have to preach to them —to warn them.
Ezekiel was told:
“You must warn them from me.”
The principle applies to us as well.
Paul speaks of “the sword of . . . God’s word.”
Use it well to champion the truth.
Train your students to be good defenders of it as well.
The time will come in Paradise after the final test
when it will not be necessary
to champion, or defend, the truth,
because nobody will attack it anymore.
Right now, whether we are adults,
teenagers, or children, let us follow and imitate Jesus
—the greatest Champion of truth!
To that end, keep studying the truth.
Keep spreading the truth.
Keep loving the truth and Jehovah, the God of truth.
Hold fast to the truth as to a lifeline
—as this is what it is!
By staying faithful, whether you survive Armageddon
or are resurrected in Paradise,
you will be a victorious champion of the truth!

cn.text: 本月的主题是
“做一个拥护真理的王牌战士”
你可能在不同的体育活动上听过
“冠军”或“王牌”这个词
什么是“冠军”、“王牌”呢?
这个词有不同的意思
在一些语言里
这个词和“场地”或“战场”有关
事实上  我们也可以在圣经里
找到类似的用法
圣经在撒母耳记上17:4
谈到战场上的王牌战士
经文说
身为一个战士
歌利亚支持了错误的一方
他带头向以色列人讨战
除了战场上
“冠军”或“王牌”一词
也可以指一个人热心支持
或拥护某个人或某件事
今天的基督徒热心地拥护及支持真理
在这方面  我们也是冠军
《守望台》在2012年
1月15日刊的第8页谈到
在随后几百年
陆续有人起来拥护圣经真理
早期《守望台》提及
这本杂志永不会畏缩不敢倡导真理
也谈到
《守望台》一直倡导
“维护王国的真理”
所以  你是一个冠军吗?
在体育竞赛里  冠军只有一个
但是对于真基督徒来说
由于我们拥护真理
所有人都能成为赢家或冠军
今天  真理常被人抨击或扭曲
导致世界充斥着谎言
和误导人的思想
所以  我们都需要拥护真理
那么  谎言是如何开始的呢?
就是从撒但在伊甸园里欺骗夏娃开始的
撒但说谎欺骗人
成为了“谎话之父”
世上所有的难题、灾难、个人的患难
战争、疾病、罪行
令人不快的事、悲伤、死亡
都是由于撒但
在伊甸园所说的第一个谎言而开始的
我们知道撒但是“谎话之父”
但今天也出现了很多“谎话之子”
我们每一个人都会受到谎话的影响
到处都是谎言
谎言是虚假的话
故意使人对实情产生误解
谎言是真理的反面
撒谎是指对有权知道真相的人说假话
谎言也包含了半真半假的话
圣经告诉基督徒要坦诚相待
保罗在以弗所书4:25谈到
“你们弃绝了谎言…要对人说实话”
对人说谎  或说半真半假的话
都会破坏彼此的信任
德国有一句谚语说
一个人一旦说谎
即使之后说的是真话
也不再有人相信
因此  我们要坦诚沟通
不会对有权知道真相的人隐瞒事实
使听者对实情产生误解  误导对方
这世界上有许多不同的谎言
有些政客欺骗民众  隐瞒事实
一些公司为了销售产品
刊登不实的广告
新闻媒体呢?
虽然许多媒体试着报道事情的真相
但我们不应该轻易相信
所有我们在报纸和电视上所看到
或从电台所听到的消息
除此之外  我们周遭还有宗教谎言
如果说撒但是“谎话之父”
那么大巴比伦
也就是世上的所有错误宗教
就是“谎话之母”了
个别的错误宗教
则可以称为“谎话之子”
有些错误宗教声称
罪人会在地狱里永远受折磨
其他说 “一次得救，永远得救”
也有些宗教说
地球会在审判日来到时被毁灭
然后好人会上天堂
还有宗教则崇拜偶像
如同保罗在罗马书1:25所说的
在我们的日常生活里
许多人会不经意地说谎
例如  一个经理收到一通电话
但是他却请秘书回答说他不在
这可以说是一个小谎
谎话有小谎、大谎  恶毒的谎言之分
一个小孩打破东西
虽然由于害怕受罚
而否认这是他做的
但这称不上是恶毒的谎言
相反地  如果一个老板为了逃税
请他的会计帮忙做假帐
这就构成了严重的谎言
他蓄意误导有权知道真相的人
他这样做也等于偷走政府的钱
我们看出不是所有谎言都是一样的
有小谎、大谎还有恶毒的谎言
撒但是恶毒的说谎者 他是说谎高手
既然耶和华厌恶说谎的人
我们就应该远避所有谎言
不论是小谎、大谎还是恶毒的谎言
既然世上有那么多谎言
我们还能找到真理吗?
有些人说“真理不是绝对的”
这就好像说
“你有你的看法，我有我的见解”
但这种说法在宗教信仰上是行不通的
上帝不是三位一体的神
人没有不死的灵魂
地球会成为乐园
上帝不认可同性恋的行为
基督徒不可以参与战争等
这些真理都是绝对的
而不是模棱两可的
因为耶和华清楚地告诉他的仆人
什么才是真理
诗篇43:3说
“求你发出你的亮光和真理”
耶和华是显明真理的上帝
耶稣来到世上的其中一个原因
就是要“给真理作见证”
耶稣在约翰福音18:37说
如果我们听从耶稣的话
阅读他在圣经里的教导
我们就能学习到真理
耶稣是真理的化身  他说
“我就是道路、真理、生命”
我们可以通过仔细研读圣经
来认识真理
真理是事情的真相
对真基督徒来说
整本圣经的内容都是由真理组成的
诗篇119:160谈到耶和华时说
“你话语的要旨是真理”
这就是为什么天天阅读圣经
仔细沉思里面的内容
举行每周家庭崇拜相当重要
此外  根据马太福音24:45-47
在最后的日子
耶稣会通过“忠信睿智的奴隶”
也就是中央长老团
向他的门徒进一步阐明圣经的真理
虽然忠信睿智奴隶的教导
不像圣经的话和耶稣的教导一样
直接受圣灵启示
但他们也是真理的拥护者
为我们提供属灵的粮食
因为根据哥林多前书13:8
在最后的日子
耶和华不会再像以前一样
以超自然的方式启示使徒和圣经执笔者
这种奇妙恩赐今天已经不存在了
所以  尽管现在没有人
能得到圣灵的奇妙恩赐
耶稣仍然通过忠信奴隶
逐步带领他的门徒执行工作
耶稣相信  忠信奴隶即使不完美
也会尽最大努力分发灵粮
你也相信忠信奴隶所付出的努力吗?
上帝话语的真理永不改变
但由于不完美
我们需要不断调整对真理的理解
今天  我们已经比一世纪的基督徒
更了解真理
可是  我们愿意跟上组织阐明真理的脚步吗?
上帝告诉但以理
将来有很多人来往奔走
真确的知识就会丰富起来
直到今天
我们还在真理中来往奔走
在基督千年统治期间
耶和华将会显明更多真理
启示录20:12提到了展开的书卷
使徒约翰说
死了的人都根据这些书卷上所写的话
按照自己的行为受审判
显然  这些书卷
将会包含千年统治期间
上帝为我们订下的新指示
由此可知
就算基督的千年统治已经结束
还有许多真理等着我们去学习
传道书3:11也说
可是  我们怎么知道
我们拥有真理呢?
公元33年五旬节
真基督徒的人数只有大约3000人
今天  我们的人数
已成长到几百万之多
每周平均也有超过5000人受浸
但是  这无法证明我们拥有真理
因为真理是不能以数字来衡量的
那么我们又怎么知道
我们拥有真理呢?
第一  如同约翰福音8:31所说
我们时刻遵守耶稣的教导
第二  我们知道我们拥有真理
因为我们像约翰福音13:35说的
彼此相爱
第三  我们知道我们拥有真理
因为根据约翰福音15:10
我们的行为
表明我们谨守崇高的道德标准
第四  我们知道我们拥有真理
因为我们遵照耶稣
在约翰福音17:14的吩咐
在这纷乱的世界里严守中立
第五  我们知道我们拥有真理
因为使徒行传15:14说
上帝拣选我们
成为“一群归他名下的子民”
耶稣说 “真理会叫你们自由”
真理使我们消除
对死亡、未来  甚至对人的恐惧
真理也使我们免受错误的见解
通灵术、占星术  以及魔法所蒙骗
真理甚至帮助我们摆脱不道德的影响
世上只有我们能享有这样的属灵自由
正如哥林多后书3:17说
“耶和华的灵在哪里，哪里就有自由”
真理能深入校园
通过什么方法呢?
就是借着我们的孩子
向同学及老师传讲真理
你是学生吗?
你有没有在学校里拥护真理呢?
你可以怎样拥护真理?
其实  除了传道之外
借着表现好行为、衣着端庄
不参加违反圣经原则的活动
以及在考试时诚实作答
这些都是拥护真理的好方法
耶和华看到你这么做  一定十分高兴
真理也能深入监狱
来自许多国家的报告显示出
弟兄们努力接触监狱里的囚犯
帮助他们恢复属灵健康
在一些监狱里
弟兄们甚至可以举行聚会
有些囚犯也在属灵上进步
已符合资格献身受浸
真理甚至能穿透围墙  深入修道院
2009年在墨西哥
有位女修道院院长由于认识真理
因而决定离开修道院
受浸成为耶和华见证人
整个世界充斥着谎言
能了解真理  是多么有福啊!
我们不只口里宣扬真理
也像以弗所书6章所说的
“用真理束腰”
我们在生活各方面持守真理
也准备好教导人认识真理
我们不只讲论真理
也在真理中行走
那些留在真理道路上的人
将会永远活下去
要帮助你的学生爱真理
按着真理生活
甚至必要时  要愿意
为耶和华和他的真理而牺牲生命
虽然很多敌人
想尽办法要使我们闭口不言
可是我们很清楚  真理无往不利
而且终必战胜这个邪恶世界
使徒保罗在哥林多后书13:8说
我们的仇敌完全无法抵挡真理
我们因拥有唯一的真理而感到自豪
这样会显得我们骄傲自大吗?
一点都不会!
不感到自豪  反而有问题
就连耶稣也自豪地说
“我就是真理”
可是  只是了解真理并不够
我们还需要拥护真理
要去找出那些渴慕真理的人
谁会帮助我们找寻这些人呢?
在约翰福音4:23  耶稣说
耶和华正寻找按真理崇拜他的人
今天  大多数人不愿接受真理
因为他们“爱黑暗而不爱光”
就算真理揭露了他们的错误行为
他们也不愿表现谦卑  改过自新
然而  我们还是要听从上帝
在以西结书的劝告
“你要…替我警告他们”
保罗把上帝的话语比做手中的剑
要用这把剑拥护真理
也要训练圣经学生用这把剑捍卫真理
乐园即将来临
人类度过最后的考验后
我们就不用再捍卫真理了
因为谁也无法再攻击真理
不管你是大人还是小孩
让我们效法
最伟大的真理拥护者  耶稣
在等候上帝大日子的同时
要不断学习真理
也要坚持不懈传讲真理
更要继续热爱真理
以及信守真理的上帝耶和华
要紧守真理  因为真理能使你得救
无论你是活着度过哈米吉多顿
还是在乐园里复活
只要一生保持忠贞  你能成为冠军
成为一位拥护真理的王牌战士!

en.text: I want to address the theme
“Young Ones—You Are Loved by Jehovah”
and his organization.
“Young Ones—You Are Loved by Jehovah”
and his organization.
But now, when we say young ones,
to whom are we referring?
As evidence of Jehovah’s love,
some may immediately think of the animated series
of videos entitled Become Jehovah’s Friend,
featuring Caleb and Sophia,
and that has indeed been evidence
of Jehovah’s and the Governing Body’s love
for little children.
We have gotten hundreds of letters of appreciation for this series
from small children and their parents,
and even from grandparents.
But what about you teenagers?
You too are still young when compared to adulthood,
and you are appreciated very much
when you show your respect and love for Jehovah.
Does the Bible indicate anything
about Jesus’ disposition as a teenager?
There are comments about him as an infant.
Also in the book of Luke, it describes Jesus
as a child of 12 years old.
Let’s look at that account and determine
if it also includes any comments
about Jesus’ attitude as a teenager.
In Luke 2:42
it describes Jesus as a preteen
in saying this,
Luke 2:42:
“And when he was 12 years old,
“they went up according to the custom of the festival.
“When the days of the festival were over
“and they were returning,
“the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem,
and his parents did not notice it.”
So his parents went looking for him
and finally found him three days later.
What was Jesus focused on as a 12-year-old?
He was sitting in the temple talking with the teachers about Jehovah.
Notice verse 47:
“But all those listening to him
“were in constant amazement at his understanding
and his answers.”
What a good example for you children
12 years of age and younger
to talk about Jehovah with confidence!
But what was Jesus’ attitude like as a teenager?
Please follow along in verses 51 and 52:
“Then he [Jesus] went down with them
“and returned to Nazareth,
and he continued subject to them,”
that is to his parents.
How old was he? Twelve.
But what comes after 12? Thirteen.
Notice verse 52:
“And Jesus went on progressing.”
You see, after 12, he “went on progressing
“in wisdom and in physical growth
and in favor with God and men.”
Evidently, then, Jesus was an intelligent,
well-balanced teenager.
But who took note of his progress as a teen?
It said: “God and men.”
Yes, godly children and teenagers
are appreciated by Jehovah and by spiritual men.
Jehovah and his organization love all you young ones
who are striving to do what is right.
But how do we know that Jehovah loves all of you?
Well, if you have your Bible, turn to Matthew chapter 19,
and here we see that Jesus showed
his high regard for young ones.
So Matthew chapter 19, notice verses 13 and 14:
“Then young children were brought to him
“for him to place his hands on them and offer prayer,
but the disciples reprimanded them.”
They did not want the young ones to bother Jesus.
But notice verse 14:
“Jesus, however, said:
“‘Let the young children alone,
“‘and do not try to stop them from coming to me,
for the Kingdom of the heavens belongs to such ones.’”
Yes, Jesus welcomed young ones,
and the Bible tells us that Jesus
is the perfect reflection of Jehovah.
So Jesus was imitating Jehovah’s love for young ones.
After many wise sayings and performing miracles,
Matthew chapter 21 describes Jesus
riding into Jerusalem as Jehovah’s anointed one.
Please notice the difference between some of the adult’s reactions
and that of appreciative young ones.
Matthew 21:15
tells us this:
“When the chief priests and the scribes
“saw the marvelous things he did
“and the boys who were shouting in the temple,
“‘Save, we pray, the Son of David!’
they became indignant.”
Who was boldly praising Jesus?
The scripture said that “the boys”
were shouting out praise.
What a contrast those young ones were
to the religious leaders who were irritated by all of this.
Young people, when you speak up about Jehovah and Jesus,
they both take notice of you.
They are proud of your stand for the truth!
But how do you know that the Governing Body
and the organization loves you?
Well, they have published many books
and magazine articles specifically for young ones.
In addition to all of the printed material, there are
the Become Jehovah’s Friend videos for children.
But, you teenagers, have you been keeping up
with all of the information specifically for you
on jw.org?
There are dozens of printed articles
on an array of subjects
that interest those of your age.
In so many ways, Jehovah and his organization show their love
and appreciation for all you dear young ones.
What can you young ones do in return?
You may say, ‘I go to all the meetings and out in service.’
Well, that is wonderful.
Some of you may have even joined
the Theocratic Ministry School already,
and you help clean and maintain the Kingdom Hall.
We warmly commend you for your good works.
But if you think about it, even more important
is having a good personal relationship with Jehovah.
In Luke 10:27 it says:
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
and with your whole strength and with your whole mind.”
To love Jehovah with your whole heart
means that you have a good personal relationship with him.
That involves more than just doing good things.
It involves praying to him
about what is in your heart.
Tell him everything you love and whatever you fear.
You can tell Jehovah very personal things;
he is not going to tell anyone else.
But he can give you the strength and wisdom
to handle matters for the best possible outcome.
Set up your own personal Bible study program
in addition to Family Worship evening.
This is how Jehovah communicates back to you,
and your relationship with him will be strengthened.
You are the next generation of adults in Jehovah’s organization.
We continue to need spiritually qualified ones
to get Jehovah’s work done.
A good relationship with Jehovah as a youth sets you up
for the best way of life as a responsible adult.
Along the way, though, you will face pressure
from Satan’s system that can test your faith.
But by loving Jehovah with your whole heart,
you can get through any test you may encounter,
and I mean any test that you may encounter!

en.text: An introduction to the Song of Solomon,
also known as Canticles.
King Solomon wrote this poetic book in Jerusalem.
It was composed sometime
after the temple was built.
Of the many songs composed by Solomon,
this is considered his greatest.
The main character is the Shulammite girl.
Other characters included in this drama
are the Shulammite’s brothers;
the shepherd; Solomon;
the daughters of Jerusalem, or ladies of Solomon’s court;
and the daughters of Zion, or women of Jerusalem.
The song is presented through a series of conversations
in which the speakers are constantly changing.
Although the characters speaking are not named,
they can be identified by what they say
or what is said to them.
The Song of Solomon consists of eight chapters.
Chapters 1 and 2 contain events that take place near the town of Shunem,
which was also called Shulem.
The Shulammite girl is brought into Solomon’s camp,
but she resists his advances
and declares that she can love only her dear shepherd.
Did you know?
Shunem was the birthplace of David’s nurse, Abishag,
and the place where the prophet Elisha often stayed with a family.
Chapters 3 to 8 describe events that take place in Jerusalem.
Solomon returns to his court,
taking the Shulammite with him in an effort to impress her.
The Shulammite tells the daughters of Jerusalem,
or ladies of Solomon’s court,
not to arouse love in her for Solomon.
The shepherd follows the Shulammite to Jerusalem
and strengthens her with warm expressions of endearment.
We should keep in mind the ancient Eastern setting of this song
in order to appreciate the poetic expressions of endearment
that may seem unusual today.
The shepherd compares the Shulammite’s eyes to those of a dove,
her hair to a flock of goats,
and her cheeks to a segment of pomegranate.
Solomon approaches her again with flattering words,
but she continues to reject his advances.
In chapter 8, the Shulammite girl returns to her home.
Having proved her exclusive devotion, she is reunited with her dear shepherd.
Their unfailing love is described as “the flame of Jah”
because Jehovah is the Originator of true love.
As you read this book,
note the chasteness of the Shulammite girl,
her loyalty to the shepherd,
and how true love originates with Jehovah,
whose sovereignty is based on love.

是以人物之间的对话呈现的
说话的人也不断转变
对话中 虽然不会提到人物的名字
但是从对话的内容
就能看出是哪些人在说话
雅歌一共有八章
第一和第二章
描述在书念城附近发生的事
这座城也叫做书伦城
书拉密少女被带到所罗门的营中
她拒绝了所罗门的追求
并坚定地表示只爱自己的恋人
你知道吗？
大卫的侍女亚比莎
就是在书念城出生的
先知以利沙
也常在那里的一户人家里留宿
第三至八章记载耶路撒冷城发生的事
所罗门把书拉密少女带回王宫
希望用财富权势赢得少女的心
但书拉密少女告诉耶路撒冷的女子
也就是所罗门宫中的妇女
不要劝她改变心意
牧羊人追到耶路撒冷
向她表达浓浓的爱意
使少女的心意更加坚定
这首诗表达爱意的方法或许很奇特
不过只要记得
写作背景是在古代的中东地区
就能理解诗中的意境
牧羊人说少女的眼睛好像鸽子的眼睛
头发有如一群山羊
双颊像一瓣红石榴
所罗门再次追求少女
虽然他说了很多甜言蜜语
少女仍旧不为所动
在第八章里
书拉密少女回到家乡
她自始至终都深爱着牧羊人
最后少女与她亲爱的牧羊人重聚
这首诗用“耶和华的熊熊烈火”
形容坚定不移的爱
因为耶和华是真爱的来源
当你阅读雅歌时
请留意书拉密少女的贞洁品德
她对恋人专一的爱情
也留意以爱统治人的耶和华
才是真爱的来源
