en.text: Thank you for joining us,
and welcome to the program!
It’s our privilege to spend the next hour
with you dear brothers and sisters.
Please join us on a field trip to Ethiopia
where we will meet Brother Stephanos Demsas.
Brother Demsas and his wife served faithfully for many years
while the preaching work was under ban.
You will enjoy their experiences.
Have you ever participated in a preaching campaign?
Our team was present when one was arranged in Armenia.
A preaching campaign is uplifting and encouraging
to everyone involved as this segment will show.
How would you react if one of your loved ones decides
to leave the truth?
It truly is heartbreaking, to say the least,
but what Bible principles can help us endure
such a challenge?
This dramatization will help us.
This is the November program
of JW Broadcasting!
We have selected the theme
“Be a Champion of Truth!”
You may have heard of the word “champion”
used in the context of sports.
What is a champion?
The word can have different meanings.
The word is related to the French word champ,
meaning “field.”
That word has its origin in the Latin word campus,
also meaning “field” or “battlefield.”
The Bible speaks of a champion on a battlefield
in 1 Samuel 17:4:
“Then a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines;
his name was Goliath.”
Goliath was a champion for a wrong cause,
namely, to take the lead in defeating
the ancient Israelites in battle.
In our modern time, according to one definition,
a champion is “an ardent defender
“or supporter of a cause
or another person.”
Christians today are ardent defenders
and supporters of the truth.
The Watchtower of January 15, 2012,
said on page 8: “Other champions
of Bible truth rose up in the centuries that followed.”
Years before, The Watchtower said:
“This magazine will never shrink in fear
from championing the truth!”
“The Watchtower has been championing
‘the cause of Kingdom truth.’”
So, are you a champion?
In a sports competition,
only one individual gets to be the champion.
But in the case of true Christians,
all can be champions of the truth.
All Christians are to defend the truth
and become conquerors —winners.
It’s necessary to defend the truth
because in today’s world
truth is being attacked and distorted.
We are surrounded by a sea of lies
and misrepresentations.
How did such lies get started?
They started in the garden of Eden
when Satan told Eve lies.
Satan, through his deceptive statements,
became “the father of the lie.”
All the problems in the world
—all calamities (also your personal calamities),
all wars, all diseases, all crimes,
all unhappiness, sorrow, and death
—started with the original lies
in the garden of Eden.
Satan is “the father of the lie.”
But today there are many “children” of the lie.
Every one of us is affected.
We are surrounded by a sea of lies.
A lie is “a false statement
“deliberately presented as being true;
a falsehood.”
A lie is the opposite of the truth.
Lying involves saying something incorrect
to a person who is entitled to know the truth about a matter.
But there is also something that is called a half-truth.
The Bible tells Christians to be honest with each other.
“Now that you have put away deceit,
. . . speak truth,” wrote the apostle Paul
at Ephesians 4:25.
Lies and half-truths undermine trust.
A German proverb says,
“Who lies once is not believed,
even if he says the truth.”
So we need to speak openly
and honestly with each other,
not withholding bits of information
that could change the perception of the listener
or mislead him.
As to lies, there are different types.
Some politicians have lied about matters
they wanted to keep secret.
Companies sometimes lie in advertisements
regarding their products.
What about the news media?
Many try to report events truthfully.
But we should not be gullible
and believe everything newspapers write
or everything we hear on radio
or see on television.
Then there are religious lies.
If Satan is called “the father of the lie,”
then Babylon the Great, the global empire of false religion,
can be called the “mother” of the lie.
Individual false religions
could be called “daughters” of the lie.
Some lie by saying that sinners
will get tormented in hell forever.
Others lie by saying,
“Once saved, always saved.”
Again, others lie by saying that the earth
will be burned up on Judgment Day
and all good people will go to heaven.
Some worship idols.
Paul wrote at Romans 1:25:
“They exchanged the truth of God for the lie
“and venerated and rendered sacred service
to the creation rather than the Creator.”
Then there are many lies of a personal nature
that people express in everyday life.
A businessman may get a phone call
but tell his secretary to answer the caller
by saying he is not in.
This may be considered a small lie.
There are small lies, big lies,
and malicious lies.
A child may have broken something but when asked initially,
out of fear of punishment, denies having done it.
This does not make the child a malicious liar.
In contrast, what if an entrepreneur
tells his bookkeeper to falsify the entries
in the books in order to save on taxes?
This lying to the tax office
is certainly a serious lie.
It is a deliberate attempt to mislead somebody
that has the right to know.
It also robs the government of what they have established
as legal income.
We can see that not all lies are the same;
there are small lies, big lies,
and malicious lies.
Satan is a malicious liar.
He is the champion of the lie.
Since Jehovah hates liars,
we should avoid all lies,
not just big or malicious lies.
But can we find the truth?
Some say, “Truth is relative.”
It is like saying, “This is truth for you,
and this is truth for me.”
This claim is not logical
when it comes to religious truth.
Either God is a Trinity or he’s not.
Either the soul is mortal or it is not.
Either there is a future paradise on earth or there is not.
Either homosexuality is acceptable to God or it is not.
Either participating in wars is permissible or it is not.
Truth is definite, not relative,
because Jehovah conveyed the truth to his servants.
Psalm 43:3 says:
“Send out your light and your truth.”
Jehovah is a Revealer of truth.
One of several reasons why Jesus came into the world
was to “witness to the truth.”
At John 18:37b,
he said: “For this I have been born,
“and for this I have come into the world,
“that I should bear witness to the truth.
Everyone who is on the side of the truth listens to my voice.”
So if we listen to Jesus, or read in the Bible
what he taught, we can learn the truth.
Jesus was the personification of the truth.
He said: “I am the way
and the truth and the life.”
We can find out what the truth is
by diligently studying the Bible.
Truth is that which is a fact.
For true Christians, the entire text
of the Hebrew and Christian Greek Scriptures
constitutes the truth.
Psalm 119:160
says of Jehovah:
‘The essence of your word is truth.’
That is why it is good to do
daily Bible reading with meditation
and weekly family worship.
At Matthew 24:45-47, we read
that for the time of the end, Jesus would appoint
a “faithful and discreet slave,” or Governing Body,
to explain the Bible to His followers
and help them to grow in understanding of the truth.
Whereas Jesus’ teachings
and the written Word of God are inspired,
“the faithful and discreet slave” is not inspired,
although it champions the truth.
Nevertheless, the faithful slave
provides spiritual food.
Whereas in the first century
there was supernatural knowledge
available for apostles and Bible writers,
in the time of the end, Jehovah does not bestow
this miraculous gift anymore, as explained
at 1 Corinthians 13:8.
Although there is no divine inspiration today,
still Jesus leads his people progressively
through the services of the faithful slave.
Jesus trusts that the imperfect faithful slave
will do its best to convey spiritual food.
Do you also trust the slave?
Whereas the truth of God’s Word does not change,
our understanding of the truth does change
because we are not perfect yet.
We understand more about the truth today
than Christians in the first century.
Do we keep up with the progressive understanding of truth?
Daniel was told: “Many will rove about,
and the true knowledge will become abundant.”
This is a gradual process.
We are still roving about.
During the Millennium, Jehovah will reveal
additional truths to mankind.
At Revelation 20:12,
it mentions scrolls that will be opened.
The apostle John reports that the dead are to be “judged
“out of those things written in the scrolls
according to their deeds.”
Evidently, then, these scrolls will contain
additional information for mankind during the thousand years.
It stands to reason that after the end of the Millennium,
there will be additional truths to learn.
Still, according to Ecclesiastes
chapter 3, verse 11:
“Mankind will never find out
the work that the true God has made.”
But how do we know we have the truth?
At Pentecost 33 of our Common Era,
true Christians numbered only about 3,000.
Today, we are millions.
And on average, every weekend
more than 5,000 are getting baptized.
But this in itself
is not proof that we have the truth.
Truth is not measured in numbers.
Why do we know we have the truth?
For one, because we remain
in Jesus’ teaching, John 8:31.
Second, we know we have the truth
because of the deep bond of love
for each other, John 13:35.
Third, we know we have the truth because our conduct
adheres to the high moral standards of truth,
John 15:10.
Fourth, we know we have the truth
because we remain neutral in the controversies of the world,
as Jesus advised at John 17:14.
Fifth, we know we have the truth
because we are God’s name people.
Acts 15:14 speaks
of “a people for his name.”
Jesus said: “The truth will set you free.”
It sets us free from fears —like the fear of death,
fear of the future, and an exaggerated fear of man.
It also sets us free from false teachings,
from spiritism, and from astrology and magic.
It frees us from immorality and its consequences.
There are no other people on earth
that are as spiritually free as we are.
Do we appreciate that freedom?
Truth leads to freedom.
Second Corinthians 3:17 says:
“Where the spirit of Jehovah is,
there is freedom.”
The truth penetrates schools. How so?
By means of our children who preach the truth
to classmates and to teachers.
Do you go to school?
Do you champion the truth at school?
How can you do this?
You do this not only by preaching but also by your conduct,
by your dress and grooming,
and by taking a stand for the truth when others want you
to participate in unchristian practices.
You also champion the truth by remaining honest
and not cheating on your exams.
And Jehovah will love you for that.
The truth also penetrates prisons.
Reports have come in from many countries
telling of the good work brothers are doing
in contacting prisoners in various prisons,
helping some to rehabilitate their lives spiritually.
In a number of such institutions,
regular meetings are being held
and several prisoners have studied to the point
of dedication and baptism.
The truth penetrates even walls of monasteries.
In Mexico, in 2009,
a nun was baptized who, because of the truth,
had left her monastery and order,
although she was the mother superior.
The world is in utter confusion.
What a blessing to know the truth!
We rejoice in it!
We have the truth on our lips.
We have the truth around our hips.
Ephesians chapter 6 says that “the belt of truth”
is fastened around our waists.
We are ready to teach it.
We talk the truth, and we walk in the truth.
Those who continue to walk
in the truth will walk in it forever.
Help your students to love the truth
and to live the truth but, if necessary,
to be willing to die for the truth and for Jehovah.
The truth is invincible
and will conquer this wicked world.
In some countries, we may have many enemies
who may want to silence us.
But the apostle Paul said
at 2 Corinthians 13:8:
“For we can do nothing against the truth.”
Neither can our enemies suppress the truth.
Do we appreciate that we have the truth
—the only truth?
Is this arrogant to say? By no means!
It would be a sin if we would not say so.
Jesus was not arrogant when he said:
‘I am the truth.’
To know the truth is not enough.
We need to champion it.
There are still many lovers of truth out there;
search for them.
Who will help you in the search?
According to John 4:23,
Jesus said that Jehovah is searching for ones
that want to worship in truth.
The majority will not listen to the truth
because ‘they love the darkness rather than the light.’
The truth may expose their sinful conduct,
and they may not have the humility
to want to repent and change.
We still have to preach to them —to warn them.
Ezekiel was told:
“You must warn them from me.”
The principle applies to us as well.
Paul speaks of “the sword of . . . God’s word.”
Use it well to champion the truth.
Train your students to be good defenders of it as well.
The time will come in Paradise after the final test
when it will not be necessary
to champion, or defend, the truth,
because nobody will attack it anymore.
Right now, whether we are adults,
teenagers, or children, let us follow and imitate Jesus
—the greatest Champion of truth!
To that end, keep studying the truth.
Keep spreading the truth.
Keep loving the truth and Jehovah, the God of truth.
Hold fast to the truth as to a lifeline
—as this is what it is!
By staying faithful, whether you survive Armageddon
or are resurrected in Paradise,
you will be a victorious champion of the truth!
Let’s now look at some examples of how our brothers and sisters
around the world faithfully champion the truth.
Chris?
Thank you, Brother Lösch.
When a dear friend or perhaps
even a family member leaves the truth,
it can be a very challenging situation.
It can truly be a test of our faith
when we see something like that take place.
While watching this dramatization,
pay attention to how the mother was able to champion the truth
by remaining loyal to Jehovah.
My name is Gabriella.
Ben and I have always enjoyed
attending the meetings.
But lately,
it’s been difficult.
Something was missing
—our son.
It was like watching a movie of someone else’s family.
I couldn’t believe this was happening to us.
Our son, Levi,
was no longer one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The elders and friends in the congregation
were so supportive and understanding.
Many of them watched Levi grow up,
give his first talk,
get baptized.
I was so torn.
I was disappointed in Levi for leaving Jehovah,
but I was more disappointed in myself.
I felt like we failed him somehow.
I kept wondering how he was doing.
Was he OK?
Then, as hard as the past few weeks had been,
it just got harder.
I knew what the Bible said
about “quit mixing in company with anyone”
who is not living according to Christian standards.
But I never thought that scripture would one day apply to me.
Later that evening, a brother was talking
about the example of Korah’s sons.
Jehovah confirmed that He was using Moses
to lead His people, not Korah.
When the people were told to move away
from the rebels’ tents, what would Korah’s sons do?
Would they put loyalty to family ahead of loyalty to Jehovah?
The Bible tells us that his sons remained loyal
to Jehovah and were blessed for it.
That night, after the meeting,
I told Ben about the text I received from Levi.
I told him everything
—how I missed Levi so much,
but that I also wanted to be loyal to Jehovah like Korah’s sons.
Ben admitted that he too
had been struggling with feelings like mine.
But then he said something
that I hadn’t thought of.
If we were to stand between Levi
and the discipline he needs,
we would, in effect, be blocking
an expression of Jehovah’s love
from reaching him.
In fact, it’s our very loyalty
to Jehovah that could save his life.
We agreed to continue to put our trust
in Jehovah and stay loyal to him.
It’s been five years now,
and while Levi still hasn’t returned to Jehovah,
I haven’t given up hope on him.
Until that day,
I’m staying busy as a regular pioneer and focusing my energies
on helping others learn about Jehovah.
I’ve come to experience firsthand
the truth of Psalm 97:10.
Jehovah really does guard his loyal ones.
What helped Gabriella overcome this difficult challenge?
For example,
when she received a text message from her son,
she applied Scriptural counsel
to her personal circumstances.
The good example of Korah’s sons
gave her added motivation so as not to allow
her feelings for her son to dictate her actions.
Instead, she was firm in her loyalty to Jehovah.
Also, her husband, Ben, had found an article
that helped the two of them appreciate
that they should make sure not to stand
between Jehovah and their son, Levi.
Instead, they wanted Jehovah’s expression of love
to reach Levi.
Whenever we are faced with a trial,
we need to remember to pray constantly
to Jehovah for guidance and to look for Jehovah’s counsel
in our literature and during our meetings.
The apostle Paul faced many challenges in his ministry.
In 2 Corinthians chapter 11, starting in verse 23,
he enumerates over 20 hardships
that he experienced in his ministry.
What helped Paul to keep his motivation strong
despite everything he faced?
In this morning worship from Bethel,
Brother John Ekrann highlights
what Paul himself said kept him going.
When you look at the words in the way
that the apostle Paul worded things,
he said: “I live by faith in the Son of God,
who loved me and handed himself over for me.”
And we can really see the very personal nature
of the ransom to the apostle Paul.
And it’s important for us to do
—as our commenters pointed out nicely—
it is important for us to personalize the ransom.
The apostle Paul, in Hebrews 6:5,
showed the very personal nature;
he understood the personal nature
of the Bible and the ransom.
In Hebrews 6:5,
he uses this expression:
“And who have tasted the fine word of God
and powers of the coming system of things.”
Well, it’s interesting he used the word “taste.”
Taste is something very personal.
Somebody can’t taste something for you.
You have to put it in your mouth in order
to really know what it’s going to taste like.
So, too, with the ransom.
And what practical ways can we “taste,”
or personalize, the ransom for us?
Let’s just consider a couple this morning.
One is personal fears.
‘Does God really love me?
Am I worthy of love?’
Sometimes the “what-ifs” and their cousins, the “could-bes,”
they come to live and never leave.
You know, if bad things or trials or difficulties happen to us,
we begin to reason, ‘Well, Jehovah God maybe doesn’t love me.’
There’s really strong reason for us
to somehow believe in cause and effect.
We see the cause of things and effect, and so after a while,
everything that happens to us, we begin to look at some cause
and even begin to think that maybe Jehovah
doesn’t love us.
Even if we’re a good person
and bad things happen to us, we begin to wonder,
‘Others my age are healthy.’
Some leaving or changing assignments,
you hear everything falls into place
for them within a few weeks.
‘I’m still looking for a job. I’m still looking for work.’
In other words, do not try to reason
that just because things don’t work out perfectly
that Jehovah doesn’t love us.
It’s not true.
We can still be doing very, very good things,
and yet some difficulties can face us.
For example, you’re driving down the road,
obeying all the traffic laws.
You pull up to a red light, you stop,
it turns green, you go through it, and you get broadsided
by some knucklehead who went through the red light on the other side.
Well, that’s not your fault.
Are you going to say: “Well, you know what?
I’m not going to obey traffic laws anymore. See, it doesn’t pay!”
Well, no!
It was his fault for running through the traffic light.
And sometimes bad, or difficult, things can happen to us.
It’s not our fault
or it’s not any sign that Jehovah doesn’t love us.
So how can reflecting on the ransom help us
when we have these kinds of personal fears?
Well, we could start with, Why do we have the ransom?
Well, because some very bad things
were happening to some good people
—us— Adam and Eve’s descendants.
I mean, Adam sinned and Eve sinned,
yet we suffer.
The ransom is Jehovah’s solution
for those who appreciate it.
It’s his way of telling us,
‘I know bad things are happening,
and I’m working to fix it.’
Yes, when we reflect on the reason
why Jehovah God gave us the ransom,
it helps us to know that Jehovah knows we suffer
from cancer and old age and the sins and mistakes of others
and even our own imperfections.
See, tasting of the ransom in this way
means we’ll not get the feeling
that Jehovah doesn’t love us when trials befall us.
To the contrary, the ransom
is the greatest expression of Jehovah’s and Jesus’ love for us
and their desire to fix the current mess we live in now.
How about, let’s consider a second way
that we could reflect on the ransom,
and that is the death of someone close to us.
Anyone who’s had someone very close to them die
knows the very helpless feeling that you have,
knowing that there’s really nothing you can do.
In that instant when they die, your hope
—your faith in the resurrection based on the ransom—
becomes more real to you than any time in your entire life.
In Acts 17:31,
in a beautiful speech that the apostle Paul gave,
he highlights
that Jesus’ death
and resurrection and the ransom was really a guarantee
that we have.
Here in Acts 17:31,
he says: “Because he has set a day on which he purposes
“to judge the inhabited earth in righteousness
“by a man whom he has appointed,
“and he has provided a guarantee
“to all men by resurrecting him
from the dead.”
So personalizing the ransom
and all that it makes possible
helps us to know that the resurrection is, not just possible,
but that Jehovah and Jesus want to resurrect
our mother, our father,
our beloved husband or a wife.
They care about each person
that has ever lived or died
and know them so intimately and so completely
that they can resurrect them completely with all their memories
and personality completely as we knew them.
I mean, how much more personal
could God’s love for us become than that?
You know, to bring our loved ones back from the dead
is the ultimate statement
of Jehovah’s personal interest
in each and every human being.
We are not just collateral damage
in Satan’s war on Jehovah.
The ransom is the way
that Jehovah plans to undo all the harm
that Satan has caused
since the death of Adam and Eve.
In fact, the resurrection is really Jehovah’s way
of proving all of Satan’s lies
completely false.
When you think about it today, Satan can perpetrate
all kinds of lies about what happens to people after they die.
‘They’re going to go here, they’re going to go there,
‘they’re going to go to some afterlife, they’re going to go to some paradise,
they’re going to come back as some animal.’
But in the new world,
when the vast majority of people
have been resurrected,
that lie isn’t going to be sold anymore.
Each one can tell everyone
what happened to them when they died
—nothing,
no afterlife.
Everyone will know that it’s nonexistence.
That lie won’t work.
See, Jehovah knew
that we would hurt terribly
at the death of loved ones,
so he gave us the ransom
as his way of telling us,
‘I know it hurts, but please know
that I have the perfect solution in mind.’
Now, we’ve just considered two ways
to reflect and meditate on the ransom,
like the apostle Paul did, to really personalize it.
We just talked about personal fears
and the resurrection,
the death of someone close to us.
Imagine how many more ways
we can benefit today
from meditating on the ransom
and how it affects us personally.
As ministers of Jehovah,
we take part in preaching the good news.
That good news includes the wonderful provision
of the ransom Brother Ekrann highlighted.
Have you ever participated in a preaching campaign?
I’m sure you have enjoyed campaigns
such as inviting our neighbors to the Memorial
or the regional convention.
On occasion, other campaigns are approved
by the Service Committee of the Governing Body
when there is a specific need in an area or language group.
We bring you a report
on a special campaign in Armenia.
Armenia is an ancient country with rich history,
situated in the lands of Mount Ararat.
In the Caucasus region, Lake Sevan
is considered to be a prized jewel.
Diversity of its flora and fauna
contribute to the unique and beautiful countryside.
Yerevan, the capital,
is a modern metropolis with picturesque views
that remind many of Paris with its trees, cafés,
and beautiful water fountains.
Recently, a special three-week preaching campaign took place.
Groups of Armenian-speaking Jehovah’s Witnesses
from six different countries
wholeheartedly responded to the invitation.
The main purpose of the campaign was to cover as many
of the 512 unassigned territories as possible
with the Kingdom good news.
Thus, an opportunity
for an interchange of encouragement was created
for both the local friends and the campaign participants.
They were warmly greeted at the airport
by local brothers and sisters.
The Witnesses made good use of their tablets and smartphones to show
videos from the jw.org website.
Armenia is also currently home
to over 11,000 Western-Armenian refugees.
A special effort was made to share with these individuals
the positive message of hope and peace from the Bible
in their native tongue, West Armenian.
Metropolitan witnessing served as an effective way
to reach these ones.
It was the first time in my life
that I participated in public witnessing,
and it was very encouraging.
When individuals would approach us and show interest,
I could explain to them the truth in their own language.
It was amazing.
It’s been very heartwarming.
People have really responded well.
They were in need of comfort
and the good news, especially those that
we came for, the Western Armenians.
Pretty much every door invited us in,
and they were very hospitable and receptive.
After we heard the announcement about the special campaign
in the Western language that’s going to take place in Armenia,
we said: “We cannot miss this.
“We have to be there and bring our share
in this very joyful preaching campaign.”
During the three-week campaign,
over 15,000 pieces
of Bible-based literature were left with interested ones,
and over 200 Bible studies were started.
We were very happy to see
how many brothers and sisters were ready to come
for the campaign in Armenia
from different countries around the world.
That response showed
that Jehovah has blessed our efforts.
Those who came from far and wide
greatly appreciated the share
they had in this special event.
Everyone was so happy to see us.
And when we were giving them a Bible,
they were so excited to find answers from their own Bible.
I’m so blessed to be here.
This has been the best vacation
that we have had as a family.
The first time I came to Armenia,
it was in 1982.
And I looked for the Witnesses,
and I hardly found just a few.
But now that I came for this campaign,
we have 11,000 Witnesses!
I’m really so happy! I really want to come back!
It is our hope that Jehovah God continues to help
all sorts of people to be saved
and come to an accurate knowledge of truth.
While we enjoy relative freedom
in many countries around the world,
at times governments impose bans
or restrictions on the preaching work.
Brother Stephanos Demsas
serves as a special pioneer in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia,
along with his wife, Leteberhan.
Their faith was tested during many years of adversity.
What helped them champion the truth?
Their story began in what is today Eritrea.
I come from a family of nine children.
I joined the navy in 1956.
That was during the time
when Eritrea was part of Ethiopia.
My brother Gebrehiwot
asked me to come to Asmara.
He was studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I was so impressed with what he shared with me
that for the rest of my vacation,
Bible study became my priority.
In time, I was discharged from the navy
and started working in Addis Ababa,
so I was able to continue studying
the Bible and get baptized.
Leti was also doing the same.
In 1960, I was attending a nursing college.
There, a nurse shared some interesting thoughts
with me from the Bible.
Ten other student nurses also showed interest.
But the college threatened us with dismissal
because there was a ban on Jehovah’s Witnesses.
When we were shown from the Bible
why true Christians are persecuted,
we renewed our determination.
Eventually, five of us were baptized.
In time, I met Stephanos,
and we were married in 1964.
Because of the ban,
the brothers were meeting in small groups.
Our trust was in Jehovah, and we made the preaching work
a matter of prayer, confident that he would help us.
We saw evidence of this
with the underground production of The Watchtower.
Our brothers were of modest means,
but they used what they had to buy a hand-operated duplicating machine
which was used in our home.
After returning from our secular work,
Leti and I would get busy making copies of The Watchtower.
We would play music so our neighbors
wouldn’t hear the sound of the duplicator.
Emperor Haile Selassie was deposed.
This Communist government quickly began
a campaign called “Red Terror”
against any supposed political opposer.
Now, just having a typewriter or a duplicating machine
could put you in prison or even have you killed.
Picking up a paper from the street
with something printed on it against the government
could put one’s life in danger.
It was common for people to disappear.
Sadly, my youngest brother,
Eyob, was a victim.
He disappeared on his way home
and was never seen again.
With the situation being very dangerous,
we were quite concerned
raising our daughter, Janet.
But as we fully trusted in Jehovah,
we felt his loving protection.
From time to time, sections of the city
were suddenly blockaded.
This happened one morning as a translator
was heading to our home to deliver stencils for printing.
Urgently, he telephoned
informing us that a house-to-house search
was under way.
Our house was full of publications
along with a duplicator and typewriters!
Just after the phone call,
three soldiers entered our compound to search.
At that moment,
I prayed silently that Jehovah would blind them.
Entering the room where the duplicator
and stacks of freshly printed literature were,
one soldier asked, “What is all this?”
“Oh, this is a duplicator that we use
to print these Bible materials.”
Completing his search,
he went outside to the commander,
who asked him, “What did you find?”
To our utter amazement,
after seeing everything, he answered:
“Nothing! We won’t find anything here.”
In the late 1970’s and into the early 80’s,
another wave of vicious persecution occurred.
A number of faithful brothers were imprisoned,
tortured, and murdered.
I was taken from my work place because of my neutral stand
and put in prison.
When I think about living through those difficult times,
I am reminded of Isaiah 54:17
where Jehovah promised us:
“No weapon formed against you will have any success.”
Finally, in 1991,
a liberal government came to power.
They gave us legal recognition
and freedom of worship.
With these difficult, dangerous years
now behind us, we were assigned to the circuit work
in Eritrea and Ethiopia.
By now, Eritrea was becoming
an independent country, and this brought about
new challenges for the brothers.
Some young brothers were arrested and imprisoned
because of their Christian stand.
Paul wrote at Hebrews 13:3:
“Keep in mind those in prison,
as though you were imprisoned with them.”
After enjoying the circuit work
for 15 years, we faced another change.
We were invited to serve at Bethel
as full-time commuters.
What has helped us to endure through the ban years
and to adjust to the many changes
is our spiritual study program.
We’re in full agreement
with Jeremiah 17:7:
“Blessed is the man
who puts his trust in Jehovah.”
It also brings us much happiness
to know that our daughter, Janet, has been serving
as a regular pioneer for 20 years now.
Each assignment has had its challenges
but many rewards and blessings.
I’m not young anymore;
I’m 77 years old.
And I’m 74 years old.
We are now serving as special pioneers.
When we think about all the changes that we’ve been through,
we realize that the words at Isaiah 6:8:
“Here I am! Send me!”
are, not just for young people, but for all of us.
It is very encouraging to see
Stephanos and Leteberhan’s determination
to stay faithful to Jehovah, come what may.
We know that Jehovah looks with delight
on their many years of service.
Some of our brothers in Canada
underwent similar persecution.
How did Jehovah help them?
Pay special attention to the numerous acts of courage
displayed by these champions of truth.
Preaching in the province of Quebec was a real challenge.
The Catholic Church
was present in every sphere of public life.
In the early ’40s, the persecution
took on quite a bit
of emphasis.
Many Witnesses were being arrested.
Any excuse was used.
Peddling without a license
—this was a favorite excuse.
Jehovah’s Witnesses were put in prison
whenever they were seen with religious literature.
It had got so bad in Quebec
that it was decided to circulate a petition,
and this petition was circulated throughout Canada.
And it called on the government of Quebec
to put an end to this persecution.
And interestingly,
some 600,000 people signed the petition.
The Witnesses distributed
a very fiery tract
called the Burning Hate of Quebec.
And in this tract,
they showed what was really happening
—the actions of the policemen,
the illegal arrests, the mob action.
Within four months,
there were 800 new court cases.
So here, for 400 Jehovah’s Witnesses,
you had 1,600 court cases.
The seriousness
of the court cases increased, in that now
they were accusing the brothers of sedition.
If convicted, it was more than 10
—maybe 12 or 15— years in prison.
We had one brother, Aimé Boucher,
who was arrested and charged with sedition.
Aimé Boucher was a very poor brother,
who lived in a rural part of Quebec.
And he actually
went to court with his ox and buggy.
And on the way to court,
he was preaching, so he was arrested again.
They had the court hearing, and he was condemned.
He was found guilty of sedition.
And his case went up to the Court of Appeal
—and at that time, the Court of Appeal of Quebec was very hostile—
and he lost on appeal,
so it went up to the Supreme Court of Canada.
And by this time,
there were several other brothers and sisters
also charged on sedition,
which meant that if he lost his case,
we had several going to prison
for very lengthy prison terms.
When Brother Boucher’s case
came before the Supreme Court,
he lost by a majority of one.
The Catholic judges all ruled against him,
and they found that the tract
the Burning Hate of Quebec was seditious.
Our lawyers looked at the situation,
prayed about it, and thought:
‘What can we do? We can’t lose this battle.’
And they realized that in Canada
there was a very rarely used provision
of asking the Supreme Court for a rehearing.
At the rehearing, one of the Catholic judges
was willing to discuss further
the issue of sedition.
And to be guilty of sedition,
you have to incite to violence.
So our attorney asked them:
“Please, look at the record.
“Show the court where Jehovah’s Witnesses
incited to violence.”
And finally, they were able to convince a court they were wrong.
And so they overturned their initial decision,
and Brother Boucher’s case
was victorious.
This dealt with all the accusations of sedition
and really brought to an end the vicious opposition,
because that case was the one the government
was hoping would work out for them.
There is one case that’s quite noteworthy in Quebec.
And it’s a case of the priest
calling up the federal police
to come and interrupt
a meeting of Jehovah’s Witnesses
and expel the speaker from the province of Quebec.
The police obeyed the priest.
They went to the meeting, they took the brother,
and they escorted him out of the province into Ontario.
And to disrupt a religious meeting was a criminal act.
For the first time —and it’s at the level of the Supreme Court—
they found that the three policemen
had to pay moral damages to the brothers
for intercepting, or interrupting, the meeting.
This has never happened before.
And when it came up to the Supreme Court,
they unanimously ruled
against the province of Quebec.
The section on religious freedom
is the result of these court cases.
Every lawyer in Canada (whether in Quebec or in English Canada),
when he studies law, must review these cases.
They are the fundamentals of religious freedom.
And they represent the different areas
—police action, government action, criminal action—
and they lay a very nice basis
for our freedoms today.
Our purpose is to be able to preach the good news
and to direct people’s attention toward the Bible.
But our court cases have helped governments,
courts, judges,
and officials to have the right point of view
on the issue of religious freedom.
The endurance and hard work of our brothers in Quebec
truly resulted in a witness to the nations.
While the hope for a positive outcome
can at times provide us with needed motivation,
we can’t always expect support
from the authorities in this system of things.
The same applies in many areas of life,
whatever trials we may face.
Perhaps you have lost a loved one in death.
Looking forward to a time just around the corner
can help us endure.
That’s also the title of this month’s music video,
Just Around the Corner.
You can hear the songbirds singing, And you watch the clouds roll by.
Then you’re walking in the valley As the sun shines in a clear blue sky.
You’re welcoming your loved ones, And you can’t believe your eyes.
Yes, this earthly Paradise Was just around the corner.
There’s a house down in the valley And a house high on the hill.
There is singing by the river As the water flows and turns the mill.
The golden fields are waiting. Let the harvesting begin.
Once the world we’re living in Was just around the corner.
It’s great to share with friends who care The things that we looked forward to.
Now every tear has disappeared. The world is young, and life is new.
There’s the sound of happy voices And the scent of new mown hay.
Now you’re calling to your loved ones As you start another perfect day.
Then we thank our God, Jehovah, For his tender loving care.
Yes, the blessings we all share Were just around the corner.
And evʹry day I smile and say, “How good to see your happy face!”
ʹCause once, it seemed, I only dreamed That you’d be in my warm embrace.
Waiting ʹround the corner Is a world I long to see.
It’s a promise from Jehovah. It’s a guaranteed reality.
And it’s hard to get downhearted When I think of what’s in store.
It’s the day I’m waiting for, And it’s just around the corner.
What a beautiful song!
Personally, I lost my father
when I was two years old.
He was a soldier in World War II and was killed in battle.
I never had an opportunity to get to know him.
Growing up, I missed having a father
because I saw everyone else had one.
So I look forward to observing the earthly resurrection
and seeing my physical father,
and I hope that both he and my mother
will want to worship Jehovah in Paradise.
Thank you for sharing that, Brother Lösch.
When my father comes back in the resurrection,
I look forward to welcoming him with open arms.
He was a keen student of history and the Bible,
and so he will want to know all about what took place
during this time of the end.
So my family and I will have a good time
filling him in on what took place.
This music video and some of the videos we’ve seen
the past few years at regional conventions
have painted such a clear picture
of the hope we have for the future.
And if we work hard as champions of the truth,
that hope will become a reality very soon.
Well said.
And speaking of champions of the truth,
we would like to conclude this program
with greetings from our brothers and sisters in Romania,
a country situated in the southeast of Europe.
Some of you may know Romania
for its traditional instrument
called the nai, or pan flute.
It’s made of wood and has around 20 pipes,
arranged in a curved array.
The pitch is adjusted with beeswax,
which is introduced in the pipes.
The brothers and sisters
in the Certeze North Congregation,
in the north of Romania, send us their love.
The congregation is located near the Ukrainian border,
an area known for its brightly colored folk costumes.
The congregation is made up of families
with many generations of Witnesses,
so they have been champions of truth
for a long time.
The truth reached this area
about 80 years ago, and now the congregation
is made up of 126 publishers.
They conduct about 90 Bible studies,
of which many attend the meetings.
Because there is a large concentration
of Witnesses in the area, the congregation territory
is only five kilometers,
or a little over three miles, from the one end to the other.
Each territory card has only about five houses.
Because of that, the congregation
regularly assists with working territory
up to 200 kilometers,
or about 124 miles away.
The brothers and sisters
of the Certeze North Congregation
send all of you champions of the truth
their love and greetings
and so do all of us at world headquarters.
This is JW Broadcasting in Brooklyn, New York.

en.text: I have learned that Jehovah can support me
under any circumstances.
I was born and raised in Karaganda, Kazakhstan.
When I was 25,
I lost my job.
A special pioneer brother from my congregation asked me,
“Why don’t you use this opportunity
to start pioneering?”
But I wasn’t sure if someone like me could pioneer.
Because he said, “Don’t worry,
I’ll support you and help you,”
I decided to give it a try.
And that brother kept his word.
He worked with me and helped me in my service.
Sometime later,
I was encouraged to apply for MTS
by our circuit overseer who had graduated
from the first class in Russia.
Even though I thought it was beyond my ability,
I listened to him and was able to attend
the fourth class.
Before graduation,
a brother on the Branch Committee asked me
if I would be willing to serve in Mongolia
as a special pioneer.
Immediately, I said yes
because I was ready to serve anywhere.
But when I realized
how much responsibility
comes with serving in a foreign assignment,
I started to wonder if I could serve in Mongolia
with my limited experience.
After graduating
in February 1999,
I arrived in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
It was about -30°C (-22°F).
There was no snow, just a dust storm.
I’d never seen anything like it before.
At that time, 17 publishers were serving in Mongolia.
When preaching,
I would recite the introduction,
and then a local publisher would continue the conversation.
Back then, everyone invited us in,
offered us tea and candy, and listened to us.
But I was upset because I couldn’t understand everything.
Often, I had to work alone
in the ministry without knowing the language.
I supplicated
Jehovah for courage
and often reflected that, right at that moment,
it was like there was no one else preaching
in all of Mongolia but me
and that the angels were watching over me.
This thinking gave me the strength
to continue preaching.
In 2001, I married a wonderful sister, Norie.
Jehovah truly blesses our efforts when we give him
our best and pray intensely.
He has helped me many times
and has patiently trained me.
And because of that,
I’ve been able to serve here
for 17 years.
I’m very grateful that we
have been able to help 20 people
come to know Jehovah.
Knowing that people, like me,
with little experience
can be used by Jehovah and his organization,
helps me appreciate
Jehovah’s mercy and patience.
I thank Jehovah from the bottom of my heart.

en.text: My name is Petr Muzny.
I studied law in different universities in Europe
—in France, England, Czech Republic—
and eventually I had my PhD,
which I defended in 2004.
I had become a Doctor of Law.
I was born in former Czechoslovakia,
under the Communist regime,
where religion or religious beliefs were not promoted.
And also the thought of God being a Creator of the universe
was considered as nonsense.
Concerning evolution,
I was, I would say, merely following
the mainstream thinking.
But I came to realize
that we should really question
things that are around us,
all the theories and explanations that are given.
But we shouldn’t take as granted all that we hear,
and especially when somebody
says that this thing is obvious,
or evident, so just don’t question.
Obey, or listen to it.
I’m now a specialist in law
and in logic —human thinking—
and there is one basic principle
which pervades the whole universe.
It’s the principle of cause and effect.
So every effect around us must have a cause.
You walk in a forest, and there,
right in the middle of the forest, you see a bench.
The bench is the effect. What is the cause?
Is this accidental or deliberate?
Somebody must have made it,
because the principle is: Something designed
must have a designer.
For me, when I see such diversity
of flowers, of trees, of butterflies,
I come to the conclusion:
The One who put that law of diversity
was there to tell us,
‘Please, enjoy life.’
Because life is beautiful,
somebody who created it must be
somebody having beautiful qualities.
Thanks to the study of the Bible,
I could put a picture,
a face —symbolically speaking—
to the One who created life.

根本是很荒谬的想法
对于进化论
我只能说
自己只是跟着那时候的主流思想走
不过 后来我发现
我们应该要有追根究底的精神
对于一些理论或别人提出的解释
我们不该全盘接受
特别是如果有人说
“这是事实 证据很明显
没什么好怀疑的
只要相信 接受就好”
我专门研究法律和逻辑学
也就是探讨人类的思考模式
在宇宙中有一个很基本不变的定律
叫因果定律
根据这个定律
每件事的发生都必定有个原因
举个例
你在森林中散步时看到一张长椅
长椅的存在是结果
那原因是什么?
碰巧? 还是人为?
当然有人制造
根据因果定律
既然一样物品是经过设计的
就一定有设计者
当我看到种类繁多的
花草 树木和蝴蝶
我得到一个结论
把这些东西设计得
这么多彩多姿的创造主
好像在告诉我们
“好好享受人生吧!”
既然生命这么美好
创造生命的那位
一定也具有很多美好的特质
我很庆幸能学习圣经
现在我好像可以清楚看到
创造主的样貌
他是真实存在的

en.text: Our worldwide brotherhood is truly special.
When our brothers are in need,
we want to help in whatever way possible.
It also brings us great joy to be with our brothers
—whether at the meetings, in the field service,
or on other occasions.
We love our brothers and enjoy spending time with them.
At the same time, because we are all imperfect,
our love and unity will be tested.
We may have our feelings hurt,
or we may hurt the feelings of others.
That brings me to the theme I would like to discuss
with you in this month’s program,
“Settling Differences Brings Jehovah’s Favor.”
It is based on Matthew 6:14.
Let’s read this important verse together.
Right after teaching his disciples how to pray,
Jesus says in verse 14:
“For if you forgive men their trespasses,
your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
To what extent do Jesus’ words affect how Jehovah
views what we do each day in our worship to him?
Consider this:
You’re concluding your day in prayer.
You pray for Jehovah’s name to be sanctified.
You pray for his Kingdom to come.
You ask that he bless the Governing Body
and the brothers taking the lead.
You share with him a few matters
of personal concern.
And then you say: “Jehovah,
“I know I am imperfect,
“and I sin against you often.
“Please forgive me for my sins.
“Let me stand before you
in a clean and approved state.”
Now the question is,
Has Jehovah heard your heartfelt request?
Will he forgive you?
Well, what did Jesus say?
Look again at verse 14:
“For if you forgive men their trespasses,
your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
Did you notice Jesus’ use of the word “if”?
That tells us that forgiveness is not automatic.
It comes with a condition, or price.
What price?
According to Jesus, ‘if we forgive others,’
the condition has been met;
the price has been paid.
What will Jehovah do for us?
Jesus said: “[He] will also forgive you.”
Really, though, is it fair or reasonable
for Jehovah to say to us,
‘Only if you forgive others,
then I will also forgive you’?
Well, suppose you get very sick and lose your job.
You’re unable to pay rent for many months.
Your situation is desperate.
You have very few, if any, options.
You worry about your wife and your children.
Say you go to the owner of the house and ask
if he would give you time to get back on your feet.
Once you get better and are able to work again,
you will do everything within your power
to pay him what you owe.
He tells you not to worry.
He understands your situation.
He will cancel your debt,
and you do not have to pay him any rent
until your situation improves.
In fact, he’ll cover your monthly expenses
until you are able to care for your family.
How would you feel about what he has done,
and would this affect how you treat others?
Well, because of our sinful nature,
we are all in debt to Jehovah
—deserving of death.
We are unable to cover our expenses.
But when we go to Jehovah in prayer
and beg for his help,
in his great mercy and kindness,
he tells us not to worry.
He has given the life of his Son to pay our debt.
And on the basis of that sacrifice,
He is willing to cover our expenses
—the sins we commit daily—
and to extend forgiveness to us until we are able
to get back on our feet,
when we reach perfection in the new world.
So think again about those simple yet powerful words
of Jesus at Matthew 6:14:
“For if you forgive men their trespasses,
your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
Is that fair?
Is that reasonable?
Is it realistic?
Without a doubt!
In fact, settling differences,
or forgiving others freely,
is one of the best ways to imitate
Jehovah’s compassionate and merciful nature.
What can help us to settle differences quickly?
The first thing we should do is to try
and let love cover over the wrong.
Can I just forgive and forget?
If we are able to do so,
this is a beautiful way to maintain
the congregation’s peace and unity.
But if we’re struggling to forget the wrong,
there are two scriptures that are especially helpful
in this matter of settling differences.
They are Matthew 5:23, 24
and Matthew 18:15-17.
Keep in mind that these texts
are not referring to the same scenarios,
nor are they to be applied
in the exact same way.
Matthew chapter 5
has a broader application
and can be used to bring peace
in most situations.
Matthew chapter 18
has a more limited application
and applies to specific situations
that are more serious in nature.
Now let’s consider the first text,
Matthew 5:23, 24:
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
“and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
“leave your gift there in front of the altar, and go away.
“First make your peace with your brother,
and then come back and offer your gift.”
To truly capture what these two brief verses mean
for you and me today,
we have to understand what Jesus’ words meant
to his first-century Jewish listeners.
Picture the scene in your mind as we transport ourselves
into the city of Jerusalem some 2,000 years ago.
It is during one of the annual festivals.
There are tens of thousands of people in the city.
You are there to make your sacrifice —a beautiful lamb.
The best one you have.
It’s clean and unblemished.
You take the lamb through a series of courts
all the way to the Court of Priests.
It has taken you most of the day to get there.
Now you’re ready to put your hands on that animal
and offer a prayer for forgiveness,
and then you remember something.
What?
Verse 23 reads:
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
“and there you remember that your brother
has something against you,”
Now you think: ‘My brother
‘does have something against me!
‘The last time I saw him,
‘he greeted everybody else but me.
‘He was upset. But what is it?
‘I don’t remember doing anything.
‘He is so sensitive!
He’s always upset with something.’
Did Jesus have all of that in mind
when he said what he did in verse 23?
No!
He did not go into detail
about what that “something” might be.
He doesn’t say who is right or wrong.
He doesn’t make a comment
about whether someone is too sensitive,
always getting upset, never satisfied,
difficult to get along with.
Why not?
Because the reason behind the “something”
is not the important thing.
What is the important thing?
That the peace has been disturbed.
There is a difference that needs to be settled.
The lack of peace between brothers
could affect their relationship with Jehovah.
That is important!
So what should be done?
We see the answer in verse 24:
“Leave your gift there
“in front of the altar, and go away.
“First make your peace with your brother,
and then come back and offer your gift.”
That animal sacrifice is important too.
There’s no doubt about that.
It represents worship to Jehovah
—like going to the meetings, in the field service,
sharing in family worship.
But according to Jesus,
what is more important?
It is settling the difference
—making peace with our brother first.
Then we will be in an acceptable position
to offer our gift of worship to Jehovah.
Yes, settling differences will bring Jehovah’s favor.
But when can we apply the principle of Matthew 5?
Whenever there is a difference to be settled.
Perhaps our brother misunderstood what we said or did.
Or maybe he didn’t misunderstand
—maybe we did give him a valid reason to be hurt.
Regardless, we notice
that he has something against us.
In that case, we make peace.
We can also use the principles of this text
when we are hurt or have something
against our brother.
We can take the initiative ourselves
to settle misunderstandings,
to resolve differences,
and to make peace with our brother.
Again, Jehovah blesses such a spirit.
Now, open your Bible to Matthew chapter 18.
We mentioned earlier that it has
a more limited application.
How so?
Notice verse 15:
“Moreover, if your brother commits a sin,
“go and reveal his fault between you and him alone.
If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.”
Here Jesus says, “if your brother commits a sin.”
That is much different than just having
“something against [us].”
We are talking about a situation that is much more serious.
What situation?
The revised Organized to Do Jehovah’s Will book,
page 136, explains
that it “involves financial or property matters,
“such as failing to repay a loan
“or committing fraud.
“Or the offense might be slander,
which seriously affects someone’s reputation.”
Of course, they are sins that could be resolved
between the individuals concerned
but are also serious enough
to merit expulsion from the congregation if not settled.
Before we start applying Matthew 18:15,
we should first consider whether it is really necessary
to pursue the matter.
Could we simply forgive the individual
for what was done or even take the loss
if it were a financial matter?
That is a personal decision.
If we decide to pursue the matter,
what do we do?
Jesus helps us in verse 15, when he says
that we reveal his fault
between the two of us alone.
We do not discuss the matter with others,
attempting to get them to side with us.
We do not go straight to the elders
and try to get them to solve the problem for us.
No, we try to resolve the matter between us.
And since our goal is to settle the difference,
maintain our relationship with Jehovah,
and help our brother do the same,
we make repeated efforts to speak with him
when our initial efforts are unsuccessful.
Keep in mind that Jesus did not say:
“Go only once and reveal his fault.”
When applying this first step, make it clear
that your motive is to ‘gain your brother.’
Also, it would be helpful to clearly state
that you are applying the first step in settling differences
as outlined by Jesus at Matthew 18:15.
Of course, this would be stated in a kindly,
nonthreatening manner
but still in a way to show the seriousness
of getting the matter settled.
What if the first step
in gaining your brother is unsuccessful?
Notice verse 16 explains step 2:
“But if he does not listen,
“take along with you one or two more,
“so that on the testimony of two or three witnesses
every matter may be established.”
Yes, we talk with him in the company of one or two more.
Would that be our best friends?
No.
The whole purpose is to ‘gain our brother.’
Teaming up with two of our best friends
could alienate our brother.
Instead, it makes sense
that we would choose other mature Christians.
How would mature Christians be helpful?
Well, are we misunderstanding things?
Could they help him to reason about the matter?
Could a solution be found?
Having spiritually mature witnesses there
may help to resolve the matter.
Generally, applying steps 1
and 2 will result in gaining your brother
and preserving the peace of the congregation.
If he does not respond to these repeated efforts
to help him, then what?
You have a decision to make.
Are you willing to forgive your brother,
even take a loss if a financial matter is involved?
If you choose to pursue the matter further,
listen to Jesus’ words recorded
at verse 17:
“If he does not listen to them,
“speak to the congregation.
“If he does not listen even to the congregation,
“let him be to you just as a man of the nations
and as a tax collector.”
At this point, the body of elders
representing the congregation will get involved.
They will review the facts of the case and determine
if a judicial committee should be appointed.
Happily, though, these situations are rare,
and matters are often resolved peacefully
before reaching such a serious point.
Think back again to that heartfelt prayer to Jehovah.
Has Jehovah heard our sincere requests?
Will he forgive?
Well, at this moment,
if you realize there is a difference with your brother
that needs to be settled,
pray to Jehovah about the matter.
Ask him to help you see
beyond the emotion and make peace.
Do not let any more time go by!
Once we have followed the simple steps outlined by Jesus
and have forgiven others,
the condition has been met;
the price has been paid.
Then what will Jehovah do for us?
Jesus said:
‘He will also forgive us.’
As a result, we will gain the peace of mind
that comes with a clean conscience,
knowing that we have Jehovah’s favor and blessing.
We can then make a valuable contribution
to the beautiful, united brotherhood
that we are privileged to be a part of.

en.text: On September 23, 2015, it was announced
at all branches that the Governing Body was requesting
all Bethel families to reduce in size.
For me personally,
when they made that announcement
on Wednesday, September 23,
that was exciting.
It was—
I knew it was momentous.
When the announcement was made,
tears welled up in my eyes
because I realized how close we are
to the end.
And I remember just closing my eyes
and saying to Jehovah,
“Whatever you want, we’ll do.”
When I received news of my reassignment,
initially I was numb.
When I got the news
about my reassignment,
I was so scared in the beginning.
It caught me off guard.
I wasn’t expecting it.
We were quite shocked and sad,
but we were encouraged by the brothers
at Bethel and also in the congregation.
The direction from the Governing Body
was that we were being reassigned
as regular pioneers.
We signed the forms for pioneering that very Thursday.
For me, I’ve always appreciated the scripture at 1 Samuel 12:22
where it states there: “For the sake of his great name,
Jehovah will not abandon his people.”
I don’t want to forget my Bethel time,
because it was lovely,
but I want to stretch forward ahead
to pioneering and really enjoy it.
We prayed specifically for a place
that is going to help us to be as simple
as possible so that we can focus our attention to the ministry.
All that I’d love to say to everyone who has been reassigned
is that Jehovah is our Father,
and he will never relinquish his responsibility as a Father.
He will take care of us.
We are losing four couples
from our congregation.
And I would like to tell
the congregations where they have been assigned to
that they are getting real spiritual people
and that they are really going to be an asset
to their congregation.
I just want to also thank
the brothers in the congregation where we are going to
because they organized secular work for us
and also, as Bonnie mentioned, accommodation.
So they made it easier for us
to look forward to our assignment.
But we know this, of course, comes from Jehovah.
And so the Branch Committee said,
“Well, we have to move quickly with this.”
We asked the family,
“Please, give us two, three weeks to work things out,”
and that is what they appreciated.
Congregations phoned in.
The Bethelites were offered jobs.
They were offered accommodation.
Our congregation is delighted
having two young Bethelites
coming and joining us.
Our congregation has quite a number of young people.
We can already see that
it’s going to benefit them quite a lot.
We’ve actually assisted them
in getting a place where they could stay,
and also we’ve assisted them to settle in
and be part of the congregation.
Welcome to our new home!
We’ve been here a little over a week now.
The brothers helped to paint the house,
to put tiles on, to clean the entire place.
So they really did a lot of work in our behalf.
Also, memories of our friends from Bethel.
It was about six months ago
when we enjoyed pioneer school.
Thanks to our brothers, we were able to find employment.
Jehovah has been answering our prayers,
and sometimes he has been answering
our concerns even before we even pray about it.
No doubt,
these extraordinary experiences in South Africa
are mirrored all over the world.
The love we show to each other is a reflection
of Jehovah’s great love for each of us,
and we thank him to be a part
of this amazing brotherhood.

en.text: There’s something common to every successful marriage
between two Christians.
It is their putting Jehovah first
and supporting each other’s personal dedication to God.
This is certainly true with Viv and Ann Mouritz,
serving in the Australasia branch.
They’ve been married for 65 years
and have a combined 131 years
in full-time service.
Listen to their advice for younger ones
deciding what to do in Jehovah’s organization.
I started pioneering in November 1948.
That’s a while ago now.
And that’s what I thought I would do—pioneer.
So I said, “Well, Jehovah, if I do what you ask me,
“I accept whatever assignment you give me,
“and I’ll just go where you send me,
and I won’t seek an assignment, but I won’t refuse one.”
That’s all I intended to do as far as I knew,
but then I had only been pioneering about a year
when I got this envelope, and the letter said:
“Please fill in the enclosed form.”
It was an application for Bethel, and I thought,
‘Goodness, I didn’t think of Bethel.
I told Jehovah I’d go where he sent me, so don’t argue, just do it.’
I was working in the printery cleaning out old ink tins
and making schedules for printing and so on.
And then I got to work on the press too,
but I wasn’t there very long when they moved me to the office.
Well, you learn a lot in Bethel.
You learn how to live with your brothers,
which you’re not used to.
You learn about Jehovah’s organization —you see how it operates.
I had the privilege of working alongside brothers who had lots of experience.
I got assigned to Metropolitan Congregation.
That’s where Ann was.
Yeah, we got married in October 1951,
and two weeks later,
I started pioneering.
I was 20 at that time when we started circuit work,
and I’d only pioneered for a year;
so of course I was very worried
and scared about having to witness with sisters
that had pioneered for years and some of them even of the anointed.
I cried halfway to Melbourne.
We got very close to the brothers and sisters
and especially to the children, so we really loved that.
And then we got the opportunity to go
to New York to the international convention
When the Society found out we were going, they sent us
an application for Gilead, and we thought, ‘Oh, my goodness.
How can we do that?’
So we said, “Well, we don’t say no.”
After the ‘58 convention,
we were assigned to special pioneer
in Canada for six months.
Brother Knorr said we were in cold storage,
so there were about 40 of us
from British Commonwealth countries.
So that was a good experience too.
We saw winter for the first time. I did, anyway.
And we took pictures of snow and ice and icicles
to show in our assignment when we got into India or Africa or somewhere.
And Jehovah had a sense of humor; he sent us to Finland.
Well, the schooling you get from Gilead
or the other schools
helps you to see Jehovah’s organization
and how it works.
We didn’t know a lot about Finland except that we knew it was cold
and clean
and a long way from Australia.
Being so far from Australia,
we knew that we wouldn’t be able to get home
to see our families, not for a long, long time.
When we moved into Finland, the brothers
in Russia and those countries were under ban.
They needed spiritual food,
and so it had to be supplied to them.
So we used to send people in as tourists, and they would meet
the brothers there and deliver the food to them.
Without Jehovah’s blessing and his spirit,
we couldn’t have done it at all.
It’s amazing to think that the amount of spiritual food
that got in there, they translated it,
and they made it available.
And we did that for over 20 years
without any mishaps.
It couldn’t happen without Jehovah’s blessing.
Leaving Finland was not easy, of course.
We had mixed feelings,
but, actually, I saw Jehovah’s hand
in the assignment
because we really got back to Australia
at a time when my parents were needing help,
so we didn’t have to leave Bethel
or full-time service to give that help.
We were asked to go to Russia in 1999.
That turned out to be two and a half years.
I was a little apprehensive about going to Russia,
but it was really one of the most memorable assignments
we’ve ever had.
In Russia, the brothers were not used to house-to-house work
because of all the years under ban.
And that was quite different because you go to the door;
you can’t just strike up a conversation.
The person wants to know why you are there.
And you can’t make
a return visit on someone you met on the street
—well, you don’t know where he lives.
If you’ve called at his house, you do, and you can make a return visit.
The brothers saw the advantage of that.
But they had to learn. It was a new thing.
Circuit overseers had to learn how to visit congregations,
and Polish brothers came in and helped a lot with that
—did circuit work— but they too had to learn.
So it was a big change for them
to come from working under ban all their lives
to now working the way the rest of the world does.
The best decision I ever made
was to put my life in Jehovah’s hands,
and to say, “You decide
where I go and what I do.”
I’ve had the feeling all along, and it’s proven true so far,
that everything I have done
has been training for something else.
So, what I’m doing now is still training.
It must be for the new world because I haven’t got
much time left in this one.
What will it be? Well, who knows?
So my recommendation to everyone is:
Don’t decide for yourself.
Let Jehovah do it.
Brother and Sister Mouritz always looked to Jehovah
for their assignments.
For Brother Mouritz, that’s meant serving
on the Branch Committees in Finland, India,
Russia, Poland, Ukraine,
and Australasia
and the privilege of making visits
to more than 70 countries
as a representative of world headquarters.
We can certainly pursue any form of service
that our circumstances allow.
But when we pray for Jehovah’s direction,
we rely on him to send us
where it benefits his organization
and ourselves the most.

en.text: Well, the big day finally arrived.
After all those months of preparation,
it was just as I imagined.
Oh wait!
That’s not me.
That’s me.
As I watched my sister get married that day,
I couldn’t help but think about my own future.
When I began dating Shane,
everything was perfect.
We spent a lot of time talking on the phone.
Everything just naturally seemed to click.
I was convinced he was the one.
But over time, I started to notice some things.
I was starting to see patterns.
And they didn’t seem to be getting better.
I wasn’t even sure our goals were the same anymore.
I felt alone.
But thankfully, I wasn’t.
My mom kindly asked how things were going,
so I told her.
“Maybe he’s not the one,” I told her.
I thought she was going to tell me
which way I should go, but she didn’t.
Instead, she reassured me
that if he wasn’t the one, I was going to be OK.
They reminded me about what Jesus said when building a tower.
“For example, who of you wanting to build a tower
“does not first sit down and calculate the expense
to see if he has enough to complete it?”
I realized that I was about to enter into a building project of my own
—my relationship with Shane—
and I too needed to “calculate the expense”
before I commit to it.
They encouraged me to talk to Shane
and tell him about the things that were concerning me.
So I did.
And my mom was right.
I was OK, more than OK, really.
Shane and I decided it was best to break off the relationship.
And some years later,
I found someone that loves Jehovah as much as I do,
and I love him with my whole heart.

我感觉很好  非常好!
我和沙恩都同意
分手对彼此是最好的决定
几年后
我找到了一个跟我一样深爱耶和华的伴侣
我全心全意地爱他

en.text: Well, everybody here calls me Honey, but my name
is Esther Lozano.
And I was born in Fresno, California,
I was baptized in 1935,
and I’ve thoroughly enjoyed my service to Jehovah.
I became a special pioneer,
and then they called me to Gilead.
I was in the fourth class of Gilead.
That was in 1944.
When I left my assignment as a special,
I didn’t even know how it was to study, but this was beautiful
how Gilead prepared us for what was in the future.
Right after Gilead,
we went to Brooklyn Bethel for two years
—Esther Lopez and I—
then I was sent to Mexico.
I came in 1947, and I’m still here.
So that makes more than 68 years I’ve been in Mexico.
When I arrived, there were 7 Bethelites,
and there were 22 missionaries.
We all lived right at the branch;
it was a branch-missionary home.
The progress in Mexico
really is because of the families being united.
And when you get the husband and wife together,
then the whole family comes in the truth.
In 1961, Sister Esther Lozano preached to our grandparents.
My grandfather first got interested
through the book From Paradise Lost to Paradise Regained.
When I placed the book
with his wife and she gave it to him,
he decided that that’s what he was looking for.
He said, “Well, when can I be baptized?”
Three visits later,
a study was started with the entire family.
And the oldest son was only 13.
He said, “I’m getting baptized too!”
About a year ago, he came
and brought me a letter and told me how happy he was
that I had gone to their home
and preached to them.
And that was a happy experience of my life.
Today, in our family,
we are 23 Witnesses spread over four generations,
and now my brother and I are serving here
at the Central America branch.
Oh, I forgot to talk about my husband.
He was the branch overseer at that time.
We were there in the same branch for five years.
We got to know each other, but I didn’t pay attention to him
because I was always in the service.
And so, I don’t know when he decided
he wanted to get married because I know
that wasn’t his goal in life.
And so I wrote Brother Knorr
and asked him if he was surprised
to hear that we were going to be married.
Then he did write me back
and also said, well this is what he said in the letter:
‘You’re always jolly and talkative when I’m around.
‘On the other hand,
‘Brother Lozano is so quiet.
‘I must say, it is an interesting combination.
‘Both of you together can serve him and aid
one another in your true worship.’
This is one of my greatest treasures,
having that letter from Brother Knorr.
Then when Rudy died,
I didn’t dwell on that.
I remembered I made my dedication to Jehovah,
and I know that he would want me
to put that first in my life.
So I did not really suffer
that much about his death
because I became even more involved
in theocratic activities.
I’m in the Correspondence.
But I’m at work about an hour and a half in the morning
and an hour and a half in the afternoon
and the rest of the time
I’m studying here in the room.
I’m so pleased that I’m still able
to go to the morning text,
and I have a part in the service.
I have two studies that I conduct every week.
It’s such a pleasure to be with people
that have dedicated their lives to Jehovah.
And that’s what makes me happy because I know
Jehovah counts them
as his precious sons and daughters.
I don’t know why,
but many of the missionaries
have come up to me and told me
that I’ve been an encouragement to them,
and really, they are the ones that encourage me.
It’s because I had such beautiful examples
to follow in all these years.
And all I can say is thanks to Jehovah
for this great privilege of serving him.

cn.text: 在这里  大家都叫我亲爱的
但我的名字是爱斯特‧洛萨诺
1919年  我出生于加利福尼亚州弗雷斯诺市
1935年受浸后
我一直很享受为耶和华服务的时光
我成为特别先驱
然后被邀请参加基列学校
我参加了第四届的基列学校
那时是1944年
我离开特别先驱的岗位时
不确定自己能否好好学习
但基列的课程真是太好了  装备我们应付未来
离开基列后  我和埃丝特‧洛佩斯
到布鲁克林的伯特利两年
然后我被派到墨西哥
1947年  我来到墨西哥
一直到现在
我在这里住了超过68年
我到的时候  有7位伯特利成员和22位特派传道员
我们全都住在分部
这是个分部和特派传道员之家
墨西哥的进展  大多因为家人之间很团结
如果丈夫和妻子都学习圣经
整个家庭就会接受真理
洛萨诺姐妹向我们的祖父母传道
《从乐园的失落到乐园的复得》这本书
让我的祖父很感兴趣
我把书留给妻子后  她就给了丈夫
丈夫发觉这正是他一直在寻找的
他说
我什么时候可以受浸啊？
拜访三次以后  整个家庭就开始讨论圣经
当时最大的儿子只有13岁
他说   我也要受浸！
大约一年前  他来看我
带了一封信  告诉我
他多么高兴我拜访他的家  向他们传道
这是我人生中一个喜乐的经验
在我们的家族四代里有23个见证人
现在我和弟弟在中美洲分部服务
喔!
我忘了说我的丈夫
他当时是分部监督
我们在同一个分部已有五年
虽然彼此认识  但我没有特别注意他
因为我都在外传道
我不清楚他什么时候打算结婚
我知道以前这不是他的人生目标
所以  我写信给诺尔弟兄  问他
听到我们要结婚的消息  是不是很惊讶
他回信给我  在信上他是这样写的
我在那里时  你总是很开朗活泼
洛萨诺弟兄则是很安静
我得说  这是很有意思的组合
你们俩可以一起事奉耶和华
也能在正确的崇拜上彼此扶持
来自诺尔弟兄的这封信  对我来说非常珍贵
鲁道夫去世后  我没有因此灰心
我记得我对耶和华的献身誓愿
也知道上帝希望我将献身誓愿摆在生活首位
所以我没有因丈夫过世而过度忧伤
因为我投入更多的属灵活动
我在写作部通信处服务
早上工作一个半小时  下午工作一个半小时
其他时间就在房间里研读
我很高兴可以参加早晨崇拜和参与传道
我每星期主持两个圣经课程
和献出一生事奉耶和华的人在一起
是很大的荣幸
这也让我很快乐
因为我知道耶和华看他们是宝贵的儿子和女儿
我不知道为什么
有好多特派传道员来告诉我  我鼓励了他们
说真的  是他们鼓励了我
这些年来
我有很多美好的榜样可以效法
我由衷感谢耶和华  给我莫大的殊荣事奉他

en.text: We begin with a report from Ukraine.
In 2014, political tensions in eastern Ukraine
boiled over into a full-blown military conflict.
Within months,
over 7,600 Witnesses
needed to flee the area to seek refuge.
Others sheltered in their homes.
How did our brothers survive physically
and spiritually through the fighting?
Relief was organized from hundreds of miles away
at the branch office in L’viv.
In the following interviews,
our brothers and sisters describe the love and care
they received from the organization and from each other.
It happened that the hostilities
started without warning,
and the brothers needed to flee quickly.
There was not enough food;
there was nothing in the stores;
there was a lack of medicine;
there was no water,
no electricity.
It was scary.
There was no stability at all.
We did not know what to do.
Should we stay, or should we leave?
There were triplets; they were seven years old.
As soon as they got into the shelter,
they started singing a Kingdom song.
The adults also joined them in singing,
and because of that, we couldn’t hear the explosions
that were happening outside.
True, we ran out of foodstuffs,
and we had no money.
But I knew we would be able to get by.
God would not let us die of hunger.
Because the shelling was happening so often, it was impossible
to conduct our usual meetings.
We also couldn’t organize the ministry in the normal way.
It was just too dangerous.
When we received the first reports about the unrest in the east,
our Branch Committee gathered
and we prayerfully analyzed the situation.
We asked Jehovah for wisdom —how to act,
how to help our brothers to be spiritually and physically safe.
We were also sending regular update reports to the Governing Body.
More than 156 tons of food
and 21 tons of clothing donated
by local brothers have been distributed
to fellow believers and also to some non-Witnesses.
We had been told that we would be receiving
about five tons of relief supplies.
So we were astounded when instead of 5 tons,
we received 15 tons!
It was lovely to find little notes
that our brothers and sisters had written
and included in the packages.
Brothers from neighboring cities responded
and offered their homes,
provided foodstuffs
and, more importantly, their brotherly hospitality.
So we are ready to make sacrifices,
to adjust our schedules,
and to even take time out from our families
to render practical help to our brothers.
For example, beginning at 6 a.m.,
I would visit the brothers and sisters
and bring them the things that they needed.
So during two and a half months of war
and two months of reconstruction,
I rode my bicycle
6,500 kilometers.
The local elders from Slavyansk
organized small congregations
and regularly conducted meetings
to support them spiritually.
Major repairs have been carried out on 20 houses
of brothers and sisters, and minor repair work
was done on 72 houses and apartments.
We prepared two more programs.
This time, not only for the congregations in the war zone
but for the whole country of Ukraine,
even for Russia and Belarus.
We even had 325,000 in attendance.
An interesting experience
was the response of the people who were not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
They belong to another religion, yet they said:
“You are the only ones that really care.
Your genuine love is shown by your deeds.”
This is what makes us different
from all other religions.
This unselfish love shown by our brothers
did not go unnoticed by my husband and my son.
My husband started studying the Bible,
and he regularly attends the meetings now.
Recently, he enrolled in the Theocratic Ministry School.
I experienced this love personally,
and I started studying the Bible again with the brothers.
Now I am preparing for baptism.
Unfortunately, one of our sisters was killed.
I realized that a person can lose
—lose everything, but that
is really nothing compared to losing your children.
The brothers and sisters listened to us.
We cried together.
I just can’t put it into words.
It is as if Jehovah is holding you in his arms
—he doesn’t let you fall—
as if he is saying to you:
‘Don’t let go, my dear one.
I’m helping you. I’m supporting you.’
With Jehovah there are no borders between nations.
I could see that this was the true religion.
We continue to pray for our brothers in Ukraine.
We’re confident of Jehovah’s love for them,
and we know he’ll sustain them through any tribulation.

cn.text: 首先是来自乌克兰的报导
乌克兰东部的政治局势趋向白热化

几个月内
有7千600多个见证人
被迫逃到其他地区  寻求庇护
其他人则待在家里避难
我们的弟兄姊妹
如何在身体上和灵性上得到保护呢？
乌克兰分部办事处位于利沃夫
离冲突的地区数百英里
他们负责组织救援物资的调配
接下来的访谈
弟兄姊妹会说明他们怎样从组织
以及彼此之间得到爱与关怀
战争毫无预警地就爆发了  我们只能尽快逃离
这里缺水又断电  没有足够的食物和药物
商店也没有任何东西  我们一无所有
当时的情况真的很恐怖
我们坐立难安  不知道该怎么办
我们该留下还是离开？
那时有三个7岁的孩子  是三胞胎
他们一到避难所就开始高唱王国诗歌
后来  大人也跟他们一起唱
歌声盖过了外头的爆炸声
我们没食物  也没钱  但我知道我们能应付
上帝不会让我们饿死
接二连三的枪战和砲火
让我们无法举行聚会  也很难安排传道活动
情势实在太危险了
分部委员会一收到暴动的消息
就马上开会讨论
我们再三祷告
求耶和华告诉我们该怎么做  怎么保护弟兄姊妹
包括灵性和实际的需要
我们也经常将报告寄给中央长老团的弟兄
当地的弟兄姊妹捐出超过156吨的食物、21吨的衣服
除了见证人
有些不是信徒的受灾户也同样得到援助
我们听说会收到5吨的物资
但令我们惊讶的是 我们收到整整15吨
每次在包裹中看到弟兄姊妹写给我们的小纸条
我都觉得好温馨
邻近城市的弟兄姊妹作出响应
开放他们的家
提供食物
更重要的是  他们表现慷慨好客的弟兄之情
我们已经做好准备
愿意牺牲自己的时间
甚至暂时放下家务  为了能够实际帮助弟兄姊妹
我会在早上六点  骑着脚踏车
载着需要的物资探望弟兄姊妹
战争和战后重建共达四个半月
在那期间  我骑了6500公里的路
斯拉维扬斯克的长老组织了小型的会众
并照常举行聚会  提供属灵的支持
有20个弟兄姊妹的家需要重建
另外72栋房子和公寓需要部分整修
我们另外准备了两个节目
不只是为了战地的会众准备
也是为了整个乌克兰  俄罗斯以及白俄罗斯
听众多达32万5千人
一些人做了很有意思的评论
虽然他们不是耶和华见证人
但是他们说
只有你们真的关心别人
你们的行为显示出你们有真挚的爱
这就是我们和其他宗教不同的地方
弟兄对我先生和儿子也表现了无私的爱
后来我先生开始学习圣经
他现在稳定的参加聚会
最近也报名了传道训练班
我亲身体验到弟兄姊妹所表现的爱心
这推动我再次学习圣经
现在  我的目标就是献身受浸
令人难过的是  有一个姊妹丧生了
人会为了失去的东西而伤心
但没有什么  比失去孩子更让人生不如死
弟兄姊妹听我们说话
陪我们一起哭
那是无法用言语表达的感受
就好像耶和华把我紧紧地抱在怀中
不让我向下坠落
他对我说
好孩子  不要放开我
我就在这里  我会支持你
这确实是纯真的宗教
因为有耶和华  我们之间没有隔阂
我们会继续为那些在乌克兰的弟兄姊妹祷告
我们确信耶和华深爱他们
也会扶持他们渡过任何难关
