en.text: How did we come to Africa?
It was because we went through Gilead.
We attended the 47th class of Gilead,
and that was in 1969.
Our first assignment
was in the Belgian Congo, which is now
the Democratic Republic of Congo.
When we got our assignment, we were not overjoyed.
All we’d heard about the Congo was war,
atrocities, mercenaries.
So we weren’t excited. In fact, Susanne cried all night.
But we had promised to serve
Jehovah with our whole soul,
and we had said, “Here we are!
Send us.”
And so we accepted the assignment.
When we first arrived in the small mining town in Katanga,
we were arrested as soon as we got off the plane.
Then there was nobody to meet us.
The telegram, which had been sent three days earlier,
arrived on the same plane.
The missionaries had all returned
to their home countries
for the international conventions.
So when we eventually arrived at the missionary home,
it was empty, and there were
only big, dead cockroaches and bullet holes in the walls.
So we were alone for three weeks
until the other missionaries arrived.
The next hurdle to overcome
was to get used to a complete new culture
and also to learn two languages.
Communication with our families
was also a problem
—there was no Internet, no phones.
The only way was by letters, and it took three weeks
or almost four weeks for a letter to get to our families
and another four weeks to get a reply.
For years, we traveled
in the bush doing circuit and district work.
This meant living in the villages
in mud huts.
And so we would get water from the river
and use candles
for our power (our electricity there)
and charcoal to do our cooking on.
We had toilets outside —a hole in the ground.
It was real village life.
To get there, we had to travel on roads
that were often almost nonexistent
or very, very bad —rocky, deep sand,
muddy.
When it was muddy, it was deep mud,
and we’d get stuck.
In fact, one trip we did, 2,000 kilometers
took us ten days.
A lot of it was sand.
And one day, we only went 70 kilometers,
and we had to dig the vehicle out 12 times.
But we got there with Jehovah’s help.
And as far as we were concerned, this was missionary life
—this was real missionary life.
This was what we’d come to do.
We felt closer to Jehovah
when we were in the bush under those difficult circumstances
than we ever have.
It was great!
We loved it, and it’s really a big part of our life.
Some ask us if we ever desired to return to Europe.
Truthfully, yes.
But only very momentarily.
The work was under ban for ten years.
To carry on a religion that was banned was a prison sentence
of between five and ten years in prison.
And we’d been caught
carrying on a religion that was banned.
We were in custody for 18 days.
Nobody knew we were under arrest
—the branch or the missionary home—
because we were so deep in the bush.
We were 2,000 kilometers away from the branch.
So it was just us and Jehovah.
Well, we saw Jehovah’s hand.
He heard our prayers,
and he answered us.
For example, we were running out of money
and a complete stranger
offered us 200 dollars (U.S.),
and that was a lot of money in those days.
The man that handled our court case was very kind.
He made a new statement, and at the end,
he wrote, “I know of no law
that prohibits me from visiting my Christian brothers.”
With that he said, “You’re free to go.”
And what a wonderful feeling it is to be free.
After we had experienced Jehovah’s help
and support, how could we be so ungrateful
as to want to leave our assignment?
That is why I said that it was
only for a moment that we wanted
to return to Europe.
Another time at a small bush assembly
there was the threat
that it would be stopped by the authorities.
So that the brothers would get spiritual food,
I divided them into two groups
—one group sat outside the assembly arena;
the other half was inside.
I put on a pair of shorts, a vest, a hat,
and sat in a camp chair; and gave my talk
so that if any authorities came, I would say, “I’m only rehearsing.”
Anyway, when the first half had heard,
the others came in and I gave the talk again.
On the day of the assembly,
the zone commissioner came,
and he said we couldn’t continue until he
checked something.
He sent his men around to check who had not paid the tax,
because lies had been said about Jehovah’s Witnesses
—that we don’t pay tax.
And he was so surprised when they came back and said,
“Boss, everybody’s paid.”
And so he stood up, and he said,
“OK, you can carry on with your assembly.”
We were so grateful to Jehovah for that.
Zambia is a real preaching paradise.
People are humble. They’re God-fearing.
And with Jehovah’s help,
we have been able to help
more than 130 people to come to baptism.
So we are happy in our assignment.
What began 46 years ago
with tears and fear of the unknown
has turned out to be a wonderful blessing,
full of privileges
and joy.
We’ve seen firsthand how Jehovah has cared for us.
In fact, he’s ‘opened up the floodgates
of heaven and poured out a blessing.’
As we look back over the years, we’re absolutely convinced
that the blessings outweighed the hardships.
If we had the chance,
we’d do it all over again.

cn.text: 我们会来到非洲
是因为参加了1969年第47届的基列学校
当初  我们被派到比属刚果
现在叫刚果民主共和国
听说刚果充斥战争、暴行、和许多民兵
所以我们并没有因为这个新岗位
感到兴奋、或开心
老实说  苏珊还因此哭了整晚
不过  我们已经答应耶和华要全心事奉他
而且还说过“我们在这里!请差遣我们!”
于是  我们就接受了这个服务
三天前就寄出的电报  跟我们搭的班机一同送达
我们在加丹加省的采矿小镇下飞机后
就马上被抓了
当时  特派传道员都回国参加国际大会
没有半个人来带我们
我们好不容易到达特派传道员之家
发现屋里空荡荡的
只有死掉的大蟑螂和满是弹孔的墙
其他特派传道员回来之前
有三个星期  只有我们孤伶伶的两个人
接着要克服的障碍是
适应完全不同的文化
还有学习两种新语言
那时候没有网路、没有电话
联系我们的家人也成了问题
惟一的方法是写信
在寄出三到四星期后  家人才会收到
我们也要等四个星期才能收到他们的回信
有好几年的时间  从事分区和区域探访工作时
要穿越许多灌木丛 才能到达探访的地区
我们住在泥草屋的村落里
我们要从河流打水、用蜡烛作为光源
用木炭生火煮饭
那里的厕所 是户外一个挖好的洞
真的是乡村生活
为了抵达目的地
我们须要越过很难走的沙石或泥巴路
有时候甚至没有路
我们的车也会陷入泥巴而动弹不得
探访工作一趟下来  总共2000公里远
要花上十天那么久
多半经过的是沙子路
有一次  我们只开了70公里远

en.text: An introduction to the book of Ecclesiastes.
King Solomon,
who ruled over Israel from Jerusalem,
wrote this book.
Ecclesiastes was completed
many years into Solomon’s reign
but before his fall into idolatry.
Ecclesiastes contains 12 chapters.
In chapter 1, Solomon discusses
the futility of human activity.
In chapter 2, he looks for meaning in life
by evaluating his many pursuits.
Solomon writes that pursuing wealth
and magnificent accomplishments
is like “chasing after the wind.”
Chapters 3 to 6 present observations by Solomon
that help us cultivate godly wisdom.
He shows that “there is an appointed time for everything.”
He encourages hard work,
and he extols the benefits of friendship.
He refers to the enjoyment of food
and the rejoicing over one’s work as “the gift of God.”
Chapters 7 to 11 provide a sobering discussion
of life in this world.
Solomon observes that life is short
and that man needs to use his time,
energy, and resources in the best way possible.
This will help him make “a good name,”
or reputation, with God.
Did you know?
Solomon alluded to the earth’s water cycle
centuries before scientists understood this process.
In chapter 12, he encourages young ones
to make wise choices before the challenges of old age arrive.
Then he sums up all that he discussed
with the words: “Fear the true God
“and keep his commandments,
for this is the whole obligation of man.”
As you meditate on the book of Ecclesiastes,
note which pursuits are futile and which are worthwhile,
how godly wisdom helps us enjoy the gift of life,
and how cultivating a relationship with God
leads to a truly meaningful life
under the rule of God’s Kingdom.

en.text: There are times when peace can be threatened.
I found that out firsthand.
We both said things we wish we hadn’t.
I thought she was just being too sensitive.
I couldn’t even concentrate on the meeting.
I thought, ‘Why is she overreacting?’
I felt like telling someone.
Maybe I should talk to my friends.
I thought about calling a relative.
Or maybe I should just go to the elders.
It was disturbing my sleep.
It was all I could think about.
The next day I volunteered to work at a Kingdom Hall project.
But earlier that morning,
I read Matthew 5:23, 24, where it says:
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
“and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
“leave your gift there in front of the altar, and go away.
“First make your peace with your brother,
and then come back and offer your gift.”
How could I make a sacrifice to Jehovah
when I’m not at peace with my sister?
I had to ‘leave my gift’ and ‘first make peace.’
We really talked from the heart.
I didn’t want to lose my sister.
And she didn’t want to lose me.
It’s amazing how wonderful it feels when you make peace.
I am so happy!
I not only gained my sister back
but I gained a truer and deeper friend.
My relationship with the congregation is stronger,
and I feel closer to Jehovah.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting!
Here’s what we can look forward to in our program:
What if your courtship reveals problems you didn’t expect?
Part 3 of the Preparing for Marriage series
will show us how we can “calculate the expense”
when considering marriage.
We go to Australia to meet Viv and Ann Mouritz.
Their life of full-time service has taken them around the world.
What advice do they have for those who are deciding
what form of sacred service to pursue?
And we’ll enjoy a music video that highlights
the theme of our program.
It will encourage us to settle differences with our brothers and sisters
and to forgive one another.
This is the October 2016 edition
of JW Broadcasting!
We begin with a report from Ukraine.
In 2014, political tensions in eastern Ukraine
boiled over into a full-blown military conflict.
Within months,
over 7,600 Witnesses
needed to flee the area to seek refuge.
Others sheltered in their homes.
How did our brothers survive physically
and spiritually through the fighting?
Relief was organized from hundreds of miles away
at the branch office in L’viv.
In the following interviews,
our brothers and sisters describe the love and care
they received from the organization and from each other.
It happened that the hostilities
started without warning,
and the brothers needed to flee quickly.
There was not enough food;
there was nothing in the stores;
there was a lack of medicine;
there was no water,
no electricity.
It was scary.
There was no stability at all.
We did not know what to do.
Should we stay, or should we leave?
There were triplets; they were seven years old.
As soon as they got into the shelter,
they started singing a Kingdom song.
The adults also joined them in singing,
and because of that, we couldn’t hear the explosions
that were happening outside.
True, we ran out of foodstuffs,
and we had no money.
But I knew we would be able to get by.
God would not let us die of hunger.
Because the shelling was happening so often, it was impossible
to conduct our usual meetings.
We also couldn’t organize the ministry in the normal way.
It was just too dangerous.
When we received the first reports about the unrest in the east,
our Branch Committee gathered
and we prayerfully analyzed the situation.
We asked Jehovah for wisdom —how to act,
how to help our brothers to be spiritually and physically safe.
We were also sending regular update reports to the Governing Body.
More than 156 tons of food
and 21 tons of clothing donated
by local brothers have been distributed
to fellow believers and also to some non-Witnesses.
We had been told that we would be receiving
about five tons of relief supplies.
So we were astounded when instead of 5 tons,
we received 15 tons!
It was lovely to find little notes
that our brothers and sisters had written
and included in the packages.
Brothers from neighboring cities responded
and offered their homes,
provided foodstuffs
and, more importantly, their brotherly hospitality.
So we are ready to make sacrifices,
to adjust our schedules,
and to even take time out from our families
to render practical help to our brothers.
For example, beginning at 6 a.m.,
I would visit the brothers and sisters
and bring them the things that they needed.
So during two and a half months of war
and two months of reconstruction,
I rode my bicycle
6,500 kilometers.
The local elders from Slavyansk
organized small congregations
and regularly conducted meetings
to support them spiritually.
Major repairs have been carried out on 20 houses
of brothers and sisters, and minor repair work
was done on 72 houses and apartments.
We prepared two more programs.
This time, not only for the congregations in the war zone
but for the whole country of Ukraine,
even for Russia and Belarus.
We even had 325,000 in attendance.
An interesting experience
was the response of the people who were not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
They belong to another religion, yet they said:
“You are the only ones that really care.
Your genuine love is shown by your deeds.”
This is what makes us different
from all other religions.
This unselfish love shown by our brothers
did not go unnoticed by my husband and my son.
My husband started studying the Bible,
and he regularly attends the meetings now.
Recently, he enrolled in the Theocratic Ministry School.
I experienced this love personally,
and I started studying the Bible again with the brothers.
Now I am preparing for baptism.
Unfortunately, one of our sisters was killed.
I realized that a person can lose
—lose everything, but that
is really nothing compared to losing your children.
The brothers and sisters listened to us.
We cried together.
I just can’t put it into words.
It is as if Jehovah is holding you in his arms
—he doesn’t let you fall—
as if he is saying to you:
‘Don’t let go, my dear one.
I’m helping you. I’m supporting you.’
With Jehovah there are no borders between nations.
I could see that this was the true religion.
We continue to pray for our brothers in Ukraine.
We’re confident of Jehovah’s love for them,
and we know he’ll sustain them through any tribulation.
Our worldwide brotherhood is truly special.
When our brothers are in need,
we want to help in whatever way possible.
It also brings us great joy to be with our brothers
—whether at the meetings, in the field service,
or on other occasions.
We love our brothers and enjoy spending time with them.
At the same time, because we are all imperfect,
our love and unity will be tested.
We may have our feelings hurt,
or we may hurt the feelings of others.
That brings me to the theme I would like to discuss
with you in this month’s program,
“Settling Differences Brings Jehovah’s Favor.”
It is based on Matthew 6:14.
Let’s read this important verse together.
Right after teaching his disciples how to pray,
Jesus says in verse 14:
“For if you forgive men their trespasses,
your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
To what extent do Jesus’ words affect how Jehovah
views what we do each day in our worship to him?
Consider this:
You’re concluding your day in prayer.
You pray for Jehovah’s name to be sanctified.
You pray for his Kingdom to come.
You ask that he bless the Governing Body
and the brothers taking the lead.
You share with him a few matters
of personal concern.
And then you say: “Jehovah,
“I know I am imperfect,
“and I sin against you often.
“Please forgive me for my sins.
“Let me stand before you
in a clean and approved state.”
Now the question is,
Has Jehovah heard your heartfelt request?
Will he forgive you?
Well, what did Jesus say?
Look again at verse 14:
“For if you forgive men their trespasses,
your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
Did you notice Jesus’ use of the word “if”?
That tells us that forgiveness is not automatic.
It comes with a condition, or price.
What price?
According to Jesus, ‘if we forgive others,’
the condition has been met;
the price has been paid.
What will Jehovah do for us?
Jesus said: “[He] will also forgive you.”
Really, though, is it fair or reasonable
for Jehovah to say to us,
‘Only if you forgive others,
then I will also forgive you’?
Well, suppose you get very sick and lose your job.
You’re unable to pay rent for many months.
Your situation is desperate.
You have very few, if any, options.
You worry about your wife and your children.
Say you go to the owner of the house and ask
if he would give you time to get back on your feet.
Once you get better and are able to work again,
you will do everything within your power
to pay him what you owe.
He tells you not to worry.
He understands your situation.
He will cancel your debt,
and you do not have to pay him any rent
until your situation improves.
In fact, he’ll cover your monthly expenses
until you are able to care for your family.
How would you feel about what he has done,
and would this affect how you treat others?
Well, because of our sinful nature,
we are all in debt to Jehovah
—deserving of death.
We are unable to cover our expenses.
But when we go to Jehovah in prayer
and beg for his help,
in his great mercy and kindness,
he tells us not to worry.
He has given the life of his Son to pay our debt.
And on the basis of that sacrifice,
He is willing to cover our expenses
—the sins we commit daily—
and to extend forgiveness to us until we are able
to get back on our feet,
when we reach perfection in the new world.
So think again about those simple yet powerful words
of Jesus at Matthew 6:14:
“For if you forgive men their trespasses,
your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
Is that fair?
Is that reasonable?
Is it realistic?
Without a doubt!
In fact, settling differences,
or forgiving others freely,
is one of the best ways to imitate
Jehovah’s compassionate and merciful nature.
What can help us to settle differences quickly?
The first thing we should do is to try
and let love cover over the wrong.
Can I just forgive and forget?
If we are able to do so,
this is a beautiful way to maintain
the congregation’s peace and unity.
But if we’re struggling to forget the wrong,
there are two scriptures that are especially helpful
in this matter of settling differences.
They are Matthew 5:23, 24
and Matthew 18:15-17.
Keep in mind that these texts
are not referring to the same scenarios,
nor are they to be applied
in the exact same way.
Matthew chapter 5
has a broader application
and can be used to bring peace
in most situations.
Matthew chapter 18
has a more limited application
and applies to specific situations
that are more serious in nature.
Now let’s consider the first text,
Matthew 5:23, 24:
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
“and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
“leave your gift there in front of the altar, and go away.
“First make your peace with your brother,
and then come back and offer your gift.”
To truly capture what these two brief verses mean
for you and me today,
we have to understand what Jesus’ words meant
to his first-century Jewish listeners.
Picture the scene in your mind as we transport ourselves
into the city of Jerusalem some 2,000 years ago.
It is during one of the annual festivals.
There are tens of thousands of people in the city.
You are there to make your sacrifice —a beautiful lamb.
The best one you have.
It’s clean and unblemished.
You take the lamb through a series of courts
all the way to the Court of Priests.
It has taken you most of the day to get there.
Now you’re ready to put your hands on that animal
and offer a prayer for forgiveness,
and then you remember something.
What?
Verse 23 reads:
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
“and there you remember that your brother
has something against you,”
Now you think: ‘My brother
‘does have something against me!
‘The last time I saw him,
‘he greeted everybody else but me.
‘He was upset. But what is it?
‘I don’t remember doing anything.
‘He is so sensitive!
He’s always upset with something.’
Did Jesus have all of that in mind
when he said what he did in verse 23?
No!
He did not go into detail
about what that “something” might be.
He doesn’t say who is right or wrong.
He doesn’t make a comment
about whether someone is too sensitive,
always getting upset, never satisfied,
difficult to get along with.
Why not?
Because the reason behind the “something”
is not the important thing.
What is the important thing?
That the peace has been disturbed.
There is a difference that needs to be settled.
The lack of peace between brothers
could affect their relationship with Jehovah.
That is important!
So what should be done?
We see the answer in verse 24:
“Leave your gift there
“in front of the altar, and go away.
“First make your peace with your brother,
and then come back and offer your gift.”
That animal sacrifice is important too.
There’s no doubt about that.
It represents worship to Jehovah
—like going to the meetings, in the field service,
sharing in family worship.
But according to Jesus,
what is more important?
It is settling the difference
—making peace with our brother first.
Then we will be in an acceptable position
to offer our gift of worship to Jehovah.
Yes, settling differences will bring Jehovah’s favor.
But when can we apply the principle of Matthew 5?
Whenever there is a difference to be settled.
Perhaps our brother misunderstood what we said or did.
Or maybe he didn’t misunderstand
—maybe we did give him a valid reason to be hurt.
Regardless, we notice
that he has something against us.
In that case, we make peace.
We can also use the principles of this text
when we are hurt or have something
against our brother.
We can take the initiative ourselves
to settle misunderstandings,
to resolve differences,
and to make peace with our brother.
Again, Jehovah blesses such a spirit.
Now, open your Bible to Matthew chapter 18.
We mentioned earlier that it has
a more limited application.
How so?
Notice verse 15:
“Moreover, if your brother commits a sin,
“go and reveal his fault between you and him alone.
If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.”
Here Jesus says, “if your brother commits a sin.”
That is much different than just having
“something against [us].”
We are talking about a situation that is much more serious.
What situation?
The revised Organized to Do Jehovah’s Will book,
page 136, explains
that it “involves financial or property matters,
“such as failing to repay a loan
“or committing fraud.
“Or the offense might be slander,
which seriously affects someone’s reputation.”
Of course, they are sins that could be resolved
between the individuals concerned
but are also serious enough
to merit expulsion from the congregation if not settled.
Before we start applying Matthew 18:15,
we should first consider whether it is really necessary
to pursue the matter.
Could we simply forgive the individual
for what was done or even take the loss
if it were a financial matter?
That is a personal decision.
If we decide to pursue the matter,
what do we do?
Jesus helps us in verse 15, when he says
that we reveal his fault
between the two of us alone.
We do not discuss the matter with others,
attempting to get them to side with us.
We do not go straight to the elders
and try to get them to solve the problem for us.
No, we try to resolve the matter between us.
And since our goal is to settle the difference,
maintain our relationship with Jehovah,
and help our brother do the same,
we make repeated efforts to speak with him
when our initial efforts are unsuccessful.
Keep in mind that Jesus did not say:
“Go only once and reveal his fault.”
When applying this first step, make it clear
that your motive is to ‘gain your brother.’
Also, it would be helpful to clearly state
that you are applying the first step in settling differences
as outlined by Jesus at Matthew 18:15.
Of course, this would be stated in a kindly,
nonthreatening manner
but still in a way to show the seriousness
of getting the matter settled.
What if the first step
in gaining your brother is unsuccessful?
Notice verse 16 explains step 2:
“But if he does not listen,
“take along with you one or two more,
“so that on the testimony of two or three witnesses
every matter may be established.”
Yes, we talk with him in the company of one or two more.
Would that be our best friends?
No.
The whole purpose is to ‘gain our brother.’
Teaming up with two of our best friends
could alienate our brother.
Instead, it makes sense
that we would choose other mature Christians.
How would mature Christians be helpful?
Well, are we misunderstanding things?
Could they help him to reason about the matter?
Could a solution be found?
Having spiritually mature witnesses there
may help to resolve the matter.
Generally, applying steps 1
and 2 will result in gaining your brother
and preserving the peace of the congregation.
If he does not respond to these repeated efforts
to help him, then what?
You have a decision to make.
Are you willing to forgive your brother,
even take a loss if a financial matter is involved?
If you choose to pursue the matter further,
listen to Jesus’ words recorded
at verse 17:
“If he does not listen to them,
“speak to the congregation.
“If he does not listen even to the congregation,
“let him be to you just as a man of the nations
and as a tax collector.”
At this point, the body of elders
representing the congregation will get involved.
They will review the facts of the case and determine
if a judicial committee should be appointed.
Happily, though, these situations are rare,
and matters are often resolved peacefully
before reaching such a serious point.
Think back again to that heartfelt prayer to Jehovah.
Has Jehovah heard our sincere requests?
Will he forgive?
Well, at this moment,
if you realize there is a difference with your brother
that needs to be settled,
pray to Jehovah about the matter.
Ask him to help you see
beyond the emotion and make peace.
Do not let any more time go by!
Once we have followed the simple steps outlined by Jesus
and have forgiven others,
the condition has been met;
the price has been paid.
Then what will Jehovah do for us?
Jesus said:
‘He will also forgive us.’
As a result, we will gain the peace of mind
that comes with a clean conscience,
knowing that we have Jehovah’s favor and blessing.
We can then make a valuable contribution
to the beautiful, united brotherhood
that we are privileged to be a part of.
There are more lessons in Matthew chapter 18
that teach us how to maintain peace and unity with our brothers.
Just as important as settling differences,
Jesus cautioned against becoming a cause for stumbling.
At a Bethel morning worship,
Brother Stephen Lett described
three ways we can avoid stumbling others.
Now, this word picture
of someone being stumbled
is quite vivid, isn’t it?
We’ve all seen someone stumbled.
In fact, we’ve all stumbled ourselves at times,
and there are varying degrees of consequences.
For example, a person can stumble,
quickly recover,
and continue almost uneventfully down the path.
Or a person can stumble,
fall, break a bone,
eventually they recover
—but only after extensive therapy.
Then again, a person can stumble,
fall, hit his head, never recover
—becoming a casualty.
Well, the situation is similar
when one is stumbled spiritually.
He can recover quickly,
maybe recover over time,
or he may never recover
—becoming a spiritual casualty.
So we cannot know the ultimate outcome
for someone who is stumbled.
So no wonder we’re cautioned to be very careful
to never be any cause for stumbling.
Open up to Matthew chapter 18,
and here’s an especially powerful scripture
in this regard.
Matthew 18:6, Jesus says:
“But whoever stumbles one of these little ones
“who have faith in me,
“it would be better for him to have hung around his neck
“a millstone that is turned by a donkey
and to be sunk in the open sea.”
Well, with graphic language,
Jesus describes how that if we cause someone
to become a spiritual casualty,
we could actually bring eternal doom
upon ourselves.
But now, here’s a question,
What could we do to cause someone to stumble?
Well, interestingly, there are several similarities
between causing someone to stumble physically
and causing someone to stumble spiritually.
Let us discuss three.
Now one, pushing someone
could cause them to stumble,
especially if they’re on uneven terrain, if you think about it.
And this is true physically and spiritually.
But think about Jehovah for a moment.
He could push any of us, couldn’t he?
He could force us to serve him.
He certainly has the power, but he never uses it that way.
Instead, he invites, he encourages;
and he explains the blessings,
the curses, depending upon how we decide.
But it’s up to us, isn’t it?
For example, at Isaiah 48:18,
Jehovah says: ‘If only
‘you would pay attention to my commandments!
‘Then your peace would become like a river
and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.’
Beseeching, but not forcing.
Now think about it, if Jehovah doesn’t force,
he doesn’t want us to force either, does he?
For example, parents
need to be very careful they don’t just simply push
their children to serve Jehovah.
But rather, lovingly,
beseechingly like Jehovah,
try to reach the heart, and of course,
clearly show them the blessings
that will come their way if they do.
Another example,
elders should never try to push Jehovah’s sheep.
I heard an experience about an elder, during his part,
asked the brothers for a show of hands
how many were going out in service the next morning.
Well, only a few raised their hand.
He proceeded to scold the congregation
that more should be going out.
Well, he then unwisely asked
for another show of hands.
You guessed it —fewer raised their hand
the second time.
Take another example,
those who conduct Bible studies
should not just try to push their students to do the right thing.
“You’ve got to quit smoking! You’ve got to get rid of those idols!”
No, not with external pressure,
but by motivating their hearts,
you motivate your students.
Or take another example, none of us
should try to push schoolmates, workmates, or relatives
to accept the truth.
A pushing approach,
shoving approach —even though motivated with sincerity—
has actually resulted in people being stumbled
away from the truth for many years.
It makes me think of the story, or the saying,
that when a person first learns the truth,
you should lock them up for about six months
to contain, or minimize, the damage they do.
Well, that saying is totally erroneous.
You shouldn’t lock that brother up; you should follow that brother.
See, that brother has zeal, doesn’t he?
But it’s true, we probably do need to help him
to properly channel that zeal,
so that he doesn’t try to force his relatives
or others to accept the truth
that he is so excited about.
But now, what is the second thing
we can do to cause someone to stumble?
Placing an obstacle in their path.
Now again, this is true physically or spiritually.
And if you think about it,
whether we put that stumbling block there intentionally
or unintentionally, the result is the same, isn’t it?
As mentioned in today’s Watchtower comments,
wholesome speech and upright conduct
can help us to avoid
ever being a cause for stumbling.
In contrast, unwholesome speech,
unclean conduct,
can easily stumble ones inside
or outside the congregation.
But now, what about in an area
where we have a Scriptural right to do something?
Now, surely exercising that right,
if it stumbles someone,
we can’t be held accountable for that, can we?
Well, open up to 1 Corinthians chapter 8,
and here —very interestingly—
this scripture answers that question.
1 Corinthians 8:9,
it says: “But keep watching
“that your right to choose
“does not somehow
become a stumbling block to those who are weak.”
Isn’t that interesting?
Even our right to choose,
if it would stumble someone,
we wouldn’t exercise that right according to this scripture.
The apostle Paul, in verse 13 of that same chapter,
he said he wouldn’t even eat meat ever again
if it stumbled his brother.
Well, like Paul, are we willing
to forgo our rights regarding,
for example, wearing a beard,
wearing heavy makeup,
using alcohol —as just a few examples—
if exercising that right
might even possibly stumble someone?
But now, what’s the third way
we could cause someone to stumble?
Failing to warn him
about a potential trip hazard.
We could call this the sin of omission.
And again, it applies physically and spiritually.
As a physical example, let’s say we see the floor
has just been mopped,
and an unsuspecting person
is approaching that wet area.
Now will we warn them?
If we don’t warn them —they fall, hurt themselves—
would we not share some responsibility?
Well, similarly,
with spiritual application,
Galatians 6:1 tells us
that if someone “takes a false step” before he’s aware of it,
what are we supposed to try to do?
“Try to readjust” such a person,
but then it adds: “In a spirit of mildness.”
Don’t push him!
But try to gently, lovingly warn
and readjust that person.
So there we have three areas
in which we must be careful we never contribute
toward someone being stumbled.
We don’t push others to serve Jehovah.
We strive to never,
even unintentionally,
put a stumbling block in their path —for example—
by insisting on exercising our personal rights.
And number three, we never fail to lovingly warn
one whom we see approaching
a potential trip hazard.
Rather than being any cause for stumbling,
we want to be a force for good, don’t we?
Helping others to stand firm
and even helping ones get up if they have fallen.
None of us want to cause our brother to stumble,
but it can happen if we’re not careful.
Why not recall the three ways
Brother Lett listed to avoid stumbling others?
You can then examine how you’re doing as a parent,
an elder, a Bible teacher,
or as a fellow worshipper in the congregation.
The effort we make toward unity is always worthwhile.

and be part of the congregation.

our concerns even before we even pray about it.

of Jehovah’s great love for each of us,
and we thank him to be a part
of this amazing brotherhood.

the brotherhood’s loyal response to theocratic direction.
Change is not always easy,
but it helps when we look at Jehovah’s blessing
on new spiritual provisions
and adjustments to the work.
Letters of appreciation from our brothers
add to the Governing Body’s confidence
that Jehovah is directing his organization.
A sister from the United States wrote this about JW Broadcasting,

a direct answer to a prayer.”

what we need when we need it.

fits well with our discussion on settling differences.
It begins with a situation between a young mother
and her mother-in-law and reminds us
to “Forgive One Another.”
Yes, you had the best of intentions. Kindnesses too numerous to mention.

Then, as a tear appears, I see. Things aren’t what they seem to be.
Before the sun slips from the sky, Let’s be sure we both see eye to eye.

Before the sun slips from the sky, Let’s be sure we both see eye to eye.
We’ll forget the things we said, And, please, let’s forgive.
Brothers today, brothers we’ll stay.

Cancel the debt; forgive and forget. That’s the way true friendship should be.
Before the sun slips from the sky, Let’s be sure we both see eye to eye.
We’ll forget the things we said, And, please, let’s forgive.
Here in our hearts, that’s where it starts.
Bonded in love, forgiving one another.
Did you see two critical areas
where we need to be forgiving?
It was in the family and in the congregation.
We’ll always have reasons
in this imperfect world to forgive.
Look for the opportunities in your life
to imitate Jehovah and forgive others.
As we conclude our program,
we take you on a visit to world headquarters
in Warwick, New York.
The Bethel family has been moving
into their new work areas.
More than 25,000 brothers and sisters
worked on the construction of the facility.
It was a united effort by temporary volunteers,
construction servants, Bethelites, construction groups,
and volunteers who previously worked
on Kingdom Hall projects.
Earlier this year, workers were making
final preparations for the arrival
of world headquarters staff.
When open for tours, visitors will enjoy
the historic Bible display,
a visual history exhibit of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and an interactive museum
explaining how Jehovah directs his organization today.
We thank Jehovah for all
who helped to complete the new world headquarters.
That includes the thousands of volunteers
but also the millions of you dear brothers and sisters
who support the worldwide work
with your regular donations.
We send you our love and pray for Jehovah
to bless our united brotherhood.
From Brooklyn, New York,
this is JW Broadcasting!

en.text: Billions of people
have died throughout history.
But the death of one person stands alone
—that of Jesus Christ.
Why did he die?
Did his death have a purpose?
To find the answer,
we need to go back to the beginning of human history.
The Bible explains
that God created the man Adam perfect,
without sin.
He was free to eat from all the trees
in the garden of Eden
—except one.
God gave the simple command
not to eat from that particular tree.
This tree symbolized God’s right
to set the standards of good and bad.
As long as Adam remained obedient to Jehovah,
he had the prospect of living forever
on a paradise earth.
But Adam did not appreciate
all the good things God had done for him.
He chose to disobey God.
As a result,
he lost the opportunity to live forever.
But he was not the only one affected.
All of his descendants
have inherited the fatal effects of sin.
By themselves,
humans could not break free from sin and death.
They needed someone to rescue them.
For this reason, Jehovah miraculously caused
one of his perfect spirit sons
to come to earth as a human.
Jesus was a perfect man,
just as Adam had been.
However, unlike Adam,
Jesus remained obedient.
This allowed him “to give his life
as a ransom in exchange for many.”
But how could the death of one man
benefit all of mankind?
Well, imagine that the manager of a large factory
steals money from the company.
His actions plunge the company into debt,
forcing it to shut down.
The workers lose their jobs
and cannot pay their bills.
Many suffer because of that one man’s corruption.
Now suppose a kind and generous man feels sorry
for all those who are suffering.
He is moved to pay off the debt and reopen the company.
By canceling that one debt,
he brings relief to all the employees
and their families.
Adam is like that corrupt manager.
When he rebelled,
he incurred a large debt of sin
and passed it on to his children.
Jesus is like the generous man.
When he gave up his perfect human life,
he paid off the debt of sin
and reopened the prospect of living forever for each of us.
You may wonder:
‘Did Jesus really exist?
‘Is believing in Jesus enough for salvation?
Is Jesus God?’
To learn more about what the Bible says
on this and many other topics,
go to jw.org.

cn.text: 从古到今有亿万人死去
但有一个人的死亡却有独特的意义
他就是耶稣基督
耶稣因为什么而死？
他的死亡跟我们有什么关系？
要找到答案，就要从人类历史的开始说起
圣经说
耶和华上帝创造了第一个男人亚当
他是完美无罪的
上帝告诉亚当
他可以随意吃伊甸园中树上的果子
只有一棵树的果子
上帝吩咐他不可以吃
这棵树象征上帝制定善恶标准的权力
亚当只要服从上帝
就能永远在地上的乐园里生活
不过
亚当没有感激耶和华给他的一切
他选择反叛上帝
结果失去了永远活下去的机会
但受影响的不只是他一个人而已
亚当的罪遗传给了他的所有后代
没有人能靠自己挣脱罪和死亡的枷锁
那谁能够拯救人类呢？
耶和华施行奇迹
派他的一个灵体儿子降世为人
跟亚当一样，耶稣是个完美的人
但跟亚当不同的是
耶稣却一直服从上帝
所以，耶稣献出的生命
可以“作为救赎许多人的代价”
耶稣一个人的牺牲
为什么能拯救世上千千万万的人呢？
想象一下
一间大工厂的经理偷了公司的钱
他害公司欠了一大笔债
结果工厂被迫倒闭
工人丢了工作，生活陷入困境
一个人贪污腐败，让许许多多的人受到连累
现在，有一个慷慨的好心人
很同情这些工人的遭遇
他付清债务
让工厂可以恢复运作
由于他还清了一个人欠下的债务
所有工人和他们的家人都摆脱了困境
亚当就像这个贪污的经理
他背叛上帝，犯下大罪

还把债留给了子孙后代
耶稣就像那个慷慨的好心人

抵偿了亚当的罪

en.text: Have you enjoyed studying the book
Imitate Their Faith as much as I have?
It’s a wonderful book, isn’t it?
And I was particularly captivated by the introduction.
There was a point in the introduction
that encouraged us to use our imagination
when we’re reading the Bible:
to see the sights, to hear the sounds,
to smell the aromas, to try to capture the feelings
of the individuals that we are reading about.
Now, of course, we don’t want our imagination to run away with us,
but at the same time, we do want to get
a solid mental picture of what we’re reading.
And that’s what I’d like to talk to you about today.
When you’re reading the Bible, try to get the whole picture.
Now we’ll use a couple of well-known Bible accounts to illustrate.
Have you been raised in a stepfamily or a blended family?
If you have, did you know that you have
something in common with Joseph, the son of Jacob?
Joseph was raised with ten half brothers
in a large blended family.
So now you want to try to view
this family as a composite.
You want to try to figure out how did people mesh
or how did they clash within this family.
What would you do?
Well, you might start by writing down some of the characteristics
of the individual members of the family.
What about Joseph’s half brothers and Joseph himself?
What do you know about them?
What about Judah, Simeon, Levi,
Dan, Naphtali —what do you know?
So write down their characteristics,
and try to figure out how they might get along.
Sometimes there is one individual incident
that’s recorded in the Bible,
but we mustn’t forget:
People’s actions have a way of affecting other people.
So when you read about a certain incident in the Bible,
try to imagine who might have been affected by that incident.
Take an example.
In the book of Genesis, we read that Jacob’s son Reuben
committed sexual immorality with Bilhah.
Well, that had an effect on other people without doubt.
Who was Reuben?
He was Leah’s oldest son.
Who was Bilhah?
Rachel’s handmaiden.
Do you think that there might have been a little animosity or tension
between Leah and Rachel sometimes,
especially when you consider how their marriages started out?
There may have been.
And it may be that the attitudes of the women
had some bearing on the attitudes of their sons as well.
So you take all of these things into consideration.
Now, Bilhah had two sons, Dan and Naphtali.
How do you think they felt when they learned
that their oldest brother, or half brother,
had committed fornication with their mother?
So there could have been tension there.
And this all goes into the mix
when we’re considering the family as a composite.
Now, do you picture Joseph at age 17
with ten much older half brothers, maybe in their 30’s,
some old enough to be his father?
Not true.
The truth is that there was only a seven-year age difference
between Joseph’s oldest brother, Reuben, and Joseph himself.
In fact, 11 of Jacob’s sons
were born during the seven-year period
when Jacob was working for Laban.
Eleven sons in seven years,
how is that possible?
It’s easy, when you remember that Jacob had two wives
and two concubines, or secondary wives.
So there didn’t have to be a nine-month interval
between the birth of the children.
In fact, some could have been born just about at the same time;
they could have been the same age.
So when Joseph was sold into slavery at age 17,
his oldest brother was no more than 24.
Some of his brothers were only a year or two older than Joseph himself.
So we’re talking about a group of young men
in their late teens and early 20’s,
and this might explain some of the hotheaded reactions
that some of those young men had.
Well, so much for the boys.
What about their father, Jacob?
What can we learn about him?
A lot.
For one thing, he was a spiritual man.
Now, this is something for you young brothers and sisters
who are contemplating marriage to think about.
Jacob was willing to go to any length
to keep his relationship with Jehovah intact.
Let’s take an example:
Genesis 29:18.
You can follow along on the screen as I read this.
And we’re talking about marriage here.
Genesis 29:18.
It says: “Jacob had fallen in love with Rachel,
“so he said: ‘I am willing to serve you seven years
for your younger daughter Rachel.’”
Now what’s the takeaway?
Jacob didn’t marry the first person who came along,
maybe some pagan woman.
He didn’t say, ‘Well, seven years is too long to wait.
I’m going to find some Philistine woman, and I’ll marry her.’
He was willing to wait so that he could marry someone
who would join him in the worship of Jehovah.
And you young folks, if you are willing to wait,
you can be sure that you will have Jehovah’s blessing as well.
Now Jacob was apparently also a bit of a romantic.
Notice verse 20.
It says: “And Jacob served seven years for Rachel,”
but notice this,
“but in his eyes they were like just a few days
because of his love for her.”
Now, isn’t that poetic?
Jacob may have learned to treasure his wife
by observing his parents, Isaac and Rebekah.
It appears that they had a strong marriage.
Just notice what we read
at Genesis 26:8,
Genesis 26:8.
It says: “After some time had passed,
“Abimelech king of the Philistines was looking out of the window,
and he saw Isaac,” that’s Jacob’s father,
“displaying affection for Rebekah his wife.”
So it appears that Isaac and Rebekah
had a warm relationship, a good marriage.
Now, what else can we learn about Jacob?
There’s an interesting detail recorded
in chapter 25 and verse 27.
It says: “As the boys got bigger, Esau,”
Jacob’s brother,
“became a skilled hunter, a man of the field,
“but Jacob was a blameless man,
dwelling in tents.”
So Jacob liked to dwell in tents.
That might explain the strong bond that developed
between Jacob and Joseph, who was his youngest for many years.
Now although Jacob liked to dwell in tents,
he was by no means a sissy.
He was a strong man, but he was a spiritual man.
That’s something for you young brothers to take away.
You want to be strong, we know you do,
but spirituality should come first.
One time, spiritual Jacob gave his sons a beautiful lesson
on how to settle a difference with a family member.
We read about it at Genesis chapter 32.
And I think all of us can learn from his example.
We learn at Genesis 32
that Jacob’s brother, Esau, was coming to see him.
Now, they hadn’t seen each other for 20 years,
and to say that their parting had been difficult is an understatement.
The fact is that when they separated more than 20 years earlier,
Esau had vowed that one day he was going to kill his brother;
now he was coming to see him.
Now, why was he so angry with Jacob?
It’s because Jacob had received a blessing from their father,
and Esau was not happy.
So Esau arrives,
and 400 men are with him.
Why 400 men?
Well, the Bible doesn’t say.
But it could be that he was trying to show
how important and prominent he had become.
How did Jacob react?
Did he try to go tit for tat?
Did he try to show how important and prominent he had become
with all of the blessings he’d received?
Did he reopen old wounds?
Did he argue with his brother?
Did he say, ‘You know I was right all along,
and you, Esau, you have been wrong’?
Did he demand an apology?
No.
There was a lot that Jacob could have bragged about.
No question about that.
There was no doubt that Jacob had Jehovah’s blessing.
Early on, we read that an angel of Jehovah
had appeared to him and said:
“I am Jehovah
“the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac.
“The land on which you are lying,
“to you I am going to give it and to your offspring.
“I am with you,
“and I will safeguard you wherever you go . . .
I will not leave you.”
Well, that’s quite a blessing, isn’t it?
But there’s more.
For a portion of the previous night
—that is, the night before Esau and Jacob met up—
Jacob had wrestled with an angel,
and as a result,
he had managed to receive another blessing.
But Jacob didn’t flaunt his blessings.
Instead, he humbled himself.
In fact, he even bowed down seven times before his brother
in front of his wives and his 11 sons.
So Jacob settled any lingering difference with Esau
not with his fists,
not with a bragging tongue, not with a weapon,
but humbly, like a real man
—like a real, spiritual man.
In contrast, how did Jacob’s ten sons
settle their difference with Joseph?
Like a bunch of cowards.
It was 10 to 1 against Joseph.
First, they decided to kill their brother,
and then they delivered him up into slavery.
Those jealous young men didn’t learn a thing
from their father’s excellent spiritual example.
Well, if you’re on the outs with a member of your family,
if you had a serious difficulty with someone,
could you try to settle the matter peacefully as Jacob did?
If the person tries to apologize, be gracious about it.
Don’t make it difficult for him to apologize.
Don’t dredge up
all of the unnecessary details about the past.
You may be in the right, as Jacob was,
but isn’t the important thing to make peace?
Jehovah loves the peacemakers.
Well, what else do we learn about Jacob?
We learn that he wasn’t his father’s favorite.
Let’s look at Genesis chapter 25
verse 28.
“And Isaac loved Esau
“because it meant game in his mouth,
whereas Rebekah loved Jacob.”
Now, this story may resonate with many of you out there,
especially if you’ve grown up in a large family
or perhaps you’ve had a number of brothers and sisters.
Now, we know your parents claim
that they always treated all of you the same,
that they never ever had a preference.
But ask the kids,
Was there anyone in the family who was the favorite?
They all know. ‘She was!’
They know this.
The parents don’t realize it, but they are giving preferential treatment.
And so this happens, and it can be disconcerting at times.
Imagine this scenario:
Imagine that you have a couple who have two children, two sons.
One is a pioneer.
He has never given his parents a moment’s grief.
The other never accepted the truth,
but he has done well in business,
and as a result, he has been generous to his parents,
and the parents are grateful, very grateful.
And the pioneer often hears the parents bragging
about the successes that his brother has had in business.
Well, the pioneer can’t help the parents materially very much,
and so he feels that there’s a bit of partiality there.
Is it hurtful?
Yes. That is life.
It’s chemistry. It’s just chemistry.
But the pioneer needs to realize
that Jehovah God appreciates his work.
His heavenly Father loves him very much
for the work that he is doing for His name.
Now, Jacob must have known
that Isaac loved his brother more than he loved him.
And perhaps he vowed that when he had children,
he would treat them all the same.
Well, if he did, he didn’t keep that promise, did he?
Everyone knew that Joseph was the favorite.
Well, have you noticed what we had to do to make a composite of this family?
We had to read from several different chapters of the Bible
You can’t always get a complete picture of an incident
by reading just one chapter, just by reading the chapter you are reading.
Sometimes you have to extract details from other chapters of the Bible.
Now let’s consider one more example
where getting the complete picture can enrich our understanding.
This is going to be a shorter one.
We’re going to consider the story of Naaman.
Now, you remember the story.
At 2 Kings 5:1,
we learn that Naaman was the chief of the army
of Ben-hadad II, the king of Syria.
But he was a leper.
Now Ben-hadad learned that there was a prophet in Israel
Elisha who could heal him of his leprosy.
And so he told Naaman that he should go to Israel
and go to the prophet and get healed.
And so word was sent to the king of Israel by letter,
and the king of Israel was asked to send Naaman to Elisha.
Now, when you think of it, this was a strange request
because Israel and Syria were often at odds.
Sometimes there were wars between them,
and now, here you have the king of Syria sending his general,
the one who is going to head the army against Israel,
and saying: ‘Well, I’d like my general to be a more effective general.
Could you please make sure that he gets healed?’
Well, somehow, he’s sent to Elisha
and Elisha kindly heals Naaman
and Naaman becomes a worshipper of Jehovah.
Well, we can imagine,
remember we’re talking about using our imagination,
we can imagine that when Naaman returned to Syria,
Ben-hadad had lots of nice things to say about Elisha.
So then, everyone lived happily ever after, right?
If we didn’t read on, we might think so.
But that’s not the end of the story.
In the next chapter, chapter 6,
we learn that Ben-hadad declared war against Israel.
Now, if Naaman was still the chief of the army,
he’d be in an awkward position.
Was he going to lead the armies of Syria
against fellow worshippers of Jehovah?
But it gets worse.
Ben-hadad learns that Elisha
is revealing the Syrians’ war strategies to the king of Israel,
so he sends a large army to capture Elisha
—the very man who had healed his general.
So much for gratitude.
Now, it’s interesting that Naaman is not mentioned
as being at the head of those armies.
Did he get out of it somehow?
Don’t ask me.
If he’s resurrected, you’ll have to ask him.
What lesson can we learn?
That the gratitude of the world is fleeting.
Some of us may get excited if there’s a favorable article
about Jehovah’s Witnesses in a newspaper
or if some TV personality makes a kind statement about us.
But what did Jehovah God say?
Genesis 3:15:
“I will put enmity between you and the woman.”
So Jehovah’s organization and Satan’s organization
are always going to be at odds.
Bible reading isn’t a chore.
It’s a joy.
Get the whole picture of what you’re reading,
and you’ll enjoy it even more.
We wish you all Jehovah’s rich blessing
as you continue to enhance your appreciation
for this sacred volume.

en.text: For me, this is a historical moment.
I was very worried about how we will succeed.
But you can see that this is not possible just by people’s efforts.
The angels are helping, and Jehovah gives his spirit.
Actually, this went beyond our dreams, what we get.
Of course, there have been many efforts put into it,
but it was worth it.
And we are very thankful
to the Governing Body that they made this possible for us.
We welcome the 60 brothers and sisters who symbolized
their dedication to Jehovah who have now joined us
as footstep followers of Jesus.
Thank you, friends, for all the love and the kindness
you’ve shown us here in Sofia.
It’s a great privilege to be here with all of you and feeling the love
that Jehovah has for us and for everyone of you as well.
I think that the best gift that we received
from our brothers was their smiles
of happiness.
We saw how the brothers and sisters,
with all their hearts, gave their time
and were thinking about how to make the delegates feel welcome.
To host this special event is really a huge privilege for us.
Thank you all for coming.
We are happy, and we look forward to seeing each other again.
We love you.
Thank you for your gifts.
I think the question we all had in the beginning was, Will we make it?
Still today, I don’t really understand how it worked out.
But we used everyone, everywhere.
We knew that the brothers here
in Bulgaria had less materially, but we also saw
that they had a big heart.
Many different languages
are spoken here, but the spirit is the same.
We experienced what an international brotherhood really is.
The local congregations helped a lot.
They prepared a pleasant surprise for every tour.
At the end, we saw joy
and happiness on the brothers’ faces.
For being here for the week, it really had such an impact on us.
It’s been wonderful.
It’s been a faith-building experience,
and it really brings us together as a worldwide organization,
and we’re privileged to be a part of it.
So when we follow instruction from the organization
regarding the ministry
and we think about the brothers’ happiness
and the joy in the ministry,
we can see the result.
We saw that in the end, Jehovah opened large doors.
We managed to accommodate our precious delegates
in the best hotels, and we saw how Jehovah
can make the impossible, possible.
These three days, we met our “relatives” from Bulgaria,
from the United States,
from Macedonia, from Serbia, Ukraine, Moldova
and we wouldn’t change this for anything else.
Some of the joyful tears we will shed in the new world,
we have experienced here.
The memory of this is beautiful. Thank you!
We are truly a family.
Da!
The feeling I had with this event is just like we had the impression
to walk for a few moments in the new world.
This is the way I felt.
We would like to help you learn how you can be on Jesus’ side,
on his side, when he completely conquers the world!
We look forward to being with you at a convention in the new world.

en.text: Sister Margarita Königer has seen
the growth of the Kingdom work all her life.
She has served as a missionary since 1966,
and we met her in Hungary,
where she has now served for about nine years.
In the 50 years since she graduated from Gilead,
Sister Königer has learned seven languages
and has served in five different countries.
And recently, she received a new assignment
—the Chinese field in Munich, Germany.
Daily reading and meditating on God’s Word, the Bible,
has given her the strength she needs
to continue with joy in her missionary assignment.

cn.text: 玛格丽塔·柯尼格尔姐妹
一生亲眼见证王国工作的扩展
她从1966年就开始做特派传道员
现在住在匈牙利，在那里服务9年了
对我来说，布达佩斯是个很漂亮的城市
周围有许多国家
好像一个大熔炉，非常国际化
这里主要是匈牙利人
不过也有不少人从世界各地来
我是个特派传道员
在中文地区服务已经9年了
我做特派传道员有47年了
第一个委派是在马达加斯加
我们主持圣经讨论
在那里传道很棒，当地人很友善
我在马达加斯加服务了四年半
后来当地的传道被禁止
我们被驱逐出境，只能带走一些行李
不过，我们也没什么东西
后来，我们被派到肯尼亚
三年后，我们的工作再次被禁止
然后，我们到了贝宁
跟认识的人一起传道
可是我们要很小心
因为那时贝宁刚成为共产国家
有一天，军方和警察都来
还有一群年轻人非常激动地喊着
（外语）E huzu! Dandan!
“为了自由，我们准备好了！”
他们包围了伯特利
我们都没办法出门
好像我们是坏人一样
隔天，有两个高大的警察来说

我们什么行李也没带就去了
在路上大家一直聊天
我们也向他们传道

然后，他们走过来说

他们就继续载我们往前行

我想，那是我特派传道员生涯中
最危险的一次经历
那时就只有我们两个女生

有些弟兄姐妹来这里
拜访他们的家人朋友之后

他们有很好的精神
我很感谢耶和华

title: 트럭 운전사들에게 생명의 길을 알려 주다

en.text: Every year, thousands of truck drivers from all over the world
crisscross the European continent.
They work hard to make ends meet for their families
but often have to spend weeks away from home.
Jesus and his apostles approached people
wherever they were.
It is this same spirit that must motivate us.
By trying to reach truck drivers wherever they can be found,
we can make sure that everyone receives a witness,
even those who would otherwise be missed.
We live in the Rotterdam area
which has a lot of truck traffic.
We cover our regular territory
once every three months,
while these truck drivers are hardly ever reached.
We noticed that 300,000 trucks
crossed France every year.
Thus, it was necessary
to explore this formidable potential for the ministry.
Many truck drivers use truck stops to take a short break
or even spend the night there.
That’s ideal for preaching.
While we are parked here,
resting,
we are cleaning the trucks;
we are washing our clothes because there is no laundry here;
and also we do our cooking.
One day on my way to France,
I had to stop in Austria
to swap drivers.
My colleague went to the bathroom, and I was alone.
At that moment, a Witness came and offered me a magazine.
Much effort is being put into reaching truck drivers
in an organized way.
We made sure all truck stops were mapped
and organized schedules so that pioneers
can preach in this territory at least once a day.
Publishers will encounter many different nationalities and languages.
The language barrier is one of the biggest challenges.
On any given morning, you can encounter up to ten different languages:
Romanian, Russian, Polish.
When I looked at the magazine, I saw that it was a Watchtower,
but I thought it was in German.
I told this brother that I did not speak German.
Then he had a look at my license plate and saw that it was Romanian.
He again offered me the magazine and told me:
“It is Romanian. It is for you.”
When I saw it, I was very happy.
I took the magazine and was very glad.
Of course, we don’t speak in tongues like the first-century Christians did.
But jw.org makes us feel like we can preach in any language.
We need to go further than just distributing publications.
We need to be real teachers,
and to do that, we can make use of the videos.
A driver had his Bible
wide open on his dashboard
and literally cried
when he watched the video Why Study the Bible?
Since truck drivers spend most of their time on the road,
it is a real challenge to follow up on those who have shown any interest.
It’s very difficult to do return visits or to start Bible studies.
You just don’t know when you will meet a truck driver again.
So we try to get their e-mail addresses as soon as possible.
The results were remarkable.
For example, in the last service year,
about 100,000 magazines were placed,
100 Bible studies were started,
and 4,000 videos were shown.
Experience shows that even if it’s not possible
to obtain an e-mail address,
the slightest witness given can have a great impact.
In time, I returned to Romania.
I started a Bible study, progressed spiritually,
got married, and now I am an unbaptized publisher.
The brother that first contacted me has no idea.
Hebrews 6:11 invites us all
‘to show industriousness’ in our ministry.
The more you invest in this form of ministry,
the more fulfillment you get from the positive response of the drivers.
It is a good thing to preach the good news at truck stops
because all drivers need to feel God’s love,
to see that God really cares for us.
And like me, they can make changes in their lives.
And they need to see that Jehovah has promised a future paradise
and how this will affect them and their families.

title: 블라디미르와 미하일: 진정한 친구는 여호와의 축복입니다

en.text: What if we face a situation in which we have access to nothing?
We are not allowed to have a Bible,
no literature with illustrations,
no videos, and no audio recordings.
What do we do?
Our recollection of what we have read in the past
can keep our spirituality intact.
One of our brothers from Russia faced such a situation.
Notice what helped him.
The year was 1963.
I was 36 at the time.
The KGB searched my home and found some Bible literature
and some publishers’ field service reports.
So I was sentenced to five years of imprisonment
for being an organizer.
That was the third time I had been imprisoned.
Some brothers and sisters and I went to the court
to support Brother Vladimir.
When he saw us, he clasped his hands
and declared, “Everything is fine!”
A KGB officer told me
that the only reason I hadn’t been imprisoned
was because I had six children.
But Vladimir was single.
I was just glad that they had arrested me and not him,
because I didn’t have a family.
In the camp, I didn’t have a Bible or any Bible literature at all.
All I had to keep me going was the knowledge I already had.
We prayed for him, and we sent greetings
and encouraging messages to him through his relatives.
Due to the strict censorship in the camp,
we were not allowed to write anything spiritual in our letters
to encourage each other.
If we did, the letters were confiscated.
But I really wanted to send Brother Mikhail something encouraging.
I was growing flowers with a group of inmates in the camp.
So instead of a sending him a letter,
I decided to send him a bouquet of flowers.
Vladimir’s sister Olga came to our home,
and she brought me a beautiful bouquet of flowers from Vladimir.
I couldn’t believe that I had received fresh flowers
from behind a barbed-wire fence —from inside the camp.
I was so touched by his act of kindness
that my heart moved me to write down some verses,
a poem, which I called “The Bouquet.”
My relatives came and visited me in the prison
and delivered to me the poem.
I kept the poem in a very secret place.
It could have been confiscated,
and I could have been punished because it was about God.
After Vladimir was released from prison,
well, he told me that my poem had really strengthened him
and that he had often taken it out
of its secret hiding place to read it over and over again.
If it hadn’t been for the support I received from Jehovah
and the prayers of friends,
it would have been much harder for me to serve my time.
The poem that I had received helped me not to feel
separated from my friends
and, most importantly, from Jehovah.
So many years have now gone by.
But we have remained firm through the difficult times,
and we continue serving Jehovah.
Lately, Vladimir and I have been trying to keep in touch by phone,
but we haven’t seen each other for seven years.
I would really love to see Vladimir again.
He doesn’t know that I’ve decided to go and visit him.
I hope that he likes the surprise.
“I see these flowers, grown by hands
“Hardened from work that prison demands.
“My friend has sent a bouquet.
“Prison three times prevented our meeting,
“But you found a way to convey a greeting.
“My joy now moves me to say:
“‘Greetings, my brother, with all of my heart.
“‘You gave me strength, although we’re apart.
“‘While you have countless trials withstood,
“‘You’ve strengthened me as best you could.
“‘Greetings, my friend on that narrow road,
“‘You were always with me through hardships untold.
“‘We worked so hard for spiritual treasure.
“‘Blessed we were for sticking together.
“‘Cruelly, my friend, you were taken from me
“‘When they tried to break our integrity.
“‘But God stood by us and helped us to cope.
“‘Conquer the evil, we did, for our dear Kingdom hope.
“‘How grateful we are and always will be
“‘For spiritual vision by which we can see
“‘The crown of life promised to those
“‘Who stay on the loyal course they chose.
“‘How much you’ve endured, long-suffering friend.
“‘But Jehovah’s mercy will never end.
“‘On a paradise earth our hands will unite,
“‘Planting more flowers to gladden His sight.
“‘Christ Jesus will heal us during his reign,
“‘So no trace of sin will ever remain.
“‘And far from the trials that we overcame,
Forever we’ll praise Jehovah’s great name!’”
True friends are such a blessing from Jehovah,
and you don’t really know who they are until disaster strikes.
During my whole life, walking in the way of the truth,
I have often thought about the words of Psalm 119:63,
where it says:
“I am a friend of all who fear you
and of those who keep your orders.”
Our serving side by side in the Kingdom work
has strengthened our friendship.
It is only that sort of friendship that will last forever!
What a beautiful friendship!
Our brotherhood truly is a blessing from Jehovah.
Brother Mikhail Savitsky spent many years as a circuit overseer,
helping the Kingdom work progress in Siberia, northern Caucasus,
and the countries of Georgia and Armenia.
In 1992, he had the privilege of being one of those
who signed the documents that confirmed legal recognition of our work in Russia.
However, we regret to inform you
that some time after this segment was produced,
Brother Vladimir Varkholik fell asleep in death.
He was 88 years old
and had served Jehovah faithfully for over 59 years.
At the time of his death,
he had served as a pioneer for some 26 years
and as an elder in the congregation for 43 years.
From his interview, you can clearly see the faith
that kept his spirituality strong through 12 years of imprisonment.
And he is a good example for us.
Did you notice one aspect of his circumstances while incarcerated?
He said:
“In the camp, I didn’t have a Bible
“or any Bible literature at all.
“All I had to keep me going
was the knowledge I already had.”
That could happen to us.
When persecution starts, we need to be prepared.
That’s one reason why it is so important
not to neglect our study of the Bible
while we have the opportunity.

en.text: A visual aid often makes a clearer
or more lasting impression on the mind
than does the spoken word.
Under the direction of the Writing Committee,
the Art Department has enjoyed
the privilege of designing and illustrating Bible literature
for almost 40 years.
The department was established sometime before 1976.
But a small team of artists had been working on illustrations
and typography
from as far back
as the “Photo-Drama of Creation.”
The work of publishing Bible literature
has seen many changes.
Now there are EPUBs, interactive PDFs,
Web design and HTML content
—all of which require
new skills as well as close collaboration
with many other Bethel departments.
The Art Department is structured into teams.
Each team is made up of designers,
photographers,
illustrators,
prop and set makers,
costume and makeup artists, as well as production workers.
The team lead and the scheduler work
directly with the Writing Department contact, known as a compiler.
After receiving an early version of the text, the three brothers discuss
the purpose and possible look of the design.
All on the team are invited to collaborate as concepts are developed.
Each member contributes to the overall design of a project.
Before any production work is started,
concepts are sketched and developed.
These sketches become a blueprint
that helps the team understand the concept,
plan the resources,
and ensure that the project stays on track.
Who is the target audience?
How will this publication be used?
The design should be clear and simple.
And it needs to work in all languages.
This is no small task.
When the design is ready, the compiler presents
a mock-up of the publication to the Writing Committee.
The committee reviews the design and makes any needed adjustments.
After the concept is approved, production begins.
Around the world, there are many
photographers who work part-time to assist
in providing images.
Photographs are also taken in our studio
and other locations.
These images help give our publications an international look.
Accuracy is vital.
A researcher provides
historical references and inspiration.
Hair, makeup,
and costumes are
designed to depict the time period and region.
Props, set design, and lighting
provide the right look and setting.
When combined, each element
helps tell the story and capture
the imagination of the viewer.
Sets are also built in 3D programs.
They can be used as art source
or as final illustrations.
Whether painted digitally or with traditional materials,
the artist renders
the illustration in a style suited for its final use.
When design meets illustration, infographics are born.
After final approval by the Writing Committee,
files are sent to the printeries
and to the website or used to create other digital versions.
In order to reach the hearts of those who
read a Bible-based publication,
hands and hearts have to be involved in its creation.
Those of us in the Art Department
consider it a privilege to give support to the most
urgent of all work
—preaching the good news.

title: 연구와 묵상을 통해 다시 기쁨을 찾으십시오

en.text: That’s my roommate, Camille.
And, well,
that’s me.
I haven’t felt like myself recently.
I started regular pioneering a couple of years ago.
At first, I was really zealous.
But somewhere down the line,
I lost that good feeling.
Soon, I was losing my joy for almost everything.
I honestly didn’t know what was wrong.
It wasn’t like I was doing anything bad.
I thought,
‘Maybe I’m just tired.’
But it wasn’t getting better.
I tried to assess what was going on with myself.
I felt love for Jehovah.
I felt love for the congregation,
but I felt unmotivated in my service.
I felt like something was missing.
As my enthusiasm waned,
my meeting attendance suffered too.
Thankfully, the loving elders in my congregation noticed,
and help was on the way.
The brothers visited to see how I was doing.
They really listened to me,
and they asked about my spiritual routine.
Well, I read the Bible every day,
but, I admitted, I’m not a natural study person.
They reminded me about the example of Mary,
Jesus’ mother.
At first, I didn’t see the link,
but as we read from the Bible, it became more clear.
Mary was known for being a faithful woman.
But what kept her faith strong?
The Bible account said that Mary paid careful attention
to words that had deep spiritual meaning
and later took time to meditate,
“drawing conclusions in her heart.”
By meditating on spiritual things,
Mary strengthened her faith and zeal for serving Jehovah.
I understand now.
I was reading spiritual food, but I wasn’t taking time to digest it,
so it wasn’t sinking down into my heart.
As a result, I was on a direct path
to spiritual burnout if I didn’t change something quick!
I began by taking control of my busy schedule.
I made it a priority to start my day with Bible reading.
I sought out quiet places
where I could meditate on what I read.
Meaningful Bible study reinvigorated
my passion for serving Jehovah,
and prayerful meditation
helped me to refocus.
Over time, making these changes
helped me to find joy in my service to Jehovah again.
The Bible says when we make time
to read and meditate on spiritual things,
we will become “like a tree planted by streams of water,”
with foliage that never withers.
And everything we do will succeed.

en.text: The city of Milan, in northern Italy,
recently hosted an important international event
—Expo Milano 2015.
It was an exposition that lasted for six months
with 145 participant nations
and 20 million visitors arriving from every corner of the earth.
What did Jehovah’s Witnesses do in order to spread
the good news to such a vast number of people?
Mobile witnessing carts were set up at strategic points
around the main entrance of the Expo.
Four hundred and fifty Witness volunteers
were instructed on how to spread
the message to the thousands of passersby.
The theme of this Expo
was “Feeding the Planet, Energy for Life.”
And, in line with this, arrangements were made
to reprint the series of articles that appeared
in a 2012 issue of Awake! magazine.
The series was entitled “Is Your Food Really Safe?”
Of course, most of the visitors would find accommodations in the city.
Therefore, congregations in and around Milan
made an effort to contact all the hotels in the area to offer the staff
and their guests an opportunity to read
this special edition of Awake! on food and nutrition.
At first, some brothers were nervous they wouldn’t be received well,
but the reaction of most of the hotel administrators
was very encouraging.
Almost everyone was happy to accept a copy of the magazine.
Thanks to your cooperation,
each month the magazines were brought to us.
It has sparked interest because people
—clients, the guests— can find an interesting magazine
to look at in their own language,
and they nearly always run out of the magazines by the end of the week.
Was it worth the effort?
Well, in a period of just six months,
over 360,000 magazines were placed
—244,000 of which were the special issue dedicated to food.
And to date, 892 people have asked to be recontacted.
In the past few years, the community of Jehovah’s Witnesses
has become much more visible in the city of Milan.
It’s not unusual to see them with their carts,
even in the more central areas of the city.
And I must say, they’re always smiling, polite, and well-dressed.
They have adopted a new method.
Now it’s the passersby who decide whether to stop
and take one of the items on display or have a brief conversation.
The Milanese people really like this method.
The topics presented are always very timely.
The display about food really stands out.
It brings to mind the general theme of the Expo—feed the planet.
I must say, it’s a great initiative.
I was able to speak to a couple visiting from China,
and I gave them a copy of the special issue of Awake!
After having explained to them that we are volunteers,
to my great surprise, they invited me to have lunch with them.
We had a really nice conversation for around three hours,
during which they asked me a lot of questions.
I left them the book What Does the Bible Really Teach?,
and it was lovely to see how they agreed that the Bible
really can improve people’s lives.
A tourist from Argentina already reads our magazines regularly in her country.
When she saw our carts, she immediately recognized our magazines,
and then she took a copy of the special June 2012 issue.
She exclaimed, “I like your magazines
because they make a person a good person!”
A school teacher, accompanied by her students,
noticed our special issue of the Awake! magazine
and told her students to each take a copy
because later on they would consider it in a class discussion.
Other school teachers present did the same,
so that in just a few minutes, we distributed 70 magazines.
A specially equipped bicycle
was used to ride back and forth between the storeroom and the carts.
As a result, the magazines were available
7 days a week, 12 hours a day.
How encouraging it is to make the most of every opportunity
to praise Jehovah!
There really is no better way to use our time.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Proverbs.
King Solomon composed the majority of the proverbs.
Solomon became king of Israel in 1037 B.C.E.,
and Jehovah gave him extraordinary wisdom.
Most of Solomon’s proverbs, or wise sayings,
were written down during his reign.
However, it seems that the entire collection
of proverbs was compiled into one book
some time around 717 B.C.E., in Jerusalem,
before the end of King Hezekiah’s reign.
The book of Proverbs provides divine guidance
for virtually every aspect of daily life
—from business dealings to family matters.
As such, it helps prepare us
for life under God’s Kingdom.
Proverbs contains 31 chapters
and may be divided into five sections.
The first three sections are attributed to Solomon.
Chapters 1 to 9 make up section one,
which consists of short discourses
containing a father’s advice to a son.
The father warns the son about the bad results
of acting on wrong desires
while emphasizing the good results
of trusting in God’s wisdom.
Section two called the “Proverbs of Solomon”
and section three called
the “Proverbs of Solomon Transcribed by King Hezekiah’s Men”
both present concise sayings
designed to make the reader think.
Many of these proverbs contrast the traits we should avoid
with the ones we should cultivate.
Many contrasts are used,
such as laziness versus diligence
and selfishness versus generosity.
These short parallels are instructive
and easy to follow.
These two sections contain
more than 500 of Solomon’s proverbs.
Did you know?
The Bible tells us that King Solomon
spoke 3,000 proverbs and composed 1,005 songs.
Chapter 30 makes up the fourth section and was written by Agur.
He uses comparisons of four
to help us reflect on godly wisdom,
such as four things that are small
yet instinctively wise.
The final chapter was composed by Lemuel.
Some believe that Lemuel is another name for Solomon.
This chapter contains a description of a capable wife.
It points out her qualities
and the positive effect she has on her family.
Godly wisdom must be sought after like hidden treasure,
but its value is eternal unlike that of silver and gold.
As you read Proverbs, note how it shows the benefits
of trusting in God’s wisdom instead of our own,
how it identifies traits we should avoid and those we should cultivate,
and how it teaches us to live under the rule of God’s Kingdom.

en.text: My name is Monica Richardson.
I studied genetics and chemistry
and then medicine in Stockholm, Sweden.
I believed in evolution because of my education.
Everybody did.
It was something I never doubted;
it was taught as a scientific fact.
And even those who perhaps believed
that there was a God believed that this God
would have used evolution in the creation process.
I want to talk about the miracle of birth.
Now, during pregnancy,
the baby is supplied oxygen via the placenta,
but at birth it will have to use its lungs.
In the womb the baby’s lungs are collapsed.
After breath, they have to become inflated.
Now, this is a very hard work for the baby to do.
So during the latter part of pregnancy,
there is a very special chemical
produced and secreted
called a pulmonary surfactant.
And that chemical is being deposited on the surface
of the peripheral parts of the lungs
where the gas exchange is taking place
to lower the surface tension.
And that means that when the baby is born
and starts to inflate its lungs, he can do it.
One wonders, ‘Is this a result of a clever,
‘intelligent conception and design,
or could it have happened by chance?’
Well, it was when the Witnesses called on me
that I really got encouraged to,
for the first time in my life, look into the Bible.
Life around us is so cleverly designed
I can’t believe there is a design without a designer.
