en.text: Millions of our brothers and sisters around the world
can recount the blessings they’ve gained
by remaining loyal to Jehovah and his organization.
And we’re privileged to have two such examples here with us today:
Brother and Sister William and Sandra Malenfant.
Brother Malenfant is a helper to the Teaching Committee,
and Sister Malenfant’s current assignment is in the Service Department.
And we’re looking forward to hearing about their rich spiritual history.
So, Bill and Sandra, we’re so happy
that we could have you here in the studio with us,
and we do look forward to learning more about you.
Maybe we would like to go back.
How did you get on the road that has led you
to so many years of faithful, loyal service to Jehovah?
It was back in 1954.
My mother had contact on and off with the Witnesses for years.
I was about 20 years old,
and she was invited to a public talk
at the Oakland Central Congregation in California.
She asked me, “Would you accompany me?”
And I said: “Yeah. Sure, I’ll be happy to go.”
Well, I recognized a young man I knew from high school at the meeting,
and he approached me after and told me I needed a Bible study.
I really didn’t want a Bible study, but he insisted,
and so I said, “Well, you can come by.”
Would you believe it?
I started a Bible study in the “Let God Be True” book.
Four months later, I was baptized.
It was exactly what I was looking for, but I didn’t realize it.
Excellent!
Now, I understand that you were also very involved with sports.
Yes, I was playing ball for a basketball team in Alameda,
and I enjoyed very much playing ball.
But then, a decision came up as to what I was going to do
because the evenings when the team played was the same time
that we had the Service Meeting and the Theocratic Ministry School.
So I had to make a decision.
And my decision was: Forget the sports,
and let’s go to the meetings and enjoy being built up spiritually.
Good choice. Thank you.
And, Sandra, your start on the road to a career serving Jehovah?
I suppose you could say that it actually started before I was born.
Before I was born, my parents started on this search for the truth.
It happened because they had lost a little girl in death,
and they went from church to church looking for some kind of comfort.
And, of course, the clergy had no comfort for them.
They just said, “Well, God wanted another angel in heaven.”
And that angered my father. He thought: ‘No.
‘If God wants another angel, he can make one.
He wouldn’t take my little girl!’
So it just happened
that one evening they were listening to the radio
—long before TV, of course—
and they heard a Jehovah’s Witness give a talk.
And the title of that talk was “Where Are the Dead?”
Imagine!
He gave all the Scriptural proof about the condition of the dead
and the hope for the resurrection.
And my father immediately said, “This is the truth!”
So they wrote to the radio station;
got a copy of the booklet of the talk;
and then, also, they started receiving
the subscription to The Watchtower.
But it wasn’t until I was born and three years old
that the Witnesses finally made contact with us.
Interesting.
In fact, it was interesting.
It was a real cold winter day, and even though I was only three years old,
I remember this family coming in.
And they stayed hours.
I even hid in the closet and went to sleep.
But, you know, it was just—
It was that contact with the visible organization
that my family needed.
Because they knew much of the truth.
They’d been reading The Watchtower for a long time.
So my elder sisters, they got baptized right away and started pioneering.
For my brother and I —we were a lot smaller, of course—
we just went along with our parents and came right into the truth.
In fact, I remember, it was just a couple of years later
that we were all going to go to the big convention
in 1950 at Yankee Stadium.
But I knew there was going to be a big baptism there,
but I wanted to go as a baptized Jehovah’s Witness.
So my father— Everybody made arrangements,
and my father baptized me
in our pond on our farm
with another young sister.
Is that right?
So that was my beginning.
You know, Ron, there’s a point I’d like to recall also.
Sandra was at a special convention back in 1941.
That’s true, even before that.
That was probably my first, you know, big event theocratically.
Our family—my brother was four years older than I,
along with my parents— we went to the St. Louis convention
where Brother Rutherford gave his famous talk on children.
And they separated— The lower level
of this place that they rented, this stadium,
was dedicated to just the young children,
well, from 5 to 18 years of age.
And it was just fantastic, you know, with this man.
When you’re small, this man would look so big and huge,
and he had this great big voice.
And I’ll never forget when he looked out on the audience, and he said:
“Behold, more than 15,000 new witnesses to the Kingdom!”
So it was very emotional.
Oh, you still remember it like it happened yesterday.
Oh, yes!
Right, how exciting!
So, what motivated you to make a choice
to get into the full-time service and give your life to Jehovah?
Well, what motivated me
was when I attended a convention, also in ’56.
I got baptized in ’54.
But in ’56, I went to a district convention in Albany, California,
and there was a pioneer booth.
Because in those days they had a booth set up at the district conventions,
and various brothers and sisters would man the booth
and answer your questions about pioneer service.
So I approached the booth, and an older sister there looked at me
and said: “You’re young and strong.
Why aren’t you a pioneer?”
I felt, ‘Well, yes. Why not?’
So I started pioneering in 1956.
That’s what motivated me.
And I was— Really, I look back at that;
it was one of the best decisions I made in my life.
Excellent!
Yeah, so you have been making wise decisions from your youth up.
Sandra, how about you?
Motivated to get into full-time service.
Well, for pioneer service, you know, it was—it was like a given.
Young people were just encouraged to pioneer.
And you knew that when you graduated from high school,
you started out pioneering.
And most of the young people were doing that.
You know, after a year or two, maybe they would get married and start a family.
But those years in pioneering —starting out their life that way—
gave them a wonderful basis for loyal service the rest of their life.
And not only that, I remember that in those days
the traveling overseer would stay in the homes
of the brothers when he served the congregation.
And we always played host
to the circuit overseer and his wife when they came.
And for my brother and I, they were role models.
My sisters, as I told you, were out pioneering in another assignment.
But for us, these brothers were so full of zeal,
and they were like heroes to us.
In particular, I remember when I was, I think, about 12 years old.
This couple came around on the circuit, Percy and Ilma Iszlaub,
they were from Australia and, of course, we loved their accent too.
And they had just graduated from Gilead,
and they were assigned to Japan,
but they had to wait a number of months to get their visa.
They served in our congregation,
and it was really them that instilled in me
the desire to become a missionary.
Beautiful.
So you were pioneering.
How did your paths eventually meet?
It was at a circuit assembly
in Oakland, California, 1956.
Very interesting things took place.
I had the job of dismantling the stage.
I had not yet met Sandra.
She was out visiting her sister who lived in the same area where I was.
And I was carrying this large piece of plywood off the stage,
and I ran right into Sandra and knocked her flat!
Well, I took advantage of the opportunity.
I thought, ‘Well, that’s not the best way to introduce yourself.’
But I said, “By the way, would you like to accompany me
to a get-together some of the friends are having?”
And she accepted. And . . .
Very good, Bill.
Well, yes, and I followed through on it.
We had a lot of association,
and after a number of months, we got married.
And both of us were pioneering
—very happy in our ministry serving Jehovah.
You really swept her off her feet. Literally.
I fell for him.
Very good.
So, shortly after you were married,
I understand that you received some direction.
Yes, the circuit overseer visited our congregation.
We were only married about a month, I think, when he came through.
I think so.
And he told us that the organization was looking for pioneers
who’d be willing to serve as special pioneers and go wherever,
where the need was great in the United States particularly.
So we told him: “Sure. We’d be delighted to do it.”
And four months after our marriage,
we received an assignment as special pioneers to Decorah, Iowa.
Now, that was a very interesting place
because there were only eight publishers in the congregation.
But we arrived and started with the meetings
there at the Kingdom Hall.
And the Kingdom Hall was up above Hunt’s Variety Store
in downtown Decorah, and we lived in a room behind it.
Well, sometimes, especially during the wintertime
because it could be very cold, there’d be no one at the meeting.
After all, there were only eight publishers.
But I was insisting that:
“No, I’m going to give my public talk, whether anyone is here or not.”
So I’d tell Sandra, “You sit there, and I’ll give my public talk.”
A one hour talk, and then I’d conduct the Watchtower Study
and have her answer every question.
Well, you know, you’re on your own like that
—not a lot of brothers around—
so you look for encouragement and company.
And we would travel down to Strawberry Point, Iowa,
to where Charles and Shirley Sinutko lived
in a log cabin —one-room log cabin.
And we’d go visit with them in order to have some mutual encouragement.
Yeah, because they were special pioneering also.
OK. Well, you were both special.
It’s a nice picture of you in that log cabin too
as you were special pioneering.
So you’re busy in that work.
What special invitation did you receive?
Well, we received the invitation to attend Gilead
—the 34th class of Gilead School—
and that was a wonderful thing after two and half years of pioneering,
special pioneering in Iowa.
Our instructors were Albert Schroeder, Maxwell Friend,
Bob Porter, and Jack Redford.
And we had a delightful time at Gilead, as you can imagine.
And we were assigned to Lebanon,
but we were unable to enter Lebanon because we couldn’t get the visa.
So, then, the organization asked us,
“Well, will you take an assignment to Morocco?”
We were ready to go anywhere.
We were pioneering with the Canarsie Congregation
just waiting to go out into the field.
So that’s how we took a boat from New York City
—five days across the Atlantic— to Casablanca.
Very nice.
Well, what was it like to be in the missionary service in Morocco?
It was very interesting.
We really enjoyed it. But, you know, we only spoke English.
So in Morocco, we had to learn French.
And the first month of our missionary service in Morocco,
for 30 days we studied the language 11 hours a day.
Well, that could get pretty tiring for 11 hours a day,
so we’d go to the French movies and count that as language time.
And then, we were moved to Tangier.
And there was a Spanish congregation in Tangier,
so we had to learn the Spanish language too.
But that was really a rich blessing
for the two of us to be exposed to that culture
and to have that privilege of serving there.
But you know what I really enjoyed?
We had a variety of people we preached to.
We had a very large Jewish population,
and they were almost all Orthodox.
But, you know, they were very forthright,
and they were open and quite curious.
You know, like they’d come up to us sometimes and say:
“Well, you’re Christian, aren’t you?
Why do you accept Jesus as the Messiah?”
So we had to get familiar with a lot of scriptures, you know,
that dealt with the prophecies the Messiah would fulfill, in the Hebrew Scriptures.
And really, it was a delight.
Sandra, do you remember, there were a lot of French people in Morocco?
Because it used to be a colony under France,
so that’s why the French language was so important.
And then we had Spanish people and many other nationalities there.
So you had four years of serving in Morocco
—faithfully, loyally meeting all those of different languages
and learning the language yourself.
So after four years, I understand that you came back to visit your family.
What events were challenging thereafter?
I think Sandra can relate that.
Well, it was usually permitted
that after you were in your assignment four years,
then you were allowed to come home
and at least have a vacation and visit your family.
And so we made arrangements to come back.
We got some tickets on a Yugoslav freighter;
took us two weeks to get back to New York.
But we got back.
We visited our family, and while there,
I had a medical examination and found out that I had a serious health problem.
Of course, we didn’t have the funds to cover that.
So Bill wrote to the Society, and we made arrangements.
They said, “Well, just take care of your situation,
and let us know when you’re free.”
So he got a job to take care
of our medical needs as well as living conditions.
But you know, we just felt like we were failures.
I’d always wanted to be a missionary,
and there we were four years into our assignment,
and we come back and poof!
We’re just there.
But, you know, Jehovah knew we were discouraged.
He knew we felt distraught about this.
So he knew just what we needed, and he gave it to us.
As I got to feeling better and we got more free
in our use of time, we started pioneering.
And Jehovah blessed our ministry just incredibly.
There were times, in this supposedly “unproductive territory”
that we had up to 25 people attending the meetings.
Many of them got baptized, and they’re our fast friends to this day.
That’s incredible!
So Jehovah knows what you need, and he provides it.
That is beautiful!
What temptation did you have to resist
when you came back and were going through these difficulties?
Well, I think it’s a temptation that confronts
a lot of brothers and sisters who return because of health reasons,
and some just end up settling down because of their circumstances.
But the temptation there was: ‘Well, you’re home.
‘You’ve already done your service in Morocco for a number of years.
‘You’ve been in the full-time ministry.
Just settle down now. Buy a house.’
But really, that wasn’t our desire.
So as soon as Sandra got on her feet
and was feeling well enough, we got pioneering.
And then I wrote headquarters, and I said: ‘Here we are.
‘We’re ready to take on whatever.
What would you like us to do?’
You know, I’d like to say here, Ron,
that I really appreciate Bill as my spiritual head
because even though these things presented themselves
in the course of our theocratic history,
he was always quick to accept the responsibility of what we felt
was our spiritual, familial, and moral responsibility
but as soon as these obligations were taken care of,
he was very quick to get us back on the road
to meet our spiritual goals that we had.
And I really do appreciate that.
Good example. Thank you.
So you made yourself available to the organization.
Where did they send you next?
A wonderful assignment.
We were sent as special pioneers to Washington D.C.,
to help start a Spanish congregation.
And that was indeed a very rich blessing.
We were there a year and a half
until that little congregation was solid and was formed.
And then we received another blessing.
We were appointed to the circuit work.
So I had the Spanish circuit in Florida
from Key West to Orlando —one circuit in the whole state.
Then we came to New York City —lived in the Bronx.
I had a circuit, and we did district work in the Spanish field.
Then, to Texas
—to what they call the Valley of Texas, the Rio Grande Valley—
for a couple of years in the circuit.
Then the district in Spanish
from Houston, Texas, to Yuba City, California.
And we loved every minute of it.
Well, that’s definitely the traveling work.
I know you were in that work for nearly ten years,
so I’m sure you really benefited
a lot of brothers and sisters along the way.
Then 1977 rolls around and you receive another invitation.
Yes, indeed!
We were doing preconvention work
in the L.A. area at the Leimert Assembly Hall,
and we received a letter inviting us to come to Bethel.
That was a very, very special privilege: to be invited to Bethel.
I went into the Service Department,
because at that time they invited a number of traveling overseers
to come in and work in the Service Department,
and Sandra went into housekeeping.
And we were both delighted to come to Bethel.
Well, sort of.
I really loved the ministry;
I loved, especially, the district work
—being with the circuit overseer and his wife
every week and out in service.
So I wasn’t too anxious for this Bethel thing.
But, you know. Jehovah, again, knows what you need.
We came here, and we started adjusting to Bethel life.
And it really proved out to be a real blessing
because we got the close association
with so many other loyal Witnesses of Jehovah.
Yes. And then for the rest of us
that have been able to work with you over the decades,
we appreciate your loyal example and working with you.
But, I understand that shortly after you arrived to Bethel,
you also received some challenging family difficulties
that you needed to deal with.
Yes, Sandra had an older sister who needed help.
Yeah. We were still adjusting, like I said.
And we heard that one of my older sisters,
who had spent most of her life in the pioneer service,
she had now entered the terminal stages in her long fight with cancer,
and she needed some homecare.
And the brothers in the organization were very kind to me,
and they allowed me some free time to go
and care for that responsibility.
Then, it was just a few years later
that my mother was facing a similar situation.
And this time, again, the brothers allowed
both Bill and me to be free to go back there.
My mother was now aged 89.
She had health situations and she lived alone, so she needed care.
And again they allowed us this time; we went back.
And just as in the case with my sister,
I was able to keep my mother home just until she died.
And, you know, we appreciate so much being granted that free time.
Even though when we left,
we didn’t know if it might mean the end of our Bethel career.
But again we felt the need to fulfill that responsibility.
And, you know, Ron, it was-it was a bittersweet experience.
This is Satan’s wicked world; death is our enemy.
And it hurts to see a loved one suffer.
But, you know, there’s the sweet side of it too,
because we had shared some wonderful moments
together with my family and experiences, shared experiences.
And we felt good that we had been able
to help these people that had been mentors for us.
Yes.  So loyalty to your family and loyalty to Jehovah.
Exactly.
So you returned back to Bethel.
You were busy in your assignments.
And, as you mentioned, you worked with many loyal ones at Bethel.
Could you share one such experience of a loyal sister?
Oh yes.
I was assigned to the Alterations Department,
the Sewing Department.
And recently before that,
Sister Gertrude and her husband, Martin Poetzinger,
had been called into Bethel, and he was a member of the Governing Body.
And she had been trained under a tailor, so she was excellent in alterations.
But most valuable were our spiritual conversations.
I learned so much from that sister.
Once, we were talking —a group of us—
about what our relationship to Jehovah really means.
And Gertrude gave us her idea,
her understanding, of her relationship with Jehovah.
She said, “You know, sometimes in life a situation presents itself,
“and it’s so personal and so touching
that you don’t tell anybody about it —except Jehovah, of course.”
And she said: “So you pray to Jehovah, and you pray to Jehovah.
And then pass a little time, and you feel he’s answered your prayer.”
She said: “You know, that is like a little thread
“that unites you with Jehovah.
“Now, this is the only person in the universe
“that shares this experience with you.
“So it’s very personal.
“OK. Time goes by;
“another situation presents itself, and you pray again.
“Well, here is another thread.
“And over a period of time, you’ve got a bunch of threads
connecting you with Jehovah.”
And she said, “And those threads are all knitted together,
and they form a cord that unites you with Jehovah.”
And then she’d say, “And don’t you ever do anything
to endanger that relationship.”
But, to me, it just— It really hit my heart.
I thought, ‘This is so true.’
Our relationship with Jehovah and our loyalty to him
has to be the first important thing in our life.
Well, thank you for sharing that.
That has affected all of our hearts. Appreciate that.
So, Bill, you have received many privileges of service
before Bethel and your 40 years since you’ve been at Bethel.
One of the privileges that you have had is traveling to different branches
as a headquarters representative, or a zone overseer.
What are some memories you have of all those various visits?
It’s a very rich privilege to do it, Ron,
to serve at that time as a zone overseer.
The brothers receive you so well.
Basically, the zone overseer, or now the branch representative,
he goes to be of encouragement to brothers.
And he visits the branch; meets with all the Bethelites whenever possible;
tries to talk to all of them, giving encouragement;
meets with all of the missionaries in the country.
And you’re received so warmly.
I remember when Sandra and I visited Tahiti.
We flew into Tahiti —Papeete, Tahiti—
and it was three in the morning when we arrived.
The brothers were absolutely wonderful.
There were about 35 brothers waiting for us there,
piling flower leis upon us, giving us a kiss on each cheek.
But the warmth of the brothers and the joy of being
with the Bethel family was something.
Well, the one sister didn’t find any room
left on your cheeks, remember, she kissed you . . .
No. So I got a kiss on the top of the head.
But the joy of the brothers was just wonderful,
and we’ve had the great privilege of visiting a number of branches.
And I understand that you traveled to Bolivia,
and you had a nice experience in Bolivia.
I just loved this work because I got to play missionary when I was out there.
And, of course, my heart was always in the missionary field.
But I remember when we went to Bolivia; since it was a smaller branch,
I was allowed to go out and work in service with the missionaries.
And they came, and they picked me up at eight o’clock in the morning.
And they said, “We are going to take you out to a Mennonite colony.”
And so I left at eight, and I didn’t get back until eleven o’clock at night.
And I was a little bit disturbed about that hour.
That late for her getting back.
Well, you see, it’s a Mennonite community.
They don’t have electricity, and we didn’t have cell phones at that time,
so he had no idea what was happening to me.
But we studied all day with this family,
and eventually, by the way, they all came in to the truth.
And their experience came out in 2005,
September 1 issue of The Watchtower,
about this family of Mennonites that came into the truth.
And now the work is spreading like wildfire among the Mennonites.
But, anyway, toward the end of the day, it was getting near dusk
and the missionary (just to tease me) said to the family,
“Well, it’s time to milk the cows now.
So bring up the meanest one you’ve got, and ask Sandra to milk her.”
So, of course, he didn’t know I was raised on a farm.
Hmm. OK.
So it had rained all day, and it was muddy and nasty out there.
But I had my high heels on, silk blouse, earrings, but we went out to the barn.
And they gave me a bucket, and I was able to milk the cow.
What a nice experience.
And she wasn’t mean at all.
Well, I’m sure you have many more experiences
to let us know about, but we appreciate you sharing those.
The Governing Body has made significant adjustments
in the work that is taking place at Bethel and the field,
and it has affected many long-time faithful brothers
—loyal brothers in the traveling work,
overseers in the congregation, overseers at Bethel.
Bill, what do you think about some of these changes
that the Governing Body has made recently?
I think they’re very wise decisions.
They know what is needed;
they appreciate the older men who have served for years.
We know that the older brothers in circuit work, district work,
wherever, they’re “worthy of double honor” because of the way
they’ve given of themselves to the work.
But we have to recognize, too, there comes a time
when we want the younger men to come along,
to accept responsibility.
And, really, when we were young,
we received responsibilities with very little background and training.
Now we’ve got all these schools for Kingdom Evangelizers
and the Kingdom Ministry School.
So many opportunities for younger ones to be trained.
And so I think it’s a wonderful arrangement.
Many thousands of young men are doing so well,
ready to accept responsibility.
It’s a blessing for the entire organization.
Well, thank you for sharing that.
That’ll benefit many brothers.
So we look at this couple before us,
and we see some who have made wise choices along the way.
So we look back at over 60 years of faithful, loyal service.
As you look back at decisions
you made in life, any regrets?
Oh, absolutely none!
We consider that whatever
we have given up or done it’s been our gift to Jehovah.
You know, when I was a little girl, I remember I used to go out on our farm
and, especially when there was a full moon, I used to pray to Jehovah.
And I’d say, “Just let me use up my life in your service.”
You know, he’s answered that prayer because my life,
the majority of it, is used up and he’s let me do it in his service.
Sort of makes me think of one of my favorite scriptures,
Jeremiah 29:11.
It’s where Jehovah, referring to his faithful, loyal ones, says:
‘I well know the thoughts I am thinking toward you,
not of calamity but of peace and a future and a hope.’
Now the calamities that we face in life,
that doesn’t come from Jehovah; that comes from Satan’s wicked old world.
But Jehovah promises us peace, a future, and a hope.
Now, how could you not be loyal to such a God?
Beautiful.
Bill, how do you view sacrifices that you have made along the way?
Well, as you know, a sacrifice
can be something you give up to serve God, perhaps.
Or a sacrifice can be what you give to Jehovah,
like David said in Psalm 54.
“I will sacrifice to you willingly.”
And that’s how I view sacrifice.
We’re happy to give of ourselves to Jehovah God—to serve him.
And I want to add, too, Sandra has been
a wonderful partner with me —willing to go anywhere,
put up with all kinds of circumstances and difficulties,
never complaining about the travel
or whatever circumstances we found ourselves in,
living very close to the earth for a number of years as special pioneers.
But Jehovah has been with us.
A scripture that I— There are a number
of good Scriptures, obviously, that we all love.
But one in particular that stays in my mind
is Romans 14:7,8:
‘We live, we live to Jehovah.
‘We die, we die to Jehovah.
So whether we live or we die, we belong to Jehovah.’
And we’ve made that decision, not just because he’s the Creator.
We’ve made the decision to give ourselves to Jehovah God.
So, absolutely, we’ve had the best life possible.
We have no regrets at all
about what we’ve done with our life, giving Jehovah the first place.
Bill and Sandra, it’s been a real privilege
to hear more about you, and I know there are more stories to tell.
How can you boil down 60-plus years of loyal service to Jehovah?
But you have given us great insights.
Thank you for sharing those gems with us.

en.text: My name is Ángel Santaliestra Fierro.
I studied medicine and surgery
at the Central University and the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona.
Childbirth is awe-inspiring.
For example, when a mother’s efforts culminate in childbirth,
that intimate bond formed between a mother and her baby
is something I will never get tired of seeing,
even though I’ve witnessed it dozens of times.
I was born into a devout Catholic family.
From the moment I started studying at the university,
everything I learned was in favor of evolution.
These studies impacted me,
even though I didn’t have a strong foundation in evolution.
But deep inside me, I believed in evolution,
but I didn’t have much of an alternative.
Perhaps my own selfishness was also to blame
because I didn’t have to answer to God for my conduct.
I could do things that I had been told as a boy were forbidden,
and so the figure of God
slowly began to crumble in my mind.
I read a book entitled
Life—How Did It Get Here? By Evolution or by Creation?
Well, I read through the whole book that very same day,
and I saw so much evidence
that I immediately wanted to show
the book to my colleagues at the hospital.
At the time, I was still finishing
my specialized training in pediatrics.
Some of them called me a heretic!
For me, that book marked the beginning of my belief
in an alternative to the theory of evolution.
We all started, both you and I,
every single human being, as a single cell.
But this single cell did not just produce a human.
It also produced the placenta.
For a mother, it’s foreign tissue,
and yet it allows her to transfer all the life
and potential she has to her unborn child.
This is truly amazing!
It must have required a lot
for somebody to have designed something like this.
This encourages me to believe that a Creator exists.
I can only conclude
that it is worth the effort to spend time
getting to know the person who designed it.

en.text: We received a report from San Francisco, California,
in the United States,
where publishers have been engaged in special metropolitan witnessing
since 2013.
It’s helping our brothers reach multiple language groups,
start Bible studies, and make disciples.
When I’m rolling the carts down to get ready for the work,
I can feel people’s eyes on me and it makes me feel proud
that I’m representing Jehovah even before I get to the location.
We have a chance to use our Bibles very regularly.
We talk to honesthearted people who are interested
in really learning what the Bible teaches.
Jehovah is reaching people in those hard-to-reach areas
where it could mean their life
to even talk about things such as the Bible.
When you’re part of the metropolitan work,
you get to welcome people being drawn by Jehovah.
We see thousands of people every day who walk by our carts.
While we’re placing literature in up to 40 different languages each week,
what’s really exciting is to see how many conversations we’re starting
and how many Bible studies we’re initiating.
We’re visible to a lot of people in the community,
especially those who were inactive or maybe were raised around the truth.
Jehovah has arranged to have his people
put right in the center of everything,
and we’re able to meet people from all over the world.
I’ve met people from Peru, South Africa,
Japan, Germany, England.
France, Italy,
Cameroon, Congo.
Beaucoup!
In Shona, a greeting would be something like . . .
. . . , which means “Would you like to study the Bible?”
. . . , which means “Would you like to study the Bible?” in sign language.
So when I asked her if she had seen the sign-language Bible,
she shook her head no, and I showed her Acts 17:27.
And as soon as it was done, she started signing, “I understood that!”
And then she said, “Didn’t you say this was a free app?”
So, right then, she started downloading it on her phone.
We had a gentleman come up and wanted to . . .
First, he said, “debate,” and then he said, “just discuss.”
But as he was talking with us, he had to catch his train
but he missed three trains
because he wanted to continue the conversation and speak with us.
It’s a really good experience because we just get to talk to people
and let them see a different side of us.
It’s not necessarily about whether we placed a book with him or not.
And in the end, he turned to my husband and I
and said, “You know, you’re really good ambassadors.”
We start Bible studies here every day,
and these studies are conducted globally.
I met Alfredo in 2014, right before the Memorial.
He approached the cart.
He had a rough life.
He was doing a lot of bad things,
and so he felt that he couldn’t overcome them.
So I told him that no matter how big his problems are,
they’re not too big for Jehovah,
and so I encouraged him to start studying the Bible again.
“Come, now,
and let us set matters straight between us,” says Jehovah.
“Though your sins are like scarlet,
they will be made as white as snow.”
When Jehovah forgives you, he forgives you completely.
I got baptized, and in the same month,
I started auxiliary pioneering.
It is such a privilege to be one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
with brothers all around the world.
If anybody is hesitant to take part
in the special metropolitan witnessing work,
maybe you’re worried about finances, time,
or you’re just afraid that it’s something different
and you won’t know what to do,
please don’t let any of those things stop you.
It’s from Jehovah.
Grab hold of it tight, and don’t let go!
Each month, the brothers and sisters
in San Francisco’s metropolitan witnessing
distribute over 5,000 publications
and start an average of 185 Bible studies.
After some initial concern from local authorities
over having literature carts at the Golden Gate Bridge,
authorities have expressed appreciation for our brothers being there
with the Bible’s message of hope.
It’s been requested that we always have on hand
the April 2014 Awake! with the cover title
“Why Go On? —Three Reasons to Keep Living.”
One afternoon an officer approached a cart and said,
“Well, your magazine worked!”
The police had just helped a young woman
who was thinking of jumping from the bridge.
When they reached her, she had the Awake! issue in her hand
and had decided not to jump.
Life in this system can be difficult for everyone,
but our witnessing work comforts people
and teaches them to know and thank their Creator for life.

en.text: The first rodeo I performed in front of an audience, I was eight years old.
We were considered one of the top two acts in rodeo.
My strength lay in my fearlessness.
Even though there was a certain amount of excitement
—it was fun to travel, to be together as a family—
it was empty.
Trick riding is like gymnastics on the back of a running horse.
We’ve had horses all of our lives.
My father specialized in training horses.
He used to send us to the mountains,
riding all day long.
And then we’d come home in the evening,
and we would start trick riding.
The way we learned was by a book.
We looked at stick pictures that showed how it should be done,
and so it was trial and error.
At the same time that we were learning, our horses were learning.
The horse that I rode just let me do anything.
My horse’s name was Sweet Lips.
I was eight when I got him, and I named him myself.
He was like my best friend.
My parents were very active in the rodeo as competitors.
My mom was barrel racing;
my father was a saddle bronc rider.
I grew up as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
but when I was very young, maybe six or seven,
my father stopped serving Jehovah.
To be honest with you,
when they announced that at the Kingdom Hall,
it really didn’t have much meaning to me at the time.
I didn’t know what it meant.
And I could see people crying, and so I cried.
But I didn’t really understand it.
Really, from that point, our family was not active as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I grew up on the road, traveling rodeo to rodeo
—from coast to coast and from the south to the north—
as far as the roads go.
The four of us rode initially
—Connie; Kelly; myself; and my brother, Jim.
Our family traveled together.
That meant a lot to me.
What separated us from the others at the time
was the high speed that we did it at and also
the difficulty with the tricks that we chose to do.
People were very excited.
They would hire us back at the same place year after year.
Throughout all that time,
we did not miss one Memorial.
We were always there. There was something in us.
We didn’t know it when we were little,
but my parents had succeeded
in planting the truth in our hearts.
My link to the truth was my grandmother.
I can remember going to the ranch and visiting her.
She was very busy, but one thing that really sticks in my mind
is she always studied —every day.
She read her Bible. Her magazines were studied.
And I think it just put a seed in there that later on started to grow.
I just felt like I needed direction.
It’s like a line was drawn in the sand.
Take one path or the other.
And so, ironically, the first book
that I picked up to read was the Bible.
One of the scriptures that probably
meant the most to me was Proverbs 3:5,6:
“Trust in Jehovah with all your heart
“and do not lean upon your own understanding.
“In all your ways take notice of him,
and he himself will make your paths straight.”
I used to think about those words
and what I would have to do to live up to them.
Although we traveled with the rodeo
about ten months out of the year,
we did go to the district convention,
and the Live Forever book came out.
And there just came a time when I knew
I—I needed to make changes.
A sister started studying with me,
and as I started reading the Bible for myself and studying,
then Jehovah became real.
All it took was one or two people,
and the whole family followed.
My father too returned to the truth.
Trick riding was our family business.
It was our livelihood, but we had decided that we were done.
We were going to stop.
With that decision would come giving up everything we knew.
I think—I think the most difficult thing
for me to do was to sell the horse
—you just, you just get such a close bond with them
when you’re putting your life in their hands like that—
but I was willing to do that.
I just—
I knew what I wanted to do; I did it.
I got baptized in October of ʼ85.
Our last performance was in February of ʼ86.
We just finished out our contracts.
I started pioneering in September of ʼ86,
and I’ve never stopped.
I also married a man who loves Jehovah.
We’ve had the privilege of working
on international construction projects.
We went to Mexico.
We went to Venezuela.
My father is an elder. My mom is pioneering.
In fact, all of my siblings have been able
to regular pioneer at some point in their lives.
We’re presently in the circuit work.
Serving Jehovah together is such a blessing.
Everything that we do every day is for Jehovah.
That’s what I wanted to do
when I made this decision.
If I would have taken that other path when I was young,
I may not be alive today.
What I did was dangerous.
Even fame and fortune in the world —there’s nothing there.
I wanted “the real life.”
I wanted to serve Jehovah.
I have no regrets.
If I could change anything
when it comes to my service to Jehovah,
I would change nothing!
I would just do it better.

en.text: This month’s theme is taken from David’s poetic song to Jehovah
at Psalm 18:25, which states:
“With someone loyal you act in loyalty.”
The Hebrew term “act in loyalty”
reminds us of God’s loyal love
—that is love motivated by commitment,
integrity, loyalty, and deep attachment.
So loyalty is more than just a feeling;
it is active; it’s rooted in love.
How comforting it is to know that Jehovah
lovingly attaches himself to those who are loyal to him!
But what motivated David to write the words
at Psalm 18:25?
The superscription reveals that it was composed
after “Jehovah rescued him from the hand of all his enemies
and from the hand of Saul.”
Think of the great joy and relief he must have felt
after experiencing firsthand Jehovah’s loyal love
and mighty saving acts.
However, throughout his life,
David experienced disloyalty at its worst:
from his king, Saul; from his wife Michal;
from his trusted counselor Ahithophel; and from his son Absalom.
He felt the deep hurt of betrayal by those he trusted and loved most.
Loyalty is a choice.
What do we find when we look back at David’s life?
David chose to stay loyal to God.
From a humble shepherd boy caring for his sheep
to a valiant king caring for the nation,
he proved to be someone loyal,
a man agreeable to Jehovah’s heart.
But it can be a real test to maintain loyalty to God
when we face injustices.
Imagine the desperate situation that David and his mighty warriors
experienced when they were fugitives,
forced to hide in the wilderness, often low on provisions.
They saw firsthand King Saul’s jealous rage.
But what choice did David make when urged by his men
to seize the opportunity to take Saul’s life?
Notice what David told his men
at 1 Samuel 24:6:
“It is unthinkable from Jehovah’s standpoint
“that I should do such a thing to my lord,
“the anointed of Jehovah, by lifting my hand against him,
for he is the anointed of Jehovah.”
David knew that if he remained loyal,
Jehovah would remain loyal to him
—He would show him loyal love.
He humbly put aside his personal feelings
and viewed matters from Jehovah’s perspective.
He chose to wait patiently for Jehovah to “act in loyalty.”
We’ll soon be facing life-changing events foretold in the Bible
that will test our loyalty to Jehovah and his organization.
So now is the time to strengthen our loyalty!
As we do, we can be sure that Jehovah knows our circumstances
—perhaps injustices we have experienced—
and will reward our loyal service.
So ask yourself, ‘What loyal actions
will motivate Jehovah to be loyal to me?’
Let’s consider three areas.
First, we can be loyal to Jehovah by defending him.
But Jehovah is the Sovereign of the universe.
How can we come to his defense?
We can learn how from the fine example of Elihu!
In the book of Job, Elihu listened patiently as Job
and his three false comforters spoke.
Notice Elihu’s reaction
at Job 32:2, 3:
“His anger blazed against Job
“for trying to prove himself right rather than God.
“He was also very angry with Job’s three companions
“because they could not find an answer
but had declared God wicked.”
A fire of righteous indignation was burning inside young Elihu.
In Job 36:2, 3,
he loyally comes to Jehovah’s defense saying:
“Be patient with me a little longer while I explain,
“for I still have words to speak on God’s behalf.
“I will speak comprehensively about what I know,
and I will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.”
Elihu courageously proved loyal
by praising, and, yes, defending God.
Why do we need to come to Jehovah’s defense today?
Because our loving heavenly Father is blasphemed in so many ways.
False religions claim that he’s part of a Trinity
and that he torments people eternally in burning hell.
Others say that he does not exist or if he does,
he doesn’t really care about us.
We know that such lies come from Satan the Devil.
We demonstrate our loyalty
by speaking in defense of Jehovah,
thereby proving Satan the liar that he is.
We boldly and zealously proclaim
that he does exist as the almighty God;
and that he is wise, just, and loving,
and that he will soon bring an end to all evil
and reward his loyal ones with eternal life.
Jehovah could make the stones cry out in defense,
yet he honors his loyal Witnesses —you and me—
with this fine privilege.
Second, we can be loyal to Jehovah by being loyal
to “the faithful and discreet slave,” the Governing Body.
Jehovah and Jesus are using “the faithful and discreet slave”
to feed us spiritually, so we owe our loyalty to that slave.
But some may say,
‘Isn’t the Governing Body made up of imperfect men?’
Yes, it is.
The last perfect person to walk the earth was Jesus himself.
There is no perfect person or organization on the globe.
But as a long-time faithful brother used to say,
“This is the best imperfect organization on earth.”
Jesus didn’t say the slave would be infallible.
He said it would be faithful and discreet.
The way we listen to and obey the faithful slave
has a direct bearing on the strength of our friendship with God.
In fact, it means our very life.
But what if the Governing Body
serves some spiritual food that is not to our liking?
Or what if we do not fully understand
or agree with a clarification of a belief?
On one occasion, Jesus’ followers, including the apostle Peter,
were confronted with a new teaching.
How did most react?
Notice John 6:60, it states:
“When they heard this, many of his disciples said:
‘This speech is shocking; who can listen to it?’”
The result?
Continuing in verse 66:
“Because of this, many of his disciples
went off to the things behind and would no longer walk with him.”
But how did Peter respond when Jesus asked them,
‘Are you too stumbled?’
At John 6:68, we read:
“Simon Peter answered him:
‘Lord, whom shall we go away to?
You have sayings of everlasting life.’”
What loyalty!
Peter’s loyalty was based on solid evidence
that Jesus was the Messiah.
His loyalty was evidence of his faith.
That is the kind of loyalty we want to imitate today.
There are times we must wait on Jehovah to clarify matters.
In the meantime, may we prove ourselves loyal like Peter
and follow closely the lead of the faithful slave,
who closely follow in the footsteps of their Master, Jesus.
At times, though, we receive counsel that touches us personally.
For instance, on JW Broadcasting we’ve received loving reminders
from members of the Governing Body to be forgiving,
to honor Jehovah with our valuable things,
and to remain spiritually alert.
Through The Watchtower and at Christian meetings,
we’re reminded to be careful about our dress and grooming,
to choose good associates and wholesome entertainment,
and to remain morally clean.
Are we quick to respond and make needed adjustments
or do we find ourselves wanting to defend our personal rights?
A situation in the apostle Paul’s life
tested his loyalty to theocratic direction.
It’s found in Acts chapter 21.
As you recall, Paul arrived in Jerusalem in 56 C.E.
after a very successful missionary tour.
You can imagine his excitement as he related in detail
“the things God did among the nations through his ministry.”
After hearing Paul’s extraordinary account,
the older men revealed to Paul
a problem in Judea that involved him personally.
Read what they said at Acts 21:21:
“But they [the Jewish believers] have heard it rumored about you
“that you have been teaching all the Jews
“among the nations an apostasy from Moses,
“telling them not to circumcise their children
or to follow the customary practices.”
Well, perhaps Paul thought, ‘Me, an apostate?
‘Really? How can they say such a thing?
‘I just finished my third missionary tour,
and look how Jehovah blessed the work!’
Nevertheless, the older men gave Paul very clear direction
at Acts 21:23, 24
that he likely did not anticipate,
and there it reads:
“So do what we tell you:
“We have four men who have put themselves under a vow.
“Take these men with you and cleanse yourself
“ceremonially together with them and take care of their expenses,
“so that they may have their heads shaved.
“Then everyone will know that there is nothing
“to the rumors they were told about you,
but that you are walking orderly and you are also keeping the Law.”
Was this the time for Paul to question
their decision or demand his rights?
He could have reasoned:
‘Didn’t you read my letter to the Galatians,
‘where it says the Law was nailed to the torture stake with Jesus?
‘I did nothing wrong!
‘Why do I have to put on this pretense
just because a few are overly sensitive?’
No.
He humbly did as they requested,
although it nearly cost him his life.
Yes, it meant swallowing his pride,
but Paul knew there were bigger issues
involved than his personal rights.
He was considerate of the consciences of others.
But more importantly,
he showed his loyalty to Jehovah and to the governing body.
Do we see the bigger issue in our life?
Let us be determined to be humble,
flexible, and obedient like Paul,
and thereby prove ourselves faithful
to “the faithful and discreet slave.”
Third, we can be loyal to Jehovah
by being loyal to the elders.
We’ve discussed loyalty to Jehovah himself and to the faithful slave,
but what about direction we receive
from the elders in our congregation?
We listen to our elders give talks
and comments at the meetings each week,
we work with them in the ministry,
and we associate with them.
This regular contact gives us more opportunities
to see their imperfections and flaws.
We could begin to focus on their weaknesses,
weakening our trust in God’s arrangement.
For example, if you zoom in
on any of our pictures in our magazines,
all you’ll see are colored spots or pixels.
But when you zoom out,
you see a beautiful photo or painting.
Similarly, when looking at our elders,
don’t zoom in on their imperfections —the spots of ink—
rather, see the big picture.
Why, then, is it so important
to strengthen our loyalty to our hard-working, loving shepherds?
Because these “gifts in men”
are an expression of Jehovah’s loyal love
as they loyally lead, feed,
and protect his precious sheep.
As the great tribulation nears, our survival will depend
on our readiness to respond to their direction,
as they follow the Governing Body’s direction.
Our loyalty is not to men,
but to Jehovah’s arrangement
made up of imperfect, but loyal men.
That is a lesson that Korah, Dathan,
and Abiram refused to learn.
In this clip from the video Respect Jehovah’s Authority,
listen to Korah’s defiant attitude toward Moses
as taken from Numbers chapter 16.
There’s Moses.
That is enough of you
because the whole assembly are all of them holy
and Jehovah is in their midst.
Why, then, should you lift yourselves up above the congregation of Jehovah?
Korah and the others made great pretenses of loyalty to God,
but completely ignored the fact
that Jehovah directly appointed Moses and Aaron.
Who, then, were they really murmuring against?
Notice Numbers 26:9:
“This Dathan and Abiram were chosen ones of the assembly
“who fought against Moses and Aaron along with Korah’s group
when they fought against Jehovah.”
While focusing on the man Moses and his imperfections,
they did not really see that it was Jehovah who was directing the nation.
They were actually fighting against Jehovah.
Their disloyalty to God’s appointed men cost them their lives.
But Korah’s sons made a different choice.
In this next clip, notice an attitude far different from their father’s.
My father and his companions
actually rebelled against Jehovah’s authority.
Their envy, pride, and ambition led to rebellion,
and in the end they brought dishonor upon themselves.
My father sought glory, but his glory was short-lived.
I’m glad, though, that my brothers and I took the right side of the issue.
It must have been hard though.
Yes, it was.
But that helps us to understand how important it is
that we do not allow friendships or family
to take priority over our relationship with Jehovah
and our obedience to him.
That’s what Father has always told me.
Mmm, yes.
Ultimately, successful direction for us humans
comes from Jehovah.
We should completely trust in his choices of appointed ones.
You see, respect for those whom Jehovah has appointed
shows respect for Jehovah’s authority.
The loyalty displayed by Korah’s sons
moved Jehovah to act in loyalty by sparing their lives.
What fine examples for us to imitate!
May we never find ourselves fighting against Jehovah
by murmuring or complaining against those
who he has appointed to lead his people today.
To see more of the good and the bad examples
of loyalty among the Israelites,
we encourage you to watch the entire Respect Jehovah’s Authority video
on JW Broadcasting.
In review, how can we show our loyalty to Jehovah?
First, by coming to his defense as his Witnesses.
Second, by maintaining our loyal support
of “the faithful and discreet slave.”
And third, by loyally following direction from the appointed elders.
As you imitate faithful examples like the sons of Korah,
like David, Peter, and Paul,
you will prove to be someone Jehovah views as loyal
—worthy of receiving his acts of loyalty forever.

cn.text: 本月的主题取自大卫的赞美诗歌
诗篇18:25，经文说
忠贞不渝的希伯来语
让我们想到上帝的忠贞之爱
这是一种基于承诺、道义和忠贞的
不离不弃的爱
所以忠贞不只是一种感觉
还要有行动，出于爱的行动
知道耶和华上帝对那些忠于他的人不离不弃
多么令人安慰
什么推动大卫写出诗篇18:25呢？
题记告诉我们
耶和华拯救他脱离所有敌人和扫罗的魔掌后
他做了这首诗
大卫亲自体验耶和华大能的拯救和忠贞之爱后
一定感到安心，也非常喜乐
不过在大卫的一生中
他曾经被一些人辜负和出卖
例如扫罗王、妻子米甲
他信赖的谋士亚希多弗
还有他的儿子押沙龙
被深爱和信任的人背叛，他一定很痛心
忠贞是种选择
回顾大卫的一生，我们看出什么呢？
大卫他选择忠于耶和华上帝
从照顾绵羊的谦卑牧童
到照顾国家的英勇君王
他证明自己是忠贞的
是合耶和华心意的人
可是当我们受到不公平的对待时
要忠贞就不容易了
想想大卫和他手下的勇士在逃难时
处境有多艰难
他们被迫躲在旷野，物资也很缺乏
他们见到扫罗因嫉妒而恨大卫
不过，当大卫的手下怂恿他把握机会杀死扫罗时
他怎么做呢？
请留意撒母耳记上24:6大卫所说的话
大卫知道，只要他保持忠贞
耶和华就会对他忠贞，表现忠贞之爱
他谦卑地把自己的感觉放到一旁
用上帝的观点看事情
他耐心等候耶和华采取行动，表现忠贞
我们很快就会面对圣经预告的大事
这会考验我们对耶和华和他组织的忠贞
所以现在就要决心保持忠贞
我们这样做就能确信
即使受到不公的对待
耶和华上帝都一定了解
而且会因忠贞奖赏我们
请想一想
我们怎么做，耶和华就会对我们忠贞呢？
让我们考虑三个方面
首先我们要表现忠贞，为耶和华辩护
耶和华是宇宙的至高主宰
我们怎样为他辩护呢？
我们可以效法以利户的好榜样
在约伯记
以利户耐心地听约伯和他的三个朋友说话
请留意以利户在约伯记32:2,3的反应
正义的怒火在以利户的心里燃烧
在约伯记36:2,3
他忠贞地为耶和华辩护，他说

en.text: ‎For sure, Maltese people are a friendly people.
‎It’s in our tradition to be like that,
‎but the Christian love that Jehovah
‎wants us to grow inside,
‎that will triple the effect.
‎In October 2015, the time finally arrived
‎for the 650 publishers on the island of Malta
‎to host over 1,500 delegates
‎for the “Imitate Jesus” Special Convention.
‎This would allow for a unique
‎and unprecedented shout of praise to Jehovah.
‎Well, the work in Malta was for a long time
‎rather restricted, and there was a lot of opposition.
‎Now, with this special convention,
‎the brothers make an impact on the people here.
‎Some of them were not aware that we are
‎a worldwide brotherhood.
‎The Maltese are very impressed with numbers.
‎So now when they see all these numbers
‎and all this activity, they’re going to change their whole minds
‎about us, and it’s going to open their hearts and minds to our message.
‎As well as making a positive impact in the field,
‎the delegates got to visit the nearby isle of Gozo
‎and have an interchange of encouragement
‎with one of the territory’s most isolated congregations.
‎We were looking forward to this for over a year now,
‎and to have the reality
‎—you see the brothers here, you can talk to them,
‎you can hug them, you see the love,
‎the sincerity— and that’s what makes the difference.
‎Hospitality was shown by means of the evening entertainment program,
‎which not only shared the local culture
‎but glorified Jehovah and the many treasures found in his Word.
‎The children loved every bit of this thing.
‎They even said: “What are we going to do when this finishes?
‎“We loved being with Jehovah’s children.
‎It’s so different than being with the children in school.”
‎By means of the convention, I have felt closer to Jehovah,
‎and I felt that I had Jehovah’s spirit.
‎And, yes, I also met many other children from different congregations,
‎and I really enjoyed that.
‎The brotherly love continued
‎as other tours were hosted all across the beautiful island,
‎allowing the visitors to see Malta and the Maltese people to see the visitors.
‎“After we made it to safety,
‎“we learned that the island was called Malta.
‎“And the foreign-speaking people showed us extraordinary kindness.
‎They kindled a fire and received all of us kindly.”
‎We extend a warm welcome to all those present.
‎We would like to give a special welcome
‎to the 1,550 delegates
‎coming from Australia, Portugal, Spain,
‎Greece, Israel, and the United States!
‎I found the truth in 1960.
‎And it was difficult at that time
‎because there was no one in the truth.
‎When I saw this crowd here,
‎I was filled with joy seeing how Jehovah has made it grow.
‎I was here in 1980 as a missionary.
‎We only had 82 people here.
‎And now look at it!
‎From that little, little group, we are now huge!
‎And that makes me very happy.
‎It reminds us of a prophecy in the Hebrew Scriptures
‎not to ‘despise the day of small beginnings.’
‎It doesn’t matter whether there are many publishers or a few.
‎The fact is that Jehovah through his holy spirit
‎can do things that we are not even imagining
‎so that there will be an increase in Kingdom proclaimers.
‎With the special convention now over,
‎a lot of us take a deep breath and say, “Ah, it’s done.”
‎But it’s not time to stop; now is the beginning.
‎The brothers and sisters give us a lot of encouragement.
‎When they came, they brought along their love as well.
‎And seeing all this makes you even want to give more.
‎Doing this for Jehovah, it’s rewarding, it is, truly.
‎The Scriptures are right.

en.text: Do you think it’s about time you had more freedom?
You may think you’re ready to be treated as an adult,
but do your parents agree?
Have you proven to them that you can handle more freedom?
You see, if you want more freedom,
you have to gain your parents’ trust.
Earning their trust takes time.
But every time you prove yourself responsible,
you get one step closer to your goal.
Some ways you can show you are trustworthy are:
diligently completing your chores,
especially without being reminded;
managing your time wisely
and being punctual;
taking care of your things;
showing that you can handle money in a responsible way;
and following through on the promises you make.
Of course, nobody’s perfect.
So if you make a mistake, it’s not the end of the world.
Follow the Bible’s advice at Hebrews 13:18
to conduct yourself “honestly in all things.”
Tell the truth and be straightforward.
If you admit your mistake and apologize,
your parents will see that you are willing
to take responsibility for your actions,
and they’ll appreciate your honesty.
But what if you feel that despite your best efforts,
your parents still aren’t giving you enough freedom?
Don’t just get annoyed
—talk to them!
Respectfully ask what they think you need to do to earn their trust.
You may be surprised to learn of some other areas
where you can show you’re responsible.
At 2 Corinthians 13:5, the Bible says:
“Keep proving what you . . . are.”
So you need to build up a record of consistency.
That way you’ll prove you’re worthy of trust.
Every step you take brings you closer to your goal.
Of course, trust is much harder to gain than it is to lose.
But the effort is worth it.
When your parents see you working hard to earn their trust,
they will likely be happy to give you more freedom,
and you’ll be another step closer to becoming a responsible adult.

사실 다윗은 사는 내내 더할 나위 없이 심한 불충성을 경험했습니다.
왕 사울, 아내 미갈, 믿었던 조언자 아히도벨, 그리고 아들 압살롬에게까지 말이죠.
가장 믿고 사랑한 사람들에게 배신을 당해 깊은 상처를 받았죠.
다윗의 삶을 보면 무엇을 알게 될까요?
양떼를 돌보던 겸손한 목동에서 한 나라를 돌보는 용감한 왕이 되기까지,
다윗은 내내 충성스럽고 여호와의 마음에 맞는 사람이었습니다.
하지만 불공정한 일들을 겪으면 하느님께 대한 충성이 큰 시험을 받을 수 있죠.
다윗과 그의 강한 전사들이 도망자로 광야에 숨는 처지가 되고
식량마저도 부족할 때가 많았을 때 그 절망적인 상황을 상상해 보십시오.
그들은 사울 왕이 시기심에 격노하는 걸 직접 경험했죠.
하지만 기회가 와서 부하들이 사울을 죽이자고 재촉했을 때 다윗은 어떻게 했나요?
사무엘상 24:6에서 다윗이 한 말에 유의해 보십시오.
“내가 손을 들어 여호와의 기름부음받은 자인 내 주를 치는 그런 일을 하는 것은
여호와의 관점에서 생각할 수 없는 일이오.
그분도 계속 충성스러운 사랑을 보이실 것임을 알았습니다.
겸손하게, 자신의 감정은 제쳐 두고 사물을 여호와의 관점에서 보았습니다.
그분이 “충성스럽게 행하실” 때를 참을성 있게 기다렸죠.
우리는 곧 성경에 예언된 중대한 사건들에 직면할 것이며,
그때 여호와와 그분의 조직에 대한 충성이 시험받게 될 것입니다.
우리는 여호와께서 우리가 겪는 불공정한 일들을 포함해 우리의 상황을 아시며
그분께 충성한 것에 대해 상주실 것임을 확신할 수 있죠.
그러면 어떤 충성스런 행동을 할 때 여호와께서도 우리에게 충성스러우실까요?
첫째, 여호와를 변호함으로 충성을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
우주에서 가장 높으신 분인 여호와를 우리가 변호하는 게 가능할까요?
엘리후의 좋은 본으로부터 배울 수 있습니다!
엘리후는 욥과 세 명의 거짓 위로자들이 말하는 걸 참을성 있게 듣고 나서 이런 반응을 나타내죠.
욥이 자기가 하느님보다 옳다는 것을 증명하려 했기 때문이다.
또한 욥의 세 친구에게도 몹시 화가 났는데,
그들이 대답을 찾지 못하면서도 하느님을 악하다고 선언했기 때문이다.
충성스럽게 여호와를 변호하면서 욥기 36:2, 3에서 이렇게 말하죠.
“제가 설명하는 동안 조금만 더 참아 주십시오.
아직도 하느님을 위해 드릴 말씀이 있습니다.
제가 아는 것을 두루 말씀 드리고 저를 만드신 분에게 의를 돌리겠습니다.”
엘리후는 용감하게 하느님을 찬양하고 변호함으로 충성한 것입니다.
오늘날 우리는 왜 여호와를 변호해야 합니까?
사랑 많은 우리 아버지께서 여러 면으로 모독을 당하고 계시죠.
존재해도 우리에게 관심이 없다고 하는 사람들도 있죠.
그런 거짓말들이 사탄에게서 온 것임을 우리는 압니다.
우리는 여호와를 변호함으로 사탄이 거짓말쟁이임을 증명하고
우리는 그분이 분명히 존재하시는 전능자이시고, 지혜와 공의와 사랑의 하느님이시며,
곧 모든 악을 없애고 충성스러운 자들에게 영원한 생명의 상을 주실 것임을
여호와께선 돌들이라도 그분을 변호하게 하실 수 있지만,
자신의 충성스런 증인들인 우리들에게 이 영예롭고 과분한 일을 맡기셨습니다.
중앙장로회에 충성을 나타냄으로 여호와께 충성할 수 있습니다.
여호와와 예수께서 충실하고 슬기로운 종을 통해 우리를 영적으로 먹이시므로,
이 종에게 마땅히 충성을 나타내야 하죠.
예수 이후로 지상에 완전한 인간은 없었죠.
현재 지구 상에 완전한 사람이나 조직은 없습니다.
예수께선 이 종이 완전하다고 하신 게 아니라,
우리가 충실한 종의 말을 얼마나 잘 듣고 따르는지는
하느님과의 벗 관계에 직접적인 영향을 줍니다.
하지만 중앙장로회가 제공하는 어떤 영적 양식이 마음에 들지 않거나,
명확해진 교리가 온전히 이해되지 않거나 동의하기 어렵다면 어떻습니까?
한번은 베드로를 비롯한 예수의 제자들이 새로운 가르침을 받은 적이 있었는데요.
이 말씀을 듣고 그분의 제자 중 많은 사람이
’충격적인 말이다. 누가 저 말을 듣고 있을 수 있겠는가?’ 하고 말했다.”
이 때문에, 그분의 제자 중 많은 사람이 떠나가고
더 이상 그분과 함께 다니지 않았다.
하지만 베드로는 예수께서 ‘여러분도 가고 싶습니까?’ 하고 물으셨을 때 뭐라고 말하죠?
베드로의 충성은 예수께서 메시아라는 명백한 증거에 기초해 있었습니다.
오늘날 우리가 본받고자 하는 충성도 바로 그런 것입니다.
문제가 분명해질 때까지 여호와를 기다려야 할 때가 있죠.
그럴 때 베드로처럼 우리도 충성을 증명하십시다.
주인이신 예수의 발자취를 밀접히 따르는 충실한 종의 인도를
종종 개인적으로 적용해야 할 교훈을 받을 때가 있습니다.
예를 들어, 우리는 JW 방송을 통해서, 용서하고, 가치 있는 것으로 여호와를 공경하고,
영적으로 깨어 있으라는 중앙장로회 성원들의 사랑에 찬 조언을 받았죠.
또한 우리는 파수대와 회중 집회를 통해 옷차림과 몸단장에 유의하고,
좋은 교제 대상과 건전한 오락을 선택하고, 도덕적 깨끗함을 유지하도록 일깨움받죠.
그럴 때 우린 신속히 반응하고 필요한 조정을 합니까,
사도 바울은 신권적 지시에 대한 충성심이 시험받은 적이 있는데,
바울은 선교 여행을 성공적으로 마치고 기원 56년에 예루살렘에 도착하는데요.
이방 사람들 가운데서 하신 일들’을 열정적으로 설명합니다!
그런데 바울의 이 특별한 보고를 듣고,
연로자들은 유대에서 발생한 바울이 관련된 한 가지 문제를 알려 줍니다.
“그런데 그들[유대인 신자들]이 당신에 대한 소문을 들었는데,
당신이 이방 사람들 가운데 있는 모든 유대인에게 모세를 저버리라고[즉, 배교하라고] 가르치면서
자녀들에게 할례를 베풀지도 말고 관습을 따르지도 말라고 했다는 것입니다.”
‘나더러 배교자라니, 아니, 어떻게 그런 말을 할 수 있지?
3차 선교 여행을 하는 동안 여호와께서 얼마나 축복하셨는지 보지 못했나?’
바울이 아마 예상하지 못했을 이러한 분명한 지시를 합니다.
우리 가운데 서원한 사람이 네 명 있습니다.
그 사람들을 데리고 가서 그들과 함께 정결 의식을 행하고,
그들에게 비용을 대 주어 그들의 머리를 밀게 하십시오.
그러면 모든 사람은 당신에 대해 들은 소문이 아무것도 아니며,
당신도 율법을 지키며 바르게 살고 있다는 것을 알게 될 것입니다.”
바울은 그 결정에 의문을 제기하거나 자신의 권리를 주장했을까요?
율법은 예수와 함께 고통의 기둥에 못 박혔다고 쓴 말을 못 봤나?
지나치게 예민한 몇 명 때문에 내가 왜 이런 겉치레 행동을 해야 하지?’
그 일로 거의 목숨을 잃을 뻔 했지만요.
바울은 본인의 권리보다 더 중요한 문제들이 관련돼 있음을 알았습니다.
더 중요한 점으로, 그는 여호와와 중앙장로회에 충성을 나타냈습니다.
우리도 삶에서 더 큰 그림을 보고 있습니까?
충실하고 슬기로운 종에게 충성을 나타내겠다고 결심해야겠습니다.
셋째, 장로들에게 충성을 나타냄으로 여호와께 충성할 수 있죠.
지금까지 여호와와 충실한 종에 대한 충성에 관해 이야기했는데요.
우리가 회중 장로들에게 받는 인도는 어떠합니까?
우리는 매주 집회에서 장로들이 하는 연설과 해설을 듣고,
이렇게 정기적으로 만나다 보면 그들의 불완전성과 결점을 더 자주 보게 될 수 있죠.
예를 들어, 우리 잡지의 삽화를 확대해 보면, 보이는 건 픽셀 즉 각각의 점들뿐이죠.
하지만 떨어져서 보면 아름다운 사진이나 그림을 보게 됩니다.
마찬가지로, 장로들을 볼 때도 점과 같은 불완전성에 초점을 맞출 것이 아니라,
열심히 일하는 사랑 많은 목자들에 대한 우리의 충성을 강화하는 것이 왜 중요할까요?
여호와의 양을 인도하고, 먹이고, 보호하는 이 사람들로 된 선물이 바로
장로들의 인도를 기꺼이 따를 것인가에 달려 있는데,
불완전하지만 충성스런 남자들로 된 여호와의 마련에 대한 것입니다.
고라와 다단과 아비람이 고집 세게 배척한 교훈이 바로 이것이었습니다.
고라가 모세에게 나타내는 반항적인 태도를 보시죠.
총회가 다 거룩하고 여호와께서 그들 가운데 계신데
어째서 당신들은 여호와의 회중 위에 자신을 높이는 거요?
고라와 그 무리는 겉으론 대단히 하느님께 충성하는 척 했지만
여호와께서 직접 모세와 아론을 임명하셨다는 사실을 완전히 무시했습니다.
이 다단과 아비람은 회중 가운데서 선택된 자들이었는데,
고라의 무리와 함께 모세와 아론을 대적하여 싸웠다.
모세라는 사람과 그의 불완전성에 초점을 맞춘 나머지
실제 이스라엘을 인도하시는 분이 여호와이심을 보지 못했습니다.
여호와께서 임명한 사람들에게 불충성한 결과 생명을 잃었습니다.
하지만 고라의 아들들은 다른 선택을 했죠.
다음 장면에서, 아버지와 얼마나 다른 태도를 나타내는지 보시죠.
우리 아버지와 그의 추종자들은 실로 여호와의 권위에 반역한 거야.
시기와 교만과 야심 때문에 반역하다가 결국 불명예를 자초했지.
우리 아버진 영광을 구했지만, 그 영광은 잠시뿐이었어.
그래도 난 우리 형제들이 그 와중에서 올바른 편에 선 것이 기쁘단다.
그렇지만 그로 인해 벗 관계나 가족이 여호와와의 관계와 그분에 대한 순종보다
우선해서는 안 된다는 점의 중요성을 깨닫게 됐지.
궁극적으로, 우리 인간에게 성공적인 지침은 여호와로부터 오지.
우린 그분이 택하셔서 임명하신 사람들을 전적으로 신뢰해야 돼.
여호와께서 임명하신 사람들을 존경하는 것이 여호와의 권위를 존중하는 것이니까.
여호와께서도 충성을 나타내시어 그들의 생명을 구해 주셨죠.
오늘날 여호와께서 자신의 백성을 인도하도록 임명하신 사람들에게 투덜거리거나 불평함으로
이스라엘 백성 가운데 충성의 좋은 본과 나쁜 본을 더 찾아보길 원하신다면,
JW 방송에서 「여호와의 권위를 존중하라」 비디오 전체를 시청해 보시기 바랍니다.
어떻게 여호와께 충성을 나타낼 수 있을까요?
첫째, 그분의 증인들로서 여호와를 변호하는 것이죠.
둘째, 충실하고 슬기로운 종을 계속 충성스럽게 지지하는 것입니다.
셋째, 임명된 장로들의 인도를 충성스럽게 따르는 것이죠.
우리 모두 고라의 아들들, 다윗, 베드로, 바울과 같은 충실한 본을 따름으로,
영원히 그분의 충성스러운 사랑을 받는 사람이 되도록 합시다.
충실하고 슬기로운 종의 인도를 따르는 것이었습니다.
중앙장로회는 어떤 방식으로 중요한 결정을 내릴까요?
베델 아침 숭배에서 데이비드 스플레인 형제가 설명할 때 들어 보시죠.
그럼, 이런 변화는 어떻게 결정되는 걸까요?
수요일 오전에 중앙장로회 형제들이 모여서 “자, 이번 주에는 뭘 바꾸어 볼까요?
형제들이 상상 못한 걸로 하나 바꿔 줄까요?”
이런 식이라면, 충실한 것도, 슬기로운 것도 아니죠.
새로운 조정이 금방 금방 연달아 발표되는 것처럼 보일지 모르지만
그런 조정을 시행하기로 결정을 내리기까지는 보통 여러 해가 걸립니다.
한 가지 예로, 현 중앙장로회가 고심해야 했던 중대한 변화 가운데 한 가지는,
‘미국에 지부 위원회를 두는 것이 가능한가?’ 하는 문제였습니다.
