en.text: We recently met Mamuka Tektumanashvili, from the country of Georgia.
He was a high-ranking officer in the special forces there for many years.
What made him realize that defending his country
is not the highest honor a man can have in his life?
This is his story.
For 18 years I served in a special unit
responsible for presidential security.
This mission demanded total self-sacrifice.
For example, the first and the last vehicles
of the presidential escort belonged to this unit.
So if an attack occurred on the president,
we were the first ones to be hit with the fire.
For the last ten years of service, I worked
as an instructor and trained new staff
to provide presidential security in the future.
Those working in this field must be fearless.
They must be professionals,
and that is what I taught to succeeding generations.
I just loved my job.
I was a fervent patriot.
I had a special regard for the flag of my country.
In one bag, I always had weapons and the flag.
Patriotism was so deep-rooted in me
that I would beat up a person
simply because he was of another nationality.
I always thought that God would never allow
people like me to draw close to him.
One day, Jehovah’s Witnesses came and preached to my wife and me.
We were so interested in the truth that my wife
even expressed a desire to study the Bible.
Because there were rumors circulating about Jehovah’s Witnesses,
I decided first to make sure that everything was decent at their meetings
and only then allow my wife to associate with them.
After the meeting, I was absolutely thrilled.
Everyone was well-mannered, with friendly, smiling faces.
I realized that there was nothing there to threaten my wife’s well-being.
On the contrary, their association would be beneficial for her.
Soon my wife and our eldest daughter got baptized.
As for me, I enjoyed associating with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Later, I also started to study the Bible.
I knew that I had to make drastic changes in my life,
but my job prevented me from doing so.
Moreover, I felt that door-to-door preaching
was far more difficult than engaging in combat.
I respected Jehovah’s Witnesses for their courage and strength.
Little by little, I too was changing for the better.
I wanted to quit my job and inform my colleagues about my religious beliefs.
So I wrote down all the Bible verses I had recently learned
and then pinned them on the wall in my office.
I also started to think about how to make a living
after leaving my job and decided to learn a trade.
I started to buy tools in order to be ready
to take care of my family.
I realized that the time had come to make a decision.
The day I quit my job
was one of the happiest days of my life.
Since then, I’ve been able to dedicate every minute of my life
to Jehovah with a clean conscience.
In a few months, I got baptized.
In the beginning, we were hardly making a living.
However, this taught me to trust in Jehovah.
I tried my best to keep service to Jehovah in first place.
I deeply appreciate the support of my brothers
and sisters and association with them.
Before, I used to carry out the orders of men
—some of which I carried out reluctantly.
But now I am happy to carry out
an assignment from Jehovah with the same spirit
that the prophet Isaiah had, who said:
“Here I am! Send me!”
As a family, we decided to move where the need was greater,
and this has united our family even more.
This is the bag
in which I always carried weapons,
but now they are replaced with a Bible and Bible literature.
In the past, I thought
I could never preach from door to door.
But now I can say with conviction
that the words of Jesus have proved true in my case:
“All things are possible with God.”
Brother Tektumanashvili now serves as an elder,
and he has also been a regular pioneer since 2014.

cn.text: 我们最近见到来自格鲁吉亚的马穆卡
他曾担任特种部队的高阶将领多年
是什么让他意识到
保卫国家并非他人生中最高的荣誉呢？
以下是他的故事
有长达18年的时间
我隶属于特种部队
负责护卫总统
这种工作需要绝对的牺牲奉献
例如，每次护送总统的车队
第一台和最后一台车都是我们的部队
如果有任何攻击行动发生
我们就首当其冲
在我那段职业生涯的最后十年
我被任命为指导员，负责训练新人
帮助他们以后能做好护卫的工作
投身这种工作的人必须是精英
也要有视死如归的精神
我一直灌输给他们这样的观念
我热爱我的工作
那时我也是个狂热的爱国主义者
对国旗怀着无上的崇敬
我的背包总是装着武器和一面国旗
爱国主义深植我的内心
我甚至会因为别人跟我的国籍不同
就随意殴打他们
我总觉得
上帝不会让像我这样的人亲近他
有一天
耶和华见证人拜访了我和妻子
我们对真理很感兴趣
我的妻子甚至表示想学习圣经
由于听到不少关于耶和华见证人的传闻
我决定先去看看他们的聚会
确定一切都没问题
再让我妻子和他们来往
聚会后我感到很兴奋
所有人都亲切有礼、笑容可掬
我看出和这群人来往
对我的妻子不但不会有任何坏处
还会有好的影响
不久后，我的妻子和大女儿受浸了
我很喜欢跟耶和华见证人来往
之后我也开始学习圣经
我知道我需要作出巨大的改变
但我的工作是很大的阻碍
此外，对我来说
逐户传道比参加战斗更困难
我很钦佩耶和华见证人的勇气
渐渐地，我对真理越来越有体会
我想要辞掉工作
也想告诉同事我的宗教信仰
我把学到的圣经真理全部写下来
然后钉在办公室的墙壁上
我也开始考虑
一旦辞掉工作要怎么继续维持生活
为了养家糊口，我决定学习做生意
还特地去买了一些工具
终于做决定的时刻到了
辞掉工作的那一天是我生命中
最快乐的日子之一
从那一刻起
我就能够带着清白的良心
将生命的每一分钟
毫无保留地都献给耶和华
几个月后我就受浸了
一开始维持生活很不容易
但这也帮助我信赖耶和华
我竭尽全力将事奉耶和华置于首位
我也很感激弟兄姐妹们的支持和鼓励
从前我听命于人
有时候服从命令是出于勉强
现在我快乐地执行耶和华的命令
我效法以赛亚先知的精神
我在这里，请差遣我
我们全家决定
搬到需求较大的地区扩大服务
这个决定让我们更团结
关系更稳固
以前，我用这个袋子携带武器
现在，我用它来装圣经和圣经书刊
以前，我觉得我一定没办法逐户传道
但现在，我可以充满信心
耶稣所说的
在上帝凡事都可能
确实在我身上应验了
马穆卡弟兄现在是个长老
从2014年他开始做先驱

en.text: I was in the military for 13 years.
Women didn’t used to belong to combat regiments.
I was the first to obtain the rank of sergeant in my regiment.
I lived the army 24/7.
The clothes I wore,
the people I associated with
—everything was military.
Being in a man’s field is very intimidating.
I felt I had to work twice as hard, be twice as fast, and be twice as good.
So I became more and more aggressive
in order to accomplish the missions that were given to me.
I let the pressure to perform
affect me in negative ways.
I did not feel anything.
I used more profanity.
I drank more heavily.
I smoked more.
It wasn’t the quality of the life that I wanted.
I felt that my life wasn’t going anywhere.
And there was a knock on the front door.
It was very surprising to learn from the Scriptures
that I could draw close to God.
But the Witnesses, they explained things in a way
that it made sense,
and I could verify all of it myself.
I didn’t understand what they meant
by ‘God could love you.’
The Witnesses showed me how to look in the Bible
and find out what the Bible said about it all.
It gave me a desire to keep going,
and things started to get a lot better.
When I put down my rifle
and I picked up a Bible, those around me,
they didn’t understand it at all.
It’s worth everything just to show someone that they can be loved.
Just to watch that change is fabulous.
It’s only with a lot of prayer and meditation
that I was able to change my personality.
Jehovah guides me.
If you put your anxiety on him,
he will give you that peace.
My husband is my joy.
He’s showing me the patience
and the loving-kindness
that Jehovah wants families
to experience.
The members of my congregation are my family.
They are my brothers and sisters.
I now have a huge worldwide family.
We have a lovely, lovely congregation.
And to be able to laugh and joke
and to talk about Jehovah, it’s wonderful.
When I was in the military,
I became a very dark and uncaring person.
Jehovah has taught me how to beat my sword
into a plowshare.
He taught me that I didn’t need
to “learn war anymore.”

en.text: Welcome to the program, brothers and sisters!
During the next hour, you will hear the story of a brother
who previously protected the president of a country.
But seeing the love among God’s people made him refocus his life
to bearing witness about the Sovereign of the universe.
We cherish our international brotherhood.
Our brothers and sisters in the former Soviet Union took great risks
during the Cold War to convey their love
to fellow Witnesses on the other side of the globe.
Does our love for Jehovah motivate us to avoid living a double life?
This dramatization will remind us of key principles
to protect us when we are tempted to draw closer to Satan’s world.
This is the July program of JW Broadcasting!
In the book Insight on the Scriptures,
under the heading “Christian,”
it makes clear that claiming to be Christian
requires more than simply
a mere confession of faith.
It is more than being a nominal Christian
—a Christian in name only.
For example, according to the Bible,
it is necessary that belief
be demonstrated by works, not just words.
And since we were born as sinners,
those who become Christians need to repent,
to turn around, to dedicate their lives to Jehovah,

including such things as fits of anger, obscene talk,
lying, stealing, drunkenness,
and as Galatians chapter 5 says: “things like these.”

Christians are to be kind and considerate,
mild-tempered and patient,
and are to exercise self-control.
They provide and care for their own
and love their neighbor as themselves.

It’s not a matter of just glibly saying,
“I am a Christian.”
But despite all of those impressive characteristics
that we just enumerated,
what did Jesus say
the main identifying quality
of a true Christian would be?
Most of you know the answer to that, but let’s read it again
from John 13:34, 35.
It says: “I am giving you a new commandment,
“that you love one another; just as I have loved you,
“you also love one another.
“By this all will know that you are my disciples

Those are the theme verses
for my discussion with you this month.
The topic is:
“Love—The Identifying Mark of a Disciple of Jesus.”
Did you notice in verse 34 that Jesus said
that he was giving them at that time a “new commandment”?
But it sounds like a very old commandment, doesn’t it?
Why, over 1,500 years
before Jesus said the words we just read,
the Law given to Moses said:
“You must love your fellow man as yourself.”
—Leviticus 19:18.
So, what was “new” about Jesus’ command
in John chapter 13?
He said that true Christians were to love each other
“just as I have loved you.”
That is what was different.
That was new,
not just love the other person as you love yourself,
but love him just like
Jesus loved His followers.
Well, what kind of love would that be?
Self-sacrificing love —and usually we think
of Jesus’ ultimate sacrifice,
his willingly giving his life
so that we might have the hope of everlasting life.
But when you think about it, that aspect of Jesus’ love
was exemplified in a self-sacrificing death!
Now, it is true, that as a Christian,
we might at some time have to give our life for a fellow Christian.

So instead of talking about a self-sacrificing death,
we want to discuss showing this new kind of love
as evidenced in a self-sacrificing life,
not necessarily our death.
You see, Jesus’ life —his three-and-a-half-year ministry—
was a self-sacrificing life of loving others.
In addition to doing good
when something requires it,
a true follower of Jesus

spiritually and otherwise.
He is to work actively for their good.
The preaching and teaching of the good news to others
—some of whom may even be hostile—

in everlasting life to the recipients.

a true Christian must ‘impart not only the good news of God
but also his very self’
in helping those who accept the good news.
It’s that kind of love

not specifically that his followers
would all be dying for each other,
but more so that they would all be living for each other.
Yes, displaying self-sacrificing love
for one another every day of their lives.
The four Gospels are a treasure trove
of Jesus’ self-sacrificing love.

every day of his life as the Christ.
His three-and-a-half-year ministry
amounts to nearly 1,300 days of life and love.
The written record of Jesus’ life is admittedly brief,
but it is grand indeed!
However, the reality of observing Jesus every day
must have been far grander than what we have in print.
What we have in print might be likened
to a photo album of Jesus’ life,
some snapshots.
By comparison, what his apostles experienced
with Jesus day after day
was like a continuous video of his example of love.
No wonder that, at John 21:25,

and I also got the help I needed from the elders.
It’s been a few years, but as I look back now,
I was one of those kids living a double life.
But now with Jehovah’s help,
I’m living the best life.
What a clear warning this is,
not only for young ones but also for those of us
who have served Jehovah for many, many years.
As we well know, serving Jehovah faithfully for many decades
is only valuable if we ‘endure to the end.’
By developing intense love for Jehovah,
we’ll be able to overcome whatever temptations or trials we face.
And speaking of enduring to the end,
Brother Mark Sanderson recently spoke at morning worship in Bethel
about how our eager expectation of the day of Jehovah
will help us to endure faithfully in this system of things.
Pay close attention to some of the ways
we show such expectation.
Well, here’s the question we want to ask this morning:
Is it actually possible to speed up the day of Jehovah?
Well, if we look at our text this morning
at 2 Peter 3:11,
we’ve had that read for us,
so we know that expression at the end
that we should “consider what sort of people you ought to be
in holy acts of conduct and deeds of godly devotion.”
But then it goes on to say:
“As you await and keep close in mind
the presence of the day of Jehovah.”
Well, now, if you look at the footnote
on this expression in verse 12,
you’ll notice that the expression
“keep close in mind” literally means
to “speed up” the day of Jehovah.
Well, now, how can we do that?
Well, it’s true we cannot bring
the day forward of Jehovah even one day,
nor can we move it back even one day.
That is not within our power. That day is set.
But how can we, then, “speed up”
the day of Jehovah as it says there in verse 12?
Well, we keep that day close in our mind.
We never let it be out of our sight.
As the footnote also says,
we “eagerly desire” it.
Well, now, if we’re persons like that,
Peter says that we’re going to be busy
in “deeds of godly devotion.”
Well, now, just as a quick reminder:
What is godly devotion?
Well, just looking at our New World Translation glossary,
here’s the definition:
It’s “reverence, worship,
“and service to Jehovah God,
with loyalty to his universal sovereignty.”
Well, what do we get from that definition?
Did you notice —reverence, worship, service?
You see, godly devotion is not passive; it’s active.
It’s reflected in action and in activity.
Well, that’s why the apostle Peter
used the expression in verse 11,
“deeds of godly devotion.”
Well, what are some of the ways that we demonstrate this quality?
Well, some of them are just very small.
For example, what about hospitality?
At 1 Peter 4:9,
when the apostle Peter wrote his first letter, he said:
“Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.”
Well, there are so many opportunities
for us to imitate Jehovah and be hospitable
—to share with others according to their needs.
And this really is an expression not only for another person
but it’s an expression of our love for Jehovah
—our desire to want to imitate him.
Well, we all acknowledge that.
But here’s the question:
When was the last time
that you acted hospitably?
Or when was the last time I acted hospitably?
You see, it’s not enough just to love the quality of hospitality.
If we are going to have deeds of godly devotion,
we’re going to have to practice it.
Here’s another one.
What about helping the elderly that are in our midst?
You know, our elderly brothers need help.
They need help to get to the meetings.
They need help to get out in the field ministry.
Some of them are confined to their homes.
Well, if that’s the case, they may need help from younger ones
to assist them with shopping or doing errands
or just doing some chore around the house.
Well, that’s something that has been mentioned
in many Watchtower articles.
It’s been mentioned at many conventions and assemblies.
It’s been mentioned at many congregation meetings.
But now here’s a question:
When was the last time
that you did something for an elderly brother or sister?
Or when was the last time I did?
You see, we need to think
about not just loving these ideas
but what are we doing to really help?
See, that’s showing deeds of godly devotion.
Well, of course, we also have to think about the more major things.
What about attending our congregation meetings?
Hebrews 10:23-25
—that scripture that we quote so many times—
says that we should ‘not forsake our meeting together.’
But it goes on to say that we should ‘encourage one another.’
So it’s not enough just to be at the meeting.
When we’re there, we want to reach out and do everything that we can
to encourage our brothers and really participate in the meeting.
You see, godly devotion is not passive; it’s active.
And so, what sort of persons ought we to be when we’re at the meeting?
Well, we know we want to be active,
fully involved with the program.
But now, of course, what’s the most important way
that we exercise these deeds of godly devotion?
Well, you’ll remember that the apostle Paul
at 1 Timothy 3:16
referred to ‘the sacred secret of godly devotion,’
and he showed there that Jesus really was that secret.
You see, he was the one who demonstrated
godly devotion in a perfect sense.
Now, Paul in that verse, 1 Timothy 3:16,
went on to say that Jesus was ‘preached among the nations.’
Well, then, that really is a vital part
of our deeds of godly devotion
—preaching about Christ Jesus, his Kingdom,
and everything that will be accomplished.
But brothers, how much incentive we have today
to be involved fully in our preaching work.
We have tools today like we have never had before.
You know, over the summer as I was attending
a number of different regional conventions in different parts of the world,
I enjoyed so much, no doubt just as you have,
using the JW Library app
and downloading the Why Study the Bible? video
in a number of different languages.
We had one real interesting experience when we were in Europe.
We got into a taxi with a driver from Africa.
And right away, we asked him what his language was.
Well, he told us it was a language not familiar to us at all.
But while he was driving,
we managed to download the Why Study the Bible? video,
and it automatically began to play as we were in the car.
Well, as soon as the man heard it, he started shouting:
“What’s happening? What’s happening?”
I think he thought he was hearing a voice from heaven
when he heard his own language in the taxi.
But we reassured him that that was not the case.
But he was so moved.
He almost didn’t want to take the fare, if you can imagine,
and initially he had been quite unfriendly.
But when he saw what was available on our website,
he was deeply moved.
Well, maybe you’ve had a similar experience.
Just as a note of future reference:
It’s probably not a good idea to play the video
when someone is driving.
Well, if we have real godly devotion that’s active,
we’re going to be busy in doing deeds of godly devotion.
You know, there’s an old saying that says:
“Time flies when you’re having fun.”
Well, you know, even scientists acknowledge that there’s truth in that.
A study that was published in the year 2012
in the journal Psychological Science said this:
Although we tend to believe
that time flies when we’re having a good time,
these studies indicate that what it is
about the enjoyable time that causes it to go by more quickly.
It seems to be the goal pursuit
or achievement-directed action we’re engaged in that matters.
Just being content or satisfied may not make time fly,
but being excited or actively pursuing
a desired object can.
Isn’t that interesting?
Well, now, if we’re the sort of persons that are busy
with holy acts of conduct and deeds of godly devotion,
reaching out for that most important goal of everlasting life,
we will speed up the coming of the day of Jehovah
in our hearts and our minds.
What deeds of godly devotion
do you remember from that fine presentation?
Among other things, Brother Sanderson explained
that one deed of godly devotion is to be hospitable to one another.
Hospitality is also the theme of this month’s music video,
which is entitled “Follow the Course [of Hospitality].”
It might be a meal or snacks or coffee Or fun and games, maybe just talking.
Jehovah is the one who put it on our table. So could we be able . . .
“Follow the course of hospitality.” Imitate God above.
Do it with true impartiality. That’s what it means to love.
The roof above our heads is from our heavenly Father.
But if we need to share, would it be a bother?
Let’s feel the joy that only ever comes from giving!
That’s Christian living.
“Follow the course of hospitality.” Imitate God above.
Do it with true impartiality. That’s what it means to love.
Some people don’t have what we have. It’s up to us to share.
Disaster strikes, then they’re without. Will we really care?
Could we open up our home and host a friend in need?
Do a kindly deed.
“Follow the course of hospitality.” Imitate God above.
Do it with true impartiality. That’s what it means to love.
That’s what it means to love. That’s what it means to love.
What a nice song!
And while that music video brings this program to its conclusion,
we’d like to encourage you to watch a video
that will be posted later this month about Sister Cindy McIntosh.
She was in the military for many years
and described herself as having become a “dark and uncaring person.”
But then Jehovah taught her
what true love means.
The video is entitled I Put Down My Rifle and is available on Video on Demand
in the “Interviews and Experiences” category.
Yes, love truly is the identifying mark of true Christians.
That’s what stands out when you
visit other congregations, perhaps when traveling.
One good example is the Nong Khai Congregation
in the northeastern corner of Thailand.
The 32 publishers send their love.
There’s a great need in Thailand,
which is why half of the 10 appointed brothers
in the congregation and half of the 18 pioneers
are “need greaters.”
Witnessing carts have been set up at a nearby border crossing,
with ten languages regularly featured.
Many copies are placed with visitors
from countries where our work is restricted.
Sometimes over 1,000 pieces of literature
are placed in a single day at the border crossing.
The Nong Khai Congregation had the privilege
of being a host congregation when a special convention
was arranged in October of last year.
And during the convention, they were surprised and overjoyed to hear
that the New World Translation was now available
in the Thai language.
We pray that Jehovah continues to bless the brothers and sisters in Thailand.
And all of you around the world, we love you very much!
This is JW Broadcasting from Brooklyn, New York.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Mark.
Mark may have become a follower of Jesus
when he was a young man
living with his mother in Jerusalem.
In fact, it seems that their home
was used as a meeting place
by the early Christian congregation.
While Mark may have had
limited contact with Jesus,
he enjoyed association
with the apostles Peter and Paul
as well as Mark’s cousin Barnabas.
He had the privilege to assist Paul and Barnabas
in the missionary work.
His ministry also took him
to such distant places as Babylon and Rome.
Perhaps between the years 60 and 65 C.E.,
while in Rome,
Mark wrote an account of Jesus’ life.
This became the third Gospel to be circulated
among the early Christian congregations.
Although most of Mark’s information is also contained in the other Gospels,
he does include some unique details.
For example, it is evident that this book was written
with a non-Jewish audience in mind,
especially the Romans.
Mark explains Jewish expressions
and customs that would have been unfamiliar
to Romans and other non-Jews.
He may have obtained much of his information from Peter,
who was an eyewitness of practically all that Mark recorded.
Peter’s eyewitness testimony may be seen
in Mark’s vivid descriptions of Jesus’ activity and feelings.
The book contains 16 chapters
and is the shortest of the four Gospels.
It covers the time period from 29 to 33 C.E.
Chapters 1 to 10 begin with John the Baptizer’s ministry
and Jesus’ baptism in the Jordan River.
Then Mark describes
Jesus’ exciting three-and-a-half-year ministry.
These chapters recount Jesus’ selection of his apostles,
many of his miracles,
and examples of his tender care
and concern for people.
Chapters 11 to 15 outline Jesus’ final week of activity
leading up to his arrest and execution.
Did you know?
Mark was likely the young man who ran away,
leaving his garment behind,
on the night Jesus was arrested.
Finally, chapter 16 shows that three faithful women
are the first to discover that Jesus has been resurrected!
As you read this Gospel,
note how Jesus demonstrated his power
over sickness, death, and the forces of nature;
how he showed his tender care and concern for people;
and how he zealously carried out his Father’s will
—providing a glimpse of his future rulership as King of God’s Kingdom.

en.text: OK, kids, it’s time to practice our Bible books!
Are you ready to try some of the Hebrew Scriptures?
Ready!
Genesis! The book that tells how Paradise was lost.
Exodus! God saved his people by his mighty hand.
Leviticus! God’s laws to keep them holy day by day.
Numbers! Some lost the chance to see the Promised Land.
Deuteronomy! Encouragement to listen and obey.
Joshua! Each family got a place to call their own.
Judges! God’s mighty ones performing mighty deeds.
Ruth! Rewarded with a family and a home.
First Samuel! God chooses faithful David to be king.
Second Samuel! The trouble in his house because of sin.
First Kings! The kingdom is divided north and south.
Second Kings! Though most were bad, a few were faithful men.
First Chronicles! The things they learned from lessons in the past.
Second Chronicles! Bad rulers lead the nation to its fall.
Ezra! His work restored true worship once again.
Nehemiah! He helped rebuild the city and its walls.
Esther! She spoke with courage when the time was right.
Job! Integrity is precious in God’s eyes.
Psalms! Inspired songs to praise God’s love and might.
Proverbs! The wisdom of its words is always true.
Ecclesiastes! The happiness that serving God will bring.
Song of Solomon! True love is ever loyal, always strong.
Isaiah! How life will be when Jesus rules as King.
The Bible is the greatest book of all.
Jehovah is its author, you’ll recall.
Let’s read it ev’ry day, to learn it and obey.
The Bible is the greatest book of all.

en.text: The islands of Micronesia
are tiny specks in the Pacific Ocean.
But these beautiful islands are home
to some 1,400 worshippers of Jehovah.
Formerly called the Guam branch,
the Micronesia branch oversees the work
in nine lands in addition to Guam.
There are currently 64 Bethel family members and full-time commuters,
but only 25 are at the branch office.
The rest have the privilege of working
in six remote translation offices.
A significant milestone
was recently reached in Micronesia.
The Kingdom Hall construction program
that began in 2008
will be complete this month.
Among the projects completed were 13 Kingdom Halls,
6 remote translation offices,
and 4 missionary homes.
Some of these projects were new construction,
whereas others were renovations.
Many experiences showed Jehovah’s blessing on these projects,
some of which were shared in this month’s JW Broadcasting program.
Despite very poor conditions
on many of these islands,
there has been a heartwarming response
to the May 2015 JW Broadcast
concerning our privilege to support Kingdom interests
through our donations.
Following the program, one couple of humble means
decided to set aside 20 U.S. dollars
each month as a donation.
Just last month, however,
their bills exceeded their income
by some 80 dollars.
Not knowing how they were going to come up with the extra money,
they thought about using the 20 dollars to help pay for the expenses.
In the end, though, they decided it was more important
to donate the funds, as they had resolved,
and look for another way to cover the deficit.
Well, shortly after making the donation,
they both were surprised to learn that they had been selected
as employees of the month for their good work.
The reward?
A cash gift of 50 dollars each.
The couple gives all the praise to Jehovah for the positive outcome.
In 2014, our branch received training
to do audio/video recording in the remote translation offices.
As a result, the publishers have enjoyed using
more videos in the ministry.
One missionary brother had invited
the Chuukese couple he was studying with
to the meeting many times,
but they had only attended once in the past year and a half.
When the video What Happens at a Kingdom Hall?
became available in their language,
the brother played the video for them.
The couple was impressed and commented
that the Kingdom Hall was very different from their church.
They attended the very next meeting,
which happened to be the Memorial.
Experiencing for themselves what they saw in the video,
they continued attending meetings.
Last year, the branch office encouraged congregations
to consider working unassigned territory.
In Micronesia, these are often
isolated atolls located hundreds of miles
from the nearest congregation.
One group sailed to the Aur Atoll
in the Marshall Islands.
On the little atoll island of Tobal,
they preached and invited the residents
to attend a public meeting the very next day.
To their surprise, 42 residents attended,
which is about 25 percent of the islands’ population.
They were intrigued by the talk entitled
“How Does God View the Dead?”
The subject was timely because a father of three children
had died in an accident,
and the local minister said it was God’s will.
Following the talk, about 20 people stayed to ask questions
—some for up to two hours.
Altogether, the group of five publishers
placed 1,000 pieces of literature
and started many Bible studies in this atoll.
Needless to say, this group is looking forward
to making another trip to this receptive territory.
At Isaiah 42:12,
it was foretold that Jehovah’s people
would “declare his praise in the islands.”
We are happy that this prophecy is being fulfilled
in the islands of Micronesia.
And it is a pleasure to bring to you all
the love and greetings from these beautiful people.

en.text: There’s a common saying at Bethel
that the only thing that is constant is change.
But frankly, that’s an understatement now, wouldn’t you say?
In fact, wherever you turn, it seems like at every occasion
we see change coming about in one way or another.
In fact, when I first submitted this outline
and think back to that day,
it has changed so much just in those few months.
It really shows that we are in a time of great change.
Of course, we’re in an organization that’s built on change.
We’re in an organization that as far back as Brother Russell
was willing to study God’s Word and see
where perhaps his belief did not align with what God’s Word said, and he changed.
And from that day forward, our organization has continued to change.
And aren’t we glad “the faithful and discreet slave”
continues to make adjustments where necessary
for the sake of the preaching work; for the sake of Jehovah’s name;
and, of course, for his people, his sheep.
So when we think about that,
we think, ‘Change is not always bad.’
Now, all change is not profound either.
We’ve had many changes right here in Bethel in the last few years
—changes that have benefited us as well.
Perhaps maybe it’s having all our Saturdays off
so we can enjoy field service with the congregation more regularly.
Perhaps it’s an extra day off when we turn 70.
So, again, personal matters can be attended to;
field service can be enjoyed more fully by these.
What a blessing!
Even to have morning worship
and our Watchtower Study in our room when we’re sick.
These are nice changes.
We can just go on and on about the things that we enjoy in changes.
But sometimes, sometimes in our life,
changes come about that maybe,
well, they cut a little deeper into our comfort zone.
Isn’t that true?
So maybe it can cause us a measure of personal anxiety
—maybe it’s fear of the unknown.
Or maybe it’s just the feeling that I don’t have as much control
in my life anymore because of this change that’s come about.
And so there is some anxiety that goes with that.
In fact, whatever the case,
if we allow ourselves to become too anxious,
the truth of Proverbs 12:25 comes about, where it says:
“Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down.”
And so it can actually prevent us from moving forward.
It can prevent us or it can slow us down sometimes and we become overwhelmed
with anxious feelings about what’s going on around me.
How am I being affected?
We use the example in the theme
to talk about those sailors on a sailing ship.
Why?
Well, because for a sailor while at sea,
it may seem that he is at the mercy of the elements.
And it’s true, he cannot control the weather,
but he can adjust to the weather.
An experienced sailor is able to keep control.
He’s able to stay on course
—by adjusting his sails, by continuing to move forward,
by catching the wind from different angles, and by allowing himself
to keep making progress
—even though at first bad weather can slow you down.
In fact, for a ship to keep moving, it has to have the winds
catching the sails.
And if you’ve ever seen a racing team that has raced these large sailing ships,
it’s amazing how they can maneuver them, how they can turn them,
how fast they can go because they are experienced.
Well, in some ways, we think
we may not have complete control over our life at Bethel.
And that’s true, we don’t.
We do have changing circumstances,
but we also can keep control of our life.
Why? Why can we say that?
Well, turn with me to our first scripture in the 46th Psalm.
In Psalm 46,
notice what it says in the very first three verses.
It says: ‘God is our refuge and strength,
‘a help that is readily found in times of distress.
‘That is why we will not fear, though the earth undergoes change,
‘though the mountains topple into the depths of the sea,
‘though the waters roar and foam over,
though the mountains rock on account of its turbulence.’
Of course, these are some pretty extreme circumstances.
I’m in no way saying that’s Bethel.
But if we think about the amount of change:
The entire earth is portrayed here as undergoing some massive changes
—mountains falling into the sea, violent oceans—and yet the psalmist said
he didn’t have to worry.
He was in control; he had no fear. Why?
Because of verse 1: ‘God is our refuge and strength,
‘a help readily found in times of distress.
That is why I will not fear.’
And the psalmist did not fear because of that.
Jehovah is our strength;
he is our refuge.
And his stability
—the fact that he can never be shaken in his stability—it grounds us.
It means that as long as we stick close to Jehovah,
then nothing is going to put us completely off balance.
And if it does for a short period of time,
if we experience a little bit of rough seas
—well, we adjust.
Why?
Because we have Jehovah, and he helps us do that.
In our discussion tonight, we’re going to consider three significant changes
—some have already happened,
some are affecting our family even now,
and others will likely affect us more even into the future.
We are also going to give attention to three Bible accounts
that will help us to see Jehovah’s unchanging love
for us and his ability to help us ride through any storm.
The first has to do with a change of location.
Now, of course, think back to January 6, 2015.
It seems like a long time ago.
It is. In Bethel time, it seems.
It was a normal day at Bethel.
You made your way down to the dining room
for some cheese and chive egg white omelet and a little muesli.
Then came that historic Bethel announcement from the Governing Body.
It adjusted what departments would be transferring to Wallkill.
You remember.
Now, not the Computer Department, not Regional Design Construction
but now the Service Department and the Branch Committee Office
would be relocating to Wallkill.
So think about that.
How many people’s lives changed
with just a few sentences in a few minutes at morning worship?
Of course, the Regional Design Construction Department
would then be moving to Puerto Rico.
Who would have thought of that?
Did you see that one coming?
Change can happen quickly.
But, of course, as a result of that announcement,
just beginning next month, some 400 members of our family
from Patterson and Brooklyn will be moving to Wallkill
in the beginning of large changes for all of us.
And as big as that was, it does seem like a long time ago.
Just when you were coming to grips with that, then September rolled around
and you came down to breakfast.
Yes, they served muesli again.
But the announcement given to the Bethel family that day
discussed additional changes to the organization.
It included a significant reduction to Bethel families around the world
and a reemphasis to the preaching work
and the assistance that could be given to that preaching work through this change.
For the United States Bethel family, we learned that we would not retain
the tunnel complex as had been previously planned.
Instead, all property in Brooklyn would be sold and any remaining departments
would have to fit within the properties upstate.
So more movement.
And that’s already, according to our recent update,
already beginning.
And we are seeing signs of that around, aren’t we?
So, of course, for many of us, what that meant
was family worship took a little detour that week.
We had to go home and talk about some of these things
because our families got affected by these changes.
Of course, individually and as a family,
we do loyally comply with any direction.
The organization has reasons
for making adjustments, and we understand that.
And so we want to be cooperative.
But for many, it does mean a big change.
Maybe leaving a complex that has been the one they’ve served at forever
—since they’ve been at Bethel.
Maybe it’s where they’ve become very close
to not just friends there but in the congregation
that they’ve served in for many, many years.
Or consider others perhaps who have relocated their aging parents
into the area of the complex they’ve been serving in.
Now, can they move them again?
Are their parents well enough to even be moved?
These are real situations.
And we understand that, of course, they could give us a measure of anxiety
that can make us seem a little bit concerned
or maybe even overwhelmed sometimes.
But how can we be helped?
What can we do so that we can move on?
What are some ways?
Obviously, we can’t change a decision.
That’s not our position, and we don’t want to.
We want to be cooperative with what’s being done.
So we’re looking for ways to do that.
Well, look at what the psalmist said, David’s words in the 40th Psalm.
In the 40th Psalm, notice what David said
—the confidence he has in verse 5.
It says: “How many things you have done, O Jehovah my God,
“your wonderful works and your thoughts toward us.
“None can compare to you;
“if I were to try to tell and speak of them,
they would be too numerous to recount!”
So maybe it’s time to personally take stock
—personally recount the saving acts that Jehovah has done
toward us personally
here at Bethel, in our family.
Perhaps, did he take you by the hand when you were nervous
about coming into Bethel for the first day?
Maybe he helped care for you when you were a new bride trying to adjust
to a new city, a new congregation, marriage
and, of course, a new job —a new work you would do at Bethel.
Can you recall when you were feeling low and he sent not just the right person
but the right person at the right time with just the right words
to help kick you back into play a little bit and maybe even protect you
from making a mistake about leaving your Bethel service some time ago?
All of us probably can recount over and over again
things that Jehovah has done to show his love toward us
and his care for us, even as David was confident.
But the question is, Do you think He can do it again?
We had a beautiful Watchtower just now that talked about faith.
And so we think about that.
Do we have that faith that He will do it again?
Isaiah 59:1 says: ‘Jehovah’s hand will not be short.’
There is nothing that cannot be accomplished
for those who are faithful to Jehovah.
So we can recount it.
It may be that we need to even write it down.
It may need to be that we pray about these things so that we say,
“Yes, I see how Jehovah has really taken care of me.”
Now, for others . . .
Another group that’s affected by that same announcement is . . .
Maybe they’re having a little anxiety
over not moving to another complex.
Maybe they had their hope set on where they were going,
and they were looking forward to it.
Of course, as all were, necessarily, because they adjust themselves.
They think, ‘OK, I’m ready. Well, now I’m not going.’
And it may be that the tendency would be to say, “Well, why not me?
“Let’s see, my department is going,
“my work is going, my friends are going.
What? Did I do something wrong?”
And yet, really, that’s not the case.
But circumstances and decisions have to be made,
and so now we find ourselves . . . We have to examine ourselves:
‘How am I going to react to those types of feelings
that come up within myself?’
Proverbs 13:12 says:
“Expectation postponed makes the heart sick.”
But the footnote to that scripture says,
where it says “expectation,” it says “hope.”
And so it could be that our hopes, or our expectations,
are not realized, and it can take a toll on us.
That’s natural.
But the question is, Will we allow it
—our emotions —to override our clear thinking?
Will we allow it to blow us off course, so to speak, or slow us down
or even maybe change our direction for a while, that,
well, we just don’t seem to be heading in the same direction we thought we were?
We’re not making as much progress as we once were.
To stay positive, to stay levelheaded, to stay on course
requires sometimes that we give a little change to our thinking
—especially if the circumstances aren’t going to change.
It is easy to compare ourselves with others, but it’s not healthy.
And Galatians 6:4 tells us not to compare.
It says don’t compare ourselves or our work
with our fellow workers in the truth or in the congregation.
So, what can be done?
Well, we would like to look at our first Scriptural account.
It really helps us to see the need to avoid comparing.
It has to do with Jesus’ selection of the 12 apostles.
Think of what it meant to be with Jesus at that time when he was on earth
—getting to know him, working, learning from him personally,
listening to him maybe day after day for some.
What a privilege!
They got to do it for three and a half years.
We would trade a lot of time even to spend just a little bit of time
learning from Jesus directly like that, wouldn’t we?
Well, undoubtedly there were many who wanted the privilege
of being one of Jesus’ closest disciples and apostles.
But the time came that only 12 were chosen.
We know there were many to choose from.
Look at what it says in Acts the first chapter.
In Acts 1,
notice when they were going to replace Judas,
who they chose from.
So after Jesus had died and ascended to heaven,
verse 21, it says this in Acts the first chapter.
Or after Jesus had died, it says this: “It is therefore necessary
that of the men who accompanied us,” in verse 21,
“during all the time in which the Lord Jesus carried on his activities among us,
“starting with his baptism by John until the day he was taken up from us,
one of these men should become a witness with us of his resurrection.”
So there were many followers.
They knew who they were, and they were able to select from them.
So imagine what it was
—a year and a half into Jesus’ ministry,
after his baptism —it was time to select the Twelve.
This is what Mark 13 says in that account.
Mark the 3rd chapter, sorry.
In Mark chapter 3, notice what it says
in verse 13.
It says of Jesus: “He ascended a mountain
“and summoned those whom he wanted, and they came to him.
“And he formed a group of 12, whom he also named apostles,
“those who were to accompany him and whom he would send out to preach
and to have authority to expel demons.”
So Jesus selected from those.
Luke’s account says he prayed all night about it first.
And then he came down, and then from the crowd of his disciples,
he selected those 12 men.
Now, picture yourself there.
What if you were one of the men who loyally stuck by Jesus since His baptism?
Maybe, like Andrew and John and Peter and James,
you were an instantaneous believer too.
You left everything, and you followed Him immediately.
You believed, and you left all things behind.
But Jesus didn’t select you as one of his 12.
How would you feel? Slighted? Wronged?
Maybe that some injustice had been done?
Would you begin to discount those who were selected?
No, of course not!
You would think: ‘OK, I’m not going to be one of those 12.
But what are the blessings I do get to enjoy?’
What were the blessings these men would still be able to enjoy?
And apparently from Acts, those men remained with Jesus.
Those followers—those disciples —stuck close to him as well.
Well, they still got to listen to him teach and preach.
They still—just a few days later, really —would be able to hear
that famous Sermon on the Mount if they had stayed right with him.
They were still entrusted with the privilege of the ministry.
In fact, Jesus sent the disciples out, the Twelve,
and then later sent 70 to preach.
So, many others enjoyed that blessing as well.
They could help others to find the Messiah,
and they still had the hope for the same reward
that those 12 apostles were going to have
—being anointed and being able to be in heaven with Jesus
after their resurrection.
So, what’s the lesson?
Well, rather than feeling passed over for something
—maybe for the type of assignment or even the location of an assignment
—we think about it, we adjust.
‘What do I have? What are things I can enjoy?’
We devote ourselves, our time, our energy, and all our mental resources
to fulfilling our ministry —what we’ve been given to do
whether it’s our work here at Bethel or in the field, things we can control.
Because what’s the option —lower our sails,
just start floating aimlessly?
None of us want to do that.
That’s not why we came to Bethel in the first place.
It also would be a very dangerous thing to do.
So we avoid that.
Instead, we stay focused on what’s most important.
Turn with me to the book of 2 Corinthians,
2 Corinthians and the 4th chapter.
Notice what it says after talking about the tribulation in verse 17
that’s “momentary and light” and going to pass.
Notice what it says though in verse 18:
“While we keep our eyes, not on the things seen,
“but on the things unseen.
For the things seen are temporary, but the things unseen are everlasting.”
What’s the lesson for us?
Everything in this system
except our relationship with Jehovah is temporary
—our work assignments, likely temporary;
our work locations, temporary;
locations we live, probably temporary too.
What doesn’t change is our loyalty,
our devotion, and integrity to Jehovah.
That’s what lasts, and that’s why Jehovah promises
in Psalm 84:11: ‘He will not hold back anything good
from those walking in integrity.’
You notice, it didn’t require a location or a job assignment.
Psalm 18:25 says: “With someone loyal
you [or Jehovah] act in loyalty.”
That’s Jehovah’s promise to all of us.
There’s another group affected by those couple of announcements,
and that’s our wives.
Now, our wives are often impacted in greater ways
than even we are by some of these changes.
Most of our dear wives, pretty much they’re going to move
if their husband is moving.
Now, stop and think about that.
How could it make you feel?
What if their move to another complex
means losing the job that they love?
Maybe they are even good at it, right?
You know what that’s like.
Or even leaving those that they are enjoying working with,
but now they’re separating.
I know for our office, our Bethel Office in Brooklyn,
we are splitting into many different directions and going.
So we are feeling very personally that movement
of members of our very close family
of office mates that will be moving too.
But for our wives, they don’t even . . .
Some of them do not yet know where they will work.
They’re waiting still on that.
So imagine how that would make them feel.
And they might even wonder: ‘Does anybody outside of my husband
even understand the anxiety I am going through?’
Are emotions involved? Absolutely!
Because often, isn’t it true that we have more detail
about what’s going to happen to us than sometimes even our wives do?
So it is good for us to think about that.
What can help our wives to cope with these feelings
and sometimes the staying balanced and staying on course
with this question hanging over their heads?
Well, we would like to consider our second Scriptural example,
that of Esther.
Of the women in the Bible, Esther was one who seemed to have very little say
on how she would spend her life.
But she willingly submitted.
Let’s turn to Esther and look at this account together.
In Esther the 2nd chapter, we want to learn a little something
about Esther first —Esther the 2nd chapter,
verse 7, in the b part.
In the second part, it says: “The young woman was beautifully formed
“and attractive in appearance, and at the death
of her father and her mother, Mordecai took her as his daughter.”
So she was a beautiful young woman
in Israel.
So no doubt, there was no shortage
of nice young men
in the nation that would have been interested,
and she probably could have had her pick.
But did she get her pick?
No.
She, along with other beautiful young women in that nation,
were taken by a pagan king, Ahasuerus.
And look what it says in chapter 2, verse 12.
It says, first it says: “Each young woman had her turn
“to go in to King Ahasuerus after completing the 12-month treatment
“that was prescribed for the women, for this was the way
“they had to fulfill their beauty treatment —six months with oil of myrrh
and six months with balsam oil and various ointments for beauty treatment.”
Verse 14, it says: “In the evening she would go in,
and in the morning she would return to the second house of the women.”
So, of course, instead of her getting to pick
a nice young man that she could raise a family with
and serve Jehovah with and maybe even be
someone who could produce the Messiah,
that was gone
because now she was with someone who didn’t love Jehovah.
A pagan, really, and he already had many wives.
So that’s a pretty difficult situation.
Could you go along with that?
Well, Esther did. Why?
Well, this is what it says.
Even Mordecai told her, ‘Don’t tell them you’re a Jew.’
Now, that may have gotten her out of that whole arrangement.
Of course, it may have cost her her life too.
But Esther 2:20 says this:
“Esther did not say anything about her relatives and her people,
“just as Mordecai had instructed. . . .
“Esther continued to do what Mordecai said,
just as when she was under his care.”
Esther put her personal preferences and comforts aside.
She did just as she was told.
And, of course, we know what happened: her act of faith, she became queen.
But also, what really happened?
Well, the 4th chapter, verse 14,
Mordecai says to her in the latter part:
“Who knows whether it is for a time like this
that you have attained to your royal status?”
Jehovah used her.
She made herself available.
Her willingly complying —even in difficult circumstances
that would have tested any Christian sister in our time
—surely shows that she had
a beautiful, a beautiful spirit.
And do you think she ever looked back and regretted that decision
—whether or not her cozy little life that she wished she would have had was lost?
If she did, if so, all she had to do was look around and see
every little boy and little girl
that she saw pass by and realize that she had something.
Her self-sacrifice helped Jehovah
in preserving that young person alive.
So she was a powerful woman of faith
that we can call a good example.
And our sisters are no different.
You aren’t simply here at Bethel because of your husbands.
You made a choice, a conscious decision to come to Bethel
—to live a life of self-sacrifice and devotion through your Bethel service.
And we know that.
You could have said no when that young man was interested in you
and he asked you, “Would you like to get married and come to Bethel?”
You could have said no. He would’ve followed you anywhere, right?
Or you sisters who are already married, and you sat down with your husband
and you prayed about it and you talked about it:
“Can we make ourselves available for this avenue of service?”
And if you would’ve said no, he would’ve stuck with you.
But you didn’t.
You put your own personal comforts aside to a measure
so that you could have this additional avenue of service.
And you know, we often talk about telling people what we did in the new system
when we’re in Paradise and others ask, “How did you spend your time?”
You’re not going to say, “Well, my husband was at Bethel, so I was there.”
You’re going to say: “No, I was at Bethel with my husband.
“And we got to serve Jehovah full-time
“in the most exciting time of the organization’s history,
“and we got to see beautiful things that strengthened our faith.
And we got to be a part of that —a part of that history.”
So it is for us.
We feel honored to serve with you sisters
that are with us, our wives.
When Proverbs 31:31 speaks, we think of you.
It says: “Give her the reward for what she does,
and let her [own] works praise her in the city gates.”
Now, that’s just one area of change.
What about a second area of change that’s affecting many of us.
We want to talk about that for just a few minutes.
And that’s the change of assignment.
We’ve been talking about reassignments.
But more specifically, we’d like to talk to you brothers and sisters
who have been working as temporary workers.
Some of you are temporary volunteers who have poured your heart and soul
into the Wallkill and Warwick projects, and we’re thankful for that.
You, many of you, have seen the project go from a pile of dirt,
to a deep hole, to beautiful structures.
At both locations, it’s been really marvelous to see the willing workers.
But now the projects are wrapping up,
and the majority of Wallkill work will be done in just a few months.
And Warwick, of course, now we got the news: move-in date of September 1.
So that’s exciting.
Some may have thought, ‘Well, if I’d just worked hard enough,
if I’d just stayed long enough, maybe I’d get to stay afterward.’
And we can’t blame you for feeling that way.
But, of course, it’s pretty clear now, many will be going home.
So, of course, that’s a change of assignment for you.
You may be wondering what you will do next.
Most, like you, are wondering, though, where are you going to get the same joy?
Where are you going to be able to do the same fulfilling work
that you made yourself available for here?
And that’s really commendable.
We’d like you to consider the account of Bezalel.
Now, we’ve talked a lot about Bezalel.
Of course, during construction we always do, right?
If you turn to the account in Exodus 31,
let’s just look at this together for just a moment.
In speaking about Bezalel, this is what it says about him.
In verse 2 of chapter 31 of Exodus,
it says: “See, I have chosen Bezalel
“the son of Uri the son of Hur of the tribe of Judah.
“I will fill him with the spirit of God, giving him wisdom,
understanding, and knowledge of every kind of craftsmanship.”
And verse 6 says: ‘Moreover, to assist him I have appointed Oholiab
‘the son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, and I am putting wisdom into his heart
‘and all those who are skillful,
so that they may make everything I have commanded you.’
Well, that was a powerful, powerful commission
by Jehovah for Bezalel.
He personally would be overseeing the building of the tabernacle,
but not just the tabernacle but everything that was in it
—the furnishings, the utensils, the ark of the covenant,
the cover of the ark, the tables,
the alters, even the clothing for the priests.
It’s really amazing
what he as well as these other skilled craftsman had been able to do!
But in a sense, isn’t that what Jehovah’s spirit
has empowered you to do in your work at Wallkill and Warwick?
You came with skills, and you learned others.
Like Bezalel, Jehovah’s spirit has helped, and it’s been evident.
And no doubt Bezalel was admired and praised for what he did,
just as we admire and praise you for much of your work.
However, once that tabernacle was inaugurated,
things changed for Bezalel.
When the tabernacle was inaugurated, Bezalel could no longer enter it.
Leviticus 16 says that only Aaron
could come into the Most Holy and only that during the appointed time.
Additionally, in Numbers 3:31, it says Bezalel could no longer
even touch the furnishings because now the Kohathites
had the sole responsibility of moving those utensils.
So now here is someone who had a personal hand in doing all of that work
for that tabernacle to be built, but now he couldn’t go inside,
couldn’t touch, couldn’t even look.
How do you think he felt?
Well, the scripture doesn’t say,
but likely to a man of devotion like him,
the work would’ve been more important than just his own personal feelings.
But we know this: What he couldn’t do
would only be overshadowed by what he could do.
He had beautiful memories.
Imagine telling his children and grandchildren of what work he did.
Imagine having them meet others who worked right alongside him.
Yes, a lasting monument to praise Jehovah —that’s what he was working on,
and that’s what you’ve been working on.
Something to praise Jehovah, to make his name known.
But imagine how thrilled Bezalel is going to be when he learns
that his faithfulness and his actions were recorded in God’s Word for all of us.
What a privilege that will be too!
What’s the lesson for us?
Don’t judge the quality or appreciation of your work
by whether or not you get to stay.
In our Bible reading this last week,
2 Chronicles 15:7 was cited.
It says: ‘But you, be strong and do not be discouraged,’
or “do not let your hands drop” down, “for your activity will be rewarded.”
Yes, you don’t need to be discouraged.
Like Bezalel, you have a lifetime of memories to share and you can appreciate.
You’ll be able to bring your family to facilities that you’ve helped build.
You’ll be able to point out things that you did.
You’ll also have memories that no one can take away from you,
and those will be precious as well.
Maybe some of those bus rides you’ll be able to talk about.
And I know that the audience here
especially can appreciate those bus rides.
A mechanic told me once he was working
on the air conditioning for the bus in the middle of the night.
He said, “You do not want a hot bus
“full of 60 hot workers
stuck in midtown-Manhattan traffic coming home.”
But think of those memories.
Think of the things that went right; think of the things that maybe had a little glitch.
Those are memories you have, and every time you get together with someone
who you served with, you’re going to talk about that.
And what was the biggest frustration that you had is now going to be something
you laugh about and talk about for an eternity.
Memories that can never ever be taken away from you.
So remember, this is not your last assignment.
We don’t retire from Jehovah’s service.
We don’t have a rocking chair somewhere on a porch,
and now we’re just going to rock ourselves into the sunset.
We have work to do, and Jehovah wants you to be part of it.
So it’s just like . . .
If you have to leave Bethel,
one of the things that someone had said before is:
“The best way to leave Bethel is to take it with you when you go.
“Take your memories with you.
“Build enthusiasm and appreciation for others in Bethel.
“Take your friendships, and never stop volunteering
for any assignment the organization needs.”
They need us. They need you to do that work.
Finally, the third and last change we want to talk about
has to do with changing circumstances personally
for many in our family.
Many of our older members of the family have served for decades.
They have witnessed an exciting growth
in the history of Jehovah’s people.
Maybe when Brooklyn was the only buildings at Bethel,
then Kingdom Farm, Mountain Farm, Wallkill, Patterson
—tremendous expansion —and now Warwick.
Many of our older ones at Bethel have experienced all of that.
They have seen all of that come.
What a beautiful privilege that they’ve had!
But maybe, some have been told that they won’t be going
with their department to Wallkill or even Warwick in some cases.
So that can be pretty disappointing.
That can stir some pretty deep-seated emotions.
They might feel as the psalmist did in Psalm 71:9, where he said:
“Do not cast me off in my old age; do not abandon me
when my strength fails.”
But we must remember that our changing circumstances
—whoever we are, wherever we serve—have nothing to do
with how Jehovah views us.
So it doesn’t change our desire to be used by him as well.
This last week Brother Larson mentioned
Isaiah the 46th chapter, and it’s an appropriate scripture
for us to consider when talking about this particular subject as well.
Isaiah 46:4, it says:
“Until you grow old I will be the same;
“until your hair is gray I will keep bearing you.
“As I have done,
I will carry you and bear you and rescue you.”
Jehovah has always done that for us.
And for you older members of the family with many decades of faithful service,
you’ve shown us how to let Jehovah do that,
so that you can get the work done.
It’s that same unchangeable God
that helps us continue to be stabilized.
It grounds us, and it guards our heart,
so that we know that Jehovah loves us
and cherishes us personally.
When our hair is gray and our strength is gone, Jehovah carries us.
So we know, you brothers and sisters did not come to Bethel
with the idea that one day you would retire.
You have worked hard. You didn’t plan for that day.
But Jehovah doesn’t view it that way.
We think about Daniel in the 10th chapter.
Jehovah described Daniel as a “very precious man.”
He was likely around 100 years of age,
and yet he was still very precious in Jehovah’s eyes
—even as you are.
So it’s important to remember that just because we cannot do
what we once did, does not mean we cannot do anything at all.
We’d like to consider, finally,
the example of the apostle John
to help us maybe get a perspective on this.
Now, of course, John was used mightily by Jehovah.
He was a man of action, of faith.
Jesus called him and his brother the “Sons of Thunder.”
So they were people who were full of action.
John 21:7 also says he’s described as “the disciple whom Jesus loved.”
He sat directly next to Jesus at mealtimes.
He was a very special friend.
Maybe even Jesus shared things with him that He didn’t
with the other disciples around Him.
He was one of the few to witness the transfiguration.
He was one of the three that accompanied Jesus
into the house of Jairus to witness the resurrection of his daughter.
He even had the honor of caring
for Jesus’ mother after his death.
Still, after Jesus’ ascension to heaven,
when all of this activity was going on,
what did John do?
Well, he preached.
He was a faithful member of the congregation.
He was with Peter when some of the most fiery speeches were given,
miracles were performed, and when they stood up to say:
‘We will obey God as ruler rather than men.’
All of those things show that John was a man of faith.
But a long time went by
when we catch up with John later in life.
In the meantime, so much else had happened.
Many had written their own Gospel, right?
Matthew had written it some eight years after Jesus’ death.
Fifteen to seventeen years later, Luke wrote his.
A few years after that, Mark wrote his.
But not John, he still hadn’t written his.
Sixty-three years later, where do we find John?
Well, apparently where most Christians were back then
—preaching or in prison.
So look at what it says, Revelation 1:9,
Revelation 1:9.
Now imagine, he’s old; he’s well into his 90’s.
He’s the last of the apostles to be alive.
Revelation 1:9 says: “I John, your brother
“and a sharer with you in the tribulation and kingdom
“and endurance in association with Jesus,
“was on the island called Patmos for speaking about God
and bearing witness concerning Jesus.”
John was old, but he was active.
His faith was intact,
and he found himself in prison.
But that’s not even fully the point.
You see, John was yet to receive, was just about to receive,
or had just received what was arguably
the greatest privilege he would ever have.
Yes, because Jehovah caused him to see a thrilling vision of the future.
It brings it all the way down to the time of the end
and the conclusion of this system of things.
He got to pen the vision of Revelation.
And then after that, he got to write his Gospel
and three other books with his name.
Do you think he was worthless?
No. He was at an all-time peak.
His value was the best ever.
But isn’t it amazing!
We think sometimes that maybe there’s nothing left for us to do,
but that’s not how Jehovah sees it.
What a grand privilege for John to cap some 70 years of faithful service!
What’s the lesson?
We never lose our value to Jehovah or his organization
as long as we remain faithful.
And it’s true that for our older ones here at Bethel,
you’ve taught us as young ones coming into Bethel
what it means to work for Jehovah.
What it means to really put yourself out for that.
The example I always think of is when it snows outside in Brooklyn.
We have a nice arrangement.
The Transportation Office will go out;
they’ll actually see if the roads can be traveled.
They’ll call the Bethel Office.
The Bethel Office will call the Branch Committee.
We’ll put an announcement together: It’s too snowy to go out.
You know what we spend the most time on?
Trying to figure out how to tell the senior members of the family
it’s OK not to go to work.
You would think we’re trying to make them renounce their faith.
And don’t let those sidewalks dry up before noon, because they’ll be out there.
They’ll be going to work.
Yes, you have taught us how to be
really devoted servants of Jehovah, and you will continue to do that.
Your example is one that comes like a tree that has maturity.
It’s so much more valuable than just a sapling
that is waiting to produce fruitage.
So it is that we know you’re like “big trees of righteousness” to Jehovah.
So these are areas that all of us face.
We haven’t covered them all.
It’s just a few we’ve considered tonight.
But we recognize that change is a fact of life, and we’re all affected by it.
It’s going to continue; we expect it to.
But we’ve all learned that the one thing that doesn’t change is Jehovah.
He’s the one who will keep us; he’s the one who will ground us,
and he is our refuge and our strength.
In our Bible examples today, do we have one that can help us
in Bezalel, in Esther,
in the apostle John, and their faithful examples?
When we go back to our illustration of sailing,
rarely is a boat able
to get somewhere sailing in a direct line.
Now, sometimes you’ll have great weather and that can happen.
But when sailing into the wind,
a sailor needs to employ what they call tacking,
and the organization has used that in talking about maneuvering and changes.
But in short, it means that they steer upwind in a zigzag fashion
so that they get the wind hitting both sides of the sail,
and it pushes them forward in spite of riding into the wind.
For us, we have the advantage.
Jesus is at the helm.
He knows exactly where he wants us to be going.
We’re not alone in going through changes at Bethel either.
First Corinthians 12:25 tells us:
“There should be no division in the body,
but its members should have mutual concern for one another.”
So our concern for others should help us
to not just think about ourselves.
We have many who are changing assignments even now
—temporary workers who are leaving, Bethel family members being reassigned,
and others who will be moving very soon.
These are changes, and they affect us.
But Jehovah is that same person,
even as we read in the 46th Psalm.
The One who can be with us no matter what.
Bigger, more exciting changes?
I appreciate Brother Lett saying that, even in his Watchtower study today.
Armageddon is coming.
Does it get any bigger than that?
Wickedness will be a thing of the past.
Paradise will be real and here.
The resurrection will happen,
and old age and death will be a thing of the past.
These are changes we can believe in, and we can look forward to.
When we think about that,
whatever changes come our way, we can be confident that
we will not just go through them, but we can actually embrace them.
We can even grow from them;
we can even make sure we’re moving ahead with them.
We can be sure that our unchanging God, Jehovah,
will stick by us,
and he’s our rewarder everlastingly.

en.text: My name is Rocío Picado Herrero.
I studied chemistry at the University of Salamanca, in Spain.
I specialize in organic chemistry.
This field focuses on the study of the carbon atom
and all the compounds that are derived from this atom.
I believed that life came about through evolution.
I remember seeing a picture in a natural science book
that depicted the embryos of different vertebrates,
and in the early stages of development, the similarities were outstanding.
But when I started studying at the university,
I began studying in detail the process
on which the evolution theory is based.
To my surprise, I discovered that these processes
were not proven facts.
As a chemist, I’m fascinated
by the distribution of atoms within a molecule.
It is interesting to note that in most living creatures
​—​whether human, animal, or plant life​—​
the basic proteins required for life are made up
of a carefully interwoven collection of amino acids.
And with the exception of glycine,
all these amino acids have two forms called D and L.
These two forms are each a mirror image of the other,
just as the right hand is a mirror image of the left.
But that cannot be superimposed.
And what is really striking is that all the amino acids
that make up these proteins belong only to the L series.
So I asked myself,
‘How is it possible for blind chance to make all the amino acids
that are essential for life belong solely to the L series?’
I reached the conclusion that there had to be a higher power,
a Creator.
Even though I had a religious upbringing,
my ideas were not clear as to who God was.
I merely viewed him as a Supreme Being
before whom we would be held accountable.
The Bible is not a science textbook.
Its purpose is not to describe the universe we live in
or the laws that regulate our universe.
But when it does mention science,
and when it discusses scientific matters, it does so with great accuracy.
And undoubtedly the greatest benefit is that it allows me to enjoy
a personal relationship with the Creator of the universe
—a universe that fascinates me from a scientific perspective.

title: 데이비 로스: 생화학자가 자신의 믿음에 대해 말하다

en.text: My name is Davey Loos.
I studied biochemistry at the University of Leuven in Belgium,
and after that time I did a PhD in the same area.
When I was a young child, I believed in the Bible.
But growing up, I kind of lost my interest in it.
When you go to university and you study life sciences
or biochemistry, for example,
you get introduced into the idea of the origin of life very quickly
and also into the principle of evolution.
The professors who taught these courses,
they were really scientists with long careers,
and they were well-established scientists, and we had a lot of respect for them.
So there was just no way to really question the principle of evolution.
In 1999, there was a war in Europe—in Kosovo
—and I remember reading in the Bible as a child
about the future events that would take place,
and I started wondering whether the war in Kosovo was one of those events.
So that led me to pick up the Bible again.
At the time, I felt that I had to reexamine my beliefs about the origin of life
and also about the principle of evolution.
Based on the theory of evolution, we would expect to see
an abundance of transitional forms to be present in the fossil record.
But when we do look at the fossil evidence, we just don’t see that.
We see that the major species
come into existence at specific times,
and their form and structure is still exactly the same
as their form and structure today.
It was actually Darwin himself who wrote in his book
that the biggest objection that could be brought against this theory
would be the fact that the fossil record
does not show an abundance of transitional forms.
And that’s what really happens if you look at the set of data
—the fossil record seems to prove the opposite of evolution.
As a biochemist, I had the opportunity to learn about
and study many different biomolecules.
And I observed that pretty much every biomolecule
is really a complex molecule.
We can look at them as nanoscale molecular motors
or machines that are performing very complex and specific tasks.
For me, the complexity that we see in nature and the complexity in those molecules
points to the fact that there really is a Creator.

en.text: When the preaching work was getting started
in such countries as South Korea,
Jehovah often used missionaries to help strengthen our brothers.
In an archived interview, Brother Chong-il Park
describes the effect this had on his sacred service
and how it prepared him for the trials he would face.
From 1939 on, our brothers
didn’t have any contact with Jehovah’s organization,
and they thought that no organization existed.
Then, in 1948,
a brother read from a newspaper
about the activity of Watchtower Society.
And it surprised the brothers.
So brothers wrote the Society, and the Society
was so happy hearing from Korean brothers,
and they answered
with many booklets in Korean.
There were two different reactions.
Some brothers was excited about preaching work.
Yet, another group questioned:
“Is that true organization of Jehovah?”
First missionary group —Brother and Sister Steele—
arrived on August 9, 1949.
All the questions were answered
by Brother Steele, and then
right away brothers were preaching
in unity.
I began pioneering
in January 1950.
And then in March 1950,
six more missionaries arrived from Gilead School.
We had only one congregation in Seoul.
And the missionaries were busy for many Bible studies.
So many interested persons coming to the meetings.
The public talk was arranged
in school auditorium —first time.
And there were
over 360 people attended,
whereas the publishers was
about 60.
The same day, Korean War broke out,
and the missionaries had to leave
on 27th of June
to Japan.
And then our brothers had to take refuge
to southern part of Korea.
I was hiding in the country.
Then few days later,
the secret police from Communist found us.
We explained to him
as a Christian we cannot participate in the war,
so we had to hide ourselves.
And then he says: “Well, I do not know much about religion,
“so I better take one of my friends
“who knows about religion.
“So I will come back tomorrow.
Don’t leave from here.”
So, then, we waited until next day,
and he came with another.
So I started preaching from the Bible
about why this war broke out
and the many problems in the world
and so on, because the fulfillment
of Jesus’ prophecy in Matthew 24.
And then they say, “Well, thank you very much
for your preaching.”
And then say, “Goodbye.”
Then two days later, the latter one came
with another friend so that we could preach to them.
During three months they were staying in Seoul,
and, in fact, they protected us.
I was picked by South Korean army
to serve the back support
of the military in front line to carry arms
to the soldiers,
which I could not accept,
so I refused it.
And then
I was beaten.
And then one day
this company has to move to another place.
I hide myself
in behind the ceiling
so that they don’t notice
when they leave the place.
And the next morning when I came down,
there was nothing left.
I walked on one street, toward one direction,
and then I found a sign
that said “International Bible Students Association.”
So I stayed with the brothers for six months.
Brother Steele came back from Japan
by himself to take care of the brothers.
In 1952, Brother Steele recommended me
to Gilead School.
So that I was invited in 22nd class.
So I took the steps
to get the passport.
And then the government find out that I didn’t serve in military.
They gave me draft notice instead of passport.
So I had to stand for the neutrality
instead of going to Gilead School, which made me to be confined
in military prison for two years.
Then 1958, I was enrolled
in Gilead School in 32nd class.
I really appreciate
that great Gilead School training.
Since my job in the branch, especially in translation work
—and translation work involves much deep knowledge—
the Gilead training
has certainly helped in translation work.
The real appreciation
about the truth and the organization,
the brothers’ qualities, the humbleness and meekness,
certainly it helped me
to follow the examples
to apply in the full-time service.
Did you note what Brother Park said he appreciated most
even after enduring persecution and prison for his faith?
It was the Christlike qualities of his brothers
and the training he received from Jehovah’s organization
—another example of the benefits that result from our meeting together.
If you’d like to find more ways to imitate Brother Park’s faith,
you can read his life story beginning on page 12
of the December 2008 issue of Awake!

titles.en: Chong-il Park: Trained by Jehovah’s Organization

en.text: I always loved music.
I got my first guitar when I was 15,
and since then it’s been my way of expressing myself.
When they asked,
“Dave, do you want to join the band?”
I didn’t have to think twice.
Making music, that’s all that really mattered to me.
I thought being a musician would make me happy.
So that is the path I followed.
Only it is not what I thought it to be.
I work here during the day to pay the bills.
I thought my life would turn out better.
But something was missing.
Instead of being happy, I just felt lost.
Man, I’m distracted!
They are friendly and look happy.
He gave me a tract and said:
“Many people are searching for true happiness.
Maybe you are one of them.”
This could help.
I quickly wrote down my address
and asked whether they would mind passing by after I finished my shift.
I was searching all right.
Actually, the answers were in front of me all along.
How come I only get it now?
You see,
I was baptized.
But I never gave the truth a chance.
Roy did come as promised.
I told him, “I’m a baptized brother.”
He really listened to me.
Then he shared Psalm 100:3:
“Know that Jehovah is God.
“He is the one who made us, and we belong to him.
We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.”
In the Bible, Jehovah is likened to a shepherd.
He knows every single one of his sheep,
and he knows when one goes missing.
A lost sheep is not a lost cause; it still belongs to him.
And Jehovah doesn’t spare any efforts
in searching for it until he finds it.
I was like one of those lost sheep.
But I still belonged to Jehovah,
and he has never forgotten about me.
Roy promised we would keep in touch
and invited me to the Sunday meeting.
Man, I was nervous that morning.
I wanted to look my best.
Roy and Matthew were waiting for me,
giving me a warm welcome
—something I’ll never forget.
How I missed this!
This is indeed Jehovah’s congregation.
This is where I belong.
The truth has never been so clear to me.
How I enjoy the close company of my brothers and sisters!
What I enjoy most is helping others
to find our loving Father, Jehovah.
With Jehovah’s help, I will never be lost again.
