en.text: What many notice when they first attend meetings of Jehovah’s Witnesses
is that they hear God’s name, Jehovah.
In this life story, Soten Yoeun relates the impact
that learning God’s name had on her
after surviving the killing fields of Cambodia.
On the killing fields in Cambodia,
I prayed to God,
but I didn’t know his name.
When I was a very young girl,
they separated our family
and they put me to work in the rice field
from five in the morning
till nine in the evening.
When you see
some other children that get killed,
you really desperately cry for help inside.
You always think that you are next.
But in my heart I always believed
that there had to be a true God somewhere,
somehow that can help me get through this.
One year later, my family decided
to escape Cambodia.
We walk close to six or seven months
to Thailand.
And I have 20 brothers and sisters
—only 4 of us survived.
I have a blind aunt
that holds on my shoulder all the time.
But one day, we got caught.
As they start shooting, I push my aunt down
to the ground and try to pretend
that we are dead.
And when I got up,
I had no idea where my parent was.
We spent many months in the jungle.
As I try to survive,
I eat whatever I can find,
and I also help my auntie to survive.
One day when I go out to look for food,
I walked so far away
I couldn’t find my way back.
I start crying really hard underneath a tree
and look up to the sky
and pray to the true God.
I was raised as a child to pray to Buddhas.
But on this night
when I start praying, I specifically said
that I’m not praying to Buddha
—I’m praying to the true God.
And I say,
“True God, if you are really here,
“please help me because I am really scared
and I’m hungry and I’m cold.”
After I pray,
I just fall to sleep under the big tree.
Eventually, I make it into the refugee camp
in Thailand,
and I was reunited with my family.
We lived in the refugee camp in Thailand
for about ten years
before we come to United States.
My searching for the true God,
it didn’t stop there.
We tried to go to different churches,
but we didn’t understand anything.
One day when I come home from school,
I met this gentlemen named Herold,
and he asked if he can talk to me about God.
I agree because I saw he have a Bible;
he must be a good man.
When he talked to me,
I tried to pay attention so hard,
but I still didn’t understand
what he was saying.
And he went very slow.
And then he said, “Your name?”
I said, “My name Soten.”
And then he said, “Your name, Soten;
“my name is Herold.
God’s name, Jehovah.”
I never thought that God had name.
And ever since that day on,
I never forget Jehovah’s name.
It’s superglued in my heart.
He gave me
his phone number.
He say he gonna ask his wife
to stop by someday,
but then I move away from where I lived.
Even though I
didn’t do the truth at that time,
I always pray to Jehovah.
After I learned God’s name,
I went back to the church.
The priest would start out
with “heavenly Father”
but leave out Jehovah’s name.
So I raised my hand.
I asked him,
“Sir, when you pray, ‘heavenly Father,’
“why don’t you say, ‘heavenly Father,
“Jehovah’?
Why you not using God’s name?”
And then he told me
that God does not force me to be here,
so I’m welcomed to leave
or stay if I want.
So because I realized
that they don’t use Jehovah’s name,
I left and never returned.
And after many years, I tried to call Herold,
but no one picked up the phone.
So I leave a message.
I was hoping that they remembered me.
Two weeks later, Herold comes to my door,
but at the time, I was working at night
and asleep during the day.
But Herold never give up; he come back.
And I keep on praying to Jehovah,
asking for someone to knock on my door.
And finally, one day I open the door,
and when I saw him, I almost couldn’t talk.
I was teared up.
I was so happy to see him
because this is the man
who introduced me to Jehovah’s name.
Eventually, I start to study with a sister,
and she helped me grow spiritually.
To know that you have a heavenly Father
that cares about you
—that was the best feeling on earth.
It makes me want to know more about him
—want to learn more about him.
I would ask questions: “Did he like this?
Did he like that?”
And then when I go to the Kingdom Hall,
I hear Jehovah’s name so many times.
I feel, that’s it!
I found my place.
I got baptized in 2013.
My blind aunt
that I help her survive through the jungle,
she’s still living until today.
And now that I can get a chance
to talk to her about Jehovah,
that was a blessing.
And I can’t stress enough how wonderful
and big privilege that I receive from Jehovah
—just to know who he is
and to learn that there is true God.
He have a name,
and his name is Jehovah.
Sister Yoeun still carries painful memories
from what she and her family suffered
because of man’s ruthless wars.
But she now has hope for the future
and the comfort of knowing her heavenly Father, Jehovah
—something we all share with her.
Sister Yoeun has the added joy
of worshipping the true God together with her husband and young daughter.

cn.text: 很多人第一次参加耶和华见证人的聚会时
听见上帝的名字“耶和华”
尹娑晨在她的人物生平里讲述
当她从柬埔寨的杀戮场逃生后
得知上帝的名字
这对她有多么深远的影响
在柬埔寨的杀戮战场上
我向上帝祷告
可是，我不知道他的名字
我还小的时候
就被迫和家人分开
我必须在稻田里工作
从清晨5点一直到晚上9点
当我目睹其他孩子被杀
我只能在心里哭喊
我总是害怕
自己就是下一个
但一直以来
我都打从心里相信着
真神是存在的
他会拯救我
一年后，我们全家人决定要逃离柬埔寨
我们花了6、7个月走路到泰国
本来我有20个兄弟姐妹
但是在逃亡期间
只剩4个活了下来
我有个阿姨眼睛看不见
所以一路上，她都紧紧抓着我的肩膀
有一天，我们被发现了
他们开枪扫射我们
我马上拉着阿姨趴在地上
假装我们死了
后来，我再爬起来时
爸爸妈妈已经不见了
有好几个月的时间
我们都在丛林里
为了让自己和阿姨活下去
我们找到什么，就吃什么
有一次我为了去找食物而迷了路
我在树下哭了起来，哭得很厉害
我抬起头仰望着天空，向真神祷告
我从小就向佛祖祈祷
但在那个晚上
我特别清楚我不是向佛祖祈祷
我是向真神祷告
我说
真神啊，我又饿又冷
而且好害怕
如果你真的存在，请您帮帮我吧！
之后，我就在那棵大树下睡着了
历经千辛万苦
我终于抵达泰国的难民营
也得以和家人重聚
我们在难民营住了十年，后来搬到美国
即使环境不同，我还是继续寻找真神
我们去了很多不同的教堂
却什么都听不懂
有一天，放学回到家后
我遇到了一位叫哈洛德的先生
他问我能不能跟我谈谈关于上帝的事
我答应了，因为我看到他手上拿着圣经
我想他一定是个好人
我很认真地听他说，可是我还是听不懂
他放慢了速度
他问我，你的名字是？
我说，尹娑晨
接着他说
你叫尹娑晨，我是哈洛德
上帝的名字是耶和华
我从来没想过上帝有个名字
从那天起
耶和华这个名字就深深烙印在我心上
我从来没忘过
哈洛德给我他的电话号码，并告诉我
他会请他太太来拜访我
可是我后来搬家了
虽然那时候我没有讨论圣经
但我还是跟耶和华祷告
我知道上帝的名字
但在教堂里，神父总是说“天父”
而不说“耶和华”
有一次，我忍不住举手发问
我问神父
你向“天父”祷告时
为什么不说“天父耶和华”呢？
为什么不使用上帝的名字？
但是他跟我说，上帝没有强迫我待在那里
要是我想离开就离开吧！
我看出他们完全不使用上帝的名字“耶和华”
我离开了教堂，再也没回去
许多年后，我试着联络哈洛德
但没有人接电话，我只好留言
希望他们还记得我
两个星期后，哈洛德到我家来拜访我
但那时候我因为晚上工作，白天都在睡觉
哈洛德没有放弃找我
我也没放弃向耶和华祷告
我求耶和华让某个人上门拜访我
终于，那天我应了门
看到哈洛德在门外
我开心得说不出话，泪流满面
当初就是哈洛德告诉我
上帝的名字是耶和华
我开始和一个姐妹学习圣经
她帮助我认识天父
知道有一位天父关心我
这种感觉真的很美好
这推动我想加深对他的认识
我常问，上帝喜欢人这样做还是那样做呢？
我去聚会所时
我听到他们用“耶和华”这个名字很多次
当下我就想，就是这里了！
我找对地方了！
我在2013年受浸
当年跟我一起逃亡的那个阿姨
也活了下来
现在我能常常跟她聊关于耶和华的事
这真是很大的福分
我觉得很难用言语表达
我所享有的这种特别的殊荣
就是能够知道真神真的存在
而且真的可以认识他
上帝是有名字的，他的名字就是
耶和华
无情的战争带来的痛苦记忆
还是影响着尹姐妹
但是现在她对未来充满希望
也因为认识天父耶和华而得到安慰
这也是我们每个人共同享有的福分
尹姐妹的另一个福分
是跟她的丈夫和小女儿一同事奉耶和华

en.text: Our theme for this month
is “Consider, Incite, and Encourage One Another All the More So.”
JW Broadcasting
—why do we enjoy it so much?
Many of you have expressed how the monthly broadcast draws you closer
to our brothers and sisters and to Jehovah’s organization.
If you’re homebound or isolated, you especially treasure these programs.
And yet, while we appreciate the advances in technology
that have made all of this possible, we know that your sincere desire
is to be present with your brothers and sisters in person
at our congregation meetings.
Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world share this feeling.
In northern Finland, for example, winters are especially cold,
even by Finnish standards.
At times, temperatures plummet to minus 50 degrees Celsius,
or minus 58 degrees Fahrenheit!
Under those conditions, it’s very difficult to drive,
much less walk long distances.
Still, the brothers love to gather together.
How do they manage it?
In one small village, there is a brother who lives near the Kingdom Hall
and has a warm garage.
On meeting nights, he uses his car
to bring each family in the congregation to the hall.
Then he parks in his garage and runs the short distance back to the Kingdom Hall.
When the meeting is over, he returns all the friends safely to their homes.
In the Bible, gatherings for pure worship
were occasions for personal association with fellow believers.
Such association required travel to a designated place.
This involved work, sacrifice, even risk.
Consider what is stated at Exodus 34:24.
This verse has to do with the command that every Israelite male
should gather three times a year for the festivals in Jerusalem.
What would that mean in practical terms?
Wouldn’t the nation be left vulnerable to attack
if no men were left to guard the land?
And if word spread among the surrounding nations
that practically everyone congregated in Jerusalem
three times a year, like clockwork, year after year,
wouldn’t it be just a matter of time before some invading army
would come and pillage an Israelite city?
At Exodus 34:24,
we find Jehovah’s remarkable answer:
“For I will drive the nations away from before you,
and I will enlarge your territory, and nobody will desire,”
yes, even desire, “your land
“while you are going up to see the face of Jehovah your God
three times a year.”
Jehovah kept that promise.
It’s a historical fact that from 1513 B.C.E.
all the way down to 66 C.E. no foreign nation ever came
to invade Israelite territory during those three annual festivals.
Jehovah placed high value on having his people
gather together in the same space.
In the Christian era, the apostle Paul wrote
at 1 Corinthians 14:23 about ‘the whole congregation
coming together to one place.’
Now, although modern broadcasting technology didn’t exist in those days,
there were other viable methods of communicating, such as writing letters,
that didn’t require people to be physically present in the same location.
Still, the apostle John, though a capable writer,
preferred face-to-face interchange with fellow Christians
as he expressed at 2 John 12.
Or consider what is stated
at Job 1:6:
“Now the day came when the sons of the true God
entered to take their station before Jehovah.”
Job 2:1 speaks of another such day.
Just imagine!
Here Jehovah himself,
though having all conceivable methods of communication at his disposal,
set specific days for his spirit creatures in heaven
to assemble in his immediate presence.
Clearly, the Scriptures encourage regular personal association
with fellow servants of God.
Virtual attendance through modern communication technology has value,
and we’re happy to use it, but it’s no substitute for being together.
And why not?
Because of what association with the congregation achieves.
It’s not just that we receive nutritious and varied spiritual food.
Meetings inform us, but so does JW Broadcasting.
Meetings encourage us, but so does JW Broadcasting.
Fellow Christians who offer comments and sing from the heart build us up,
and yet we can hear that also on JW Broadcasting.
It’s when we’re together —all together in one place—
that others can hear us and draw encouragement
from our heartfelt convictions, our smile, our handshake.
Meetings give us opportunities to show our brothers and sisters
that we esteem them as worthy of our time,
attention, and concern.
That is why we go and visit our brothers who are homebound or isolated
because we want to show them that we love them.
Moreover, in a special way,
our meetings bring us under the influence of holy spirit.
At Revelation 2:7,
the glorified Jesus said:
“Let the one who has an ear hear
what the spirit says to the congregations.”
We need that spirit to help us resist temptation,
to embolden and equip us for the ministry,
and to enable us to make sound decisions.
Still, there’s a reason to attend meetings
that’s even more important than the pleasant company,
the peaceful atmosphere, the genuine refreshment,
the sense of belonging, the opportunities to give,
or even the fact that meetings are a means by which
we receive Jehovah’s holy spirit.
The key reason why we gather together
is stated at Psalm 26:12:
“My foot is standing on level ground;
in the great congregation, I will praise Jehovah.”
Yes, the principal reason why we gather together in person
is to give Jehovah what he deserves
—praise, glory, yes, worship.
Our meeting attendance shows Jehovah
that we want to draw close to him and his Son.
In his abundant love, Jehovah invites many more to serve him and keep living.
Because he lives eternally,
Jehovah can nurture those relationships forever.
The Adversary can offer no such hope of endless life,
so he promotes selfishness, pride, and other negative traits
that isolate people from one another, even when they are in the same room,
engaged in the same activities.
In contrast, our great God is drawing his people
closer to himself, to his Son,
and to one another so that we “may all be one,”
as Jesus prayed as recorded at John 17:21.
And it’s not just the act of converging
on the same location that unites us either.
Lots of people coexist in the same space when they go to a market,
attend a sporting event, or use public transportation.
Crowding of itself does not equate with unity.
What makes the true Christian congregation different?
Notice how Hebrews chapter 10,
verses 24 and 25 answers this question.
Now here we find the divinely inspired standard
for all our gatherings:
“And let us consider one another so as to incite
“to love and fine works, not forsaking our meeting together,
“as some have the custom, but encouraging one another,
“and all the more so as you see
the day drawing near.”
Now, what does it mean to “consider one another”?
What does it mean “to incite to love and fine works”?
And in what way might we ‘encourage one another’?
The verb “consider” could also be rendered
“be concerned about; pay attention to.”
So when we “consider one another,”
we show interest that goes far beyond a brief greeting.
And when we pay careful attention to one another, we’re better prepared
to incite, that is, to motivate one another, to stir one another to action.
And how might we do this?
Not by making comparisons or shaming our brothers,
for that would hardly be “encouraging one another,”
we endeavor to lift one another’s hearts when we’re together.
And when we do this to the best of our ability,
then we can be confident that Jehovah’s spirit will do the rest,
and that our brothers will feel strengthened.
It’s evident, then, that true worship
means participation; it requires a response.
Another noteworthy example of this is the encouragement we both give
and receive when we sing together with our brothers and sisters.
In ancient Israel, at times they had a chorus,
such as the one described in Nehemiah chapter 12
that we talked about in our midweek meeting back in February.
Much of Israel’s group singing was antiphonal,
that is, some of the singers prompted others to respond.
For instance, Psalm 106 which begins and ends with the words
“Praise Jah!” or “Hallelujah!”
encouraged the people to say in response: “Amen!”
Psalm 136 was written
to allow for different choruses to answer one another.
Now just imagine responding choruses
singing these alternating lines:
“Give thanks to Jehovah, for he is good;
“his loyal love endures forever.
“Give thanks to the God of gods,
“for his loyal love endures forever.
“Give thanks to the Lord of lords,
for his loyal love endures forever.”
And on it went for 26 verses!
To this day, singing demonstrates
our heartfelt response to the goodness of Jehovah.
What a joy it is to sing in company with others who are moved
to pour out the depths of their feelings to Jehovah!
And now at our Kingdom Halls, we’re accompanied by orchestral renderings
of many of our songs —another reason to sing out
at our midweek and weekend meetings.
And speaking of the midweek meeting, how are you enjoying the new format?
More of the program is devoted to delving into the Bible itself.
Time spent on preparing us for our public ministry
focuses more than ever on situations we face in field service.
And the meetings move along at a satisfying pace.
Yes, JW Broadcasting is a wonderful blessing,
a powerful means to talk to and fortify our brothers
around the world —simultaneously.
Still, nothing can replace the experience
of worshipping Jehovah in concert
with our fellow servants of God at congregation meetings.
When a meeting concludes and we lift our heads
after the final prayer, we find ourselves surrounded
by others who love Jehovah and support his sovereignty.
These important benefits are detailed
in the April 2016 study article
“Why Should We Meet Together for Worship?”
This month, we’re studying that article worldwide.
Later, in October, we begin a special campaign
to invite the public to our meetings.
If you do not yet regularly associate with Jehovah’s Witnesses
or if you travel away from your congregation, use jw.org
to find a meeting you can attend.
Click: “About Us,” “Meetings,”
and “Find a Location Near You”
or simply scroll to the bottom
of any jw.org page
and click “Attend Our Meetings.”
At our meetings, you’ll experience what it means
to consider, incite, and ‘encourage one another all the more so
as we see the day drawing near.’

cn.text: 这个月的主题是
“彼此关注、激发爱心, 要做的比以往更多”
为什么我们都喜欢收看 JW 电视网呢？
很多人说 电视网拉近我们与弟兄姊妹的距离
也让我们更紧密地跟随耶和华的组织
如果你住在偏远地区 相信你一定很珍惜这些节目
科技的进步确实让我们享有这些福分
不过 我们更希望能够参加聚会
在聚会所和弟兄姊妹实际互动
全世界的耶和华见证人都有同感
例如 芬兰北部冬天非常寒冷
对芬兰人而言也是这样
有时候 气温会骤降到零下50度
在这样的情况下 开车很不容易
如果是长途跋涉就更不用说了
但弟兄姊妹还是喜欢聚在一起
他们是怎么办到的呢？
在一个小村庄 有个弟兄住的离聚会所很近
而且有个温暖的车库
在有聚会的晚上
他会开车载所有家庭到聚会所
再把车停回到他家的车库
然后跑一小段路回聚会所
结束后 再把所有人安全的送回家
在圣经时代 以色列人会固定举行大型集会
从事正确崇拜
他们长途跋涉到指定的地方
除了要付出心力 做出牺牲 甚至要冒生命危险
请留意出埃及记34:24
这是所有以色列男子都需要遵守的诫命
他们全体一年要三次上耶路撒冷过节
为什么这会有生命危险呢？
试想想 如果没有任何男子留守
没有人保卫国土
整个以色列民族是不是很容易受攻击呢？
一旦附近的民族听说
所有以色列人会一年三次聚集在耶路撒冷
周而复始 整个以色列国境仿佛空城
这不就给那些外族军队
一个入侵抢掠的绝佳时机吗？
不过 出埃及记34:24耶和华保证
连“贪图”的人都没有
耶和华信守承诺
历史表明 从公元前1513年到公元66年之间
在犹太人庆祝这三大节期的时候
从没有任何外族人前来侵略
上帝的子民齐聚一堂崇拜他
这是耶和华十分重视的
在基督教时期 使徒保罗写下的
哥林多前书14:23提到了
“全会众聚集起来的时候”
当时 并没有我们今天使用的这些科技产品
但他们还是能够通过书信互相交流
不需要大家实际到场会面
不过 做为一个胜任的执笔者
使徒约翰却在约翰二书第12节说
他更喜欢和信徒同工实际面对面谈话
请也考虑约伯记1:6经文说
约伯记2:1也谈到另一个类似的场合
全能的上帝能够用各种奇妙的方式和他的天使沟通
尽管如此 他们还是在一个预定的日子
聚集起来站在耶和华面前
不错 这些经文都鼓励我们
要和上帝的其他仆人经常聚集起来
虽然用网路视讯或音讯参与聚会很方便
我们也适当地善用这些工具
但这绝不能取代我们实际参加聚会
为什么呢？
因为我们聚会 并不是单纯吸收灵粮而已
更是为了与会众来往
现在的 JW 电视网节目
就像聚会一样 有造益我们的演讲
有鼓励人心的经验

title: 성경 교육 덕분에 멕시코에서 글을 배우다

en.text: Jehovah’s people have always considered the studying of his Word
to be an essential part of life.
God’s Law to Israel commanded that the king “must read from [the Law]
all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Jehovah his God.”
In the Mayan territories of Yucatán, Mexico,
our brothers are helping people learn to read God’s Word for themselves.
People’s lives change when they can finally read the Bible on their own
and more readily ‘learn to fear Jehovah their God.’
One out of every six people on earth doesn’t know how to read.
Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world
have organized literacy classes to help such ones.
I don’t like to read.
I used to sleep at the meetings.
In our territory,
most people speak the Mayan language, but very few can read it.
On occasion I would give a talk, and when I would
cite a scripture, most of the audience would look it up.
But then I would see a blank stare on their faces
because they couldn’t read the text.
I was moved to learn how to read
because I wanted to learn about Jehovah and study his Word, the Bible.
So a sister came to my house to teach me.
Literacy classes are often conducted on an individual level.
After a person has had their Bible study, they can spend some time
to practice reading skills.
But when the local elders notice
that there are many that can benefit from this training,
they can schedule a larger class
at the Kingdom Hall.
The study material used for this purpose is the brochure
Apply Yourself to Reading and Writing.
It’s available in 30 languages in the Central America branch territory.
Other study materials can be used as well, as long as they help
the development of the students enrolled in the class.
And we use a board on which we write,
for instance, words that are difficult to pronounce.
This helps in the reading of complicated words.
There are some who are, well, very quick learners.
On the other hand, others go word by word.
But as they practice, they start getting the hang of it.
I’m good at masonry work,
but learning to read
is not easy.
Reading at his age is a big challenge.
You need to understand that each student learns differently.
With some, you need to be very patient.
The first word I learned to write was Jehovah.
“It’s like this,” I tell him.
He says, “It’s ‘cause you’re not being patient with me!”
Having a sense of humor is a big help in the learning process,
so as not to focus on errors and mistakes.
Since 1946, when records began being taken in Mexico,
more than 152,000 people have learned to read and write,
thanks to these training efforts.
The Secretary of Public Education
in the State of Mexico has recognized the work and the great help
these literacy classes have been to the local citizens.
The skills they learn help in their day-to-day life,
but also it helps them to learn more about Jehovah
and to be able to teach others.
I used to have to memorize everything I was going to say,
but now I can read
short scriptures to people directly from the Bible.
As the students progress in the class, they demonstrate
the words found at 1 Timothy 4:15,
which says in part
“so that your advancement may be plainly seen by all people.”
And these benefits are plainly seen in the students.
My husband was an alcoholic,
he smoked, and he used bad language.
But he made big changes in his life,
and we see that this training has been a big help.
We really see these great blessings.
Reading helped me to get baptized.
Helping other people to improve their reading skills
makes me feel very happy.
I feel great because I see on their face the joy they get
from reading and understanding the information.
Well, I’ve benefited so much.
For instance,
now we read the Bible together as a family.
It makes me very happy.
We’re more united as a family.
Our children respect my husband more,
like the father he is.
Now I’m a ministerial servant.
When I go preaching door to door,
some people say, “I don’t know how to read.”
But then I tell them,
“I didn’t know either, but I learned about Jehovah.
And you can too!”
If I learned to read, anybody can.

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—남아프리카 공화국 지부에서 발송되는 출판물

ko.text: 우리는 새로운 성경 출판물을 받을 때마다
그것을 준비한 사람들의 많은 수고를 떠올리게 됩니다.
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”은 우리의 믿음을 강화해 주는
시기적절한 영적 양식을 주의 깊이 마련합니다.
그러면 영적 양식은 어떻게 우리에게 전달됩니까?
중앙장로회의 출판 위원회는 성경 출판물의 인쇄와 발송을 감독하며
그 과정에서 수많은 형제 자매들이 출판물을 전달하는 일을 지원합니다.
출판 위원회는 세계적인 왕국 활동을 위해 기부되는 헌금이
그들은 특정 지역의 형제들의 필요를 고려하며
형제들이 구역에 있는 사람들에게 효과적으로 전파할 수 있도록
이 동영상에서는 어떻게 이토록 넓은 지역에 출판물이 공급되는지
또 이러한 노력이 사람들에게 어떤 좋은 영향을 주는지 보여 줍니다.
이 일은 여호와께서 자신의 백성들은 물론
우리가 전파하는 사람들에게 가지고 계신 깊은 사랑을 잘 보여 줍니다.
남아프리카 공화국 지부의 새로운 발송 창고에서는
이 거대한 창고는 축구장 두 개를 합친 것보다 더 큰데,
케냐 북부 지역에 있는 카쿠마 회중은 난민촌에 있습니다.
이곳에서 전파하는 형제들은 여러 언어로 출판물을 신청할 수 있어서
난민들에게 전파하면서 그들이 나타내는 반응을 보면
그들의 슬픔이 희망으로 바뀌는 것을 볼 수 있죠.
남수단에서 케냐까지 천 킬로미터를 걸어 난민촌에 왔어요.
목이 마른데 아주 시원한 물을 마시는 것 같죠.
남수단 상황이 안정되면 다시 돌아갈 거예요.
여호와의 증인이 된 지금 빨리 돌아가서
어머니께 진리를 전해 드리고 싶은 마음이 간절해요.
이곳 카쿠마 난민촌에서 배운 걸 아버지께도 가르쳐 드릴 겁니다.
제가 영적으로 성장하는 데 크게 도움이 돼요.
하느님께서 사람들이 지금도 목적 있는 삶을 살고
미래에 고통 없이 영원히 살기를 바라신다는 것을 알 수 있죠.
특별한 코드를 사용해 출판물의 위치를 찾습니다.
3층 높이의 선반까지 출판물들을 안전하게 올려놓을 수 있습니다.
지금 옮기고 있는 출판물은 포르투갈어 「성서의 가르침」 책입니다.
앙골라에서는 전도인 한 명이 평균 네 건이 넘는 성서 연구를 사회합니다.
연구생들이 하느님의 말씀에 따라 생활을 변화시키는 것을 볼 때면
성경 공부를 시작하면서 마음의 평화를 얻게 됐어요.
여호와께서 다른 사람들도 그러한 평화를 맛보도록
매달 1100만 부 이상의 잡지와 집회 교재가 인쇄됩니다.
계획된 집회와 전파 활동에 맞춰 각 회중으로 발송합니다.
가장 많은 양의 배부용 잡지가 발송되는 나라 가운데 하나는
잠비아는 전도인 한 명당 인구 비율이 85명인데,
전도인이 그렇게 많은데도 여전히 배부용 잡지 주문량이 많습니다.
우리는 루사카에서 대도시 증거 활동을 하는데
하고 물어보는 사람들을 흔히 볼 수 있죠.
모든 그리스도인들에게 꼭 필요한 내용이 들어 있어요.
세상이 지금보다 훨씬 더 나아질 거예요.
저 말고도 이 잡지를 읽는 사람이 아주 많습니다.
이 출판물을 읽고 하느님에 대해 배울 수 있어서 정말 좋아요.
배운 내용을 다른 사람들과 우리 아이들한테도 알려 주고 있어요.
매달 6만 개가 넘는 출판물 상자가 발송됩니다.
배달을 하는 형제들을 위해 특수 제작됩니다.
비가 많이 내리는 지역으로 보내지는 상자들은
먼 거리를 손으로 날라야 하는 상자에는 끈을 달기도 합니다.
출판물들은 목적지별로 차곡차곡 쌓아 단단히 포장합니다.
말라위 형제들은 집회 때 볼 출판물을 받을 수 있어 감사해합니다.
하지만 출판물을 들여오는 것이 어려웠던 때도 있었습니다.
우리의 활동이 여러 해 동안 금지되어 있었죠.
지금은 아무런 제약 없이 하느님을 섬길 수 있습니다.
집회 참석과 전파 활동을 자유롭게 할 수 있죠.
이제 출판물도 마음껏 받아볼 수 있습니다.
발송되는 출판물 상자 하나하나는 많은 사람에게 희망을 주고
사랑과 돌봄을 느낄 수 있게 해 줍니다.

들여다볼 수 있게 해 주신 것에

이 마지막 날에 사는 것 자체가
하지만 여호와께선 이걸 바꾸실 수 있는데,
앞으로 우리가 그런 일을 겪게 될 때
우리에게 실용적인 도움이 될 수 있는 것 몇 가지를

어떻게 영으로 충만해질 수 있는지 언급합니다.

왕국회관 건축에 든 총 비용을 계산해요.
왕국 활동의 여러 부면에 눈을 뜨게 되었어요.
이 건축 팀들이 직면하는 어려움들에 대해 알고는
의료 시설도 없는 곳에서 일하기도 해요.
아주 외딴곳에 왕국 회관을 지을 때는
자재를 운송하느라 아주 애를 먹기도 하고요.
제가 하는 일은 특별 파이오니아 순회 감독자,
그리고 그 아내들의 건강 문제를 돕는 겁니다.
최선의 치료 방법을 찾는 일을 하고 있습니다.
그리고 의료 비용을 해결하는 일도 돕고 있습니다.
어떤 기쁨을 얻고 있는지 말씀해 주시죠.
그동안 여호와를 섬기는 행복을 앗아갈 만한
몇 달밖에 살지 못할 거라는 소식을 들었어요.
“셜리야, 네 엄마와 난 널 여호와께 이미 바쳤단다.
물론 부모님은 기뻐하셨고 저도 정말 기뻤죠.
여호와께서 내 상황을 모르셨을 거라고 생각하니?
그분이 나와 네 엄마를 돌봐 주실 거야.”
우주에서 가장 안전한 곳에서 돌봐 주셨어요.
아버진 이미 부활 파티를 계획해 놓으셨는데,
파티 때 제 길르앗 경험을 말씀드리겠다고 약속했죠.
그리고 물론 많은 간구의 기도를 한 것이에요.
큰 것에서 일상생활의 작은 것까지 말이죠.
그 고난을 통해서 배운 게 있는데,
로렌소 형제도 기쁨을 잃을 뻔한 어려움을 겪으셨다죠,
콩고에서 몇 년 동안 야외 봉사를 마음껏 즐기다가
베델 생활에 적응하는 일이 쉽지 않았습니다.
제 자신과 주변 사람들의 불완전성 모두요.
깨달은 건 낙담의 원인에 너무 초점을 맞추면
혼자 힘겹게 싸운다는 느낌도 받은 적이 있어요.
그런 상황에서 무엇보다 도움이 된 건,
부서 내 감독자들과 지부 위원을 비롯한
어떤 땐 모든 걸 제쳐 두고
그 형제들이 각자의 책임을 돌보느라 바쁜데도,
부서의 기술적 문제를 다루는 감독자가 아니라
목자이자 친구처럼 저를 대해 주는 걸 보면서
정말 도움을 받고 제가 달라지게 되었어요.
여호와를 섬기며 기쁨을 유지하는 데 도움이 될까요?
여호와께서 다양한 사람들을 어떻게 대하시는지 배우면서,
얼마나 자비롭고 합리적이고 친절하신 분인지 더 깨달았어요.
임무를 수행할 수 있도록 쉬고 음식을 먹게 해 주셨고요.
적어도 두 번 같은 약함에 굴복했죠.
처음엔 아합을 돕고 후엔 아하시야를 도왔죠.
하지만 여호와께선 여호사밧에 관해 요약하실 때
그가 여호와의 눈에 옳은 일을 했다고 하셨죠.
마음속 좋은 반응까지도 기뻐하신다는 사실에 감동했어요.
우리 안에 있는 좋은 걸 찾으려고 얼마나 애쓰시는지,
또 우리도 그렇게 할 때 얼마나 기뻐하실지 깨달았죠.
제 이해가 얼마나 부족했는지 깨닫게 해 주었습니다.
저도 이 특성들을 나타내려고 애써 왔죠.
개인의 타고난 능력으로 어떤 특성을 나타내는 것과는
모든 일이 순조로울 땐 잘 참지만,
일이 순조롭지 않을 때는 어떻게 될까요?
이건 정말 참을 수 없다고 생각하게 될 수도 있죠.
여호와께선 우리가 자신에게 수월할 때가 아니라
자신의 열매는 일관성 있게 나타나지 않는데
그래서 매일 여호와의 성령에 의지하기 위해
시간을 내서 그분의 말씀을 매일 묵상하고
자신의 어려움에 관해 구체적으로 기도해야 하죠.
더 잘 대처할 수 있기를 바랍니다.
여호와를 섬기며 기쁨을 유지하는 데 도움이 될까요?
누굴 섬기는지에 달려 있다는 걸 배웠어요.
다윗에게 보이신 용서, 충성, 사랑에 대해 배웠죠.
수업을 하면서 마치 이스라엘인들과 함께 여행하고
또 다윗과 함께 있는 기분이 들었어요.
강사 형제들이 그런 특정 상황에 우릴 데리고 가셨죠.
그 상황에서 나타난 여호와의 특성을 생각해 보면서,
저도 어디서든 그 똑같은 하느님을 섬길 수 있다는 게
언제나 기쁨을 찾을 수 있을 거라 확신합니다.
어떤 교훈이 기쁨을 유지하는 데 도움이 될까요?
우리의 사랑을 강하고 깊게 하는 것입니다.
성서에 관해 전에는 전혀 몰랐던 점들을 배웠어요.
그분을 섬기면서 늘 행복할 거라고 믿습니다.
여호와를 섬기도록 다른 사람을 도울 때
자기 하느님 여호와께 희망을 두는 사람은
계속 행복을 찾도록 그분이 도우시기를 기도합니다.

ko.text: 학생 여러분과 그 가족 또 초대받은 친구분들
공립 학교, 사립 학교, 직업 학교,
그럼 길르앗 학교는 어떤 학교에 속할까요?
세상의 고등 학문을 위한 학교도 아닙니다.
원래 학교는 돈이 있고 여유 있는 사람들이
물론 지금 우리 시대에는 대부분의 나라에서
부자나 가난한 사람이나 학교에 다닐 수가 있지요.
그래서 많은 젊은이들이 여러 대학에 가는데,
한 연구 조사를 언급하면서 이런 내용을 실은 적이 있습니다.
“돈을 더 많이 벌기 위해서” 라고 말했다.’
‘어떻게 다른 사람에게 유익을 줄 수 있을까?’,
유익이 될 수 있을까 하는 겁니다.
언제나 여호와께서 앞자리에 와야 하지 않겠습니까?
훨씬 더 부유하게 해 주지 않았습니까?
예수 시대 사람들은 물질적으로 부유한 걸
부자들이 가장 먼저 구원받게 된다고 생각했죠.
그분은 거기에 고통을 더하시지 않는다”라고 했지요.
필요한 것을[물질적 필요를] 공급해 줌으로 축복[하신다.]”
화면에서 그 점을 보실 수 있습니다.
이 「파수대」 기사의 삽화는 무엇을 보여 줍니까?
자신의 노력이나 다른 사람의 선물 때문이 아니고요.
그 역시 여호와의 축복 덕분에 부자가 되었지,
아브라함이 소돔 왕에게 한 말에서도 알 수 있는데요,
그는 소돔 왕의 소유물을 전투에서 되찾아 왔죠.
‘하늘과 땅을 만드신 가장 높으신 하느님 여호와께
당신의 것은 아무것도 가지지 않을 것입니다.
소돔 왕이 아브라함을 부자로 만들지 않았죠.
그분의 축복은 결코 고통을 주지 않죠.
또 물질적으로 부유한 그리스도인들도 더러 있었는데,
지부 사무실, 번역 사무실 등을 건축하고
또 출판물을 무가로 배부할 수 있죠.
형제들의 작은 헌금이 모여 큰 일을 이룹니다.
어떤 나라에선 하루에 한 끼만 먹는 형제들이 있는데,
두세 끼를 먹을 형편이 안 되죠.
여호와의 축복을 받지 못하고 있는 건 아닙니다.
어려운 시기에 물질적으로 서로 돕게 하십니다.
그러므로 학생 여러분은 이제 임지로 가더라도
그리고 여기 참석해 계신 가족 분들도
그분께 더 나은 봉사를 드릴 수 있도록
제139기 길르앗 학교를 곧 졸업할 여러분에게
예수 그리스도께서 아주 오랜 삶 동안
지혜에 관한 영감받은 말씀을 읽어 보겠습니다.
‘이 내용이 예수나 그분이 여호와께 받은 훈련과
그 의미를 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
예수께서는 창조물 중에 처음 나신 분이었죠.
날마다 그분이 각별히 좋아하시는 자가 되어
단지 학문이나 배움에 대한 열망 때문이었을까요?
두 분 다 서로 사랑하셨음을 알 수 있죠.
우리 모두가 기억해야 할 점이 있습니다.
또 우리가 잘 배우고 부지런한 학생이 될 때
「파수대」에서 어떻게 이 점을 잘 묘사하는지 들어 보십시오.
건축가와 시공자의 관계에 비할 수 있습니다.
또 그렇게 일한 노력의 결과를 보면서
이 우주를 위한 여호와의 설계를 보면서 느꼈을
첫 인간을 위한 설계를 보면서 말이죠.
예수의 본을 통해 분명히 배울 수 있는 점은
먼저 숙련된 학생이 되어야 한다는 거죠.
예수께선 여러 임무를 맡으실 수 있었고
그것은 여호와의 목적을 이루는 데 기여했습니다.
수확하는 일에 능숙한 일꾼이 될 수 있고,
다른 신성한 봉사의 임무도 맡을 수 있습니다.
그러면, 절대 교실을 떠나지 않는 면에서
지친 사람에게 적절한 말로 대답할 줄 알게 해 주셨다.
주권자인 주 여호와께서 내 귀를 열어 주시니,
교실에서 또 수업을 받고 배우라는 거죠.
예수께선 새로운 교실이라 할 수 있는 이 땅에서
개인에 맞게 베푸시는 특별한 훈련 덕분에
지금까지 잠언과 이사야에 나온 예를 봤는데요,
예수께서 배우고 또 배운 걸 적용하려는
열심을 갖고 계셨음을 보여 주는 예가 많습니다.
일례로, 열두 살 된 예수가 없어졌을 때,
‘자신이 겪은 고난으로부터 순종을 배우셨다’고 알려 주죠.
우리도 그런 경험을 통해 배우려고 해야 합니까?
오늘날 여호와의 교실에서 배우려는 우리 모두에게
그 누구보다 오랫동안 여호와를 섬겨 오셨지만,
결코 여호와의 교실을 떠난 적이 없으십니다.
이 점을 통해 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
하느님의 동료 일꾼이 되는 특권을 기뻐하며,
그리고 삶의 경험을 통해 계속 배우고,
모리스 형제가 훌륭한 베델 강의를 했는데요,
사람들을 과거 속에 가두어 두지 말도록
한때 조언을 받았다는 걸 아실 것입니다.
그에 대해 더 알아보는 게 좋을 것 같습니다.
바룩이 그 맡은 일을 막 시작한 때였을 것입니다.
쉴 곳을 찾지 못했다’ 하고 말한다.
내가 심은 것을 뽑아 버릴 것이다.
더 이상 그런 일을 추구하지 마라.
바룩이 맡은 일을 막 시작한 때라고
사람들을 과거 속에 가두는 문제와 관련 있죠.
사실 후에 바룩에게 특권을 더 주셨죠.
바룩이 그런 말을 했다는 기록은 없습니다.
자신이 하고 있는 일에 만족하지 않았습니다.
뭔가 다른 일만 바라서는 안 됩니다.
예레미야서는 시간 순으로 기록된 것이 아닙니다.
바룩이 두루마리를 기록한 후의 사건을 알려 줍니다.
여호와께서 그에게 하신 모든 말씀을 불러 주었고,
바룩은 그 말씀을 두루마리에 받아 적었다.”
‘나는 갇혀 있어서 여호와의 집에 들어갈 수 없습니다.
내가 불러 준 대로 두루마리에 받아 적은
여호와의 말씀을 소리 내어 읽어 주십시오.
여호와의 집에서 백성이 듣는 가운데 읽어 주십시오.’”
자, 이제 예레미야는 이 모든 내용을,
예언자 예레미야가 자기에게 명령한 대로 다 행하여,
우선 그는 두루마리를 백성들에게 읽어 주었고,
예레미야를 죽이려고 했던 바로 그 사람들인데,
이 말을 듣고 난 방백들은 왕도,
이 말을 들을 필요가 있다고 결정했죠.
그럼, 바룩이 그렇게 열심히 쓴 두루마리는
왕 앞에서 한 부분을 읽고 나면,
왕은 매번 그걸 칼로 베어 불에 던졌습니다.
공들여 한 작업이 헛수고가 된 적이 있으신가요?
그 첫째 두루마리에 적혀 있던 모든 말을 기록하여라.’
그런데 누가 그 일을 할 건가요?
사실, 바룩은 그것 역시 불태워질지 알 수 없었지만,
그 두루마리는 아주 귀중한 것이 되었습니다.
앞으로 얼마나 가치 있게 쓰일지 몰랐죠.
예수, 사도 바울을 비롯한 많은 사람이
그 일에 바룩이 기여할 수 있었던 거죠.
때때로 우리도 지금 하고 있는 일이
앞으로 얼마나 가치 있게 쓰일지 알지 못합니다.
바룩은 얼마 동안 임무를 계속 수행했습니까?
그가 충성스럽게 예레미야 곁에 있었다고 알려 줍니다.
우리 졸업생 여러분에게 어떤 교훈이 될까요?
너는 자신을 위해 큰일을 추구하고 있다.
부활된 후로 이 말을 천 번도 더 들었어요.”
어느 때나 사용할 수 있는 도덕 나침반을
31절을 읽을 텐데 계속 펴 두시면 좋겠군요.
이 말씀을 가리켜 흔히들 황금률이라고 하죠.
불완전한 사람들에 둘러싸여 지내게 될 것입니다.
그것도 인류 역사상 가장 어려운 상황 속에서
그에 더해, 불완전한 사람들이 함께 일하고,
너무 놀라거나 너무 성급하게 판단하지 마십시오.
사실, 여러분이 감정 상하던 바로 그날
여러분도 누군가의 감정을 상하게 했을지 모르니까요.
여러 차례 상하게 해 드렸을 가능성이 아주 높습니다.
거의 매번 우리 죄를 용서해 달라고
여러분은 얼마나 기꺼이 다른 사람들을 용서하고
다른 사람이 거듭해서 감정을 상하게 하더라도
그러면 어떻게 이런 감정을 제쳐 두고
도움이 되는 다섯 가지 방법을 알려드리죠.
아무 생각도 안 들 수 있죠.
다른 사람이 어떤 행동이나 말을 하든
우리의 행동에 책임을 져야 할 사람은
상대방의 마음에 영향을 줄 수 없습니다.
형제 자매들이 더 나은 사람이 되고
“계속 주십시오. 그러면 사람들도 여러분에게 줄 것입니다.”
다른 사람들도 그렇게 하도록 도울 수 있는
길르앗 학교 과정 내내 강조된 것이죠.
모든 사람이 여러분이 내 제자라는 걸
우린 형제 관계를 매우 소중히 여깁니다.
그러나 우리가 서로 더 이상 용서하지 않는다면,
이제 오랫동안 길르앗 강사로 일해 온
여호와께선 그 기도에 크게 마음이 감동되셔서,
하지만 한나가 드린 두 가지 기도는
그 기도를 무척 소중히 여기신 거죠.
사무엘은 그 기도에 관해 얼마나 많이 들었을까요?
한나의 기도에 담긴 감정과 생각과 마음으로
이제 여러분 각자가 임지에서 임무를 수행할 때
한나가 하지도 않은 일에 대해 비난했을 때였죠.
그 아들들이나 먼저 돌보시죠’ 라고 하지도 않았고,
지금도 내가 취했다고 생각할까?’ 하고 말이죠.
‘얼굴에 더는 수심이 없었다’고 분명히 알려 줍니다.
하지만 동족을 위해 수십 년간 힘을 쏟고
그가 도와 주려고 했던 바로 그 동족이
이 기도의 기적이 계속되게 할 것입니까?
현재 우리 모두 임명받은 일이 있지만,
내일 그 임명이 바뀔 수 있습니다.
그럴 때 여러분은 자신의 가치에 대해
여러분은 어떤 업무나 임명에 헌신한 게 아니라
늘 초점을 맞춰야 할 가장 중요한 건
수업 중에 얼마나 자주 토의를 했습니까.
‘지혜는 그것이 한 일로 옳다는 것이 증명된다’라고 한
어떤 나쁜 말을 해도 걱정하지 말고
그 말을 믿을 사람이 아무도 없게끔
가난한 자를 잿더미에서 들어 올려” 주신다고요.
한나는 이 사실을 직접 체험해서 알았죠.
이 말에 분명 다윗도 깊은 감명을 받았는데,
이 기도의 기적이 계속되게 한 겁니다.
기적이 계속 이어지게 할 수 있습니다.
여러분이 할 수 있다는 걸 압니다.
즉 잿더미 속에 있는 것을 보고 어떻게 하셨죠?
때문에 여러분은 뗄래야 뗄 수 없는 사이가 되었죠.
‘왜 그 형제는 그런 상황이 된 걸까?
중요해 보이지 않는 사람이 낙담해 있을 때
그 사람이 더 성장하고 성숙해진 걸 보면
우리는 더 약한 사람들을 짐으로 여기거나,
그러니까, 내가 이 아이를 장막으로 데려가면
여호와께선 틀림없이 아이를 돌봐 주실 거야.’
한나는 알고 있는 점들을 연결해서 판단할 수 있었죠.
깨끗이 해결하시는 걸 본 다음에 데려가야지.
여호와의 손이 자신의 삶에 작용하는 걸 보았고,
나를 보호하시고 지켜 주실 거’라고 생각했습니다.
사무엘은 그 기적이 계속되게 한 겁니다.
그의 소매 없는 작은 겉옷을 적셨을까요?
어머니가 손수 만들어 준 그 겉옷에
또는 엘리의 아들들의 타락한 영향 때문에
이 어린 소년은 얼마나 많은 밤을
국가 조직을 안정시키는 데 기여한 것처럼,
더 의미 깊은 관계를 시작할 수 있는
여호와와 그분의 조직 마련에 고착하는 것이
그분이 충성스러운 자들을 지켜 주신다는 걸

Jehovah’s people have always considered the studying of his Word
to be an essential part of life.
God’s Law to Israel commanded that the king “must read from [the Law]
all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Jehovah his God.”
In the Mayan territories of Yucatán, Mexico,
our brothers are helping people learn to read God’s Word for themselves.
People’s lives change when they can finally read the Bible on their own
and more readily ‘learn to fear Jehovah their God.’
One out of every six people on earth doesn’t know how to read.
Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world
have organized literacy classes to help such ones.
I don’t like to read.
I used to sleep at the meetings.
In our territory,
most people speak the Mayan language, but very few can read it.
On occasion I would give a talk, and when I would
cite a scripture, most of the audience would look it up.
But then I would see a blank stare on their faces
because they couldn’t read the text.
I was moved to learn how to read
because I wanted to learn about Jehovah and study his Word, the Bible.
So a sister came to my house to teach me.
Literacy classes are often conducted on an individual level.
After a person has had their Bible study, they can spend some time
to practice reading skills.
But when the local elders notice
that there are many that can benefit from this training,
they can schedule a larger class
at the Kingdom Hall.
The study material used for this purpose is the brochure
Apply Yourself to Reading and Writing.
It’s available in 30 languages in the Central America branch territory.
Other study materials can be used as well, as long as they help
the development of the students enrolled in the class.
And we use a board on which we write,
for instance, words that are difficult to pronounce.
This helps in the reading of complicated words.
There are some who are, well, very quick learners.
On the other hand, others go word by word.
But as they practice, they start getting the hang of it.
I’m good at masonry work,
but learning to read
is not easy.
Reading at his age is a big challenge.
You need to understand that each student learns differently.
With some, you need to be very patient.
The first word I learned to write was Jehovah.
“It’s like this,” I tell him.
He says, “It’s ‘cause you’re not being patient with me!”
Having a sense of humor is a big help in the learning process,
so as not to focus on errors and mistakes.
Since 1946, when records began being taken in Mexico,
more than 152,000 people have learned to read and write,
thanks to these training efforts.
The Secretary of Public Education
in the State of Mexico has recognized the work and the great help
these literacy classes have been to the local citizens.
The skills they learn help in their day-to-day life,
but also it helps them to learn more about Jehovah
and to be able to teach others.
I used to have to memorize everything I was going to say,
but now I can read
short scriptures to people directly from the Bible.
As the students progress in the class, they demonstrate
the words found at 1 Timothy 4:15,
which says in part
“so that your advancement may be plainly seen by all people.”
And these benefits are plainly seen in the students.
My husband was an alcoholic,
he smoked, and he used bad language.
But he made big changes in his life,
and we see that this training has been a big help.
We really see these great blessings.
Reading helped me to get baptized.
Helping other people to improve their reading skills
makes me feel very happy.
I feel great because I see on their face the joy they get
from reading and understanding the information.
Well, I’ve benefited so much.
For instance,
now we read the Bible together as a family.
It makes me very happy.
We’re more united as a family.
Our children respect my husband more,
like the father he is.
Now I’m a ministerial servant.
When I go preaching door to door,
some people say, “I don’t know how to read.”
But then I tell them,
“I didn’t know either, but I learned about Jehovah.
And you can too!”
If I learned to read, anybody can.
Our theme for this month
is “Consider, Incite, and Encourage One Another All the More So.”
JW Broadcasting
—why do we enjoy it so much?
Many of you have expressed how the monthly broadcast draws you closer
to our brothers and sisters and to Jehovah’s organization.
If you’re homebound or isolated, you especially treasure these programs.
And yet, while we appreciate the advances in technology
that have made all of this possible, we know that your sincere desire
is to be present with your brothers and sisters in person
at our congregation meetings.
Jehovah’s Witnesses around the world share this feeling.
In northern Finland, for example, winters are especially cold,
even by Finnish standards.
At times, temperatures plummet to minus 50 degrees Celsius,
or minus 58 degrees Fahrenheit!
Under those conditions, it’s very difficult to drive,
much less walk long distances.
Still, the brothers love to gather together.
How do they manage it?
In one small village, there is a brother who lives near the Kingdom Hall
and has a warm garage.
On meeting nights, he uses his car
to bring each family in the congregation to the hall.
Then he parks in his garage and runs the short distance back to the Kingdom Hall.
When the meeting is over, he returns all the friends safely to their homes.
In the Bible, gatherings for pure worship
were occasions for personal association with fellow believers.
Such association required travel to a designated place.
This involved work, sacrifice, even risk.
Consider what is stated at Exodus 34:24.
This verse has to do with the command that every Israelite male
should gather three times a year for the festivals in Jerusalem.
What would that mean in practical terms?
Wouldn’t the nation be left vulnerable to attack
if no men were left to guard the land?
And if word spread among the surrounding nations
that practically everyone congregated in Jerusalem
three times a year, like clockwork, year after year,
wouldn’t it be just a matter of time before some invading army
would come and pillage an Israelite city?
At Exodus 34:24,
we find Jehovah’s remarkable answer:
“For I will drive the nations away from before you,
and I will enlarge your territory, and nobody will desire,”
yes, even desire, “your land
“while you are going up to see the face of Jehovah your God
three times a year.”
Jehovah kept that promise.
It’s a historical fact that from 1513 B.C.E.
all the way down to 66 C.E. no foreign nation ever came
to invade Israelite territory during those three annual festivals.
Jehovah placed high value on having his people
gather together in the same space.
In the Christian era, the apostle Paul wrote
at 1 Corinthians 14:23 about ‘the whole congregation
coming together to one place.’
Now, although modern broadcasting technology didn’t exist in those days,
there were other viable methods of communicating, such as writing letters,
that didn’t require people to be physically present in the same location.
Still, the apostle John, though a capable writer,
preferred face-to-face interchange with fellow Christians
as he expressed at 2 John 12.
Or consider what is stated
at Job 1:6:
“Now the day came when the sons of the true God
entered to take their station before Jehovah.”
Job 2:1 speaks of another such day.
Just imagine!
Here Jehovah himself,
though having all conceivable methods of communication at his disposal,
set specific days for his spirit creatures in heaven
to assemble in his immediate presence.
Clearly, the Scriptures encourage regular personal association
with fellow servants of God.
Virtual attendance through modern communication technology has value,
and we’re happy to use it, but it’s no substitute for being together.
And why not?
Because of what association with the congregation achieves.
It’s not just that we receive nutritious and varied spiritual food.
Meetings inform us, but so does JW Broadcasting.
Meetings encourage us, but so does JW Broadcasting.
Fellow Christians who offer comments and sing from the heart build us up,
and yet we can hear that also on JW Broadcasting.
It’s when we’re together —all together in one place—
that others can hear us and draw encouragement
from our heartfelt convictions, our smile, our handshake.
Meetings give us opportunities to show our brothers and sisters
that we esteem them as worthy of our time,
attention, and concern.
That is why we go and visit our brothers who are homebound or isolated
because we want to show them that we love them.
Moreover, in a special way,
our meetings bring us under the influence of holy spirit.
At Revelation 2:7,
the glorified Jesus said:
“Let the one who has an ear hear
what the spirit says to the congregations.”
We need that spirit to help us resist temptation,
to embolden and equip us for the ministry,
and to enable us to make sound decisions.
Still, there’s a reason to attend meetings
that’s even more important than the pleasant company,
the peaceful atmosphere, the genuine refreshment,
the sense of belonging, the opportunities to give,
or even the fact that meetings are a means by which
we receive Jehovah’s holy spirit.
The key reason why we gather together
is stated at Psalm 26:12:
“My foot is standing on level ground;
in the great congregation, I will praise Jehovah.”
Yes, the principal reason why we gather together in person
is to give Jehovah what he deserves
—praise, glory, yes, worship.
Our meeting attendance shows Jehovah
that we want to draw close to him and his Son.
In his abundant love, Jehovah invites many more to serve him and keep living.
Because he lives eternally,
Jehovah can nurture those relationships forever.
The Adversary can offer no such hope of endless life,
so he promotes selfishness, pride, and other negative traits
that isolate people from one another, even when they are in the same room,
engaged in the same activities.
In contrast, our great God is drawing his people
closer to himself, to his Son,
and to one another so that we “may all be one,”
as Jesus prayed as recorded at John 17:21.
And it’s not just the act of converging
on the same location that unites us either.
Lots of people coexist in the same space when they go to a market,
attend a sporting event, or use public transportation.
Crowding of itself does not equate with unity.
What makes the true Christian congregation different?
Notice how Hebrews chapter 10,
verses 24 and 25 answers this question.
Now here we find the divinely inspired standard
for all our gatherings:
“And let us consider one another so as to incite
“to love and fine works, not forsaking our meeting together,
“as some have the custom, but encouraging one another,
“and all the more so as you see
the day drawing near.”
Now, what does it mean to “consider one another”?
What does it mean “to incite to love and fine works”?
And in what way might we ‘encourage one another’?
The verb “consider” could also be rendered
“be concerned about; pay attention to.”
So when we “consider one another,”
we show interest that goes far beyond a brief greeting.
And when we pay careful attention to one another, we’re better prepared
to incite, that is, to motivate one another, to stir one another to action.
And how might we do this?
Not by making comparisons or shaming our brothers,
for that would hardly be “encouraging one another,”
we endeavor to lift one another’s hearts when we’re together.
And when we do this to the best of our ability,
then we can be confident that Jehovah’s spirit will do the rest,
and that our brothers will feel strengthened.
It’s evident, then, that true worship
means participation; it requires a response.
Another noteworthy example of this is the encouragement we both give
and receive when we sing together with our brothers and sisters.
In ancient Israel, at times they had a chorus,
such as the one described in Nehemiah chapter 12
that we talked about in our midweek meeting back in February.
Much of Israel’s group singing was antiphonal,
that is, some of the singers prompted others to respond.
For instance, Psalm 106 which begins and ends with the words
“Praise Jah!” or “Hallelujah!”
encouraged the people to say in response: “Amen!”
Psalm 136 was written
to allow for different choruses to answer one another.
Now just imagine responding choruses
singing these alternating lines:
“Give thanks to Jehovah, for he is good;
“his loyal love endures forever.
“Give thanks to the God of gods,
“for his loyal love endures forever.
“Give thanks to the Lord of lords,
for his loyal love endures forever.”
And on it went for 26 verses!
To this day, singing demonstrates
our heartfelt response to the goodness of Jehovah.
What a joy it is to sing in company with others who are moved
to pour out the depths of their feelings to Jehovah!
And now at our Kingdom Halls, we’re accompanied by orchestral renderings
of many of our songs —another reason to sing out
at our midweek and weekend meetings.
And speaking of the midweek meeting, how are you enjoying the new format?
More of the program is devoted to delving into the Bible itself.
Time spent on preparing us for our public ministry
focuses more than ever on situations we face in field service.
And the meetings move along at a satisfying pace.
Yes, JW Broadcasting is a wonderful blessing,
a powerful means to talk to and fortify our brothers
around the world —simultaneously.
Still, nothing can replace the experience
of worshipping Jehovah in concert
with our fellow servants of God at congregation meetings.
When a meeting concludes and we lift our heads
after the final prayer, we find ourselves surrounded
by others who love Jehovah and support his sovereignty.

In this life story, Soten Yoeun relates the impact
that learning God’s name had on her
after surviving the killing fields of Cambodia.
On the killing fields in Cambodia,
I prayed to God,
but I didn’t know his name.
When I was a very young girl,
they separated our family
and they put me to work in the rice field
from five in the morning till nine in the evening.
When you see some other children that get killed,
you really desperately cry for help inside.
You always think that you are next.
But in my heart I always believed that there had to be a true God
somewhere, somehow that can help me get through this.
One year later, my family decided to escape Cambodia.
We walk close to six or seven months to Thailand.
And I have 20 brothers and sisters
—only 4 of us survived.
I have a blind aunt that holds on my shoulder all the time.
But one day, we got caught.
As they start shooting, I push my aunt down to the ground
and try to pretend that we are dead.
And when I get up,
I had no idea where my parent was.
We spent many months in the jungle.
As I try to survive,
I eat whatever I can find, and I also help my auntie to survive.
One day when I go out to look for food,
I walked so far away
I couldn’t find my way back.
I start crying really hard underneath a tree
and look up to the sky
and pray to the true God.
I was raised as a child to pray to Buddhas.
But on this night
when I start praying, I specifically said
that I’m not praying to Buddha
—I’m praying to the true God.
And I say,
“True God, if you are really here,
“please help me
“because I am really scared
and I’m hungry and I’m cold.”
After I pray, I just fall to sleep under the big tree.
Eventually, I make it into the refugee camp in Thailand,
and I was reunited with my family.
We lived in the refugee camp in Thailand
for about ten years before we come to United States.
My searching for the true God, it didn’t stop there.
We tried to go to different churches,
but we didn’t understand anything.
One day when I come home from school,
I met this gentlemen named Herold,
and he asked if he can talk to me about God.
I agree because I saw he have a Bible; he must be a good man.
When he talked to me, I tried to pay attention so hard,
but I still didn’t understand what he was saying.
And he went very slow.
And then he said, “Your name?” I said, “My name Soten.”
And then he said, “Your name, Soten; my name is Herold.
God’s name, Jehovah.”
I never thought that God had name.
And ever since that day on, I never forget Jehovah’s name.
It’s superglued in my heart.
He gave me his phone number.
He say he gonna ask his wife to stop by someday,
but then I move away from where I lived.
Even though I didn’t do the truth at that time,
I always pray to Jehovah.
After I learned God’s name, I went back to the church.
The priest would start out
with “heavenly Father” but leave out Jehovah’s name.
So I raised my hand.
I asked him, “Sir,
“when you pray “heavenly Father,” why don’t you say
“‘heavenly Father, Jehovah’?
Why you not using God’s name?”
And then he told me that God does not force me to be here,
so I’m welcomed to leave
or stay if I want.
So because I realized
that they don’t use Jehovah’s name,
I left and never returned.
And after many years, I tried to call Herold,
but no one picked up the phone.
So I leave a message.
I was hoping that they remembered me.
Two weeks later, Herold comes to my door,
but at the time, I was working at night and asleep during the day.
But Herold never give up; he come back.
And I keep on praying to Jehovah,
asking for someone to knock on my door.
And finally, one day
I open the door, and when I saw him,
I almost couldn’t talk.
I was teared up.
I was so happy to see him
because this is the man who introduced me to Jehovah’s name.
Eventually, I start to study with a sister,
and she helped me grow spiritually.
To know that you have a heavenly Father
that cares about you
—that was the best feeling on earth.
It makes me want to know more about him —want to learn more about him.
I would ask questions: “Did he like this?
Did he like that?”
And then when I go to the Kingdom Hall,
I hear Jehovah’s name so many times.
I feel, that’s it!
I found my place.
I got baptized in 2013.
My blind aunt that I help her survive through the jungle,
she’s still living until today.
And now that I can get a chance to talk to her about Jehovah,
that was a blessing.
And I can’t stress enough
how wonderful
and big privilege that I receive from Jehovah
—just to know who he is and to learn
that there is true God.
He have a name,
and his name is Jehovah.

My name is Rocío Picado Herrero.
I studied chemistry at the University of Salamanca, in Spain.
I specialize in organic chemistry.
This field focuses on the study of the carbon atom
and all the compounds that are derived from this atom.
I believed that life came about through evolution.
I remember seeing a picture in a natural science book
that depicted the embryos of different vertebrates,
and in the early stages of development, the similarities were outstanding.
But when I started studying at the university,
I began studying in detail the process
on which the evolution theory is based.
To my surprise, I discovered that these processes
were not proven facts.
As a chemist, I’m fascinated
by the distribution of atoms within a molecule.
In living creatures, the 20 amino acids
that are vital for the synthesis of life,
the basic proteins required for life,
interestingly, are all levorotatory or left-handed.
So when a ray of polarized light arrives,
these amino acids divert the light toward the left.
There is no explanation for this because the logical thing would be
that if this were a random process, half would be right-handed
and the other half would be left-handed.
I asked myself, ‘How could evolution produce compounds that are levorotatory
and precisely the ones essential for life?’
In the end, I had to conclude that there must be a force,
a Designer, a Creator of life and of the elements
and the amino acids required for life.
Even though I had a religious upbringing,
my ideas were not clear as to who God was.
I merely viewed him as a Supreme Being
before whom we would be held accountable.
The Bible is not a science textbook.
Its purpose is not to describe the universe we live in
or the laws that regulate our universe.
But when it does mention science,
and when it discusses scientific matters, it does so with great accuracy.
And undoubtedly the greatest benefit is that it allows me to enjoy
a personal relationship with the Creator of the universe
—a universe that fascinates me from a scientific perspective.
My name is Davey Loos.
I studied biochemistry at the University of Leuven in Belgium,
and after that time I did a PhD in the same area.
When I was a young child, I believed in the Bible.
But growing up, I kind of lost my interest in it.
When you go to university and you study life sciences
or biochemistry, for example,
you get introduced into the idea of the origin of life very quickly
and also into the principle of evolution.
The professors who taught these courses,
they were really scientists with long careers,
and they were well-established scientists, and we had a lot of respect for them.
So there was just no way to really question the principle of evolution.
In 1999, there was a war in Europe—in Kosovo—
and I remember reading in the Bible as a child
about the future events that would take place,
and I started wondering whether the war in Kosovo was one of those events.
So that lead me to pick up the Bible again.
At the time, I felt that I had to reexamine my beliefs about the origin of life
and also about the principle of evolution.
Based on the theory of evolution, we would expect to see
an abundance of transitional forms to be present in the fossil record.
But when we do look at the fossil evidence, we just don’t see that.
We see that the major species
come into existence at specific times,
and their form and structure is still exactly the same
as their form and structure today.
It was actually Darwin himself who wrote in his book
that the biggest objection that could be brought against this theory
would be the fact that the fossil record
does not show an abundance of transitional forms.
And that’s what really happens if you look at the set of data
—the fossil record seems to prove the opposite of evolution.
As a biochemist, I had the opportunity to learn about
and study many different biomolecules.
And I observed that pretty much every biomolecule
is really a complex molecule.
We can look at them as nanoscale molecular motors
or machines that are performing very complex and specific tasks.
For me, the complexity that we see in nature and the complexity in those molecules
points to the fact that there really is a Creator.
Did you see common ground that could help you
in your next discussion with someone who believes in evolution?
When Sister Picado Herrero’s chemistry research
showed evidence of design,
she called to mind her view of God from her religious upbringing.
The person you meet who believes in evolution
might also have unanswered questions about God from their upbringing,
and they may respond to the simple evidences
of a Creator that you present.
Brother Loos was moved by world events
to pick up the Bible and reexamine his beliefs.
Everyone we meet, even firm believers in evolution,
are affected by world conditions and may listen to our message of hope.
So when someone says that he believes in evolution,
don’t be quick to assume that he’ll reject the good news.
Really, our ministry and other aspects of life often improve
when we slow down, take our time,
and as our music video admonishes:
“Don’t Run Fast.”
You can walk, but please don’t run. It’s hard to do when you’re having fun.
But there’s a reason we don’t race; When you’re with the friends,
It’s not the time or place.
Don’t run so fast. Take your time and make things last.
Learn to love the things you do. Just don’t run fast.
You’ve got things you have to do, People to serve, who depend on you.
But don’t forget why you’re here; Learn to love the friends;
Let them know you care.
Don’t run so fast. Take your time and make things last.
Learn to love the things you do. Just don’t run fast.
You can run to someone’s door. Is there someone home?
Well, you’re not real sure. But look around and see everyone,
People walking by. Can you talk to one?
Don’t run so fast. Take your time and make things last.
Learn to love the things you do. Just don’t run fast.
Oh. Just don’t run fast!
Of course, we shouldn’t run at all in the Kingdom Hall.
But in a figurative sense, this counsel, not to run fast,
applies to more than just our young ones.
As we saw, even when we’re busy with important theocratic work,
we can still take the time to consider, incite,
and encourage our brothers.
And rather than rushing through our field service,
we want to imitate Jesus’ focus on finding people
and reaching hearts.
Jehovah reaches our hearts in ever so many ways,
such as when we attend our spiritual gatherings.
By now, some of you have already attended
the 2016 “Remain Loyal to Jehovah!” regional convention.
But millions of us still have an exciting three days ahead
with 47 well-prepared talks,
18 songs that we’ll sing to Jehovah,
and more than 50 audio and video presentations,
including 2 feature-length dramas.
All of these program parts have been prepared to help us
remain loyal to God despite serious challenges.
For instance, how can we maintain our loyalty
when under stress or temptation?
What did Jehovah personally teach Job
that can strengthen our loyalty?
And why does the Bible say that Jehovah’s loyal love
is more precious than life itself?
To find out more of what you can expect,
review the full convention program,
which can be downloaded from jw.org.
You won’t want to miss any part
of the “Remain Loyal to Jehovah!” convention program!
As we close, we bring you greetings
from the Las Perlas-Ngäbere congregation in Panama.
The Volcán region is the highest point in the country,
enjoying a cool climate for growing coffee
and a variety of vegetables.
The busy harvest work from October to December
brings large numbers
of Ngäbere-speaking people to the area.
Their kind nature gives our brothers excellent opportunities
to teach them about God’s Kingdom.
Local brothers and sisters
provide regular support to the Ngäbere Remote Translation Office.
And some are making the effort
to learn the language to assist in the congregation’s spiritual harvest.
We send them our warm Christian love
and greetings in return and pray for them to continue in their zealous spirit.
We thank you and hope you’ve enjoyed our program.
This is JW Broadcasting
from Brooklyn, New York!

en.text: The Big Red Island is renowned
as a place of incredible beauty and diversity.
About 75 percent of the plant and animal species
found in Madagascar live nowhere else on the planet.
Another form of diversity on the island has to do with the directive
given by Jesus at Luke 12:42
that he would appoint a ‘faithful and discreet steward
‘over his body of attendants
‘to keep giving them their measure of food supplies
at the proper time.’
Doing so for the diverse needs of this large island was the main reason
for the original branch buildings
that were constructed, which were dedicated
December 7, 1996.
However, because of remarkable growth,
it was not long before it became too small
and construction was started once more.
Isaiah 54:2
foretold that this would happen
during the time we are living in.
And so it became necessary to “make the place
“of your tent more spacious. . . .
And make your tent pins strong.”
These newly expanded branch facilities
were dedicated by Brother Mark Sanderson
of the Governing Body on Saturday,
January 24, 2015.
Brothers and sisters, it is a great privilege for me to be here today
for the dedication of these expanded facilities in Madagascar.
The diversity among Jehovah’s unified people
was well represented by the hundreds
of brothers and sisters at this special event.
Included were guests from 15 different countries,
along with longtime Witnesses,
Bethelites, circuit overseers,
special pioneers, and missionaries.
Even some of the first missionaries were among the visitors.
In his dedication talk, Brother Sanderson
highlighted our ongoing spiritual building work
with those to whom we preach and with ourselves.
We have to help our students and our children
to build their own relationship with Jehovah.
Is it your desire that we should dedicate these buildings
to the worship and service of our God, Jehovah?
The expansion gives more office space
for the Malagasy translation team for added projects.
This is a key to serving the food in the right language.
So that spiritual food can be served in the right locations,
the new offices for the Local Design/Construction Department
help them to care for the construction
of Assembly and Kingdom Halls throughout the country.
These buildings serve as spiritual banquet halls
for the more than 660 congregations.
But what about food in the right format?
One of these formats is Braille for the visually impaired.
In the main office complex, a Braille Transcription Department
has been added that produces Braille publications in Malagasy.
One blind sister commented:
Receiving Braille publications in my mother tongue
has really touched my heart.
Thank you.
The facilities now include a new sign-language studio
for recording Madagascar Sign Language publications
on DVD and jw.org.
With publications in this video format,
sign-language congregations and groups are actively helping the deaf
to “hear” the good news in the language of their heart.
A special meeting was held the day after the dedication program,
which proved to be historic
as 28,683 people attended
either at the Assembly Hall
or via a live stream video tie-in at their Kingdom Halls
to listen to a special talk
given by Brother Sanderson.
This represented nearly all
of Jehovah’s people in Madagascar.
Through these newly expanded branch facilities,
“the faithful and discreet slave” continues to provide the people of Madagascar
spiritual food supplies at the proper time,
at the right locations,
in the correct languages, and in up-to-date formats.

en.text: Here at Wallkill, we have two rotary presses.
Each prints something called a signature,
which is virtually the same as a 32-page brochure.
The press can print up to 94,000 signatures per hour.
If these were stacked on top of each other,
they would reach the height of a 30-story building every hour!
The process begins with a 3,000- to 4,000-pound roll of paper.
It’s loaded along the press, rolled into place,
trimmed, and lined with double-sided tape.
Before the previous roll is finished, the new roll is loaded onto the splicer.
By means of double-sided tape,
this roll is attached to the expiring roll.
Next, the paper advances to the four print units,
which apply ink on both sides of the paper at the same time.
The presses use a technique called offset printing.
This process uses printing plates designed to allow water
to repel ink from the nonimage areas
and attract ink to the image areas.
The plate then transfers the ink to a rubber blanket,
which then transfers the ink to the paper.
Four colors of ink are used to create the images.
They are black, cyan, magenta, and yellow.
The ink on the paper is applied in tiny dots.
By using this technique, a wide range of colors can be achieved.
Now the paper goes through the dryer,
which maintains a temperature of around 400 degrees Fahrenheit
Solvents from the ink are evaporated inside the dryer.
Next, in order to set the ink so that it will not smear,
the paper travels through a series of rollers filled with chilled water.
Now that the ink is dry,
the paper is folded and cut.
Finally, the conveyer brings the cut signatures
out of the press, and they are checked for quality.
They are then processed and distributed to the congregations.

en.text: Psst! Hey!
Check this out!
Gossip.
It may seem like nothing more than harmless talk.
Or is it?
If you’ve ever found out somebody was talking about you
behind your back, then you know
gossip can hurt!
The Bible says at Proverbs 12:18
that words can ‘stab like a sword.’
So how can you make sure that you  aren’t the one doing the stabbing?
Are you supposed to stop talking completely?
At Philippians 2:4, the Bible says
we’re supposed to be interested in the lives of others.
So it’s normal to talk about other people.
But that talk can quickly turn ugly
and damage a person’s good reputation.
So, what can you do before  this happens?
For example, when comments about others get sarcastic or negative,
that’s a sign the conversation is going in the wrong direction.
Don’t get dragged in!
Change the subject!
You have to take action—and fast!
Take responsibility.
You see, even if you’re not the source of a rumor,
repeating it can make you guilty of spreading falsehood.
Instead, save yourself a lot of pain
by following the Bible’s wise counsel
at 1 Thessalonians 4:11:
“Mind your own business.”
Before you start talking about others, ask yourself:
‘Do I really know all the facts?
‘If what I say gets repeated,
‘is the other person’s reputation going to be damaged?
And what about my own  reputation?’
Remember, whenever harmful gossip
creeps into your conversation, take action!
The people around you will feel happy —and so will you!

ko.text: 젊은 시절에 현명한 결정을 내린 좋은 본이라고 할 수 있습니다.
그는 1900년에 태어나 23세에 침례를 받고 1928년에는 전 시간 봉사를 시작했습니다.
여호와의 증인들의 지하 활동을 책임 맡게 되었으며
강제 수용소에 감금되기까지 8개월 동안 그 일을 했습니다.
어떻게 왕국 멜로디를 작곡했는지에 관한 감동적인 경험담을 들어 보시기 바랍니다.
전 늘 작곡을 하고 싶은 마음이 있었어요.
다들 아시겠지만, 우린 수용소에 있는 동안
굶주림에 시달렸고, 힘에 겨운 노동을 했고, 견디기 힘든 괴롭힘을 자주 겪었지요.
항상 그랬듯이 형제들을 세워 줄 방법을 찾고 싶었습니다.
작센하우젠 수용소에 있는 동안 정말 우린 한마음으로 연합되어 있었죠.
서로 격려할 수 있도록 함께 부를 노래를 만들고 싶었어요.
매일 아침 우린 오라니엔부르크에 있는 하수 처리 시설의 공사 현장까지 행군했습니다.
이 공사에 저를 포함해 40명 정도 되는 형제들이 징발되었는데
행군을 하는 동안 제 머리 속에는
’붐 붐 바담 밤 타람밤밤바’ 하는 곡조가 맴돌았죠.
점점 멜로디가 만들어졌고 그렇게 해서 노래가 완성되어 갔어요.
하지만 가사를 종이에 쓰지 않고 어떻게 수용소 안으로 들여갈 수 있었을까요?
절 도와줄 형제를 몇 명 찾았어요.
행군하는 중이나 일터에서 손수레를 미는 동안
한 형제에게 첫 구절을 반복해서 알려 주고 암기하게 했죠.
또 다른 형제들에게 세 번째 네 번째 구절을 알려 줬어요.
저녁에는 형제들이 각각 맡은 구절을 암송하게 했죠.
아침에 우리 40명의 형제들이 오라니엔부르크 거리를 행군하는 동안,
우린 이미 지칠 대로 지쳐 있었어요.
그때 한 사람이 이 멜로디를 흥얼거리기 시작하면
큰 소리로 노랠 부르고 싶은 마음을 억눌러야 했습니다.
수용소로 바로 끌려 들어가 심한 처벌을 받았을 겁니다.
연설을 했고, 파수대 기사를 가지고 함께 연구도 했죠.
그렇게 진정한 평화를 주는 시간을 갖고 특별한 격려를 나눴어요.
기름부음받은 자인 프로스트 형제는 1987년에 지상 생애를 마쳤습니다.
2차 세계 대전과 함께 9년간의 수용소 생활이 끝난 후,
그는 10년 동안 독일 지부 사무실의 감독자로 봉사했죠.
그때는 지부 위원회가 활동을 감독하는 마련이 시행되기 전이었습니다.
프로스트 형제가 투옥된 곳과 비슷한 강제 수용소에 있던 한 형제가 직접 그린 것입니다.
약간 다르긴 해도 지금 노래책에 있는 노래죠.
프로스트 형제는 자신이 만든 노래가 노래책에 실린 걸 알고는 매우 기뻐하면서
내가 만든 서투른 가사가 아름다운 3개의 구절로 다듬어졌다고 말했습니다.
원래는 프로스트 형제가 만든 이 노래, ‘증인들아 전진하여라’를 찾으실 수 있습니다.

en.text: Brother Erich Frost was a young man in Germany
who set a good example in making wise decisions early in life.
He was born in 1900, baptized 23 years later,
and entered the full-time ministry in 1928.
Not long after, he was put in charge of the underground work
of the persecuted Witnesses of Jehovah in Germany,
caring well for that assignment for eight months
until he was incarcerated.
In this archived audio recording,
you will hear the fascinating experience of how Brother Frost
composed a Kingdom melody in the middle of Sachsenhausen
—a Nazi concentration camp.
I always had the desire to compose music.
As everybody knows, we had the hardest work
and suffered the hardest in the concentration camps.
We were starved, the labor
exceeded our strength, and the harassment was often unbearable.
So, as usual, I wanted to find a way to build up the brothers.
We had such a fine unity there in the Sachsenhausen camp.
I felt moved to compose a song
that we could sing together for our mutual encouragement.
Every morning we marched to the construction site
of a sewage plant in Oranienburg.
Our labor group consisted of about 40 brothers
under the strict watch of the SS.
While marching, my mind went back and forth
and “Bum Bam Badam Bam Tarambambamba.”
And gradually, a melody formed.
That’s how the music was developed.
But how could the verses enter the camp
without being able to write them down?
I found a few brothers who helped me.
I repeated the first verse to one of them until he knew it by heart,
either while marching or while driving the wheelbarrow at work.
I told the second verse to another brother,
still to others the third and the fourth.
In the evening, I asked each of the brothers to recite his verse.
That’s how the song came to life.
In the mornings, when the 40 of us were marching
through the streets of Oranienburg, we already felt worn out.
When one started humming that melody,
the entire labor group trembled with excitement.
We had to control ourselves to not break out in loud singing.
That would have been dangerous, of course.
They would have brought us back to the camp
and severely punished us.
As we sat together in the evenings and someone started humming that melody,
quite a number of us sang along, and we rejoiced.
Our eyes were shining.
This gave us new courage and hope.
We also had evenings of worship.
Talks were given, and we had copies of The Watchtower that we studied together.
So we were able to have some real times of peace
and special encouragement and felt uplifted by that song.
Brother Frost, who was one of the anointed,
finished his earthly course in 1987.
After World War II and nine years of imprisonment,
he served as the overseer of our branch office
in Germany for ten years.
This was before the arrangement was instituted
of having a Branch Committee oversee the work.
The very descriptive paintings that you saw in this segment
were painted by a brother who was imprisoned
in a concentration camp similar to the one Brother Frost was in.
And I’m sure you recognized the song.
You can find it in our songbook, though the tune is a little different.
When Brother Frost found out that his song had been included in it,
he was overjoyed and said, “My clumsy lyrics
were transformed into three wonderful verses.”
If you turn to song 17 in your songbook,
you’ll find the song originally composed by Brother Frost
—“Forward, You Witnesses!”

ko.text: ‎‪가족의 영성을 지키는 ‎‪아주 훌륭한 방법 한 가지는
‎‪가족이 서로 더 가까워지게 ‎‪해 준다는 걸 잘 보여 줍니다.
‎‪다양한 날씨와 멋진 경치를 보면 ‎‪절로 감탄이 나오죠.
‎‪산을 몇 개 넘은 다음엔 ‎‪배를 타고 갑니다.
‎‪차에 탄 채로 강을 건너니까 ‎‪기분이 아주 색달랐어요.
‎‪여기 보시면, “모든 성경은 하느님의 ‎‪영감을 받은 것”이라고 했죠.
‎‪여긴 화장실이나 샤워 시설 같은 ‎‪편의 시설이 전혀 없죠.
‎‪씻을 수 있는 데가 ‎‪바이칼 호수뿐인데, 엄청 차가워요.
‎‪그래서 야외 봉사 모임을 할 때 ‎‪팀을 나누고,
‎‪경험상 보면, 옷차림이 사람들의 ‎‪호감을 얻는 데 도움이 될 수 있거든요.
‎‪어떤 경우엔 토의가 진행되는데, ‎‪대화가 길어질 때도 있어요.
‎‪잘 받아들이는 사람을 만날 때가 ‎‪더 많아서 참 힘이 나요.
‎‪이런 격지 봉사 덕분에 ‎‪아들이 영적으로 발전할 수 있었어요.
‎‪부모 입장에서, ‎‪가장 큰 축복이라고 할 수 있죠.
‎‪하지만 기도를 드리고 ‎‪첫 번째 집 문을 두드린 다음부터는
‎‪출판물을 보고 관심이 생겼을 때 ‎‪편지할 수 있게 말이죠.
‎‪캠프 파이어나 게임도 하고 ‎‪음악도 즐기면서 시간을 보내죠.
‎‪하루 중 전파 활동에 먼저 힘을 쏟고,
‎‪이 여행의 별미 중 하나는 ‎‪바이칼 오물이라고 하는
‎‪이렇게 격지 봉사를 하면서 ‎‪가족 사이가 더 튼튼해졌습니다.
‎‪여호와께서 우리의 노력을 축복해 ‎‪주신 걸 생각하면 너무 기쁩니다.
‎‪함께 영적인 일에 초점을 맞추는 ‎‪가족을 보면 늘 격려가 됩니다.
‎‪거의 봉사되지 않은 구역에서 ‎‪전파하는 데 관심이 있으신가요?
‎‪회중 봉사 위원회가 검토한 뒤 ‎‪해당 지부 사무실로 보낼 것입니다.

en.text: An excellent way of maintaining the spirituality of the family
is by spending quality time together in the ministry.
We would now like to introduce you to a family from Russia.
They traveled far away to work together
in unassigned territory in Siberia.
Their experience confirms how spiritual activities
not only build up our faith but can also bring our family
closer to each other.
We are traveling to a very interesting territory.
It is on the shores of Lake Baikal.
From where we live, it is 600 kilometers.
We have so many memories to take home.
The scenery is always stunning in all types of weather.
Here there are beautiful cliffs and valleys.
We cross several mountain passes.
Then we go by ferry.
It felt very strange being in the car while crossing the river.
When we have the opportunity, we witness
to people we meet on the way.
Why do sincere people trust the Holy Scriptures?
Please have a look at what it says here:
“All scripture is inspired of God.”
We usually serve in isolated territory for a week or more.
We have come to the same place where we were last year,
so we already know a lot about it.
Living in a tent
is very different from living in the city.
Here we don’t have
any conveniences, like a toilet or a shower.
The only place to wash is in Lake Baikal, which is freezing.
This simple life is like an adventure.
As we have quite a big group
—there are 12 of us —we have also organized
our spiritual routine.
We consider the daily text together and take part
in discussing our publications using the questions.
We have a friendly, relaxed atmosphere.
Everybody enjoys it.
Our isolated territory, where we are preaching,
is a rural area.
Here we don’t have any prepared maps.
So when we have our meetings for field service,
we divide up, all taking different streets.
We also think about what clothes to wear.
Experience has shown that our clothes
can help us to win over these people.
So we try to dress simply. We don’t wear ties.
The people there are kind.
Sometimes they even invite us in.
We can have discussions with some of them—sometimes long ones.
There you meet more receptive people
than unresponsive ones,
and that really is encouraging.
It makes you just want to keep on preaching
without stopping.
The trips have helped our son make spiritual progress.
For us as his parents, that is the greatest blessing.
For example,
after one of these trips, he became an unbaptized publisher.
This territory is different
from what I am used to, so I was worried.
I didn’t know what sort of people lived there
or what their attitude was toward Witnesses.
But after praying when knocking on the first door, my fear disappeared.
I was able to place 270 tracts.
While we were witnessing,
we showed the people the addresses in our publications
so that they could write
if they found what they had read interesting.
We usually start witnessing about 12 noon, and we finish
around 5:00 p.m.
Then the relaxation part of our day begins.
We have a campfire,
some games, some music, and fun.
Early in the day, we used our energy in the ministry,
and afterward we were able to relax and enjoy each other’s company.
So we combine both our ministry and relaxation.
One of the delights of these trips is the fish
—the famous Baikal omul.
These trips really strengthen the unity in our family.
We really have drawn closer together.
It is invigorating and enriches us spiritually.
We experience pure joy from knowing
that Jehovah has blessed our efforts.
We feel like we have our batteries charged for the entire year.
It is very encouraging to see
such a spiritually focused family.
And did you notice that it was after one such trip
that their son became an unbaptized publisher?
I’m sure that brought much joy to his parents.
Are you interested in a preaching assignment
in territory seldom worked?
If so, form a group of no more than 20 publishers
and ask the elders in your congregation for further instructions
and an Application for Territory Seldom Worked.
Once you have filled out the form, the Congregation Service Committee
will review it and submit it to your local branch.
